name: Aaron
bio: (Egypt: 13th century BC) Elder brother of Moses & his spokesman in Egypt. The Old Testament credits Jehovah as performing thru Aaron such miracles as causing Aaron's rod to blossom, although some modern magicians suspect conjuring skills. For example, his Rod-to-Snake effect reads like the old snake-charming trick of making the reptile go rigid & straight by pinching a nerve behind its head. During their flight from Egypt, the Hebrews made Aaron their first priest. However, during Moses' absence, he overreached himself by agreeing to make a golden calf for them to worship. This act angered Moses and brought Jehovah's punishment upon the nation. Aaron died during his people's subsequent wandering in the wilderness. The priesthood remained in his family and latter-day priests were wont to at least claim decendancy from him. [Ex.4.14-16; 6.20; 7.1-12; 28-32; Num.12; 17; 18; 20; 33.38, 39; Deut.10.6; Dif; CI]

name: Aaronson, Sam[uel]
bio: (Poland: 1901-9 Feb 1964) Immigrated with parents to USA in 1907. Inspired by & learned from public library magic books. Semi-promagician. Edited Twenty-Six Originals [1957,23pp]. Edited M-U-M 1957-64. Wrote Sam Aaronson Lecture #1 (18pp). Trick in HMM.

name: Aasen, Einar
bio: (Norway: 7 Apr 1902-12 Dec 1984) Merchant in Sandefjord, Norway. Amateur magician noted for skilful manipulation. [St]

name: Aba-Daba
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 24 Jan 1947- ) Stage name of Carlos Emilio CALDERÓN RAMÍREZ. Learned in 1960 from school friend. Civil engineer in Mexico City. Semi-pro comedy close-up & stage magician since 1971. Article in New Invocation. [Wh3]

name: Abbott, Annie
bio: (Milledgeville, Georgia, USA: 1861--15 Nov 1915) Born Dixie Annie Jarratt, marrying Charles N. Haygood. At age 17. Began performing in 1885 in imitation of Lulu Hurst. Billed as "The Little Georgia Magnet". Toured her famous weight-&-strength-resistance act in England (1891, 1910-11), the Continent & Egypt (1892), Russia (1893), & USA 1893-96 when temporarily retired until 1904-1911 when again toured until permanently retired. She was followed by many imitators who performed as “Annie Abbott” and “Annie May Abbott” who performed in New Zealand (1899-1900), Australia (1900), and India (1913), and continued to as late as 1918..[LR5/2003;Daw#179-182;Pr;Wal]

name: Abbot, Anthony
bio: See: Oursler, Fulton

name: Abbott, David P [helps] "Dave
bio: (Falls City, Nebraska: 22 Sep 1863-12 Jun 1934) Inspired by school show of the Obedient Ball. Wealthy businessman & loan shark. Amateur magician who performed for invited guests in his private theater in his home. Perfected the Talking Teakettle in 1907. Invented the Talking Vase in 1909. Wrote Behind the Scenes with the Mediums (1907, 328pp; 5th ed revised, 1916, 328pp), The Marvelous Creations of Joseffy (1908, 24pp), The History of a Strange Case (1908, 50pp), The Spirit Portrait Mystery (1913), and the posthumously published David P. Abbott's Book of Mysteries (1977, 183pp). Articles in Open Court Magazine. [Pr; Sphinx3/19]

name: Abbott, Percy
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 3 May 1886-26 Aug 1960) Orphaned at age 8. Became interested in magic at age 12. Left home at age 14 to tour vaudeville circuits in Australia. Pro performer. Manager of H.L. Hutchinson's "New York Novelty Company" in Sydney 1909-Oct 1911. Then on own as dealer in his "Magician's Supply Depot" in Sydney since late 1911. Leaving his business to brother Clarence, Percy toured Australia & Far East 1914-24. Ghost show & "Hall of Novelties" shop in a Sydney arcade 1916. Moved to USA in 1925. Co-founder & co-owner (with Harry Blackstone) of the Blackstone Magic Company in Colon, Michigan, 1927-31. Founder-owner in 1933 (with Recil Bordner as junior partner since 1934) of Abbott's Magic Manufacturing Company in Colon. Retired in 1959. Pirated & marketed (since Dec 1933) "Doc" Zola's Squash, which became known as "The Trick that built the Abbott Magic Company". Similarly with Gwynne's Temple of Benares (since 1940). And again with Fox's Miracle Gimmick (by 1949). Invented (or so he claimed) Spotting the Block (by 1925), Bowl of Water Vanish (by 1940), Name It (miniature bar, by 1940), Fountain Bouquet (by 1940), Squeez-It (by 1940), & The Tiger (Feb 1940). Published Tops 1936-59. Wrote Abbott's Magic for Magicians (1934, 56pp), etc. Tricks in New Tops. Memoir is A Life Time in Magic (1960, 132pp). [McC;Se;Wal;Des;Ho]

name: Aboukir
bio: See: Bouche, Albert

name: Abrams, Max
bio: (New York City, New York: 7 Oct 1935-13 Feb 1998) Inspired around age 8 & learned at age 11 from Carrington's The Boy's Book of Magic at school library. In Los Angeles since 1943 & a lawyer there since 1959. Vintage jazz buff. Amateur magician & mentalist. Semi-pro used magic book seller since c1983. Published Fifth Dimensional Telepathy & edited a collation of Annemann's $50.00 Manuscript (1976). Wrote Annemann: The Life and Times of a Legend (1992, 8+619pp). Reviews in Genii since 1987. [LR11/91;Wh]

name: Absolon, Blanka
bio: (Prague, Czechoslovakia: 26 Nov 1944- ) Stage name of Blanka Ocelíková. Learned in 1961 from husband Karel. Part-time model & guide to historical Prague. Pro magicienne since 1973, as husband's partner (as the "Duo Absolon") with classical magic & historical illusion acts, which latter won the 1988 Dragon Award. Also does solo act as an alchemist. Mother of Lucie & Petr Absolon. [Wh2]

name: Absolon, Karel
bio: (Zelvice, Czechoslovakia: 28 Apr 1940- ) Stage name of Karel Ocelik. Learned at age 16 from high school classmate. Electrotechnical engineer until turned full-time magician in 1973. With partner-wife Blanka works as "Duo Absolon" (in USA as "The Absolons") both a classic magic act & a medievally-themed one, which latter won the Dragon Award in 1988. Also lectures. Has played USA (3 times), Japan, Korea, & Africa, mainly at magic convention galas. Several TV shows. Invented Key Routine (1972), Illusion with Witch (1977), Cane to Live Snake (1983), & Four Legs Five Hands (1985). Their daughter Lucie & son Petr work both with them & as separate acts. [Wh2]

name: Absolon, Lucie
bio: (Prague, Czechoslovakia: 12 Feb 1969- ) Stage name of Lucie Ocelíková, daughter of Blanka & Karel. Learned since childhood from parents. Pro stage & close-up magicienne since age 18. Also a tap dancer. Does a science-fiction themed show featuring the Electrical Lady & Appearing Motorcycle. Sometimes works in parents act. Invented Appearing Motorcycle on Park Bench (1988). [Wh2]

name: Absolon, Petr
bio: (Prague, Czechoslovakia: 9 Dec 1967- ) Stage name of Petr Ocelík, son of Blanka & Karel. Learned from childhood from parents. Pro since age 18, specializing in comedy stage magic, magical MC, & tap dancing. Pet effects: routine with Coca Cola boxes & levitation of shoe. Sometimes works in parents act. [Wh2]

name: Acer, David [pronounced ACK-er]
bio: (Montreal, Canada: 27 Feb 1970-) Debuted in comedy magic as “The Running Gags” trio with Rick Bronson & Richard Sanders ca1990. Pro stand-up comedian and magician in Montreal plus each half-year on tour. Invented Quartermain (1984) & Nomem Omen (1991). Wrote Natural Selections & Synergy: The Commercial Magic of David Acer (1999) with German tr by Oliver Erens as Die Magie des David Acer (1999, 148pp). Tricks in Magic Manuscript (1985) & Linking Ring (1998 Parade). [LR4/98]

name: Achmed Ali Bey
bio: See: Bey, Achmed Ali

name: Ackerman, Allan
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 13 Oct 1947- ) Inspired around age 9 seeing a full-evening show. USO shows 1964. Math lecturer (MA) at U of Nevada at Las Vegas 1971-present. Proprietor of computer store. Semi-pro close-up & card magic. Wrote Effects from the Magic Mafia (1970), The Esoterist (1970, 45pp), Here's My Card (1978, 109pp), & Las Vegas Kardma (1994, 176pp). Also several books for the GBC on gambling. Tricks in Genii & Technomagic. Video. Video bit (1994) & video series (1997). [Wh]

name: Ackermann, Dr Aaron
bio: (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: 26 Jun 1901- ) Urologist in Rio de Janeiro. Semi-pro magician as "Prof. Aronack". Wrote Segredos da Magia (1934) & O Mágico das Salas (1949) plus many pieces in Rio's daily newspaper Correio da Manhã. Founding President of the Colégio Brasileiro de Mágicos in 1963 & 1st Editor of its journal Magus. [Quatro Ases9/79]

name: Ackermann, Georg
bio: (Germany: 1889-13 Apr 1968) Pro magician. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Bird Cage. Father of Trikson, a boy manipulator who played the Scala, and Constanze (Ursula Ackermann), a magicienne in the 1950s & 60s.

name: Ackermann, Pedro
bio: (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: 11 Jun 1904-18 Jan 1932) Amateur, aka "Pearson". Younger brother of Dr Aaron Ackermann with whom he co-authored Segredos da Magia (1934).

name: Acoba, Robert (Bobby)
bio: (Makawao, Maui: 1939 - 13 May 2011) Professional bartender and bar magician. Attended Waipahu High School. He was a bartender at the Ilikai Hotel when he started going to a local magic shop to learn some tricks to perform for bar patrons. Worked in Aaron's, Nicholas Nickolas, Nick's Fishmarket, Chart House, Red Vest, the Ilikai at poolside and at the Top of the I, and Honolulu Club.

name: Adachi, Ryuko
bio: (Japan: 20 Jul 1896-13 Oct 1982) Became an apprentice of Kimura Malini in Osaka. Pro since 1922. Moved to Tokyo after WWII. Audiences liked his magic with comical touch. Awarded the Geijutsusai Shorei Sho [Art Encouragement Prize] by Japan government in 1966. Past President of Nihon Kijutsu Kyokai [Japanese Professional Magicians Association] in 1967. Performed for the Emperor Hirohito at his birthday party in 1971.

name: Adair, Alan
bio: (England: fl.1st decade of 1900s-1910s) Stage name of Basil Leakey. Pro, living in Sydenham. Trick in Magic (1905). Played St. Georges Hall in Sep 1917.

name: Adair, Ian [Hugh], MIMC
bio: (Kilmarnock, Ayrshire, Scotland: 20 Dec 1940 [sic]-) At age 7 or 8 inspired by & learned from a gift box of tricks & The Boys Book of Magic. Amateur debut at charity benefits, specializing in dove and childrens magic. Pet effect: Catching Doves in a Net. Pro since 1957 when he joined Supreme Magic Co as assistant to Edwin Hooper. In 1960 used stage name of "MagicIAN Adair". Made MIMC in 1972. General Manager of Supreme Magic Co since 1987. Now (1995) owner of Abracadair Magic Ltd in Barnstaple, Devon. Inventor or improver of over 3,000 effects, all marketed. Prolific author with over 150 books & booklets on magic & allied arts, including the popular 5-volume Encyclopedia of Dove Magic (1968-87) & The Encyclopedia of Children's Magic (1991, 414pp). Editor of Trixigram & Magical Express (1994-96, 10 issues). Many articles in Genii, Abra, Magigram, New Pentagram, Wizard, Magic Wand, Magical Digest, Budget, MUM, etc. 4 Linking Ring awards for "Parades". [LR9/04Wh2]

name: Adair, Popo
bio: See: Roberts, Allan

name: Adami
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 21 Jul 1891-5 May 1945) Stage name of Willi Adamczewski. In 1934 appeared with Helmut Schreiber & 2 other magi in a Berlin radio magic special, Germany's 1st. Died in Berlin. [Roh]

name: Adams, Eddie J [oseph]
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 29 Mar 1924-) Inspired at age c7 when father taught him Rattle Bars. Learned from books. Semi-pro magician (illusions, sleight-of-hand, hypnotism, & vent) since age 13 in New Orleans. Assistant-wife is Anna. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Thumb Tie. Articles in Linking Ring & MUM. 1987 Abbott's Get-Together 1st place for vent. [MUM4/89;MUM6/64;Wh2]

name: Adams, Ernest Henry, MIMC
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Surveyor. Amateur magician. Co-founded (with Neil Weaver & Herbert J. Collings) The Magic Circle in 1905. REF: Peter Warlock in New Pentagram (Jul 1988), 44-45.

name: Adams, Graham, MIMC
bio: (Carlisle, England: 15 Nov 1893-21 May 1974) Skilled part-time pro cardman. Disciple of Erdnase (the book). Friend of John Martin. A teacher of Bobby Bernard. Wrote & privately issued a few copies of small but valuable works, including Mr. Erdnase: His Book (1931, 31pp, in 6 copies). Wrote "The Card Work of Graham Adams" series in The Pentagram, reprinted in The Best of Pentagram Card Magic (1990), 141-228.

name: Adams, Jack
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro stage magician since 1974 while a student at Florida International U. His assistant 1974-c1977 was Diane Bray. Now works out of New York City. Known for his polished role as "Merlin the Magician".

name: Adams, S[oren] S[orenson] "Sam
bio: (Aarhus, Denmark: 1869-20 Oct 1963) Brought to USA at age 2. Pro wholesale maker of magic props & joke items (S.S. Adams Co.) in New Jersey since 1906. In 1918 bought Theodore DeLand's entire line of trick cards & gaffed decks. Designed the Adams' League Deck of marked cards. In the 1940s his 40,000 square-foot factory had 90 employees. In 1949 he absorbed his main competitor, Jules Traub's Fun, Inc. The company is still (2002) in existence (in Neptune, New Jersey), passed to his son Joseph "Bud" Adams (born c1917) and thence to grandson Chris Adams. Adams was a world-class practical joker. Invented over 650 joke-shop items, of which he patented 40, including the world-infamous Sneeze Powder (1906), Bingo Shooting Device (1907), Snake Can (1908), Dribble Glass (c1908), & Joy Buzzer (1932). [Zo]

name: Adanos
bio: See: Eriksson, Hilding

name: Adelphia, Del
bio: (USA: -10 Feb 1917) Billed as "The Cowboy Magician". Minor pro in Western states, then moved East after his brother, Jack Adelphia, was caught stealing some of Raymond's props for him. Pet effect: the Vanishing Bird and Cage, which, after his death, brother Jack sold to Blackstone in 1918. [Pr]

name: Adrion, Alexander
bio:
(Berlin, Germany: 17 Nov 1923 – 27 Feb 2013) Stage name of Gerhard Engelsleben. Interested in magic since age 13, studying it under Conradi next year. Studied philosophy & psychology in university. Pro in West Germany since 1949, specializing in what he calls "Kammerspiele des Scheins" [Chamber Magic] & insists is a "fine art". 1950 Munich Gold Medal. Toured throughout Europe, performing & lecturing on the philosophy & history of magic. Retired in 1990. Avid magic collector. Wrote Zauberei, Zauberei (1968), Die Kunst zu Zaubern (1978), Taschen-Diebe (1992, 160pp), etc. Articles. A 4-part TV documentary film Houdini (1968). TV documentary on Robert-Houdin (1969). See DuMont, Adrion's ZauberKabinet (1980). [Daw#197;Win;Des;Wh2]

[See also: de Lille, Adrien de Lille, Victor]

name: Ady, Thomas, M.A.
bio: (Britain: fl.1600s) A non-magician. Wrote A Candle in the Dark (1655, 172pp; with 1990s facsimile reprint) to refute King James' Demonologie (1603), which was itself a credulous witch-hunting refutation of Reginald Scot's secular Discouerie of Witchcraft (1584). Ady's chapter titled "The Juggler" (pp28-46) lists the common magic tricks & describes the style of performance in his time. [CI;TS]

name: Agapis, Die
bio: (Germany: 18 Aug 1941-) Stage name of Jürgen Heinz. Illusionist. 1978 MZvD 1st prize in illusion; 1979 FISM 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Agnoly, Christian Natale
bio: (Klagenfurt, Austria: 14 Dec 1902-) Educated in Austria, Italy, & USA (high school). Moved to USA. Tile salesman in Bridgeport, Connecticut. Took private magic lessons from F.E. Powell & Agosta Meynier. Semi-pro private shows. [SAM]

name: Agosta-Meynier
bio: (Nimes, France: 9 Oct 1861-16 Dec 1942) Stage name of Auguste Meynier. Pro since age 13 (1874). In 1903 became founding-President of the Association Syndicale des Artistes Prestidigitateurs. Edited its journal, Le Prestidigitateur, 1919-25. Quit the ASAP in 1928 to found the Syndicat International des Artistes Prestidigitateurs & become its President 1928-39. Had the largest collection of magic books in France. [Dif;Go2;Vo55;St]

name: Agoston, Chevalier Gustav
bio: (Ödenburg [now Sopron], Hungary: 5 Nov 1826-10 Mar 1897) Stage name of [Carl] August Böhm. Pro with Cups-&-Balls, etc, since 1861. Moved to Switzerland 1870-71. Toured a riverboat magic & ghost show on the Rhine in 1872. Lost all his money in 1892 & died in a Berlin poorhouse. Father of Willy Böhm. [Dif;St;Vo57;Cl]

name: Agrippa von Nettesheim
bio: See: Arnold, Th. F. K.

name: Aguilar, Conde de
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 21 Jan 1909-13 Feb 1988) Stage name of Saúl Fernandes d'Aguilar. Pro debut in 1926 with a fakir act, later (by 1936) as illusionist. Moved to Barcelona for 12 years. Worked with assistant-wife "July" (Júlia Domene Cruz de Aguilar). His exposés on Portuguese TV in 1954 were deplored by local magicians. Toured Morocco, Portuguese colonies, France, England, Germany, Greece, Egypt, & Argentina (1969 & 1974). [Cam]

name: Aguinaldo, Don
bio: (São Clemente, Loulé, Portugal: 8 Sep 1909-9 Jul 1976) Stage name of Aguinaldo RAMOS CONDUTO. Pro illusionist since 1939. Toured Spain with circus in 1945. Played the Coliseu in Lisbon in 1946. Died after a fatal heart attack during performance with the Portuguese Circus. [Cam]

name: Ah Foon
bio: See: Little, George

name: Ah Hing
bio: See: Hing [Sr.], Ah

name: Ah Ling Soo
bio: See: Dew, Danny

name: Ahmad, Professor
bio: (Charkhari, India: 23 Oct 1865-dead by 1950s) Stage name of Mirza Ahmad Husain. A Muslim, his father was a district magistrate. Pro since 1890, featuring a Western-style magic act. [Magic6/02,12/04]

name: Aich, Jewel
bio: (Piroj Pur, West Pakistan [now Bangladesh]: 10 Apr 1950-) Inspired as boy seeing local folk magicians, learned at age 6 by "imitating a circus-magician without anybody's help". High school principal & non-fiction writer. Semi-pro illusionist by 1971, full-time since 1980s. Specializes in illusions, mental magic, & close-up. Pet effects: Aga, Cups & Balls, Milk Can Escape, the Buzz-Saw, & his own Giant Disecto as a head-chopper. Tours a full-evening show. Billed as "The World's Most Artistic Illusionist" & praised by Sid Lorraine & Elizabeth Warlock, among others. His principal assistant (& wife since 1985) is Bipasha (born 1960). Four world tours: 1982, 1986, 1988, 1989. He is not only the leading magician in Bangladesh but also its top paid entertainer. Invented Giant Disecto (1981), Flower Garden from Nowhere (1984), Invisible Flight of Bipasha (1986), Wonderful Rhythm (1987), etc. TV bits. [MC11/89;Wh2]

name: Aimes. Richard
bio: (Phoenix?, Arizona: fl.1980s) Originally a chimney sweep. Self-taught from books as child in Phoenix. A Chavez graduate. Pro magician, billed as "The Magic Chimney Sweep". [Mag]

name: Ainslie, Arthur
bio: (Britain: c1871-13 Jan 1940) Stage name of Arthur Wellesley Odell Pain, aka "F.M. Archer". Student of Devant. Pro kid-show magician since 1910s. Played St. George's Hall in 1914. Wrote Water Wizardry (1922). Retired from magic in 1926. [CI]

name: Airaksinen, Aino [pronounced IGH-rahk-si-nen]
bio: (Nilsiä, Finland: 6 Jul 1948-) Partner-wife of Jorma Airaksinen as "Finn Aspen" or "The Asps". [Win2]

name: Airaksinen, Jorma
bio: (Paltamo, Finland: 6 Oct 1942- ) Self-taught at age 12. Pro since 1973. Does manip act (with doves & poodles) & illusions. NMK Nordic Champion 1975, 1976, 1986. 1976 FISM 3rd prize in general magic under stage name "Bolen". Later (with wife Aino Airaksinen) as "Finn Aspen" or "The Asps". Has worked nightclubs throughout Europe. TV bits in Scandinavia & Spain. [Win2]

name: Airaksinen, Olavi
bio: (Finland: 20 Feb 1945-) Pro in Finland. 1963 Magic Circle 1st Prize & "Young Magician of the Year".

name: Akamatsu, Yoichi
bio: (Sakai City, Osaka, Japan: 25 Jul 1943-) Learned since 1956 from books. Bridge engineer. Amateur magician specialized in close-up. Pet effect: Coins thru Table. 1971 [sic] Tenkai Prize. Wrote Yoichi Akamatsu's Creative Works in Magic (1972, in Japanese). Invented Dice thru Table routine in 1985. Many tricks in Svengali. [Wh2] Äkerlind, Jonnie SEE: "Casino, Jonnie"

name: Akopian, Arutian
bio: (Igdir, Turkey: 25 Apr 1918-13 Jan 2005) Of Armenian parents who moved to Soviet Armenia. Inspired at age 20 seeing a magician. Pro stage magic & sleight-of-hand with cards, silks, etc. People's Artist of the Armenian SSR. Wrote a booklet (Fokusı na Estradzie) of 50 magic tricks in Russian in 1964. Also wrote Fokusı i Fokusniki & W świecie dziwów (1982?, 111pp, in Polish). Played the Friedrichstadtpalast in East Berlin in 1974. 1974 Karlovy Vary 2nd prize in manip. [Win; Genii8/65] "Al the Only" SEE: Ulman Jr, Al

name: Alachini
bio: (Łomża, Poland: 28 Aug 1895-16 May 1970) Stage name of Bronisław Szymański. Moved to Germany. Machinist & watchmaker in Germany. Worked as prop maker for Bartl & Willmann in Hamburg in early 1920s. Pro illusionist. Returned to Poland in 1948. Teacher of Janusz Gozdzik. Died in Koszalin. [Mec]

name: Aladdin, Johnny
bio: (Bridgeport, Connecticut: 23 Apr 1919- ) Stage name of John Joseph "Jack" Randall. Of Irish extraction. Learned at age 13 from magic set & as member of YMCA magic club. Pro since 1940, specialized in close-up, illusions, & hypnotism. Student of Tenkai in Hawaii 1941-44. A specialty in 1958 was shirt-pulling. Marketed his "Video" ESP trick in 1958. Star performer in Far East c1959-c1964. In USA c1965. In Vietnam c1966-c69 with Japanese partner-wife "Taki" (see). From 1975 until c1986 worked with Chinese assistant-wife "Lani" (see). Toured Europe in 1981. Worked Las Vegas c1986-89. Father of Kelley Randall. [NT8/89;HMM9/58;Wh2]

name: Aladin [also Aladyn]
bio: (Chodorow, Poland: 1941- ) Stage name of Jerzy Stryjski. Pro illusionist-manipulator with assistant "Miriam". [Mec]

name: Alain le Magicien
bio: See: Chahin, Alain

name: Alakazam, Henri
bio: (Sjaelland, Denmark: 14 Dec 1934-) Stage name of Henry Hermansen. Inspired at age 7. Pro comedy magic with assistant-wife Ann Christiansen (ex-ballet dancer) to whom he taught magic. [Dif] "Alan, A. J." SEE: Lambert, Leslie

name: Alan, Alan
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-90s – 4 $ ^{th} $ July 2014) Stage name of Alan Rabinowitz. Popular pro escape artist for many years since the 1940s, working theater, cabaret, & circus shows. Invented the Burning Rope escape in 1948 & Sharpshooter (bullet thru chosen card). In 1980s was a pro dealer-demonstrator in London (as manager of the late Tommy Cooper's "Magic Spot"). 2 audios.

name: Alan, Don
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 22 Feb 1926-15 Apr 1999) Stage name of Donald Alan McWethy. Chavez graduate 1947. Protégé of John Snyder Jr & Bert Allerton. Pro close-up since 1949. Bartender-magician at Schulien's 1951-54. TV "Magic" weekly series (26 half-hour shows) in Chicago 1952-53; ABC-TV "Magic Ranch" (13 half-hour shows) 1961. Many TV bits with Sullivan (1960 & 1961), Carson, Allen, Douglas, etc. Wrote Close-Up Time with Don Alan (1951, 20pp; repr 1970), Pretty Sneaky (1956, 48pp; repr 1960 & 1968), & The Rubber Circus (1958, 15pp). Tricks in New Phoenix. Video (1988). Bio and collected tricks is Jon Racherbaumer, In a Class by Himself: The Legacy of Don Alan (2001, 309pp). In 1989 Mike Rogers wrote that "Don Alan is the most copied professional close-up magician in history". Many would agree. Died in San Diego of Alzheimer's complications. [Wh]

name: Alan, Wayne
bio: (Washington, D.C.: fl.1970s-80s) Learned at age 10 from library books. Pro stage illusionist & close-up magician. Pet effect: Ultimate Zig Zag, which he invented. Wrote Patented Illusions (1980, 80pp). Works with assistant-wife Sandy. FISM 1st prize in grand illusion. Operated the 700-seat Annapolis Theatre of Magic 1986-87 in Annapolis, Maryland. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Alban & Stella
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-80s) Learned as a child. Pro on East Coast with a pseudo-Chinese act. Worked mainly country fairs & carnivals. [HMM6/54] SEE UNDER: Coussinet, Adrien

name: Alban, Jack
bio: (France: fl.1950s-90s) Stage name of Alban Ducret. Pro with electric magic act. Played Casino Estoril in 1975. President of SNIVS 1984-present. [Mer]

name: Alban's
bio: See: De Valette, Henry

name: Albany
bio: See: Coussinet, Adrien

name: Albany, A.-Jean
bio: (Switzerland: 28 Jun 1873-9 Sep 1940) Stage name of A.-Jean Goldschmitt. Moved to France. Amateur. [Rob;Dam]

name: Albee, E[dward] F[ranklin]
bio: (Machias, Maine: 8 Oct 1857-11 Mar 1930) Vaudeville impresario. As chief aide to B.F. Keith, succeeded on the latter's death in 1914 to ownership or control of some 1,500 theaters across the USA & Canada, virtually dominating vaudeville in those countries until 1927 when Joseph P. Kennedy acquired the majority of Keith-Albee stock. A ruthless businessman, Albee reportedly coined the motto "Never give a sucker an even break" later (1941) made famous by W.C. Fields. [Lau; WWWA; Var]

name: Albenice, [John] “Al
bio: (USA: 1913-3 Dec 1957) New York resident. Pro, beginning with silent illusion act in carnival side-shows & amusement parks. In late 1930s switched to intimate magic with patter, working mainly niteclubs. Played the New York Palace in 1951 & 1954. Invented Serpent Silk in 1941. Wrote Reel Magic (1941, 55pp; 2nd rev ed 1950, 82pp). Died in New York City of heart attack. [HMM11/49,10/51,1/58]

name: Alber, Professeur
bio: (Saumur, Maine-et-Loire, France: 24 Jun 1858-26 Jun 1941) Stage name of [Jean-Jacques-]Édouard Graves. Pro salon magician. Joined the ASAP in 1905. Wrote numerous works, notably Les grands trucs de la prestidigitation (1904), De l'illusion (1909), Manuel du prestidigitateur (1927), La prestidigitation moderne (1927), & Une, deux ... disparaissez (1930). Autobio is Trente années d'un art mystérieux (1924). Many articles in magic magazines. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Albert, Montague
bio: (South Africa: c1866-7 Feb 1916) Stage name of Armstrong, aka "Professor Albert". Pro. Played England where he lived much of his life until returning home in 1901 with latest sleights & illusions, including the Aerial Fishing. [St;Magic12/01]

name: Alberti
bio: See: Pickman, Jean-Lambert

name: Alberti, Giuseppe Francesco Antonio
bio: (Italy: fl.1740s) Scientist. Wrote I Giuochi Numerici: fatti Arcani Palesati [Numerical Games: Arcane Facts] (Bologna: 1747; repr in Venice 1780, 1788, 1795, and in Naples 1814). Borrowed from English, French, & German books. The illustrations (16 engraved plates for later editions) were taken from Ozanam's book (1st ed 1756). A copy of the 1788 3rd edition was auctioned for $2,420 in 1990 by Swann Galleries who also auctioned a 1795 4th edition in 1993 for $1,870. [St]

name: Alberti, Gustav
bio: (France: fl.1860s-70s) Pro card magician in French provinces 1860-75. Invented the Ambitious Card & the Rising Cards from a hand-held tumbler. One of his few contemporaries mentioned by Robert-Houdin. [Cl;Vo55]

name: Albertini de Roubaix
bio: (Sémeries, Nord, France: 9 Mar 1884-10 Oct 1944) Stage name of Adolph-A. Géhéniaux. Pro debut at age 18. Charter member of CSP 1904. Joined the ASAP in 1921.

name: Alberto, Professor
bio: (England: fl.1870s-1890s) Stage name of Albert Tiltman. Amateur magician to pro stage illusionist c1874. Toured India in 1875. Did the Sands of the Desert trick by 1892. [Cl;Pr]

name: Alberto, Professor Harold
bio: (Australia: 14 Aug 1882-10 Jun 1964) Stage name of Harold McAuliffe. Pro comedy magician in Australia & New Zealand since 1901, touring the vaude circuits. Billed as "The Gay Deceiver". Pet effect: Growing Plant, using the "more water" line as running gag. Toured England in 1915. Moved to USA in 1922. Technical advisor, coach, & technical director in Hollywood. In sanitarium for nervous breakdown in 1951. A suicide. [Wal; Magic2/03] (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Albert E. Borkland. Wrote Entertaining: Conjuring & Mind Reading (1909, 118pp), of which 73 pages are on conjuring.

name: Albertus Magnus
bio: (Lauingen, Swabia, Bavaria: 1193 [or 1206]-15 Nov 1280) Born Albert Graf von [Count of Bollstadt. German philosopher, teacher, & scientist. Joined the Dominican order c1223. Wrote on theology (his famous Summa theologiae) & natural science (including alchemy). Teacher of St. Thomas Aquinas. Sainted in 1662 and in 1931 made the patron saint of students of the natural sciences. Said by some authorities to have practiced magic. Bio is A. Garreau, Saint Albert le Grand (1932). [Daw;Dif] Albini, Lieut. Fred Albini, Herbert A. "Bert" (Norwich, England: May 1851-13 Feb 1930) Stage name of Frederick Baxter Ewing. Pro by 1881 until retired c1915. [Pr;Vo56] (Poland: 1860-29 [sic] May 1913) Born Abraham Laski, aka "Rosini" & "Albini the Great". Polish Jew who immigrated at age 6 months to England where his family name was unknown even to his wife. Moved to USA in 1891. By 1911 he tropped with 12 assistants. Invented Galatea (early 1880s) & the Albini Egg Bag (by 1891). Died of dropsy in Chicago. [Pr;Ch; Sphinx9/10; Magic4/03,3/10; HMM1/59]

name: Albino da Silva, João
bio: (Viana do Castelo, Portugal: 26 Jan 1869-4 Mar 1939) Debut in 1891. Pro illusionist. 1897 Concurso de Ilusionismo 1st place. Played Spain, France, Italy, Brazil, & Argentina. [Cam] Albo, Dr Robert J[ames] "Bob", MD, MIMC (Oakland, California: 8 May 1932 – 21 Feb 2011) General, vascular, & oncological surgeon in Piedmont, California. Physician for the Golden State Warriors, the Raiders, & formerly the A's. Amateur magician. Has world's largest and finest collection of antique magic props, with over 6,000 items plus 30 [sic] posters, all over 50 years old. Partner in the Palace of Magic shop on Pier 39 in San Francisco & junior partner in Magic Island at Newport Beach (& formerly of its Houston branch). 1984 AMA Special Fellowship. 1989 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1 video (forthcoming 1991). Co-authored 8 books on magic prop makers & their products, beginning with The Oriental Magic of the Bambergs (1973, 228pp). Also (with Deutsch & Johannsen), The Magic of Germany (1994), The Magic of America (1995, 103pp), & The Magic of Holland (forthcoming). [Bo#263;Genii7/88;Wh]

name: Albrecht, Don[ald Lee]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 29 May 1930-) Cartoonist, animator, art-director-producer. Amateur magician. Inspired seeing amateur uncle do card tricks. Learned age c12 from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set. Since c1972 illustrations & cartoons for Genii, Son of Bat Jr, Bat Droppings, Magic Manuscript, Arcane, & Epoptica. Authored The Magic Cartoons of Albrecht (1988, 50pp). [Wh]

name: Albright, Clayton
bio: (USA: fl.1970s) Collector, notably of antique apparatus.

name: Albright, Howard P.
bio: (USA: -15 Sep 1947) Dealer (Unique Magic Studio) by 1936 in Albany, New York, where since 1937 he published Inside Dope & Confidential Bulletin as house organs. Invented Uni-Mentality (1935) & The Gileegaloo Bird (by 1936). Wrote Super-Psychic Mental Effects (1933; repr 1948, 52pp), Super-Sensitive Fingertips (1933; repr 1948, 42pp), Mental Power! (1934), Peculiarities of the Pasteboards (1934), Klever Card Codes (1934, 35pp), Novelty Card Magic (1935), Cards-o-Destiny (1935), Slate Stunts [c1939], Publicity-Trix [c1940], Advanced Card Magic (1948, 23pp), Forbidden Wisdom (1948, 23pp), etc. Tricks in Tops. [St]

name: Albright, Michael
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s) Edited The Conjurer 1975-76.

name: Alcock, Dr James [Edward], PhD
bio: (Central Butte, Saskatchewan, Canada: 24 Dec 1942-) Learned at age 12 from books. Amateur close-up & mental magician since 1979. Psychology professor at York U, Toronto. Skeptical of telepathy & the paranormal, he wrote Science and Supernatural: A Critical Appraisal of Parapsychology (1990, 186pp). [Wh2]

name: Alden, Catherine
bio: See: Daniel, Cathy

name: Aldini
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 12 Oct 1917-Aug 1989) Stage name of Alex Weiner. Learned as kid. Pro. Moved to Southern California in 1945. Managed one of Merv Taylor's Disneyland shops for 7 years in the late 1950s to early 60s &, later, other shops including his own. As "Al Aldini" wrote 4 booklets: Rough Stuff (1956, 24pp, with Joe Berg); Roughingly Yours (1969, 48pp), New Concepts in Magic (1970, 37pp), & Novel Concepts with Cards (1970, 46pp). Video (1988). [Wh]

name: Aldrich, Charles T.
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 1870-20 Nov 1953) Joined circus at age 12. Pro. Entered vaudeville by 1899. Had 2 acts: as quick-change artist including magic when impersonating Ching Ling Foo & as a tramp juggler-magician. Toured top theaters of Europe 1899, 1901, 1902, 1906-14 (including in 1st Royal Command Variety Performance show in 1912). In 1914 played Abanazar role in Chin-Chin in this New York musical. Played the New York Palace in 1928. Retired in the 1930s. [Pr;Ch]

name: Aldrich, Steve
bio: (Fort Benning, Georgia: c1955-) Pro close-up & stage magician since 1974. [Genii9/88;Mag]

name: Alemaro
bio: (Mexico: 1970-) Stage name of Alejandro MARTINEZ ROSAS. Pro stage & closeup. Prize winner. [Ran]

name: Alex
bio: (Stara Sól, Poland: 1920- ) Stage name of Kazimierz Kuźma. Pro illusionist-manipulator with Polish circus. [Mec;Nad]

name: Alexander
bio: See: Heimbürger, Alexander Conlin [Sr], Claude Alexander

name: Alexander, David
bio: (Long Beach, CA 22 Dec 1943 - 14 Dec 2010) Magician/silhouette artist/writer. Original member of the Long Beach Mystics in mid-1950s. Mentored by José Frakson for seven years. In mid-1960s was first resident magician at the Hotel Claremont in San Francisco. First curator of the Carter Collection of rare magic and memorabilia. Several years as a cruise ship magician. First magician hired by Princess Cruises. Toured throughout Mexico and Central America, including 12-months in Acapulco. David presented his act in English, Spanish, French and Japanese, and performed on TV in the United States, Japan, Korea, the Philippines, Taiwan, Mexico, and Central America. David was also a professional silhouette artist, and his work can be found in collections around the world. Wrote The Complete Professional Pickpocket, the definitive work on stage pickpocketing 1979. Articles in magic magazines.

name: Alexander, Professor Max
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 31 Mar 1848-15 Sep 1924) Stage name of Carl Max Alexis Rhodin. Pro illusionist since 1880. Toured England (1872, 1880-86) & Latvia (1889-1905). His two successive assistant-wives were "Rhombello" & "Rosa Alexander". Father of "Brazil Jack" & "Max von Rhodin". "Authored" The Parlour Magician: A Handy Book for the Amateur Conjuror (London: 1876, 48pp), which was a stock book published by H.G. Clarke & Co to which Alexander merely added his own title page. [Dif;Vo58]

name: Alexander, Miss Rosa
bio: (Sundbyvester, Denmark: 10 Nov 1865-19 Jun 1946) Stage name of Augusta Petrine Josephine Alexander (née Krocs), 2nd wife of Max Alexander with whom she worked an anti-spiritualist cabinet act. Mother of "Max von Rhodin". [Dif]

name: Alfano
bio: (Germany: 2 May 1927-) Stage name of Heinz Mackenbach. Magician & magic collector. [Nad]

name: Alfie
bio: See: Moore, J. Paul

name: Alfini
bio: (Danzig, Germany [now Gdansk, Poland]: 31 May 1911-31 Mar 1983) Stage name of Hans Syllwasschy. Died in Schwerin, East Germany. [Roh]

name: Alfredson, James B[ernard] "Jim", AIMC
bio: (East Lansing, Michigan: 11 Feb 1937-) Part-time pro until mid-twenties. Amateur (ex-college teacher, editor) collector of magic magazines since c1954, now living in Lansing, Michigan. Edited Magicol 1973-88. Co-winner (with Daily) 1987 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote A Short Title Checklist of Conjuring Periodicals in English (1976, with George L. Daily Jr), the definitive A Bibliography of Conjuring Periodicals in English: 1791-1983 (1986, 395pp, with Daily), Newmann: The Pioneer Mentalist (1989; repr 1990, 60pp), & Jean Hugard (1997, 82pp). Article in Collectors' Forum. [Se;Wh2]

name: Ali, Hadji
bio: (Middle East: fl.1920s-30s) This Arab was a pro regurgitator of colored nuts and spouter of water & flame. A famous 1913 Friedländer poster, showing a water-spouter and billed as "Aly" from Egypt, is probably of him. Worked in US vaude (& Coney Island) in 1920s-30s. Played Sydney, Australia, billed as the "Egyptian Enigma". A short-subject color film of his act showed in US movie-houses in the late 1930s. Died in the USA in the 1940s. [Pr;Ch;HMM12/46,9/57]

name: Ali-Ben-Ali
bio: (USA: -15 Dec 1957) Stage name of Henry Gould. Did a Pauline-type hypnotism act, which he did on Raboid's ghost show in 1930s. Thence straight magic on cruise ships in 1950s. On Jack Paar's TV show in 1955. Died in New York City. [HMM2/55]

name: Ali Bey
bio: (Newark-on-Trent, England: 7 Jan 1905-Aug 1975) Stage name of David Charles Lemmy. Pro illusionist in late 1940s-50s with pseudo-Arabian act. [Hudd;Daw2]

name: Ali Bongo
bio: See: Bongo, Ali

name: Alipio
bio: (Spain: 1958-) Stage name of Alipio Rabazo. Pro street magician in Europe. [Ran]

name: Allan
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 10 Jan 1909-6 Jan 1990) Stage name of Albin Neumann. Ex-radio technician. Student of Larette and Arcano. Pro magician since 1925, working private parties in Europe & the Orient. After WW II lived in Vienna. Consultant to police on gambling & cheating methods. Died in Vienna. Wrote Die 4. Dimension (n.d.); Simsalabim (1953); Korrigiertes Glück (1954), about sharps; Falsche Geister; echte Schwindler (1969); & Mögliche Unmöglichkeiten (1982), etc. Co-edited (with Lang & Zerzawy) "Bibliographisches Lexicon der Magie". [Al;St]

name: Allan, Fred
bio: (Valongo, Portugal: 23 Nov 1955- ) Stage name since 1978 of Ivo Helder Welch MARTINS DE SOUSA, aka "Ivo". Amateur manipulator. 1979 Figueira da Foz 1st prize in manip. Wrote Início à Manipulação (1983, 49pp). [Cam]

name: Allan, Wilfrid, MIMC
bio: (Hornsey, England: 1904-27 Sep 1938) Pro society magician. Often played Maskelyne's. [Go2;St]

name: Allemann
bio: See: Mann, Al

name: Allen, Harry
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 30 Jan 1957-) Stage name of Harold Allen Gersl. Learned at age 10 hanging around Irv Cook's Daytona Beach Magic Shop (now simply Daytona Magic) where he later worked until 1976 when he become a partner and full-time magician. Specializes in close-up, particularly with cards & coins. Also tours with their "Magic Shop on Wheels". Wrote 6 books of comedy gags & one-liners: Sleight of Mouth (186pp), Sleight of Tongue in Cheek (23pp), Sleight of Foot in Mouth (21pp), Sleight of Lips (23pp), Sleight of One Liners (1991), Sleight of Tongue (19pp). Tricks in MUM. [Wh5]

name: Allen, Ken
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-80s-dead) Worked in Abbott's New York shop (by 1952). Pro performer-dealer-prop maker (Ken Allen Products) in Union City, New Jersey, from 1954 until sold in 1965 to Bob Follmer of Rochester, New York. Edited Allen's Attic 1954-62 (24 issues) as house organ. Invented Chinatown Quarter (by 1954), Jumping Gems (1954), George (1954), Soo-Zee (in 1950s), & Alvin the Chipmunk sucker card trick (1959). Marketed Carl Wolf's Lock of Gibraltar & Tom Seller's Monkey Bar (1955). Wrote Do-It-Yourself Lecture No.1 (1957, 29pp), Pilfered Patter No.1 (1958, 23pp), & Tips: Tricks, Ideas, Patter & Suggestions (1959, 56pp).

name: Allen, Len
bio: (Britain?: fl.1940s-50s) Anglo-Indian living in London. Pro stage (working as "Lenz") & demming at Hamley's in 1940s. Specialized in "Sightless Vision". Retired by early 1970s. [Wad]

name: Allen [Jr], Lyman [H.]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: c1911-18 Apr 1992) Engineer (until retired c1975). Semi-pro magic dealer, specializing in secrets. Invented Blok-Kord in 1941.

name: Allen, Paul
bio: (Bluff City, Tennessee: 4 Sep 1907-13 Aug 1961) Minor pro magician, actor, marionette worker. Aka "Paul Balfonte" & "Fra Diavolo". Toured with USO in 1943. Bio is William E. King Jr., "Fra

name: Allen, Rick
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 4 Nov 1939- ) Stage name of Frederick Allen Klycinski. Inspired at age 12 as stage volunteer. Moved to southern California in teens. Advertising executive. Semi-pro comedy magician. Since 1976 in northern California mainly producing & directing fund-raising shows (recently starring Dennis Loomis). Has toured Far East, India, & South America. [Wh2]

name: Allen, Robert "Rob
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 14 Dec 1950-) Stage name of Robert Allen Brozek. Learned at age 8 from Xmas magic set. Pro stage & stand-up since age 20. Married his assistant Carol in 1973. First worked niteclubs & cruise ships; then opening act; & now school shows, the Buffalo zoo, etc, near their Niagara Falls home. Also does a hyp act. President of PMA. Editor of State of the Art. Invented Open Front Doves to Duck 1970. [Wh5]

name: Allen, Stan MIMC
bio: (Oakland, California: 6 Apr 1950-) Stage name of Stan[ley] A[lbert] Sokolski. Learned at age 12 from sister's gift of a Disneyland trick. Joined Long Beach Mystics junior magic club at age 15. Influenced by Marvyn Roy and fellow members of the Mystics, developed at the Magic Castle in the early '70s. Pro comedy stage magician from 1971 until 1985, worked predominately cruise ships and comedy clubs, as well as producing corporate sales meetings and trade shows. Noted for his rabbit-puppet routine. Owner of The Magic Shop in Los Alamitos, California, 1973-77. Founding editor-publisher of Inside Magic 1985-91 and Magic Magazine 1991-present. Produces Magic Live! Convention (2001, 2004, 2007, 2009). 1993 AMA Award of Merit. 1998 Magic Circle John Nevil Maskelyn Award. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Allen, Steve
bio: (New York City, NY: 26 Dec 1921-30 Oct 2000) Radio disc-jockey to songwriter & star talk-show host of radio & TV. Learned from grandmother's gift of a magic set. Hosted TV's The Tonight Show 1953-57 & The Steve Allen Show 1956-61. Wrote over 50 popular books, including How To Be Funny (1987, 290pp) and Make 'Em Laugh (1993, 339pp). Died in LA of a heart attack. [Wh5]

name: Allen, Woody
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 1 Dec 1935- ) Stage & pen name of Allen Stewart Konigsberg. Famous American-Jewish comedian, author, actor, & filmmaker. Self-taught amateur magician since a young boy. Of the card tricks he does for friends he says "I get a sense of pleasure from it like a concert pianist putting his hands on the keys." Worked for Circle Magic on 51 $ ^{st} $ and Broadway, NY in the 1950s while also writing for Sid Caesar. Wrote The Floating Lightbulb (1982), a play about a magician, which had its world premier in Britain in 1990. Plays a magician in movie Scoop (2006). Bios are Eric Lax, Woody Allen (1991, 377pp) & Lee Guthrie, Woody Allen (1978, 183pp).

name: Allerton, [Albert Allan] "Bert
bio: (Lynn Center, Illinois: 1 Jan 1889-22 Feb 1958) Stage name of Albert Allen "Bert" Gustafson, of Swedish extraction. Interested for years; but inspired by 1934 SAM Convention to become semi-pro, learning that year from the Tarbell Course & became semi-pro in Chicago. Oil sales executive until 1939 when resigned to turn full-time pro close-up magician. As pro worked The House of Murphy in Los Angeles 1939-40, the Persian Room (Sir Francis Drake Hotel) in San Francisco 1940-41, & the Pump Room (Ambassador East Hotel) in Chicago 1941-55, plus the Cotillion Room (Hotel Pierre) in New York City 1941 & 1945. SAM President 1946-47. See Robert Parrish, Bert Allerton's The Close-Up Magician (1958, 73pp; repr 1964 & 1977) & Reinhard Müller, Allerton-Horowitz-Daley (1994/1996, 18pp). Allesi, Ron[ald] [LR12/2004;Genii6/94;LR6/96;St;Bo2;Sphinx6/45;Genii4/41;SAM] (Jamestown, New York: 31 Jan 1947- ) Learned magic in 1962. Pro school shows & USO (c1970-72). Major dealer since 1973 in Dunkirk, then since 1988 in Fredonia, New York, now Milford, Ohio. Covers all fields of magic, particularly antique & rare apparatus, books, & vent figures. Since 1980 plays only at private parties. [Wh]

name: Allison, S. "Tubby
bio: (England: fl.1940s) Woodworker for Walter Wandman in Birmingham in 1930s. Dealer (Star Magical Manufacturing Company) in Birmingham, late 1945-Jan 1949. Thence moved to Canada. [McC]

name: Allison, Van K.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Edited The Conjuring Record (Bronxville, NY) 1913-15 (24 issues).

name: Allport, Michael
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Pro illusionist with assistant-wife Jennifer, touring world & working in the Sarrasani Circus in 1968 & on cruise ships in the 1980s. Alma. The Mysterious (Malvern, Victoria, Australia: 18 Nov 1880-17 Mar 1956) Stage name of Oswald Henry Bishop. Son of a bootmaker. A tinsmith by trade. Possibly introduced to magic by making metal props for Alf "Czerny" Lumsden. Pro vaudeville illusionist since 1900, as "Alma", "Pang Sue Foon", & finally "Pharos" (1912-16). Toured Australia & New Zealand 1900-12. Deserted his family to tour Pacific Islands, Asia & USA 1913-1916 when he retired from stage. Moved in 1917 to Maui, Hawaii, where became businessman, getting US citizenship in 1920. Performed 2,000 hours with USO in WW II. Retired from business in 1946. Father of Will Alma. [Alm;Daw2]

name: Alma, Will, OAM, MIMC
bio: (Malvern, Australia: 4 Nov 1904-6 May 1993) Stage name since 1924 & legal name since 1949 of Oswald George William "Will" Bishop. Born into showbiz family, his father being "The Mysterious Alma". Learned from Devant's Magic Made Easy. Debut as amateur in 1918. Also worked as juggler in 1924 as "Will E. Dropit". Pro illusionist since 1926, touring his own show until 1931 when settled in Melbourne as proprietor of "The Alma Magical Company", a mail-order factory in Melbourne until 1940. Technician & chief assistant for Levante's "How's Tricks" show 1940. Mechanic with Tivoli Theatre 1945-48. Toured Korea & Far East with Army unit 1956. MIMC 1958. A heart attack in 1965 forced his retirement. Donated his fine collection of magicana (begun in the 1930s) to The State Library of Victoria in 1976. Again performing & working on the collection. In 1991 received the Order of Australia (OAM) from the Queen. Edited Will Andrade's Magical Review 1928-29 (6 issues), Will Alma's (Magical) Magazine 1934-38, Here's Tricks 1939-41 (8 issues), & The Magic Circle Mirror 1971-77. [Bo#209;LR9/89;Magicana#197;Wh2]

name: Almonacid Garcia, Agapito
bio: See: "Roden"

name: Alonzo, Ed
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Learned at age 7. Debut at age 10. Pro illusionist. 1983 AMA Junior Achievement Award (shared). [Mag]

name: Alpha
bio: (France: fl.1970s-90s) Pro stage magic. Silent act with birds (budgerigars). Played the Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1978-79. Wrote La magie des cartes pour la scène (1983) & La magie des perruches (1991, 60pp). Video bit (1994).

name: Al-Rex
bio: (France: fl.1960s) Stage name of André Huet. Pro illusionist with assistant-wife "Nidja". [Dif]

name: Alston, John
bio: (Jacksonville, Florida: 17 Feb 1917- ) Stage name of Alston Cockrell. Learned in 1927 from Xmas gift magic set. Actor/promoter. Pro magician with full-evening illusion show until retired in 1978. Pet effects: Sub Trunk, Aga Levitation, rope & coin routines. [Wh2]

name: Alstrand, William D. "Bill" "Poogie Poogie
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 26 Mar 1902- ) Stage name of Walter F. Moesmer. Pro with club & stage show, doing cards, silks, & small illusions. In US Army in WW II in the Pacific, Italy, & France. Did school shows in 1960s. Tricks in Genii & HMM. [WWM]

name: Altani, Oskar
bio: (Germany: -25 Sep 1940) Pro since age 16, first as manipulator, then since 1910 with 2-person memory act with his wife as "Lillian Michael & Partner". Toured South & North America. [St]

name: Altini
bio: (Germany: 17 Jul 1938-) Stage name of Dr Franz Alt. [Roh]

name: Alvaro, Professor Dr N. P.
bio: (India: 1882-1943) Pro magician & illusionist of the old school. Toured India, Far East, & England. Published in several European journals, including Goldston's. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Alvero".

name: Alxeno
bio: (Stanisławówo, Poland [now Ivano-Frankovsk, Ukraine]): 24 Mar 1935- ) Stage name of Alexander Malyk. Pro illusionist. 1983 Lódz 3rd prize. Tricks in Hokus-Pokus (Poland). [Mec;Nad]

name: Aly
bio: See: Ali, Hadji

name: Alyett
bio: (Marseille, France: 22 Mar 1885-1 Sep 1975) Stage name of Alfred Auzet. Pro illusionist since c1910. After WW I toured South-east Europe, the Near East, and as far as Ceylon. Played the Casino de Paris c1928. Founder-owner of the Grand Palais des Illusions magic theater in Paris 1928-31. Founder-owner of the Wunderschau Palast in Berlin 1931. 1932 Ville de Paris Grand Prix & Silver Medal. Retired to Marseille by 1968. [Dif;Bou;Rob1]

name: Amac
bio: (Britain: 1890?-3 May 1961) Stage name of Robert William "Bill" MacFarlane. Pro illusionist by around 1916. Invented the baffling Elusive Lady illusion by 1921, soon making it his entire act. Played the New York Palace in 1925 (twice) & 1926. Invented The Third Man Walks Out card trick (1951). [Pr;Ho]

name: Amalfi
bio: (England: fl.1950s) Stage & pen name of William F. Tunnah. Pro kid-show magician. Wrote Santa's Workshop (1957, 51pp).

name: Amanda, Madame
bio: See: Oeser, Marie

name: Amando
bio: See: Bader, Egon

name: Amarante, Francisco
bio: (Aveiro, Portugal: 15 Dec 1888-10 Oct 1950) Pro manipulator with coins, etc. For political reasons moved in 1920 to Brazil where he often toured with circuses. Died in São Paulo. [Cam] Amarasekara, Mudaliyar A. C. G. S. "Sekara" (Dodanduwa, Ceylon: 2 Mar 1883- ) Professional portrait painter and, since 1908, art teacher. Amateur magic, vent, shadowgraphs, & lightening sketches, performing as "Gay Deceiver". Debut in 1916. 1946 British Ring trophy. Wrote a book in Singhalese, Esbandum [Conjuring], and one in English, Gay Deceiver. [Go2;Le] Amarasekara, D. V. A. S. (Colombo, Ceylon: 30 Nov 1918-) Aka "Gay Deceiver Junior". Son of Mudaliyar Amarasekara who taught him magic. Amateur. Studied at Oxford in 1946 but soon dropped out. [Go2;Le]

name: Amasis
bio:
"Amateur" [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

[See also: Hartop, A. W.]

name: Amato, Bruce [Michael]
bio: (Hartford, Connecticut: 18 Jun 1961-) Self-taught in 1972. Pro kid-show, close-up, hyp, & restaurant table-hopper since 1976. Lectures on restaurant & kid-show magic. USA rep for Supreme Magic Company since 1989. Wrote The Restaurant Technique of Bruce Amato (1989, 34pp). Columnist in Magigram since 1988. Articles in MUM. [Wh2]

name: Amaya
bio: See: Brush, Ada Mary

name: Amazo, Don
bio: See: Rose, Donald W. "Don"

name: Ambroise
bio: (France: fl.1770s) Pro showman working Paris (1775, 1777) & London (1771 & then in 1776 when he worked with Brunn). Ambroise is the earliest known performer to combine magic & Chinese Shadows in one show, his "théatre des recréations de la Chine". [CI]

name: Ambrose, Prof.
bio: (Mahanoy City, Pennsylvania: 10 Feb 1820-) Taught by his pro father around 1885. Pro magician & teacher.

name: Amedeo
bio: (Italy: 1890-1974) Stage name of Amedeo Vacca. Moved to USA in youth. Debut in 1910. Pro, including as advance man for Houdini (1924-26). In 1938 became one of the earliest magicians (& the 1st American citizen) to work cruise ships (for the Canadian-Pacific Line). Featured fire-eating. Invented Phantom Buzzer (1951). See Frank Garcia & George Schindler, Amedeo's Continental Magic (1974, 115pp) & Charles Kalish, Amedeo, The International Deceptionist: A Lecture. Audio.

name: Amico
bio: See: "Hamik-Amico, Fritz"

name: Ammar, Michael [Anthony] "Mike
bio: (Charleston, West Virginia: 25 June 1956-) Inspired seeing 1st magic show. Learned in 9th grade from books bought thru 25¢ Douglas Magicland catalog advertised in a comic book. Graduated West Virginia U in 1979 with MBA. Pro close-up since 1979. AMA Best Close-up 1982 & 1984; Best Lecturer 1983 & 1984; Best Parlour 1986 & 1991. 1982 FISM 1st Prize for close-up (shared with Aurelio). 2008 DRAGON Award (with wife Hannah). Married Frances Willard's daughter Hannah in 1990. Wrote The Topit Book (1983, 119pp); 7 booklets, all translated into German by Michael Gerhardt; The Magic of Michael Ammar (1991, 328pp); & The Complete Cups & Balls (1998, incl 2 videos). Co-editor (with Adam Fleischer) of Magical Arts Journal 1987-88, sole editor 1989-present. 10 times on Merv Griffin TV show, twice on Johnny Carson show. 10 videos (1985, etc); 1 audio (1990). [Bo#213;Wh]

name: Ampthill, Lord, MIMC
bio: (Rome, Italy: 1869-7 Jul 1935) The 2nd Baron Ampthill. Amateur magician. 5th president of The Magic Circle 1931-35. [WWW]

name: Amwell, Lord
bio: See: Montague, Frederick

name: Amrein, Ade
bio:
And, Dr Metin (Istanbul, Turkey: 17 Jun 1927- ) Inspired as a child. Professor in Theater Department of Ankara U & authority on the performing arts in Turkey. Amateur magician, performing only for friends, and collector of magic books & apparatus. Wrote Magic in Istanbul (Calgary, Canada: Hades International, 1978, 67pp). Also Insanüstülük Taslayanların (1981), an exposé of paranormal claims.

[See also: "Duval, Ade"]

name: Anders, Professor
bio: (France: -15 Jan 1926) Stage name of Georges Blanchet. Pro sleight-of-hand. [Cl]

name: Anders, Fritz
bio: (Germany: 1841-1910) Pen name of Max Allihn. Roman Catholic priest at Weissenfels-an-der-Saale. Amateur magician. Wrote Der junge Tausendkünstler (1877, 320pp), a decent compilation of tricks for boys that went thru its 3rd edition in 1890 & was reprinted in 1978.

name: Anders, Günter
bio: (Germany: 14 Jun 1939-) Magician. 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Anderson
bio: (Belleville, Seine, France: 21 Oct 1858-11 Jul 1933) Stage name of Émile[-Alphonse] Duval. Pro by 1889. Director of Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1889-92. Toured his Cirque Féérique Anderson 1905-1932. Joined the ASAP in 1921. Ended his career at the Cabinet Fantastique 1932-33. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Anderson, Ada
bio: See: Anderson, Isabella Jean

name: Anderson, Alice Hannah
bio: (Britain: 30 May 1847- ) Stage name of Alice Hannah Anderson, 2nd daughter of J.H. & Hannah Anderson. Assisted him as "Flora Anderson" & "F. Anderson" by 1858 to as late as 1868. Sang & did the Magic Portfolio & Hindu Decapitation. NOTE: Not to be confused with "Jennie Anderson" (no relative) who drowned in New Zealand in 1875. [Mar;Bay]

name: Anderson, Angeline
bio: (USA: 1849-Jan 1921) Born Angeline Trumeller. Recruited in Philadelphia as assistant by J.H. Anderson. Billed as "Leona Anderson". Married J.H. Anderson Jr in St. Louis in 1867 as his 2nd wife. [Bay]

name: Anderson, Bella
bio: See: Anderson, Isabella Jean

name: Anderson, Blanche
bio: See: "Anderson, Jennie"

name: Anderson, Columbia Harriett
bio: (New York City, NY: 12 Aug [or 11 Oct] 1851-) 3rd & oldest daughter of J.H. & Hannah Anderson. Learned assisting her father. Remained in USA with mother & John Jr when father returned to Britain in 1862. Alive as late as 1875. [Bay;Daw2]

name: Anderson, [Roger Douglas] "Doug
bio: (Houston [sic], Texas: 18 Jan 1959-) Inspired in 1973 seeing Bill Bixby's TV series, "The Magician". Learned from purchase of Linking Rings and Spongeballs from Jeffries Magicland. Pro since 1976 working cruise ships & theme parks. Specialized in comedy stand-up & illusions. Wrote Straight Talk about Theme Park Magic (1984, 150pp) & Straight Talk about Cruise Ship Magic (1989 forthcoming). Articles in Genii, Magic Manuscript, Linking Ring, & Magical Arts Journal. [Wh2]

name: Anderson, Eliza
bio: See: Anderson, Helena Elizabeth [NO!.....]

name: Anderson, Flora
bio: See: Anderson, Alice Hannah

name: Anderson, Gene [Allen]
bio: (Grand Forks, Minnesota: 21 May 1941- ) Raised in East Grand Forks. Inspired at age 8 when uncle showed him a trick. Learned by buying a 65¢ book. Paid debut at age 19. Trophy at 1964 TAOM Convention. Invented Origami Hat (1964, for which he won 1964 TAOM originality prize) & his Newspaper Tear (1967). PhD chemist with Dow Chemical since 1970. Thence a part-time pro stage & close-up magician & MC. Specializes in a paper act featuring his T&R Newspaper. Also invented Star of David Paper (a fold & cut, 1972). Wrote Newspaper Magic (1968, 144pp, with Frances Marshall; French tr 1981 by Vollmer) & Topper's Mad, Mad Magic (1974). Tricks in Linking Ring & reviews in Genii. Audio. Video (1991). [LR5/87; Mag; Wat; Wh2]

name: Anderson, George B.
bio: (USA: c1909-13 Jan 1985) Learned first trick at age 6. Newspaper & radio mystery writer in Chicago; owner of ad agency; & semi-promentalist-magician. Then pro mentalist. Then back to TV as creator-producer of the successful Chicago "Magic" TV show starring Don Alan since 1952. Wrote How to Be a Junior Magician, It Must Be Mindreading (1949, 57pp), You, Too, Can Read Minds (1968, 63pp), Magic Digest: Fun Magic For Everyone (1972, 288pp), Dynamite Mentalism (1979, 28pp), Overcoming Magical Hazards (1980), George Anderson's Lecture Notebook (1980, 35pp), etc.

name: Anderson, Harry
bio: (Newport, Rhode Island: 1952-) Joined magic club at age 12. At age 16 in 1968 turned pro as one of the 1st street magicians in San Francisco where he also worked seasonally at the Cannery during his high school & college years. Also worked streets of Austin and New Orleans (1976). Then returned to San Francisco, adding mentalism, a two-person escape act in 1977 when he married Leslie Pollack (mentalist & occultist), & finally stage & TV comedy magic. 1981 AMA Best Stage Magician. Co-star of movie The Escape Artist (1982) & star of the TV series Nightcourt Jan 1984-1992 on which he did occasional magic and Dave's World since 1993. Also on TV Cheers program as "Harry the Hat". 1989 AMA Magician of the Year. Owns a magic shop in Ashland, Oregon. Moved to Seattle in 1990. Wrote The Shadow and Other Card Mysteries (1982), Games You Can't Lose: A Guide for Suckers (1989, with Turk Pipin), etc. Bio & tricks is Mike Caveney, Harry Anderson: Wise Guy (1993, 167pp). [Mag;Camp;Wat]

name: Anderson, Helen
bio: (London, England: 13 Apr 1846-1916 [sic]) Eldest daughter of J.H. Anderson. Learned by 1858 assisting in his shows as, variously "Eliza" (1858, 1860), "Lizzie" (1865, 1868), "Lena", & "Helen". Briefly toured on own as "Helen Anderson". Married Alfred Miles Holmes in 1877. [Bay;Cl;Daw2;Magic7/09]

name: Anderson, Helena Elizabeth
bio: See: Anderson, Helena Elizabeth

name: Anderson, Isabella Jean
bio: (Aberdeen, Scotland: 21 May 1853-7 Nov 1944) Eldest of 3 daughters of non-magician Alexander Anderson who lent her in 1864 to his older brother J.H. Anderson as a stage assistant, billed as "Ada Anderson" & "Bella Anderson". Also used in his "Sleeping in Air" illusion in 1865 & 1868. In 1871 immigrated to Canada with her family. Grandmother of Constance Pole Bayer, biographer of the Anderson dynasty. [Bay]

name: Anderson, Jennie
bio: (near Banbridge, County Down, Northern Ireland: 1855-17 Jan 1875) Stage name of Jane Verten (née Whiteside). Brought to New Zealand at age 1. Pro gymnast (trapezist & tightrope dancer). Then on 12 Mar 1874 debuted as NZ's 1st pro magician (as well as magicienne). Toured with a variety troupe in that country in 1874-75 under successive stage names of "Miss Blanche Fane", "Miss Blanche Anderson", & "Miss Jennie Anderson". Drowned in a stagecoach accident while fording the Waitaki River on South Island. Bio is James V. Reilly, Darling Jennie (1991, 28pp). NOTE: Because she was incorrectly identified as Anderson's daughter in an Australian [sic] newspaper report of her death, she's been mistaken for Alice Hannah Anderson.

name: Anderson, Professor J[ohn] H[enry]
bio: (Craigmyle, Aberdeenshire, Scotland: 16 Jul 1814-3 Feb 1874) Born John Anderson, adding the Henry later. Learned c1835 when apprenticed to "Big Scott" (Longhurst). Became a Mason. Debut on own in 1837. Took Sir Walter Scot's soubriquet of "The Wizard of the North" in 1839 [sic]. Married Longhurst's daughter Hannah (1819-1866) in 1842. In the 1840s possibly invented the Dissolving Die & the Parasol (1). Played the major theaters in Britain. Toured Europe (1847), the USA (1851-52), Australia (1858-59), Hawaii (1859), & the USA (1859-62). When he returned to Britain for the last time in 1862, his wife, eldest son (J.H.A.Jr), & youngest daughter (Columbia) chose to remain behind. Distinguished by his elaborate staging and notorious for his bombastic advertising. Bankrupt in 1866, henceforward played only minor venues in Britain. Died in Darlington, England. Authored several pamphlets including The Fashionable Science of Parlour Magic [1843, 71pp; many revisions & reprints until c1862]. Wrote Anderson's Note-Book: or Recollections of His Continental Tour (1860, 80pp). Bios are E.D. H[ington], Biography of John Henry Anderson (1858), J.B. Findlay, Anderson & His Theatre (1967, 26pp), & almost definitively Constance Pole Bayer, The Great Wizard of the North: John Henry Anderson (1990, 174pp). [Ch:Daw:Cl:Pr:Fr:La:Wal:Mol

name: Anderson Jr, John Henry "Johnny
bio: (Manchester, England: 24 Sep 1843-23 Jun 1878) Elder son of J.H. & Hannah Anderson. Learned assisting father by 1858. With father on the latter's 2nd world tour (1858-62). When his father returned home, John Jr remained in USA (with his 1st wife Angeline, mother Hannah, & youngest sister Columbia). Pro with own act by 1864, touring USA (1864), Canada (1874), & England (1875) with moderate success before his death in the USA. [Bay;Pr;Wal;Cl;Mo]

name: Anderson, Lena
bio: See: Anderson, Helena Elizabeth

name: Anderson, Leslie
bio: (USA: 1952- ) Born Leslie Pollack. Mentalist & occultist. Married Harry Anderson in 1977. Learned from him their two-person pro escape act and later taught him their two-person mental act. Wrote Eight Brass Monkeys (1982). Trick in Magick. [Wat]

name: Anderson, Lizzie
bio: See: Anderson, Helena Elizabeth

name: Anderson, Louisa [or Louise]
bio: (USA: 1840-1934) Stage name of Mary Antonia Leuger, mistress of J.H. Anderson with whom she worked as an assistant by 1858 & did second-sight act by 1865 to as late as 1867. Also billed with him as "Miss L. Anderson" & "Miss L.S. Anderson" (in 1860). Bore him 2 children: Mary Antoinette (1959-1940) & Joseph ("Jo", 1861-1939), both becoming stage players. Wrote a small book of poems. Married Dr Hamilton Griffin c1867. [Bay]

name: Anderson, Margaret Gordon
bio: (Scotland: 1857-1937) 3rd & youngest daughter of non-magician Alexander Anderson who in 1864 loaned her to his older brother J.H. Anderson with whom she worked as an assistant, billed as "Nellie Anderson". In 1871 immigrated with her family to Canada. [Bay]

name: Anderson, Nellie
bio: See: Anderson, Margaret Gordon

name: Anderson, Oscar Longhurst
bio: (Swindon, Wiltshire, England: 19 Aug 1848- ) 2nd & youngest son of J.H. & Hannah Anderson. Learned assisting father. Pro until around 1870 & alive until 1874. Wrote Master Oscar Anderson's Illustrated and Alphabetical Enumerations ... of his Father's ... Entertainment [c1875, 32pp]. NOTE: His often ascribed date of death in 1920 results from confusion with Philip Prentice Anderson. [Bay;Pr;Cl]

name: Anderson, Professor Phillip
bio: See: Anderson, Philip [Prentice]

name: Anderson, Philip [Prentice]
bio: (London, England [sic]: Jan 1844-Feb 1920) Illegitimate son of J.H. Anderson & "Miss Prentice" who died in childbirth. Toured as assistant with father 1858-67. Worked as pro illusionist on own as "Signor Rubini" 1867-71, playing London (1867-69) & USA (1870-71). Joined Heller as assistant during latter's 1871-72 portion of his Australia-India tour. Philip then proclaimed his patrimony, working again on own as stage illusionist in his father's style & appropriately billed as "The Great Wizard of the North" & as "Prof. Anderson, Wizard of the North". Toured South Asia (India, Hong Kong, Batavia) 1873-81 & India again (with a movie projector) in 1897-98, & Australia (4 times, 1881-1900). During this period he was assisted by his American-born 1st wife Louise Maude Anderson, then by his 2nd wife Blanche Louise Daniels (born 1869) who was also billed as "Blanche De La Cour" or "Mlle Blanche" (in 1897-99). Retired in 1900 to Camperdown, Australia, as a pharmacist & dentist, living there as late at 1911. Died in Birmingham, England. NOTE: I accept Bill Kuethe's theory that Philip Prentice Anderson, "Professor Phillip Anderson", & perhaps also "Phillip C. Davis" are the same person. Kuethe's chronology is almost seamless. Sometimes also mistaken for Alfred Miles Holmes. See also Constance Pole Bayer, The Great Wizard of the North (1990). [Bay;Magician Mthly2/20;Pr;Cl;Fr;Rey;Mo; Ch;Wal;Bar]

name: Anderton, Professor
bio: (Sheffield, England: c1851-5 Aug 1909) Stage name of Albert A. Haslam. Minor pro sleight-of-hand artist at English fairs until c1890 when he left magic to became a circus worker and later a movie exhibitor. [CI]

name: Andini [pronounced an-DEE-nee]
bio: (Winchester, England: 1 May 1955- ) Stage & pen name of Andrew John Molock. Inspired at age 7 seeing David Nixon on British TV. Moved to Australia by 1971 when he became a pro entertainer (including magic). 1984 Australian Convention of Magicians (Melbourne) 1st prize in close-up. Does both close-up & stage illusions as well as general entertainment including singing telegrams. Collector of pre-1925 magic books & Rooklyn memorabilia. Vanished from the magic scene in 1990. Edited Jean Hugard Magical Magazine 1981-82 (15 issues), The Drum (Queensland Society of Magicians) 1983-86. Editor-publisher of The Magazine With No Name in Burleigh Heads, Queensland, 1986-1989. TV bits. [Wh5]

name: Andino
bio: (Germany: 23 Mar 1961-) Stage name of Andreas Michel. Interested in magic c1969/70. Semi-pro & collector (history & playing cards) in Bonn, later Koblenz. 50+ articles in Simsala Bonn, etc.

name: Andoe, Mr. F.
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s) Pro. Billed as "The Great Magician King" in 1842 when he played throughout the British Isles. [Magic6/03]

name: Andra, Rolf
bio: (Hegne, near Constanța, Germany: 24 Aug 1907-4 Mar 1998) Stage name of Josef Fuchs. Moved to Switzerland. Learned from book. Pro with full-evening show billed as "The Laughing Magician". Wrote Kartenkombinationen (1940, 40pp), Kartenmagie (1956), Die Symphonie der Asse (1957), Das konische Kartenspiel (1962), Magische Impressionen (1964), & Zauber der Asse (1965). 1987 MZvD Magician of the Year. Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, etc. [Magie7/89;Win;Nad]

name: Andrade, Will[iam Charles]
bio: (Australia: 1864-11 Nov 1939) Bookseller (since 1898) & also magic dealer (by 1901) & manufacturer in Melbourne since 1912 plus a branch shop in Sydney 1919-39. Although successful in the business, he was not a magician. Drowned while swimming. The Sydney business was then bought by Harry Job. Under pen name "Charles A. Prince" had ghosted 50 Simple Card Tricks [early 1920s]. Published Will Andrade's Magical Review (1928-29, 6 issues, edited by Will Alma) as house organ. His firm edited Mystery Club Magazine (1941, 6 issues). [McC;McC2]

name: Andre, Bob
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: -dead) Amateur magician, business executive, and commercial inventor ("Snap-on Blocks," etc.). Invented Anti-Gravico. Sold it in 1943 for $24 to John Isley who soon miscredited its invention to himself when he marketed it next year.

name: André, Victor
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro magic to second sight. Played the London Pavilion c1892. Silent-code mindreading with Madame André by 1902. [Cl; Magic8/02]

name: Andreal's
bio: See: Ravessoud, André

name: Andreas, Günter
bio: (Germany: 14 Jun 1939-) Illusionist, aka "Black & White". 1981 MZvD 3rd prize in illusion; 1983 Baden-Baden 2nd prize in illusion; 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Andreoletti, Carlo
bio: (Italy: fl.1850s) Billed in 1858 as a physician to the King of Sardinia & as having played Paris. Pro sleight-of-hand. Played the St. James's in London in May 1858 at which time he gave a Command Performance for Queen Victoria at Buckingham Palace.

name: Andréor
bio: See: Dupin, André

name: Andress, Charles "Uncle Charlie
bio: (Brockville, Ontario, Canada: 15 Jan 1852-26 Aug 1933) Moved to Michigan as boy. Inspired & learned at age 9 as apprentice to British magician Capt. Thomas. Pro vent-magus since age 12 when he toured the mid-west & south. Circus owner from age 20 until 1916. Thence toured as magician. Died in Great Bend. [Levitator9/74;Pr;Bo3]

name: Andrews, Max
bio: (Britain: 1918-1988) Stage name of one McAndrew. Learned by age 11. Worked for a time in his father's printing shop. Prop maker since 1935. Manager, Hamley's Conjuring Department, 1940-1946-? Pro dealer (as Vampire Magic) in London 1938-1958. Also ran a photo studio in London as a sideline. Moved to New Zealand (where he worked cabarets) and thence to Australia where he worked briefly in Alf Hayes' magic shop in Sydney before retiring. Died in Australia. Invented the Dice Frame Escape (by 1939). Wrote Sixteen Card Index Gems (1943, 36pp), Sixteen Thumb Tie Gems (1947, 49pp), etc. Published-edited The Magic Magazine 1952-56 (54 issues) as his house organ. [Daw94;St]

name: Andrews, Milton Franklin
bio: See: "Erdnase"

name: Andrews, Val[entine]
bio: (Hove, England: 15 Feb 1926-12 Dec 2006) Inspired at age 7 by watching both his amateur father & The Great Carmo. Learned at age 8. Debut at age 12 (1938). Pro performer since 1943. Aka "Val Vox" 1938-48 & "Vanson" 1948-51. Prolific author since 1952 of over 200 booklets on various aspects of magic and 6 popularized magical biographies: Murray (1974), Good-Night Mister Dante (1978, 111pp), A Gift from the Gods—the Story of Chung Ling Soo (1981), "Life ...Dull it 'Ain't!: Horace Goldin, The Triumphs and Tragedies (1983), Once Hung a Guilded Lamp: The Life and Times of Will Goldston (1986), 'Gentleman George' Sanger (1989), and The Dante Scrapbook (1990, 52pp). Wrote (with Fergus Roy) Illusions (1985, 144pp). Memoirs are Dedicated Magic (1971, 153pp) & Four Seasons in the Life of Val Andrews (1984, 60pp). 2 audios. Edits The Magical Nostalgic 1992-present. [Wh2]

name: Androletti
bio: (Italy: fl.mid-1700s) Pro. [CI]

name: Andrucci, Al
bio: See: "Heba-Haba Al"

name: Andrus, [Gerald] "Jerry
bio: (Sheridan, Wyoming: 1918-26 Aug 2007) Interested at age 12 seeing performance of a reformed spiritualist medium. Joined the International Society of Junior Magicians at age 16. Close-up. Noted for tricks not using misdirection. Mentor of Ray Hyman, Loren Pankratz, etc. Lecturer. Invented the Linking Pins (1954, his version), Panoramic Shift (by 1955), & Paradox Box. 1979 AMA Best Lecturer. 1988 AMA Creative Fellowship. Wrote one book, Andrus Deals You In (1956 [sic]), 190pp), & several booklets, including Safety Pin-Trix (1955, 70pp), Andrus Deals Again (1957, 6pp), Up Close with Andrus (1957, 9pp), Sleeving from the Deck (1961, 18pp), Sleightly Miraculous (1961, 15pp), The Miser's Miracle (1961, 19pp); Steals and Palms (1961, 34pp), Kurious Kards (1973). Tricks in HMM, New Directions, & Onyx. [Genii10/89;HMM9/57;Mag;Wat]

name: Andruzzi, Tony
bio: See: "Palmer, Tom"

name: Andy
bio: (Germany?: 5 Sep 1949-) Stage name of Andreas Wahler. Magician. 1987 MZvD 1st prize in general magic; 1991 FISM 3rd prize in mentalism. [Nad]

name: Angel
bio: (USA: 1969-) Stage name of Chris Sarantas. Pro rock illusionist. [Ran]

name: Angelico, Sam
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 18 Jan 1955-) Inspired at age 12 seeing Geoffrey Crozier. Learned working in magic shop. Pro magician since age 18 with silent comedy act. Toured Europe, Britain, & USA. 1985 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic. Several worldwide TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Anguinet, Mlle. Bénita
bio:
(France: fl.1850s-70s) Pro stage illusions in French provinces before 1856 when she made her debut in Paris at the Théâtre de Prestidigitation in the Bois de Boulogne. (The J. Voignier Collection includes a photograph of her Paris show.) The only magicienne mentioned by Robert-Houdin. In later years she lived in Madrid, performing as "Madame Benitte" when touring Portugal in 1868. [Dif;Cam]

[See also: Bourguignon, Jacques]

name: Angus, Gina
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s-80s) Pro. Assistant-wife of Tom Angus until his death in 1980. Thence with single act.

name: Angus, Tom
bio: (Britain: -1980) Pro with assistant-wife Gina Angus.

name: Aniko
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 11 Jan 1949-) Stage name of Anikó Ungár. Taught by her amateur father. Pro since 1975 in Europe with balls, silks, cards, & flower productions, working in delightfully short wardrobe. Also does kid-shows. In USA 1988.[Win]

name: Annabelle
bio: See: Cox, Mr.

name: Anna-Lou
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Marion Way. Self-taught pro magicienne (ex-actress) in exotic costume with livestock production act as "Anna-Lou & Maria" with a series of different "Marias." [Mar]

name: Annemann, Theo[dore] John "Ted
bio: (East Waverly, New York: 22 Feb 1907-12 Jan 1942) Born Theodore John Squires, adopted by Stanley Anneman at age 2, Ted adding the second "n" in 1930. Inspired at age 10 watching schoolmate do the Ball & Vase. Learned at age 14 when bought a Gilbert magic set. IBM member #245 (1922). Debut c1925 at age c18 with the Doc Kries medicine show. Pro mentalist. Pet publicity stunt: Bullet Catching. Voted one of the 10 Card Stars in 1938, although he was uncomfortable with sleights. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Founded-edited The Jinx 1934-41 & The Sign of Exceptional Magic 1935-35 (6 issues). Committed suicide by asphyxiation. Invented window envelope by 1931, Remote Control by 1932, & Flat Rabbit in 1937. Wrote several books, including The Book Without a Name (1931, 53pp), Card Miracles [c1932, 12pp], 101 Methods of Forcing (1932), 202 Methods of Forcing (1933, 35pp), Exclusive Conceptions with Cards (1933), Sh-h-h—It's a Secret (1934, 36pp), Mental Bargain Effects (1935, 12pp; repr 1955, 24pp), Complete One Man Mental and Psychic Routine (1935, 24pp; repr 1956), En Rapport (1937, 22pp), & The Incorporated Strange Secrets (1939; 1956, 19pp). A major collection of his tricks appeared as Practical Mental Effects (1944, 31pp; repr 1963). Under pen-name of "Drummond" also wrote Climax Card Routine (1933). See Max Abrams, Annemann: The Life and Times of a Legend (1992, viii+621pp). [Genii11/92;Th;Se;Ho]

name: Anonyma
bio: (Bavaria, Germany: 22 Dec 1884-18 Jun 1913) Stage name of Amy Clément (Mrs Clément de Lion). Pro singer-dancer-ventriloquist. Worked both single & in husband's act. First female vent to appear in Germany. Drowned while swimming in Bavaria.

name: Anstro
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Stage name of Joseph F. Fuigle. Invented "Anstro's Four Ace Trick" (1910) & the "Anstro Forcing Deck" (by 1914).

name: Anthony
bio: (Britain?: fl.1900s) Pro. In 1906 engaged in bitter controversy with Carlton over invention of the Die Box trick. [Dif]

name: Anthony, Dr.
bio: See: Rybakowicz, Anthony

name: Antón, Javier
bio: (Zaragoza, Spain: 19 Jun 1947- ) Self-taught magic at age 3. Jeweller in home town. Semi-pro in general magic & theme illusion act with daughter Ana. 1984 Spanish Grand Prix and 1985 FISM Grand Prix to "Javier & Ana". Pet effects are with cats, fish, & doves. Invents & builds all tricks in his act, particularly Lights in the Fingers. [Wh5]

name: Antonelli
bio: (Munich, Germany: 10 Jan 1870- ) Stage name of Christian Ammon. Pro illusionist & stage magician. Was operating a small magic shop ("Magische Zauberkunst") in Teplitz-Schonau by 1923 when he issued a catalog. [Sal]

name: Antonio, Carlo
bio: (France?: fl.1750s) While living in Morocco, he wrote Le Trésor des jeux [The Treasury of Games] (Geneva 1759; & The Hague: 1759). This copies word-for-word the Cups-&-Balls section in Ozanam (1725 ed) and adds some dozen other tricks.

name: Anverdi, Tony
bio: (Hoorn, Holland: 20 Aug 1925-31 Jan 1995) Stage name of Antonius Albertus "Tony" de Vries. Interested in magic since age 10. Baker & amateur magic clown until 1950 when he turned pro. Originally specialized in liquid magic, later electronic magic. Lecturer. A major inventor, he sold his apparatus mail order from his home in Leiden. Wrote Anverdi's Miracles with Liquids (1965, 44pp) & 50 Years of Magical Creations (1992, 190pp). 1975 AMA Creative Fellowship. [Genii9/64;Wh2]

name: Appel, Professor W.
bio: (Germany: fl.1830s) Pro.

name: Apperson, John [William]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 13 Feb 1942-) Learned in 1966 from local magic store tricks. Left Dow Chemical in 1973 to become a police sergeant in Granite City, Illinois. Semi-pro stage & strolling magician since 1975. Pet effects: Rice Bowls & Spell Bound. [Monti;MUM4/85;Wh2]

name: Applegit, Elmer M.
bio: (USA: fl.  $ 1^{st} $ decade of 1900s-50s) Amateur in Morristown. Invented One Card Pete (by 1943). Tricks in Hugard's Annual: 1937 & HMM. Edited M-U-M 1956-57.

name: Arai, Shinichi
bio: (Japan: 1954; fl.1980s-90s) Amateur card magician in Tokyo. One of the best creators and performers in Japan. Close up magician. Marketed his original tricks as Affections series. Regular contributor for The Magic magazine. Organizer of Tappurito Close-up convention since 1983.

name: Araki, Shigeo
bio: (Japan: -1 Mar 1981) Published and edited Kijutsu Kenkyu [A Study of Magic], most notable and full-fledged magicians' periodical (seasonal) in the Japanese magic history at that time that started in spring 1956 and lasted over twenty years (vol.1 to vol.86). Owner of Chikara Shobo that published Kijutsu Kenkyu and other qualified magic books.

name: Araújo, Dr. Jorge [dos Santos Cabral]
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 4 Feb 1929-) Physician. Amateur magician. Wrote Falando de Ilusionismo (1981, 83pp), Invenção do Ilusionismo (1982, 59pp), & Truques de Illusionismo (1984, 120pp). Tricks in Quatro Ases. [Cam] Arbaffs, The (Germany?: fl.1880s) Herr Arbaff and "Izabel, the Spanish Lady Conjurer" (also "The Beautiful Spaniard") did a mixed act in South America in 1882 and England c1885. NOTE: A woman, perhaps the same, performed in Germany in the 1910s as "The Beautiful Spaniard". [CI]

name: Arbré, Charles
bio: (Olmütz, Moravia, Austria [now Olomouc, Czech Republic]: 17 Jan 1846-4 Nov 1907) Stage name of Eduard [sic] Carl Baum. Ex-piano teacher. Pro magician. Partner with Agoston in late 1870s & later with Johann Benesch. Toured automata in Sweden (1880). Employed Max Auzinger 1885-87 from whom he learned the Black Art act, which he performed independently in 1886 in Hamburg as "Ben Azra El Muz". Toured Europe: Vienna (1886), Balkans, Sweden, Denmark, Holland, & England until 1891. In 1906 became a hotel keeper in his birthplace until his died the next year. [Vo58; Dif; St; Cl]

name: Arbuckle, Mr.
bio: (Scotland: fl. 1st decade of 1800s) Student of Boaz. Pro. Billed as "The Caledonian Conjuror" when toured England in 1809. [Dif]

name: Arbuthnot III, Charles
bio: (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 1 Sep 1888-) A Mason. Businessman. Amateur card & rope magic. Inspired at age 51 (1939). Articles for Genii, Linking Ring, & Jinx. [Th]

name: Arcanus
bio: (Austria: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Hans Schütz. Minor variety magician. Taught Allan & Borosé. In 1938 moved to Britain as political refugee, returning to Austria after WW II to work as a graphologist. [Al] (Chemnitz, Germany: 9 Jun 1902-1971) Stage name of Max Schybol. Died in home town. [Roh]

name: Arcuri, Lawrence P. "Larry
bio: (New York City, NY: -13 Dec 1980) Journalist. Amateur magician. Founded the New York Magic Table in early 1940s. Invented "The Vanishing and Reappearing Necktie" (1945, which got a 1946 mention in Ripley's Believe-It-Or-Not cartoon) & "The Dancing Bow Tie" (1946). Edited The Spellbinder. Articles in Linking Ring.

name: Aremi
bio: (Poland: 29 Mar 1933- ) Stage name of Marek Zdrojewski. Pro illusionist. Wrote Czarodziej Twardowski (1984, 46pp) & Sztukmistrz Twardowski i polonijni iluzjoniści (1986, 136pp). [Mec;Nad]

name: Arenholz, William J. "Bill
bio: (Falfurrias, Texas: 29 Nov 1891- ) Executive with New York Telephone Company. Interested in magic as semi-pro since 1932 when he was a student of Al Baker. Impaired of hearing, he did a full-evening pantomime Oriental magic act as "Foo Ling Yu", his mask made by Mrs Dai Vernon. [Genii1/42]

name: Areny Plandolit, Dr Pablo de
bio: (Spain: 1876-1936) Physician in Barcelona. Sometime official of the Republic of Andorra. Amateur magician. Wrote the popular Las Maravillas de la Magia Moderna (Barcelona: 1913; reprinted 1945 & 1947). Father of Javier de Areny-Plandolit.

name: Areny-Plandolit [Gassó], Dr Javier de
bio: (Pobla de la Granadella, Lérida, Spain: 14 Oct 1907 [sic]-28 Mar 1982) Son of the above. Dentist in Barcelona. Amateur magician. Founding member of ACAI in 1932.
