Wrote Anuario Español de la Prestidigitación (1942) & Bibliografía Española de la Prestidigitación (Barcelona: 1944, 32pp; 2nd ed enlarged 1950). President, S.E.I., 1951. Had largest collection of magic books in Spain (over 5,000 volumes by 1950), which was finally sold piecemeal. [St;Xe]

name: Argola, M.
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 28 Apr 1936- ) Stage name of Dieter Michel. Magician & magic collector in Berlin. Contributor to Zauberkunst. [Roh;Nad]

name: Arian
bio: (Germany?: 17 May 1951-) Stage name of Karl-Heinz Kolster. Magician in Germany. 1978 MZvD 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Ariel
bio: (Bayamo, Cuba: 14 Jun 1894- ) Stage name of Carlos Aristides COSTA ALLAGA. Pro full-evening show 1912-16. Thence music & voice teacher and amateur magician in Havana. [WWM]

name: Ariens, Mister
bio: See: Arienzo, Tommaso

name: Arienzo, Tommaso
bio: (Naples, Italy: 2 Feb 1900-9 Jul 1966) Learned at age 18. Pro comedy stage manipulator as "Tom Walls", then "Tomaso", & finally "Ariens" & "Mr Ariens", capitalizing on his resemblance to Buster Keaton. [Magia Moderna1966]

name: Aristo
bio: (Szczucin-Dabrowa, Poland: 1907-Jan 1986) Stage name of Józef Czerniawski. Pro illusionist. [Mec;Nad]

name: Arland, Paul
bio: (Skibbinge, Denmark: 30 Mar 1921-) Pro comedy magician 1941-64, known for his "The Merry Angler" act, which he created in 1943. Left pro magic in 1964 to become a radio-TV producer in Copenhagen. 1979 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. FISM jury 1979, 1988. President, Danish Magic Circle since c1986. [Dif]

name: Arlecchino
bio: See: Madsen, Bill

name: Armah
bio: See: Armstrong, William J.

name: Armandi
bio: (Holland: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Ad Wurkum. 1970 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic (shared with Topper Martyn).

name: Armenteras [Estalella], Antonio de
bio: (Madrid, Spain: 7 Jun 1900-5 Feb 1985) Lawyer & journalist. Amateur comedy magician since late 1930s. 1953 Spanish National Congress of Magic (in Segovia) 1st prize in comedy magic. Wrote Enciclopedia de la magia (1956), História de la magia (1962), & Juegos de manos (1972). Articles in magic magazines. [Xe]

name: Armida
bio: See: Oeser, Marie

name: Armando [Pereira] de Matos, Professor
bio: (Porto, Portugal: 9 Jan 1905- ) Teacher & director of a commercial school in Porto. Amateur magician since 1940. In 1956 co-founded (with Eduardo Franco) the Magiarte magic shop in Porto. Wrote ABC de Cartomagia (1963, 130pp). Articles in Magia & Boletim Magiarte. [Cam]

name: Arminio, Carlo
bio: (Austria: 1868-) aka Charles d'Arlion, real name Karl Wawrinsky. Student of George Heubeck. Pro. Used many Hofzinser tricks. Major collector of magic books & props. [St]

name: Armour, Richard
bio: (Scotland: 25 Dec 1885-26 Feb 1969) Semi-pro in Glasgow. Aka "Conjurer Dick" (from Professor Hoffmann's 1886 novel of that title). Edited Magic of the Scottish Conjurers Association (Glasgow: 1945, 29pp; USA ed 1947). Collected props, mainly brass, that were acquired by Dawes in 1964.

name: Armstrong, Bruce
bio: (Montreal?, Canada: fl.1970s) TV host. Edited Encyclopedia of Suspensions and Levitations (1976, 275pp). Column in Levitator.

name: Armstrong, Ellen E.
bio: (USA: c1904-) Afro-American. Resident of South Carolina. Daughter of J. Hartford Armstrong in whose show she assisted & did a mindreading act. Toured father's show in the southern states after his death in 1939 until the late 1940s, as the only black woman magician with a touring show. [Genii2/92; Ebony12/49]

name: Armstrong, George
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s - 11 $ ^{th} $ July 1985) Stage name of William George A. Jenkins. Semi-pro performer-publisher. Edited-published The Magic Wand 1945-57, The Magic Wand Yearbook 1946-48, & The Wizard 1947-56 (Jack Lamonte taking over as editor in 1954). Published Pentagram. Wrote Tricks of the Trade (1946, 24pp), Premonition (1949), & Chandu's Psychoanalysis (1950). Tricks in Phoenix.

name: Armstrong, Professor J[ohn] Hartford
bio: (Spartanburg, S. Carolina: c1876-16 Jun 1939) Afro-American. Pro. Learned c1886-89 as apprentice to a Haitian magician. Beginning in 1889 toured southern & eastern USA with own troupe for 50 years, playing exclusively to black audiences. On his death, his daughter, Ellen, took over the show. Contributor to Linking Ring. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame. [Genii2/92]

name: Armstrong, William J[ohn]
bio: (Brighton, Massachusetts: 29 Apr 1891-31 May 1948) Aka "Armah, the Oriental Mystic", "Pooshee Pooshee", & "William John Lee". Pro, originally in vaudeville. Taught John Booth c1926. A pioneer close-up magician in top American east coast hotels & private parties in the early 1930s, incorporating fortune-telling by cards, palmistry, or crystal gazing. Also played vaude with wife as "Fairman & Lee". Toured Central & South America. Retired during WW II to Miami, Florida, where he died. [St;WWM]

name: Arnardo
bio: (Sarpsborg, Norway: 19 Oct 1912- ) Stage name of Arne Anderson. Pro circus trapezeist & contortionist who became a magician in 1941. Also 2-person mindreading with assistant-wife Gerd. Worked also as circus director & in other branches of showbiz. [Dif]

name: Arno, Bob
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 18 Apr 1940-) Stage name of Arnold Munthe. Learned in 1954 as member of Swedish Junior Magic Circle. Pro comedy magician & stage pickpocket since 1959. Also freelance photographer in Far East in 1960s. Has played showrooms in over 80 countries, including such major venues as the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1970 & 1977. TV bits. [Mec;Wh2]

name: Arnold, J. Harvey
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Pro dealer (Arnold Magic Company) in Princeton, New Jersey, in 1910s. Editor-publisher of Impromptu Trixter, whose lone issue in Jul 1915 is a rare collector's piece. It was the official publication of the National Conjurer's Association.

name: Arnold, Les[lie David]
bio: (Long Beach, California: 13 Sep 1945-) Grandson of The Great Leon & nephew of Leon M. Leon. Learned around age 11-12 from elder brother & his Mysto Magic set & then helped by his uncle. Pro illusionist since his 20s. Occasional illusion builder for Mark Wilson, Copperfield, Don Bice, & Mark Kalin. TV bits. [Wh]

name: Arnold, Rudy
bio: See: Nemeskay Jr, Rudolph A.

name: Arnold, Th. F. K.
bio: (Germany: fl. 1st decade of 1800s) Wrote, as "Enslin dem Jüngern", Zaubereien und Wunder (Hamburg & Mainz: 4 parts, 1801-05), on methods for creating apparitions with mirrors, liquids, or powders; and, as "Agrippa von Nettesheim", Das Ganze der Taschen-spielerkunst (Leipzig: 1805, 239pp; repr 1805 & 1821).

name: Arnold, Theodore H. "Ted
bio: (USA: 1 Aug 1903-15 Oct 1938) Wealthy New York amateur mentalist, magician, & apparatus collector. Compiled the first annual index for The Jinx. Bequeathed his travel-trunk of props to Dai Vernon.

name: Arnolis, Jean
bio: (Souverain-Wandre, Liège, Belgium: 14 Jul 1905-10 Feb 1970) Pro sleights & vent as "Monarque", a paper-magic act as "Paperman", & a pickpocket act as "Jean Lupin". Toured Belgian Congo, Madagascar, Mauritius, etc. AFAP Master Magician. Collector of magic documents in Brussels. Adopted Al Parker. Wrote Découpures magiques de papier (1938), Les mains magiques (1946 with Pierre Balister, issued in only 4 copies), & Je suis prestidigitateur (1962). [Dif;WWM;Go2;Bou]

name: Arnould
bio: (Vierzon, Cher, France: 23 Jul 1850-13 Feb 1920) Stage name of Gustave-Adrien Zaleski. Of Polish parentage. Debut in 1873 as magician-comic-singer. Toured French Indo-China & southern China 1875-76, Spain 1888, Argentina c1888, Egypt 1891. Played the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1896-98. Then played cafés. Charter member of CSP 1904. Article in Illusionniste #125. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Aronack
bio: See: Ackermann, Aaron

name: Aronson, Simon [H.]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 13 Sep 1943- ) Inspired & learned at age 8 from Mandrake & Gilbert magic sets. Corporate lawyer in Chicago. Semi-pro card, close-up, & mental magic in Marlo's Chicago inner circle since c1965. Pet effects: Quadruple Spellbound & Two Person Telepathy (with wife). Wrote The Card Ideas of Simon Aronson (1978, 127pp), A Stack to Remember (1979, 36pp), Shuffle-Bored (1980, 27pp), Sessions (1982, 138pp, with David Solomon), The Aronson Approach (1990, 173pp), Simply Simon (1995, 308pp), & Try the Impossible (2001, 275pp). Tricks in Hierophant, Kabbala, Genii, Linking Ring, Sticks and Stones, Marlo's Magazine, & Inoltre. [LR2/02;Wh5]

name: Arppe, Eric Reinhold
bio: (Helsinki, Finland: 1892-1977) Studied in Helsinki under Danish magus "Dr Faust". Pro stage magician since 1911 including in Estonia. Aka "Eric Reinhold". Pet effects: Levitation, Linking Rings, ball manip, coin catching, flowers. Retired in 1934 to open a hair dressing salon in Finland. [St]

name: Arren, Bobby
bio: See: "Voltaire"

name: Arrom
bio: (São Paulo, Brazil: 17 Jan 1915- ) Stage name of Renato Morra. Aviator. Amateur magician in São Paulo. Published-edited O Tacape Mágico 1945-68. Co-founded the Centro de Estudos Mágicos (CEMA) 1965 in São Paulo. [Fam]

name: Arrowsmith, Rev. George Ernest, MIMC
bio: (Torquay, England: 17 Jul 1887-11 Feb 1978) Debut at age 13 in 1900. Founding member of Exonian Magical Society & Cambridge U Magical Society. Clergyman. Amateur magician specializing in mental magic. Wrote Magical Mentalia (1942, 66pp; repr 1950), Magical Originalia (1943, 67pp), Arrowsmith's Mystery Box (n.d., 90pp), & Arrowsmith's Assorted Mysteries (1967, 44pp). Tricks in Magic Circular, etc. [Th]

name: Arsène
bio: See: Taylor, Harold

name: Arsenio, Vittorio
bio: (Brindisi, Italy: 1 Jan 1911-5 Feb 1986) Moved to Egypt at age 1. Learned at age 15 from book. Pro since 1930 as stage magician & cardician. Debut in Cairo night club, then toured the Mediterranean until 1939, and finally France, Germany, & Italy. [Magia Moderna 1984 & 1986]

name: Artadoni
bio: (Sulejów, Poland: 1925-1987) Stage name of Tadeusz Paraszewski. Student of H.W. Belachini in Lódz. Pro manipulator & giant memory act. Mentor of Jerzy Mecwaldowski. Amateur painter. [Mec]

name: Artemus
bio: (Dublin, Ireland: 25 Apr 1890-1954) Stage name of Arthur Hayes. Taught by Joe Ovette. Minor pro variety magician. Played Chicago in 1911 & London in 1914. [Hudd]

name: Arthur, Dirk
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) 1977 AMA Junior Achievement Award. Pro animal illusionist working Las Vegas, Bahamas, etc. [Mag]

name: Arthur, Franch
bio: (Denmark: 1877- ) Semi-pro kid-show magician. Founding President of the Danish Magic Circle 1934-35. [Dam2]

name: Artinelly
bio: (Spain: 1902- ) Stage name of José de Ibarreta. Originally a croupier in Portuguese casinos. Later pro magician. Lived in Buenos Aires in 1956.

name: Arturo
bio: (Wyoming, Iowa: 1920-29 Jan 1994) Stage name of Charles Larkey. A Mason. Inspired as a young boy seeing a Blackstone show. After WW II he toured the mid-West with his own show & with other shows. Worked for Abbott's around the 1960s. Invented Cutting a Girl in Sixths, etc. Proprietor of Arturo's Magic Studio in Topeka, Kansas, during the late 1970s and early 1980s.

name: Arx, Von
bio: See: Nicol, Charles Albert

name: Asahi, Tomo
bio: (Japan: fl.1900s-10s) Pro sleight-of-hand. Toured USA 1909-1919, playing the New York Palace in 1913, 1918 (twice), & 1919. He featured Thumb Tie and Water Fountain Illusion. [Pr]

name: Ascanio [y Navaz], Dr Arturo de
bio: (Canary Islands, Spain: 22 Mar 1929-6 Apr 1997) Magistrate in Madrid. Amateur close-up magician. A leading master of sleight-of-hand & prominent magic theorist. In 1956 when Ascanio had already mastered the Kaps & Vernon methods & created his original color-changing knives routine, David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg judged him "the best magician I ever saw in Spain or in Latin America". 1959 Spanish National Congress (in Seville) Grand Prix. Invented Ascanio Spread by 1970. In 1971 co-founded the Escuela Mágica de Madrid. Visited USA conventions in 1982 & 1989 and FFFF 1997 in Las Vegas. Died of a heart attack with a deck of cards in his hands. Wrote Navajas y Daltonismo (1958, 250pp), English tr by José de la Torre as Ascanio's World of Knives (1975, 95pp); La Magia de Ascanio (2 vols, 1977, 1980), English tr as The Magic of Ascanio (forthcoming 1992); The Psychology of Palming (1982 tr, 24pp); El Manejo de la Carta Doble (1982), with English tr as About the Handling of Double Cards (1982). See John Racherbaumer, The Ascanio Spread (1976, 35pp). Articles in Epilogue, Magie, etc. [Bam,p.293]

name: Ashdown, David
bio: See: Gill, Richard

name: Ashton [III], David [Fredric]
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: fl.1970s-90s) Taught by Roy Kissell, Karrell Fox, Warren Stevens, & Milt Kort. Pro magician. Mentalist since late 1970s. Substitute medium of the Magic Castle's Houdini Séance Room for 3 years in late 1980s. Moved to Portland where retired from magic to become a writer & producer of audio & video learning programs. Effects in Magick, Genii, New Invocation, & MUM. [Mag]

name: Asi-Kitch-San
bio: (Aukland, New Zealand: 17 Jul 1897-19 Jun 1987) Magician & Juggler. Performed during World War I. Founder Member of the Society of New Zealand Magicians 1920. Honorary Member of the Society of New Zealand Magicians. SEE: Yanagawa, Asakichi

name: Aspen, Finn
bio:
"Asps, The" SEE: Airaksinen, Aino & Jorma

[See also: Airaksinen, Aino & Jorma]

name: Assan
bio: (Grodno, Poland [now Belarus]: 1945-) Stage name of Henryk Salkiewicz. Pro illusionist & manipulator. 1981 Sofia 2nd prize. 1984 Austria 1st prize in general magic. [Mec]

name: Asta, Joe
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 3 Jun 1901-1971) Stage name of Josef Aksamit. Student of Austrian magician Rolf Hansen. Pro stage illusionist in the Viennese style. Toured several countries. [Mec]

name: Astley, Philip
bio: (Newcastle-under-Lyme, England: 8 Jan 1742-18 Oct 1814) Riding master. Performed magic while on horseback. Widely miscredited as the creator of the modern circus when in 1768 he presented the second show to include all the traditional acts: gymnasts, animal trainers, circus riding, & pantomime. Played Paris in 1772 & 1782 and toured the Continent 1782. Wrote Natural Magic: or, Physical Amusements Revealed (1785, 45pp). Died in Paris. See A.H. Saxon, Enter Foot and Horse (1968), which is a history of Astley's circus & the Cirque Olympique. [Sal;Daw]

name: Astor, Mister
bio: (Choumen, Bulgaria: 18 Nov 1943- ) Stage name of Antranik [sic] Shavarsh Arabadjiyan. Learned 2 small tricks from grandmother in 1949. Pro magician since 1963, specializing in close-up, illusions, manip, mental, & comedy magic. Gave his 1st 1-man 2-hour show in 1968. In 1975 founded Bulgaria's 1st magic club (for professionals) & its chairman since 1978. Won 13 convention prizes 1974-81, including in Bulgaria (1974), Czechoslovakia (1978), Norway (1978), USA (1981). Since 1983 tours a large illusion show (with 5 dancers & a singer) to hotels in Europe, Africa, Asia, & Australia. Dealer (Astor Magic Studio) in Sofia. Since 1989 runs a 100-seat theater ("Magic Theatre—99") in Sofia. Over 100 TV bits internationally. [Mec;Wh2]

name: Astor, V[ictor] J[amnitzky]
bio: (Ungvar, Hungary: 22 Sep 1922- ) Stage name of Victor Andreas Jamnitzky since 1950 (previously as "Nicoletti"). "At age 8 I saw a magician and started thinking." Pro magician since 1941. Moved to West Germany. Mail-order magic dealer-publisher ("Astor") in Wuppertal 1970-present. Published books by Rodolfo, Jahn Gallo, & Kovari. Invented over 200 effects. Wrote Die magische Präsentation, Das Superhirn, Das Buch mit den sieben Siegeln, Das System der Magie, & Der Astor Lernkursus. Articles in Abra, Magische Welt, & Magie. [Wh2]

name: Astrallvi
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 26 Jul 1938-) Stage name of Andrzej Słowiński. Son of an architect. Pro illusionist & manipulator. TV bits in Poland. [Mec]

name: Astrid
bio: (Germany: -30 Jun 1971) Stage name of Hilde Hufenbach. Pro assistant-wife of Kurt "Truk" Hufenbach as "Astrid & Truk" 1951-56, accompanying him with her own card & cigarette manipulations. (Mül)

name: Astroi
bio: (France: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro. During summer season of the Exposition in Nancy, France, became the first magician to perform airborne before an audience (of 8 passengers), doing so at 2,000-feet in a dirigible with the Egg Bag & the Card in Cigarette. [Magic10/06,3]

name: Atelenta
bio: (Scotland: fl.1920s) Wife of Rex Palmer "Comanche Jim" Gordon. Pro escape artist in Scotland. [Mar]

name: Atkins, Jack
bio: See: Iversen, Tommy

name: Atkins, [Henry Jeffery] "Jeff", MIMC
bio: (Southampton, England: 3 Sep 1919-19 Mar 2001) Learned at age 12 (or 7?) from box of tricks. Company director oof a stationery firm in Southampton. Amateur magician as "Jeffalo" 1936-42. Then semi-pro with an historical act, "Illusions of the Masters". Pet effect: Asrah Levitation. A stalwart of the British Ring, including British Ring Past President. IBM President 1977-78, only the 2nd Briton to hold that office. Wrote The Magic Kettle: Any Drink Called For (1972, 32pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Abra, & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Atkins, Tommy
bio: See: Iversen, Tommy

name: Atsukawa, Masao
bio: (Japan: 8 May 1933 - 3 Feb 2009) Prize-winning mystery writer under anagrammatic pen name of "Awasaka Tsumao". Won the 1990 Naoki Award for outstanding popular literary work of the year. Studied magic with Tenkai. Amateur card magician. 1969 [sic] Tenkai Prize. Atsukawa Creativity Award that was named after him produced many talented magicians over the years. Wrote Creative Works of Masao Atsukawa (1970). 1 video bit (1993).

name: Atterbury, Sheldon [McChesney]
bio: (Sierra Madre, California: 4 Apr 1921-) Learned 1927-40 from Mysto Magic and Chandu Magic sets. Chavez course 1947. Then briefly pro stage, close-up & sleight-of-hand. 2 PCAM awards 1948. Co-founder of Johnson Products 1968. Accountant & real estate broker (now retired) & semi-pro magician. Magic teacher c1970-c80. Tricks in Tarbell Course #7 & New Tops. [Wh2]

name: Aubert
bio: (France: fl.1st decade of 1800s) Opened a magic shop in Paris in 1808. Having passed through several owners, it still exists as Magie Moderne, the world's oldest continuously operated magic dealership. Aubrey — the Magician (USA: 1931-2 May 1989) Stage name of James Crabe. Chavez School graduate. Pro manipulator & illusionist on West Coast. Many TV bits in 1950s. Trick in MUM. Then became a prize-winning Hollywood movie & TV cinematographer. [Genii1/89;Wat]

name: Auburn, [Thomas Rochford] "Tom
bio: (Montreal, Canada: 7 Jul 1917-3 Jan 1990) Son of English immigrants. Inspired seeing Cardini, Thurston, & Blackstone. Learned at age 12 from Thurston's card book. Paid debut in 1930. Popular pro close-up magician in Montreal since age 18. Aka "Magic Tom". Pattered in both French & English. Did local TV show 1960-75 (4,000 performances), being the longest-running TV show in Montreal. Played Hawaii many winters in early 1980s. In late 1980s until his death still did 75-100 shows per year. Collector. [Tops7/73; Daw2; Wh2]

name: Auer, James [Matthew] "Jim
bio: (Neenah, Wisconsin: 2 Dec 1928-) Learned in early teenage from books. Journalist. Semi-promental & psychic magic. Wrote The Spirit is Willing (1961, 56pp). Articles in Genii & Magigram. [WWA;Wh2]

name: Auguste
bio: See: Lassaigne, Auguste

name: Aurelio
bio: See: Paviato, Aurelio

name: Aurifeuille, Antoine
bio:
Austin, A. Everett "Chick" (USA: -1957) Museum director, initially as head of the Wadsworth Atheneum in Hartford, Connecticut, until 1944. Amateur magician with sleights and stage apparatus, performing regularly in the Atheneum's theater as “Osram, The Man of Multiple Mysteries”. Thence Director of the Ringling Museum in Sarasota, Florida, until his death. Bio in Steven Watson, Prepare for Saints (New York: Random House, 1998), 156-162, 309-315.

[See also: De Caston, Alfred]

name: Austral, Professor
bio: See: Hammond, H[arold] C.

name: Authors, Yvonne
bio: (Britain: 11 Dec 1951-) Winner of Craig Trophy 1971 & 1982. Married Terry Watson.

name: Auweiler, Josef
bio: (Germany: 7 Aug 1921-) Magician and magic history collector in Köln, Germany. Aka "Francesco Altini". [Nad]

name: Auzet, Alfred
bio: See: "Alyett"

name: Auzinger, Max
bio: (Munich, Germany: 26 Jul 1839-14 May [sic] 1928) Comedian & son of comedians. Stage director in Berlin. Invented the Black Art act in 1885. Aka "Maxistan A. Uzinger" at debut as magician on 28 Jun [sic] 1885 when he premiered his novel act in Berlin at the Castan brother's Panoptikum. Later worked as "Ben Ali Bey". Assisted by his daughter Leopoldine. Died in Berlin. [Win;Vo56;Rob;St;CMM12/07]

name: Auzinger, Leopoldine
bio: (Germany: -7 Feb 1949) Daughter of Max Auzinger whom she assisted in oriental costume as "Sulamith" in his Black Art act in the late 1880s. Died in Berlin. Avadon, David [nmn] "Ava, Fakir of" SEE: Hughes, Isaiah Harris (Los Angeles, California: fl.1960s-80s) Learned at age 9 from library books. Pro intimate table & stand-up magic & pickpocket act since c1969. Society & trade show performer. Co-author of The Berg Book (1983). Tricks in Magick. Book reviewer for Epoptica & Genii. Prop reviewer for Genii since 1991. Collector. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Avalon, AI
bio: See: Haviland, Hal

name: Avelino, José [Maria]
bio: (Braga, Portugal: 25 Jul 1859-2 Mar 1939) Pro illusionist. [Cam]

name: Avelino da Silva, José
bio: (Ilha do Faial, Azores, Portugal: 1887-Mar 1966) Pro escapist & magician. Moved to USA, working as "Diavolino", & settling in New Bedford, Connecticut, in 1949. [Cam]

name: Awerino, [Juri Kyrilovich]
bio: (Tiflis, Georgia, USSR: 6 Oct 1931- ) From a Russian circus family. Circus acrobat-clown-jugger 1944 to 1966 when switched to circus illusion-show magic. Now does 20 minute illusion act with the Moscow State Circus. [Magische Welt6/90;Win]

name: Avis, Jack [Arthur], MIMC
bio: (Beckenham, Kent, England: 27 Jul 1921-8 Jan 2004) Inspired & learned at age 12 from tricks in Wizard comics. Amateur card & close-up magician since then, initially with stage name "Siva". 50 years in printing trade before retiring. Hobbies: cabinet making & book binding. Magic Circle Reference Librarian since 1990. Died of heart attack. Invented Message from Hades (1953) & the Siva Count (5-as-4) by 1977 when published by Mentzer. Wrote Minds in Duplicate (1956, 32pp). Tricks in Pentagram, New Pentagram, Gen, Abra, Phoenix, Hugard's, Pallbearers, Chronicles, Linking Ring, MUM, Pabular, Epilogue, Ibidem, & Technomagic. [Wh2] Avner the Eccentric (Atlanta, Georgia: fl.1960s-90s) Stage name of Avner Eisenberg. Pro mime combining magic, juggling, clowning, acrobatics, etc. Studied mime with Jacques LeCoq in Paris & with Carlo Mazzone-Clementi in California. Debut in 1967. BA degree in theatre 1971. One-man show on Broadway 1984-85 & Hollywood 1991. An international star. Played "The Jewel" in movie The Jewel of the Nile (1985). [Genii2/90]

name: Avon, Dr.
bio: See: Kollmann, Dr. Artur

name: Ayala, Joaquin
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 21 Mar 1963-) Stage name of Joaquin AYALA ALDAVE. Inspired in 1975 seeing magic on TV. Debut at age 12. Lawyer in Mexico City. Part-time pro since c1985, specializing in stage magic (mainly bird act with parakeets) done to music. Also close-up. Works with assistant-wife Lilia. Has played Las Vegas, Magic Castle, New York City, Spain, & Tokyo NHK-TV. Played the Zona Rosa in Mexico City 1989-90. Managed by James Randi. Invented Floating Clarinet (1984) & Diamond Zombie to Lamp (1986). Articles in several Mexican journals. [Ran;Wh2]

name: Ayalon, Eytan
bio: (Tel Aviv, Palestine [now Israel]: 19 May 1927-) A Mason. Journalist. Part-time pro magician in Pardes-Hana. Specializes in mental, card, rope, & burlesque magic plus chapeaugraphy. AFAP Master Magician since 1967. Founder-President of Cercle Magique Jules-Dhotel in 1963 in Haifa as a branch of the AFAP. ..... [Bou;Wh5]

name: Ayam
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 20 Feb 1959- ) Stage name of Francisco Manuel Viana MAYA SANTOS since his debut in 1975. Protégé of Jodivil. 1977 2nd prize in manip at the 4th Festival Mágico in Portugal and 1979 Grand Prize at the 5th Festival. [Cam]

name: Ayling, Will[iam Richard], MIMC
bio: (Portsmouth, England: 2 Mar 1914-23 May 1992) Learned from a box of tricks. Since 1930 has been variously an amateur, semi-pro, & pro magician with close-up, general magic, & illusions. President, British Ring, 1981-82. Lecturer & collector. Collapsed and died at the roadside while traveling to a show. Wrote The Art of Illusion (1968, 237pp; repr 1971), Genii Presentations (1972, 163pp), Oriental Conjuring and Magic (1981, 384pp, with Sam Sharpe), Knowing the Egg Bag (1988, 36pp), Ganson Supreme (1988), etc. Tricks in Abra, Genii, & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Ayra, Mago
bio: (Santiago de Cuba, Cuba: 9 Apr 1943- ) Stage name of José ALVAREZ AYRA. Learned from book by W. Ciuró. Pro. Toured East Bloc. TV program in Cuba 1977-80. [Xe]

name: Ayrens, Claude
bio: (France: fl.1970s) Stage name of M Goddefroy. Pro. Played the Cabinet Fantastique in Paris in 1977.

name: Azagara, Prince
bio: (Lezignan, France: 3 Jun 1947- ) Stage name of Jean Arnal. Learned at age 14. Pro, originally with fakir act that included snake-charming. Then alternating as illusionist, working with pumas, leopards, doves, & rabbits. Played Lisbon & the Paris Olympia in 1972 & the Casino de Paris 1976-79. [Win;Al]

name: Azardo
bio: See: Miret, Charly

name: Baba, Ali
bio: See: Greystoke, R. Temple

name: Babetti
bio: (Belgium: fl.1940s-c1960s) Stage name of Van Gheluwe. A circus clown in Europe before 1940. Joined the Free French Army in 1941 as an entertainer, touring the Belgian Congo, Nigeria, Egypt, & Palestine. After WW II he moved to Zaire, performing as a magic clown & teaching magic. [Dif]

name: Backhaus, Willy
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 30 Aug 1888-1 July 1968) Amateur magician in Leipzig. Wrote Magischer Zeitvertreib (1908, 185pp). Many tricks in Der Zauberspiegel. Died in Leipzig, East Germany.

name: Bader, Egon
bio: (Germany: 24 Jul 1933-) Stage magician as "Amando". President of MZvD-OZ Freiburg.

name: Badley, Ben[jamin] R.
bio: (Baton Rouge, Louisiana: 26 Dec 1895 [sic]-19 Sep 1950) Inspired at age 7 seeing Leon Herrmann. Learned at age c11 from gift of Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Pro since 1911 when joined a touring hypnotist. Moved to St. Louis in 1916. Played southern states in road shows & carnivals as "Devo from Dixieland" until c1918. Added hypnotism to his act of small magic in WW I while in US Army. In 1927 became 1st person to present hypnotism over radio (on local station with a 24-hour "window sleep"). In 1930s became an estimator for a St. Louis engraving firm. In 1943 co-refounded (with Roba Collins & Richard Durham) St. Louis Society of Magicians. Articles in Sphinx, Linking Ring, & Tops. [Monti;Tops7/43;SAM;WWM]

name: Bael, Dr. Theodore
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Ted Olshanski. Inspired at age 8 by Ron Urban and Ed Marlo. Pro stage magic to mentalism. [Mag]

name: Baffel, Will
bio: See: Keene, Robertson

name: Bagshawe, Edward [F.]
bio: (Britain: 1902 or 1903-17 Feb 1940) Pro dealer (Bagshawe & Co.) in London early 1920s-1940. Invented the Reverso deck in 1921, the Optica deck by 1928, & A Message From Beyond by 1932. Wrote Exclusive Problems in Magic (1924, 90pp), Novel Mysteries (mid-1920s, 6 booklets totalling 234pp), The Ie Walke Mysteries (1927), & Twenty Magical Novelties (1930). As house organs published & edited Magical Monthly 1923-26, Talks on Tricks 1926-27, & Magical Journal 1927-33. Committed suicide. His business was then absorbed by Davenport's. A bio article by Farelli is in J.B. Findlay's Sixth Collectors Annual (1954). [St;Le]

name: Bai, Ottorino
bio: (Milan, Italy: 2 Mar 1921- ) Businessman in Milan. Amateur magician since 1938, specialized in mental magic as "Misterius". President of C.L.A.M. [Wh5]

name: Bailey, Michael [D. H.], MIMC
bio: (Harrow, Middlesex, England: 1930- ) Learned at age 14 & gave 1st paid show at age 17. After Army service became an ad man & semi-pro magician. MIMC 1952 (youngest ever). In 1950s worked kidshows, clubs, cabarets, & variety plus many TV bits in Britain, Germany, Sweden, & the USA. Magic Circle Silver Wand 1960. In 1971 turned full-time pro comedy & trade show magician, working mainly trade shows. A Royal Command performer & popular M.C. Magic Circle President 1998-2003 Invented Aerial Penetration (1965) & Skyscraper Boxes (1972). Played part of magician in Kubrick's film Barry Lyndon (1975). Reporter for Magic Circular. Wrote The Magic Business (1998, 390pp). [MUM6/2003;MC10/84;Mag;Wh5]

name: Bailey, S [amuel] Willson "Sam
bio: (Cambridge, Massachusetts: 19 May 1875-30 Jun 1935) Learned at age 5 from Xmas gift box-of-tricks. Pro, touring several seasons as "The Boy Magician". Assisted William E. Robinson. Pro dealer with prop-maker partner W. Albert in Boston as Bailey & Tripp Magical Company from 1896 to late 1919 when Tripp died. Then in Cambridge ("Cambridgeport") as S. Willson Bailey Co. to 1925 when his shop was bought out by Ducrot. SAM membership #61 & IBM #97. Wrote (with Harold A. Osborne) Wrinkles: A Few Suggestions and Innovations (1910, 62pp). [Albo95; Sphinx7/35; Dor]

name: Baird, Bill
bio: (South St. Louis, Missouri: 5 Mar 1914-8 Aug 1978) Stage name of William "Bill" Keckritz. Debut at age 15. Protégé of Paul LePaul. Pro mind-reader to manipulator. Played USO in WW II & Korean War. His ex-wife, Florine Manners, trooped her own magic act in the 1950s. [Monti;Pr;HMM11/53] NOTE: Bill Baird is not to be confused with famous puppeteer Bil Baird (d.1987).

name: Baird, Paula [Franklin]
bio: (Hastings, England: c1918-16 Nov 1998) Inspired by accidental Xmas gift of magic set. Tuition from Leo Martin c1931. Semi-pro by age 15. Demmed at Gamage's 1938. Pro manipulator with own act. Toured North Africa with ENSA 1941-44. 1948 FISM 2nd prize in manip. Magic Circle Silver Wand. Society entertainer in 1940s & 50s billed as "the Queen of Magic". Retired in early 1960s. [Mar;LR9/92]

name: Bakalar, Marvin
bio: (New York City, New York: 9 Nov 1943-) Learned at age 7 from tricks bought by father. Real estate salesman in New York. Semi-promentalist and close-up & stage magician since 1973. Played Magic Towne House 1974-79. Producer of "Chamber Magic" show at Title Theatre in Greenwich Village 1979-80. Proprietor of Le Chat Noir magic club 1979-81, which featured the "Chamber Magic" show 1980-81. Radio & TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Baker, Al
bio: (Poughkeepsie, New York: 4 Sep 1874-24 [or 31?] Oct 1951) Learned at age 12 when father taught a simple trick, then from a Hoffmann book. Pro comedy magus since 1895, soon adding vent. A Chautauqua star c1911-c1928. Partner with Martin Sunshine of Broadway Magic Shop in New York City in early 1930s (since 1931). Mentor of Bill Arenholz, Leslie P. Guest, etc. One of the 5 original members of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1932. Voted one of the 10 Card Stars in 1938. Named 3rd Dean of American Magicians in 1938. SAM Hall of Fame. Father-in-law of Jay Marshall 1940-53. Invented the Think Stop Trick (by 1919), Untying Silk (by 1919), probably the Purse Frame (late 1920s), the Baker Slate (in 1929), the Albaka card trick (1933), the Baker-Scope (by 1936), Number Please (by 1936, with Walsh), the Chewing Gum Trick (by 1937), Biting a Plate (by 1940), Al Producto (by 1940), The Vanishing Pencil (by 1941), Vocalepathy (by 1941), The Travelling Pencils (by 1941), & the Umbrella Move (by 1949). Wrote 4 books: Al Baker's Book (1933, 2 vols, 32+32pp), Magical Ways and Means (1941, 135pp), How to Perform Mental Magic (1949, 116pp), & Pet Secrets (1951, 111pp), all classics. Also the booklets Al Baker's Complete Manuscript (1923) & Cardially Yours (1933). Tweed Robinson is writing a book on Baker's life & magic. [Pr;Se; Sphinx9/33;Ho;WWM]

name: Baker, Dr [Robert William] "Bob", MD
bio: (New York City, NY: 7 Dec 1951-) Inspired at age 5 seeing TV magic show. Physician. Semi-pro close-up mentalism. Wrote Shared Thoughts (1985, 97pp). Articles in Genii, Seance, Vibrations, & Hocus Pocus. [Wh2]

name: Baker, Carroll
bio: (Johnstown, Pennsylvania: 28 May 1931-) Joined a dance company in Florida where she was trained in magic by Burling Hull in 1950. Thence as "Karol Carroll, The Girl with the Magic Jewels" she did her magic-dance act throughout Southern towns with the Kemp Time Vaudeville Circuit for a mere $20 per week plus expenses. Moved to Hollywood where she got a movie bit part in 1953. Then to New York City where she joined the Actors Studio in 1953, soon doing Broadway plays & TV dramas. Back to Hollywood to play opposite James Dean in Giant (1956) & the title role in Elia Kazan's Baby Doll (1956), which got her an Academy Award nomination. Thence downhill in several U.S. & foreign films. Bio by Maurice Zolotow in American Weekly (24 Mar 1957). Autobio is Baby Doll (1983), see pp25-26. [HMM4/57;Katz]

name: Baker, Harmon E.
bio: (USA: 2 Apr 1887-31 Jul 1993) Inspired at age 8 meeting Herrmann the Great. Entered vaudeville at age 15. A Mason. Pro magician as "The Baffling Mr. Baker". After WW I was a manager of a physical therapy equipment company. Appeared on Johnny Carson show in 1983. Oldest living member of the IBM in 1990 when he was still performing. On his death at age 106 he was probably the world's oldest living magician. [Ostomy Quarterly,V.29,#4]

name: Baker, [John Edwin] "Jack
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 1914-5 Oct 1980) Born John Kessler. Adopted by Wyman Baker's adoptive parents c1936. Aka "Dr Silkini" & "Dr Sin" in 1940s-50s when doing a straight magic & illusion act with spook-show closer. [Walk2;Tay]

name: Baker, Roy
bio: (England: fl.1950s-80s; died 10 Nov 2006) Stage name of Geoffrey R. H. Hursell, aka "Zaharee". Pro performer (with hyp act) & mail order dealer (in Rainham, Kent). Invented the Fez Egg Bag (Abdul's Fez) by late 1960s. See Hugh Miller, Baker's Bonanza (1969; reprinted 1972). Wrote Baker's Capers (1983). [La2]

name: Baker, Steve
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: fl.1960s-80s) Aka "Mr. Escape". Pro escapist. One HBO-TV special. Adviser on movie The Escape Artist (1982). [Mag]

name: Baker, Walter
bio: (USA: 1887-31 Aug 1993) Billed as "Baffling Baker". Pro vaude comedy magician & sleight-of-hand artist based in Chicago. Featured Cards on the Sheet of Glass, Card in Cigarette, & Linking Rings plus one illusion as closer. Played Australia in 1915. Worked as builder for Thayer's & was dealer-prop maker on own. In 1926 he replaced Jim Sherman as the commissioned writer of what later became the famous Tarbell Course, himself being replaced later that same year by Harlan Tarbell. [Ho;Wal] Baker, Wyman A. (probably in Sharon, Wisconsin: c1917-4 Sep 1996) Born Wyman Calkins, thence adopted as a child by the Bakers. Pro stage magician since 1930s, touring mid-West with straight magic act that ended with Spook Show that in the 1940s was the whole act as "Dr Silkini". His brother Jack did the same, also as "Dr. Silkini". [Walk2]

name: Balabrega
bio: (Hälsingborg, Sweden: 20 Aug 1857-20 Jun 1900) Stage name of John M. "Bal" Miller, aka "The Swedish Wonder". Inspired as a child in Sweden by seeing Prof Le Tort. Learned soon after moving to the USA at age 11 when he read a magic book. Pro since 1878. Invented Pillory Escape (by 1882). Killed on stage during performance by a petrol tank explosion in Pernambuco, Brazil. Next year Martinka's received and sold his entire outfit (45 trunks). [Pr;Mo;Vo58;Magic3/01,6/01]

name: Balandras, Michel
bio: (France: 20 Feb 1943-) Aka "Alan Kid". Co-publisher-editor (with Jean-Yves Prost) of Arcane in Bagé-le-Chatel since 1975.

name: Balasco, Bodine
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 10 May 1949- ) His real name. Raised in Kentucky. In 1972 took degrees at UCLA in Speech Communications & Social Psychology. Pro close-up & gambling demo since his debut at The Crazy Horse Saloon in Malibu Beach, California, in 1974. Originally billed as "The Last of the Riverboat Gamblers" when working Mississippi boats. Now, billed as "An Evening with the Last of the Riverboat Gamblers", he does a full 2-hour act. Also does trade shows. [Mag;Wh]

name: Balducci
bio: (Italy: fl.1720s-30s) Pro exhibitor of pseudo-automata since 1720. Toured Germany c1738. [St]

name: Balducci, Ed[mund Mariano]
bio: (USA: c1907-9 Feb 1988) Civil engineer. Amateur cardman in New York inner circle. Close friend of Ed Marlo. Introduced his famous Card in Wallet effect in 1958 in Apr HMM. Invented the Cut-Deeper Force. Tricks in HMM, Pallbearers, & Chronicles.

name: Baldwin, Professor Samri S.
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 21 Jan 1848 [sic]-10 Mar 1924) Inspired in youth seeing the Davenport Brothers' act. Pro mentalist since c1865. Aka "The White Mahatma". Toured Australia (1878, 1879, 1884, &1887) & India. Retired from the stage in 1899 to become an unsuccessful merchant. Made a stage comeback 1904-06. Consultant to Thurston 1920. Died in San Francisco. Invented Spirit Handcuffs (by 1898) & possibly Clipboard (specifically the wax impression method, by 1897). Memoir is The Secrets of Mahatma Land Explained (1895). See Thomas A. Sawyer, My Dear Friend Baldwin (1972, 9pp) for excerpts from his correspondence. [Pr;Wal;Mo]

name: Balfonte, Paul
bio: See: Allen, Paul

name: Balister, Pierre
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 5 Aug 1900-29 Aug 1965) Pro magic dealer-mechanic in Brussels. Co-wrote (with Jean Arnolis) Les mains magiques (1946 in only 4 copies).

name: Ball, Sieur
bio: (Britain: fl.1820s) Pro. Pet effect: Egg Bag. [Fr]

name: Ball, Fred [Douglas]
bio: (Davenport, Iowa: 28 Dec 19-) Moved to Honolulu, Hawaii. Pro actor-comedian since 1960. Under own name as actor, mainly TV ("Hawaii 5-0" & many others filmed in Hawaii). On local TV as magician "Professor Fun" 1967-c1984. Also night club comic-magician as "Freddie Shaka" 1967-present. Plus part-time local booking agent (Fun Enterprises) since c1979. Edited Ballsheet 1971?-1974?, an annual magic newsletter. One trick in Genii. [Wh2]

name: Ball, Professor W[alter] W[illiam] Rouse
bio: (Britain: 1850-4 Apr 1925) Barrister & distinguished mathematician. Amateur magician. Collector of mechanical toys & owner of largest collection in Britain of mathematicians' portraits. Professor at Trinity College, Cambridge U, in 1919 when he co-founded the Pentacle Club & was elected its first President. Wrote Mathematical Recreations and Essays (1892, 240pp; 1947 revised), which includes a section on card tricks. [WWW; Daw2]

name: Balla, John
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1902- ) Physician. Amateur magician, working in the Vanek style. Member of M.A.M.E. since 1930. [WWM]

name: Ballantine, Carl "Jipper
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 27 Sep 1917 – 3 Nov 2009) Stage name of Meyer Kessler. Inspired at age 12 by his barber who would do the Thimbles while cutting Carl's hair. Originally a printer. Then in Chicago in the 1930s doing pro straight magic, first as "Count Marakoff" & "Carl Sharp", then, since the early 1940s switched to comedy magic as "Carl Ballantine" billed as "The Amazing Mr. Ballantine". Played the New York Capitol in 1950. The Ed Sullivan TV show in 1953, & the Las Vegas El Rancho Vegas in 1956. Also a TV comedian ("McHale's Navy", etc) since 1959 & movie actor since 1965. Won Tannen's "Louie". 1985 AMA Performing Fellowship. [LR5/06;HC;Berg;Wh2]

name: Ballester Diez, Dr. Miguel
bio: (Spain: fl.1970s) Specialized in cigarette manip. 1973 1st prize in manip at 2nd Festival Mágico (Portugal).

name: Balli, Vittorio
bio: (Florence, Italy: 29 Mar 1935- ) Inspired at age 6 seeing an amateur. Pro stage & mental magician since 1960 as "Victor". Edited Italia nella Magia 1963 (2 issues) & II Prestigiatore Moderno 1976-present. Wrote Victormagia '81, Victormagia '85, La Magia di Victor, etc. Articles in Magia Moderna, II Prestigiatore Moderno, CEDAM, etc.

name: Balsamo
bio: (Siedlcach, Poland: 1922-) Stage name of Zbigniew Grigoriew. Pro with manip & giant memory acts. [Mec]

name: Balsamo, Giuseppe
bio: See: "Cagliostro, Count Alessandro di"

name: Balton
bio: (Graz, Austria: 25 Jan 1902-29 Aug 1955) Stage name of Anton Ball. Pro card magician. Played the major venues. Growing blind in his last decade, committed suicide. [Vo57]

name: Balzar, Harry
bio: (Josefstadt, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 11 Jan 1879-26 Mar 1947) Stage name of Jindrich Balzar. Moved to Paris where he worked as retoucher for the famous photographer-portraitist Reutlinger. Pro magician since debut in 1905 in Paris at the Étoile-Palace. Initially with coin manip act, later with card & silk tricks. In 1906 worked with partner as "Les Balzaros". Toured Europe & USA. Known for elegant performance. Active member of Magicky Klub Praha. Died in Prague. [Dif;Vo57;St]

name: Bamberg, David [Tobias] "Dave
bio: (Derby, England: 19 Feb 1904-19 Aug 1974) Aka "Syko" 1917-27, "David King" 1921, and "Fu-Manchú" (based on Sax Rohmer's famous thriller character "Fu Manchu") since 1929 (except for "Fu Manxu" in Barcelona in 1933 & "Fu-Chan" in New York City in 1937). Only son of pro magician Tobias "Theo" Bamberg ("Okito") and his English wife, Lily. Brought by parents to USA in 1908. Learned from observing father. Became USA citizen in 1916. As "Syko" (a name suggested by Houdini) worked as Julius Zancig's assistant in mindreading act 1917-18. On own as "David King" toured western USA & back across Canada in 1921. Briefly as mitt-reader ("Prof. Zaza") on Atlantic City's Boardwalk 1921. Toured USA as uncle Ed's assistant 1923. On own toured Serbia, Czechoslovakia, & Austria 1924. As Okito's assistant 1924-25 toured Germany, Paris, Belgium, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, & England. Moved to Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1926. Toured Brazil & played Buenos Aires 1926-27 as assistant to The Great Raymond. Pro illusionist on own since mid-1927. Toured Spain (plus Gibraltar, North Africa, & Portugal) 1932-34. Moved to Mexico City in 1934. Toured Mexico and played Havana 1936 & New York City in 1937 when he was voted into the New York "Inner Circle". Toured Latin America from 1937 until 1941 when he returned to live in Mexico City. Made 6 feature films in Mexico in 1943-44 (and released between 1943 & 1949). Only the first three show his magic: El Espectro de la Novia (1943), La Mujer Sin Cabeza (1944), & El As Negro (1944). Based in Argentina since 1947. Toured Spain 1955. Returned to Argentina where he semi-retired in 1966. Dealer ("Centro Mágico") in Buenos Aires 1966-74. SAM Hall of Fame. 1984 CMI Order of Magic Lamp (posthumous). Wrote Los Secretos de Fu-Manchú: "The Devil Doctor" (c1933). Articles in Sphinx 1937-53. Trick in Tarbell #5. Much bio info (often incorrect) is in Robert J. Albo, Oriental Magic of the Bambergs (1950); & particularly Robert E. Olson, Illusion Builder to Fu Manchu (1986). His own superb autobio is Illusion Show: A Life in Magic (1988, 331pp). The definitive work on his films is Enrique Jiménez-Martínez, "Films of Fu Manchu" [sic], Linking Ring (Sep 1977). NOTE: "Fu Manchu" is wrong English form of his stage name, despite fact that the Sax Rohmer character on which it is based was spelled "Fu Manchu". David Bamberg's letterhead & signature was always "Fu-Manchú" to give the correct Spanish pronunciation. [OI;Pr;Geni8/74;Ch;Fu]

name: Bamberg, David Leendert
bio: (Leiden, Holland: 1786-29 Jan 1869) Learned assisting father Eliaser Bamberg for 9 years. Pro sleight-of-hand on own since 1812. Appointed Court Conjuror to King William II in 1834. Invented Bamberg Egg Bag. Retired at age 82. Father of magician Tobias Bamberg. [Pr]

name: Bamberg, David Tobias "Papa
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 9 Aug 1843-20 Jul [or May?] 1914) Only son of Tobias Bamberg. Taught by pro father. After studying to be an actor chose to be a magician after seeing Compars Herrmann. Became a pro illusionist in 1866 at age 23. Appointed Court Conjuror to King William III in 1870. Taught 21-year-old H.J. Burlingame in 1873 in Rotterdam. Toured Indonesia & South Asia 1907 [sic] for 6 months. Died in Amsterdam. Of his 6 sons, 3 became magicians: Theo, Emile, & Eduard. NOTE: Volkmann errs on death date as "9 Aug 1913". [Pr]

name: Bamberg, Eduard "Ed
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 23 Jul 1889-1951-dead) Youngest son of David Tobias Bamberg. Learned at age 10 assisting father in Holland. Pro shadowist & sleight-of hand artist. Aka "Nelusco". Moved to USA, working as "Ed Rickard" with assistant-wife Hattie (who juggled). Played Australia in 1917 (as "Nelusco & Hurley") & 1938 (as "Eddie Ricard"), being the only Bamberg to tour there. [Pr;Bam;Wal]

name: Bamberg, Eliaser [Leendert]
bio: (Leyden, Holland: 1760-1833) Probably the natural or adoptive son of Jasper Bamberg. Prosleight-of-hand artist & exhibitor of automata at fairs & in public squares. Following loss of a leg c1793 in a powder explosion on the Dutch warship on which he was serving, was nicknamed "Le diable boiteux" [The Crippled Devil] due to his wooden leg, which he used as a servante. Played Berlin in Jul 1823. Claimed in 1823 playbills to have been a student of Pinetti. Father of David Leendert Bamberg. Died in Leyden. [Pr;Bam]

name: Bamberg, Emile [born Emanuel]
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 11 Nov 1883-23 May 1966) Learned as assistant to father David Tobias "Papa" Bamberg. Pro pianist & semi-pro manipulation who gave magical soirees. Was musical director for nephew David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg's big show in New York City in 1937. Elder brother of Eduard & younger brother of Theo. [Pr;Bam]

name: Bamberg, Jasper
bio: (Holland: 1698-1780) The only documented source is an early 1800s Dutch book (Vader Simon Witgeest). Calls him an "alchemist and necromancer" since attending a lecture in the Hague in 1778 by Cagliostro. While seeking the occultist's Philosopher's Stone, he also exhibited Phantasmagoria, that is, producing images of the dead from clouds of smoke from an urn, presumably by the Magic Lantern trick. The book states that he was the natural or adoptive father of Eliaser Bamberg, the true founder of the Bamberg magic dynasty. [Bam;Pr]

name: Bamberg, Lillian "Lily
bio: (England: c1879-Oct [sic] 1946) Born Lillian Maud Poole, daughter of the impresario of the Hippodrome Theatre in Winchester [sic]. In 1903 eloped with Theo "Okito" Bamberg to Bristol where she became his 2nd wife. David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg was born 9 months later. As her husband's stage assistant, billed as "Soy Too" (1913), "Soy Lung Kee" (1920), etc. Died in Mexico City. [Bam;Pr]

name: Bamberg, Marie Dean
bio: (England: -16 May 1950) Born Marie Dean. Main stage assistant of The Great Raymond until 1920 when Theo "Okito" Bamberg stole her away in London. Became the 3rd Mrs Bamberg in 1948. Died in Chicago of throat cancer. [Bam;Pr] Bamberg, [Tobias Leendert] "Toby", then since 1903 "Theo" (Amsterdam, Holland: 15 Jul 1875-28 Jun 1963) Aka "Okito". Eldest son of David Tobias "Papa" Bamberg. Learned at age 11 assisting father. Pro illusionist with pseudo-Japanese act since 1893. Invented vanishing wand in 1887 & fall-apart box (jointly with Carl Willmann) by 1908. Played the Lisbon Coliseu 1900; Casino de Paris 1900, 1901, & 1902 (4 weeks); the Paris Folies-Marigny 1902 (2 weeks); Madrid; & the Winchester Hippodrome 1902-03. "Toby" (Tobias) informally became "Theo" (Theodore) in 1903 at the insistance of his bride. Then played the London Tivoli 1903 (as "Okito & Polising"); St. Petersburg 1904; Europe 1904 (including Russia again); Japan c1905 (as "Lung Tchang Yuen"); Europe 1906-07, Indonesia & South Asia (1907 [sic], with his father); & the Paris Folies-Bergère in 1907. Moved to New York City 1908-1919 (becoming USA citizen in 1916). Invented the Okito Box in 1909. In 1909 swapped his "Okito" name & act for Doc Nixon's flat in Brooklyn. Magic dealer (Bamberg Magic and Novelty Co., as partner with Joseph Klein) in New York City 1909-1914. Troped as prop builder & shadowist with Thurston 1910-11, Rouclere in summer 1911, & Thurston again in 1911-12. Toured USA on own 1913-19 as "Houang Yuen" & "Theo Bamberg". Toured South America in 1919 as assistant & shadowist with Carl Rosini, resuming his "Okito" name & act in Buenos Aires. In 1920 moved to England, touring there in 1920 & playing London's St. George's Hall 1921, 1925, & 1929. Toured South Africa 1920; and Egypt & India 1923-24. Toured Europe 1924-25, playing the Berlin Wintergarten (1924 & 1925), the Vienna Ronacher (1924), the Berlin Scala (1924), the Paris Empire (1925), Belgium, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, Hungary, & Czechoslovakia. Played the Paris Empire again in 1925. Toured South America 1925-26; thence in 1927 Algiers, Morocco, Russia, & Egypt. Toured Argentina & Brazil (with son David) 1932. Lived in semi-retirement in Holland 1932-39 when he fled to Latin America where he toured with his son David. In 1947 moved permanently to the USA, working at Berg's Magic Studio in Chicago 1947-51. Assistant to Don Redmon in Kentucky 1951-52 when retired to Chicago where he died. 1935 Sphinx Award. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote (as "Okito") Quality Magic (1921, 99pp). Unreliable autobio snippets are in his Okito on Magic: Reminiscenses and Selected Tricks (1952, 216pp, with Robert Parrish; 2nd rev ed 1968, 242pp). Tricks in Tarbell #5 & MUM. [Bam;Pr;Berg;Par;Dif;Bo#188;Ho;Magic1/03]

name: Bamberg, [Theodore] Tobias
bio: (Holland: 11 Nov 1812-20 [or 24] Apr 1870) Eldest son of D.L. Bamberg from whom he learned as assistant. [Pr;Roh] Bamman, Howard [Edward Paul] [surname pronounced BAH-mahn] (Chicago, Illinois: 19 Jun 1916-6 Mar 1997) Inspired at age 12 seeing Dante & Blackstone. Public relations by profession (retired). Semi-pro stand-up comedy magic & MC since 1938, as "Howard Edward Paul", "Howard Paul", & "Paul Howard". Column in New Tops mid-1960s. IBM President 1966-67. Executive Editor, The Linking Ring, 1967-1992. [LR5/92,7/66,5/97;Wh2]

name: Bancroft, Frederick
bio: See: Bronson, Frederick

name: Bangemann, Walter
bio: (Hannover, Germany: 5 Oct 1907-16 Nov 1973) Well-known close-up magican in western Germany. Co-founder in 1934 & life-long active member of the Hannover chapter of the German Magic Circle. Died in Hannover, West Germany. [Roh] "Bangs Sisters, The" (USA: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Sisters Lizzie & May Bangs. Famous pseudo-psychic mediums in Chicago. In 1894 they invented Spirit Painting, which reportedly led Isaac K. Funk (of Funk & Wagnalls publishers) to convert to Spiritualism. In 1909 David P. Abbott succeeded in reproducing the effect & gave the secret to other magicians.

name: Banks, Alfred
bio:
Bannon, John A.

[See also: "Ching Wu"]

name: Banks, Ted
bio: (England: c1892-3 Sep 1942) Stage name of Edward Coppin. Originally with the Fred Karmo vaudeville troupe in its 1910-11 season in the USA when he met Blackstone. Stage manager for Blackstone 1923 until his death, with time out working at Abbott's. His death, from a heart attack, was precipitated by the stress of the previous day's fire-alert evacuation of Blackstone's audience & props from the Lincoln Theater in Decatur, Illinois. (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Lawyer in Chicago. Amateur. Wrote Mirage: Modern Card Magic (1986, 58pp), Avante Card One (1989, 16pp), Secret Weapons (1990, 24pp), Impossibilia (1990, 142pp), & Smoke and Mirrors. Edited "The Card Corner" column in Linking Ring 1990-92. Tricks in Linking Ring, Genii, & Magic. See also Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), The Very Best of John Bannon (1988, in French). Video (1990) & video bit (1994).

name: Banshee, Dr. Ogre
bio:
Kelly, George Marquis Mondor, Card

[See also: Calvert, John]

name: Barak
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 2 Feb 1952-) Stage name of Eduardo "Lalo" AZRAK CHEREM. Learned magic as child. Civil engineer until 1983 when became full-time pro magician, specializing in mentalism, close-up, & stage comedy magic. Does some illusions & works trade shows. Pet effect: Coin Matrix. Won 3 national 1st place trophies in close-up & one 2nd place. Invented Barak's Magic Glue. Articles in BUM & Magia. Forthcoming book on own effects. [Wh3]

name: Baran, Jennifer
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Borh Jennifer Smith. Partner of Jody Baran since high school, marrying him soon after while working a theme park. Articles in Magic Manuscript.

name: Baran, Jody
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Learned at age 8. Pro stage debut at age 8 in Chicago. Named Junior Magician of the Year at age 10. Kid-shows to theme park to cruise-ship illusionist who performs (since high school) with partner-wife Jennifer as "The Barans" with their "Sophisticated Sorcery" act. Their teachers have been John Moehring, Henk Vermeyden, & Neil Foster. Their act has won the 1985 IBM Stage Magician of the Year & the 1986 Tokyo World Cup 1st place. [MM3/89]

name: Barbas Cardoso, João Maria
bio: (Portalegre, Portugal: 21 May 1924-) Amateur magician in Lisbon. Aka "Osodrac". Articles in

name: Barbaud, Roger[-François-Xavier-Joseph]
bio: (Limoges, Haute-Vienne, France: 12 May 1845-24 Oct 1936) Moved to Toulouse. Legion of Honor medalist. Amateur magician. Wrote Manuel complete de prestidigitation (4 vols, 1910-35). In 1931 founder-President of Club Commandeur-Cazeneuve in Toulouse. [Dif]

name: Barbour, Victor D.
bio: (France: 26 Mar 1912-) Mentalist. (USA: 19 Aug 1884-28 Jun 1946) Wealthy amateur prop collector with magic theater in Palm Beach, Florida. Sold most of his large prop collection to Robert Anderson who resold it in 1945 to Joe Berg. [Ir;Albo95]

name: Barck-Holst, Björn
bio: (Sweden: 11 Nov 1897-21 May 1949) Dental surgeon. Amateur magician as "Mac Urga" esteemed in Scandinavia. One of few non-pros to give a command performance for the Swedish royal family. Had major collection of Swedish magicana, which since 1981 belongs to the Sveriges Magi-Arkiv. [St]

name: Baret, Bishop Marie-Paul-Pierre
bio: (France: 9 Jan 1862-14 Oct 1940) Former Roman Catholic missionary in the Far East and bishop. Amateur sleight-of-hand artist & correspondent with Prof Hoffmann. Wrote under pen name "Magus" Magie blanche en famille (1891, 352pp; repr 1894) & Le Magicien amateur (1897). Also as "Magus" wrote articles on magic for French popular press. Charter member in 1936 of the Amicale des Magiciens du Sud-Est. [Dif]

name: Bargeon
bio: (France?: fl.1880s) Pro, billed as "Illusionist and Anti-Spiritualist" when he performed at the Théâtre de la Ville in 1883. [Rey]

name: Barini
bio: (Saint-Germain, Dordogne, France: 15 Dec 1896-) Stage name of Pierre Gontier de Biran. Founding President of the Sphinx Sarrois society in Sarrebruck in 1931. [Rob1]

name: Barkann, Roger
bio: (Jersey City, New Jersey: 25 Jun 1909-dead) Stage name of Barkaan Rosinoff, aka "The Trojan Trixter" (1930-33). Semi-pro 1928, then amateur. By profession, an insurance company executive. Started vogue of poetic patter. First mentor of Cy Endfield. Wrote Patent Pending. Tricks in Sphinx, Genii, & HMM (1944). [Th;WWM]

name: Barlow, Fred[erick]
bio: (England: 23 Sep 1903-) Stage & pen name of P.J. Clack. Edited Journal of the Institute of Magicians (1938, 10 issues). Wrote Mental Prodigies (1951, 256pp), a text on how to perform Lightning Calculation & other mental feats. His wife-partner was Marie.

name: Barnello, Signor
bio: (Decatur, Illinois: 8 Sep 1857-30 Apr 1910) Pen name of E.A. Barnwell, aka "The Human Volcano". Pro magician & fire-eater. While living in Cerro Gordo, Illinois, in 1893 he edited The Magician, of which only 2 copies of this monthly are known to exist, both of the Vol.1, No.2 (Jul 1893) issue. It was the 1st magic magazine published in North America. Wrote a rare paper-bound book on 100 fire-eating tricks titled The Red Demons, or the Mysteries of Fire [c1893; reprinted 1909, 64pp; & 1964]; & Barnello's Voodoo Incantations.

name: Barnes, Chesley V.
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Wife of amateur magic collector Dr Morris N. Young. Edited the American Dover editions (1953 & 1954) of Wilfrid Johnson's books.

name: Barnet, Sylvan
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City: 1926-) Learned at age 11. Amateur. [Th]

name: Barnett, Bruce [Gordon]
bio: (Augusta, Maine: 1951- ) Learned at age 6 from Tarbell #1. Computer scientist. Semi-pro since age 21 in close-up & mental magic. Articles in Chronicles, Invocation, Magick, New Direction, & Vibrations. Wrote "From the Right Brain" column in Vibrations. [Wh2]

name: Barnett, Jack
bio: (England: -2 Feb 1946) Conjuror & bookseller. Father of "Lucille".

name: Barnett, Joseph L[loyd] "Joe
bio: (New York, NY: c1900-8 Dec 1989) Lawyer in New York City. Amateur magician since c1910, specializing in impromptu close-up. Dean of the Magician's Table in New York. Columnist for MUM. He is the "subject" of Judge Bryant's Barnett on Sleights [1955], a gag book with blank pages that was subsequently "reissued" by Richard Himber (in several copies), Tony Lopilato (2 copies), & Lou Tannen (1 copy). [Th]

name: Barnett, [Daphne] Lucille
bio: (London, England: 1924- ) Taught by father Jack Barnett, a bookseller & amateur magician, & by Ellis Stanyon. Debut in 1938. Performed as "Lucille". Noted magic book collector & dealer. Pro manipulator 1939-late 1940s when married & moved to USA. [Mar]

name: Barnhart, Russell T. "Russ
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-90s) Amateur card worker & gambling historian. A regular at the Round Table in Chicago until moved to New York City. Wrote Two Second Deals (1974, 14pp), The Master Palm (1975), Casino Gambling (1977, 221pp), & Gamblers of Yesteryear (1983). Translated Eugene Villiod's La mâchine voler (1905) as The Stealing Machine (1977, 221pp), his Comment on nous vole au jeu! (1909) as How They Cheat You at Cards (1979, 189pp), & another book of his, which was translated as Crooks, Con Men, and Cheats (1980, 131pp). Articles or tricks in Genii & Onyx. [Wh5]

name: Barnouw, Erik
bio: (The Hague, Holland: 23 Jun 1908-2001) Brought to USA as child. Became interested in magic at age 14 as cataloger of John Mulholland's growing magic book collection, which was even then considered second only to Houdini's. Wrote The Magician and the Cinema (1981, 128pp), a scholarly work on the important role of conjurers as pioneers of moving pictures, written while Barnouw was with the Library of Congress. Autobio is Media Marathon (1996). [CA]

name: Baro
bio: (Poland: 1937-) Stage name of Władysław Barczewski. Pro illusionist & manipulator.

name: Barón de Carlos
bio: See: Carlos, Barón de

name: Baron, Harry, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 28 Aug 1919-27 May 1991) Stage name of Harry Albert Boughen. Learned at age 5 from uncle's pocket tricks. Pro magic dealer since 1940. Also close-up magician & lecturer. Owned MBC Magic Studio in London in 1953. In 1953 co-founded (with Joe Stuthard) The Kaymar Magic Co in Billericay, Essex County, originally a wholesaler to Hamley's & Gamage's, then until his death a retail-wholesale shop. Also managed Gamage's magic department during its last 25 years. Edited anthologies My Best Card Trick (1953, 31pp) & My Best Close-up Trick (1954, 36pp). Wrote Card Tricks for Beginners (1960, 136pp), Magic for Beginners (1967), Close-Up Magic for Beginners (1972, 160pp), etc. Edited Magic Info 1976-81. Tricks in Abra. [Wh2]

name: Baronio, [Anthony Richard] "Tony
bio: (Hazelton, Pennsylvania: 24 Mar 1954-) Inspired seeing Wilson's "Magic Land of AllaKazam" TV show in early 1950s. Learned from library books. Elementary school music teacher in home town. Part-time pro close-up, stage, mental, & kid-show magician since c1975, doing 250-300 shows yearly. Makes & sells several original tricks, including 4th DIemension (1990) & Floating Flame (1991). Wrote On Location with Tony Baronio (1984, 25pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript & Mortimer's Magic Magazine. [MM1/90;Wh5]

name: Barret, Bishop [misspelling]
bio:
Barrie, The Great (Canada: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro illusionist.

[See also: Baret, Bishop]

name: Barrington, Frederick
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Stage name of Charles C. Lebey. Semi-pro.

name: Barrs, Percy
bio: (Wigan, Lancashire, England: 16 Sep 1883-) Pharmacist. Semi-pro straight magic in school shows. [Go2]

name: Barrs, Richard
bio: (Richmond, Surrey, England: 12 Jun 1919-) Learned as a boy. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand since 1932 when he won competition at Maskelyne's. [Go2]

name: Barry, [Richard Ernest] "Dick
bio: (Medina, Ohio: 30 Apr 1933- ) Learned in late 1930s from books & watching magicians. Police officer in Santa Monica (retired after 30 years). Semi-pro parlor magician c1969-87 when went full-time pro. Also does mentalism. Pet effect: Goldfish Production. Audio. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Barth, Johann Anton
bio: (Germany?: fl.1740s) Pro sleight-of-hand at Paris fairs in the 1740s. [Dif]

name: Bartl, János
bio: (Hungary: 13 Apr 1878-Hamburg: 27 Sep 1958) Roman Catholic. Pro travelling magician as "Aradi" before 1910. Moved to Hamburg, Germany, where (with his wife Rosa, daughter of Joseph Leichtmann) he became a pro dealer (Bartl's Akademie für moderne magische Kunst) in 1911. Then became partner with Carl Willmann as "Vereineinigte Zauberapparate Fabrik Bartl & Willmann" 1919-1924. Buying out Willmann, he continued on alone as "Carl Willmann—Janos Bartl Nachfolger [successor]" until around 1935. Father of Elli Bartl & father-in-law of Egon von Lautenstein. [Magie2/94;Roh;Dif;Mec]

name: Bartl, Elli
bio: (Hamburg: 22 Nov 1913-) Only daughter of János & Rosa Bartl. Married Egon von Lautenstein and, after his death in 1967, a Herr Schlossmann. In 1993 was living in Sweden. [Roh]

name: Bartl, Rosa
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 17 Jul 1884-23 Sep 1968) Eldest daughter of Joseph Leichtmann & sister of Melanie Steinböck. Wife (since 1910) of János Bartl whom she assisted in his magic shop business in Hamburg since 1911. Director of Bartl & Willmann's teaching division around 1919-1924. Soon before her death (in Hamburg) she sold the business to Carl-Gerd Heubes. Mother of Elli Bartl. [Magie2/94;Roh]

name: Bartolacci, Alfonso
bio: (Milan, Italy: 27 Jan 1953- ) Mentalist, aka "Alan King". Wrote Confidenze di un Mentalista (1989, 40pp). Article in Qui Magia.

name: Barton, Fred
bio: (England: 1922-18 Jun 2001) Comedy act 1943 with his wife Jennie Parry, 1952 children's entertainment. Wrote The Land of Make-Believe. [Abra #2891]

name: Barton, James
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 21 Apr 1858-30 Apr 1935) Aka "El Barto". Learned at age 11-14 as apprentice for 3 years (c1869-72) to Antonio Blitz. Pro on own since 1874. Pet effects: Billiard Ball Box, Water into Wine, & the Torn & Restored Paper Strip. A Lyceum circuit star c1922-34. [Pr]

name: Bartoni, Karl
bio: (England: fl.1980s) Protégé of Alan Alan. Pro escape artist until switched to mentalism in 1986.

name: Bartram Jr, Richard [R.]
bio: (Huntington, West Virginia: 10 Sep 1953-) Inspired in 1961 when he "saw Slydini on TV & realized there was more to magic than Mark Wilson." Commercial artist. Pro magic shop demonstrator (Magic Maker Costumes) in Huntington, West Virginia, since 1988. Specializes in Close-up, mentalism, & bizarre magic. Invented Pasteboard Impalement (1989). Wrote Close-Up of the Damned (1985, 45pp) & Mystification (1993, 110pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Apocalypse, New Invocation, & Trap Door. [Wh2]

name: Basch, Ernst [Dietrich Wilhelm]
bio: (Bovenden, Hannover, Germany: 21 Nov 1838-24 Jan 1909 [sic]) 2nd [sic] son of magician Hirsch Basch (by 2nd wife, Johanne Ahrens). Brother of magicians Heinrich & Friedrich and half-brother of Friedrich Joseph. Pro magician from his debut in Bremen in 1860. Aka "Cagliostro II" in 1867 when he played the Cagliostro-Theater in Oldenburg. Had his own Cagliostro-Theater, a transportable building (supposedly holding up to 1,600 spectators, although it was only 44x16x8 meters) for his many tours of Holland, beginning in the Hague on 8 May 1872. Pet effects: Magic Lantern & Pepper's Ghost. Gave his last stage show in 1887 (again in Bremen). In 1887 became a major magic dealer-prop maker & repairer in Hannover, advertising 5,000 items. Continued until his death there when succeeded by his son-in-law, Hermann Mellini. Houdini characterized Basch in his last year as "the richest manufacturer of illusions in the world. [Win;Dif;Vo56;St;Sal;Roh]

name: Basch, Ernst Hermann Robert
bio: (Hannover, Germany: 23 Jun 1882-3 Sep 1975) Elder son of Antoinette Basch and Jacop Ahrens (who changed his name to Basch!). Began as tightrope artist in England. After a serious fall he turned to magic with stage name of "Valvero". In 1934 married Hedwig Toepfer. Did stage work (with wife) as late as 1964. Died in Hamburg, West Germany. [Roh] (Germany: 1852-6 Apr 1937) 4th son of Hirsch/Heinrich Basch. Popular pro magician. Known for his many-colored light fountains that he toured with the Circus "Carré". Buried in Hannover. [Roh]

name: Basch, Friedrich Joseph
bio: (Hildesheim, Hannover, Germany: 21 [sic] Mar 1834-20 [sic] Mar 1877) Eldest [sic] son of Hirsch Basch (by 1st wife, Sophie Eime). Coverted from Judaism to Christianity in 1849. Half-brother of magicians Ernst, Heinrich, & Friedrich Basch. As "Wilhelm Basch" worked as assistant to Hermann "Mellini" Mehl's actor father during which time he taught Mellini his first tricks. In 1859 married Mellini's sister Johanne Mehl (1835-1890). Then pro on own. Toured Europe, but mainly Germany & Holland, as "Professeur F.J. Basch". Wrote Basch als Goochelar en Duizendkunstaar (Gouda: in Dutch) & Grandes Soirées de physique amusante (Dresden: 1860, in French). Died in Breslau. [Roh;Vo56;St;Mül]

name: Basch, Hedwig
bio: (Südende, Teltow, Germany: 26 Dec 1900-) Born Hedwig Toepfer. In 1934 married Ernst H.R. Basch. Did a silk act as "Hedi Mora". Did stage work with husband as late as 1964. Still alive in Hamburg at age 94. [Roh]

name: Basch, [Carl] Heinrich [Wilhelm]
bio: (Bovenden, Germany: 10 Oct 1841 [or possibly 24 Feb 1847]-11 Jun 1876) 3rd [sic] son of Heinrich (formerly Hirsch) Basch (by 2nd wife, Johanne Ahrens). Brother of Ernst & half-brother of Friedrich Joseph Basch. Formally became a Christian in Mar 1847. Pro magician. Toured a "Phantasie-Theater". Often performed in Holland, dying there in Wintschoten. NOTE: Robelly probably errs in giving date of death as 1 Jul. [Vo56;Rob;Roh] Basch, Hirsch (later Heinrich) (Holzminden, Germany: 1 [or 27] Mar 1810-20 Jan 1866) 2nd son of German-Jewish engraver Nathananel Herz (& his wife Ester Jacob) who had changed the family surname to Basch sometime around 1808. Hirsch renounced the Jewish religion and changed his given name to Heinrich, probably in 1839 when his 2nd wife, Johanne Ahrens also converted to Christianity. Pro travelling magician, marionette worker, & juggler who played mainly thru western Germany. In 1864 entered an insane asylum in Hildesheim where he died 2 years later. Founder of the famous dynasty of German magicians. Father of Friedrich Joseph, Ernst, Heinrich, & Friedrich Basch. [Roh]

name: Basch, Wilhelm
bio: See: Basch, Friedrich Joseph

name: Bastard, Roger
bio: (Chinon, France: 3 Apr 1881-) Pottery manufacturer in Tours Indre et Loire. Semi-pro general magician. Worked most venues except cabarets & fairs. [WWM]

name: Bastino Junior
bio: See: Holderried, Michael

name: Batchelor, Tom
bio: (Canada: fl.1970s) A leading Canadian cardman. Wrote Canadian Card Control (1971, 52pp).

name: Bates, Henry
bio: (England: fl. 1900s-10s) Photographer (owned a shop in Brighton) & mechanic who made magic props for toy shops until discovered by David Devant. Then since 1902 he built several props & illusions for Devant, including his "Obliging Kettle" = Magic Kettle (1902), Mascot Moth (1905), Indian Rope Trick (1907), & The Cryptic Die Box. Also made Selbit's "Mighty Cheese" = Wrestling Cheese (1912). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Bate". [Bam,p.65]

name: Batt, Christopher
bio: (Britain: -16 Jul 1904) A Mason. A company official & semi-pro magician as "Endor" in Dublin, Ireland, where for many years he was the main local magician. Invented "Endor's Demon Envelope" (a double envelope). [Magic7/04]

name: Battle, Alfred J.
bio: (London, England: 15 Feb 1879- ) Brought to USA at age 2. Inspired & learned when bought magic set at age 12. Debut in Manila in 1899. Pro as assistant & then partner to Dr. Ward, a San Francisco magician; then, when Ward retired, on own touring the USA. Magic-shop dealer in San Francisco around 1930s. Aka "Professor El-Tab". [Th]

name: Baudot, Léon
bio: (Vaudeurs, Yonne, France: 15 Apr 1852-27 Mar 1927) Pro dealer in Paris 1873-1913 when he passed his shop to Henri Billy.

name: Bauer, Joel
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-90s) Pro, working mainly trade shows & cruise ships. Wrote Hustle, Hustle: Making Magic Pay (1983, 138pp), etc. [Mag]

name: Bauer, Josef
bio: (Munich, Germany: 11 Dec 1902-17 Mar 1981) Died in Munich, West Germany. [Roh]

name: Bauer, Karl
bio: (Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany: 6 Jan 1895-8 Aug 1961) Invented many tricks & props. Major contributor to Magie. Died in Augsburg. [Roh]

name: Bauer, Ron[ald Raymond]
bio: (Yakima, Washington: 3 Mar 1938-) Learned at age c11 reading 2 gift books: Thurston on cards & Downs on coins. Writer in Detroit area. Semi-pro magician since his teens, specialing in close-up & stage for adults & kids. Also works industrial shows. 1967-74 founded & ran "Mr. Trix Enterprises", a repertory group of magicians, clowns, & puppeteers. Tricks in Tops, Genii, MUM, & several books. [Wh2]

name: Baur, Eberhard
bio: (Dessau, Germany: 26 Sep 1944- ) Self-taught by books & tricks since age 10. Pro manip in East Germany, specializing in oversized balls. 1974/75 Karlovy Vary 1st Prize; 1975 Prague Grand Prix; 1976 Oslo 1st Prizes in manip & closeup. Added illusions after 1978 to make a 60-minute act. Has played in 20 European countries. Several TV bits. [Win]

name: Bavli, Guy
bio: (Israel: 24 Aug 1971-) Mentalist particularly known for key bending.

name: Baxt, Robert
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 29 Dec 1961- ) Learned at age 11 from magic shop tricks. Pro comedian & comedy magician since 1978, paying way thru college law school (JD in 1985). Plays mainly comedy clubs. 1985 FISM 3rd prize in comedy magic. Wrote Stabbed in the Baxt (1986, 29pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript. TV bits in USA, Japan, Spain, & South America. [Wh2]

name: Baxter, Bobby
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 14 Jun 1920- ) Stage name of Edwin Jerome Ziegler. Raised in St. Augustine, Florida, where he taught himself magic at age 10. Pro comedy magician. Played such venues as the Orpheum Theatre in Vancouver in 1943, the Cotillion Room in New York in 1946, Ed Sullivan Show in 1949, & a regular at Magic Towne House 1970s-80s & Mostly Magic since 1979. [Tay;Wh]

name: Baxter, lan
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 22 Nov 1946-) Amateur cardman to (recently) full-time pro magician. Pet effect: Ambitious Card. Wrote Ten on Deck (1970, 38pp). Co-edited (with Barry Govan) Blueprint 1974-78. Pet Tricks in New Directions. Tricks in Linking Ring (3 "Parades") & Tarbell. [LR2/91]

name: Bayer, Constance Pole "Connie
bio: (Toronto, Canada: 1908- ) Born Constance Pole. Great-great-grand-niece of J.H. Anderson thru her grandmother, Isabella Jean Anderson, an ex-JHA assistant who had immigrated to Canada in 1871. Artist & writer. Married a Mr Bayer in 1948. A non-magician, as biographer of the Anderson dynasty Bayer wrote The Great Wizard of the North: John Henry Anderson (1990, 174pp). [Wh2]

name: Bayly, Mr.
bio: (Britain: fl.1750s-80s) Pro sleight-of-hand, puppets, & mechanical scenes. Moved to Colonial America c1767 where he continued to perform as late as 1783 when, infirm, he seemingly retired or died. [Ch]

name: Beadle, Edward
bio: (USA: fl.1870s-1910s) Robert Heller's manager until 1878. During that time he was the likely inventor of the Coin Ladder. Inventive master prop-maker with shop at 1193 Broadway in New York City 1893-1909 when taken over by the Bamberg Magic & Novelty Co. Beadle continued to keep an office in the building until he left the magic field. [Albo95; Magic10/02]

name: Beale, Ken[neth]
bio: (USA: -Jul 1979) Amateur cardman in New York since 1940s, San Francisco 1971-74, & finally again New York. Articles in HMM, Ibidem, Pallbearers, Phoenix, Epilogue, Epotica Yearbook, & Arcane.

name: Beam, Steve[n L.]
bio: (Fort Knox, Kentucky: 5 Feb 1958- ) First interested in magic at age 11. Finance Director of Housing Authority in Raleigh, North Carolina. Part-pro magician since 1977, specializing in close-up, card, comedy, & club magic. Owner of mail-order "Trapdoor Productions" in Knightdale, North Carolina since 1980. Editor of The Trapdoor 1983-present. Invented Quick Change (1978), The Card Book (1979), Upside Down (1984), Super Stack (1983, revised 1989) Wrote They don't make trapdoors like they used to (1978, 42pp), Magic—The Vanishing Art (1979, 100pp), Inside Outs (1979, 27pp, with Don Morris), Card Tricks from Mount Olympus (1980, 73pp), Steve Beam on Coins (2 vols, 1981, 1982), The Changing of the Cards (1982, 39pp), Diary of a Deranged Deck (1983, 20pp), Super Stack (1983), etc. [Wh2]

name: Bean, Gordon [Tarleton]
bio: (Schenectady, New York: 14 Apr 1959-) Pro card magician. Contributor to Genii (column), Labyrinth, Magic, & Magic Circular. [Wh01]

name: Bean, Orson
bio: (Burlington, Vermont: 22 Jul 1928-) Stage name (from Orson Welles & the Boston bean) of Dallas Burrows since 1948. Learned at age 8 from a Mysto Magic set. Worked as pro comedy magician 1948-52 when switched to straight comedy. Designed a magic set in 1950. Pet comedy-magic routine: The Paper Eucalyptus Tree = "Bean-pole" (since 1953). Autobio is Too Much Is Not Enough (1988, 207pp). [HMM8/52,9/55;Wh]

name: Beata, La
bio: (Saarbrücken, Germany: 12 Mar 1904-4 Oct 1977) Stage name of Berta Maria Geilen-Zimmer. Died in hometown. [Roh]

name: Beatrice, Mdle.
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s) Pro, working a variety of standard stage tricks in London & the provinces 1880-84 with Madame Rose.

name: Beaufort, Douglas
bio: (England: 1864-13 Apr 1939) Stage name of Douglas Edward Walter Broad. Learned magic in 1880 as piano-accompanist to Professor Weber. Debut in 1882. Pro society magician in London since 1886. Played Morocco in 1892. Autobio is Nothing Up My Sleeve! (1938, 287pp), which was ghosted by Frank S. Stuart who flagrantly aadded fictitious bits. [La;Wal;Magic7/04] "Beaumont the Great" SEE: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Beaumont, Professor
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s) Minor pro illusionist. Pet effect: The Suspension. [Fr]

name: Beaumont, Harold G.
bio: (England: -28 Dec 1959) Magical inventor, including the Stretching Card (1952).

name: Beck, Joyce [Adelle]
bio: (Loma Linda, California: 20 Aug 1955-) Learned at age 7 from father's self-working tricks. Later tutored by Vernon, Goshman, Miller, Pooley, & Daryl. Pro close-up, walk-around, & parlor magicienne since 1988. Billed as "Dutchess of Deception", "Lady of Legerdemain", & "Princess of Prestidigitation". Pet effects: Dollar Bill to Lipstick, Sponge Bunnies, Bill Switch. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Beck, Leonard N.
bio: (USA?: fl.1970s-80s) Curator of Special Collections, Library of Congress Rare Book Room until retired in 1986 or 87. Amateur magician.

name: Beck, Martin
bio: (Germany: c1867-16 Nov 1940) At age c16 moved to USA with a troupe of German singers & became the top booking agent for the Orpheum vaude circuit, which covered western USA & Canada. Managed Houdini since 1899 & booked Okito 1907-08. Eventually B.F. Keith took control of the Orpheum Circuit. [Var;NYT;Lau]

name: Becker, [Friedrich] Ferdinand [Rudolph]
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 1813-1855) Learned assisting Bosco. Pro apparatus magician by 1834 [sic] at fairs & other minor venues throughout Europe. In 1839 his assistant was Heimbürger. Pet effect: catching borrowed rings fired from a cannon. Died in Russia. Father of Rudolf Becker. [Cl;Sal]

name: Becker, Herbert L.
bio: (Canada: fl.1970s-90s) Student of Burling Hull. Magician & escape artist. Pro since 1972-1978 sometimes with Delta “Designing Women” Burke as his assistant. Stage name was “The Great Kardeen”. Retired in 1978. Wrote All the Secrets of Magic Revealed (1997, 144pp).

name: Becker, [Lawrence] Larry
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 13 Aug 1929- ) Inspired in 1943 seeing a Dante show. Former head of an ad agency & marketing syndicator (Becker-Kanter). Top-line mentalist. Semi-pro c1969-c1984 & pro since then. Pet effects: Russian Roulette & Headline Prediction. 1981 Mentalist of the Year. Prolific inventor of effects including Credit Card Grinda (1995 with Roy Roth). Wrote Larry Becker's World of Super Mentalism (2 vols, 1977, 1979, 156+275pp), Mentalism for Magicians (1981, 66pp), Stunners (1992, 464pp). Trick in Genii (1955). Video (1986), video segment (1988). [LR10/98;Wh2]

name: Becker, Rudolf
bio: (Troppau, Germany: 1 Apr 1835-1 Jul 1895) Son of Ferdinand Becker. Popular pro. Died in Vienna. [Vo57;Sal]

name: Beckerelli, Jean
bio: (Luxemburg: 1860-1935) Stage name of Jean Becker. Moved to Switzerland where he was a popular pro magician. For many years worked mainly luxury hotels & roadside inns.

name: Beckman, Fred
bio: (Montréal, Canada: 1905-4 Jul 1971) Stage name of J.O. Wilfrid Bélanger, of French descent. Inspired at age 10 seeing F.E. Powell show. Gave up architectural studies to debut as pro illusionist in 1925. Operated the House of Illusions, a magic theater in Dominion Park, Montréal 1930-34. In WW II did shows for the Canadian Army (until 1943) & the USO. His plans to do a movie on Houdini in Canada in 1950 aborted. Under own name edited the issues of Le Monde Magique in 1965. [Dif; Genii1/66]

name: Beckmann, Darryl [Lee]
bio: (San Francisco, California: 20 Nov 1945-) Learned at age 7. Pro comedy, kid-show, & illusionist as "The Amazing Beckmann" since age 12. Won awards in Europe after getting out of US Army. Founder-owner Magic Market & Novelty shop in Seattle, Washington, since 1974. Joined there since 1978 by his wife, Sheila Lyon. Wrote The Life and Times of Alexander (1994, 380pp). [Wh5]

name: Beckmann, Johann
bio: (Hoya an der Weser, Germany: 4 Jun 1739 [sic]-3 Feb 1811) German technologist. Professor of philosophy at Göttingen U since 1765. Died in Göttingen. Wrote the encyclopedic Beyträge zur Geschichte der Erfindungen (Leipzig: 5 vols, 1780-1805; English tr as John Beckmann, A History of Inventions and Discoveries, 4 vols, London: 1797; repr 1814, 2,050pp; 1877), of which Vol.3 contains a useful essay on conjuring mainly from Greek & Roman sources.

name: Bedognetti, Peter
bio: (Zug, Switzerland: 26 Feb 1957-) Learned at age 11 from books. Mechanical engineer. Semi-pro street magician since c1964 as "Pedro". Now pro dealer-teacher (Pedro Magie) in Zürich since 1984, being joined by Michael Suter as partner in 1989. Editor Gimmick to present. [Wh2]

name: Bee, Percy
bio: (Britain: 1905-1973) Pro. Aka "Eric De Reske" in 1940. Wrote (with Norman Cliffe) The Great 'Socco' Comedy Watch Routine [1947].

name: Beebe, Dr Ray[mond L.], DDS
bio: (Michigan, USA: 11 Sep 1898-) A dentist by profession since 1922 in Los Angeles. Learned magic as a boy but did not become a serious amateur until c1940. Invented "Audacity" telephone trick (1944) & "Bisect-U" rope trick (1944). Tricks in Sphinx, Genii, HMM, etc. [Genii11/66;Th]

name: Beeckmans, Roger
bio: (Belgium: fl.1960s) As "Murillo" did dove act, general magic, & the Indian Trunk illusion. 1965 Liège 1st prize for general magic with son Pierre as "Murillo and Partner". Edited Echo Magique (1965, 9 issues). [Bou]

name: Beedie, Professor
bio: (Aberdeen, Scotland: 1 May 1868-11 Apr 1946) Stage name of George Biddie. Pro magician of the old school. Moved to USA at age 19. Toured 10 years there with Alexander Herrmann & Barnum & Bailey circus. Then returned to Scotland where he worked until his death. Wrote Conjuring Up-to-Date [Edinburgh: c1890]. [Vo56]

name: Behnke, Leo [Ralph]
bio: (Hollywood, California: 2 Mar 1933-) Learned 1st card trick at age 9, then at job with the Merv Taylor Magic Company. After US Navy service, pro performer-dealer since 1956.
