Opened & managed Merlin's Magic Shop at Disneyland for 6 years. Toured Europe in 1959 with John Daniel in two-person magic act. With Mark Wilson's Magic Land of Alla Kazam TV series 1960-65. Mail-order book dealer 1972-80. Curator of the Copperfield Collection in Las Vegas until 2000. Wrote Entertaining with Close-Up (1962, 15pp), Entertaining with Cards (1962, 25pp), Impromptu Magic from the Magic Castle (1980, 236pp), Party Magic from the Magic Castle (1980, 239pp), Professional Close-up (1989, 112pp), Magic for Bartenders—Encore (1992, 83pp). Edited The Collected Mental Secrets of C.A. George Newmann (1991, 600pp), Corporate Presentations (1992, 124pp), Thread Reference (1992, 45pp), Find the Ace (1993, 56pp). Articles in Genii, New Lines from Lawton, etc. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Beite, Iso [pronounced I-soo bai-TEY]
bio: (Sweden: 21 Dec 1913 [sic]-31 Mar [sic] 1970) Pro. Known as "the singing magician".

name: Bekker, Henry
bio: (England: 30 Jul 1880- ) Stage name of Harry Chalkley, aka "Henri Bekker". Pro comedy magician since 1903. Played St. George's Hall in 1925. In ENSA in WW II. Endowed with a oversized penis, he wielded it to advantage in his occasional stag shows for fellow magi. [Magic5/03]

name: Belachini
bio: (Lódź, Poland: 10 Mar 1898-Nov 1985) Stage name of Henryk Wolsztajn. Apprenticed after WW I in José Stuller-Bosco's magic factory in Danzig. Pro illusionist. Founded a magic factory in Krakow. Moved back to Lódź in 1930. Teacher of Artadoni. [Mec;Nad]

name: Belais, Arnold
bio: (New York City, NY: 4 Nov 1890-29 Jan 1973) Jewellery maker 1906-30, thence insurance agent. Semi-pro magician, billed as "Mister Fication" & "The Smok-King". Invented Multiplying Pipes (marketed in 1948). Tricks in Magic (1911) & HMM. [SAM]

name: Bélanger, Wilfrid
bio: See: "Beckman, Fred"

name: Belante, Ted
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro mentalist-hypnotist, working two-person mentalism, initially with wife Debbie (now divorced). Wrote What's Your E.S.P. Quotient (1982).

name: Belcher, Len
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-90s) Schoolteacher (retired). Mentalist & childrens magician. Wrote Len Belcher on Two-Person Mentalism (1974, 47pp) & Best of Belcher. Tricks in Abra.

name: Bel-Kassem
bio: See: de Bischop, Philippe

name: Belphegor
bio: (Germany: 3 Dec 1944-) Stage name of Siegfried Pützer. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Bell, David
bio: (Australia: 1886-29 Jun 1949) Semi-pro since 1906. Pro since 1915, specializing in Masonic, kid-show, & society functions. Founded the Melbourne branch of Australian Society of Magicians in 1920. Resident magician at Melbourne Aquarium 1943-48. [Alm]

name: Bell, Monika
bio: See: "Denis, Alain"

name: Bellachini
bio: (Posnań [or Ligota], Poland: 1 [sic] May 1827 [sic]-24 Jan 1885) Stage name of Samuel Berlach (or Bellach), which Clarke claims he took from an earlier German pro. Parents were Polish-Jewish inn-keepers. Learned tin-working. Moved to USA at early age. Returning to Europe, he made his debut in Portugal in 1840. Popular pro illusionist in Central Europe, touring with a succession of assistants: John Steinmetz (a black), Anton Kratky-Baschik (until 1852), & Ernest Thorn (until 1871). Named Court Conjuror by Wilhelm I of Germany in 1864. Reported to have invented the Eggs from Mouth effect. Died in Parchim. Father of Tamara Bellachini. NOTE: Some 60 later magicians, mainly German, took his "Bellachini" stage name. [Dam;Sal;Win;Dif;Cam]

name: Bellachini Jr.
bio: (Berlin?, Germany: 17 Jan 1896-14 Aug 1975) Stage name of Theodor von Schledorn. Aka "Bellini" & "Bosco". Died in Berlin. [Dam2]

name: Bellachini, Die Marburger
bio: See: Strack, L.

name: Bellachini, Arado
bio: (Rauschenberg, Germany: 1 Apr 1893-1971) Stage name of Wilhelm Mann. Worked in circus until turned to magic with full-evening show of classic illusions. Toured variety theaters through Europe. [Roh]

name: Bellachini, Gerty
bio: (Thorn, Germany: 12 Mar 1895-18 Feb 1956) Born Gertrud Will. Married pro magician Ludwig Lebram, she performed as "Lebram-Bellachini". Remarried to Richard Pfandt, she worked as "Gerty Bellachini". Performed in eastern Germany in 1930s-40s. [Roh;Wit]

name: Bellachini, Joachim
bio: (Siegen, Westphalia, Germany: 1856-16 Jun 1901) Stage name of W. Jochum since 1885. Trained as assistant to the Basch brothers. Then as last assistant to Samuel Bellachini, taking the latter's stage name on his death in 1885. Toured Switzerland, Italy, Holland, & Russia. Died in Frankfurt. [Vo56;St;Dam]

name: Bellachini, L.
bio: See: Strack, L.

name: Bellachini, Leonard
bio: See: Lebram, Ludwig

name: Bellachini-Schweizer
bio: (St. Martin, Rheinpfalz, Germany: 12 Apr 1886-4 Oct 1969) Stage name of Franz Schweizer. Pro illusionist. Aka "Franzardi", "Bellachini III", & "Garvin". Died in home town.

name: Bellachini, Tamara
bio: (Germany: 1860-) Stage name of Hedwig Berlach. Only daughter of Bellachini (Berlach). Promagicienne. Appeared as character in Hermann Bahr's novel Drut (Berlin: 1909). Retired in Leipzig. [Magie12/27; Dam2]

name: Bellachini III
bio: See: "Bellachini-Schweizer"

name: Bellachini XIII
bio: See: Deutsch, Rüdiger

name: Bellini, Pietro
bio: (Austria: 1903-1975) Stage name of Adolf Pokorny. Amateur. Died in Lisbon, Portugal.

name: Bellman, Dan[iel]
bio: (Ulverston, Lancs., England: 6 Jul 1902-c1945) Drapery assistant. Amateur comedy magician. Wrote with Eric C. Lewis Magic as We Do It (1935, 28pp), The Magic of 1936 (1936), & The Magic of 1937 (1937, 73pp). On own wrote Patter, Tricks and Quips (1933) & Cheerful Conjuring (1938, 49pp). Tricks in Linking Ring. [Le;WWM]

name: Belmonte, Nora
bio: (Germany?: fl.1880s-1st decade of 1900s) As assistant since 1888 to Max Berol in memory & later non-verbal telepathy act used stage name of "Madame Konorah" & billed as "The White Witch". Did her lightning calculation act in Boston in 1903. [Mo]

name: Beltempo, Domenico
bio: (Germany?: 20 Apr 1947-) Magician as "Nico". 1983 Baden-Baden 1st prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Belucci, Hector
bio: (Argentina: fl.1950s) Illusionist as "Yadu" & inventor-builder of illusions. [Bam,p.271]

name: Belzak, Adrian
bio: See: Green, John C.

name: Belzoni, Giovanni Battista
bio: (Padua, Italy: 14 Aug 1778-3 Dec 1823) 13th child of a barber. Entered circus. Moved to England in 1803. Learned magic as member of Gygell's troupe at London fairs. Strongman & later, since 1812, semi-pro magician. Became an explorer & Egyptologist. Bios are M. Willson Disher, Pharoah's Fool (1957) & S. Mayes, The Great Belzoni (1959). [Daw;Sal]

name: Beme, Sixten
bio: (Sweden: 15 Jul 1924-27 Jan 2001) Journalist. Lived in Stockholm. Amateur card magician. Inspired by Paul Harris, Beme Invented examinable card linking effects. See El Duco, The Complete Card Linking (1979) and wrote One Card Link (1996). Tricks in New Directions & Linking Ring.

name: Bemelman, Joseph [Jacobus Maria] "Jos
bio: (Lisse, Holland: 29 Nov 1953-26 Jun 2006) Inspired seeing a magician on TV at age 4. Learned magic at 10. Pro close-up & stage magician since age 18. Aka "Julian" (1973), "Jos Bema" (1973-78), & "Tommy Wonder" (since 1979). 1972 Junior Magician of Holland; 1979 FISM 2nd prize in close-up; 1988 FISM 2nd prize in general magic. Died of lung cancer. Wrote 2 lecture-note booklets: Original Magic from Holland (1977) & Wonder Material (1982); plus The Books of Wonder (1996, 2 vols, 343+352pp with Stephen Minch). See also Gene Matsuura, Tommy Wonder Entertains (1983). Articles in Pabular, Genii, Linking Ring, & De Magier. Invented a version of Diminishing Cards (c1972) & Floating Cage (1987). [LR5/96;Wh2]

name: Ben Ali
bio: (Egypt?: fl.c.1930s) Pro in Egypt with modern Western-type card & cigarette manip act. A favorite of King Farouk. [St]

name: Ben Ali Bey
bio: See: Auzinger, Max

name: Ben-Ali-Bey
bio: See: Buchhardt

name: Ben Said
bio: See: Hartop, A. W.

name: Ben, David G[ordon]
bio: (Toronto, Canada [sic]: 5 Mar 1961- ) Learned sleight-of-hand at age c16. Protégé of Ross Bertram. Full-time pro 1980-88, initially working at Morrissey Magic until 1983. Lawyer in Toronto. Part-time pro magician in Toronto 1989-present. Articles & routines in Pabular, Epoptica, Precursor, Apocalypse (including under his hoax name "Robert D. Michaels"), Linking Ring, Genii, New Invocation, & New Pentagram. [LR11/96;Wh2]

name: Benatar, Rafael
bio: (Caracas, Venezuela: 29 Jan 1956- ) Learned at age 9 from father and pro "Gran Henry". Began serious study at age 21. Pro since age 31 as both musician (renaissance & baroque with plucked instruments) & magician (close-up, mainly with cards). Pet effects: Cups & Balls, Triumph, Ambitious Cards. Moved to Madrid. Several national prizes, including 1989 Ascanio Prize & 1991 Florensa Prize. Wrote Cubiletes en Transito (1989, 20pp; English tr as Transit Cups & Balls) & Cartas Certificadas (1990, 136pp; English tr forthcoming). Tricks in Circular Escuela Mágica de Madrid & Linking Ring (1-man Parade in 1994). 3 videos (1997). [LR4/94;Wh5]

name: Bender, Steve[n Robert]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 4 Jun 1942- ) Learned & performed magic in 1960 at age 18 "to pay for a car I damaged". Thence pro kid-show magician as "Kelso the Clown" & "Mr Pickle". Founder-owner of Ickle Pickle Products, Inc, a maker of quality kid-show props in St. Louis, Missouri, since 1976. Invented Ickle Pickle Nickel, Animal Balloon Penetration, Zipper Gag Bag, etc. [Wh2]

name: Benedict, Dr Francis G[ane], PhD
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 3 Oct 1870-14 May 1957) PhD (Heidelberg) 1895. Chemist & physiologist. Amateur magician. Lectured on "Science and Art of Deception". Benedict, Professor Hugall [Daw#69;WWWA] (England: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro drawing-room magus in Kent. Billed as "The Thanet Wizard". Invented the Diminishing Glove by 1902 & the Torn and Restored Newspaper by 1903. Tricks in Magic (1902-1905). [Daw#127]

name: Benesch, Johann
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 1845-1907) Pro. Aka "Berantini" & "Brandini". Worked briefly at different times as partner with both Guel Salern & Charles Arbré. Played the Kratky-Baschik Zauber [Magic] Theater in Vienna as "Brandini".

name: Bénévol, Professeur François
bio: (Piacenza, Italy: 15 Jul 1865-29 May 1939) Born Francesco Luigi Maria Benevolo [sic]. Semi-pro magician. Moved to France in 1894, taking the French form of his name. Pro since 1898, touring France with his own troupe from 1899 until his death. Pet effects: manipulating cards & coins while wearing gloves, the Indian Trunk, & Decapitation. Died coincidentally on the day of the last legal use in France of the guillotine for execution. Bio is Jacques Garnier, Bénévol, le maître du mystère (1969). [Dif;Vo55;Sil]

name: Bengalis
bio: See: Sauty, Émile

name: Bengtsson, Thomas
bio: (Uddevalla County, Sweden: 28 Oct 1967-) Pro since 1990 as "Tom Stone", specialized in close-up. 1986 Scandinavian championship; 1987 Swedish cahampionship 3rd Prize in Card Magic; 1992 Swedish championship 2nd Prize in Stage Magic; 2001 Swedish championship 1st Prize in Close-up. Wrote The Warpsmith's Toolbox (1993, 60pp), The Warpsmith Returns (1996, 50pp), and several smaller booklets in both Swedish and English. Editor-publisher of Dr. Faustus Journal (1995-1997) and editor of Nordisk Magi (since 2001). Contributor to Genii, Magic, Channel One, Syzygy, Pegasus (Denmark), Magic Master (Sweden), & Arcane (France). [Wh01]

name: Benitte, Madame
bio: See: Anguinet, Bénita

name: Bennett, Doug
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Close-up performer. Wrote Extra Sensory Deceptions. Invented Criss-Cross Cards & BewildeRing. Tricks in Genii. [Wat]

name: Bennett, Horace [Eugene]
bio: (Richmond, Virginia: 9 Jul 1925-28 Dec 1990) Learned as child from easy tricks bought by parents. Learned the "real" work in 1945-46 by reading Hugard's Modern Magic Manual. Insurance underwriting investigator. Semi-pro close-up worker since 1954. Sometimes aka "Baffling Bennett" since 1964. Invented Paleface Pasteboards (1968), etc. Wrote 10 books: Prize Winning Magic (n.d.), Bennett's Best (1975, 115pp), On Your Feet (1978, 84pp), Bennett's Fourth Book (1981, 70pp), Downs Palm Technique (1981, 17pp), Alternate Handlings (1983, 96pp), Familiar Themes (1985, 111pp), The Bennett Touch (1986, 136pp), & Magic Afoot (1988, 121pp). Tricks in Hugard's (3), New Phoenix (5), MUM (1), Gen (35), Pallbearers (3), Epilogue (1), Talisman (7), Magic & Spells Quarterly (1), Mantra (1), Epoptica (1), & Linking Ring ("Parade"). [Wh2]

name: Bennett, Dr Zina B., MD
bio: (USA: 30 Oct 1891-2 Jul 1965) Physician [sic] in Detroit since 1916. Amateur magician, specializing in jumbo card manip. Marketed his ZinaB fanning deck (by 1947). Collector of magic props, letters, autographs, & 600 rare books. As a Mason, he was active in the Invisible Lodge. Married Suzy Wandas in 1959. [Scroll of Merlin 11/43; Dif]

name: Benson, Roy
bio: (USA: 1915-New York: Dec 1977?) Stage name of Edward F.E. McQuade. Classical composer. Pro comedy magician specialized in sleight-of-hand. Invented the Long Pour in the late 1930s. Played the New York Palace in 1950 & 1953 & Ed Sullivan's TV show in 1954. Assistant-wife since 1949 was "Conye", Leon Mandrake's ex-wife Lola ("Narda"). Did new act as "Roye & Connye" in 1960. 1977 AMA Performing Fellow-ship. Tricks in Genii. Died of emphysema. [Ran;HMM2/46;Des;Wat]

name: Bentley, Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Inspired at age 8. Student of Michael Skinner. Pro movie & TV actor. Semi-promagician. [Mag]

name: Bentley, Ray
bio:
Benyon, Edgar "The Great" (Auckland, New Zealand: 1901-14 Sep 1978) Stage name since 1925 of Edgar Wilson Beynon, aka "Bam-Boo-Zalem". Moved to Christchurch as child where at age 5 was inspired seeing Chung Ling Soo show. Debut in 1908. Pro comedy magic & variety show, including quick-change. Since 1918 toured the world: Australia 1918-20 & 1929, South Africa, Far East, England c1922-c1939 (including St. George's Hall in 1932), and Ireland in 1939-49 with a big tent show combining the props of Nikola, Rupert Howard, & after 1944, Cahn. Returned to New Zealand in 1949. 1969 Grand Master of Magic Award (New Zealand). Bio is Jim Reilly, Same Man — Different Clothes (1994, 132pp). [Pr;Wal]

[See also: Richardson, Cedric R.]

name: Benzais, John "Johnny
bio: (USA: 1940-1967) Learned at age 14 from apparatus tricks he bought from dealers. Three years later, bored with these, he turned to sleight-of-hand. Semi-pro close-up artist. Worked a Svengali pitch for Dave Walker. Author & lecturer. Wrote (with Al Aldini) The Best of Benzais (1967, 108pp). Tricks in Pallbearers, Gen, The Bennett Touch (1986), & Magic Afoot (1988). [NJ#33]

name: Beranek, Leopold
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 1899-14 Mar 1971) Pro illusionist & magic dealer in Prague. Edited Mago magic magazine. Wrote several books. [Mec;Nad]

name: Berantini
bio: See: Benesch, Johann

name: Bercelini
bio: (Holland: 2 Apr 1892-) Stage name of H. van Berkel. Debut in 1908. Popular pro second-sight act with wife.

name: Berdo
bio: (USSR: 1940-) Stage name of Jerzy Berdowski. Of Polish parentage. Pro manipulator. [Mec]

name: Berezovsky, Mikolay Ivanovich
bio: (Russia: 1900-) Pro magician. [Nad]

name: Berg, [Josef] "Joe
bio: (Pinsk, Russia [now Belarus]: 13 Dec 1902-19 Feb 1984) Stage name of Josef Bregman. Moved to USA in 1914. Learned magic in Chicago from Johnny Platt. Assistant to Edwin Brush around age 17. Ran magic counter in H.C. Evans & Company's retail outlet for crooked gambling devices 1924-25. Semi-pro dealer as the Princess Magic Shop in Chicago 1925-33, originally in partnership with Sam Berland & Harry Faber. Then as Berg's Magic Studio 1936-51. Moved in 1951 to Los Angeles, running an upstairs studio on Hollywood Boulevard 1952 to 1974 when retired. A prolific inventor & improver of tricks & a master maker of trick decks. 1960 TAOM Close-up Award. 1973 AMA Creative Fellowship. 1983 AMA Masters Fellowship. His son, Ronnie Berg, worked with him in Hollywood. Invented Bashful Queen (early 1920s), Super Wallet (1932), Rainbow Fanning Deck (1934), Ultra-Mental Deck (1936), & Atomic Mystery Deck (1953). Wrote Here's Magic (1930, with Nelson Hahne), Berg's Private Card Problems, Here's New Magic (1937, assisted by Martin Gardner), Rough Stuff (1956, 24pp, with Al Aldini), & The Berg Book (1983, 315pp, with David Avadon & Eric Lewis). Tricks in Felsman's, Sphinx, Tarbell #5, Genii, Linking Ring, & Tops. [Genii7/74; Mag;WWM]

name: Bergen, Edgar
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 16 Feb 1903-29 Sep 1978) Stage name of Edgar John Berggren, son of Swedish immigrants. During high school years learned vent, magic, & hypnotism simultaneously from a 35¢ wizard's manual. Mentor was Joe Berg. Pro since high school, but quickly dropped the hyp & soon dropped the magic, keeping to vent with his dummy, "Charlie McCarthy". Played both Chautauqua & Lyceum circuits. Played the Palace in New York in 1929. Later added "Mortimer Snerd" & "Effie Klinker" as dummies. Star of radio since 1936 & movies since 1938. Amateur magician. Wrote How to Become a Ventriloquist (1938). SAM Hall of Fame 1990. [Mag;St;Berg;Katz]

name: Bergeron, Bev[ely J.]
bio: (Baytown, Texas: 29 Dec 1930- ) Inspired by seeing Harry Willard c1940. Learned in 1946 assisting Willard. Featured as "Rebo the Magic Clown" in Mark Wilson's local TV series "Magic Circus" 1958 & then Wilson's weekly national TV series "The Magic Land of AllaKazam" 1960-65. Worked Florida's Disney World "Diamond Horseshoe Review" as "Pecos Bill" 1971-86. 1984 CMI Order of the Magic Lamp. IBM President 1996-97. Editor-publisher Bergeron Bee 1964-present. Wrote Willard the Wizard (1978, 154pp). Videos (1990 & 1992). [LR7/96; Se; Ogden; Mag; Bo3; Wh]

name: Bergfeld, Margitta
bio: (Beeskow, East Germany: 29 May 1952-) Semi-pro partner-wife of Werner Bergfeld in their kid-show act in East Germany. [Nad]

name: Bergfeld, W[erner] S[iegfried]
bio: (Halle, East Germany: 23 Dec 1948-) Semi-pro with partner-wife Margitta working kid shows. Collector (biographies, letters, posters) in Mühlhausen. [Nad]

name: Bergheer
bio: (Germany: fl.1870s-80s) Pro. [CI]

name: Berghof, Jean
bio: (Lemberg, Austrian Galicia [now Lvów, Ukraine]: 1869-12 Apr 1935) Major pro illusionist. Aka "Jean Baronide". Died in Berlin. [Vo57;Roh]

name: Berglas, David, MIMC
bio: (Born "somewhere on the Continent" of Europe: 30 Jul 1926- ) Fled Nazi Germany, moving to Britain at age 12. Lying about his age, joined US Army (Intelligence) in WWII. Learned magic in 1947 after meeting Ken Brooke. Studied psychotherapy. Pro since 1953 with unusual magic, pick-pocketing, memory feats, & mentalism. TV debut in 1953. Starred in several TV series in Britain (1955-67, 1986), Holland (1966-69), Germany, & Sweden. MIMC 1958 (youngest ever). 1996 Magic Circle Magician of the Year. King Rat of the Grand Order of Water Rats 1978-79. 1980 Swedish Magic Circle Gold Plaque. British Ring Past President. President, The Magic Circle, 1989-98. Father of Marvin Berglas. Wrote David Berglas Reveals—Nearly Everything (1967), The David Berglas File No.1 (1976), & A Question of Memory (1988, 128pp, with G.L. Playfair). Bio & tricks are David Britland, The Mind & Magic of David Berglas (2002, 556pp). Audio. Video. [MUM9/92;BO#254;Hudd;La2;Wh2]

name: Berglas, Marvin [Roy]
bio: (London, England: 3 Jan 1959-) Elder son of David Berglas who taught him magic in 1976. Pro dealer (Marvin's Magic) in London, opening in Hamley's in 1987 & at Harrod's in 1988. Wrote Marvin's Magic File-O-Trix (1989, 200pp). [Wh2]

name: Bergman, Jerry
bio: (Romania: c1922-12 Apr 1992) Orphaned & adopted at age 17 by Czechoslovaks. Escaped Nazi occupation in 1940, fleeing to New York. Pro comedy magician by 1942, touring the world. TV bits in USA in 1950s-60s. Finally with Carnival Cruise Line. [Tay]

name: Bergson, Sidney S. "Syd
bio: (England: 1905-24 Jan 1980) Moved to USA as child. Hotel manager. Amateur magician & mentalist in Miami. Dealer in mental effects. Mentalism column in Linking Ring in 1970s. [Wat;HMM6/53]

name: Berkel, Betty
bio: See: Odips

name: Berkie, Louis
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 25 May 1912-15 Apr 1997) Jew. Moved to San Antonio, Texas, after WW II Army service. Learned in 1946. Pro since 1949, specialized in kid shows. Known as "King of the Wooden Nickels". Magic dealer ("Fun 'n Magic Shop", informally called the "ELBEE Company") in San Antonio until his death when Eloy Foster took over. Wrote & published 4 booklets. [Wh3]

name: Berland, Sam[uel]
bio: (USA: c1904-27 May 1987) Pro close-up. Teamed with Harry Faber as "The Faberlands". Since 1925, dealer in Chicago, originally in partnership with Joe Berg & Harry Faber. In 1926 Berland was bought out by Berg and founded the Central Magic Company in Chicago, which he sold to J.C. Fabian in 1954. 1986 AMA Creative Fellowship. Prolific inventor, including Enchanted Cigarette Holder (in 1935), Devil Dollar (by 1940), Coinception (1946), Sparko (by 1948), & U-Can-Do Cards (marketed in 1950). Wrote Berland's New and Original Tricks (1933, 42pp), Novel Cigarette Tricks (1934, 48pp), Xclusive Trix (1935, 25pp), Berland's Biltrix (1940, 7pp), Match-effex (1940), Blue Ribbon Card Tricks (1942, 27pp), New and Original Tricks with Watches (1942, 64pp), Berland's Book of Routines (1950, 30pp), More Exclusive Tricks (1961), Tricks for Today and Tomorrow (1970, 32pp), The Close-Up Magic of Sam Berland (1986), etc. Tricks in Genii. [Mag;Berg,29,30]

name: Berlany
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 28 Sep 1884-May 1945) Stage name of F. Alfred Hoffmann. Pro magician for some time. In 1920 co-founded the Berlin chapter of the German Magic Circle. As a craftsman (particularly in cardboard), worked for Conradi-Horster. Collector in Berlin. He died there on fireman's duty during an Allied bombing in WW II.

name: Berle, Milton
bio: (Harlem, New York City, NY: 12 Jul 1908-27 Mar 2002) Stage name of Mendel Berlinger. Star comedian of movies (since 1937) & TV (1948-56), the latter earning him the title "Mr. Television". Amateur magician since 1919 when Nate Leipzig gave him an old deck & taught him a simple false shuffle. In 1924 included a comedy card trick in his vaude act. Taught Bill Derman his 1st card trick. Often featured magicians on his TV show. Autobio is Milton Berle (1974) & a memoir is B.S. I Love You (1988, 286pp). [Katz]

name: Berlinski, Allen [Roy]
bio: (Detriot, Michigan: 9 Sep 1938-) Learned at age 9 from magic set. Industrial designer with General Motors. Magic collector. Design director, American Museum of Magic. Wrote Purvis: The Newcastle Conjuror (1981, 40pp). Articles in Magicol, Magical Bookie, Magic Cauldron, & The Hoffmann Collector. [Wh2]

name: Bernadotte-Nordenstam, Carl Rudolf
bio: (Sweden: 1863-1942) Natural son of Charles XV, King of Sweden and Norway, by a Swedish countess; but admitted to the Court. Completing his medical studies at Uppsala U, he moved to Norway in 1905, soon becoming an avid amateur magician, performing in many countries.

name: Bernard
bio: (France: fl.1760s) Pro card magician & illusionist. Played the Paris fairs in 1769. He was the first reported to have presented the Extinguisher Trick & is possibly its inventor. [CI]

name: Bernard, Bobby, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 19 Mar 1931-10 $ ^{th} $ Nov 2014) Stage name of Bernard Samuel Lerner since 1946, aka "Bernard Vincent" for mental act (1948 only). Learned magic in 1936 visiting Davenport's, later lessons from Edward Victor & Graham Adams. Stage & film actor (since 1947) & teacher of stagecraft. Also pro performer & teacher of magi, specializing in close-up, mentalism, plus a costume act as "Isaac Fawkes". Magic collector. 1969 British Ring Conventioners Trophy. Invented Magic Mirror (1954) & Bernard Coin Box (1961). Articles in Abra, Genii, Apocalypse, Pentagram, Technomagic, etc. See Lewis Ganson, Bernard's Lesson on Dice Stacking (1979) & Val Andrews, The Coin and Card Magic of Bobby Bernard (1982, 123pp). TV bits since 1948. In 1989 did the Sawing in opera "El Re in Ascolto" on Covent Garden stage. 4 videos, 1 audio. [Wh2]

name: Bernardi
bio: (Denmark: 1902-22 Apr 1946) Stage name of Bernhard Eskilsen since 1927 when he became a pro escapist in Sweden. 1st assistant-wife 1927-29 was Miss Hilden (which see). Aka "Mr Bosco, the Man with the Mask" in early 1930s. Worked in Denmark 1944-45. Died of heart attack while finishing an underwater sack escape in Rønne, Denmark. [Ran]

name: Bernat
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 19 Jun 1909- ) Stage and pen name of Juan Bautista BERNAT SARRÓ. Watchmaker ("Joan Bernat") in Lloret de Mar. Amateur manipulator & card magician since self-taught in 1944. 1952 FISM 1st prizes in manip & table magic. Member of Escuela Mágica de Madrid. Co-authored (with Esteban Fabrégas) Cartomagia (1953, 550pp). Wrote La Magia de Bernat—30 Años Después (1980, 123pp), Manipulaciones (1982), & Cartomagia a Una Sola Mano (1987, 106pp). Articles in Ilusionismo, Misdirection, Circular Escuela Mágica de Madrid, & several foreign magazines. Videos. [Ilusionismo1/90;Xe;Cam;Wh5]

name: Berndt, Friedrich "Fritz
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 16 Nov 1840-1907) Ex-lithographer. Student of Hofzinser. Popular pro magician since 1860. Toured Balkans & Germany (1875). Moved to Berlin in 1875 where played 9 years at "Metzner's Konzert-Salon". Thence did private society shows, giving his 2,000th in 1902. Wrote Das Non plus ultra der Zauberei (1862, 96pp, as by "Fritz Berndt jun."), Der gewandte Zauberkünstler [1876, 66pp; reprinted 1882], & Wie schützt man sich gegen Falschspieler? [1900, 32pp]. [Magie12/88;Vo57;Al;St;CMM7/07]

name: Bernhardt, Frau Caroline
bio: (Germany: fl.1830s-80s) Minor pro magicienne from Berlin. Pet effect: Decapitation. Played Breslau in 1850 & Vienna in 1883. [Dif]

name: Bernini
bio: (Germany: 11 May 1895-) Stage name of E. Leist. [Roh]

name: Bernstein, Eugene "Gene
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 1896-dead) Lawyer in Chicago (clients included Joe Berg & Rufus Steele). Semi-pro hypnotist in Chicago. Introduced to magic by Joe Berg & Johnny Platt. SAM President 1939-40 & IBM President 1942-46, the first person to hold both offices in these two leading American magical associations. IBM Medallion of Honor. Acquired most of Joseffy's props. Tricks in Greater Magic, My Best, & Magic Digest. [Th;Berg]

name: Bernthaller, Bela
bio: (Hungary: fl.1920s) Amateur. Vice-President of MAME in 1929. Teacher of Odry & Rothler.

name: Berol, Max[amillion]
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 21 Jan 1868-25 Mar 1930) Stage name of Max Buldermann. Aka "Max Berol-Konorah" when working with assistant Nora "Konorah" Belmonte (see). Pro mentalist & illusionist. Invented Mene Tekel Board by 1898. Troped his act (including brother William) through Europe, Japan (in 1899), & the USA (1906-08). Another brother, Felix Berol, invented Askme (1906). [Al;Cl;Dam2;CMM10/07]

name: Berry, Jay Scott
bio:
(USA: 26 Sep 1960-) Raised in Reno, Nevada. Self-taught in early teens. Moved to Hollywood at age 17, working for Hollywood Magic & doing street magic. Pro stage & close-up. In 1979 became a Magic Castle Junior Member. 1982 FISM 2nd prize in general magic. Has played several venues in Europe. Lecturer. Author. 2 videos (1994). [Genii11/90;Wat]

[See also: "Leipzig, Nate"]

name: Berry, Pierre
bio: (Montreal, Canada: 28 Apr 1860-26 Jan 1926) Moved to Bordeaux, France, at early age. Moved to Paris in 1882. Worked a mind-reading & hypnotic act with his wife "Hamilta" by 1910. Toured the French colonies. Died in Paris. [Vo55;Magic11/10]

name: Bert. Annie
bio: (France: fl.1950s-60s) Born Huguette Delysiolle. Pro sleight-of-hand magicienne as "Lady Masking". Took stage name of "Annie Bert" after 1953 when she married Guy Bert. Featured at Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1958-59, 1968-69. NOTE: Misspelled "Anny".

name: Bert, Black
bio: See: Fredström, Bertil

name: Bert. Guy
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Stage name of Henri Guibert. Pro dealer & illusion builder (including for the Folies-Bergère) in Paris. Published Les Annales de l'Illusion (1945-47, 21 issues) & Le Vade Mecum de la Magie (1947-48, 6 issues). Editor of L'Illusionniste 1947-51. 1950 FISM 2nd prize for invention. Married "Annie Bert" in 1953. [St;Dif]

name: Bertini
bio: See: Gocke, Siegbert

name: Bertlam
bio: See: Lambert, Hubert

name: Bertol, Louis N.
bio: (Switzerland: 23 Jun 1894-17 Feb 1971) Moved to New York City at age 8. Prolific designer & builder of original childrens magic effects. Retired to Arlington, Virginia, by the 1950s. Wrote 2 Linking Ring "Parades".

name: Bertram, Charles
bio: (Woolwich, England: 26 Apr 1853-28 Feb 1907) Stage name of James Bassett. Inspired around age 12 seeing J.H. Anderson perform. Learned first trick in 1869 while travelling in Belgium from a local amateur. A failed wine merchant, he turned pro magician in 1885, working in theaters & particularly at private shows where he was known as Britain's leading society magician. Became a Mason. Taught Mdlle Patrice, Mino the Mystic, & L.H. Branson. Pet effect: Card Stab. Toured North America in 1892. World tour 1899-1901, covering India (1899-1900), the Far East, Australia (1901), New Zealand, & the USA. Died of cancer in London. Memoirs are Isn't It Wonderful? (1896, 301pp) & A Magician in Many Lands (1911, 315pp). Bio is Edwin A. Dawes, Charles Bertram: The Court Conjurer (1997, 360pp). [Cl; Go2; Pr; Wal; Bam, pp16-17; La]

name: Bertram, Clown
bio: (Clacton?, England: fl.1920s-50s) Stage name of Albert Edward Harvey. Pro magic clown, vent, chapeaugraphy, paper tearing, Punch & Judy, & living marionettes. Operated childrens theater in Clacton-on-Sea 1920s-c1940. After WW II moved to London as a society entertainer. Wrote Entertaining the Modern Child (1956, 23pp). [Abra8/49]

name: Bertram, [John] Ross
bio: (Toronto, Canada: 28 Jul 1912-10 Jun 1992) Of Canadian-born parents, his father of Scottish descent, his mother of Welsh. Inspired at age 8 seeing Thurston. Learned as schoolboy from reading Hoffmann's Modern Magic and Erdnase. Debut at age 14. Pro general magic from c1932 until 1974 when retired from performing due to illness. A pioneer in trade & industrial show magic. Pet effects: coin magic & cups-&-balls. Mentor of David Ben. Designed Ross Bertram cups (early 1950s). Wrote The Magic and Methods of Ross Bertram (1978, 165pp; repr 1996) & Bertram on Sleight of Hand (1983, 255pp; repr 1996). Many articles & tricks in Ibidem, etc. TV bits. [Genii2/53;Bo#224;Wh5]

name: Bertrand, Alban
bio: (Belgium: fl. 1930s-50s) Barrister & amateur magician. Founding President of Société Belge de Prestidigitation in 1930 & Cercle de Prestidigitation de Belgique in 1934. Died in early 1950s.

name: Bervas, Les
bio: See: Ruegg, Théodore & Vassal, Marcel

name: Besoni, Arthur
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-20s) Pro vent-magus who specialized in historical magic. Did kid-shows in England by c1910. Played St. George's Hall in London often in 1914 & 1920.

name: Bessemans, Albert, M.D.
bio: (Belgium: fl.1930s-50s) Professor & later Rector of Ghent U. Dedicated his life to unmasking pseudo-psychics. In 1949 founded the Comité Belge pour l'Investigation Scientifique des Phénomènes Réputés Paranormaux. Lectured & wrote on this subject. Brother of Paul Bessemans.

name: Bessemans, Paul
bio: (Belgium: -1956) Semi-pro. Innovator. Specialized in Chinese-type effects. Aka "Paulo Fantas". Brother of Albert Bessemans.

name: Besson, Jacques
bio: (France: 1540-1576) Engineer & inventor. Wrote a text in Latin as Theatrum instrumentorum, which was published in 1569 with French tr as Théâtre des instruments mathématiques et mécaniques (Lyon: 1596). Includes the first exposé of the Inexhaustible Barrel device. [Cl;Dif]

name: Bessy, Maurice
bio: (Nice, France: 4 Dec 1910-15 Nov 1993) Prominent French film writer & critic since 1928. Administrator-General of the International Cannes Film Festival, 1972-78. Non-magician. Wrote Georges Méliès, mage (1945, with Giuseppe Lo Duca); Les truquages au cinéma (1951, with Introduction by Orson Welles), on cinematic special effects; Histoire en 1.000 images de la magie (1962; Engl tr 1963), on occult magic; Orson Welles (1963, 223pp; Engl tr 1971, 195pp); Le Mystere de la Chambre Noire, (Paris: 1990, 200pp), a history of film animation; etc. [CA;Wh]

name: Betts, Dorothy
bio: See: Dobson, Betty

name: Bevan, Donald
bio: (Birmingham, England: 27 Aug 1933-) Inspired at age c11 seeing a magician work at school. Pro childrens magician since 1965. Pet effects: Sponge Balls, Cards Across, & production routines. Associate editor of Abracadabra from 1965 until 1980 when he became that venerable magazine's 2nd editor, a position he still holds. Articles in Abra (many) & Magigram (1). Has also edited & produced most Goodliffe Publications since 1965. [Wh5]

name: Bey, Mohammed
bio:
Bey, Achmed Ali Talented Black Art performer. Name chosen obviously to imitate Achmed Ben Ali (Max Auzinger) the inventor of the Black Art act. Toured with his own show and then with the Wash Norton troupe in US and Japan.

[See also: Horowitz, S. Leo]

name: Beynon, Edgar
bio: See: "Benyon, Edgar"

name: Bialla, [Oscar] Ralf
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 19 Apr 1921-29 [sic] Jul 1975) Pro manip & illusions in West Germany, sometimes working with assistant-wife Inge. 1950 Munich 1st prize. Toured Europe, including the East Berlin Friedrichstadt-palast c1950 & Portugal in 1952. Later added the Bullet Catch. Killed by a fall in the Alps. [Win;St;Cam]

name: Bi-Ber-Ti
bio: See: Bieber, Arthur

name: Bidart, Victor-Joseph
bio: (Dour, Belgium: 28 May 1867-21 Jun 1925) Pro magic & hypnotic act. [Dif;Vo58]

name: Biddle, Elmer
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-60s) Card man & magic dealer (Unique Novelty in early 1930s & Unique Magic Company in mid-1940s) in Los Angeles. Invented Biddle Move, which he published in Apr 1947 in Genii & then in Hugard's Magic Monthly in Jun 1947. Other tricks in HMM.

name: Bieber, Arthur
bio: (Britain: -11 Mar 1913) Skilled billiard ball manipulator. Headed his own "Bi-Ber-Ti" troupe. In Rome in 1910. Shot & killed himself on Continental train at Charing Cross station, London. [Daw2;Vo57]

name: Bienvenue
bio: (France: fl.1790s-1810s) Pro. Played Brussels 1800 & 1811. [St]

name: Biet, Ted
bio: (Dutch East Indies: fl.1980s) Moved to Holland. Card magic. Invented Ted Biet Rising Card.

name: Bigbee, North
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-60s) Amateur since teens. Newspaperman, playwrite, screenwriter, & free-lance writer for magazines. Aka "North". Wrote 40 New Mental Mysteries (1962, 76pp; reprinted 1969 as Stage Mentalism, 76pp). Tricks in Sphinx, Eagle Magician, Magic World, New Tops, New Phoenix, New Jinx, & HMM.

name: Bigelow, Norman [George] "Buddy
bio: (Leominster, Massachusetts: 12 Aug 1944-) Born Henry Hebert but name changed on his adoption. Inspired at age 8. A master locksmith & safesmith in Fitchburg, Massachusetts. Pro escapist since age 18 as "Bigelow". Pet effect: The Doors of Death. In 1985 founded Escape Masters International, the world's only club for escape artists. 1988 Escape Masters' Masters Award. Editor of Escape Master Quarterly. Invented several escapes, including Story Tomb Escape (1985) used by Copperfield in his 1989 TV special). Wrote 10 booklets on escapism, including Exposé for the Specialist & Death Blow-The Houdini Murder Theory. Articles & escapes in Escape, Escapism, & MUM. [MUM3/94;Bo2;Wh2]

name: Billard
bio: (France: fl.1740s) Pro at the St.-Germain fair in Paris in 1748, advertising numerous tricks. [Cl;St]

name: Billing, Louis
bio: (Finland: 1888-1980) Pro magician, originally solo playing fairs. Then, since 1935, with a Black Art act with his Danish father-in-law, Buckhardt. [St]

name: Bilis, Bernard
bio: (France: 1957-) Learned as small boy from a magic set. Pro close-up & one of the top French cardmen. Wrote Close-up French Style (1976, 52pp) & French Pastboards (1980, 63pp). Articles in Mad Magic. Video (1985) & video bit (1994). [Lo]

name: Billy, Henri
bio: (Paris, France: 1883-Jan 1971) Pro magic dealer & publisher in Paris 1913-33, having taken over the shop of Léon Baudot. Sold his shop to André Mayette in 1933.

name: Bils, Adolph
bio: (Germany: fl.1840s-70s) Pro, specializing in pyrotechnic displays.

name: Binarelli, [Antonio] "Tony" MIMC
bio: (Rome, Italy: 16 Sep 1940- ) Learned in 1952 from magic book. Semi-pro card magic & close-up 1960-71. 1967 & 1970 FISM 2nd prize for card magic. Pro since 1972, including mentalism (1977-82). Returned to straight magic in 1982 plus much MC work. 1989 Italian press award for magic & entertainment. Edited Qui Magia 1988-present. For magicians wrote Playmagic (4 vols, 1976, 1979, 1985, 1989). Articles in Linking Ring, Coven, Qui Magia. For general public wrote Dopo cena con il mago (1972), Quinta dimensione (1977), Occhio al baro (1982), & Tutti i trucchi del gioco d'azzardo (1985). See Gary Ouellet, Class Act: The Magic of Tony Binarelli (1991, 200+pp). TV bits both nationally and internationally since 1972. [LR3/2005;Wh2]

name: Binet, Alfred [pronounced BEE-neh]
bio: (Nice, France: 8 Jul 1857-18 Oct 1911) French psychologist. Wrote Psychologie de la Prestidigitation (Paris: 1894; with English tr as Psychology of Prestidigitation, 1896), a pioneering use of stop-action photography to study sleight-of-hand artists. Later famous for work on child psychology & inventor of the original standardized test for human intelligence (1905). A bio is Theta H. Wolf, Alfred Binet (1973, 376pp)

name: Bingo, Joe
bio: (USA: fl.1960-80s) Learned at age 13. Semi-pro comedy magic. Claims, probably as a hoax, an autobiography, A Lifetime of Comedy and Magic from Vaudeville to Poverty. [Mag]

name: Biow, [Richard M.] "Dick
bio: (New York City, New York: 5 May 1920-) Learned at age 16 from friends, then in WW II by lessons from Al "The Spongeball King" Cohn. Commercial writer. Amateur close-up magician. Pet effects: Cups & Balls, Out of This World, & Bill in Lemon. Tricks in Phoenix & Arcane. [Wh2]

name: Birch, Mabel
bio: (USA: -6 May 1985) Born Mabel Sperry. Musician. Joined McDonald Birch's show as marimba-xylophone player & main box-jumper. Married Birch in 1931. After c1950 took over as the show's booker. The couple retired in 1964. [Pr]

name: Birch, [George] McDonald "Mack
bio: (Columbus, Ohio: 28 Jan 1902-28 Apr 1992) Aka "Birch the Magician". Raised in McConnellsville, Ohio. Inspired at age 10 by brother's magic set, learning from then until age 17 when in 1919 he turned pro stage magician with a minor Chautauqua circuit. A star of the Lyceum & Chautauqua circuits 1919-26. Thence as independent. Married his assistant Mabel in 1931. Pet effects (since 1931): Vanishing Pony, "Scimitar" (cutting a girl into four parts), Challenge Box Escape, & "The Silk Mirage" (silk production). 1936 Sphinx Award. Did their last show in 1964 at the Scala Theatre in London & retired to Malta, Ohio. 1980 AMA Masters Fellowship. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr;LR7/92;Ho]

name: Biro, [Peter Andreas] "Pete
bio: (Oakland, California: 1 Jun 1933-) Photo-journalist in California. Inspired at age 16 by a co-worker. Semi-pro stage & close-up magician since 1949. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Card in Balloon. Edited Pete's Leaflets 1973-76. Writes "The Reel Works" column for Genii c1978-c1990. Wrote lecture notes Son of Greater Magic #1 (1990). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Bisbee, Jess C.
bio: (Spencer, Iowa: 1890-3 Jun 1955) Aka "The Great Mahala". Pro tent show owner & magician.

name: Bishop, Ron[ald], MIMC
bio: (Watford, Herts., England: 10 Aug 1903-1995) Learned in 1911 from box of tricks. In fashion trade in London & Leicester. Semi-pro manipulator & (after retirement to Felixstowe) a childrens magician. Past President British Ring. Wrote Laughter all the Way (1968, 130pp). Articles in Magicana (New Zealand), etc. [Wh6]

name: Bishop, Washington Irving
bio: (New York, USA: 4 Mar 1856-13 May 1889) Worked with Anna Eva Fay's spiritualist troupe, becoming her manager. Solo since 1876 as an "Anti-Spiritist", exposing Miss Fay. Pro muscle-reader since 1877 when taught that technique by J. Randall Brown. Invented non-contact mind reading in 1881 when he first exhibited it in Britain. Invented the blindfold drive publicity stunt in 1885 when he first performed it with horse & carriage in New York City. His controversial death may have occurred during a premature autopsy. Wrote (probably ghosted by W.H.F. Wicks) Houdin and Heller's Second Sight (Edinburgh: 1880, 78pp). [Jay;Pr]

name: Bitzer, [George William] "Billy
bio: (Roxbury, Massachusetts: 21 Apr 1872-Apr 1944) Born Johann Gottlob Wilhelm Bitzer. Self-taught. Pro as magic shop salesman (Magic Introduction Company) in New York City from 1894 until 1907 when he turned movie cameraman (Birth of a Nation, Intolerance, etc) for D.W. Griffith at Biograph from 1908 to 1920. Autobio is Billy Bitzer: His Story (1973). [Bar;Katz]

name: Bixby, Bill
bio: (San Francisco, California: 22 Jan 1934-21 Nov 1993) TV star actor: My Favorite Martian 1963-66, The Courtship of Eddie's Father 1969-72, The Incredible Hulk 1978-82, & Goodnight, Beantown 1983-84. Amateur magician. Magic Castle member (#A-215) since 1963. Star of NBC-TV series The Magician (1973-74) for which he took extra magic lessons. [Mag]

name: Blacaman
bio: (Sicily, Italy: -c1941) Pro fakir act, specializing in hypnotizing animals & live burial. One of his boy assistants was the young Tihany. Played the Paris Empire with Theo "Okito" Bamberg 1925 and the Lisbon Coliseu 1925-26 & 1936. Toured Mexico 1938-40 when Paco Miller's brother was his agent. See Martins Oliveira, Blacaman e os seus truques (Portugal: 1926), an exposé. NOTE: Reports that he died in 1929 of asphyxiation during a live burial performance in Cordoba, Argentina, refer to a man who stole his name. [Dif]

name: Black Carl
bio: See: Carl, Black

name: Black Herman
bio: See: Herman, Black

name: Black, Fred
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Rancher in Thedford, Nebraska. Expert amateur cardman. A pioneer in Perfect Riffle Shuffles, corresponding with T. Nelson Downs in the mid-1920s. Gave Downs the Faro tables that appear in Hugard & Braue's Expert Card Technique (1940). Profiled in a Ripley's "Believe It Or Not". [HMM9/50]

name: Black, Ishii
bio: (Adelaide, Australia: 22 Dec 1858 - 19 Sep 1923) Stage name of Henry James Black after moved to Japan at age 7 or 8, becoming naturalized citizen & adopted into a Japanese family. Stage name was Kairakutei, Black. Pro comic teller in Japanese vaudeville. Wrote "Japanese Magic" in Magician Monthly (Sep 1914-Nov 1915); reprinted as The Magic of Ishii Black (1992). [Sphinx1/33]

name: Black, Mr
bio: See: Schwarz, Ernst

name: Blackledge, J[ohn] Elder
bio: (Indianapolis, Indiana: 7 Feb 1891- ) Interested in 1902 & was only pupil of Ed Maro (in 1906). Architect in New York City. Semi-pro society magician & lecturer 1930s-60s. A favorite of President Franklin D. Roosevelt. Tricks in HMM & Tarbell #5. [SAM;Ho]

name: Blackman, Al[fred]
bio: (USA: -1973) Amateur collector of magic magazines, magic courses, bibliographies, & other reference works. By 1957 when he stopped collecting his was the largest such collection in the USA. In the late 1950s this fine collection passed intact (except for duplicates) to the Library of Congress. Died in Beverly Hills, CA. [LR5/95]

name: Blackmore, Kent [Stuart]
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 27 Feb 1961-) Learned at age c8 from books. Clerk & computer operator. Amateur magician, specialized in mental magic & magic history. Wrote Oscar Eliason: The Original "Dante the Great" (1984, 32pp; 2nd ed 1987, 40pp) & Levante: His Life No Illusion. [Wh2]

name: Blackstar, Medrano
bio: (Long Lake, Washington: fl.1930s-40s) Full-blooded Spokane Amerindian. Stage name of I.E. Camille, aka "Chief Blackstar, the Cherokee Magician". Learned Indian magic from grandfather and Western magic from Tarbell course. Semi-pro since 1930 with full show in Northwest USA of small magic, escapism, mental magic, & Hindu effects. Column in Genii in early 1940s. [WWM]

name: Blackstone, Gay Blevins
bio: (Ft. Worth, Texas: 27 Mar c1949-) Born [Arla] Gay Blevins, the name she still uses professionally. At around age 19, as a dancer on The Dean Martin Show in 1968, she was first exposed to magic as assistant to Orson Welles. Then worked as assistant to several magicians at the Academy of Magical Arts' annual "It's Magic" shows until 1970 when Blackstone Jr got her for his act. Principal assistant to Blackstone Jr since then. They married in 1974. 1989 Dragon Award to both. [LR5/2003;Mar;Wh]

name: Blackstone, Harry
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 27 Sep 1885-16 Nov 1965) Born Harry Boughton [sic]. Pro stage illusionist since c1906. Originally performed as "Bouton", then "The Great Stanley", "Francisco", 'Harry Careejo", "Mr. Quick", "C. Porter Norton", "LeRoy Boughton", "Beaumont the Great", "Fredrik the Great" (1915-18), & finally "Blackstone" since 7 Jan 1918. Throughout his career his principal assistant & stage manager was younger brother "Pete Bouton". Pet effects: Vanishing Birdcage (since 1917), Dancing Handkerchief (by 1918), Bear Illusion (by 1918), & Frank Hall's Floating Lightbulb (since 1931). IBM Member #10 (1922). Co-founded (with Percy Abbott as partner & manager) a magic dealership, the Blackstone Magic Company, in Colon, Michigan, 1927-31. Between Thurston's death in 1936 & Dante's return to the USA in 1940, Blackstone was America's undisputed top stage illusionist. In WW II toured 165 US military posts with USO. Retired in 1959 & moved in 1960 from New York (where he had kept an apartment since 1926) to Los Angeles. SAM Hall of Fame. Father of Harry Blackston Jr. Invented or at least introduced the Vanishing Automobile (in 1923) & the Auto Tire Illusion in (1935). Wrote 2 books ghosted by Walter B. Gibson: Blackstone's Secrets of Magic (1929, 265pp; several reprints) & Blackstone's Modern Card Tricks (1932). 3 TV bits (1950s). Bio is Dan Waldron, Blackstone: A Magician's Life (forthcoming 1999). [Pr;Ch;Par;Fi;Tay;Fu;Ho]

name: Blackstone Jr, Harry
bio: (Three Rivers, Michigan: 30 [sic] Jun 1934-14 May 1997) Only child of Harry Blackstone & his 2nd wife, "Billie Mathews" (Mildred Phinney). Debut around 1954. Married Almeda Louise Hornaday in 1955 in Japan while he was serving with the US Army. Pro stage illusionist since 1970. In 1974 married Gay Blevins, his principal assistant (since 1970) & 3rd wife. Pet effects: Floating Lightbulb & Vanishing Birdcage. AMA Magician of the Year 1979 & 1985. SAM Hall of Fame. 1989 Dragon Award to Harry & Gay. 1993 AMA Performing Fellowship. 1997 Christopher Award (posthumous) for Best Illusionist. Toured both a full-evening show & a short act. One of the half dozen top stage magic acts in North America in the 1970s-90s. AMA Board Member since 1994. Ill with pancreatic cancer, he died of bacterial infection. Wrote (with Charles & Regina Reynolds) The Blackstone Book of Magic & Illusion (1985). Video. Many TV bits. [Jef;Fi;Mag;Wat;Walk;WWE]

name: Blackton, J[ames] Stuart
bio: (Sheffield, England: 4 Jan 1875-13 Aug 1941) Immigrated with his widowed mother to New York City at age 10. In 1894 framed a magic act with fellow-immigrant Albert E. Smith, the latter as magician with Blackton acting as chalk-talker and lightning cartoonist. In 1896 made a short animate film for the Edison Company. In 1897 [sic] Blackton & Smith went into the new cinema business when they formed the Vitagraph Company, which began production next year. Blackton worked mainly as a creative producer & director, Smith as the business brains. Its quick success soon led them to choose to drop their magic. In 1906 Blackton used stop-motion photography to make Humorous Phases of Funny Faces, the world's first cartoon on motion-picture film. In 1925 they sold Vitagraph to Warner Brothers for $735,000. Blackton died in poverty. Bios are Anthony Slide, The Big V: A History of the Vitagraph Company (rev ed 1987); & Marian Blackton Trimble, J. Stuart Blackton: A Personal Biography (Metuchen, NJ: Scarecrow Press, 1985). Blackton appeared in two films: The Twentieth Century Tramp (1902, also titled Happy Hooligan and His Airship) & A Vitagraph Romance (1912, documentary). [Bar;Katz]

name: Blackwood, Dan
bio: (USA: -c1986) Pseudonym of Daniel O'Brien. Pro mentalist-hypnotist in New Jersey. Wrote The Psychic Entertainer's Handbook of Professional Presentations (1984).

name: Blaeser, [Andrew] "Andy
bio: (USA: c1898-) Pro, working a double-act with Ade Duval (as "Amrein & Baeser") by 1917, finally in vaudeville, Lyceum, & Chautauqua as "The Duval Brothers" 1921-1924 when they were known as Ade & Andy Duval. In 1924 Blaeser married and settled down, leaving the travelling life of magic. [Pr;Bos]

name: Blaine, David
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: c1973-) Real name David Blaine White. Street magician in New York City. 1997 ABC-TV special.

name: Blaisdell, Frank E., MD
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Wrote Original Magic (251pp), More of Magic (97pp), Just Ropes, Rings & Ropes, and Rope Escapes (95pp), Magical Fun with Magic Squares (86pp), & The Eight King Setup for the Mentalist (24pp).

name: Blakan
bio: (Spain: fl.1950s) Stage name of Ricardo Novella. Pro. In 1956 made magic apparatus with Picart.

name: Blake, Charles
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Sleight-of-hand artist & mental magician in New York area. Actor in play Dead End in 1937. Taught magic to Tallulah Bankhead in 1939. [Jinx#32]

name: Blake, George
bio: (England: 5 Nov 1893-Aug 1979) Stage name of George William Blakemore. Semi-pro. Edited The Budget & Entre Nous 1941-42 (15 issues). Invented Uncanny Hanks (1952). Wrote several booklets including The ABC Triple Divination (1951), Master Magic (1961, 48pp), More Master Magic (1964, 48pp), Comedy Magic (1966; repr 1974, 56pp), Loopy Loop (1967, 22pp), Major Magic (1968, 55pp), & Commercial Card Magic (1972, 49pp). Audio. Tricks in Mantra. [Wat]

name: Blanchard, Peter
bio: (Britain?: c.1921-2004) Sales director for a pharmaceutical firm. Amateur magus. Edited the magic column in The World's Fair 2001.

name: Blanche, Madame
bio: (Europe: c1916-) Ballet dancer when at age 16 inspired to take up magic by seeing Larette. Pro magicienne & manipulator. In 1938 (she claims) appointed Artist-Magicienne to the Yugoslavian Royal Court. [Jinx#81]

name: Blanche, Abel[-Louis-Joseph]
bio: (Dijon, Côte-d'Or, France: 20 Jan 1870-19 Sep 1941) ASAP Secretary-General 1921-34. Autobio is Notes et souvenirs d'un illusioniste (1935, 51pp). Articles. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Bland, J[oseph]
bio: (Britain?: -1898) Professional name since c1855 of Giuseppe Bolasco, of Italian ancestry. Spelled surname "Blande" until c1861 when dropped the "e". Pro dancing master at Cremorne Gardens, Chelsea, London. Then a magician. And a pro dealer (The Magical and Conjuring Repository; Bland's Magical Palace) in London from 1855 until 1899 when his shop was absorbed by Hamley's. NOTE: Did not, as misattributed by Stanyon, write the anonymous The Parlour Magician; A Handy Book for the Amateur Conjurer, which was a stock book originally published in 1863 by Clarke's. Perhaps did write the anonymous Chapeaugraphy, or Twenty Five Heads under One Hat (1895, 57pp; reissued as by J.G. Hamley). [Daw94]

name: Bland, Will
bio: (Australia: fl.1910s) Pro vaudeville illusionist. In USA for 5 years during late 1910s. Did a series of magicians profiles in The Sphinx.

name: Blaney, [Rebecca Joyce] "Becky
bio: (Houston, Texas: 30 Sep 1956-) Eldest of 3 daughters of Walter "Zany" Blaney from whom she learned as part-time assistant. Won an IBM teenage magic contest in 1974. In 1975 was first woman to receive the Senior Adult trophy at the IBM Convention in Little Rock. Full-time pro comedy stage magician since 1986. Plays the Magic Castle twice yearly since 1986. TV bits. [LR11/94;Wh2]

name: Blaney, Walter [Edwin] "Zaney
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 11 Feb 1928- ) Inspired at age 9 by classmate doing show-&-tell & then seeing Blackstone show. Learned from library magic books. Debut in high school. Billed as "Zaney Blaney" since 1946. Took dramatic arts degree in 1950 from U of Texas. Full-time pro stage comedy magician since 1950. Pet effects: Repeat Vanishing Birdcage & Blaney method of Shirt Removal. In 1965 founded "Show Stoppers Company" in Houston, Texas. TAOM President 1970-71. International President of the World Alliance of Magicians until 1999. Father of Becky Blaney. Awards: 1960 TAOM Werner Trophy for Best Comedy Act & Crofts Award for Act Most Interesting To Children. 1986 Las Vegas Seminar Silver Lion Award. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame. Invented his Ladder Levitation in 1955, premiered it at 1965 IBM Convention, & marketed it since 1986 (first to Copperfield); Giant Rabbit Production from Shopping Bag (1960); Blaney Live Feet Thin Sawing (1960, built & premiered 1980); Blaney Lighted Sword Cabinet (1969, built & premiered 1979). Articles in Linking Ring, Genii, Tops, Lines from Lawton, MUM. Several TV shows beginning with Carson in 1973. [Bo#319;MUM1/92;MUM1/75;Se;Wh]

name: Blantz, Father [James] "Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Roman Catholic priest & amateur magician. Missionary in Bangladesh & Uganda 1960-61. Polished his skills studying with Jim Ryan in Chicago. 1965 TAOM Close-up Award. 1967 IBM Card Magic Competition winner. A Magic Castle regular since 1972. [Mag]

name: Blau, [Robert NMN] "Bob
bio: (Houston, Texas: 3 Oct 1902-11 Aug 2001) Taught small tricks by parents at age 8. Pro platform & stage magician since 1917. Also as juggler "Aldo" 1940-45. Pet effects: Spirit Cabinet, cards, & coins. Still active at conventions & occasionally performing as late as 1998. Wrote Bob Blau's World of Magic (1985, 53pp) & Spirits on the Stage (1994, 30pp). Tricks in Sphinx (1920-25), Linking Ring, & Seance (1989). [LR2/99;MUM2/70;WWM;Wh;Wh5] Blavatsky, Madame Helena P. [that is, Elena Petrovna] (Ekaterinoslav, Russia: 1831-8 May 1891) Religious leader of the Theosophist Movement. Toured widely, spreading the doctrine and stressing psychic factors in religion. In 1875 co-founded the Theosophical Society in the USA & in 1879 a branch in Bombay. Wrote Isis Unveiled (1877) & The Secret Doctrine (1888), the first giving the earliest account of the Sword Suspension (as a genuine Hindu mystery) as well as early credulous accounts of pseudo-psychics. An early exposé is Arthur Little, Madame Blavatsky and Her Theosophy (1897). See also Peter Washington, Madame Blavatsky's Baboon (1995, 470pp).

name: Blei, Felix [misspelling]
bio: See: Bley, Felix

name: Blevins, Gay
bio: See: Blackstone, Gay Blevins

name: Bley, Felix [pronounced BLIGH]
bio: (Tremessen, Germany: 1 Jun 1874- ) Moved to USA. Pro in 1900 with own magic show. A top manager-agent (with the Hugo Brothers agency) for magicians, beginning in 1900 with Morton Clivette & continuing with The Great McEwen (1908-09), Nicola (since 1909), Dante (since 1911), Fasola (1912-29), Annie Abbott (1913), LeRoy-Talma-Bosco (1914), Herbert Flint (1915), Charles Carter, Grover George (1924-25), S.S. Henry (1931-34), & Edwin Brush (1934). Best known for booking foreign tours & acting as advance man. SAM & IBM member. Edited the magic news page in The Billboard. NOTE: Although his name was probably Blei he spelled it "Bley" on his letterhead. [Pr;WWM]

name: Blind, Adolphe
bio: (Geneva, Switzerland: 10 Oct 1862-23 Aug 1925) Aka "Le Professeur Magicus". Inspired at age 9 by a magic show. In 1878 at age 16 established a magic shop ("Bosco, Blind et Cie") in Geneva. His hand-written Le Cagliostro, published in Geneva 1878-79, was world's 2nd magic magazine & the 1st in French. A founding member of ASAP in 1903 & early member of the CSP. At age 62 while giving a charity show in Geneva died of a heart attack. Wrote The Bibliography of Conjuring & Kindred Deceptions (1920, 84pp, with Sidney W. Clarke), a pioneering but now outdated work; and Les automates truqués (1927). Major collector of books (2,134 vols), autographs (916), & other bits of magicana. His collection eventually passed to Jean Garance. [Dif;St]

name: Blitz
bio: (USA: fl.1880s) Stage name of David Batents, one of the many magicians who took Antonio Blitz's stage name. Pro until went insane around 1888. [Mo] Blitz of Moravia, Signor (Germany: fl.1820s) Advertised as a student & assistant of Philadelphia. Pro stage magic in British Isles, assisted by his 2 sons. Played the Coburg Theatre, London, 1826. Possibly invented the Inexhaustible Portfolio. [Cl;Fr]

name: Blitz Jr., Signor
bio: (Britain: fl.1820s) Learned assisting father, Blitz of Moravia. Pro stage work in London by 1827. Pet effect: Bullet Catching. [Fr;Ch;Cl]

name: Blitz, Antonio
bio: (Deal, England: 21 Jun 1810-28 Jan 1877) Stage name of Antoni van Zandt, aka "Signor Blitz of Moravia", which he stole from the above. Son of a merchant. Pro vent & magus since 1825. Pet effects: Plate Spinning (by 1830) & Bullet Catching (by 1830). Moved in 1835 to USA where he became a top-line star until retiring in Philadelphia in 1860. Father of Harry "Haba Haba" Blitz. Autobio is Fifty Years in the Magic Circle (1871, 432pp), a somewhat misleading book. [Ch;Pr;Mo;Magic10/01]

name: Blitz, Francois
bio: (USA: fl.1880s) Stage name. Minor pro in USA around 1880.

name: Blitz, Harry [or Theodore?]
bio: (USA?: -Jun 1915) Son of Antonio Blitz & his Scottish wife. Pro in USA, performing as "Haba Haba". Died in Minneapolis. [Cl;Ch]

name: Bloch, Richard I [saac] "Rich", AIMC
bio: (East Orange, New Jersey: 15 Jun 1943- ) Demoed in Ted Collins' shop in East Orange in 1950. Lawyer in Washington, DC, since 1968. Semi-pro mail-order manufacturer (Collectors' Workshop) in Washington, DC, since 1981. Collector. AIMC 1987. Auctioned his collection in 2006 through Martinka.com. Wrote These are a Few of My Favorite Things (1984, 35pp). Invented Stull System, Perfect Time Watch, etc. Reviewer for Magic Manuscript until 1989. [Wh]

name: Blodgett, Sherwood Brandon
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 1887-) Amateur since c1905, living in Atlanta, Georgia. Pet effects: vest pocket tricks. Contributor to Sphinx & Linking Ring. [WWM]

name: Blondin, Charles
bio: (St.-Omer, France: 28 Feb 1824-19 Feb 1897) Stage name of yellow-haired Jean-François-Émile Gravelet. World-famous French wire & rope walker. In 1859 became first person to rope-walk (1,100 feet) across Niagara Falls. Retired in 1896 at age 71. Died in London. His name was adopted by magicians for Blondino, the effect where a ball rolls back-&-forth on a cord stretched between the hands of the magician. [Ogden]

name: Bloom, Gaëtan
bio: (Paris, France: 24 Oct 1953-) Stage name of Jean-Louis Gaëtan Blum since 1971. Learned at age 6-8 from magic set, lessons age 10 from Dominique Webb & age 13 from Jean Merlin. Pro comedy magician since age 18, initially assisting Gerard Majax. Then solo as top-line close-up. Pet effects: Standing Card, Microphone Routine, Instant Vanishing-&-Reappearing Shoe, Boxing Gloves Card Manipulations. Invented Bloom Gimmick in 1985 & Card in Tape Recorder. Wrote (with Jeff Busby) Gaetan Bloom's Visible Monte (1986, 24pp). Co-editor Le Magicien 1992-present. Tricks in Journal de la Prestidigitation, Pabular, & Genii. 2 videos (1984, 1986). Now (1995) researching a bio of Winston Freer. [Wat;Wh5]

name: Blount, Gerald R. "Jerry" "Jer
bio: (Mount Airy, North Carolina: 1927- ) Published Talisman 1970-71 and was its 2nd and last editor in 1971. Managed Phil Thomas' former Yogi Magic after it moved to Ellicott City, Maryland, 1986-87. Later moved to Williamsburg. Tricks in Genii & Linking Ring (5/96). NOTE: His rumored birth in England is, he says, false.

name: Blow, Windy
bio: (Britain: c1911-1986) Stage name of Charles Cole. Pro lightning cartoonist & balloon twister, which act he pioneered in Britain along with Wally Boag. Learned balloons in WW II when, having got TB, his physician advised blowing up balloons to strengthen his lungs.

name: Blue William
bio: (USA: 1 Aug 1900-16 Dec 1929) Stage name of Wilford J. Williams Jr.

name: Bluffman, Mr.
bio: See: Lindgren, Karl Gerhard

name: Bluffman, Professor
bio: See: Dawes, Dr Edwin A.

name: Blum, [Morris] "Strong
bio: (New York City, NY: 29 Mar 1884-18 Aug 1945) In youth joined circus as strong man, later playing vaude, dime museums, & burlesque. After 1909 took up magic as hobby & soon became semi-pro in New York area. Collector of magic books. [SAM]

name: Blume, Max [pronounced BLOOM-uh]
bio: (Germany: 28 Nov 1864-6 Feb 1941) Toured Germany & Switzerland with vent & magic act. Then pro magic dealer in Altona, Germany, c1898. Wrote Bauchredner (1890), a booklet on vent. [St;Die Magie1/33]

name: Bluemle, Robert L[ouis] "Bob
bio: (Anderson, Indiana: 6 Nov 1933-) Learned at age 9 from Bert Wheeler's Magic Shop tricks. Studied under Duke Stern, Tahman Conrad, Bert Easley, & Danny Dew. Senior partner in a Scotsdale, Arizona, law firm. Semi-pro mentalist as "Dr Juris". Pet effects: Those relating to time. Also collector. Wrote The Incredible Dr. Jaks (forthcoming 1993 or 1994, c350pp). Articles in MUM & Lota. [MUM11/88:Wh2]

name: Blumen
bio: (Italy: fl.1950s) Stage name of Enzo Ficco. Pro. Toured Spain & Portugal in 1959.

name: Blumenfeld, Emanuel
bio: (Germany: 1 Mar 1811-May 1885) Jew. Pro magician & circus director. [Dam]

name: Blumenfeld, Professor [Johann?]
bio: (Germany: -24 Jan 1906) Aka "St. Jean Bosco". Lived in England where he was known as "Blumenfield". Shot dead on-stage in Basle, Switzerland, by a volunteer assistant while doing the Bullet Catch with a revolver. [Magic2/06,34;Cl]

name: Blyth, Will [J.], MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1873-7 Jan 1937) Worked for London Salvage Corporation. Semi-pro childrens magician. Invented Sympathetic Blocks. Wrote Paper Magic (1920, 99pp), Match-Stick Magic (1921), Handkerchief Magic (1922, 123pp), More Paper Magic (1923, 124pp; repr 1938), Impromptu Conjuring (1924), Money Magic (1926), Effective Conjuring (1928), & How to Become a Conjuror (1934). Articles in Magic Circular. [Wat]

name: Boardé, C. L. [pronounced bor-DAY]
bio: (Bronx, New York City, New York: 12 Aug 1921-1 May 2000) Pen name from "Clip Board" of Warren J. [or K.] Schoonmaker. Statistician in electronics & marketing. Amateur mentalist. Edited a club newsletter. Wrote The Borrowed Brain (1946); Mainly Mental (3 vols: 1947, 132pp; 1950, 132pp; 1999), a classic; & One-On-One Mentalism (1997, 106pp). Article in Vibrations, etc. [LR7/2000]

name: Boaz, Herman
bio: (Germany: fl.1770s-1820s). Pro, aka "The Sieur Boaz". Toured the British Isles 1772, 1795, 1811-16. Taught Mr. Arbuckle. Wrote The Juggler's Oracle: or, The Whole Art of Legerdemain Laid Open (London: 1826, 84pp). [Daw#204;Fr]

name: Bobby
bio: (USA?: c1910-15 Dec 1918) Houdini's pet Fox Terrier whom he trained to escape from ropes, handcuffs, & straitjackets. Also sommersault expert. [Daw#123;MUM#69] Bobo, J. B. [christened with initials only] (Texarkana, Texas: 11 Feb 1910-12 Sep 1996) This American's unusual name was legitimately come by, being his French immigrant great-grandfather's legal contraction of Beaubeaux to accommodate his new neighbors. Inspired by seeing Eugene Laurant on the Chatauqua circuit, Taught first tricks at age c14 by Ed Reno, Eugene Laurant, & a travelling salesman. Studied the Tarbell Course in 1927. Pro close-up & kid-show stage magician since c1928, having given nearly 14,000 shows throughout the USA, but mainly in Texas & the central states. 1978 AMA Literary Fellowship. Lectured throughout the States, mostly at school assemblies. Wrote Watch This One! (1947, 124pp); the classic Modern Coin Magic (1952, 358pp; with 4 new chapters added in 1966, 519pp) with French tr as Le prestidigitation des pièces de monnaie (1956); & The Bobo Magic Show (1984, 188pp). Video (1987), video segment (1988). Articles in MUM, Legerdemain, & Genii. [LR8/86; Th; NJ#9; Wh2]

name: Bocado
bio: (Stuttgart, Germany: 16 Mar 1902-2 May 1958) Stage name of Theo Bozenhard. Second President of the East German Magic Circle (Magischen Zirkels der DDR). Died in Bad Elster. [Roh]

name: Boccal le Bergamasque
bio: (Bergamo, Italy: fl.1510s) Pro in Italy in 1517. Pet effects: Cups & Balls, swallowing wine & spewing out dry flour, producing insects from a spectator's nose, etc. Boccal is the earliest magician known to have performed on shipboard (on the Adriatic Sea). [Ch;Dif]

name: Boccani, Fritz
bio: (Zeitz, Germany: 6 Jan 1904- ) Stage name of Fritz Bock. Son of Paul Bock (a nephew of F.W. Ufer) from whom he learned as assistant at age 11. Pro in Zeitz. Toured Frankfurt, Stettin, Karlsruhe, & nearby cities with a full-evening magic show. Later assisted by his son Manfred Boccani (born 3 Oct 1934). [Roh]

name: Bodie, Albert Edward
bio: (Macduff, Scotland: c1889-1915) Learned assisting father Walford Bodie. Pro illusionist.

name: Bodie, Dr Walford
bio: (Macduff, Scotland: 11 Jun 1869-19 Oct 1939) Stage name of Samuel Murphy Brodie. As a child taught himself magic & vent. Pro vent & magician-showman since 1890s. First played London in 1903. Wrote The Bodie Book (1905; repr 1907, 193pp) & Stage Stories (1909, 208pp). His sister-in-law, Mary Henry Walford, worked as "Mystic Marie". [Jay;Daw;Le]

name: Bodinei, George
bio: (German East Africa: fl.1910s-20s) A black African. Served in German Army in East Africa in WW I, gaining rank of lieutenant. Moved to North Africa, becoming a pro magician by 1919 as "Prince Ali Raji", billed as "Oriental Magic, African Magician".

name: Bodley, Rev. Donald E. "Don
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Minister. Amateur gospel magician. Wrote Lessons in Scripture (25pp) & More Lessons in Scripture (30pp). Trick in Tops.

name: Boehlke, Richard
bio: (German-American: 5 [or 6] Oct 1874-15 Sep 1923) Ex acrobat & gymnast. Pro illusionist as "Herr Bolke". Pet effect: Creo = Vampire.

name: Bofeys, Professor
bio: (England: 1920s-50s) A founding member of the IBM British Ring in 1928. Hosted the first British Ring convention in 1931 at his home in Cheltenham.

name: Bohlen, Arno von
bio: See: Bolek, Heinz

name: Bohlen, Henry
bio: (Germany: 1907-) Moved to USA in 1926. Semi-pro as "Bohleno". Wrote Bohleno's Five Original Performance-Proven Mysteries (London: 1947, 14pp). Invented Handkerchief and Rope Penetration (by 1941) & Top Start, which won the 1949 SAM Convention  $ 1^{st} $ prize. [St]

name: Bohleno
bio: See: Bohlen, Henry

name: Böhm, Willy
bio: (Plauen, Germany: 22 Sep 1869-) Son of "Gustav Agoston". Circus magician c1882. Later became a musical clown.

name: Boiteau, Paul
bio: (France: fl.1850s) Wrote Les cartes à jour et la cartomancie (1854; reprint 1859, as by "d'Ambly").

name: Bolek, Heinz
bio: (Germany: 4 May 1912-) Pro illusionist (including circus) as "Arno von Bohlen". With assistant Rita took 1967 FISM 2nd prize in grand illusion. [Nad;Al]

name: Bolen
bio: See: Airaksinen, Jorma

name: Boles, Don
bio: (USA: c1930-3 Jul 2001) Pro, long with carnivals. As "Rex Dane" he also did a mindreading act (with wife Jackie). Retired from magic as a piano tuner in Atlanta, Georgia, where he died. Wrote Midway Magic (1963, 51pp), The Midway Showman (1967), The Modern Wizard's Manual (1970), etc.

name: Bolke, Herr
bio: See: Boehlke, Richard

name: Bologna, Pietro
bio: (Italy: fl.1790s-1800s) Minor pro magician & actor in England. In 1800 he bought Haddock's automata that he and his 3 sons then exhibited for many years. At Xmas 1806 he played Pantaloon in the hugely successful Mother Goose pantomime at London's Covent Garden theater. [Cl;Fr]

name: Bolz, Fred
bio: (Germany?: 26 Feb 1933-) Pro comedy magician in Germany. Had "Fred Bolz Zaubertheater" in Bonn. 1975 MZvD 2nd prize in comedy magic; 1984 MZvD 3rd prize in comedy magic. [Nad]

name: Bongo, Ali, MIMC
bio: (Bangalore, India: 8 Dec 1929-8 March 2009) Stage name of William Oliver Wallace, of Scots-Irish parents. Raised in England. Marketed 1st invention at age 16. Co-founded Medway Magical Society 1947. In London worked at the Unique Magic Studio 1954-56, the Chavel Magic Corner 1956-60, & managed Hamley's Magic Studio 1960-64. IBM British Ring Shield 1964. Developed his "Shriek of Araby" act in early 1960s. Full-time pro comedy magic since 1964. 1972 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" award. 1975 AMA Best Lecturer. British Ring Past President. Advisor for TV series of David Nixon 1970-78 & Paul Daniels 1979-present, plus other theatrical shows. 1991 David Berglas Award. 1993 AMA Masters Fellowship. Wrote The Bongo Book (1966, 64pp), Be A Magician (1979), & Ali Bongo's Book of Magic (1980). 1980 AMA Creative Fellowship. Tricks in Abra & Genii. [Win;Genii11/66;Mag;La2;Wh]

name: Bonheur, Fortuné
bio: (Paris, France: 1 Jun 1886-1951) Jew. Son of Isidore Bonheur. Pro magician 1902-14. [Dif]

name: Bonheur, Isidore
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 5 Dec 1839-29 Jan 1890) Jew. Pro stage hypnotist & second-sight act since 1857 with his brother Ferdinand until 1873 when the latter was replaced by Raynaly and later by De Thorcey. Wrote (with brother Ferdinand) Manuel de magnétisme (1865). Father of Fortuné Bonheur.

name: Bonney, Dr T. C. "Doc", DDS
bio: (Aberdeen, South Dakota: 15 Feb 1882-) Dentist. Amateur magician. Learned magic at age 12. Articles in Sphinx, etc. [Dor]

name: Bontjes, J. Gary
bio: (Peoria, Illinois: 12 Dec 1935-6 May 1985) Realtor. Amateur magician. Collector of magic lecture notes (world's largest) & magic books. Wrote A Checklist of Magic Lecture Notes (1962) & 3 others. Contributed to Magic Cauldron. SAM President 1971-72. SAM Hall of Fame. "Boomskie" NOTE: Stage name of a succession of assistants for the Herrmanns' shows, including a black with Alexander Herrmann and Adelaide Herrmann and M.H. Everett as assistant to Leon Herrmann. Booth, Rev Dr John [William Nicholls], LittD, MIMC (Meadville, Pennsylvania: 7 Aug 1912 - November 11, 2009) Inspired at age 10 by a magic set. Learned at age 14 from W.J. Armstrong ("Armah"). Semi-pro at 15 (in 1927). Edited-published Canada's second (after W.G. Edwards's Edwards Monthly) magic magazine, The Canadian Magician's Digest (1929, 3 issues). Organized the first Canadian magic convention (Hamilton, Ontario) 18-19 Apr 1931. Pro 1934-Mar 1940, as a prominent society, nightclub, & hotel magician. In 1938 also worked alternate venues as "Jancini". 1937 Sphinx Award. Then an ordained Unitarian minister (1942 until retired in 1975). Part-time pro celebrity platform lecturer 1943-58, touring world-wide. 1977 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1983 SAM Hall of Fame. 1985 & 1988 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award; 1987 Magic Circle "John Nevil Maskelyne Prize". Invented Pull-Down (late 1920s) & Booth's Baffling Block (1928). Wrote over 400 articles (since 1928) for Linking Ring, Sphinx, Genii, & Magicol. Also (since 1930) 12 books on magic: Super Magical Miracles (1930), Forging Ahead in Magic (1939, 154pp; reprinted 1944), Marvels of Mystery (1941, 146pp; reprinted 1946 & 1963), The John Booth Classics (1975, 252pp, being a reprint of the two previous books plus "A Conjurer's Reminiscences"), Psychic Paradoxes (1984, 243pp), Wonders of Magic (1986, 289pp), Dramatic Magic (1988, 243pp), Creative World of Conjuring (1990, 268pp), Conjurians' Discoveries (1992, 274pp), The Fine Art of Hocus Pocus (1996, 287pp), Extending Magic Beyond Credibility (2001, 272pp), Magical Mentalism. Also wrote books on religion, travel, & genealogy as "John Nicholls Booth": Fabulous Destinations, The Quest for Preaching Power, The Story of the Second Church in Boston. An index of his 1963-88 Linking Ring articles is Ben Robinson & Amy Janello (editor), Memoirs of a Magician's Ghost (1988, 243pp). [Genii4/81;Bo#219,#320;Th;Mag;WWA1970-82;Ho;Wh]

name: Booth, Walter R.
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1910s) Pro magician who by 1898 became a pioneer director in cinema, heading Robert Paul's film-making productions until 1906 when he went with The Charles Urban Trading Co where he made Britain's first animated cartoon, The Hand of the Artist (1906). [Bar;Bo2] "Boraucks, Borris" [misspelling] SEE: Borsuks, Boris

name: Bordner, Greg [his full name]
bio: (Three Rivers, outside Colon, Michigan: 24 Dec 1951- ) Son of Recil Bordner. Pro dealer in Abbott's since childhood (except for 4 years at Michigan State U). Owner of Abbott's since 1981. Pet effect: Wunderbar. [Wh]

name: Bordner, Recil J. [pronounced REE-sil]
bio: (Edon, Ohio: 20 Sep 1910-8 Sep 1981) Did semi-pro magic in home town while working on the family farm. Taking an advance on his inheritance, he became a magic dealer, joining Percy Abbott as junior partner at Abbott's in early 1934. Co-invented (with U.F. Grant) Amputation (by 1940). Sole owner of Abbott's since 1959. Bought the Petrie-Lewis Mfg. Co. in 1968. On his death in 1981 Abbott's passed to his son Greg.

name: Borelly, [Adolphe-Casimir]
bio: (Paris, France: 4 May 1824-7 Dec 1901) Pro card magician. Toured widely until settled in Vichy. [Dif]

name: Boretti
bio: (Darmstadt?, Germany: 14 Dec 1948-) Stage name of Erich Hammann. 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in kids magic. Dealer ("Magic by Boretti") in Neustadt, Germany. Tricks in Magie. [Nad]

name: Bornstein, [Isaak Meyer] "Mike
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 28 Apr 1921-20 Jan 2005) Raised in the Bronx. Inspired around age 9 seeing a street magician pitching a 25¢ packet of magic. Pro performer (as "Kolma") with a pseudo-Chinese act in the 1940s, using one of the few masks made by Jeanne Vernon. Invented Penny Ante (by 1948) & Floating Dollar Bill (1977). Mail-order dealer-manufacturer in Manhattan from late 1970s to 2003 when sold to Meir Yedid. Lecturer. Authored (some written by Walt Lees) 7 booklets, including Latest Money Magic (1988) & Mike Bornstein's Original Commercial Routines with Okito & Boston Boxes (1990, 44pp). Articles in MUM, Apocalypse, & Backstage. TV bits. Videos (1989, etc). [MUM2/92;Wh2]

name: Borosé, Hans [pronounced bow-ROW-sah]
bio: (Austria: 19 Feb 1894-Feb 1972) Austrian Jew. Stage name of Hans Spitzer. Pro manip. Student of Arcano. Fled to England in 1938, working in ENSA in North Africa in WW II. Returned to Vienna in 1945. Wrote Wiener magisches Skriptum (1951, 182pp). [Al;Dam]

name: Borosko
bio: (Saint-Imier, Switzerland: 25 Jul 1880-3 Oct 1967) Stage name of Jules Sautebin. Originally a watchmaker, turned pro stage magician. Operated a travelling show since the 1920s. 1927 Concours Magicus (Paris) 1st prize. 1947 Paris 1st prize for invention. Retired in 1957. Maker of fine mechanical props. [Dif]

name: Borra, Boris
bio: (Jagodina, Serbia, Yugoslavia: 26 Apr 1921-Schillingsdorf: 10 Sep 1998) Stage name of Borislav Milojković since 1942. Son of a merchant. Learned some tricks at age 14. Pro circus manip since 1937 to pick-pocket act as "The Thief of Baghdad". Moved to Austria in 1947 where he became a citizen next year. Played the Coliseu in Lisbon in 1951. Star of the Bertram Mills Circus in Britain in 1950s. Many TV bits. Father of Charly Borra. Middle brother of Borra II & Borra III. [Ran;Win;Dif;Fi;Bo2;Cam]

name: Borra, Charly
bio: (Austria, Vienna: 5 May 1945- ) Stage name of Karl Milojković. Son of "Boris Borra" (by latter's Czech wife, née Kludsky), who taught him his pickpocket act. Billed as "Prince of Pickpockets". Pro in Austria. Worked in Circus Busch-Roland.

name: Borra II
bio: (Yugoslavia: 1918-) Stage name of Dragisa Milojković. Older brother of Boris Borra & Borra III. Pro pickpocket act.

name: Borra III
bio: (Yugoslavia: 1923-) Stage name of Vojislav Milojković. Younger brother of Boris Borra & Borra II. Pro pickpocket act.

name: Börsch, Jörgen
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 18 Jan 1941- ) Learned in 1950 from older brother Peter. Public relations consultant & now circus producer-manager-director (Cirkus Cirkus Jörgen Börsch) in Copenhagen plus Holiday on Ice, Hell-Drivers, etc. Amateur magician, performing publicly since 1952. Aka "Jorgano" & "Jorgan" until 1970s. Pet effects: Die Box & Rice Bowls. Collector. Edited Magi (Denmark) ..... Contributor to Magikeren (Norway) & Trylle-Journalen (Denmark). [Genii.....;Wh6]

name: Börsch, Peter
bio: (Denmark: fl.1950s-90s) Partner in clothing store in Hillerød. Collector of magic & circus. Elder brother & teacher of Jørgen Börsch. [Daw2]

name: Borsuks, Boris
bio: (Lithuania: fl.1950s-60s) Lived in Western Europe. Pro pickpocket in circus & variety theaters. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1955. [Al;Cam] NOTE: Name misspelled "Borris Boraucks" &, I suspect, he is the same man as Boris Borra.

name: Boscar, Professeur
bio: See: Ceillier, Rémi

name: Boscart, Sthey
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro with cigarette manip and kid-show acts in New York & New England. Also ran a Ghost Show in 1930s-40s as both "Boscart" & "Dr. Bosco". [Walk2]

name: Bosco
bio:
Bernardi Blumenfeld, Professor Boscart, Stihey Elliott, Dr James W. NOTE: The 8 successive comedian "Boscos" with the "Le Roy-Talma-Bosco" troupe were Leon Bosco (since 1904), Mac Laube, Daly, Wilmot Hastings (to 1913), Dr James W. Elliott (1913-17, the only pro magician in the group), Milton Barley, Thomas Mullens, and Gene Le Roy (Servais Le Roy's nephew). Charlie Chaplin played "Prof. Bosco" in his 1928 silent movie The Circus.

[See also: Bellachini Jr]

name: Bosco, Dr.
bio: See: Boscart, Sthey

name: Bosco, Signor Alfred
bio: (Italy?: fl.1850s) Pro magus-vent. Played the Strand Theatre in London in 1857 & the Theatre Royal in Birmingham c1860. Clarke speculates that he may be the same as Eugene Bosco. On the contrary, I suspect he was the Bosco that the Era Almanac reported having died in Britain 22 Apr 1906 at age 72. [CI]

name: Bosco, Bart
bio: See: Rogers, Mike

name: Bosco, [Giovanni] Bartolomeo
bio: (Turin, Piedmont, Italy: 3 Jan 1793-7 Mar 1863) While serving with Napoleon's army in Russia in 1812 (at age 19) he was wounded & taken prisoner, practicing sleight-of-hand while imprisoned in Tobolsk. Returned to Italy in 1814. Pro since 1823. A master of the Cups-&-Balls for which he invented the Bosco Palm and the double pocket (by 1833). Toured & lived in Russia 1823-1828 when he moved to Austria. Played Hungary (1829), Germany (1830), Denmark (1830), Germany (1831-32), France (1833), Egypt (1839), Turkey (1840), Russia (1842), Prague (1845), London (1851), France (1851-52). Died popverty-stricken in Dresden. Father of Eugene Bosco. Ghosted autobio is Der alte Bosco und seine Kunst (c1860, 40pp). See John Carter, Bosco als Kartenkünstler (Hamburg: 1848, 78pp). [Dif; Sil; Pr; Ch; Hou]

name: Bosco, Eugene
bio: (Lombardy, Italy: 1823-1891) Stage name of Carlo Bosco since 1852, illegitimate and only son of Bartolomeo Bosco. Pro by 1852. Toured Europe, particularly Italy, with his assistant-son Italo Bosco. Moved to England c1855, learning English and performing there with some distinction until 1857 when an exploding pistol shattered his hand. Died in Hungary in poverty. Invented the Sand Frame. Father-in-law of Zanarelli. [Fr;Pr;Dif;Hou]

name: Bosco, Giovanni [Melchior]
bio: (Becchi, near Turin, Piedmont, Italy: 16 Aug 1815-31 [sic] Jan 1888) Natural son of Margarida Occhiena & Francisco Luis Bosco who died when Giovanni was 2 years old. Successively a shepherd, apprentice tailor, blacksmith, & confectioner—all the while working as a street magician. In 1841 at age 20 entered a seminary & was soon ordained a priest. He was, I suppose, the first "gospel magician". Founded the Society of St. Francis of Sales (the Salesian monks) in 1857. Beatified in 1929 & cannonized in 1934. His feast day is January 31st. At the initiative of Robert "Tréborix" Olivaux, the Roman Catholic Church made Saint Giovanni Bosco the official patron saint of magicians. Bios are Henri Ghéon, Secret of St. John Bosco (1936) & Lancelot C. Sheppard, Portrait of a Parish Priest (1958). [Cam;Dif]

name: Bosco, Leon
bio: (Britain?: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro comedian in British music halls. Recruited in England in 1904 by star vaudeville illusionist Servais Le Roy to act as the fat buffoon-magician in his popular Le Roy-Talma-Bosco team. He was replaced (by 1913) by 7 other successive "Boscos". [Pr; Magical World 10/13]

name: Bosco, St. Jean
bio: See: Blumenfeld, Professor
