name: Bosco-Olms
bio: See: Olms, John

name: Bossi, Vanni
bio: (Italy: -5 Dec 2008) Expert close-up coin man. Tricks in MUM (3/96).

name: Boston, Dr Arnold "Doc", DDS
bio: (New York City, New York: 27 Jan c1920-) Inspired at age 10 seeing Blackstone show. Taught in 1940s by Al Flosso. Dentist in Secaucus, New Jersey (his patients included Amadeo, Roy Benson, Dunninger, Al Flosso, Jack Flosso, Frakson, Bobby Reynolds, John Scarne, & Lou Tannen). Semi-pro sleight-of-hand expert (mainly card magic) in 1940s-50s in the New York inner circle & semi-pro two-person mental act with daughter Michele. Disqualified at 1988 FISM card competition for using a "stooge" when, in fact, he had simply fooled the judges. With assistant-wife Betty London recently (late 1980s) finished extended engagement at the Atlantis Hotel in Atlantic City. Invented Mental Giant (marketed by Tannen's in 1955), Evolution of a Knot (published in Hugard's Magic Monthly), & the Telematic Prediction box (1957). Contributor to Tarbell Course. NOTE: Did not invent the Boston Box. [Wh2]

name: Boston, George L.
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 6 Jan 1905-14 Mar 1975) Aka "George L. Merlin". Inspired in 1915 at age 10 seeing Thurston show & immediately learned from books & then buying tricks from Roterberg's shop. Semi-pro debut in 1916. Pro stage magician as assistant to Duval Brothers 1924-28, assistant to Birch 1928, assistant to Howard Thurston 1928, stage manager to Harry Thurston 1931-32, assistant to Carter 1933, assistant to Mel-Roy, assistant to Virgil 1937, chief assistant to Will Rock 1938, assistant to Nicola 1938. A manic-depressive, he was fired by all of the above. Improved after moving to Los Angeles. Assistant to Blackstone on 1943 USO tour. In 1944 switched to mentalism. Associated with Jim Sherman's shop in Chicago in 1945. Worked in Abbott's LA shop since 1948. On original AMA Board of Directors 1962-64. His good autobio (written with Robert Parrish) is Inside Magic (1947, 224pp). Wrote Super Quiz (25pp). NOTE: Did not invent the Boston Box as assumed by Bobo & copied by Waters.

name: Bosworth, Harry
bio: (Hillsborough Barracks, Sheffield, England: 1902-c1980) Great grandson of J.H. Anderson & grandson of A.M. Holmes. Debut at age 9. Pro. Assistant to Houdini until 1926. Dealer in Nottingham with B.B.C. (1946, 2 issues) as house organ. [Bay]

name: Böttcher, Eckhard
bio: (Germany: 28 Nov 1942-) Performed as "E. Böttcher & Uta". Pro dealer since 1970s, originally with Zauberzentrale München (Munich), now with Zauber-Butike in Puchheim. 1981 MZvD 3rd prize for invention. Popular lecturer. Wrote 50 magic booklets. [Nad]

name: Botelho, Francisco
bio: (Pico da Pedra, Portugal: 14 Feb 1962-) Vent & magician since debut in 1975. Aka "Chico Botelho" & "Frabot". Toured Canada & USA in 1978. Invented Zig-Zag Dove, publishing it in Apr 1980 in Linking Ring. Wrote Ventriloquarte (1979, 44pp) and Ideias Mágicas (1979, 92pp). Tricks in Quatro Ases & Linking Ring. [Cam]

name: Bothwell-Maye, E. G.
bio: (Douglas, Isle of Man, Great Britain: 16 Oct 1885- ) Aka "Dorian". Semi-pro drawing-room & platform work. Inventor & improver. Trick (by "Dorian") in Magic Wand (1923). [Go2]

name: Bouché, Albert
bio: (Belgium: 1877-1934) Conjuror & collector of automata. Aka "Aboukir". Taught Dalton who got his collection (thence sold to L. Tummers & then Klingsor).

name: Boudreau, Leo H[arry] "Lou
bio: (Woonsocket, Rhode Island: 31 Aug 1942-) Interested since 1950 when played role of a magician in school play. Electrical engineer & patent agent in Alexandria, Virginia. Semi-promental magic since 1960, aka "Kronin" 1963-79. Wrote Quintaces (1983). Psimatrika (1986), Spirited Pasteboards (1987, 233pp), & Skullduggery (1989). [Wh2]

name: Boulevard, M.
bio: (France?: fl.1780s-90s) Minor pro street magician. Won a conjuring contest against Highman Palatine at Bush Tavern in Bristol, England, in 1788. Continued to perform at English fairs and tavern rooms until as late as 1795. [CI]

name: Bourset, A[dolf]
bio: See: Lüders, C. E.

name: Bourdin, Serge
bio: (Paris, France: 26 Jan 1911-1989) Photographer in Paris. Amateur stage magician as "Truc & Cie". AFAP Master Magician. Edited Annaure des Magiciens 1968-1969 & Annaure des Magiciens 1975-1976. NOTE: Not Maurice Féaudiérre who wrote on circus as "Serge". [Bou2]

name: Bourguignon, Jacques
bio: (France: fl.1750s-60s). Stage name of Jacques-Damien Angelo. Pro. Had a booth at the St.-Germain fair in Paris in 1756 & 1760.

name: Bouthoux de Lorget
bio: (France: fl.1780s) Pro. Performed in Paris in 1786, giving 2½-hour shows. [CI]

name: Bouton, Pete
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: -1 May 1968) Stage name of Peter Boughton. Younger brother of "Blackstone" with whom he worked since 1910 as illusion builder, principal assistant, & stage manager. [Pr]

name: Bowen, Dr Owen Henry, MD, MIMC
bio: (Criccieth, Caernarvonshire, Wales: 1885-14 Jan 1957) Physician. Amateur drawing-room magician. [Go;Go2]

name: Bowman, Bill
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Amateur magician in Seattle. Invented Clipped in 1940s & published it in Jun 1954, creating the dollar bill & paper clip craze that year

name: Bowsher, Alex
bio: (London, England: 26 Sep 1905-) Semi-pro comedy magician. [Go2]

name: Bowyer, Tom
bio: (Wolverhampton, England: 15 Jun 1902-25 Nov 1949) Moved to Canada, performing as "T. Van Russell". A movie flac. Semi-pro sleights & small magic. Invented Simplex Enlarging Thimble (by 1932), Repeat Bill Trick (by 1936), & the Conrary Match Box (by 1942). Reviewer for Linking Ring. Died in Toronto. [Th;Bo3]

name: Boxley, Cas [C.]
bio: (Rushville, Indiana: 3 Apr 1919- ) Moved at age 3 to Oakland, California, where he was raised. Inspired at age 10 seeing Thurston show. Learned from public library books & members of the Oakland Magic Circle. Pro stage magic since 1937, beginning in San Francisco night clubs. In 1938 joined comedian-MC Eddie Cochrane's vaude show touring Northwest & Midwest. In 1940 or 41 taught magic to Cochrane who went out on own. In 1949 met & married Marie & as "Boxley & Marie, the Miracle Masters" they played hotels, night clubs, & TV. Then toured a 2-hour show thru 39 states 1958-62. A skilled craftsman, Boxley made & decorated most of his props. Divorced Marie (who died 19 Jun 1992) after 25 years of marriage. Pet effects: Broom Suspension, Sympathetic Silks, Rising Cards, & earlier Creo. Retired in 1970s. [NT12/88; Mag; Tay; Wh2]

name: Boyar [Jr], [Vincent] "Vynn
bio: (Beacon Falls, Connecticut: 21 Sep 1913-27 Jan 1989) Electronics engineer. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand & club shows in Connecticut in 1940s. Edited the 1949 M-U-M Bulletin trial issue, Aladdin's Lamp 1954-57 (38 issues), & National News Letter 1966-67. SAM President 1967-68. SAM Hall of Fame. Tricks in Phoenix & HMM. NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Boyer". [Th]

name: Boyer, Vynn" [misspelling]
bio: See: Boyar, Vynn

name: Boz, Signor
bio: See: Weston, Arthur

name: Brachetti, Arturo
bio: (Turin, Italy: 13 Oct 1964-) Quick-change artist. A star of the Flic-Flac review that toured the Continent & the London "Y" show. Guest star & presenter of Fisher's "The Best of Magic" TV show, 1990. [Fi2]

name: Bradshaw, William
bio: (England: fl.1690s) Minor pro. Worked Bartholomew Fair in 1690 with sleight-of-hand and knife swallowing. Brahams, Anthony [William Henry], MIMC (London, England: 24 Mar 1932-) Inspired by father's tales of magicians he had seen. Learned at age 10. Chartered accountant & sales promotion director. Semi-pro close-up since age 21, one of its early pioneers in London. [Wh2]

name: Brahma, Pierre
bio: (Marseille, France: 25 Feb 1933-) Stage name of Pierre Bramma. Learned from a magic book. Protégé of pro Alain Noël in 1956. 1958 FISM 3rd prize in manip; FISM Grand Prix 1964 (shared with Mr. Cox) & 1976; 1988 British Ring 3rd prize for manip. Pro stage magic with a jewel act & with large coins. AFAP Master Magician. Played Casino Estoril in Portugal 1965, 1978, 1981. Autobio is La malle des Indes (1979). Tricks in Magicus-Journal. [Win;Dif;Bou2]

name: Branch, Justin
bio: (England: fl.1970s-80s) Card magician. Wrote Cards in Confidence (nd, 2 vols, 304pp), Multiple Assemblies, & Progressive Card Magic.

name: Brandon
bio:
(Britain: fl.1520s-30s) Pro magician. Principal "Juggler" (magician) of King Henry VIII from 1521 to 1535. [CI]

[See also: Benesch, Johann]

name: Brandon, Arthur “Milo
bio: (Ohio, USA: c1916-1998) Began as "Milo the Magician" in c1949 as Dave Lustig's protégé until 1950 when went on own. Worked in a Corpus Christi, Texas, magic shop in 1951. TV bit in 1951. Then teamed with Roger Coker as "Milo & Roger", pro comedy & straight magician-illusionists who played major variety theaters & nightclubs of the world (including Vancouver in 1961). They moved to Thailand in 1976. They retired in 1995 following their performance in Monte Carlo. Roger died in 1997. Wrote Milo & Roger: A Magical Life (1999, 418pp). [Tay;Fi2;HMM2/50,7/50,4/51,11/51]

name: Brandon, Don
bio: See: Estes, Donald

name: Brandon, James
bio: (USA: c1965-) Pro illusionist. Has performed in Europe and Las Vegas. 1988 Desert Magic Seminar 1st Prize. 1988 Japan Magic Olympics 3rd Prize.

name: Brandon, Joan
bio: (USA: c1920-) 10-piece orchestra leader and pro magicienne. With bar act 1937-42. Toured Europe 1938-39. First female magician to appear on TV (BBC in London, Paris, & NBC in New York, all in 1939). Thence stage magic & hypnotism in 1940s to early 1950s. Played the NY Palace in 1950, 1951, 1952, & 1953. [Th;Tay]

name: Braniek, Karl
bio: (Poland?: 23 Nov 1940-) Magician in Poland, aka "Carolus Morgano". [Nad]

name: Branson, Major L[ionel] H[ugh], MIMC
bio: (England: 1879-18 Apr 1946) Aka "Lionel Cardac" as stage name & (according to his son Tony) "Elbiquet" as pen name. Learned in 1887 from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Student of Charles Bertram (ca.1889). Amateur sleight-of-hand magus, except in 1913 when as "Lionel Cardac" he played London's Palace of Varieties for 3 weeks & making a 25-minutes conjuring demo film for the Hepworth Company. British Army officer, including two secret intelligence assignments in China in 1904. Also in WW I as Chief Field Censor did some more secret intelligence work. Notable practical joker. His two younger sons, Tony (b.1909) & Cyril (b.1918), both became amateur magicians. Wrote Indian Conjuring (1922, 103pp) & 2 other books as "Elbiquet": A Text-Book of Magic [1913, 200pp] & Supplementary Magic [1917]. Autobio is L.H. Branson, A Lifetime of Deception (1953, 209pp). [Le]

name: Branson, [Anthony] "Tony", MIMC
bio: (England: c1909-1989) Son of L.H. Branson who taught him magic as a child. Architect in Sevenoaks, Kent. Amateur magician. In ENSA in WW II. Later a childrens magician. TV bits.

name: Braude, Dr Ben[jamin] B., DDS
bio: (USA: c1902-11 [sic] Sep 1992) Dentist in New York City. Amateur magician specializing in card tricks. Autograph collector. Ghosted Scarne on Card Tricks (1950). Wrote Tricks and Treats (1971, 37pp). Tricks in HMM. Braue, Fred[erick George] "Fritz" [pronounced BROW-ee] (Alameda County, California: c1906-3 Jul 1962) Newspaperman in Oakland. Semi-promagician since 1919, specialized in card magic sleights of which he was a master & an innovator. Invented rear palm (in 1935), Braue Addition (1945), Braue Reversal, Homing Card (1948), etc. Died of lung cancer. Left his magical writings & memorabilia to Lloyd Jones. Wrote The Fred Braue Notebooks in some 1,000 pages during a 30-year period (published 1985-1997 in progress) & wrote (all with Jean Hugard) Expert Card Technique (1940, 448pp; 2nd ed 1944; 3rd ed 1950, 474pp; with French ed in 1955), Miracle Methods (4 vols, 1941-1943, 32+24+32+22pp; repr 1974), The Invisible Pass (1946, 29pp), Fred Braue on False Deals (1977), Showstoppers with Cards (1948, 16pp), The Royal Road to Card Magic (1st Brit ed 1948; 1st US ed 1948, 292pp; repr 1954, 302pp), etc, all key works. Edited Hugard's Magic Monthly 1959-62. NOTE: Often mispronounced BROW-ay &, accordingly, twice misspelled "Braue". Trick in Genii. [Wh91;Th]

name: Braun, Anastazy
bio: (Poland: -1956) Pro manipulator, illusionist, & acrobat in Polish circus. [Mec]

name: Braun, Franz [pronounced BROWN]
bio: (Hennef-Sieg, near Cologne, Germany: 14 Apr 1923-) Learned age 12-14 from tricks from Bartl's shop. In life insurance business. Amateur card magician & collector. Pet effects: mathematical tricks. 1962 MZvD Karl Schröder-Gedächnis-Ring recipient. Edited Magie 1960-65. Editor-publisher of journals The Playing Card & Die Zauberkugel Jan-Dec 1967 (4 issues). Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, & Magisches Magazin. [Magische Welt #2/82; Wit; Wh2]

name: Braun, John, MIMC [pronounced BROWN]
bio: (Hamilton, Butler County, Ohio: 4 Sep 1896-22 Jun 1988) Mechanical engineer with Proctor & Gamble until retired in 1961. A Shriner. Inspired & learned magic around age 12 by father showing a mathematical trick. Inspired again in 1912 seeing Germain. Debut in 1920. Semi-pro. Founding member Queen City Mystics (Cincinnati) 1922. IBM President 1946-47. IBM Medallion of Honor. Edited The Linking Ring 1942-48, 1965-67. 1979 AMA Literary Fellowship. Book editor & wrote many articles. Wrote Subtle Problems You Will Do (1937, 75pp, with Stewart Judah) & Keith Clark's Rope Royale (1942, 14pp). [Bo#189;Th;SAM;WWM]

name: Braund, George R., MIMC
bio: (Loughborough, England: 17 Jun 1903-18 Jul 1961) Comedy magus. Semi-pro to pro private party high society close-up. Self-billed as “The Biggest Thing in Magic”. [Go2;HMM1/52;Wat]

name: Braunmüller, Rudolf
bio: (London, England: 20 Jan 1935-München: 2 Apr 2001) In 1939 moved from London to Switzerland & then to Germany. Pro. Edited Intermagic 1973-1996-?. Dealer in Munich, Germany, co-founding (with G. Puchinger) Zauberzentrale München in 1975-1981. Thence a new & second-hand dealer (Zauberstudio Braunmüller) in Münich. Also a collector, magic tour director, & translator of US & British magic books. 1984 MZvD Writer of the Year. Died of cancer.

name: Brauns, Dr Fred, MD, PhD
bio: (Germany: 1885-1963) Stage name of Ferdinand Bruns. Pro lightning calculator & memory expert.

name: Bravour, Fred
bio: (Basel, Switzerland: 3 Jan 1950-) Stage name of Fred Lüscher. Learned at age 4 from books. Promental & stage magician since 1971. [Wh2]

name: Bray, Diane
bio: (Durham, North Carolina: 10 Dec 1952- ) Pro, having learned in 1974-c77 as on-stage assistant to Jack Adams while they were students at Florida International U. Since 1981 she has been partner to Max Howard whom she married in 1986. In their historical "Professor Gus Rich" act she plays his assistant, "Mr Jim Bailey". [Wh2]

name: Brazil Jack
bio: (Bergen, Norway: 28 Sep 1871-7 Nov 1952) Stage name of Carlo Max Alexander Rhodin. Eldest son of "Max Alexander" (by his first wife, "Rhombello", a Brazilian). Pro circus manager and magician, shadowist, musician, cowboy rope & pistol tricks. Started own circus in 1902. Older half-brother of Max von Rhodin. [Dif]

name: Brazil, Michael "Mike
bio: (Jennings, Missouri, 1960s-70s) Pro. In 1969 began making sets of Linking Rings & Dove Pans as a mail-order dealer-manufacturer of metal apparatus. In 1972 expanded & incorporated as Rings 'N Things Magic Company in St. Louis, Missouri. Dropped his company and magic in 1980 & selling to his partner Sandy Byrne. [LR8/04]

name: Brearley, John, MIMC
bio: (Britain: -25 Jan 1971) Invented the Stamp Album trick in 1926. Wrote ConJUNIORing (1945, 92pp).

name: Breda, Vera
bio: (India: fl.1810s-1820s) Hindu. Pro, billed as from Madras. He toured Britain from 1818 until 1826 or 1827. Pet effects: burnt-&-restored thread, egg bag, & shooting birds off an artificial tree balanced on his forehead. [CI]

name: Breese, Martin [Ranicar]
bio: (London, England: 13 Sep 1937 – 23 Feb 2012) Inspired in 1946 seeing Harbin & Jasper Maskelyne. Pro publisher-dealer (Martin Breese Ltd, later Martin Breese International) in London since 1978, with over 60 book titles & 100 audio cassettes on "Magiccassette" label. Also publishes Spell-Binder (1981-84), The Sorcerer (1983-present), novels, biographies, etc. Proprietor of The Magic Lounge in London for 5 years. Editor of Sorcerer 1983-present. Wrote The Harbin Book (1983) & The Magic of AI Koran (1983). [Wh2]

name: Brema, Carl
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 2 Feb 1864-26 Feb 1942) Stage name of Karl Friedrich Brehmer. Moved to USA in 1868. Inspired at age 12 as instant stooge to travelling magician Robert Nickle. Pro debut in 1886. Did comedy magic as “Herr von Blitzen” before WW I. Dealer in Philadelphia "Brema's Magic Shop" since 1892, then from 1919 as "Carl Brema & Son" until 1932 when he retired. Died in a mental institution. Inventor of Billiard Ball Box (in 1893), Brema Box (c1920), Ball thru Bolt; possibly Rattle Bars (in 1925), Ball and Tube (by 1926), Brema Nut=Spirit Nut (by 1927), and possibly Cubio & the 21 Cent Trick. Bio is Richard Buffum, The Brema Brasses (1981). [Dor]

name: Brema, William "Bill
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 4 Jul 1887-25 Nov 1949) Stage name of William Brehmer, only son of "Carl Brema" from whom he learned as stage assistant. Joined father's magic shop business in 1919 when it soon became "Carl Brema & Son," succeeding on Carl's retirement in 1932 and selling the business in 1934 to the Fildermans. Bill then worked as a brass prop maker for Percy Abbott in Colon, Michigan, and back in Philadelphia for Mike Kanter 1943-until his death from a heart attack. [Buf]

name: Bremer, Jan
bio: (Poland: 1861-1928) Pro illusionist & manipulator. Teacher of Remerbi. [Mec]

name: Brenda
bio: (Durham, North Carolina: 18 Oct 19) Grew up on farm in Morrisville, N. Carolina. Stage name of Brenda Payne, née Copeland. Learned Jack Payne Jr's family unicycle & juggling act c1968, touring with him as "The Saxons". Soon married him, moving to Sacramento, California, in 1970. Learned magic later that year from Bob Brown, doing an international tour almost every year since then as his principal partner billed as "Bob Brown & Brenda". Fills in with "The Saxons" act. Often on own in US & Canada with gambling demo or dove act, particularly at school shows. [MUM11/84;Wh]

name: Brengman, Gerrit
bio: (Bruges, Belgium: 1944-) Learned at age 13. Semi-pro comedy magician. Lived in Zaire for a time until returning to Belgium in 1972. Articles. [Xe]

name: Brenon, John
bio: (Ireland: fl.1780s). Pro. Moved to USA by 1787 when he performed in New York City. [Se]

name: Brenon, Mrs John
bio: (Ireland: fl.1780s). Pro sleight-of-hand. Moved to USA where in 1787 she became the first magicienne to perform there. [Se]

name: Brent, Lu
bio: (Camden, New Jersey: 24 Nov 1903- ) Of Russian-Polish parents. Born Boleslaw Jósef Lubrant, changed to Benjamin Joseph Lubrent. Aka "Lu-Brent". Also signed himself "B. Lu Brent". Inspired at age c15 seeing Horace Goldin show. US Army Signal Corps 1921-27. Semi-pro since 1927 & pro since 1930. Invented Cig-O-Test by 1932, the build-it-yourself Card Castle in 1945, Two Into Ones (folded $2 bill opens into two $1 bills) in 1948, the Diminishing Bills in 1950, & Bill to Matches in 1961. Wrote Novel Magic (1932; repr 1946, 43pp), Torn and Restored Magazine Cover (1939, 8pp; 2nd ed 1953, 9pp), Super Card Mysteries [1933], Five Star Card Effects (1943), Fifteen Star Card Effects (1956, 26pp), Totally Refreshing Ideas & Carefully Kept Secrets (1966, 38pp), & Lu Brent's Best Magic Tricks (2 vols, 1969, 1974, 42pp+45pp). Articles in Sphinx, Jinx, Tops, Phoenix, Ireland's YB:1952, Dope Sheet, Genii, Pallbearers, & Magigram. [Th;WWM]

name: Breslaw
bio: (England?: c1726-16 May 1803) Imitator of the original Philip Breslaw. Died in Liverpool. [Daw2]

name: Breslaw, Philip
bio: (Germany: 1726-10 Nov 1783) British-Jewish parents. Pro. Moved to England in 1760. Likely inventor of Clock Dial (1777). Inspired but did not write Breslaw's Last Legacy (1784). [Dam;Fr]

name: Bretma, B. "Bert" "Bertie
bio: (England: -25 Oct 1936) Stage name of Albert "Bert" Brown. Craftsman. Collaborated in Servais Le Roy's factory before WW I. With Stanley Norton as partner formed the Norton-Bretma Manufacturing Company 1919-1920 when bought out Norton to become the Bretma Manufacturing Company, which he sold to James Shannon in 1922. In early 1920s joined the Carmo troupe as stage manager. [Daw94]

name: Brewster, Sir David
bio: (Jedburgh, Scotland: 11 Dec 1781-10 Feb 1868) Physicist specialized in optics. Invented the kaleidoscope in 1816. Knighted 1832. Perfected the stereoscope 1849-50. Wrote Letters on Natural Magic (1832, 351pp) with French tr as Nouveau Manuel de magie naturelle et amusante (1839). Includes pages on such conjuring-related items as Phantasmagoria, optical illusions, ventriloquism, & Vaucanson's automaton Duck.

name: Briant, E[rnest] Leslie "Les
bio: (London, England: 3 Aug 1891-18 Oct 1965) Bank lawyer. Resident of Rosario near Buenos Aires since 1912. Semi-pro magician since 1920. Aka "Lafayette, the Argentine Wizard". South American reporter for The Sphinx. In 1938 co-founded the Circulo Mágico Argentino. [WWM; Bam, pp.128, 153,270-1]

name: Bridges, Dr Milton Arlanden, MD
bio: (New York City, NY: 20 May 1894-19 [or 9] Aug 1939) Inspired on 8th birthday by a box of tricks. Physician since 1919 in New York City. Amateur magician (as "Dr. Pontes"). Major collector of magic books. His collection of 6000 books & 200 magazines—most old & in fine condition—was bought in 1940 by H. Adrian Smith. Articles in Sphinx & Linking Ring. NOTE: Middle name often misspelled "Arlander". [Tops11/37;SAM;Go2;St]

name: Brieuc, Yann
bio: (France: 12 Sep 1963-) 1988 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic. Aka "Yannick Cabaret".

name: Briggs, J[ohn] Albert
bio: (Sheffield, England: 17 Nov 1884-4 Aug 1969) Magician in Sheffield since age 18. Edited The Conjurer there 1910-11. Moved to Australia in 1913 [sic]. Dealer in Alexandria, NSW, as Austral Magical Company 1920-33, thence under own name 1934-69. Pro performer as "Albert Russell" (1920), "Merbak" (1922 & 1938), "The Great Chandu" (1938), & "Rajah Singh" (1938). Founding member & 1st President of Australian Magic Circle 1923 & Australian Magicians' Club 1944. A notoriously contentious man. Edited Magic Mirror 1921, The Conjurer (Australia) 1922-38, Magic in Australia 1924-25 (4 issues), & Box and Dice 1946-53? (22+ issues). Wrote Stage Magic, Dinkum Magic (1928), Magical Revelations (1941), & Practical Magic (1946). Tricks in Magic (1910) & Linking Ring (Mar 1971 "Parade").

name: Brindamour, George W.
bio: (Cannon Falls, Michigan: 1870-31 Jul 1941) Stage name of George W. Brown since 1897. Photographer & amateur magician in Woonsocket, RI, until 1897 when turned pro. Toured throughout USA & abroad with sleight-of-hand, illusions, handcuff-king act, & mind-reading. Sailor Martin, his assistant in the escape act, later became an escapist. Died in Los Angeles after long illness. [CMM4/07;St;Mo;Silver]

name: Brinkfort, Louis
bio: (Assens, Denmark: 7 Mar 1888-30 Apr 1958) Pro oriental act. Also did a Buried Alive publicity act as "Raja Lou Chakras". Wrote Den hvide Fakirs Tryllebog. NOTE: Misspelled "Binkfort" by Goldston. [Go2]

name: Brisbois, David [Paul] [pronounced BRISS-boy]
bio: (Webster, Massachusetts: 13 Jul 1962- Chemist doing computer circuitry. Pro magician since c1980. Aka "David the Mystifier". Assistant & protégé of Bernard Whitman whose show & stage name of "Fu Ling" he got in 1984, thence touring the oldest pseudo-Oriental act on the East Coast, including cruise ships in 1985. Did his 1st full-evening show at the 1986 Boston Magicale. [Wh]

name: Britland, David [John]
bio: (St. Helens, Merseyside, England: 16 May 1958-) Learned at age 10 from library books. TV researcher & illustrator. Amateur magician, specializing in cards, close-up, & mentalism. Edited The Talon 1978-81, New Talon 1986-present. Wrote several books & booklets, including Cardopolis (1984, with Marc Russell), Master of the Game (1988, 16pp), & The Mind & Magic of David Berglas (2002, 556pp). Articles in Abra, Pabular, Sorcerer, Spell-Binder, Magigram, Talon, New Talon, & Magic Manuscript. Editor & illustrator for Martin Breese. [Wh2]

name: Briton, Alf[red J.]
bio: (Australia: 1903-2 Feb 1985) Moved to Australia. In the public book-trade with Foyle's in Sydney. Amateur close-up magician. ..... [McC;Alm]

name: Britt, Greg [Elgregoe] NZM
bio: (Born Christchurch, New Zealand 12th March 1960-) Started magic about 14 years old thru overseas trips with his parents buying magic tricks. Owned and operated Elgregoes Castle of Magic 1986 to 2001 which included many lecture tours of New Zealand. Performed over 450 TV appearances both in New Zealand and Australia. NZ Grand Master of Magic 2009 & also included in the Queens New Years Honours List. 19th March 2009 the Governor General inducted Elgregoe into the New Zealand order of Merit. This was in recognition of his antibullying school shows seen by over half a million students.

name: Brock, Tudor [Edward], AIMC
bio:
(Barry, Glamorgan, Wales: 9 May 1913-10 Aug 1994) Learned at age 10 from tricks in magazines. RAF officer (until retired). Semi-pro close-up & stand-up magician since 1946. Edited Malayan Magician for a time. AIMC 1964. Wrote The Great Wong's Routine for the Chinese Rings (1964, 16pp). Articles in Abra, Pentagram, New Pentagram, & Linking Ring. [Wh2] Brockman, Sydney A. "Syd" (USA: -23 Mar 1984) Performer & magic dealer in Seattle, Washington, 1950s-70s. Bought Foley's Magic Shop there in 1958. Did over 10,000 hours entertaining in hospitals for USO. 1965 PCAM President. [Genii6/65]

[See also: Lkein, Helmut]

name: Brodien, Marshall
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro, formerly in trade shows. Renamed the old Svengali Deck "TV Magic Cards" since c1972, making a small fortune until he sold the rights. Entertainment director of Toto's circus & magic restaurant in Chicago since 1989.

name: Bronson, Frederick
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 22 Jan 1867-25 Sep 1897) Debut in 1878 as "De Castro, the Boy Magician". Unsuccessful, he turned dentist & insurance agent. Then full-time pro illusionist as "Frederick Bancroft". Toured Europe & India in mid-1890s. Wrote (as Bancroft) on "Yogi Magic in India" in Scientific American (1897). Died in Charlestown, South Carolina, of typhoid fever. [Pr; Magic2/02]

name: Brooke, Ken
bio: (Yorkshire, England: 3 Nov 1920-26 Feb 1983) Inspired by uncle Walter. Learned at age 7 or 8 from a magic set. Pro street pitchman of magic. Aka "Paul Kelvin" at time he joined British Ring in 1948. Working for Alan Milan's theatrical costume shop in Bradford c1947 when he introduced a magic counter. When in 1948 Milan sold to him (with Paul Veroni as backer) it became the Veroni House of Magic. Then on own in Bradford as the "Ken Brooke Magic Shop" 1951, which soon went bankrupt. Moved to London with Harry Stanley's Unique Magic Studio 1952-65 as manager-demonstrator. Then again on own as dealer (the Ken Brooke Magic Place) from 1966 until 1982 when a stroke forced a sale to Paul Stone. A teacher of Janet Clare. 1975 AMA Special Fellowship. 1981 AMA Performing Fellowship. Died in London. Invented Squircle (1952). Wrote Ken Brooke's Magic: The Unique Years (1981, 222pp) & the Ken Brooke Series (10 vols, 1981-1984). See Derek Lever, Ken Brooke and Friends (1988) & Anthony Brahams (ed), Ken Brooke's Magic Place (1995, 326pp). Audio (1987 as reissue). [Daw94, pp39, 59; Fi;Wat]

name: Brookes, Arthur [C.]
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) In London edited Tricks in 1901 (9 issues; repr 1904 & 1908), the world's first weekly magic magazine. It was sold at newsstands. [St]

name: Brooks, Dick
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro. Played The Magic Towne House since 1973 & since 1974 its co-owner (with Dorothy Dietrich). Executive editor of Hocus Pocus 1978-82 (18 issues).

name: Brooks, Herbert [Brady]
bio: (England: 17 Mar 1873-12 Dec 1923) Pro, first as a society magician, then in variety. Moved to USA in 1903 [sic] when he began playing big-time vaudeville circuits. Invented his famous Brooks Trunk escape, which he debuted well before 1912, changing it from a wood trunk to one of steel in 1915. Toured England 1913-14 & Australia 1915. Then toured the USA until he died in Arizona. Invented Any Card Called For (by 1915) & Cards from Pocket. SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr;Wal;Ho]

name: Brooks, Howard
bio: (USA: 1909-18 Feb 1984) Pro comedy magician. Invented the Brassiere Trick in late 1930s & Time Tape by 1964.

name: Brooks, Robert L. "Bob
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 14 Jun 1926- ) Taught by Ernest "Fess" Marx in 1946. Safety consultant & publisher in Wilmington, Delaware. Semi-pro close-up & mental magician since 1948. Pet effects: Ring off Rope, Thimbles, Endless Rope. Delaware Magician of the Year 1979 & 1980. President of Society of Osiris 1990. Tricks in Apocalypse. [Wh5]

name: Broome, Joseph
bio: (Germany: fl.1730s) Pro sleight-of-hand. Moved to the American colonies by 1734 when he performed in New York City.

name: Brown, [Robert Forester] "Bob", AIMC
bio: (Sacramento, California: 22 Jul 1921- ) Highly successful life insurance & investment salesman in Sacramento for 35 years ($400 million in sales). Inspired & learned magic at age 11 from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set & then Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Semi-pro illusionist. Tours internationally once a year since 1967 & since 1969 with an assistant or partner. These have been Iris Kobesel (ex-Miss England c1964) 1969-70 as sole assistant; then Brenda Payne (as main partner) 1970-present; Linda Jonason (ex-Miss Sacramento) 1972, 1974, etc; Kathy Thiere (fashion model) 1974-c1985; Becky Bayne (who also acted as his ghost writer for 10 years) 1987-present, or Eileen Tichenor 1988-present. AIMC 1997. A master of public relations in magic with articles on this in Genii, Magic Manuscript, & Qui Magia. [MC5/91;MUM11/84;MM6/81;Qui Magia9/89;Mag;WatWhl Wat;Wh]

name: Brown, Derren [Victor]
bio: (Croydon, England: 27 Feb 1971- ) Pro with mind reading, hypnotism, and close-up. Wrote Pure Effect (2000, 163pp) & Absolute Magic (2001, 230pp). [Wh01]

name: Brown, Dota C[laudius]
bio: (New Haven, Indiana: 3 Mar 1913-10 Oct 1996) Learned from Benito Chavez. Pro school assembly magician since 1929 as "Mysterious Brown". Taught magic to Max Terhune c1928-31 in exchange for vent lessons. Thence did both vent & magic. As vent used George McAthy's first figure ("Harley") since c1937. Retired in 1957. Wrote Story of Harley (1983), Neil Foster (1988, 48pp), Tracing Grandpa's Footsteps (1989), & The Whole Ventchilada. [Wh2]

name: Brown, Edward G[eorge], MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1893-1947) Bank manager. A top amateur sleight-of-hand artist. See Trevor Hall, The Card Magic of Edward G. Brown (1973, 211pp).

name: Brown [Jr], Ed[ward H.]
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Prof. of Genetics at U of Illinois. Amateur magician. A top maker of hand-gaffed cards.

name: Brown, Evans
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-1920s) Pro vaudeville & Chautauqua magician. Inventor of gaffed-card tricks, including the Print Card Trick (by 1914), The Joker's Own Topsy-Turvy Deck (by 1924), The Joker's Own Wonder Deck (by 1924), & The Wonder Triple-Force Deck (by 1924).

name: Brown, H. "Box
bio: (Southern States, USA: fl.1840s-70s) Afro-American slave who escaped to the North in 1849. Pro magician in 1870s. [Pr]

name: Brown, John
bio: (England: c1830-1910) Pro apparatus maker in London. Invented several trick cards, including reinvention of the flap card. Also improved De Kolta's Spring Flowers with steel wires. [St]

name: Brown, John Randall
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 28 Oct 1851-4 Jul 1926) Ex-newspaper reporter. Pro muscle reader from 1872 until retired by 1923. [Jay;Pr;Mo]

name: Brown, Jonathan Neal "Jay" "Jasper
bio: (Melrose, Massachusetts: 10 Nov 1954.) Learned in 1963 from library books. BA in English & Theater 1976. Moved to Los Angeles in 1978. Pro stage magician since 1978, his assistant-fiancée Liane Miyake joining him in 1984. Pet effects: Linking Rings, Billiards. AMA Best Stage Magician award 1985, 1988. Invented Room Service. Articles in Genii, Magicana, etc. TV bits. [Jef;Wat;Wh2]

name: Brown, [Herbert] Judson
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-dead) Magic builder. Invented progenitors of the Brainwave Deck (by 1929) and the Haunted Deck (by 1933). Wrote Take a Card (1930, 10pp, with Jack McMillen).

name: Brown, Mel[vin Westley]
bio: (Emmett, Idaho: 4 Dec 1926-10 Mar 1995) Learned around age 8 buying tricks. Chavez graduate c1950. Night Manager, Mark Hopkins Hotel, San Francisco, 1956-86. Part-time pro cardman. Wrote Steve Bruecker & Mike Rogers Present Their Three Shell Game Routine (1985, 15pp). Articles in Pallbearers, Genii, Arcane, etc. [Wh]

name: Brown, Mysterious
bio: See: Brown, Dota C.

name: Browne, Mysterious
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 13 Mar 1890-) Semi-pro since 1925, pro vaude magician since 1931 with illusions & mentalism as "Mysterious Browne". [WWM]

name: Browne, Charles Earl
bio: See: Browne, Charles Earl

name: Bruce, Gordon [Robert]
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 15 Nov 1952-) Musician (cellist) with Scottish National Orchestra. A top amateur closeup cardman in Scotland, having been taught by Roy Walton. Magic collector. Taught Jerry Sadowitz. Tricks in Pabular, Opus, & Magic.

name: Bruecker, Steve[n Wayne]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 28 Aug 1952-) Learned in college in 1973. Physical education teacher in southern California. Semi-pro close-up magician since c1979. Mentor is Mike Rogers. See Mel Brown, Steve Bruecker & Mike Rogers Present Their Three Shell Game Routine (1985, 15pp). [Wh2]

name: Brum, Dr Eduard
bio: (Switzerland: 12 Oct 1933-) Amateur magician (as "Brumoli") & magic collector in Zürich. [Nad]

name: Brumfield, Arthur W. C. "Doc
bio: (Indianapolis, Indiana: 12 Oct 1890-1 Oct 1944) Dealer (The Welworth Company) in Indianapolis 1920s-30s in partnership with Charlie Maly. Published & edited (and actually wrote) Jack Merlin's "... and a Pack of Cards" (1927-28). Collector of magic books. [WWM]

name: Brumoli
bio: See: Brum, Dr Eduard

name: Brunelle, Jon
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Pro close-up in Chicago. Works trade shows & the lecture circuit.

name: Brunn
bio: (Germany: fl.1770s) Pro. Performed in London jointly with Ambroise in 1776. [CI]

name: Brunnet, Prof. [Pierre-] Édouard
bio: (Paris, France: 20 May 1824-after 1882) Pro in Paris, including at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1873-79 where he was a partner with Émile Robert-Houdin. Introduced the Indian Basket Trick (2) = Malle des Indes to France in 1874. [Dif; Vo55; Ch]

name: Bruno, Mr.
bio: See: Nurmi, Bruno

name: Brush, Ada Mary
bio: (USA: -1953) Born Ada Mary Porter. Second wife of Edwin Brush, assisting in illusions & doing crystal gazing & song since around 1926 when billed as both "Amaya" & under her maiden name. [Pr]

name: Brush, Charles R. "Baffles
bio: (Zanesville, Ohio: 12 Nov 1892-28 Jan 1949) Businessman. Semi-pro magician since 1907. Pet effects: flower magic. Wrote Flower Magic (1933, 20pp). Columnist for Linking Ring & Sphinx under pen name of "Baffles". Died in Los Angeles. [St;WWM;Dor]

name: Brush, Edwin
bio: (Garden Prairie, Illinois: 21 Mar 1873-14 Mar 1967) Stage name of Edward M. [or H.] Brush. Pro since 1902. A star with the Lyceum (1902-27) & Chautauqua (since 1904) circuits. Since c1926 sometimes worked with 2nd wife Ada Mary Brush. [Pr;Berg;Dor]

name: Brusini, Paolo
bio: (Goita, Mantova, Italy: 25 Jan 1911-27 Feb 1963) Learned in 1934 from Rossetti's books. Pro manipulator since 1946, with cigarettes, cards, coins, & doves. Toured Europe.

name: Bryson [Jr], Rhett [Bennett]
bio: (Atlanta, Georgia: 9 Oct 1943- ) Learned in 1950 buying tricks decks in drug store. Associate Professor of Drama at Furman U in Greenville, South Carolina. Semi-pro close-up & comedy magician since 1970. Pet effects: Linking Rings, 20th Century Silks, Arm Chopper. Collector. Invented Captive Coins (1975) & Unmatchable (1989). Wrote jointly with Dexter Cleveland as "Algonquin McDuff" The M.C. Bit Book (1980, 48pp; repr), McDuff on Close-up (1981, 44pp), & Spirit Cloth Book (1984, 50pp). As Rhett Bryson wrote small magical ideas (1989, 62pp), which at 2½" x 5" is one of few miniature magic books ever published. Tricks & articles in Linking Ring. Writing a book on life & magic of Edward M. Massey. [Wh2]

name: Buatier, Joseph
bio: See: de Kolta, Buatier

name: Bucha, Fritz
bio: (USA?: fl.1890s-1920s) Pro mechanic & stage manager for Kellar by 1902 to Kellar's retirement in 1908 (during which employment he pirated a copy of Kellar's Aga Levitation). Then stage manager/mechanic for Thurston (1908 to mid-1909), Carter (since mid-1909), and Dunninger (since 1925, taking over from Jarrett). Father of Albert Bucha (a minor sleight-of-hand artist in 1902). [Ch; Magic10/03,1/10]

name: Buchanan, Lovell Lee
bio: (Ephrata, Pennsylvania: 22 Mar 1949- ) Learned at age 8 from Sneaky Pete magic set. Semi-pro magician since 1975, pro since 1987, specializing in stage magic. Pet effects: Linking Rings, Soft Soap, & Three-Card Monte. Collector of theatrical posters. President of Show Stoppers, Inc, theatrical company. Wrote Magic Lamp (1977, 30pp). Articles in MUM, Genii, Linking Ring. [WWEast,Wh5]

name: Bucheli [Sabater], Carlos
bio: (Switzerland: 9 Apr 1903-19 Apr 1981) Pro illusion & fakir act. Aka "Carlston". Lived & worked mainly in Spain. A founding member of the A.C.A.I. in Barcelona in 1932. Dealer (El Rey de la Magia) in Barcelona 1932-1981. Taught Tong-Billy. [Xe]

name: Buchinger, Mathias
bio: (Anspach, near Nuremberg, Germany: 2 Jun 1674-1722) Pro calligrapher & sleight-of-hand man, which was quite a feat considering he was born without hands, feet, or thighs. Pro by 1708 touring Germany, France, and the British Isles (where he used "Matthew" as his given name). [Jay;Daw;Ch]

name: Buck, Monsieur
bio: (France: fl.1830s-50s) Stage name of William Smith. Minor pro in England where he played London's New Strand Theatre in Feb 1837 on the bill with Ramo Samee. Father of George William Smith. [Fr;Magic7/04]

name: Buck, George William Smith
bio: See: Smith, George William

name: Buckhardt
bio: (Denmark: c1863-1941) Moved to Finland in the 1890s. Pro illusionist, specializing in a Black Art act as "Ben-Ali-Bey". Father-in-law of Louis Billing. [St]

name: Buckingham, Geoffrey, MIMC
bio: (St. Albans, England: 2 Jul 1902-9 Sep 1996) Engineer. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand manipulator of coins, balls, & thimbles. 1949 FISM 1st prize in manip; 1951 FISM Grand Prix (given by default when Frakson declined the award). Wrote It's Easier than You Think (1952, 191pp; repr in 2 vols). Movies on billiard ball & thimble manip (1950s). British Ring Past President. 1971 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. SAM Hall of Fame. [Mag;Des]

name: Buckley, Arthur H[erbert]
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 15 Dec 1890-20 Feb 1953) Inspired at age 18 seeing Allan Shaw show in New Zealand. Learned from Down's Modern Coin Manipulation. Debut 6 months later (still 1908) as "Young Dante, King of Koins". Thence pro coin-cardman as "Mysto" in Australia & New Zealand. Moved to USA in late 1919 [sic]. By 1925, also as "Mysto", worked two-person mind-reading with partner-wife Helen. Briefly in Australia c1939-c1943 when resettled in Chicago where became an electrical engineer. Died of a heart attack. Invented Knock 'Em Dead (by 1928) & the muscle pass (by 1948). Wrote The Burglar (1921), New and Improved Effects with Cards (1921), Improved and Original Card Problems (1924, with Goldenberg), Card Control (1946, 219pp; repr 1973), Gems of Mental Magic (1947, 132pp, with John Brown Cook; repr 1973), & Principles and Deceptions (1948, 222pp; repr 1973), the last 3 all classics. Trick in Tarbell #5. [McC;Wal;Berg;Dor;St] Buerger, William A. (Detroit, Michigan: 1 Jun 1854-12 Jun 1931) Aka "The Scientific Wizard". Invented Razor Blade Trick in 1930.

name: Buff, R[ufus] C[laude]
bio: (North Carolina, USA: 11 Oct 1899-6 Mar 1990) Aka "Claudio the Magician". In 1920 moved permanently to Knoxville, Tennessee. Self-taught. Mainly rope magic. IBM member #46. Retired from performing in 1958. Co-edited (with Louis Murphy) Watague Wizards Bulletin 1921-24 (19 issues). Edited Modern Magi 1943-56, Ghost of the Past 1977-78 (2+? issues), Buff's Leaflets 1980-84, & New Modern Magi since 1984. Wrote 3 booklets, including Claudio's Mysteries (1940). Reviewer for Dragon. [Th]

name: Buffaloe, [James Gerald] "Jim
bio: (Memphis, Tennessee: 1929- ) Learned at age 9 from aunt's gift of Gilbert magic set. High school choral conductor & composer in St. Louis, Missouri, until retired in 1986. Semi-pro magician since 1954, now mainly doing school assembly shows. Tricks in Linking Ring (including two 1-man "Parades"), Legerdemain (Germany), & a major contributor to Bobo's Modern Coin Magic. See Phil Willmarth, Buffaloed: The Magic of Jim Buffalo (1998, 224pp). [LR6/85;LR12/87;Wh2]

name: Buffum, Richard D. "Dick", AIMC
bio: (Long Beach, California: 5 Mar 1921-23 Sep 2003) Inspired & learned magic at age 12 from a library copy of Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Newspaper columnist (Los Angeles Times) until retired in 1987. Amateur magic collector-lecturer. Publisher (Abracadabra Press, founded 1979) of fine press books, including 3 on magic. 1986 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award. Wrote The Cone and Balls (1961, 10pp) & 2 valuable histories of major magic manufacturers: "Keep the wheels turning..." (1977, 303pp) on the Owen company & The Brema Brasses (1981) on the Bremas, father & son. [Bo#200;Wh2]

name: Buhicrosan, Tannaker B. N.
bio: (Japan: c1836 – 10 Aug 1894) Born between Dutch father and Japanese mother. He organized a Japanese traveling troupe in 1867 and appeared in Australia and NZ via European countries. He acted as an impresario, manager, translator and Butterfly performer as well. Since 1869 he resided in England to manage various Japanese troupes and entertainers. Organizer and producer of the Japanese Village 1885-1887 in Nightbridge, London.

name: Bull, Arthur F.
bio: See: “Francisco”

name: Bull, David M[errifield]
bio: (Excelsior, Minnesota: fl.1970s-90s) Semi-pro illusionist as "Le Grand David" since 1977 with Le Grand David Company, a repertory troupe in Massachusetts headed by Cesareo "Marco the Magi" Paelez. 1985 SAM Magician of the Year award (shared with "Marco the Magi" & "Seth the Sensational"). Brother of Webster Bull. [Wh2]

name: Bulson, Dr Eugene L. "Gene
bio: (USA: 1894-13 Apr 1954) Hospital administrator. Amateur close-up magus & collector. Invented Pencil thru Nickel in 1930 & Changing the Currency by 1940. 1951 Sphinx Award. Close friend of Al Baker & Sid Lorraine. His manuscript notebooks are in the Busby Collection (ex-Lorraine Collection). Trick in Ireland's YB 1953.

name: Burford, Allan
bio: (England: fl.1940s-90s) Civil & mechanical engineer. With pen name "Paul Duvolo" wrote (commissioned by Alf Briton) the Paul Duvolo Course of magic in late 1950s for the otherwise fictitious "Paul Duvolo School of Magic". [McC]

name: Burford, Byron
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Painter. Semi-pro magician doing ghost shows in Midwest 1949-51. [Walk2]

name: Burger, Eugene "Gene
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1 Jun 1939- ) Inspired at age 7 by gift of Mysto Magic set. Philosophy teacher turned full-time pro close-up in 1978. Teacher of (Michael Anthony, Danny Orleans, etc). AMA Best Lecturer 1985, 1986. A specialist in Bizarre Magick. Noted for his serious approach to presentation. Wrote Secrets and Mysteries for the Close-Up Entertainer (1982, 98pp), Eugene Burger on Matt Schulien's Fabulous Card Discoveries (1983, 44pp), The Secret of Restaurant Magic (1983, 28pp), Audience Involvement (1983, 27pp), Intimate Power (1983, 90pp), The Craft of Magic and Other Writings (1984, 64pp), Spirit Theatre (1986, 192pp), The Performance of Close-Up Magic (1987, 120pp; repr 1991), The Experience of Magic (1989, 140pp), Strange Ceremonies (1991, 104pp), Magic & Meaning (1995, 200pp, with Bob Neale), etc. Articles in Seance, Magician, Magic Menu, etc. Videos (1985, 1987). [Genii5/91;Wat]

name: Burger, Mark
bio: (San Francisco, California: 3 Apr 1948-) Only son of Marvin "Buma" Burger. Learned since childhood in his father's magic shop, the House of Magic in San Francisco, and its proprietor since 1984. [Wh]

name: Burger, Marvin M. "Buma
bio: (USA: c1916-6 Nov 1984) Aka "Buma the Magician". Inspired by & learned from father's gift of magic set at age 9. Comedy magician whose pet magic phrase was "Booma booma, pickle in the ear." Pro dealer in San Francisco as "Buma Magic" ca1945-1967 out of his garage, thence in shop as "House of Magic". Mentor of collector Bob Albo. Died from a heart attack. Father of Mark Burger. [Albo95,pp51-53]

name: Burgess, Clinton
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 7 Aug 1880-2 Nov 1932) Cardman. Amateur debut in 1898 at Majestic Hall in New York. Minor pro since 1902 when he played Tony Pastor's Theater. Invented the 1st gaffed card case (1904). Collector. Compiled Elliott's Last Legacy (1923), which led to his bitter break with Houdini. Proprietor (with Robert El Roy) of The Metropolis Magic Mart. Edited Magikal Booke Worme (1930, 1 issue). Member of the "Secret Six". Contributor to Sphinx & Osirian. [Dor;Dif;Silver]

name: Burghardo, Dono
bio: (Grönenbach/Allgäu, Germany: 11 Jun 1919- ) Stage name of Anton Burghart (or Burghard). Pro since 1947 with classical effects and mentalism. Lecturer. Wrote Le Jeu avec le Subconscient (1984, French tr by Vollmer). His son Berndt became a comedian (as "Mister Bluff"). [Win;Mül;Nad]

name: Burke, [Edward] "Eddie
bio: (Burslem, Stoke-on-Trent, England: 29 Nov 1934-) Learned at age 12 from a trick bought in Woolworth's. Pro magician & hypnotist since 1954. Aka "Zavier" 1950-62 & "Pauline & Eddie" 1962-79. Dealer (Magictrix) in hometown 1970s-80s. Wrote Your Chance in Showbusiness (20pp) & Club & Cabaret Mentalism (1972, 25pp). Articles in Abra, Budget, & Magical Digest. Invented Bag to Costume (1970), Color Changing Hat (1979), & Psychometry Pads. [Wh2]

name: Burke, Seamus
bio: (Kilkenny, Ireland: 4 Mar 1888-) Inspired reading an article by Brunel White in the World's Fair theatrical paper to develop an act of entering rather than escaping confinement. Premiered this act, which he coined "enterology", on 16 Dec 1935 in Manchester at The New Hippodrome. Burke left the stage in 1938 after two years and became for the next decade assistant secretary to Gracie Fields. His autobio is From the Earth to a Star: My Incredible Life (Dublin: 1956). [Jay]

name: Burko
bio: See: Urk, J.

name: Burlingame, Clyde H.
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1910s) Son of H.J. Burlingame. Pro.

name: Burlingame, H[ardin] J[asper]
bio: (Manitowoc [sic] Falls, Wisconsin: 14 Jun 1852-27 Aug 1915) Raised in Chicago. Around age 20 moved to Rotterdam, Holland, to enter commercial business. Taught magic there in 1873 by David Tobias Bamberg. Took stage name of "Jasper Bamberg" to honor his teacher's ancestor. Then from 1873 to 1879 toured Holland, Germany (where he knew the Basch family), & Switzerland as correspondent for American newspapers & performing as a semi-pro magician. In 1891 also became a part-time publisher in Chicago as "The Clyde Publishing Co." In 1895, having bought the magic business of Sid Macaire, Burlingame retired from performing to become a full-time magic dealer-publisher in Chicago (as "Chas. L. Burlingame & Co." and "Ralph E. Sylvestre" plus continuing with "The Clyde Publishing Co."). Sold this business in 1906 to Frank Ducrot (Brooklyn Magic Co). Father of Clyde H. Burlingame. His strong collection of magic books & scrapbooks (begun in 1872 & seriously since 1895) passed to Dr A.M. Wilson in 1918. Now in the Byron Walker Collection, making it the world's oldest. Wrote Leaves from Conjurers' Scrap Books (1891, 274pp), Around the World with a Magician and a Juggler (1891, 172pp; repr 1896), History of Magic and Magicians (1895, 50pp; repr 1895 & 1974), Tricks in Magic (3 vols, 1895-1898, 258pp), Herrmann the Magician (1897, 298pp; repr 1942 as Magician's Handbook), Bibliotheca Magica (1898, 34pp), Gambols with the Ghosts (1901), How to Read People's Minds and Teach Dogs to do Conjuring Tricks (1905, 48pp). [Magic7/01;Pr;Cl;Albo95;Br,p58]

name: Burmain, Professor Firbank
bio: (Britain: fl.1830s-70s) Minor pro. [Fr;Dif]

name: Burne, S. Wynne
bio: See: Collins, Stanley

name: Burnett, Victor
bio: (England: fl.1970s) Stage name of Victor Fiveash. Works with assistant June.

name: Burns, E. S.
bio: (Denmark: 1874-) Stage name of Emil Sorenson. Moved to USA where opened his magic shop & factory (Atlas Trick & Novelty Co.) in Chicago sometime before 1903. Sold his shop & inventory to Roterberg but continued to make props and opened another shop in Chicago, which he ran until 1920. [Albo95; CMM6/08]

name: Burrows, J[ames] F.
bio: (USA: 25 Dec 1867-7 Apr 1934) Pro society magician by 1900 with vent, smoke pictures, & lightning sketches. Moved to England. Wrote Some New Magic [1904, 36pp] & Programmes of Magicians [1907, 36pp]. As "Karlyn" wrote The Lightning Artist [c1905, 82pp], The Stage Artist [c1912], Secrets of Stage Hypnotism (1912, 71pp), & Stage Hypnotism, Stage Electricity and Bloodless Surgery (1914), etc. [Vo56;Bur]

name: Burrus, Joseph
bio: (USA: c1958-31 Oct 1990) Escapist. Billed as "The Amazing Joe, successor to and better than Houdini." Killed on Halloween during a benefit show when crushed by earth & concrete blocks while attempting escape from a buried plastic coffin in Fresno, California. Burrus had been too impatient to rehearse.

name: Burry, Ad.
bio: (Germany: 1863-) Pro. [Dam2]

name: Burt, Brad[ley Allen]
bio: (Tucson, Arizona: 14 Sep 1952-) Inspired at age 5 by mother using misdirection to vanish a brooch & later seeing magicians work live & Mark Wilson on TV. Learned at age 12 from Hay's The Amateur Magician's Handbook, which he bought in a second-hand bookstore. Debut at age c18 at summer camp, charging 25¢ admission. Pro teacher at the B & H School of Magic in Los Alamitos c1972-78. Manager of Chuck Martinez's "Magicians' World" in San Diego c1979-1987. Owner-dealer of "Brad Burt's Magic Shop" in San Diego since 1987. 16 videos (1990-96). [Wh]

name: Burtini
bio: (Britain: c1900-4 Feb 1969) Stage name of William Leonard Powell. Worked at the Birmingham Mint. Semi-pro dealer in Birmingham, England, specializing in metal & glass props by 1946 until he sold the business in 1951 to Davenport's. Built & popularized Benson Dulay's Multum in Parvo (1947) for which he won the 1948 FISM 1st Prize for Invention; & Fred Mills' Multum in Reverse (1948). See Fabian, Burtini's Cups and Balls Routine (1946, 18pp) & Fabian, Burtini's Linking Rings Routine (1947, 16pp). [Daw94]

name: Burton
bio: (Belgium: 18 Feb 1856-2 Jul 1912) Stage name of Arthur Beudin. Pro. Wrote Les secrets de la prestidigitation et de la magie modern (1900). [Vo58;St]

name: Burton, Lance
bio: (Louisville, Kentucky: 10 Mar 1960-) Inspired by Channing Pollock. Taught by Harry Collins & John Thompson. 1977 Abbott's prize. 1980 IBM Gold Medal. Moved to Los Angeles 1981. Pro stage magician. Pet effect: Zombie. 1982 FISM Grand Prix, the 1st American to win that coveted award for his dove production act. Played the Johnny Carson show 10 times since 1981 & the London Palladium in 1988. Since 1982 works mainly Las Vegas (at the Tropicana & since 1991 at the Hacienda). Married magicienne "Melinda" in 1993 (divorced by 1997). TV bits. 1996 TV special produced by Gary Ouellet. Since Jun 1996 works the 1,200-seat Lance Burton theater in the Monte Carlo Hotel in Las Vegas, reportedly with a long-term $100,000,000 contract with the hotel owners. Invented and premiered his "Duel with Mr. Death" illusion in 1984. Other awards: 1982 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year; 1984 AMA Best Stage Magician; 1986 & 1992 AMA Magician of the Year; 1996 Christopher Award as outstanding illusionist. [Bo#275;MUM4/94;LR11/93;Jef;Genii12/91;Steven n's Cat#13;Ran;Mag;Wat]

name: Burton, [Stephen Edward] "Steve
bio: (Anderson, Indiana: 6 Jul 1956- ) Learned at age 13 from free issue of Genii advertised in Popular Science. Pro in Houston, Texas, since 1980, specialized in close-up, stage, mentalism, & MC work. Pet effects: own inventions using computers. Played Magic Island (Houston) 1984-87. In 1985 as "Daedalus" co-founded (with Martin Lewis) the MicroMagicon, the first on-line computer conference of magicians. In 1988 founded and edited Abracadata, the first computer on-line magazine. Publisher as Steve Burton Magic since 1995. Invented Hidden Input Statement (1984) & created the art of Mainframe Magic (1984-present). Co-edited (with Richard Kaufman) V.8 of The Tarbell Course in Magic. Compiled The Tarbell Companion (1995). Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, Ruminations, etc. [Wh2]

name: Busby, Jeff[rey William], AIMC
bio: (Chicoutimi, Quebec, Canada: 23 Feb 1954-) Inspired & learned at age 7 by picking out at local library a copy of Fischer's Illustrated Magic. Moved to USA in 1965. Pro performer to pro dealer-publisher-manufacturer of quality magic (Jeff Busby Magic, Inc) since 1975, successively in Oakland, San Francisco, again Oakland, California, & since 1991 in Wallace, Idaho. A major collector of magic books & booklets. Invented the E-Fold principle (by 1972), the Omega Count (in 1974), Royal Backs (1975), Poltergeist Block (1981 with Don Albrecht), Versa-Table (1994), & a pioneer in computer magic. Youngest AIMC in 1983 (reinstated 1988). Married magicienne Vicki Grismer in 1988. Edited Arcane since 1980, Epoptica 1982-89, & Thaumaturgist since 1987. Edited & wrote many books & booklets, starting with Into the 4th Dimension ... and beyond (1973), Michael Skinner's Intimate Magic (1982, 45pp), The Paul Fox Checker Cabinet (1985), The Automated Sefalaljia Book (1995, 56pp), The Secret of the Palmettos (1998), etc. With joint pen name (with Paul Burton Spencer) of "Burton Williams" wrote Dice—Squares, Tops and Shapes (1982, 104pp). Co-authored (with Bart Whaley & Martin Gardner) The Man Who Was Erdnase (1991, 434pp), which won the SAM Special Library Award. See Craigie Snader, Pre-Epoptica Writings 1976-1981 by Jeff Busby (1988, 24pp). Tricks & articles in Chronicles, Magicien, etc. [Magicien3/94;Wat;Wh]

name: Busch, Paul
bio: (Germany: 15 Mar 1947-) Magician with partner-wife Paula Busch in the Circus-Busch. [Nad]

name: Bush, Conrad C. "Connie
bio: (Prospect Park, New Jersey: 30 Oct 1903-Fort Walton Beach, Florida: 15 Feb 1998) Stage name of Conrad C. Bosschieter. Learned in 1910 from local magician. Part-time pro since 1915 as "Conrad Bush". Senior Accountant until retired in 1979. Amateur close-up magician with cards, coins, & ropes. Joined the SAM in 1931. Articles in Jinx, Gen, Pallbearers, MUM, Linking Ring, & Epoptica. See Joseph K. Schmidt, Connie Bush's Color Isolation (1988). [LR8/97;MUM7/91;SAM;Wh2]

name: Bustelli, Ranieri
bio: (Tuscania, Viterbo, Italy: 1899-1977) Pro illusionist with big stage show. [Sil]

name: Butler, Ladson
bio: (Charleston, South Carolina: 22 Nov 1877-early 1951) Inspired by David P. Abbott's Behind the Scenes with a Medium. Butler's 1917 circular letter is responsible for preserving the correct version of the Han Ping Chien Move. Invented Whispering Queen around 1918. Amateur with Chinese Act & pseudo-Chinese patter as late as 1939. Buffalo, New York, correspondent for Sphinx. Tricks in HMM. [SAM;Dor]

name: Butler, Paul
bio: (Holland, Michigan: 14 Dec 1952-) At age 8 inspired watching Wilson's Magic Land of AllaKazam TV series & learned from magic set. Full-time pro stage magician 1971-81, thence semi-pro while working as a Hollywood screenwriter. Pet effects: Card Duck & Card in Wallet. Wrote Jim Ravel's Theatrical Pickpocketing (1988, 137pp). Co-authored (with Peter Pit) The Magic Castle (1989, [56pp]). [Wh5]

name: Button, Lo
bio: (Germany?: 17 Nov 19-) Stage name of Lothar Knopf. 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in comedy magic; 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in mentalism. [Nad]

name: Bux, Kuda
bio: (Akhnur Jammu, Kashmir, India: 17 Feb sometime before "1905" [as falsely given in his passport]-5 Feb 1981) Stage name of Khuda Bakhsh, aka "The Man With the X-Ray Eyes", aka "Professor K. B. Duke". Pro mentalist. Moved to England in 1935, introducing fire-walking there that year. Toured USA in 1938. 1971 AMA Performing Fellowship. See Roald Dahl, "The Amazing Eyes of Kuda Bux", Argosy (Jul 1952) for a credulous account. [Bo#156;Ran;Mag;Des]
years: 17 Feb sometime before "1905" [as falsely given in his passport]-5 Feb 1981

name: B.W.
bio: See: White, Brunel

name: Byford, Archie
bio: (Britain: Nov 1887-31 Dec 1962) Printer. Amateur magician, inventor, MC. Printed the blue-covered unauthorized version of Stanley Collins' Anthology of Love Poems that was later marketed by Davenports.

name: Byrne, Robert
bio: (Dubuque, Iowa: 22 May 1930-) Learned at age 10 from books on card tricks by Blackstone & Thurston. Writer in Mill Valley, California, & world authority on pool & billiards. Amateur close-up magician. Tricks in Genii. [Wh2]

name: Byron, Marion
bio: (USA: c1919-) Younger sister of Roberta Byron, with whom she did a pro double-act as "Roberta & Marion" in Britain in early 1930s and semi-pro in USA in early 1940s.

name: Byron, Roberta
bio: (USA: 1917-) Learned from father R.J. Byron, a Philadelphia lawyer and amateur magician. Amateur as "Roberta", worked an expert sleight-of-hand act at the first British Ring Convention in 1931. Became the first Honorary Member of the British Ring. Then with a popular and long-remembered double "oriental" act in England with younger sister Marion. Rated in 1934 by Goldston as "probably the most expert lady magician in the world". Returning to the USA, she dropped magic in mid-1930s to become a lawyer in Philadelphia, soon marrying lawyer John J. Badley. Last reported working semi-pro shows with her sister at the Philadelphia Food Fair in both 1940 & 1941 in a 300-seat theater. [Go;Go2;Le;Dam2]

name: Cachadiña, Tony
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 12 Jan 1943- ) Stage name of José Antonio CACHADINA [SALAMANCA]. Learned at age 14. Impresario in Barcelona. Amateur close-up & card magician since 1957. Early member of the Escuela Mágica de Madrid. 1973 FISM 3rd prize in card magic; 1975 Baden-Baden 5th prize in close-up; 1976 FISM 2nd prize in card magic. Editor of Ilusionismo. Articles in Misdirection, Ilusionismo, & Circular de la EMM. [Xe;Wh5]

name: Cadet
bio: (France: fl.1680s) Pro intinerant magician who was performing at Paris fairs in 1689. [CI]

name: Cadet, Max[ime-Henri-Clément]
bio: (Rennes, France: 30 Oct 1882-28 Jan 1914) Chemical engineer in home town. Amateur magician. Wrote Les trucs de la mémoire (1911). [Dif]

name: Caesar, Frank
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 1872-1948) Originally a bookbinder. Then pro magician since debut in 1889. Toured USA. In 1922 settled down in Chicago as a magic dealer-manufacturer. Tarbell named his Caesar Rope Gimmick (1930) after him. [St]

name: Cagliostro, Count Alessandro di
bio: (Palermo, Italy: 2 Jun 1743-26 Aug 1795) Admitted pseudonym, although probably not that of Giuseppe Balsamo, as long & widely assumed. A street urchin & thief until 1768 when he launched his celebrated career as an international charlatan, alchemist, & healer. His minor skills as a magician enabled him to "change" hemp to silk, pebbles to pearls, & powder to roses. A Freemason & founder of the Masonic Egyptian Rite. Also a Rosicrucian. In Naples married Lorenza Feliciani (born ca1759) who became his accomplice. In Portugal in 1771 & Strasburg in 1780. For his alledged role in the theft of the fabulous Du Barry necklace imprisoned in the Bastille 1785-86 until tried & acquitted with honor. In 1789 in Rome arrested, tried, convicted of heresy, & condemned to death by the Holy Inquisition; but the Pope commuted the sentence to life imprisonment. Died 6 years later in prison in the Castle of San Leone. Inspired several magicians. Orson Welles played the "Balsamo/Cagliostro" lead role in the 1947 film Black Magic. Bios are Vie de Joseph Balsamo, connu sous le nom de Comte Cagliostro (Paris: 1791); W.R.H. Trowbridge, Cagliostro (1910); Henry Ridgely Evans, Cagliostro; A Sorcerer of the Eighteenth Century (1931, 83pp); Berco, Världens störste Skojare (Stockholm: 1945); Frank King, Cagliostro: The Last of the Sorcerers (1929; Thomas Carlyle, Count Cagliostro (1883); Vassallo, La Signora Cagliostro (1919). Novels based on him are the elder Alexander Dumas, Memoirs of a Physician; Goethe, Grand Cophta; & Carlos Malheiro Dias, O Grande Cagliostro (Lisbon: 1905; 2nd ed., no date, 412pp). [Ogden97;Pr;Fr;Ran]

name: Cagliostro
bio: See: Fornalski, Jósef

name: Cagliostro II
bio: See: Basch, Ernst

name: Cagliostro, Professor
bio: (Austria: fl.1870s) Stage name of Henry Smith. Pro. Played Germany in 1870s. [Vo57;Dif]

name: Cagliostro-Bellachini
bio: (Germany: 1873-1953) Stage name of Richard Heufel. [Roh]

name: Cahn, Sir Julien
bio: (Britain: 21 Oct 1882-26 Sep [sic] 1944) Wealthy businessman, sportsman, philanthropist. Amateur magician. Vice President of the Magicians' Club. His 352-seat (51'x30' stage) private magic theater (incorporating an air raid shelter & costing £73,000) built in 1938 at Stanford Hall, Nottinghamshire, was the finest in Great Britain and, possibly, the world, giving many charity benefits. After his death his apparatus went to Benyon. NOTE: Given name often misspelled "Julian". [Daw#157-#160; Go2; Le]

name: Caird, Fred
bio: (Scotland: fl. c1920s) Stage name of Frederick "Fred" J. Smith. Lived in Dundee. Invented a clever cube-off-ribbon effect that Goldin gave to Okito who gave it in 1932 to David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg who presented it as the Mystery of the Fourth Dimension. David later adapted the method to his The Thief of Baghdad effect. [Bam,p160]

name: Cairy, Clyde F[rank]
bio: (Ames, Iowa: 2 Oct 1913-27 Nov 1980) Inspired at age 16. Veterinarian. Skilled amateur cardman & mental magician. Invented the "Dick Tracy Card Trick" (1945). Trick in Hugard's Magic Monthly (1944). Co-invented (with Paul Swinford) "Computer Cards" in 1969 (re-released as "Cyberdeck" 1986 & 1996). [Th]

name: Calafatti, Basilius
bio: (Austria: 1 Jan 1800- 27 May 1878) Pro in Austria since 1820. Assistant to Sebastian von Schwanenfeld from 1830 to 1834 when he bought the latter's tent show in Vienna's Prater park. [Al]

name: Caldwell, [Louis Michael] "Mike
bio: (Kansas City, Missouri: 1926-18 Aug 1995) At age 16 inspired seeing Blackstone & Will Rock to buy a magic set. Joined a touring carnival, turning pro comedy magician. At 20 moved to Chicago where he worked small nightclubs. USO in WW II. Then toured nightclubs in 42 states & 10 foreign countries. TV bits. Popular MC. Pet effect: Burnt & Restored Hank. Famous for his acrobatic "Caldwell flip", which landed him flat on his back with a resounding thump. Diabetic & overweight most of his life, he gradually retired from show business & moved to California to run a travel agency. [LR2/83;Des]

name: Caligari, Dr.
bio:
Geilen, Wilhelm

[See also: Burford, Byron]

name: Calkins, Dr I[rving] R., MD
bio: (USA: 31 Oct 1895-) Surgeon in Springfield, Massachusetts. Amateur magician.

name: Callini
bio: (Starachowice, Poland: 1951- ) Stage name of Marian Radlak. Pro illusionist & manipulator.

name: Calostro
bio: See: Doidge, Robert W.

name: Calvert, John
bio: (New Trenton, Indiana: 5 Aug 1911 – 27 Sep 2013) Born Elbern [sic] Madren Calvert. Legally "John Calvert" since 1940. Inspired in 1919 (age 8) seeing Howard Thurston show. Semi-pro with Ralph Pierce (alternating as each others assistant) until 1933. Full-time pro since 1934 as illusionist, manipulator, & close-up artist. First movie appearance was in Honky Tonk (1941) where he doubled for Clark Gable in the card-sharping takes. Thence starred in several feature films until 1948. First of several world tours with his large troupe began in 1949. Pet effects: Dancing Hank, T&R Magazine, Flying Organ, & Vanishing Elephant. 1983 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1989 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. 1998 Christopher Lifetime Achievement Award. Since 1988 at Holiday Inn Grand Cayman with his principal assistant (& wife) Tammy. Noted for his succession of private planes & luxury yachts (the most recent being the 65-foot The Magic Castle II) with which he tours the world. Still active at 97 in 2009. Invented Buzz Saw (head version), Haley's Comet, Flying Saucer, etc. Bio is William V. Rauscher, John Calvert: Magic and Adventures around the World (1987, 305pp). 3 audios. Video (1988). [LR8/04;Pr;Magia Moderna12/2000;Ch;LR2/02;Fu2;Tay;Wh2]

name: Calvert, Tammy
bio: (Singapore: 31 May 1942- ) Stage name of Barbara Anne de Mello. Of Portuguese-Asian parentage & multilingual. In 1960 this Singapore movie starlet was hired away as assistant to John Calvert who taught her magic. Married Calvert in 1970 in Singapore (remarried in USA in 1983). Memoirs in William V. Rauscher, John Calvert (1987), pp.178-189. [Cam;Wh2]

name: Camacho Barriga, João António
bio: (Beringel, Portugal: 7 Apr 1931- ) Civil engineer in Beja, Portugal. Amateur magician & magic historian. Aka "Jónio". Avid collector of magic books & photos. Wrote the magic page for the popular monthly Alentejo Ilustrado 1959-67. 1973 Figuera da Foz 1st prize for invention; 1977 Figueira da Foz 1st prize for card magic. Co-edited (with Osodrac & Saiur) Quatro Ases 1975-79. Wrote the scholarly Dicionarário do Ilusionismo em Portugal (1978-81, 13 parts, 424pp). Also O Ilusionismo em Portugal: Sua História (1963, 28pp), Os Ilusionistas e a sua Ética (1975, 26pp), O que é o Ilusionismo (1977, 16pp), A Troca do Baralho (1979), A Esferográfica (1982, 116pp), Sombras Chinesas (1982, 16pp), and Curso de Magia Teatral: Como se Faz um Ilusionista. Original tricks & articles in O Ilusionista, Ilusionista, O Mágico, Miro Português, Quatro Ases, Ilusionismo (Spain), Journal de la Prestidigitation (France), etc. [Cam]

name: Cameron, Charles W.
bio:
(Scotland: 31 Oct 1927-7 Jan 2001) Bizarrist magician. Aka "Daemon". Edited The Cauldron 1967-68. Wrote 13 booklets: Witches Brew (1967, 36pp), Handbook of Horror (1969, 43pp), 'Mind' Your Magic (1972, 64pp), Devil's Diary (1976), Macabre and Mental Mysteries (1981), & Castle Dracula Mentalism (1997, 87pp). Tricks in Swami (1973-74). [www.dragonskull.com;LR3/2001]

[See also: Campbell, C. B.]

name: Cameron, Henry "Jack
bio: See: Carmo

name: Cameron, Juanita
bio: (Britain?: fl.1910s) Stage name of Juanita "Mitzi" Martin, assistant-wife of Peter "Loudon Cameron" Martin. Aka "D'Olivera".

name: Cameron, Loudoun
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 29 May 1878-) Stage name of Peter Martin. Learned as assistant to his elder brother. Pro illusionist & sleight-of-hand artist working with assistant-wife Juanita. Played Dublin in 1902. Billed as "The Maclaines" when they played Hamburg c1910. [Magic12/1900,6/02]

name: Cameron, Nell
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Assistant-wife of Mal Cameron. Wrote Manual for Magicians and Their Assistants (1949).

name: Cameron, Rita
bio: See: Carmo, Rita

name: Camilo
bio: (Spain: fl.1980s) Stage name of Camilo Vasquez Aleman. Close-up. FISM 1st prize in close-up.

name: Camirand, Guy D[aniel]
bio: (Trois Rivieres, Quebec, Canada: 23 Sep 1942-) Learned at age 8 from grandmother's gift of a Gilbert magic set. Marketing consultant in Sillery, Quebec. Amateur magician since age 12, specializing in close-up & mental. Operates the Camirand Academy of Magic Inc in Sillery (later Longueuil) since 1979 in partnership with Gary Ouellet. Pet effects: Automatic Coffee Stirrer, Homing Ring, & Supershells (all Camirand Academy effects). Wrote Automatic Coffee Stirrer (1980, 12pp). [Wh5]

name: Campbell, C. B.
bio: (USA: fl.1900s-10s) Aka "Camella" as a small-town magician from Altoona, Pennsylvania. Pro magic dealer as founder-owner of The Quan Company in New York City in 1909.

name: Campbell, [Alexander] Loring
bio: (Sapulpa [sic], Oklahoma Territory [now Oklahoma]: 19 Mar 1905-11 Jan 1979) Inspired at age 7 seeing Ten Ichi & at age 12 seeing vaude comedy magi Hugh Johnson & Walter Baker. Pro from age 15 with minstrel show as "Campbello, the Clown Magician" & since age 18 with a Chinese act. Thence into vaude. A star of Lyceum (since 1925) & Chautauqua (since 1926). Aka "The Great Alexander". Worked in Abbott's LA shop since 1948. Retired in 1955. 1978 AMA Special Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote This Is Magic! (1945, 54pp) & Magic That Is Magic (1946, 76pp). Columnist for Tops. Tricks in Genii. [Pr;Th;Mag;WWM]

name: Campbell, Duncan Lorne
bio: See: "Ellis, Jardine"

name: Campbell, Jeffrey L[ynn] "Jeff
bio: (Bradford, Pennsylvania: 26 Aug 1952-) Learned at age 9 from magic set. Pro close-up magician, specializing in Cups & Balls and coin assemblies. Dealer (The Joke Shop) in Waukesha, Wisconsin, since 1972. Article in Linking Ring. Invented Mirrorcles (1981), Crystal Cups (1983), & Tip-Tip (1985). Co-authored (with Ronald L. Dayton) Crystal Cups (1983, 15pp) & Doing Coin Magic for the Change (1987, 15pp). [Wh2]

name: Campbell, Mary Ann
bio: (Little Rock, Arkansas: 11 Sep 1943- ) Born Mary Ann Briscoe Campbell. Married Guy E. Campbell in 1974. Instructor, then associate professor of money management at U of Arkansas in Little Rock. Runs own financial education firm as Money Magic, Inc. Learned magic as a hobby from lessons in 1975. Since 1977 has used her magic to illustrate money management points in her classroom & on PBS and ABC TV. Taught magic to football coach Lou Holtz c1978 when he was at Arkansas; and he has continued to use it in pep-talks to his players. [LR3/02; LR5/79; Mar; Wh2]

name: Camps Martin, Alfredo
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 31 Oct 1923-5 Nov 1984) Amateur since youth. Performed as "Camps" in Spain & Portugal. CEDAM President 1972-? Major collector of apparatus. [Xe;Cam]

name: Canaris
bio: (Greece?: fl.1880s) Aka "Count Canaris". Minor pro in USA (1885) & Australia (1887-88). Possibly the same as "Canari's" who joined the French ASAP in 1905 and the Alexander Canaris who toured South America in 1908. [Cl;Wal;Mo;CMM2/08]

name: Canasta, Chan
bio: (Krakow, Poland: 9 Jan 1920-22 Apr 1999) Son of a Polish-Jewish educator, most of whose family died in the Holocaust. Stage name of Chananel Mifelew. Moved to Britain by 1947. Had own TV show. Pro card magician & mind-reader. USA TV bits with Steve Allen in 1954 & Arlene Francis in 1957. Later a pro painter. Wrote Book of Oopses (mid-1960s). Bio & tricks in David Britland, Chan Canasta: A Remarkable Man (2000, 111pp). [HMM11/54,12/57;Wat]

name: Candide
bio: See: Stevens, Amy

name: Canick, Michael
bio: (New York City: 30 May 1953-) Learned at age 5 from gift magic set. Pro with mentalism & corporate work for 30 years. Major collector since c1988 of books on magic in fiction. Started selling magic books in 1994 from home, c1996 from office, and 1999 with shop. Column ("Corporate Magic") in Genii. Wrote A Price Guide to Magic Books: 1639-1990; Magic in Fiction: A Short-Title Checklist (1998, 40pp); & Clayton Rawson: Magic & Mystery. [Wh02]

name: Cannell, J. C.
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s) Journalist. Amateur magician. A Vice-President of the Magician's Club. Wrote The Secrets of Houdini (1931, 279pp; repr 1932, 1938, 1973), In Town Tonight (1935), & The Quaker Oats Book of Magic (in Dutch tr as Het Meesterboek der Tooverkunst, 1938) and compiled Modern Conjuring for Amateurs (1938).

name: Cannon, Dr Sir Alexander
bio: (England: -18 Mar [or May] 1963 [or 1967]) Physician & mystic. Amateur magician with private magic theater, "The Enchanted Hall", in his home on the Isle of Man. Audio. [Le;SAMS Magazine12/55]

name: Cannon, P. H.
bio: See: "Hatton, Henry"

name: Canonge [Francesh], Fructuoso
bio: (Montbrio, Tarragona, Spain: 1824-15 Jan 1890) Pro, living in Barcelona. Toured Latin America in 1860. Autobio is Apuntes biográficos del prestidigitator español D. Fructuoso Canonge (1872; 2nd ed 1875; 3rd ed 1882). [Xe;Dif]

name: Cantarelli, Alfredo
bio: (Curitba, Brazil: 16 Oct 1905- ) Stage name of Alfredo Maximilo "Max Mund" Mundet [or E. Zahn?], of German parents. Moved to Germany in 1913. Pro illusionist. Toured South America, Near East, & the Balkans with a big full-evening show, returning to Germany in 1937. After WW II toured widely, including Holland, Belgium, & South America. Played his "Abrakadabra" review at the Teatro Avenida in Lisbon in 1958. [St;Al;Cam;HMM5/60]

name: Can't, [Abraham] J. Abe [pronounced can-TOO]
bio: (Mexico: 24 Nov 1896-27 Aug 1949) Pro. Aka "Professor Tucan" when working in Mexico City. Moved to California. Pet routines: cigarette manip, then (since 1940) dove magic. Toured USA, working in a "Charro" (Mexican gentleman's cowboy costume), carrying the dove loads in the serape across his shoulder as reportedly suggested by Paul Fox. Killed in auto accident in Atlanta, Georgia. His dove act inspired Channing Pollock's. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. [HMM11/50;St;Wat;Ch;Tay]

name: Capelli
bio: (Tuscany, Italy: fl.1820s-30s) Pro with sleight-of-hand and trained cats. Played London, including its fairs, for several years beginning in 1829. [Fr;Cl]

name: Caperta, Carlo
bio: (Czechoslovakia: fl.1960s-70s-dead) Stage name of Karl Petrak. Pro illusionist. [Mec]

name: Capper, Alfred
bio: (Southampton, England: c1865-11 Mar 1921) Pro muscle-reader who included some conjuring. Wrote Confessions of a Thought-Reader (1901, 7pp, as offprint from Universal Magazine) & A Rambler's Recollections and Reflections (1915, 322pp). [Daw2]

name: Capra, Jean-Baptiste
bio: (France: fl.c1590) Aka "Montalboto". His card tricks for Marie de Medici (future wife of French king Henry IV) around 1590 won him a gold chain worth 220 livres. This is the earliest reported prize given to a magician. [Dif]

name: Capretta
bio: See: Chefalo, Magdalena

name: Carambo
bio: See: Cavalli, Mario

name: Carazini
bio: (Kentucky, USA: fl.1950s-90s) Stage name of Jim Williams. Pro theater & cabaret comedy smoke act in Las Vegas, Mexico, & 5 years at The Crazy Horse in Paris. 1970 AMA Best Stage Magician (shared). TV bits including 2 Carson shows in 1972 & 1978. Disappeared from the magic scene around 1990 & reportedly in Europe. [Mag]

name: Carbel
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 22 Jul 1898-9 Oct 1952) Stage name of José Carlos REBELO. Moved to Brazil in 1918 at age 20. Pro since 1926 with vent, sleights, & illusions. Worked with Mickelie Baby in 1938. Later worked as "Fantame". [Cam]

name: Carbines, Robert [Benjamin] "Bob
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 30 Dec 1887-...) Moved to Australia at age 2. Accountant. Semi-pro manip with coins & cups-&-balls by 1910. [McC; Magic Mirror2/1910]

name: Carboni
bio: See: Kindbom, Sven Eric

name: Card, Madame
bio: See: Eagle, Georgiana

name: Cardac, Lionel
bio: See: Branson, L. H.

name: Cardano, Gerolamo
bio: (Padua, Italy: 24 Sep 1501-20 Sep 1576) Mathematician & philosopher. Under the Latin spelling of his name, Hieronymous Cardanus, wrote several major books that touched upon conjuring & card cheating, including De Subtilitate (1550); Liber de Ludo Aleae (c1564 ms), English tr in Ore (1953), 181-241; & Piazza Universale (1582). Autobio is De Vita Propria Liber (1643), English tr as The Book of My Life (1930, 331 pp). Bios are H. Morley, The Life of Girolamo Cardano of Milan (2 vols, 1854), Oystein Ore, Cardano: The Gambling Scholar (1953, 249 pp), & Alan Wykes, Doctor Cardano (1969, 187 pp). [Dif; Ch]

name: Carddan
bio: See: Rushworth, Geoffrey W.

name: Cardini, Richard "Dick", MIMC
bio: (Bryn-Teg [?], near Cardiff, Wales: 24 Nov 1895 [sic]-11 Nov 1973) Son of Price Pitchford & Alice Maude Skinner. Stage name since 1923 of Richard Valentine [sic] Pitchford. Aka "Val Raymond" 1919-23. Learned as a child. Pro since 1918, initially very small time, including busking in London (1919) & demming at Gamage's (1920). Then toured Australia 1923-26. In 1926 moved to USA where he married Swan Walker, who became his assistant thru rest of his career. Debuted his famous silent act in 1927. Noted for flawless technique, superb misdirection, & elegant style. Played such top vaudeville houses as the New York Capitol Theatre (1932, 1934, 1939, 1947, 1949), the London Palladium (1932, twice in 1933, & 1938), & the Paris Alhambra (1933). And such posh nightclubs in New York City as the Casino de Paree for 14 weeks in 1934 & the Cotillion Room in 1949. Being a magician's magician, he was voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936. Declared one of the 10 Card Stars in 1938. SAM President 1941-42. In 1942 he helped launch his brother, Robert Pitchford, in magic. Retired in 1966. 1968 AMA Performing Fellowship. 1970 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. NOTE: John Booth's conclusions that Cardini's middle name was "David" and that he was born "1 March 1896" in "St. Thomas parish" to "Richard Pitchford" & "Mary Ann Thomas" resulted from choosing the wrong birth records. See John Booth, Creative World of Conjuring (1990), 140-144. [Zo;Pr;MUM12/91;Abra.....;Bo#236;Genii4/42;Fi; Wal;Tay;Ho;Sphinx11/27]

name: Cardini, Swan
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 20 Feb 1903-27 Dec 1993) Stage name of Swan Pitchford, née Walker. Hotel bookkeeper-cashier at time she "went backstage to see him [Richard Cardini] at theater in Jackson, Michigan. Three days later he asked me to marry him." They married in Chicago in 1926 when she became his assistant, working in bellhop uniform. Retired with him in 1966. [Pr;Mar;Wh2] Cardo, The Great (Benares, India: 2 Jun 1901- ) Stage name of Shree Probhat Kumar Chatterjee. Pro Eastern & Western magic act since 1929. Wrote Indra-Jal. [Go2]

name: Careejo, Harry
bio: See: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Carey, Chris
bio: (Rochester, New York: c1950-) Learned magic at age 12 from Jimmie Davis at a boy's club. Pro with own production company (The Sho-Pro Team, Inc) in Atlanta, Georgia, producing shows across the USA since 1970s. Wrote Do the Stuff That's You (1980, 64pp), Vol.2 (1994, 84pp), & Find the Stuff That's You (1989, 271pp).

name: Carey, Vin[cent M.]
bio: (Massachusetts, USA: 5 Apr 1898-27 Sep 1975) Pro magician (aka "Carini"), clown (aka "Vino the Clown"), & juggler. Dealer (The American Magic Co.) in Baltimore 1940s-60s. Founder & former President of the International Juggler's Association. Wrote 3 booklets.

name: Carini
bio: See: Carey, Vin

name: Carl, Mr
bio: See: Wiesinger, Carl E.

name: Carl, Black
bio: (USA: fl.1890s) Aka "Black Dante" in Australia in 1899.

name: Carl, Professor James
bio: (Derby, England: 1875-22 Feb 1955) Stage name of James A. Wakefield. Politician (town councillor) in Derby. Semi-pro magician, specialized in cigar magic. Became godfather of David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg in 1904. Wrote Practical Conjuring (1911, 28pp).

name: Carleet
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Stage name of Harry Howe. Magician & escapist. Lived in Bradford. Invented the Barrel Escape (by 1911).

name: Carlini
bio: (England: -13 Jan 1969) Stage name of Charles R. Humpage. Son of "Professor Herwinn". Minor pro who flourished around the turn of the century.

name: Carlisle, Stanton
bio: (Britain: 28 Jan 1928-14 Jun 1990) His real name he insisted, despite the unlikely coincidence that it is same as the mind-reader protagonist in William Lindsay Gresham's fine novel of carnival life, Nightmare Alley (1946). John Wade suggests his real name may have been Richard Stanton. Learned as a boy from an Ernest Sewell magic set he swapped for with a school friend. After RAF service turned pro magician c1948, working music halls with a standard act plus kid shows, both as "Rinaldo". Then pro mentalist since 1950s as "Stanton Carlisle". AIMC 1990. Wrote several booklets, including Mentalism for Connoisseurs, Mentalism De Luxe, & Mentalism: Inner Secrets 1 (1990, 85pp). Tricks in Pentagram (a 1-man issue), Magigram, etc.

name: Carl-Lyle
bio: See: Laughlin, Lyle

name: Carlo
bio: See: Wiesinger, Carl E.

name: Carlo, Dr.
