bio: (Toledo, Ohio: 1 Aug 1909- ) Stage name of Carlo Sommers. Pro & dealer (Carlo's Magic Shop) in Toledo in early 1940s. Organized Toledo Magician's Society in 1942. Invented Balls of Fire, What's On Your Mind (by 1947), Carlo Glass Production (1958), & Rubber Dove. Still active in 1960s. [LR12/46;HMM3/55]

name: Carlos, Barón de
bio: (Tordera, Spain: 24 Apr 1935- ) Stage name of Carlos de CARLOS FERRER. Pro comedy & general magic. Prizes in Spain, Portugal (1966), & 1976 FISM 3rd prize in comedy magic. Plays Spain, Portugal, Germany, & Switzerland. Father of Mária Victoria CARLOS (see). [Xe]

name: Carlos, Mária Victória
bio: (Tordera, Spain: 9 Jun 1966-) Daughter of Barón de Carlos who taught her magic at age 9. Pro magicienne as "Fada Victòria". Performs at hotels in Catalonia. [Xe]

name: Carlosbach, Dr.
bio: (France: fl.1820s) Itinerant street magician who toured France. The first such seen by young Robert-Houdin in Blois in 1824. [CI]

name: Carlotti, Antonio
bio: (Italy: fl.mid-1700s) Pro. [CI]

name: Carlston
bio: See: Bucheli, Carlos

name: Carlton
bio: (Holloway, London, England: 1881-27 Jun 1942) Stage name since 1902 of Arthur Philps and "Carlton Philps" before then. Inspired in 1896 seeing a street conjurer and by working as a telegraph boy in then-amateur magician Maurice Garland's cigar shop. Debut c1897 as a busker, then pro comedy magician billed as "The Human Hairpin" (weighing only 126 pounds at over 6 feet). In London played the Alhambra in 1902, the Palace 46 times since 1902, the Pavilion often since 1903, & St. George's Hall in 1925. Introduced the modern sucker version of the Die Box in 1909. Toured the world, including the Continent, Australia 1907, USA 1911, South Africa, & Egypt. Retired (weighing 210 pounds) in 1936. Autobio is Twenty Years of Spoof and Bluff (1920, 299pp). [Pr:Wal:Dif:Vo56:Le:Fi:Bam p 651] [Pr;Wal;Dif;Vo56;Le;Fi;Bam,p.65]

name: Carlton, Paul
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-30s) Marine artist. Amateur magician. Wrote (with anonymous help from Max Holden) the infamous series of "It's Fun to be Fooled--It's More Fun to Know" magic exposé ads for Camel cigarettes that appeared in 1933. Wrote the Magician's Handy Book of Cigarette Tricks (1933, 36pp), a tie-in exposé pamphlet also put out by Camel's. {Daw#51}

name: Carlyle
bio: See: Laughlin, Lyle

name: Carlyle, E. Raymond
bio: See: Fowler, Ed

name: Carlyle, Francis
bio: (USA: 1911-27 Dec 1975) Stage name of Francis Xavier Finneran. Pro card magician since early 1930s. Invented Transposition in Reverse (by 1941), Carlyle's Card = Business Card Move (in 1943), & Locatrix (by 1948). Cruise ship work on New York-Rio de Janeiro run 1950. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1955. A teacher of Peter Maloney, etc. 1974 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. Wrote a set of Lecture Notes (published in 1980s). See Roger Pierre, The Magic of Francis Carlyle (1975, 186pp). Died of the effects of alcoholism. [LR8/93;Mag]

name: Carmans, Die
bio: See: Puchinger, Günter

name: Carmelini, Max
bio: (Russia: 1862-5 Sep 1935) Stage name of Max Malzin. Pro comedy magus in Russia as "Karmelini". After Russian Revolution (1917) moved to Hungary & often toured Germany & the Continent. Taught Steven Forgacs. [Vo57;Mec]

name: Carmelli, Professeur
bio: (Armentières, Nord, France: 26 Jul 1850-12 Aug 1919) Stage name of Auguste-Joseph Coëne [Cohen]. Jew. As a boy became a celebrated acrobat with a circus where he studied magic from the troupe's magician. Although partially crippled at the Battle of Sedan in 1870 and eventually confined to a chair, he became a successful pro magician. Starred in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique 1886-87 and the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1888-98. Then had his own travelling magic theater, the Théâtre-Salon Carmelli, 1890-c1911; but finally returned to the Cabinet Fantastique 1915-18. Teacher of "Charl's" & H. Le Roy (his nephew). [Dif;Vo55;Dam;Rey]

name: Carmen, Vince
bio: (Shelby, North Carolina: 19 Aug 1943- ) Stage name of James Cain. Learned at age 5 or 6 from gift Mandrake magic set. Worked as actor, musician, etc until c1964 when became pro illusionist. Toured Spain, Latin America (1979-80), New Zealand (1984 & 1991), California with Circus Vargas (1981). At Circus-Circus in Las Vegas 1988-89. Pet effects: Split Fans & such classic illusions as the Sub Trunk. Played the Zombie in horror film Body Shop (early 1970s). Articles in State of the Art. [Wh]

name: Carmichael, Allan [Thomas]
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 14 Nov 1936-) Inspired in 1949 by demo in department store. Sales trainer/motivator in Sydney. Semi-pro close-up magician since 1975. Pioneered restaurant magic in Australia. Worked Barnaby's Restaurant 1985-89. Articles in Blueprint. [Wh2]

name: Carmier, Andrew [Lewis]
bio: (Fitchburg, Massachusetts: 8 Nov 1898-) Mechanical engineer in Detroit with automotive industry. Semi-pro magician since 1929. Tricks in Sphinx. [WWM] Carmo, The Great (Melbourne, Australia: 8 Nov 1881-1 Aug 1944) Of Scottish parents. Stage name of Henry "Harry" "Jack" Cameron. A pro strongman-juggler-contortionist in Australia, he moved in 1910 to England where he became a pro magician around 1914. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1921. Circus owner 1928-1930 when it was destroyed by successive snow & fire disasters. Returned to magic & occasional circus appearances. [Fi;Pr;Wal;Dif;Ch]

name: Carmo, Rita
bio: (London, England: 3 Feb 1906-5 Sep 1979) Stage name of Rita Cameron née Rogers. Learned 1923 as apprentice to Carmo whom she married in 1944. Pro with own act 1946-51 when retired. [Mar]

name: Carney, John
bio: (Des Moines, Iowa: 23 Jan 1958-) Inspired at age 7 when read book on Houdini. Learned at age 13 from books. Debut by age 18. Moved to Los Angeles to become a leading protégé of Dai Vernon. Also student of Faucett Ross. Pro close-up & comedy stage magician since age 22. Works mainly the comedy club circuit, private functions, & banquets. 1985 AMA Best Close-up Magician. 1988 FISM 2nd prize for close-up. 1989 AMA Best Close-up Magician. 1991 FISM 2nd prize for close-up. Wrote Carney Knowledge (1983, 57pp), Carney Up Close, Conjuring con Carney, & Carney Uncovered. See also Stephen Minch, Carneycopia (1991, 296pp). Tricks in Richard's Almanac, Genii, etc. 2 videos (1985, etc). [LR9/86; Bo#204-205; Wh2]

name: Caro
bio: See: Miller, [A.] Caro

name: Carolus
bio: (Fousseret, Haute-Garonne, France: 25 Feb 1891-1 Jun 1987) Stage name of Louis Carsalade. Pro shadowist & mentalist. Since 1937 worked with his partner-wife as "Carolus & Magdola". In 1952 they won the FISM 1st prize for mentalism & he the prize for Hand Shadows. Later she worked as "Eveline". Author of many popular non-magic books. [Dif]

name: Caroly, Jean
bio: (Rochechouart, Haute-Vienne, France: 15 Jul 1868-2 Dec 1955) Stage name of Jean-Augustin-Charles-Joseph Faugeras. Moved to Paris at age 15. Pro performer since 1888 & dealer since 1896 when he opened a magic manufacturing plant (Maison Caroly) in Paris. Edited-published L'Illusionniste 1902-14. Charter member of the Chambre Syndicale de la Prestidigitation 1904. CSP 1st & 2nd prizes for invention in 1906. Did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Ka-Ro-Ly". Proprietor of shop in Paris (Académie de Magie) 1908-1930 when retired, turning over company to nephew, Caroly II. Wrote books in French. Article as "Jean de La Vigne" in Journal de la Prestidigitation (1955). [Dif;Vo55;Magic6/02;Dor]

name: Caroly II
bio: (Rochechouart, Haute-Vienne, France: -25 Mar 1950) Stage name of Charles Faugeras, nephew of Jean Caroly. Dealer (Académie de Magie) in Paris 1930-50. [Dif]

name: Caroselli, Al[fred Louis]
bio: (Buenos Aires, Argentina: 8 Sep 1889-8 Jan 1950) Moved to USA in 1901. Inspired in 1902 by father, an artist & amateur magician. Debut in 1906. Pro magician & musician, briefly with Walter Domzalski as partner. Pet effect: Linking Rings. Maker of custom-built props 1930s-40s in Detroit. Manager of Abbott's branch shop in Detroit. [SAM;St;Scroll of Merlin12/43]

name: Carr, John Dickson
bio: (Uniontown, Pennsylvania: 30 Nov 1906-27 Feb 1977) Amateur magic buff (friend of Rawson, Gresham, etc). Famous author of detective novels (including under his pen name "Carter Dickson") many of which, since his first in 1930, have scattered references to conjuring. Also wrote The Life of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle (1949, 304pp). Lived in Britain 1940-48 & 1951-65. Worked for M.I.5 in WW II. [Daw#142-#144,#212]

name: Carrandi Jr, Mario
bio: (Santa Clara, Cuba: 17 May 1942-) Inspired seeing Fu-Manchú show in Havana in 1949. Learned from father's gift of a Mysto Magic set. Moved to USA in 1953. Amateur. Magic collector & mail-order dealer since 1968. Co-owner of Tannen's Jan 1987-Nov 1988 until sold share to Tony Spina. Thence full-time mail-order dealer in antique & old magic books in Belle Mead, New Jersey. [Bo#208;Albo95;Wh]

name: Carrer, Charles "Charley
bio: (USA?: -13 Jan 1972) A star vaudeville juggler. Built & repaired most of the props for his famous magicienne wife, Dell O'Dell.

name: Carrington
bio: (Quatremare, Louviers, France: 29 Nov 1895-16 May 1971) Stage name of Joseph Buhot. Pharmacist turned pro illusionist in 1922. Toured a large show throughout France 1926-1962 when he semi-retired due to ill health. His principal assistants were his successive wives, "Manola" (Louisette Guay) & "Manita" (Line Saban). Director of journal Scênes et Pistes. [Dif;Bou;Rob1]

name: Carrington, Hereward
bio: (Jersey, Channel Islands [British owned]: 17 Oct 1880-12 Dec 1958) Moved to USA in 1899. Amateur magician and famous although self-servingly credulous investigator of psychic phenomena. Lived many years in Los Angeles where he died. Wrote Hindu Magic ([1909], 52pp; rev ed), Handcuff Tricks (1913, 61pp), Side-Show and Animal Tricks (1913, 66pp; repr 1973), The Boys' Book of Magic (1920, 284pp), Magic for Everyone (1927; repr 1942, 138pp), & (with B.M.L. Ernst) Houdini and Conan Doyle (1932, 255pp). Also wrote extensively on psychic phenomena, from The Physical Phenomena of Spiritualism (1908, 440pp; repr 1920), thru Eusapia Palladino and Her Phenomena (1909), to Psychic Oddities (1952). See Paul Tabori, Pioneers of the Unseen (1972) for bio sketch.

name: Carroll, [Harrison John] "Harry
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 25 Dec 1948-) Learned at age 9 from friend Ray Mertz. Semi-pro close-up 1972-82, working Forks Hotel 5 years in mid-to-late 1970s. 1979 Linking Ring Parade Award. Billed as "Harrison, The Man with the Magic Touch". Full-time pro trade-show magician in North America & occasionally abroad since 1982. [Wh2]

name: Carroll, José
bio: (Calatayud, Zaragosa, Spain: 19 Sep 1957-5(?), Jan 2004) Stage name of José "Pepe" FRANCO LARRAZ (not, as rumored abroad, a relative of the late dictator). Inspired in 1967 seeing TV magician. Learned from magic books. A creative & technically fine cardman. Pro card & close-up magic since 1980. Pet effects: gambling demos & flourishes (spreads, etc). 1982 FISM 2nd Prize for card magic; 1988 FISM 1st Prize for card magic. Member of Escuela Mágica de Madrid. Wrote Effects and Presentations (1983), 52 Lovers (Vol.I, 1988, 180pp; Vol.II, 1991), & New Poosha d' Poosha Routine (1988). Articles in Misdirection, etc. [Wh2]

name: Carroll, Lewis
bio: (England: 27 Jan 1832-14 Jan 1898) Pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson. Math teacher at Oxford until 1881, then popular writer. Avid amateur magician. See John Fisher, The Magic of Lewis Carroll (1973, 288pp) & Martin Gardner, The Annotated Alice (1960).

name: Carroll, Shelley
bio: (Lansdale, Pennsylvania: fl.mid-1970s-90s) Stage name of Carol Lee Shelly. Learned in 1974 from classes at The Garcia-Schindler School and Derek Dingle. Debut in 1974. Pro sleight-of-hand since 1975. Since 1980s runs a booking agency with partner Derek Dingle. [Se]

name: Carrothers, Ted
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: fl.1970s-80s) Comedy magic. Pro dealer ("Ted Carrothers Magic Studio") since 1970s in Toledo, Ohio, a general magic shop also giving instruction, acting as agency, & with a large book section including a secondhand room. Edited, as house organ, Abracadabra Club Newsletter 1977-1983-present.

name: Carson, [John William] "Johnny
bio: (Corning, Iowa: 23 Oct 1925-23 Jan 2005) Raised in Norfolk, Nebraska, where at age 12 he learned from a magic set and went semi-pro at age 14 as "The Great Carsoni". As a US Navy ensign 1945-46 informally entertained his sailors with magic and added vent (with his figure "Eddie"). While in college at the U of Nebraska and after worked semi-pro club dates 1946-51 when he went full-time with radio & TV. Ever-genial host of The Tonight Show on TV, 1962-92, often show-casing magicians. 1976 AMA Special Fellowship. Best bio, including much on his magic, is Ronald L. Smith, Johnny Carson: An Unauthorized Biography (1987). See also Douglas Lorence, Johnny Carson: A Biography (1975), Paul Corkery, Carson: The Unauthorized Biography (1987) & Craig Tennis, Johnny Tonight. [Mag; WWA] "Carsoni, The Great" SEE: Carson, [John William] "Johnny"

name: Cartelli
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: Jan 1922-25 May 1993) Stage name of Herbert Knetsch. Pro magician in Hamburg since 1939. Specialized in card magic. Wrote Heiterer Zeitvertreib für Jung und Alt (1946, 31pp).

name: Carter, Charles J[oseph]
bio: (New Castle, Pennsylvania: 14 Jun 1874-13 Feb 1936) Aka "Carter the Great". Debut at age 10. Toured with the Kickapoo Indian Medicine Show. A top-line international pro illusionist since 1900 with large-cast full-evening show. Bought Martinka's shop in 1917 & sold it in 1919 to Houdini. Eight world tours from 1907 until 1936 when he died in Bombay. Wrote Magic and Magicians (1903), Personal Magnetism (1929, 71pp, a self-help pitch book), & Secrets of Oriental Magic (1932). His props passed to, successively, his widow in 1936, jazz musicians Peter Clute & Turk Murphy in 1966, and (what was left after considerable pilferage in storage) in 1991 for $25,000, to Bill Smith & Mike Caveney who plan major restoration. Bio is Mike Caveney, Carter the Great (1995, 375pp). See also Garry R. Frank & Phil Temple (compilers), The Carter Scrapbook (1992, 96pp). [Ch;Pr;Rey;Wal;Fu2;Berg]

name: Carter. Corinne
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-30s) In 1894 married Charles Carter who taught her magic. Pro escape artist 1894-95 to two-person mind-reader in Carter's show. Mother of Larry Carter.

name: Carter, Judy
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Learned magic at age 8. In 1971 became 1st woman to work the Magic Castle's Close-Up Gallery. Pro club & college comedy magic. Runs comedy workshops. Wrote Stand-up Comedy: The Book. [Mag]

name: Carter, Lawrence J. "Larry
bio: (El Paso, Texas: 9 Mar 1895-dead) Learned c1910 as apprentice to father Charles Carter. Pro illusionist. Took over father's show in early 1935. Last performance in San Francisco at Xmas 1936. His mother put the show in storage, refusing access to her son who became a car salesman in San Francisco until his death.

name: Carter, Nelson "Nic
bio: (Duisburg, Germany: 31 Aug 1880-4 Oct 1950) Stage name of Werner Steven. Pro card manipulator, billed as "The Man With 100,000 Cards". Toured Russia & Far East before WW I. In Russian PW camp in WW I. Then toured USA & Europe. [Vo57;St]

name: Cartex
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 13 Aug 1910-18 Nov 1956) Stage name of Ramon CAMPRUBI ALEMANY. Pro stage magician in Europe. Played Portugal in 1946. [Xe]

name: Carthy, Al
bio: (France: 1913-21 Jun 2004) Stage name of Mac Ronay. Pro As Mac Ronay played the Crazy Horse Saloon 1957-58 with a burlesque magic act. Played Ed Sullivan TV show 1961 twice. Since the 1970s as "Al Carthy" does his robot-themed comedy magic. [HMM1/59,5/61;Playboy7/61; Abra #3050]

name: Cartier, Dr Georges
bio: (France: 12 Aug 1920-15 May 1989) Physician. Amateur magician. Wrote (with Zum Pocco) Encyclopedie des boules de billard (2 vols, 1985, 1987, 250+300pp).

name: Cartier, Pierre
bio: See: "Clark, Keith"

name: Cartini
bio: (Germany?: 12 Aug 1946-) Stage name of Helmut Dobrowolny. 1975 MZvD 3rd prize in manip. [Nad]

name: Cartis
bio: (Rome, Italy: 20 Dec 1874-24 Oct 1952) Stage name of Nicolas Casini. Son of a Roman hotel proprietor, he ran off to become a circus acrobat. Pro magic debut at age 18. Original stage names were "Cermann" & "Cermano". Worked circuses with pseudo-Chinese act with wife & 2 daughters, Lydia & Yolande.

name: Carts, Charles "Charlie
bio: (France?: fl.1940s-50s) Pro card man, specializing in card-memory work. Played the USA 1949-54, working nightclubs, including the Cotillion Room in New York in 1954. Pattered in French accent & billed as from Paris. TV bits.

name: Carver, Robert "Bob
bio: (USA: -23 Apr 1988) In teens in Macon, Georgia, did a 2-person act with J.C. Doty as "Heavy & Weight". Pro close-up worker. Pet effect: Chop Cup. Invented Professor's Nightmare in 1950s.

name: Casaubon, Dr. George E.
bio: (USA: c1916-) Stage name of the Rt. Rev. Monsignor Vincent N. Foy. Roman Catholic priest. Amateur card man. Wrote Deceptions with a Short Card (1946, 56pp) & Salt Sorcery (86pp). [Abra#1118]

name: Cascabel
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 29 Apr 1922- ) Stage name of Vladimir Ruzicka. Pro with assistant-wife Vera Ruzickova.

name: Casino, Jonnie
bio: (Vingaker, Södermanland, Sweden: 14 May 1923- ) Stage name of Jonnie Åkerlind. Pro sleight-of-hand & mentalism, working the variety circuits 1949-59. Former magic collector, with most nearly complete collection of Swedish-language magic books, which was sold in 1987 to David Philipson, magic dealer ("D. Katz Productions") in Stallarholmen. Wrote (as Åkerlind) Svensk Bibliografi för trollkarlar (1963, 88pp). Articles in most Scandinavian magic magazines. ..... [Dif;Wh5]

name: Caspian, David
bio: (Canada: 1965-) Stage name of David Peck, although used real name at first. Pro with silent manip act. Won Abbott's Senior Contest. Lives in Toronto where he is a regular at Harper's Restaurant & Dinner Theatre.

name: Cassidy, Robert E. "Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Lawyer (now ex). Semi-pro mentalist. Co-founder of Psychic Entertainers Association in 1978. Edited Vibrations 1978-81 & 1984. Wrote Pseudo-Mentally Yours (1977, 32pp), The Art of Mentalism (2nd ed 1984), The Art of Mentalism II (1996), & Principia Mentalia, Vols 1 & 2 (1996, 60pp). He vanished from the mentalism scene from 1989 to 1996.

name: Castelli, Signor
bio: (Normandy, France: fl.1800s-1840s) Stage name. Pro itinerant sleight-of-hand artist with a Pinetti-like repertoire, plus his charlatan eating-a-man-alive advertisement. Played Brussels (1809, 1836, 1842) & Mexico (1824). His performance at Angers in 1828 is detailed in

name: Castelli, Giovanni
bio: (Italy: fl.1790s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist and apparatus conjurer. Played Bologna in 1799. Probably the same as J. Castelli, below.

name: Castelli, J.
bio: (Italy?: fl.1820s) Pro apparatus magician in Europe. Played Martinique & Trinidad in 1823, billed as "Professor of Philosophical Amusements". Probably the same as the above Giovanni Castelli. [Ch]

name: Castle, Fred[erick], MIMC
bio: (Elham, Kent, England: 8 Apr 1909-Jun 1997) Inspired at age 19 seeing friend doing show. Schoolmaster. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 20. Also a top jumbo-card worker since 1932 when saw Herbert Milton work with them at Maskelyne's. MIMC 1948. 1976 IBM 1st prize for close-up. Pet effect: Hand of Cleopatra, which fooled Dai Vernon during Castle's 1981 tour of USA. Wrote Magic With Giant Cards: A Lecture (1981, 14pp). [Wh2]

name: Castle, Martin
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Stage name of Jim Turner.

name: Castro, David de
bio: (Portugal: 6 Mar 1838-1888) Stage name of David Augusto Borges de Alvim Morais e Castro. Son of a Portuguese baron. Wealthy amateur magician, having learned at age 17 from a box of tricks. In 1864 built a large private magic theater, the Teatro Minerva, in the garden of the Carrancas Palace in Oporto for the amusement of his friends. Wrote 3 large magic books: O Prodígio nas Salas (1872; 2nd ed; 3rd ed 1890, 238pp), O Thesouro da Magia (1884, 395pp), & A Carteira de Satan (1888, 276pp). [Cam]

name: Castro, Ernest, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 17 Sep 1904-1971) Semi-pro kid-show magic. Worked with wife April. [Go2]

name: Castro, Fernando
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 13 Oct 1936- ) Stage name of Francisco Fernando da Silva Castro. Learned in 1952 from Martins Oliveira. Aka "Saviloff" & then since 1955 "Savil". Bank clerk (computer operator). Part-time pro magician since 1955, specializing in card, close-up, & mental magic. Chief Editor Magia (Portugal) 1960-65. Dealer (Savil Magic Shop) in Ermesinde, Portugal, since 1978. Articles in Ilusionista 1957-62, Quatro Ases 1975-77, & correspondent for Tacape Mágico (Brazil). ..... [Cam;Wh5]

name: Cathery, Jean-Michel
bio: (Biel, Switzerland: 1 Dec 1948- ) Stage name of Jean-Michel Salz. Amateur debut in 1964. Pro manipulator & illusionist in clubs & the Nock Circus. In 1972 with assistant-wife Catherine toured West Germany, Italy, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, & Switzerland. In 1973 toured Japan & Thailand. With Noch Circus again in 1974 & 1976. In 1977 played Copenhagen & Hamburg. Pet effects: Linking Rings, Ropes, and tricks with doves, dogs, & a crocodile. [Win;Al]

name: Catiller, Fred[erick L.], MIMC
bio: (Newport, Kentucky: 10 Dec 1912-17 Jan 2001) Son of a vaudevillian. Salesman. Semi-pro stage & close-up since age 32. Moved to southern California in 1962. Joined the Magic Castle in 1968. MIMC 1987. [Monti;LR9/2000;Mag]

name: Cattarius, Eva
bio: (Hindenburg, Upper Silesia, Germany [now Zabrze, Poland]: 30 Sep 1942- ) Pro partner-wife of Manfred Cattarius as "Les Cattarius".

name: Cattarius, Manfred
bio: (Spiesen, Germany: 15 Jan 1939-) Pro since 1967 with doves, rabbits, cats, & manipulations with cards, cigarettes, & coins while wearing gloves. 1975 MZvD 2nd prize in general magic; 1978 German championship in general magic. Played the Paris Olympia in 1970s. Billed with partner-wife Eva as "Les Cattarius". Prominent lecturer. [Win;Mül;Nad]

name: Caulk, William B.
bio: (USA: 1860-) Taxidermist in Terra Haute, Indiana. Semi-pro magician as "Prof. William Benjamin" with stage magic & spirit cabinet. Articles (all under real name) in Hopkins (1897), The Rover Magazine for Young Readers (Chicago: Oct-Dec 1899 & Jan-Feb 1900), and Mahatma (1903).

name: Causyn, Jacques
bio: (France: fl.1960s-90s) Aka "Mystrias". Several prizes in AFAP competitions. Chief editor of Le Journal de la Prestidigitation 1966-?. Chief editor of L'Illusioniste. Contributer to Les Cahiers de la Magie. Noted apparatus collector. [Bou;Mer]

name: Cautares, John [Jean?]
bio: (France: fl.late 1500s) Amateur? Moved to London where in the early 1580s he gave sleight-of-hand lessons to Reginald Scot & probably others.

name: Cavalli, Mario [Humberto]
bio: (Langenthal, Switzerland: 3 Oct 1959-) Learned at age 13. Aka "Carambo" until reverted to own name. Semi-pro since 1980 with partner Veronique Schorer in stage act with bubbles. Won 1986 Austrian Congress (Seefeld) 1st prize in stage magic, 1986 French Congress (Bordeaux) 1st prize in stage magic, & 1987 Monte Carlo Golden Wand. Pro since 1988. [Wh5]

name: Caveney, Michael "Mike", MIMC
bio: (Arcadia, California: 17 Jun 1950- ) Pro stand-up magician, initially mainly with trade shows. Joined Johnson Products as part-time consultant in 1972. Married mime-magicienne Tina Lenert in 1979. Publisher of major magic books in Pasadena since 1980, first as "Magical Publications" then since c1993 as "Mike Caveney's Magic Words". Toured in 1980 with the Richiardi show. Wrote Magicomedy (1981, 171pp), The Great Leon (1987, 133pp), Carter the Great (1995, 375pp), etc. 1988 Henry Ridgely Evans History Award; 1991 Dragon Award (jointly to Mike & Tina); 1996 Christopher Award for Literature. [Bo#192;Se]

name: Cavett, Dick
bio: (Gibbon, Nebraska: 19 Nov 1936-) Learned from magic books & tutored by Eugene Gloye. Semi-pro at age 14 with local shows in Lincoln. 1952 IBM Best New Performer trophy for his silk-thru-ring & cut rope routine. Of this performance Melbourne Christopher wrote: "He had a fine sense of timing and excellent stage presence." Turned to radio & TV work as a star talk-show host. Then, as amateur magician, took lessons from Slydini. Remains an avid hobbyist. Host of many TV magic specials. Memoirs are Cavett (1974) & Eye on Cavett (1983). [MM6/83; HMM7/52]

name: Cazeneuve, Le Commandeur Bernard-Marius
bio: (Toulouse, France: 12 Oct 1839-12 [sic] Apr 1913) Inspired by seeing Bosco in 1852. Pro stage magician since 1854. Pet effects: Card tricks, the Egg Bag, Second Sight (by 1877), Giant Memory, the Box Trick (by 1876), and the Vanishing Bird & Cage. Toured France (1863), Russia (1865), Turkey (1866), Italy (1869), Spain (1872), USA (1876-77), possibly Australia (1877-78), France (1878), Portugal (1885), Madagascar (1886), etc. Taught his niece & later assistant, "Reine de Solange". Memoir is A la cour de Madagascar: magie et diplomatie (1896); English tr by Ben Robinson as A Magician in Madagascar (in progress, 1989). Bio is F. de Montandon, Aventures de Cazeneuve (Nice: 1864). Subject of Pierre Benoit's novel, Le Commandeur (1959). [Dif;Mo;Pr;Vo55;Wal]

name: Cazman, Henri
bio: (Paris: 1864-2 [or 9?] Feb 1917) Stage name of Richard Henry T. Plumb. Moved with his father to England in 1867 at age 3. Pro illusionist who flourished in 1890s, playing the London Empire in 1891. World tour. [Pr]

name: Cecil, Harry [E.]
bio: (USA: 1889-1964) Chocolate manufacturer in Detroit. Semi-pro comedy magician since 1903. Toured abroad in WWI with a YMCA unit, doing a magic act framed for him by S.S. Henry. Active in the IBM, founding & chairing its Sick and Convalescent Committee since 1934. Wrote Magic that Perks (1937, 72pp). Column in Tops (since 1936).

name: Cedric
bio: See: Richardson, Cedric R.

name: Ceillier, Prof Dr Rémi[-Louis-Marie-Joseph]
bio: (Rennes, France: 23 Dec 1883-21 Apr 1943) Science teacher in Paris. Amateur magician as "Professeur Boscar", specialized in manipulation. Collector of documents on members of the ASAP. Wrote Les Principes psychologiques et techniques de l'Illusionisme (1922); as "Boscar", Dix séances d'Illusionisme (1927; new edition 1948), a popular beginner's book with Spanish tr as Juegos de Manos (1931; 1941; 1946); L'Escamotage chez Rabelais (1934); & Manuel Pratique d'Illusionnisme et de Prestidigitation (2 vols, 1935, 1936). This last work was judged at the time by Jules Dhotel to be the best and most nearly comprehensive book on magic. Jean Hugard made a typescript English translation privately for Lloyd Jones, a carbon copy of which is in the Library of Congress. Edited the bi-lingual (French-Spanish) Le Monde Occulte (1924-25, 6 issues). Translated Devant's Secrets of My Magic in 1938. Articles in Illusioniste, Passez-Muscade, Journal de la Prestidigitation, etc. [Dif-Rob1-WWW]

name: Celeste, La
bio: See: Josolyne, Agnes Blanche

name: Cellar, Willi
bio: (Gundelfingen, Germany: 29 Sep 1885- ) Stage name of Willi Keller. Pro since 1906. In variety. Co-founded the Hannover chapter of the German Magic Circle in 1934. [WWM;Roh]

name: Cellini
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Jim Sullivan. Pro street magician in San Francisco (late 1970s-early 80s), New Orleans, New York City (1981), Europe. Works in renaissance garb with gibecière. Pet effects: Linking Rings, Cups-&-Balls, etc. Assistant is "Eileen". Rated best at street magic by Frank Garcia & Mike Rogers.

name: Cellsus, Vernon
bio: See: Wickes, Samuel L. Whittington

name: Cerceda, Adolfo
bio: See: "Corda, Carlos"

name: Cervine, Scott [pronounced sir-VEEN]
bio: (USA: 1962-) Pro stage worker. 1982 AMA Junior Achievement Award. 1985 NY Magic Symposium 1st Prize. 1985 FISM 3rd prize in general magic. Desert Magic Seminar 2nd Prize 1988 & 1992. [Wat]

name: Cervon, Bruce, AIMC [pronounced SIR-von]
bio: (Akron, Ohio: 20 Jun 1941 - 24 May 2007) Stage name of Andrew Bruce Cernava, a grandson of Yugoslav immigrants. Inspired around age 7 when father taught him a one-hand cut. Soon self-taught from Gilbert Mysto Magic set & the card section reprint from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Pro close-up & stand-up magician since 1964 when he moved to Hollywood. 1971 AMA Best Lecturer. AMA Best Close-up Magician 1973, 1976. Expert court witness on gambling. AMA Treasurer 1978-94 & Secretary since 1994. Co-publisher (with Louis Falanga & as successor to Larry Jennings) of L&L Publishing since 1990. Wrote The Real Work: Card Secrets of Bruce Cervon (1976, 64pp), The Cervon File (1987), Ultra Cervon (1990, 186pp, with Stephen Minch), etc. See Mike Maxwell, Bruce Cervon's The Black & White Trick and Other Assorted Mysteries (1989, 151pp), and Stephen Minch, Bruce Cervon: Hard-Boiled Mysteries (1998m 192pp). Produced The Vernon Chronicles (4 vols, 1988-92), including as Vol.4 co-edited (with Keith Burns, He Fooled Houdini: Dai Vernon a Magical Life (1992, 308pp)). Tricks in Genii, Pallbearers, Epilogue, Ibidem, Cardiste, Hierophant, Talisman, Linking Ring, Magic & Spells, Magick, MUM, Richard's Almanac, & in books by others. Bruce Cervon Castle Notebooks (2008, published posthumous). TV segments. 2 audios; 2 videos ("Ultra Cervon). [Genii5/90;Bo#216;Jef;Mag;Wh2]

name: Chabernot
bio: See: Sena, Antonio

name: Chabert, Ivan Ivanitz
bio: (Avignon, France: 10 May 1792-28 Aug 1859) Stage name of Julian Xavier Chabert. Pro with incombustible act 1817-1829 when he first played London & the provinces. Moved to USA in 1831, soon leaving magic to open a drug store in New York City. Died of TB. [Jay;Daw]

name: Chadwick, Bruce
bio: (Midland, Texas: 7 Jun 1958-) Learned at age 8 by father's birthday gift of a few tricks. BA in religion & MAs in theater arts & religion. Pro apparatus maker & mail-order dealer (Magic by Bruce Chadwick) in Fort Worth, Texas, since 1980. Performs stand-up, stage, & illusion magic. TAOM President 1987-88. Wrote The 1988 TAOM Convention: A History of Its Planning and Execution and several manuals on Gospel Magic. Articles in Linking Ring & Second Sight. [Wh2]

name: Chahin, Alain
bio: (France: 1941-) Semi-pro magician specialized in general magic, kid shows, & close-up as "Alain le Magicien". Collector. Wrote Petit Lexique Magique: Anglais-Français-Américain (1973). [Bou2]

name: Chakras, Raja Lou
bio: See: Brinkfort, Louis

name: Chalon
bio: See: McCafferty, LeRoy

name: Chalon [misspelling]
bio: See: Châlons

name: Châlons [pronounced shah-LAWN]
bio: (France: 1789-1825) Aka "The Swiss Conjuror". Pro by 1816 in Paris. Played London theaters in 1820-21. NOTE: Often misspelled "Chalon". [Fr;Cl;St]

name: Chambers, [Francis T.] "Frank
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 12 Nov 1924-) Learned at age 10 from magic set. Engineering manager, now retired in Republic of Ireland. Amateur close-up magician. Articles in Genii & Magic Circular. [Wh2]

name: Chambers, Lloyd W.
bio: (Clearwater, Kansas: 19 May 1906-15 Jan 1960) Demonstrator-employee with Thayer's in Los Angeles 1934-41. US Navy officer 1942-45. Dealer (Chambers Mfg Company) in Kansas (Topeka, then Wichita/Clearwater) in 1946-59. Wrote Original Ideas in Magic (1941, 26pp). When he died his large collection of Thayer magic was bought by Joe Stevens.

name: Chambly, E.
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 31 Aug 1863 [or 30 Aug 1871]-15 Jan 1926) Stage name of E. Jakobus Wunnink. Pro illusionist. Toured Europe. Later, around 1890, taking over the business of Oscar E. Lischke, became a prop maker in Hamburg. On his death, the business passed to Carl Willmann. [Al;St;Dif]

name: Chammas, Dr.
bio: (Brazil?: -30 Jul 1958) Stage name of Chafik Chammas. Lived in Brazil where toured as a pro magician. [Fam]

name: Chams, Mago
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 11 Dec 1927- ) Stage name of Oscar VIVANCO BARCELÓ since 1960. Learned in 1951 from magic shop tricks. Pro general magic since 1960, specializing in livestock effects. Proprietor of magic school (Casa Mago Chams) in Mexico City 1961?-present. [Wh2]

name: Chan Wing
bio: See: Cramer, Stuart

name: Chandéri, François
bio: (France: fl.1710s) Aka "Siamois". Pro cups-and-balls in 1713 at the Paris fairs of St.-Germain & St.-Laurent. [St;Cl]

name: Chandler, Claude, MIMC
bio: (Britain: 12 Nov 1896-10 May 1977) Pro magus-vent-actor after WW I. Worked both private parties & variety theaters. Presented Devant's "Revue of Magic" at St. George's Hall in 1922 & had other engagements there. As vent worked his original "On the Bust" drunk act with a plaster sculptured head. Often played "Abanazar" in the Aladdin pantomime. Possible inventor of Card in Balloon. Father of "The Magical Claudine". Vice-President, The Magic Circle, 1958-77. [St;Wat; A-B-C of Magic Sets#12]

name: Chandler, Harold [Sydney]
bio: (New Zealand: 1909-30 Dec 1992) Aka "Chandu". Pro stage magician and prop maker. Wrote Lets Make Magic (n.d.; 2nd ed rev, 1970, 34pp as Chandu's Magical Varieties). Founding-editor Magicana 1953-55. Waikato Magic Circle's 1989 Grand Master of Magic award (New Zealand). Contributor to Magicana. [Magicana#157,#221,#238]

name: Chandler, Ken[nard Hall]
bio: (Rochester, New York: 3 Jan 1951-) Learned at age 26 working as respiratory therapist with ill children. Pro mentalism, close-up, & comedy magic. Works as both "Chandler & Company" & a single as "The Amazing Chandler". Pet effects: Metamorphosis, Neilsen Cage, Key Bending, Q&A, etc. PEA President 1989-present. Wrote With a Little Help from My Friend (1986) & Profitable Magic Pure and Simple (1987). Articles in Vibrations. [Wh2]

name: Chandra
bio: See: Harto, James S.

name: Chandu
bio:
Chandler, Harold

[See also: Briggs, J. Albert]

name: Chang
bio: (Panama City, Panama: 2 Dec 1889-29 [sic] Apr 1972) Stage name of Juan Pablo Jesorum, son of a  $ \frac{1}{2} $ Spanish- $ \frac{1}{2} $ Indian father & a 3-fourths Spanish- $ \frac{1}{4} $ Chinese mother. Learned as assistant-interpreter to The Great Raymond 1907-c1910 with whom he did a world tour in 1908. Then on own as "The Great Pablo" until 1913. Thence as "Li-Ho-Chang" with a pseudo-Chinese act until 1935 after which he continued it as "Chang". Pro illusionist with large full-evening show. Toured all 6 continents, beginning in 1921. Mainly worked Latin America where he was David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg's main competitor. Otherwise toured USA (c1928, 1932, c1939, &1953), Southern Africa, India, Burma, Southeast Asia, China, Portugal (1938, 1947, 1953, 1954), Spain (1938, 1947-49, 1954), Australia (1938-39), Philippines (1939), & Angola (1956). A millionaire from his magic & his movie business in Panama. Died in Mérida, Mexico. NOTE: His death was prematurely announced in 1971 in a Variety obit that was dutifully copied by Linking Ring. [Pr;Bam;Wal;St;Fu;Ch;HMM8/58]

name: Chan-In
bio: See: Chanin, Jack

name: Chanin, Jack
bio: (Kremenchug, Ukraine, Russian Empire: 15 Jan 1907-9 Nov 1997) Moved to USA at age 15. Inspired at age 17. Preferred manip magic. Did a pseudo-oriental act as "Chan-In" & "Chan-Jak". Pro dealer ("Chanin's Studio of Magic") in Philadelphia 1930-81 when retired & sold to Rick Matevish. Also worked in 1932 as main assistant in Bill Brema's shop in Philadelphia. 1983 AMA Creative Fellowship. Invented Miracle Shoe Lace (by 1941), Color Changing Shoe Lace (by 1941), Your Card, Please (by 1941), Katch-O-Kard (1950), Wool It (1952), etc. Wrote 9 booklets: Seven in One (1928), The Three Shell Game (1934, 8pp), Hello, Sucker! (1934; 2nd ed rev 1948, 80pp), Jaysee Silk Color Change Supreme (1936, 10pp), Cigar Manipulation (1937, 80pp), Grand Finale: or Silks at Your Fingertips (1937, 13pp), Further Adventures of the Seven in One (1938, 15pp), Handle with Gloves (1941, 26pp), & Encyclopedia of Sleeving (1947, 81pp). Column in Linking Ring. Bio is David E. Haversat, Chanin: The Man With The Magic Hands (2002). [Th;HMM10/53;Des]

name: Chanti
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s-20s) Stage name of Tom McDermott. Minor music hall magus and quick-change artist by 1906-07 when he played Australia to 1912. Sometimes billed as "The Danish Marvel". Moved to USA where continued to work. Retired by 1950s when worked as night watchman at an off-Times Square TV theater. Father of George Chanti. [HMM4/53,5/53;Wal]

name: Chanti, George
bio: (At sea: 1907- ) Stage name of George McDermott. Born of British parents. Revived his father's quick-change act. Played Australia in 1945. [Wal]

name: Chaos, Dr.
bio: See: Kelly, George Marquis

name: Charles
bio:
$ ^{} $Charles, Lance (Walnut Grove, Minnesota: 20 Oct 1910-1 Feb 1993) Stage name of Charles E. Lantz. Invented plunger rising cards in 1933. Practiced law in hometown 1937-late 1980s. Semi-pro magician since age 13. Wrote Tricks for the Few (1933) & Magic for the Few. IBM President 1974-75.

[See also: Silber, Charles]

name: Charlier, Fernando
bio: (USA?: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro card magician. Toured the American mid-West (1890s), Norway, & Britain (1902). [Magic5/02]

name: Charra, Albert
bio: (France: fl.1960s-80s) Close-up magician & mentalist in Grenoble. Aka "Burt Deck". AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Silver Medal 1989. [Bou2] Charles, Jon Trick in Arcane.

name: Chase, N[athaniel] E.
bio: (USA: fl.1850s-60s) Pro prop maker in Pittsfield, New Hampshire, 1851-1866. Father of C. Milton Chase.

name: Chaudhuri, Tony
bio: (India?: c1955-) Interested by age 16. Pro close-up magus in Ann Arbor, Michigan, with table hopping & kid shows. Wrote Bedazzled (1977). Tricks in Swami & Mantra.

name: Chavigny, Jean
bio: (Blois, France: fl.1940s-60s) ..... Wrote Le roman d'un artiste: Robert-Houdin (1943, 183pp; 2nd ed, 1969). "Chef, The Magic" SEE: Koch, Paul W.

name: Chen, Juliana
bio: (Hunan, China: fl.1990s) Stage name of CHEN Zhi-Ling. Pro. 1992 Grand Champion of China; 1992 IBM winner; 1996 Congress Nacional de Magio Grand Prix; 1996 Magic Hands Competition winner; 1997 FISM in Manip. [Wh01]

name: Cheniu, Paul
bio: (France: fl.1860s-80s) Pro. In 1868 Robert-Houdin wrote: "I have seen this sleight [sleeving] performed by M. Paul Chenu, a friend of mine with a special fancy for the magic art, who used to execute it with such rare skill that, however tight might be the sleeve, he would have succeeded, I verily believe, in shooting the coin up it." See Robert-Houdin, The Secrets of Conjuring and Magic (1868/1977 tr), 59. Played the Théâtre Robert-Houdin sometime during its ownership by Méliès, that is, after 1888. NOTE: Surname might be "Chelu". [check Dif .....] +Chesbro, Verne for "1970" read "1960"

name: Cha'Peau
bio: (Stuttgart, West Germany: 20 May 1962-) Stage name of Roland Schopp. Comedy quick-change with magic act. Also chapeaugraphy. 1978 German champion in general magic; 1987 MZvD 1st prize in comedy magic; 1988 FISM 2nd prize in comedy magic.

name: Chapender, Martin
bio: (Liverpool, England: 1 Jun 1879-9 Feb 1905) Stage name of Harold Martin M. Jones. Inspired by seeing T. Nelson Downs. Brilliant pro manipulator. Invented Gloves to Dove in 1904. Trick in Mahatma. Died of a brain abcess (meningitis). Inspired formation of The Magic Circle, which originally considered naming itself after Chapender. [Daw#99-199;Pr;Go2;Vo56;La2;Bur]

name: Chaple, Ken
bio: (fl.1960s) Invented Popsy-Pegs.

name: Chaplin, Sir Charles [Spencer] "Charlie
bio: (London, England: 16 Apr 1889-25 Dec 1977) Moved to USA in 1910 with a vaudeville troupe. Film star as "Charlie Chaplin" since 1914. Magic buff, having been taught his first trick by his magically inclined older half-brother, Sydney. Autobio is My Autobiography (1964). A good bio is David Robinson, Chaplin: His Life and Art (1985).

name: Chapman, Frank[lin M.]
bio: (USA: 1902-15 Jul 1954) Inspired at age 10. Advertising executive & semi-pro magician. Editor-publisher Chap's Scrapbook 1938-40 (reprinted 1978). Wrote several booklets, including Ten Stunners with a Nail Writer & Twenty Stunners with a Nail Writer (1944, 27pp). Articles & columns for Sphinx & Genii. [Th]

name: Chappell, Lynette
bio: (Mombasa, Kenya: c1954-) Stage name of Coleen Forsyth. Daughter of a British engineer. During the Mau-Mau Rebellion, moved with parents to Rhodesia. Trained as a dancer in London, returned to East Africa where she was introduced to magic in 1964 when hired by John Calvert for his second tour of Kenya. Later, as a dancer with the Lido de Paris, brought to Las Vegas where soon hired by Siegfried & Roy, for whom she is now their featured principal assistant and personal coordinator. Became US citizen in 1988. [Genii1/83]

name: Char
bio: See: Vorobiev, Alexander

name: Charell
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 15 Mar 1934-) Stage name of Gert Thiemann. Pro comedy patter & manip magician in East Germany since 1954. Played the East Berlin Friedrichstadtpalast in 1970. TV bits. [Win]

name: Charke, Charlotte
bio: (England: 1713-1760) Youngest & detested tomboy daughter of Colley Cibber (1671-1757), the noted British actor, theater manager, & playwrite. Married Richard Charke, a violinist, at age 16. Worked, successively, as a stage actress, actress with strolling players, a puppet-master, performer at fairs, tavern-keeper in Drury Lane, and a conjuror's assistant in Petticoat Lane, the first recorded female in that role. A notable London character, her autobio is A Narrative of the Life of Mrs. Charlotte Charke (1755). Charlemagne the Magician (USA: fl.1960s) Stage name of Charles Linn. Pro.

name: Charles, Prince
bio: (London, England: 14 Nov 1948- ) The Prince of Wales was inspired by & learned magic in 1956. Member of the Magic Circle since 1975 as MIMC with Gold Star no less. Bio is Anthony Holden, Prince Charles (1979).

name: Charles, Jon
bio: (Bedfont, Middlesex, England: 3 Mar 1936-) Stage name of Charles Robert Chamberlain. Learned at age 9 or 10 from magic set. Moved to Edmonton, Canada, in 1967. Industrial engineer, later hospital administrator. Semi-pro close-up & stand-up comedy magician, table hopping at Japanese Village Restaurant since 1978. In 1985 became full-time table-hopper. Trick in Arcane. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Charles, Kirk
bio: (Norman, Oklahoma: 23 Nov 1947-) Introduced to & learned magic in 1960 when father took him to a Miami magic shop. Pro close-up & comedy magic since 1976, initially as "The Wiz" 1976-77, thence under own name. Also writes & produces several one-man theater pieces involving bizarre magick. Since 1980 has lived in Seattle where he does restaurant magic. Wrote Improv Magic (1977); Tricked; Tips on Table Hopping (1981); Manual of Restaurant Magic (1987), which Lorraine (among others) rates "best" on the subject; & Standing Up Surrounded (1990, 94pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Invocation, & Magic Menu. Audio (1990). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Charles, L. [pronounced SHARLS]
bio: (France: fl.1810s-20s) Pro vent-magus. Toured France, Britain (1813-29), & the USA (1819, 1821). [Cl;Mo]

name: Charles, Lance
bio: (Walnut Grove, Minnesota: 20 Oct 1910-1 Feb 1993) Stage name of Charles E. Lantz. Semi-pro magician since age 13. Practiced law in hometown 1937-late 1980s. Wrote Tricks for the Few (1933), where he falsely claimed invention of Lawrence Kam's Plunger Rising Cards; & Magic for the Few. IBM President 1974-75.

name: Charles, Maurice
bio: (England?: fl.1910s-20s) Stage name of Charles Lazzell. Pro. Played St. George's Hall 1918 & 1923.

name: Charlier [pronounced SHAR-lee-ay]
bio: (France?: fl.1870s-80s) Probably a professional card sharp when on the Continent. Around 1873 moved to England where he taught card sleights to Charles Bertram, Professor Hoffmann, Samuel Heilbut (c1880), & others. Worked publicly only once, in London in 1882 with Bertram's show. Invented the Charlie pass & the Charlie System for marking cards. Vanished from London in 1884. Reappeared fictionally as "Mons Ledoyen" in Hoffmann's novel, Conjurer Dick (1886). REF: Bertram (1896), 109-115; Ptinos in Midget Magician, V.1, #9-V.4, #2-4. [Cl;Vo56;St] NOTE: I suggest that Charlier was the "D" whom Robert-Houdin describes at length in his autobiography (Ch.XI). Bertram reported that the elderly Charlier said that he'd once had Robert-Houdin as a pupil. And indeed R-H describes a long card session in Paris around 1843 with a young man, presumably French, who claimed to be of good local family and appeared to R-H from his dress and manners to be so. "D" admitted to being a cardsharp and proved himself one of that breed by demonstrating many fine tricks of that trade. These included a system of marking cards similar, possibly identical, to the Charlier System, which Charlier called his "ponctuation"--a clue to his nationality, as that is the French word for punctuation, although he knew several languages before appearing in England.

name: Charlier, Fred
bio: (Leeds?, England: c1890-) Stage name since 1912 of Fred Thorp. Hired in Leeds in 1906 by Walter Jeans who taught him card manip, which he performed originally as "Carl Fredric". Minor pro card manipulator & illusionist.

name: Charl's
bio: (Paris, France: 17 Jul 1888-3 Dec 1942). Stage name of Charles-Albert-Émile Droxler. Student of & successor to Carmelli. Pro with illusions and (with wife "Frélia") mind-reading. Collaborated with Commandeur Piétro. Joined the ASAP in 1921. [Dif;Rob1]

name: Charlton, [Christopher Henry] "Chris", MIMC
bio: (Hanley, England: 27 Mar 1887-27 Nov 1963) Pro debut in 1904, adding his trademark Any-Drink-Called-For bit in 1905. Pro in big-time variety since 1915. In London played the Coliseum in 1927 & 1929, the Palladium in 1931, & the Pavilion in 1933 for 2 weeks. Toured the world, including Australia & New Zealand 1925, France 1929, Germany 1929, USA 1929-30, France 1930, Germany 1930, USA & Canada 1930-31, USA 1931-32, etc, covering 40+ countries. Performed on BBC-TV on 29 Aug 1949. Retired sometime after. Invented the EYE Count in 1940. Trick in Psycho #7 (1953). Gave his fine collection of magic magazines & books to The Magic Circle Library. Silent film (1923). [Pr;Wal;Tay;Ho;La2;WWM;Hudd]

name: Chart. Ralph. MIMC
bio: (Cranleigh, England: 29 Apr 1891-12 Nov 1965) Pro variety stage magic. Under stage names of "Raoul" and "Raoul Chart", posing as "Le Magicien Française" in Belgium & "Raoul, the French Magician" in Britain. Charvet, David [Douglas] [pronounced shar-VAY] (Seattle, Washington: 4 Nov 1961-) Learned magic c1968 from Kool-Aid magic set & library books. Ex-photographer. Pro illusion builder & collector since 1980. Chief stage assistant & stage manager to Stan Kramien 1984-present plus doing own shows & lectures. Wrote Jack Gwynne (1986, 297pp), a good biography that won the John U. Zweers Scholarship Award; Kramien (1989); The Bill in Lemon Book (1990, 70pp) on Jarrow; & The Great Virgil (1991, 250pp). Articles in MUM, Genii, & Magic. Host of local radio & TV series. [Wh2]

name: Chasan
bio: See: Nicol, Charles Albert

name: Chase, C[harles] Milton
bio: (Pittsfield, New Hampshire: 16 Dec 1851-30 Apr 1928) Son of N.E. Chase. Pro dealer & prop-maker in Boston since 1866 when he took over his father's business to become the 1st in the USA to devote the business exclusively to magic. In 1882 bought Adams & Co. His mail-order shop (not open to the public) catered to such major magi as William Robinson, Harry Keller, & Alexander Herrmann (for whom he invented the "Yakayo" illusion). Ill, he sold his shop in 1910 to Ducrot. Died in Boston. His collection wasn't sold (at private auction) until 1994. [Albo95; Mahatma11/1899]

name: Chassino
bio: (France: 9 Apr 1869-27 Jan 1955) Stage name of Éléonor Chassin. Pro since 1888 as shadowist (working with his feet) & imitator of bird calls. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1906. Toured USA 1905-14 & 1920-26. Retired in 1926 in France. [Dif]

name: Chaude, Marius A[ndre]
bio: (New York City, NY: 7 Apr 1877-18 Apr 1941) Pro comedy-dialect & straight magic. Aka "Silent Maurice". 3 world tours. [SAM]

name: Chaudet, [Louis William] "Bill" [pronounced shaw] DAY
bio: (Hollywood, California: 19 Nov 1921- ) Tutored by adopted uncle Blackstone for 2 weeks every year since 1930. Toured with the Blackstone show 1946 & 1947 as assistant & understudy. Then on own since 1948, doing comedy magic (with successive assistant-wives Ruth & Jana), close-up, & a pickpocket act. Works fairs, amusement parks, trade shows, conventions, & cruise ships. Invented Mike Suspension & Sub Telephone Booth. Articles in Genii, Conjurers Magazine, Tops, & MUM. Magic adviser on many TV series & 2 movies. TV bits. [Mag;Tay;Wh2]

name: Chaudeur
bio: (France: fl.1710s) Pro cups-and-balls. Worked the Saint-Laurent Fair in 1713.

name: Chavez, Benito "Benny" "Ben
bio: (Ormok, Leyte, Philippines: 1901-Nov 1962 [sic]) Moved to USA in 1920. Pro magician since 1922. Played vaude circuits in 1930s with wife Marian. They toured Canada (1936 & 1939) & Australia (1939). Magic teacher as co-founder (with Marian) in 1941 of the Chavez Studio of Magic. In 1946 it became the only magic course accredited by the G.I. Bill. In 1951 moved the studio to Hollywood. [Genii12/62; Vue12/50; Wal; Tay]

name: Chavez, Marian
bio: (Nebraska, USA: 27 Oct 1909-Nov 1978) Married Benito Chavez in 1932. Pro with him on vaude circuits in 1930s. Co-founder in 1941 (since 1962 sole owner) of Chavez Studio of Magic. On her death, the school passed to Neil Foster & Dale Salwak. Wrote Home Study Course in Prestidigitation and Showmanship (17 lessons, 1960-62, 530pp) & dove magic book in 1968. 1973 AMA Special Fellowship. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Marion". [Wal]

name: Cheer, "Professor" Charles "Chas." "Charlie
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Pro stage & circus comedy magician. Living in Seattle in 1942 when joined bandleader Benny Meroff's "Funzafire" show together with Jack Gwynne. Invented Professor Cheer's Comedy Rope Trick by 1945. [HMM12/58] "Chef, The Magic" SEE: Koch, Paul W.

name: Chefalo, Magdalena "Magda
bio: (Italy?: -12 Feb 1939) Born Magdalena Capretta Palermo. In USA in 1910 became assistant to Raffaele "Chefalo" Cefalo whom she soon married. Performed with him as "Capretta & Chefalo" in the USA in 1910. Changed permanently to "Palermo & Chefalo" when they toured England later that same year. [Pr]

name: Chefalo, Ralph
bio: (Bonito, Sicily, Italy: 8 Apr 1885-3 Jun 1963) Stage name of Raffaele Cefalo. Moved with parents at age 12 to Boston where he learned magic as a teenager. Debut at age 14. Pro sleight-of-hand & illusions, his 20-ring Linking Ring routine being famous. Toured England (1910, 1913 or 14, 1930, & c1939), South America, Portugal (1914, 1915, & 1929), Spain, Canary Islands (1917), Australia (1926 & 1933), & Latin America (1938-39). Carrying a large troupe, he had two successive principal assistants, both of whom he married. The first, Magdalena, worked with him as "Capretta" (in 1910) & "Palermo" (1910-39). The second, also named Magdalena, he married around 1940. They chose to remain and work in Nazi-held Europe during WW II. Played Holland (1948), Portugal (1948, 1954, & 1955), & Argentina (1963). In 1963 on tour in South Korea he died in Seoul. NOTE: His given name is often misspelled. [Pr;Sil;St;Ch;Go;Go2;Wal;Dif]

name: Chelman, Christian
bio: (Belgium: fl.1980s-90s) Close-up & bizarre magick. See Mad Magic #45 (1983) for an all-Chelman issue. Wrote Capricornian Tales (128pp).

name: Chen Kai
bio: (Herida, Yucatan, Mexico: 30 Aug 1939- ) Stage name of Julio HIJUELOS CERVERA. Learned at age 13 from magic book. Architect in Mexico City. Part-time pro stage magician since 1960, specialized in livestock act with doves & wildcats. Co-founded 3 Mexican magic clubs, including the Circulo de Magos Mexicanos (IBM Ring 164) in 1965. Several awards, including 1963 TAOM Best Foreign Act & 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. Articles in CEDAM, Adair's Encyclopedia of Dove Magic, etc. TV performer in Mexico 1960-89. [Wh3]

name: Cheong, [Charles] "Charlie
bio: (China: fl.1960 working in Hong Kong by ct & his 3

name: Chesbro, Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Nephew of Verne Chesbro. Post Office worker. Semi-pro bartender-magician. Invented Coin in Lighter (in late 1970s). Wrote The Tipnician (1982, 64pp; French tr 1984 by Vollmer).

name: Chesbro, [Forest] Verne
bio: (North Adams, Massachusetts: 9 Jan 1913-) Inspired & learned around age 10 by gift of a box of tricks. Debut at age 15 in high school with a ½-hour act. Pro. Wrote Tricks You Can Count On (1960, 36pp, with Larry West; repr). Uncle of Bob Chesbro. [Th]

name: Chevalier, Albert
bio: (Nottingham, London, England: 21 Mar 1861-) Pro actor since age 16. Well-known comedian in Britain. Amateur magician. Played Abanazar in Aladdin in 1888. Magic Circle member since 1908. Autobio is Before I Forget (1901). [MC1/89] Chevalier, Louis [pronounced sheh-VAL-yeah] (France: fl. late 1800s) Pro dealer in Paris. [Vo55]

name: Chevalier Noir, Le
bio: See: Simonson, Nils

name: Chezaday
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 23 May 1966-) Stage name of Steve[n Joseph] Cesare since 1974 when he learned from friend's magic set. Part-time pro "rock illusionist" since 1984. Features (since 1988) his 6-foot python, "Monty". Three SAM & Abbott's competition prizes 1984 & 1988. Invented Any Way You Slice It (1988) & Other Side of the Mirror (1989). TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Chicot
bio: See: Sargent, Epes W.

name: Chin Sun Loo
bio: See: "Hugard, Jean"

name: Ching
bio: ( ? : fl.1950s) Billed as "The Oriental Mystifier", working in full dress suit. Pro manip with cards, candles, & Zombie. Toured Canada in 1952 & the USA in 1954. [Tay]

name: Ching, Chang Yeh
bio: (China: fl.c.1960s) Top pro illusionist in Taipeh, Formosa.

name: Ching Lau Lauro
bio: (Cornwall?, England: fl.1810s-1830s) Probably the stage name of a Cornishman surnamed Ching. An equilibrist by 1828, adding magic & vent to his pseudo-Chinese act in England & on the Continent by 1834 to 1839. Aka "Professor Ching", "Mons. Ching", & "M. Ching". Pro. [Fr;Cl;Pr;Magic4/03]

name: Ching Ling Foo
bio: See: FOO Ching Ling

name: Ching Wu
bio: (England: fl.1910s-40s) Stage name of Alfred Banks. Initially a scenic artist. Pro magician since Jun 1918 when he toured the former Chung Ling Soo show with Lou Robinson. Father of "Cingalee" & "Kharkov". Played the Alhambra in Paris in 1919.

name: Chislett, Thomas H[erbert]
bio: (Rotherham, England: 8 Jan 1886-25 Jan 1979) Semi-pro mental magician. Wrote Spirits in the House (1949, 118pp). Tricks in Magic. [WWM]

name: Chmarlovski, Evgueni
bio: (USSR: fl.1980s-90s) Pro magic clown with the Moscow Circus. Features act with a crow, monkey, fox, & rabbit. TV bit in Britain. [Fi2]

name: Chockolate
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 17 Nov 1939-) Pseudonym of Jorge Mancilla. Pro apparatus maker since 1965. Pet effects: Zig-Zag & Crystal Casket. Invented Double (Comedy) Bird Cage 1983. [Wh3]

name: Chop Chop
bio: See: Wheatley, Alvin H.

name: Choriki [or Cho-Rai-Ki]
bio: (China: c1898-) Pro. Lived 40 years in Japan. Toured USA in 1930s. Pet effects: Water Bowl Production & Kuma Tubes. [Dif] "Chris -- The Magician" SEE: Agnoly, Christian Natale

name: Christ, Henry T.
bio: (USA: 1903-13 Sep 1972) Advertising executive (?). Amateur cardman. Invented the Christ force in 1934 & Dead Man's Hand in 1937. Tricks in Jinx.

name: Christenberry Jr, Earle J[ohn]
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 5 Mar 1927- ) Inspired in 1946 seeing a magician in Army show. Court reporter in New Orleans. Amateur close-up & magic historian in New Orleans. IBM President 1973-74. IBM Medallion of Honor 1993. Authored The History of Magic Wall Calendar (1988 & 1990). Articles & tricks in Linking Ring. [LR8/93;Wh2]

name: Christianer, Louis F.
bio: (USA: -1929) Pro. Co-owner (with Floyd Thayer) of Thayer & Christianer's The Magic Shop of the West in Los Angeles 1912-16. Invented the card sandwich in 1917. Wrote at least 14 booklets: Effective Tricks, Effective Card Tricks (16pp), More Effective Card Tricks (24pp), Modern Magical Effects, Magical Notions (20pp), New Magical Conceptions (20pp), String Tricks (16pp), More Effective Tricks, An Effective Coin Act (16pp), Cigarette Tricks, Domino Deceptions, Modern Ventroloquism, Club and Stage Patter, & Original Deceptions (1919, 24pp).

name: Christman, Edward
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Aka "Chris the Sailor Cartoonist". Pro magician-cartoonist. [Dor]

name: Christoph
bio: (Germany?: 28 Feb 1944-) Stage name of Mieritz Christoph. Billed with assistant as "Christoph & Lou". 1981 MZvD 1st prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Christoph, Bruno
bio: (Neu-Weissensee, near Berlin, Germany: 1 Sep 1892-11 Aug 1964) Student of Henri Maletzki. Pro comedy manipulator. In 1930s toured variety theaters throughout Europe from Oslo to Istambul & from London to Moscow. In 1943 was forbidden by the Berlin police to perform because of his anti-State attitude. After WW II in East Germany where he died in Berlin. [Win]

name: Christopher, Brian
bio: See: Mignosa, Chuck

name: Christopher, Frank
bio: (USA: -29 Apr 1921) Pro vaudeville magician.

name: Christopher, Milbourne "Chris
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 23 Mar 1914-17 Jun 1984) Inspired & learned at age 6 by amateur father showing a string trick. Lessons in teens from Ernest Marx. Pro since 1933. Toured Europe 1937. Used pen name "Frank Joglar" for news column in Hugard's Magic Monthly since 1949. Edited M-U-M 1951-1956. On 27 May 1957 he presented the world's first TV network magic special, "The Festival of Magic", a 90-minute show for NBC-TV. SAM President 1957-58. Edited Hugard's Magic Monthly 1959-61. President of Magic Collectors Association 1959-62 & 1964-65. 1972 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1976 AMA Best Lecturer. SAM Hall of Fame. Prominent exposer of occult fraud. Invented Stretching a Rope (1933), the Bend Away Steal (1950), TV Production Box (Apr 1951), Forgetful Freddie (Jun 1951), High Sign (Dec 1951), & the Vanishing Card Case. His fine collection of magic books totals over 4,000 titles, including many antiquarian & rare works. His widow, Maurine, as curator of The Milbourne Christopher Collection, is now arranging for its use by appropriate scholars. A catalog of the 1,118 books from 1589 to 1900 is The Milbourne Christopher Library (1994). Wrote several major historical books, including Panorama of Prestidigitators (1956, 44pp), Panorama of Magic (1962, 216pp), Houdini: The Untold Story (1969, 281pp; paperback repr 1976, 334pp), ESP, Seers & Psychics (1970, 268pp), The Illustrated History of Magic (1973, 452pp), Mediums, Mystics & the Occult (1975, 273pp), Houdini: A Pictorial Life (1976, 218pp), & Milbourne Christopher's Magic Book (1977, 240pp; paperback repr 1979, 216pp). Also wrote several booklets, including Stretching a Rope (1938, 13pp), Tips on Tricks (1941, 25pp), More Tips on Tricks (20pp), Magic at Your Finger Tips (1947, 46pp, with Hen Fetsch), 50 Tricks with a Thumb Tip (1948, 23pp), Conjuring with Christopher (1949, 71pp), Cig-Card Tricks (1949, 8pp), One Man Mental Magic (1952, 11pp), 100 Tips on Tricks (1953, 41pp), Varied Deceptions (1953, 152pp), More One-Man Mental Magic (1954, 15pp), & Panorama of Prestidigitators (1956, 44pp). Columns in Hugard's Magic Monthly (since 1949) & Linking Ring. Many articles & tricks in Sphinx, New Phoenix, Genii, Conjuriana, Gen, Magic Cauldron, Epilogue, etc. [Se;Wat;NT4/61;Fu2;St;Th]

name: Chu, “George” Wang Yu
bio: (China: 1906-24 Apr 1994) Pro in Shanghai in 1930s. Moved to Hong Kong where in 1939 became the main dealer in Hong Kong (Chu's Magic Studio). Opened a branch in Taiwan in 1974. Father of Peter CHU & CHU Pak Kwan. [Abra #2520]

name: CHU Pak Kwan
bio: (China: fl.1950s-90s) Founder-owner of Hong Kong mail order Magic Studio (now Kwan's Magic) since 1952.

name: Chu, Peter
bio: (Hong Kong: fl.c.1960s-70s) Son of George Chu & younger brother of CHU Pak Kwan. Pro magician, working in Western style in Hong Kong.

name: Chu Chin Fu
bio:
Chudleigh, Reginald A. (Forest Gate, London, England: 19 Feb 1888-) Aka "Valentine Presto". Semi-pro close-up. [Go2]

[See also: Sitta, Alberto]

name: Chung, Dr.
bio: See: Vernon, Dai

name: Chung Ling Soo
bio: See: Robinson, William E.

name: Chung Wu
bio: See: McKechnie, Steve

name: Chwałka, Tadeusz
bio: (Rzeszów, Poland: 13 Mar 1933-) Pro illusionist. Aka "Cornelli". Member of MZvD. [Mec;Nad]

name: Cicardi" [pen name]
bio: See: Nielsen, Gene

name: Cielen, James
bio: (Canada: c1966-) While in kindergarten inspired by and learned from a cereal box trick. Amateur since age 10. Pro close-up & dove act. 1988 IBM Gold Medal. 1989 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. [LR10/88]

name: Cimó, Padre Salvatore
bio: (Agrigento, Italy: 29 Feb 1912-22 Jan 1985) Roman Catholic priest. Amateur magician & magic collector. Wrote 15 books, including Enciclopedia Cartomagica (1958, 839pp) & Enciclopedia dell'Illusionismo (7 vols, 1965-73, c2000pp). [Magia Moderna1985]

name: Cingalee
bio: (England: Aug 1966) Stage name of A. Claude Banks, son of Alfred "Ching Wu" Banks & brother of "Kharkov". Pro illusionist with silent pseudo-Chinese act in 1940s-50s. Father of Paula Lee. [Hudd]

name: Cinimod, P.
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Dominic "Dom" Paolino. Pro dealer in Philadelphia.

name: Ciraldon
bio: (USA: 12 May 1884-15 Apr 1946) Stage name of Murray Bliss Butler.

name: Ciré
bio: (Finchley, England: 1895-5 Jul 1982) Stage name of Sydney Charles Musgrave Burton. Originally had a walking robot act. Started magic c1937. Pro magician in 1940s-50s. [Daw2]

name: Cirnoc, P. H.
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Ernest Nurthen. Pro escape artist in Britain as The Cirnocs, the elder of whom was merely the lecturer died in 1903. As "Conreich" failed to get a booking after a trial show at the Oxford Music Hall in London in Jun 1900. Made a poor showing against Houdini in 1900 in both London & Dresden. In 1901 in Essen-Ruhr was arrested as a swindler. Toured Australia in 1903-04, again without success. [Magic8/01]

name: Ciuró [Sureda], Padre R. P. Wenceslao
bio: (Castelltersol, Barcelona, Spain: 1 Mar 1895-21 Apr 1978) Roman Catholic priest since 1917. Prominent amateur magician, aka "Ling-Kai-Fu". A founding member of the A.C.A.I. in Barcelona in 1932. Wrote 13 magic books in Spanish, including Juegos de Sobremesa & Illusionismo Elemental (1954). [Xe;Cam;Dif]

name: Clam
bio: (France: fl.1900s) Pro. Pet effect: The Linking Rings. [Dif]

name: Clare, Janet
bio: (London, England: 25 Jul 19- ) Learned at age 14 by joining Student Section of London Society of Magicians. Tutored by Ken Brooke & Roy Johnson. Executive secretary in London. Semi-pro close-up & cabaret magicienne since 1970. President London Society of Magicians. [Wh2]

name: Clarence, H. G.
bio: (England: fl.1870s-90s) Aka "Professor Nunez", "Professor Nunc-Nunez". Minor pro, mainly as a London society magician. Played the London Crystal Palace in the 1870s. Toured Portugal (including Lisbon) in 1886. [Pr]

name: Clark, [Elbert V.] "Bert
bio: (USA: c1875-4 Feb 1955) Mechanic & since 1908 a locksmith. Befriended Houdini by challenging him with handcuffs. Thence often assisted Houdini prepare his escapes. Died in East Providence, Rhode Island. [HMM3/55;Silver]

name: Clark, [Robert Lee] "Bob" "Bobby
bio: (Omaha, Nebraska: 21 Dec 1916-16 Sep 1987) Learned at age 10. Pro since late teens, specializing in manipulative & dove magic. Toured Canada in 1942. Wrote Magic Sleightly Done (1954). Tricks in Modern Magi. [Tay]

name: Clark, Keith
bio: (Alsace-Lorraine [sic], Germany: 26 Apr 1908-20 Apr 1979) Stage name since 1926 of Pierre Feyss, of French parentage. Moved to Nice, France, after WW I. Pro since 1926. Aka "Pierre Cartier" (in 1938 & 1972), "Pier Cartier", & "Kepi Clarque" (after 1930s). Pet effects: cigarette manip & the Inertia Trick (eggs in glasses). Played London, USA (1932-35), Australia (1935), & USA (1936-1950s). Returned to France in the 1950s. Authored the classic Encyclopedia of Cigarette Tricks (1937, 308pp, ghosted by J. Hugard; 2nd ed rev 1952, 318pp) with French tr by Sardina (1958, 381pp); Keith Clark's Rope Royale (1942, 14pp, by John Braun); Celebrated Cigarettes (1943, 21pp); & Silks Supreme (1943, 18pp). Charter member of the Club Magique de Paris (IBM Ring 191) 1969. Played Portugal in 1972 (as "Pierre Cartier"). A suicide. NOTE: He sometimes falsely claimed for patriotic reasons to have been born in Nancy, France. [Pr;Wal; LIFE, 7 Apr 1941]

name: Clark, [Alfred] Owen
bio: (Britain: 1877-22 Sep 1929) Aka "Owen" & "Clark". Debut in 1891. Pro illusionist, escapist (with the Substitution Trunk by 1903), shadowist, & chapeaugraphist. Toured a Maskelyne & Devant troupe in Britain (1908), Australia-New Zealand (1908), & USA (twice, including 1912). Played the Paris Alhambra in 1912. Often played St. George's Hall 1909-24. Invented several illusions. [Pr;Wal;Go;Go2;St;Vo56;Magic6/04,12/10]

name: Clark, [Alton Renerick] "Ren", MIMC
bio: (Cross Cut, Texas: 4 Aug 1904-3 May 1991) Inspired as child seeing Willard the Wizard show. Learned at age 12 from catalog & magic shop tricks. Graduated Texas A&M in 1924 with electrical engineering degree. Successively engineer, bank clerk, hotel & club owner, & manufacturer. Amateur close-up & parlour magician as "Ren, the Magician". Also with pseudo-oriental stage act. IBM President 1947-48. Founded TAOM in 1948. His Fort Worth home living/dining rooms have a 12x16 foot stage & convert to 100 seats for magic shows. Articles in Linking Ring. Drafted an autobi-cum-trick book (forthcoming). [MC5/90; Genii6/42; SAM; Wh2]

name: Clark, Robert E.
bio: (Texhoma, Oklahoma: 23 Dec 1907- ) Pro with full-evening show with cards, coins, ropes, etc, as "Clarke the Magician". [WWM]

name: Clark, Tony
bio: (USA: 1 Mar 1966-) Stage name of Antonio Gublet since 1988. Learned at age 6 from deck of TV Magic Cards & made amateur debut at age 13 with dove act in Connecticut. Student of Slydini 1986-87. Won the 1988 SAM stage contest. Pro since 1989 with his original dove & mask act, working Southern California. 1990 Christopher Award for best newcomer in magic. Since 1996 plays a full-evening show at the Lake Tahoe Horizon. Dealer (Tony Clark Productions) in Las Vegas (then Staeline) since late 1990s. Tricks in MUM. 1 audio tape; 3 videos (1996).[MUM11/96;MUM12/93]

name: Clarke, Cyril P.
bio: (London, England: 2 Nov 1894-) Pro manipulator. Toured with Chung Ling Soo, Pooles Myrioramas, & Dr Bodie. Then semi-pro in London. [WWM]

name: Clarke, Dudley [Wrangel]
bio: (Johannesburg, South Africa: 27 Apr 1899-7 May 1974) Raised in England. Taught magic by age 12 by his godfather-uncle Sidney Wrangel Clarke. British Army officer 1916-1947. As a founder in 1940 of the Royal Marine Commandos, he gave them that name. As head of "A Force", the British deception planning & operations section in the Middle East & Mediterranean Theatres 1940-45, he was the most innovative & successful of all British WW II military deceptionists. Headed public opinion research department of the Conservative Central Office, 1948-52. Wrote Golden Arrow (1955, 253pp), an international crime thriller. Director, SECURICOR Ltd. Bio is David Mure, Master of Deception (1980, 284pp). [CA]

name: Clarke, Harry, MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1892-1970) Owned a printing business. Long associated with Harry Stanley's Unique Studio for which he often acted as printer. Wrote Magic (1962, 127pp).

name: Clarke, Jay
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Pro stage magician who also worked a midnight spook show as "Jaclare" as early as 1936 when he played Vancouver. [Tay]

name: Clarke, Maxwell
bio: See: Cole, Leslie

name: Clarke, Sidney W[rangel]
bio: (Stonegrove, England: 19 Jun 1864-12 Jul 1940) Inspired to magic as boy seeing Dr. H.S. Lynn. Barrister. Amateur magician & bibliographer-historian of magic. Edited The Magic Circular 1909-14. Magic Circle council chairman 1924-35. SAM Hall of Fame. Uncle & magic teacher of Brig. Dudley Clarke. Wrote (with Adolphe Blind) The Bibliography of Conjuring: And Kindred Deceptions (1920, 84pp). Wrote the classic 291-page "The Annals of Conjuring" series in Magic Wand 1924-28, of which 4 copies were issued in 1929 as a single volume (reprinted 1983 & 2001). Bio is Edwin A. Dawes, The Barrister in The Circle (1983, 123pp).

name: Clarvis
bio: (Britain: fl.late 1500s) Invented the Flick Book (by 1584). "Claud, The Great" Claudine, The Magical SEE: Williams, Claud (Britain: 23 Jun 1935-) Stage name of Claudine Chandler. Taught by father Claude Chandler. Pro stage act from 1958 until retired in 1971 to marry singer Chester Harriot. [Mar]

name: Claudinet
bio: (Velez-Blanco, Almeria, Spain: 29 Dec 1902-1981) Stage name of Justo TORRECILLAS RUIZ. Moved to Argentina. Performed childrens magic. Wrote Magia Humorística, Las Cartas, Sombras Chinescas, La Varita Mágica, etc. [Xe]

name: Claudio
bio: See: Buff, R. C.

name: Clawson [Jr], [Stanley] Hastings "Hal
bio: (Salt Lake City, Utah: 1874-1912) Pro magician & hypnotist at turn of century. Played Mexico & South America in 1st decade of 1900s. Then managed Will B. Wood in 1908 & F.E. Powell in 1909, both during their South American tours. Died in Philadelphia of delirium tremens. Maternal great uncle of Richard Hatch. Clayton, The Mystic (USA: 24 Oct 1874-) Stage name of Henri [or Henry?] Wilbur. Pro vaudeville mindreader with crystal ball. Partner in 1919 with The Great Leon in their ambitious but short-lived "Famous Oriental Miracle Show". Flourished 1910s-20s.

name: Clément, Guillaume
bio: (Malines, Belgium: 18 Jun 1871-20 Aug 1953) Step-son of Jules Grandsart. Stage debut at age 5. Pro sleight-of-hand magician, chapeaugraphist, shadowgraphist, equilibrist, juggler, etc, as "O'Williams" & "Williams". Married "Miss Walter". Owner-director of his family's travelling Théâtre Grandsart-Courtois 1905-1914. Died in Paris. Article in Illusioniste. [Dif]

name: Clements, Wilton S. "Wil
bio: (Kentucky, USA: Jul 1898-2 Nov 1985) Taught at age 11 by Greensport "Sport" Logsdon, an itinerant magician. Teacher in Chicago since 1936. Semi-pro as "Clem, the Magic Man" & "Wil Staar" with assistant-wife "Janii" (Jane) whom he married c1934. Retired in southern California. Article (with Janii) in Linking Ring (1983). [LR10/84]

name: Clempert, John
bio: (Poltava, Russia: 19 Apr 1878-May 1940) Pro wrestler turned escapist around turn of century, billed in England as "The Man They Cannot Hang" in 1909-1910 when Houdini pressured him into stopping copying his act. [Daw#219;Magic10/09;HMM8/57]

name: Cleopatra
bio: See: Kasfikis, Valeria

name: Cleveland, Dexter
bio: (Spartanburg, South Carolina: 25 Oct 1947-) Learned at age 6 from Xmas magic set. Investor in Spartanburg. Semi-pro magician since age 16 as creative consultant. Collector. Wrote jointly with Rhett Bryson Jr (as "Algonquin McDuff") 3 booklets plus tricks in Linking Ring. Invented Exploding Table (1985). [Wh2]

name: Cleveland, Harry G.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-1930s) Likely a stage name. Resident of Cleveland & Lakewood, Ohio. Invented "Presto Fly" card trick in late 1909 & "You Do As I Do In The Dark" by 1936. Tricks in Magic (1910 & 1911).

name: Clever, Eddie
bio: (Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania: 3 Jul 1904-15 Mar 1975) Stage name of Edward D. Rupp. Inspired by & learned from Keen the Magician while working in a medicine show 1920-24. Thence pro on his own until 1934 when turned semi-pro with magic and, later, mentalism. Invented "Psychic Contact" (by 1928). Co-edited Linking Ring "Parade" 1941-48, then as Editor 1948-c1968. Columns in Tops & Genii. Wrote Thought Wings Onward (86pp). [Th; NJ#22; Zombie5/53; WWM]

name: Cleverman
bio: (Reims, France: 31 Mar 1798-8 Dec 1878 [sic]) Stage name of François Lahire. Pro. Director of

name: Clifford, Jack J.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Stage name of a Mr Ackerman. Did a vaudeville hyp act until switched in the 1930s to doing a Spook Show. Then as "Punjab, India's Royal Illusionist" did straight magic. [Walk2]

name: Clinton, [Francis Wright] "Frank
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 15 May 1899-15 Nov 1988) Learned as child buying tricks from local shop. Debut at age 10 doing charity shows. Real estate examiner in Brooklyn. Semi-pro magician, specialized in general magic & lectures. Aka "Frank Howe". In WW II did USO shows. In 1977 moved to Norfolk, Virginia, where he taught magic. Father of Janet Clinton. [SAM]

name: Clinton, Janet
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: c1941-) Aka "Pixie". Taught by father Frank Clinton. Debut at age 8 on New York TV. Pro comedy & kid show magician. Now (1980s) Mrs Janet C. Goldbach. [Se]

name: Clive, Henry
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: c1881-14 Dec 1960) Stage name of Clive O'Hara, son of a physician. Pro debut in 1900 (in Adelaide). Toured West Australia in 1902 as "Clive the Conjuror" & "Nikola". Moved in 1903 to USA where billed as "Henry Clive, The Debonair Magician". Toured New Zealand briefly in 1905 before returning to USA. Left magic sometime after 1917 to became a commercial artist in Hollywood, doing magazine covers & many film posters. [Wal;Ho;Magic12/00,1/01,9/02,2/03;HMM3/61]

name: Clive, Paul, MIMC
bio: (England: c1906-1 Dec 1987) Brother of Douglas Craggs. Pro dealer (Witchcraft Magic, then Paul Clive & Co Ltd.) in, successively, London, Andover, & Blackpool 1935-1956-? Wrote Card Tricks without Skill (1946, with 5,000 copies printed; 2nd ed 1949, 200pp; 3rd ed 1959, 264pp), a minor classic. [Daw94] Clivette. Morton 1913 to become a Greenwich Village painter, poet, & antique dealer. [Pr] (USA: 1868-8 May 1931) Aka "The Great Clivette". Began as pro juggler, unicyclist, & tambourine spinner. Turned magician, illusionist, & shadowist c1895 with Orpheum circuit. Toured USA & Europe. Added mind-reading in 1909. Retired in

name: Close, Michael "Mike
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Pro close-up, mainly as restaurant magician. Articles in Linking Ring, Arcane, Magic, & Magic Menu. Wrote Workers (1990, 36pp) & Workers #2 (1991, 52pp). Video bit (1993).

name: Closson, George E [stmond]
bio: (Fort Ann, New York: 1 Jun 1859-11 Nov 1921) Minor dealer in Troy, New York, 1883-1921. Founded the Brotherhood of Magicians in New York City in 1905, one of the earlier magic societies in America, which folded in 1916. Edited Brotherhood Secrets 1906-1916. [Albo95]

name: Cloutier, Carl
bio: (Canada: fl.1980s-90s) Pro closeup. 1992 IBM 1st Prize; 1992 London closeup contest 1st prize; 1993 Gold Lion's Head; 1994 FISM 1st Prize in Closeup. 2 videos (1994).

name: Clower, R[andy] L.
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Aka "Oraxes". Bizarre magickian. Wrote The Book of Shadows (1983, 30pp).

name: Clute Jr, Cedric E[rrington] "Ced
bio: (Ross, California: 12 Feb 1931- ) Founder & manager-bartender of The Magic Cellar in San Francisco's Barbary Coast, 1969-78. In that period it was the only venue in the Bay Area providing regular employment to stage & close-up table magicians, as well as being the main gathering-place for local & visiting magi. Edited Footlights 1972-77 (4 issues). Co-edited (with Nick Lewin) Sleight of Crime (1977, 301pp), a short-story anthology of fictional magician-detectives. Now Historian of Amador County. Clute is a leading authority on Carter the Great. [Wh]

name: Coby, Rudy
bio: (Up-state New York, USA: 1964-) Learned from parents' Xmas gift magic set at age 9. Debut at age 14 or 15. Pro comedy magician & prominent in New Wave magic. International star, playing the Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris 1989 (4 months), Trump Casino in Atlantic City (repeats), etc. Tricks in Genii & MUM. Video bit. TV bit. [Genii2/90]

name: Cochrane, Eddie
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-70s) Pro stage comic & MC. Taught stage magic by Cas Boxley in 1940 or 41. Thence pro comedy stage magician by 1942 when he played the Beacon Theatre in Vancouver, Canada. Toured Europe with USO shows in WW II. Then left magic to become a top theatrical agent in Los Angeles for John Daniel, etc. [Tay]

name: Cochrane, June Elizabeth
bio:
"Codare -- The Maine Mystic" SEE: Codere, Romuald A.

[See also: "Merlin, June"]

name: Cody, Sebastian
bio: (London, England: 6 Oct 1956-) Learned at age 6 from a magic set. Film & TV producer with the Open Media production company. Amateur magician. Articles in Abra. Produced The Secret Cabaret, a 6-part TV series on magic & allied arts (forthcoming early 1990 on Channel 4 in England). [Wh2] Codere, Romuald A.

name: Coghlan, Arthur
bio: (Waterville, Maine: 22 Aug 1912- ) Pro since 1930 as "Codare the Maine Mystic" with sleight-of-hand & patter act. [WWM] (Liverpool, England: 9 Jul 1932-) Self-taught c1943 seeing store demo. Auto mechanic. Moved to Australia where became full-time pro illusionist & escapologist in 1975. Pet effects: Appearing & Disappearing Horse and Appearing & Disappearing Motorcycle. Invented steel keg escape (1975) & stage trap for horse. Gave over 6,500 40-minute big illusion shows at Magic Castle at Nobby's Beach. [Wh5]

name: Cohen, Al[fred Lee]
bio: (Wilmington, Delaware: 11 Jan 1926 [sic]) Learned in college from his roommate, an amateur. Became partner in father's novelty shop in Washington, DC, in 1947, adding a line of magic tricks in 1950. Pro magic dealer (Al's Magic Shop) in Washington, DC, since 1950, with a high rating for businesslike honesty. Invented Dots Impossible (by 1974) & Dots Incredible (by 1974). Edits Washington Wizards since 1976 as house organ. Considered one of the finest demonstrators. Performs comedy magic as "Pernell Zorch". Articles in Linking Ring. Father of Stan Cohen, his partner. [MUM6/94;Wh]

name: Cohen, Jean
bio: (Holland?: -c1943) Pro in Holland. With brother Joseph operated the Theatre Cohen from 1939 until seized by the Gestapo. Burned alive in a Nazi extermination camp. [Dif]

name: Cohen, Joseph
bio: (Holland?: fl.1930s) Brother of Jean Cohen. Pro in Holland as "Youpi". In WW II arrested by the Gestapo, disappearing in a Nazi extermination camp. [Dif]

name: Cohen, Stan[ley A.]
bio: (Washington, D.C.: 29 Apr 1950- ) Taught by father, Al Cohen. Works pro as "Dubow the Magician" 1972-present. Since 1973 full-time assistant-demonstrator & now equal partner in "Al's Magic Shop" in Washington, DC. [Wh2]

name: Cohn, Al[bert]
bio: (USA: - c1980) Magician since 1910s. Pro dealer in New York City (the Greenwich Toy House at 125 W. 49th St & then on 8th Avenue as The Magic Center) from 1941 until he sold in 1951. Tutored Dick Biow. Known as "The Sponge Ball King". Tricks in HMM. Retired to Florida. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Cohen" & therefore confused with Al Cohen of "Al's Magic Shop". [SatEvePost3 Feb 51;Jinx#139]

name: Coker, Roger
bio: (Akron, Ohio: c1931-18 Mar 1997) In the early 1950s teamed as "Milo & Roger" with Arthur "Milo" Brandon, which see. They retired in 1995. Bio is Brandon's Milo & Roger (1999, 418pp).

name: Colberg, Karl
bio: (Germany?: 23 Nov 1915-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Colburn, Zerah
bio: (Cabot, Vermont: 1 Sep 1804-2 Mar 1840) Pro lightning calculator since age 16. Toured USA, England, Scotland, & Ireland from 1812 to 1814. Autobio is A Memoir of Zerah Colburn (1833, 204pp). Uncle of the eminent railway engineer of the same name. [Magic10/02;St;Dif]

name: Cole [Il], Frank
bio: (Pawtuxet, Rhode Island: 12 Jan 1913-29 Sep 1968) Son of a dairy farmer. Amateur until 1935 when married Margaret "Peggy" Gwynne (daughter & assistant of Jack & Anne Gwynne) with whom he did a pro night-club act. [St]

name: Cole, Gladys [Pretoria]
bio: (Brisbane, Australia: 14 May 1900-23 May 1990) Gladys Pretoria Costin married Les "Levante" Cole in 1919. From then until his retirement in 1975 she was his musician (piano & accordion) & shadowgraphist. Mother of "Esme Levante". [Daw2]

name: Cole, Judson "Jud
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 27 Dec 1894-2 Oct 1943) Stage name of Milton Greishaber. Pro vaude comedy magician. Pet effects: Kling Klang & card flourishes. [Pr;Ho]

name: Cole, Leslie [Robert] "Les", MIMC
bio: (London, England: 23 Jan 1912-Blackpool: 1 Mar 1993) Amateur magician & collector (puzzles and magic books & apparatus). Aka "Maxwell Clarke". Former Librarian of the Magic Circle Library, London. MIMC 1990 His large collection was bought intact in 1994 by David Copperfield. [Daw94,p.72-74; Abra #2459]

name: Coleman
