bio: (USA: fl.1850s-60s) Invented the well (in 1860).

name: Coleman, [David Bateman] "Dave
bio: (USA: 23 Jul 1890-) Pro since 1905. With the Doc Nixon show 1915-16. Thence semi-pro. As "Doc Hokum" he created the first pitchman act in 1928. Co-edited (with Jimmy Trimble) Presto (1937, 1 issue). [St]

name: Coleman, Earle J[erome]
bio: (Chicago: ca.1942-1 Mar 2005) An academic by profession, Dr. Coleman was a Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Virginia Commonwealth U from 1971 until 1977. Amateur magician. Articles in Journal of Magic History and New Tops. Wrote Magic: A Reference Guide (1987, 1988).

name: Coligny, Jean de
bio: (Germany: c1879-22 Jan 1926) Stage name of Christian H. Burckel. Pro. Moved to Russia in 1912, living in Odessa until his death. [St]

name: Colin
bio: (France: fl.1970s) Stage name of François Chaplot. 1979 FISM 3rd prize in general magic. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Chaplow".

name: Collinet, Gaston-Louis
bio: (Passavent-en-Argonne, Marne, France: 9 Feb 1880-4 May 1960) Pro. Founded the Théâtre Collinet, a magic & cinema theater in Paris 1902. Charter member of the CSP 1904. [Dif]

name: Collings, Herbert J.
bio: (London, England: 1883-29 Mar 1958) Pro stage magician, giving over 10,000 shows from his debut in 1899 until his death. Did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Col Ling Soo". Toured Britain, France, Switzerland, & the Riviera. Co-founder (with Neil Weaver & Ernest K. Adams) of The Magic Circle in 1905. Played St. George's Hall 1912, 1919, 1922, & 1927. Gold Medalist, The Magic Circle. President, The Magic Circle 1928-31, 1954-58. President British Ring 1947-48. Article in Hughes News. [Pr;Go2;St;Le;Rey;Magic5/09] Collins, A. Frederick (USA?: fl.1910s-30s) Wrote The Book of Magic (1916, 177pp), The Book of Puzzles (1927, 190pp), & Mirth and Mystery (1931).

name: Collins, [Beulah M.] "B
bio: (USA: c1919-23 Jun 2002) Wife of Ted Collins, whom she married in WWI. Assisted Ted in his Mecca Magic shop in New Jersey and someimes in his magic act. Mother of their daughter, “Bunnie” Collins. [LR9/02]

name: Collins, [Bunette Hope] "Bunnie
bio: (Newark, New Jersey, USA: 13 Nov 1959-) Daughter of Ted Collins from whom she learned since age 4 as assistant in his act & Mecca Magic shop. Inspired by Vernon lecture at age 10 to take up close-up & card work. Pro magician, registered clown, & mime since age 24. Tannen's demonstrator 1984-86 (replacing John Mueller on his retirement) & manager Jul-Dec 1986. 1st magicienne invitee to FFFF. Full-time close-up & cabaret performer since 1987. Articles in Magic Manuscript. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Collins, Harry L[eon]
bio: (USA: c1920-3 May 1985). Pro trade-show magician with Frito-Lay, etc. Taught Lance Burton. Wrote Helpful Hints on Magic [c1972, 16pp].

name: Collins, James "Jim
bio: (Highgate, London, England: c1860-6 Mar 1942) Learned assisting Houdini 1908-1926 & then with Hardeen in late 1930s. Pro carpenter-metal worker. Possibly invented the flash wand.

name: Collins, [Louis E.] "Roba
bio: (USA: -21 May 1965) Pro tent & school-show magician & mentalist in the South in 1920s-30s as "The Great Roba". Moved to St. Louis in 1943. In 1946 co-refounded (with Ben Badley, etc) the St. Louis Society of Magicians. Wrote "Magic Outdoors" columns in Tops & Linking Ring. [Monti] (Rotherhithe, London, England: 31 Aug 1881-22 May 1966) Inspired around age 20 seeing Prof Willis do the Conus Aces & immediately learned from Sach's Sleight of Hand. Pro since 1916 when he played St. George's Hall. A non-smoker & non-drinker, he despised his audiences. Retired in 1939. Collins, Stanley [Martin] Invented the Jumping Rubber Band (1911), Collins Count (1912), Collins Four Aces (1912), Penetrating Card (1915), & Nic's Napkins (by 1928). Wrote Original Magical Creations (1914, 111pp), Deceptive Conceptions in Magic (1920, 112pp), Collins' Card Conceits [1925], A Conjuring Mélange (1947, 256pp), & a chapter in Bobo's Modern Coin Magic (1952). As "S. Wynne Burne" wrote Anthology of Love Poems (1929), a rare forcing book. Other poetry force-books as "S. Martin" & "S. Frank Harris". Also wrote as "Bold Pincher". Articles in Magician Monthly, Magazine of Magic, Sphinx, Linking Ring, Collectors Annual, Pentagram, & Magic Cauldron. Bio is Thomas A. Sawyer, Stanley Collins: Society Entertainer & Magic Collector (1984). See Thomas A. Sawyer, Men of Letters: Stanley Collins and Trevor H. Hall (1991, c70pp). [Daw#126,#199,#223;Magicol2/95;Magigram10/89;St;Th;Le]

name: Collins, [Frederick Alderton] "Ted
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 17 Feb 1919-23 Aug 1993) Inspired seeing Houdini at age 4. Paid debut at age 12 in 1931. Physical therapist & chiropractor. Invented Panama Rope Mystery in 1941. In US Army in WW II playing USO shows in Europe. Pro dealer (with wife Beulah who died in 2002) as founder-owner of Mecca Magic, Inc. in New Jersey since 1945, originally in home in Newark, then in shop in East Orange, & finally in Bloomfield. Also taught magic. Edited Mecca Magic News 1958-60 (22 issues). Wrote Wax Fax (1953, 20pp). Father of Bunnie Collins. [Wh2]

name: Colombi, Carlos H.
bio: (Pigue, Argentina: 12 Jul 1915- ) Son of the Mayor of Pigue. Inspired as boy in 1928 [sic] seeing David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg. Leading amateur in Buenos Aires. 1948 Sphinx Award. Articles in New Tops. [Bam]

name: Colombini, Aldo
bio: (Maranello, Modena, Italy: 19 Mar 1951-) Learned at age 19 reading Rossetti's Magia delle Carte. A top pro stage & close-up artist in Italy since age 22. Formerly aka "Fabian". 1976 FISM 2nd prize in close-up plus two Magic Castle awards. Pet effects: C&R Rope & Oil-&-Water. Moved in Jul 1993 to USA where he opened Mamma Mia Magic in southern California in Spring 1994. Received US citizenship in 2001. Wrote over 25 books, including Magia con Palitas (1975), Magia con Cubilettes, Impact (1991), React (1994, 100+pp), What's Up Deck? (1995, 160pp), Mama Mia Rope Routine (1995, 48pp), etc. See Lewis Ganson, Colombini's Cups and Balls Routine (1977). Tricks & columns in most major magazines, including Qui Magia, Magia Moderna, Magigram, Magic Info, Apocalypse, Linking Ring (including 3 "Parades" & a column since 1998), Laughmakers, & Genii (a column). Video (1989). [L&LPub2/2000;LR10/94;Wh5;Wh01]

name: Colorni, Abraham
bio: (Italy: c1540-c1597) Mechanical engineer & amateur magician in Ferrara. Invented the Rising Cards around 1574. [Dam2;Ch]

name: Colson, Odette
bio: (France: fl.c.1930s) Daughter of "Robertson" and "Lucile". Married Roger Jeannet and became a pro illusionist in his circus, the Cirque Gruss-Jeannet. [Dif]

name: Colta, Charles J.
bio: (Harrisburg, Pennsylvania: 23 May 1890- ) Stage name of Charles Joseph Jones. Pro vaude & club act. Also with partner as "Colta and Colta, The Merry Magicians". Pet effect: Linking Rings. [WWM] Colville, Charles A. (Canada: 1911-1987) Semi-pro magician in Toronto. Aka "Count Quick". Co-founded (with Douglas Colvin) Society of Canadian Magicians in 1968. Edited SCM Bulletin 1970-1971.

name: Comanche Jim
bio: See: Gordon, Rex Palmer

name: Combest, Daniel
bio: (USA: -c1979) As "Little Red Riley" he played school shows throughout Texas. John Cornelius was his clown-magician assistant c1964 whenever Combest played San Antonio. At 350 pounds, his billing as "The World's Biggest Magician" was correct, beating out Matt Schulien by 25 pounds.

name: Comden, Harold
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Invented Topit by 1920.

name: Comitre, José
bio: (Spain: 1894-1957) Pro. Aka "Rocambole". Toured Portugal (1928, 1933, & 1935). (Geneva, Switzerland: 22 Jun 1788-25 Nov 1859) French parentage. Learned in 1810 in Bordeaux from an amateur conjurer named David. Pro since 1812 with sleights, apparatus, & vent. In 1814 a stunning performance before King Louis XVIII won him the title of "Physicien du Roi". Made a Chevalier of the Legion of Honor by King Louis Philippe. Opened the Théâtre Compte 1814?-c1850 where he alternated his performances with those of his troupe of actors, creating successful business thru clever advertising. Retired in 1854. Died in Rueil. Probably invented Rabbit from Hat Trick (in 1814) & did invent Ladies Looking Glass (by c1815) & Growth of Flowers (by c1850). Wrote Voyages et seances anecdotiques de Monsieur Comte (1816, 252pp) & Nouveau manuel complet sorciers (1829; German tr as Kleines Handbuch der Taschenspielerkunst, 1834, 186pp). [Dif;Fr]

name: Comus, Sieur
bio: (Paris, France: 1731-1807) Stage name of Nicolas-Philippe Ledru. Pro by 1762. Possible inventor of the servantante, which he was using by 1765-66 when he played London for 3 months, and again in spring 1766 and in 1770. Invented the Blindfold Deal by 1766. Died in Geneva. [Dif;Cl;Fr]

name: Comus [II], Sieur
bio: (France: -1820) Pro by 1793-95 when he played the English provinces & London. Played Bordeaux in 1805. His pet effect was to always win Piquet while blindfolded, a trick he taught Ponsin shortly before his death. [CI;Fr;Magic2/01]

name: Comus, Ernest
bio: (France?: fl.1870s) Pro. Appeared with Alexander Herrmann in London in 1870. Also on own with his "Séance de Magie Rose" in both London & Paris.

name: Con-Conelli
bio: (Germany: fl.late 1940s-60s) Stage name of Conrad [sic] Schulz. A bookbinder who turned pro magician after WW II with cigarette manip & card tricks.

name: Condon, Joe
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Aka "The Amazing Condon". Engraver by trade. Semi-pro with magic, illusion, hypnotism, mentalism, fortune-telling, & escapes. Makes props & trophies for magicians. [Mag]

name: Conklin, Jerry
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro full-evening show in USA & Canada. Works circuses & schools. Lives in Colon, Michigan. Conley, James A. "Jim" (Caldwell, Idaho: c1917-25 Jul 1986) Inspired as boy seeing MacDonald Birch show. Pro illusionist by 1936. Dealer ("Conley's Magic Studio") in Hollywood in early 1940s. Member of Los Magicos. Sergeant in US Army in WW II. Had large collection of films of magicians. [Fu2]

name: Conlin [Sr], Claude Alexander
bio: (Alexandria, South Dakota: c1872 [sic]-5 Aug 1954) Pro mentalist & magician since 1907 as "Alexander, The Man Who Knows" & "Dr. Q". His chief assistants 1915-27 when he closed his full show were the Nartell Twins, Marguerite "Marge" (25 Oct 1895-6 Apr 1996) & Marie (25 Oct 1895-early 1990s). Died in Seattle. Wrote Life and Mysteries of the Celebrated Dr. Q (1921, 165pp; 3rd repr 1946), a classic. Also wrote Inner Secrets of Psychology. A vaudeville star for 35 years when retired rich in Los Angeles. Sold his show (7 tons) to Bob Nelson who later resold much of it, including the show's title, to Leon Mandrake. See Darryl Beckmann, The Life and Times of Alexander (1994, 380+pp). [Pr;Ran;Rey;HMM9/54]

name: Connus
bio: See: Conus

name: Conover, Tim
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s; -2 Feb 2011) Pro trade-show magician & mentalist. Co-wrote (with Scotty York) Revolutionary Routines with Aces (1995, 32pp). (Britain: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of Harold Saunders. Articles in Abra.

name: Conrad, Doc Tahman?
bio: (USA: -1974) Carnival worker. In 1954 did the Siberian Chain Escape on TV's Super Circus show. Mortally wounded rehearsing the Russian Roulette trick, he lived long enough to absolve his assistant.

name: Conradi-Horster
bio: See: Horster, F. W.

name: Constanti
bio: (Baranovich, Byelorussia, Russia: 1910-) Stage name of Konstanti Gorski. Pro manipulator & illusionist. Often played outside Russia. A teacher of Jerzy Drewla.

name: Constanze
bio:
Contento, Marcelo A. R. (Ramos Mejia, Buenos Aires, Argentina: 19 Jan 1955- ) Taught 1st trick at age 6 by brother, got first book at 8. Engineer & amateur magician. In 1985 turned full-time musician, magician, & magic dealer. Does close-up, stage, & club magic. Also does a hand-shadow act taught him by David Bamberg. Founder-proprietor of Casa de Magia in Buenos Aires 1981-c1988. Moved to USA in 1988 where he co-founded (with brother Victor) Marcelo Contento Productions in 1991. Invented Lightning Bolt (c1977), etc. Prizes in Argentina & Brazil 1978, 1985, 1987. Articles in Cerca de la Magia (Venezuela), Misdirection (Spain), Selecciones Magicas (Argentina), & EMAGIC (Argentina). [MUM3/2000;Wh2]

[See also: Ackermann, Georg (her father)]

name: Contigliozzi, Franco F.
bio: (Rome, Italy: 7 Feb 1930-1995) Learned magic in 1930s. Amateur. Collector. Major dealer (Curiosità e Magia) in Rome until his death. Article in Magic Manuscript. [Wh5]

name: Conus
bio: (France: -1836) Stage name of Cotte, aka "Le Sieur Conus" & "Connus". Famous pro by 1789, specialized in the Cups-&-Balls. Played London often 1789-99. Invented the Four Ace Trick & possibly Cards Across. [Fr;St]

name: Conus II
bio: (France: fl.1830s-40s) Taught by father Conus I. Pro.

name: Conus III
bio: (France: c1821-May 1905) Stage name of Fossier, son-in-law of Conus II. Pro, originally under own name, by 1874 when he played Brussels. [Dif]

name: Cony, Alexandre
bio: (Paris: 31 Jan 1862-12 Apr 1929) Stage name of [Victor-]Alexandre Yonc. Pro magician & marionettist. Partner with Jules Legris in early 1890s. Father of Gaston Cony, famous marionettist, editor (Inter-Forain), & director of the Guignol de Paris.

name: Conyears, Ross
bio: (Invergordon, Scotland: 1856-25 May 1901) Stage name of Alexander Ross. Learned by tuition from Ellis Stanyon in 1889 in London. Then pro conjuror & vent. Pet effects: Linking Rings and Cap & Pence. Died of pneumonia. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Conyers". [Magic8/01]

name: Conyers, George
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Amateur. Played St. George's Hall on 27 Sep 1918 when he won an open competition for amateurs.

name: Cook, Cecil E. "Cec
bio: (Australia: 1916-late Feb 1970) Learned at age 10. In 1928 began working in Will Andrade's magic department. Pro performer in Sydney. Manager of the Magic Department of Mick Simmons emporium in Sydney 1935-1960. Edited Mick Simmons' Magical Bulletin #1 (1935)-#12. Wrote Fifty-one Impromptu Conjuring Tricks that you can do (1946, 48pp). Owned his own shop ("Cecil Cook's Novelty Supply" then "Cec Cook's Magic Shop" 1961-70. [McC]

name: Cook, Irv[ing]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 2 Apr 1941-) Learned at age 9 working for a semi-pro. Pro dealer since 1966 (Daytona Beach Magic Shop, now simply Daytona Magic) in Florida. Took in Harry Allen as partner in 1976. They also tour with their Magic Shop on Wheels. Pet effect: Professor's Nightmare. Articles in MUM. [Wh5]

name: Cook, John Brown
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 4 Jul 1908-17 Apr 1978) President of Reliable Electric Company in Chicago. Amateur coin & mental magic. Wrote (with Arthur Buckley) Gems of Mental Magic (1947, 132pp; repr 1973, 122pp).

name: Cooke, G[eorge] A[lfred]
bio: (Cheltenham, England: 27 May 1825-2 Feb 1905) Partner since 1865 of J.N. Maskelyne with whom he jointly invented the Box Trick (in 1865) & Will, the Witch and the Watch (in 1873).

name: Cooke, Prof. Harry G.
bio: (Norwich, Connecticut: 1 Feb 1844-Jun 1924) Aka "Hovatini" & "Major Cooke, the American Wizard". Pro spirit cabinet act. Founded Los Angeles Society of Magicians. [St]

name: Cooper, Jim
bio: (USA: -9 Aug 1970) Pro cardman with gambling demos.

name: Cooper, John R.
bio: (Clarksburg, West Virginia: 1932-) Learned at age 9. Radio-TV broadcaster in his home town. Semi-pro stage & platform magician & vent since age 24. Aka "Dr. Mysto". Edited Spooks Speak 1952-53 (7 issues). Article in The Magnet (1954). [Wh2]

name: Cooper, Len
bio: (New York City: 2 Jan 1928-2 Jan 2003). Learned magic from a Svengali deck. Pro magician. Married Bernice in 1956 after which she became his partner. Founder-owner in Toronto Browser's Den of Magic 1975-1995 when sold to Jeff Pinsky and retired.

name: Cooper, Murray [James]
bio: (Hobart, Tasmania, Australia: 26 Jul 1950-) Learned at age c12 mail-ordering from "Weirdo's". Music teacher in Adelaide. Semi-pro close-up & childrens magician since 1980. Works restaurants, shopping malls, etc. 1988 Australian Convention of Magicians 2nd place close-up. Co-editor (with Gerry McCreanor) Blueprint 1978-81. Articles in Magigram, Apocalypse, & Blueprint. [Wh2]

name: Cooper, Neville [John]
bio: (Southsea, Hampshire, England: 7 Jun 1924-) Learned at age 7 from box of tricks. Engineer & chairman of manufacturing company. AIMC 1957. Semi-pro since 1958. Pet effects: C&R Rope, Giant Memory, & Cards Across. [MC7/90;Wh5]

name: Cooper, [Thomas Frederick] "Tommy
bio: (Caerphilly, Wales: 1922-15 Apr 1984) After WW II service with the Guards in North Africa, soon became a highly popular pro comedy magician in Britain, aided by intense TV exposure. Wrote Tommy Cooper's Just Like That! (1975). Owned a London magic shop ("Tommy Cooper's Magic Spot"), which was managed by Alan Alan. Died during a live TV show. [Hudd;Le]

name: Copper, Ger
bio: (Holland: c1952-) Stage name of Gerrit Kopper. Taught by Henk Vermeyden. Pro sleight-of-hand. FISM 2nd prize in manip 1976 for his fast work & Grand Prix 1979 (shared with Soviet couple Kubikuzena & Sultangali) for his candle act. AMA Visiting Magician of the Year 1978 & 1983.

name: Copperfield, David
bio: (Metuchen, New Jersey: 16 Sep 1956-) Stage name of David Seth Kotkin. Inspired at age 12 seeing a department store magic demo & immediately took lessons and began performing in 1968 as "Davino". Pro stage illusionist, blending magic with music & plot. First public triumph in 1975 as star of stage magic-musical "The Magic Man", which played for 8 months. His main illusion consultant since 1977 has been Don Wayne. Others include André Kole, John Gaughan, & Jim Steinmeyer. Has done 16 TV specials from 1977 thru 1995. Co-starred in film Terror Train (1980) for which he also supplied the illusions. 1980 AMA Magician of the Year. Headliner at Caesar's Palace (1984, 1989, 1990, 1991). Toured South-east Asia 1988 & Europe 1993. Bought the Mulholland Library in 1991 for $2,200,000 and has added considerably to it since. In 1995 received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. He is one of the two or three top international stars in magic, doing some 500 shows a year. Forbes magazine reported his 1991-92 income as $35 million, making him the world's 17th highest paid entertainer & the highest paid magician (ahead of Siegfried & Roy at $30 million). In 1993 alone he grossed $26 million. In 1996-97 Forbes rated him the 7th highest paid entertainer with $85 million (with S&R 19th at $58 million). [Bo#273;LR3/93;ABC of Faxic#50;Ran;HC;Se;MM10/83;WWE]

name: Cora, Madame
bio: (USA: -c1902) Stage name of Mrs Ursula Bush, aka "Madame Cora de LaMond". Pro mesmerist & magician since early 1860s. In 1872 toured Australia (where she introduced Troublewit) & New Zealand in 1873. In South Africa in 1877 when she murdered a young female vocalist in her troupe. Her death sentence was commuted. Back in Australia in 1878, 1889, & 1891. Probably died in Durban, South Africa. [Wal;Mar]

name: Coram, T.
bio: (Halifax, England: 1883-26 Mar 1937) Stage name of Thomas Mitchell. Pro variety magician & vent as "The Military Ventriloquist" with his figure "Jerry". Gave 4 Royal performances.

name: Corda, Carlos
bio: (Argentina: 1923-1979) Stage name of Ismael Adolfo CERCEDA. Aka "Don Alvan". Pro magician, once touring with Ade Duval. Reportedly did a whip-cracking act. As Adolfo Cerceda wrote (with William King) The Folding Money Book (1963, 46pp; repr 1975). Tricks in Genii. [Cam]

name: Cordelier, François
bio: (Cassy-en-Morvan, Saône-et-Loire, France: 22 Jul 1839-28 Nov 1914) Originally, 1865-67, a juggler & equilibrist known as "Léon de Paris". Turned pro magician in 1867. Aka "Docteur Méphisto" & "Monsieur Riz-au-lait". Later (by 1886) with a telepathy act as "Docteur Satan" & "Capitaine Satan" & "Professeur Icks", touring the Orient & South Africa, before returning to France. In 1890 played the Casino de Paris as "Leo Cordelier". Wrote as "Hicks" L'art de gagner aux cartes, ou les tricheurs démasqués (1904). [Vo55;Dif]

name: Cordelier, Leo
bio: See: Cordelier, François

name: Cordianino
bio: (Poland?: -1975) Stage name of Kordian Wach. Pro circus illusionist in Poland. [Mec]

name: Cordova, Colonel
bio: (USA?: fl.1870s) Stage name of William White Maitland. Pro stage magic & spirit manifestation act. Played London in 1874. [CI]

name: Corduan, Dr Paul
bio: (Soldin/Neumark, Germany: 17 Feb 1894-4 Jan 1961) Amateur? Died in Wismar. [Roh]

name: Corin, Matt[hew]
bio: (USA: -7 Oct 1998) Student of Pete Biro, Jules Lenier, & Clarke Crandall. Judged one of the top 25 close-up artists by George Anderson in 1972. Invented Mondo Monte in 1975. Articles in Talisman, etc. Dealer (as Busby-Corin, Inc) in Oakland, California, 1979 until disappeared in 1980. Thence adopted stage & legal name of Nathan "Nate" Phillips. He resurfaced in the mid-1990s, moving in 1997 to Coeur d'Alene, Idaho. Died of accidental carbon monoxide poisoning while sleeping in his car (faulty muffler).

name: Corinda, Tony, MIMC
bio: (England:  $ 16^{th} $ May 1930 – Norfolk, England:  $ 1^{st} $ July, 2010) Stage & pen name of Thomas William Simpson. Corinda was a variation on the name Conradi. Joined The Magic Circle in 1954. An ex-laboratory assistant turned pro mentalist & dealer. The Magic Shop in Tottenham Court Road was originally run by Dick Chavel, and later taken over by Corinda. Corinda also had the magic concession in Hamleys Toy Shop in Regent Street. This was located in the basement of the store and was run for a period by Ali Bongo, who also demonstrated magic at the Tottenham Court Road location. Wrote the classic series, 13 Steps to Mentalism (1958-60, 424pp; repr in 1 vol, 1960, 424pp), plus Mini-Slate Magic (1958, 20pp, probably partly ghosted by Jon Tremaine), Teletrickery (1961, 13pp), & The Complete Guide to Billet-Switching (1976, ed by Ralph Read).

name: Cornelius, John [Henry], AIMC
bio: (Lamesa, Texas: 22 Apr 1948-) Learned by working in a San Antonio magic shop. Pro. Worked as "Corny the Clown" c1964 as magic-clown assistant for travelling magician Daniel "Little Red Riley" Combest. In 1968 pitched Svengalis for S. David Walker at the Texas Hemisfair. 1979 FISM 1st prize in close-up; 1985 FISM 1st prize in card magic. Invented FISM Flash (1973), Cornelius Card System (by 1980), etc, & popularized Terge Nordnes's effect as Fickle Nickel (c1972). Wrote Cornelius Card System (1980) & Magician's Datebook (1981). See Pallbears Review & Mad Magic #42 (1982) for all-Cornelius issues. Other tricks in Epilogue, Magic Manuscript, & MUM. Audio (1986). 2 videos (1993) & video bit (1994). [LR4/92;Wat;Wh]

name: Cornelli
bio: See: Chwałka, Tadeusz

name: Cornillot, Monsieur
bio: (France: fl.1820s) Learned from Pinetti. Pro. Toured England 1822-23. [Hou,81-82;Fr]

name: Cornwall, David
bio: (England: fl.1690s-1710s) A showman at English fairs in 1698. Did the Egg Bag at Southwark Fair in 1713. [CI]

name: Corodini
bio: (Hungary: 1886-22 Aug 1955) Stage name of Nicholas Göndör. Popular pro comedy magician. Toured often in Germany. Died in Budapest. NOTE: Missspelled "Corrodini". [Vo57]

name: Coross, Gy[ula]
bio: (Hungary: c1895-20 Feb [or Dec?] 1942) Pro. Specialized in liquid magic with the help of chemicals & ingenious apparatus. Died in Berlin. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Corros". [Vo57;St]

name: Corrodini" [misspelling]
bio: See: Corodini

name: Corten, Doc
bio: (Schwerin, Germany: 4 May 1885-1966) Stage name of Dr Hans Cordshagen. Aka "Doc-Corten". Amateur? Trick in Magie (May 1936; repr in Linking Ring Jul 1936). [Roh]

name: Cortes, Ronny H[yacinth], AIMC
bio: (Tampa, Florida: 8 Mar 1914- ) Learned in 1924 from Gilbert Mysto Magic set. Chemist. Semi-pro stage & close-up since 1932. Articles in MUM. SAM Hall of Fame & Magic Museum Secretary & Librarian 1971-present. 1980 SAM Best Mental Magic Trophy. AIMC 1984 (for blindfold act). 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. [MUM6/75;Wh2]

name: Cortini
bio: (Tilsit [not Königssberg], Germany: 6 Apr 1890-14 Nov 1954) Stage name of Paul [sic] Korth. Inspired in 1902 seeing a circus magician. Pro since 1918, first with manip (famed for Miser's Dream) in cabarets, then as illusionist. Played the London Alhambra in 1925 & the Berlin Wintergarten in 1927. Toured USA (including the New York Palace Theatre) & Canada 1929 [sic]-30. Popularized but did not invent the Torn and Restored Newspaper (by 1928). Billed as "The Man with 100,000 Dollars". Issued many different palming coins. Died on stage in Copenhagen doing the Misers Dream. Bio is Hans Höller, Cortini (1990, 100pp, in English). [Win;Vo57;Ho]

name: Cosac
bio: (Lwow, Poland: 1911-1979) Stage name of Zygmunt Kozak. Pro illusionist, giant memory act, and as "Ak-Mek" a fakir act. [Mec]

name: Cossari, Joseph "Joe
bio: (Kulpmont, Pennsylvania: 1903-10 Mar 1980) Inspired at age 7. Pro manip & 6-minute card fan act. See John Fedko, The Joe Cossari Card Act (1978, 27pp). [Mag]

name: Costa Brito, Dr Frederico Carlos da
bio: (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: 4 Sep 1854-27 Sep 1919) Professor of pharmacy in Rio. Amateur magician, having studied with Carl Herrmann. Invented some effects used by Patrizio & Frizzo. Wrote Revelações da Magia Moderna (1903) & Manual Completo do Prestidigitador (1905, 96pp). Articles on magicians in Rio newspapers. [Magic12/01]

name: Costi. Davide
bio: (Cairo, Egypt: 24 Nov 1955- ) Amateur manip in Italy. ..... In 1986 won both the Italian close-up championship & the Ron MacMillan close-up competition. Member of Escuela Mágica de Madrid. Lectures throughout world. Invented the Floating Count for cards. Trick in MUM. Many TV bits. [Wh5]

name: Cotgrave, John
bio: (England: fl.1640s-50s) Layman. Writer of books on games, including Wits Interpreter, the English Parnassus (1655, with later editions in 1662 & 1671). This popular book taught English gentlemen various "admirable accomplishments" including a section (pp.143-175) of magic tricks lifted from Scot.

name: Cotten, Joseph "Jo
bio: (Petersburg, Virginia: 15 May 1905-1994) Radio, stage, & film actor. Amateur magician. Did magic on live stage only in 1943 when featured in Orson Welles' The Mercury Wonder Show doing the Sub Trunk with Rita Hayworth & Marlene Dietrich & a solo Escape Trunk as "The Great Joseph--Wizard of the South". Coached by Tommy Hanlon, he did one magic trick (the Glass of Wine from Handkerchief) in movie Since You Went Away (1944). Autobio is Vanity Will Get You Somewhere (1987, 235pp). [Katz]

name: Cottet, Martin [pronounced co-TAY]
bio: (Switzerland: 1963-) Stage name of Martin Gottet. Pro. Originally with Marco Tempest as "The United Artists". Has played the Hollywood Magic Castle & the Monte Carlo Casino. [Ran]

name: Cottier, Emmanuel
bio: (Switzerland: 1858-1930) Mechanic & watchmaker in Carouge, near Geneva. Made automata & operated a mechanical theater for shadow shows.

name: Cotton
bio: See: "Uferini, Willi"

name: Coucke, Fernand
bio: (Roubaix, Lille, France: 15 Oct 1929- ) Learned magic in 1945. Manager in furniture business in Lille. Semi-pro close-up & mental magic as "Ferdson". AFAP Master Magician. Collector. President of Nord-Magic-Club since 1967. President of AFAP (1968-73) & FISM. AFAP Gold Medal 1973. Articles in Revue de la Prestidigitation. [Bou2;Wh2]

name: Coulen
bio: (France: fl.late 1500s) Pro. First known performer of the Gun Trick by 1597 when reported in the Theatre of God's Judgements (1597, p.120), which is the English translation by Reverend Thomas Beard of an as yet untraced French book. NOTE: Name generally misspelled "Coulew", beginning with Houdini.

name: Coulew" [misspelling]
bio: See: Coulen

name: Courcelles, Jacques
bio:
(Belgium: fl.1950s) Cardman. 1955 FISM 2nd prizes for manipulation & card magic.

[See also: Colville, Charles]

name: Courtois, Louis
bio: (Waesmunster, East Flanders, Belgium: 28 Oct 1785-1866) Son of French parents. Moved to France. Pro. When his daughter Julie married Joseph Grandsart, the two men combined to found the Théâtre Grandsart-Courtois. Died in Paris. [Dif]

name: Coussinet, Adrien-Louis
bio: (France: 27 Jun 1841-26 Dec 1910) Lived in Paris. As "Albany" was pro stage magician, mimic (of musical instruments & animals), whistler, lightning artist, & since 1886 2-person mind-reading act (silent code) in France. Worked on the Egyptian Hall in London in 1893 billed as "Alban and Stella". NOTE: Name misspelled "Adrian Coussmet" by Houdini. [Rob;Vo55;Cl]

name: Cox, Mr.
bio: (Stettin, Germany [now Szczecin, Poland]: 9 Jul 1932 [sic]) Stage name of Jürgen Wolfgramm. Lives in West Germany. Ex-stage actor. Pro illusionist since 1958. 1964 FISM Grand Prix (shared with Pierre Brahma) & 1973 [sic] FISM 1st prize for invention. Since 1976 works with partner-wife "Annabelle" aka "Magic-Lady" (Annelise Wolfgramm, born 4 Apr 1938). Now works the Hansa [theme] Park in Sierksdorf. [Win;Mec]

name: Cox, James
bio: (Britain: -1788) Famous clockmaker & jeweller in London. Made & exhibited 56 automata in 1772 at his museum in Spring Gardens near Charing Cross. Sold all these in 1775 at public lottery where they fetched the large sum of 120,000 guineas, many going to China & Russia. His Silver Swan is in the Bowes Collection at Barnard Castle, England. In 1781 Katterfelto made his London debut at Cox's Museum. Wrote A Descriptive Inventory (1772, 71pp), which is the catalog for the lottery.

name: Cox, L. Raymond
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 24 Feb 1908-26 Sep 1948) An actor-director who turned full-time pro comedy magician in 1929. Pet effect: Nest of Boxes. Wrote Tips and Tricks (1934). [SAM;St]

name: Cox, William Edward
bio: (USA: 1915- ) Mechanical engineer. Semi-pro magician. Best known since 1932 as an early and credulous parapsychologis when he first associated himself with Dr. Rhine's parapsychology. research at Duke University. Wrote Mentalism and Magicians: Some Conclusive Arguments about a Modern Problem (1972, 20pp).

name: Crabb III, Robert Talmage (Tabby)
bio: (Patauxent River Naval Station, MD: 7^{th} Oct 1945 – Leslie: 18^{th} Apr 2011) Father was Robert Talmage Crabb Jr. and mother Gladys Crowson Crabb. He grew up in Americas, graduated from Americas High School in 1963, and from Georgia Southwestern College with a degree in political science. Tabby was drawn to music at an early age and was a gifted musician. He played in several local bands, moved to Houston, Texas, where he was a member of the original Urban Cowboy Band at Gilley's and was an extra in the Urban Cowboy movie. He pursued an individual music career and moved to Nashville, Tenn., where he built a recording studio, Flatwood Studio in Lebanon, Tenn. He also founded Tabman Magic, in which he built props and illusions for magicians all over the world. He was famous for his Tabman tables, casino chips, knife through arm, and fine hardwood magicians' wands. He built props for Amazing Jonathan and Paul Kozak in the 90s and helped David Litchman create the MAGIC bbs back in 1989 as well as helping to found IBM Ring 2100. He made videos, loved trains and photography and boating which he collected, and was proud to be a member of the USO Tour in Vietnam.

name: Crabtree, Roger L. "Rog", MIMC
bio: (Springfield, Ohio: 17 Jan 1932 - 23 Dec 1993) Inspired at age 7 seeing Blackstone. Learned from gift of Gilbert Magic set next Xmas. Airline pilot. Semi-pro close-up comedy magician & MC since age 20. Pet effect: close-up with mice. 1973 & 1974 TAOM best close-up. 1974 IBM best close-up. TAOM President 1977-78. IBM President 1981-82. IBM Secretary 1983-1991. MIMC 1989. Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, MUM. See Lewis Ganson, Crabtree Connection (1981). [Wh2]

name: Craggs, Douglas, OBE, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 11 Apr 1897-9 Jan 1989) Student of David Devant. Pro vent-magus. Aka "Roy Douglas". Honorary Secretary, The Magic Circle, 1940-45. Wrote The A.B.C. of Ventriloquism (1944, 52pp), a classic; & Masterpieces of Magic (1946, 77pp). Brother of Paul Clive. [Go2]

name: Craig, Earl
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-50s) Stage name of Arthur E. Baird. Self taught. Pro magician. Played 9 years in England. Then since 1936 hosted the USA radio network "Professor Quiz" show. Retired to St. Petersburg, Florida. [St]

name: Craig, Mystic, AIMC
bio: (Passaic, New Jersey: 15 Oct 1900-21 Oct 1987) Stage name of William M. [or E.] "Bill" Vagell. Inspired at age 13 seeing Thurston show. At age 13 joined carnival. Tutored by Professor Lowry & Harry Rouclere. Debut as pro in 1913. Mainly in vaudeville. Wrote The Elusive Canary: The Last Word on Cages (1936, 33pp, ghosted by Jean Hugard). With USO 1943-45. Retired after WW II. Tricks in HMM. SAM Hall of Fame 1985. His collection of movies of magicians, which he filmed during his travels is now in the Magic Castle Library. [LR12/84; Th; SAM; Wat]

name: Crambrook, W. H. M.
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s) Pro magician, magic teacher, & dealer with shop (The Necromantic Tent) in London by 1841 when he published the 1st edition of his magic catalog, which no longer exists. His 2nd catalog (1843) was the 48-page Crambrook's Catalogue of Mathematical & Mechanical Puzzles, Deceptions and Magical Curiosities. The 1843 copy from the Finlay Collection sold to the Ellenbogen Collection in 1979 and thence later to the Sperber Collection and was photo reprinted in 1990 by Collectors' Workshop. The only two other known 1843 originals are in the collections of David Copperfield (ex-Leslie R. Cole Collection) and that of the late J.H. Grossman.

name: Cramer, Sam
bio: (Poland: 28 Sep 1904-) Moved to Canada at age 5. Magician since late 1920s. Pro dealer in Montreal (Cramer's Magic and Joke Shop) c1930-1980s. Published-edited as house organs Cramer's Monthly Broadcaster 1930 (3 issues) & Broadcaster 1932 (3 known issues).

name: Cramer, Stuart [Price] "Stu
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 16 Jul 1911-15 Apr 2003) Learned at age 8 from uncle Herbert Cope, a Chautauqua lecturer & amateur magician. Aka "Mr. Meriweather". Advertiser & lawyer. Part time pro stage, close-up, & pseudo-Chinese mental magician as "Chan Wing" 1948-65. On TV as "Chan Wing" 1950, "Prof. Nemo" 1953-54, & "Mr. Meriweather" 1959-61. Full-time trade-show magician 1970-85. Pet effects: Cups-&-Balls, Linking Rings, & Miser's Dream. Wrote The Secrets of Karl Germain (1962, 76pp) & Germain the Wizard and his Legerdemain (1966, 156pp), which effectively preserved the art of Germain in much the same way as Fischer did for Hofzinser. Articles in Sphinx, Jinx, Linking Ring, Hugard's Magic Monthly, New Tops, New Phoenix, Magicol, MUM. [LR1/79:NT4/64:HMM8/50:Wh5] Crandall, Clarke C[aryle] "The Senator" (USA: 1906-19 Jun 1975) Pro comedy close-up. Pet effects: Six Card Repeat & C&R Rope. Managed Al Sharpe's Studio of Magic in Chicago 1956-57 when he bought it, operating it until 1958 and then until next year as wholesale. Invented "Poker Player's Nightmare" (by 1964). Edited The Senator's Pink Sheet 1957-59 as house organ. Columnist for New Tops since 1962. Moved to Hollywood by 1970. AMA Best Lecturer 1970, 1974. Taught Gary Michaels in 1974. Wrote Entertaining with Magic (1952), How to Stack Dice [1974, 18pp], & The Best of Senator Crandall (1998, 108pp, ed. by Neil Foster, based on his New Tops column). [LR8/75;LR2/02;Mag]

name: Crandon, Mina
bio: (Ontario, Canada: 1886-1 Nov 1941) Born Mina Stinson. Moved to Boston in teens. Married Dr Le Roi Goddard Crandon, MD, in 1918. Pseudo-psychic since 1923 in Boston where her powers were studied in 1924-25 by several scientists plus magicians Fred Keating (who was skeptical), Hereward Carrington (who believed her), Eric Dingwall (who was skeptical), & Harry Houdini (who claimed he exposed her). Bios are J. Malcolm Bird, 'Margery' the Medium (1925); Christopher (1975), 192-227; & Thomas Teitze, Margery (1973).

name: Crane, Lawrence "Larry
bio: (Roscommon, Ireland: 1878-14 Dec 1950) Aka "The Irish Wizard". Inspired at age 6 assisting his pro father "The Great Crane" in the Trunk Escape. Moved to USA in 1885. Self-taught at age 14. Worked as assistant to A. Herrmann 1892-93 when went to England. Pro stage magician. Played the Folies-Bergère in the 1920s for 5 weeks. Died in Boston. [Pr]

name: Cranel, Loch David
bio: (San Diego, California: 18 Nov 1948-) Learned at age 13. College professor in home city. Semi-pro since 1963 with comedy magic, escapes, & illusions, doing 50% for charity. Aka "Captain Kirk" (1980s) & "Bafflin' Bill Cody" (1990s). [Wh2]

name: Craven, [Thomas Eugene] "Tom" "TC
bio: (Akron, Ohio: 2 Nov 1934-) Learned in 1962 from father & friends. Credit manager. Semi-pro close-up magician & mentalist. In 1975 with John Quine taught a non-credit magic course at Akron U, one of their students being Richard Hughes. Worked trade shows as pro 1978-84. Lectures throughout USA & Canada. 1987 FFFF Roastee. Wrote Tom Craven's 16th Card Book (1981, 16pp) The Card Magic of John Quine (1988, 20pp), T.I.P.S. (42pp), & Tom Craven Presents a Trade Show Lecture. Articles in Linking Ring, Minotaur, Apocalypse, & Pabular. Column in Linking Ring since Nov 1990. [Lo2;Wh2]

name: Crawford, Harry
bio: (USA: 1924-) Pro illusionist with assistant-wife Gloria. [Wat] (Columbia, Tennessee: 21 Aug 1871-3 Oct 1952) Printer by trade in Nashville. Inspired by a travelling salesman-magician. Learned at age c20 from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Debut c1895 (at age 24). Semi-pro sleight-of-hand & small effects. Originated Calendar Magic. IBM President 1938-39. Edited Linking Ring 1938-41. [Dor;Th;WWM]

name: Crayford, Charles
bio: (Bexleyheath, England: 22 Jun 1879-10 Apr 1960) Pro. Aka "The Kentish Mystic". Wrote Fifty Best Conjuring Tricks (1923), etc.

name: Cremer Jun., W[illiam] H[enry]
bio: (Britain: -1892?) Son of W.H. Cremer, a brushmaker at 10 Bridge Street, Westminster, London, whose shop he took over & ran as pro magic dealer-publisher-teacher by 1851. Taught Robert Heller c1950. Relocated shop to 27 New Bond Street 1859-61 & to 210 Regent Street 1861-1892 whence it passed to the Parkins & Gotto general & fancy goods emporium. Authored (possibly ghosted by hacks) The Secret Out (London: 1870, 307pp), The Magician's Own Book (1871, 325pp), Hanky Panky (1872, 328pp; repr 1874 & 1875), & Magic No Mystery (1876, 333pp). Also several non-magic books. REF: Dawes in Magic Circular, V.79 (1985), 480-481, V.80 (1986), 6-9.

name: Crimmins Jr, John J. "Jack
bio: (USA: 19 Aug 1904-2 [sic] Mar 1961) Inspired & learned magic in 1917 at age 13. Advertising executive in Yonkers, New York. Amateur magic collector with one of six largest book collections in USA at death. Edited Walsh's Spongeball Manipulation (1936), Annemann's Full Deck of Impromptu Card Tricks (1943, 79pp), Annemann's Practical Mental Effects (1944, 310pp), & Annemann's Miracles of Card Magic (1948, 109pp). Tricks in Genii, etc. Book review column in HMM 1948-61. [Th]

name: Cristall, Leslie, AIMC
bio: (England: fl.1940s-60s) Wrote My 25 Years of Magic (1966, 26pp).

name: Criticus
bio: See: Findlay, James Black

name: Crivello, [David Francis] "Dave
bio: (Alton, Illinois: 1906-) Amateur magician by 1940. Salesman until 1950 when became hotel manager. Amateur magician. Retired to Fort Lauderdale, Florida in 1960. [Wh2]

name: Crombie, Donald [Griff], MIMC
bio: (Wolverhampton, England: 12 May 1904-11 Sep 1998) Learned in 1927 from Tarbell Course. Solicitor until retired. Amateur magician since age 25, specializing in close-up & mental magic. President of British Magical Society 1938-39 & 1977-78. MIMC 1942. In 1947 founded Wolverhampton Circle of Magicians. British Ring President 1978. [Wh2]

name: Crochet
bio: (Rotterdam, Holland: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Gerrit Haak. Operetta singer to film actor. Then since 1932 as pro stage illusionist with many assistants. Toured abroad including Scandinavia. [Dif;St]

name: Cros, Daniel
bio: (Paris, France: 1940- ) First interested in magic at age 6 from parents gift of magic set. Pro close-up since 1962. Moved to USA in 1964 to become resident magician at the Desert Inn in Las Vegas. Invented Daniel's Seahorse (1983), Super Twilight (1983), The Enchanted Stradivarius (1987), Omni Board (1988), & Skeletini (1989). Wrote 3 booklets, including The Close-up Magic of Daniel Cros (1983). Video (1987). [Wh2]

name: Crosby, Professor
bio: See: Taylor, E. Cooper

name: Crosby, Jan
bio: (Norway: 5 Mar 1940-) Pro illusionist & escapist. 1971 NMK Nordic Champion. [Mec]

name: Cross, Mal
bio: (New York City, NY: 5 Oct 1939-) Learned at age 12 from Mike Tanner's Circle Magic shop. Pro street magician in New York City 1972-82 with an exclusive on Shubert Street in center of theater district. Then pro close-up club dates & TV. Did his famous water trick in movie The Devil and Max Devlin (1981). Articles in Magic Manuscript. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Crossen, Ken[dall Foster]
bio: (Albany, Ohio: 25 Jul 1910-) Science-fiction & mystery writer-editor since 1944 as Ken Crossen, "Richard Foster" (with the "Green Lama" pulp series), "Christopher Monig", & "Clay Richards". Amateur magician. Tricks in Phoenix. [CA]

name: Crosthwaite, Rev Dr Roger
bio: (Solimull, Warwickshire, England: 13 Nov 1938- ) Inspired at age 7 by Fabian. Taught Erdnase at age 11 by Cyril Golding. Clergyman (Church of England) since 1965. Amateur cardman plus pick-pocketing & mental magic. 1980 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. AIMC 1980. Wrote Card Notes (1982, 100pp), Inner Sanctum Card Magic (forthcoming 1994), & Roger's Thesaurus (1995, 256pp, with Justin Higham). Tricks in Gen, Abra, Magigram, Genii, Technomagic, LR (a 1-man Parade), etc. See Walt Lees, The Commercial Card Magic of Roger Crosthwaite (1981, 47pp). 6 videos. [LR7/94;Wh2]

name: Crowther, Arnold
bio: (Chatham, Kent, England: 6 Oct 1909-1 May 1974) Learned magic at early age. Pro sleights, vent, chapeaugraphy, Punch, marionettes, & puppets. [Go2]

name: Crowe, Raymond [Christopher]
bio: (Adelaide, Australia: 16 Feb 1962-) Pro with cabaret, stage, and platform magic. 1978 Sydney International Convention of Magicians Best Manipulation; and 1996 25th Australian Convention of Magicians, Wizards Inn Award. Wrote Raymond Crowe Hand Shadows (2000, 16pp). Tricks in Genii (Mar 1989). TV bit (1997 Worlds Greatest Magic IV) [Wh01]

name: Csuri, Frank F[ay]
bio: (Salank, Hungary: 3 Oct 1911-22 Jul 1994) Born Ferencz Istran Csuri. Moved to USA in 1920. Inspired in 1924 by father's card tricks & taught by friend. In 1927-29 bought the Tarbell Course. Engineer (BE) until retired in 1977. Semi-pro manipulative magician since 1937 (except Army service 1941-45). Compiled-edited 7 legendary sets (six copies each) of retyped letters & notes, which he distributed to underground members in the 1960s. Only those of Dr Jacob Daley and Faucett Ross have been published. The others are Bill Woodfield's Gambling and Magic Notes (1961), The Magic of Charles Earle Miller (1962-69), Illusion Secrets (Thayer), Collected Works of Edward Massey, & The Magic of Paul Fox. Tricks in Genii, Tops, Linking Ring, MUM, & Regow's Magical Review. [Thaumaturgist11/94;Wh2]

name: Cubis
bio: (Ljungby, Sweden: 6 Feb 1899-31 Dec 1983) Stage name of Eric Dinnetz. Began in 1925 [sic] as assistant to Solimann. Wrote Avslöjade trix och Kortkonster (1941, 16pp). [Dif] Cubitt, A. S. (England: 1877-1930 [or 1927]) Pro, aka "Stanley Witcher". Mechanic-electrician & maker of magic apparatus. Long employed by the house of Maskelyne as their workshop superintendent at St. George's Hall. Invented the Yogi's Star illusion, which was premiered by Devant in Sep 1913.

name: Cucchiani
bio: (Italy: fl.1810s-1820s) Pro vent-magus who performed in London in 1814 & 1825. [Fr]

name: Cuckoe, William
bio: (Britain: fl.1590s) Pro intinerant conjuror by 1592 when he was already an old man. Performed in clothes of many colors. [Cl]

name: Cudennec, Daniel-Jean, AIMC
bio: (Motreff, Finistère, France: 3 Jun 1944-) Inspired at age 7 by a touring magus. Teacher. Semi-pro magician as "Dany Trick", specialized in kid-shows & close-up. AIMC 1984. Major collector of magic & vent books. Reviews for L'Illusionniste & La Revue de la prestidigitation. Wrote Miette: Physicien (1994, 16pp). Had own TV series & TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Culliton, Patrick [Kevin]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 18 Sep 1944- ) Stage, film, & TV actor since 1964. Semi-pro magician with a Houdini act that toured 150 colleges full-time, 1974-c78. Collector & historian. 1978 AMA Best Lecturer (on Houdini). Wrote & acted (as Orson Welles) in his 1984 stage production at the Variety Arts Center of "Orsino and the Love Goddess". Article in Genii. [Wat;Wh]

name: Culpitt, "Fred
bio: (Camberwell, London, England: 9 May 1877-8 Oct 1944) Born Frederic Willis Cullpitt. Pro comedy patter illusionist since 1892, initially as "Cull-Pitt", then "Culpit", & "Culpitt", this last being the most usual. Toured Australia 1909. A regular at St. Georges Hall, London, playing there 1913-15, 1918, 1921, 1923-24, 1928-29, & 1933. On 1 Oct 1936 became first magician to appear on a regularly scheduled TV broadcast in Britain. Invented the world-famous Doll House illusion (by 1927) & the Silk to Egg Trick. Wrote Laughter and Legerdemain (1928). Articles in Magic Wand. [Dif;Fi;Vo56;Wal;Pr;Ho]

name: Culpitt, Miss Rosa
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s) Pro. (London, England: 1857-1922) Stage name of Charles Garner. Pro, having learned muscle-reading as assistant to Washington Irving Bishop. Then went out on own as "Stuart Cumberland" with a muscle-reading & spiritualistic exposé act. Toured USA (1883), Europe, Australia (1886), & Portugal (1887). Memoirs are A Thought-Reader's Thoughts (1888, 326pp), People I Have Read (1905, 192pp), & That Other World (1918). [Pr;Wal;Mo]

name: Cummings, Clare[nce Royal]
bio: (Birmingham, Michigan: 4 Feb 1912-31 Oct 1994) Learned at age 11 from gift of all props from magician George Pullin who was switching to vent. Semi-pro magician since 1930. Aka "Billy Squire" 1931, "C. Royal" 1934, & "Clare Cummings" since 1946. Salesman for DuPont in Detroit 1938-70 when retired to become full-time magician. Played "Milky the Clown" on Detroit TV 1950-1964. Co-invented Out to Lunch (1946, with Bob Ellis) & Idiot Rope (1954, with Bob Lewis). [NT8/74;LR5/59;Wh2]

name: Cummings, Walter E[dward]
bio: (Utica, New York: 9 Sep 1904-Feb 2000) Inspired in 1926 seeing Paul LePaul perform. Learned from magic books in public library. Tarbell Course student in 1927. Pro manipulator & close-up since 1932. Pet books: Buckley's Card Control & Erdnase. A Chavez student & teacher 1950-52. Billed as "Prince of Cards". Vernon dubbed him "Moves Cummings". 1982 Magie Montréal Award. Articles in Linking Ring with original ace routines & sleights. Video. [Wh2]

name: Cummins, Kent [Carter Radley]
bio: (Del Rio, Texas: 6 Jan 1943-) Learned around age 6 from a gift Mysto Magic set. Paid debut in 1953 at age 10. Promotional consultant & semi-pro magician & juggler in Austin, Texas, until 1986 when went full-time pro with walkaround & stage magic plus teaching & collecting. Pet effect: The Sawing (done in audience). 1960 TAOM Junior award. TAOM President 1982-83. Wrote Bungling Juggling (1964, 31pp) & Ideas for Your Spookhouse (1964, 24pp). Tricks in Genii, Linking Ring, Magic Manuscript, Hocus Pocus, Laugh-Makers, etc. [MUM12/95;Wh2]

name: Cummins, Paul W.
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Raised in New York City where he learned closeup from Gene Maze, David Roth, Harry Lorayne, etc. Moved to Florida where became a pro card-&-coin table hopper, bar magician (5 years), & Sarasota's Magic Moment restaurant. Wrote From a Shuffled Deck in Use, Pt.1 (1996, 41pp) & Pt.2 (1996, 36pp). Tricks in Apocalypse, Precursor, Onyx, & the NY Magic Symposium books.

name: Cunning
bio: (Utah, USA: fl.1900s-40s) Stage name of Robert "Bob" Cunningham. Pro escapist-jail breaker-magician in USA. Toured Australia & New Zealand in 1902. Wrote Cunning the Jail Breaker (1907). [Wal]

name: Cunningham
bio: (Britain: fl.c1840s) Minor pro. Toured Scotland & north England. Pet effect: The Gun Trick. [Fr]

name: Curiel
bio: (Germany: fl.1890s) Pro. Credited by Hoffmann (Later Magic, 459) with invention of the Wandering Oranges.

name: Curry, Paul [J.]
bio: (USA: 19 Aug 1917-19 Feb 1986) Inspired at age 9. Hospital administrator. Talented & creative amateur magician. Invented Touch (by 1937), Curry Turnover Change (by 1940), Out of This World (by 1942), The Power of Thought (1947), & Open Prediction (late 1940s). Wrote Paul Curry Presents: Out of This World (1942, 10pp), Something Borrowed, Something New (c.1942, 35pp), Power of Thought (1947, 5pp), Magician's Magic (1965, 269pp), Paul Curry Presents (1974, 108pp), Out of This World--And Beyond (1975, 20pp), & Special Effects (1977, 92pp). 1977 AMA Creative Fellowship. Tricks in Hugard's Annual of Magic: 1937, Phoenix; HMM, Ibidem, Epoptica, etc. See also Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Paul Curry (1986, in French). [Th]

name: Curtin, Joseph J.
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Edited Magic Manuscript 1987?-present.

name: Curvelo d'Ávila, João
bio: (Penafiel, Portugal: 1 Jan 1847-14 Sep 1912) Magician, vent, mentalist, & hypnotist. Moved to Brazil in 1871. Wrote the first two magic books published in Brazil: Segredos da Magia Branca (Rio de Janeiro: 1882, 118pp) & O Mágico Moderno (Rio de Janeiro: 1882, 188pp). [Cam]

name: Cyprian, Reverend, O.F.M. (Cap.), MIMC
bio: (New Rochelle, New York: 13 Dec 1938-10 Apr 2015) Religious name of Harvey Murray, a Capuchin friar in the Franciscan Order. Amateur card expert, known to fellow magi as "Father Cyp". Wrote several booklets on card & close-up magic. See Frank Garcia, The Elegant Card Magic of Father Cyprian (1980, 80pp) & Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Father Cyprian (1983, in French). Also has compiled world's largest catalog of films involving magic (over 500 titles) plus "several thousand pieces of memorabilia". MIMC 1988. SAM President 1989-90. [Wh2]

name: Cyraldo
bio: (Britain?: fl.1940s) Stage name of Cyril Gibbons. Invented "Tubes, Silks and Liquids".

name: Cyro
bio: (Britain: c1903-11 Oct 1977) Stage name of Cyril Brighton (not Baker). Pro magician, clown, & illusion builder. Co-inventor (with Eric Lewis) of Lighted Bulbs from Mouth in 1930s. Trick in Linking Ring.

name: Czernewitz, Alfred
bio: (Germany?: fl.1980s-90s) Amateur in Bonn & later, Rheinbach. Collector of magic books & biographies. Edited Simsalabonn, ZAUBERreport 1992-present, & Zauber-Praxis 1992-present. In 1991 authored a bio of Potassy. Published Mauerspechte (1992, 118pp).

name: Czerny
bio: (Ballarat, Victoria, Australia: 1869-1929) Stage name of Alf[fred] G[eorge] Lumsden. Salesman. Amateur magician to semi-pro in 1902. Pro debut in 1906 as "Czerny", touring Australia, Tasmania, & New Zealand with full-evening show. Retired from stage in 1909, becoming a journalist since 1916. Again a semi-pro magician in 1921 as "Lumsden". [Wal]

name: Czili, Gyula
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 30 Aug 1961- ) Learned at age 16 in magic club. Pro close-up magician since 1986, specialized in coin tricks. Karlovy Vary 2nd place for close-up 1982 & 1983. 1986 Hungarian magic congress 1st place for close-up. Magic manufacturer-exporter (Joker Magic) in Budapest since 1987. [Wh2]

name: Czitaszwili, [David Josifowicz] "Dik
bio: (Poland?: 1913-) Pro manip. Pet effect: The Vanishing Radio, for which he won a prize in 1936.

name: D. Christopher
bio: (Rupert, Idaho: 24 Feb 1964-) Stage name of Terry [Ray] Commons since c1987. Inspired at age 7 by touring magi. Learned at age 9 from library books. Studied mainly theater & design in college. Illusionist, with 6-person act featuring his penguin, "Popper". Designs all his own props except for Kole's Dream Vision & Blaney's Hoop. Also does table-hopping & parties in Provo, Utah, his present residence. 1989 TAOM Stage Trophy. [Wh]

name: Dacri, Steve [Robert]
bio: (Worchester, Massachusetts: 22 Mar 1956 – 11 Feb 2011) Learned at age 6 from a Mandrake magic set & mail-order tricks. Pro comedy close-up since age 13. Also works trade shows. Also works as pro screen writer & film director. Pet effect: Martians (sponge balls). Edited Magic Market 1972-74. A Magic Castle regular since c1975. Invented 60+ close-up effects including Micro-Penny (by 1972). Wrote Penny Fantasy (1972), Commercial Close-Up (1978, 16pp) & Fooling People (1983, 150pp). Articles in MUM & Genii. Videos, including "Magic Secrets" (1987), which has sold over 20,000 copies. [LR10/2005; Mag; Wat; Wh5]

name: Daemon
bio: See: Cameron, Charles W.

name: Daemon Ecks
bio: See: Palmer, Tom

name: Dagmar
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-50s) Stage name of Charles Dagmar, aka "The Great Dagmar". Minor pro illusionist & straight magician on East Coast. Taught John Scarne c1918. Retired in 1952 & sold his big apparatus.

name: Dahms, John P[aul]
bio: (San Diego, California: 22 Jul 1922-9 Mar 1998) Learned at age 6 from Chandu magic set. Master carpenter until retired in San Diego. Amateur magician. For several years has made fine wooden props (wands, Die Boxes, Nest of Boxes, cups, Chop Cups, etc) that are collectables. His line was marketed by Mike Rogers 1987-89 & by Jeff Busby Magic since 1989. [Wh]

name: Dahms, Peter
bio: (Halle, East Germany: 18 Sep 1946-) Pro manipulator with cards, oversized balls, & silks. 1962 East German prize for young magician. 1977 Karlovy Vary prize in manip. Sometimes performs with assistant-wife as "Duo Hasard". [Win]

name: Daily [Jr], George L[ouis]
bio: (Stamford, Connecticut: 24 Oct 1940- ) Learned at age 12 from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set. Sales manager for chemical firm in York, Pennsylvania. Semi-pro performer 1956-79. Serious collector of magic magazines since 1972 & semi-pro dealer in them since 1973 as owner-manager of mail-order "Magicana for Collectors". Co-winner (with Alfredson) 1987 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award. The Daily Collection, begun in 1972, has been the world's largest magic magazine collection since 1978. By 1989 it comprised over 1,100 titles with c45,000 issues. (Daily bought the Paul Koch Collection in 1974 & bought Ellenbogen's collection of magi's coins & tokens c1989.) Editor Magic Collectors' Bulletin 1979-present. Wrote (with James B. Alfredson) A Short Title Checklist of Conjuring Periodicals in English (1976) and A Bibliography of Conjuring Periodicals in English: 1791-1983 (1986, 395pp), the latter being the most nearly definitive book on its subject. Column on tokens in Collectors' Forum. Articles in Magic Cauldron. [Wh]

name: Dailey, Frank [Walter]
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 7 Nov 1919- ) Attorney in Indianapolis, Indiana. Learned magic at age 5 or 6 from Mysto Magic set, etc. Semi-pro magician since mid-1930s. Pet effect: Guatemala Rope. Collector (particularly of Tampa & the Davenport Brothers). Married Margaret Giddens in 1969. SAM President 1983-84. 1991 AIMC. Articles in MUM, Linking Ring, Magicol, Perennial Mystics, & Magic SYMbol. [MUM8/83;Wh5]

name: Dailey, Margaret, AIMC
bio: (Jefferson County, Indiana: 22 Oct 1919-29 Jun 2003) Née Giddens. Computer programmer & systems analyst (retired in 1983). Inspired & taught by her husband, Frank Dailey, since their marriage in 1969. Amateur mental magician. Pet effect: inBloch's Let There Be Light. SAM Registrar & Treasurer 1984-88. Managing Editor of Magic SYMbol 1988-present. SAM President 1990-91, the 1st woman to hold that office. AIMC 1992. [MUM7/90;Wh5]

name: Dakson
bio: (Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil: Jun 1886-3 Dec 1959) Stage name of Paulo Dacorso. Business rep in Rio de Janeiro. Knowledgeable semi-pro magician & magic historian, writing articles for newspapers & for João Peixoto. [Cam]

name: Dalal, Sam [Phiroze]
bio: (Benares, India: 4 Mar 1946- ) Learned at age 12. Civil engineer by college training. Manager by profession until retired in 1975. Semi-pro magician as "Sam the Sham" 1968-75. Since 1975 a full-time pro magic dealer-manufacturer as owner of a retail & mail order magic shop (Electro Fun) in Calcutta. With 50 full-time workers in manufacturing alone, it is the largest magic business & exporter in India. Prolific inventor, including Crystal Thought Condenser (by 1973), Miracle Match, Delna Device, Phantom Phlush, etc. Edited Swami 1972-74 (36 issues) & Mantra 1975-77 (28 issues). Wrote Cabaret Capers (20pp), Sound Mentalism (1971, 16pp), Magic with a Marked Deck (1972, 13pp), Magic with an E.S.P. Deck (1973, 17pp), Magic in the Morris Manor (1974, 128pp, with Bud Morris), My Favorite Verse (1976, a force book), plus some instruction booklets. Articles in Magigram, New Pentagram, Magick, Abra, Linking Ring, Talisman, Invocation, Magic Net, Swami, Mantra, etc. [Wh2]

name: Dalban, Vincent
bio: (London, England: 23 Dec 1896-4 May 1938) Stage name of Vincent Moreland Harris. Pro since 1914 as society & variety magician (specializing in sleight-of-hand card magic & illusions) & mentalist, billed as "The Master Phantasist". Invalided out of British Army in 1918. Worked for a time in 1919, but then again ill. Toured music halls in 1920s. Reviews in Magic Wand as late as 1935; tricks in Jinx. [Le;WWM] d'Alcy, Jehanne (France: fl.1890s-1950s) Stage name of Charlotte-Stéphanie Faes, aka "Fanny Manieux". Principal female assistant (and mistress) of Georges Méliès at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin in Paris. Appeared in many of his films beginning in 1896 with The Vanishing Lady. Since 1897 her then fashionably ample figure was also seen nude in some of his stag films. Left stage & cinema to buy & manage a small candy-and-toy shop in Paris. In 1925 the widow d'Alcy married widower Méliès. d'Alcy, Léo (Saintes, Charente-Inférieure, France: 18 Dec 1857-3 Mar 1926) Stage name of Émile Roché. Pro illusionist (ex-bank employee). Founding member of the ASAP in 1903. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Dale, [Richard Henry] "Dick
bio: (Duluth, Minnesota: 22 Nov 1939-) Raised in Waukesha, Wisconsin. Taught pocket tricks at age 7 by father. Paid debut at age 8. After college had a variety of careers in Flint, Michigan. Part-time pro magician since 1972 with stand-up, close-up, & stage (including black art as "The Wizard of Aahs" since 1976). Moved c1986 to San Diego area where he is a full-time magician and, briefly, dealer (Magic Works). [Magiccurrents11/88;Wh2]

name: Dale, E[dward] J.
bio: (Britain: -22 Mar 1900) Expert electrician & optician. Main assistant & secret stage confederate to Robert Heller until the latter's unexpected death in Philadelphia in Nov 1878. Thence partnered W. Golden Mortimer for a few years. Returned to England where he left magic to open a large electrical shop in London in Oct 1882 as "H. & E.J. Dale, Manufacturing Electricians". [Magic12/01]

name: Daley, Dr Jacob, MD
bio: (Russia: 26 Mar 1897-17 Feb 1954) Moved to USA where raised in New York City. Plastic surgeon. Inspired by & learned from his medical colleague, amateur magician Dr Henry C. Falk, in 1934. Thence a skilled amateur cardman. Favorite book: Erdnase. 1939 Sphinx Award. Nicknamed "Doc" by magicians & "Jack" by physicians. Invented Cavorting Aces & Daley's Last Trick. Posthumously voted one of the Card Stars in 1955. See Karl Fulves (ed.), Jacob Daley's Notebooks (1974, 195pp). Tricks in Jinx, Genii, Phoenix, MUM, & New Phoenix.

name: D'Almoras, Raymond
bio: (Lille, Nord, France: 12 Nov 1868-28 Apr 1944) Stage name of Raymond-Émile Boyaval. Protégé of Alfred "Donato" d'Hont from age 15 until 1900. Thence on own with pro sleight-of-hand. Widowered in 1904, in 1908 he married young Antoinette Dartenset with whom he worked a 2-person mindreading act, she as "Mariska". [Dif; Vo55]

name: D'Alton, Md'lle. Emelie
bio: (Britain: -1945) Stage name of Mrs Carl Hertz (née Emily Dalton) and his main assistant & singer by 1886. After his death in 1924, she worked briefly but unsuccessfully in 1925 in England, billed as "Widow of the Late Carl Hertz". [Pr;Bar]

name: Dalton
bio: (Belgium: 1914-) Stage name of Louis Marchand. Learned from A. Bouché. Pro 1934-1954. Contributor to early issues of Presti. Acquired Bouché's collection of automata, later selling it to L. Tummers.

name: Dalton, Paul
bio: (Lithgow, Australia: 29 Aug 1912- ) Inspired by Australian illusionist "Theo". Amateur until 1938 when turned pro, specializing in manip act with cards, cigs, thimbles, pipes, & billiard balls. Toured major theaters in Australia & New Zealand. Then toured England & Europe 1953-58. Later switched to a Charlie Chaplin impersonation act with comedy magic as "Pete Dene", billed as "The Trump of Tramps". Retired in 1988.

name: D'Alvini
bio: (Hoxton, London, England: 4 Oct 1847 - 14 Jul 1889) Stage name of William Peppercorn. Pro circus gymnast, then juggler. Taught magic at age 18 by Frank Hiam, he added that art to his repertoire. As "D'Alvini, the Jap of Japs" he toured troupe through Europe. Married Isabella English, who joined his troupe as "Madame Kara". Teamed with Patrizio 1883-86, touring South America & the West Indies. From there he moved to the USA in 1886, touring the USA (working as "William Armstrong") on own or with Kellar (1887) and, finally, A. Herrmann (1888-91), dying on tour in Chicago. Bio in H.J. Burlingame, Around the World with a Magician and a Juggler (1891). [Pr;Cl;LR2/51]

name: Damautus
bio: (Spain: fl.1540s) A Spanish knight. Amateur cardman who visited Milan in 1543 in the retinue of Emperor Charles V of Spain. His feats were eyewitnessed & reported by Cardano. [Ch;Dif]

name: D'Amico, Carmen "Carmi
bio: (USA: - 27 Apr 1973) Pro card sharp & carnival game operator. Amateur card magician in Chicago. He invented the D'Amico Spread & Propelled Lapping (jointly with Ed Marlo in 1952). Wrote A Devilish Miracle (1948, 8pp, with Marlo) & Classical Foursome (1956, with Marlo). NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Damico".

name: Dammann, [J.] Günther
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 8 Mar 1910-early 1940s?) German Jew. Taught by Ernest Thorn, he took up magic in 1924. Amateur magician, aka "Robertini". Wrote 3 historical books: Die Juden in der Taschenspielerkunst (1933, 101pp; English tr by Richard Hatch forthcoming), Meister der Zauberkunst (1936, 31pp), Zauberkunst und Zauberkünstler (1937, 125pp). In letters, H. Adrian Smith warned Dammann that his 1933 book on Jewish magicians might inspire Nazi wrath. Dammann was sent to a Nazi extermination camp near Riga, Latvia, where presumably he perished. [St;Go2] "Damon" NOTE: Fictitious hoax magician created by Bill Madsen & run by him with help from L. May, P. Siegel, & N. Bigbee in New Jinx from 1965 until 1968.

name: Danar
bio: See: Taylor, Dana

name: Danby, Jules
bio: (Britain?: fl.1910s) Stage name of Daniel J. Brewer. Invented the Ghost Tube (by 1919).

name: Dandu
bio: See: Dew, Danny

name: Dane, Rex
bio: See: Boles, Don

name: Daniel, Cathy
bio: (Washington, D.C.: 6 Oct 1940- ) Born Catherine Cynthia Birch. Miss Virginia 1960 & in Miss America Pagent. Dancer with Barry Ashton Productions 1965-67. Thence as "Catherine Alden" & "Cathy Daniel" with John Daniel as main assistant in Reno, Miami, & Puerto Rico until they retired from the stage in 1970. Also assisted Alan Wakeling & Orson Welles. [Wh5]

name: Daniel, John [Alden], MIMC
bio: (Pasadena, California: 23 Dec 1931- ) Inspired at age 9 when "Saw a bad magician & thought I could do better". Pro illusionist (having trained under Valleau) since after 1948 when toured Spook Shows as "Doctor Doom" (having bought name & show from Lou Harris) & "Doctor Satan" with assistant-wife Irene Daniel (later Larsen). Co-owner of Owen Brothers in late 1950s when he designed many illusions, including the modern version of the Thin Model Sawing. In 1959 toured 2-person magic act in Europe with Leo Behnke. In 1960 bought Owen Magic. 1968 AMA Best Stage Magician. Producer-star "ShaZzam! review in Miami Beach 1969-70. With assistant-wife Cathy retired from stage in 1970. Dragon Award to John & Kathy Daniel 1998. Father of Dante Larsen. Writing his autobio, Shazzam!: The Book. [HMM5/59;Wh2]

name: Daniels, Dana
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Pro comedy magic & juggling on cruise ships & at Disneyland. [Mag]

name: Daniels, Martin
bio: (South Bank, Cleveland, England: 19 Aug 1963-) Son of Paul & Jackie Daniels. Taught by father at age 13. Pro since age 18. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Daniels, Debbie
bio: See: McGee, Debbie

name: Daniels, Paul, MIMC
bio: (South Bank, Cleveland, England: 6 Apr 1938-) Stage name of Newton Edward Daniels. Son of cinema managers. Inspired & learned at age 11 from How to Entertain at Parties. Debut as teenager. Pro since 1969. TV debut in 1970. Aka "The Eldanis" (with 1st wife Jackie Daniels). Pet effect: Chop Cup. The top-rank pro magician in Britain since late 1970s, now international star. Host & star of the 4 successive weekly programs, "The Paul Daniels Magic Show", on BBC-TV 1979-88. 1982 AMA Award of Merit. 1983 AMA Magician of the Year. In 1988 married his assistant (since 1979), Debbie McGee (see). Won 1988 Magic Circle "The Maskelyne Award" for "service to British Magic". 1989 David Berglas Award for "outstanding contributions to magic". 2001 DRAGON Award (with wife Debbie McGee). Resumed his popular TV show in 1989. King Rat of Grand Order of Water Rats 1995. Father of Martin Daniels. Wrote Paul Daniels' Magic Book (1980), More Magic (1981), Paul Daniels Magic Annual (1983), & 77 Popular Card Games and Tricks (1985). See John Fisher, Paul Daniels and the Story of Magic (1987, 287pp) & Barry Murray, Paul Daniels Adult Magic (1989, 160pp). Videos (1982, 1989) [LR5/90; Mag;Wh2]

name: Danilin, Vladimir
bio: (USSR: c1952-) Interested in magic since age 18. Pro manip act with sight gags. Works with assistant-wife Elena. 1983 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix with 1st prizes in both comedy magic & closeup. Competed at FISM 1988. In England in 1989 filming a Thames-TV bit for Fisher's "The Best of Magic" show. 1991 FISM Grand Prix. Video bit (1991). [Nad]

name: Danilo
bio: (Denmark: 10 May 1912-1985) Stage name of Paul Danielsen. Director of a photographic firm in Copenhagen. Semi-pro magician. 1951 FISM 3rd prize in presentation with partner "Kjeldsen" (not "Killson"). [St] Dante the Great (Salt Lake City, Utah: 8 Jul 1869-29 Nov 1899) Stage name since 1896 of Oscar Eliason, a Mormon. Son of Swedish immigrants, his father being a jeweller. Taught by magic-buff father. Amateur debut in 1889. Pro since 1893. In 1898-99 (with wife & brother as assistants) toured Texas, Mexico, Cuba, Canada, New Zealand, & Australia where he was shot in a hunting accident, dying 3 days later. Bio is Kent Blackmore, Oscar Eliason: The Original 'Dante the Great' (1987 revised, 40pp). [Pr;Wal;Magicana] "Dante--King of Coins" SEE: Buckley, Arthur H.

name: Dante, Madame
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Edmunda Eliason, née Hammer. Originally worked a Georgia Magnet-type act. Married Oscar "Dante" Eliason in 1892. Worked as his assistant, billed as "Mdlle. Edmunda". Then, as his widow, she worked in 1900-03 in Australia in male court dress as "Madame Dante", then returning to the USA and apparent retirement. [Wal;Pr;Magic3/01]

name: Dante
bio: (Salt Lake, Utah: 9 Jan 1875- ) Stage name of Franklin "Frank" Eliason, younger brother of Oscar "The Great Dante" Eliason for whom he worked as main assistant in the 1890s. Waller judged him "the best masculine assistant I have ever seen." After Oscar's death, Frank took the "Dante" title in 1900, touring in Australia & New Zealand 1900-1904 and then back in the USA until as late as 1910. [Pr]

name: Dante, Domenico
bio: (Marostica, Italy: 28 Dec 1947- ) Learned at age 23 in university. General manager. Pro magician since c1986. President, Club Magico Italiano, 1989-present. Dealer (Progetto Magia) in Thiene, late 1980s-present. Wrote a book on dove production (42pp). Articles in Magia Moderna. [Magia Moderna12/89;Wh5]

name: Dante, René
bio: (Campeggine, Italy: 31 Jul 1879-11 Jan 1943) Stage name of Irenée Cocconu. Pro. Moved to neutral Switzerland c1939, operating a magic theater there until it was destroyed during a misplaced aerial bombardment in 1940, which put Dante in hospital until his death 2½ years later. [Dif]

name: Dantel
bio: See: Richardine Jr

name: Dantini
bio: (USA: c1900-14 Mar 1979) Stage name (combining those of his idols, Dante & Houdini) of Vincent Cierkes. Pro magician & mentalist, initially as assistant to Rajah Raboid in 1932. In 1946 stooged in Orson Welles' Broadway production of "Around the World". Did spook shows in 1950s-60s. Then worked nightly for 15 years at the Peabody Book Shop & Beer Stube in Baltimore. [Walk2]

name: Danton
bio:
Grelel, Lee (tentatively)

[See also: Raw, Stuart Drayton]

name: Danut, Bucfing
bio: (Galati, Romania: 14 Jan 1961- ) Learned magic at age 16. Pro since age 18. Founder-manager in 1990? of Entertainment Studio 22 in Galati. Visited USA in 1992. [Magicus-Journal3/90]

name: D'Arcy, Peter
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s) Stage name of Peter Syrett. Wrote Children's Parties a Specialty (1972, 96pp).

name: Darder [Marsa], Dr Antonio
bio: (Catalonia, Spain: fl.1930s-50s) Amateur. President of Asociación Catalana de Aficionados al Ilusionismo 1932-36, Spain's first magic society. Founder-president Sociedad Española de Ilusionismo 1943-48. Wrote Las ilusiones del Ilusionista (1943), Ilusionismo Cerebral (1945), Bibliographía Española de la Prestidigitación (1950)...

name: Darewin
bio: See: "Darwin, Gary"

name: Darius, Prince
bio: (Bombay, India: 7 May 1936- ) Stage name of Dara Rustomji Kaka since 1984. Parsee. Self-taught magic in 1948. Policeman in Tanganyika until 1961 when moved to England. Thence systems analyst until 1984 when became full-time magician with stage, childrens magic, & table-hopping. [MC8/90]

name: Dark, Yamato
bio: (Shimane, Japan: 1 Nov 1926 - 10 Aug 1991) Stage name of Takuzo Hasegawa. Pro comedy magician in Japanese variety theaters.

name: Darling, [Carl] Aage
bio: (Denmark: 7 Apr 1893-31 Jan 1987) Pro debut in Copenhagen in 1908. Toured Scandinavia for the next 59 years. Comedy mentalist, working with his assistant-wife "Madame Ilka" (died 1948). Wrote Darlings Mentale Mysterier (1948), and Tele-Hypnose. One book in translation (by C. Steffensen) is I'll Read Your Mind! (1953, 51pp). Dealer ("Hokus-Pokus") in Copenhagen 1958 to 1960s when succeeded by Aage Rasmussen. [Dif;St]

name: Darnell, Nani
bio: See: Wilson, Nani

name: Darnelle, Jerry
bio: (Luxembourg: fl.1960s) Pro stage magician. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1961.

name: Dart, Ed[ward W.]
bio: (Kansas City, USA: fl.1920s-60s) Learned in youth. Moved to New York City in 1903. Successful insurance salesman by 1909. Amateur magician. Active in SAM since 1929. In 1945 co-founded (with Proskauer & Gibson) Conjurors' Magazine, taking over in Apr 1947 from Proskauer as publisher. Columns in Genii on New York (1949-52) & the MDA (1960s). Edited The Conjurer's Book of Stage Illusions (86pp). [Genii12/65; Genii8/66; St]

name: Darwin, Chevalier
bio: See: Thorn, Heinrich

name: Darwin, Gary
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 19 Sep 1935- ) Stage name of Gary Lee Meador. Inspired at age 6 by grandfather's trick. Semi-pro close-up since age 14, originally in San Diego where his mentor for 7 years was Tommy Woo. Moved to Las Vegas in 1954. Pro (originally with own name, then briefly "Darewin" with death-defying act, finally "Darwin" since c1969) in Las Vegas for 2 years in 1965-66 (at the Flamingo, Lido, & Desert Inn). Thence part-time pro close-up magician working club dates and working in the hotel business until retiring in 1998 to go full-time with magic. Founded & hosts the informal weekly "Darwin's Magic Club" 1968-present. Collector (more than 7,000 books; 3,000 props; 700 posters; 2,000 photos; 5,000 autographs). A mentor of many magicians, including Melinda. A world authority on thumb tip magic. Wrote Darwin's Thumb Tip Miracles (1981, 129pp), Darwin's Close-Up Miracles (1982, 40pp), Darwin's Thumb Tip Secrets (1984, 19pp), Darwin's Thumb Tip Thinking (1986, 20pp), Who Invented the Magic (1988, 28pp), & Magic Autograph Poster Gallery (1989). Tricks in New Tops & Genii. [MUM6/88;NT4/66;Wh]

name: Daryl
bio: See: Martinez, Daryl

name: Das, Sankar
bio: (India: 1928-) Hindu. Pro illusionist. Author. [Mec]

name: Datas
bio: (Newnham, Kent, England: 20 Jul 1875-23 Aug 1956) Stage name of William John M. Bottle since 1902. Gifted with a seemingly superb visual memory (and reportedly later aided by audience confederates) he premiered his giant memory act at the Standard Music Hall, Victoria, London on 16 Jun 1901. An instant success, he played the Palace next February when its manager, Charles Morton, billed him as "Datas, the Man of Memory". Toured the USA in 1904 & Australia in 1910. Inspired the character of "Mr. Memory" in The Thirty-nine Steps, John Buchan's 1915 classic spy novel (& Alfred Hitchcock's 1935 film version). Autobio is Datas: The Memory Man (1932). Wrote Memory by "Datas": A Simple System of Memory Training (1910). [Jay;Wal;Daw2]

name: Daturi
bio: See: de Bischop, Philippe

name: Davenport, Betty
bio: (London, England: 1934- ) Eldest daughter of George Davenport, who taught her magic. Worked in Davenport's since 1948 & its proprietor since 1962. Married Fergus Roy in 1963. Mother of "Bill Davenport" & "Roy Davenport".

name: Davenport, Bill
bio: (London, England: 25 Nov 1966- ) Stage name of William George Roy. Eldest son of Fergus Roy & Betty Davenport. Learned in 1979 from family. Computer consultant. Semi-pro close-up magic. Pet effect: Cups & Balls. 1987 Scandinavian close-up champion. 1988 Italian close-up champion. [Wh2]

name: Davenport, George "Gilly", MIMC
bio: (London, England: 22 Apr 1905-19 Jan 1962) Stage & professional name of George Ryan. Eldest son of Lewis & Julia Davenport. Pro magician & dealer. His father's gradually declining health caused George to increasingly assume management of Davenport's magic shop. Half-brother of Gus Davenport. Father of Betty Davenport. Father-in-law since 1959 of Roy Walton (by younger daughter Jean) & since 1963 of Fergus Roy (by elder daughter Betty). [Genii2/81;Go2]

name: Davenport, Gus, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 8 May 1912-4 Mar 1973) Stage & professional name of Augustus George Ryan (until 1962 when legally changed surname to Davenport). Son of Lewis & Wynne Davenport. Taught at early age by father. Pro close-up & comedy performer until 1949, except for WW II service in Royal Navy. 1937 MZvD prize-winning stage act in Berlin. Pet effects: Three Shell Game & throwing a false knot onto a rope. Made MIMC in 1949. Handled the wholesale [sic] side of Davenport's 1950s-60s. Published several effects in Demon Telegraph & Baron's anthology. Half-brother of George Davenport & father of John Davenport [Daw94,p.72]

name: Davenport, Ira Erastus
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 17 Sep 1839-8 Jul 1911) Pro pseudo-psychic in world-famous spirit-cabinet act with younger brother William. Billed as "The Davenport Brothers" they toured the USA 1855-64, Europe 1864-68, USA 1868-75, Europe 1875-76 and India & Australasia 1876-77. After his brother's death in Australia, Ira returned to the USA to become a farmer. An attempted comeback in 1895 with William Fay failed. Bio is T.L. Nichols, A Biography of the Brothers Davenport (1864, 360pp). An early exposé is "Herr Dobler" [W.G. Smith], Expose of the Davenport Brothers (Belfast: 1869, 48pp). [Pr;Dif;Wal]

name: Davenport, John
bio: (Tonbridge, Kent, England: 14 Oct 1948-) Learned as child from father, Gus Davenport. Company director in Leicester. Amateur magician. Historian (of Davenport family) & collector. Articles in Magic Circular & ABC of Magic Sets. [MC12/81;Wh2]

name: Davenport, Julia
bio: (London, England: 20 Dec 1882-30 Dec 1909) Born Julia Dwyer. Mrs Lewis Davenport (his first wife) from 30 Aug 1904 until her death from TB. Pro magicienne, both as single & as partner with husband when they were billed as the "Lightning Magicians and Illusionists". Mother of George Davenport.

name: Davenport, Lewis, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 26 Dec 1881-14 May 1961) Stage name of George William John Ryan [not "Brein" as often stated] since 1898. Juggler to pro sleight-of-hand magic at age 14 to magic dealer since 1898 as founder of Davenport's in London. Played music halls 1904 to 1930s, including some top theaters (claimed over 1,000 performances at St. George's Hall 1916-23). Also toured Europe, South Africa, & South America. Specialties: billiard ball & thimble manip, color-changing waistcoats, and illusions (for his stage shows). His successive assistant-wives were Julia (died 1909) & Winifred "Wynne" Davenport (married 1910). Father of George & Walter (by Julia) and Augustus "Gus" & Winifred "Wyn" (by Wynne). Lewis's illness gradually caused him to pass the magic shop management to George. Davenport, Roy Edited Demon Telegraph 1933-1940s. Invented improved version of Parasol in 1916. Wrote The Wizard's Pack of Cards (n.d., 4pp). [Geni2/81;Ho] (London, England: 7 Jan 1972- ) Stage name of Fergus John Roy since 1985. Son of Fergus Roy and Betty Davenport Roy. Younger brother of "Bill Davenport". Learned at age 6 from family. Student. Semi-pro magician since 1982 (age 10), specializing in manip with coins, thimbles, billiard balls, & Linking Rings. By age 17 had appeared over 20 times on TV. By 1989 had received more major national & international awards at his age (17) than any Briton in history: 1986 Dutch Magic Circle best foreign act; 1986 Home Counties Championship best act; 1986 Austrian Magic Circle 1st in manip; 1987 Scandinavian Magic Circle 1st in manip; 1987 British Magical Grand Prix Champion; 1988 Italian International Congress 1st in manip; & 1988 World Junior Magic Championship (in Puerto Rico) grand prize winner. [Wh2]

name: Davenport, William Henry [Harrison]
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 1 Feb 1841-1 [sic] Jul 1877) Pro pseudo-psychic with elder brother Ira in the original Cabinet Act since 1855. Died on tour in Sydney, Australia. [Pr;Wal]

name: Davenport, [Bessie Winifred] "Wynne
bio: (London, England: 7 Jun 1891-8 Nov 1981) Born Winifred Ford. Originally a pianist with a novelty musical act in British music halls. 2nd wife of Lewis Davenport (married 25 Dec 1910) & his assistant (as "Winifred Wynne") in 1920s & 30s. Step-mother of George Davenport & mother of Gus Davenport. "Davenport Brothers, The" SEE: Davenport, Ira & Davenport, William

name: Davey, S. J.
bio: (England?: fl.1880s-dead by 1892) Amateur magus & prominent psychic researcher in collaboration with Richard Hodgson.

name: David, Le Grand
bio: See: Bull, David M.

name: David, Jonathan
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Christopher A. "Chris" Faria. Inspired as boy seeing Fantasio and Mark Wilson on TV. Pro magus-vent since 1975. Author. (Norway: 23 Jan 1960-) Stage name of Björn David Fevåg. Pro. NMK Nordic Champion 1981, 1982, 1984. 1982 FISM 1st prize in manip. 1985 FISM 1st prize in general magic. [Mec]

name: Davids, Doris
bio: (USA: 1900 - 27 Feb 1988) Since 1930 worked as a sales clerk in Collins Pentz' Eagle Magic shop in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Pentz gave her the business on his retirement in mid 1950s (he died in 1956) and she ran it until her own retirement in 1971. The shop is now owned by Larry Kahlow (see). [LR6/2001]

name: Davies, Garth W[ilfred] Pryce
bio: (Haverfordwest, Wales, Britain: 21 Apr 1939-) Learned at age 7 from Trixy magazine. Civil servant (computer expert), now working in Luxembourg since 1970s. Semi-pro magician since age 16 (1955) with childrens and cabaret magic. Aka "Garth the Magician" since 1959. Has played in over 15 countries. Pet effects: Billiard Balls, Sponge Balls, Newspaper Predictions. Over 25 tricks in Abra, Magiram, Magic Info, & an article in Magic Circular. TV bits in Britain & Austria. [Wh5]

name: Davies, Henry, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 27 Dec 1911-9 Mar 1990) Learned at age 7 from books. Gave 1st paid magic show at age 13. Stage manager (Old Vic). Semi-pro childrens magician as "Will-A-Maze" since 1930. Collector. Reference Librarian, The Magic Circle, since 1960. The Magic Circle Silver Wand for special service to magic. In 1988 still did 3 or 4 kid-shows per week. MIMC 1989. [NT6/88;Wh]
