name: Davies, Phil[ip]
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s-1910s) Mechanic. Worked for Harry Leat's prop factory in Walworth, England. Then toured as mechanic with Billy "Chung Ling Soo" Robinson, leaving the troupe in 1909 in Australia where he remained. As "Dujeen" managed the "I.G. Magical Manufacturing Depot" in Sydney 1910-1912. [McC; Daw94, p29]

name: Davis, A[lbert] Berkeley "Berk
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 6 Mar 1930-8 Aug 1991) Learned at age 8 or 9 when taught by magician Bill Cardno. Data processing manager. Amateur close-up magician, then since 1989 semi-pro. Pet effects: Cups-&-Balls, McDonald Aces, Out of this World. Invented Third Sight (1989) & Miracle of The Eighties (1989). Tricks in Linking Ring, Genii, Apocalypse, MUM, & Mentzer's Cavalcade series. [LR4/89;Lo2;Wh2]

name: Davis, Alex P.
bio: (USA: fl.1890s) Pro sideshow magician with Sell's Bros Circus, touring USA & Australia (in 1891-92). NOTE: Not to be confused with "Phillip C. Davis". [Wal]

name: Davis, [W.] Alexander
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s-90s) Pro vent-magus. Invented the sliding b Die Box in 1886. [CMM2/08,179;Wal]

name: Davis, Alfred S.
bio: (Forest Gate, London, England: 22 Jul 1893- ) Aka "Stanlyn". Amateur. Articles. [Go;Go2] Davis, Austin A. (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Brother of Henry Davis. Pro booker for several magicians, including Birch (1926-32) & Laurant (1932-33). [Pr]

name: Davis, Henry Hudson
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Brother of Austin Davis. Pro magic-show booker-manager for Marquis, Birch (1932-35), S.S. Henry (1936), Wallace, Homar, & Mel-Roy (1936). [Pr]

name: Davis, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1950s-80s) Pro, originally as "Magicton". 1951 FISM 2nd prize in manip; 1953 Grand Festival International de la Magie 1st prize. Starred at the Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1965-66, 1970-71, 1980.

name: Davis, Phillip C.
bio: See: Anderson, Philip [Prentice]

name: Davis, [Fred] Richard
bio: (Lake Village, New Hampshire: 13 Dec 1875-3 Jan 1933) Self-taught. Pro illusionist since 1903. A star of Lyceum (c1915-c1923) & Chautauqua (c1915-c1928). Retired in 1932. [Pr]

name: Davis, Scott [Hilton]
bio: (Monterey Park, California: 19 Jul 1951-) Learned around 12-13 from library books & meeting escapist Earl Lockman. Semi-pro magician in high school & college. TV producer-director for Maryland public TV. Amateur magician since 1976, specializing in mentalism & spirit magic. Pet effect: Key-R-Rect. Wrote Ray Piatt's Caper Case Book (1984, 25pp), Ray Piatt's Caper Case Book Two (1988, 36pp), & Television for the Mentalist (1988, 20pp). Editor Vibrations 1986-present. Publisher-editor Seance 1988-present. Articles in Magick, New Invocational, Vibrations, & Seance. [Wh2]

name: D'Avison
bio: See: Davison, Robert

name: Davison, E[ddie] Malcolm, AIMC
bio: (Bradford, England: 11 May 1921-14 Jan 1993) Semi-pro magician & psychic entertainer. Aka "Malcolm Morlee". Inventor of "The Man in the Iron Mask". Tricks in HMM. [Budget3/93]

name: Davison, John H.
bio: (Mattewan, New York: 21 Dec 1868-15 Jun 1940) Pro. Edited The Linking Ring 1937-38. IBM President 1937-38.

name: Davison, Robert
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Lived in Bolton, England. Pro illusionist as "Mephisto" & "D'Avison". Wrote (as Davison) Mysteria: A Book of Modern Magical Marvels for Magicians (Bolton: n.d. [1905], 12pp).

name: Davison, William H.
bio: See: "King, Carlton"

name: Dawes, Amy
bio: (Gateshead, England: 16 Mar 1929-) Born Amy Rogerson. In 1950 married Edwin Dawes from whom she learned and then did an amateur double act, most recently in Victorian style as "Professor Bluffman & Madame Patrice". Since 1967 also does her own "Magic Ragtime" rag picture act. Wrote the bio section on British magiciennes in Frances Marshall's Those Beautiful Dames (1984). [MUM11/89; Mar]

name: Dawes, Dr Edwin A[lfred], PhD, DSc, MIMC
bio: (Goole, Yorkshire, England: 6 Jul 1925-) Learned from Xmas gift German magic set. Amateur debut at age 9. PhD 1947. Professor of Biochemistry at the U of Hull since 1963. Amateur magician (aka "Kingstonian" & "Professor Bluffman"). Magic collector, major historian, & lecturer. President, The Scottish Conjurers' Association, 1958-63 & Honorary Life President since 1973. President, IBM British Ring, 1972-73. Honorary Vice-President & Historian, The Magic Circle. SAM Hall of Fame 1984. 1984 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award. 1985 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1988 Magic Circle "John Nevil Maskelyne Prize". Edited S.A.M.S. Magazine 1960-73. Wrote Isaac Fawkes: Fame and Fable (1979, 8pp), The Great Illusionists (1979, 216pp), Vonetta: Mistress of Mystery (1982, 8pp), The Barrister in The Circle (1983, 123pp), Henri Robin: Expositor of Science & Magic (1990, 72pp), The Magic of Britain (1994, 78pp), Charles Bertram (1997, 360pp), & Stodare: The Enigma Variations (278pp). With Arthur Setterington co-authored The Book of Magic (1986, 192pp; in USA as The Encyclopedia of Magic). Historical series (over 235 articles since .....) as "A Rich Cabinet of Magical Curiosities" plus reviews in The Magic Circular. Articles & reviews in Thistle, Budget, Abra, Magic Cauldron, Journal of Necromantic Numismatics, Magicol, etc. See Brian McCullagh, The Magical Writings of Edwin A. Dawes: A Reference Guide (1955-1996 (1997, 30pp, with supplement to 1997)). [MUM11/89;Wad;Wh2]

name: Day, Billy
bio: (England: fl.1950s) Pro kid-show magician. Built tables & vent figures for Davenport's & Unique. Invented Blow-Van in 1955.

name: Day, John
bio: See: Tremaine, Jon

name: Day, Maurice
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Pro childrens magician. Editor of Alakazam 1990-present. Articles in Abra, Magic Circular, Magical Express. Kidshow column in Linking Ring since Jan 1998.

name: Day & Levani
bio: See: Esler, James A.

name: Dayanand, B.
bio: (Calicut, Kerala, India: 20 Feb 1933- ) Born Basava Dayanand Prabhu. Learned at age 9 from books & magician friends of his family. Artist & graphic artist. Semi-pro close-up & parlor magician. Editor-publisher The Ringlet 1983-present & Jumbo Mambo 1988-present. Invented Color-changing Bracelets (1984), etc. Collector with 900 magic books. Articles in Ringlet, Jumbo Mambo, Magic Wand (India), etc. [Wh2] "Dayn, Gid" SEE: Hull, Burling

name: Dayton, Ronald J[ohn] "Ron
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 10 Mar 1945- ) Inspired at age 9 seeing a tent-show magician. Learned in 1955 from a Xmas gift Mysto Magic set. Raised in Port Washington, Wisconsin, where he lives & works for a gardening equipment manufacturer since 1969 as an assembler. Amateur magician, aka "Conraday". Has marketed over 25 coin & key effects, including Unequal Mystery (Blendo to Professor's Nightmare) 1985, Dayton Razor Blade Miracle (variant on the swallowing), & Ultimate Cigarette thru Half 1986. Since 1980 wrote 20 books & booklets, all but 1 published by Hades & mainly on rope magic, including Ropes with a Different Twist (1980, 107pp), Rope without End (1981, 112pp, with R.C. Buff), Secret Thoughts (1983, 80pp), Cord-ially Yours (1983, 45pp), The Whole Art of Clippo Revealed (1987, 37pp), Strange Reflections (1989, 55pp), Dayton's Delights (1991, 490pp), Spoof, It's Magic (1993, 152pp), & 2 with Jeffrey L. Campbell (see). Tricks in Abra, Bluff's Leaflets, Magic Manuscript, Magigram, MUM, Linking Ring (including a 1-man Parade), Magic SYMbol, Houdini-Gram, & a book by Fulves. Writes "Dayton's Deceptive Thoughts" column in MUM. [LR3/90;Wh5]

name: Dean, Carl
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Stage name of Dean Metcalfe. Magic Circle Young Magician of the Year. Pro.

name: Dean, [Richard George] "Dicky
bio: (London, Ontario, Canada: 29 Nov 1938-) Inspired by & learned from Xmas gift of a Walter Gibson book at age 10. Chavez graduate 1956. Teacher & semi-pro stage magician. Then, since 1974, a popular full-time pro in eastern Canada with assistant-wife Marg. Specialties: doves, cards, Zombie. Pet effect: Zombie. Wrote The Dean Speaks (1969), Using Magic in Teaching (1975), & Magic (1975). Articles in Genii, New Tops, Linking Ring, & Pentagram. 6 TV shows on CBC. [MUM8/2003;Wh2]

name: Dean, Henry
bio: (England: fl.1720s) Wrote The Whole Art of Legerdemain, or Hocus Pocus in Perfection (London: 1722, 126pp; with many reprints up to 1983), a work of such sophistication for its time that, as Jeff Busby points out, its Cups-and-Balls routine could play well today--patter and all. This fact, as well as others throughout the book, argues that Dean was no mere layman hack writer, as widely accused. Probably the same man as London magic dealer "H. Dean" who operated a bookshop on Tower Hill by c1758 to at least 1763 and advertised his wares in Henry Dean's book. [TS]

name: Dean, [John Richard] "Jack
bio: (Memphis, Tennessee: 20 Nov 1926-) Learned age 8 from his brother & a neighbor kid's magic set. Semi-pro school shows since age c12, adding mentalism in high school. A professional mechanical engineer until retired in 1986. Dean, Marie Edited-published The Mentalist 1964-65. Full-time dealer ("Jack Dean's Stagecraft") in Memphis, Tennessee, since 1987, catering mainly to mentalists. Inventor-maker of marketed effects, particularly electronic. Does occasional kid shows. Wrote Psychic Sight (1994, 29pp), The Enforcer (27pp), The Equivoque Choice (35pp), & Soothsayer (47pp). Tricks & articles in Linking Ring, Mental-Wise, Magic Thesaurus, The Mentalist, Invocation, & New Invocation. [LR6/54;Wh5] SEE: Bamberg, Marie Dean

name: Dean, Wally
bio: See: Drandorf, William

name: De Barr, Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1860s-70s) Protégé of Compars Herrmann during one of the latter's USA tours in 1860s. Pro stage magic. Sold all his props to Robert Nickle c.1870s.

name: Debarr, Philippe
bio: (France: fl.1850s) Fairly popular pro sleight-of-hand artist. Toured Portugal in 1851. NOTE: Clarke misspells his name as "Philip Debar".

name: DeBarros, Jules
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: c1931-). Learned at age 5 or 6. Joined the IBM at age 18. Pro close-up & stand-up since 1971. Billed as "The Baron". Wrote Coins of Ishtar (1971, 69pp) & Techniques and Principles of Sleight-of-Hand (1982). [Mag] "Debbie" SEE: McGee, Debbie de Biere, Arnold (Poland: 14 Mar 1876-6 Aug 1934) Stage name of Arnold Bierstein (or, some say, Arno Bere). Polish Jew. Brought to USA as child. Learned at age 15 from a box of tricks. Famous pro sleight-of hand artist & illusionist. Pet effects: egg bag, thumb tie, vanishing birdcage, & billiard ball manip. Toured Europe 1903-04. Moved to England in 1904. Toured Australia in 1912 & New Zealand in 1913. Played St. George's Hall, London, in 1919-20 & 1922-23. Died in London. [Pr;Dif;Win;Ch;Wal;Go;Go2;Ho] de Bischop, Philippe (Brussels, Belgium: 7 May 1880-1961 [sic]) Debut as semi-pro illusionist in 1905, touring Belgium, Holland, & France. As "Bel-Kassem" 1909-14 with an oriental act. Aka "Kedour". After WW I turned pro & toured Europe & North Africa with his assistant-wife Eliane as "Ph. de Noran & Daturi". In 1924 returned to Belgium where he gave private shows. Dean of Belgian magicians by 1950. Taught "Freddy Fah". [St]

name: De Blois, Lorne
bio:
de Bodt, Gérard (Belgium: fl.1940s-60s) Amateur magician & manipulator. Wrote Les Carnets de Jerry Jee (1953). Co-edited (with L. Tummers) Presti.

[See also: Houghton, Norman]

name: DeCamps, Eric [Michael]
bio: (Queens County, New York: 16 Feb 1958-) Seriously interested seeing Henning's 1st TV special in 1976. In construction business in New York City. Semi-pro close-up since 1979. Pet effect: Ramsay's Cylinder & Coins. 1989 SAM 1st place (Silver Medal) for close-up. Wrote Compendium I (40pp). Articles in Apocalypse, Magic Manuscript, & Magic Menu. 1 video (1988). See Gary Ouellet, Eric DeCamps Coin Connection (1987). [MM3/87;Wh2] Décamps, Michel SEE: "Zum Pocco" de Caston, Vicomte Alfred (Paris, France: 1821-1882) Aka "Antoine Aurifeuille". Pro cardman & memory feats. He was the mysterious magician whom Charles Dickens saw in Boulogne in 1854. Toured Russia & Poland 1857-58. In Paris by 1868. Memoirs are Les vendeurs de bonne aventure (1846), Voyage en Russie et en Pologne [1858], Tricheurs: scènes de jeu (1863), Les marchands de miracles (1864), & some fiction. [Dif; Vo55; CI]

name: De Caston, Herbert
bio: (South Africa: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Semi-pro in Cape Town. Did a conjuring & juggling act in Japanese costume. Trick in Magic (1906). Wrote Peerless Prestidigitation (1910, 30pp). "De Castro--the Boy Magician" SEE: Bronson, Frederick de Cavananghi, E. (Italy: fl.1870s) Pro sleight-of-hand with cards, coins, silks, and small flags. Toured New York & Boston in 1878. [Mo]

name: De Coligny, J. J.
bio: (France?: fl.1910s) Pro manip by 1911. de Coucy Short, Mayow E. (Southsea, Hampshire, England: 10 Dec 1902-) Semi-pro. [Go2] de Courcy, Howard (Corzoneso, Switzerland: 24 Sep 1914-9 Mar 1990) Stage name of Martin Veglio. Moved to England at age 1. Learned at age 14 from Goldston's Simple Conjuring Tricks. Student of Goldston and Jack Demain. Pro card manip act on British variety stage. His featured assistant, "Garbo", was a canary. Invented the One-Hand Riffle Shuffle by 1945. Retired in 1970. Section in Goldston's Tricks of the Masters. [Wizard1/50;Go2] de Courcy, Ken (Hastings, England: 10 Mar 1922-23 Jul 2008) Stage name of Kenneth William Gurney de Courcy Tyler since 1942. Learned at age 6 from parents gift of an Ernest Sewell magic set. Tutored by Stanley Collins 1938-42. Pro debut 1945-47 touring Southeast Asia for ENSA. Semi-pro c1947-c1964 while in business. Specializes in cabaret & close-up. Stage act with assistant-wife Sue de Courcy since 1969. Pet effect: Knife thru Coat. 1989 AMA Literary Fellowship. British Ring President 1989-90. Wrote over 60 booklets, beginning with Genial Improbabilities (1949, 62pp; repr 1968), then Zodiac Telepathy (1951, 17pp), Automentalism (1953, 15pp), Dubbelkross and Simulkross (1955, 16pp), Son of Pentertain (1974, 29pp), Creditable Conjuring (1983). Edited The Budget for 17 years & Magigram since 1966. Edits-publishes The Coffee-Break Chronicle (limited to 100 subscribers) 1988-present. Articles in Abra, Gen, New Jinx, Tops, Genii, MUM, Swami, & Mantra. [Abra#2330;MUM3/88;Mag;Wh2] de Courcy, Sue (London, England: 31 Dec 1947- ) Stage name of Susan Jennifer Tyler since 1969 when she married & became assistant to Ken de Courcy, having learned magic from him in 1966. Aka "Suzanne" since 1980, working as single. Accountant. Pro childrens, cabaret, & close-up magicienne since 1985. Pet effects: T&R Tissue & Dizzy Dominoes. Articles in The Coffee-Break Chronicle. [Wh2]

name: Decremps, Henri
bio: (Beduer-en-Querci, Lot, France: 15 Apr 1746-1826) Lawyer & student of physics & music. Amateur magician. Had celebrated literary feud with Pinetti in mid-1780s. Admitted to his close friend Ponsin that while he had learned exactly how most sleights were done he had mastered none. Wrote 4 books on magic in French: La magie blanche dévoilée (Paris: 1784). English tr by Thomas Denton as The Conjurer Unmasked (1785, 89pp). Portuguese tr from Denton as O Pelotiquiero Desmascarado (Lisbon, 1791, 102pp; repr 1820 & 1832). Italian tr as La Magia Bianca (Messina: 1793). Spanish tr as La Magia Blanca Descubierta (Valencia: 1833). His next three books were Supplément à La magie blanche dévoilée (Paris: 1785); Le Testament de Jérôme Sharp (Paris: 1785, 328pp) with German tr as Neuer Beytrag zur natürlichen Magie (Berlin: 1788, 159pp); & Codicille de Jérôme Sharp (Paris: 1788, 244pp). His first book is a recognized classic and the others deservedly so. His 5th and last book has little on magic but covers much material on the swindling methods of quacks and sharpers: Les petites aventures de Jérôme Sharp (Brussels: 1789, 266pp) with English tr as The little Adventures of Jerome Sharp (Brussels: 1793, 174pp). [Dif]

name: Dedi
bio: (Egypt: fl. around 2600 BC) Resident of Ded-Snefru in southern Egypt. The earliest named professional magician (posing, it is presumed, as a wonder worker), as reported in the Westcar Papyrus, noting his performance before the Pharoah Cheops of the decapitation & restoration of the heads of a goose, a duck, & an ox. This act was richly rewarded. Dedi was said to be 110-years old at that time, which if true would make him not only the longest-lived magician on record but also the oldest to still perform at that age. It is more likely that he was the first magician to create his own legend. [Dif;Daw;Ch]

name: Dee, John, Dr.
bio: (Britain: 1527-1609). British mathematician, geographer, and astrologer in the service of Queen Elizabeth I. Much overrated as an occultist, a subject to which he was drawn after 1582 by Edward Kelley, a serious "skryer" (spirit medium). The best biography is Benjamin Woolley, The Queen's Conjuror: The Science and Magic of Dr. Dee (2001, 394pp).

name: Dee, John
bio: (Switzerland: fl.1950s) Stage name. 1958 FISM 1st prize for illusions.

name: Dee, Wee Willy
bio: See: Drandorf, William

name: D'Egerton, Ebert
bio: (Britain?: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pen name of Walter D'Egerton. Wrote Aids to Wizardry (London: [1908], 86pp]. "De Fakas, The" SEE UNDER: Pitchford, Robert

name: De Fontenelle, Jean-Simon-Etienne-Julien
bio: (France: 1790-9 Feb 1842) Chemist and physician. He wrote 2 books: Manuel de la physique amusante (1826) & Manuel complet des sorciers, ou de la Magie blanche dévoilée (1829).

name: De Graeve, Dirk
bio: (Avelgem, W. Flanders, Belgium: 19 Mar 1946-) At age 23 (1969) learned from Jean Garmijn. Engineer. Amateur until 1974. Pet effect: Salt Trick. In 1974 bought (with 4 equal partners) "Mephisto-Huis" from Cas G. Ziekman of Amsterdam, Holland, and moved it to Kortrijk, Belgium, where it is the main magic shop & one of the larger ones in Europe, changing its name & legal status to "Mephisto NV" after 1989. [Wh2]

name: DeGraham
bio: (USA: fl. 1940) Stage name of Donald Graham Palmer. In 1945 invented & marketed the DeGraham Utility Outfit, a black-art board, which enabled black-backed cards to disappear when turned toward the audience. de Grisy, Le Comte Edmond (France: 1760-1829) Son of Count de Grisy who was killed in the French Revolution in 1792. Edmond fled to Florence where he studied medicine, taking his degree in 1796. Moved to Naples where he learned magic in 1796 by seeing a performance by Pinetti and figuring out some of his methods. Pro debut on 20 Aug 1796 in Naples. In Rome married 18-year old Antonia Torrini c1802. While performing the Gun Trick in Strasbourg in 1826, he shot and killed his son Giovanni. Imprisoned for 6 months for this accident. Then took the stage name of "Torrini" in 1827. Met Robert-Houdin in Jul 1828. Died of typhus fever at Lyon in 1829. Perhaps only a fictional character created by Robert-Houdin, as generally believed since 1943 when Jean Chavigny attempted to debunk this part of Robert-Houdin's autobiography on the grounds that his research in French archives had turned up no independent evidence of any magician of that name. However two authorities have since claimed independent evidence. First, McArdle (1963, p.43) who cites and summarizes an otherwise unreported source: Jean Lecoq's Le histoire de famille DeGrisy (1831), which McArdle claimed confirms all major points mentioned by Robert-Houdin. Second, Dr Metin And, Magic in Istanbul (1978, p.33), who cites an unspecified Turkish source mentioning an unnamed foreigner who built a theater in the palace of Sultan Selim III (ruled 1798-1807), just as Robert-Houdin claimed De Grisy told him he had done. I find no listing of the Lecoq book in either the Bibliotheque Nationale's published catalogue or the main French publishing lists for 1831-32.

name: Deighton, Maurice [Walter]
bio: (London, England: 31 Dec 1922-) Learned at age 10 from aunt's Xmas gift of magic set. Railway clerical officer (now retired). Pro magician since 1982, specialized in kid-show, cabaret, close-up magic. Also lectures (including USA & Canada) plus demming at conventions for Castle Magical Services. Articles in Abra & Magigram. [Wh2] "De Jean, Gene" de Kastrozza, San Martino SEE: McIntosh, Gene SEE: Kastrozza, Prof. San Martino de de Kolta, Buatier (Lyon, France: 18 Nov 1847-7 Oct 1903) Stage name of Joseph Buatier since 1873 or 74. Inspired around age 16 seeing a magic show. Debut as amateur around 1868 in seminary show. Pro since 1870 when he joined the troupe of Julius Vido de Kolta, touring Europe until 1873. Thence, on own, toured France (from 1874 to 1903), Spain (1874), Portugal (1874), London (1875-76, 1883, 1886, 1888-89, 1891, 1895, 1897), Holland (1881), Belgium (c1881), Russia (1886), USA (1891, 1902-03). Joined the SAM in Oct 1902. Was on 2nd USA tour that year when died suddenly of Bright's disease in New Orleans. Nearly all tricks and illusions presented by him were of his own invention. Buried in London. Invented Vanishing Birdcage (1875), Buatier Pull (1875), Multiplying Billiard Balls (1875), Cocoon (1885), Vanishing Lady (1886), Spring Flowers (by 1890), The Captive's Flight = The Human Cage (1891), The Ladder = The Miracle (1897), possibly Rapping Hand (by 1899), Expanding Cube (1902), etc, etc. Bio is Peter Warlock, Buatier de Kolta: Genius of Illusion (1993, 217pp). [Daw#97-98,#103,#105,#118;Dif;Ch;Pr;Fi;Go2;Bur] de Kolta, Julius Vido (Hungary: fl.1860s-70s) Showman & impresario. Seeing Joseph Buatier perform card tricks for friends in a café in the latter's hometown of Lyon, De Kolta induced the 22-year old amateur to turn pro by joining his troupe of travelling players and tour Europe. They parted company by 1873 & by 1874 Buatier was on his own as "Buatier de Kolta".

name: Delacie, Don
bio: (USA: 14 Mar 1888-4 Oct 1917) Stage name of Henry Schneider. "De La Cour, Blanche" SEE UNDER: Anderson, Philip [Prentice]

name: Delafiaure
bio: (Strella, Italy: 22 Apr 1821-22 Sep 1896) Stage name of Luigi Francesco Delafiora. Pro stage magician & proprietor of a travelling circus. Based mainly in France where he was known as "Louis-François de Lafiora". Toured Africa (1848) & Brazil (4 years). Returned to Europe in 1852, touring Africa until 1866. Then converted his circus to the travelling Théâtre Delafiora, touring it throughout the Continent (including Portugal in 1885) until his death in 1896 when it passed to his son, Célestin. [Rob; Dif; Cam]

name: Delafioure, Louis
bio: (France?: c1876-1919) Grandson of the original Delafioure & son of Célestin. Pro magician with stage name of "Frego". Inherited the Théâtre Delafioure in 1903, touring it until his death in 1919, which marked the end of the 53-year run of this famous 3-generation travelling magic theater. [Dif]

name: DeLage, Al[fred]
bio: (New Bedford, Massachusetts: 1914-15 Jan 1998) Learned in 1922 from Mysto Magic set & father's pocket tricks. Pro club & stage magic, working his whirlwind "The World's Fastest Magician" act with his successive assistant-wives Shirley (1936-55) and Margaret (1955-present). Played the New York Palace in 1950 & 1956. SAM Parent Assembly Magician of the Year 1976 & 1977. Invented Fastest Trick in the World, 6-Foot Blendo, Rabbit to Fishbowl, & Triple Dog Production. Wrote 3 lecture notes. Articles in MUM & Tops. [LR1/92;Des;HMM1/51;Wh2]

name: De La Mano
bio: (Austria: fl.1830s-80s) Stage name of Zell Dreitzehn. Toured Europe for 4 decades before his 1st USA tour in 1876, the 3rd & final one being in 1881. [Yankee Magic Collector #3]

name: DeLand Jr, Theodore L.
bio: (USA: 25 Sep 1873-25 Jan 1931) Semi-pro magic dealer (engraver & later Superintendent of the U.S. Mint in Philadelphia by 1908). Designed the covers for first two issues of Edwards' Monthly (1909). Famous for his line of trick cards. Began privately making gaffed decks as early as 1905 when he printed for Henry Hardin the latter's Monte Cristo Deck. Invented & marketed The Devil's Own (1906), Phantom Card (1907), X-Ray Deck (1907), the Clock System for marking cards (by 1908), Yogi Wonder (early 1908), The LeRoy [sic] Four Ace Trick (1908), Pickitout (Jun 1908), Knock Out (Jul 1908), Fadeaway Card (late 1908), The Haunted Ace (late 1908), Papel Blanco (late 1908), Nox-em-all (late 1908), Inhumanata or The Devil's Dream (late 1908), Wonder Change (early 1909), The Spotter or the Educated Die (Mar 1909), from suggestion by Gus Bohn), Sphinx Card Trick (mid-1909), Rainbow Card Cremation (late 1909), Vanishing Pack of Cards (late 1909), Two Card Monte (c1909), DeLand's Dollar Deck (1910), Million Dollar Mystery (1) (late 1910), Perfection Changing Card (early 1911), Fly-a-way (early 1911), DeLand's Rising Cards (by early 1912), Surprise (by early 1912), Best Ever (by 1913), Four Dollar Deck = Wonder Pack (by 1914), Tip Top (by 1914), Toko Card Trick (by 1914), Eureka (by 1914), Card Locator (1914), Inverto (by 1919), Nifty Deck (1919), Dope Deck (1920), & Irish Card (= The Leopard Card, a changing card). Issued his Trickards Catalogue in 1914, which listed 33 of his inventions. In 1918 sold his entire existing line (including engraved plates) to S.S. Adams but continued to invent until 1922. Died in the insane asylum in Norristown, Pennsylvania. Bios by Walter Gibson in both The Conjurors' Magazine (May & Nov 1940) & True Police Cases (Dec 1950). Richard Buffum is planning a book on DeLand's life & gaffed cards.

name: DeLap [Jr], [Truman Henry] "Tony
bio: (Oakland, California: 4 Nov 1927- ) Learned magic at age c10 from amateur neighbor Les Sterner's Tarbell course. Artist, moving to Southern California in 1965 whence he has taught at U California Irvine until 1991. Amateur magician specialized in card magic. Pet effects: Slow Motion Aces & other Vernon material. In 1974 filmed a 4-hour tape of Vernon. Collects magical graphics. [Wh] de Lara, Paul (Britain: -25 Dec 1919) Amateur? Member of The Magic Circle. Father of Rita de Lara. [Daw2] de Lara, Miss Rita (Britain?: fl.1920s) Stage name of Marguerite de Lara, daughter of Paul de Lara. Pro sleight-of-hand stage magic in Britain.

name: Del-Ardo
bio: See: Magnuson, W.G.

name: DeLarno, MIMC
bio: (New Zealand: 1935 – April 2006) Stage name of R[obert] Burns Scandrett, known as "Burns". Learned around age 7. Pro dealer (DeLarno's Magic Centre) 1956-1996. His main shop was in Christchurch, New Zealand, with a branch (owned by Alf Hayes) in Sydney, Australia, since 1966. Was one of largest magic dealerships in South Pacific. Has done cruise-ship magic and performed in Britain, USA, Australia, & Japan. Over 200 TV appearances in 4 countries, including own TV show in New Zealand. Pet effect: The Sawing. MIMC with Gold Star in 1989. NZ “Grand Master of Magic” (2001). Tricks in Genii & MUM. [McC; Magicana#134] de la Torre, José (Cuba: fl.1950s-90s) Aka "Grandini". Amateur. Moved to USA. Wrote Magicana of Havana (1975, 80pp) & Real Magic (1978, 127pp). Translated Ascanio's World of Knives (1975). de la Vega, Michel (France: fl.1950s-70s) Pro illusionist with Sub Trunk, etc. Played the Cirque Medrano in Paris in 1957, Canada in 1960, & the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1967, 1969, 1973. [HMM9/60]

name: DeLawrence, George
bio: (Tennessee, USA: c1887-21 Feb 1928) Stage name of George Silver. Pro Lyceum magician & cardman. Minor dealer in Chicago in 1910s, operating as "The De Laurence Company" specialized in the occult. Wrote Some Card Effects and Magical Talks (1919), A Vaudeville Magic Act (1919, 28pp), Modern Card Effects and How to Perform Them (1920, 80pp, with J.C. Thompson), Impromptu Magic with Patter (1922, 80pp), Pithy Patter (31pp), Miscellaneous Handkerchief Tricks (37pp), How to Answer Questions in Crystal Gazing, Mysteries of Crystal Gazing, The Silky Slicker, etc. Trick in Felsman's (Oct 1919). [Dor; Magical Bulletin 10/20]

name: Delbert, Donna
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of John Hill. Pro sleight-of-hand artist, fire-eater, & lightning calculator. As a US Army private & deserter in England after WW II he played the London music-halls for 3 years while disguised as a woman & billed as "The Outstanding American Lady Magician". Arrested by US Military Police in 1949 & sentenced to 2 years prison. In 1953 MC'd (in drag) a show of the IBM's annual convention in Philadelphia. [Dif]

name: Delcassan, André
bio: (Paris, France: 13 Jul 1907-28 Aug 1982) Learned magic in youth. Pro as "Satanas" since age 24. Charter member in 1936 of the Amicale des Magiciens du Sud-Est (Nice) & in 1937 of the Club des Magiciens Bibliophiles. In 1939 he became a pro lightning calculator. Also did mentalism as "Sanas". His son was also a magician. [Dif]

name: Delf, Mickey
bio: (Linz, Austria: 19 Sep 1921-17 May 1991) Stage name of Max Lidauer. Moved to Switzerland by 1970s, living in Berne. Pro manipulator. Developed an innovative Cups-&-Balls routine.

name: Del Gardi, Rita
bio: (Nashville, Tennessee: 14 Jun 1902- ) Stage name of Rita Privette. Pro vaudeville illusionist since 1919. Moved to New York City. Played Vancouver's Beacon Theatre in 1935 billed as "The Female Deceiver" with a female assistant. Pet effects: Costume Trunk & Needle Trick. [Tay;WWM;HMM7/58]

name: Delhi, Mago
bio: (Mexico: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Pascual HERNÁNDEZ BECERRIL. Pro? in Mexico City. 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. de Lille, Adrien (France: fl.1820s) Stage name of Adrean Goujon. Pro travelling magician. Father of "Victor de Lille". NOTE: I am unable to resolve the Adrian/Adrien & De Lille/Delille spellings used by members of this family. All versions appear in their own paper.

name: Delille, Adrian
bio: (Millau, Aveyron, France: 22 Jun 1833-18 Jul 1915) Stage name of Adrien Goujon, son of "Victor de Lille". Pro. Toured the Orient in 1873 with François de Villers as his assistant. Brother of "Louise Delille". [Dif]

name: Delille, Mademoiselle Louise
bio: (France: fl.1850s-80s) Stage name of Mlle Goujon. Pro magicienne in Paris. Sister of "Adrian Delille". [Dif] de Lille, Victor (France: fl.1830s-50s) Stage name of Victor-Bonnaventure-Antoine Goujon, aka "Mons. Adrien". Son of "Adrien de Lille". Pro magician, with fantasmagoria and plate & top spinning. Played The Strand in London in Jan 1838, Boston in Jun that same year, & France as late as 1859 when he was also doing vent. NOTE: Billed in London as "Mons. Adrean" & in Boston as "Mons. Adrian". Father of "Adrian Delille" & "Louise Delille". [Dif;Mo]

name: De Line
bio: (France: fl.1880s) Pro. Killed his son-assistant doing the Bullet Catch in 1890. de Linski, [Chrétien-Jean-Baptiste] (USA: 1827-16 [or 18?] Feb 1882) Pro. Toured the world. Played the Drury Lane Theatre (London) in 1853, billed as the "Great French Wizard". Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1881-82. [Dif; Vo55] de Liński, Louis (Warsaw, Poland: 1764-) Pro. Debut in France with "experimental natural magic". Killed his wife-assistant on stage at Arnstadt on 10 Nov 1820 doing the Bullet Catch. [Mec;Fr;Dif] de Linski, Louis (France?: 1831-) Pro who performed in the tradition of his namesake although with less lethal consequences. [Mec] de Lion, Clément (Copenhagen, Denmark: 31 Dec 1875-18 [sic] Aug 1965) Stage name of Knud Valdemar Clement. Inspired by & learned from his pro father at around age 15. Debut at age 17 as amateur & in 1897 as pro at the Arena Theatre in Copenhagen's Tivoli Gardens. Famous for card manip 1899-1901, playing the London Palace in 1900. Briefly ran a magic shop in Copenhagen until c1900. Then in 1901 at Innsbruck, Switzerland, became the first to do the ungaffed Multiplying Billiard Balls (12 of them!), for which he became world-famous during tours of Europe & North America, playing Italy (1901), the London Palace (1902), Paris Olympia (1902), Spain (1906), USA (1908 & 1910 plus 2 later years), England (1911), etc. Husband of "Anonyma" (see). Charter member of the CSP 1904. Retired from theater work in 1922, settling in Nice where he played occasional cabaret dates until 1935. Moved back to Denmark after WW II. See Ellis Stanyon, Original Tricks of Clement de Lion (1902). Wrote Tryllebogen (1910). Articles in Prestidigitateur. Many autobio articles in Magikeren. [Pr;Magic4/02;St;Dif;Mo]

name: Delisle, Sieur
bio: (France: fl.1740s) Pro sleight of hand. Worked the Cups and Balls and the Omelette Baked in a Hat at the St.-Germain fair in Paris in 1749. [Dif;Cl] Dell and Her Doves (England: fl.1960s) Stage name of Dolores "Dell" Johnson. Cabaret & theater magicienne. 1963 Craig Trophy for her dove production act. TV bits.

name: Deller, Mac
bio: (Switzerland: -early 1970s) Real name Robert Dolder. Pet effect: Bullet Catch, inspiring Ralf Bialla to add this effect to his repertoire. A suicide. [MUM3/95, pp.14,15.]

name: Delmar, Russell
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-80s) Stage name of Anthony DiSario. Pro dealer (The Magic Center) in New York City for many years since buying it from Al Cohn in 1951. [Des]

name: Delmo, Arthur
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Arthur Miller. Pro society conjurer in Edinburgh in 1901.

name: Del Monte
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Stage name of Charles M. Reagan. Inspired by seeing Thurston show. Taught by his mute friend, Miaco. Semi-pro pantomime magic act with female assistant. Hypnotist. [Th]

name: Delord, Jacques
bio: (France: 1928-) Stage name of Roger Lajunias. Pro magician in Paris. Wrote Sois le magicien (1971), Sois l'enchanteur (1972), L'éternel magicien (1973), Les ateliers du magicien, & Mes premiers tours de magie (1978). Articles in Mad Magic & Magicus-Journal. de Lorget, Bouthoux SEE: Bouthoux de Lorget

name: Delphin
bio: (France: c1881-8 May 1938) Stage name of Jules Sirvaux. A dwarf (or midget). Pro magician in Paris before 1900. Later popular in theater & cinema. A suicide. [Dif]

name: Delphin de Mazaubert
bio: (Camiran, Gironde, France: 15 Feb 1886-14 Jun 1960) Stage name of Jean Goujon. Secretary to Pickman in 1904. Debut as pro stage medium "Delphin" in 1907. [Dif]

name: Del Ray
bio: (Hubbard, Ohio: 27 Nov 1927 – Pittsburgh, Penn: 18 Nov 2003) Stage name of Raymond "Ray" Petrosky, aka "Seymour Potowsky", aka "Delbert Raymond". Learned from gift magic set as a child in an orphanage. An assistant to Blackstone in 1940s. Pro close-up & card magic. Also famous for dice work. Played Ed Sullivan TV show in 1951 & the New York Palace in 1953. 1991 AMA Performing Fellowship. Retired 1993. NOTE: Sometimes misspelled "Del Rey". Refused to teach anyone any of his methods: "When I go...my secrets go with me." [LR1/2004;Phoenix#231;HMM7/51;Des]

name: Delson, Miss Renée
bio: (France: fl.1930s) Pro illusioniste. Toured France with Bénévol's troupe 1938-39. (Britain: -8 Apr 1900) Stage name of Israel Clark. Pro illusionist.

name: Delvards-Link
bio: (France: 20 Nov 1867-17 Jun 1929) Stage name of Jean-Marie-Georges Pétrod. Pro. Joined the ASAP in 1921. [Vo55]

name: Delveen
bio: (England: fl.1910s) Stage name of H. Naylor. Billed as "Delveen the Mystic". Edited The Magical Record 1915-18 (15 issues).

name: Delvin, Jack, MIMC
bio: (Bromley, Kent, England: 6 Oct 1932-) Stage name of Jack Ogan [sic] since c1945. At age 6 inspired by a neighbor's trick & learned reading "The Yellow Peril" magic books & buying tricks from Woolworths. Honed skills managing London store's magic section & as assistant to Jack Hughes. Pro club worker in London & Europe ages 20-35 & again since age 45. Specializes in illusions, mental magic, & childrens shows. Had long-running radio show on mental magic. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Book Tests. Invented Pearl Necklace Mystery (Superette, 1959) & Rocket Ship X (1950s). MIMC 1977. Adviser for TV shows. Wrote Magic of the Masters (1977, 240pp). Articles in Abra. Many TV bits. [MC7/85;Wh5]

name: Delvin, Ralph
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-50s) Stage name of Ralph D. Widocks. Society magician. Noted for his live canary "Sally" who picked out selected cards. [Daw2]

name: Demain, Jack
bio: (Canada: fl.1920s-40s) Debut in 1921. Pro manip with coins, cigs, thimbles, & cards.

name: Demaline, Jesse
bio: (Britain: c1910-14 Mar 1990) Insurance salesman. Articles in Abra, etc. See Brian Lead & Roger Woods (editors), The Magic of Jesse Demaline (1990, 120pp). de Manche, Henri (Britain: fl.1890s) Stage name. Invented De Manche Change by 1903. [Daw#121]

name: De Mario
bio: (Italy: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Mario Delladdio. Pro in Turin.

name: De Meglio
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-1910s) Stage name of J.W. Riley. Manager of H. Wiles's "Conjuring, Toys & Fancy Goods Shop" in Manchester. Wrote Magical Programmes and How to Present Them (1914). [Daw2] de Merry, Jean, AIMC (Geneva, Switzerland: 25 Feb 1930-) Stage name of Jean Graf. Inspired & learned at age 10. Paid debut at age 15. 1952 FISM 1st prize in vent. Pro magus-vent 1952-69 when went semi-pro. AFAP Master Magician 1955. Collector of over 3,000 books & pamphlets. Edited Magicus 1954-55 (6 issues). Current editor of French edition of Hokus-Pokus. Wrote Je suis ventriloque (1972) & 11 other magic books. Articles in Linking Ring and columns in Revue de la prestidigitation & Hokus-Pokus. Currently (2001) drafting a French-language dictionary of magic. [LR8/01;Dif;Wh2]

name: DeMuth, Fred[erick K.]
bio: (USA: c1885-15 Nov 1961) Worked at the Corning Glass Works for 38 years. Amateur magic inventor & performer. Invented the DeMuth Milk Bottle (by 1932) & a version of the Salt Trick. Reportedly devised the locking device for the Penetration Frame. Tricks in Jinx, New Jinx, etc.

name: Dene, Peter
bio: See: Dalton, Paul

name: De Nijs
bio: See: "Ten-i-Chi"

name: Denis, Alain
bio: (France: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Alain MONTILLA [CASTELLSEGUER]. Moved to Spain. Pro since his debut in Barcelona in 1962. Works with wife "Monika Bell" (Gracita Guerra). They took 1st prize in stage magic at 1971 Spanish National Congress (in Saragossa). Toured Portugal 1972-73. [Xe]

name: Denis, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Educator in Cerville. Semi-pro childrens magician & vent. AFAP Bronze Medal 1982 & Silver Medal 1988. [Bou2]

name: Denise
bio: (Huddersfield, England: 25 Jan 1868-20 Jun 1940) Stage name of Herbert Denison. Prosleight-of-hand & illusions on Blackpool beach. Wrote Puzzledom (1907; reprint 1911) & Book of Magic [c1907]. Bio is Reg Parkinson, Denise: Prestidigateur and Illusionist (1986).

name: Denk, Dr Karl
bio: (Austria: 24 Jun 1886-1948) Comedy magician in Vienna in 1920s & 30s. [Al]

name: Dennison, Edward
bio: (England: -4 Jun 1954) Student of Walter Jeans. Pro manipulator. Aka "Morrell" & "Remarque". Inventor of several tricks, including Return to Karnak & Silver Phantom, sold by Ken Brooke at his magic shop in Bradford in the 1940s. Father of Gene Dennison. [Daw2]

name: Dennison, Gene
bio: (England: fl.c1940s) Son of Edward Dennison. Worked as pro magician at age 15. Aka "Morrell junior, the Prince of Magic" & "Rafayelle". "de Noran, Ph." SEE: de Bischop, Philippe

name: Denton, Thomas
bio: (Yorkshire, England: -1 Jul 1789) Bookseller in York, then magic publisher in London & probably a magician. Translated Decremp's The Conjurer Unmasked (1785) with the addition of 5 new tricks, suggesting Denton's personal knowledge of magic. Hanged in front of Newgate Prison for possession of counterfeiting tools. [Daw;Cl]

name: Denys, Jos
bio: (Kuurne, Belgium: 1 May 1965-) Learned at age 15 from Jean Garmijn. Amateur to pro (as dealer). Stage name: "Djoziny". Employee with Mephisto-Huis 1978-1986. Co-founder & co-director (with Jean Garmijn) Select Magic in Kortrijk 1987-present. [Wh5]

name: Deodato, Signor Joseph
bio: (Mesuraca, Catanyaro, Italy: 18 Dec 1867-) Pro sleight-of-hand conjuror, fire king, & sword swallower. Toured Canada & USA 1907-08. [CMM6/08] de Paula, Peter (USA: 1953-) Learned at age 8. Pro since age 13. Stage act of mime-&-magic, with 3 world tours. Star of road-show version of Doug Henning's The Magic Show in the late 1970s. [Mag;Wat]

name: DePrince, Dr T[hessalonia Jackson]
bio: (Cap-Haïtien, Haiti: 13 Sep 1952-) Black. Interested in magic at age 7 from grandfather's stories of Dr Alexander the Great. Moved to USA as child. Since age 18 part-time pro with mentalism, close-up, & hypnotism, specializing in cold reading & spook magic. Then became Voodoo priest in New York City. Wrote 2 occult books & reprinted a Nelson catalog under own name. Article on zombies in New York in Journal of American Folklore (1983). [Wh2]

name: Derka-Hartung, Rudolf
bio: (Austria: fl.1910s-20s) Travel photographer based in Vienna. Amateur manipulator. Lived with Indians in Peru & Ecuador before WW I. After the war travelled throughout South America. [Al]

name: Derman, Lou
bio: (New York City, New York: 26 Sep 1914-15 Feb 1976) Radio & TV comedy writer since 1944, finally in Hollywood. Taught magic by younger brother Bill Derman. Semi-pro comedy close-up. 1971 AMA Award of Merit. 1973 AMA Best Lecturer. AMA Board of Directors 1974. Wrote Add Comedy to Your Act (1972, 50pp). Memoir of his time (1937-43) as a postal clerk is You Can't Mail an Elephant (1958). Wrote columns "Magic at the Castle" in Genii & "Legerdermania" in Linking Ring. [Mag]

name: Derman, William [NMN] "Bill
bio: (New York City, New York: 15 May 1916-21 Jan 1997) Younger brother of Lou Derman. Comedy writer & TV game show package producer. Taught first card trick in 1950 by Milton Berle while working for him as a gag writer. Taught in 1951 by Doc Hurwitz & George Sands while writing Shari Lewis' act. Founding Member (#68) of the Magic Castle. At age 59 turned pro (ex-TV comedy writer) card magician at trade shows 1975-87 as "Mr Cards". Retired in 1987. Invented Bill Derman No-Slit Card in the Envelope (marketed in 1987). Tricks in Genii, Apocalypse, & the Hugard-Braue Royal Road to Card Magic. Wrote Card Tricks that Get the Money and The Patter that Gets the Bookings (1993, 121pp), which includes much bio info. Article in Genii. [Wh5]

name: Derner, Adolf
bio: (Elberfeld, Germany: 4 Dec 1882-21 Jul 1956) Stage name of Adolf Derner, aka "Tom Jersey", "Jersey Tom", "Tom Tommsen", "Jersey Tommsen" (1930s). Pro manipulator by 1910 with card, coin, silk, & cigarette tricks. Also shadowist. After WW I did stage magic. Retired during WW II when his hands were destroyed during an Allied bombing. Died in Wuppertal-Barmen, Germany, the year after his wife's death. [Vo57;St;Al;Mül]

name: De Rocroy, Le mystérieux
bio: (Boukafénis, Oran, Algeria: 27 Oct 1890-18 Nov 1962) Stage name of Pierre[-Marie-André] Dessertine. Of French parentage, his father being a bank director in Oran. Pro manip & illusionist since 1907. Played the Folies-Bergère 1916. Invented Satanella & La Moto Éclipsée (1916) illusions. Wrote Comment on devient Magicien, On peut voler aux cartes, etc. [Dif;Rob1] de Rovère, Jules SEE: Rovére, Jules de

name: De Roze
bio: (Switzerland: fl.1930s) Pro. Introduced Rhyss's Bar Act to the USA in 1934-36 when he played New York City. [Pr;Ho] de Russe. The Countess (Britain?: fl.1910s) Pro, combining magic with a protean act. Performed in England in 1910. de Saurin, Mons. (Britain?: fl.1840s) Minor pro. Played English seaside resorts in 1842 as "The Wizard of the West". Played London c1843 as "Mons. de Saurin". [Fr;Cl] de'Seevah, Henri, MMC (England: -3 Apr 1963?) Stage name of Henry Hancock. Pro dealer in Birmingham in 1950s. Motto was "An Effect in the Show is Worth a Dozen in the Cupboard". NOTE: I suspect a confusion over date of death with the following.

name: De Seive, Will
bio: (North Shields, England: -23 Apr 1963) Stage name of William H. Wilson. Semi-pro society magician & shadowist by 1910. Moved to USA in 1913. Improved & popularized Kolar's Magic Shears as Clippo (1937). Invented Koda-Kard (by 1940) & Infracardo (by 1941). Wrote What! No Card Tricks? (1933), Sensational Card Tricks (1934), & These Card Tricks (1936, 24pp). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "De Sieve". [Th;Magic3/11]

name: Désirée, Mdlle. Aimée
bio: (England: fl.1880s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Mrs G.W. Hunter. Aka "Mystia". Pro sleight-of-hand since 1889. Played the London Pavilion in 1890. Toured Australia in 1909 when she sometimes worked a comedy double-act with her husband--she as the slick "modern" magician, he as the bumbling "old-fashioned" one. Retired in 1909. [Wal;Cl]

name: Desfor, Irving "Doc
bio: (New York City, NY: 13 Apr 1907-27 Nov 1993) Professional photographer with AP 1929-1972 when retired, continuing as freelance columnist for AP until 1979 when he moved to Florida. Amateur & semi-pro magician since 1931 when taught by Dr Joseph Fries. Desfor did his "Photo-Magic" act since 1948 in USA, Europe, & Singapore. World-famous for his photographs of magicians in action, beginning with Blackstone in Dec 1938 [sic]. In 1978 donated nearly 40,000 [sic] of his photos to the American Museum of Magic. Authored Great Magicians in Great Moments: A Photo Album (1983, 208pp, 157 photos). His photos have appeared in most major magic journals over past 50 years. 1984 AMA Special Fellowship. [Magic12/93;Se;SAM;Wh2]

name: Desideri, Lamberto
bio: (Rome, Italy: 15 Aug 1935-8 Aug 1996) Learned in 1948 from books. Chemist. Semi-pro magician since 1958, specialized in card magic. Magic dealer (La Porta Magica) in Rome since 1981. Edited Inoltre 1976-81. Wrote Trattato di Technica Cartomagica (3 vols, c500pp), Lezioni di Arte Magica (5 vols, 1982-91, c1,000 pp, with Vinicio Raimondi), & Cartomania (50pp). [Wh2]

name: Desimo
bio: (Germany: 17 Nov 19-) Stage name of Detlef Simon. 1987 MZvD 2nd prize in comedy magic. Had own TV series ("Halli Galli") in 1993. [Nad]

name: De Soboll, F[elix] Stephen
bio: (Tacoma, Washington: 17 Oct 1896-) Educated at the Kramer Academy in St. Petersburg, Russia. Semi-pro illusionist, mentalist, & hypnotist in New York City as "Dr. Z". Wrote popular magazine articles on suggestion & hypnotism. [Go2;WWM]

name: DeSouza, Marc P[aul]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 31 Jan 1954-) Inspired in 1960 seeing friend's birthday party magician & watching Mark Wilson's TV show. Real estate developer. Semi-pro stand-up manipulator, close-up magician, & lecturer on East Coast. Aka "Marc Conrad" 1971-75. Pet effects: Linking Rings, Zombie, Giant Coin manip, & Cups-&-Balls. Collector of lecture notes (over 700 sets). Awards: 1978 & 1989 SAM 1st place (Silver Medal) for stage magic, etc. Invented Alice thru the Windowpane (1978) & Therewolf Coins (1987). Wrote 5 booklets 1978-87. Articles in MUM, Linking Ring, Trapdoor, & Magic Menu. Column in Mortimer's Magic Magazine since 1989. Video (1991). [Wh2]

name: Dessoir, Prof Dr Dr Max, MD, PhD
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 8 Feb 1867-19 Jul 1947) Professor of Psychiatry & Psychology at Berlin U 1897-1935. Skeptical student of the occult. Amateur magician as "Edmund W. Rells", performing for charity. Wrote as "Edmund Rells" Psychologische Skizzen (1893, 191pp), which includes his pioneering essay "Zur Psychologie der Zauberkunst". This piece appeared in English as "The Psychology of Legerdemain", Open Court, VI (1893), 3599-3602, which was reprinted in Burlingame's Around the World with a Magician (1896 ed), 137-165, & in Burlingame's Herrmann the Magician (1897), 7-41. An Italian tr is in Prestigiatore Moderno (Oct 1893). Also reprinted by Dessoir as "Zur Psychologie der Taschenspieler-kunst" in his Vom Jenseits der Seele. Wrote under own name Vom Jenseits der Seele (1917, 344pp; 6th ed 1930), & Okkultismus in Urkunde (1925). [Al]

name: Dethlefsen, [Thomas A.] "Tom" "Tad
bio: (USA: -11 Dec 1965) Semi-pro as "Dave Larsen". Dealer in San Francisco as the "San Francisco Magic Studio" 1941-1944, initially as partner with Bob Stull, thence on own as "Golden Gate Magic Co." Co-founder in 1953 of Fellowship of Christian Magicians. First mentor of collector Bob Albo. [Albo95,pp31-32,50-51; Genii8/49]

name: De Thorcey
bio: (Paris, France: 26 Apr 1853-15 Aug 1937) Stage name of Albert-Ferdinand Guyot. Ex-painter of miniatures. Pro magician. Played the Folies-Bergère in 1879. A founder-member of the Chambre Syndicale de la Prestidigitation in 1904. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Deu [Pomereda], Carlos
bio: (Spain: -1940) Amateur illusionist in Catalonia. Charter member of the Asociation Catalana de Aficionados al Illusionismo in 1932. Father of Emilio Deu. [Xe]

name: Deu [Sivit], Emilio
bio: (Spain: -20 Aug 1970) Son of Carlos Deu. Printer in Barcelona (since having been financed by David Bamberg in 1933). Amateur magician. Aka "Edys". Charter member of the Asociation Catalana de Aficionados al Illusionismo in 1932. A pioneer of modern card magic in Spain. [Xe;Bam,p292]

name: Deutsch, Rüdiger
bio:
(Preschen, Germany: 28 Mar 1941- ) Locksmith by trade in Heinbron, West Germany. Photographer, magic historian, restorer, & collector (specializes in mechanical tables & stands). Semi-pro illusionist with 19th century pastiche act as "Bellachini XIII". 1975 Baden-Baden 9th place in close-up magic; 1975 MZvD 2nd prize in closeup; 1982 MZvD Magician of the Year.

[See also: Gravatt, Glenn G.]

name: De-Val, David
bio: (Oldham, England: 1 Dec 1938 - 30 Apr 2002) Stage name of David Frederick Littler. Locksmith by trade. Semi-pro escape artist and maker of apparatus for escape artists. Wrote Key to Escapes (n.d., 17pp), Key to Lock Picking (1981), How to Escape from Handcuffs, Lock Picking (2 vols, 1987, 27pp, and 1988, 32pp), & How to Escape from Handcuffs (1992, 16pp). Video (1991). [Bo2;Magigram,V.11,#7]

name: De Valette, Henry
bio: (Aix, France: 19 Jul 1883-) Pro as "Alban's". Collector of documents & photos. On 1927 Concours Magicus jury. [WWM]

name: Devano, Harry, MIMC
bio: (Ellon, Aberdeenshire, Scotland: 24 Nov 1918 - 29 Jul 1996) Stage name of Harry Waldie "Mitch" Mitchell since 1946. Customs & Excise official in 1940s. Learned magic in 1945 from library books. Semi-pro close-up, mental, & platform magician since 1947. Invented & made his first Devano Rising Card Pack in Jun 1948, the Haunted Match Box = Rising Matchbox in 1949, & Memorizing a Dictionary in 1949. MIMC 1957. Deputy Chief Inspector to Gaming Board 1969-78. A few articles in Abra & Magic Circular. [MC9/82;Wh2]

name: Devant, David, MIMC
bio: (Highgate, London, England: 22 Feb 1868-13 Oct 1941) Stage name since 1885 of David Wighton, son of Scottish landscape artist James Wighton. Learned around age 15 from a book. Debut in 1885. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Played the London Crystal Palace 1893. In 1905 taken on as partner by J.N. Maskelyne. First president of The Magic Circle 1905-06. Serial publication in The Royal Magazine in 1909 of his forthcoming Tricks for Everyone raised a furor about exposing. Gave Royal Command Performances 1912 & 1913. Left partnership with Maskelyne in 1915 to go on own. Teacher of Arthur Ainslie, etc. In 1920 retired from stage by illness (paralysis agitans) but continued as writer & teacher. Prolific inventor, including Artist's Dream (1893), perhaps color change (1893), the vest servante (around 1893), Birth of Flora (1895), Mascot Moth (1905), Glass Lined Trunk=Beau Brocade (1909), & Vanishing Motorcycle=Biff (1913). Wrote Hand Shadows (1901, 8pp), Magic Made Easy (1903, 209pp; reprinted 1921), Tricks for Everyone (1910 [actually Nov 1909], 136pp; repr 1913), Our Magic (1911, 316pp, with Nevil Maskelyne; repr 1946 & 1992), Lessons in Conjuring (1922, 152pp), The Best Tricks and How to do Them (1931, 124pp), & Secrets of My Magic (1936, 288pp; repr 1971; with French tr by Ceillier as Mes sécrets d'illusionniste, 1938). Performed solo in 5 one-reel silent movies (4 in 1896; 1 in 1897). Early memoir is Woes of a Wizard (1903, 183pp), a later one is My Magic Life (1931, 287pp; reprinted 1971). Bio is Sam H. Sharpe, Devant's Delightful Delusions (1990, 231pp). [Pr;Ch;Cl;Go2;Bar;Dif;Vo56;Magic6/06,6/09]

name: Deveen
bio: See: Wood, Jack

name: Deveen, [David] "Devil
bio: (London, England: 24 Apr 1900-late Aug 1989) Stage name of A.W. Parsons. Pro manipulator 1920s-60s, touring Britain, the Continent, and the world. Worked his silent act with 6 female assistants. Wrote Cigarette Magic and Manipulation [1929, 38pp] & Expert Cigarette Magic (1932, 59pp; repr 1936). [Hudd]

name: De Vega, Alex, MIMC
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 10 Sep 1891-9 Jan 1971) Stage name of Alexander Mackay "Alex" Stewart. Initially pro illusionist with full-evening show that toured Britain for several years. Then physiotherapist. Also pyrotechnist with "Stewart's Displays", continuing as illusionist on semi-pro basis. In 1922 was hired by Houdini to investigate the "Crewe Circle" of pseudo-psychics. First President of Scottish Conjurers' Association 1924. Invented the Divided Lady illusion ("The Great Divide") by 1945. Wrote A Whirlwind of Wizardry (1919, with Chris van Bern) & Summertime Sorcery (1939, 17pp). Also wrote 13 manuscripts (1926-48), including Formula X (1947) & The Devil's Whisper (1948). Articles. [Daw#202;Silver] de Vere, Camille (Paris, France: c1886-25 Jul 1909) Learned from his father, Charles de Vere. Pro. Joined the ASAP in 1905. Died of diabetes. de Vere, Charles (London, England: 18 Sep 1843-21 Dec 1931) Aka "Professor de Vere". Born Herbert Shakespeare Gardiner Williams. Inspired by seeing shows of J.H. Anderson and Jacobs. Pro since age 19. Dealer in London by 1873 (when issued 1st catalog) to 1878 when he briefly opened a small magic theater in Brussels. Then a pro dealer in Paris 1878-1924 when retired there. A founding member of ASAP in 1903. Retired in 1924. Husband of Julia de Vere and father of Camille & Ionia de Vere. Wrote Professor De Vere's Book of Magic (1875, 48pp), which was merely a stock book published by H.G. Clarke & Co to which De Vere added his own title page; etc. NOTE: Toole Stott (#241) misattributes M. Schele de Vere's Modern Magic (1873) to Charles de Vere. [Daw94;Pr;Dif;Vo55;Fr] de Vere, "lonia" (Paris, France: c1886-) Younger daughter of Charles de Vere (Williams). Born Ionia (?) Williams (her given name is not yet established), aka "Ionia". Taught by father and mother Julia ("Okita"). Pro from 1910. Played the London Hippodrome 1911. Retired in 1919 after her marriage. [Mar;Dif] de Vere, Julia (Sturminster-Newton, England: 12 Dec 1852-27 Jul 1916) Julia Williams née Ferrett, aka "Okita". Taught c1877 by husband Charles de Vere. Pro illusionist with own act 1877-1892. Died in Paris. Mother of "Ionia". [Daw94;Dif;Mar] de Vere, M. Schele (USA?: fl.1870s) Likely pen name. Wrote Modern Magic (New York: G.P. Putnam's Sons, 1873, 466pp), misattributed to Charles de Vere by Toole Stott (#241).

name: De Vere, Richard
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Charles R. Mawe. Pro illusionist. 1989 British Magical Grand Prix Champion.

name: De Verli
bio: See: Verli, E. de

name: Devil
bio: (Fossano, Cuneo, Italy: 14 Apr 1946- ) Stage name of Giuseppe Piumatti. Learned at age 18 in Turin. Pro close-up & comedy magician since 1970. Pet effect: Cigarette Levitation. Works cabarets. Lecturer & illusion designer. Dealer ("Devil Studio Magio") in Turin until moved c1990 to Monte Carlo. Played USA in 1988, 1989, 1990. Articles in II Prestigiatore Moderno, Magicus, Arcane (France). [Wh5]

name: De Ville
bio: (Cornimont, Vosges, France: 26 Feb 1894-6 Aug 1937) Stage name of Georges[-Élie] Gehin. In 1936 co-founded (with Louis Damet) Studio Sphinx. Pro sleight-of-hand. Killed in motorcycle accident. [Dif;Rob1] de Villiers, [François] (Malta: c1854-1930) French parents, British nationality. Self-taught as boy, then in 1873 by assisting French magician Adrian de Lille on a tour of the Orient. Moved to USA in 1883, playing in lyceum, vaudeville, & with his own full-evening show. Became US citizen. Toured abroad, including South Africa (1903), Australia (1911), & the Orient. Retired to India where he committed suicide. Aka "The Great Villiers". [Wal;Magic4/02,7/03;Cl]

name: Devine, Andy
bio: (Flagstaff, Arizona: 7 Oct 1905-1977) Stage name of Jeremiah Schwartz. Comic actor in many Hollywood films (since 1926) & on 2 TV series. Amateur magician. [Katz]

name: Devlo
bio: (Halifax, Yorkshire, England: 6 Jun 1910- ) Stage name of Cyril Shaw. Debut in 1923. Pro stage act. [Go2] "Devo from Dixieland" SEE: Badley, Benjamin R.

name: Devo, Carl
bio: See: Goldston, Will

name: Devo, La
bio: See: Goldston, Leah

name: DeVoe, Gene
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 4 Jul 1918-27 Dec 1989) Stage name of Eugene P. Zimmerman. Inspired seeing Thurston & learned from magic set. Mentor was Ben R. Badley who also suggested his stage name. Pro magician with full-evening show since 1946. Pet effects: Aerial Fishing & Multiplying Bottles. Dealer (as "DeVoe Magic Den" in St. Louis & later Kirkwood) since 1954 when he bought Lindhorst's shop. Soon also bought out Harold Sterling's shop. Twice President of MDA. Retired in late-1980s. Mentor of Mike O'Dowd. [Monti; MUM2/90; Genii10/89; MUM5/63] (Britain: c1830-c1910) Aka "Major Devono". Minor pro since 1852, mainly in northern provincial music halls. Played London in 1857-58, including Sadlers Well's Theatre. Invented the Watch Bag for the egg-bag version of the Broken and Restored Watch. Still doing his old-fashioned act in 1901. [Vo56;Cl;Magic9/01]

name: Devono
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s) Son of Devono. Performed in India c1878. [CI] Devono, Joseph "de Vos, Gloria" SEE: "Gloria"

name: Devos, Jackie
bio: (Ardooie, Flandre, Belgium: 2 Jan 1929-) Pro manip & stage magic. 1955 FISM 3rd prize in manip with stage name of "Jacky Fox".

name: Dew, [Daniel W.] "Danny
bio: (Yazoo City, Mississippi: 25 Dec 1906-26 Sep 1996) Hotel chef & caterer until retired in early 1970s. Part-time pro society magician. Toured with wife Melba who did sand & rag pictures. After WW II briefly operated (with Gene Baker) the Phoenix Magic & Novelty Company in Phoenix, Arizona, 1946. Made the Paul Fox apparatus 1959-c1981. Acquired many of the props of Fox & Cardini, both of whom were close friends. Taught Bob Bluemle, etc. 1976 AMA Special Fellowship. Tricks in Genii, Arcane, Hugard books, etc. Survived by wife Melba. [Wat]

name: Dewey, Herb[ert Edward]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 12 Mar 1935- ) Raised as a Roman Catholic. Learned in 1960 from books by Robert Nelson. Dental technician. Semi-pro psychic-reader, mentalist, & hypnotist since 1960. Wrote (with Thomas K. Saville) Red Hot Cold Reading (1984, 78pp); "Shadow Man" [pseud], The King of the Cold Readers (1989, 77pp); & Psycho-Babble (1996, 107pp). Pet effect: Cold Reading. [Wh2]

name: Dexter
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 12 Jul 1848-) Moved to England c1870, working as assistant to Dr. Lynn 1873-79. Next 2 decades toured England, the Continent, & the Colonies. Then ran travelling shows & became a music hall manager. [CI]

name: Dexter, Bert
bio: (Britain: -1965) Stage name of H. Sowerby. Specialized in Rag Pictures. [Genii1/66]

name: Dexter, Douglas, MIMC
bio: (England: 1878-21 Sep 1937) Stage name of Bernard Douglas Marks. Schoolmaster & international fencing champion. Superb semi-pro magician with many improved tricks. Played St. George's Hall in 1925. Visited USA in 1934. [Le;Go;Vo56;Ho;Magic6/09]

name: Dexter, S[idney] Edward "Eddie
bio: (Chiswick, England: 1 Apr 1901-6 Mar 1978) Stage name of E. Cohen, aka "Dexterious Dexter". Part-time pro kid-show magic, vent (with "Jackie"), & hypnotism. Past President British Ring. Wrote Entertaining with Contact Mind-Reading (1952, 26pp) & Entertaining with Hypnotism.

name: Dexter, Will, MIMC
bio: (St. Anne's, England: 13 Sep 1906-5 Nov 1985) Pen name of William Thomas Pritchard. Learned magic as youth from Neil's The Modern Conjurer. Journalist until retired in 1969. Designed crossword puzzles for Daily Telegraph 1970-84. Semi-pro magician, specializing in mentalism. Wrote The Riddle of Chung Ling Soo (1955, 223pp); Identity Parade (1955, 11pp); Sealed Vision (1956, 66pp); Everybody's Book of Magic (1956, 183pp; repr as Famous Magic Secrets, [n.d.], 141pp); 101 Magic Secrets (London: Jun 1957, 158pp; US ed 1957); This is Magic (1958, 204pp; repr as Secrets of the Conjurer's Craft, [n.d.]); & Feature Magic for Mentalists (1975, 151pp). Ghosted books for Robert Harbin. Edited Magic Circle Magic (1963, 265pp). Tricks in HMM, Pentagram, Mantra, etc. [Magico12/86,8/93]

name: D'Henny
bio: (Ribeauvillé, Haut-Rhin, France; 9 Dec 1873-11 Feb 1961) Stage name of Jean-Baptiste Denny. Pro sleight-of-hand. [Dif] d'Hont, Alfred-Édouard (Chénée, Liège, Belgium: 9 Mar 1845-14 Nov 1900) Ex-Belgian journalist. Pro hypnotic act, working both under own name & as "Donato". Mentor of Dalmoras. Published Le magnetisme (1884). Died in Paris. [Dif;Vo58;St] d'Horabic, Holtum (Lercara, Sicily, Italy: 12 Nov 1866-3 Mar 1932) Stage name of Don Joachim Chibbaro. Pro 2-person mindreading with assistant-wife "Yama". Joined the French ASAP in 1905. [Dif]

name: Dhotel, Dr Jules
bio: (Neufchâteau, Vosges, France: 16 Nov 1879-16 Jun 1967) Learned magic in WW I from Robert-Houdin's Comment on devient sorcier. Physician by profession. Amateur poet, sculptor, & music composer. Amateur magician. Joined the ASAP in 1921. 1927 ASAP Prix d'honneur. President ASAP 1941-45; President AFAP 1945-51 & 1958-63; first President of FISM 1948. Past editor-in-chief Journal de la Prestidigitation. Wrote under pen name of "J. Hédolt" Une Rêve (1927); Le papier multiform (with André Mayette); & the monumental Prestidigitation sans bagages (5 parts, 1936-45), partial English tr by Paul Fleming as Magic with Small Apparatus (1947, 302pp). [Dif;Rob1]

name: Di Sato
bio: See: Thiery, Harry

name: Diaconis, Dr Persi [Warren], PhD
bio: (New York City, NY: 31 Jan 1945-) Learned magic at age 5. Pro, specializing in sleight-of-hand, 1960-72. Aka "R. Sid Spokane II". Invented the Himber Ring (1961). Professor of Statistics at Harvard U since 1986. Now amateur magician. 1982 MacArthur Foundation $192,000 grant. Edited (& wrote introduction to) Vernon's Revelations (1984). Translating Prévost's 1584 book. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Diamond, Hal
bio: (Erie, Pennsylvania: 12 Sep 1948 – 30 Nov 1995) Stage name of Harold E. Henderson. Learned magic in 1955 after seeing "Mr. C" (Chuck Creighton) work a Masonic picnic. Pro stage magician & illusionist since 1960. World tour in 1988. Selected as the magician for the 1989 US Presidential Inaugural Parade. Columnist for New Tops 1979-present & Magic Manuscript 1983-85. Wrote Promotion in Motion (1979, 2 reprints), The Bunny Book (1987), Creative Clowning (1988), Rabbit Attack (forthcoming 1989). [Wh2]

name: Diamond, Kathy
bio: (California, USA: fl.1980s) Stage name of Kathy Krabbenschmidt. Pro close-up. Married & dropped magic. Moved to Australia.

name: Diamond, Paul
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 21 Jul 1928-) Pro dealer ("Paul Diamond's Magic Company") in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, 1964-1995. Lectured throughout North America, Asia, & Europe. Wrote several booklets. See John Racherbaumer, Paul Diamond's Big-Easy Card Cunning (1992, 44pp). 11 videos (1986). 2 audios. [Se;Mag;Wh] "Diana the Enchantress" SEE: Zimmerman, Diana

name: Diavol
bio: See: Poulleau, Georges

name: Diavolo, Fra
bio: See: Allen, Paul

name: Diaz, José
bio: (Spain: fl.1940s-60s) Pro. Founder-President of the Sociedad de Illusionismo de Melilla in 1955. Tricks in New Phoenix.

name: Dicared
bio: (France: 19 Feb 1916-1961) Stage name of André Pichard. Debut at age 18. Pro comedy manipulator. Charter member of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Marseille 1943. Played Paris 1945-47 until went insane. Later recovered enough to perform in the provinces. [Dif]

name: Dick, Harris B[risbane]
bio: (USA: -1916) Succeeded his father, William B. Dick, as owner of Dick & Fitzgerald publishers 1898-1916 in New York City. Amateur magician. Wrote several booklets on cards as "Trumps, Jr.", including The Game of 500. Also edited Dick's Games of Patience or Solitaire with Cards (1908) & Dick's Hand Book of Cribbage. Died suddenly in the Boston subway. Willed over $1 million plus a moderately important collection (begun by his father) of books and art works to New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, which they received in 1917. (USA: 1827-1901) Amateur magician. Entertainer. Major publisher (Dick & Fitzgerald) in New York City of books on popular entertainment, including several on magic beginning in 1857. Dick, William B[risbane] Under pen-name "Trumps" wrote The American Hoyle; or Gentleman's Hand-Book of Games (1864, 491pp; 17th ed, 1899, 529pp), The American Card-Player (1866, 151pp), & The Modern Pocket Hoyle (9th ed, 1877, 387pp). I suspect he is the "Leger D. Mayne" who compiled D&F's What Shall We Do Tonight? (1873). Compiled Modern Whist (based on Cavendish). In 1868 his company reprinted anonymously Gerritt M. Evans' How Gamblers Win. His son, Harris B. Dick (see), wrote in 1910 that "my father was an enthusiastic magician, and I believe had imported to this country, if not the first, one of the very first French apparatus for performing tricks." William retired from publishing in 1898, passing his company to son Harris. REF: Books at Brown, V.34 (1987), 108-114; Bulletin of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, V.12 (New York: 1917), 48, 50-56, 157-158.

name: Dickens, Charles
bio: (Landport, England: 7 Feb 1812-9 Jun 1870) Famous writer & novelist. Avid amateur magician. Bios focussed on his magical interests are Edwin A. Dearn, Charles Dickens, Amateur Conjuror (Shanghai: 1926), J.B. Findlay, Charles Dickens and His Magic (1962, 18pp), & Stephen S. Tigner, "Charles Dickens in and about Magic", Journal of Magic History (1979), 88-110. The definitive general bio is Fred Kaplan, Dickens: A Biography (1988). [Daw]

name: Dickmann-Minalono
bio: (Commentary, Allier, France: 13 May 1870-15 Mar 1947) Stage name of Nicholas-Joseph Minalono. Moved to Paris in 1889 to become a painter & engraver. By 1890 turned to magic, including hypnotism, lightning sketches, mimicry, & clowning. Charter member in 1928 of Agosta-Meynier's Syndicat International des Artistes Pretidigitateurs. Founder & director Studio de la Magie in Paris in 1928. A major figure in French magic. [Dif;Go2]

name: Dickson, Abb
bio: (Atlanta, Georgia: 31 Aug 1948- ) Stage name of Abner Pope Dickson Jr. Inspired at age 10 by a school show magician. Semi-pro comedy magic since his senior year in high school. Pro comedy magic since 1970. Toured his own "Presto!" illusion show with a cast & staff of 30 in the USA, Canada, Hawaii, & Puerto Rico 1975-86. Later specialized in industrial & trade shows. Then increasingly involved in his parents' funeral parlour business (in Atlanta) of which he is now the owner, making him again a part-time pro. Pet effects: Snake Basket & Disembodied Princess. IBM International President 1997-98. International President World Alliance of Magicians since 1999. Invented several illusions. Articles. Has appeared in 8 Orson Welles films (including the never finished The Magic Show) & as actor or magician in 5 other films. [LR7/97;Genii1/89;Se;Mag;Wh2]

name: Dickson, Stanley
bio: (Filey, Yorkshire, England: 21 Jul 1893-) Learned magic at age 15. Amateur debut in 1911. Pro drawing-room magic & sleights since 1913. Inventor & improver. [Go2]

name: Dickson
bio: (Avesnelles, Avesnes, France: 4 Oct 1857-27 May 1939) Stage name of Le Comte [Count] Paul-Alfred de Saint-Génois de Saint-Breucq. Learned magic at age 17. Pro illusionist since 1880. Also worked marionettes. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1883-86 during which time he was also its co-director. Later operated the Théâtre Dicksonn in Paris 1889-94. Played the Casino de Paris 1909. Wrote 7 books in French, from Mes trucs (1893, 214pp) to Mes trucs dévoilés (1928). [Dif;Vo55]

name: Dicky, Géo
bio: (Chaumont, Haute-Marne, France: 23 Mar 1882-1961) Stage name of Georges Vitrey. Artist. Semi-pro magician. [Rob1]

name: Die 2" [The 2]
bio: See: Fine, Robert & Hierling, Thomas

name: Dienst, Paul
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 4 Aug 1879-26 Jan 1954) Died in Vienna. No other details furnished. [Roh]

name: Diestel, Charles J.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-40s) Learned assisting Jean Hugard 1919-20. Minor pro illusionist & cigarette manipulator. Invented (or at least manufactured) the Diestel Dropper (by 1940) & the Diestel Rising Cigarette (by 1940).

name: Dietrich, [Carl B.] "Bud
bio: (East St. Louis, Illinois: 7 May 1922- ) Inspired at age c10 seeing Dante & Blackstone. Learned at age 14 from brother Paul. Pro close-up since 1957 & since 1962 industrial & then mainly trade-shows. Pet effect: Linking Rings (with 3 rings). Generally rated one of world's top 6 trade-show workers. Wrote (with Dick Jarrow) The Trade Show Handbook [1973, 46pp]. Invented Double Impact (1973) & Chain Reaction (1980). Articles in Genii, MUM, & in Marshall's The Success Book. [Monti;LR9/89;MUM4/84;Genii8/70;Mag;Wat;Wh2] Dietrich, Charles A. (USA: c1886-13 Aug 1967) Aka "Dietric & Company". Pro. Invented "The 'Yogi' Bare-Arm Vanish" of a ball in 1909. [Pr;Magic7/11,79]

name: Dietrich, Dorothy "Dottie
bio: (Erie, Pennsylvania: fl.1970s-80s) Inspired by young brother. Learned from books. Pro escape artist. Played The Magic Towne House in Manhattan since 1973 & its co-owner (with Dick Brooks) since 1974. [Se;Mar]

name: Dietrich, Marlene
bio: (Schöneberg [a suburb of Berlin until 1920], Germany: 27 Dec 1901-6 May 1992) Stage name of Marie Magdalene Dietrich. Minor actress on German stage (since 1922) & in film (since 1923). Moved in 1930 to Hollywood where she starred in films until 1957. Became US citizen in 1939. Debuted in magic in Aug 1943 as stage assistant of Orson Welles in his Mercury Wonder Show in Hollywood, substituting for Rita Hayworth. Also did magic in USO shows in WW II in the USA (1943-44) & Europe (1944-45), including impromptu magic for US G.I.s in Europe--close-up tricks she had learned from Welles who had also taught her mindreading that she used with both Welles & Danny Thomas at GI shows. See Miss Dietrich sawn in half (by camera trickery) in Welles' magic show segment in the 1944 film Follow the Boys. Autobio is Marlene (1989, 273pp). Good bios are Steven Bach, Marlene Dietrich: Life and Legend (1992, 626), Donald Spoto, Blue Angel: The Life of Marlene Dietrich (1992, 335pp), and Maria Riva, Marlene Dietrich (1993, 790pp).

name: Dietro
bio: (Germany: 17 May 1914-) Stage name of Georg Dietrich. Magician. Senior of the MZ-Dresden-Putjatinhaus. [Nad]

name: Dieudonné
bio: (France: 1829-Apr 1903) Ex-comedian. Owner of Café de la Chartreuse in Paris. Semi-pro magician, working for clients at his café. Toured Switzerland & Sweden. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Dif. Max
bio: (Champagnac-les-Mines, Cantal, France: 25 Dec 1911- 6 Feb 1999) Stage & pen name of Maxime Roux. Typographer & linotypist, later proof-reader in Limoges. Amateur magician (general magic) & magic historian. AFAP Master Magician since 1949. Aka "Chang" with pseudo-Chinese act in 1956. Also performs with assistant-wife "Francita" (Eva Roux). Founding President Cercle Robert-Houdin du Mimousin 1964. AFAP Gold Medal 1978. In 1988 awarded the AFAP Golden Wand (1 of only 3 recipients). Wrote Histoire et évolution technique de la prestidigitation (3 vols, 1971-74), the largest & most nearly comprehensive history of magic, winning the 1977 Prix Georges-Méliès. Also Mythologie du merveilleux (1982) & Histoire illustrée de la prestidigitation (1986). His 216-page autobiography is La baguette magique: Comment on devient sorcier (1988). [Bou;Wh2]

name: Digani
bio: (Germany: 3 Aug 1943-) Stage name of Dieter Garnier. 1981 MZvD 3rd prize in general magic. Dealer (as "Zauber-Digani") in Bonn by early 1990s. [Nad]

name: Di Martino, Francis
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Aka "Omar Thin". AFAP Bronze Medal 1979 & Silver Medal 1987. Dimmare, James [pronounced dih-MEHR], MIMC (Vancouver, Canada: 10 Oct 1960-) Stage name of James Murray Dimmère. Family name was anglicized to Dimmer in the 1800s and changed back to Dimmare in 1980. Inspired at age 13 seeing TV magician, Debut at 15. Full-time pro since age 16, specializing in a dove act, which he perfected by studying with Channing Pollock c1982. Other influences from Doug Henning, Shimada, Johnny Thompson. Coached Jason Latimer for Clear cup and ball routine to win FISM. Moved to Southern California. Assistant-wife (since 1988) is Lisa (daughter of Haruo & Deanna Shimada). Tours USA & Europe. 1983 PCAM 1 $ ^{st} $ Place Stage & Outstanding Showmanship and Presentation, 1989 AMA Best Parlour Magician, 1991 Special Appreciation Award Prince Rainier of Monaco, 2002 Stage Magician of the Year from AMA, 2004 two Merlin Awards from IMS, 2007 & 2008 Canadian Magician of the year. Invented Shrinking and Vanishing Bird cage (1981), Compacted (1996), Appearing Electric Guitar for Topas (1989). TV bits. Book Spectacle (1990 by Stephen Minch). See bio in Magic June 2004.[LR11/89; Genii2/92; Trixigram9/89]

name: Dinardi
bio: (Alpreichenau, N. Silesia, Germany [now Poland]: 18 Jun 1911- ) Stage name of Alfred Körber. [Roh]

name: Dingle, Derek
bio: (London, England: 1 Jul 1937- N.Y. City: 11 Jan 2004 stroke) His real name. Learned at age 8 from a magic set & later, after moving to Canada (in Toronto 1965-69), by lessons from Ross Bertram & Eddie Fechter. Lived in New York City since 1969. An engineer turned pro close-up sleight-of-hand & cardman in 1975. Invented The Fastest Pass in the World, etc. Ran a booking agency with partner Shelley Carroll (see) since 1980s. Died of a stroke. See Harry Lorayne, Dingle's Deceptions (1971, 57pp); & Richard Kaufman, The Complete Works of Derek Dingle (1982, 219pp). Tricks & articles in Epilogue, Chronicles, & Magic. Videos (1985 & 1997). TV bits (since 1974). [Mag;HC;Thauma#34]

name: Dingwall, Dr Eric [John] "Ding", MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1890-1986) Anthropologist. Honorary Assistant Keeper, British Library. Student of erotica and psychic investigator. Inspired by investigating alleged psychics, he became an amateur magician by 1909 when he joined The Magic Circle. Wrote (or edited) several books on the occult, including The Haunting of Borley Rectory (1956, with Trevor Hall & K.M. Goldney) & Four Modern Ghosts (1956, 111pp, with Trevor Hall). Generally rather credulous of his subjects, including "Margery". Also wrote The Girdle of Chastity (Paris: 1923, 164pp), a study of chastity belts. [WW;Bo#223]

name: Dircks, Henry
bio: (Britain: fl.1850s-70s) Civil engineer by profession. Semi-pro ghost show. Often assisted Professor Pepper, as during the latter's USA tour in 1872. Wrote The Ghost! As Produced in the Spectre Drama (1863, 102pp; 2nd ed 1864, 124pp). Also wrote The Life, Times, and Scientific Labours of the second Marquis of Worcester (1865, 624pp), which only touches some effects relevant to conjuring. NOTE: Misspelled "Dirks".

name: Dixey, Henry E.
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 6 Jan 1850-25 Feb 1943) Stage name of Henry Dixon. Pro comedy magic (& pro comedian). Played the New York Palace in 1913. [Pr]

name: Dixon
bio: See: Wegener, Claus

name: Diabel, Zdenek
bio: (Czechoslovakia?: 1 Sep 1933-) Magician in Czechoslovakia. Member of MZvD. [Nad]

name: Dleisfen
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-30s) Stage name (by reversal plus letter switch of surname) of R.M. Nesfield. Pro. Secretary of the British Ring 1928-33. Edited The Budget. Trick in Magical Journal. See Bagshawe, Dleisfen's Visible Penetration of a Thimble [1936].

name: Dobler, Herr
bio: See: Smith, William George

name: Döbler, Ludwig [Leopold]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 5 Oct 1801 – Türnitz, Niederösterreich, Austria: 17 Apr 1864) Learned engraving, chemistry, & psychics. Pro magician since 1825. Toured Austria, Germany (where Goethe befriended him in 1831), France, Holland, Belgium, Prussia, Scandinavia, Russia, & England (1842 & 1844, billed as "Louis Döbler"). In 1840 introduced the feat of lighting his stage with candles by firing his pistol (actually by a chemical process, not electricity). Invented the Witches' Cauldron by 1842. Made Court Conjuror to Fredrick Wilhelm III of Prussia. Retired in 1848, the most famous & acclaimed magician in central Europe. [Ch;Win;Dif;Cl;St;Fr]

name: Dobrin, Harry
bio: (Latvia: 1 Sep 1907- ) Inspired by grandfather "Dobrin, Master of the Thousand Tricks". Learned as youth from family. Moved to USA. High school shop teacher. Semi-pro magician, performer, & prop maker (in New York City). Invented the Dobrin DoubleLocking Slate (by 1944) & the Periscope Slate (1945). [Th]

name: Dobson, Wayne, MIMC
bio: (Leicester, England: c1958-) Protégé of Roy Johnson. Pro close-up & stage magic since age 21. Played the London Palladium in 1989. Star of British TV with own 6-part series on ITV in 1990. MIMC 1990. Although a victim of MS, continues to perform as of 2004. Wrote Wayne Dobson's Pro-File (1984, 91pp).

name: Doc-Corten
bio: See: "Corten, Doc"

name: Docweiler, M.
bio: (USA: fl.1840s-1st decade of 1900s) Learned c1845 by tuition from a pro. Pro stage magic from 1860s to as late as 1901.

name: Docweiss
bio: See: Weiss, "Dr" Aaron

name: Dodd, Frank N.
bio: (USA: 29 Mar 1870-9 Jan 1943) Amateur in New York City. Aka "Effendi" (from his initials). Tricks in Jinx.

name: Dodge, Arthur" [pen name]
bio: See: Sawyer, Thomas A.

name: Dodson, Betty
bio: (USA: -29 Oct 1993) Assistant to Okito during his Louisville years in the early 1950s. Kid-show magicienne as “Dorothy Betts”. Wife of William Dodson. [LR10/98]

name: Dodson, Goodlette [H.]
bio: (Nashville, Tennessee: 21 Oct 1889-26 Jan 1970) Inspired in 1924. Semi-pro card flourisher in Birmingham, Alabama. Wrote Exhibition Card Fans (1935, 50pp). [St]

name: Dodson, William B. "Bill
bio: (USA: -26 Apr 1991) Electronic engineer in Louisville, Kentucky. Semi-pro magician. Invented electronic props for Nelson Enterprises since 1946. Consultant to Del Ray & Tommy Tucker. Columnist ("Electronic Magic") in Linking Ring in mid-1950s. Husband of Betty Dodson. Brad Henderson informs me that Dobson built "some of the finest crooked gambling devices ever made." The gaffed tables he made for the Mafia led to his testimony before Kefauver's US Senate investigations of organized crime in 1951-52. [LR10/98 but where misspelled "Dobson"]

name: Doerflinger, William [Main] "Bill
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 30 Jul 1910-Dec? 2000) Learned at age 15 as a pro's assistant, from magic dealers, & reading books. Editor-writer in book publishing in New York City. Part-time pro club & platform magician since age 19. With assistant Daniel P. Mannix toured Nova Scotia & the Southern States in late 1930s. Collector of apparatus, books, & memorabilia. Authored The Magic Catalogue: A Guide to the Wonderful World of Magic (1977, 243pp). Articles in MUM & Magicol. Toured USSR in 1988. [Wh2]

name: Doidge, Robert W.
bio: (Roxbury, Massachusetts: 12 Oct 1892- ) Promentalist as "Calostro". Collector & publisher (Calostro Publications) in Somerville, MA, of books on mind-reading. Wrote (with David J.

name: Dokoty
bio: (Switzerland: 2 Aug 1890-) Stage name of Jules Voirol. Pro illusionist, performing in all types of venues except circus. [WWM]

name: Dolan, Paula
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-60s) Billed as the "Dancing Illusionist" & "Dancing Magiciene [sic]". Played the NY Palace in 1955 and the Boston "Magicale" 1956, 1959, & 1963.

name: Dolinoff, Daniel
bio: (Russia: -1966) With wife Raya was post-WW II Russian refugee. Pro black-art dance act as “The Dolinoffs” by 1949, “Dolinoff & the Raya Sisters”, & “Dolinoff & Raya”. Played the Palace 1949-57 (5 times). Moved to USA in early 1950s. Toured the world. Raya also died in 1966. [HMM2/50;Hudd]

name: Dom
bio: See: Domzalski, Walter H.

name: Dominique
bio: (France: c1932-) Stage name of Dominique Risbourg. Pro manipulator & vent since 1948 at age 16. FISM 3rd prizes for presentation in 1948 (at age 16) & 1950. Added pick-pocket act, billed as "The Man With 300,000 Suspenders". Toured U.S. nightclubs 1952-55, 1959. Video. [Ran;Bo2;Dif]

name: Domi-Nho
bio: See: Plessis, Dominique

name: Domino, Signor
bio: (Germany: 1836-1893) Pen name of Emil Cohnfeldt. Wrote Das Spiel, die Spielerwelt und die Geheimnisse der Falschspieler (Breslau: 1886, 210pp), a technical manual of card sleights; Wandernde Künstler (Berlin: 1892); & Dreihundert wunderregende Zaubereien (Leipzig: n.d.).
