name: Domzalski, Walter H. "Dom
bio: (USA: 12 Sep 1894-8 Aug 1949) Law student & amateur magician in 1921. Briefly a pro magician with partner Al Caroselli. Then a lawyer in Detroit. A founder of the International Magic Circle. Seven Circles column ("Around the Icebox") & reviews. [Scroll of Merlin1/44;Dor]

name: Donar, Professor "Pop
bio: (USA: fl. 1890s-1930s) Stage name of R.D. Bleau. Minor pro. Played Tony Pastor's in New York City in 1901 with a rabbit vanish and sleight-of-hand. Retired in New York City, becoming a regular at Ducrot's. [HMM7/56]

name: Donat, Professeur
bio: (Belgium: c1881-28 May 1937) Stage name of Jules Ludswig. In 1918 moved to Montréal, Canada, where he open a hairdressing salon. Semi-pro magician. [Dif]

name: Donato
bio: See: d'Hont, Alfred-Édouard

name: Dondorf, Bernard
bio: (Frankfurt-am-Main, Germany: 19 Mar 1809-13 Jun 1902) Died in Frankfurt. No other details reported. [Roh]

name: Dondrake
bio: See: Drake, Don

name: Donister, Colin, MIMC
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-50s) Stage name of Donald Farley. Honorary Librarian of the Magic Circle. Compiler of The Magic Circle: A Catalogue of the Reference Library and Lending Library (1952, 95pp).

name: Donovan
bio: See: Williams, Gary Lee

name: Dooley, Billy
bio: See: “Dulay, Benson”

name: Dooley, Dixie [Dwyane]
bio: (Oakhill, West Virginia: 8 Nov 1954- ) Pro since mid-1970s as "Mr Dixie Dooley" with escapes, illusions, & close-up. Since c1978 his stage assistant is Jennifer Moore, marrying her in 1980. Toured Britain repeatedly since 1982. Hosted a TV magic series on Augusta, Georgia, 1981-86, which is still shown there. Moved in 1986 to Las Vegas where he is a star performer, initially at the Bourbon Street 1986-87 & now as resident magician at O'Shea's 1989-present. Also did world tour in 1989. Collector of Houdiniana. Wrote Exploits of the Amazing Mr. Dooley (c1982, 16pp) & Mr. Dixie Dooley Presents Las Vegas Jokes, Bar Bets, & Tricks for the Amateur Trickster (1988, 16pp). Video (1990 forthcoming). [Wh]

name: Doom, Dr.
bio: (USA: fl.c.1960s) Stage name of John Lee Clifton. Wrote Call the Doctor! (n.d., 19pp) & Theater of Blood (n.d., 8pp).

name: Doom, Dr
bio: See: Daniel, John

name: Door-Leblanc
bio: (Duerne, Rhône, France: 23 Jan 1865-6 Dec 1945) Stage name of Georges-François Blanc. Pro stage magic since age 27, touring most of the world with only a few appearances in France. Assisted by his wife ("Saltana Hakoum") in mind-reading act. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Doré
bio: See: Swatosch, Michael

name: Doré, Ruth
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Stage name of Ruth S. Levy, later Ruth Doré Ballard. Daughter of "Theo Doré". Student of Hugard. Pro sleight-of-hand. Did USO tour in WWII. [Des]

name: Doré, Theo
bio: (New York City, NY: 26 Oct 1892-8 Apr 1985) Stage name of Theodore T. Levy. Son of a tailor who taught him magic. Minor pro kid-show magus in the New York City area. Wrote Magnetrix (1971, 54pp). Prolific author of over 300 articles, including in Huggard's Magic Monthly. Father of Ruth Doré. [Genii9/83;WWM]

name: Doreen
bio: See: Palmer, Jay

name: Doreng, Oscar
bio: (Denmark: 6 Apr 1904-) Trained as engineer. Pro magician with all-round program including Black Art act. Toured Finland in 1950.

name: Dória, Professeur Raúl [Montes da Silva]
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 6 Jan 1878-15 Sep 1922) Amateur. Wrote Ilusões (c1897). In 1912 co-founded the Internacional Instituto de Recreações Scientificas. [Cam]

name: Dorian
bio: See: Bothwell-Maye, E. G.

name: Dorian, Robert "Bob
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 28 Dec 1951- ) Inspired & learned ESP act as psychology student at Notre Dame. Pro mentalist as "The Amazing Dorian". Moved to Los Angeles in 1973. Took over Romark's act. 1988 AMA Award of Merit. Narrator of American Movie Classics on TV in 1990s. [Wh]

name: Dorien
bio: See: Osterlind, Richard

name: Dorini
bio: (Laibach, Austrian-Hungarian Empire: 8 May 1885-Aug 1954) Stage name of Eduard Dornig. Nephew of "Gaston". Pro comedy magician since 1920 in the Vienna magic tradition with cards, balls, silks, & the Rising Cards. [Vo57;Al]

name: Dormoy, Jean-Pierre
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Cabaret magician as "Alexis". AFAP Bronze Medal 1979 & Silver Medal 1987. [Bou2] Dornfeld [later Dornfield], W[erner F.] "Dorny" (Chicago, Illinois: 7 Oct 1892-5 Sep 1982) Inspired at age 13 reading old magic catalog. Pro comedy magician (mostly small tricks & an occasional illusion) & MC. IBM Member #4 in 1922. Toured Australia in 1927. SAM President 1931-32. Author of patter books including Trix and Chatter (1921, 286pp), Dorny on Trix (1954, 40pp), & Dorney's Comedy Blackouts (1962, 64pp). Named 6th SAM Dean of Magicians in 1973. 1978 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Articles. Chuck Stanfield was writing a bio at the time of his own death in 1991. [Bo#197;LR7/2004;Dor;Wal;Des]

name: Dorotti, Kleo
bio: (Russia: 1900-) Stage name of Klawdia Grigorievna Karasik. Pro magicienne. Assistant to Kasfikis until 1929 when she went solo in circuses as pro illusioniste. [Nad]

name: Doty [Jr], J[ames] C.
bio: (Macon, Georgia: 31 Mar 1927- ) In teens did a 2-person act with Bob Carver. Maker of signs & custom props (The Making Thing Company) in Lithia Springs, Georgia. Amateur magician with Drunk Act. Decorated Tom Mullica's Tom-Foolery magic bar in Atlanta c1978. [LR8/89]

name: Douglas, Bert
bio: (Aberdeen, Scotland: 1897-9 Mar 1974) Stage name of Douglas Robert Smith. Moved to Canada in 1920. Semi-pro magician. A Freemason. Wrote at least 13 booklets, including Original Magical Problems (n.d.), Original Magic for All (1927), Club Magic (1930), Magic Worth Knowing (1931, 63pp), Magical Patter (n.d.), ABC Book of Patter (n.d.), More Club Magic (1935), Modern Club Act and Chemical Rabbits (1935), Magic as You Like It (1935), Patter in Rhyme, Old Tricks Made New (1941). Tricks in Tarbell #5 & Tops. [LR5/74]

name: Douglas, Delbert D.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-70s) Co-owner (with brother Lyle) Douglas Magicland magic shop in Dallas, Texas, 1915-1949 & sole owner 1949-1970 when the shop was bought by to Gene Jeffries. [Albo95]

name: Douglas, Lyle
bio: (USA: -7 Jun 1982) Pro dealer originally as a mail-order house (Douglas Magic Company) in Dreamland, Texas, in 1911. Then with brother Delbert operated as retail shop (Douglas Magicland) 1915-1949 when sole ownership passed to Delbert. Wrote 33 Card Mysteries (1924, 64pp, although mainly a catalog). [Albo95]

name: Douglas, Roy
bio: See: Craggs, Douglas

name: Douglas, Mike
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Stage magician with parakeets & a cat. 1989 Desert Magic Seminar 3rd prize.

name: Douglass, Michael D, AIMC
bio: (Pasadena, California: 1 Mar 1956-) Taught by John U. Zweers. Emergency Services Coordinator for State of California & semi-pro radio & TV actor. Semi-pro stage & parlor magician & vent since 1974. SAM President 1991-92. Articles in MUM. [MUM8/91;Wh5]

name: Dovini
bio: See: Proudlove, Stan

name: Doward
bio: (Britain: fl.c1840s) Minor pro who toured Scotland & north England. Pet effect: The Gun Trick. [Fr]

name: Dowd, Thomas M. "Tom" "Tommy
bio: (Hardin County, Ohio: 1 Jun 1912-1 Nov 1995) Of Irish extraction. Farmer to lawyer to judge. Amateur since childhood when inspired by W.W. Durbin's show. Purchased the Egyptian Hall from Durbin's widow in 1940, selling all but the building to David Price in 1953. IBM Treasurer 1958-79. Trick in HMM. Elder brother of amateur magician Robert C. Dowd.

name: Dowler, Arthur
bio: (Stoke-on-Trent, England: 30 Dec 1894-17 Jan 1953) Pro comedy magic since late middle age. Invented the Legs Table. Co-founded (with H. Stanley, G. Leaney, & J. Hughes) Unique Magic Studio in London in 1946.

name: Downes, T.
bio: (England: fl.1850s) Pro magician, lecturer, & prop maker in London by 1857 when he performed at the Royal Colosseum. [Cl;Daw94]

name: Downs, T[homas] N[elson] "Tommy
bio: (Garwin, Iowa: 16 Mar 1867-12 Sep 1938) Raised in Montour & Marshalltown, Iowa. Debut in 1883 at age 16 with coin manip. Pro coin & card manipulator since 1891. World-famous as "King of Koins". Toured England & the Continent 1899-1901 & 1904, playing only the top music halls such as the London Palace (1899) for 6 months, the Berlin Wintergarten (1900) for 8 weeks, the Casino de Paris (1900), & the Folies-Bergère (1904). Founder-owner of the London Magical Company in London, England, around 1901. SAM member #149. Retired in comfort in Marshalltown in 1912. SAM Hall of Fame. Prolific innovator in coin magic. Invented back-and-front palm (1884), click pass (by 1900), Eureka Pass (by 1900), Downs Palm (by 1902), edge palm, Coins to Glass (by 1909), Coin Star, Downs Change (by 1909), possibly estimation (by 1909), & Dime and Penny Trick (in 1917). Authored Modern Coin Manipulation (1900, 244pp, ghosted by W.J. Hilliar; repr as Tricks with Coins, 1902, 170pp; 1905, 174pp); & The Art of Magic (1909, 334pp, ghosted as well as "edited" by J.N. Hilliard; repr 1921, 348pp & 1980, 348pp), which is a major classic. See also Nathan Dean (ed.), Conjuring with Coins (1912, 125pp). [Pr;Dif;Ch;Go2;Ho]

name: Dr. Q
bio: See: Conlin [Sr], Claude Alexander Larsen, William W.

name: Dr. X
bio: See: Silver, George

name: Dr. Z
bio: See: De Soboll, Felix Stephen

name: Dracstein
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Stage name of Cliff Bennett. Pro. [Tops1/39]

name: Draculas, Dr.
bio: See: Mondor, Card

name: Dracup, Reverend Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Church minister. Prominent gospel magician. Wrote 4 books on the subject: Magic with an Upward Look (166pp), Magic that gives an Upward Lift (136pp), Magic That Points to the Upward Life (1988, 158pp), & A Magician Goes to Church.

name: Drake, David, AIMC
bio: (Vancouver, Canada: 25 Jan 1931-23 Aug 1998) Stage name of David Campbell Foote. Learned at age 10 from catalog tricks. Moved to Toronto in 1950s. Part-time freelance screen & TV writer. Pro magician since 1969, with close-up & platform for adults, children, trade shows, etc in Toronto area. Tricks in Tops, Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, Precursor, & Pentagram. Died of liver cancer. [LR10/98;LR8/81;Wh2]

name: Drake, Don
bio: (Kalamazoo, Michigan: May 1939-) Inspired as kid by Blackstone. Pro as "Dondrake" since began demoing at Stevenson's Wizard Magic Shop in NY Times Square Square subway in 1950s. Also worked for Tannen's, EZ Magic, & Flosso. Specialist in Black Art work and author of Black Art Breakthroughs. Now lives in Las Vegas. [MUM6/2001]

name: Drake, Simon
bio: (England: fl.1980s) Pro magician in London where he mainly works the pop-music scene. Featured on Sebastian Cody's London TV series "The Secret Cabaret" (scheduled for 1990 on Channel 4).

name: Draklof
bio: See: Folkard, Charles J.

name: Drakon
bio: (Itabuna, Brazil: 7 Oct 1921- ) Stage name of Alcides Barbosa de SOUZA. Top-line pro magician in Brazil. Manip, stage, kid-show, & comedy magic. 1964 Grand Prix for Illusions & 1965 Grand Prix of the Brazilian Magic Competitions, plus other prizes. Played the Casino Estoril, Portugal, in 1968. [Cam]

name: Drandorf, William
bio: (USA: c1917-23 Apr 1992) Pro card & cig manipulator as "Wee Willy Dee" in 1930s-40s, mainly on East Coast. Closed his act with a string puppet, "Willie Jr.", that did a couple of production tricks. Invented giant card rise using rubber roller & Ultra Milk Vanish (marketed in 1953). In 1950 turned to straight standup comedy as "Wally Dean" until retirement in 1981. Tricks & routines in Phoenix. [MUM8/92]

name: Drane, Edward O. "Ed
bio: (USA: -19 Mar 1974) Pro magician as "Enardoe". Invented the Eureka Deck (by 1928) & the Enardoe Playing Cards deck of marked cards. Dealer (Edward O. Drane & Co.) in Chicago by 1952 when published Okito on Magic. In 1967 his shop was absorbed by Morris Costume Company. [Mec]

name: Dratton, Charles
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Resident of London. Co-wrote (with Gilbert Stout) Conjuring for Conjurers (n.d. [1907], 16pp [or 24pp]. Issued a catalog of "original tricks" in 1909.

name: Draun, Steve
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Close-up in Chicago inner circle. Wrote The Magic of Steve Draun (1988, 43pp) & Secrets Draun from the Underground. Tricks in Apocalypse. 1 video (1998).

name: Dreilinger, Sam[uel L.]
bio: (USA: -1 Jan 1979) President of Eastern Metal Spinning Co in New York City. Amateur magician by late 1920s & magic collector. Invented the Auto-Mazo Deck and possibly Color Changing Necktie. Elected first President of Magic Collectors Association 1950-51. Sold his collection of magic books in 1953 to John McManus.

name: Drewla, Jerzy
bio: (Lwów, Poland [now Lvov, Ukraine]: 20 Apr 1936 [sic]) Studied magic since age 14. Student of Salvano & Constanti. Pro by 1968 with manip & small illusions. Toured many years in East Germany. [Win;Mec] Driebeek, Robert A. M. "Bob" (Holland: 8 Feb 1922-7 Aug 2002) Worked at a freight-shipping company in Rotterdam. Semi-pro comedy magician. Invented Necktie Servante in late 1930s, Tosheroon, & the Driebeek Die. Aka "Aenigma". Early mentor of Fred Kaps. 1953 Dutch Grand Prix. Tricks in Abra, Gen, etc.

name: Driest, Dr Jörg
bio: (Germany?: 4 Dec 1939-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Drioux, Auguste[-Jules]
bio: (Lyon, France: 3 Mar 1884-25 May 1937) Taught by father. Semi-pro debut in 1899 (age 15) with stage name "Pass" doing Cups-and-Balls. Aka "Té-Dé" in WW I. Wrote Nos Tours favoris: Galerie universelle des prestidigitateurs (2 vols, 1914). Edited Passez Muscade: Journal des Prestidigitateurs 1916-1935. Compiled Annaure des Prestidigitateurs (1924). Claimed world's largest collection of magicians photos in 1932. [Dif;Vo55;WWM]

name: Drisbach, Julius
bio: (USA: -Feb 1944) Sometimes misspelled Dresbach. Pro card & coin worker by 1920. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. German immigrant who worked at Martinka's around 1911 where he introduced his tube. NOTE: Vernon's claim that Drisbach invented the Hand Dye Tube for color change of silk thru fist is wrong. It was invented independently by James Carl & Robertson Keene.

name: Driscoll, Paul
bio: (Texas: 1958-) Hosted weekly TV show in Houston in his teens. Now works corporate shows, cruise ships, etc. [Ran]

name: Driver
bio:
Droullat, Charles A. (Barcelona, Spain: fl.1910s) Pro shadowist, introducing color shadowgraphs in 1914 in act (with his assistant-wife Marina) called "The Joannys". [Pr]

[See also: "Kudarz, Robert"]

name: Droz
bio: See: Jaquet-Droz

name: Drummond
bio: See: Annemann, Theo[dore]

name: DuBois, [William] Richard "Dick
bio: (New York City, New York: 7 Jan 1905-25 Mar 1965) Semi-pro close-up & escapes. Aka "Duleni". Worked at Holden's 1949. In 1949-50 hosted TV's "Magic in the Air" series. SAM President 1950-51. In 1951-52 replaced Zovello as NBC-TV's "The Magic Clown". Crueship worker in late 1950s. [Go2;HMM10/60]

name: Ducaine, Paul
bio: (England: 1909 - 15 Nov 1999) Stage name of Sidney "Sid" Smith. Close-up worker. British Ring Past President.

name: Ducarel, C[ecil]
bio: (Durham, England: c1854-18 Oct 1938) Stage name of Thomas Samuels. Dealer & collector in Leeds 1900s-30s.

name: Ducatillon, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1930s-80s) Founder-President in 1939 of the Nord-Magic-Club (Lille). AFAP Gold Medal 1989.

name: Ducret, Étienne
bio: (France: fl.1890s) Wrote Traité complet des tours d'Escamotage anciens et nouveaux ou la prestidigitation expliquée (Paris: 1893) & Tours de Cartes, anciens et nouveaux (Paris: 139pp).

name: Ducrot, Frank "Duke" "Fritz" [pronounced DU-CROW]
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City: 7 May 1872-24 May 1939) Stage name of T[heodore] Francis Fritz. Pro vaude magician (1900-15), including European tour when he played St. George's Hall in 1912, to star status with the Chautauqua (since 1916) & Lyceum circuits (1915-20), to club dates. Joined SAM in 1902 as Member #15. Invented the cigarette dropper (1902) & blendo (by 1909). Edited Mahatma 1901-06. Pro dealer first (by 1906) out of his apartment as the "Brooklyn Magic Co" in Brooklyn where he bought out or absorbed 38 firms, including the magic shops of Burlingame (in 1906), Otto Maurer, H.L. Judd, & C. Milton Chase. Then in Manhattan as the "Hornmann Magic Co" from 1921 (when he bought Martinka's) to his death. An "avid collector of magic shops" (as Jack Flosso recalls him), Ducrot bought out 5 additional magic shops, including those of Sam Bailey (1925) & Clyde Powers (1920s). In 1939 [sic] the business was auctioned for $585 to Al Flosso.[Pr;Br,pp53,56-58;Dor;Ho]

name: Duda, Cristel
bio: (Halle [sic], Germany: 29 Apr 1937-) Pro assistant to husband Werner Duda as the "2 Dudas" in East Germany. [Win]

name: Duda, Werner
bio: (Wolfen, Germany: 28 Nov 1934-) Pro stage magician since 1972 with assistant-wife Cristel as the "2 Dudas" in East Germany. [Win]

name: Dudash, Gary [Charles]
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 29 Dec 1948-) Learned at age 12 from a TV-advertised Thurston's 400 Tricks You Can Do. Semi-pro close-up & mental magic since age 21. Aka "Derringer" & "Durango". Pet effects: Key-R-Rect plus own "minor" tricks that he mail-order markets. Columnist in Vibrations. [Wh2]

name: Dudeney, Henry Ernest
bio: (Mayfield, Suxxex, England: 10 Apr 1857-24 Apr 1930) Amateur magician who enjoyed entertaining children at parties with sleight-of-hand, charades, and other party games. World's most prolific inventor of puzzles since publishing his first book, The Canterbury Puzzles (1907). Often collaborated with leading American puzzle inventor, Sam Loyd. Dudeney, unlike Loyd, was scrupulous in giving credit to the inventors of puzzles other than his own. REF: Martin Gardner (editor), 536 Puzzles and Curious Problems by Henry Ernest Dudeney (New York: Scribner's 1967).

name: Duffie, Peter [W.]
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 1957-) Began learning at age 8. Card magician, one of the more creative in Great Britain. Wrote Alternative Card Magic (1982, 33pp, with Jerry Sadowitz), Contemporary Card Magic (1984, 47pp, with Jerry Sadowitz), Close-up to the Point (1984, 30pp), Quartet (1986, 16pp), Inspirations (1987, 119pp, with Jerry Sadowitz), Imagine (1991), Obsession (1992), Ulterior Motifs (1992), Card Selection (1992), Applications (1993, 46pp), Cards In Principle (1994, 24pp), Effortless Card Magic (1997, 164pp), etc. Tricks in Magic, Magic Magazine, Profile, The Crimp, & LR (1995 1-Man Parade).

name: Dugwar
bio: (India: fl.1870s-80s) Probably Hindu. Pro juggler & probably a magician. Played London 1877-80, including the Royal Polytechnic. [CI]

name: Duijker, Hubrecht A[nthonie]
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 12 Feb 1942-) Learned in 1955 from Larette studio. Wine critic (30 books) & games writer (3 books). Amateur close-up magician with stage name of "Anthony Verhulst" (since 1980). Pet effects: card tricks. Founder-Editor of Informagie, 1989-present. [Wh5]

name: Duke, Paul
bio: (Kiev, Russia: 17 Feb 1895-28 Jun 1981) Moved to USA. Learned assisting Houdini. Pro club magician since 1935. Played the Paris Alhambra c1935. ..... [Pr] du Laar, Professeur (France: fl.1890s) Stage name of Jérôme Dulaar. Pro. Operated his own Théâtre Mondain in 1898. [Dif]

name: Dulay, Benson
bio: (Northampton, England: 1899-Jul 1991) Stage name of William "Billy" Dooley. Pro comedy illusionist since 1919 as "Billy Dooley". Invented several tricks, including Multum in Parvo, which Burtini introduced in 1947. Bio sketch in Dexter (1956), 93-94, 117. [Hudd]

name: Duleni
bio: See: Du Bois, Richard

name: Dundy, Elmer S. "Skip
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Entered showbiz as assistant to magician F.E. Powell. Then created the famous Trip to the Moon illusion in Buffalo, New York. In 1903 co-founded (with Frederick Thompson) Luna Park on Coney Island. Moved Trip to the Moon to Luna Park in 1904 at which time this vast 100-acre fantasy amusement park with its theaters & rides was averaging 90,000 customers per day. It was destroyed by fire in 1944. In 1905 Dundy & Thompson opened the huge Hippodrome theater in central Manhattan. [HMM7/57]

name: Dunhill, Ed
bio: (Providence, Rhode Island: 4 Dec 1938-) Stage name of Edward G. Di Giulio. Learned at age 16 from friends Jimmy Ray & Tony Kardyo. Pro since 1960 with stage, close-up, & mental magic. Wrote Miracles in Magic from My Friends (1990, 86pp). Tricks in Magic Info. [Wh5]

name: Dunn, Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Illustrator. Amateur magician. Wrote Magic for All (1947; repr as Make Magic, 1957, 160pp), a collection of his syndicated comic-strip tricks for King Features. Often stooged for Dunninger in 1950s. [HMM10/55,6/56]

name: Dunn, Bruce
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Amateur magician in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Noted for his bizarre satires & spoofs of magic collectors & collecting, publishing-editing L'Majik Satirica (1973, 3 issues), New Image L'Majik Satirica (1974-79, 13 issues), & Pseudo Sorcery (1978-80, 8 issues). As a serious magazine published-edited Notes on the Attic (1982-84, 28 issues) & Pro-Maso. Wrote Pandora's Box (1973-76 as 7 supplements to Chaos), The One-Handed Card Cutter, & The Two-Handed Card Cutter.

name: Dunn, Ricki
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 2 Apr 1929 – 25 Jan 1999) Stage name of Fred Revello. Of Italian [sic] ancestry. Learned card tricks at age 5 from his father, a pro gambler. Pro as sideshow fire-eater (at age 14) to clown to magician (briefly) to pickpocket act (since 1950). Played the NY Palace in 1955. Had bit part in movie The Bellboy (1960). Now billed as "America's Funniest Pickpocket". Plays mainly night clubs, hotels, & cruise ships. Wrote Ricki Dunn's Pickpocket Act (forthcoming). Tricks in New Phoenix. [Bo2; Tops12/63; HMM8/55; Mag;Wh2]

name: Dunning, R. K.
bio: See: "Kahn"

name: Dunning, Mrs R. K.
bio: See: "Kahn, Miss/Madame"

name: Dunningarto
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Minor stage pro with card & ball manip & silk sleights. Adding stage illusions supplied by Gamage's & assisted by Miss Devo (Leah Goldston, see), he played London's Alhambra in 1906. Pet effect (1906-07): producing full 52 card-deck 1-by-1 from back palm (using extra-thin cards). REF: Warlock (1986), 29-31. [Magic11/09]

name: Dunninger, Joseph "Joe
bio: (Lower East Side, Manhattan, New York City, NY: 18 Apr 1892-9 Mar 1975) Son of poor German immigrants, his mother a Jew, his father Roman Catholic. Inspired seeing Kellar in 1898. Learned from a magic book. Semi-pro magician since c1909 doing magic, illusions, & mentalism. Invented & marketed 2 card tricks by 1912: "TRI-Card Mystery" & "Cards Illusionary". Played New York's Eden Musée for 57 weeks in 1913-14. Specialized in mentalism since 1920. Played the New York Hippodrome in 1921 & the Palace in 1926. Did mentalism on radio in 1929 & 1943-44. Star of TV series in New York 1948-50 & nationally in 1955-56. Parkinson's Disease forced his retirement in the early 1970s as America's most famous mentalist. 1975 AMA Masters Fellowship. Authored the following works (almost all ghosted by either Walter B. Gibson or David Lustig): Houdini's Spirit Exposés (1928, 111pp); Inside the Medium's Cabinet (1935, 228pp), a first-hand account of his exposés of fraudulent psychics, including Nino Pecoraro; How to Make a Ghost Walk (1936, 82pp, ghosted by Gibson); Dunninger's What's On Your Mind (1944, 192pp, ghosted by Gibson); Dunninger's Magic Tricks (1951, 144pp); 100 Houdini Tricks You Can Do (1954, 143pp); The Art of Thought Reading (1956; repr 1962); Dunninger's Complete Encyclopedia of Magic (1965, 288pp; repr 1970), collected reprints of his articles in Science and Invention Magazine; Dunninger's Monument to Magic (1974, 222pp), etc. See James McKnight, Dunninger's Act Complete (manuscript reviewing a 1927 act in Indianapolis). Memoir ("as told to Walter Gibson") is Dunninger's Secrets (1974, 332pp). Audio. [Zo;3/2003;True2/50;Ran;Pr; Ch;HC;Fi;Jinx#70;Ho;HMM10/46;LR11/51]

name: Duo Absolon
bio: See: Absolon, Blanka & Absolon, Karel

name: Duo Matrix
bio: See: Szubert, Andrzej

name: Duo Elmann
bio: See: Elman, Irène & Elman, Vlastimil

name: Duo Hasard
bio: See: Dahms, Peter

name: Duo Tamesis
bio:
Duperrey, [Célestin-François] [surname pronounced dew-PEAR-ay] (London, England: 21 Apr 1843-27 Apr 1913) Of French parents. Pro illusionist by 1887. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1888-94. [Dif;Vo55]

[See also: Eleisa, Fee & Hornung, Werner]

name: Dupin, André
bio: (France: fl.1940s-50s) Pro. As "Les Andréor" with assistant-wife combined illusion with dance 1945-57. As "Andréor" starred in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique 1957-58. [Dif]

name: Duprez, Professor Louis
bio: (France: fl.1870s-90s) Educated in England. Pro since 1873. Played Piccadilly Hall in London in 1881. Toured the British provinces in 1883, featuring animals, Vanishing Birdcage, Bullet-Catching, a dark séance, & the Rising Cards for which he was said to have introduced the hand-held swinging houlette. At Xmas 1892 his performance at Maskelyne's included his version of the Vanishing Lady with 3 dogs. Wrote Drawing-room Magic and Spiritualism (Plymouth: n.d., 28pp). [Cl; Magic10/03]

name: Duraty
bio: (Boulogne, France: 28 Jun 1936- ) Stage name of Jean-Fred Combet-Joly. Learned in 1946 from books & amateurs. Advertiser. Semi-pro close-up & comedy magician & MC since 1950. AFAP Bronze Medal 1979. A Director of La revue de la prestidigitation 1982-86. 1984 Crandall Trophy. AFAP Silver Medal 1986. Lecturer & magic book dealer in Versailles. Wrote Magie pour les amis, Magie pour rire, Frissons magiques, & Cours de tartes. Articles in Arcane (France), Revue de la Prestidigitation, & Linking Ring. [Bou2;Wh2]

name: Durbin [Jr], W[illiam] W[arner] "Bill" "Uncle
bio: (Kenton, Ohio: 29 Sep 1866-4 Feb 1937) Lawyer, businessman, politician, & federal executive. Amateur magician since 1893 (pro 1897-1902) giving full-evening shows locally. Built the Egyptian Hall in Kenton, Ohio, in 1895 as a small private magic theater, which was decorated with his collection of over 3,000 posters & photos. Driving force in developing the IBM of which he was Member #212, organizing & hosting its 1st convention in 1926. 2nd IBM President 1926-1937. Edited Linking Ring 1927-37. Wrote a force book (in 1904 under pen name of "W.P. Huntington"). Wrote Who's Who in Magic (1926-27). Memoir is "My Life in Magic", which ran serially in The Linking Ring Sep 1935-Jun 1937. [LR5/2004;LR8/94;Bo#197;Dor;Ho;WWM]

name: Durga, Mlle.
bio: (Germany?: -1974?) Pro illusionist, touring Europe, 1909-10. Pet effect: Onaip = Floating Piano. [Dif;Rey]

name: Durham, Geoff[rey]
bio: (England: fl.1980s-90s) Pro. Until recently worked as "The Great Soprendo", a pseudo-Spanish magician comedy act for children & adults. Now more conventional stage magic. Husband of comedienne Victoria Wood with whom he often works a 2-person act. TV bits.

name: Durham [Jr], Richard [Edgar] "Dick
bio: (Bradford, Arkansas: 14 Dec 1912- ) Learned in 1923 from parents Xmas gift magic set & in 1927-28 from the mail-order Tarbell Course. Semi-pro magician as "Roba The Mystic" in early 1930s. Aka "Durham The Magician" in mid-1930s to 1942, including playing tent shows in the South. Thence plays club shows as a semi-pro. Co-founded (with Ben Badley & Roba Collins) St. Louis Society of Magicians in 1943. Invented several effects & plastic props, including "Durham's Safety Pin Thru Hank" (1950) & "Utility Tumbler" (1963). Articles & tricks in Seven Circles, Tops, & Genii. [Tops8/44;Wh2]

name: Durno, J. H.
bio: (Rockford, Illinois: fl.1890s) A major pro illusionist with the Lyceum circuit. [Pr]

name: Dusenberg
bio: See: Ericsson, Carl-Johan

name: Dusenberry, H. Syril "Sy
bio: (San Francisco, California: -22 Aug 1982) Learned at age 13 from gift box-of-tricks. Electrical engineer. Amateur magician. Founding President of Pacific Coast Society of Magicians (now SAM Golden Gate Assembly #2) in San Francisco in 1912. Articles in Sphinx & Magic (1914 & 1919). Wrote Making Magic Pay (1923; repr 1997, 24pp). [Dor]

name: Dusheck Jr, Steve[n John]
bio: (Hazelton, Pennsylvania: 10 Sep 1944-) Learned at age 8 from parents gift Mandrake magic set & at age 11 from Sneaky Pete deluxe magic set. Invented Waltzing Matilda, marketing it in 1967 at which time he became a pro dealer as "Steve St. Eve" but retired c1970 over disgust with dealer piracies of his inventions. Field engineer (computer repair). Invented Wunderbar & later (inspired on first seeing the 1956 Hennig-Kaps' Floating Cork) to market his variant in 1975. Thence a semi-pro mail-order dealer under own name as "Original Manufacturing Company" in Hazelton. Invented over 200 marketed effects, his Waltzing Matilda still selling 1,000 per year. Wrote Dusheck's Thumb Tip Magic, Dusheck's Coin Magic, Dusheck's Card Magic, Dusheck's Mental Magic, & Dusheck's Close-up Magic (166pp). Tricks in Magic Manuscript, MUM, New Directions, etc. Column in Mortimer's Magic Magazine since 1989. Video. [MM1/89;Wh2]

name: Dutt, A[mar] N[ath]
bio: (Lahore, Punjab, India: 1884-27 Nov 1937) A true Hindu, although often mistaken for a Westerner by both some fellow magicians & magic historians. Son of a physician in Lahore. Went to Edinburgh to study medicine but soon moved to USA where he learned magic assisting in a Ringling Bros sideshow. Pro stage magician by 1905 as successively "Ram Bhuj", "Ishmael", & finally (by 1920) as "Linga Singh" (posing as a Sikh). Played the London Coliseum in 1911, St. George's Hall in London 1920 & 1921, the Paris Empire 1924, the Berlin Wintergarten 1926, the Buenos Aires Casino 1931, & the London Trocadero Restaurant in early 1937. After his death (from pneumonia) in London all his props were burned on his instructions. [St.Ch:Pr.Ram p158:Difl [St;Ch;Pr;Bam,p158;Dif] "Duval Brothers, The" SEE: Blaeser, Andy & Duval, Ade

name: Duval, Ade
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 31 Dec 1898-13 Aug 1965) Stage name of Adolph Albert "Ade" Amrein. Inspired in 1915 seeing Thurston. Learned by buying from Felsman's magic shop. Debut by 1917, working with Andrew Blaeser as "Amrein & Baeser" & "The Duval Brothers" on Chautauqua & Lyceum circuits 1921-1924 when went solo. Introduced his unique "A Rhapsody in Silk" act (named by Paul Fox) on 8 Jun 1928. Since 1928 his assistant-wife was True Duval (see). Switched to vaudeville stardom that July. Played the New York Capitol & Palace theaters in 1931. Toured England 1935 (including the London Palladium); the Continent 1935-36 (including the Berlin Wintergarten in 1935) & 1939; and Australia 1939-40 & 1947. In 1940 invented the 1st practical stage method for the Smoking Thumb effect created in 1938 by movie comedian Stan Laurel. Played the New York Palace again in 1951. Retired in 1955 & sold his silk act Al Sharpe. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote A Rhapsody in Silk (1962, 64pp). [Pr;Par;Bos;Wal;Ch;Dor;Tay]

name: Duval. True
bio: (Lincoln, Nebraska: -8 Sep [sic] 1956) Stage name of Gertrude Estelle "True" Amrein, née Erickson. With an all-girl band until she married Adolph Amrein ("Ade Duval") on 2 Aug 1928, becoming his assistant in their famous two-person silk act. Died in Portales, New Mexico. [Pr;Mar]

name: Duveen
bio: See: Davies, Phil[ip]

name: Duvivier, Dominique
bio: (Paris, France: 8 Sep 1950-) Inspired at age 8 seeing Peter Lorre in Lang's classic movie M. Pro magician since 1972, specializing in cards & close-up. Magic teacher. Part owner of magic nightclub Le Double Fond, which opened in Paris in 1988. In 1991 took over from Michel Hatte as proprietor of Mayette Magie Moderne. Invented Printing (1974), Translucent Cards (1982), Chameleon Cards (1983), etc. Wrote La magie de Dominique Duvivier (1974) & Cartomagie Année 2001-2008 (1974-83, 368pp). See also John Racherbaumer, Magie Duvivier (1996, 179pp) & Jeff Busby, Dominique Duvivier's Einstein's Blackboards (1996, 20pp). Articles in Journal de la Prestidigitation & Magic Manuscript. Review columns in Magie 1974-81. Co-editor Le Magicien since 1992. Videos (1982, 1987-89, totalling 30 hours). [Thaumaturgist11/94;Wh2]

name: Duvolo, Paul
bio: See: Burford, Allan

name: Eads, Bob
bio: (Washington, D.C.: fl.1960s-80s) Pro close-up at trade shows, on cruise ships, etc. 1972 AMA Best Lecturer. Thence to magazine publishing in Las Vegas in 1980s. [Mag]

name: Eagle, G. Barnardo "Barney
bio: (Barnet, Middlesex, England: c1800-4 May 1861?) Son of an innkeeper. Pro. Aka "Barnardo", "Na Barno", & billed as "The Royal Wizard of the South". Early rival of J.H. Anderson. Author (ghosted) of Barnardo's Hand-Book of Magic [c1846, 26pp]. Toured Australia in 1856 & 1861. Father of Georgiana Eagle. [Cl;Wal]

name: Eagle, Georgiana
bio: (England: fl.1840s-80s) Georgiana Gilliland née Eagle. Taught by pro father Barnardo Eagle. Pro second-sight act by 1841-46 as "The Mysterious Lady" and 1872-86 with hypnotic act as "Gilliland Card" & "Madame Card". See H.E. Wingfield, An Introduction to the Study of Hypnotism (1910), 165-166. [Mar;Cl;Pr]

name: Earle, Lee [nmn]
bio: (Columbus, Ohio: 22 Jun 1945- ) Born Lee Loudy, which he later changed to Lee Earle. Learned as child. Moved to Phoenix, Arizona, in 1960. 1st mentor was Don Seth. Semi-pro magician since 1961. Pro mentalist since c1985. Worked 2 years as the medium in a twice-nightly séance in a private home. Now tours the Sun Belt as a psychic entertainer. Wrote Super Dupery (1987, 33pp), First Impressions (c1988, 32pp), The Classic Reading: An Introduction to the Gentle Art of Cold Reading (1989, 16pp+70 minute audio cassette), On Second Thought (1989, 40pp), Manifestations (1989, 46pp+6 one-hour audios), Making Manifestations: Building the Commercial Seance (1989, 32pp), Mélange à Trois (1990), & Mnemonics for Psychic Entertainers. Columns in Seance & MUM (1993-95). Edits-publishes Syzygy: The Journal of Contemporary Mentalism since 1994. Tricks in Vibrations & MUM. 2 audios, 1 video. [MUM12/94;Wh]

name: Easley, [Herbert Cecil] "Bert
bio: (Shawnee, Oklahoma Indian Territory: 16 Dec 1904-12 Nov 1987) Inspired by & learned from Grady Nicholson c1924-c26. Acrobat & specialty dancer. Pro comedy magician c1940-1947 as "The Tipsy Trickster". Left stage in 1947 to be a magic dealer (Bert Easley's Fun Shop) in Phoenix, Arizona. 1948 PCAM Caryl Fleming Trophy for comedy magic. Retired in 1975, turning the shop over to his son, Herbert "Herb" Easley Jr. 1985. AMA Performing Fellowship. Taught Bob Bluemle, Paul Estes, etc. Wrote Doing Magic for Youngsters (1948, 36pp) published in same volume with Eric P. Wilson's booklet.

name: Eason, [William H.] "Doc
bio: (Taft, California: 21 Dec 1933-) Took over Bert Easley's Fun Shop in Phoenix, Arizona, on his father's retirement in 1975. (Waterbury, Connecticut: 22 Jul 1947-) Professional speaker. Learned magic in 1977 (age 30), Bob Sheets being his mentor. Pro as bartender-magician since 1977 at Bob Denver's Tower Magic Bar & Restaurant in Aspen, Colorado. Pet effects: Card on Ceiling, Card under Glass, Bill in Lemon. Wrote (with Michael Ammar) Aspen Bar Magic. Video: Rocky Mountain Magic (1990). Tricks in Genii & Magic Menu. 3 videos (1998). [Genii11/91;Wh2]

name: Eastman, Charles C.
bio: (Haverhill, Massachusetts: 1903-24 Nov 1992) Introduced to magic shilling for Al Flosso at Coney Island around late 1910s & then with Gordon's Ten-in-One Circus at Revere Beach. Invented "Phantamo" (by 1932) & "New Chinese Mystery Blocks" (by 1932). Since c1924 wrote & co-authored 24 booklets & manuscripts, including Manipulative Magic (23pp); More Manipulative Magic (25pp); Expert Manipulative Magic (1933, 40pp); Enthusiastic Magic (1935, 20pp); & Tenoki's Horoscope of Life (1935), a forcing book.

name: Ebel, Dieter
bio: (Germany: 13 May 1927-) Magician with assistant "Valentina". 1978 MZvD 1st prize in closeup & 2nd prize in card magic; 1981 MZvD 1st prize for invention; 1984 MZvD 1st prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Eck, Johnny
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland?: 27 Aug 1911-) Stage name of John Eckhardt. Although born a complete male, his legs and lower organs were compressed into his torso, making him appear to have been cut off at the waist. Exhibited in carnival freak shows since 1924. Co-star of Tod Browning's 1932 film horror classic Freaks. Exhibited at 1933 Chicago World Fair. Having a perfectly formed twin brother (Rob), George Boston recommended to Howard Thurston that they be used for the Sawing in Two. Thurston toyed with the idea but perceived too many problems. After Thurston's death in 1936, Rajah Raboid did use Eck at one performance, the audience shock being so great as to force its abandonment. Then with Rob into theatrical rental business in Baltimore as The Eckhart Brothers. A bio is in Richard Lamparski's Whatever Became of ...? (1985), 50-51. [Genii4/62]

name: Eckam, Elmer G.
bio: (Rochester, New York: c1891-6 Dec 1963) Learned at age 13. Debut assisting Ray Hogan. Pro to semi-pro (clothing cutter) & dealer with shop (Art in Magic) in Rochester. Published-edited Eckam's Echo 1937-40 as house organ. After his death the magic shop was bought in 1965 by Norm Sehm.

name: Eckartshausen, Karl von
bio: (Bavaria, Germany: 1752 - 1803) A Hofrat (judge) in Bavaria. Amateur magician. Wrote 5 magic books in German between 1788 & 1803, largely based on earlier authors including Simon Witgeest. These are Aufschlüsee zur Magie (Munich: 4 vols, 1788-92; 2nd ed 1792-95), Entdeckte Geheimnisse zur Aufklärung des Volkes über Aberglauben und Irrwahn (Munich: 1790), Verschiedenes zum Unterricht und zur Unterhaltung für Liebhaber der Gaukeltasche (Munich: 1791, 36+345pp), Selbst approbierter praktischer Taschenspieler (Gratz: 1791), & 50 ganz neu erfundene und bewährte Kunststücke von verschiedener Art (Leipzig: 1803). [St;Hou]

name: Eckl, Ed[win E.], AIMC
bio: (St. Marys, Pennsylvania: 9 Feb 1934-) Encouraged by Gene Gordon & Rev Sherman Epler, he learned magic at age c14-15. Chemist. Amateur close-up magician, specializing in comedy effects. Pet effects: Card Duck & visual puns. Mail-order & wholesale dealer as founder-owner "unikorn magik" (in Beverly, Massachusetts) 1971-present, which also publishes Bill Miesel's Precursor 1983-present. In 1977 first published (and later marketed as "Möby-Zip") the old but rare zipper variant of Afghan Bands. Invented "Manila Folder". Wrote Gardyloo (1977, 32pp). Tricks in Linking Ring, MUM, Genii, New Tops, SOB, SOB Jr, Magic Manuscript, Precursor, etc. [NT4/72;Wh2]

name: Edelhoff, Klaus
bio: (Germany: 18 Feb 1942-) Kid-show magician as "Zauber-Klaus". 1981, 1984, & 1987 MZvD 3rd prizes in childrens magic. [Nad]

name: Edeling, Haakon
bio: (Skire, Denmark: 21 Jan 1906- ) Lithographer in Vejle & then Copenhagen. Amateur to semi-pro magician. Joined Danish Magic Circle in 1937 [sic]. 1938 Frankfurt International Magic Congress 2nd prize. After WW II turned pro & toured his elegant act abroad. 1947 Paris International Magic Congress 2nd prize for presentation; FISM 1st prize for presentation 1948, 1950, & 1st prize for stage magic 1952. NMK Nordic Champion 1958 & 1959. Pet effect: Butterfly Trick. Tricks in Conjurors' Magazine. [St;Dif]

name: Edernac, Pierre
bio: (Paris, France: 3 Jul 1919-) Stage name of Pierre Genin. Learned as child. Protégé of Caroly II. Pro manip, close-up, & inventor. Toured most of Europe, including 14 times at The Crazy Horse in Paris. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Silver Medal 1970 & Bronze Medal 1971. Professor in the National Circus School. A teacher of Fee Eleisa. AFAP President 1973-76. AFAP Gold Medal 1983. [Win;Bou;Bou2]

name: Edgar, Professor
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Edgar Oates. Minor illusionist & collector of magicana in Stoke, Devonport, England.

name: Edler, Carl
bio: (Berlin: 15 Jan 1877 – 5 Mar 1945) Pro ventriloquist. Amateur close-up magician of great skill. Invented many tricks. [Al;Roh]

name: Edmanson, Robert W.
bio: (England: 1890-29 May 1949) Pro magician & ventriloquist since 1909, touring only in Britain. Later specialized in childrens shows. [St]

name: Edmonds, Gregory B[ishop] "Greg
bio: (Goldsboro, North Carolina: 9 Dec 1957-) Writer/communication consultant. Learned at age 9 from Houdini Magic Set. Semi-pro magician since age 16. Specializes in mentalism & stand-up magic. Full-time professional magician/illusionist and later mentalist, during period 1983-1986 and 1992-1995. Served as agent for Marie Hinson Blood (Houdini's niece), 1983-1999. In 1988 co-founded (with Lyle Brite) Wonder Arts in Columbia, S. Carolina. Won three Linking Ring Awards (Howard Bamman Trophy for best mental effect twice; best close-up effect). Was editor of Vibrations and contributing editor to the Linking Ring and first executive editor to the IBM web portal. Taught a course in magic at the University of South Carolina. Tricks in Linking Ring (including a 1974 "Parade"). Cofounder of Ars Praestigium (2010). Invented: The Retractable Thumb Writer. Wrote Mind Set #1 (1993). Mind Set #2 (1995). PsiCles (2000) TV bits. [LR2/93;Wh5]

name: Edmüller, Andreas
bio: (Simbach, Bavaria Germany: 16 Apr 1958-) Amateur cardman in 1980s. Edited The Holdout (1982, 3 issues). Articles. Video.

name: Edmunda, Mdlle.
bio: See: "Dante, Madame"

name: Edward, James W.
bio: (Britain: 1911- ) Amateur debut at age 13. Semi-pro kid-show pseudo-Chinese act since 1930.

name: Edwards, Sir
bio: See: LaRue, [W. R.] "Buddy"

name: Edwards, Charles "Charlie
bio: (England: 1883?-Apr 1958) Pro street magician.

name: Edwards, Doug
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro mind-reader in New York City. Invented Wonder-Pen-Tration & 1-2-1 Bill Switch (1997). See Harry Lorayne, Doug Edwards Packs a Wallop (forthcoming 1997).

name: Edwards, Lee
bio: (Burbank, California: 17 Apr 1946 – 4 Apr 2004) Stage name of Lee Lorris Sprague. Inspired by & learned from a pocket trick bought at Disneyland at age 9. Pro illusions, manip, & mentalism since age 18. Works stages in USA, Canada, Mexico, & Australia, as well as cruise ships & trade shows. Having bought the ShazZam! show name and props from the Daniels he resold it in 2000 to Canadian illusionist Blair Marshall. Pet effects: Asrah Levitation, Back Stage, & Lazy Magician. Co-authored 5 booklets. Magic consultant for 3 TV shows, 2 movies, & TV commercials. Several TV bits & commercials. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Edwards, Ronald B. "Ron
bio: (Guelph, Ontario, Canada: 16 Apr 1910-30 Apr 1976) Inspired around age 10 seeing Thurston show but did not learn until around age 30. Amateur magician. Employee with Eastman Kodak, then insurance saleman. Tricks in Phoenix & New Phoenix. [Th]

name: Edwards, Sidney
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Pro card manip. Played St. George's Hall in 1924.

name: Edwards, W. G. "Will
bio: (Canada: fl.1900s-10s) Minor magic dealer (The W.G. Edwards Co) in Bridgeburg, Ontario, by 1908 when issued a catalog. Edited-published Edwards' Monthly Feb 1909-Jul 1910 (16 issues), Canada's 1st magic magazine. Edwards moved his company to Buffalo, New York, in late 1909. At that point he co-published with Downs the latter's classic The Art of Magic. Invented & marketed several gaffed-card tricks, including Canadian Wonder (Jul 1908); Dioramic Cards (1908), which were also readers; Contrario = Goblin Cards (by 1909); & Perplexo (1909).

name: Edwin
bio:
Rojas, Edwin "Edwin the Enigma" SEE: "Noble, Lee"

[See also: Hooper, Edwin]

name: Effendi
bio:
"Effess" [pen name in Magic] SEE: Sandford, Frank

[See also: Dodd, Frank N.]

name: Effy
bio: (Egypt: -c1943) Stage name of Hassanian Mohamed Chérifian Desouki. Pro sleight-of-hand. Moved to France in 1924. Worked Paris cafés, then circus, finally music-halls. Later worked with wife Halima as "Effy & Halima". Played the Coliseu in Lisbon in 1938. During WW II arrested in France by the Gestapo and shot. [Dif]

name: Effy, Halima
bio: (Egypt?: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name. Pro sleight-of-hand, working with her husband as "Effy & Halima". In WW II arrested in France by the Gestapo & deported to a concentration camp in Germany. Surviving, she resumed work in France as "Halima Effy".

name: Egelo
bio: (Norway: 23 Oct 1932-) Stage name of Egil Berg. Pro magician, impresario of magic, & dealer ("Egelo's Crazy Shop", nor Egelo's Magic Shop") in Oslo, Norway. 1988 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. Wrote Den Moderne Tryllebok (n.d.).

name: Egypta
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Minor pro magicienne.

name: Ehrens, Ben
bio: (USA: -Jan 1944) Amateur card magician in New York. Specialized in gambling demos. Member of the "Secret Six" in the 1930s.

name: Ehrhardt, Prof. Carl
bio: (Magdeburg, Germany: 19 Jun 1810-18 Mar 1860) Pro of old school. Worked exclusively in hometown area. Did execution illusion in 1857. [St;Al]

name: Eifert, Merlin
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Dealer (St. Louis Magic Studio) in St. Louis, Missouri, in early 1940s. Invented Linking Coathangers (1940s). Moved to southern California. [Genii6/67]

name: Eggleston, Charles Roltare
bio: See: "Roltare"

name: Egonni [pronounced ay-GOO-nee]
bio: (Hedemora, Sweden: 20 Sep 1911-18 Jul 1977) Stage name of Egon Norström. Pro stage magician since age 22. Charter member of the Göteborg Magiska Klubb in 1942. [Dif]

name: Eileen
bio: (Verona, New Jersey: 14 Sep 1958- ) Stage name of Eileen Lally Tichenor. Make-up artist in Sacramento, California. Semi-pro, having learned in 1988 as an assistant to Bob Brown. Works his stage & close-up shows as "Bob Brown & Eileen" both as assistant & as magicienne (Linking Rings, etc). World tour 1989. [Wh2]

name: El Barto
bio: See: Barton, James

name: El Condor
bio: (Scotland: fl.1960s) Stage name of James Graham. Pro.

name: El Duco
bio: (Jönköping, Sweden: 2 Nov 1941 – 30 Sep 2008) Stage name of Christer Gustavsson since 1965. Learned from magic set in 1955. Sales engineer. Performed for friends, then semi-pro at parties & in parks until 1979. Since then semi-pro magic inventor & mail order dealer ("El Duco's Magic") in Malmö, Sweden. Invented & marketed over 200 effects, including "Ring in Salt", & "Fireproof". Organizes the annual "Magic Weekend" in Sweden 1986-present. Wrote Out of My Hands, El Duco Impromptu, & Simple Ideas in Magic No.1, Simple Ideas in Magic No.2. Contributed to Apocalypse, Genii, Magic Manuscript, etc. [Wh2]

name: El Globo
bio: (Sweden: 11 Mar 1933-) Stage name of Ulf Mörling. Journalist. Semi-pro comedy illusionist. TV series 1976-78. Wrote Lär dig trolla (1971) & Lätta trolleritrick som Du kan göra själv (1983). [Mec] "el Ricco, Christer" SEE: Nilsson, Christer

name: Elbiquet
bio:
"Eldanis, The" SEE UNDER: Daniels, Paul

[See also: Branson, L. H.]

name: Eldin, Peter
bio: (Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire, England: 7 Apr 1939-) Stage name of Peter John Fails since 1958. Learned in 1948 from library books. Pro freelance writer (over 70 non-fiction books, mainly for children) since 1973. Semi-pro close-up & mental magician since age 15. Pet effects: C&R Rope, Salt Transpo, & impromptu close-up effects. Editor of Magic Circular 1990-1998. Edited the magic column in World's Fair 2002-2004-present. Wrote Amaze and Amuse Your Friends (1973, 121pp), The Trickster's Handbook (1976, 126pp), Ali Cat's Make Magic (1977), Isn't that Amazing! (1979, 128pp), Kingfisher Pocket Book of Magic (1985, 189pp; in USA 1985 as The Magic Handbook), Card and Conjuring Tricks (1989, as "Gordon Hill"), & Crazy Magic (1989, 128pp). Has also ghost-written for other magicians. Articles in Abra, Budget, & Magic Circular. [Wh5]

name: Eldoonie, Dr.
bio: (Kingston Township, Delaware County, Ohio: 17 Mar 1949- ) Stage name of Eldon D[ean] Wigton. Inspired at age 6 by Mark Wilson TV show. Learned at age 6-7 from library books. Pro since 1981 with stand-up & stage magic, specializing in a Medicine Man Pitch from his restored 1929 Model A Ford "Medicine Wagon". Has toured Canada (1978) & Europe (1979 & 1982). 1984 USA coast-to-coast blindfold drive in 10 days. On 29 Nov 1989 set Guinness record for World's Fastest Magician (115 effects in 2 minutes). [Wh5]

name: Eleisa, Fee
bio: (Berlin, West Germany: 27 Sep 1951- ) Stage name of Elizabeth Hornung (née Lennartz). Married Werner Hornung in 1976. Taught by Ali Bongo, Edernac, Mazakian, Vondrazec, & Dubsky. Pro stage magicienne since 1979. Sometimes worked with husband as "Duo Tamesis". 1979 FISM 1st prize for women. Featured at the 1980 IBM & 1982 FISM conventions. Invented Dog-Zigzag. Co-producer (with husband Werner Hornung) of Europa-Zauber-Theater. TV bits in Europe, USA, & Chile. 21 shows at the Magic Castle. [Wh2]

name: Elias
bio: (France: 1864-1926) Stage name of Elie-Marie-François Chautard. Pro stage mind-reader & hypnotist. A founding member of the CSP in 1904. Joined the ASAP in 1905. Wrote Les révélations d'un magnétique and Trucs ingénieux pour obtenir les phénomènes de la transmission de pensée, du magnétique et de l'hypnotisme (1904). [Dif]

name: Elias, Neal C[harles]
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 6 Mar 1921-21 Sep 2005) Learned at age 12 from library copy of Thurston's card book. Railroad clerk (retired). Amateur card magician & origami expert. Pet effects: "Almost anything of Marlo, Vernon, Jennings." Wrote At the Table (1946, 20pp) & The Jiggle or Shake Pass with Variations (1946, 11pp, with Bob Taylor). Tricks in Ibidem, Arcane, Epoptica, Precursor, & Technomagic. For his origami see David Venables, Neal Elias Selected Works 1964-1973 (1981). [Wh2] Eliason, Oscar SEE: "Dante the Great"

name: El-Iskendari el Kusi. Hasan ben Muhammad
bio: (Turkey: fl.1400s) Wrote Fi-l-hiyel el Babiliyye fi-l-Hizana el-Kamiliyye. This 15th century manuscript in Arabic devoted entirely to magic illusions & tricks is the earliest known work on the subject, preceding by over a half century the published books by Prévost and Scot. [Cam]

name: Ellenbogen, Raphael "Ray
bio: (New York City, NY: 1924-17 Feb 1999) Amateur magician since age 15 when taught by Raymond at a summer day camp. Aka "The Great Raphael" 1944-47. Major magic collector (books, magazines, catalogs, antique apparatus, coins & tokens) until 1989 when dispersed by sale & auction. Articles in Magicol, MUM, Mystics Quarterly, Perennial Mystics. [Wh2]

name: Elliot, Lieut.-Colonel. R[obert] H[enry]
bio: (Britain: -9 Nov 1936) Ophthalmic surgeon, serving in the Indian Medical Service and later the British Army in India. Amateur magician & prominent member of The Magic Circle, chairing its Occult Committee. Wrote The Myth of the Mystic East (1934, 301pp). [Daw#215]

name: Elliott
bio: See: Medici, Tiziano

name: Elliott, Bruce [Walter Gardner Lively Stacey]
bio: (New York City, NY: 30 May 1914-22 Mar 1973) Inspired watching Thurston show. Learned at age 9 from Mysto Magic set. Debut in early 1920s at tennis clubs. Freelance writer-editor in New York City by profession. Amateur magician. Assisted Annemann in editing Jinx until 1941. Demonstrator for Stuart Robson's magic shop. This convivial fat man edited The Phoenix 1942-54. Helped on many of his magic projects by his wife, "Bunny". before she separated. His home in Manhattan at 284 West 70th was a weekly gathering place for magi. Died in New York hospital of injuries after being hit by an automobile. Wrote 4 often reprinted books: Magic as a Hobby (1948, 240pp, with Foreword by Orson Welles), Classic Secrets of Magic (1953, 226pp), The Best in Magic (1956, 235pp; British ed as Magic: 100 New Tricks), & Professional Magic Made Easy (1959, 231pp). Editor of Volume 6 (1954, 409pp) of the revised edition of the famous Tarbell Course in Magic. Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, & New Phoenix. Under Walter Gibson's "Maxwell Grant" pen name wrote 15 of the last novels about The Shadow. [CA;Th]

name: Elliott, "Bunny
bio: (Kahose, New York: 10 Oct 1912 or 1913-13 Aug 1996) Born Rose Bedrick. Date & place of birth uncertain because of mother's questionable immigration status. Married Bruce Elliott (see), assisting him in his various projects, particularly in producing his Phoenix magazine. Being short (at 4'10") was in demand by local illusionists for testing box apparatus. Separated from Bruce and moved to California with daughter Judith. Died of stroke.

name: Elliott, Dr James William, MD
bio: (Rumford, Maine: 27 Apr 1874-28 Jan 1920) Learned at age 10 from amateur father. Retired as physician to be a top pro cardman. Toured as partner with former pupil Barney Ives in 1908. Invented the Spelling Trick (1910). Toured as "Bosco" with the Le Roy-Talma-Bosco troupe 1913-17. Died of diabetes. See Elliott's Last Legacy (1923, c300pp, compiled by Clinton Burgess, edited by Oscar Teale, & published by Harry Houdini). [Pr;Go2;Silver] Elliott, Lyle A. (Hamilton?, Ontario?, Canada: 1947-18 Apr 1980) Pro silent manip act plus silks, flowers, & salt in the 1970s, billed as "Fabulous Mr. Lyle".

name: Ellis, Jardine
bio: (Britain: c1881-1 Feb 1923) Stage name of Duncan Lorne Campbell. Pro street then stage magician. Played St. George's Hall in 1919. Invented the Jardine Ellis ring (1921) & the Glass of Wine Production. See Stanley Norton, A Few Jardine Ellis Secrets (1925). [Fi]

name: Ellis, Robert "Bob
bio: (USA: 1920-1984) Lawyer & politician in Huntington, West Virginia. Semi-pro magician. Invented Out to Lunch (1946, with Clare Cummings), Alive Box, Miser's Dream with Dollar Bills, & Vishnu Rope (by 1948). NOTE: Tarbell V.5 wrongly credits "Thimble Production" to Ellis. [LR9/85]

name: Ellis, [Timothy Ronald] "Tim
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 8 May 1963- ) Learned at age 10 from a "Hanky Panky" magic set. Winner of several magic awards since 1979. Producer-performer of many magic shows since 1980. Pro close-up, comedy, cabaret magician & illusionist & escapist since 1982. Founder-owner of Magic Unlimited in 1980. Bought Bernard's Magic Shop in Melbourne c1993. Partner-wife is Sue-Anne Webster (born in Sydney). 1991 FISM Special Prize of the Jury; 1994 FISM 2nd Prize in Close-up; 2001 FFFF MVP. Wrote The Secret Diary of Tim Ellis (1992), Ellis in Wonderland (2000, with Sue-Anne), etc. Publisher-editor Australian Magic Monthly 1989-1995, 2000. Articles in Magic Circular, Magic Makers, Genii, Aladdin, Innovator, MUM, Linking Ring. Invented Freddy Krueger Card Trick (1990) & Deckstress (1994). TV commercials & bits. Video (1995). [Genii3/89:Wh5:Wh01]

name: Ellison, Dr Saram R., MD
bio: (St. Thomas, Ontario, Canada: 17 [sic] Jan 1852-25 Mar 1918) Inspired as boy seeing travelling magician. Moved to USA. A Mason (33rd Degree) & physician in New York City. Author of a medical book on cocaine. Co-founded (with W.G. Mortimer & F. Martinka) the Society of American Magicians in 1902, with Ellison as Member #1. He coined its name. A pioneer amateur magic collector (including buying W.E. Robinson's original book collection. Had 600 titles by 1902. In 1908 its 2,000 items were offered for sale for $3,000 by Martinka's. The collection was acquired by Dr Samuel C. Hooker who gave it in 1936 to the New York Public Library. A bio sketch is Epes W. Sargent, Saram R. Ellison (1915, 12pp). [Magic4/02, 10/03, 10/08]

name: Elma
bio:
Elman, Ilina [or luna or Juna or Irène or Irena] (Libochovice, Czechoslovakia: 22 Mar 1935-) Pro assistant to husband Vlastimil Elman in their

[See also: Majcher, Eustachy]

name: Elman, Rudolf
bio: (Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 15 Feb 1912- ) Pro manipulator.

name: Elman, Vlastimil
bio: (Libochovice, Czechoslovakia: 10 [or 21] Jan 1924-) Joined the Prague Magic Circle in 1940. Ex-auto mechanic. Pro magician since 1954 with manipulation act with assistant-wife Ilina Elman as the "Duo Elmann". Played East Germany in 1964. [Win]

name: Elmo, Gene
bio: (San Lucido, Italy: 4 May 1914-2 Aug 1997) Stage name of Eugene Guglielmo since 1960. Moved to USA as boy in 1925. Inspired at age 12 seeing Black Herman & then reading Downs' The Art of Magic. Invented numerous tricks. Pro dealer-manufacturer (Elmo Magic Supreme) in Brooklyn, New York, 1975-ca1990, then as just "Gene Elmo" in New Port Richey, Florida. Best selling tricks: Test Tube Baby & Birth of a Dove. Pet effect: Needle Trick. Articles in HMM, Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, & Magic Info. [Wh2]

name: Elmo, Frank
bio: (USA: 25 Jun 1865-30 Jul 1935) Stage name of Frank Wolf.

name: Elmsley, Alex[ander]
bio: (St. Andrews, Scotland: 2 Mar 1929-8 Jan 2006) Took up magic in 1946. As student at Cambridge U was Secretary of the Pentacle Club and majored in physics & math. Patent agent turned computer expert. Amateur card & close-up magician, one of the top innovators in Great Britain. Major contributor to Faro mathematics. 1972 AMA Creative Fellowship. Invented Ghost Count = Elmsley Count in 1954, Between Your Palms, Point of Departure, Diamond Cut Diamond, Color Changing Faro Shuffle, Fate's Datebook, & Mouse Magic. Wrote Elmsley's 4 Card Trick (1967), Cardwork (1975). See Stephen Minch, The Collected Works of Alex Elmsley (Vol.1: 1991, 424pp; Vol.2: ..., 512pp). Tricks in Abra, Pentagram, Ibidem, Pallbearers, Epilogue, Chronicles, & Magic. 4 videos (1997). [L&L Presents#1]

name: El Neco, Hector
bio: See: Neco, Hector El

name: Eloise
bio: (USA: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro magicienne on vaude circuits by 1901 when she played the Boston Music Hall. [Mo]

name: El-Tab, Professor
bio: See: Battle, Alfred J.

name: EI-Wyn
bio:
Greystoke, R. Temple (used "EI-Wyn" in 1930)

[See also: Peck, Elwyn C.]

name: Emalo
bio: See: Loew, Emil

name: Emerson & Jayne
bio: (Britain: -1995) Stage name of Jack Emerson Skinner. With wife Joy worked as "Mr Emerson & Miss Jayne". Pro illusionists, best known for their version of the Flying Carpet, which they introduced in their ultra-violet act by 1964. Often play the Aladdin Xmas panto. Later sold their black-art act to the current "Emerson & Jayne". [Hudd]

name: Emerson, Arthur J. "Art", MIMC
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 17 Oct 1928- ) Learned in 1937 from a Gilbert magic set. Twenty years US Army until retired as Lieutenant Colonel in 1971. Teenage performer in USO show and burlesque. Amateur cardman. Met Larry West in 1966 to form Emerson and West in 1967 as inventors, manufacturers and wholesalers of 121 magic effects until 1997 when E&W was sold to Hampton Ridge Magic and then to Fun, Inc. Sold 500,000 copies of Color Monte. Favorite inventions: The Whole Thing and Pegasus Page. Wrote Tell-Tale Timepiece (1982, 44pp, with Larry West). MIMC 1988. Tricks in Swami & Mantra. First bio in MUM (Nov 1977).

name: Emerson, Dr. Frank
bio: (USA: fl.1890s) Minor pro touring with the Oregon Medicine Company, a medicine show. In Mahatma May 1900 was first to suggest use of the Jacob's Ladder to work the earlier Spirit Cloth apparatus.

name: Enardoe
bio:
(Scranton, Pennsylvania: 10 Nov 1914-16 Apr 1995) Movie writer, producer, director. Amateur card magician since age 12 or 13 when at a boys' summer camp he was taught sleight-of-hand magic by his counsellor, Roger Barkaan. After Yale became a theater director in New York City and Montreal. Moved in Sep 1940 to Hollywood where taught card tricks to Orson Welles in 1942. He traded teaching card tricks to Welles's business manager, Jack Moss, for an apprenticeship in their Mercury Company in 1942. Then directed eight short subjects (for M-G-M) and seven "B" features from 1942 to 1951. To promote his film Gentleman Joe Palooka (Monogram, 1946) he toured veteran's hospitals with an act of comedy song, & magic assisted by ingenue Marilyn Monroe. To escape an anti-Communist Congressional subpoena (Bill Woodfield points out that the first Mrs Endfield was a Marxist) he moved in 1951 to England. There he directed 14 movies, including the semi-classic Zulu in 1962, followed by Sands of the Kalahari (1965) and The Universal Soldier (1971), his last. Then retired. Magic figures prominently in three of his films: The Sound of Fury (1951), Tarzan's Savage Fury (1952), & The Limping Man (1953), and by passing reference in most others. See Lewis Ganson, Cy Endfield's Entertaining Card Magic (3 parts: [1955], 64pp; [1956], 54pp; [1958], 60pp; reprinted in one volume, Bideford, England: Supreme Magic, n.d.). Tricks in Phoenix, Sphinx, Gen, and Linking Ring. A bio is Jonathan Rosenbaum, "Pages from the Endfield File", Film Comment (Nov/Dec 1993), 48-55. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Enfield" and place of birth wasn't "South Africa" as widely published. His reported 1983 death was greatly exaggerated. [Katz;Wh5]

[See also: Drane, Edward O.]

name: Endor
bio: See: Batt, Christopher

name: Eng, Harry
bio: (c1940 – San Diego, CA: 29 Jun 2006) Died of a heart attack, former minister and teacher; self-taught magician; known for creating “impossible” objects (tennis balls, card cases, locks, books, footballs etc. inside glass bottles). See Magic Aug 1996, p. 35. Engblom, Christian [Turku, Finland: 3 Mar 1972- ) Pro close-up and card magic. Invented Antifaro (by 2001). Trick in Genii (2001). [Wh01]

name: Engelo
bio: (Poland: 1923-) Stage name of Kazimierz Edwin Czarny. Pro manipulator & illusionist in Poland.

name: Engin, Oguz
bio: (Turkey?: 28 Sep 19-) Manipulator. Deutsche Jugendmeisterschaft (Berlin) 1984 2nd prize in manip & 1985 1st prize in manip & declared Deutscher Jugendmeister; 1987 MZvD 1st prize in manip. [Nad] Engstrom, A. B. (USA: fl.1830s) Art teacher in Philadelphia. Amateur magician. Wrote The Humorous Magician Unmasked (1836, 90pp), a collection of parlor tricks "as exhibited by Monsieur Adrian and other performers".

name: Enoc, Roy
bio: (England: -died in WW I) Invented the Milk Pitcher (c1917) jointly with Louis Nikola.

name: Enochs, E[dward] Loyd
bio: (Britain: 1897-1968) Moved to USA as a young man. Maker of fine apparatus (marketed as "Loyd Magic") in Pasadena and later Modesto, California, 1930s-50s, which he sold thru Thayer's, etc. Conceived & built Tommy Martin's famous act. Wrote (as "Loyd") Loyd's Master Manipulation of Thimbles (1931; repr 1949, 37pp) & Producing Lighted Cigarettes (1936, 22pp). Article in Genii. [Genii4/67]

name: Enslen, Karl
bio: (Stuttgart, Germany: 1759-1848) Pro exhibitor of automata & other mechanical devices such as the Magic Lantern. As "Charles Enslen" played Paris in 1785 & London in 1786. [St]

name: Enslin dem Jüngern
bio: See: Arnold, Th. F. K.

name: Enson, Val
bio: See: Walker, Val

name: Ensor, Harrie [Francis]
bio: (Australia: 1901-21 May 1967) Pro until 1922 when turned semi-pro in Sydney. Aka "Herbert Holmes", which name he lent to Alf Briton's The Herbert Holmes Course in Magic & the fictitious "Herbert Holmes School of Magic". Major book collector. Memoirs series in The Imp 1945-49. [McC]

name: Enzfelder, Dagmar "Daggi
bio: (Graz, Austria: 14 Sep 1938- ) Language student. Pro assistant-wife since 1960 [sic] when married Oskar Enzfelder, learning from & working with him as "The New Houdinys". In their "New Houdinys" escape act, she does the escapes as "Miss Houdiny". [Win;Wh2]

name: Enzfelder, Oskar Joe "Ossi
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 19 Mar 1933- ) Learned in 1943 by lessons from Rolf Hansen & Alfred Kessler. Originally a jazz musician. Then pro illusionist & escapist since 1958. With assistant-wife Dagmar Enzfelder as "The New Houdinys" since 1960 they play circuses & revues throughout Europe. Since 1975 also works with 4 cheetahs & a dog. They have won the 1968 International Circus Oscar, 1968 Russian Circus Award, 1975 Kalanag Trophy, etc. Over 100 TV bits. [Win;Wh2]

name: Eperny, Charly
bio: (Pagny-sur-Moselle, France: 13 Mar 1897-9 Jul 1974) Stage name of Richard Robert Reinhold Karl Eichhorn, son of a German glassblower working in France. Pro stage manip & illusionist since his debut at age 16 at the Berlin Apollo theater in Feb 1914. Aka "Chiang Fu" when presenting his elaborate pseudo-Chinese act as "Chiang Fu & My Wong". Otherwise worked in dress coat. Toured Germany, Austria, Switzerland, & Italy. Moved to Vienna in 1948 with his assistant-wife Martha. Died in Vienna. Wrote several books in German, including Aus meinem Repertoire (1939, 56pp), Magische Feinheiten (1942, 104pp), Moderne Zauberei (1943, 88pp), Enzyclopädie der Mikromagie (2 parts, 1956, 1965-66), Dr. Stanley Jaks Buch (1961), Das grosse Stuller-Bosco Buch (1963), Wunder mit Riesenkarten (1965). [Win;St]

name: Epstein, Docteur Adam Salomon
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1827-1914) Polish Jew, the family name being Epsztain. Moved as youth to England where he learned magic. Pro apparatus magician since 1845. World tour 1848-53. Thence toured Russia (1855), England (1855, 1870), Germany (1860), France (1869 when he was slightly wounded doing the Bullet Catch at the Cirque Napoléon), Sweden (1876), Finland (1880 & 1897), Denmark (1902). Died in Switzerland shortly before WW I (& not as reported in Russia c1885). NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Eipstein". [Dif; Vo58; CI; Dam; St; Magic7/02]

name: Erdnase, S. W.
bio: (Hartford, Connecticut: 28 Nov 1872-6 Nov 1905) Pen name of Milton Franklin Andrews. Had an avoid amateur interest in magic since boyhood in New England. Pro card sharp since age 18, working throughout the USA & in Sydney, Australia. Died in San Francisco, a suicide (and murderer of his current mistress) to evade arrest on false charges of previous murders. Invented diagonal palm shift, longitudinal shift, & S.W.E. Shift (all by 1902). First person reported using close-up pad (winter of 1901-02) & possibly its inventor. Wrote (with major help, particularly on patter, from James S. "Harto" Harte on the "Card Tricks" section) Artifice Ruse and Subterfuge at the Card Table (1902, 205pp), better known by its cover-title of The Expert at the Card Table. Probably edited for language by William Hilliar. This classic book (never out-of-print) on card sharping sleights had a profound influence on many card sharps and most leading card conjurors (including Jack Merlin, Vernon, Charlie Miller, LePaul, Farelli, Daley, & Braue), causing them to rethink & expand much of their sleight-of-hand repertoire. Its only translation is the Spanish El Experto en la Mesa de Juego (Madrid: 1988). Bio is Bart Whaley with Martin Gardner & Jeff Busby, The Man Who Was Erdnase (1991, 448pp). See also Dai Vernon, Revelations (1984, 224pp); & Darwin Ortiz, The Annotated Erdnase (1991, 270pp). NOTE: Often misidentified as "Edward S. Andrews" & "James Andrews". [Bo2;Bo3;Bo#231;Dif]

name: Erens, Oliver, MD
bio: (Heidelberg, Germany: 2 Feb 1967-) Learned in 1977 from magic set. Physician. Amateur card magician specializing in Triumph effects. Collector. Aka "The Fox". MZvD Magic Writer of the Year 1995/96. Wrote Inside CardMagic (3 vols, 1995, 1996, 1997, 112+222+108pp), Concertos for Pasteboard (Engl. tr by Erens of his CardMagic Vol.1 (2001, 234pp), and Zaubereien und Tricks mit Karten (1998, 80pp). Tricks in Magische Welt, Magie, & Genii. Translator of English tricks & articles. [Wh5;Wh01

name: Ergatoudis, John [George]
bio: (Limassol, Cyprus: 3 Jul 1941-23 Dec 2004) Learned around age 10 buying tricks & from books. University lecturer in Leeds, England. Magic collector since 1962 with nearly 6,000 books, several thousand magazines, & many wood and metal props. Also has thousands of mechanical puzzles. [Wh5]

name: Ericson, Eric "Jolly
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 18 Oct 1924-) Learned magic at age 10 in Stockholm. Moved to Malmö in 1936. Semi-pro in early 1940s until military service, then full-time pro. IBM member since 1946. Edited Trollkarlen in 1952. Magic dealer in Malmö (importer of USA tricks) in early 1950s. In 1955 became travelling salesman to opticians, retiring in 1982. [St;Wh5]

name: Ericsson, Carl-Johan
bio: (Arvika, Värmland, Sweden: 27 Jan 1936-) Learned at age 15 from library book. Teacher of Greek & Latin. Semi-pro mentalist since 1959 as "Ernest A. Dusenberg". Pet effects: Bloch's Perfect Time & other predictions. Articles in Tricks (Sweden). 1986 Swedish 1st prize in close-up. [Wh2] (Britain: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Eric Ferguson. Pro manipulator with a pseudo-drunk Cardini-type act with cards, thimbles, & billiard Erikson balls. Played Australia in 1937 (while a teenager) & 1948. [Wal]

name: Eriksson, Hilding
bio: (Norway: 31 May 1916- ) Semi-pro as "Adanos" until 1946, thence as "Eric Hildini". Editor of Magiens Verden since 1946. President of the Norwegian Magic Circle 1949-51. 1978 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. [St]

name: Eriksson, John Erik
bio: (Sweden: 18 May 1911-) Engineer in Borås, Sweden. Semi-pro as "Mr John".

name: Ernst, Professor
bio: (Magdeburg, Germany: 19 Jun 1810-18 Mar 1860) Stage name of Carl Ehrhardt. Died in Magdeburg. [Roh]

name: Ernst, Bernard M[orris Lee]
bio: (Uniontown, Alabama: 17 Mar 1879-28 Nov 1938) Jew. Lawyer & amateur magician. Collector. Houdini's lawyer (by 1922 to Houdini's death). SAM President 1926-27. Wrote (with Hereward Carrington) Houdini and Conan Doyle (1932, 255pp). [Go2; WWWA]

name: Ervin, Dr. E[dward] G.
bio: (Dubuque, Iowa: 18 Aug 1875-7 Jan 1947) Dentist in Kansas City, Missouri. Amateur magician. Dealer (secretly). Invented Spring Bills (by 1944). Wrote 4 booklets 1937-44, collected as Club Deceptions (1944, 52pp). See Dariel Fitzkee, The Strange Inventions of Dr. Ervin (1937). Tricks in Jinx. [Th;WWM]

name: Escamo
bio: (Britain: c1867-13 Dec 1902) Stage name of Charles Waldon. Pro magician. Esler, James A. (Carrickfergus, N. Ireland: 29 Mar 1884-12 Jan 1967) Author under pen name of "Day & Levani" of Conjuring Apparatus Up-to-Date (1912).

name: Estes. Donald
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: fl.1940s-50s) Inspired & learned from age 6 from neighbor Harry Willard. Pro with own ghost show as "Don Brandon" 1947-52. Then with a full-evening show. [Walk2]

name: Estes, Paul W [ellington]
bio: (Lincoln, Nebraska: 13 Jul 1944-) Inspired by uncle's sleight-of-hand. Moved to Phoenix, Arizona, in 1956. Learned at age 13 from mentors Bert Easley & Don Seth. Semi-pro magician since age 17 playing club dates in Arizona & West Coast 1961-69. Scenic & lighting designer in Phoenix since 1970. Teacher of magic to kids in local Rabbits In Our Hat Magic Club, as Director 1975-present. Edited Gimmick (Phoenix) 1975-78 (72 issues). Articles in Gimmick & Lota. [Wh2]

name: Eston
bio: (Magdeburg, Germany [sic]: 4 Jan 1900-) Stage name of Edwin Kramer. Pro quick-tempo comedy magic act titled "Express-Magie" with assistant-wife Lora Eston. Worked mainly in Germany but toured Europe, including Finland (1952). After WW II added parrots to act. [St;Al;Roh]

name: Eswin, Eric
bio: (Batavia [now Djakarta], Dutch East Indies [now Indonesia]: 5 Oct 1941- ) Stage name of Eric Eswin Warlicht since c1984. Learned magic in 1962. Psychologist (officer in Royal Netherlands Army). Semi-pro magician since 1980 when won the Dutch magic championship. President of Dutch Magical Union 1984-present. President of FISM 1985-88. Articles in Hocus, Genii, Magic Manuscript, & Ilusionismo. Invented Electrical Paradox (the Chinese Sticks using lamp bulbs). [Wh2]

name: Etherington, Graham [Richard]
bio: (Ealing, England: 29 Mar 1938-) Learned at age 8 from mother's gift of second-hand magic set. Moved to Australia in 1951. Paid debut at age 16. Telecommunications technician-executive. Semi-pro magician as "Ricardo the Magician" since 1958 & "Ricky the Clown" since 1960, specialized in cabaret & childrens magic. President, Australian Society of Magicians, 1973-76, 1979-present. Partner (with Barry Govan) in Abracadabra Promotions, which promotes trade & show & TV products 1985-present. Articles in Trestle Board, Blueprint, Magic Makers, & Genii. [Genii3/89;Wh2]

name: Eudel, Dr François
bio: (France: fl.1950s-70s) Amateur in Paris. Charter member of the Réunions d'Études Magiques in 1951. Articles in Magicien.

name: Eugén
bio: (Sweden: 3 Nov 1904-7 Jun 1963) Stage name of H.E. Hansson. Pro debut at age 18 with magic, mentalism, & hypnotism with assistant-wife. Worked various circuits. [St]

name: Evanion, Henry
bio: (Kennington, England: 1 Jan 1832-17 [sic] Jun 1905) Born Henry Evans. Minor pro since 1849 as "Mr. Evans" (1849), "Evan Ion" (1857), & finally, after legal name change, as Henry Evanion since 1858. Played the British provinces, Paris (1865), & London (the Crystal Palace in 1877 & 1879). Collector of magicians playbills (including the Savren Collection), which he sold off to the British Museum in 1895, Mr Kornmann (London bookseller & amateur magician), & Houdini (in 1904-05). Died in London of throat cancer. Bio in James Hagy, Early English Conjuring Collectors: James Savren and Henry Evanion (1985, 141pp). [Daw#205;Pr;Hou;Cl]

name: Evans, Celeste
bio: (White Rock, British Columbia, Canada: fl.1950s-90s) Stage name of Ruth Evans. Inspired to become a magician as child seeing Alan Lambie show. Learned from books. Taught sleight of hand by Jon Kirby. Debut in early teens. Miss Canada. Pro, first with travelling tent show, then club dates. Excellent dove act. Toured Asia & Europe (4 times). Toured the Congo with UN troops in 1961. Married her manager Harry Breyn in 1962 when moved to Chicago where later left magic to become a booking agent (Breyn Management), which she took over after his death. [Se;MUM1/98;Tay]

name: Evans, Fred W[alker]
bio: (Jersey City, New Jersey: 28 Feb 1943- ) FBI Special Agent. Amateur magician since 1958 and magic collector (periodicals, bibliographies, books) since 1975. Editor-publisher Collectors' Forum 1991-1995. [Wh5]

name: Evans, Gerritt M.
bio: See: Grandin, Edward M.

name: Evans, Dr Henry Ridgely, LL.D.
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 7 Nov 1861-29 Mar 1949) Inspired as child seeing Albert Niblack. Learned in 1876-77 reading Cremer's The Secret Out & Hoffmann's series in Every Boy's Annual. Journalist, then in U.S. Department of Agriculture 1894-1934. Amateur magician, specializing in history of magic. Wrote Hours with the Ghosts; or, XIX Century Witchcraft (1897, 302pp; reprinted 1902 as The Spirit World Unmasked), Magic and Its Professors (1902, 220pp), The Old and the New Magic (1906, 348pp; 2nd ed 1909, 516pp), Adventures in Magic (1924, 87pp), The History of Conjuring and Magic (1928, 235pp), Cagliostro (1931, 83pp), A Master of Modern Magic (1932, 58pp), Some Rare Old Books on Conjuring and Magic (1943, 21pp), etc. USA correspondent for Magic. Also articles under pen name "Mysticus". As a 33rd Degree Mason he wrote several masonic tracts & Magicians and Freemasonry (n.d., 28 unnumbered pages). [LR5/49; Tops9/37; Th; SAM]

name: Evans, Val[entine B.]
bio: (USA: 1896-3 Feb 1981) Inspired around age 9. Pro cardman. Invented "Val Evans Rising Cards" & "Optegramma" = Chinese Compass (1945). Wrote Patter, Gags and Bits of Business for Magicians (26pp); Stacks and Stacks of Cards (1941, 35pp). Tricks in Jinx. Lived in Peabody, Massachusetts. [Th]

name: Evanson, Jeff
bio: (Toronto, Canada: 17 Aug 1959- ) Pro with second-sight mentalism with Tessa Evanson (born London, England, 26 Feb 1962) as "The Evansons". 1997 PEA Dunninger Award & 1999 World Magic Seminar Sarmoti Award. Tricks in Magick & Vibrations. [Wh01]

name: Eveline
bio: See: "Magdola"

name: Eve'n Alan
bio: See: Vejr, Alan

name: Even, Horst [Dieter]
bio: (Germany: 21 Jul 1934-) Magician & dealer ("Magic by Les Evens") in Dudweiler, Germany, in 1980s-90s. [Nad]

name: Evens, Les
bio: See: Even, Horst

name: Everett, M. H[udson]
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1930s) An American black. A "skilful magician" according to H.R. Evans. Pro assistant to Bancroft (until 1897) and then as "Boomskie" to both Leon Herrmann (1898) & Adelaide Herrmann (1900). When he confessed to stealing some of her diamond rings, she had him jailed. While still in jail in Dec 1900 he exposed some of Adelaide's tricks in 3 USA newspapers. Evidently all was forgiven because he attended her funeral in 1932. [Magic4/01, p61 & 12/01, p21; Pr]

name: Everhart, Frank
bio: (Pennsylvania, USA: 10 Sep 1921-31 Jul 2004) Pro bartender-magician at the Ivanhoe restaurant in Chicago in 1950-71. Often credited as inventor of the Chicago Opener card effect. Noted for his "Sam the Bellman" card routine. Mentor of Max Howard. Retired. Moved to Key West in 1998. His son, Frank Everhart Jr (born c1973), is also a bartender-magician.

name: Evil, Dr.
bio: See: "Morris, Philip"

name: Faber, Harry
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-80s) Pro vaude magus in early 1920s teamed with Sam Berland as "The Faberlands". Invented "The Peculiar Pencil" = Topsy Turvy Pencil by 1924. In 1925 co-founded (with Sam Berland & Joe Berg) The Princess Novelty Shop in Chicago but almost immediately pulled out. [Berg,29,30] "Faberlands, The" SEE: Faber, Harry & Berland, Sam

name: Fabian
bio: (Britain: 1912-8 Dec 1965) Pen name of Ernest Raymond "Ray" Griffiths. Literary & Technical Editor of Abracadabra 1946 until death. Wrote T.N.T.: Twelve New Tricks (1946; repr 1968, 52pp), Burtini's Cups & Balls Routine (1946, 18pp) & Burtini's Linking Rings Routine (1947, 16pp). [Genii1/66]

name: Fabian, Prof. J. C. "Fabe
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Photographer. Semi-pro magician. Wholesale dealer & demonstrator as owner of Fabian Enterprises in Chicago. Bought Sam Berland's shop in 1954. Famous in 1954 for his stay-lit Pixie Cigarettes.

name: Fabian, Peter
bio: See: Schuster, Peter

name: Fabjance, John
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-80s) Former assistant to Blackstone. Pro dealer (Fabjance Studios) in St. Louis, Missouri (where managed by Ken Summers), and then Bethalto, Illinois, where he edited Legerdemain 1977-81 (41 issues) as house organ. Specialized in miniaturized illusions.

name: Facitos, Los
bio: See: Hansen, Leif Rosengaard

name: Fackler, Harold E.
bio: See: "Sterling, Harold"

name: Faggi, Carlo
bio: (Milan, Italy: 2 May 1946- ) Taught rudiments of magic in 1952 by his hobbyist father. Pro performer & dealer as "Fax il Mago". Wrote Stupire (1985, 800pp). 1988 Guinness book record for straitjacket escape. [Wh5]

name: Fagin, Tom
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s) Pro card man. Played St. George's Hall in 1925.

name: Fah, Freddy
bio: (France: fl.1930s-50s) Stage name of Robert Woolley, aka "Crackbanger". Taught by De Bischop. Pro. Pet effects: silk magic, Chinese Sticks, & balloons. Played the Chicago Hilton in 1959. [Dif]

name: Fakir Kronblom
bio:
"Fakir of Ava" SEE: Hughes, Isaiah Harris Marshall, William "Fakir of Blackwells" SEE: Hagen, Charles J. "Fakir of Ispahan" SEE: Taylor, Prof. E. Cooper "Fakir of Oolu" SEE: Sylvester, Alfred "Fakir of Vishnu" SEE: Robinson

[See also: Hedengren, Nils]

name: Falanga, Louis [L.] "Lou
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 24 Jul 1955- ) Learned at age c8 when uncle taught some tricks. Moved c1973 to Lake Tahoe area where he trains ski-lift operators. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 25. Pet effect: Stack of Quarters. Long-time friend & student of Larry Jennings. Co-publisher (with successively Larry Jennings, Bruce Cervon, & alone) of "L&L Publishing" 1986-present. See Mike Maxwell, Lake Tahoe Card Magic (1985, 88pp). Articles in Apocalypse, Magic Manuscript, & Genii. [Lo2;Wh2] Falck of Königsberg (Germany: fl.1830s) Pro. Claimed to be a student of Pinetti. Played London in 1835 with the Inexhaustible Bottle, etc. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Falk" by Clarke. [Hou,182-184;Cl]

name: Falconi, Signior
bio: (Italy: fl.1780s-1810s) Pro. Played Mexico City (1786), New York City (1787), Baltimore (1787), Boston (1796), & New York City (1816). [LR7/2004;Ch;Mo] "Falk of Konigsberge" [misspelling] SEE: Falck of Königssberg

name: Falk, Georg [Emil]
bio: (Meissen/Elbe, Germany: 17 Aug 1909-5 Oct 1985) Dealer in Meissen, East Germany, for some years prior to his death in that city when the business went to Peter Falk. [Roh]

name: Falkenstein, Glenn
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 3 Feb 1932 – 4 $ ^{th} $ July 2010) Inspired by seeing magicians work at father's nightclub. At age 15 got job demming at Abbott's magic shop. Speech therapist in Los Angeles. Semi-pro mentalist. 1972 AMA Best Stage Performer. Since 1978 works a double mind-reading & spirit cabinet act with Frances Willard, whom he married in 1984. Video (1989, with Frances). 1990 Dragon Award (with Frances); 1991 Dunninger Award (with Frances); 1994 SAM Hall of Fame (with Frances); 1996 AMA Stage Magician of the Year (with Frances). [Mag;HC]

name: Faluggi
bio: (Argentina: fl.1920s) Minor pro, working the provinces with a show of card work of the old school & other small tricks.
