His one attempt at a full illusion show copied from Dante in Buenos Aires in 1927 flopped. Father of Polo (see). [Bam, pp132-133] [Sothin], 70 Jose [pronounced fah-MAH-dahs] (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: 10 Apr 1908-9 Jul 1991) Inspired around age 8 seeing Sidney Richards' show. Linguist, translator, & journalist. Amateur magician since 1916. Used stage name "Professor Colmar" in 1930s. Founder & Secretary of Sociedade Brasileira de Magia, 1930-41, the first magic society in Latin America. Moved to USA in 1941, living in New York City. Co-founded Magic Collectors' Association 1950. Had large collection of magicana, particularly magazines in many languages. Articles in Sphinx, Linking Ring, Magical Bookie, Magicol, Spellbinder (USA), Le Prestidigitateur, Magie, Hade-e-Gram, Magikeren, Cigam, Malayan Magician, C.E.D.A.M., O Tacape Mágico, etc. [LR11/34;WWEast;Wh2;WWM]

name: Fane, Blanche
bio: See: "Anderson, Jennie"

name: Fanta, Otto
bio: (Germany?: 1882-1959) Stage name of Otto Knippstein. Pro billiard-ball manip & card, flower, & silk magic.

name: Fantame
bio: See: "Carbel"

name: Fantas, Paulo
bio:
Fantasio, Ricardo [pronounced fahn-TAH-zee-oh] (Buenos Aires, Argentina: 3 Oct 1936-) Stage name of Ricardo Roucau since 1961. Learned in 1943 from a magic set. Pro performer since 1957, working cabaret, stage, & manip, initially as "Ricardo", then "Larry". Moved to USA in 1961, becoming "Fantasio". Works internationally, sometimes with wife Monica (born Margarita) as assistant, playing the Ed Sullivan Show (5 times), Latin Quarter, Radio City Music Hall (1969), Desert Inn, Hollywood Palace, etc. Toured Latin America 1974-76. Famous since 1967 for his line of coiled plastic-sheet props, beginning with the Fantasio Cane, which he now manufactures in Coral Gables, Florida. Many awards, including 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. 1991 SAM Hall of Fame. Recently added a comedy magic act as "Señor Funtasio". 1995 Dragon Award for Fantasio & Monica. Father of "Jackie Fantasio". Invented over 150 effects. Wrote Magic with Canes (1979, 70pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript, Linking Ring, Genii, MUM, Magic Info, & Journal de la Prestidigitation. 2 videos (2nd in 1988). Wrote Magic with Canes & Candles (1990, 94pp). See also David Ginn, Fantasio Book (6 vols, 1971-1982). Video (1989). TV bits. [LR6/96;Magic6/95;MUM1/92;NT8/66;Wh2]

[See also: Bessemans, Paul]

name: Fantasio, Jackie
bio: (New York City, NY: 9 Nov 1964-) Stage name of Jacqueline Roucau (now Mrs Santiago Alcade). Inspired by & learned from pro father Ricardo "Fantasio" Roucau. As one of his assistants, she toured 3 years throughout Latin America 1974-76. "Fanto the Magician" SEE: Olkowski, Frank SEE: Schröder, Margarete

name: Fara
bio: (Kiel, Germany: 19 Jun 1901-19 Dec 1989) Amateur. Aka "Bobby Maybach". Created the award of the Hofzinser Ring in 1932 in Vienna, which he gave to Ottokar Fischer. Died in Nürnberg. [Nad;Roh]

name: Farchmin, Robert
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Purser with French overseas airlines. Amateur magician. Wrote Card Tricks, French Style (1977, 41pp).

name: Farelli, Victor
bio: (Dublin, Ireland: 22 Dec 1888-12 May 1955) Stage name of Victor Michael Farrelly [sic]. His parents were Scots. Learned as student of David Devant. Expert pro cardman & close-up magician. Probably invented the close-up case (years before 1939). Retired in 1939. Translated Odin's Les Anneaux Chinois as The Odin Rings (1931, 68pp). Wrote The Master Speller (1930), Farelli's Card Magic (2 vols, 1933; 3rd ed 1934, 54pp) with French tr by Gaultier as La Magie des cartes (2 vols, 1937); Convincing Coin Magic (1946, 91pp); Thanks to Leipzig! (1948, 53pp); 3 booklets on routines of John Ramsay (see); & Magical Bibliographies: A Guide (1953, 28pp). Tricks in HMM. NOTE: Real surname has been misspelled "Farelly" & year of birth misgiven as "1898". [St]

name: Farinaccia, Ivo
bio: (Pescara, Italy: 23 Jan 1964-) Learned in 1975 reading a magic magazine. Pro since 1980. Dealer. Inventor & improver. Tricks in Magia Moderna, II Prestigiatore Moderno, & Qui Magia. [Wh5]

name: Farmer, Robert [Arthur J.] "Bob
bio: (Smith Falls, Ontario, Canada: 11 Sep 1948-) Learned at age 5 when mother taught him a card trick & father a rope trick. Lawyer, screenwriter, & film producer. Highly inventive amateur magician, specializing in cards, close-up, & mentalism. Wrote Tsunami (1988, 20pp), Deja VooDoo (1989, 18pp), Headhunter (1989, 12pp), & Beat 'em, Cheat 'em, Leave 'em Bleedin' (1994, 40pp). Articles in Hade-e-Gram, Linking Ring, Pabular, Epoptica, Genii, Magic, etc. [Lo;Lo2;Wh2]

name: Farradini
bio: (Denmark: 1886-) Stage name of A. Ramholt. Pro.

name: Fartun
bio: See: Huber, Harry

name: Fasola, Gustave
bio: (Britain: c1870-14 Jan 1929) Stage name of Fergus Greenwood. Minor pro illusionist by 1902, working in Hindu costume. Visited Thurston in USA in 1909 when the two jointly invented the Lady and the Lion illusion. Toured Australia (1911), New Zealand (1912), India, South Africa, Egypt, Palestine, Turkey, Italy, Spain. First hit the big-time by playing the Coliseum in London in 1919. Toured the Continent (including the Lisbon Coliseum in 1922), South America (1921), & USA (1924-28). Invented the Appearing Elephant (late 1920s). [Pr;Wal;Vo56;Magic7/11]

name: Fassman
bio: (Spain: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of José Mir Rocafort. Popular pro 1-man mental & hyp act. Toured Portugal in 1946 & 1947, Mexico in 1955. [HMM4/55,12/59;Bam,pp.245-6]

name: Faster, Willi
bio: (Strassburg, Germany: 4 Jul 1896-29 Apr 1973) Amateur magician, specialized in close-up, salon magic, & illusions. Aka "Reigamrebored". Magic teacher. Joined the German Magic Circle (MZvD) in 1931. Organized the 1936 International Magic Congress in Munich. MZvD President 1958-69 & thence its Honorary President. Mayor of Triberg for several years until retired in Offenburg/Baden. NOTE: Given name often misspelled "Willy". [Bou;Rob1]

name: Faure-Nicolay
bio: (near Marseille, France: fl.1860s-70s) Pro stage magician. Performed for French emperor Napoleon III at Châlons in 1869. Played the Teatro Trindada in Lisbon in 1871. [Dif]

name: Faust
bio: (Germany: c1480-1536 or 1539) The real Georg Faust, a German astrologer & practitioner of witchcraft, became legend in 1587 when Johann Spiess's Historia von Dr Johann Fausten first mingled fact with reports of earlier wonder-workers to add the pact with Mephistopheles. The legend was further dramatized & popularized by many writers, notably Marlowe in his 1589 stage adaption of Spiess as The Tragical History of Dr. Faustus; by Johann Nikolaus Pfizer in his 1674 version, which added the element of Faust's love for a poor girl; by Goethe in his drama Faust (1831); Gounod in his opera Faust (1859); and Thomas Mann in his novel Faust (1948). Faust This legendary figure proved a natural model for several modern conjurers who took the name. Others conjure the image in their advertising posters, as with the Devil's imps who whisper in the ears of Kellar & Raymond. And Orson Welles' 1937 stage adaptation of Marlowe's play as Doctor Faustus added such trickwork as a Black Light stage. See R. Petsch, Faustsage und Faustdichtung (1966). (Denmark: fl.1900s-1910s) Stage name of Christian Lind-Hansen. Lived in Helsinki, Finland, where he opened a magic shop. Taught Eric Arppe. In 1910 published his Det tjungonde arhundradets trollerikonst [Twenty Centuries of Magic] (Helsinki: 1910, in Swedish; and simultaneously in Finnish as Kahdennenkymmenennen vuosisadan taikatemput) [St] "Faust the Magician" SEE: Taylor, Granville

name: Faust, Dr.
bio: See: Hoy, David

name: Faust, Robert "Bob
bio: (USA: 1929-) Stage name of Robert James. Learned assisting Virgil. [Wat]

name: Faustino
bio: (Metz, France: 27 May 1892- ) Stage name of Maurice Chevallier. Pro magician & juggler, specializing in Japanese feats. Inventor of tricks. Joined the ASAP in 1921. Collector of magic books, photos, lithos, & magazines. Articles in Monde Occulte, Boletim Magico, & Passez-Muscade. [Rob1;WWM]

name: Faustinus
bio: (Fredensborg, Denmark: 1868-1946) Moved to Copenhagen where he became interested in magic and spiritualism. Pro magician & anti-spiritualist. Toured Germany & Scandinavia. In 1914 co-founded (with Dr Alfred Lehmann) an institute for psychic research in Copenhagen. [St]

name: Fausto
bio: (Figueira da Foz, Portugal: 5 Mar 1914-) Stage name of Fausto CANICEIRO DA COSTA. Amateur & prime mover behind magic shows in Portugal. Bio is 50 Anos de Ilusionismo e não só (1984, 120pp; 2nd ed 1985). [Cam]

name: Fawkes [also Faux & Fawks], Isaac
bio: (Britain: c1675-25 May 1731) Learned reportedly from another itinerant magician in Britain. Pro performer at English fairs, c1720-1731. Exhibited automata with Pinchbeck. Bio sketch is Edwin A. Dawes, Isaac Fawkes: Fame and Fable (1979, 8pp). [Daw;Daw#226;Hou;Fr] Fawkes the Younger (Britain: fl.1730s-40s) Learned as apprentice to father Isaac Fawkes. Pro on own from 1731 to as late as 1746.

name: Fax il Mago
bio: See: Faggi, Carlo

name: Fay
bio: (Karlsburg, Germany: 11 Mar 1854-) Stage name of Berta [not "Bertha"] Müller. Pro anti-spiritualist & sleight-of-hand magicienne. [Sal]

name: Fay, Anna Eva
bio: (Southington, Ohio: c1851-20 May 1927) Born Anna Eva Heathman. Aka "Annie Fay" & "Annie Eva Fay". Married Henry Melville Fay, working a top-line pro pseudo-psychic two-person mind-reading act from 1874. Married David H. Pingree in 1881. Contrary to some historians, it was not until after the turn of the century that she introduced Nevil Maskelyne's Dancing Handkerchief into her act. Elected first Honorary Lady Associate of The Magic Circle in 1913. Retired in 1924. [Pr]

name: Fay, Mrs. Eva
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: c1872-15 Sep 1931) Daughter-in-law of Anna Eva Fay. Stage name of Anna Fay, née Norman. Married John T. Fay in 1898, working a pseudo-psychic two-person mind-reading stage act as "The Fays". After husband's death in 1908, she went solo as a vaudeville psychic star, billed as "The High Priestess of Mysticism". Married to Harry Mylett 1910-24. [Pr]

name: Fay, Frank
bio: See: Csuri, Frank F[ay]

name: Fay, John Truesdell
bio: (Akron, Ohio: 1877-21 Dec 1908) Only son of Anna Eva Fay & Colonel Melville Fay. Learned from mother. Married Anna Norman ("Eva Fay") in 1898, working a pseudo-psychic two-person mind-reading act as "The Fays" & "The Marvelous Fays". Committed suicide.

name: Fay, "Colonel" [Henry Cummings] Melville
bio: (USA: fl.1870s) Pro pseudo-psychic. Married Anna Eva Heathman with whom he worked a successful two-person mind-reading act.

name: Fay, William Marion "Bill
bio: (USA: 1839-16 Jul 1921) Of German parentage. Pro pseudo-psychic medium in Buffalo, New York. Senior assistant with the Davenport Bros until 1873 when he teamed with Kellar until 1875 when he returned to the Davenports. Moved in 1876 to Australia. An attempted comeback in USA with Ira Davenport in 1896 failed. Died in Melbourne. [Pr;Cl;Ch;Wal]

name: Fayne, Charles "Chuck
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 1940- ) Has a PhD in music. A student of Vernon. Pro close-up & stage. 1988 AMA Best Lecturer. Article in LR. [Mag] "Fays, The" SEE: Fay, Eva & Fay, John T.

name: Feates, Bomelio
bio: (England: fl.early 1600s) A tinker by trade. Semi-pro magician. [CI]

name: Féaudiérre, Maurice
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Journalist in Paris. Historian of the circus & French radio-TV. Magician & ventriloquist. AFAP Master Magician. Wrote (as "Serge") La Route des Cirques (1945). Article in Journal de la Prestidigitation (1953). [Bou]

name: Feben, Hal
bio: (England: -1957) Pro. Living in Portsmouth when co-edited (with Len Hughes) Top Hat since 1950.

name: Fechner, Christian
bio: (Agen, Lot et Garonne, France: 25 Jul 1944 – Paris: 26 Nov 2008) Professional film producer in France since c1975, producing 34 films including Camille ClaudeI (1989). Learned magic at age 12 from "Kle-ro", a side-show fair magician. Semi-pro illusionist since age 17, including some time with circus. 1979 AFAP Bronze Medal. 1979 FISM 1st prize in grand illusions (using his own Bar Stool Levitation) & 1st prize in invention (Vanishing TV). Since then he has performed on stage only 4 times, preferring to invent & produce magic. 1981 AMA Award of Merit. A major magic collector with 5,000 books (2,000+ in French), 500 posters, props, & automata -- all displayed in his castle in Bordeaux. Prolific inventor of illusions. In 1981 invented the famous version of the Floating Piano that he gave to Norm Nielsen in 1982. Wrote Soirées Fantastiques (2 vols, 1988). A bio sketch by Amy Stevens is in the Winter 1990/91 Stevens catalog. NOTE: Ads for the Gamolo Levitation that used a photo of Fechner doing his Bar Stool Levitation falsely imply that these two effects & methods are the same. [Mad Magic #29]

name: Fechter, [Edwin J.] "Eddie
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 16 Feb 1916-31 Mar 1979) Learned as small boy in his father's tavern. Pro bartender-magician by 1945 around Buffalo. Had own bar c1956 to 1958 when he & wife Evelyn bought the Forks Hotel in nearby Cheektowaga, which thence was a major venue for magicians. Founded the FFFF in 1971. A teacher of Derek Dingle, Brian Gillis, Harry Harrison (late 1970s), Bob King, etc. See Jerry Mentzer, Eddie Fechter's Dice Holdout Methods for Magicians (1974, 64pp); Jerry Mentzer, Magician Nitely: The Magic of Eddie Fechter (1974, 148pp); Ray Mertz, Eddie Fechter Lecture Notes; & Jerry Mentzer, The Magic of Eddie Fechter (1993, 250pp).

name: Fedko, John [Theodore], AIMC
bio: (Northampton, Pennsylvania: 2 Feb 1929-) Learned magic in 1939 from Ukrainian-born ex-pro magician grandfather John Osychka. Inspired seeing Blackstone. Engineer by profession. A Chavez graduate. Semi-pro magician since 1947 with silent close-up card, coin, & ball manip. US Army officer 1951-71. Magic teacher. Semi-pro mail-order dealer (Fedko Magic Company) in Camp Hill, Penn., until 1977 when moved it to Santa Ana, Calif. Wrote Magic Classics, The Joe Cossari Card Act (1978, 27pp), How to Make a Card Castle (1979, 8pp), The Magic of John Fedko (1983, 311pp, edited by Nick Merlo), & Magic Treasures (1996, 168pp, edited by Tom Clifford). Tricks in Genii, MUM, Tops, Magick, & Qui Magica. 7 videos. [MUM11/76;Mag;Wh5]

name: Feinman, Jeffrey
bio: (USA: c1944-) Learned at age 11. Amateur comedy & card magician in New York City. Wrote The Catalogue of Magic (1978, 159pp).

name: Feldman, Irv[ing]
bio: See: "Fields, Eddie"

name: Felix, Uncle
bio:
(Berlin, Germany: 14 Oct 1877-15 Aug 1965) Died in Banzkow. [Roh]

[See also: Smith, Charles Neil]

name: Felsman, [Arthur P.] "Art
bio: (USA: 3 Nov 1888-2 Apr 1964) Comedy magic act in teens with brother Carl as "Felsman & Arthur". Dealer ("Felsman Magic Store") in Chicago (having bought out Roterberg's shop) 1916-1924. Edited Felsman's Magical Review 1919-23. In 1930s ran the second travelling magic shop in the USA (One-Arm McDonald's was first.) In 1941 co-owned (with Harry Blackstone) the short-lived "Blackstone Magic Shop" in Oak Park, Illinois. [Dor;Berg,50]

name: Felsman, Carl
bio: (USA: fl.1900s-20s) Pro debut in teens with brother Art as "Felsman & Arthur". Then pro manip on own.

name: Fenichel, [Joseph] "Joe
bio: (USA: ca1910-2005) Mail-order magic dealer-manufacturer in Brooklyn, New York, in 1960s-70s. Possibly invented the Acrobatic Card (by 1968).

name: Fenner, C. Foster "Charlie
bio: (USA: 1887-23 Jan 1967) Pro vaude magic until the 1920s when he worked mainly smaller venues in New England billed as "The Prince of Magicians". In last years published-edited El-Pro-Per 1958-67, the quarterly of his "C. Foster Fenner Junior League Magic Group" in Cranston, Rhode Island. Many articles in other magic magazines. [MUM12/93]

name: Fenton, Robert "Bobby
bio: (Seattle, Washington: 1921-1980s) Learned at age 8 from a gift magic set. Toured as assistant to Virgil in 1941. In 1942 replaced Jerry Bergman on Major Bowes tour. In US Army (101st Airborne) 1943-44 until wounded in the Battle of the Bulge. Pro assistant with Card Mondor's "Living Nightmares" spook show, then with Virgil's world tour 1952-56. Assistant with Mark Wilson's AllaKazam TV show 1960-65. Then several years with Wilson's company. Finally with John Gaughan's factory until died in a fire.

name: Ferero, Jack P.
bio: (New Jersey, USA: fl.1940s-80s) Accountant & semi-pro magician. Pro dealer as co-owner of Tannen's in New York City 1976-c1986. [Se]

name: Fern, Alfred George
bio: (Watford, England: 16 Nov 1906- ) Aka "Ah Foo". Inspired as volunteer assistant to a conjurer. Semi-pro pseudo-Chinese act, etc. [Go2]

name: Fernandes, Stephen A[nthony]
bio: (New Bedford, Massachusetts: 4 Apr 1950-) Roman Catholic priest since ordained in 1976. Learned magic from books in 1960. Amateur performer and, since 1983, semi-pro collector (16,000 magic magazine issues plus hundreds of catalogs, some books, & posters. Articles in Boston Mini-Wizard, Collectors' Forum, Flash Paper, Genii, Geniis Magic Journal, Hade-E-Gram Magizette, Journal de la Prestidigitation, Magic, Magic Carpet, Magic Net, New Jinx, Open Sesame, Pips, Top Hat, Yankee Magic Collector. Preparing a supplement to Alfredson & Daily's Bibliography of Conjuring Periodicals in the English Language. [Geniis Magic Journal 9/92; Wh5]

name: Fernández, Padre Pedro
bio: (Argentina: fl.1980s) Father Pedro is a priest in Buenos Aires. Publisher of Selecciones Magicas.

name: Ferrari, Angela
bio: See: Schmitt, Anita

name: Ferrentino, John
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro comedy stage magician. Wrote Comedy Clubs for All Magicians (1985, 52pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript & NY Magic Symposium books.

name: Ferro, Pat
bio: (Germany?: 30 Jul 1945-) Stage name of Peter Flanhardt. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Ferry
bio: See: Gerats, Ferry

name: Ferusa, Prof.
bio: (Portugal: fl.1930s-70s) Stage name of Ferrer Sousa. Pro magician. Worked 2-person telepathy -40s). Lived in Angola 75. Performed in às Vezes "Fetaque, The Great" SEE: Sanders, Fetaque

name: Fetsch, [Henry Nicholas] "Hen
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 10 Jul 1912-1 Jan 1961) Inspired seeing Carl Rosini show. Learned from Gilbert Mysto Magic set. Lessons in teens in Baltimore from Ernest Marx. Also quick-change artist. Died in Baltimore. Invented the Fetsch Force (by 1940), Past-Present-Future (1943), The Magic Spell (1947, deck based on a Stewart James principle), Band-It Card (1949), Multi-Magic Glass (1950), Silk Epic (1951), Mental Epic (1952), Breaking the Sound Barrier (1953), A Minor Miracle (1955), Symbolologic (1955), Wallet Wallop (1955), & Twin Twain (1958). Wrote Miniature Card Magic (1943, 6pp), Milk Pitcher Magic (1946, 26pp), Magic at Your Fingertips (1947, 46pp, with Milbourne Christopher), Secret (1952, 7pp), Chinatown Quarter Magic (1955, 12pp), The Five O'Fetsch (1956, 9pp), Magic with Canes (1960, 48pp), etc. Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, Dope Sheet, New Jinx, HMM. [Th]

name: Fetzer, Ren
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-60s) Invented Dovan by 1966.

name: Fialho, Philippe
bio: (France: - Mar 2001) Wealthy semi-pro close-up magician in the south of France. Pet effects: Chink-a-Chink and Cups-&-Balls. Sponsored Hamman's 1973 trip to FISM. His family owns the concessions for Lourdes. NOTE: Often misspelled "Phillipe Fiahlo". [Wat]

name: Fickel, Adalbert
bio: See: Frikell, Adalbert

name: Fickel, Wiljalba
bio: See: Frikell, Wiljalba

name: Fidler, Paul
bio: (USA: 1950-) Pro nightclub bird act in Las Vegas, etc. [Wat]

name: Fiedler, Lubor
bio: (Brno, Czechoslovakia: 26 Apr 1933 – 2nd Sep 2014) Learned at age 8 from uncle's gift of tricks. Chemical engineer & amateur magician. Moved to Austria in 1967, becoming a pro magician that year. Magic inventor & mail-order dealer. Invented Lubor Die = Gozinta Box (1966), Flying Color Cards (1978), Showstopper Card (1987), Invisible Zone (1996), Brain Box (1997), etc. Wrote Neue magische Ideen (1963, 38pp), Magische Fantasien (1978, 94pp), & Lubor Fiedler dreht durch (1980, 104pp). See Bill Palmer (translator) Lubor Fiedler's Magical Fantasies/Lubor Fiedler Goes Wild (1989). Tricks in Magic Info, MUM, etc. TV bits. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Field, Prof. Charles Edwin
bio: (London, England: 15 May 1835-13 Apr 1912) Pro performer-dealer-teacher in London. Played the Royal Aquarium (c1880-95, twice daily in his dealer's stall), Crystal Palace (1905), & West Pier in Brighton. Taught several later major magi. Ended career working sea-side resorts & died in poverty. [LR9/89;CI]

name: Field, Matt[hew]
bio: (The Bronx, New York: 27 Jun 1944-) Birth name Matthew Eliot Biberfeld. Legally changed to Matthew Field 1981. New York City radio broadcasting exectuve and interviewer. Learned magic at age 8 from Howard Thurston's 400 Tricks You Can Do. Amateur from 1974, professional since 2006, editor of 70 magic books (among them Darwin Ortiz at the Card Table by Richard Kaufman, Martin Gardner Presents, The Performance of Close-up Magic by Eugene Burger, Stodare: The Enigma Variations by Edwin A. Dawes, The Vernon Touch by Dai Vernon, Secrets of Brother John Hamman by Richard Kaufman, Card Craft by J.K. Hartman, Mysteries of My Life by René Lavand, Jennings '67 by Richard Kaufman). Moved to England in 2004. Video reviewer for Genii magazine (2000-2004), editor The Magic Circular (Jun 2005-present). Studied card magic with Richard Kaufman 1986-7 & close friends with David Roth & Patrick Page. Received J.N. Maskelyne award of Excellence in Magic Literature from the Magic Circle (2007). Wrote articles for Genii, The Electronic Grymoire, Precursor, The Magic Circular, The Guardian (Ali Bongo obituary). Bio on The Magic Circular (1966, v99, p149).

name: Fields, Eddie
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 5 Feb 1915-30 Sep 2001) Stage name since 1939 of Irv[ing] (formerly Isadore) Feldman. Medicine oil pitchman, astrologer, pro mindreader (with George Martz) in nightclubs & at state fairs, pool expert (never a hustler). Invented the Invisible Deck. Co-edited (with Dave Robbins) Magic is Fun magazine 1946-47. Wrote (with Michael Schwartz) Invisible Secrets Revealed (1978, 39pp). See Jon Racherbaumer, The Artful Dodges of Eddie Fields (1968; repr 1976, 109pp); Stephen Minch, A Life Among Secrets: The Uncommon Life and Adventures of Eddie Fields (1992, 237pp); and Eddie Field's Secret Diary (1992, 24pp). [Wh]

name: Fields, Henry
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 1927- ) Pro graphic designer & photographer until retired in Los Angeles as a real estate investor and, inspired by seeing Kuda Bux, traded photography lessons for lessons in mentalism with a pro at the Magic Castle. Turned semi-pro mentalist. Autobio note in Burton S. Sperber, Miracles of My Friends (1982), 38-42. Wrote How to Package, Market and Sell "Mentalism" for Big Time Corporate Events (1992, 37pp).

name: Figaro
bio: (Hungary: fl.1980s-90s) Stage name Istvan SZABÓ. Pro manipulator. Co-owner (with son, also named Istvan Szabó) of oldest magic shop ("Figaro") in Budapest. [Mec]

name: Figner, Leopold
bio: (Mühlhausen, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 8 Dec 1854-10 May 1932) Learned in Prague as assistant to "José". Toured Europe. Semi-pro cardman in Munich. Charter member of the Munich branch of the German Magic Circle in 1921. Was a clerk & merchant most of his life. Died in Munich. Wrote 3 books in German: Geheimnisse der Kartenkunst (1921, 80pp), Offenbarungen aus dem Reiche der Kartenkunst (1924, 90pp), & Höhere Kartenkunst (1927, 142pp). [Dam;Al]

name: Figueroa, Fred C.
bio: (USA: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Aka "Arbaces". Wrote The Abusive Use of Sleights (1909, 4pp), possibly the first published lecture notes on magic.

name: Fillebrown, Charles F.
bio: (Salem, Massachusetts: 2 Dec 1834-28 Jun 1903) Pro magic & vent since c1851. [Pr;Mo]

name: Findlay, James B[lack] "Jimmy
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 9 Jun 1904-15 Jul 1973) Moved c1944 to Isle of Wight where he became a hotel owner. Amateur manipulator & major collector of magic books (6,000 titles), posters, & playbills. Semi-pro dealer in & publisher of magic books. Edited the Thistle for a time & Collectors Annual 1949-72. Wrote 10 booklets, including Scottish Conjuring Bibliography (1951, 60pp), How's Your Library? (1958, 36pp), Conjurers Coins and Medals (1964, 72pp), Anderson & His Theatre (1967, 26pp), & The Wee Books (1972, 16pp). Articles in Collectors Annual, Sphinx, Abra, Magic Wand ("Collecteana" column), Magic Circular, Conjuriana, Magical Bookie, & Magic Cauldron. Also wrote articles under pen name of "Criticus". His superb collection of magic books, willed to his son, Dr David W. Findlay, was dispersed at public auction in 1979-80. A catalog is Findlay's Ninth Collectors Annual (1975, 280pp). [Go2;La2]

name: Fine, Robert
bio: (Germany: 29 Jul 19-) Stage name of Robert Loeffel. Pro close-up magician in West Germany. Since 1984 often works with partner Thomas Hierling as "Die 2", doing a gambling demo & card act.

name: Fink, Ray J.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) In 1924 edited Magic World and Magical Review (Philadelphia). In 1930s as "Ralston" toured the East Coast with his full-evening "Show of Wonders", which c1938 was the last magic show to play the Fifth Avenue Theatre in New York City. [HMM8/58]

name: Finley, Arthur
bio: (Brooklyn, NY: Oct 1887-13 May 1958) Commercial artist in New York City. Amateur cardman by mid-1920s. One of the 5 original members of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1932. Invented (as pointed out by Busby) the Royal Marriages plot by 1941, the tent vanish sleight by 1941, the Cheek to Cheek method by 1948, & the Tilt Off Load used in Vernon's C&B routine. [LR8/01; Magicol2/96; Bat8/46; Wat]

name: Finnell, [Eugene E.] "Gene
bio: (Fillmore, California: 23 May 1929-8 Apr 2002) Worked for Union Oil Company until retiring in 1989. Amateur cardman. Wrote Spelling the Aces (1967), The Free Cut Principle (1967, 25pp). See Karl Fulves, Gene Finnell's Card Magic (1973, 76pp). Tricks in Pallbearers, etc.

name: Finney, Michael [Arthur]
bio: (Woodland, California: 5 Aug 1954-) Learned in 1979 from bartender-magicians. Semi-pro comedy magician 1979-1983 when turned pro. Pet effects: Six Card Repeat & Card on Forehead. Video segment (1990). [LR6/2001;Jef;Wh2]

name: Firnholzer, Ernst
bio: (Germany: 9 Oct 1903-24 Dec 1961) Pro journalist & actor in Munich. Amateur magician. Wrote Zaubern leicht gemacht (1934, 63pp; 4th ed 1936, 129pp). Died in Munich.

name: Fischbacher, Siegfried
bio: (Rosenheim, Germany: 13 Jun 1939- ) Inspired at around age 10 by gift of box of tricks. Soon learned from a magic book. Debut at age 14. Pro, working German cruise ships 1960-65 as bartender magician. Thence as "Siegfried" in top illusionist team of "Siegfried & Roy". Have played regularly in Las Vegas since c1970, originally at the Tropicana, MGM, & Stardust ("Lido de Paris" in early 1970s at $1,800 per week) before moving to the Frontier in 1981. AMA Magicians of the Year, 1976, 1984. At $6,500,000 per year (in 1987), their show at the Frontier was not only the highest paid magic act but the highest paid variety act in the world. They worked 3,538 shows before nearly 3 million customers at the 800-seat Frontier Hotel Music Hall 1981-88. Became USA citizen in 1988. Toured Japan 1988-89, performing 38 weeks in a 3,000-seat tent-theater. Played Radio City Music Hall in late 1989 & reopened their Las Vegas show in November 1989 at the Mirage Hotel where in September 1990 they gave their 10,000th career show. Their initial Mirage contract was $57,500,000 for 5 years. The act closed in 2003 when Roy was incapacitated by a stroke. Forbes magazine rated S&R the world's 19th highest paid entertainers with a 1996-97 gross of $58 million. Among magicians they stand 2nd (behind Copperfield at 7th place with $85 million). 1991 Christopher Award (with Roy) for best stage magicians. Awarded (with Roy) the German Magic Circle (MZvD) Kalanag-Gedächnis-Ring in 1993. Autobio (with Roy & Annette Tapert) The Truth Behind the Magic (1992, 320pp; with German tr as Die Geschichte eines Welterfolges, 1992, 341pp). [Win;Jef;HC;Walk]

name: Fischer, Ottokar
bio: (Leschau, Moravia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 10 Nov 1873 – Vienna: 1 Dec 1940) Moved with parents to Vienna in 1883. Learned as student of A. Fredmar & then in 1895 or 1896 from Heubeck. Amateur to pro as "O.F. Marteau", working in the Kratky-Baschik Zaubertheater in Vienna from 1898 & managing it 1902-1911. Co-founded Magischer Klub Wien in 1908 [sic] & its first President 1908-1914. Dealer-manufacturer ("Wiener Kunststätte für Magie") in Vienna 1914-28. Edited Die Magischen Telefunken 1921-23 (3 issues). Magic collector. Teacher of several magicians including Hans Trunk, Graziadei, & Dolf von Rudeen. Hofziner Ring recipient 1933-35, its first. Voted an absentee member of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Suffered under Nazi regime, his wife being a Jewess. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. Author of 7 books in German, including J.N. Hofzinser Kartenkünste (1910, 220pp), English tr by S.H. Sharpe as J.N. Hofzinser's Card Conjuring (1931, 183pp; 2nd ed rev 1973, 200pp, as Hofzinser's Card Magic); Das Wunderbuch der Zauberkunst (1929, 224pp), English tr by Barrows Mussey & Fulton Oursler as Illustrated Magic (1931, 206pp); Aus Eins mach Zehn (1938, 183pp); & Johann Nepomuk Hofzinser Zauberkünste (1942, 320pp), English tr by Richard Hatch as The Magic of J.N. Hofzinser (1985, 215pp). Tricks in Jinx, Hugard's Magic Monthly, etc. [Vo57;Go2;Win;Sphinx4/41;Bam, pp103-104]

name: Fischer, Torsten
bio: (Germany: 16 Apr 1971-) Amateur magician & collector. Edits Sammler-Sammel-Surium 1991-present. [Nad]

name: Fiscus, Dave
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) School teacher. Semi-pro kid-show magician. Wrote The Birthday Magician's Handbook (1980), a comprehensive 225-page work.

name: Fish, John
bio: See: Poisson, Jean

name: Fisher, Aaron Benjamin
bio: (Washington, DC: 3 Mar 1976- ) In movie industry. Amateur specialized in card magic. Tricks in Magic, Genii, Minotaur, & Trap Door. Wrote The Sleight Album (30pp) & The Paper Engine (forthcoming 2001). [Wh01]

name: Fisher, John [Martin], MIMC
bio: (Southampton, England: 8 Jan 1945- ) Taught in 1953 by grandfather. TV producer with BBC until switched to Thames-TV in 1988 as head of variety programming (including its magic shows). Amateur magician. Producer of BBC-TV's "Paul Daniels Magic Show" 1979-88. Producer of Thames-TV "The Best of Magic" two miniseries, 1989 & 1990. 1984 AMA Award of Merit. 1989 Magic Circle Magician of the Year. 1990 David Berglas Award. 1990 AMA Special Fellowship. Major collector of books, paper ephemera, & old props relating to magic & allied arts. Authority on magic history. Executive Curator of the Magic Circle collection since 2002 Wrote John Fisher's Magic Book (1968, 192pp), The Magic of Lewis Carroll (1973, 288pp), Never Give a Sucker an Even Break (1976), Body Magic (1979, 158pp; French tr 1984 by Vollmer), & Paul Daniels and the Story of Magic (1987, 287pp). Edited J.N. Maskelyne Automata (1989). Articles in Abra, New Pentagram, MUM, & Magic Circular. [Genii2/91;MC12/88;Wh2]

name: Fisher, Ray[mond Michael]
bio: (Glen Ridge, New Jersey: 22 Aug 1936-) Learned around age 5 from kid's tricks & books. Actor-writer in New York City. Semi-pro close-up & mental magic since 1978. Played the Magic Towne House (1978-79) & Mostly Magic (1980-81). Articles in Hocus Pocus. [Wh2]

name: Fislage, Robert
bio: (Germany: 4 Sep 1951-) Magician & dealer ("Stolina Magie") in Oelde, Westf., Germany, since taking over Otto Stolina's shop in 1976. [Roh]

name: Fitzgerald, [Thomas B.] "Tom
bio: (Wilmington, Delaware: 17 Jan 1919-5 May 1996) Inspired & learned magic around age 6 from amateur father. Commercial artist/draftsman in Delaware until retired in 1972. Semi-pro comedy magician & vent since 1940s. Dealer (Tom's Magic Studio) from home. Invented Mental Choice (1950), Hole Connection (1955), Spikes thru Coin = Spiked Coin (1957), Snappy Magic Video Tape (1988). Wrote 3 booklets, including Snapp Magic--As You Like It, & "Magic Market" column in MUM. Tricks in Sphinx, New Phoenix, Genii, Magick, Linking Ring, Mantra, etc. Illustrated Thompson's My Best (1945). [Th;Wh2]

name: Fitzkee, Dariel
bio: (Annawan, Illinois: 14 May 1898-1977) Pen name of Dariel Fitzroy. Acoustical engineer in San Rafael, California. Semi-pro magician. Toured an unsuccessful full-evening magic troupe 1939-40. Publisher (St. Raphael House) of several magic books 1935-1949. Dropped magic around 1960, reportedly from disgust with his colleagues. Wrote Cut and Restored Rope Manipulation (1929), Linking Ring Manipulation (1930), Misdirection for Magicians (1935), Contact Mind-Reading Expanded (1935, 35pp), The Strange Inventions of Dr. Ervin (1937), Jumbo Card Manipulation (1937, 33pp), Showmanship for Magicians (1943, 187pp), The Only Six Ways to Restore a Rope (1944, 48pp; repr as Rope Eternal, 1957, 52pp), The Trick Brain (1944, 316pp), Magic by Misdirection (1945, 227pp), Rings in Your Fingers (1946, 120pp), & The Card Expert Entertains (1948, 171pp). The so-called "Fitzkee Trilogy" (comprising Showmanship, Trick Brain, & Magic by Misdirection) is a classic. Translated Rezvani's book. Book reviews for Genii. [Th]

name: Fiumedoro, Alio John "Ali
bio: (USA: c1910-Jan 2001) Machinist, musician, & amateur magician in Boston. Invented Animated Rope, which won the Fleming Trophy in 1951 for most original trick at that year's SAM-IBM convention. Marketed that same year by Holden's.

name: Flamo
bio:
(Gosport, Hampshire, England: 14 Sep 1911-) Learned as a schoolboy. Debut in 1925. Semi-pro. [Go2]

[See also: Wiesinger, Carl E.]

name: Flavian
bio: (Newwark, New Jersey: 6 Jun 1951- ) Stage name of [Dennis] Flavian "Flav" Petrulio. Of Italian extraction. Raised in Caldwell, New Jersey. Became interested in hypnosis & psychic science at age 10 when treated by a psychic healer for illness. Pro mentalist & hypnotist since 1980, specializing in ESP mind games & hypnosis. Hosts his "Journey to the Center of Your Mind" cable-TV show in New Jersey & New York City 1980-present. [Wh2]

name: Fleischer, Adam J.
bio: (USA: 1963-) Founding publisher-editor of Magic Manuscript 1979-85. Founder-impresario of The New York Magic Symposium 1982-87. Edited The Magic Dealer 1980-83 & co-edited (with Michael Ammar) Magical Arts Journal 1987-88. Wrote The Magic Hedonists Brainstorm in the Bahamas (1984), etc. [Wat]

name: Fleischman, [Albert] Sid[ney]
bio: (Brooklyn, NY: 16 March 1920 – Santa Monica, CA: 17 March 2010) Writer. Inspired at age 9 seeing Harry Snyder, a carnival sleight-of-hand artist. Amateur sleight-of-hand as "Sid Fleischman" & "Carl March". Pet effects: Cards to Pocket, 3-Shell Game, Linking Rings. Invented Card from the Fly (1938), Million Dollar Gimmick (by 1944), The Lady Disrobes (by 1944), & Floating Room Only (1947 with Bob Gunther). Wrote Between Cocktails--With a Packet of Matches (1940, 32pp; repr 1962), Mr. Mysterious' Secrets of Magic (1975), & The Charlatan's Handbook (1993, 228pp). Also 5 booklets (all with Bob Gunther): Ready, Aim—Magic!, Call the Witness (1943, 30pp), Top Secrets (1947), The Blue Bug (1947, 19pp), & Call the Next Witness [1940s]. Tricks in Jinx (including as "Albert Sidney"), Genii, Hugard's Magic Monthly, & Magick. Also wrote 1987 Newbery Award-winning children's fiction book about a family of magicians in the Old West, Mr. Mysterious & Company (Boston: Atlantic Monthly Press, 1962, 151pp; translated into 14 languages). It also won the 1969 Mark Twain Award & Lewis Carroll Award. Autobio is The Abracadabra Kid: A Writer's Life (1996, 198pp), which won the 1996 American Library Association's non-fiction book-of-the-year award. [CA;Th;Wh2]

name: Fleming, Caryl S[tacy]
bio: (Cedar Rapids, Iowa: 13 Oct 1890-2 Sep 1940) Banker in Los Angeles. Amateur magician. Aka "Swami Fleming". Amateur magician. Founding member of Los Magicos in 1933 in southern California. PCAM President 1934-39. Co-invented (with C.W. Fricke) Pip Fluid = It's a Pip (1937) & then invented its multi-color version, Chameleon Colors (by 1940). In 1938 founded the International Alliance of Magicians. Mentor of Chester Morris. Died of a heart attack while doing a card trick for guests. Tricks in Genii. [Genii9/41;SAM;Go2]

name: Fleming, [James William Alchin] "Jim
bio: (Australia: 17 Mar 1911-3 Jun 1986) Tool maker. Magic dealer-manufacturer (Green Frog Magic) in Sydney in 1939 when issued as 64-page catalog. Did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Foo-Lim". [McC]

name: Fleming, Dr Paul, PhD
bio: (Muddy Creek Forks, York County, Pennsylvania: 30 May 1889 [sic]-30 Dec 1976) Stage name of Paul Fleming Gemmill. Inspired in 1901 seeing Kellar, Rouclere, Keene, etc, shows. Pro since 1906. Assistant to Eugene Laurant (1909-10) & Karl Germain (1910-14, as "James"). On own as a Chautauqua star since 1915, beginning that summer when he toured as "Karl Germain". Thence semi-pro (& Professor of Economics at Swarthmore), retiring in 1967. Publisher of magic books. Wrote The Paul Fleming Book Reviews (2 vols, 1944, 1946). Brother of Walker Fleming. [Daw#234-235;Pr;SAM;WWA;American Mag3/46]

name: Fleming, Walker
bio: (USA: 24 Mar 1887-21 Jul 1971) Stage name of Walker Fleming Gemmill since 1915. Pro assistant to brother "Paul Fleming" 1915-60. Thence semi-pro as collector, magic dealer & publisher (The Fleming Book Co.) in York, Pennsylvania, since 1942. In 1946 bought the late Leo Rullman's collection & stock of magic books. [Pr]

name: Fleshman, Dan[iel Thomas]
bio: (Oceanside, California: 9 Oct 1958-) Learned at age 16 from Scarne on Card Tricks plus uncle's lessons on deck stacking. Pro close-up since age 23. Lecturer. Pet effects: Card to Wallet, Ring & String, Cups & Balls. Wrote Lecture I (1980, 20pp), Lecture II (1981, 22pp), The Excellence of Danny Fleshman (1983, 95pp, with Mendoza), Magician Tested Audience Approved (1985, 64pp, with Mendoza), The Very Best, Yet (1990, 78pp), Coin Miracles (1991, 70pp), Up Close with Dan Fleshman (forthcoming 1991, c75pp), Working Restaurants for Fun and Profit (32pp), Encounters of the Close-up Kind (1995, 61pp). Tricks in Genii & Magic Menu. Video bit (1993). [Genii7/85;Wh5]

name: Fletcher, Dr Duncan J. B., MIMC
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 11 Apr 1922-17 Jul 1995) Learned in 1936 from tuition by retired pro James Macfarlane. Physician in Glasgow. Semi-pro magician since 1940, specializing in stage & close-up. Pet effects: Multiplying & Color Changing Billiard Balls and Six Card Repeat. President of Scottish Conjurers' Association for 12 years. British Ring President 1976. Lectured to public on magic history. TV bits in Scotland. Died of viral pneumonia. [LR1/76;Wh6]

name: Fletcher, Ken
bio: (Asbury Park, New Jersey: c1937-) Learned from tricks in his father's five-&-dime store & reading Hay's Learn Magic at age 13. Did kid-shows in high school. Left sales management in 1974 to become pro magic dealer, founding Magic Masters, now a 7+ store chain for beginners.

name: Flezki
bio: (Holland: 1 Jul 1904-) Pro cigarette & card manip. With his assistant wife as "Les De Flezkis" took the 1946 Amsterdam 3rd prize & the 1948 FISM 2nd prize for presentation. [St]

name: Flint, Herbert L.
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1910s) Pro stage hypnotist since c1890. [Pr]

name: Flip
bio: (Rotterdam, Holland: 1 [or 3?] Jun 1941- ) Stage name of Flip Hallelaan Van Vollenhove, aka "Flip Hallema". Inspired at age 9. Ex-graphic artist. Pro stage comedy magician since 1969. Since 1979 lives in both Barcelona & Holland. Wrote Some Manuscriptricks (1982, 43pp). Video (1984). Tricks in Mad Magic #16 (all-Flip issue) & Epoptica. TV bits in Spain. [Xe;HC;Mag]

name: Flockton, Mr.
bio: (England: 1740-7 [sic] Apr 1794) Sleight-of-hand plus performing dogs & pigeons in London c1760-94. Bequeathed his show to Gyngell & the widow Flint. [Fr;Cl]

name: Flora, Brian R[oss]
bio: (Albuquerque, New Mexico: 14 Jun 1950 – 24 Aug 2002) At age 6 inspired by & learned from amateur father. Pro since 1981. Does private comedy shows, family, & festival shows as "Professor Flora". Also mental magic as "Ian Ross". Mail-order dealer (Flora & Company) in home town since 1977, including publishing since 1984. Wrote Selling Your Act (1982, 29pp). 15 audio-tapes (1984-89, including 6 with co-authors Docc Hilford, Richard Webster, Dave Harper, Gene Nielsen, & Alexander Thomas). Video reviewer for Genii since 1979. 3 videos (1987, 1989). Died in home town of a massive heart attack. [Wh2]

name: Florences [Gili], José
bio: (Tamarite de Litera, Huesca, Spain: 15 Nov 1872-30 Jun 1944) Pro manip act with cards, coins, & finally (by 1914) cigarettes. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1909. In 1914, arriving from the Continent & South America, he played New York billed as "Something New in Magic" with his novel cigarette manip act. Again played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1923, 1938, 1939-40. In various countries billed as "Florenzo", "Florenza", "Florenzi", & "Florence". Worked with assistant-wife "Miss Selika" (see). [Dif;Cam;Ch;Pr]

name: Florensa Casasus, Dr Alfredo
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 12 Dec 1926-) Physician. Moved to Madrid in 1941. Amateur vent-magician, aka "Florensa" & "Charlie Rinox". Wrote many booklets in Spanish, including Lecciones de Ilusionismo (Madrid: 60 parts, 1960-1985), Magia con cartas, Ilusionismo moderno, El libro del ilusionista aficionado, & Cartomagia Fácil. [Xe]

name: Flo-rey, Professor
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: fl.1950s-80s) A pro opera baritone before WW II. After WW II service learned from Chavez School of Magic on GI Bill. Part-time pro illusionist. Radio announcer by trade. [Mag]

name: Floridor
bio: (France: 1930-) Stage name of Bernard Birebont. Pro stage magician. Starred at Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1959-60, as "Floridor et Sylvie" 1969-70, 1974-75, and as "Floridor et Jenny" 1979-80.

name: Flosso, Al
bio: (New York City, NY: 10 Oct 1895-13 May 1976) Stage name of Albert "Floss" Levinson, aka "The Coney Island Fakir" (named in 1930s by Milton Berle). At age 10 inspired seeing Harry Bouton ("Blackstone") & learned from tricks bought at Martinka's. Pro since age 13, his shills including future magus Charles C. Eastman & future comedian Bud Abbott. Coney Island & circus sideshow magician & pupeteer 1915-39, including being featured in "Palace of Mystery" big illusion show at Atlantic City pier 1938-39. Dealer in New York City since late 1939 (when he succeeded Frank Ducrot) as the Flosso-Hornmann Magic Company in New York City. Played the Ed Sullivan TV show 1950 & 1952. SAM Hall of Fame. Trick in HMM. His son Jack succeeded to the business. Bio is Gary R. Brown, The Coney Island Fakir: The Magical Life of Al Flosso (1997, 139pp). [LR5/06; MUM10/95; Magico18/73; Genii1/67; Mag; Se; Des; Albo95, pp54-55]

name: Flosso, Jack "Jackie
bio: (Brooklyn, NY: 11 Feb 1926 - 5 Oct 2003) Stage name of Jack Levinson, aka "Al Flosso Jr". Taught by father Al Flosso by working in his shop since "a mere lad". Pro performer, specializing in comedy stand-up magic. Trick in HMM (1945). In Japan with USO 1960-61. Succeeded his father as owner of Flosso-Hornmann Magic Inc in 1976, selling to Ted Bogusta in Dec 2000. [Wh2]

name: Flosso, Lillian “Lily
bio: (USA: -1963) One of 6 daughters of magician Louis Krieger. Married Al Flosso in 1924. As “Madame Xenia” did circus sideshow mindreading act with husband 1924-25. Mother of Jack Flosso (b.1926). Died of complications from diabetes. [Br,pp14,46-47,107]

name: Floyd, Mary
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-40s) Born Mary Robinson. Married Walter E. Floyd with whom she (as "Mohala") did a pro two-person mind-reading act. SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr]

name: Floyd, Walter [Edwin] "Pop
bio: (Chelsea, Massachusetts: 12 May 1861-21 Aug 1940) Inspired by seeing Harrington in 1874 & tutorials from him. Learned (as "Al Nickle") assisting Robert Nickle. Pro since 1879 doing small magic and two-person mind-reading with wife Mary. A star of Chautauqua (by 1913). Pet effect: Miser's Dream, which he was performing when dropped dead on stage. SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr;Phoenix#117] "Floyds, The" SEE: Floyd, Mary & Floyd, Walter

name: Fogel, Maurice J.
bio: (East End, London, England: 7 Jul 1911-30 Oct 1981) Inspired & learned at age 12 from magic books in a London public library. Pro since debut in 1929 as assistant to Rameses. Worked as "The Magical Impressionist" 1935-36, impersonating famous magicians. Mentalist since 1939. Pet publicity effect: Bullet Catching 1941-60. Probably invented Russian Roulette (in 1970) & did invent Cheating the Gallows (2, by 1978). Wrote 5 booklets. Audio (1970s). In 1971 his only child, Nadine, married magician Chris Woodward. Died in London. [Fi;HC;Hudd;Le]

name: Fogg, Walter S[tokes]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 12 Nov 1890-11 Sep 1942) Inspired seeing Kellar show. Industrial advertiser. Amateur magician. Writer of dealers ads and ghosted several magic books, including C.H. Hopkin's classic "Outs": Precautions and Challenges (1940, 79pp). [SAM]

name: Foley, Jean G.
bio: (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 22 Aug 1903 [sic]-21 Jul 1994). Inspired seeing Thurston show in 1915. Taught by father. Student of Silent Mora. Since 1919 pro vaude & later nightclub magician, mainly as card manipulator billed as "The Man with the Smooth Hands" & "The Captain of the Deck". IBM Member #6 since 1923. Did a rube act as "Toby Trix" 1935-36 & a French act as "Jean Folé" 1936-37. With Rajah Raboid's show in 1937. Moved to Seattle in 1943. Columnist in Linking Ring since 1947. Pro dealer (Foley's Magic Shop opposite the Palomar Theatre) in Seattle 1946-58 when sold to Syd Brockman & retired from magic to become a clothing salesman until finally retired c1973. [LR8/93;LR8/87;Bo#163]

name: Folé, Jean
bio: See: Foley, Jean G.

name: Folkard, Charles J [ames]
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-1910s) Pro magician specialized in sleight-of-hand. Worked as "Draklof", "Chas. Volcard", & "Volkard". Wrote Tricks for the Trenches and Wards (series 1 & 2, 1915). REF: Dawes in MC, V.91 (1997), 62-63.

name: Folkmann, Max
bio: (Germany: fl.c1910s) Brother of Ludwig "Bellachini" Folkmann. Pro manipulator as "Forini". [Al]

name: Folletto
bio: (Lomellina, Italy: 21 Mar 1853-20 Feb 1919). Stage name of Giuseppe Ferrari. Son of a pharmacist. Moved to Paris where he was known as "Joseph Ferraris". Legal adviser to the Théâtre Robert-Houdin as early as 1901. Pro magician in Paris by 1905. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1905, 1914-17. Called magic the "Queen of the Arts". [Dif;MC10/50;Sil;Vo55;Cl;Illusioniste4/07]

name: Fontaine, Michel
bio: (France: 1936-) Semi-pro illusionist since 1960s as "Mac Fink". Main director of La revue de la presti-digitation until 1986. AFAP Bronze Medal 1989.

name: Fontana, Sonny
bio: (Caracas, Venezuela: 1957- ) Semi-pro with magic, Chinese Shadows, & origami. [Xe]

name: Fontanas
bio: (Belgium: -6 Dec 1966) Stage name of Maurice Fontaine. Amateur manipulator. [Dif]

name: Fontenelle
bio: See: De Fontenelle

name: Foo, Ching Ling
bio: (Yang Tsuan, outside Peking, China: 11 Mar 1854-1923?) Stage name of QUA Chee-ling. Pro. Played Singapore c1898. Toured the West with great success: USA (1898-1900), South Africa (1904), London (1904-05), Europe (1909-12), USA (1912-15). Had famous feud with Chung Ling Soo. Buried in Peking. SAM Hall of Fame. Invented or at least introduced to the West the Foo Can (in 1898), the Torn and Restored Paper (in 1898), & the Human Volcano routine (1898). [Pr;Dif;Mo]

name: Foo-Lim
bio: See: Fleming, Jim

name: Foo Ling Yoo
bio: See: Schultz, Edd

name: Ford, Gus
bio: See: Roberts, Allan

name: Ford, Stephen
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Close-up magician & manip. Dittia Shield 1988 & 1989. Zina Bennett Trophy 1989.

name: Forgacs, Steven
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1896- ) Architect. Taught magic by Carmelini. Amateur. Founding Secretary of M.A.M.E. in 1924. [WWM]

name: Forini
bio: See: Folkmann, Max

name: Fornalski, Józef
bio: (Poland?: 1912-c1990) Pro magician as "Eugeniusz Śniadecki", "Eugen Sima", & "Cagliostro". Died in Poznań, Poland. [Nad]

name: Forns Jordana, Juan
bio: (Badalona, Catalonia, Spain: 9 Apr 1916-) Learned magic at age 12. Pro, originally as "Caballero Sallim" & "Caballero Forns". Then with pseudo-Chinese act, originally (early 1940s) as "Ling-Fu", later (since 1946) as "Li-Chang". Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1945 & 1960. Often performed in circus throughout Europe. [Xe]

name: Forrester, Stephen [James]
bio: (St. Albert, Alberta, Canada: 1 Jan 1961-) Learned at age 12 from a Downs reprint. Math teacher in Calgary. Part time street & restaurant magician since 1979, specialized in cards & coins. Stage name is “Merlin the Magician”. Full time job as locksmith. Several local & regional awards since 1979. Local TV bits since 1980. Collector & historian. Major influence was Micky Hades. Has one of the larger magic book collections with approx. 7500 books and complete magazine runs. Wrote The Art of Street Magic (1989, 46pp), A Bibliography of Classic Authors in Magic and Related Arts (1993, 440pp), The Annotated Discouverie of Witchcraft Booke XIII (2000, 108pp). Articles in Magicol, Perennial Mystics, Linking Ring, Collectors' Forum, Yankee Magic Collector, Magic SYMbol, Geniis Magic Journal, Escapist Newsletter, Northern Peaks. [Wh2]

name: Forst, Ferry
bio: (Austria: 27 Dec 1912- ) Pro circus illusionist. Played Portugal in 1954. With Circus Barklay in Berlin 1955, Bertram Mills Circus in Britain in 1950s. Toured USA with Ringling Bros.-Barnum & Bailey Circus in 1960 & Dobritch-Circus in 1962. Played the Deutschlandhalle, Berlin, 1966-67. [Al;HMM4/60]

name: Forster, Jan [Matthias]
bio: (Göttingen, West Germany: 19 Nov 1958-) Learned at age 8 from magic book, later by lessons from Joe Nex & Henk Vermeyden. Since 1979 developed his "Smoker's Dream" act. 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in manip. 1981 Prague Grand Prix. Pro since 1982 with close-up & stage manip. 1983 Bologna Gold Medal. 1984 MZvD 1st prize in manip. German Magic Champion 1984-86. Articles in Magie & Magische Welt. TV bits. [Magie2/86;Wh5]

name: Forster, Prof. Dr. Toni
bio: (Reichertshofen, Bavaria, West Germany: 25 Jan 1949- ) Taught by father at age 5, then self-taught. Clinical psychologist in Dachau. Semi-pro mentalist since 1978. Pet effect: No-prop mindreading. Articles in Magie & Vibrations. 1981 MZvD 1st prize in mentalism. 1982 FISM 3rd prize in mentalism. [Wh2]

name: Forsyth, W. Donald
bio: (Scotland?: fl.1900s-30s) Aka "The Caledonian Conjurer". Learned magic in 1903. Semi-pro, touring through Europe.

name: Forton, Piet
bio: (London, England: 1 May 1938-) Stage name since 1956 of [Ferdinand] Pieter [Benjamin] de Beaufort. Son of a Dutch father & Swiss mother. Raised in Holland 1939-1945. Moved to Switzerland in 1945. Inspired in 1955 by Ravelli & learned from books. Art history teacher. Semi-pro magician since 1955 for adults & children, specializing in card, close-up, & stage magic. Invented Pop Out Move (1960). FISM 1st prize in card magic 1961, 1964, & 1967. Articles in Linking Ring, Gen, Abra, Magische Welt, Epoptica, etc. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Foska
bio: (Louviers, Eure, France: 1874-4 Sep 1951) Stage name of Célestine Dugard 1905-08 when, pretending to be a Hungarian, she worked a popular two-person mind-reading act in France with Roskoff. [Dif]

name: Fossier
bio: See: "Conus III"

name: Foster, Charles H.
bio: (Salem, Massachusetts: 1833 [sic]-15 Dec 1885) Famous pro pseudo-psychic billet reader by 1862. Toured USA, Europe, & Australia from 1870 to 1875 when he retired. Teacher of Bert Reese. Died in an insane asylum of alcoholism. Bio is George C. Bartlett, Charles H. Foster: The Salem Seer (1891, 157pp). [St]

name: Foster [Jr], [Edgar] Neil, MIMC
bio: (Aurora, Illinois: 1921-11 Mar 1988) Inspired at age 9 seeing Blackstone show. Protégé of local pro, William F. Becker. In Chavez College as student & then teacher 1947-51. Full-time pro 1951-59. With Ireland's around 1958. With Abbott's 1959-79, including as editor of The New Tops 1961-79. 1977 AMA Performing Fellowship. Partner (with Dale Salwak) of Chavez School from until his death in 1979 when Chris Jakway assumed Foster's place. Author & book editor, including Tops Treasury of Illusions (1965, 100pp). Bio is Dota Brown, Neil Foster (1988, 48pp). [Bo#207]

name: Fowler, Ed
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 1931- ) The adopted son of one of Houdini's former mechanics who inspired & introduced him to magic. Also inspired at age 9 seeing Blackstone. Worked with a Ghost Show until joined the U.S. Air Force. After military service worked as an escapist. Moved to southern California where worked as a Hollywood film technician. Semi-pro mentalist as "E. Raymond Carlyle". The 1st Resident Medium for the Magic Castle's Houdini Séances c1965-75 when replaced by Sandy Spillman. Articles in Magick, etc. [Mag] Fowler, [Augustus Gerald] "Gus", MIMC (Birmingham, England: 1 [not 11] Nov 1888-4 Jan 1960) Pro since 1906. Billed since 1910 as "The Watch King", his innovative 17-minute act used only watches & clocks as props, most of which were made by his friend, Bertram Evans. Invented the Travelling Garter (by 1925). Played St. George's Hall in London in 1909 (650 shows) & 1919; the Berlin Wintergarten in 1911; the Folies-Bergère in Paris in 1913; and the New York Palace twice each in 1922 & 1923. Toured Australia 1925. Retired in 1930. [Pr;Wal;Ch;Ho;WWM;Magic5/10] "Fox Sisters, The" SEE: Fox, Kate & Fox, Margaret

name: Fox, Imro
bio: (Bromberg, Germany: 21 May 1862-4 Mar 1910) Stage name of Isidor Fuchs, son of a German-Jewish merchant. Learned around age 13 from father's Xmas gift of box of tricks. Moved to USA in 1874, reportedly as a restaurant chef in Washington, DC. Pro comedy magician since 1879 as vaudeville star. Indeed that year he introduced the one-person comedy magic act to vaudeville. Toured the USA with Servais LeRoy & F.E. Powell as "The Great Triple Alliance" 1898-1900. Toured Europe alone 1890-92 & 1901-02, including the London Alhambra (1901), the Berlin Wintergarten (1901), & the Casino de Paris (1902). A pet effect (which he named) was the "Piano Card" (by 1902). Played Britain again in 1907. Noted for whirlwind performance style later used by Goldin. Died on tour in USA. Wrote Shadowgraphs and How to Make Them [New York: c1901, 20pp]. A trick in Vaudeville Review (1905). [Pr;Dam;Dif;Go2;Bur;Lau;Magic10/01,5/02,10/03]

name: Fox, Jacky
bio: See: Devos, Jackie

name: Fox, Karrell, MIMC
bio: (East Rainelle [sic], West Virginia: 30 Jan 1928 - 12 Mar 1998) Inspired by & learned from props left at his father's hotel by a skip-out magician in 1937. Debut at age 11. Demoed for Harold Sterling's & Abbott's Detroit shops in early 1940s. Appeared on Ed Sullivan's TV show at age 18 at which age he co-owned a magic shop in Detroit. Studied psychology in college & hypnotism in London for a year. Pro comedy magician-mentalist-hypnotist, playing many roles. Billed as "King of Korn" (by 1947 & ever since). Succeeded Clare Cummings as "Milky the Clown" on Detroit TV c1964-c1967. Mentor of Mark Tripp. Many inventions including "T.V. Trick" (1956) & "Spots Before Your Eyes" (1957). Many trophies & awards, including 1949 Sphinx Award, 1981 AMA Best Lecturer, 1983 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award, & 1985 AMA Creative Fellowship. IBM President 1986-87. MIMC 1988. 1993 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. 1997 Christopher Award for Lifetime Achievement. Died at Las Vegas Desert Seminar in his sleep. Wrote several booklets including Kornfidentially Yours (1954, 49pp; repr 1961) & 6 books: Clever Like a Fox (1976, 200pp), Another Book (1979, 320pp), Abra-K-Fox (1983, 128pp), For My Next Trick (1986, 184pp), My Latest Book (1988, 160pp), Much Ado About Something (1995, 164pp). Articles in most major magic magazines, including New Phoenix. 2 videos (1984 & 1989). [Se;Bo#268;MM8/81;Wh2]

name: Fox, Kate
bio: (Bath, Canada: c1842-2 Jul 1892) Brought by parents to USA, moving to Hydesville, Rochester, NY, in 1847. Younger sister of Margaret Fox with whom on 31 Mar 1848 at age 6½ she began the spirit rappings that soon became world famous among both spiritualists & magicians. Their authorized self-exposé is Reuben Briggs Davenport, The Death Blow to Spiritualism (1888, 247pp). See also R. Pearsall, The Table Rappers (1972). [Pr] (Bath, Canada: c1840-8 Mar 1895) Older sister & partner of Kate Fox in their pseudo-spiritualistic act. Bio is E.W. Fornell, The Happy Medium: Spiritualism and the Life of Margaret Fox (1964). [Pr]

name: Fox, Margaret
bio: (Chillicothe, Ohio: 9 May 1898-10 [sic] Dec 1976) Stage name of Paul Fuchs. Moved to Chicago where he was an Art Deco designer for the Black, Starr, & Frost silversmith company and teacher of engraving. Pro society magician. Suffering from TB, he moved to Colorado Springs, Colorado, by 1932. Member of the "Secret Six". Voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936 as an absentee member. Invented Brainwave Deck (1930), Paul Fox Cups (1932), Cocktail Shaker (1936), Miracle Gimmick (1947), Paul Fox Beer Trick (1959), etc. A major apparatus designer & improper. 1974 AMA Creative Fellowship. See Frank Csuri (ed), The Magic of Paul Fox (typescript in 6 copies). Tricks in Sphinx, Arcane, & in 2 books by Bobo.

name: Foy, Msgr. Vincent
bio: See: "Casaubon, Dr. George"

name: Frabot
bio: See: Botelho, Francisco

name: Frack, Julius
bio: (Sindelfingen, Germany: 11 Mar 1975- ) Stage name of Stefan Zucht. Student. Semi-pro stage magician. Articles in Magie. 1996 Silver Magic Rings (Lausanne); 1996 German Champion of Magic (Dresden); 1999 Dauphins Magiques (St. Etienne). [Wh01].

name: Frakson, José
bio: (Madrid, Spain: 7 Feb 1891-15 Apr 1981) Stage name of José Jimenez Seville. Pro manipulator throughout Europe & South America since 1912 when originally billed as "d'Olivarès". Played Lisbon in 1913, the Paris Olympia in 1913-14 (for 7 months), the Paris Cirque d'Hiver in 1925, the New York Palace in 1926, 1927, & 1928; the Paris Empire in 1930, & the Berlin Wintergarten in 1931. Returned to Spain at age 40 (c1931) to retire. When his property was seized by the Franco régime in 1936 during the Spanish Civil War, Frakson fled Spain and began again to perform in England & France, moving to the USA in 1937, becoming an American citizen in 1945. World-famous for his cigarette manip act but also did fine card & coin tricks. Refused the 1951 FISM Grand Prix, which went to Geoffrey Buckingham by default. Retired finally in Los Angeles around 1951, although he did play the New York Cotillion Room in 1954. 1970 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1972 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. After Franco's death (1975) returned to Spain in the late 1970s. [Bo;Pr;Dif;Genii8/81;Mag;Cam;Ho]

name: Frame, Tom
bio: (Canton, Ohio: 1960-) Introduced by a TV magic set at age 13. BA in clinical psych at Ohio State (1982). Semi-pro. Authored 3 Linking Ring One-Man Parades (1980, 1996, 2001), Framed! (1991) Tricks in Apocalypse, Trap Door, Linking Ring, Magic, Channel One, & Onyx. [LR4/01]

name: Framello
bio: (Germany: 24 May 1920-) Stage name of Franz Amler. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Franc-Morvand
bio: (Mesvres, S.-et-L., France: 12 Nov 1901-) Stage name of Louis Nectoux. Amateur in Autun. AFAP Master Magician. Collector. [Bou1;Rob1]

name: Frances, Lady
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Stage name of Frances E. Hess. Learned in 1934 assisting semi-pro husband Larry Hess. Pro with small apparatus & manipulation. Toured own act after 1946. In 1953 switched to TV producing in Cincinnati. [Mar]

name: Francesco di Milano
bio: (Milan, Italy: fl.1540s-50s) Wrote Quale Potrai Facilmente Imparare Molti Giochi di Mano [How You Can Easily Learn Card Tricks] (Milan: 1550). This very rare booklet in Italian, emphasizing card magic, is the earliest known magic manual. It was published 34 years before the works of the Frenchman Prévost and the Englishman Scot. He proclaimed himself as "known throughout the world as 'The Juggler' [il Bagatello]". [St;Cl]

name: Francese, Alberto
bio: (Italy: fl.1620s) Wrote Rari e mirabili giuochi di carte (Bologne: 1622), an early book of card tricks. Probably was the magician known as "Pirlimpimpim". [St]

name: Francis, Adrian
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Minor stage magician. Lived in Mellom (in Cumberland) & London. Invented "La Belle Adrienne", a non-trap, non-optical, surrounded version of the Vanishing Lady by 1901 when it was marketed by De Vere's Paris shop.

name: Francis, Day
bio: (USA: fl.1810s) Pro sleight-of-hand & human salamander act. Played Philadelphia in May 1816. Billed as "Emperor of all the conjurors" during appearances in Boston in Jul & Sep 1816. Wrote Stanislas Outdone (Philadelphia: 1818), a 48-page collection of tricks taken from earlier books. [Mo]

name: Francis, Douglas
bio: (Liverpool, England: 8 May 1915-) Stage name of Douglas Francis Jones. Cardman & Drunk Act as "On the Way Home". Wrote Right Under Your Nose (1947, 36pp) & Spectator's Choice (1953, 30pp).

name: Francisco
bio: See: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Franciscus, W. C.
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 1863-) Learned magic at age 14. Pro vaudeville magician. [Dor]

name: Franck, Prof.
bio: See: Guillemin, François

name: Franco, Eduardo [Mendes]
bio: (Figuera da Foz, Portugal: 15 Jan 1913-) Industrialist. Amateur magician. In 1959 co-founded (with Armando de Matos) the Magiarte magic shop in Porto. Founding member in 1959 of the Clube Ilusioniste Fenianos. [Cam]

name: Frank, Mago
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 12 Feb 1956- ) Stage name of Francisco José SUÁREZ ROSAS. Inspired in 1967 seeing Enrique Partida Bush show. Pro comedy magician since 1968. Also vent (with rabbit figure "Blas"). Leading kid-show magician in Mexico. 1976 TAOM Close-Up Trophy. 1978 Florida Magic Association 1st Prize in close-up. 1986 Magicruise 2nd place in close-up. President of Asociación Latinoamericana de Ilusionistas. 1989 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. Wrote Introducción a la Magia con Cartes (1979, 64pp). Invented-published Mago Frank's Coloring Book (1987), a flip book. Invented Mago Frank's Cards from Sleeve. Published Directorio Magico de Mexico [1988]. Edits monthly newsletter De Mago a Mago 1989-present. [Wh3]

name: Frank, Gary R.
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1953-) Learned in 1961. Pro stage, illusion, & close-up. Owner of Fantastic Magic Company in Granada Hills, California, since 1975. Wrote 1,2,3,---It's Magic (1978), Chung Ling Soo: The Man Behind the Legend (1987), & Chung Ling Soo: The Man of Mystery (1989). Compiled (with Phil Temple), The Carter Scrapbook (1992, 96pp). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Frank, Skipper
bio: See: Herman, Frank J.

name: Frankl, Moritz
bio: (Pécs, Hungary: 22 Oct 1873-) Youthful travelling magician through Austria, Hungary, & Germany 1880-88. In Austro-Hungarian Navy in summer 1892 when sentenced to 6-year prison term for insubordination.

name: Franklin
bio: (Germany: fl.1990s) Stage name of Frank Schmidt. Pro. Combines magic, mime, & dance. 1994 magic hands 1st place trophy. Played the 1995 SAM Convention. Franklin and his Doves (England: fl.1950s-70s) Stage name since 1959 of Frank Booker. Taxi driver in London. Semi-pro dove & card magic since 1959, having been taught by Channing Pollock. Officially took over Pollock's act when the latter retired in 1969. [HMM2/60]

name: Franklin IV, Benjamin
bio: (USA: c1914-21 Jan 1986). 4th generation descendant of the American founding father. Prosleigh-of-hand. Pet effect: Card Scaling. (Springfield, Ohio: fl.1950s) Stage name of Frank McKinnon. Pro with ghost show (Dr. Franklin's Spooks on the Loose) for 5 years in 1950s. [Walk2]

name: Fran-Klint
bio: (Havana, Cuba: 18 Oct 1887-16 Sep 1950) Stage name of Francisco di Paula Lucas ARANAZ BERGADO, of Spanish parents. Moved to Spain where he left his father's watchmaking shop to learn magic in 1911. Pro since debut in Lisbon in 1912 as a hand shadowist. After 1915 (when again in Lisbon but this time at the Coliseu), inspired by Watry, changed to card & cigarette manip, working in black gloves. Played Paris often since 1916, Australia 1924, London (St. George's Hall) 1925, etc. Died in Paris where he had lived for some time. [Dif;Cam;Wal;Ch]

name: Franzardi
bio: See: "Garvin"

name: Frascati
bio: (Austria: 15 Mar 1899-1970) Stage name of Willy Mayr. Pro. [Al]

name: Frasier
bio: (England: fl.1820s-30s) Minor pro. In 1828 worked Bartholomew Fair, taking in a paltry £26 (a sixth what the Pig-faced Lady got). Retired c1840. NOTE: Name also spelled Frazer.

name: Frazee
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City: 18 Jun 1881-28 Sep 1957) Pen name of William "Bill" Meyenberg. Pro with Redpath & Chautauqua circuits. Assistant to Carl Rosini 1920-24. Later worked clubs. Wrote "Squawks" column in Sphinx since 1926. Moved to Philadelphia in 1932. [St;Ho;WWM]

name: Frazer
bio: See: Frasier

name: Fred, Mahruk
bio: (Germany: 17 Jul 1929-) Stage name of Kurt Hampel. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Freddi
bio: (Poland: fl.1930s) Stage name of Alfred Janiszewski. Pro illusionist. Co-edited magic monthly Ze świata czarów 1930-38. [Mec]

name: Frederica
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 22 Feb 1919-31 Jul 1984) Stage name of Tommy Frederick. Debut at age 12. Pro performer-dealer-collector. Articles in Gen. See Lewis Ganson, The Magic of Frederica (1981).

name: Frederick, Carl
bio: (USA: 4 Feb 1863-6 Feb 1923) Stage name of C. Fred Crosby. Fredmar, A. (Vienna, Austria: c1870-c1914) Stage name of Alfred Freiherr von Kendler. Taught by C. Herrmann (the latter's only student except his brother Alexander). Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Toured Germany & England. First teacher of Ottokar Fischer c1895.

name: Fredric, Carl
bio: See: "Charlier, Fred"

name: Fredrick, Ron
bio:
"Fredrik the Great" SEE: "Blackstone, Harry" Fredrik, Alexander

[See also: Zollweg, Ron]

name: Fredrik, Alexander
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 23 Apr 1878-) Pro illusionist by 1901 on Lyceum circuit. Aka "Fredrik the Great" until c1913 when forced to release that stage name (together with a large stock of playbills), which both Willard the Wizard and Dante later acquired & used until the paper ran out. [Pr]

name: Fredström, Bertil
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 24 Apr 1956- ) Inspired in 1965 seeing Swedish magicians Mills, Marvillo, & Ken Hardy. Manager with IBM-Sweden. Amateur magician since 1970 as "Black Bert" & semi-pro since 1975 with stand-up & childrens magic. 1974 Nordic junior champion in close-up. President, Swedish Magic Circle, 1982-83 & 1988-89. Articles in Trollkarlen, Geni, & Trolleri som Hobby. [Wh5]

name: Fredwick, S.
bio: (USA: 7 Jun 1891-14 Aug 1947) Stage name of Fred E. Wicks.

name: Freeman, Gordon
bio: (Britain: 20 Sep 1889- ) Stage name of Gordon Swingler. Public debut at age 10. Pro comedy magic. At Maskelyne's in 1925. [Go2;Cl]

name: Freeman, Paul
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Pro ambidextrous manip act with cards in 1913, when he became the first magician to manipulate while wearing gloves. [Ch]

name: Freeman, [Mark Stephen] "Steve
bio: (USA: 1951- ) Accountant. Amateur cardman. Articles in Genii. [Wat]

name: Freer, Winston H.
bio: (USA: -29 Apr 1981) Aka "Doc Maxam". Co-invented (with U.F. Grant) the Alagen Rope (by 1939). Invented Tantalacto (by 1940), The Maxam Rope (by 1940), The Be-Deviled Egg (by 1940), First Finger of Fate (1954, with Stewart James), & the Half-Wit Deck. Wrote 25 Rice Bowl Methods (1954, 18pp, mimeo) & Compiled Magic of Doc' Maxam (1954, 31pp). Tricks in Genii, Mantra, etc. His bio & tricks are being (1995) researched by Gaetan Bloom. [Wat]

name: Fregoli, Leopoldo
bio: (Rome, Italy: 2 Jun 1867-1936) Pro music-hall quick-change artist to pro magician. A pioneer of Italian cinema, he made a silent movie of his quick-change act in 1899 and other comic shorts (including his magic) that he added to his stage program. Autobio is Fregoli Racontato da Fregoli (Milan: 1936). Bios are Mario Verdone, Leopoldo Fregoli (Rome: 1964) & Jean Nohain, Frégoli, 1867-1936: Sa vie et ses sécrets (Paris: 1968). [Ch;Bar;Dif]

name: French, Henri
bio: (Europe: fl.1890s-1920s) Pro magician, acrobat, unicyclist (with his "The Drunk on Wheels" routine), juggler, & animal trainer. Toured the USA a few years before the turn of the century, including New York City in 1900. Thence to Europe where he played London's Empire in May-Jun 1901. Toured Australia 1913 (including the Melbourne Tivoli), 1920, 1925, & 1927. [Wal; Magic8/01]

name: Frenette, Gerry [Joseph]
bio: (Amherst, Nova Scotia, Canada: 8 Aug 1959-) Learned in 1978 from library books & magic sets. Semi-pro illusion builder since 1984 when he founded "Magic Makers" with wife Leonora with whom he co-invented the "Woman's Revolution" illusion. [MUM4/99;Wh5]

name: Freund, Gustav
bio: (Germany: fl.1910s) Wrote Zauber-Apparate selbst herzustellen (1910, 53pp; 2nd ed 1923).

name: Freundt, Heinz
bio: (Germany [sic]: c1920-) Moved to Austria. Watchmaker in Salzburg. Amateur manipulator. 1976 FISM 1st prize in close-up. Specializes in floating effects. [Mec]

name: Fricke, Charles W., LL.M., J.D., LL.D.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-50s) Judge by profession in California. Wrote several standard books on criminal law, beginning in 1926 & including Criminal Investigation. Amateur magician. Co-invented (with Caryl Fleming) Pip Fluid = It's a Pip (1937). Tricks in Genii.

name: Friedrich, Hanns
bio: (Nürnberg, Germany: 26 Nov 1890-22 Jan 1972) Teacher in Dinkelsbühl. Amateur magician. Noted for poetic patter. Died in Munich. Wrote Kartenzauber ohne Fingerfertigkeit (1941, 118pp; repr 1943) & Der verhexte Tisch: Kleine Illusionen (1942, 123pp; 3rd repr 1944). Articles in Magie & Die Zauberkugel.

name: Friedrich, Nicolai Alexander
bio: (Frankfurt, Germany: 9 October 1976- ) Lawyer. Part-time pro magician with stage, parlor, mentalism, & close-up. Invented The Smile of the Mona Lisa (1996). 1997 MZvD Magician of the Year.; 1998 Sarmoti Award; 2000 FISM 3rd Prize in Mentalism. Contributor to Kaufman's Flicking Fingers (1998). [Wh01]

name: Fries, Dr Joseph H[arman] "Joe", MD
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City: 22 Jun 1903-) Pediatrician in Brooklyn. Amateur magician as "Fries". Taught Irving Desfor in 1931. Pet effects: rope tricks. Tricks in Jinx, HMM, etc. [SAM;Go2;Th]

name: Frikell, Adalbert
bio: (England: - Scarbourough: 26 Aug 1889) Only legitimate son of Wiljalba Frikell from whom he learned as apprentice. A Mason. Pro since as early as 1862. Lived in Germany but briefly toured Britain most years since 1875. Gave Command Performance at Sandringham 1877. Played the Egyptian Hall 1880 for 3 months. Died in Scarborough of a burst blood-vessel. [Magic4/02,6/02;Cl;Pr;Daw]

name: Frikell, Gustav
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s) Stage name of Henry W. Llewellyn. Credited by Cremer on title pages of some editions as having contributed to both The Secret Out & The Magician's Own Book. [Magic11/01, 9, & 1/03, 34]

name: Frikell, Samri
bio: See: Oursler, Fulton

name: Friell, Wiljalba
bio: (Sagan, Prussia [sic]: 27 Jun 1818 - Kötschenbroda: 10 Oct 1903) Stage name of Friedrich Wilhelm Frickel, aka "W. Frikel" & "Wiljalba Frickell". Learned assisting a touring magician. On his own as a pro at age 16 in 1834. Pet effects: Linking Rings, changing heads of fowl, & productions. Toured Germany, Hungary, Wallachia, Turkey, Egypt, Finland (1843-44), England (1857-58, including a record-breaking 22 weeks at the St. James's Theatre in London), Russia (1858), England (1859-60), & USA (1873). Widely but wrongly credited with having introduced the wearing of black evening clothes for magicians. Retired in 1896. Wrote Professor Wiljalba Friell's Lessons in Magic or, Two Hours of Illusions, without the Aid of Apparatus (London: [1858], 28pp). [Pr;Cl;Fr;Magic11/01,6/02;Sal;St;Mo]

name: Frischkorn, Dr Carl S.
bio: (USA: -1954) Aka "The Great Karland". Magic collector. Died in Norfolk, Virginia.

name: Frisenette, George [Carl]
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 16 Jul 1900-) Pro with full-evening show since 1925. Specialties: hypnotism & mind-reading. [WWM]

name: Fritz, Jürgen
bio: (Germany: 28 Jul 1953-) 1983 Baden-Baden 3rd prize in general magic; 1984 MZvD 3rd prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Fritz, T. Francis
bio: See: "Ducrot, Frank"

name: Frizzo
bio: (Milan, Italy: 1852-1894) Stage name of Enrico Longone. Tutored in magic by Compars Herrmann & in hand shadows by Campi. Pro magician-shadowist. In late 1800s was first to combine shadowgraphy with magic. Taught magic to Molini. Toured Europe (playing the Folies-Bergère in 1880), Asia, & S. America (1888) where he remained, dying in an insane asylum in Uruguay [sic]. Wrote Memoria Transcendentale (Milan: 1880) & Frizzi Mefistofelici (1881). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Langone". [Sil;Dif;Pr;St]

name: Fröhlich, Joseph
bio: (Altaussee, Austria: 18 Feb 1694-27 Jan 1757 [sic]) Pro since 1725. Court Conjuror & Jester to two Electors of Saxony (in Dresden) including August the Strong. Famous enough by 1737 to be memorialized that year in a Meissen porcelain statuette. Toured Germany, Switzerland, & Poland. Died in Marienmont near Warsaw. Bio is Carl Willnau (pseudonym of Dr Carl Naumann of Leipzig), Ein Schelm, der es gut meint (Leipzig: 1942), a 443-page biographical novel. NOTE: Surname also spelled Frölich, Froelich, & Frölig. [Hokuspokus Zauberkunst,32-33;Zm;St;Cl;Al]

name: Fromer, [Leroy] "Roy
bio: (USA: 1937-14 Dec 1991) Social worker. Semi-pro close-up magician, mindreader, vent, & fire eater. Learned at age 10 from his grandmother's magic books. Protege of S. Leo Horowitz. Mail-order dealer (Galaxy Magic Co) in Manchester, New Hampshire, editing its house organ, The Medium 1971-72 (6 issues). Then owned The Magic Shop in Stamford, Connecticut. Wrote Floating Ball Magic (1972), etc. Tricks in Genii, Swami, etc. TV bits. [MUM6/93;LR7/92]

name: Frost, Thomas
bio: (Britain: 1821-1908) Although a political journalist with only a layman's knowledge of magical methods, he wrote the first history of magicians, The Lives of the Conjurors (London: 1876, 360pp; reprinted 1881, 353pp; facsimile repr of 1st ed 1971), a classic. Also wrote The Old Showmen and the Old London Fairs (London: 1874, 388pp; repr 1875 & 1881) & Circus Life and Circus Celebrities (1875, 328pp). [Tops8/37;Vo56]

name: Frye, John W.
bio: (USA: 28 Nov 1901-25 Oct 1973) Pro illusionist. [Pr]

name: Fu Chan
bio: See: Bamberg, David

name: Fu Ling
bio: See: Brisbane, David

name: Fu Ling Yu
bio: See: Arenholz, William J.

name: Fu-Manchú"; "Fu Manchu" [pronounced FOO man-CHOO]
bio: See: Bamberg, David

name: Fujiwara, Kuniyasu
bio: (Japan: fl.1990s) Invented “Magical Window” & “Fuji Ching”, a finger-chopper effect that won the 1992 Atsukawa Creativity Prize.

name: Fujiyama, Shintaro
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 1 Dec 1954-) Stage name of Naoya Tsuchido. Pro, working both traditional (wazuma) & Western style. Pet effect: the water illusion and butterfly trick.

name: Fukai, Hiromasa
bio: (Osaka, Japan: 27 Jan 1950-) Pro stage & close-up performer since 1979. Also dealer in Osaka. Two world tours in 1980s with assistant-wife "Kimika" (Kyoko Fukai, born 1952) as "Fukai & Kimika" with a parasol & quick-change act. 1985 FISM 2nd prize in general magic. 1989 Desert Magic Seminar 2nd prize. Dealer & maker of fire magic. TV bits. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Masahiro". [Bo#239;Wat]

name: Fukano, Atsushi
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 13 Mar 1963-) Learned in 1975 when bought Silk-to-Egg at department store. Specializes in close-up. Pet effect: Coin thru Table. Pro since 1980 when he joined Tenyo Company for which he became a part-time inventor in 1988. Trick in Magic Manuscript. [MM11/89;Wh2]

name: Fulbert, Maxim
bio: (Saint-Josse-Teen-Nodde, near Brussels, Belgium: 31 Oct 1884-31 Oct 1945) Stage name of François-Joseph Van Opdenbosch. Prosleight-of-hand artist, innovator, & (since 1921) prop maker. Toured Europe. [Dif;Vo58;Rob1]

name: Fulves, Karl
bio: (USA: 27 Jul?, fl.1950s-90s) Amateur close-up & cardman. Aka "Ralph Gironda". Publisher (Gutenberg Press) of magic books in Teaneck, New Jersey, 1969-present. 1986 AMA Literary Fellowship. Prolific & influential (although sometimes cranky) writer & editor. Edited Midnight Magic Monthly 1959-60, The New Phoenix 1965, Pallbearers Review 1965-75 (also contributed under many pen names), Epilogue 1967-76, Interlocutor 1975-89, & Chronicles 1978-89. Wrote Riffle Shuffle Set-Ups (1968; 2nd ed 1974, 98pp), Faro & Riffle Technique (1969, 90pp; repr 1974), The Book of Numbers (1971, 47pp), Mexican Monte, & Other Tricks (1972, 32pp), Notes from Underground (1973, 62pp), Packet Switches (1974, 2 vols, 56+66pp), Close-Up Mental Magic (1974, 54pp), Riffle Shuffle Technique (3 parts, 1974, 1975, & .....), Riffle Shuffle Set-Ups (1974), Methods with Cards (3 vols, 1975), The Magic Book (1977, 1975pp), Transpo Trix (1978, 80pp), Curioser (1980), Color Quick (1980, 50pp), A History of the Brainwave Principle (1983, .....pp), etc. Also, having been introduced by Martin Gardner, wrote 10 popular magic books for Dover Press: Self Working Coin Magic (....., 130pp), Card Tricks for Children (....., 47pp), Self-Working Card Tricks (1976), Self-Working Mental Magic (1979, 121pp), Self-Working Table Magic (1981), More Self-Working Card Tricks (1984), Self-Working Paper Magic (1985, a force book where 4th word in each chapter is "tricks"), Easy-to-Do Magic Tricks for Children (1993, 32pp, & Easy Magic (1995)). Also wrote or edited books on Daley, Finnell, Hummer, Jordan, Maze, & Slydini (see). Trick in Swami. [Wat]

name: Funk, Christlieb Benedikt
bio: (Germany: 1736-1786) Professor of natural science at Leipzig U. Wrote Natürliche Magie (1783; repr 1806), a 271-page treatise on non-supernatural magic with some minor card tricks & numerical recreations. [St]

name: Funke, J. Jakob
bio: (Germany: fl.1810s-20s) Under pen name of H.A. Kerndörffer wrote Carl der Tausendkünstler (1810; 6th ed. 1825, 343pp) & Neueste psysikalische Belustigungen (1811).

name: Funtasio, Senor
bio: See: "Fantasio, Ricardo"

name: Furkey, Frank R[olland]
bio: (Springfield, Massachusetts: 20 Oct 1929-) Inspired in 1944 (age 14) seeing Joe Karson do Zombie & then learned magic at Karson's magic shop. Long-time factory representative. Amateur magician to semi-pro as "Frank Rolland" since 1965, specialing in Cups & Balls and card tricks. Pet effects: Rising Cards & Chop Cup. Collector. In 1975 coined jargon term "cardiac" for a rabid cardman. Now retired in Marietta, Georgia. [Wh2]

name: Furlong, [Andrew J.] "Ande" "Andy
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-80s) Mentored by Gus Bohn. Pro performer. Then managed Holden's Philadelphia magic shop in late 1940s (succeeding Rudy Saxon) & Holden's New York shop in 1950-51. Invented "Ande's Aces".

name: Furmanov, Anatol Aleksandrovich
bio: (USSR: 1929-) Pro illusionist & manip. [Mec]

name: Furota, Masatoshi
bio: (Kita Kyusyu, Fukuoka, Japan: 15 Dec 1926 - 27 Dec 2003) Learned in 1955 as student of Tenkai. Amateur manipulator. 1969 medalist at international magic convention, Eindhoven, Holland. Editor of The New Magic, a Japanese-language journal. Chairman of the Tenkai Prize committee. Rep of the JMA with FISM. Wrote 3 books in Japanese, Co-authored (with Tenkai) The Thoughts of Tenkai (1971 bilingual in Japanese & English). Tricks in Genii, etc. [Dif,Wh2]

name: Fürst, Alexander
bio: (Germany: 1868-c1960) Stage name of Alexander Trippe. Invented the Tanagra illusion in 1889. Died in Hamburg, impoverished. [Zm;Al]

name: Furst, Arnold
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 21 Jun 1918 – Los Angeles: 22 Feb 2002) Stage name of Arnold Furstenberg (since 1939). First interested in magic in 1928. Pro comedy magic & hypnosis since 1939, first with school shows in Los Angeles 1939-42, thence into vaude & night club work, touring world with USO 1943-46 & in USA with a full-evening show 1948-54. World tour manager for Ormond McGill 1955-56. Instructor at the Hypnotherapy, Hypnotism and Psychological Institute of Tokyo, Japan, 1963-72. A teacher of Chuck Vincent, etc. A Mason, he was an officer of the Invisible Lodge. Invented Fresh Fish (1938).
