Wrote Famous Magicians of the World (1957); Magic for Monsters (1960, 56pp; repr as Kid Stuff, V.6); Mightier Than the Bullet (1961, 66pp), 2nd ed as How to Get Publicity in Newspapers [and] Other Media (1975, 95pp); & Great Magic Shows (1968). Program reviews in Genii. Also wrote 4 books on hypnosis 1959-82, beginning with Case Studies in Hypnotherapy (1959, 163pp, with Lester T. Kashiwa, MD). [MUM6/2002;Des;Wh2]

name: Furst, Dr Bruno
bio: (Metz, Alsace-Lorraine, Germany: 13 Mar 1891- ) German Jew. Learned mnemotechnics in Munich from C.L. Poehlmann ("Pelman"). Criminal lawyer in Frankfurt for some 15 years. Fled Hitler's Germany, first to Czechoslovakia, then the USA in 1938. In 1942 he opened his School of Memory and Concentration in New York City. [Zo]

name: Fusier, [Léon]
bio: (Amiens, Somme, France: 4 Aug 1851-4 Mar 1901) Famous pro chapeaugraphist (15 characters) since 1870 with his "Monsieur Tabarin" comedy act, which included some magic. Played the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1879. Long suffering from pleurisy, he died in a German sanitorium. [Vo55;Dif]

name: Futagawa, Shigeo
bio: (Yokohama, Japan: 7 Jul 1943-) Inspired at age 15 by TV magic show. Pro close-up since 1972, specialized in card & coin magic. Invented several packet tricks & coin routines. Lectured in USA. 1983 Tenkai Prize. He is one of best creators and performers in Japan. Wrote Introduction to Coin Magic (1978, 199pp; French tr 1986 by Vollmer) and, in Japanese, other books, including Futagawa Shigeo no Hon [The Book of Shigeo Futagawa] (1984). Editor Fushigi 1989-present. Articles in Fushigi. Publisher and editor of Magic House magazine. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Fyre, Tamara
bio: (South Africa: c1961-) Stage name of Michelle Parker. Pro dancer since age 17 in South Africa. Then as magician's assistant. Moved to USA. Since 1987 works as pro illusionist with Tim Kole as "Fyre & Kole" as both assistant & with own spot. Later replaced by Jenny Lynn.

name: Gabriel, Alfred "Alf", MIMC
bio: (London, England: 8 May 1905-1996) Pro tailor & semi-pro band drummer (retired) in London. Learned magic in 1948 from tutorials & reading books. Semi-pro stage magician since c1950. Long-time music maestro for London Society of Magicians & the British Ring. British Ring President 1973-74. Articles in Abra, Budget, Magic Circular, & Zodiac Society Newsletter. [MC2/87;Wh6]

name: Gabriel, Joseph
bio: See: "Joseph"

name: Gács, Rező
bio: (Budapest, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Hungary]: 16 May 1911-11 Jan 1987) Claimed that at age 13 he was taught magic by a Chinese pearl merchant in return for having saved him from drowning. Pro magic & pickpocket act as "Rodolfo". Taught Tosari & Kovari & encouraged Joe Korengo to become pro. Named Peoples' Artist of Hungary in 1960. Top pro in East Europe at time of death. Wrote Achtung Ich Trixel (W. Germany). [Win;Rey] Gagnon, [Thomas Albert] "Tom" [pronounced GAN-yon] (Sault Sainte Marie, Michigan: 8 Nov 1945-) Quality control manager with Chrysler Corporation. Amateur close-up magician & major illustrator of magic books, including The Vernon Chronicles. Wrote Sleightly Original (1981, 113pp). Also a 1985 Stars of Magic issue (New Series, Vol.2, No.3). Tricks in Epoptica, etc. [LR12/96;Wh]

name: Gaillard, Alain
bio: (France: 8 Aug 1942-) Semi-pro as "Alan Ghayar", specialized in manipulation & close-up. Charter member of the reconstituted Magic-Club Rennais 1967. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Bronze Medal 1974 & Silver Medal 1976. Wrote (as "Alan Ghayar") 33 Tours (1973) & Magie Creative. [Bou;Bou2]

name: Galasso, Horatio
bio: (Italy: fl.1590s) Wrote Giuochi di carte e di memoria (Venice: 1593), one of the earliest books on card & memory tricks. [St]

name: Gale, John
bio: (England: fl.1790s) Wrote Gale's Cabinet of Knowledge; or Miscellaneous Recreations, including the most celebrated Card Deceptions ever Exhibited (London: 1796, 336pp; 3rd ed 1800).

name: Gali-Gali, Luxor
bio: (Port Said, Egypt: 23 Oct 1902- ) Stage name (adding the "Luxor" in 1952) of Mahguob Mohammed Hanafi. Taught by pro father "Gali-Gali" who had him working on cruise ships at age 10. Pro close-up. Lived in Paris 1926-31. Played the Casino de Paris in 1934. Moved to USA by 1935, becoming citizen in 1944. Pet effect: Cups-and-Balls with baby chicks. Played the Ed Sullivan Show (TV) in 1950 & 1961 and the London Palladium in 1951. Moved to Las Vegas in 1963. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal 1970, 1972, & 1973. TV bits. NOTE: Name often misspelled "Galli-Galli" & not to be confused with "Guili-Guili". [Pr;Ho;Al'HMM7/50,12/58]

name: Gali Gali, Zouki
bio: (Greece: fl.1970s) Stage name. Pro. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1977.

name: Galindo, Ramon G.
bio: (near Monterey, Mexico: 1921- ) Moved to Austin, Texas, at age 2. Learned in childhood. With US Army in WW II. Master tailor (Ace Custom Tailers) in Austin. Taught serious magic c1952 by Herman Yerger. Semi-pro magician with parakeet act (since 1955). TAOM Al Sharpe Trophy for Originality in Presentation 1957 & 1958. TAOM 1962 trophy for Best Originality & Showmanship. Makes tailored wardrobes for magicians. Toured Mexico, Japan, France, Hong Kong, Spain, etc. Wrote A Bird in the Hand (1983). In 1988 his son & daughter, Jason (age 10) & Jennifer GALINDO CABALLERO (age 8), won the TAOM Junior Stage Trophy. Movie (1958), 2 videos. [Genii/1/91]

name: Gallici, Henri
bio: (Dax, Landres, France: 3 Jan 1868-8 Jan 1950) Son of Pietro Gallici. Dropped studying pharmacy on his mother's death in 1888 to became a pro magician. In 1890 married Mlle Sabine Rancy, daughter of famous circus master Théodore Rancy (whose son, Napoleon, soon married Gallici's sister, Marie). The couple ran the travelling Théâtre Gallici-Rancy 1897-1914, successor to the Théâtre Gallici-Loramus. During off-season months, Henri toured, including Russia in 1912. Memoir is Les Forains peints par eux mêmes (1903). [Dif]

name: Gallici, Pietro
bio: (Lugano, Italy: 16 Sep 1834-12 Jan 1897) Son of a merchant family, running away from home at age 17. Learned magic working in a German circus for 6 years. Pro illusionist. Brother-in-law of "Loramus", jointly operating the Théâtre Gallici-Loramus at the Orleans fair 1895-97. Died in France. Father of Henri Gallici. [Dif;Vo57]

name: Gallico, Paul [William]
bio: (New York City, NY: 26 Jul 1897-15 Jul 1976) Journalist & novelist of Hungarian ancestry. Introduced by Orson Welles to The Magic Circle in 1959 he became a magic buff & skeptical student of the occult with a large collection of books on the subject. Wrote 40 books including the "Mrs. 'Arris' series & 3 with magic or pseudo-occult themes: Too Many Ghosts (1959), The Hand of Mary Constable (1964), & The Man Who Was Magic (1966). Died in Monaco. [CA]

name: Gallivert
bio: (France: fl.1780s) Self-claimed student of Comus. Played Düsseldorf in 1780. Featured mind-reading & egg tricks. [St]

name: Gallo, Joey
bio: (Buffalo?, New York: c1968-) Son of Lou Gallo & younger brother of Mike Gallo. They inspired him at age 9 to learn magic. By 13 he was performing for adults. Amateur close-up cardman. Tricks in Apocalypse. Also a magic illustrator. [Lo2]

name: Gallo, Lou
bio: (Dunmore, Pennsylvania: c1932-30 Sep 2004) Steelworker (retired in 1986). Learned from a Svengali deck. Learned sleights at age 26. Mentor (since 1960) was Eddie Fechter. Amateur cardman. Invented Gallo Pitch (by 1982). Father of Joey & Mike Gallo. See Kaufman & Phillips, Meet Lou Gallo (1996). [Lo2]

name: Gallo, [Michael] "Mike
bio: (USA: c1956-) Son of Lou Gallo & elder brother of Joey Gallo. Inspired by age 6 watching magicians at Fechter's in Buffalo, New York, where he was raised. Amateur to pro close-up card & coin man. Top demonstrator for Tannen's in early 1980s. Now works private parties. See Stephen Hobbs, Siamese Coins (1996, 44pp). Tricks in New Directions & LR. [Lo2]

name: Galloway, Andrew "Andy
bio: (Benwhat, Ayrshire, Scotland: 12 May 1940-) Learned in 1949 from tricks in a boy's annual. Student of John Ramsay since 1956. Golf club maker. Amateur close-up magician. In late 1980s had 3 fingers of right hand crushed by a hydraulic vise. Wrote The Ramsay Legend (1969, 62pp; repr 1975; 2nd revised ed 1985), The Ramsay Classics (1977, 108pp), Diverting Card Magic (1980, 56pp), & The Ramsay Finale (1982). Articles in Abra, Pabular, & Magic Circular. Video (1985; reissued 1989). [Wh2]

name: Galvin, Wallace
bio: (Louisville, Kentucky: fl. 1st decade of 1900s-20s) Pro vaude manip & Chinese rings act by 1908. Toured Europe 1908-09 (including England in 1908), Europe 1910-13, Australia 1915, & England 1922. Known for his comedy multiple eggs-from-empty-hat production, which he used by 1915. [Pr;Wal]

name: Gambini
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Christian Gambin. Comedy magician living in Sarcelles.

name: Gambliano, Signor
bio: See: Gambling, John

name: Gambling, John
bio: (England: 1870-24 Mar 1954) Pro of the old school since 1888. Aka "Signor Gambliano". Toured Algeria & Morocco. British Ring President 1951-52. Column in Hughes' News. [Vo56;St;HMM8/50]

name: Gamolo
bio: See: Molovinsky, Gale

name: Gamulecki, Anton
bio: See: Hamulecki, Anton

name: Gancia, Mike
bio: (England: fl.1970s-2000s) Stage name of Michael Gillam. Close-up magician. Popular compere. Tricks in New Talon, etc. President, British Ring, 2001-2003.

name: Gandon, François-Antoine
bio: (Paris, France: 26 Jul 1812-11 Nov 1864) Pro second-sight act with young nephew. Wrote La seconde vue dévoilée (1849). [Dif;Ch]

name: Ganinet II
bio: (Germany: fl.1920s-30s) Eccentric magician billed as "Der Mann mit den 1000 Tricks". Best known for his glove trick.

name: Gann, [Ronald L.] "Ronnie
bio: (USA: c1934-1 Feb 2001) Pianist, singer, & ham radio magazine editor. Semi-pro conjuror since 1955 as "Rogan the Magician". Pro close-up since 1959 as "Mr. Mystery". Bought Holden's Magic Studio in Boston in 1963 & closed it in 1966 thru bankruptcy. Then performed ESP until the 1980s. Died of myelofibrosis. Edited Holden's Holdouts 1963-64 (4 issues) as house organ. Wrote The Wizard of Odds (1963). [NJ#17]

name: Gans, Arthur D [aniel Joseph]
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 4 Aug 1890-1963) Semi-pro since 1904 as "Gans, The Modern Magician". Specialties: silks, flags, paper tear, slate & spiritualistic effects. Worked as safety agent for the B&O Railway, doing magic lectures on safety. Sid Lorraine believed he was "probably first" in USA to use magic in lectures to the laity. Attended the 1926 IBM convention. [WWM]

name: Ganson, John Herbert "Jack
bio: (Leeds?, England: 1886-1951) Pub manager and, since around 1910 in London, bar magician, possibly the world's first. Father of Lewis Ganson.

name: Ganson, Lewis "Lew
bio: (London, England: 15 Apr 1913-22 Dec 1980) Pro close-up (except for time in Royal Army Ordnance Corps 1939-58, rising from private to lieutenant-colonel). Edited The Gen 1958-70. 1968 AMA Literary Fellowship. Died in London. Prolific editor & author of 58 books & booklets since 1946, including Routined Manipulation (3 volumes, 1950-54, 118pp+133pp+254pp), Magic of the Mind (1959, 114pp), & the partly auto-biographical The Ganson Book (1982). Several of these books are devoted to specific magicians: Endfield, Vernon, Slydini, Malini, Ron MacMillan, Marconick, & Faucett Ross. Many tricks in Abra & Gen. Memoir is The Ganson Story

name: Ganthony, Robert
bio: (2 audiotapes). See also Will Ayling, Ganson Supreme (1988). (Britain: -11 Mar 1931) Society entertainer, vent. Wrote Practical Ventriloquism and its Sister Arts (1893, 155pp; repr 1938, 116pp), Amateur Entertainments (1893, 66pp), Bunkum Entertainments (London: 1895, 188pp; pirated reprint as Kellar's Variety Entertainments, Chicago: 1901, 188pp), Random Recollections (1899, 244pp), and "A Thousand Miles a Minute", a magical farce presented at St. George's Hall in 1913. [Cl; Daw2]

name: Garance, Jean
bio: (Geneva, Switzerland: 1 Apr 1937-) Stage name of Jean-Marie Peretti. Pro with general magic. Edited Magicus in early 1960s. Acquired the fine old A. Blind collection. Bought Sauty's magic shop in 1967, operating it initially as the "Académie de Magie Jean Garance" then as "Le Truc Store" in Geneva 1967-present. Stage act with assistant-wife Line Garance. FISM President 1990-91. Tricks in Revue de la Prestidigitation. [Xe;Bou]

name: Garcia, Frank
bio: (New York City, NY: 8 May 1927-15 Jul 1993) Son of Spanish-born parents. Inspired at age 9 seeing David "Fú-Manchu" Bamberg show in NYC in 1937. Learned around age 11 by buying books (including Erdnase). Debut c1942. Pro since 1945. Worked at Holden's 1948-50, ending as manager. Billed as "The Man With The Million Dollar Hands". Invented Utilo Cup (1953). Joined the staff at Tannen's in late 1958. Also noted expert on gambling cheating methods. Co-founder (with George Schindler) of the School for Magicians (in New York City) 1973-78. Wrote Frank Garcia's Sponge Balls (1959, 14pp), Frank Garcia's Billiard Balls (1960, 23pp), Marked Cards and Loaded Dice (1962, 274pp), Million Dollar Card Secrets (1972, 128pp), Super Subtle Card Miracles (1973, 214pp), Million Dollar Card Secrets (1974, 96pp), All in a Nutshell (1974, 81pp); with French tr by G. Lammertijn, 45pp), Amedeo's Continental Magic (1974, 115pp), with George Schindler, Magic with Cards (1975, 175pp), with George Schindler; repr), The Encyclopedia of Sponge Ball Magic (1976, 224pp); German tr as Das Lexikon der Schaumgummiball, 1976), Wild Card Miracles (1977, 147pp), Exclusive Card Miracles (1980, 76pp), Exclusive Card Secrets (1980, 80pp), etc. See Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Frank Garcia (1979, in French). Tricks in Phoenix, New Phoenix, HMM, Chronicles, Magic, etc. Did "New York News" column for Magic Manuscript. Videos (1983, 1985, 1986). [Se]

name: Garcimore
bio: (France: fl.1970s) Pro. Starred in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique 1976-77. Wrote Les secrets du magicien (1976).

name: Garden, Bert
bio: (Hannover, Germany: 17 Jul 1931-) Stage name of Albert Ganzo (or Granzo). Pro juggler & magician since 1954. [Mül]

name: Gardii, Teodor
bio: See: Ivanov, Fyodor G.

name: Gardner, John [Edmund], AIMC
bio: (Seaton Delaval, Northumberland, England: 20 Nov 1926-) Learned magic at age 9 from a Gamagic magic set. Pro magician with American Red Cross Entertainments Department 1943-44. Royal Marine Commando 1944-46 with commission in 1945. At Cambridge U 1947-50 with BA & MA. Member of Pentacle Club 1947-50. Anglican Church priest in mid-1950s. Theater & arts reviewer 1958-63. Pro novelist since 1963 with 40+ novels, including 13 James Bond spy novels since 1979. Magic figures in passing in some of these books but runs full bore in Confessor (1995, 394pp). Since c1990 has returned to magic as amateur with closeup & mental magic, which he performs at charity & benefit shows. AIMC 1994. Pet effects: Triumph & Book Tests. [Thaumaturgist11/94 & 3/95; Writers' Directory: Who's Who in Spy Fiction; Murder Ink; Wh5]

name: Gardner, Martin [nmn]
bio: (Tulsa, Oklahoma: 21 Oct 1914 – 22 May 2010) Inspired by & learned at age c10 from father's papers-on-knife trick & later from local Tulsa magic buffs, including Roy "Wabash" Hughes, Logan Waite, & Roger Montandon. Took Tarbell Course. Amateur close-up magician, specialized in cards. Lived in Chicago for 20 years, taking a BA in philosophy & meeting the magic inner circle of Dorny, Marlo, Platt, etc. In 1947 moved to New York, associating with the inner circle of Vernon, Daley, Curry, etc. 1975 AMA Literary Fellowship. Moved to Hendersonville, North Carolina c1980. Professional writer, particularly in science & puzzle fields: In the Name of Science (1952), Science: Good, Bad and Bogus (1981), the "Mathematical Games" column for Scientific American 1957-1982, etc. A man of many talents, he also edited The Annotated Alice (1960). Has used the pen name "George Groth" occasionally since c1936, but only on non-magical works. Invented Lie Speller (c1935). On magic wrote Match-ic (1935, 26pp), After the Desert (1940, 21pp), 12 Tricks with a Borrowed Deck (1940, 22pp; repr 1964), Cut the Cards (1942, 34pp), Over the Coffee-Cups (1949, 34pp), Mathematics, Magic and Mystery (1956, 174pp, which is also a force book where 15th word of every chapter is "of"), Encyclopedia of Impromptu Magic (1978, based on his 1951-58 series of articles in Hugard's Magic Monthly), How Not to Test a Psychic (1989), & 3 booklets. Also wrote (under pen name of "Uriah Fuller") 2 delightful exposé booklets on Uri Geller: Confessions of a Psychic (1975, 41pp) Further Confessions of a Psychic (1979, 70pp), & Martin Gardner Presents (1993, 424pp). Co-authored (with Bart Whaley & Jeff Busby) The Man Who Was Erdnase (1991, 434pp), which won a SAM Special Library Award. Tricks in Sphinx, Genii, Jinx, New Jinx, Phoenix, New Phoenix, HMM, Swami, Mantra, Arcane, Epoptica, Pallbearers, Epilogue, Linking Ring, Ibidem, etc. [Magic4/94;Bo2;CA;Th;Wh2]

name: Gardner, Roy
bio: (West Germany: 29 Mar 1952-) Stage name of Reinhard Haase. Semi-pro magician. 1973 Düsseldorf "Magic Up-to-Date" Convention Grand Prix. 1976 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic with partner Wittus Witt. Articles in The Magic Magazine, Magic Info, & Magische Welt.

name: Garenne, Professor Henri
bio: (Britain: fl.1860s-1890s) Stage name of "Dr." H. Frank Lind. Minor pro from 1864 to 1895, mixing anti-spiritualistic demos with straight magic. Wrote The Art of Modern Conjuring, Magic, and Illusions [1886, 351pp], a partial plagiarism of Hoffmann's Modern Magic. [CI]

name: Garland, Maurice
bio: (London, England: fl.1890s-1910s) Learned magic as a boy. Cigar shop owner & amateur magician to pro society magician. Noted practical joker. A founding member of The Magic Circle in 1905.

name: Garmijn, Jean
bio: (Brugge, Belgium: 4 May 1943-) Learned at age 16 solo thru dealers. Stage name: "Gardini". Mentor of Dirk De Graeve & Jos Denys. Social worker to full-time magic dealer since 1976. Co-director Mephisto-Huis 1974-1986. Co-founder & co-director (with Jos Denys) Select Magic in Kortrijk 1987-present. [Wh5]

name: Garnier [pronounced GAR-nee-ay]
bio: (France: fl.1750s-60s) Aka "Le Menteur" [the Liar]. Pro sleight-of-hand with cards & Cups-and-Balls plus marionnettes & mechanical figures. Played the St.-Germain fair in 1751. [CI]

name: Garnier, Jacques
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Amateur magic historian & collector in Orléans. Wrote Bénévol, maître du mystère (1969).

name: Garrett, Dan[iel Edward], AIMC
bio: (Valdosta, Georgia: 5 Sep 1951- ) Grew up in Douglas, Georgia. Learned from library books at age 10. Pro magician since c1966, working cabaret, close-up, trade, & kid shows (as "Dan the Wizard"). BS in Physics from Georgia Tech. 1979 TAOM Close-Up Trophy. Mail-order dealer (wholesale-retail) of some dozen original tricks (as "Dan Garrett Magic") in Lithonia, Georgia. Columnist ("Pandora's Box") in M-U-M c1985-present. AIMC 1987. Wrote Close Up Connivery lectures #1 (9pp) & #2 (1988, 20pp). Article in Magic Menu. Video: Close-Up Connivery (1991). SAM President 1994-95. [MUM8/94;MUM11/85;LR9/88;Lo2;Wh]

name: Garrett, Teral
bio: (Albany, Kentucky: 8 Jun 1914-1970) Inspired at age 12. Pro debut in 1935. Preferred mental magic. Mail-order dealer (Teral Garrett's Magic Shop) in hometown 1940s-50s. Edited The Corsair 1940-45?, Magic Banner, & Psycho-Gizmo 1951-65. Wrote Magicians' Directory Encyclopedia (Vol.1, 1946, 18pp), Twenty-Six Living and Dead Tests (1948, 29pp), Publicity Miracles, etc. Pen name as "Psycho" since 1952. Articles in Tops, Dragon, & Linking Ring. [Th;St]

name: Garrus, J[ames] T[aylor]
bio: (Orlando, Florida: 4 May 1908- ) Amateur. In Dec 1928, when met by Sid Lorraine, he was an undergraduate at Cambridge U (Peterhouse), 1926-30, first in Modern Languages, then in Law. While there he was Secretary of the Pentacle Club, the campus magic society. Noteworthy because he introduced the Center Tear to Lorraine who then diffused it to other magicians. Returned to Chicago in 1931 to enter the Illinois Bar. Got Cambridge M.A. in 1934. Still in Illinois in 1961 when Cambridge U lost track. "Garth the Magician" SEE: Davies, Garth W. Pryce Gartner, C. A. (Germany: fl. first decade of 1900s). Amateur magician. Wrote Amüsante Künste und Wissenschaften [1906, 3 vols, 111+142+136pp] & Gedankenlesen und Hellsehen (1907, 136pp).

name: Garvin-Bellachini
bio: (St. Martin, Rheinfalz, Germany: 12 Apr 1886-5 Oct 1969) Stage name of Franz Schweizer. Pro manip & illusionist since age 17, at first as "Franzardi", later as "Garvin". Trouped a six-person company through Germany. Lived in Ehrenfriedersdorf 1939-50. Died in home town. [Win;St;Al]

name: Gaston
bio: (Austria?: fl.1880s-90s) Stage name of H. Kastner. Amateur comedy magician. Uncle of "Dorini". Articles in Zauberspiegel. [Al]

name: Gatti, Arno
bio:
Gaughan, John "Johnny", MIMC [pronounced GONE] (Knoxville, Tennessee: 1 Nov 1940-) Learned in 1954 at age 14 working for Mark Wilson. Semi-pro in college where he took BA degree in industrial design. Moved to California. An expert mechanic & woodworker, in 1971 he founded own illusion-show design shop (called John Gaughan Associates since 1975 [sic] when joined by Eric Lewis) in Glendale, California. Illusion designer-builder for Mark Wilson (since 1961, while working for Owen Magic Supreme), Reveen, Blackstone Jr, Copperfield (since c1972), Henning (since 1975), André Kole, Siegfried & Roy, Orson Welles (1984), Al Belmont, Francis Ford Coppola, Michael Jackson, & The Pendragons. Associate producer of "Snoopy's World of Magic" touring show since 1989. Inspired in 1974 by Robert Albo to become an apparatus collector & builder-restorer of automata. Has world's largest collection of restored automata, including Kellar's Psycho (1987) and Robert Houdin's Antonio Diavolo & Blooming Orange Tree. Wrote (with Jim Steinmeyer) Antonio Diavolo (1986, 24pp) & The Mystery of Psycho (1987, 64pp). 1971 AMA Award of Merit. 1984 AMA Creative Fellowship. MIMC 1988. SAM Hall of Fame. 1989 Christopher Award for best new illusion. [Genii4/89;Wh]

[See also: Ufer, Arno]

name: Gault, Gilbert
bio: See: Hull, Burling

name: Gaultier, [Albert-]Camille, LL.D.
bio: (Andelys, Eure, France: 24 Jan 1872-20 Dec 1943) Lawyer. Amateur sleight-of-hand magician, having learned on physician's advice to do finger exercises to cure numbness. Wrote the classic La Prestidigitation sans appareils (1914, 558pp) with English tr by Jean Hugard as Magic Without Apparatus (1945, 527pp). Translated Farelli's Card Magic as La Magie des cartes (2 vols, 1937). [Dif: Illusionniste1/14]

name: Gauthron, Maurice
bio: (France: fl.1940s-80s) Engineer. Amateur magician (specialized in cards & coins) & mentalist. 1948 FISM honorable mention for invention. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Interim President 1968. AFAP Silver Medal 1970, Bronze Medal 1971, & Gold Medal 1975. [Bou]

name: Gautier, Louis
bio: (Blackheath, Kent, England: 26 Aug 1866-25 May 1943) Portrait painter. Amateur comedy magician. President, The Magicians' Club, 1930-34. [Go;Go2]

name: Gavilondo, Duarte
bio: (Cuba: fl.1980s) Pro stage magic. Brother of Luis Gavilondo, often as a double act.

name: Gavilondo, Luis M.
bio: (Cuba: fl.1970s-80s) Brother of Duarte Gavilondo. Pro stage magic with assistant-wife Isora. Tricks in Magigram.

name: Gawariker, R. H.
bio: (Poona, India: 2 Jan 1882- ) Amateur sleights & illusions. Articles. [Go2]

name: Gazeka, Len
bio: (Britain: 1896-12 Apr 1975) Stage name of Leonard Poulton. Pro music hall act as "Gazeka and his magic carpet". [Daw2]

name: Geary, Walter
bio: (England: fl.1930s-50s) As "Wu-Fang-Sing" wrote The Oriental Temple of Magic (1937), Magic for the Bairns (1948), & Effects by Ten Well-Known Magicians (1958). Tricks in Magic Wand.

name: Geddes, [John Reid] "Johnny
bio: (Edinburgh, Scotland: 1918-) Pro kid-show magic & (as "John Reid") comedy magic. Edited Monthly Mirror (1950-52, 21 issues). Also booking agent since 1955. Wrote several booklets, including Gags with Gimmicks (1956, 60pp), It's Strictly Comedy (1958, 12pp), & Dope on Deception (1988, 16pp). Columnist for Magigram. Tricks in Abra, Magic Magazine, etc.

name: Geilen, Wilhelm "Wilt
bio: (Cologne, Germany: 14 [sic] Mar 1880-9 Jul [or Jun] 1974) Of Dutch parentage. Moved to Holland. Circus acrobat until 1920 when turned pro stage magician with vaudeville & full-evening show. Specialized in sleight-of-hand & spiritualistic effects. Toured Paris, London, Vienna, Budapest, Petersburg, Brussels, Riga, etc. Founded Dutch chapter of the German Magic Circle in 1922. In 1936 awarded the German Magic Circle's "Standarte". In prison during WW II. Aka "Professor Melachini" (in Holland), "Melo Smith", & "Dr Caligari". Continued to perform until 1960s. Articles. His bio by Alfred Czernewitz was published in German in 1993 (140pp). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Geiler" & stage name misspelled "Mellachini". [St;Rey;WWM]

name: Geipe, Geo
bio: (Sweden: 7 Jan 1891-1 [sic] Aug 1946) Stage name of Georg Hultgren. Former restauranteur. Pro magician in Sweden. Worked with assistant-wife Ida 1920-30. [St]

name: Geissler-Werry, W[erner]
bio: (Düren, Rheinland, Germany: 13 Apr 1925-Jul 2000) Stage name of Werner Geissler since 1951. Inspired at age 12 seeing a manipulator at fair. Manipulator 1945-70, thence psychic effects. Pro magician, dealer & prop maker ("Trickgerätefabrik") in Düren-Niederau, West Germany, since 1950. Founder-editor Die "Magische" Welt 1952-present. Received the Golem statue (Prague Magicians) in 1973 for best European magic journal. Awarded the Hofsinzer Ring by Punx in 1985, being its 4th recipient. Inventor & manufacturer of over 100 tricks, including Vanishing Coke Bottle, Durania Multiplying Billiard Balls, Blitz-Cocktail, Brainwave Coin Box, & Magic with Poker Chips, which Erhard Liebenow made world famous. Also made appearing candles & can (after 1970) es of sheet plastic (copying Fantasio). Wrote Die gezwungene Wahl (1955). Articles in Magische Welt, Magie, Magic Around the World, etc. [Wh2] SEE: Tucker, Stephen

name: Geller, Uri
bio: (Tel Aviv, Israel: 20 Dec 1946-) Son of a Hungarian Jewish immigrant. Self-proclaimed psychic. Pet effects: metal bending & teleportation. Pro since 1969. Thence a world celebrity with debuts in USA in 1972, England in 1973, Australia & New Zealand in 1975, etc. Lives in London. Autobio is My Story (1975, with John Fuller). See also Martin Ebon (ed), The Amazing Uri Geller (1975, 168pp). Good exposés by skeptics are Uriah Fuller [pseudonym of Martin Gardner], Confessions of a Psychic (1975, 41pp); Uriah Fuller, Further Confessions of a Psychic (1979, 70pp); James Randi, The Magic of Uri Geller (1975, 308pp); James Randi, The Truth about Uri Geller (1982); Ben Harris, Gellerism Revealed (1985, 95pp). [Ran]

name: Gemmill, Paul Fleming
bio: See: "Fleming, Paul"

name: Gemmill, Walker
bio: See: "Fleming, Walker"

name: Gentleman Jack
bio: See: Iversen, Tommy

name: Geoffrey, Douglas
bio:
George, The Great (Zanesville, Ohio: 1887-14 Sep 1958) Stage name of Grover G. [sic] George, aka "George the Magician". Debut at age 10. Pro illusionist, playing mainly in Latin America, eventually retiring in Brazil. [Pr;Ho;Bam,p.129]

[See also: Mackentosh, Douglas Geoffrey]

name: George, Douglas H[enry] "Doug
bio: (Wellington, New Zealand: 20 Apr 1920-2004) Learned 1927-29 by watching pros. Sign-writer & painter. Semi-pro general magician as "The Amazing Mr Douglas" since age 16. Pet effects: Passe Bottles & Sword Box. Assistant to John Calvert (in New Zealand in 1950) & Benyon and repaired equipment for Virgil. [Magicana6/87;Wh5]

name: Gerard, Erik [E.]
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 19 Nov 1955- ) Learned around age 10 from gift magic set. Pro comedy magician since 1980. Aka "The Wizard and Oz" (his parakeet assistant). Since 1987 works also with assistant Dianne Lind, marrying her at the Magic Castle in 1989. They play cruise ships, casinos, & amusement parks. Lecturer. Articles in Genii. [Geni11/87; Mag; Wh2]

name: Gerats, [Ferdinand Alexander] "Ferry
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 2 Mar 1950-) Learned in 1958 from books. Pro comedy close-up, stage, & mental magic since 1983, working as "Ferry" until 1986 & as "Ferry Gerats" since then. Invented Vacuum Clean Card Rise in 1979. 7 awards from Dutch Magical Union 1976-80. 1979 FISM 3rd prize in comedy magic. Co-director Hocus 1980-85. Wrote Spelen met de Bottom (1986, 16pp). Tricks in Hocus & Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]

name: Gerber, [Herrick Martin] "Rick
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 14 Jan 1958-) Learned at age 5 from parent's gift tricks. Pro close-up, stage, & nightclub magician and balloon sculptor since age 20. In 1973 became 1st Junior Member of Magic Castle. As the "Official Anheuser-Busch Magician" since 1973, believes he may be "the only full-time corporate magician in the world". TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Gerhardt, Michael J.
bio: (Tettnang, West Germany: 19 Feb 1958-) Inspired in 1960s seeing Silvan doing card manip on TV. Learned from books. 1981 MZvD 3rd prize in card magic. Pro club close-up & trade-show magician with cards & coins since 1984. Aka "Kowa". Pet effects: Himber Ring, Rising Cards, Color Changing Hanks. Works West Germany, Switzerland, Austria, & cruise ships. Wrote Feinheiten (1982, 42pp). Effects in Apocalypse, Linking Ring, Magische Welt, Aladin, Magie, & in books by Lorayne and Mendoza. Does German translations of the books of Michael Ammar. [Lo;Wh2]

name: Germain, Karl
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 12 Feb 1878-9 Aug 1959 [sic]) Stage name since 1898 (spelled "Germaine" from 1899 to 1906) of Charles Mattmueller Jr. Learned in 1886. Then in 1892 father gave him Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Debut in 1893. Pro stage magician & illusionist. A star of both Lyceum (since 1899) & Chautauqua (1905-16). In 1906-07 toured the British Isles, including 1 month at St. George's Hall. An elegant, skilled, & highly innovative magician whose stage career was ended by blindness in 1916. Invented Germain Water Jars (1908) & Rabbit Tray (in or by 1906). Possibly invented the first dove routine and the full-light spirit séance. See Stuart Cramer, The Secrets of Karl Germain (1962, 70pp). Bio is Stuart Cramer, Germain the Wizard and His Legerdemain (1966, 152pp). [Pr; Magicol5/89]

name: Gerrard
bio: (England, fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Arthur Gerrard Goad. Pro with full-evening show.

name: Gertner, Paul
bio: (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 1953-) Stage name of Paul Joseph Gaertner. Learned at age 16 from library book & then lessons from Ron Slanina. Pro close-up since 1975, specializing in trade shows at which he is widely rated among world's top six, earning (in 1996) reportedly earned up to $2,500 per day. Taught Gary Michaels in 1975. Invented Reverse Matrix in 1979. 1978 Tokyo 2nd prize. 1983 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. 1985 FISM 1st prize in close-up. 1996 AMA Close-up Magician of the Year. Authored 2 sets of lecture notes (1978, 1987) & Forcing a Card in the Classical Manner (1980). See Richard Kaufman, Paul Gertner's Steel and Silver (1994, 200+pp). Articles in MUM, Linking Ring, & Arcane, plus Japanese, French, & Italian journals. TV bits in USA, Japan, & Britain, including 3 times on the Carson show. [Lo;Magic5/92;Wh2]

name: Géry, Dr Jacques
bio: (France: fl.1940s) Amateur in Metz. Wrote Les principles brillants de la manipulation des cartes (1949, 114pp, with preface by & photos of Jean Valton). [HMM4/50]

name: Gesbert, Alain
bio: (Paris, France: 9 Feb 1956- ) Learned at age 9 from books. Electronics engineer. Amateur magician specialized in mentalism & bizarre magick. Founding chairman of Mindon Mania 1989-present. Wrote Etat de Rêves (1988, 35pp). Articles in Revue de la Prestidigitation, Magicus Journal, & Apotecari. [Wh2]

name: Ghosh, Professor S. C.
bio: (Calcutta, India: fl.1880s-early 1900s) Pro with both Western & authentic Indian magic. In 1882 in Calcutta co-founded the Friends' Necromantic Association, the predecessor of the Indian Magicians Club. Played Paris in 1900 during a world tour with a large illusion show. [St]

name: Giampaoli, Ugo
bio: (Terracina, Italy: 24 Jul 1905- ) A midget. Pro magician. [Dif]

name: Gibbons, Robert C[harles] "Bob
bio: (Syracuse, New York: 24 May 1942- ) Learned as a child & then as hobbyist. At age 33 (c1975) left job to become full-time pro stage & comedy magician, working trade shows, fairs, & parties with partner-wife Cathy ("Sweetheart the Clown"). Also clown & dealer (magic & clown supplies). Founder-publisher Laugh-Makers 1982-present. Column in Laugh-Makers. [Wh2]

name: Gibson, Litzka Raymond
bio: See: Raymond, Litzka

name: Gibson, Walter B[rown]
bio: (Germantown, Pennsylvania: 12 Sep 1897-6 Dec 1985) Inspired by & learned magic at age 13 from Mysto Magic set & later from reading Neil's The Modern Conjurer. Professional writer of non-fiction (by 1922) and fiction (since 1931). Semi-pro magician. Associate Editor of The Magic World 1920-24. Managed a Philadelphia magic shop in the mid-1920s. Edited Tales of Magic and Mystery 1927-28 (5 issues) and Seven Circles 1931-34. 1939 Sphinx Amateur Medal. Co-edited (with Bruce Elliott) Phoenix 1942-44, edited Conjurors' Magazine 1945-48. Married Litzka Raymond in 1949, his third wife. 1971 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1979 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame 1990. Invented the Amazing Card Location = Master Card Location (in 1920s), Nickels to Dimes (by 1926), the Double Bill Tube (c1927), & Oil and Water in 1940. The most prolific ghost-writer (some of the books "by" Thurston [1922-29], Blackstone [since 1929], Dunninger, Radner, & Kreskin) & author in magic, with over 50 full-sized books. These include The World's Best Book of Magic (1927, 319pp), The Book of Secrets (1927), The Bunco Book (1927, 96pp; 1946 revised, 114pp), Houdini's Escapes (1930, 317pp), Houdini's Magic (1932), Professional Magic for Amateurs (1947, 225pp; repr 1948 & 1974), Magic Explained (1949, 188pp; repr 1958), The Master Magicians (1966, 221pp), The Complete Illustrated Book of Card Magic (1969, 470pp), Popular Card Tricks (1972, 48pp), Mark Wilson Course in Magic (1975, with Mark Wilson), The Complete Illustrated Book of Close-Up Magic (1980), & Walter Gibson's Big Book of Magic for All Ages (1980). Tricks in Magic World. NOTE: Although Houdini hired Gibson as his ghost writer for a series of simple tricks, Houdini died too soon for any to appear. A literary phenomenon, Gibson wrote over 300 novels & 1,500 publications using more than 60 pseudonyms, including 282 as "Maxwell Grant" (since 1931 [sic]) for his "The Shadow" series (1931 [sic] thru 1949), a character that he took from the popular radio series. A 22-page bio is William V. Rauscher, Walter B. Gibson: Man of Letters and Literature (1986). A 382-page bibliography of his writings is J. Randolph Cox, Man of Magic and Mystery: A Guide to the Work of Walter B. Gibson (1988). [Bo#189;Se;Th;Buf]

name: Giczi, István
bio: (Hungary: fl.1980s) Pro childrens magician.

name: Giddings, Alfred [James]
bio: (Luton, England: 29 Nov 1872-19 Feb 1948) Aka "Arthur Marriott". Pro two-person mind-reading act with wife as "The Marriotts" (including 9 months at St. George's Hall in 1908); and then since 1910 as "The Zomahs". Toured South Africa, Australia (1912), & New Zealand. Later toured USA, Canada, & West Indies. Founded the Institute of Magicians in 1934. [St;Wal]

name: Gifford, Bob
bio: (USA: -19 Nov 1945) Pro magician of the old school. Worked circus. Later a side-show fire-eater as "Professor Gifford".

name: Giglio, Vincenzo
bio: (Capua, Italy: 23 Dec 1892-4 Dec 1965) Chancellor in Naples. Amateur magician & collector. Founded Ring 108 Napoli, the 1st IBM "Ring" in Italy. [Magia Moderna1965]

name: Gilbert, A[Ifred] C[arlton]
bio: (Salem, Oregon: 15 Feb 1884-24 Jan 1961) Interested at age 12. Learned when Alexander Herrmann "showed me simple tricks" after a show. Pro performer. Held world's record in the pole vault 1908-09. Pro dealer in New Haven 1908-16 when he joined John Petrie's Mysto Mfg. Co. as co-owner. Thence (after Petrie left) into general toy making as The A.C. Gilbert Co., 1916-1952 when retired. Famous for his Mysto Magic sets, Erector sets (which he invented), Gilbert Chemistry sets, & American Flyer trains. Wrote Gilbert's Handkerchief Tricks (1920), Gilbert Knots & Splices and Rope-tying Tricks (1920), & Magnetic Fun (1920). Autobio is A.C. Gilbert & Marshall McClintock, The Man Who Lives in Paradise (1954; 374pp; facsimile repr 1997). [Magic1/93;SAM;WWA]

name: Gilbert, Blair L.
bio: (Horicon, Wisconsin: c1870-26 [or 28?] Nov 1947) Radio dealer. Semi-pro mail-order magic dealer (Gilbert Novelty Magic Company, "Gilmagico", & B.L. Gilbert Co.) in Chicago by 1919-1931-? with house organ as Gilbert's Magical Broadcaster. Wrote The Gilbert Papers (1973 revised, 222pp). [Dor]

name: Gilberti
bio: (Italy: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Marino Giberna. Semi-pro magician. In 1971 founded the Scuola dei Piccoli Prestigatori di Trieste, a school for young magicians in Trieste.

name: Gilbreath, Norman L.
bio: (USA: 31 Mar 1936-) Computer expert in Los Angeles. Amateur magician. Invented the Gilbreath Principle by 1955 & published it in Jul 1958 issue of Linking Ring. Invented Color Magnets in late 1950s & published it in 1966. His theoretical booklet, Magic For An Audience, was published as a series of 3 articles in Genii (Mar, Apr, May 1989). [Wh2]

name: Gili, José Florence
bio: See: Florencees Gili, José

name: Gill, Richard [Saxby], MIMC
bio: (Hindhead, Surrey, England: 28 Mar 1938-) Learned from book. Debut at age 12 as "Richard Gilligan". At 18 became a circus illusionist as "Ivanov Khan" & finally as "Peter Petroff", working British, French, & Spanish circuses. Also worked marionettes as "Croc" & did mind reading as "Ashdown". Founder-director Polka Children's Theatre in London 1967-88. Toured own illusion shows in 1969, 1971, 1974, 1977, 1988-89. [MC1/89;Wh2]

name: Gill, Robert G. "Bob
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s) Librarian. Amateur magician. Wrote Magic as a Performing Art: A Bibliography of Conjuring (1976, 252pp), for which he won the 1976 Bowker Bibliography Prize, surprising considering the high percentage of errors. Articles in Magigram.

name: Gillis, Brian
bio: (Niagara Falls, New York: 1970s-90s) Tutored by Eddie Fechter. Pro (ex-teacher & businessman) close-up at theme shows, clubs, & restaurants. HBO-TV segment. [Jef;Mag]

name: Ginn, David [Franklin]
bio: (Atlanta, Georgia: 13 Jun 1946- ) Learned in 1958 (age 11) from Boy Scout friend. Amateur, then since 1971, pro kid-show & school-show magician. His sometime assistant-wife is Lynne (née Miller) whom he married in 1969. Pet effect: stage sponge-ball production with 3"-4" balls. Wrote 47 books & booklets since 1969, including Magic that Moves Me (1971, 78pp), Professional Magic for Children (1976, 244pp), Colorful Magic (1980, 112pp), Kidbiz (1982, c300pp; 2 reprints), Nearly Unpublished (1989, 56pp), & Laughter Legacy (1998, 224pp). Wrote "Entertaining Children" column in MUM c1977-present. Edits Autumn's Leaflet 1980-present. Audios (1984, 1985). 2 videos (1989, 1990). [Wh2]

name: Giobbi, Barbara
bio: See: Giobbi, Roberto

name: Giobbi, Roberto
bio: (Basle, Switzerland: 1 May 1959 - ) Learned magic in 1973 from library books. Amateur close-up 1973 to 1988 when turned pro. 1987 MZvD Writer of the Year. 1988 & 1991 FISM 2nd prizes for card magic. 1991 Grand Prix at Swiss congress. Translator of books by Ascanio, Tamariz, Cir & Nops, Marconick, Burghardo into English, German, & French. One of 35 members of the prestigious Escuela Magica de Madrid and contributor to their La Circular. Wrote over 50 books (including translations) & booklets, including The Cardmanship of Roberto Giobbi (1985); A Gambler's Dream (1986); Card Stories (1986); Fantasia in As-Dur (1987); CardPerfect (1987); Roberto-light (1988); Roberto Extra-Light (1992); Roberto Super-Light (1995); Grosse Kartenschule 1-5 (1992, 1994, 2003), which was translated into 6 languages, into English as Card College, V.1 (1995, 250pp), V.2 (1996, 250pp), V.3 (1998, 300pp), V.4 (2000, 315pp) & V.5 (2003, 330pp). Articles in over 50 magazines: Pabular, Arcane (France), Journal de la Prestidigitation, Abracadabra (GB), Magie, Magische Welt, Hokus-Pokus, Qui Magia, Magical Arts Journal, regular column "The Genii Session" in Genii. 3 videos (1988) and 2 DVDs (2001 & 2004). Ebooks: Grosse Kartenschule 1&2, Card College 1&2, Ask Roberto, A Gambler's Dream. Documentary (50 min.) II Giardino dei Giochi Segreti by Swiss TV TSI. His wife Barbara Giobbi has been illustrator of Hokus-Pokus, Magie and other periodicals as well as of Roberto's books since 1986. [Wh2]

name: Giordmaine, John [Nichol] "Johnny", MIMC
bio: (Rabato, Malta: 26 Sep 1898-19 Jan 1974) Stage name of Giovanni Nicola Giodmaina. Learned magic in 1908. Moved to Canada in 1919 at age 17 & settled in Toronto 2 years later. Electrical engineer for 10 years until 1931. Semi-pro magician since 1926 & pro since 1931 billed as "The Gay Magician". Demoed in Whitlam's magic shop until 1930. Toured N. America & Europe. On 28 Aug 1933 became first magician to appear on TV in Canada, performing live in Toronto on closed-circuit at Eaton's department store where he sold magic in the magic, games, & toys department from 1930 to 1960. Many TV bits including the Ed Sullivan Show in 1957. The 5-foot tall magician died in Toronto soon after a heart attack. Tricks in Genii. [LR3/74;Bo3;Ran;SAM;St;WWM]

name: Giorgio, Tony
bio: (New York City, NY: c1923 – 1 Feb 2012) Inspired at age 9 by seeing Blackstone, Gwynne, and Cardini. Pitched magic sets as first job. Did magic in carnival side show at age 13. Semi-pro card man & close-up. Also movie & TV actor. Articles in Genii. Edited "Magicana" column in Genii since 1992. 1993 AMA Close-up Magician of the Year. [Mag]

name: Giovanni, Dr.
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 23 Nov 1896 [sic]-Aug 1977) A Jew. Stage name of Adolph Herczog. Studied medicine in youth. Pro comedy magic & pickpocket act, introducing the latter in London in 1929. Pet effect: Ring on Wand. Played the New York Palace in 1932. Entertained President Roosevelt, King George VI, & Winston Churchill. Toured USA 1944, Canada 1952, Brazil 1953, & Japan 1957. [Vo57;Ran;Bo2;Dif;Tay;Ho]

name: Giovenzana, Luigi
bio: (Milan, Italy: 1885-1953) Pro dealer.

name: Girardelli, Monsieur Benserade
bio: (Switzerland?: fl.1820s-30s) Of Italian parentage. Learned from uncle Châlons. Pro in Paris. Toured Britain in 1825. Retired in 1834. [Cl;Fr]

name: Girardelli, Josephine
bio: (Venice?, Italy: fl.1810s) Aka "The Fire-Proof Female from Germany". Toured England in 1814. [Jay;Cl]

name: Giraud, Jules
bio: See: "Warlock, Peter"

name: Gironda, Ralph
bio:
Giulani, Georges SEE UNDER: Tschunggmałl, Christian

[See also: Fulves, Karl]

name: Givan, [Joseph P.] "Joe
bio: (Greeley, Colorado: 25 Sep 1962-) Learned at age 4 from mother's Xmas gift of magic set. Pro close-up & stage magician & lecturer. Billed as "The Supernaturalist". 1987 IBM Gold Cups award. 1988 FISM 1st prize for close-up. Pet effects: Spirit Cabinet, Ring in Gum Machine, & Stick to Snake. Invented Test of Time (1987). Wrote Magic from the Attic (1987, 30pp). Articles in Genii & Magical Arts Journal. TV bit in Britain. [LR6/97; Genii10/91; Jef; Wh5]

name: Gladfelter, Dr John H[enry], PhD
bio: (Tomahawk, Wisconsin: 17 Oct 1926-) Psychologist. Learned at age 9 from books. Amateur mentalist & close-up performer since then. Pet effect: Red Hot Mama. Edited Circle 1958-65. TAOM President 1964-65. [Wh2]

name: Gleason, Jackie
bio: (Brooklyn, New York : 26 Feb 1916-24 Jun 1987) Born Herbert John Gleason. Amateur magician & practical joker. Comedian from clubs to TV & film stardom. By 1951 his TV "Reggie Van Gleason" character sometimes did a burlesque magic act or his "Poor Soul" character would stooge for guest magicians like Russell Swan. Bios are W.J. Weatherby, Jackie Gleason (1992, 2522) & Jim Dishon. The Golden Ulysses (1956). Bios are W.J. Weatherby, Jackie Gleason (1992, 253pp) & Jim Bishop, The Golden Ham (1956). [HMM9/51, 7/53; Katz]

name: Glen, Laurence
bio: See: Spitari, Laurance W.

name: Glennan, Al
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Stage name of Glenn Walters. Stage magic & manip. 1986 British Ring Shield & Dittia Shield. Glenroy the Midget (USA: 30 Nov 1887-12 Jun 1919) Stage name of Glen Mead Royston.

name: Gloria
bio: (Langendreher, Germany: 28 Feb 1918-13 Nov 1985) Stage name of Anneliese Voss. On 7 Feb 1942 [sic] became 2nd wife of Helmut "Kalanag" Schreiber. Daughter, Brigitte Schreiber, born Jan 1944. Pro star assistant to him since 1947 as "Gloria de Voss". Separated from Kalanag in 1960 when she was replaced, successively, by Nana Gualdi & Anita Schmitt (billed as "Angela Ferrari" & "Madame Schmidt"). Died in Stadthagen. NOTE: Kalanag's claims that she was Swedish or Danish were mere publicity hype. [Dif;Roh]

name: Gloria, Giovanni
bio: (Venice, Italy: 17 Jun 1882-27 Jun 1958) Pro magician. Toured a magic & film show thru Germany, Switzerland, & France before WW I. Discharged from Italian Army, he moved permanently to Nice, France, in 1918. Charter member of the Amicale des Magiciens du Sud-Est (Nice) 1936. Wrote Les trucs du lacet (1950). Died in Nice. [St]

name: Gloviczki, Peter [pronounced Glow-vicky]
bio: (Hungary: fl.1970s-90s) Semi-pro manipulator & illusionist. 1973 FISM 2nd prize in manip. Known for his "Peter's Plexi Prediction" (by 1974) & "Real Linking Ropes" (marketed by Tenyo in 1990). Moved to USA and became a heart surgeon at Mayo Clinic. [LR8/97]

name: Glow, [Aubrey] Brian
bio: (Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada: 4 May 1957-) Inspired at age c8 seeing Ed Sullivan TV show & self-taught from library books. Pro illusionist & illusion builder since 1973. Specializes in spectacles combining magic, music, dance, & pyrotechnics for plays, operas, & symphonies. Since c1985 directs largest (10 to 24 persons) touring illusion show ("Fantasy Unlimited") in Canada. Invented several fire illusions, including Flaming Pyramid of Death. 1-man issue of New Invocation (forthcoming). Article in Magic Menu. [Wh2]

name: Glowacz, Ottokar
bio: (Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 1883-1942) Illusionist. Long-time President of Prague Magic Club. In WW II arrested by the Gestapo & perished in the Nazi concentration camp at Majdanek, Poland. [Mec]

name: Gloye, Dr Eugene E[rnest], PhD [pronounced GLOY]
bio: (Michigan City, Indiana: 29 Aug 1927-) Inspired at age 12 seeing Ed Reno. Learned from original Tarbell Course. Debut at age 15. Began as an outdoor showman in the Midwest, continuing as a semi-pro illusionist while in college studying psychology. Tutored Dick Cavett, launching him as a semi-pro magician. Psychologist by profession (with PhD in 1954). Amateur magician. Invented Watch Out (1946), Fan-Ta-Bill (1947), Mazda Glass (1955), Double Exposure (c1956), & the Togetherness Deck. Wrote 9 books & booklets, including Theatrical Magic (1978, 230pp) & Harlan Tarbell (1993, 60pp). Numerous articles & tricks since 1944 in Dragon, New Phoenix, New Tops, Genii, etc. Columnist ("Our Magical Heritage") in Linking Ring 1976-present. Illustrator for Magic, Inc. [Wh2]

name: Gocke, Siegbert
bio: (Germany?: 23 Jul 1940-) Magician in Germany with assistant as "Bertini & Ly". 1975 MZvD 3rd prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Godfrey, Brian "Tish
bio: (London, England: 28 Jul 1899-) Semi-pro cabaret magic act in London, originally straight, later comic. [Go2]

name: Godfrey, Peter
bio: (London, England: 16 Oct 1899-4 Mar 1970) Pro at age 11 with Swifts Circus in Ireland. After WW I turned stage & vaudeville actor. Then 1925-33 as founding stage producer-director of the Gate Theatre in London where he did 250 plays, but always keeping a hand in magic as MC & performer. Long associated with Jasper Maskelyne. Moved to USA in 1937 & Hollywood in 1939 where he became a movie director with M-G-M, doing 21 "A" & "B" features 1939-56, plus bit roles in 6 films (1938-47), & was a member of Los Magicos. In WW II did USO magic shows with his assistant-wife ex-actress Renee Haal. Gave private stage shows for friends. Marvyn Roy & Alan Wakeling were his magic assistants in late 1940s. Pet effect: Nest of Boxes. SAM Hall of Fame (1985). Switched to TV production in 1950s. Bio in William R. Meyer, Warner Brothers Directors (1978), 134-141. [Katz; Go2; HMM12/51, 1/53; Wat]

name: Godfrey, Terry [Neal] "Godfish
bio: (Phoenix, Arizona: 15 Dec 1959-) Learned at age 8 from books. Danny Dew Award for manip 1975 & 1976. Moved to San Diego. Pro since 1982, specialized in outdoor shows at shopping malls, fairs, & festivals. Aka "Great Godfrey". [Wh2]

name: Godzyni
bio: (Lwów, Poland [now L'vov, Ukrainia]: 1927-) Stage name of Kazimierz Godzoner. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Worked 35 years in the Polish circus. [Mec]

name: Goebel, George
bio: (USA: 1932-) Costumier in Baltimore. Semi-pro illusionist with large full-evening show late 1960s to early 1980s. [Walk]

name: Goebel, Dr Joseph
bio: (Mainz, Germany: 11 Jan 1912-23 Jan 1995) Amateur as "Jan Gol". Many tricks in Magie. Died in Holland. [Roh]

name: Goethe, Johann Wolfgang von
bio: (Frankfurt, Germany: 28 Aug 1749-1832) Famed German dramatist, novelist, poet. A magic buff. Wrote poem "Der Zauberlehrling" (1797) and play Faust (written 1806-31). In 1831 saw Ludwig Döbler perform & invited him home. Magic-related bio bits are in Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993), 93, & throughout. Autobio is Dichtung und Wahrheit [Poetry & Truth] (1811-33).

name: Gogia Pasha
bio: (Dehra Dun, India: 28 Aug 1910-19 Dec 1976) Stage name of Dhanapat Rai "Dhanraj" Gogia. Originally educated as a physician. Pro illusionist & sleight-of-hand in India. Pet effects: Indian Basket Trick & Miser's Dream. Toured Singapore & Australia (1940), Germany (1950), & Canada (1956). 1958 FISM 2nd prize for close-up. Played the Vienna Ronacher in 1958 & Ed Sullivan's TV show in 1960. [Ran; Wal; HMM12/56]

name: Gol, Jan
bio: See: Goebel, Dr Joseph

name: Gold, Harry
bio: (Scotland: 1880-1958) Stage name of Harry Marshall. Pro conjurer who toured the English-speaking countries.

name: Golden, Theo[dore] T.
bio: (Wind Ridge, Greene County, Pennsylvania: 9 May 1879- ) Lawyer & investment counselor. Amateur magician. SAM President 1937-38. [SAM]

name: Goldfinger
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 1949- ) Afro-American. Stage name of Jack Vaughn. Inspired watching Wilson's Magic Land of AllaKazam TV series. Learned some sideshow tricks like fire-eating from magician Clarence "Chandu" Hunter. Debut in teens. Pro with assistant-wife Dove, an Hawaiian, as "Goldfinger and Dove", their act winning the 1979 & 1983 AMA Stage Magician of the Year awards. [Bo#326;Mag]

name: Goldin, Horace
bio: (Vilna, Poland: 17 Dec 1873 or 74-22 Aug 1939) Stage name of Hyman Elias Goldstein. Jew. Inspired at age 12 watching a gypsy conjurer in Poland. Moved to USA in teens. Learned by tuition from an amateur & later from Albini. Debut at age 23. Top pro illusionist since 1901 when he played the London Palace for 16 weeks. Toured the world since 1901. Played the Paris Alhambra in 1909 & 1911. In Sep 1913 became the 1st magician to play the New York Palace. Toured Australia in 1916 & the USA again in 1920-21. In London played St. George's Hall in 1925 & 1927 and the Palladium in 1931. Noted for his fast-paced style. Invented Film to Life (1920), Sawing a Woman in Two (1921, inspired by Selbit's Sawing Thru effect), & the Buzz Saw Illusion (1931). President, The Magicians' Club, 1934-39. Died in London. His act was then bought by Cecil Lyle. Autobio is It's Fun to be Fooled (1937, 286pp). Bio is Val Andrews, Life, Dull It Ain't (1983). Wrote The Mystery Book (1923) with German tr as Das Buch der Geheimnisse [c1925, 24pp]. [Dif;Ch;Fi;Pr;Wal; Mo;Go;Go2;Ho;Magic9/01,10/01,8/04,7/07,1/09]

name: Golding, Will [also Bill]
bio: (England: fl.1930s-60s) Stage name of William Washer. Pro. Wrote Magic for All [c1931]. As “W. Gee” wrote the weekly magic column for World’s Fair until 1935. Served time in the early 1960s in Parkhurst Prison where he performed for fellow inmates.

name: Goldkette, Prof. Louis
bio: (Denmark: 1778-1833) Jew. Pro. Toured widely in Europe. [Dam;Sal]

name: Goldman, Bill
bio: (New York City: 15 May 1950-) Raised in Chicago. Pro, beginning as a restaurant magician & graduating to become one of the top corporate & tradeshow magi. Column ("On the Road") in Magic. One-Man Parade in Linking Ring (1994). [LR6/94]

name: Goldschmidt, Dr Augusto J.
bio: (Brazil: 1859-1927) Lawyer in Rio de Janeiro & general in the Brazilian army. Amateur illusionist.

name: Goldstein, David
bio: (London, England: 25 Dec 1896- ) Aka "Cardoni". Amateur. Articles. [Go2] (Ithaca, New York: 1950- ) Aka "Max Maven". Interest triggered by being taught his cousin's 2 tricks. Learned around age 8 from gift magic set. Top-line pro mentalist since 1974, performing in over 20 countries. Consultant to Blackstone Jr, Lance Burton, David Copperfield, Doug Henning, Jeff McBride, The Pendragons, Mark Wilson, and Penn & Teller. Also produced & directs magic shows (with partner David Belenzon). 1980 AMA Best Lecturer. 1988 Tenkai Prize, its first non-Japanese recipient. Wrote The Blue Book of Mentalism (1976, 28pp); Verbal Control (1976, 8pp), The Red Book of Mentalism [1977, 20pp], Scattershot (1977), The Green Book of Mentalism (1977, 24pp), Masque (1980), New Magic of Japan (1988, with Richard Kaufman), a Japanese-English issue of his Tenkai Prize book (1989), Focus (1990, 150pp), Thavant (1991, 47pp), Max Maven's Book of Fortunetelling (1992, 256pp), Thabbatical (1994, 130pp), etc. Prolific contributor of tricks (over 1,000 since 1965), essays, articles, & reviews to most major international magic magazines, including Swami & Mantra. For all Goldstein issues see Linking Ring (10 "Parades" since 1975), New Jinx, Magick, Richard's Almanac, Pabular, Genii, Mad Magic #27, etc. See also Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), The Very Best of Phil Goldstein (1988, in French). Columns in Magiram since 1990 & Magic since 1991. Many TV bits plus hosting 8 specials in Japan. Video (1985). [Bo#191;Se;Magie10/88;Ran;Lo2;Wat;Mag;Wh]

name: Goldston, James Mayer
bio: (Liverpool, England: 1883-3 Jan 1905) Younger brother of Will Goldston. Aka "Mokana", after the 8th Century charlatan in Khorasan. Minor pro with handcuff escape, etc. Died of malaria in Calcutta.

name: Goldston, Leah
bio: (Liverpool?, England: fl.1900s-30s) British Jewess. Mrs Will Goldston, aka "Van Dyke Brown". Actress & comedienne as "Leah Laurie" & "Lee Laurie". Began magic c1901 with husband as "Devo & Laurie, the Royal Mahatmas", then on own as "La Devo". Semi-pro illusionist c1902-10. Played London's Alhambra in 1906 assisting Dunningarto. Noted for reviving De Kolta's Expanding Cube 1908-09. Separated from husband for last decade of his life & probably outlived him. [Dif]

name: Goldston, Will
bio: (Liverpool, England: 23 Sep 1878-24 Feb 1948) Stage name of Wolf Goldstone (not "Goldstein"). British Jew. Inspired at age 11 or 12 by a box of tricks. Learned 1892 from visits with Prof. Alexander & reading Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Debut as apprentice at age 17 in 1898. Aka "Carl Devo" c1898-1907, initially with Black Art. Pro magician to pro magic dealer. Managed the Conjuring, Theatrical, & Entertainment Departments at Gamage's 1905-14. Founded The Magicians' Club in 1911, serving as Treasurer throughout but running it as a one-man self-serving club, until it passed into limbo in WW II. Owner-manager of Aladdin House (Will Goldston Ltd) 1914-48 in London. Husband of Leah Goldston & uncle of Dolly Spence. Edited The Magician Monthly 1904-13, The Magician Annual 1907-12, The Magazine of Magic 1914-22 & 1930-34, Goldston's Magical Quarterly 1934-40. Prolific author, including Secrets of Magic (1903, 102pp); Latest Conjuring (1905, 148pp); Crystal Gazing (1906, 36pp), Tricks and Illusions for Amateur and Professional Conjurers (1909, 135pp), The Young Conjurer (1910, 94pp), Juggling Secrets (1911, 96pp); his famous "locked book" series: Exclusive Magical Secrets [1912], More Exclusive Magical Secrets [1921, 506pp; reprinted 1977], Further Exclusive Magical Secrets [1927, 361pp]; Simple Conjuring Tricks (1913, 126pp); Modern Card Tricks without Apparatus (1915, 109pp); Paper Tricks (1919, 94pp); Sand, Smoke, and Rag Pictures (112pp), Great Magicians' Tricks [1931, 394pp]; Secrets of Famous Illusionists (1933, 285pp); Tricks that Mystify (1934, 359pp); Who's Who in Magic [1934, 114pp]; Great Tricks Revealed (1935, 304pp); & Tricks of the Masters (1942, 207pp). Memoir is Sensational Tales of Mystery Men (1929, 324pp). Bio is Val Andrews, Once Hung a Gilded Lamp: The Life and Times of Will Goldston (1986). Much bio material is in J.B. Findlay's Fifth Collectors Annual (1953). [Daw94;MC10/87-1/88;Dam;St;Go2;Vo56;Rob1;Dor; Bur;La2]

name: Goma
bio: (near Chemnitz, Germany: 1896-28 Feb 1964) Stage name of Martin Gott Neubert. Pro, specializing in silk magic. Pet effect: Inexhaustible Bottle. Died in Köln (Cologne), West Germany. [Mül;Roh]

name: Gondar, Heinz
bio: (Dessau, Germany: 21 Jan 1912-23 Apr 1982) Stage name of Heinz Gieppner. Died in Stuttgart, West Germany. [Roh] (France: fl.1560s-70s). Grandson of the previous Gonin. Pro magician. [Cl;Dif] Gonin

name: Gonin
bio: (France: 1515-1547). Pro sleight-of-hand. [Dif;Cl] (France: fl.late 1600s). Pro in Paris. The fame of the Gonins was such that it led to the French catch-phrase "Un tour de Maître Gonin" (literally, "a trick of Master Gonin"), meaning any artful or cunning device. [Cl;Dif]

name: Gonzalez Jr, Mario J[oseph] "Mad Man
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 18 Oct 1935-10 Oct 1997) Learned at age 5 from mother's gift of magic book. Pro comedy & dove magic since age 15. Worked at Tannen's 1951-57, 1976-79, & 1988-89. Director of Tannen's Magic Camp 1975-79. Also on own as hotel, nightclub, & cruise ship magician. Pet effects: Linking Pins & Hopping Half. Invented Little Joe's Rope Trick, Telekinesis Key, etc. Tricks in books by Elliott, Garcia, Kaufman, Lorayne, Tarbell, & Tarr. Died of heart failure. [Wh2]

name: Gonzalez Ylabaca, Enrique
bio: (Santiago, Chile: 3 Nov 1927- ) Inspired in 1938 seeing local Fu-Manchú show. Lawyer in Santiago. Amateur close-up & mental magic in private homes as "Henry D'Ici". Chilean Magic Circle co-founder 1961 & President 1969-present. Articles in Aquelarre. [Wh3]

name: Good, Arthur
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s) Aka "Tom Tit". Translated La science amusante (1889) as Magic at Home: Book of Amusing Science (1890, 250pp; reprinted 1969 as The Victorian Book of Magic).

name: Goodliffe, MIMC
bio: (Nottingham, England: 1912-26 Dec 1980) Nom de magique of C[harles] Goodliffe Neale. Inspired around age 7 by semi-pro neighbor De Brusia. Briefly a pro performer & magic dealer. Then a full-time dealer in R.C. Church furniture. Founding editor-publisher of Abracadabra 1946-80 & several magic books. Wrote Simply Wizard (1946, 17pp; repr 1968). MIMC 1960. 1970 AMA Special Fellowship. 1978 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" award. Memoirs are The Goodliffe Years (2 audiotapes). See also Owen Griffiths (editor) for 3 privately circulated typescript compilations of Goodliffe's Abra editorials: 25 Years with Goodliffe, 1946-1970 (1971, 307pp), 25 Years with Goodliffe, 1972/1973 (1973, 44pp), & Be Businesslike (1973, 354pp). [MUM2/80; La2]

name: Goodsell, David R[ay Robbins], AIMC
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 4 Aug 1939- ) Inspired at age 11 by school magician & Dell O'Dell TV show. Headmaster of private schools in Oklahoma City and (since 1990) in Idyllwild, CA. Semi-pro magician in early 1970s until turned amateur, specializing in magic history. Editor of MUM 1976-present. SAM President 1986-87. Articles in MUM. [Wh2]

name: Goodwin, Bill
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro closeup & lecturer. 1983 AMA Junior Achievement Award (shared). 4 sets of lecture notes 1982-88. Trick in Magic. [Wh2]

name: Goodwin, John J.
bio: (USA: -11 Apr 1920) Pro by 1905, living in Brooklyn. Billed as the "Roller Skating Magician". Died in Springfield, Long Island.

name: Gordien [Sr], Henry "Hank
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 1890-9 Feb 1967) Minor pro in New York City as street magus & finally Minneapolis as sideshow & vaude magus. Invented Mystic Tube (1927). Introduced Emil Jarrow's Salt Trick to the USA in the early 1930s when he taught it to Faucett Ross. However, Gordien had invented his own method, the Salt Gimmick. Tricks (9 of them) in Greater Magic (1938). [Br,pp5-8;Pr] Gor-Don, The Great (Iowa, USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Gordon Andrews. Jewellery store manager & semi-pro escapist. [Mag]

name: Gordon, Barry
bio: (London, England: 28 Sep 1923-early 1993) Learned in 1943 from books, pros, & advice from Davenports. Engineering sales manager. Semi-pro close-up, mental, & cabaret magician since 1945. Moved in 1948 to Birmingham where has been full-time pro since 1980. Manager & demonstrator at "Magician's Mecca" magic shop in Birmingham 1953-c60. As house organ edited Mecca News 1953-57. Again as dealer under own name 1979-89. Co-owner (with Stan Willey) of Magic Centre (large shop, manufacturer, publisher) in Birmingham 1989-closed in early 1990s? Articles in Hughes News & Abra. [Wh2]

name: Gordon, Frank E.
bio: (New York City, NY: 25 Dec 1891- ) At age 13 as "Okomo" assisted Wilfred the Wizard for several years. At age 15 changed stage name to "El Gordo", then at 22 to own name. Played major circuits in USA & Europe. Pro comedy magician until age 29 when left stage for merchandise business in Michigan, moving to Los Angeles in 1929 where he worked semi-pro. [SAM]

name: Gordon, Gene
bio: (Albany, New York: 15 Oct 1903-6 Sep 1994) Stage name since age 7 of Gordon Eugene Avery. Inspired at age 7 seeing Tex McGuire act & immediately purchased the Appearing Flower Bush by catalog. Co-founder/owner of mail-order Wayne Magic Company 1919-20. At age 18 in 1922 co-founded the IBM (with Len Vintus, Don Rogers being recruited by them as Member #3) & became first co-editor (with Ernest Schieldge) of The Linking Ring 1922-26. Pro in 1925 to semi-pro comedy performer with a Lyceum & vaude show. Pro dealer (Gene Gordon's Magic Shop) 1945-69 in Buffalo, NY. 1981 AMA Masters Fellowship. Invented Piff Paff Poof in early 1930s. Wrote "Patter and Presentation" column in New Tops. Autobio is Gene Gordon's Magical Legacy (1980, 364pp). Column in Linking Ring. [Bo#197;LR5/80;WWM]

name: Gordon, Henry
bio: (Montreal, Canada: 9 Mar 1919-) Learned in 1940 from a coin-magic book. Electronics engineer. Pro mentalist since 1950. Pet effect: None or All. Member of CSICOP. Wrote Extrasensory Deception (1987, 227pp), an exposé of paranormal claims; It's Magic (1988, 92pp), a kid's intro to conjuring; Channeling into the New Age (1988, 198pp); & Henry Gordon's World of Magic (1989, 169pp). Also wrote "It's Magic" column & many feature articles on magicians for Toronto Star newspaper. [Wh2]

name: Gordon, Rex Palmer
bio: (Tain, Scotland: 11 Jul 1880-) Toured with Buffalo Bill and as "Rex Ricardo" with Houdini. Pro escapist as "Comanche Jim the Wonder Cowboy", billed as "The Man you cannot Hang". Husband of "Atelenta", a Scottish escapist of the 1920s-40s. Nephew of world champion (1897-99) heavy-weight boxer Bob Fitzsimmons. Still alive in 1950s.

name: Gordon, Scott
bio: (Dumont, New Jersey: 1949- ) Learned magic at age 7. Pro entertainer. Semi-pro with mental & bizarre magic since age 15. Pet effects: Million to One & Key-R-Rect. Founding member of Psychic Entertainers Association 1978. Co-editor (with Tony Raven) of Psychikos 1980-81. Articles in Psychikos & Vibrations. [WWE;Wh2]

name: Gordon, Stuart J.
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 19 Jun 1930-) Lawyer in Los Angeles. Amateur close-up magician since learned at age 12 from father & books. Lawyer in Los Angeles, including for such magicians as Dai Vernon, Charlie Miller, Johnny Thompson, Ricky Jay, Larry Jennings, David Roth, & Bruce Cervon. [Wh5]

name: Gorham, [Austin C.] "Ace
bio: (New Bedford, Massachusetts: 5 Mar 1901-19 Dec 1978) Magic debut at age 12. Socony-Vacuum Oil Company manager since 1925. Semi-pro magician & mentalist since 1925. SAM President 1951-52 & IBM President 1971-72. Invented The Ace Dictionary Test (1955) & Fabtastrick (1957). Wrote People Know Everything! (1959, 16pp). Tricks in New Phoenix, New Jinx, & Genii. [Genii6/64; NJ#13; Des]

name: Goshman, Albert "Al
bio: (New York City, NY: 6 Dec 1920-12 [sic] Feb 1991) Born Albert Goshwinsky. Learned c1942 from book. Pro close-up & dealer (specializing in spongeballs). AMA Best Close-up Magician 1968, 1975. 1971 AMA Magician of the Year. Invented Ding Dong in 1972. 1982 AMA Best Lecturer. 1983 Desert Magic Seminar 4th prize. Autobio & tricks are in Patrick Page & Albert Goshman, Magic by Gosh: The Life and Times of Albert Goshman (1985, 149pp). Audio (1970s). Video segment (1986) & video (1987). See Mad Magic #10 for all Goshman issue. Tricks in HMM & Genii. [HC;Mag;Wh]

name: Gottlieb, Emil
bio: (Brno [Brünn], Moravia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 9 Apr 1851-4 Aug 1934) Son of a senior Austrian army officer. Pro as "E. Georg Homes". Also briefly with wife as "Homes & Fay" [or "Holmes & Fey"?] toured 2-person mind-reading act in Austria & Balkans. Then toured Europe & Turkey with Ernest Thorn. Teacher of Prince Hendrik of Holland. One of first to introduce cinema to Vienna. Died in Vienna. [Vo57]

name: Goudar, Ange
bio: (Holland: fl.1750s) Edited L'Histoire des Grecs ou de ceux qui corrigent la fortune au jeu (The Hague: 1758), an early exposé of card cheats. [Dif] Goulet, Raymond J[ohn] "Ray" [pronounced goo-LAY] (Cambridge, Massachusetts: 20 Jan 1930-) Inspired & learned in 1944 when he found Holden's Magic Shop & Herman Hanson in Boston. Since 1946 as part-time pro sleight-of-hand artist, escapist, vent, & fire-eater. With assistant-wife Ann (née Ford, whom he married in 1949) they performed as "The Raymonds". They worked 22 trans-Atlantic cruise-ship crossings as "The Raymonds" on the USS United States, plus several Caribbean cruises, c1964-c1975. Also performed a solo mentalist act as "Ray Raymond". Retired from performing in 1992. Major collector (over 1,000 pieces of apparatus & 6,500 older books & booklets). Dealer & publisher (Magic Art Studio) in Watertown, Massachusetts, since 1976. The main shop includes a 50-seat magic theatre and the Mini Magic Museum, which houses his apparatus collection. Tricks in MUM. NOTE: Not, as Booth reported, born Raymond Joaquim before legal name change in teens to Goulet, an error resulting from confusion with Ray's step-father whose surname was Joaquim. [LR2/06;Bo#271;Wh]

name: Govan, Barry [John]
bio: (Ballarat, Victoria, Australia: 1 Dec 1943-) Inspired at age 17 by a retired American gambler. Learned from Erdnase in 1960s. Publisher. Semi-pro magician (close-up & cards) & magic teacher since 1960s. Co-edited (with Ian Baxter) Blueprint 1974-78. Partner (with Graham Etherington) Abracadabra Promotions since 1985, a promotion company thru entertainment, particularly magical. Wrote Close-up Magic--Restaurant Style (52pp), One Pitch is Worth a Thousand Words (32pp), Dice and the Purse, & Close-up Magic--Restaurant Style 2 (1992, 52pp). Tricks in Gen, Apocalypse, S.O.B. Jr, Pabular, MUM, Magic Makers, Blueprint, Linking Ring, Genii, New Directions, & Australian Magic Magazine. [Magicana#193;Wh2]

name: Gové, Chris[topher Raymond]
bio: (Sliema, Malta: 23 Oct 1959-) Learned at age 13 from gift magic set. Purser for Air Malta. Amateur close-up & mental magician since age 16. Articles in Is-Sammar [The Wizard]. Invented Key-Fabulation in 1986. [Wh2] Gowango, The Great (USA: fl.1890s) Afro-American. In 1899 he was the only black magician playing American vaudeville. [Lau]

name: Gower, Chris[topher], AIMC
bio: (Hammersmith, London, England: 22 May 1953-) Trained as medical lab scientist. Started own business as locksmith in 1982. Semi-proescapist. Owns largest collection of restraints in Europe. [Daw2]

name: Goázdik, Janusz
bio: (Poland: 1937-) Taught by Alachini. Pro illusionist in Polish circuses, specializing in childrens magic. [Mec]

name: Grabel, Lee
bio: (Portland, Oregon: 12 Mar 1919-) Born Lee Grabeel, now changed to Lee Grabel. Inspired c1930 seeing Professor Turtle. Debut in 1931 at age 12. Pro illusionist, tropping a big (20-ton) show. Married Helen Foster in 1944 & made her his principal assistant as "Helene". Pet effects included the Floating Piano, which he reinvented in 1949 with his own method. Also invented Teeter-Totter illusion (1949), etc. In 1954 Dante designated him his eventual successor under the stage name "Danton". Retired from magic in 1959 (to manage his real estate investments), storing his show. Then 2 performances in 1970 & toured for 20 weeks in 1977. Lee & Helene toured an occasional "little show" in the late 1980s. Bio is Ormond McGill, The Magic and Illusions of Lee Grabel (1986, 217pp). [MUM7/02; LR2/88; Fu; Tay; Wh2]

name: Graf
bio: (Austria?: fl.mid-1800s) A leading pro apparatus maker in Vienna. [CI]

name: Graf, Victor
bio: (Vienna: 16 Jul 1908-) Skilled amateur. Long-time Vice-President of Vienna Magic Club. [Al]

name: Gräfe, Otto [pronounced GRAY-fa]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 30 Dec 1855-11 Oct 1938) Died in Stettin, Germany. [Roh]

name: Graham, Dr Harvey P[olhemus] "Doc", MD
bio: (Newburgh, New York: 31 Oct 1917-) Learned in 1932 from magic set. Physician (pathologist). Amateur magician since 1940. Tricks in Phoenix. [Wh2]

name: Graham, Henry "Harry
bio: (England: fl.1850s) Ex-circus clown. Minor pro magician who toured the English provinces posing as whoever was the current rage in London, including Anderson, Phillippe, Frikell, Robert-Houdin. [Ch;Cl]

name: Graham, Lyston
bio: (USA: 26 May 1846-8 Apr 1920) Stage name of Robert Spice.

name: Graham, Phillip "Phil
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Aka "Mr. Fantastic, The Psychadelic [sic] Prestidigitator". Semi-pro since age 13. A Chavez graduate. [Mag]

name: Graham, Walter B[ishop]
bio: (Omaha, Nebraska: 16 Apr 1923-) Learned from a 25¢ copy of Howard Thurston's Card Tricks. Debut at age 12. Publisher (Modern Litho, Inc) in Omaha, including magic books 1959-1989 (when sold to his partner Dick Boettcher, an amateur magician). Thence continued his separate mail-order graphics business (Dot Page-Up Supplies), also in Omaha. Semi-pro magician, playing church & birthday party dates with both comedy magic & mentalism acts. Wrote How to Become a Magician for Fun and Profit (1967, 92pp). Edited Magic Collector Reprint Series 1969-73. Articles in Magic Cauldron. Mentor of Doug Webster. 1987 Henry Ridgely Evans History Award. [MUM10/92;Wh]

name: Grandin, E[dward] M.
bio: (Maine, USA: c1837-) Professional card & dice sharp. Dealer-manufacturer as the "Sporting Man Emporium" of gambling "tools" (marked decks, holdout machines, loaded dice, etc) in New York City 1864-1877-?. As "Gerritt M. Evans" wrote How Gamblers Win (1865, 84pp; rev 1868, 112pp; repr c1920). NOTE: Name misspelled "E.N. Grandine" by Asbury.

name: Grandsart, [André-]Joseph
bio: (Bruges, West Flanders, Belgium: 18 Nov 1813-30 Jun 1882) Son of a Frenchman. Moved to France. Pro. Married Julie Courtois, daughter of Louis Courtois, with whom he founded the travelling Théâtre Grandsart-Courtois in France until 1877 when he retired, passing his theater to his younger son, Jules Grandsart. [Dif;St]

name: Grandsart, Jules[-Arthur]
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 1 Jan 1845-6 Jan 1905) Younger son of Joseph Grandsart. Pro sleight-of-hand artist, juggler, & equilibrist. In 1877 took over direction of his father's travelling Théâtre Grandsart-Courtois. Step-father of Guillaume Clément who succeeded to ownership of the theater. [Dif]

name: Grandsart-Courtois, M.
bio: See: Grandsart, Joseph Grandsart, Jules

name: Grant, Cary
bio: (Bristol, England: 18 Jan 1904-28 Nov 1986) Only son of lower middle class English parents. Stage name of Archibald Alexander Leach since 1932 when he began the film career that led to stardom and retirement in 1966. Amateur magician, having been inspired at age 13 watching magicians while working as an electrician's assistant at the Bristol Empire and Hippodrome variety theaters. Moved to USA in 1920 with Bob Pender's vaudeville troupe with which he took on all sorts of jobs including with magic acts until 1927 when he became a Broadway actor until 1931 when he went to Hollywood to break into the talkies. Member of Board of Directors the Academy of Magical Arts 1969-79, thence Member Emeritus. Berri Lee was his protégé in the late 1960s. Best researched & balanced bio is Graham McCann, Cary Grant: A Class Apart (1996). See also Geoffrey Wansell, Haunted Idol (1984), Warren G. Harris, Cary Grant: A Touch of Elegance (1987), and the scurrilous Charles Higham & Roy Mosley, Cary Grant: The Lonely Heart (1989). [Mag]

name: Grant, Gene
bio: (Vicksburg, Mississippi: fl.1950s-90s – 18th January 2013) Real estate broker in Vicksburg & semi-pro mental magician as "Phantini". Wrote Phantini's Lost Book of Mental Secrets (1955, 21pp), Phantini's Mental Key (1956, 28pp), Phantini's Incredible Mental Secrets (2 vols, 1980, 1981). Marketed original tricks. Tricks in Linking Ring 1957-1993.

name: Grant, General
bio: (Somerville, Massachusetts: 19 Aug 1931- ) Stage name of General [sic] Grant Murphy Jr. Inspired seeing the Tony Curtis "Houdini" movie. Learned first sleights during hospital stay in 1952. Pipefitter in Natick, Mass. Semi-pro dove worker & close-up magician in New England since 1953. Since late 1970s markets several original effects. Invented Ribbons to Doves, Dove to Silk, Vanishing Zombie Ball (1982), etc. Lecturer since 1982. Wrote How to Make a Living by Stealing (Doves of Course) (1981, 29pp), General Grant's Lecture Notes, #2 (29pp), #3 (1993, 60pp). Tricks in MUM. [MUM12/96; MUM2/93; MM1/90; Wh5]

name: Grant, Tiny
bio: (USA: -1959) Stage name of Ralph G. Matthieson, aka "King Grant". His nickname "Tiny" belies his billing as "World's Largest Magician". Dealer as Tiny's Magic Co. after WW II in Denver, Colorado, where he issued Cat.#1 (1946, 186pp). Wrote Patter and Gags (1951, 24pp)

name: Grant, U[lysses] F[rederick Simpson] "Gen
bio: (USA: 12 Jan 1901-1 Mar 1978) Pro magic dealer since 1925, first in Pittsfield, Massachusetts (as "Grant's Magic Shop"), then in New York City (until 1939). Then for a short time (around & including 1940) with Abbott's staff in Colon, Michigan. Finally (by Dec 1942) again as independent dealer in Columbus, Ohio, where Norm Menge joined him as partner in 1944. 1975 AMA Creative Fellowship. His estate has continued his dealership as MAK Magic. Prolific inventor and improver, sometimes under the pseudonym "Frank Zella", of many tricks, including A Message From the Deep (by 1928), Grant's Rope Trick (by 1930), Square Pig = Pig Turns Around (by 1931), Bullet-Proof Girl (by 1932), K.O. Card Trick (by 1932), Master Trick Deck (by 1932), Mystic Pearls of Persia (by 1932), The Farmer and the Witch (by 1935), Walking thru a Ribbon (by 1935), Invulnerable Lady = Dagger Chest Illusion (vanished head version, early 1930s), Dick Tracy Himself (by 1936), Phant-O-Dial (c1939), Alagen rope (with Winston Freer by 1939), Movies to Life (by 1939), Grant's Diminishing Cards (by 1940), Automat Deck (by 1940), The Zella Thought Projector (by 1940), Slow Motion Bill Switch (by 1940), Million Dollar Bill Mystery (by 1940), Little Silk House (by 1940), Comedy Rope Trick (by 1940), Ropes of Bengal (by 1940), Television Telephone (1940), Amputation (with R. Bordner in 1940), Grant's Cocktail Cup (1940), Super X Levitation (1942), Cow Trick (by 1944), Temple Screen (1944), Sacred Altar Light (by 1945), Zella Nite-Club Cylinders (by 1945), Little Gem Beer Keg (1945), Chink Cans (by 1947), Nite Club Table (by 1947), Kard-U-Reka (1947), Cards and Slate (by 1948), Devil's Newspaper (by 1948), Slate of Mind, Dial-X (1951), with Reynolds, Bottle Cap-N-Pennies (1953), Bengal Net (1953), Flat Model Money Maker (1954), Chen-Lee Water Suspension (1954), Crystal Silk Cylinder (1954), Una-Mind (1957), Candle-Lite (by 1958), Transparent Rice Bowls (1959), and Strat-o-Spheres (by 1962). Wrote many booklets, including Twenty Five Tricks and Ideas (1931), Flap Slate Wrinkles (1931, with H. Adrian Smith), Tricks with Cellophane (1932), Rising, Floating, Dancing Silk (1933), El Ropo (1933), Rope Trick (1933), El Ropo (1933), Grant's Patter Folio (1934), Illusion Secrets (1934), Grant's Thirteen Mysteries [1934, 18pp], Flash Magic (1935, 8pp), Magician, Ghost and Girl (1935), Tricks with a One-Way Deck (1935, 21pp), The Blue Ribbon Combination (1935), 25 Rising Card Tricks (1935; repr 1970, 36pp), The Barrel and Broom Illusion (1936), Chinese Magic and Illusions (1936), Jumbo Card Tricks (1937), Ninety Nine Tips and Gags (1937), Counterfeit Card Miracles #1 (by 1940), Nite Club Illusions (1940, 32pp), Counterfeit Card Miracles #2 (1940), Paper Magic (1941, mineo), C.L.I.P.: Clever Little Ideas Presented by U.F. Grant (1947, 11pp), Tricks for Kid Shows (1951, 14pp), Grant's Three-Card Monte (1951, 5pp), Rope, Chain and Box Escapes (1954, 19pp), Gen Grant's Manual of Magic (1964), 25 Rising Card Tricks (1970, 36pp), Bodies in Orbit. Tricks in Sphinx, Tarbell #5, New Phoenix, etc. See Don Tanner, Grant's Fabulous Feats of Mental Magic (1954, 21pp) & Robert J. Smith, Grant's Brilliant Card Magic (1955, 16pp). [Mag;St]

name: Grässe, Dr. Johann Georg Theodor
bio: (Grimma, Saxony, Germany: 31 Jan 1814-27 Aug 1885) Bibliographer & writer. Published the world's first bibliography of magic & allied arts, the 175-page Bibliotheca Magica et Pneumatica (Leipzig: Wilhelm Engelmann, 1843; reprinted 1986). Died near Dresden. [Dif]

name: Grassi, Antonio
bio: (Italy: 12 Jun 1814-28 Jan 1874) Popular pro. [Sil]

name: Gravatt, Glenn [G.]
bio: (Sabetha, Kansas: 4 Dec 1899-17 Apr 1984) Police officer. Amateur magician. Best-remembered for his flagrant publishing of others' tricks without permission. Yet awarded the 1980 AMA Literary Fellowship. Died in San Francisco. Wrote (in "collaboration" with his fictitious alter ego "Doctor Wilhelm Von Deusen") Encyclopedia of Self-Working Card Tricks (2 vols, [1936], [1937], 451+150pp). Wrote Jap Box Tricks (1937, 123pp), Final Selection (1957, 89pp), Glenn Gravatt's Treasure Trove of Tricks (1971, 290pp), Fifty Modern Card Tricks You Can Do! (1974, 50pp), Fifty More Modern Card Tricks (60pp), Thayer Quality Magic Catalog Instruction Sheets (4 vols, 1978 etc), Collected Writings of Glenn Gravatt (1974, 254pp), More Collected Writings of Glenn Gravatt, & Goldmine of Magic (1984, 232pp). Many articles in magic magazines, including Genii.

name: Graves, Edward [Anthony Albert]
bio: (Britain: c1900-31 Jul 1965) Circus expert & co-founder of Clowns International in 1945. Wrote weekly magic page for The World's Fair 1940 [sic]-1965. Also wrote on automatic coin machines as "Sevarg" and did some circus articles as "Anthony Albert". [Daw2] Gravito, The Great (USA: 22 Mar 1880-16 Mar 1949) Stage name of Albert Franklin Davidson, aka "The Great Gravity". Pro juggler & magician. Worked mainly circuses & fairs, later also vaudeville & nightclubs. [St]

name: Grayson, Gary
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Pro illusionist. In 1963 became a charter member of the Magic Castle. Owner of Magic Unlimited. [Mag]

name: Graziadei, Valentino
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 19 Oct 1898-30 Dec 1965) Of Italian parentage. Pro card magic since age 18. Student of Dario Paini & Ottokar Fischer. In 1924, at the Vienna Magic Circle, David Bamberg taught him his own short-card routines, which became the basis of Graziadei's successful act when he later toured Italy. Died in Vienna. Tricks in Hokus-Pokus. Christian "Magic Christian" Stelzel is writing a book about Graziadei. [Win;St]
