name: Grdina, John J.
bio: (Slovenia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Yugoslavia]: 26 May 1885-2 May 1975) Moved with parents to Cleveland USA as a 5-year-old boy. Inspired in 1900 [sic] seeing Kellar show. Learned 1907-08 by lessons from A.K. Freund. Debut in 1907 [sic] with his assistant-bride. Newspaper publisher to pro stage magician. Played vaudeville for 10 years. Pet effects: Kellar's Ring Trick, Nest of Boxes, & Natural Growth of Flowers. Then became banker & semi-pro magician. Trick in Zombie. [SAM]

name: Great Scott
bio:
(Ottawa, Canada: 1896-29 May 1969) Inspired "as a youngster" seeing vaude magicians in Ottawa. Learned at age 15. Moved to New York City. Invented Interlocked Card Production (in early 1910s). Pro vaudeville (small & big time) card manipulator from 1912 to 1929. Thence businessman (until retired in 1959) & semi-pro private & club-date magician in New York City. Voted a member of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Wrote Professional Card Magic (1961, 159pp; repr 1979), a minor classic. Tricks in HMM. [Bo3]

[See also: Guinn, Scott]

name: Green, Harry
bio: (New York City: 1 Apr 1892-31 May 1958) Stage name of Harry Blitzer. Pro vaudeville comedian using “Jewish” patter. Amateur cardman, a favorite in WW II and after of Winston Churchill to whom he showed thought transference on 30 Nov 1944 & Curry's Out of This World. A pet effect was the "37" psychological force. Infamous for his exposures on British TV. Wrote Harry Green Says You Are a Magician (1956). Died in London. [Fi]

name: Green, John C.
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 26 Mar 1866-26 Aug 1951) Aka "Adrian Belzac". Learned assisting Jim Harrington in American dime museums. By age 20 was a minor pro touring in USA & rural Canada, with store shows, side-shows, & circuses. One of the 1st to exhibit motion pictures in Canada. Still touring at age 83. Died in his home in Mundare, Manitoba. [Pr;Bo3]

name: Green, Jonathan H[arrington]
bio: (near Lawrenceburg, Indiana: 1813- ) A card and dice sharp for 12 years until reformed in 1842. In 1850-52 he investigated the New York gambling scene for the New York Association for the Suppression of Gambling as its Executive Agent in charge of the Intelligence Office. His exposés were An Exposure of the Arts and Miseries of Gambling (1843, 360pp; 2nd ed, 1845, 324pp; 5th ed, 1847; 6th ed, 1848, 336pp), Gambling Unmasked! (1844, 193pp; 1847, 312pp), The Secret Band of Brothers, or the American Outlaws 1847; 3rd ed, 1848), An Exposition of Games and Tricks with Cards (1850, 96pp; 1852, 96pp; 1852, 96pp; repr as Gamblers' Tricks with Cards, 1865, 114pp), Gambling in Its Infancy and Progress, or, a Dissuasive to the Young Against Games of Chance (1849), Report on Gambling in New York (1851), and Gambling Exposed (1857) His memoir is Twelve Days in the Tombs; or, A Sketch of the Last Eight Years of the Reformed Gambler's Life (1851, 259pp), repr as The Reformed Gambler: or, The History of the Later Years of the Life of Jonathan H. Green (1858, 259pp).

name: Green, Lennart [Sven]
bio: (Västervik, Sweden: 25 Dec 1941- ) Learned simple tricks from older friends at ages 7 to 10, serious reading after age 19. Physician (GP). Amateur magician specialized in cards & closeup. 1989 International Close-up Competition (London) 3rd prize. 1991 FISM 1st prize in card magic. Invented Green Angle Separation (GAS) in 1961. Wrote 1-2 Separation [1989, 10pp] & The Green Angle Seoaration [1990, 20pp] Tricks in magic magazines. [Wh8]

name: Green, Paul [Scott]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 8 Jun 1950- ) Learned in 1957. A top pro society & nightclub magician in Los Angeles. Taught Jason Randal in exchange for karate lessons. Also taught magic course in Los Angeles Community College. In 1990s turned to trade-shows. Wrote Take a Stroll with Me (1989, 16pp), Miller's Dice (1995, 2pp), & Nothing up My (Green) Sleeves! (1998, 28pp). Articles & tricks in Genii, Talisman, & MUM. Columnist for The Magic Menu. [Magicana#223;Mag;Wh2]

name: Green, Roy
bio: (London, England: 1926- ) Taught magic by John Cantrell. In WW II served in British camouflage unit in Middle East and Royal Army Medical Corps. Moved to California. Wrote The Maskelyne Caper (1972). [Mag]

name: Greenbaum, Jules
bio: (Germany: c1870-1925) Born Grünbaum, a German Jew. As a youth moved to USA. Pro manipulator &, later, illusionist until 1900 when he retired from the stage to become a movie maker. [Dam]

name: Greenberg, Alan C[ourtney] "Ace
bio: (Wichita, Kansas: 3 Sep 1927- ) Raised in Oklahoma City. At age 15 inspired seeing Blackstone Sr & learned from library books. Investment banker since 1949 with major Wall Street firm of Bear Stearns, including as Chairman & CEO of major Wall Street firm of Bear Sterns with a salary of $5.3 million in fiscal 1991. Amateur close-up magician. Taught by Slydini c1960. Pet effect: Slydini coins. Co-publisher (with Richard Kaufman) as "Kaufman & Greenberg" 1979-97. [WWA;Wh5]

name: Greenfield, Felix
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro mentalist. Had 30-minute Mutual Network radio mindreading show, The Man of Magic, which began in 1944, with Greenfield as host & mindreader, assisted by British film star Wendy Barrie. In 1950 he co-produced NBC-TV's The Great Merlini, a half hour crime drama series written by Clayton Rawson & starring Chester Morris.

name: Greer, [Eric] Shawn
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 16 Dec 1962-) Pro close-up on stage (with coins and Linking Rings) and street. (with Cups & Balls and knots). Invented a 10-coin production. Collector of magic books. Wrotes Notes on Cups and Balls (1995). [Wh01]

name: Gregals
bio: See: “Lazern, Emile”

name: Greget, John A[ndrew] "Andy
bio: (San Pedro, California: 20 Jan 1949-) Learned at age 10 buying at Disneyland magic shop. Amateur close-up magician. Magic & gambling collector. Articles in Magick. CPA until turned full-time magic dealer in 1988. [Wh2]

name: Gregory
bio: (England: fl.1790s) Minor pro. Played Bartholomew Fair once in the late 1790s when billed as "Successor to the late Mr. Lane, the Real King's Conjurer". Pet effect: Torn and Restored Card. [CI]

name: Gresham, Jon, MIMC
bio: (South Bend, Indiana: 12 Aug 1900-) Semi-pro since 1922 with cards & balls. [WWM] (Cottingham, England: 22 Apr 1930-1 Mar 1995) Stage name of John Francis Gresham. Pro fire eater in late 1940s-early 1950s, billed as "Europe's Youngest Fire Eater." Aka "Prof Spark". Retired in 1969 to become a collector. Owner of Penny Arcadia, a museum of amusement machines in Pocklington. [Budget3/95]

name: Gresham, William Lindsay "Bill
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 1909-Sep 1962) Raised in Brooklyn. Saw first magicians before WW I at Coney Island. Served as a medic with the International Brigades in the Spanish Civil War 1938. Writer and amateur magician. Wrote Nightmare Alley (1946, 275pp), an acclaimed novel (made into a movie in 1947) of carnival life whose protagonist is a mentalist; Limbo Tower, a novel; Monster Midway (1953, 307pp), a study of carnival life; and Houdini--The Man Who Walked through Walls (1959, 306pp; paperback repr 1961, 263pp). Suicide by sleeping pills after learning he had cancer.

name: Greville, Mlle. Marie
bio: (England?: fl.1880s) Stage name of Marie Becker. Worked as the "medium" with French magicians Guibal & Verbeck Jr in England in the late 1880s.

name: Grey, Lawrence "Larry
bio: (England: fl.1910s-1940s) Moved to Toronto and then New York City. Associated with Dai Vernon (who taught him the art of silhouette cutting in 1917) & Garrick Spencer. Pro comedy sleight-of-hand magician, billed as "The Dizzy Wizard". For each trick in his act he impersonated a different celebrity, including Cardini, Jimmy Durante, W.C.Fields, Stan Laurel, & George Arliss. [Ho]

name: Greystoke, R. Temple
bio: (Shady Grove, Alabama: 11 Jan 1901-17 Mar 1973) Stage name of Wreford Stough "Ray" Price, aka "Rah-Mona". Pro illusionist. A star of both Lyceum (since 1921) & Chautauqua (since 1923). Apprenticed in Ghost Shows under Elwyn "El-Wyn" Peck c1929. Did Ghost Shows 1930-41 as "El-Wyn", "Ali Baba", "Dr. Bey Shan", etc. Returned to straight magic 1941-1955 when retired to Phenix City, Alabama, to sell autos. [Pr;Walk2;HMM7/58]

name: Griff
bio: See: Griffith, Tony "Griff"

name: Griffin, Ken [Leo]
bio: (Jester, Oklahoma: 5 Sep 1914-28 Jan 1988) Pro illusionist (ex-cowboy & master saddle maker) since 1946. AMA Award of Merit (to Ken & Roberta) 1980. Retired in 1983. Wrote (with wife-assistant Roberta) both Illusion Show Know-How (1972, 104pp) & The Professional Entertainer's Booking and Selling Manual (1991, 200+pp). [Bo#212]

name: Griffin, Richard
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Dove act, including Linking Rings. 1989 Magic Circle Young Magician of the Year; 1990 British Ring Shield & Dittia Shield. (USA: c1916-17 Oct 1996) Born Roberta Schramm. Movie actress in 1930s. In 1942 married Ken Griffin who later trained her in magic, becoming his principal assistant (as "Roberta") 1946-1983. Since 1988 worked on own. Pet effects: Rag Pictures & X-Ray Eyes. Wrote (with Ken) both Illusion Show Know-How (1972) & The Professional Entertainer's Booking and Selling Manual (1991). Articles in Genii & Billboard.

name: Griffith, Tony "Griff", MIMC
bio: (Romford [or Ilford], Essex, England: 1 Sep 1934-) Learned from tricks bought thru comic book ad. Primary school teacher (in North Somerset) & semi-pro magician. Left teaching in 1986 to become to full-time pro magician, working mainly school & trade shows & lecturing. 6 tours of USA. Lectured in Britain, USA, & Europe. Currently lives in Bristol with wife Judith. Wrote Griff on Cards (1963, 36pp), Griff on Close-up (1967, 48pp), An Invitation to Mystery (1967, 64pp), Science Fun (1991), The Magic of Science (2007), Reflections (2007), Further Reflections (2008), Final Reflections (2009), Ultimate Reflections (2010). Articles in Gen, Genii, Alakazam, Mantra, & Hierophant #7. 1 Linking Ring Parade (1997). TV bits. [LR8/97;Genii9/78;Mag;Wh2]

name: Griffith, W.
bio: (Britain: fl.1780s) Pro magician by around 1780. Performed for King George (III?) & Royal Family at St. James's Palace. Kept a small shop where he sold props & medicines and taught magic in London, first at The Hole in the Wall near St. Clement's Church in the Strand and later in Harrow Court off Fleet Street. This was, after H. Dean's, the world's second earliest known magic shop. Around 1780 published and claimed to have written The Whole Art of Legerdemain, which was merely an abridged (to 24 pages) piracy of Dean's book.

name: Griffiths, Owen, MIMC
bio: (Britain: c1917-28 Oct 1989) Childrens magician. Served in India with Royal Artillery in WW II. Then joined Singapore Police, rising to Superintendent. Returned to England after 1959 when Singapore became independent. Edited 3 privately circulated typescript compilations of Goodliffe's Abra editorials: 25 Years with Goodliffe, 1946-1970 (1971, 307pp), 25 Years with Goodliffe, 1972/1973 (1973, 44pp), & Be Businesslike (1973, 354pp). NOTE: No relation to E. Raymond "Fabian" Griffiths.

name: Grigg, Johannes
bio: (Hungary: c1690-) Had only one hand & no legs. Pro stage conjuror with Cups-and-Balls (also equilibrist & musician) in Germany & England. NOTE: His surname is usually misspelled "Brigg" in English & French sources. [Jay]

name: Griggs, Jack
bio: (Isleworth, Middlesex, England: 14 Mar 1936-) Police officer (retired). Learned magic at age 22 from library books & then from amateur Dr McKee. Semi-pro childrens magician and Punch-&-Judy man since age 25. Tricks published in Abra & marketed by Supreme, Davenport's, & Inzani-Henley's. Editor of The Budget 1979-present. [Wh5]

name: Grimaldi, Joseph "Joe
bio: (London, England: 18 Dec 1778 [sic]-31 May 1837) Bastard son of an Italian ballet-master & a Cockney chorus girl. Apprenticed since age 2½ as an acrobat, juggler, swordsman, dancer, singer, & mime in addition to his duties as prop-maker, scene-painter, & choreographer. As a theater clown since 1800 & famous since 1806 -- considered England's greatest & the "father of modern circus clowning" -- the very name of his stage character, "Joey", becoming circus jargon for clown. Sometimes used magic in his act, inventing several bits of "trickwork" such as transforming four wheels of cheese into a coach, changing a lobster into a red-coated soldier by boiling in water, building a man-sized figure of vegetables that would come to life and duel with him. Retired by illness in 1823. Autobio is Charles Dickens (editor), Memoirs of Joseph Grimaldi (1838; repr 1853; annotated ed by R. Findlater 1968, 311pp). Bio is Richard Findlater, Grimaldi, King of Clowns (1955, 240pp). The Mulholland Library incorporates the Kay Robertson Collection of Grimaldi memorabilia. [Ogden]

name: Grimes, Lester [A.]
bio: (Blackinton, Massachusetts: 7 Jan 1884-) Inspired at age 10 by grandpa, William H. Taft (cousin of President Taft & assistant in 1851-52 to J.H. Anderson). Engineer in New York & then New Jersey. Semi-pro magician since 1906. Billed as "The Paper Wizard" did an all-paper magic club act. Trick in Hugard's Annual (1938-39). [SAM;WWM;HMM11/55]

name: Grimm, Georg
bio: (Germany: fl.1830s-40s) Wrote Neuestes Spielbuch oder gründliche Anweisung zur Erlornung der beliebtesten Karten- und Bretspiele ... nebst den Regeln und Gesetzen der verschiedenen Billard-Kegel und Ballspiele (Leipzig: 1840, 384pp), which is an early exposé of the shift (1 & 2 handed), false shuffles, and second dealing.

name: Grimmond, George
bio: (Streatham, London, England: 20 Apr 1901-6 Mar 1985) Pro illusionist & escapist since 1914. Wrote Engineering as Applied to Magic. [Go2]

name: Grimshaw, Bayard, MIMC
bio: (Romiley, Cheshire, England: 26 Aug 1902-14 Dec 1993) Learned at age 8 or 9 from magic section in a child's encyclopedia. Amateur close-up worker plus general magic with assistant-wife Marion. Semi-pro, then pro 2-person mind-reading act with Marion as partner in cabaret & private shows 1943-72 when retired. Magical journalist, collector, & historian. Edited The Magi 1953-58. Last editor of the magic page for The World's Fair 1965-72. Edited The Budget 1974-79. Articles in Genii, New Tops, Abra, Magigram, New Pentagram, etc. [Wh2]

name: Gringras, Samuel
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) A rabbi. Publisher in New York City of Jewish religious works and (since 1978 as "Magico") of occasional reprints of magic classics (beginning with Chap's Scrapbook) & Magico Magazine (1979-81, 4 issues). Trick in Mantra (1976).

name: Grippo, [James V.] "Jimmy
bio: (Mosquito, Italy: 1897-15 Jan 1992) Moved to New York City c1927 where he learned magic. Also a hypnotist. Amateur debut in 1930s. Professional prize-fight manager. Then pro close-up. Coached Veronica Lake in magic for her role in movie This Gun for Hire (1940). Resident magician at Caesar's Palace in Las Vegas since 1966. 1980 AMA Performing Fellowship. 1991 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote (with Geno Munari) The Magic of Jimmy Grippo (1981). Bit parts in several movies. Several TV bits. [Mag;HC;SAM]

name: Grismer, Ray[mond Joseph]
bio: (Wallace, Idaho: 6 Jul 1927- ) Inspired as child seeing a magician. Learned from Erdnase & Fischer's Illustrated Magic. Jazz pianist until c1963 when traded piano lessons for card magic with Dai Vernon. Thence school teacher and semi-pro magician & lecturer. Foremost inventor of finger-ring & rope tricks since late 1960s. Aka "The Idaho Flash". Wrote many booklets, including The Punch Letters (1988, 23pp). Tricks in Talisman, Arcane, Epoptica, Genii, & Linking Ring. Video (1992). Father of Vicki Grismer. [Wh]

name: Grismer, [Victoria Lynn] "Vicki
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 13 May 1958- ) Elder daughter of Ray Grismer. Learned a few tricks in teens. Inspired to study seriously by 21st birthday visit at Magic Castle so she could join as Regular Member. Taught by father. Semi-pro card work at clubs & fund-raisers. Married magic dealer Jeff Busby in 1988, whence known as Victoria Grismer Busby. [Wh]

name: Grivolas, Claude[-Agricol-Louis]
bio: (France: 6 May 1855-7 Nov 1938) Pro magician. Later an industrialist. Entered the cinema business to become one of the builders of the Pathé film empire. [Bar] (Germany: 20 Nov 1895-14 Aug 1981) Pro since 1914, initially as "Groasser-Bellachini". Died in Mannheim, West Germany. [Mül;Roh]

name: Gronowska, Zorika
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1918-Sep 1982) Stage name of Zofia Pliszewska. Pro illusioniste. Died in Katowice. [Mec;Nad]

name: Gross, Art[hur Hartley]
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 11 Feb 1920-) Learned at age 9 from Xmas gift magic set. Moved to Northern California. Pro close-up, mental, & platform magic 1938-42. Worked the San Francisco World's Fair ("Greenwich Village" & Sally Rand's "Gay Paree") in 1939. Thence semi-pro as "Victor St. Leon" while working as salesman & builder (retired in 1980s). Teacher of Bill Devon, Bob Brewer, & Gary Beutler. Articles in Tops & Bat. [Wh2]

name: Gross, Henry
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Learned at age 10. Pro since teens until went into little theater &, later, as writer-editor in New York City. Wrote Pure Magic! (1978, 225pp).

name: Grossi, Professor Carlo
bio: (Italy: fl.1880s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro with card tricks, flag production, and trunk escape. But his telepathy and muscle-reading routine (done with "Madame Roux") was the mainstay of his full-evening show. Toured India (with the World's Entertainers) in 1903, Australia in 1904-05, & England 1907. Also toured Portugal. NOTE: Misreported to have been a Frenchman. [Wal; CMM7/07; Magic8/03; Cam] Grossman, Dr John Henry "Doc", MD, MIMC (Rochester, New York: 17 Aug 1914-8 Sep 1992) Learned at age 11 from a German magic set. Retired pelvic surgeon & gynecologist. Amateur close-up magician. Magic historian & collector. Co-founded Magic Collectors Association in 1950. Performed with wife-assistant as "Prince Vishnu & Princess Rama". Columns "Ask the Doctor" in MUM 1957-1991 & "Americana" in Magic Circular 1960-1990. Many articles in over 9 magazines including Magic Cauldron. President of Magic Collectors Association 1962-64 & its Honorary Lifetime President 1966-92. MIMC 1967. SAM Hall of Fame. Most of his collection went posthumously to Nelson Nicholson. [Se;Wh2]

name: Grote
bio: (Britain?: fl.1940s) Stage name of Carl Grotefeld. Pro close-up.

name: Grubin, Arnold L.
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY: 30 Jul 1929-) Inspired by & learned from uncle. Amateur. Specialized in silk magic. [Th]

name: Grüner, Kurt
bio: (Germany: 20 May 1938-) Magician. Teaches magic & does magic advertising & promotions in Heidelberg. [Nad]

name: Gruppetta, D.
bio: (Valletta, Malta: 26 Apr 1898-) Semi-pro. Invented Instanto Ink and Water, Everlasting Colour Change, The Mystery of Transmission, etc. [Go2]

name: Guarracino, Mario [Rosario]
bio: (Naples, Italy: 20 Jul 1968-) Learned at age 8 from magic sets & a friend. University researcher in Naples. Semi-pro magician since age 15. Specializes in kid-show magic. Pet effects: Guillotine & Zig-Zag Girl. Reviewer for Magia Moderna since 1985. President, Ring 108 Napoli, 1991-present. [Wh5]

name: Gubisch, Wilhelm
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 24 Oct 1890-) Anti-occult researcher. Wrote Hellseher-Scharlatane-Demagogen (1961).

name: Guder, Ferdinand
bio: (Austria: 1842-14 Apr 1878) Aka "Ling Look". Older brother of Louis Guder. Pro sword-swallower & fire-eater. The Guder brothers were hired by Kellar in Panama in 1876 and toured with him until their deaths. Ferdinand died after a liver operation in Hong Kong. [Pr;Vo57;Ch;Dam2]

name: Guder, Louis
bio: (Kaltenleutgeben, Austria: 1852-7 Oct 1877) Aka "Yamadeva". Younger brother of Ferdinand Guder. Pro contortionist & escape artist. While touring with Kellar, died of a ruptured artery on shipboard near Hong Kong. [Pr;Vo57;Ch;Dam2]

name: Guerin, Bernard
bio: (France: fl.1970s-80s) Semi-pro. Leading illustrator of French-language magic works including La Revue de la Prestidigitation, L'Illusioniste, & the 9 books of Jean de Merry. [Mer]

name: Guerrero, Nino
bio: (Texas, USA: fl.1950s-80s) Inspired seeing a local Texas magician. Learned from tricks purchased thru Douglas Magicland catalog. Pro since 1950s. Later taught by Frakson. Performs as "Nino" throughout the USA, Canada, & Latin America. [Mag]

name: Guest, Claud
bio: (Australia: fl.1910s) Lived in Melbourne. Toured Australia as "Wong Toy Sun" since 1911 when he framed a Chinese act, which he continued to his retirement. [Wal]

name: Guest, Leslie P.
bio: (Pelham, New York: 6 Sep 1898-5 Mar 1981) Protégé of Al Baker 1916. Moved to Cincinnati in 1921. Charter member Queen City Mystics (Cincinnati) 1922. Pro magician & shadowist 1931-37. Then salesman in New Jersey & semi-pro magician. Edited MUM for a time after 1938 & 1968-76. Invented “U Name It—I Find It (by 1936) & "Melo-Dy-Namo" (1948). SAM President 1952-53. Dealer (Guest Magic Service) in Summit, New Jersey. His house organ, which he edited, was Guest Magic Chat 1968-72 (11 issues). Wrote Melo-Dy-Namo (1948, 15pp); & Lecture-Demain (1972, 42pp), an analysis of magicians' lecture notes from his extensive collection. Tricks in Genii & New Phoenix, memoirs in MUM. SAM Hall of Fame. [SAM;WWM]

name: Guetle, Johann Conrad
bio: (Germany: fl.1790s-1840s) A private tutor in Nürnberg. Amateur magician. Wrote 11 books in German between 1791 & 1842, all popular expositions of magic tricks.

name: Guibal, Adolph Fernau
bio: (France: c1845-c1896) Aka "Charles Guibal". Learned interpreting for & assisting Verbeck in 1885. Pro. Toured England (late 1880s), USA (1892-96), & Mexico. [CI;Pr;Vo55]

name: Guidry, Felix F.
bio: (Louisiana?, USA: fl.1900s-40s) Afro-American. Pro in the South. Mentor of Ben R. Badley since c1906.

name: Guillemin, François.
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Semi-pro. Aka "Prof. Franck" [sic]. Wrote Les sorciers d'aujourd'hui (1971), based on a field study of the witch doctors of Africa; & Magie traditionelle (1977). [Dif]

name: Guinn, Scott Freeland
bio: (Tacoma, Washintgton: 7 Jan 1964-) Learned in 1972 from a Xmas magic set and then in 1987 from Mark Wilson's book. Pro since 1992 with close-up, parlor, and platform. Pet effects: Sponge Balls, Coins Across, Ropes, Linking Rings, Bill in Lemon, Card Magic. Invented Guinn Utility Backslip 1997. Wrote Great Scott! It's Card Magic (2000, 75pp), Great Scott! It's Coin Magic (2000, 59pp), Great Scott! It's More Magic (2000, 63pp), Never Miss a Trick (2000, 54pp), Officiously Yours (2000, 49pp), Great Scott! It's Even More Magic (2001, 152pp). Tricks in Linking Ring, Visions, Smoke & Mirrors. [Wh01]

name: Guitar, Pressley [H.]
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) His real name. Worked out of Abilene &, later, Dallas, Texas, as manufacturer-dealer of gaffed coins. Invented Cigarette thru Quarter.

name: Guitry, [Alexandre-Georges Pierre] "Sacha
bio: (St. Petersburg, Russia: 21 Feb 1885-24 Jul 1957) Born to a French actor and his wife while touring Russia. Stage and film director-actor. Amateur magician with sleight-of-hand. Played a conjuror in his play L'Illusionniste (1917) and a cardsharp in his film Le Roman d'un tricheur (1936), the latter based on his novel Mémoires d'un tricheur (1935, 139pp). Bios are James Harding, Sacha Guitry: The Last Boulevardier (1968, 277pp) & Bettina Knapp, Sacha Guitry (1981, 245pp). [Katz]

name: Gulmar, Profesor
bio: (Cuba: -28 Aug 1983) Stage name of Gulmar COHEN-HENRIQUES CORELLA. Pro 2-person mind reading act with assistant "Elsa" (Ana Elsa Iser). Toured the Americas, Europe, Asia, & Africa in circus & theaters. Moved to Spain. [Xe]

name: Gunn, L[en] O[liver]
bio: (Starkville, Mississippi: 13 Oct 1896- ) Pro since 1922. Moved to Los Angeles. Then semi-pro on West Coast. Invented "Grab-It" (1932). Column in Genii in late 1930s-early 1940s. Dealer ("Magician's Supply Co.") in Los Angeles area. SAM Hall of Fame. [WWM]

name: Gunnarson, Dean [Wayne]
bio: (Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada: 27 Jan 1964-) Raised in San Antonio, Texas. Inspired at age 9 by mother's gift of a book on Houdini. Moved back to Winnipeg in 1975. Pro escape artist since age 18. Pet effect: Jail Breaks. Holds Guinness Record (1989) for escape from a car crusher (2 min 7 sec). Youngest person & 1st Canadian appointed SAM International Ambassador. TV appearances. A protégé of James Randi, whose designated successor he now is. [Ran;Wh2]

name: Gunther, Robert J. "Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-60s-dead) Former Disney artist. Amateur on West Coast. Billed as "The Sophisticated Sorcerer". Edited Sophisticated Sorcery (1936, 13pp). Co-authored (with Sid Fleischman) 5 booklets: Ready, Aim—Magic!, Call the Witness (1943, 30pp), Top Secrets (1947), The Blue Bug (1947, 19pp), & Call the Next Witness [1940s]. Tricks in Genii. Co-invented (with Fleischman) Floating Room Only (1947).

name: Gurtler Jr, Bob
bio: See: "Kole, André"

name: Gussner-Robin
bio: (Germany: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro magician in Elberfeld. In 1907 published a 7-page promotional brochure.

name: Gustafson, Dick
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) PhD chemist who switched to career in magic. Pro magician & illusionist with assistant-wife Joanne). Works clubs & particularly trade shows, where he is today one of a half dozen top performers. Wrote Professional Illusion Building for the Home Craftsman (1993, 46pp).

name: Gustavsson, Christer
bio: See: "El Duco"

name: Gutelli
bio: (Germany: 31 Dec 1941- ) Stage name of Claus-Dieter Gutmann. 1978 MZvD 1st prize in childrens magic. [Nad]

name: Gutheil, Oscar H.
bio: (Orange, California: 15 Jan 1915-) Inspired at age 5 seeing Thurston show. Moved to Columbus, Ohio. Mentor was H. Adrian Smith. Semi-pro stage act as "Oscar Hugo". Wrote (as "Oscar Hugo") Magi Card Systems (1942, 98pp) & edited (as "Oscar Hugo") Magian 1946-47 (3 issues). [SAM]

name: Guyot, Edme-Gilles
bio: (Besançon, France: 1706-1786) Mathematician by profession. By 1769 was also a dealer in magic props, the earliest known in France. Wrote Nouvelles récréations physiques et mathématiques (1740; with many reprints to 1800). The third volume includes a long section covering some 50 conjuring tricks based in large part (and with proper acknowledgement) on Ozanam. While Guyot went beyond Ozanam in detailing sleights for the Cups and Balls, he omitted his predecessor's coverage of card tricks. Also in German tr by J. Ch. Thenn as Neue phyikalische und mathematische Belustigungen (7 vols, 1772-77). [Dif]

name: Gwynne, Anne
bio: (North Braddock, Pennsylvania: 8 Sep 1896-12 Sep 1979) Born Anna Laura Apel. Aka "Princess Fan Tan". Taught by Jack Gwynne, becoming his chief assistant by 1914 and marrying him in 1915. [Pr;Mar]

name: Gwynne, [Joseph McCloud] "Jack
bio: (Braddock, Pennsylvania: 12 Apr 1895-7 Dec 1969) Of Irish descent, his paternal grandfather having anglicized the surname from the original Gwinn. Son of a Methodist minister. Inspired in 1907 by a schoolmate's tricks. Learned in 1908 at age 12 from aunt's gift of a magic set. Pro illusionist since 1913. In New York City played the Capitol in 1931, the Hippodrome in 1932, & the Palace in 1933 & 1951. Did magic in or for 5 Hollywood movies 1940-41. Toured worldwide with bandleader Benny Meroff's "Funzafire" show 1942-45. Regular guest with "Super Circus" TV show 1951-55. SAM Hall of Fame 1969. Pet effects: Stack of Fishbowls (since 1918), Flipover Box (since 1928), Temple of Angee (since 1935), Anti-Gravity Glasses (since 1942), and the Sand Trick (by 1955). SAM Hall of Fame 1969. Prolific inventor/improver/builder. Invented Flipover Box in 1928, Temple of Angee = Temple of Benares in 1935, and Flying Carpet in 1967. For his bio & repertoire see David Charvet, Jack Gwynne: The Man, His Mind, and his Royal Family of Magic (1986, 297pp). [Pr;Par;Fu2;Tay;Ho]

name: Gydesen, [Waldemar John] "Walter
bio: (Rhinelander, Wisconsin: 14 Nov 1917-15 Jan 1996) Learned at age 10 from magic set. Collector since 1931 of posters (recently sold off), catalogs, & letters in New Britain, Connecticut. Used name "Walter Gydesen" since c1935. Worked for Abbott's 1937-38, Jim Sherman's National Magic Co 1938-39, and as manager of Magic Inc's retail department c1973-c1986. Executive Secretary of Magic Collectors Association by 1969 to present. Wrote 2 booklets, including Tricks with a Sand Frame (n.d.). One time editor of Houdini-Gram. Articles in Dragon & Magicol (of whom he was a former editor). Retired to New Britain, Connecticut. [MUM4/79;Wh2;Wh]

name: Gyleck, Olaf T.
bio: (Denmark: 1886-20 Apr 1967) Taught by amateur father. Moved as child to USA where he was raised in Dixon, Illinois. Pro vaude magician 1907-10 when settled down as a semi-pro. Invented "Ideal Card Effect" = "Mephisto Memory" (by 1919), "Acme Telephone Mystery" (by 1919), & "Gylleck's Challenge Tape Tie". [Dor]

name: Gyngell Senior
bio: (Britain: -1833) Stage name of Daniel Gyngell. Pro since 1788, first as assistant to Flockton, then, after the latter's death in 1794, as his successor. [Hou;Cl;Fr]

name: Gyngell, Master
bio: (Britain: c1796-) Stage name of Joseph D. Gellini Gyngell, aka Gellini Gyngell. Learned c1816 as apprentice to father, Gyngell Senior. Pro as lecturer, pyrotechnist, & high-rope walker until at least age 70 (in 1866). [Hou;Cl] Gysel, Robert H. "Bob" [pronounced by him both GUY-ZIL & GEE-ZIL] (Toledo, Ohio: 18 Nov 1880-5 Jan 1938) Pro mind-reader since 1901 & card manipulator by 1902. Then semi-promentalist-lock picker & full-time machine operator in a Toledo auto plant. Active in exposing psychic frauds, sometimes helping Houdini. IBM Member #637 until expelled in 1928. A trick in Jinx. Bill Miesel is (1995) writing a bio. [Go;Go2;Silver]

name: Gysin, René
bio: (France: fl.1960s-80s) Painter in Paris. Amateur? stage & close-up magician. Aka "Gilden". AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Bronze Medal 1976, Silver Medal 1988, & Gold Medal 1989. [Bou]

name: Ha-Hem-Bey
bio: See: Martin-Bontemps, Auguste

name: Haar, John Calvin
bio: (Fremont, Ohio: 27 Dec 1951- ) Learned at age 25 from a friend teaching a rope trick. Railroad worker since c1969. Semi-pro close-up magician since c1982. Specializes on invisible thread levitations. Wrote 2 lecture notes: The Micro Thread Separation Manuscript (1987, 7pp) & Invisible Thread (1988). [Wh2]

name: Haarz, Erwin
bio: (Osnabrück, Germany: 4 Dec 1931-5 Nov 1974) Founded the Osnabrück branch of the MZvD. Died in his home town. [Roh;Nad]

name: Haas, Alexandre
bio: (Brazil?: c1874-) Pharmacologist living in São Paulo, Brazil. Amateur magician & collector by 1919. Published many notes about magic & magicians in the local press until as recently as 1952.

name: Habitt, Joseph
bio: (Austria?: fl.1820s) Pro stage magician in Germany. Performed his "Egyptian Magic" act in Breslau in 1827. Published a 64-page pamphlet in 1829 attacking 6 journalists who had unfavorably reviewed his performances. Hackman, [Ralph Elias] "Eli" [pronounced E-lye] (Carlisle, Pennsylvania: 27 Jun 1872-25 Nov 1962) Active in magic since age 11. Railway station superintendent in Philadelphia. Semi-pro magician, ventriloquist, and Punch-&-Judy operator. Developed mechanical Punch-&-Judy figures. Mainly a childrens entertainer. On 11 Apr 1923 broadcast world's 1st Punch-&-Judy radio show. Invented Eli's Die Box (by 1924). [SAM;WWM]

name: Haden, Conrad H. "Connie" [pronounced HAYD-en]
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-80s) Amateur coinman & expert craftsman in Brooklyn. Invented Pen Nail Writer = Mental Pencil (1944), Pen-Silly = Breakaway Pencil (1945), expanded shell (late 1940s), & Traffic Lite (1960, a color-changing checker). Made nail writers for some 20 years beginning c1941. Moved to Florida. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Hayden".

name: Hades, Brian M[arlowe]
bio: (Edmonton, Alberta, Canada: 5 Feb 1953-) Elder son of Micky Hades. Learned as child assisting in some of his father's larger stage shows. Amateur performer and pro in father's magic business as head of the publishing division, Hades Publications, until 1988 when he bought that division, the largest magic publishing house in Canada & one of the world's larger ones. Located in Calgary.

name: Hades, [Michael P] "Micky
bio: (Morecambe, Alberta, Canada: 27 Apr 1926- No middle name, the "P" being a letter only [without a period]. His legal signature is "Micky Hades". Aka "The Great Hades". Born in a farmhouse to parents who had emigrated from the area of Poland/Austria. Soon orphaned. Inspired at age 10 in Fall 1936 seeing John C. Green's travelling show. Learned by figuring out some of Green's effects & doing them successfully, thence from books. Debut in teens. Pro, touring Canada until settled down in 1962 as magic dealer & publisher (Micky Hades) in Calgary. Owned a branch shop in Seattle 1974-95. 1991 AMA Literary Fellowship. Incapacitated by a stroke in 1995. Father of Brian M. Hades. Edited Hade-E-Gram 1957-71. Wrote several booklets, starting with The Make-Up of Magic (1962, 72pp), Novel Magic with the Appearing Cane (1963, 49pp), Bang! (1968, 35pp), Magic the Way I See It (1968, 36pp), The New Make-Up of Magic (1974, 132pp), The Conjuror's Book of Stage Illusions (1974, 86pp), The Best of Magic Around the World (1975, 137pp). Trick in Swami. [Se;Wh] Hadji/Hadschi/Hajji/Haci NOTE: Arabic title indicating the user is a Moslem who had made the obligatory pilgrimage (hajj) to Mecca. Thus check under given name, as with Hadji Ali, Hadji Baba, Hadschi Halef, & Haci Sahin.
years: 27 Apr 1926- No middle name, the "P" being a letter only [without a period]. His legal signature is "Micky Hades". Aka "The Great Hades". Born in a farmhouse to parents who had emigrated from the area of Poland/Austria. Soon orphaned. Inspired at age 10 in Fall 1936 seeing John C. Green's travelling show. Learned by figuring out some of Green's effects & doing them successfully, thence from books. Debut in teens. Pro, touring Canada until settled down in 1962 as magic dealer & publisher (Micky Hades

name: Haenchen [Jr], Fred[erick C.]
bio: (Joliet, Illinois: 26 Aug 1903-6 Jun 1983) Debut at age 12. Pro magician with full-evening show in Lyceum & Chautauqua circuits 1923-1931 (billed as "Mysterious Haenchen") when became engineer in Oklahoma City & semi-pro magician. Became a prop maker (Haenchen & Co) from 1931 until 1976 when with new partner George Robinson the company became Viking-Haenchen (later Viking). [WWM;Albo95]

name: Hafler, Raymond W. "Ray
bio: (Ohio, USA: 1910-4 Aug 1982) Debut in U.S. Navy (where he served 24 years as officer) with a flash magic act for service shows. As civilian, a court recorder in Long Beach, California. Did semi-promentalism in the Al Koran manner. Trick in MUM.

name: Hagen, Charles J [oseph]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 9 Mar 1877-29 Oct 1925) Born Karl Hagen. Moved to USA. Aka "The Fakir of Blackwells". Pro dealer, founding Presto Company in New York City in 1905. Edited The Boy Magician 1909-10 (12 issues) & The American Magician 1910-12 (27 issues), both in New York City. Founded the National Conjurers' Association in 1911. Edited N.C.A. Recorder 1913-?, National Conjurers' Association Members Private Publication 1916-20, & N.C.A. Digest 1920-21. First life member of the SAM. [Sphinx4/19;Dif]

name: Hagoort, Jan L. "John
bio: (Holland: fl.1920s) Comedy magician. Pet effects: Bag Escape, Cake Baked in Hat. Visited New York City in 1926 as "The Holland Mystic".

name: Hagy, James [C.], MMC
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 9 Feb 1955- ) Interested in magic since age 8. Lawyer in Chicago. Amateur magic historian. Edited Mystics Magazine 1966-72 (74 issues), Mystics Quarterly 1976-81 (15 issues), & Perennial Mystics 1983-present. Wrote Early English Conjuring Collectors: James Savren and Henry Evanion (1985, 141pp), The One Young: William Henry Young and His Times (1986, 94pp), & Magic for Free (1987). Articles in Perennial Mystics, Magicol, Magic Cauldron, New Tops, etc. [Wh2]

name: Hahne, Nelson C. [pronounced HAHN-ee]
bio: (Dayton, Ohio: 9 Dec 1908-4 Oct 1970) Inspired as youth seeing many famous vaudeville magi & learned from aunt's gift of Hoffmann's Later Magic. Pro commercial illustrator and later art director in the advertising field. Amateur magician. Since 1924 illustrated over 23 magic books plus catalogs and The Linking Ring since 1924 at age 18. Invented the Penetrating Silk (1926), which Joe Berg marketed; & the color-changing "Poker Chip of Camelio" (by 1932). Retired in 1960s to Pompano Beach, Florida, where he died of cancer. Co-authored 3 booklets: Here's Magic (1930, with Joe Berg), Modernism in Pastebord (1930, with Ralph Hull), & Smart Magic (1935, with Ralph Hull). Tricks in Linking Ring, Sphinx, etc. [LR7/95; LR6/49; Th] Haig-Brown, The Rev. William John L. "Bill" (Sutton, Surrey, England: 10 Apr 1915- ) Inspired at age 6, learned at age 8. Semi-pro comedy act. Became Curate of Thames Ditton. Did a Blindfold Drive in 1941. In WW II (as captain in British Army in Europe) co-founded (with Harry Lewis) the Antwerp Magicians' Table in 1945, which closed in 1948. [Go2]

name: Haines, Ronald "Ron
bio: (Fayette County, Ohio: 13 May 1906-8 Apr 1974) Pro dealer & publisher (Haines House of Cards) in Cincinnati (later the Norwood suburb), Ohio, since c1950. In mid-1950s bought the business of John W. Snyder Jr. SAM President 1964-65. Taught Dale Penn. A Mason, he was President of the Invisible Lodge at time of death. SAM Hall of Fame. Compiled 36 Tricks with Fa-Ko Cards (32pp, edited by John Braun). His collection of playing cards was one the world's larger and his collection of gaffed cards one of the more nearly complete. Both collections are now in the SAM Hall of Fame and Magic Museum.

name: Hains, Oldrich
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 3 Aug 1925-) Magician in Czechoslovakia. Member of MZvD. [Nad] "Hal" [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

name: Haldane, Richard
bio: (Quebec, Canada: 1910-25 Apr 1990) Stage name of Ivor Roberts. Of Welsh parents. Learned at age 13. Amateur debut in 1927 in Winnipeg. Provaudeville magician c1929-1956, touring Western Canada & USA. Retired in 1960s.

name: Hale, Cheryl [Denese]
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 1957-) First interested in magic in 1981 when met Howard Hale whom she married in 1982. Debut as assistant at conventions in 1982 for Abb Dickson (again in 1985) & John Calvert. Part-time assistant to Rick Walker 1983-present, working trade shows & private parties. Occasional dual act with Howard Hale 1983-present. Co-owner (with Howard) of Magicland shop in Dallas since 1983. [Wh2]

name: Hale, Howard [Hester], AIMC
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 15 Dec 1951- ) Inspired & learned magic at age 11 from father & uncle, both amateur magi. Pro close-up, parlor, & manip since 1978, working both as single and, since 1983, with partner Cheryl (whom he had married in 1982). Pet effects: Linking Rings, Billiard Ball manip, & Production of Mirror Ball. Since 1983, co-owner (with Cheryl) of Magicland in Dallas (as successor to Gene Jeffries). 1978 TAOM Club Act Trophy & Best Act of Convention. 1984 Bill Baird Award for manip. 1985 Ben Chavez Memorial Award for sleight-of-hand & 1985 IBM Gold Medal. AIMC 1987. Wrote Jewels of Magic (1985) lecture notes. [LR9/85; Genii6/87; Wh2]

name: Halef, Hadschi
bio: (fl.1920s) Pro illusionist in Europe.

name: Haley, Louis C.
bio: (Madison, Wisconsin: 1878-dead by 1937) Inspired in 1890 seeing the A. Herrmann show. Piano teacher & semi-pro magic dealer (Haley Magic Co.) in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1920s. Wrote The Dramatic Art of Magic (1910, 74pp). Trick in Genii. [Dor]

name: Hall, Dorothy
bio: See: Harbin, Dolly

name: Hall, Francis B. "Frank
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Amateur in Gladwyne, Pennsylvania. Invented the Floating Light Bulb in 1929 and premiered by him at that summer's meeting of the Philadelphia SAM Assembly. Marketed by him to Blackstone (2 models in 1931) & a few other stage illusionists. [Sphinx7/31]

name: Hall, G[ranville] Stanley
bio: (Ashfied, Mass.: 1 Feb 1844-24 Apr 1924) Studied psychology in Germany under Wundt & Helmholtz 1876. In 1878 received his Ph.D. from Harvard (under William James), the  $ 1^{st} $ American doctorate in psychology. Lectured at Harvard. At Johns Hopkins 1883-87. In 1884 became a co-founding vice-president of the American Society for Psychical Research at which point he began studying conjuring, becoming a life-long avid amateur. In 1887 founded the American Journal of Psychology, the 1st such in the USA & the  $ 2^{nd} $ important one outside Germany. In 1888 co-founded Clark University (in Worcester, MA) where he served as President and Professor of Psychology until retiring in 1920. Founded the American Psychological Association in 1891 By 1893 he'd awarded 11 of the 14 psychology doctorates given in the USA, including to Jastrow (in 1886). Published a pioneer paper on children's lies (1890). Amateur magus, having studied with Yost and Hermann, bought many sleight-of-hand tricks and a "kit of tricks". Performed for guests in his own home, always explaining the tricks afterwards. Autobio is Life and Confessions of a Psychologist (1923, 622pp). Bios are Lorine Pruette, G. Stanley Hall (1926, 266pp) & Dorothy Ross, G. Stanley Hall (1972, 482pp).

name: Hall, H.
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s) Billed as "The Great Wizard" & "The Great Wizard of the North". Minor pro at London fairs 1840-45. Pet effects: Bullet Catch, Chinese Rings, Morison's Pills, Magic Dice, & Enchanted Caddy.

name: Hall, Lou
bio: See: Hull, Burling

name: Hall, Newton "Newt
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro comedy night-club magician as "Hal Newton" in the 1930s-50s. Managed Holden's magic shop branch in Philadelphia in 1940s. Tricks in Jinx.

name: Han, Trevor [Henry], MA, PhD, MIMC
bio: (Wakefield, England: 28 May 1910-8 Mar 1991) Chartered surveyor & lecturer on bibliographic studies. Amateur magician since 1930s & collector of magic books (many of which are now in The Magic Circle Library). MIMC 1947. Wrote The Testament of Ralph W. Hull [1945, 116pp], Nothing is Impossible [1946, 62pp], Reading is Believing (1947, 104pp; repr [1969]), A Bibliography of Books on Conjuring in English from 1580 to 1850 (1957, 96pp), Old Conjuring Books (1972, 228pp), The Card Magic of Edward G. Brown (1973, 211pp), & Some Printers and Publishers of Conjuring Books, 1800-1850 (1976, with Percy Muir). In the occult field wrote several important books, including The Haunting of Borley Rectory (1956, with Dingwall & Goldney), Four Modern Ghosts (1958, with Dingwall), Strange Case of Edmund Gurney (1964, 219pp), Search for Harry Price (1978), and The Enigma of Daniel Home (1984, 148pp). Articles in Budget, Abra, Magic Circular. See Thomas A. Sawyer, Men of Letters: Stanley Collins and Trevor H. Hall (1991, c70pp). [MC6/91;La2]

name: Halle, Johann Samuel
bio: (Germany: fl.1780s-1800s) Teacher at the cadet corps in Berlin. Wrote Magie; oder Die zauberkräfte der Natur (Berlin: 4 volumes, 1783-86, averaging 575pp each). Although containing no conjuring tricks as such, this work is often included in bibliographies of early magic because of its descriptions of several electrical, mechanical, and optical experiments. Also wrote Fortgesetze Magie (Berlin: 12 vols, 1788-1801). Includes complete programs of Pinetti & others plus explanations of many automata and illusions. The 16 volumes total some 9,000 pages.

name: Hallema, Flip
bio: See: "Flip"

name: Hallett, David
bio: (Britain: -23 Apr 1984) Ex-accountant. Served 6 years with RAF in WW II. Pro childrens magician. Played Buckingham Palace 3 times for the Queen. Wrote It's Not Magic! [1960s, 48pp]. [Daw2]

name: Hamblen, Rolland [A.]
bio: (USA: -late 1970s) Demoed for Thayers in mid-1930s. Full-time pro on Pacific Coast in 1930s-40s. Co-invented (with Bill Larsen Sr) the metal plates version of Card in Wallet. Wrote Hamblen's Four Possible Impossibilities [1933]. Died in Oregon. [Tay]

name: Hambujer
bio: (Denmark [sic]: 1848-1924) Pro sleight-of-hand. Played Dublin (1859) & Boston (1860). [Vo58;Cl;Mo;Fr]

name: Hamburg, Prof. Ernst
bio: (Germany: -1 Jun 1926) Pro magician of the old school.

name: Hamburger, Dr Louis P., MD
bio: (USA?: fl.1890s-1920s) Physician. Amateur magician. Famed for levitation of glass of water from fingertips, a trick that reportedly baffled Sigmund Freud.

name: Hamik-Amico, Fritz
bio: (Austria: 1900-1938) Stage name of Fritz Hamik, aka "Amico". Ex-actor & singer in Vienna. Pro kid-show magician, specialized in flower tricks. Retired in last years, confined to sickbed. [Al;St]

name: Hamilta
bio: See: Berry, Pierre

name: Hamilton
bio: (Neuvy-sur-Loire, Nièvre, France: 25 Mar 1812-26 Feb 1877) Stage name of Pierre-Étienne-Auguste Chocat. Robert-Houdin's assistant (since 1850), brother-in-law (since 1852), & successor (1852-61) as director of the Théâtre Robert-Houdin. Invented Lifting a Child by Its Hair in 1860. Retired in 1862. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Hamilton, "Doc
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Minor pro illusionist at an amusement pier in Long Beach, California, where he premiered Thayer's Monster Guillotine in the late 1920s.

name: Hamilton, James, AIMC
bio: (San Pedro, California: 22 Jul 1942-) Stage name of James Hamilton Muszalski since 1960s. Learned at age c8 from aunt's Xmas gift of a Great Foodini magic set. Semi-pro in Long Beach 1958-1979 when went full-time with close-up, stage, & lectures. Moved to San Francisco in 1980 where he also works as a street magician. Magic collector & historian, specializing in the Herrmanns. Wrote Alexander Herrmann: The Napoleon of Necromancy (c1996) & The Herrmanns in San Francisco (c1996). Articles in Magicol & Revue de la Prestidigitation. [Wh2]

name: Hamilton, John P.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Amateur cardman in New Hampshire. Discovered the Free Cut Principle & applied it in his Eyes of the Gods card trick (1948), the Australian Deal (1951). Invented Scientific Rope, Computer Deck, & Silk Flight (1958). Articles in Phoenix 1945-52, HMM (since 1956), & Pallbearers.

name: Hamilton, Warren
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Pro prop maker. Invented & made the Jo-Anne version of the card duck since 1946.

name: Hamley, J[ohn] G.
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro dealer with W.& F. Hamley, the main toy shop in London. Invented Palmo Ball (by 1903). Reprinted under own name Bland's Chapeaugraphy; or Twenty-five Heads under one Hat (London: n.d., 57pp).

name: Hamley, William Henry
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s) Pro dealer with W.& F. Hamley's London toy shop.

name: Hamman, Bro. John [C.], SM
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 3 Sep 1927-5 Dec 2000) Brother of Society of Mary. Learned at age 25 while recovering from polio. Famous amateur cardman since having been publicized in 1958 by Paul LePaul. Highly & subtly creative, he invented the Final Ace (1953), the Hamman Count (1958), Homing Card (1959), Micro Macro (1959), Fan-To-See (by 1964), Hal-Deuce-Ination (by 1966), Flushtration Count (by 1969), Gemini Count (1974), Blushing Joker, etc. 1981 AMA Creative Fellowship. See Paul LePaul, LePaul Presents the Card Magic of Bro. John Hamman, S.M. [1958, 47pp]; Stephen Minch, Seven Deadly Miracles (1984, 37pp); & Richard Kaufman, The Secrets of Brother John Hamman (1989, 252pp). Tricks in Apocalypse, Pallbearers, Epilogue, Magic, MUM, etc. 1 video (1991). [Monti-MUM/5/71; HMM/6/58] [Monti;MUM5/71;HMM6/58]

name: Hammond, H[arold] C.
bio: (Australia: fl.1940s-70s) Magician in Sydney, Australia. Performed as "Professor Austral".

name: Hamulecki, Anton Markowicz
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1753-1850) Son of a Prussian colonel. Reportedly learned magic assisting Cagliostro. Moved to Russia where his surname was spelled Gamulecki. There he exhibited static illusions & many automata and founded the first museum for automata in Russia. [Mec]

name: HAN Ping-chien
bio: (China: fl.1900s-20s) Pro stage magic. Toured the West with major success: USA (1909, 1914-16, 1922-23), London (1912-14), & Paris (1912). Invented the Han Ping Chien move (by 1914) & possibly (or Laurant) the Crash link by 1917. [Pr;Dif]

name: Hanajima, Setsuko
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s) Pro magicienne in Tokyo with dove & spring-flower production act.

name: Hanco
bio: (Britain: -1903) Stage name of Theodore Bernstein. Pro escapist who enjoyed a brief fame in England in 1903 before killing himself because of jealousy over his female assistant. Pet effect: the Barrel Escape. [CMM11/06]

name: Handy-Bandy
bio: (Germany: 30 Sep 1960- ) 1984 MZvD 3rd prize in closeup. [Nad] (Egypt: 1899-1933) Stage name of Fuad Makarius. Lived in Germany. Pro stage magic (with scenery made in Berlin theater workshops). Did both Japanese & Egyptian acts. His co-star assistant-wife was "Nadja-Nadyr" whom he had met in Berlin c1923. They played London in 1927. Pet effects: 4-Aces with jumbo cards & Vanishing Lamp (made by Conradi-Horster). Died in Berlin.

name: Hanlon Jr., Tom "Tommy
bio: (Parkersburg, West Virginia: 14 Aug 1923- Beginning as pro c1938 toured East Coast with a comedy magic act with a giant and a dwarf. Moved to Los Angeles. Main assistant in 1943 with Orson Welles' Mercury Wonder Show and in Welles' illusion segment in the 1944 film Follow the Boys. Then mainly in New York City area, in theaters and nightclubs with flash act ("Tommy Hanlon & Jeanne") since mid-1940s. Played the New York Palace a record 47 times (in 1950, 1952, 1954) and did USO shows in 1952 (with wife Murphy). Moved to Australia for nightclub bookings and became a daytime TV star 1961-78. Since 1978 has co-owned three circuses in Australia, the current one being that nation's largest, the 60-truck and caravan Silvers Circus. [Tay,p.44;Wh]
years: 14 Aug 1923- Beginning as pro c1938 toured East Coast with a comedy magic act with a giant and a dwarf. Moved to Los Angeles. Main assistant in 1943 with Orson Welles' Mercury Wonder Show and in Welles' illusion segment in the 1944 film Follow the Boys. Then mainly in New York City area, in theaters and nightclubs with flash act ("Tommy Hanlon & Jeanne"

name: Hansen, Arthur
bio: (USA: 1893-) Pro escapist, aka "Suicide Hansen". [St]

name: Hansen, Geoffrey
bio: (Richmond, California: 1 Sep 1953- ) Inspired by 2 films: Dante in A Haunting We Will Go & Pollock in Europe by Night. Learned magic during hospital stay as child in the 1950s. Pro manip, stage magic, illusions, mentalism, hypnotism, & escapes. By 1977 he had appeared in over 40 countries throughout the world, mainly in the Far East and Pacific. Starred in French TV film Mandrake (1976). A karate expert (7th degree black belt), he appeared in 4 Hong Kong kung-fu films 1977-79, 3 of which included his magic. Articles in Genii, MUM, Boletín Unico de Magia, etc. Writes "Personality Parade" column in New Tops since 1989. [NT1/89;Wh2]

name: Hansen, Leif Rosengaard
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 4 Jan 1946-) Interested in 1958 by a magic catalog. Pro circus illusionist since 1966, touring Europe as "Los Facitos" 1966-74 & thence as "Lee Pee Ville". Married his partner, Pia, in 1967. Worked amusement parks since 1981. Since 1984 has longest-running magic illusion show with ballet & large animal illusions in Germany at "Phantasialand" near Cologne. Presented his pirated version of Copperfield's Flying in 1993. TV bit. [Win]

name: Hansen, Rolf
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 10 Oct 1885-18 Aug 1959 [sic]) Stage name of Rudolf Hans "Rolf" Holba. Son of a leather merchant. Ex-engraver. Pro magician since 1912, initially in Austria & Germany. Toured USA in summer 1914. Did 40 tricks in 10 minutes. After WW I toured variety theaters throughout Europe. A teacher of Oscar Enzfelder in 1943 & Joe Asta. Died in Vienna [sic]. [Win;St;Al]

name: Hansen, Walter J.
bio: See: “Lazern, Emile”

name: Hanson, Herman
bio: (Esperod, Sweden: 26 May 1882-12 May 1973) Inspired around age 10 by travelling magician. Moved to USA in 1897. Pro stage magic since 1906, briefly as "Hansone and Company", then as "Mystic Hanson Trio" & "Hanson and the Burton Sisters". Married his assistant, Lillian Burton, in 1915. Stage manager & understudy to Howard Thurston 1929-35. Managed Holden's Magic Shop branch in Boston 1936-60. SAM President 1942-43. Named 5th SAM Dean of American Magicians in 1959. SAM Hall of Fame 1968. Wrote Howard Thurston's Floating Ball Routine (20pp). Articles & tricks in Barnstormer & MUM. Autobio is Hanson & Zweers, The Magic Man (1974, 104pp). [Pr;Ho;HMM5/61]

name: Hanson, Lillian
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: c1899-26 Jan 1987) Born Lillian Burton. Dancer. Principal female assistant to Herman Hanson 1914-35, marrying him in 1915. With sister Gladys they played vaude as "Hanson and the Burton Sisters" & "The Magic Man and his Magical Maids.

name: Hanussen, Erik Jan [sometimes "Van"]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 2 Jun 1889-24 Mar 1933) Stage name of Hermann Steinschneider, son of an Austrian-Jewish comedian. Famous pro pseudo-psychic (telepath, muscle-reader, prophet, etc) since 1918. By 1930 converted to both Protestantism and Nazism. Prominent in Nazi circles until murdered in Berlin under mysterious circumstances now known to have been as a result of a secret arrest & execution by the Nazi SS. Wrote Worauf beruht das? and Das Gedankenlessen/Telepathie (Vienna: 1920). Autobio is Meine Lebenslinie (1930). See Erich Juhn, Leben und Taten des Hellsehers Henrik Magnus (Vienna: 1930) for a 264-page novel exposing the methods of a thinly disguised Hanussen, written by one of his dismissed assistants. Suppressed by the Viennese courts, this book is quite rare. Subject of 2 dramatic movies: Hanussen (1955) & István Szabó's Hanussen (1988), which won a 1989 Oscar nomination for Best Foreign Film. [Ran;Dif;Mec;St;Rey]

name: Hapner, Max
bio: (Caldwell, Kansas: 4 Aug 1930-) A leading semi-pro at school shows, etc, with assistant-wife Salli. Works mainly the Central states (living in Manitou Springs, Colorado since c1960). Pet effects: Bubbles & the Basket Trick. [Wat;Wh]

name: Hara, Prince
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Pro illusionist & stage pickpocket.

name: Harad, [Charles F.] "Doc
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-60s) Amateur cardman in Indianapolis. Did a mediocre Ghost Show in Indianapolis in 1929. Taught the Thumb Tie by Harry Willard. Invented "Grab-a-Dollar" (by 1944). Wrote 1 manuscript, Harad's Super Two Card Location [c1935] who's rights he sold to Abbott. Article in Genii. NOTE: Rumors of being killed in 1974 while rehearsing a Russian Roulette routine confuse him with Doc Conrad. [Walk2]

name: Haraldini
bio: (Germany: 15 Jul 1935-) Stage name of Harald Bockstatt. Pet effect: infinite production of lit candles. 1973 FISM 1st prize for comedy magic.

name: Haran, Joannes
bio: (France: fl.1760s) Pro at St. Germain Fair in Paris 1762 when his props were destroyed by fire. [Cl]

name: Harary, Franz
bio: (Ann Arbor, Michigan: c1962-) Inspired by a magic trick in a cereal box. Attended first magic convention at age 13. Major pro illusion inventor-designer for, among others, the 1983 Rose Bowl, the 1984 Michael Jackson tour, Alice Cooper, & David Copperfield. Performs, mainly at conventions, in "Rock Magic" style. Developed (with Mark Kornhauser) a comedy version of the Eric Lewis Twister illusion. Invented Walking thru a Girl (1988), etc. His factory is in Los Angeles. 1987 Jack Gwynne Trophy. TV bits.

name: Harbin, Dolly
bio: (Britain: 23 Dec 1907-30 Nov 1982) Born Edith Lilian Philp. Took stage name of "Dorothy Hall" while studying drama in London in late 1920s. Pro magic debut as "Dorothy Hall". Demoed at Gamages. Married Ned "Robert Harbin" Williams in 1932. Played Maskelyne's in 1933. Became assistant to Robert Harbin. Further teaching from Harbin and Fred Barlow. Pro illusionist during WW II in Britain & India. Later toured as assistant to her husband, including Canada (1949) as "The Sensational Harbins". [Pr;Mar]

name: Harbin, Robert
bio: (Kokstaad [or Balfour?..., South Africa: 12 Feb 1908 [sic]-12 Jan 1978) Stage name of Edward Richard Charles "Ned" Williams. Son of a Cornishman. Learned magic as a boy from books. Pro illusionist, initially as "Ned Williams". Moved to London in 1929 at age 19. Took "Robert Harbin" as stage name at his debut at Maskelyne's (St. George's Hall) in 1932 [sic]. In WW II toured with ENSA. Toured Canada & the USA in 1949-50, ending with a week at the New York Palace. TV bit on NBC-TV's 1957 "Festival of Magic" show. Worked on a cruise ships in last few years. Prolific inventor of stage illusions, including Vanishing Radio (early 1940s), Dippy Magnet (1950), Stonehenge (1950), Block Control (1950), Little Tipler (by 1965), Topsy-Turvy, Assistant's Revenge, & Zig-Zag (1965), the last being one of the most famous of all illusions. 1970 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" award. 1971 AMA Creative Fellowship. 1976 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote Something New in Magic (1929, as "Ned Williams"), Demon Magic (1938, 56pp), Paper Magic (1956, 103pp), How to be a Wizard (1957, 175pp, ghosted by Will Dexter; repr 1968 as How to be a Conjuror), Paper Folding Fun (1961, 102pp), The Magic of Robert Harbin (1970, 193pp, edited by Peter Warlock), Illustrated Teach Yourself Magic (.....; with Spanish tr as Ilusionismo, 1979), Harbincadabra (1979, 311pp), etc. Tricks & comment in Magician Monthly, Hughes News, & Abra. 1 or 2 movie shorts. Several TV bits. Audio. See also Martin Breese, The Harbin Book (1983, 38pp). [LR2/92;Wad;Pr;Mag;Le;La2;Tay;Go]

name: Harcourt, Fred
bio: (Britain: 1867-12 Jan 1906) Debut at age 8. Billed as "The Boy Magician". Minor pro illusionist, working both music halls & carnivals. Played the London Empire in 1901. Toured Australia 1902. [Wal;Cl;Bur] (Budapest, Hungary [not Appleton, Wisconsin, as he claimed]: 29 Feb 1876-12 Jun 1945) Stage name of Theodore W. "Theo" "Dash" Weiss (born Ferencz Deszo Weisz). Immigrated to USA in 1878 [not 1874] with mother & siblings. Learned assisting older brother Houdini. Adopted "Harden" in 1900 when left the Houdini Brothers to take his own act on the road but later that year modified it to "Hardeen", which he kept. Pro escape artist. Toured Europe c1900-c1907. According to Dawes, Hardeen was first to appreciate potential of straitjacket escape in full view. Hired by Houdini, he headed Houdini's unsuccessful Film Development Corporation that produced newsreels and feature films 1922-1926, leaving the stage for that period. SAM President 1929-30. Did the magic act in Olson & Johnson's Hellzapoppin' Broadway comedy show in the early 1940s. Wrote The Life and History of Hardeen: 20 Years of an Eventful Career on the Stage [c1926]. NOTE: Manny Weltman was first to establish from birth records the true place & month & day of Hardeen's birth, which he published in Houdini: Escape into Legend (1993). Ronald Hilgert's study of ship records had correctly implied his birth in Hungary. [Pr;Gib;Mo;Ho]

name: Hardeen Jr
bio: See: Makentosh, Douglas Geoffrey

name: Hardin, Henry
bio: (Hartford, Connecticut: 2 Nov 1849-5 Jan 1929) Nom de magique of Prof. E[dward] A. "Ed" Parsons. Pianist & academic music teacher in New Haven. Semi-pro close-up magician. Highly innovative, having invented several of the tricks attributed to magic supply houses by Hoffmann in 1903. Dealer in New Haven (Henry Hardin & Co) ?-1905-1909-? SAM member #91. Invented Monte-Cristo Deck (by 1905) & Princess Card Trick (by 1905). Popularized Stanyon's Top-of-Pocket Dodge in 1905. Wrote Memorandum of Magic [1905], his catalog of original tricks.

name: Harding, Bart
bio: (Rosyth, Fife, Scotland: 20 Apr 1919- ) Stage name of Arthur Frederick Bridgman since 1950. Learned magic at age 10 from library books. Carpenter to full-time pro magician in 1970, specializing in kid-show & mental magic. Pet effects are his own "Princess's Necklace" (for children) & "Fantastic Memory" (for adults). Private dealer in Southampton. Invented the Bart Harding Stacked Deck. Articles in Magic Circular, Club 71, & Magigram. [Wh5]

name: Hardy
bio: (Aichach, Bavaria, Germany: 12 Jan 1949-) Stage name of Erhard Smutny [sic]. Self-taught at age 10 then studied with Henk Vermeyden. Pro in West Germany, specialized in childrens magic. Tricks in Magische Welt. Guinness record for longest magic act (60 hours). Took over Max Haug's shop in Pfronten/Rieth. [Win] Hardy, The Great (Belgium: fl.1980s) Pro illusionist and world champion card thrower.

name: Hardy, Ann
bio: (Belgium: fl.1950s-60s) Stage name of Anny Dierckxsens (Madame Joseph Dierckxsens). 1952 FISM 1st prize for women.

name: Hardy, David "Dave
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 15 May 1924-22 Dec 1996) Corporate-commercial lawyer in San Francisco. Amateur magician since 1968 when bought TV Magic Cards from a pitchman in Selfredge's in London. Specializes in card & mental close-up. Has represented Johnson Products, Goshman, Busby, & others in magico-legal matters. Tricks in Magick. Died of heart attack after long bout with cancer. [Wh]

name: Hardy l'Enchanteur
bio: (France: -12 May 1987) Stage name of Jean Tardy. Pro illusionist in 1930s-70s. Founding-President of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Saint-Etienne 1938-65. AFAP Master Magician. [Dif;Bou]

name: Hardy, Ken
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 23 Feb 1945-) Stage name of Kenneth Olofsson. Semi-pro manipulator. NMK Nordic Champion 1967, 1968, 1970. Wrote Trolla med Musse (1974, 188pp). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Olofsson". [Mec]

name: Harkey, David [Ray]
bio: (Springfield, Oregon: 25 Jun 1959-) Inspired at age 5 by having a nickel pulled from his ear by amateur Lowell Rhoden. Learned as Eagle Scout from special magic issue of Boy's Life & then purchased Multiplying Billiard Balls. Pro close-up & parlor magic, originally as "David Ray". 1988 PCAM 1st Prize for close-up & 1st Prize for innovation. 1989 Linking Ring Trophy for Best Parade. Lectures widely. Wrote Simplicities (1988), Body Language (1989, 29pp), From the Depths (1989, 22pp), & Simply Harkey (forthcoming 1990). Has published over 80 effects: Linking Ring (2 "Parades"), Genii, New Directions, Apocalypse, New Tops, & Epotica. [Wh2] "Harland, The Wizard" SEE: Townner, Harland

name: Harmington
bio: (Cavaillon, Vaucluse, France: 10 Jul 1860-28 Aug 1947) Stage name of Charles Rey, natural son of Marie Rey & Charles Fauque. Later legally changed his name to Charles Fauque [often misspelled "Fanque"]. Pro sleight-of-hand & illusions. Played the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1886-90. Joined the ASAP in 1905. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Harper, David "Dave
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Stage name of Millard Grubb. Pro mentalist & hypnotist. Audios (1988 & 1991), video bit (1988).

name: Harrell, Jerry Foster
bio: (Moristown, Tennessee: 10 Jul 1947- ) Learned in 1960 at age 14 in Phoenix, Arizona, at Rabbits in Our Hats Magic Club and working at Bert Easley's magic shop. Semi-pro since 1970 at age 23. As "Jay Foster" 1970-73 on Bozo TV show in Richmond, Virginia. Pet effects: Close-up & Jack Miller's Rings. Now a video production manager at Old Dominion U. Tricks in Genii (1976) & Linking Ring (1980). [Wh01]

name: Harries, Bengt [pronounced HARR-iss]
bio: (Norrköping, Sweden: 16 Nov 1927- ) Stage name of Bengt Gösta Harry Mobäck. Younger son of Harry Harries who taught him since early childhood. Pro prop maker in father's magic shop ("Harries") since age 17. Took over "Harries", the leading magic shop in Sweden, as co-owner (with elder brother Lennart) 1960-76 & as sole owner 1976-present. Collector of magic books. [Wh2]

name: Harries, H[arry]
bio: (Sweden: 28 Jan 1892-18 Apr 1980) Stage name of Karl Harry Mobäck. Got his start by replacing Uno Sunell in the Sunell brothers escape act in 1912. Pro circus juggler to comedy magician & escapist. In 1910 founded "Harries" (in Norrköping), which soon became Sweden's leading magic shop, running it together with his assistant-wife Annie & their 2 sons, Lennart & Bengt (who now runs the business). [Dif:St]

name: Harries, Lennart
bio: (Sweden: 16 Apr 1918-11 Feb 1976) Stage name of Lennart Mobäck. Elder son of Harry & Annie Harries. Co-proprietor (with Bengt Harries) of Harries Magi in Norrköping 1960-76.

name: Harrington, Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1870s) Stage name. Minor pro in dime museums. Taught John C. Green c1879.

name: Harrington, Jonathan
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 1809-4 May 1881) Inspired at age 11 seeing a vent. Debut in 1826. Pro comedy vent-magus since 1829. Aka "Old Harrington". [Pr;Ch;Mo]

name: Harris, Ben [Christopher]
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 25 Nov 1959- ) Inspired at age 5 seeing carnival magician do Cups & Balls. Pro since 1979, specializing in original card & close-up magic and psychic effects. Did restaurant magic full-time 1979-87. Magic dealer, manufacturer, & exporter of mail-order BHM Industries in Brisbane 1980-early 1990s. Invented Epic Flight (1982) & Cosmosis (the original & much-pirated floating match-over-card effect). Edited Australian Magic Magazine 1983-85 & New Directions 1985-present. Won 1985 award for TV investigative reporting exposing Uri Geller. Dropped out of pro magic in early 1990s. Wrote 17 books & booklets 1980-90, including For Close-Up Magicians' Eyes Only! (1980, 44pp; repr 1985), Magic from which Memories are Made (1981, 130pp), Killer Klose-Up (1983, 77pp), Out of His Mind! (1985, 130pp), Gellerism Revealed (1985, 95pp), Off the Wall (1988, 104pp), & Mad Fax and Other Mysteries (1990, 96pp). Articles & tricks in Magic Circular, Genii, MUM, Magic Manuscript, Apocalypse, New Directions, Skeptical Inquirer, LR, & the Australian editions of Playboy & Penthouse. Audios (1985, etc), video (1985). [Geni3/90;Lo2;Wh2]

name: Harris, Lou[is R.]
bio: (London, England: 28 Dec 1912- ) Moved to USA where c1935 he learned magic at National Magic shop in Chicago. Semi-pro illusionist. Assistant to Blackstone at various times from c1939 to c1952. Assistant to Dante in early 1940s. Pro illusionist since c1942. Aka "Harris & Harris" 1945-46. With the Dr. Ogre Banshee spook show 1946, then as the original "Dr Doom" until 1947-49 when he sold name & show to John Daniel & Harland Towner for $170 and left magic for retail business. [Wh5]

name: Harris, Paul
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Inspired at age 5 by a Svengali pitchman & gifts of a Svengali deck & Cups-and-Balls. Invented Cardboard Connection (1977) & Twilight. Pro close-up until late-1980s when briefly switched to film industry as scriptwriter (initially for Nice Girls Don't Explode). In 1989 again on magic lecture tour in USA & abroad. Prolific author, including Super Magic (1977, 134pp), Las Vegas Close-Up (1978, 150pp), Close-Up Entertainer (1979), The Inner Circle (1980), Break-Through (1981), Close-Up Fantasies--Finale (1981), A Close-Up Kinda Guy (1983), Close-Up Seductions (1984), Secrets of the Astonishing Executive (1991, with Bill Herz), and The Art of Astonishment (1996, 3 vols, 312+323+324pp). See also Jerry Mentzer, The Magic of Paul Harris (1976, 67pp). Tricks in MAJ (1987), Magic, etc. 5 videos (2 in 1985, 1 in 1988, 1 in 1989, 1 in 1996).

name: Harris, S. Frank
bio:
(Derby, England: 4 Jun 1894-20 Jul 1970) Businessman in Derby. Semi-pro comedy magician, doing a schoolmaster act. Trick in Ibidem.

[See also: Collins, Stanley]

name: Harrison
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 25 Dec 1948- ) Stage name of Harrison J[ohn] "Harry" Carroll, billed as "Harrison, The Man With the Magic Touch". Taught at age 9 by friend Ray Mertz. In late 1970s studied with Eddie Fechter. Semi-pro until 1982 when went full-time with close-up & some mental magic. Now mainly works trade shows. Pet effect: Flaming Credit Card. Tricks in Linking Ring, etc. [Wh2]

name: Harrison, Charles
bio: (Frolesworth, Leicestershire, England: 27 Oct 1890-3 Jul 1974) Learned magic at age 11. Paid magic debut at age 16. In British Army in WW I. School headmaster to director of handicraft center. Semi-pro magician 1910s-50s, specialized in cards. Aka "Rajah Khan". Trick in Magic Wand. [Go2] "Harrison, Harry" ERROR for "Harrison" (Harrison Carroll)

name: Harrison, Jim
bio: (Sweden: 1908-1950) Stage name of Harry Gimström. Merchant in Horndal, Sweden. Semi-pro magician. Performed together with Max Hofzinser for King Gustav V.

name: Harrison, Vincent
bio: (Canada: fl.1940s) French-Canadian from Montreal. Aka "Kaiser". Invented Spear-It Knife (in early 1940s), which was marketed by Tannen's in 1948 & published in Tarbell #5 later that year. Also invented a Silk Blow method. [HMM9/48]

name: Hart
bio: (Britain: fl.1760s-80s) Pro conjuror & exhibitor of trained dogs & pigeons since as early as 1768 when he began billing himself as the "King's Conjurer". [Cl]

name: Hart, Christopher [John]
bio: (Nanaimo, British Columbia, Canada: 22 Feb 1961- ) Learned at age 13 from library book. Pro since age 23, specializing in manipulative magic. Pet effect: T&R Music Sheet. Moved to Hollywood. Plays mainly casinos, clubs, & corporate shows in the USA with appearances in Canada, Japan, & China. 1986 NY Magic Symposium Gold Cup. TV bits in USA & Japan. Played "Thing" in the 1991 The Addams Family movie. 1997 Grand Prix at the First International Magic Festival and Competition in Shanghai. [Wh2]

name: Hart, John "Johnny
bio: (Britain: 1945-) Protégé of Harry Stanley in teens. Pro birdman to illusions. Magic Circle Young Magician of the Year 1961 with his budgerigar act. In USA in 1965 playing the Ed Sullivan Show (TV), Las Vegas, & Reno. Co-star (with Zee) at the Magic Castle (London) 1985-86. Retired due to illness in 1993. [Genii5/65;Wat]

name: Hartley, Frank
bio: (USA: -1922) Card magic.

name: Hartling, Pit
bio: (Frankfurt-am-Main, Germany: 25 Sep 1976-) Student (in 2001) of literature & psychology at Frankfurt U. Semi-pro magician with card magic & comedy. 1994 FISM 2nd Prize in Card Magic. Member since 2000 of the Escuela de la Magia. Tricks in Kaufman's Flicking Fingers (1998), Genii, Magic, plus German, French, Dutch, & Spanish magic periodicals. Wrote The Little Green Lecture: Lecture Notes (1998). [Wh01

name: Hartman, J[erard] K[ent] "Jerry
bio: (New York City, NY: 1 Mar 1934- ) Learned card magic at ages 8-10 from amateur father. Lawyer with investment counseling firm. Amateur cardman since childhood. Wrote 7 booklets: Secret Subtraction (1970), Odd Lifts (1971), Packet Magic (1972), Means & Ends (1973), Super Dupes (1974), Card Fare (1975), & Loose Ends (1978). Plus 2 books: Card Craft & After Craft. Over 200 pieces in Pallbearers Review, Epilogue, Chronicles, Apocalypse, Richard's Almanac, Linking Ring, Kabbala, Precursor, Magic, etc. See Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of J.K. Hartman (1982, in French). [Lo;Lo2;Wh2]

name: Hartman, Paul
bio: (San Francisco, California: 1910- ) Pro dancer, actor, magician, & singer. Teamed with wife Grace as "The Hartmans". Broadway debut in 1932. Also did a burlesque magic act in their 1950 "Tickets, Please" Broadway show. [This Week20 May 1950;HMM6/50]

name: Hartman, Ray
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Pro assistant to Doc Nixon (1914) & Tampa (1918). "Hartmans, The" SEE UNDER: Hartman, Paul

name: Harto, James S. "Jim
bio: (Webster, Massachusetts: 7 May 1870-5 Nov 1933) Stage name of James S. Harte since 1894. Self-taught. Amateur debut in Webster at age 12, adding vent that same year. Pro since debut at age 14 at Bristol's Curio Hall dime museum, Worcester, Mass., with magic & a side-show illusion. Toured with A Night With the Spirits magic show & several major circuses. Friend of Houdini since 1895. Married Catherine M. Wren in 1901. Contributed in 1901 to the "Card Tricks" section in Erdnase's The Expert at the Card Table (1902). Then toured his Leon Harto Magic Show (1903) & did more circuses. Wrote Successful Money Making Enterprises (by 1905). Did successful vaudeville crystal gazing act as "Chandra the Mystic". Wholesale magic dealer-prop maker (as "James S. Harto") in Indianapolis since 1905. In the 1920s he grew increasingly insane from tertiary syphilis. In sanitarium in 1930 when his wife took over management of the business. His effects were auctioned by her in 1944. Bio is Thomas A. Ewing, Two Hartes That Beat As One (1993, 47pp). [Wh91;LR12/33;WWM]

name: Hartop, A[rthur] W.
bio:
(Britain: fl.1900s-30s) Minor pro illusionist as "Amasis" (1909-25), "Li Sing Foo" (1919 when toured a Chung Ling Soo type act authorized by Lou Robinson), "Ben Said, the Egyptian Funjurer" (1922-34), & "Prof. Johnny Hottoff". Played the London Coliseum in 1910, the Paris Empire in 1912, & London's St. George's Hall often from 1922 to 1934. [Pr;Magic7/10;Magical World10/13]

[See also: "Harto, James S."]

name: Hartz, A[ugustus] F[rederick] "Gus
bio: (Liverpool, England: 8 Sep 1843-21 May 1929) Son of German immigrants (father was a jeweller/watchmaker) who on moving to England changed their name from Hartz to Hart. Thus born Augustus Hart. Learned assisting older brother J.M. Hartz, moving together to London in 1853. Moved together to New York City in 1866 where with Gus as assistant they performed for a year before touring America (including California & Salt Lake City) until 1870. In Dec 1870 they became magic dealers (Hartz Magic Repository) on Broadway until 1876 when sold the business to W.J. Judd. Gus then performed alone as "Professor Hartz". Moved to Cleveland, Ohio, where in 1884 he dropped magic to become a theater manager until retired wealthy in 1920. Memoirs in Cleveland Leader (3 & 17 Feb 1901) & The Linking Ring (Jun 1927). [Pr:Vo56;LR6/97;Mo, p95]

name: Hartz, George
bio: (Liverpool, England: fl.1870s) Younger brother of A.F. "Gus" & J.M. Hartz whom he followed to the USA by Feb 1871 when he opened a magic shop in Boston, advertising props, lessons, & private parties. Moved shop with new partner (John?) Levy late that year to New York City where they went out of business around 1874. [Mo, pp70-71; LR6/97]

name: Hartz, Joseph Michael "Joe
bio: (Liverpool, England: 10 Aug 1836-29 Jun 1903) Born Joseph Michael Hart. Older brother of A. F. "Gus" Hartz (see) & George Hartz. Inspired at age 12 seeing Robert-Houdin show. Self-taught in father's watchmaking shop. Debut in 1854 in London where he moved in 1858, becoming a pro & prop maker-dealer. Since 1859 worked only with glass props, an act he'd been assisted in developing by Henri Herrmann. Played the London Crystal Palace c1860 for 3 months. Worked in USA 1866-81 as "M. Hartz". Dealer (with partners A.F. Hartz & John Levy) on Broadway in New York City 1870 until 1876 when sold to W.J. Judd. Leaving his brothers Gus & George behind, he moved back to England in late 1881, switching to pure sleight-of-hand. Invented Devil of a Hat routine by 1883. Died of Bright's disease at home in London. Wrote Hartz's New Book of Magic (1866, 24pp; repr 1869) & Professor Hartz's Tricks and Diversions with Cards (1875, 510pp). See Professor Hoffmann, "Recollections of Hartz" in his Magical Titbits (1911), 67-211. [LR6/97;Cl;Ch;Pr;La;Go2;Vo56;Mo,p66-67,95;Albo95; Magic10/01,7/03,9/03]

name: Hartz, Larry
bio: See: Stenner, Robert Mason

name: Hartz, Leo
bio: See: Horowitz, S. Leo

name: Haru-Kawa
bio: See: "Veno, Robert"

name: Hase, Kazuyuki [pronounced HAH-SAY]
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Resident of Kamakura. Former student of cinema at Nihon U. Amateur magician. Comedy close-up.

name: Hasegawa, Haruko
bio: (Japan: fl.1950s - 19 Jun 2005) Aka Sanko Hasegawa. Pro. Wife & widow of Satoru Hasegawa whom she succeeded as Chair of the Nihon Kijutsu Renmei [Japan Magicians Association] 1955-present, which with 600 members is the largest or second largest magic society in Japan. She hosted the 1976 PCAM convention that was held in Tokyo.

name: Hasegawa, Satoru
bio: (Japan: 1915-23 Oct 1955) Pro. Founder-Chairman of the Nihon Kijutsu Renmai [Japanese Magicians Association] 1933-55. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Satore". [Mec]

name: Haselmayer, Professor Louis
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 18 Sep 1839-19 Apr 1885) Learned by lessons from Hofzinser. Amateur to pro (by 1865 when he was assistant to Compars Herrmann). Toured USA (1868), New Zealand (Feb-Oct 1872 & 1881), Australia (1872, 1873, 1874, 1880, 1882), China (1881), & India (1881). Invented the Stylocarfe (a type of xylophone) by 1868 when he played it during his act. By 1872 had added plate-spinning & performing mice & canaries. Died in Vienna. Autobio & tricks as New Book of Magic (Melbourne: [1870s?], 40pp). [Magicana10/90; Bo#199:Vo57:St-Mo:Wal:Magic6/02] Bo#199;Vo57;St;Mo;Wal;Magic6/02]

name: Haskell, Robert "Bob
bio: (USA: 1914-1972) Pro since age 19. Nightclub work on West Coast. In WW II toured with assistant-wife Madelaine. 1951 Sphinx Award. Played the magician's assistant in Hollywood movie The Mad Magician (1954). Tutored Dick Zimmerman. Invented the Split Deck (by 1955), "X" Salted Shaker (in 1957), Cashacheck (by 1959), Deep Freeze, Thirst Go, Candelite, & possibly the Appearing Candle (by 1964). Wrote The Magic of Haskell (1962, 32pp). Article in MUM. [St]

name: Hatal, Michael
bio: (Hungary: -28 Oct 1899) Pro magician. Killed performing the Bullet Catch at the Hungarian Odd Fellows Hall in New York City. [Mahatma11/1899]

name: Hatch, Richard [Clawson] "Dick
bio: (Pasadena, California: 24 May 1955-) Inspired at age 10 by grandfather teaching him how to vanish a card. Two degrees in physics from Yale. Full-time pro close-up & platform magician since 1983. 1985 New England Close-up Competition 1st prize. Has worked the Magic Island in Houston, Texas, since 1986. Has toured USA & Europe. Pet effects: Gypsy Thread, Cups-&-Balls, Everywhere & Nowhere, & Linking Rings. A magic historian. Founder co-owner (with Charlie Randall) of H & R Magic Books. Edited-translated Fischer's The Magic of Johann Nepomuk Hofzinser (1985). Is currently translating the Hofzinser card book & Dammann's Lives of the Jewish Conjurors. Articles in Genii, MUM, Magicol, Epoptica, & Yankee Collector. NOTE: Incorrectly called "Dick" by persons who don't know him well. [Wh2]

name: Hathaway
bio: (Worcester, Massachusetts: 9 Jun 1891 [sic]-) Stage name of John Hathaway Butler. Inspired as youth seeing Kellar, Albini, & Brindamour shows. Pro since age 19 with magic & illusion act on Orpheum circuit, etc. After 1919 worked double-act with assistant-wife as "Hathaway & Ruth" until 1930s when Ruth was replaced by "Doreen the Exotic" (Doris, his new wife). Then did minor crystal gazing act as "Dr. Martin". Famous for his Card in Balloon apparatus, which he marketed by 1940. [Pr;WWM;Th]

name: Hatta, Kazuo
bio: (Japan: fl.1960s) Pro manip & dove act. Toured Europe in 1960s. [Dif]

name: Hatte, Michel
bio: (Valognes, Manche, France: 2 Jul 1931- ) Self-taught at age 10. Pro dealer ("Mayette Magie Moderne") in Paris since 1965 when he took over from André Mayette. In 1991 the shop passed to Dominique Duvivier. AFAP Master Magician. Collector. Wrote De l'utilisation des fleurs à ressort en prestidigitation (1976, with J. Hodges) & Grands Illusions. Articles in Le Magicien & Revue de la Prestidigitation. [Wh5]

name: Hatton, Henry
bio: (New York: 16 Dec 1837-24 Dec 1922) Stage name of P[atrick] H[enry] Cannon since 1867. Inspired seeing Heimbürger, J.H. Anderson, & Macallister. Self-taught. Wrote (as P.H. Cannon) the 12 "Lessons in Magic" series, which ran from 1865 to 1867 in Our Young Folks magazine (Boston). Notable because, like Hoffmann's later Modern Magic, it was largely based on Ponsin. Pro since 1867 when he interrupted the "Lessons in Magic" series to begin touring. Retired to become a writer. Joined SAM in May 1902 as Member #21. Co-authored (as "Henry Hatton" with Adrian Plate) Magicians' Tricks: How They Are Done (1910, 344pp), a classic that Henry Hay rightly called the "first American general textbook" of magic. Its chapters had originally appeared in The Century Magazine, but the co-authors drew the wrath of many colleagues for public exposure by permitting key sections to be reprinted in St. Nicholas, a best-selling magazine for boys. Hatton weathered this scandal to become President of SAM 1912-14. Was 2nd editor of MUM. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr]

name: Hauer, Cornelius
bio: See: "Larette, C. H."

name: Haug, Max
