bio: (Pfronten/Rieth, Germany: 16 Apr 1913-18 Jul 1975) Operated a magic shop in Pfronten/Rieth until it was taken over by Hardy. [Roh]

name: Hauptmann, H[enry] R. "Harry
bio: (Australia: fl.1930s) Newspaper reporter in Sydney. Founding editor The Imp (Sydney) 1935-37. As "Rex, the `Ace' Magician" wrote 2 booklets: The Wicked Uncle & How to Routine Magic (32 pages). Tricks, articles, & reviews in The Imp & article in Sphinx. [McC]

name: Haviland, [Henry] "Hal
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-1960s) Pro magician. Played Vancouver in 1944. Did USO shows in WWII. In 1950s worked as "Al Avalon". Then in 1960s as clown with the Polack Brothers Shrine Circus. [Tay]

name: Haviland, Jimmy "Jim
bio: (London, England: 30 Apr 1932-18 Feb 1991) Pro street magician in Britain, aka "Jimmy the Street Conjuror".

name: Hawkesworth, Eric
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-70s) Pro, specializing in paper magic. Wrote booklets for beginners: Practical Lessons in Magic (1967, 71pp), Conjuring (1971, 86pp), & A Magic Variety Show (1973, 96pp).

name: Haxton, Francis, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 20 Jun 1907-30 Jan 1995) Learned at age c12 from gift magic set, then Hoffmann's book of card tricks. Building engineer. Amateur close-up with cards. Pet effect: Platform Aces. Longtime correspondent of Stewart James. London Society of Magicians Gold Medal. British Ring President 1960-61. In 1960s at annual British Ring Rings performed burlesque stage magic with Peter Warlock as "Diabola & Deb" and "Rudy & Trudy". They also played this latter act in Holland & Italy. Died in Leicestershire. Many card effects in Linking Ring, Pentagram, New Pentagram, Abra, Magicana, Tops, New Phoenix, Pallbearers Review, Hugard's Magic Monthly, Ibidem, Magiram, etc. [LR4/95;NT12/69;Wh2]

name: Hay, Henry
bio: See: Mussey, June Barrows

name: Hayashi, Hakumin
bio: (Japan: fl.1960s) In 1968 became first recipient of the prestigious Tenkai Prize. Wrote Nyoigoma no subete [The Self-rotating & Levitating Top] (1969).

name: Hayden, Allan
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro comedy close-up magician & lecturer. Wrote Card Sharp on Duty (1983, 71pp), etc.

name: Hayden, Whit" [misspelling]
bio: See: Haydn, Whit

name: Haydn, Whit
bio: (Clarkesville, Tennessee: fl.1960s-90s) Learned magic at age 10. Studied philosophy & theology in college. Pro close-up magician, beginning as a street magician in New York City 1968-69. Thence worked theme parks, the Magic Castle (1970s), & now mainly trade & industrial shows. 1980 AMA Stage Magician of the Year. 1996 AMA Parlour Magician of the Year. [Jef;Mag]

name: Hayman, Jack
bio: See: Hyman, Jacob

name: Hayworth, Rita
bio: (New York City, NY: 17 Oct 1918-14 May 1987) Stage name since 1937 of Margarita Carmen Cansino, born of a Spanish father & an American Anglo-Irish mother, she was a fine professional Spanish dancer until 1935 when she began her Hollywood film career. Orson Welles trained her in 1943 as his principal stage-magic assistant, and they played several USO dates that year. Married Welles in 1943, separated in 1947, and divorced in 1948. Died of Alzheimer's disease. Bios are Barbara Leaming, If This Was Happiness (1989, 404pp); and Joe Morella & Edward Z.

name: Hayes, Alf[red Thomas], MIMC
bio: (Sydney, Australia: fl.1950s-90s) Learned at age 7 from purchase of magic set. Pro magician since 1962, specializing in children magic, close-up, & as MC. 1969 Stockholm 1st prize in micro-magic. Founder-owner "DeLarno's International Magic Centre" (the Sydney branch of LeLarno's magic shops) since 1966. MIMC 1991. Articles in Abra, Geniis Magic Journal, & Magicol. TV bits. [McC; Magicana#8/89;Wh4]

name: Hayes, Talbot
bio: (Somersetshire, England: 1858-) Learned as a schoolboy. Performed at schholz & parties. Left England in 1878 for Australia. Settled in South Africa since 1879. Pro magic & illusion variety magician in 1895-96 season but thence a business owner in Cape Town & semi-pro magus. South Africa correspondent for Magic since 1900. Tricks in Magic. [Magic8/02]

name: Healy, Lynn
bio: (Kingston, Ontario, Canada: 30 Apr 1959-) Inspired by & learned magic from library books at age 9. Semi-pro stand-up since 1976. Moved to USA in 1980. Married to Jeff Busby 1980-86. Recently, working out of her San Francisco apartment as a seamstress ("Lynn's Sewcery"), making topits and other fabric props. [Wh]

name: Heaney, Gerald V.
bio: (Berlin, Wisconsin: fl.1910s-30s) Son of a wealthy local jeweller. Pro as founder-owner-manager of the Heaney Magic Company in his hometown 1914-1930s, which also published a few books. Also toured the mid-West in vaudeville as "Heaney the Great" around 1920. Bought out the Lindhorst Magic Shop in 1919 and absorbed the Oaks Magical Co in the 1930s. Acquired several of Jane Thurston's props in 1938. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Heany".

name: Heath, Royal V[ale]
bio: (New York City, NY: 6 Jan 1883-25 Jul 1960) New York banker, stockbroker, & amateur expert in math. Amateur magician. Invented Tapp-It (1925) & Diciphering Dice (1927). Wrote mathematic (1933, 128pp; repr 1953). Tricks in Sphinx & HMM. [Th]

name: Heba-Haba Al
bio: (USA: -1991) Stage name of Al Andrucci. Pro bartender-magician in Chicago since 1940s.

name: Hebenstreit, Alwine
bio: (Germany?: 23 Feb 1933-) Assistant-wife of Horst Hebenstreit ("Mikado") with whom she performed in Germany as "Hexy & Mikado". [Nad]

name: Hebenstreit, Horst
bio: (Germany?: 21 Mar 1934-) Magician in Germany as "Mikado" with assistant-wife "Hexy" (Alwine Hebenstreit) as "Hexy & Mikado". [Nad]

name: Hector, Dr D. S., PhD
bio: (Sweden: fl.1890s-early 1900s) Chemistry teacher in Malmö, Sweden. Amateur magician. Translated Hopkins' Magic as Magiens Värld (Stockholm: 1899) & Hoffmann's Modern Magic as Trollkonsternas Bok (1918). Father of Nils Sture Hector.

name: Hector, Nils Sture
bio: (Malmö, Sweden: 10 Apr 1900-20 [sic] May 1965) Son of Dr D.S. Hector (see). Left law studies to become successful pro magician as "Hector El Neco". Played Copenhagen (by 1923) & Finland. Wrote 30 Trolleri-tricks och tidsfördriv (1941), 52 förbluffande kortkonster (1942), Trolleritricks för scen och salong (1943), Trettio förbluffande kortkonster (1950), Tretiosextrolleri tricks (1950), & Sim Sala Bim (Halmstad: 1963). [Dif;St]

name: Hédé
bio: (Paris, France: 4 Feb 1883-27 Aug 1950) Stage name of Édouard-Jules Durand. Son of a lithographer. Debut as pro magician-ventriloquist at age 17. Also as "Les Wardson-Hédé" did 2-person mindreading with partner-wife Rénalda. In 1920 founded the Théâtre Unic, a travelling show, which lasted until 1941 when it was wrecked. Retired in 1948. [Dif]

name: Hedengren, Nils
bio: (Finland: 16 Oct 1913-) Senior clerk in Helsinki. Amateur comedy magician as "Fakir Kronblom". Committee member of Finnish Magic Circle (Taikapiiri) since 1947.

name: Hédolt, J.
bio: See: Dhotel, Jules

name: Heft, Rodney M [atthew] "Rod
bio: (London, England: 26 Jun 1944- ) Inspired around age 4 by seeing a Robert Harbin show & bought a few tricks. Immigrated to Canada in 1955, becoming a naturalized citizen. Began serious study in 1960 with Hay's The Amateur Magician's Handbook. Pro teacher. Amateur magician & historian of Canadian magic. Column "Canadian Conjuriana" in Levitator. [Bo3;Wh]

name: Heil
bio: (Germany: fl.1830s) Popularized the Decapitation Trick (with knife) in Germany in 1831.

name: Heilbut, Samuel
bio: (Britain: -1914) A student of Charlier c1880. A clever amateur who performed for charity. Carried all his props in his pocket. Lived in London. [Cl]

name: Heimbürger, [Johann Friedrich] Alexander
bio: (Münster, Germany: 4 Dec 1819-25 Jul 1909) Aka "Herr Alexander". Son of a Prussian policeman. Inspired by seeing Ludwig Döbler. Learned in 1839 assisting German magician Ferdinand Becker at fairs. Then with the exhibitor Kalewsky in 1840. Pro apparatus conjurer on own in 1841-42 when he toured north Germany with phantasmagoria, etc. Toured USA 1843-44 & Latin America 1844-1852 or 1854 (with shows in USA again in 1846 & 1849). Pet effects: Goldfish Bowl production (in Chinese garb), Spirit Bell, & Aerial Suspension (by 1850, although he told Houdini he had invented it in 1845 or 1846). In 1854 [or 1852] returned to Münster where he could afford to retire immediately. Houdini visited him there in 1903 & 1906. Memoir to 1844 is Alexander, Ein moderner Zauberer (1882, 2 vols, 293+296pp). Wrote Das Zauberbuch (1st ed, [1900]; 2nd ed, 1901; 7th ed, 1913, 128pp). [Win;Pr;Sal;St;Cl;Mo]

name: Heinemann, Otto
bio: (USA: 1862-25 Mar 1934) Of German parentage. Moved to Germany. Pro illusionist by 1902. Toured USA as “Mellini” before 1906. Managed the Passage Panopticon theater in Berlin until 1907. Toured Europe. An infamous copyist, which puts in doubt the claim Invented several he illusions, including reportedly Aga, which he at least premiered in Berlin before WW I. Died in Berlin. [CMM12/06,4/07,8/07;St;Al] Heinrich, Dr Kurt A., MD (Berlin, Germany: 22 Aug 1899- ) Inspired at age 14 seeing birthday party magician. Surgeon & urologist. Amateur magician, specializing in parlour tricks, cards, & mind reading. Moved to New York City in 1936. [SAM]

name: Heldman, Ernest "Ernie
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 1915-8 Nov 1977). Pro since 1930s. Hosted weekly TV "The Parade of Magic" show on KSD-TV St. Louis 1947-1962. In 1960s moved permanently to New Orleans. Invented Tarot Thought! Tricks in New Phoenix & articles in Linking Ring. [Monti]

name: Heller, George Waldo
bio: (New York City, NY: -1932) Stage name of George Waldo. Pro stage illusionist. Toured Australia in 1889, 1891, & 1931. In later life as a businessman & semi-pro magician, occasionally toured India or South Africa until his death. [Dor;Wal]

name: Heller, George Washington
bio: (Williamsburg, Virginia: 22 Feb 1860-20 Aug 1928) Raised in Richmond & Washington, D.C. Manufacturer & amateur magician. Joined SAM in 1902 as Member #23. [SAM]

name: Heller, Haidee
bio: See: Heller, Robert

name: Heller, Harry
bio: See: Warnecke, Bruno

name: Heller, Robert
bio: (Faversham, Kent, England: 10 Aug 1829 [sic]–28 Nov 1878) Stage name since 1851 of William Henry Ridout Palmer. Son of a church organist. Student in 1844 at King's School, Canterbury [sic]. Concert pianist. Inspired to take up magic by seeing Robert-Houdin in London in 1848. Taught by W.H. Cremer Jr. Pro stage magician since 1851. Toured USA 1852-1868. Also did famous second-sight act with "Haidee Heller" (no relation but billed as his sister) 1868-78. World tour 1869-73, played Britain & Ireland 1874-77, returning to the USA in 1877. Died next year of pneumonia on tour in Philadelphia, a wealthy man. His main assistant and secret stage confederate until his death was E.J. Dale & his manager had been Edward Beadle. Invented the Duck Tub (1868) & possibly the Coin Ladder. Bios are Harry Clapham, Melody Magic (1932) & Frank Koval, Robert Heller: Music and Mystery (1985, 20pp). See Harry Hermon, Hellerism: Second-sight Mystery (1884, 129pp). [Pr;LR4/2003;MUM1/83;CI;Ch;Hou;Vo56;Wal;Mo;Bur;Magic5/07]

name: Hellins, Harry
bio: (USA: 13 May 1868-6 Jan 1924) Pro vaudeville illusionist, juggler, & musician.

name: Hellis, Professor Robert
bio: (Britain: fl.1860s-90s) Photographer by trade. His "Robert Hellis & Company" also operated in London at 13 Silver Street, Kensington, as letterpress & general printers. Semi-pro minor magic dealer ("Magical Athenæum") at the Silver Street address from early 1870s to c1890. Teacher (of Prof Hoffmann in 1873 & Dr Holden) and performer. Was a contact for Charlier. Retired from magic c1890 to work full-time at photography as "Hellis and Son, Photographers". Invented Hellis change by 1876. [Daw94;Cl]

name: Hellström, Axel
bio: (Augsburg, Germany: 23 Dec 1893-27 Jan 1933) Stage name of Axel Vogt by 1928 when he moved to USA. Pro muscle-reader. Returned to Germany in 1933, dying in Munich. See Robert A. Nelson, Hellstromism (1935, 21pp). Uncle of the following. [Jay;Berg;St;Ran]

name: Helms, Harry
bio: See: Heyne, Henry B.

name: Helms, Mercer
bio: (New York City, NY: 20 Apr 1933-) Inspired in 1940s seeing MacDonald Birch. Learned in 1945 from Gilbert magic set. Full-time pro since 1962 with dove act. Compiled index to Tarbell's original mail-order course. Articles in Tops. TV bits. Featured in film Warlock (1991). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Hemingway, David
bio: (Bradford, Yorkshire, England: 1936-) In Preston, Lancashire, full-time pro dealer 1960-80, then since 1981 as "Designer Magic" a major illusion builder & consultant to illusionists & TV shows. Wrote How to Ensure a Full Datebook (1965, 20 unnumbered pages), etc. Edited Close-up Magic Bulletin 1962-69 (22 issues). Articles in Abra, Linking Ring, etc. NOTE: Surname often misspelled with 2 "m"s. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Henderson, [James Bradley] "Brad
bio: (Frankfort, Kentucky: fl.1980s-90s) Pro with sleight-of-hand, mind reading, and bizarre magic. Collector of rare magic books & mechanical apparatus. Teacher of magic. 1998 TAOM Comedy Magic Award. Has designed magic sets for toy companies. Wrote 2 manuscripts: The Dance (2001, on cold reading under a pseudonym) and Three Pieces with Commentary (2001, on close-up). Contributor to books by Ammar, Lovell, Racherbaumer, and L&L. [Wh01]

name: Henderson, Prof. Milton
bio: (USA: late 1840s-11 May 1925) In U.S. Navy in Civil War, serving on Monitor vs. Merrimac. Popular pro society magician in New York City.

name: Hendricks, Forrest P.
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 11 Jan 1909-14 Dec 1991) A Mason. Learned magic at age 13 from a magician. Pro for c30 years, specialized in mental magic. US Air Force in WW II. Then amateur in St. Louis, Missouri, where he worked in insurance. Edited The Spirit of St. Louis 1929-41 (23 issues), the official bulletin of IBM Ring #1. IBM President 1953-54. Articles in Linking Ring. [Monti;St;Wh2]

name: Hendricks, Thom
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Newspaperman in Birmingham, Alabama. Semi-pro magus as "Thomas the Magician". Published-edited The Magnet 1953-61 (37 issues). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Henricks" & "Herrick". Hendrickson, E[dgar] A. (Brooklyn, New York: 30 Jul 1860-1917) Learned in 1874 by tuition from a pro.

name: Hendrik
bio: (Holland?: 1876-1934) Prince of the Netherlands and "Heinrich" of Mecklenburg-Schwerin. Amateur magician, taught by Austrian magician E.G. Homes.

name: Hennicke, Professor
bio: (Ireland: fl.1870s-90s) Minor pro. Toured Britain, New Zealand (1877), Australia (1878-90), India (1890). Billed as "The Great Wizard of the East". Pet effects: Aerial Suspension (in 1877 with Mrs Hennicke as "Miss Burdetta Stella") & the Needle Trick (1877-78). [Wal;Cl]

name: Hennig, Bruno
bio: (Zinten, East Prussia, Germany [now .....]: 6 Jul 1927 [sic]- ) Inspired in 1949 seeing a magician. Public relations manager in Oldenburg, West Germany. Semi-pro comedy magician as "Joro". Pet effects: Wandering Bottle & Guillotine. Invented the Floating Cork in 1956. Awarded the 1990 MZvD Kalanag-Gedächnis-Ring. Wrote Joros Becherspiele (1981). Over 50 articles in Magie, Magische Welt, & Aladin. A bio (by Uwe Schenk & Michael Sondermeyer) is Das Joro-Buch 1993 (176pp). [Wh2]

name: Henning, Doug[las James]
bio: (Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada: 3 May 1947-7 Feb 2000) Inspired at age 6 seeing TV magician. Learned from book. Debut at age 14. Wrote teen column for Micky Hades Hade-E-Gram around 1960. Took Honors B.Sc. in physiological psychology from McMasters U. Pro stage illusionist. Tutored by Dai Vernon and Slydini. First public triumph in 1974 as star of Broadway magic-musical The Magic Show. A Canadian-made feature-film version starring Henning has so far been released only in Canada in 1981. 8 TV specials since 1975. 1976 AMA Award of Merit. 1977 AMA Magician of the Year. Married Barbara DeAngelis in 1977. Played the Las Vegas Hilton in 1978. Starred in his 2nd Broadway magic-musical, Merlin, in 1983. Many TV bits, including 9 on the Carson show 1975-86. Went on "indefinite" stay in India, developing the Maharishi Vedaland Theme Parks. Died in Los Angeles of liver cancer. Wrote (with Charles Reynolds) Houdini: His Legend and His Magic (1977, 192pp). [Se;Rey;HC;Walk]

name: Henri
bio: See: Lyle, Henry L.

name: Henri, Mons.
bio: See: Novra, Henry

name: Henry, M[onsieur]
bio: (Britain: fl.1780s-1820s) Stage name of Galbraith. Pro since 1788 when he played London at the Lyceum & Astley's. Billed as "Professor of Natural Magic". Played the Adelphi Theatre in London 1824-29 for several weeks each year. Falsely claimed invention of aerial fireworks. [Cl;Fr;Pr]

name: Henry, S[heldon] S[pahr]
bio: (Jamestown, Ohio: 13 Sep 1891-18 Aug 1947) Pro illusionist since 1907. Aka "Professor Henry". A star since 1912 of both Lyceum & Chautauqua circuits in the USA & Canada. Briefly did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Li Chung Soy". Toured Mexico, Cuba, & China. Played US Army camps in WW I. Retired c1939. [Pr;St;Ho;WWM]

name: Henry, T. Shekleton, BA
bio: (Australia?: fl.1890s) Skeptical student of spiritualism. Wrote Spookland (Sydney: 1894, 80pp; repr Chicago: 1902, 74pp).

name: Hensel, Eduard
bio: (Austria: -1928) Theater painter & actor. Amateur magician. Also sold magic props in Innsbruck. Wrote Das Buch der Geheimnisse (1877, 43pp), Der Vortrag des Zauberers (1897, 80pp, with Conradi), & Lexicon der Magie (1898, 184pp), plus several small brochures, including Zauberlieder & Die moderne Magie. Died in Berlin. [St]

name: Hepsonh
bio: (France: 31 Mar 1876-26 Apr 1942) Stage name of Gaston[-Georges-T.] Goy. Lawyer to magistrate to lawyer. Amateur magician, specialized in coins & general magic. Collector of documents. ASAP Vice-President 1928-39. NOTE: Misspelled "Hepsonn". [WWM]

name: Herbert, Jack
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 1906-4 Jan 1970) Stage name of Herbert Jungclaus. Pro. Lived in Chicago. [Pr]

name: Herbert, [Terence James] "Terry", MIMC
bio: (West Norwood, London, England: 4 Feb 1935- ) Articles in Abra, Magic Circular, Magic Magazine, Magical Digest, & Magigram. Video segment (1988). Many TV bits in South America, Britain, Europe, & Japan. [MC10/83;Wh2] Herby, The Great (Torres Vedras, Portugal: 7 Dec 1955- ) Stage name of José Francisco Caroça Costa, aka "Carrilho Caroço". Debut in 1969. Pro general & card magic after 1973, touring USA, Canada, Hungary, Yugoslavia, Germany, & Cyprus. [Cam]

name: Hercat, Prof.
bio: (England: 1843-10 [or 26] Apr 1913) Stage name of R.D. Chater. Originally a journalist, later an actor when in 1865 or 1866 while performing in Australia, he was inspired to take up magic by seeing Joseph Jacobs. Then pro stage illusionist (also some vent) since 1868. Invented She, which he debuted at Egyptian Hall in 1888. Also invented the Blue Room (by 1891 when performed by Kellar). In 1891 he played Waterloo House in London. Thence gave only private shows & began writing. Wrote Card Tricks and Conjuring Up-to-Date (1895, 121pp; new ed as Conjuring Up-to-Date, 1908, 142pp), Hercat's Ventriloquist and Ventriloquial Dialogues (1905, 104pp), Latest Sleights, Illusions, Mind-Reading and New Card Effects (1906, 157pp), Chapeaugraphy, Shadowgraphy and Paper-Folding (1909, 89pp), & Hercat's Simple Tricks (1912, 78pp). [Pr;Go2;St;Cl;Vo56]

name: Herfurt, Kurt [Franz]
bio: (Potsdam, Germany: 1 Apr 1935- ) Learned at age 9 from book. Computer engineer in Munich. Semi-pro magician since age 15, specialized in comedy stage & trade-show magic. Aka "Wokurelli" before 1979; since 1980 billed as "Kurt Herfurt--Comedy in Magic". Articles in Genii & Magie. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Heriot
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of J.P. Goldthorpe. Humorous magician & shadowist by 1901. Minor dealer & manufacturer (Heriot) in Oldham by 1909.

name: Hermalin
bio: (Britain: Jan 1886-) Stage name of Robert Jackson. Inspired seeing Walton & Lester, the comic conjurers. Pro music hall magic since 1900. Sold all his props to Houdini in Paris in 1914. Wrote Workable Wizardry [1923]. [Go2]

name: Herman, Black
bio: (Amherst, Virginia: -1935) Afro-American. Stage name of Herman Rucker. Top pro black straight magician & illusionist until his death. Inspired Gene Elmo c1926. Wrote Secrets of Magic: Mystery and Legerdemain. Died in Louisville. [Ebony12/49]

name: Herman, [Francis Joseph] "Frank
bio: (New York City, New York: 8 Nov 1916-5 Jan 2000) Raised in Poughkeepsie. Learned at age 10 from Gilbert Mysto Magic set & library books. Paid debut at age 12. Pro since age 17 demonstrating Mysto Magic sets. Added troublewit & vent to his comedy act. Moved to Los Angeles in late 1930s. Demonstrator for Bert Wheeler (1938-39) & Floyd Thayer. Assistant to Russell Swan in 1939. In US Air Corps Special Services 1942-45. 9 years on local TV as "Skipper Frank" in 1950s & with the "TV Magic Party" in 1960s. 1st to do full-week stand-up at Magic Castle. Pet effect: Professor's Nightmare. Invented Jake the Snake (1940), etc. Wrote 9 booklets including 15 Methods for Doing the Cut and Restored Necktie (1942), Necktie Magic (1971, 19pp) & That's the Troublewit (1982). Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, Tops, Gypsy Trader, etc. [LR3/80; MUM6/89; Mag;Wh2]

name: Hermann, Melot
bio: (France: 1 Jan 1879-dead) Pro sleight-of-hand stage magician since c1895. Toured Britain (1901-02 & 1908) & Paris (1902 when he played the Olympia). Pet effects: Soup Plate-&-Handkerchiefs and the telescoping Flagstaff. Retired in 1913 in Switzerland. [Cl;Magic11/01,3/02;Bur;CMM11/06]

name: Hermann, Michaelis [also Moritz]
bio: (Krosnowice, Poland: 1 May 1835-13 [sic] Feb 1901) Popular pro performer & prop maker in Berlin. Prospered from giving private shows there. Court Conjuror to Kaiser Frederick III in 1880s. Invented Stroubeika by 1888. Died in Berlin. Wrote (as "Moritz Hermann") 2 books in German: Die Geheimnisse der Falschspieler (1900, 64pp), which exposes gamblers' tricks; & Moderne Salonzaubereien zur Unterhaltung in Gesellschafts-kreisen (1900, 118pp). [Vo56;St]

name: Hermanutz
bio: (Germany: fl.1840s) Minor pro sleight-of-hand artist. Tutored Georg Heubeck 1844-45.

name: Hermes
bio:
Hero of Alexandria (Alexandria?, Egypt?: c.20 A.D.-) Also known as "Heron of Alexandria". Student of the Alexandrian engineer Ctesibius. Greek engineer, mathematician, & natural philosopher in Alexandria. His famous treatise on pneumatics, written in Greek manuscript around the year 62 AD, mainly comprises scientific explanations of many of the tricks used by Greek priests in gimmicking their temples with automata to awe the multitude. He describes 12 magic altars, over 40 magic vases and water bowls, and the bronze horse whose head could be cut through without severing it. First printed in 1575 in Italy in Latin tr, as Spiritalium liber. Earliest Italian translations were Gli artifitiosi et curiosi moti spirituali (1589) & Spiritali di Herone Alessandrino (1592). An English tr is Bennet Woodcroft (editor), The Pneumatics of Hero of Alexandria (1851, 117pp; facsimile reprint 1971). Major commentators have been Thomas Ewbank, Albert de Rochas, & Albert A. Hopkins. [Daw;St;Ch;Dif;Tops8/36]

[See also: Sherman, Robert]

name: Herpick, [James] "Jimmy" "Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro close-up. Manager in New York City for 21 years (1937-late 1958) of Tannen's for whom he also did demoes & catalog illustrations. Colonel in US Air Force. Articles in Phoenix. Invented Super-Stretch Rope (1946), Cash Vanish (1950), Phantom Pencil (1952, which won the MDA trick-of-the-year award), Ultra Blindfold (1957), Flame Thot (1957), etc. Left Tannen's in 1958 to become a successful mutual-fund salesman in Detroit and then retired. Bio by Lustig in Top Hat Topics, V.3, #8 [c.Jun 1957].

name: Herrero, Prof.
bio: (Silves, Portugal: 25 Jul 1953- ) Stage name of Dagoberto Cabrita de CAMPOS. Pro fakir (taught by Pragjir, an Indian) & illusionist since 1971. Toured Spain, South Africa, & Mozambique with circuses. 1977 Figueira da Foz 2nd prize in fakirism. Wrote Faquirismo e Vida (1980, 60pp). [Cam]

name: Herrmann III
bio: See: Herrmann, Leon

name: Herrmann, Adelaide
bio: (London, England: 11 Aug 1853 [sic] - 19 Feb 1932) Born Adelaide Scarcez, of Belgian parents. A pro dancer, she met Alexander Herrmann who married her in the USA in 1875 & trained her in magic. She then became his principal female assistant. Aka "M'lle Addie", etc. After Alexander's death she became a famous pro magician on her own, initially with nephew Leon as "Herrmann the Great Company" Jan 1897 thru May 1899. Then as solo magician with large troupe in vaudeville since Jun 1899. Toured Europe in 1902 when she played the London Hippodrome, Paris Folies-Bergère, Berlin Wintergarten, etc. Retired around 1928. Died of pneumonia in New York City. [Pr;Ch;Se;Mo;Rey;Magic9/02]

name: Herrmann, Alexander
bio: (Paris, France: 10 [sic] Feb 1844 [sic]-17 Dec 1896) Aka "Herrmann the Great". Youngest son of Samuel Herrmann. Learned as apprentice to older brother Compars Herrmann 1852-59. Thence on own as pro with debut in Spain in 1859. In contrast to the serious style of Compars, Alexander stressed humor in his performances. Became a Mason. Toured Europe 1859-61, USA 1861-62 (with Compars), Europe & Turkey 1862-67, USA 1867 (with Compars), Europe & South America 1868-69, USA 1869 (with Compars), London 1870-73 (when he played 1,000+ nights at Egyptian Hall). Toured to USA for first time alone 1874-75. In 1875 married Adelaide who was thence his main female assistant. Became US citizen in 1876. Played Paris 1878, Brazil 1883, & Europe (including Portugal) 1885. In Paris in 1885 agreed with Compars that Compars would have exclusive performance rights in Europe & Alexander in the Americas. Thence did so, playing the USA except for Mexico (1888). Bio is H.J. Burlingame, Herrmann the Magician: His Life, His Secrets (1897, 250pp). [Pr;Ch;Gib;Dam;Mo]

name: Herrmann, Compars
bio: (Pattensen, near Hannover, Germany: 23 Jan 1816-8 Jun 1887) Eldest child of Samuel Herrmann, a Jewish itinerant conjuror, from whom he learned as assistant. Moved to Paris. Learned magic at age 10 as assistant to father. Pro illusionist, probably since 1847, touring England (1848), Europe, & Turkey with an illusion act pirated from Robert-Houdin. Moved to Vienna in 1851 when he became a student of Hofzinser and began adopting the latter's sleight-of-hand techniques, props, & several routines. Then toured Europe, including Portugal (1859) & Spain (1860). Toured North & South America 1859-65, including USA (1861-62 with Alexander). Toured England (1863) & Portugal (1863). In 1865 became an Austrian citizen & temporarily retired. From 1867 to death, back on the road, including USA (1867, 1869, both with Alexander), France, Romania, Portugal (1876), Serbia (1882), Italy (1883), Austria (1883), Russia (1884), Germany (1886), & Denmark. In 1882, while vacationing in Belgium, he taught Queen Marie Henriette some tricks daily for a month, which she often showed her attendants. In 1885 in Paris he agreed with Alexander that henceforward he would have exclusive performance rights to Europe & Alexander those in the Americas. Probably invented the Floating Wand (by 1869). [Pr;Ch;Gib;Fi;Win;Magic12/02]

name: Herrmann, Felix
bio: (London, England: 21 Feb 1881 [sic]-10 Nov 1938) Stage name of Felix Alfred Kretschmann [sic], nephew of Adelaide Herrmann. Moved to USA where he learned assisting uncle Alexander c1895. Pro illusionist on own since his 1903 debut at the New York Eden Musée. Legal name change to Felix Alfred Hermann in 1918. Retired in 1937 in New Orleans. Died there next year of complications from auto accident. [Pr;St]

name: Herrmann, Henri
bio: (Germany: fl.1850s-1st decade of 1900s) Minor pro. Worked in England, 1856, 1864-1906. In 1859 helped J.M. Hartz develop his "Crystal Magic" act. [CI]

name: Herrmann, Klaus
bio: (Germany: 19 Jul 1927- ) Amateur magician (as "Mytox") in Pohlheim, Germany. Noted collector of magic posters. [Nad]

name: Herrmann, Leon
bio: (Paris, France: 13 Mar 1867-16 May 1909) Learned as apprentice to uncle Compars Herrmann. Pro debut on own at Folies-Bergère in 1891. Toured (with Adelaide) his late uncle Alexander's show from Jan 1897-May 1899 in the USA, being the "Herrmann" that Howard Thurston "mystified" on 23 Oct 1898 at the Tabor Grand in Denver, Colorado. Toured his own show in USA since late 1899, visiting Paris yearly, with brief tours in Europe, including Moscow (1908) where he developed pneumonia, forcing his return to Paris where he soon died. Sometimes called "Herrmann III". [Pr;Dam;Mo;Magic7/04,5/07]

name: Herrmann, Samuel
bio: (Berlin, Germany: -1868) Of Russian-Polish Jewish parents. Married Anna Sarah Meyer of Hamburg. Founded the great Herrmann dynasty of magicians. His older brother was supposedly also a magician. Itinerant pro magician, working minor venues in Germany & France 1817-55, retiring in Paris by 1860 on a pension provided by Compars, eldest of Samuel's 16 children (8 males & 8 females) & the only one born in Germany, the others all being born in Paris. [Pr;Ch]

name: Herron, Carl
bio: (East Side Manhattan, New York:: 1932-) Father was an ex-carny & sidewalk pitchman. Bizarre Magickian. Took his stage name, "Brother Shadow", from satanist Aleister Crowley's reply to those who called him a magician that "I would rather be known as the Brother of the Shadow". Also performs as "The Wizard" in New York state where he lives. Wrote (as "Brother Shadow") The Empress: A Professional Act of Mind Reading (1995), Have Seance, Will Travel (1997, 20pp), The Papers of Gautama Siddhartha (1997, 28pp), Ten Little Indians (1998, 9pp). Articles. [LR12/2003; LR3/2001]

name: Hershal, Professor Will
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of William Henry Tingle. Minor pro as the "Up-to-date Magician". Lived in Ashton-under-Lyne in 1900.

name: Hertz, Carl
bio: (San Francisco, California: 14 May 1859-20 Mar 1924) German-Jewish ancestry. Stage name of Leib [sic] Morgenstern. Debut at age 18. Moved to England in 1884. A major pro stage magician. His basic 15-minute act comprised card tricks, the Vanishing Birdcage, plus an illusion. Toured the Continent, USA (1887), the Continent (1888), Australia (1892), & USA (1896). In 1896 after returning to England, he began a round-the-world tour that took him to South Africa, Australia (1896), New Zealand, Fiji, India (1898), Burma, Singapore, the Philippines, Borneo, Shanghai, Japan, Hawaii, & the USA, returning to England in 1898. Toured Europe 1902-03, Denmark 1906, USA 1906-07, & Europe 1910-11. After his sudden death in Coventry, his widow ("Amilie D'Alton") continued his show briefly. Autobio is A Modern Mystery Merchant (1924, 319pp). [Pr;Wal;Ch;Go;Go2;Bar;Vo56;Magic1/02,6/03,1/04,9/04;Dam]

name: Herwinn, Professor
bio: (Birmingham, England: 31 Oct 1861-18 Mar 1946) Stage name of William Humpage. Learned in 1882 from amateur friend. Pro magician & illusionist in Bristol. Invented thumbtip c1885 & claimed invention of the Siberian Transport Chain. Father of "Carlini". [Daw#228;Magic8/03;Vo56]

name: Heteb, Joad
bio: See: Selbit, P. T.

name: Heubeck, Georg
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 30 Aug 1829-8 Mar [sic] 1899) Son of a rich Viennese goldsmith. Inspired in 1844 seeing German magician Hermanutz. Tutored by Hermanutz 1844-45 & by Hofzinser 1846-48. Pro since 1852. Aka "Pian Leonardo". Toured Germany 1866-70 when returned to Vienna. Involved with the Kratky-Baschik Theater in Vienna 1873-81. Toured Hungary 1884 & the Balkans 1885. Taught magic to over 100 students, including Carlo Arminio, Ottokar Fischer, Carl Husa, & Franz Marschall. Bed-ridden & impoverished from 1890 until death in Vienna. [Win;Vo57;St;Al;Zauberwelt6/1897,7/1897,4/1899]

name: Heubes, Carl-Gerd
bio: (Germany: 18 Oct 1933-) Pro magician as "Carlini". Retail dealer (as "Zauberzentrum Janos Bartl") in Hamburg since buying out Rosa Bartl c1968. [Nad]

name: Heuer, Rudolf "Rudi
bio: (Austria: 1960-) Pro manipulator in Vienna. Aka "Mister Jo-Jo". 1982 FISM 3rd prize in manip. Played the magic congress in Łódź, Poland, in 1983. [Mec]

name: Heverly, [Linden Vernon]
bio: (New Albany, Pennsylvania: 27 Nov 1888-4 Feb 1929) Debut at age 13. Pro as mindreader ("Zartola") c1895-1907 when resumed family name and turned to straight magic & illusions as "Heverly the Great". Specialized in watch & clock tricks. Invented "Miss America" (by 1928). Wrote Novelty Act De-Luxe with Watches and Clocks (28pp). [Pr]

name: Hewes, Frank D.
bio: (Albany, New York: 1862-22 Sep 1917) Billed as "Hewes the White Yogi". Minor pro since 1869 (age 7). Invented Sword Suspension in 1899. Did 500 shows at New York's Eden Musée from 1911 to 1913 when he retired. [Pr

name: Hexy
bio: See: Hebenstreit, Alwine

name: Heyl, Earle G.
bio: (USA: c1879-11 Oct 1960) Semi-pro magician in Philadelphia, moving to Baltimore in 1933. Aka "Sedrick Hoyt", "Chunk Ling Do", & "I Make Faces". In late 1940s did 26 radio shows on magic history & anecdotes. Father of Edgar G. Heyl.

name: Heyl, Edgar G. "Ed
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 1 Jul 1911-23 May 1993). Son of Earle G. Heyl, who taught him magic. Chemical engineer since 1931 in Baltimore. Amateur magician, magic collector. Edited Hell 1937 (8 issues). Semi-pro dealer in old magic books 1948-1980s, issuing over 150 catalogs. President Magic Collectors' Association 1965-66. Aka "Dr. Livingstone, I presume". Edited book review column in Hugard's Magic Monthly 1961-63. Wrote Conjuring Books, 1580-1850 (1963, 62pp) & Cues for Collectors (1964, 64pp). Articles in Collectors Annual, MUM, Linking Ring, Magic Cauldron, Magicol, Journal of the Token and Medal Society, etc. See F. W. Kuethe Jr, A Catalogue of the Edgar G. Heyl Collection (1993).

name: Heyne, Henry B.
bio: (USA: 13 May 1868-6 Jan 1924) Former orchestra musician turned pro magician & juggler in circus & vaudeville as "Harry Helms". Published-edited (under real name) the 2 known issues of The Magic City (1902). [St]

name: Hiam, Frank
bio: (England: c1841-26 Dec 1899) Pro magician. Taught D'Alvini c1865. Magic dealer (Hiam's) in London since 1866 when inherited shop from grandfather Frank Steer. Invented Tray of Proteus. Died of pneumonia. Father of Henry Hiam. [Daw94;Cl]

name: Hiam, Henry "Will
bio: (England: c1865-27 Aug 1900) Aka "Henri Hiam". Pro dealer in London with father Frank. The shop was absorbed by Hamley's in late 1900 when he died of a stroke, leaving no descendants to carry on. [Daw94;Cl]

name: Hiawatha
bio: See: Johnson, Hiawatha

name: Hicks, Le Professeur
bio: See: Cordelier, François

name: Hierling, Thomas
bio: (Frankfurt, West Germany: 12 May 1962-17 Jan 1991) Learned in 1982 buying magic shop tricks. 1984 German champion in card magic. Pro comedy close-up since 1984, often working with partner Robert Fine as "Die 2" with a gambling demo & close-up. Wrote New Wave Close-Up (1987, 127pp, in German). Articles in Magie. A suicide, supposedly because of money problems. [Magie1/87;Wh2]

name: Higham, Justin
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Amateur card magician in London. Editor-publisher Technomagic 1990-present. Wrote Card Man-uscript & Inside Out.

name: Hikita, Tenko
bio:
Hilburger, Michael A. "Lunchbox" (Buffalo, New York: 13 Jan 1940- ) Learned in 1952 (age 12) when father introduced him to Gene Gordon who demonstrated Rub-A-Dub-Dub. High school teacher. Semi-pro since 1955 billed as "Magic with Michael" doing comedy close-up & cabaret. Pet effects: Malini Egg Bag, & Bill in Wallet. Has worked the Forks Hotel since 1972 & Thurston's Palace of Mystery 1979-83. Tricks in Miesel's Appetizers books (1982 & 1984) & Genii (8/86). [Wh5]

[See also: "Tenko, Princess"]

name: Hilden, Miss
bio: (Germany: 1906-) Stage name of Hildegard "Hildy" Neureiter. Pro escapist since 1927 when worked as assistant-wife of Bernardi (see). Left him in 1929 to work on own. During WW II entertained German troops as "Hilden-Wahl" (after her 2nd husband). Retired in 1945. Now (1992) as Hildegard Ohlsson lives in Sweden with her 3rd husband. [Ran]

name: Hildini, Eric
bio: See: Eriksson, Hilding

name: Hilford, Doc
bio: (USA: c1959-) Pro psychic entertainer, travelling thru the USA (including as street performer in San Francisco) until settling in Phoenix c1990. Editor New Invocation 1990-present. Lecturer & trade-show worker. Invented "The Brother of All Book Tests". Wrote Keeping the Center (1990, 26pp plus audio cassette). 22 audio & videos (1990-97). [MUM10/94]

name: Hill, Cedric Waters, MIMC
bio: (Maryvale, Queensland, Australia: 1891-Mar 1975) Amateur magician. Group Captain, RAF. Escaped with E.H. Jones from Turkish POW camp at Yozgad in WW I by using a ouija board, pseudo-spiritualism, & faked mindreading to dupe the commandant. Illustrated The Road to Endor (1920). Participated in Australia Air Race 1930. Memoir is The Spook and the Commandant (1975). Jones also did a book on this incident. [Daw2]

name: Hill, Gordon
bio: See: Eldin, Peter

name: Hill, Pitt
bio: (Germany: 2 Dec 1952-) Stage name of Peter Helten. 1978 MZvD 2nd prize in childrens magic. [Nad]

name: Hill, Thomas
bio: (Britain: c1528-c1599) Wrote Naturall and Artificiall conclusions (London: Ihon Kyngston, 1581, 32 unnumbered leaves). This is the earliest known edition of a work reported to have been first published in 1566 and reprinted in 1570. Hill, a rather well-known hack writer and translator from the Italian, probably wrote this booklet himself, despite his claim that it was merely his translation of a work by "sundrie scholars of the Universite of Padua in Italy." In either case it is a household encyclopedia of the type popular since the spread of printing to Europe, giving useful hints on medical recipes, etc, including (as Harry Price first noted) several crude conjuring tricks such as "How to tourne water into wine". Important only because it predates Prévost and Scot.[TS]

name: Hilliar, William J[ohn] "Big Bill
bio: (Oxford, England: 27 Nov 1876-15 Nov 1936) Inspired at age 14 seeing Dr Lynn, Prof Duprez, & Bosco. Learned working in vaudeville troupe. Pro debut at 19 as "Professor Lenox". Taught both Stanyon & Selbit. Wrote Novel Hand Shadows (1900, 47pp). Ghosted both T. Nelson Downs' Modern Coin Manipulation (1900) & Howard Thurston's Card Tricks (1901). Invented the Card Reel, which he published in the latter book, credited to Thurston. Wrote Modern Magician's Hand Book (1902, 440pp), actually a cut-&-paste piracy of his own works and those of others. Moved to USA in June 1901. First editor of The Sphinx 1902. SAM membership #67. Thence back to performing with circus sideshows & in winters in vaudeville. Finally as circus & carnival press agent. With Barnum & Bailey 11 years. In 1919 became the first magic correspondent for The Billboard. Tricks for Mahatma & articles for Sphinx. Despondent over health, committed suicide by gunshot. [Bo#198;Pr;Sphinx3/19.5/32.12/36;Dor]

name: Hilliard, John Northern
bio: (Palmyra, New York: 18 Aug 1872-14 Mar 1935) Reporter to amateur magician to advance man for Howard Thurston (by 1929). Invented the large ring in 1897 & the Telephone Trick in 1905. Ghosted T. Nelson Downs' The Art of Magic (1909, 334pp), wrote Greater Magic (1938, 993pp; reprinted 1956 in 5 vols as The Greater Magic Library; the card section being reprinted as Card Magic, 1944, 580pp), both classics, and 1 booklet. Also wrote Leaves from My Notebook (1935, 47pp). Note that at 993pp, Greater Magic is the largest magic book published. Tricks in Magic (1905). Coined the term "finger-flinger". [Pr]

name: Hilton, Henry
bio: (London, England: c1884-1 May 1956) Stage name of Henry Arthur Smith. Pro general magician living in London by 1910, billed as "The Dexerous [sic] Deceiver". [Ho]

name: Himber, [Herbert] Richard "Dick
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 20 Feb 1900 [or 06 or 07]-11 Dec 1966) Minor big-band leader since 1934. World-class practical joker & notable eccentric. Semi-pro magician. Mail-order magic dealer since 1945 out of his New York City apartment. Prolific inventor-improver, claiming over 500 tricks (most invented by others), including The Man from Mars (1941, invented by Orson Welles), the Milk Pitcher (by 1943), Fifth Dimension Card Frame (by 1944), Throw Out Rope Trick (1944), Three Ring Circus (1944, with Orson Welles), Wonder Box (1945, made by Merv Taylor), Ghost Glass (1947), Now You See It card trick (by 1947), Twin Trix (by 1948), Rocket Vanish (1948, with Lou Tannen), Cup of Plenty (1950, a lota teacup), Canada Dry Changing Bottles (1950), Eternal Light (1954), Rainbow Die Box (1956), Write a Rope (1956), Big Opener (1956), Staggering = Himber Ring (1961, invented by Diaconis), & Bill-Fooled = Himber Wallet (1963, suggested by Sam Schwartz). See Ed Levy (editor), Richard Himber: The Man and His Magic (1980, 128pp). Tricks in Genii. [Zo;HMM11/56;Albo95]

name: Hindman, Dale [Raymond]
bio: (Van Nuys, California: 9 Oct 1953- ) Grandson of Ray Muse who taught him first tricks at age 5. Banker in Los Angeles area. Semi-pro stage & theme magic. 1978 SAM Best Mental Effect; 1982 SAM Best General Magic Act. Manager of the Magic Castle by 2002. Articles in MUM & Genii. [Wh2]

name: Hines, Clayton M.
bio: See: "Mardoni"

name: Hing [Sr.], Ah
bio: (Portland, Oregon: 13 Sep 1918-15 Apr 1993) Chinese-American, Pro magus (& fire eater) with Chinese act. Moved to San Francisco in 1939 to work the Forbidden City nightclub as house magician. Assistant-wife since 1940 was Bertha Lew. Served in the U.S. Army in WW II. They then toured in vaudeville in West Coast theaters (including Vancouver in 1961) until the 1960s when left magic. "Only double I [Card Monder] ever knew who exchange places. If Hing got bombed Bertha would do the act and he would assist!". [Tay]

name: Hinkson, Ralph
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Amateur in Buffalo, New York. Co-edited (with Bob Weill) the "Fake Jinx" issue (1939). First editor of Hocus Pocus 1940, the IBM Ring 12 bulletin.

name: Hiraiwa, Hakufu [pronounced HIH-RYE-WAH]
bio: (Japan: fl.1960s - 6 Jul 2005) Wrote Stage Magic Highlights (Tokyo: Araki, 1961). His Zusetsu Nihon No Tejina is one of the most significant books on Japanese magic history.

name: Hirata, Haruhito [pronounced HIH-RAH-TAH]
bio: (Japan: fl.1970s-90s) Close-up. Lecture tour of USA in 1981. Wrote Something from the East (1980, 9pp of lecture notes). Invented the Hirata Master Move (by 1995).

name: Hirose, Johnny
bio: (Osaka, Japan: 22 Mar 1948 - ) Birth name is Yoshio Hirose. Pro stage and close-up worker. Pet effects are dove production, hindu basket trick. Invented The Invisible Hole (Pen Through Bill). Tricks published in Apocalypse, Richard's Almanac. Video The Magic of Japan (1993)

name: Histed, Louis S., MIMC
bio: (Britain: c1897-10 Oct 1965) Customs & Excise official. Amateur magician & major magic inventor. Invented Square Circle in 1930. Wrote The Magic of Louis Histed (1947, 159pp; repr 1968). Tricks in Abra. [Le] "H.L." [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

name: Hladik, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1960s) Doctor of Sciences, writer, poet, & song writer in Paris. Amateur magician. Aka "Naej Kidalh". AFAP Master Magician. Wrote Prestidigitation et Illusionnisme (1967) with Portuguese tr as Prestidigitação e Illusionismo (c1971, 144pp). [Bo]

name: Hlavać, Otokar
bio: (Prague, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 12 Jul 1883-1942) Pro magician. Founding President in 1922 of the Magicky Klub Praha, Czechoslovakia's first magic club. Perished in the Nazi concentration camp at Majdanek, Poland. [Nad]

name: Hoard, Paul
bio: See: Bamman, Howard

name: Hoare
bio: (Britain: fl.1820s) Minor pro. [Fr]

name: Höbel, Eugen
bio: (Germany?: 26 Jan 1928-) Aka "Mario". 1975 MZvD 3rd prize in card magic. [Nad]

name: Hocus Pocus
bio: (Britain: fl.1620s-30s) Stage name of the leading conjurer in England during the reign of King James I (1603-25), as reported by both Ben Jonson (in 1625 & 1632, spelling his name "Hokos Pokos") & Thomas Ady (in 1655). Self-styled because he used "hocus pocus" as his main magic words. Played Bartholomew Fair. Probably the main teacher of Hocus Pocus Junior. Dead by 1640.

name: Hocus Pocus Junior
bio: (Britain: fl.1630s) Pen name, as he admits, of the author of the justly famous The Anatomie of Legerdemain (London: 1634, 28 unnumbered leaves; 2nd ed "with many additions", 32 unnumbered leaves). Many reprints followed, including facsimiles by McArdle in 1950 of the 8th ed & by Burton in 1997 of the 1st ed. A German translation first appeared in 1667. Based mainly on Scot and Rid but with some additional tricks plus a new and well-informed description of the Cups-&-Balls. The text implies an educated amateur writer. And he explicitly states that he was a strictly amateur magician taught as a "spectator of divers professors" who, as he added next year in the 2nd edition (1635), performed at London's great Bartholomew Fair. That edition also specified that his teachers included "my Senior", presumably one of the professors who worked the great fair. NOTE: There is a false but common belief that Hocus Pocus Junior is not a pen name but merely the book's main title. This odd view was uncritically accepted by Houdini (1909), Clarke (1924), H.A. Smith (1940), McArdle (1950), Farelli (1952), Stenman (1952), Christopher (1973), Toole Stott (1976), Lamb (1979), Grossman (1983), Sharpe (1983), Reynolds (1985), & Voignier (1998). That view was rejected by Mecwaldowski (1985), Whaley (1990), Busby (1997), & Burton (1997).

name: Hodges, James
bio:
(France?: 1928-) Set designer in Paris. Semi-pro comedy magician & balloonologist. Famous illustrator of Flash Magicien (1970), 50 Grandes Illusions, Mad Magic magazine, etc. Co-published (with Jean Merlin) Mad Magic 1975-84. Wrote Sculpteur de ballons (1972), Les Ballons (1972), Sexy-Magic (1973), Magie théâtre et lumière, Chapeau de Tabarin (1973), Notes sur la ventriloquie, De l'utilisation des fleurs à ressort en prestidigitation (with Michel Hatte), & 15 illusions avec l'universal (1985). Articles in Mad Magic. [Dif]

[See also: Weber, Herman L.]

name: Hodgson, Richard
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 24 Sep 1855-20 Dec 1905) Took his law degree (LL.D.) in 1878 & moved to England that year. A life-long psychic researcher. Amateur magus who used this knowledge in investigating psychics, particularly in collaboration with Mr S. J. Davey. In 1882 co-founded (with Prof. Simon Newcomb) the American Society for Psychical Research. Moved to the USA (Boston) in 1887 to become Secretary of the ASPR, a post he held until his death. Converted to spiritualism by Mrs. Piper. Died in Boston. Articles in Proceedings of the Society for Psychical Research. Bio is A. T. Baird, Richard Hodgson (1949, 310pp).

name: Hoe, Yank
bio: (Italy: fl.1880s-1900s) Stage name of Signore Morenos. Pro stage magician with small tricks by Dec 1885 when he made his London debut at the Trocadero doing the Card in Cigarette, etc. In USA in 1891 with wife Omeni also doing 2-person billet reading. Invented Sympathetic Coins by 1891. Again (or still) in USA in 1896. Alive as late as 1906 in Europe. [Cl; Conjurer's MM, 15 Sep 1906, 13]

name: Hofeller, Sigmar Kaiser
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 12 Nov 1895-3 May 1964) Aka "Sigmar--The Magician". Inspired by magic show. Learned from purchased tricks. Insurance executive in Houston, Texas. Semi-pro magician. [Th]

name: Hoffman, Charles "Charlie
bio: (Providence, Rhode Island: 1 Aug 1896-1966) Pro since 1929 with a sleight-of-hand act. Developed his cocktail bar act by 1935, which he made famous since 1938 as "Think-a-Drink Hoffman". Invented Levit Liquid (by 1940). Moved to Southern California in late 1940s. Played the New York Loew's State in 1945 & 1946. Opened Nevada's Cal-Neva Club in 1948. Played the New York Palace in 1949 & Britain (including the London Palladium) for 4 weeks later that year. [Pr;Tay;WWM;Ho] [check Genii obit for 2/66.....]

name: Hoffmann, Professor
bio: (London, England: 23 Jul 1839-23 Dec 1919) Pen name of Angelo John Lewis, a barrister (since 1861) & writer. Amateur magician since learning in the early 1860s from a book and then lessons from Hellis (in 1873) and Charlier. In 1873-77 he published a series of 48 articles titled "Modern Magic" for Routledge's Every Boy's Paper, which launched his career as the most prolific & influential magic author & translator until modern times. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote the classic Modern Magic (1876, 511pp) and Tricks with Cards (1889, 250pp), Later Magic (1903, 554pp) as well as the progressively inferior More Magic (1890, 457pp), Magical Titbits (1911, 229pp), & Latest Magic (1918, 222pp). Also wrote Card Tricks Without Sleight-of-Hand (1877, 96pp); Drawing Room Amusements (1879, 504pp); a novel, Conjurer Dick (1886, 256pp); Baccarat, Fair and Foul (1891, 119pp); Puzzles Old and New (1893, 394pp); Mechanical Puzzles (1896, 144pp); Miscellaneous Puzzles (1901, 130pp); King Koko (1904, 127pp), another novel. Tricks & articles in Magic, Chamber's Journal, Indoor Amusements, etc. Translated Robert-Houdin's Les Secrets de la Prestidigitation et de la Magie as The Secrets of Conjuring and Magic (1878 [sic], 371pp), Robert-Houdin's Magie et Physique Amusante as Secrets of Stage Conjuring (1881, 252pp), Robert-Houdin's Les Tricheries des Grecs dévoilées as Card Sharping Exposed (1882), L.P.'s Prestidigitation moderne as Drawing-Room Conjuring (1887, 181pp), & Arthur Good's La Science amusante as Magic at Home (1890, 240pp). Tricks in Magic. Bio is J.B. Findlay & Thomas A. Sawyer, Professor Hoffmann: A Study (1977, 67pp). [Go2; Bur; Vo56]

name: Hoffmann, Franz
bio: (Neustadt/Wstr., West Germany: 10 Oct 1949-) Learned in 1956 from magic set. Pro since 1972 with wife Monika as "Santo & Monique", initially with manip act, then since 1981 doing 2-person telepathy. 1983 Baden-Baden 2nd prize in mentalism; 1984 MZvD German Championship (in Osnabrück) 1st Prize in Mental Magic; 1985 MZvD Magician of the Year for "Santo & Monique"; 1985 FISM 1st Prize in Mental Magic. Effects in Magie & Magische Welt. Many TV bits in Germany & Switzerland. [Wh5]

name: Hoffmann, Monika
bio: (Neustadt/Wstr, West Germany: 28 Jul 1950-) Pro since 1972 as "Santo & Monique" with husband Franz (see). [Wh5]

name: Hofzinser, Dr Johann Nepomuk, PhD
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 19 Jul 1806-11 Mar 1875) Learned magic by 1828. Government bureaucrat. Amateur magician, then semi-pro from 1854, then full-time pro since 1865 when he retired from government. Invented the shell coin (by 1847), envelope card (1847), book test (early 1850s), Everywhere and Nowhere (c1860), Black Art Table (1872), slit glass (by 1875), spring balls (by 1875), probably Flags of All Nations (by 1875), probably flag pole (by 1875), card frame, card star, probably floating wand, dancing cane, mirror glass, and probably the small packet effect. See Ottokar Fischer, J.N. Hofzinser Kartenkünste (1910, 219pp), English tr by S.H. Sharpe as Hofzinser's Card Conjuring (1931, 183pp); and J.N. Hofzinser Zauberkünste (1942, 320pp), English tr by Richard Hatch as The Magic of Johann Nepomuk Hofzinser (1985, 215pp). Reinhard Müller, Hofzinser and the Magic of the 19th Century: Card Magic in Germany (1994, 22pp). [St;Go2]

name: Hofzinser, Max
bio: (Hudiksvall, Sweden: 1 Oct 1885-23 Sep 1955) Stage name of Josef Levin. Jew. Interested in magic since 1902. Pro illusionist since 1908. Appointed Royal Illusionist to Swedish kings Gustav V and Gustav VI Adolph. Owned a magic shop in Norrköping. Wrote booklets: Handbok i tankeöverföring (1928), Litet sällskapstrolleri (1928), & Litet trolleri för sällskapskretsen (1939). [Vo58;St;Dif;Ran]

name: Höhn, Hans
bio: (Germany: 7 Mar 19-) Magician & magic collector in Munich, Germany, in 1980s-90s. [Nad]

name: Holbach, Hans-Peter
bio:
(Germany: fl.1960s) Edited Zauberbrille. Co-founded (with Rigobert Hoeck) in 1964 the Internationale Magierloge & editor of its bilingual (German & English) journal, Magivision, since 1964.

[See also: Coleman, Dave]

name: Holbrook, [Emmett Bradford] "Brad
bio: (Baton Rouge, Louisiana: 8 Aug 1927- ) Inspired seeing a magician "and headed straight to the library." Lawyer in home town. Semi-pro close-up & club magic since 1950. Articles in Magic Circular. [Wh2]

name: Holden, Dr.
bio: (Worcester, England: 1 Feb 1844-c1913) Stage name of John Watkins. Learned c1860 from Sed Hamlah, a Moroccan; then sleight-of-hand from Prof. Hellis in London. Pro 1877-1913. Autobio is A Wizard's Wanderings from China to Peru (1886, 170pp). [Pr:Vo56]

name: Holden, Howard
bio: See: Kattner, Wilbur

name: Holden, Max, MIMC
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 20 Aug 1884-3 Jul 1949) Stage name of William Holden Maxwell, of Scottish parents. Inspired as youth seeing school magic show in Glasgow where his parents had moved. Self-taught. Debuted in 1896 with uncle, Fred Henson, a small-time juggler, whom he assisted while doing some magic. Pro magician in British theaters 1905-c1907 when returned to USA. Added hand-shadows to his act since 1909. Worked with assistant-wife Bessie as "Holden & Le Claire" 1910-c1914. Then after 1917 with assistant-(successive) wives Helene & Tess as "Holden & Graham". In 1919-20 toured Britain (including the London Coliseum in 1920) & played the Paris Alhambra in 1920. Returned to USA in 1921. Then toured England (1921, again at the Coliseum), South Africa (1921), Australia (1922) whence they returned to the USA that year. Toured England 1924-25. In 1929 left stage to become a major magic dealer (Max Holden Magic Shop) in New York City, with branches in Boston (opened 1936) & Philadelphia (opened 1938), which he operated until his death. Wrote Clever Card Tricks that Anyone Can Do (1934, 12pp, writing as "Maxwell"); Modern Hand Shadows (1935, 31pp); Programmes of Famous Magicians (1937, 68pp; repr 1968); & Manual of Juggling (1947) with French tr as Max Holden's Manuel de jonglerie (1952, 104pp). Column in Genii. [Pr;Han,pp56-64;St;Wal;Go;WWM]

name: Holden, [Elizabeth] "Tess" "Tessie
bio: (Newcastle, England: fl.1910s-60s) 3rd & last wife of Max Holden. Worked with him as "Holden & Graham" from c1918 until he left the stage in 1929 to open magic shops. Mother of William "Bill" Melbourne Holden (born in Melbourne, Australia, in 1922). Proprietor (with son Bill) of Max's 3 magic shops from his death in 1949 until 1963 when she had sold them off separately. [Pr]

name: Holderried, Michael
bio: (Germany: 31 Jul 19-) Lives in Oppenweiler, West Germany. Magician in post-WWII Germany with assistant-wife Andrea as "Bastino Junior". Conducts magic tours. [Nad]

name: Holgup, Nivel
bio: See: Plough, Alvin

name: Holland, Frank
bio: (Britain: 1893-) Learned at age 17. Amateur. Widely travelled in Europe, performing in public. [Go2]

name: Holland, John [Anthony], MIMC
bio: (London, England: 6 Feb 1924-). Learned c1933 from gift magic set & buying tricks & books. Consulting engineer. Amateur & semi-pro close-up & stage magician since 1938. Pet effects: Rings, Egg Bag, Oil & Water, & Slow Motion Aces. Admitted to the Magic Circle at age 18. MIMC 1967. Articles in Pentagram & Wagic Wand. Reviewer of magic books for Magic Circular (since c1957) & Epoptica. Formerly used "Kingfisher" as pen name. [Wh2]

name: Höller, Hannes "Hans
bio: (Krefeld, Germany: 29 Jun 1929-17 Nov 2003) Inspired seeing Bellachini-von Schledorn. Librarian. Amateur magician since 1943. Aka "Mac Magic". Collector of magic history & magic performances on slides. Received the 1st MZvD "Writer of the Year Award" for 1981. Author-publisher of Die Quahl der Wahl (1973; 2nd ed 1974) with French tr by Vollmer as L'embarras du Choix (1980); Tamariz's Münzen Meisterlich (1977), Trick-Karten-Tricks (1977), Lauter Lacher (1980), Heiterkeit weit und breit (1980), Meistermagie aus Italien (1981), Cortini (1990, 100pp, in English). [Wit;Nad]

name: Hollingsworth, Scott
bio: (Houston, Texas: 24 May 1938-) Learned at age 7 from library books. Pro close-up. 1970 TAOM Close-Up Trophy. Resident magician at Magic Island, Houston, since 1984 and entertainment director & MC since 1986. Wrote The Restaurant Magician (60pp), The Close-Up Stool (20pp, lecture notes), & The Strolling Magician (69pp). [Wh2]

name: Holly, Frederick
bio: (London, England: 23 Oct 1911- ) Learned magic at age 10. Semi-pro since age 18. [Go2]

name: Holmes, Alfred M[iles]
bio: (Sheffield, England: 1836-1916 [sic]) Learned in early 1850s assisting James Taylor. Circus contortionist. Assistant to J.H. Anderson in 1856, billed as Mr Flexmore. Pro on own after 1874. Married Anderson's eldest daughter, Helena Elizabeth, in 1877. Retired from stage in 1902 to manage the Empire Theatre in Sheffield. NOTE: Not to be confused with "Phillip Anderson", as Christopher (1973) did. [Cl; Vo56; Bay]

name: Holmes, Donald
bio: (Albion, Michigan: 23 Sep 1879- ) Pro name of Donald H. Alsdorf (not "Aladorf", as often misspelled). Pro mail-order dealer ("Donald Holmes") in Texas in 1909, later in Kansas City, where he issued catalogs by 1916 (#3) to at least 1930 (#19) and, as house organs, Holmes' Trade Sheet 1916 (4 issues) & Holmes' Magical Notes and Comments 1917-20 (39 issues). Wrote Some Modern Conjuring (1909, viii+78pp), New Card Tricks (39pp), Tricks with Prepared Cards (32pp), & The Magic Art (1920, 234pp). This last volume was announced as the first in a complete course in magic; but no further volumes appeared.

name: Holmes, James L.
bio: (Bradford, England: 5 Feb 1892-15 Oct 1980) Semi-pro magician. Moved to USA in youth. In US Army in WW I. Prominent in IBM. Expert baton twirler. [Daw2]

name: Holmes, Dr. S.
bio: See: Mackay, Hugh

name: Holms
bio: See: Olms, John

name: Holt, Randy
bio: (Orlando, Florida: 28 Nov 1955-) Inspired at age 7 by seeing Mark Wilson vanish a coin. Taught by Steve Spill. Close-up.

name: Holtz, [Louis] "Lou
bio: (Fallansbee, West Virginia: 6 Jan 1937-) Roman Catholic. College head football coach since 1969, most recently at U of Arkansas 1977-83, U of Minnesota 1983-85, & Notre Dame 1986-present. Amateur magician since being taught by Mary Ann Campbell at U of Arkansas c1978. Uses it mainly in pep-talks to his players. See Douglas Looney & Don Yaeger, Under the Tarnished Dome: How Notre Dame Betrayed Its Ideals for Football Glory (1993). [WWA]

name: Homar, Hermann
bio: (Emporia, Kansas: -20 Feb 1966) Stage name of Homar H. Woulfe, aka "Homar, the Wizard of the West". Inspired in 1900 when found a Judd's Magical Repository catalog in a trash can. Pro since 1920 in Lyceum & doing private parties. Partner & assistant in Joe Berg's magic shop in Chicago 1936-45. Tours managed by H.H. Davis. [St;Dor]

name: Homcheck, [Joseph] "Joe
bio: (Pennsylvania, USA: 1923-24 May 1989) As WW II vet on GI Bill graduated Chavez School 1947. Thence semi-pro magician. Tricks in HMM & one-man "Parade" & cover in Feb 1954 Linking Ring. Retired from US government in 1975 when he began teaching magic. Owner of The Magic Shop in central Pennsylvania 1987-89. Invented many effects marketed by Jim Klein's American Magic Company. [Zombie7/52]

name: Home, Daniel Dunglas
bio: (Currie, Scotland: 20 Mar 1833-21 Jun 1886) Most acclaimed psychic medium of 19th century, famous for his levitation at Ashley House in 1868. Never exposed. Died in Paris. Inspired J.N. Maskelyne's "Levitation Extraordinary" in 1875. Autobio is Incidents in My Life (1858) with French tr as Révélations sur ma vie surnaturelle (1864). Bios are Mme Dunglas Home, D.D. Home: His Life and Mission (1921) & Elizabeth Jenkins, The Shadow and the Light (1983, 352pp). [Dif]

name: Homes, E. Georg
bio: See: Gottlieb, Emil

name: Homme Masqué, L'
bio: (Arica, Chile [sic]: 15 Feb 1851-1913?) From an aristocratic Spanish family. Stage name of José Antenor de Gago y Zavala, so-called because he worked in a black mask "for private reasons". Aka the "Marquise d'O" & "Marquis d'Orighuela de Gago". Pro society magician since his debut in Berlin in 1895. Married "Zirka". Invented Expansion of Texture (by 1909). Reportedly committed suicide. [St] Höokenberg, Lieutenant Wilhelm [pronounced HUR-kern-bear] (Arboga, Sweden: 17 Mar 1808-9 Jul 1869) Stage name of Knut Höokenberg. Pro. Wrote 2 books in Swedish: Den Nya Häxmästaren (1843, 88pp) & Troll-och Swartkonster från Finland (1853, 121pp) and 1 in Finnish. [Vo58;Dif]

name: Hooker, Dr Samuel C[ox], PhD
bio: (Brenchley, England: 19 Apr 1864-13 Oct 1935) Moved to USA as adult, living in Brooklyn. Wealthy chemist. Amateur magic inventor, private performer (Hooker's "Impossibilities", which included his Hooker Rising Cards), & collector of magic props & books. Sold his prop collection to Charles Larson in 1934 & gave his fine book collection in 1936 to The New York Public Library. His rising card apparatus was given to John Mulholland. [Wat;Albo95;Bam,pp.93-94]

name: Hooper, [Kenneth] Edwin
bio: (Bideford, Devon, England: 5 Aug 1925-17 Jul 1992) Learned at age 10 from book. Debut at age 14. In WW II in Army doing troop shows. Summers worked Punch & Judy at Wollacombe beach. Aka "Edwin the Magician" since 1947, specializing in kid-shows. Full-time pro since 1951. In 1954 with his savings & a £200 loan he moved back to his home town of Bideford & founded the Supreme Magic Company, which grew to become one of the world's 3 largest magic manufacturer-dealerships. 1977 Louis Bertol Trophy. President, British Ring, 1977-78. AFAP Bronze Medal 1983. 1992 AMA Lifetime Achievement Award. Due to ill health sold Supreme in 1987, remaining as Honorary President. Reentered business in 1989 as Edwin's Magic Arts. Married to magicienne Ray Silver 1957-72. Their son, Michael Hooper, was with Supreme for a while, but since dropped out of magic. Inventor-improver of over 1,300 marketed effects, including 13 Little Pigs, Surprise Box, & Hen Bag. Wrote Edwin's Magic (2 vols, 1989, 286+310pp), A Host of Surprises (1990, 313pp), & Edwin's Magic Finale (1991, 320pp). Articles in Magigram, Pentagram, Linking Ring, MUM, Magic Manuscript, Magic Circular, Genii, Wizard, Budget, etc. Video (1990). [Magigram10/77; Se; Wh2]

name: Hooper, William, MD
bio: (England: fl.late 1700s) Wrote Rational Recreations (4 vols, 1774, c1200pp), which drew heavily from Guyot.

name: Hope, Eaton
bio: See: "Leroy, Arthur"

name: Hopkins, Albert A[llis]
bio: (USA: 1869-1939) Layman. Art expert in New York City. Associate editor of Scientific American for 44 years. Author-editor of the classic Magic: Stage Illusions and Scientific Diversions, including Trick Photography (1897, 556pp; repr 1967 & 1977; Swedish tr as Magiens värld, 1899). Friend of Houdini.

name: Hopkins, Charles H. "Charlie
bio: (USA: 22 Apr 1899-1948) Inspired & learned at age 11. Printer & philanthropist in Philadelphia. Amateur magician. Authored the classic "Outs": Precautions and Challenges (1940, 79pp), which was actually written by Walter Fogg. Published J.G. Tompkins Jr's classic My Best (1945). [Th]

name: Hopkins, Nevil Monroe
bio: (USA: -26 Mar 1945) Chemist, researcher, & teacher. Amateur magician. Wrote Twentieth Century Magic (1898, 160pp).

name: Horace
bio: (France: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Yves Guinzbourg. Stage magician. AFAP President 1976-80. AFAP Silver Medal 1978. [Bou2]

name: Horn, Roy
bio: (Nordenham, Germany: 3 Oct 1944-) Aka "Roy" of "Siegfried & Roy". Learned assisting Siegfried Fischbacher when they teamed up in 1960, working German cruise ships the next 5 years. Star pro stage illusionist in Las Vegas working the Frontier Casino until 1988. Became USA citizen in 1988. Then worked the Mirage. Incapacitated by a stroke in 2003. For details of their world-famous joint act see under Siegfried Fischbacher. [Win;Jef;HC;Walk]

name: Hornmann, Professor Otto
bio: (USA?: 14 Apr 1869-23 Jan 1920) Stage name of Otto Horn. Pro comedy magus in New York City area from late 1800s into 1st decade of 1900s, including on the Proctor circuit & with circuses. Then pro magic dealer in Manhattan, New York City, beginning in 1907 as the small "Otto Supply Co" & finally as the major "Hornmann Magic Co" until his death in 1920 when Houdini bought the shop. [Albo95]

name: Hornung, Werner [Siegfried]
bio: (Pforzheim, Germany: 2 Jul 1915- ) Learned magic since age 12 as a student of Kassner, then Friedrich & Fredo Marvelli. Pro illusionist in West Germany since 1959. Aka "Baron Tamesis" since 1959. Magic impresario as founder & producer of the Europa-Zauber-Theater since 1958 plus several large special magic shows. In 1979 married his assistant, "Fee Eleisa" (see), sometimes performing with her as "Duo Tamesis". [Win;Zm;Wh2]

name: Horowitz, June O[live], AIMC
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 12 Sep 1913- ) Mrs Sam Horowitz née Warsaw. At age 6 inspired by and learned from amateur father, Abe Warsaw, a manufacturer & semi-pro magician. Symphony violinist, college math teacher, insurance underwriter. Semi-pro close-up sleight-of hand since c1928. Married Sam Horowitz in 1937. Has performed internationally. IBM President 1987-88, the first woman to hold that office. AIMC 1992. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, etc. [LR7/87; Mar; Wh2]

name: Horowitz, S[amuel] Leo "Sam
bio: (USA: 1894-1971) Aka "Leo Hartz", "Dr. Chung", and "Mohammed Bey". Pro since teens. One of the 5 original members of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1932. Member of the "Secret Six". Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. Mentor of Roy Fromer. Invented Tilt (1st version) c1941 & Spirit Cartography. Wrote 3 booklets: Mohammed Bey's routines for the Jardine Ellis Ring on Stick (1952, 8pp), Mohammed Bey's Routine with the Okito Coin Box, & More Mohammed Bey Routines with the Okito Coin Box (1956, 11pp), the latter 2 being reprinted together as Mohammed Bey's Routines with the Okito Coin Box and More (1963). Tricks & articles in Greater Magic, Jinx, Sphinx, Phoenix, New Phoenix, HMM, & Pallbearers Review.

name: Horowitz, Sam[uel]
bio: (Toronto, Canada: 19 Jul 1912-24 Aug 1997) Married June Horowitz in 1937. Insurance agency owner in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where he had been local IBM Ring President. Amateur close-up since c1975 when taught by wife. [Wh2]

name: Horster, [Carl] F[riedrich] W[ilhelm]
bio: (Crossen an der Oder, Prussia: 15 Jan 1870-30 Aug 1944) (NOT "Friedrich Wilhelm Conrad Horster" or "Conrad A. Horster"). Aka "Conradi-Horster" since 1895. Son of a postal clerk. Inspired at age 9 seeing "Armida" perform. Finished high school in Dresden. Magic dealer & prop maker since 1890 (first in Dresden, later Nürnberg, finally Berlin on fashionable Friedrich-Strasse) as "Horsters Akademie für magische Kunst", "Horsters Zauberzentrale", etc. His many students included Georg von Hülsen, chamberlain of Kaiser Wilhelm II. Performed throughout Germany 1890-1914 & entertained troops during WW I. Active in forming magic clubs including "Maja" in Berlin in 1924. His business, among the world's most famous between the wars, was continued after his death (near Berlin) by his widow, Gertrud Horster, and did not close until the early 1990s. Publisher (as "Horster") of many magic books 1895-1937. Edited-published the second German-language magic magazine, Der Zauberspiegel, 1895-1908 & 1924-29. Prolific author (as "F.W. Conradi") of some 37 books in German, including Der moderne Kartenkünstler (1896, 232pp), Das Universum der Magie (1905, 200pp; 3rd ed, 4 vols, 1923, 96+96+96+256pp), Die vollendete Kartenkünstler (1917, 160pp), and Ich kann Zaubern (1939, 80pp; repr 1950). [Zauberkunst#4/83;Vo57;St;Dif]

name: Horster, Gertrud
bio: (Germany: -2 Mar 1953) Born Gertrud Scholz. Wife of F.W. Horster in his magic shop business in Berlin. On his death in 1944 succeeded him as head of the business. Died in Berlin. Her brother, A. Scholz, continued the business until 1959 when bought out by Peter Ülsmann. [Roh]

name: Hortiny
bio: (Gouveia, Portugal: 1 Aug 1942 [sic]) Stage name of José Carlos GOMES PITA. Moved to Angola at age 1. Learned magic (self-taught) at age 9 in Angola. Public debut in 1958. Semi-pro magician (general & close-up) & went since 1968. Moved back to Portugal in 1977. Full-time dealer ("Mãos Mágicas--Estúdio Hortíny") in Coimbra, Portugal, since 1979. 1979 Figueira da Foz 2nd prizes in card magic & close-up magic. Invented Aquarium (cage of birds to fish aquarium) 1981. Wrote Colectanea Mágica (1987, 107pp) & Cocktail Magic (1988, 153pp). Publisher-editor Top Hat Magic 1986-87 (5 issues). Articles in Quatro Ases. [Cam;Wh5]

name: Horwitz, Basil
bio: (South Africa: fl.1980s-90s) Investment advisor. Amateur mental magician. Invented Horwitz Wallet c1984. See Martin Breese, The Mental Magick of Basil Horwitz, Vol.1 (....., 65pp) & Vol.2 (....., 76pp) & Bob Gill, Mental Magick of Basil Horwitz, Vol.3 (1994, 91pp) & Vol.4 (1979, 74pp). Tricks in Pabular. 2 audios.

name: Hösch, Joe
bio: (Germany: 1 Jun 1899-3 Mar 1972) Stage name of Karl-Josef Hösch. Taught by avid amateur father in Würzburg. Pro for 25 years. Toured Germany, Luxembourg, France, etc. Died in Würzburg. [St]

name: Hotowka, John [Anthony]
bio: (Bradford, West Yorkshire, England: 5 Dec 1959-) Learned magic at age 19 as a hobby. Optician (retired). Semi-pro close-up magician since 1981. 1986 British Ring Zina Bennett Cup for close-up. Full-time pro since 1988. Does trade shows in Britain & Europe. Wrote Every Thing You Wanted to Know About Table Hopping, But Were Afraid to Ask! (1985). Tricks in Abra, Chicanery, Magigram, & Genii. [Wh2]

name: Hottoff, Professor Johnny
bio:
Hotz, Leigh A. (Cleveland, Ohio: 6 Nov 1958-) Pro magic consultant (as "A Tricky Business LLC") and owner of a chain of magic shops ("Wizard Magic Shop"). Won the 1988 Terry Seabrook Award (SAM). Invented many effects for corporate clients. [Wh01]

[See also: Hartop, A. W.]

name: Houang Yuen
bio: See: Bamberg, Theo

name: Houdi, John
bio: (Skelleftea, Sweden: 1 Nov 1964- ) Stage name of Johnny Erik Lindholm. Learned in 1974 from father's gift of magic set plus a local magician. Pro general magician since 1984, working mainly trade shows. Won several Scandinavian & Swedish competition championships. Articles in Magical Arts Journal & some Scandinavian journals. [Wh2]

name: Houdini, Beatrice "Bess
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY: 23 Jan 1876-11 Feb 1943) Stage name of Wilhelmina Beatrice Weiss née Rahner. Of German Catholic parentage. On 22 Jul 1894 the diminutive vaudeville dancer married Houdini from whom she then learned magic as his assistant. Moved to Hollywood in 1934. The rest of her post-Houdini career (lecturing & public appearances) was managed by Dr Edward Saint from 1934 until his death in 1942.

name: Houdini, Harry
bio: (Pest [now Budapest], Hungary: 24 Mar 1874-31 Oct 1926) Stage name of Ehrich Weiss (born Erik Weisz). Of Hungarian-Jewish parents, his father being a rabbi. Immigrated to USA on 3 Jul 1878 [not 1874] at age 4 with mother & siblings, his father following later. The family name was henceforward spelled Weiss and his first name was re-spelled Ehrich. At age 9 saw his first magician (Dr Lynn). Moved to New York City in 1888 when taught his 1st sleight-of-hand tricks by friends Jake Hyman and Joe Rinn. Inspired to become a professional by reading Robert-Houdin's Memoirs in 1890 and then in 1891, at Hyman's suggestion, adopted "Houdini" as stage name. Elder brother of "Hardeen". Mail-order dealer in New York in 1898 when he published his Magic Made Easy catalog & offered lessons. Thence pro sleight-of-hand, later escapism, coining the term "escapologist" in 1910. Toured Europe (1900-04, 1904-05, 1908-10), Australia 1910, England 1910-11, Europe 1912-13, Europe 1913-14, all with great success. Pet effects: Substitution Trunk & escapes. President, The Magicians' Club, 1911-26. SAM President 1917-26. Played such top venues as the New York Hippodrome (twice in 1918, the first for 19 weeks, his all-time record run). Starred in 4 motion pictures 1918-23. Toured his 1st full-evening show of magic, escapism, & psychic exposés in USA 1925-26. Died in a Detroit hospital of peritonitis. Invented Substitution Trunk (1893), Strait Jacket Escape (1896), Jail Breaker publicity stunt (1900), packing box escape (1902), Milk Can Escape (in 1908 jointly with Kukol & Vickery), Water Torture Cell (1912), & Flight of Time (1925). Willed his fine collection (then the world's largest) of 5,200 magic books to the Library of Congress. Edited The Conjurers' Monthly Magazine 1906-08 & MUM 1917-26. Wrote (with various ghosts) many books & pamphlets, including Magic Made Easy (1898), The Right Way to Do Wrong (1906, 96pp), The Unmasking of Robert-Houdin (1908, 319pp; rev ed, 1909, 333pp), Handcuff Secrets (1909, 109pp), Miracle Mongers and Their Methods (1920; repr 1929 & 1980, 240pp), Magical Rope Ties and Escapes [1921, 78pp], Houdini's Paper Magic (1922, 206pp), & A Magician Among the Spirits (1924, ghosted by Oscar Teale; repr 1972, 294pp). The premier biographical work is Kenneth Silverman, Houdini!!!: The Career of Ehrich Weiss (1996, 465pp). Good ones are Gresham (1959, 306pp), Christopher (1969, 281pp), Randi & Sugar (1976, 191pp), and Manny Weltman, Houdini: Escape into Legend--The Early Years, 1862-1900 (1993, 95pp). Lesser bios include Harold Kellock, Houdini: His Life Story (1928, 384pp); J.C. Cannell, The Secrets of Houdini (1931; repr 1932, 1938, 1976); B.M.L. Ernst & Hereward Carrington, Houdini and Conan Doyle (1932, 255pp); Walter Gibson & Morris Young, Houdini on Magic (1953, 280pp); Bernard C. Meyer, Houdini: A Mind in Chains (1976, 197pp); Milbourne Christopher, Houdini: A Pictorial Life (1976); Walter B. Gibson, The Original Houdini Scrapbook (1976); Doug Henning & Charles Reynolds, Houdini: His Legend and His Magic (1977, 192pp); Raymond Fitzsimons, Death and the Magician (1980); Roland Lacourbe, Houdini et sa légende (1982); and Brian Lead & Roger Woods, Houdini: The Myth Maker (1987). Pseudo-biographical movies are Houdini (1953) & The Great Houdinis (1976). [Pr;Berg;Wal;Bar;Fu2;Ho]

name: Houdiny, Miss
bio:
"Houdinys, The New" SEE: Enzfelder, Dagmar & Enzfelder, Oskar

[See also: Enzfelder, Dagmar]

name: Houghton, Norman [DeBlois] "Norm
bio: (Montreal, Canada: 3 Feb 1909-4 Mar 1998) Raised in Toronto. Inspired at age 12 seeing a sideshow magician. Editor (retired at age 72). Semi-pro close-up magician, as "Lorne De Blois" in 1930s & "Blois Houghton", but added Punch & Judy work after WW II. Invented Kismet mental effect in 1982. Wrote Wit & Wizardry: The Magic of Norm Houghton (1998, ed by Tom Ransom). Articles in Abra, Apocalypse, Bat, Genii, Ibidem, Jinx, Linking Ring, Magic and Spells Quarterly, Magic Wand, New Pentagram, New Phoenix, New Tops, HMM, Pallbearers Review, Ruminations, Trap Door, & Sphinx. [LR12/97;Wh2]

name: Houston, [Henry] "Harry
bio: (England: 16 Sep 1888-5 Jul 1955) Pro. With Maskelyne & Devant at St. George's Hall 1908-09 with a pseudo-Chinese act. Assistant to The Great Raymond 1911. Married Luella Raymond in India in 1912. Left stage c1914 for theatrical management (his clients included Carmo in 1920s). [Pr]

name: Hovatini
bio: See: Cooke, Prof. Harry

name: Howard, [Clifford Peter] "Max
bio: (Welch, West Virginia: 23 Apr 1942-) Son of a mining engineer & school teacher. Learned some magic at age 8 & since age 13 was "Maxwell the Magician", contributing in the late 1950s a column to On Stage & tricks to Genii. Pro actor since 1966. In 1971 inspired & tutored by Frank Everhart to become a magician. Since 1975 also pro stage magician, originally as "Max B. Nimble" in a TV kid-show series that ran 15 months in Cincinnati, winning a 1977 Emmy. Worked as street magician in New York City 1980-81. Since 1981 works mainly as "Professor Gus Rich, the Wizard of the Blue Ridge", an historical act based on the late 19th century travelling magician of that name. His assistant-wife in this act is Diane Bray (see). Also as performer & "interlocutor" on the Mississippi Queen riverboat 1988-89. Authored Showmanship: The Art That Conceals the Art (1986, 38pp), Magic from the Great Southern Sleight of Hand Show -- and More (38pp), Conversations with Myself (35pp), & Effective Presentations (32pp). 1 video (1993). [LR9/92;Wh]

name: Howard, Rupert
bio: See: Raw, Stuart Drayton

name: Howarde, Carl
bio:
Howarth, David A. S., MIMC (Britain: fl.1960s-90s) Specialist & dealer in electronic magic in Sale, Cheshire. Carries the Anverdi line of electronic props. Wrote Winners All (1962, 24pp). Tricks in Linking Ring (including a 1966 one-man "Parade").

[See also: Irving, Carl [Howard]]

name: Howatt, Gordon M.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Wrote The Travelling Ghost Card Illusion (1942), The Restless Spook (1943), & Let's Make Magic (1945), all reprinted in one volume as Let's Make Magic! (1966, 76pp).

name: Howe, Frank
bio: See: Clinton, Francis W.

name: Howe, Norman [Jefferson] "Normie
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 20 Feb 1905-) Mechanical engineer. Learned magic at age 31 visiting Holden's shop in Boston. Semi-pro childrens & comedy magician as "The Magical Magpie". Prolific magic artist-illustrator for Holden's shop, Barnstormer (for 30 years), MUM, etc. Reviews in Barnstormer. Invented magic tables and "Applause, please" trick. [MUM12/57;Wh5]

name: Howell, Thomas
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s-1930s) Pro mechanic. Invented the Will, the Witch and the Watch trick cabinet in 1872. With Alexander Herrmann's troupe in 1888 as its Master Mechanic. Also as apparatus builder for Devant and Thorn. Finally with the Maskelyne troupe until it dissolved in 1935. Father of Wally Howell. [St]

name: Howell, Wally
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-30s) Son of Thomas Howell. Pro mechanic, initially as chief builder for DeBiere then since the 1920s with the Maskelyne troupe as stage manager (after Frank Mack) until it dissolved in 1935. Howie, John A. M. (Scotland: -24 Jul 1978) Scientist with Imperial Chemical Industries. Amateur close-up magician. Linking Ring Award Winner. Wrote Routines with the Jardine Ellis Ring (1955, 31pp). Tricks in Pentagram. [Daw2]

name: Hoy, David [E.] "Dave
bio: (Evansville, Illinois: 21 Jul 1930-2 Apr 1981) Son of a Baptist lay preacher & a reverend in his own right. Spent a year as missionary in South America. Thence radio broadcaster in Evansville. Semi-pro to pro mentalist to psychic as "Dr. Faust". Invented the Tossed Out Deck by 1963. Edited Ministers' Magic Service 1958 (4 issues). Wrote Spiritism (c1955), Magic of the Eye (c1955), Magic with a Message (1956, 70pp), Bold and Subtle Miracles of Dr. Faust (1963, 28pp), & David Hoy's Psychic and Other ESP Party Games (1965, ghosted by Walter B. Gibson). Bio is John Godwin, Super-Psychic: The Incredible Dr. Hoy (1974). [NJ#26]

name: Hoyt, Harlowe R [andall]
bio: (Beaver Dam, Wisconsin: c1882-24 Oct 1970) Drama critic for Cleveland Plains Dealer 1917-62. Amateur magician & close friend of Howard Thurston. Wrote Town Hall Tonight (1955).

name: Hubbard, Clarence T.
bio: (Hartford, Connecticut: fl.1910s-20s) Manager with Aetna Life Assurance Co. Semi-pro pattern magician. [Dor]

name: Huber, Baptist
bio: (Munich, Germany: 1877-24 Dec 1934) Amateur in Munich. Invented many tricks, including Candle with Electric Primer. [Al]

name: Huber, Harry
bio: (Germany?: 6 Jan 1949-) Magician in Germany as "Fartun". [Nad]

name: Huber, Henry C.
bio: (Strassbourg, Alsace-Lorraine, Germany: 17 Jan 1886-7 Sep 1946) Son of a hostelier. Ran away from home in 1904 to become pro magician. Moved to USA in 1905. Salesman in Clyde Power's New York City shop. Stage magic & did straight-jacket escape as publicity stunt in 1930s. Billed as "The Great Huber". In 1937-38 toured with Carl Rosini their "Battle of Magic" show in Canada & USA. Married Rosini's assistant & sister-in-law, Dorothy "Dolly" Barclay, in 1938. They toured with USO in WW II. [Pr;St;Ho;WWM]

name: Huber, Volker
bio: (Offenbach-am-Main, Germany: 4 Feb 1941- ) Amateur magician since 1950 as "Wülhunza Schröter". Publisher ("Edition Volker Huber") of magic & circus books and art dealer in Offenbach, West Germany. Has reprinted such rare magic books as the catalogs of Bland and Hamley.
