Collector of magic books, prints, posters, playbills, & early apparatus. Magic historian. Articles in Magische Welt. Column in Die Magie. [Bo#317;Wh2]

name: Huckabee Jr, Phil H.
bio: (Texarkana, Texas: 6 Jul 1915-8 Jul 1993) Learned at age 9 from Xmas magic set. Salesman. Semi-pro stage & school-show magician since 1942, working the southeast. 1961 TAOM Daddy Crofts "Act Most Interesting To Children" award. Invented Floating Rabbit 1980. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, & Phoenix. [Tops11/48;HMM10/50;Wh2]

name: Hudson, Charles M.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-80s) Professor of English at U of Missouri (now retired). Inspired as adult in 1942 when invited to a meeting of magicians. Amateur card man. Wrote "The Card Corner" column in Linking Ring 1966-84. [Lo2]

name: Hudson, Homer
bio: (Colorado Springs, Colorado: 19 Mar 1906-11 Apr 2001) Moved to Pasadena. Pro musician in 1930s-40s with his "Homer Hudson Harmonettes" band. Then sign painter & silk screener. From late 1930s until retired in 1995 was a famous builder of magic props of wood and silks. [LR7/2001]

name: Hudson, Walt
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 31 Jan 19-) Inspired at age 10 seeing a magician. Semi-pro since age 16. Then pro in side-shows, clubs, & stage. Wrote "Magical Whirligig" column in New Tops 1973-recently. Author of 5 booklets, including Bring on the Kids (1975, 36pp), Magic with Human Gimmicks: The Stooge Book (1979, 32pp), Cottontail Capers (1979, 10pp), & A Volunteer from the Audience (with Tom Ogden). Articles in MUM, Linking Ring, Magic Manuscript, Tops, & New Tops. [Wh2]

name: Hueber, Theodore "Ted
bio: (Pittsburg, Pennsylvania: 1893-) Semi-pro manipulator since debut in 1929.

name: Huffman, Dan
bio: (Huntington, West Virginia: 5 Oct c1963-) Close-up & mentalism, turning full-time pro in 1986. Wrote Gidrah (1987). Tricks in New Invocation & Linking Ring (2 "Parades").

name: Hugard, Jean, MIMC [pronounced GENE & ZHAHN hew-GARD]
bio: (Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia: 4 Dec 1872-14 [sic] Aug 1959) Stage and pen name of John Gerard Rodney Boyce. Inspired in 1880 seeing Haselmayer show. Learned a week later reading Robert-Houdin's Secrets of Magic, then Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Debut in 1896. Pro since 1900, originally as "Oscar Kellmann", then "Jean Hugarde", later aka "Chin Sun Loo". Toured New Zealand in 1903. Moved to USA in 1916, working vaude 1916-18 & in own magic theater in Luna Park (at Coney Island) 1919-29 when retired in Brooklyn to write and edit magic. Totally blind during last 7 years. Myra Benson was his assistant throughout his career. Invented & marketed the All Backs card effect (in 1930) and invented the Automatic Deck (1933) & The Mask of Balsamo (by 1940). Founded & edited Hugard's Magic Monthly 1943-59. Named 4th SAM Dean of Magicians in 1951. MIMC 1955. SAM Hall of Fame. Prolific author: Ten Card Feats (1932, 14pp typescript), The Automatic Deck and Opening Routine (1933, 9pp mimeo), Mental Magic with Cards (1935, 35pp), Card Manipulations (5 parts, 1934-36, 44+34+48+36pp; repr 1973, 163pp), Close-Up Magic for the Night Club Magician (1934, 36pp; 2nd rev ed, 1938, 57pp), Coin Magic (1935, 88pp), Thimble Magic (1936, 42pp), Silken Sorcery (1937, 83pp; repr 1975 as Handkerchief Magic), Money Magic (1937, 59pp), Encyclopedia of Card Tricks (1937, 402pp, as editor; repr 1961 & 1975), The Magic Annual for 1937 (1937, 141pp), More Card Manipulations (4 parts, 1938-41, 50+52+55+54; repr 1974, 205pp), The Magic Annual for 1938 & 1939 (1939, 137pp), & Modern Magic Manual (1939, 339pp; repr 1957, 373pp), Sealed Mysteries of Pocket Magic (1943, 15pp); and, mostly later, as co-author with Fred Braue (see) of several key books. Wrote Houdini's "Unmasking": Fact vs. Fiction (1957, 80pp). Ghosted Keith Clark's Encyclopedia of Cigarette Tricks (1937) & most of Hilliard's Greater Magic (1938). Tricks & articles in Magic (as Gerard Boyce), Magic Wand, Osirian, Hugard's Magic Monthly, etc. Bios are Jean Hugard Testimonial (1945) & James B. Alfredson, Jean Hugard (1997, 72pp). [Th;Wal;St;Ch;Dor;Ho]

name: Huggins, Wilfred "Wilf
bio: (Suffolk, England: -3 Nov 1977) Taught by "Bezique". Pro street magician since 1907. Founded the Hocus Pocus Society. Published-edited The Midget Magician 1951-60. Used joint pen name (with Herbert Pratt) of "Albert F. Wind" (partial anagram of "Bert" + "Wil"). Wrote Secrets of the Street Conjurers (1939, 19pp). Trick in HMM (1949). [Daw#166]

name: Hughes, Isaiah Harris
bio: (Essex, England: 24 Dec 1813-24 May 1891) Moved to USA as child. Pro stage magician, aka "The Fakir of Ava". He or a namesake played Australia in 1854. Kellar apprenticed as his assistant in 1860. Retired in 1870. [Pr;Ch;Wal]

name: Hughes, Jack
bio: (Exeter, England: 1906-31 Dec 1981) Inspired at age 20. Self-taught from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. A cabinet maker by trade, he made wooden props for Goldston 1936-37 & Davenport's. In British Army in WW II. Then pro dealer & prop maker, initially as co-founder-owner (with Harry Stanley & Arthur Dowler) of Unique Magic Studio Apr 1946-May 1948. Then founded own "Maker of Magic" shop in London, moving it to Kings Lynn in Norfolk in mid-1970s. Father of Bernard "Zelka" Hughes. Invented Television Frame (1936-37), Attaboy (late 1930s), Coins in Glass=Copenetro (1939), Chair Suspension, How Much (1947), Percy the Penguin (1948), Giant and the Dwarf (by 1950), Clatter Box (by 1963), etc. Edited Hughes News as house organ 1953-59 (12 issues). See Derek Lever, The Jack Hughes World of Magic (1982, 196pp). [Daw94]

name: Hughes, Richard [Edward]
bio: (Fort Sill, Oklahoma: 16 Jul 1954-) Interested as child but learned in 1974 from non-credit course at Akron U taught by Tom Craven & John Quine. As part-time newspaper photographer since 1972 has built a large collection of magicians in performance. Worked with Marie Marshall 1976-85 running her late husband Horace's feather flower business. Pro stage magician & lecturer. Also proprietor of Hughes Magic Co in Ravenna, Ohio, since 1985 when he took over the Marshall Company. Wrote Feather Flower Lecture Notes (1985, 17pp). Articles in Genii, New Tops, MUM, & Linking Ring. [Wh2]

name: Hügli, [Friedrich Albert] "Fritz
bio: (Bern, Switzerland: 16 Feb 1870-12 Jan 1940) Psychologist in Bern. Amateur magician since youth. Wrote 5 books in German: Moderne Magie (1902), Zwölf Schlager der Magie (1922, 76pp), Magische Miniaturen (1926, 64pp), Leichte Zauberei (1927, 162pp), & Zauber-und Kartenkunststücke ohne Apparate (1930, 96pp). Articles in Zauberwelt, Zauberspiegel, Magie, Linking Ring, etc. [St]

name: Hugo
bio: See: Shaw, Mark

name: Hugo, Oscar
bio: See: Gutheil, Oscar H.

name: Hugos, François
bio: See: "Hugos, Franz"

name: Hugos, Franz
bio: (Germany: fl.1910s-30s) New stage name of Hugo Dittrich since 1914 at beginning of WW I, patriotically replacing "François Hugos". Pro magician, telepath, & stage hypnotist. Wrote Magie, Hypnotismus, Okkultismus [c1920, 24pp].

name: Hull
bio: (USA: 7 Aug 1881-27 Jul 1931) Stage name of Adam Hull Shirk.

name: Hull, Burling[ame Gilbert]
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY: 9 Sep 1889-19 Nov 1982) Inspired by and learned in 1893 at age 4 when invented first trick. Pro since 1907 or 1908 when he began his life-long career as a mail-order magic dealer in New York City, initially under own name. Soon turned to teaching and writing booklets on specialized subjects in magic. His first book was Expert Billiard Ball Magic (1910, 63pp), an instant success and also the first step-by-step photo-illustrated how-to magic book. Subsequently a prolific author, including Bulletin of Latest Sleights and Improved Tricks (1914, 31pp), Master Sleights with Billiard Ballss (1914, 31pp), 33 Rope Ties and Chain Releases (1915, 46pp; repr 1947), A Modern Handkerchief Act (1915), Twelve Sealed Message Reading Methods (1920), How to Answer Questions for Crystal Gazing and Mind Reading Acts (1927, 42pp), Nine Great Card Feats (1933), Fifty Sealed Message Reading Methods (1935, 52pp), Double Magic with Cards (1935), Your "Break" in Show Business (1955, 27pp, as anonymous); Stage Illusions for the 1,2 or 3 Performer Show (1959; 2nd ed 1972, 39pp), The Dictionary of Mentalism (1961; 3rd rev ed 1973, 2 vols, 208206pp as The Encyclopedic Dictionary of Mentalism), Gold Medal Showmanship for Magicians and Mentalists (1971, 99pp), & Houdini's Greatest Mystery (1982, his last book). Trick in Genii. NOTE: Climax Card Routine (1933) was written by Annemann & not by Hull, as the latter sometimes claimed out of pique. Invented the Card Problem (late 1908), Electra = The Trance Cards (early 1909), Cards Mysterious (by 1909), Svengali Deck (by mid-1909 when pirated by W.D. LeRoy), Menetekel Deck (by mid-1909 when pirated by LeRoy), Where? = The Ghost Card (late 1910), and improved Frank Hall's Floating Lightbulb (in 1931). Retired to Deland, Florida, in 1975. Although an important figure in magic, his often outrageous claims and many empty promises led him to be widely known as "Hurling Bull". Used many pseudonyms, including "Clif [sic] Westfield" (in 1907), "The White Wizard" (1912-18), "Gilbert Galt" (pen name of novelettes in pulp magazines c1916), "Gilbert Gault" (as pretend magic editor in 1930s), "Sylvester Walters" (as pretend editor of Sealed Mysteries), "Volta" (stage name since 1932), "A.R. Smith Jr" as editor of Stage Magic (1935, 6 issues), "Lou Hall" (his pretend agent in 1950s), & "Gid Dayn" (1959-61, his coy rendering of "God Damn"). Memoir is The Edison of Magic and His Incredible Creations (1977, 112pp). Audio. A full bio by Samuel Patrick Smith is in progress. [Albo95,p38]

name: Hull, Henry, MMC
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Premiered (& possibly invented) Magic Welding when presented at The Magic Circle's 4th Grand Séance on 5 Apr 1909. [Magic5/09]

name: Hull, Ralph W.
bio: (Deavertown, Ohio: 5 Jul 1883-20 May 1943) Inspired at age 6 seeing neighbor & amateur, Col. Gray, do a coin trick. Debut at age 20 at school show. Pro cardman for 6 years until 1911. Then as pottery factory executive in family business in Crooksville, Ohio. Prolific inventor of trick card deck and card effects, including Mental Discernment (by 1932), Color Discernment (by 1932), Cards of Chance (by 1932), Elusive Joker (by 1932), Name-O-Card (1932), N.R.A. Deck (1933), Cosmic Ray Cards (1933), Nudist Deck = Mental Photography Deck (1934), Mirage Deck (1934), Photographic Card (by 1935), Nu-Idea Deck (1935), Jim Jam Cards (by 1936), Delirium Tremens (by 1936), Tuned Deck (by 1938), & Coo Coo Cards (by 1940). Also invented Goofy Dice (by 1940). Wrote Eye-Openers (1932, 20pp), More Eye-Openers (1933, 28pp), Fifteen Minutes with a Rope [late 1930s; 2nd ed by Snyder, 1942), Modernism in Pastebord (1934, with Nelson Hahne), Smart Magic (1935, with Nelson Hahne), etc. See Trevor H. Hall, The Testament of Ralph W. Hull [1945, 116pp].

name: Hulse, Homer R.
bio: (USA: 1896-1958) Pro in Atlanta, Georgia, since 1921, often working as "Ramo". Invented Transparent Change Bag (1954). Taught Robert "tabman" Crabb in 1957.

name: Hummel, Joachim
bio: (Germany: 22 Dec 1922-) Magician as "Wilba". Dealer ("Hummel Magie") in Vlotho, Germany. [Nad]

name: Hummer, Robert "Bob" "Bobby
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Publisher. Semi-pro magician. A notable eccentric. Invented Hummer Card Mystery (by 1940), Fantastic (by 1941), Parity Principle, Whirling Card (by 1944), & Poker Chip Trick (by 1947). Wrote Half-a-Dozen Hummers (1940, 12pp), Six Trix for 1944 (1944, 7pp), Little Stranger (c1945, 4pp), Photography (c1945, 4pp), Mathematical 3-Card Monte (1951), Three Pets (1953), & Face-up Face-down Mysteries (c1945, 3pp). Tricks in Jinx & Ireland's YB: 1952. See Karl Fulves (ed), Bob Hummer's Collected Secrets (1980, 109pp). [NT6-9/64]

name: Hündchen, Franz
bio: (München-Gladbach, Germany: 28 Jul 1877-24 Dec 1932) Pro magician. Worked under numerous stage names: "Jaffa", "Rubin", "Taifun", "François", "Maskana, der Mann mit der Maske", etc. [Vo57]

name: Hunt, Mr.
bio: (England: fl.1810s) Pro.

name: Hunt, Douglas M.
bio: (USA: c1919-27 Apr 1997) Prof of Mechanical Engineering at Rutgers U for 20 years. Amateur magus. Co-wrote (with wife Kari Hunt) The Art of Magic (1967), which was reprinted in Britain as The Art of Conjuring (1975, 179pp).

name: Hunt, Nicholas
bio: (Devonshire, England: 1595-1648) Graduated from Oxford in 1616 with BA degree. A devine & mathematician. Invented & wrote the world's first force book, Newe Recreations, or The Mindes release and solacing (London: 1631, 286pp). Copies are in the British Library & the Huntington Library. REF: Edgar Heyl, "Hunt's Newe Recreations", Linking Ring (Jan 1966), 21-25. Hunter, G[eorge] W[allace or Walter], MIMC (England: 16 May 1850-16 May 1936) Inspired in 1878 seeing conjurer in a Chicago music hall where he was himself working as a minstrel-show comedian. Learned same year from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Thence in England as a pro variety-hall comedian (& song writer). Amateur magician & noted expert on pocket tricks. Toured Australia 1899, 1903, & 1909 as comedian. Invented Snapper (in 1910s), Acrobatic Matchbox (by 1927), Hunter Puzzle Knot = Shoelace Tie, & the Cigar Production. Probably invented the Card Castle (by 1882) & the Gypsy Switch (1920s) Voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936 as an absentee member. Husband of "Mdlle. Aimée Désirée" (see). At death left the then comfortable sum of £38,221 (=$200,000). Trick in Pallbearers Review. [Wal;Go;Go2;Vo56]

name: Hunter, Norman
bio: (Sydenham, London, England: 23 Nov 1899-23 Feb 1995) Pro. Joined The Magicians' Club in 1920. Appeared in Maskelyne's Mysteries in 1932 & 1934. Contributor of magic column in Practical Mechanics magazine. Wrote New & Easy Magic (1925), Hey Presto! (1931), New Conjuring without Skill (1935, 104pp), Successful Conjuring for Amateurs (1951, 256pp, ed by F.G. Camm; repr 1954), & The Puffin Book of Magic (1968; reprinted 1972 as Magic Tricks). Also wrote the "Professor Branestawn" books.

name: Hunter, Rudy [Terrence]
bio: (London, England: 8 Jan 1965-) Raised in Toronto, Canada. Learned at age 8 from gift magic set. Pro close-up magician, psychic entertainer, & graphologist since 1987. Articles in Magical Arts Journal & Magick. [Wh2]

name: Huntington, Howard
bio: (Omaha, Nebraska: 7 Sep 1905-1991) Learned from magician father's collection of magic books. Semi-pro c1923 to pro 1928-50. Thence again semi-pro until 1961 when retired by a heart attack. Performed the upside-down straitjacket escape as "The Great Huntington".

name: Huntington, W. P.
bio: See: Durbin, William W.

name: Hurlbut, Jack
bio: (USA: -died in 1980s) Interested as a child. TV news cameraman and producer-director in Madison, Wisconsin, until turned pro magician, specializing in close-up. Host-manager of the Magic Castle for several years around the early 1970s. Then moved to Las Vegas. [Mag]

name: Hurst, Lulu
bio: (Cedar Valley, Georgia: 1869- ) Billed as "The Georgia Wonder". In 1883 at age 14 the 110-pound girl created the super-gravity act. A sensation, she earned $1,000 per night. Retired in 1885 and later married Paul Atkinson. Autobio is Lulu Hurst, The Georgia Wonder Writes Her Autobiography (1897). See also The Revelations of the Georgia Wonder (1897, 267pp). [Pr;Jinx#93]

name: Hurst, Minola Mada
bio: (USA: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro with her "Queen of the Magic Kettle" act using liquid air. [Daw2]

name: Hurwitz, Dr. Abraham B. "Abe" "Doc
bio: (USA: 1906-29 Sep 1981) Aka "Peter Pan, the Magic Man". Magic teacher with NY City Park Department, teaching George Sands (1937), etc. Member of the Legerdemainiacs troupe in early 1940s. A teacher of Bill Derman in 1951. Designated Official Magician for New York City. Trick in HMM. Wrote Magic for Non-Magicians (1975, with Shari Lewis) & Elastrix (1979, 40pp, with Ed Mishell). Father of Shari Lewis whom he taught magic.

name: Husa, Carl
bio: (Austria: fl.1870s-1910s) Student of Heubeck. Opened his "Zauberkönig" magic shop in Vienna in 1876, which was soon absorbed by R. Klingl's shop. Husa moved to Prague where he founded another magic shop in 1892. [Hokuspokus Zauberkunst,p56]

name: Hussan, Sayad
bio: (India: fl.1880s) Moslem, billed as from Hyderabad. Pro. Pet effects: basket trick, blowing knot off hank, cut-&-restored thread, cut-burnt-& restored turban cloth, cups-&-balls, rabbit-from-empty-basket, pigeon-from-shawl, vanishing bottles, and cooking-on-volunteer's head. Played London in 1886 with a mixed Moslem-Hindu troupe. [Cl]

name: Hutchinson [Senior], Wilford
bio: (England: 8 Oct 1888-7 Oct 1963) Pro playing throughout Lancashire with Paper Folding and Paper Tearing. Then dealer-prop maker (under "Ashlyn" trade name) in Ashton-under-Lyne from c1913 until the end of 1939. As house organ published-edited Conjurer's Chronicle 1919-39. Articles in Midget Magician. [Daw94;Daw#203]

name: Hutter, Nicholas
bio: (Belgium: c1850-1911) Aka "Raphael N'Hutter". Pro sleights & illusions. Edited Le Fantastique 1903-08. Joined the French ASAP in 1905. Dealer in Brussels c1912. [Vo58] Hutton, Darryl Canada: 3 Sep 1945- ) Pro as "Darryl the Wizard" in Kenilworth, Ontario. Wrote Doveworkers' Handbook (2 vols.), Modern Ventriloquism. etc. [www]

name: Hylton, Al
bio: (West Indies: fl.1930s) Black. Illusionist in West Indies & Latin America with a Calypso & Voodoo themed illusion act. Played New York's Teatro San José c1939. [HMM8/58]

name: Hymack, Mr.
bio: (Scotland: c1860-1940) Stage name of [Quentin] Henry "Henry Mack" McPherson. Pro with a comedy magical quick-change act in British variety (billed as "The Human Chameleon") from 1907 until retired in 1925 when his wife suddenly died in New Zealand. Had played Germany in 1908 (as "The Man With the Gloves") and toured Australia & New Zealand in 1924-25. [Wal;Ch;Vo56;Dif;CMM10/07]

name: Hyman, Jacob "Jake
bio: (New York City, NY: -9 Sep 1942) Amateur magician in 1888 when he taught 16-year old Ehrich Weiss his first magic tricks. In 1890 coined "Houdini" as Weiss's soon to become immortal stage name. Then briefly pro as Houdini's 1st partner as "The Brothers Houdini" in 1891. After 4 months, disappointed with the poor bookings, left the act and, taking the stage name "Jack Hayman", did a song & dance act with magician brother Joe. [Genii10/91;Gib;Silver]

name: Hyman, Ray
bio: (Chelsea, Massachusetts: 23 Jun 1928-) Inspired at age 7 by birthday box of tricks from father. Worked his way through college as a pro-mentalist doing mind reading, palmistry, & hypnotism. 1953 PhD from Johns Hopkins U. Moved in 1961 to U of Oregon where he has been Professor of Psychology at U of Oregon since 1964. There, among other things, he teaches a seminar on the "Psychology of Deception". Semi-pro-platform magician & mentalist. A noted skeptical investigator of psychic phenomena, he is a founding member of the Committee for the Scientific Investigation of the Paranormal (CSICOP) & serves on the editorial board of its journal, The Skeptical Enquirer. Co-invented (with Irv Weiner) The Prophet's Beard (1957). Wrote The Nature of Psychological Inquiry (1964, 116pp), which includes an analysis of the methods of Jerry Andrus; & "The Psychology of Deception", Annual Review of Psychology, V.40 (1989), 133-154. Also Water-Witching USA (rev ed 1979, with E.Z. Vogt); The Elusive Quarry: A Scientific Appraisal of Psychical Research (1989, 447pp), a collection of articles. Magic tricks in Linking Ring (including 2 "Parades"), Phoenix, New Phoenix, New Jinx, Barnstormer, & Magick. [LR10/86;Wh2] Ⅲ

name: Ibhar
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Mrs. Mawson. Pro. Assistant-wife of "Pharos" until Oct 1907 when toured her own Black Art act.

name: Ibn Batuta
bio: (Tangiers: .....) Pen name of Sheikh Abu-Abdullah Mohmed, known as "Ibn Batuta" (The Traveller). In 1325 he set out on a journey that took him through southern Asia as far as China and back. In 1355 he completed the famous manuscript describing this journey. ..... In ..... he saw a performance of the Indian Rope Trick. His eyewitness account is the basis of all later descriptions of this classic effect. See Ibn Batuta, Travels in Asia and Africa (.....).

name: Ickman
bio:
"lcks, Professeur" SEE: Cordelier, François

[See also: Alberti [Pickman]]

name: Illus
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Anagramatic stage name of Jean Lluis, aka "Ulema". Close-up & dove manip. Founding President of Groupement Régional des Magiciens Girondins 1967-72. Wrote ILLUSions (1970) & ColombILLUS (1971). [Bou2]

name: Illusio
bio: (France: fl.1950s-60s) Stage name of Don Lucry. Pro general magic with assistant-wife Mayanne Lucry (died 1966) with whom he also did a 2-person telepathy act. They played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1962.

name: Imam
bio: (Comilla, Bengal, India [now Bangladesh]: 2 Apr 1942- ) Stage name of Imam Hossain. Learned magic at age 10 from a street magician. Pro close-up & cabaret magician since 1965. Went to Canada as engineering student. Thence moved to USA in 1970. Regular at Magic Towne House (c1977-80). Founder-owner of Mostly Magic in New York City Apr 1979-Apr 1993 when it closed after 5,039 performances. 1989 IBM Parent Assembly Magician of the Year. TV bit in Britain. [MM7/89;Fi2;Wh2]

name: Impey, Eric F.
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s) Stage name of Cecil Griffin. Invented "Locato" trick deck (by 1936). Edited Magic Journal 1932-33. Author. [Le]

name: Inaudi, Jacques
bio: (Onorato, Piedmont, Italy: 13 Oct 1867-25 Nov 1950) Became French citizen in 1882. Famous pro mental calculator since debut in 1890. Played the Lisbon Real Coliseu in 1895. World tour in 1903. Played the Lisbon Coliseu dos Recreios in 1911. Died in France. See Martins Oliveira, Inaudisme Scientifique (1924, 32pp in French & Portuguese). [Dif;St;Wal]

name: Inez, M.
bio: See: Vernello, Inez

name: Inge, Benito
bio: (USA: 22 Oct 1875-13 Jun 1942) Stage name of Dr Anson B. Ingels, MD.

name: Ingleby, Thomas
bio: (Dundee, Scotland: -11 Aug 1832) Pro from 1807 until his death. Wrote (or had ghosted) Ingleby's Whole Art of Legerdemain (1815, 106pp), which explains some 50 tricks, & Ingleby's New London Conjuror [c1825, 12pp]. Died in Ireland. For the death of his widow in 1839 see John Godwin, The Murder of Christina Collins (1981; enlarged ed 1990, 38pp). [Cl;Hou;Fr;Pr;Magic12/06]

name: Ingleby Lunar
bio: (Britain: fl.1820s-30s) Possibly a nephew of Thomas Ingleby. A minor pro, working in Britain 1826-36. [Fr;Cl]

name: Inglis, Alfred
bio: See: "Stodare, Alfred"

name: Ingo
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 29 Oct 1889-10 Dec 1947) Stage name of Rudolf Heindl. Pro since 1912. Toured Europe 1913-25. Pet effects: Bullet Catching from six-shooter, Needle Swallowing, Cups & Balls. [Vo57;St;Al]

name: Innis, S. Victor
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Cardman. One of the first gambling lecturers. Wrote The Inner Secrets of Crooked Card Players (1915), an important booklet, the first to mention tabled Faro Riffle Shuffles used by gamblers to run up complex poker stacks. Also wrote Six Greatest Mystifying Tricks with an Ordinary Pack of Playing Cards [1915, 4pp].

name: Inzani, Remo
bio: (Britain: fl.1950s-70s) Pro dealer (Inzani-Henley Studio of Magic, later Inzani-Henley Magic Company) with partner John Henley in London from 1959 to early 1970s. "lonia" SEE: de Vere, Ionia

name: Ionova, Lidia
bio: (USSR: fl.1980s) Pro. Star illusionist with the Moscow State Circus. Toured Britain in 1985.

name: Ireland, Frances
bio:
(Palermo, Italy: 1904-18 Apr 1985) Naval engineer. Amateur magician since age 20. Collector. Articles in Magia Moderna & Inoltre. [Magia Moderna1985]

[See also: Marshall, Frances Ireland]

name: Ireland, L[aurie] L[owell]
bio: (Minnesota, USA: 1899-27 Apr 1954) Joined circus in teens (1915) when (according to Martin Gardner) his job was "cranking the apparatus for a floating lady illusion". Demonstrator in Berg's "Princess Magic Shop" in Chicago 1925-26, except the summers when he travelled with a carnival, operating the weight-guessing concession. Then since 1926 a full-time pro dealer in Chicago (Ireland Magic Shop). Invented the Ireland Thimble Holder, Cage of Ophira, Multiplying Golf Balls (by 1931), the red-black shuffle (by 1935), and Jo-Ann Duck (by 1937). Wrote Ireland Writes a Book [1931, 35pp], Exclusive Magic From Our Notebook [1933, 22pp], with King], etc. Edited Ireland Yearbook 1934-54. In 1940 married Frances Ireland, who continued the business after his death from cirrhosis of the liver. [Berg,p31]

name: Irisah, Mlle.
bio: (France?: fl.1910s-20s) Stage name. "La belle Irisah" was a pro magicienne with Alyett's world touring troupe from 1914 to 1920, including Egypt. [Dif]

name: Irven
bio: (Austro-Hungarian Empire?: 1905-) Stage name of  Loutgan. Pro card manipulator in Czechoslovakia. [Nad]

name: Irving, Bernard
bio: (Britain: c1891-16 Jun 1931) Started with Gamage's at age 15, managing its magic department since 1914, & became a director in 1929. Edited The Magician Monthly 1914-1931. A suicide. [Daw94]

name: Irving, Carl H[oward]
bio: (Australia: fl. 1st decade of 1900s-1930s) Performed and wrote as "Carl Howarde". Handcuff & comedy juggling acts. Founding member of Australian Society of Magicians. Then became a dentist. Correspondent for Conjurors' Magic Monthly. [McC]

name: Irving, Jean
bio: (Binghampton, New York: 21 Dec 1873-5 Jan 1944) Stage name of Irving Eugene Watson. Pro trapeze artist & fire-eater until age 18 when became a pro magician with full evening and Lyceum shows. Played Tony Pastor's. President, National Conjurers Association 1918-19. [WWM]

name: Isaacs, Peter
bio: (Canada: 1951-2 May 1986) Pro theme park & restaurant magician in Toronto. Aka "Peter Salem". Student of magic in the cinema. Co-author (with Jim Helik) of 101 Tricks, Tips and Ideas with the Appearing Soda Can (1984, 54pp). A suicide.

name: Isaksson, Ingemar
bio: (Sweden: 24 Sep 1936-) Amateur & collector in Halmstad. Edited Trolleri Samlaren 1966-68. Wrote Danska Trolleriböcker: Danish Conjuring Books, a Checklist (1969). Contributor to Magic Cauldron. Isbecque, Claude "Isely, The Mystic" SEE: Isley, John

name: Isley, John
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Demonstrator in a magic-&-joke shop in until 1943 when he went into home-industry business for himself in Cleveland as "The Mystic Isely" (note spelling shift) on the basis of his virtual piracy of Bob Andre's Anti-Gravico.

name: Ishida, Takanobu
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Card magician. 1991 Atsukawa Creativity Award with paper-tea puzzles.

name: Isola, Émile
bio: (Blida, Algeria: 4 Sep 1860-17 May 1945) Son of a Jewish tailor. Inspired as boy seeing visiting European magicians. Moved to Paris in 1880. Pro manipulator. In 1892 with younger brother Vincent opened a theater of magic, the Théâtre Isola. With an aristocratic profile & monocle, Émile specialized in large illusions. In 1897 the Isola brothers dropped their performance of magic to buy and manage several major theaters in Paris: the Parisiana, the Olympia (1898), Folies-Bergère (in 1902), Gaieté-Lyrique, Opéra-Comique (1913 for 12 years), Théâtre Mogador (1925), & Théâtre Sarah-Bernhardt. Loosing their money in the Depression, they retired in 1936. Bio is Pierre Andrieu, Souvenirs des frères Isola (Paris: 1943). [Dif; Vo55; Dam; Bar]

name: Isola, Vincent
bio: (Blida, Algeria: 24 Jul 1862-31 Aug 1947) Inspired as boy seeing visiting European magi. Moved to Paris in 1880. Pro & in 1892 with older brother Émile opened the Théâtre Isola. Vincent specialized in sleight-of-hand with cards & silks. For further bio see previous entry. [Dif;Vo55;Dam;Bar]

name: Ivan, Joseph
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Pseudonym of Joseph "Joe" Rachun. Pro dealer in Brooklyn, New York. Edited Fakir 1941-47 (25 issues).

name: Ivanov, Fyodor Gordieevich
bio: (Russia?: 1888-1957) Son of G. O. Ivanov from whom he received all his props in 1904. Pro magician in Russia as "Teodor Gardii". [Nad]

name: Ivanov, Gordiev Osipovich
bio: (Russia?: 1858-1922) Pro magician in Russia until 1904 when handed over to his son F. G. Ivanov. [Nad]

name: Ivardo
bio: (Norway: 2 Mar 1918-) Stage name of Ivar Brunnström. Owner of a women's hair salon. Semi-pro magician in Norway. Founding President of Den Magiske Ring Oslo 1947. 1976 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic.

name: Iversen, Tommy [Willy Jörgen]
bio: (Randers, Denmark: 30 Apr 1921-18 Nov 1984) Aka "Tommy Atkins", "Jack Atkins", "Jack Million", "Jack Karta", etc. Pro circus juggler, acrobat, & clown, plus ventriloquist & stage pickpocket act. Retired in 1979. 1983 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. NOTE: Surname has been misspelled "Inversall". [Bo2]

name: Ives, Barney
bio: (USA: fl.1st decade of 1900s-1910s) Stage name of Walter G. Barney. Pro card manipulator-inventor. Former student and one-time partner (in 1908) of Dr J.W. Elliott.

name: Ivey, Arthur
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Magic dealer in Islington, London. Edited Magical Mail 1921 (5 issues) & Zodiac 1928-29 (6 issues). NOTE: Not to be confused with following entry. [Daw2]

name: Ivey, Arthur, MIMC
bio: (England: c1891-20 Jun 1975) Magic historian. Curator of The Magic Circle Museum for many years. Article in Hughes News. [Daw]

name: Ivo
bio:
Jäämaa, K. A. Ilmari (Finland: 24 Oct 1888-8 Dec 1934) Publisher. Amateur magician. Wrote Taikakirja [Magic Book] (Porvoo: 1913; with later editions as Taikurin kirja, 1921 & 1938). This was the first significant Finnish-language magic book. Also wrote Ajanvietteen ihmekirja (1935). [St]

[See also: "Allan, Fred"]

name: Jack, Brazil
bio: See: "Brazil Jack"

name: Jackilson
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Stage name of Jacques Lefebvre. Pro. Starred off-and-on at the Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1944-69.

name: Jacks, Stanley
bio: See: Jaks, Dr. Stanley"

name: Jackson, Theodore
bio: (USA: -1905) Afro-American. Pro. Houdini rated him "the best colored magician".

name: Jacky's
bio: (Vire, Calvados, France: 16 Apr 1939-) Stage name of Jackie Georgelin. Learned at age 10. Teacher. Semi-pro magician since 1952, specialized in stage magic. Articles in Journal de la Prestidigitation, etc. [Wh]

name: Jaclare
bio: See: Clarke, Jay

name: Jacobini
bio: (Poland: 1870-1930) Stage name of Kazimierz Kantorowicz. Pro illusionist. [Mec]

name: Jacobs, Mr.
bio: See: Jacobs, Joseph

name: Jacobs, Jean-Baptiste
bio: (France: 7 Dec 1847-14 Jan 1942) Pro stage magic. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1887-88. Ended career as an astrologer when known as "Ely Star". [Dif;St]

name: Jacobs, Joseph
bio: (Canterbury, England: 1813-11 Oct 1870) Aka "Mr. Jacobs" and "M. Jacobs". British Jew. Pro magus-vent since 1834. Billed as "Jacobs the Magician" & "The Wizard Jacobs". Did the Linking Rings since 1835; possibly invented Ink and Water (Bowl-of-Ink to Goldfish), which he added to his act in 1846; & did a Robert-Houdin copy act since 1849. Toured USA (1854), Australia (1855-56, 1857-58, & 1865-66), & New Zealand (1858). Father of J.S. Jacobs. [Daw;Fr;Wal;Cl;Magican;Magic9/07]

name: Jacobs, Professor [J.S.?]
bio: (England?: fl.1870s) Claimed to be the son of Joseph Jacobs, if so his initials were J.S. Pro magician & vent. Toured New Zealand in 1875. A suicide. [Magicana]

name: Jacobs, [Robert] Lee
bio: (Gallipolis, Ohio: 26 Jan 1942-28 Apr 2003) Raised in Pomeroy, Ohio. Learned by age 5. Semi-pro stage comedy magician since age 12 & dealer (initially as Jacobs Illusion Shows) since age 15. College English teacher until 1967 when left academia to become full-time pro mail-order dealer (Lee Jacobs Productions) in Pomeroy. Married to Myriam Ruthchild 1977-88. Edited Jake's Journal 1961-62 (3 issues) as house organ. Wrote Christmas Comedy for Pro Performers (1968, 27pp), The Real Methods and Secrets of the Challenge Escape from 75 Feet of Rope (1975, 44pp), The Promotion (1976, 44pp), etc. Edited Irving Desfor's Great Magicians in Great Moments (1983). Tricks in Genii, etc. TV bits. [Se;Wh]

name: Jacobs, Mark
bio: (USA: 25 Oct 1904-) Carpenter in Hamilton, Ohio. Inspired at age 29 listening to radio show "Chandu--The Magician" (Will Lindhorst). Amateur. Invented Ri-Ro-Ri (1942), Screwy (by 1945), & Corky (by 1945), which were marketed by John Snyder Jr. Tricks in Linking Ring. [Th]

name: Jacobsen, Clayton Lowell
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 24 May 1913- ) Aka "Rudy Roxo". Semi-pro comedy act with small effects & illusions. Wrote (as "Rudy Roxo") Modern Master Magic (1940, 47pp). Worked briefly with Thayer's until Jan 1950 when he bought the name & stock of retail supplies from Bill Larsen & moved the business to Traverse City, Michigan, where it almost immediately failed, the final catalog (#10) being printed but unpublished. Tricks in Genii. [Go2]

name: Jacoby-Harms, Prof.
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: c1850-c1900) Pro magician-escapologist. Played London in 1885. Invented Jacoby Rope Tie (by 1887). Wrote Eine Geister-Soiree (1886, 19pp), a poem with spirit photos; & Illustrierte Zauber-Soiree für Privat-Aufführungen im Salon (1887, 111pp). [Vo56]

name: Jacoby-Stein
bio: (Andernach, Germany: 21 May 1889-24 Aug 1980) Moved to Austria. Pro illusionist 1909-1938. Aka "Kü-Wang-Sü". In 1921 founded the Frankfurt branch of the German Magic Circle (MZ). Moved to Austria where he died in Linz. [Mül;Roh] Jacqueline Eddy and Company (Holland: fl.1960s-80s) Dutch troupe of father (Eddy Schuyer), mother (Jacqueline), and 2 daughters (Josephine & Sylvia) who performed together as a team and not as magician and assistants. Toured the Continent & Britain since the mid-1960s.

name: Jacques, Pierre
bio: (France: 1939-) Stage name of Pierre Goetz. Pro stage pickpocket act. Wrote Complete Course in Pick Pocketing (1983, 91pp). Video.

name: Jacquet-Droz" [misspelling]
bio: See: Jaquet-Droz

name: Jacquinot, Marcel[-Louis]
bio: (Vesoul, Haute-Saône, France: 6 Oct 1935-) Teacher & technician in the construction industry. Amateur magician & writer on magic. Inspired at age 11 seeing Chefalo. [Dif]

name: Jade
bio: (Sumatra, Indonesia: 30 Nov 1962- ) Stage name of Pik Sin "Fanny" TJIN. Of Chinese descent. Moved to Taiwan at age 6 and to USA at age 9. Pro San Francisco magicienne with silent stage act in Chinese costume. 1990 IBM Gold Medal International Award of Excellence in Stage Performance; 1999 Golden Mandrake Award (France); 1999 SAM Best Female Magician of the Year. [MUM1/98;Wh01]

name: Jadini
bio: See: Jappsen, Gerhard

name: Jaffa
bio: See: Hündchen, Franz

name: Jaffar, Professor
bio: (Hungary: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Lusztig PÁL. 1965 Brazilian Magic Competition (Rio de Janeiro) 2nd prize in grand illusions.

name: Jahn, Viggo
bio: (Denmark: 24 Oct 1907 [sic]) Pro manipulator. 1948 FISM Grand Prix. Toured Europe & USA (since 1953 for 6 years with his assistant-wife Jane, including as "Viggo & Jane" since 1955). Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1948 & the New York Palace in 1954. Since 1956 a partner in Leo Nielsen's "Topp's Magic" shop in Saksköbing, Denmark. 1987 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. [Dif]

name: Jakobi, Heinz
bio: (Vogelsdorf near Berlin, Germany: 21 Apr 1902-7 Apr 1976) Pro magician in Berlin. Worked several years after WW I in Conradi-Horster's shop. Sold his own goods after WW II. [St;Roh]

name: Jaks, Dr. Stanley
bio: (Deutsch-Krone, Dantzig, Germany: 26 Jul 1903-5 Jan 1960) Stage name of Siegbert Jaks (not "Herbert Siegbert"), aka "Jax", "Jack Stanley", & "Stanley Jacks". Jew. Studied at the Berlin school of arts & crafts. Originally pro close-up comedy magic. In mid 1930s fled Nazi Germany, moving to Liechtenstein. Taught Jean-Marc in 1945. Moved to USA in 1946, receiving the honorific title "Doctor" that year (not from Annemann in 1938). Soon turned to mentalism. Got US citizenship in 1951. 1952 Sphinx Award. Toured Britain in 1953. Died at home in Manhattan of a heart attack. Invented Supersonic Card Prediction (by 1948), Incredible Prediction (by 1949), Multiball (1952), The Four Blacks (1953), Mind-Ray (1955), What Card (1955), & Mental Image (1958). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, Tarbell #5, Gen, New Phoenix, MUM, HMM, & Swami. Bio & tricks is Robert Bluemle, The Incredible Dr. Jaks (forthcoming, c350pp). See also Charly Eperny, Dr. Stanley Jaks Buch (1963); & Sid Lorraine, Dr. Jaks (1979, an audio tape). [Ran;St;Fate10/52]

name: Jakway, Chris[topher Lyn]
bio: (Kalamazoo, Michigan: 25 Aug 1963-) Learned at age 5 from magic set. Met Neil Foster c1977. Graduated Chavez College 1979. Taught there since 1980. Pro sleight-of-hand plus stand-up comedy magic & straight comedy at clubs. Duke Stern Trophy c1979. Bill Baird Award 1987. In 1988 succeeded Foster as head of Chavez College of Magic at Battle Creek, Michigan. [Wh]

name: James
bio: See: "Fleming, Paul"

name: James, Kevin
bio: (Toul, Muerthe et Moselle, France: 28 Apr 1962- ) Stage name of Kevin James Lowery, son of an American. At age 7 inspired seeing TV magic & learned from library books. Pro since age 14. Does a Charlie Chaplin-theme comedy magic act with partner, noted Columbia-born clown Antonio Hoyos. 1988 AMA Parlour Magician of the Year. Worked the Las Vegas Tropicana in 1990, the Paul Daniels TV show in 1990, the Las Vegas Riviera in 1994, etc. Pet effects: It's Alive, Floating Rose, Chaplin Doll, Perrier with a Twist. Mail-order dealer in Las Vegas as "Imagination Unlimited". Invented It's Alive! (a comedy amputated arm illusion) 1987. Articles in Genii. Co-produced (with Rudy Coby) the Vaudeville 2000 show. [Bo#284;LR6/99;Wh5]

name: James, [John George] Stewart
bio: (Courtright, Ontario, Canada: 14 May 1908-5 Nov 1996) Of Scots ancestry. Learned on 7th birthday. IBM member since 1926. Prolific & highly creative inventor, he published first trick ("Surprising Suspension") in 1926. Major later effects include Ball of Fortune = Medallion (Jun 1929 in Sphinx, with later revisions), the Mosteller Principle (1929), the synonym principle (in 1930s), Miraskill (1935), Headline Prediction (1938), Sefalaljia (1939), Fantastic Facsimile (by 1940), Lac-Lite (by 1940), The Book of the Dead (by 1940), Tip-See (1940), Remembering the Future (1947), Jamesway Poker Deal (1948), & First Finger of Fate (1954, with Freer). 1982 AMA Creative Fellowship. Edited Abbott's Encyclopedia of Rope Tricks (3 vols, 1941, 1962, 1980), a classic series; and wrote booklets: The Nullifactor [1954, 8pp], First Call to Cards (1954, 28pp), Magic Mine No.1 (1957, 28pp), & Case for Cards (1958, 22pp). Many tricks in magazines, including in Sphinx (1926), Canadian Magician's Digest (1929), Jinx, Phoenix, New Phoenix, New Tops, Pentagram, Ibidem, Epoptica, & the all-James issue of Arcane #10 (1983). See P. Howard Lyons & Allan Slaight (editors), Stewart James in Print: The First 50 Years (1989), which at 1,025 pages was the then largest page-count of any book about a single magician ever published in English. See also Allen Slaight (editor), The James Files (2000, 3 vols, 1770pp). [LR1/97;Bo3;Genii3/91]

name: James, Val
bio: (England: fl. 1st decade of 1800s) Popular British magician who worked double-act in 1800 with brother Fitz James who did vent.

name: Jamieson, [George] Allan
bio: (Scotland: 6 Jun 1891-10 Mar 1980) Semi-promagician & magic collector with much material on J.H. Anderson. In his later years companioned Mrs Olga Fone (Goldston). [Daw2]

name: Jamison, R. M.
bio: (El Moro, Colorado: 19 Nov 1884-) Learned magic in travelling shows. Owner of monument works in Trinidad, Colorado. Amateur magician. Invented Spot Sticks in 1944. Moved to Canoga Park, California, in 1946. Tricks in Sphinx, Hugard's Annual of Magic (1937); Jinx, Phoenix, HMM, & Genii. [Th]

name: Jan
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-80s) Inspired seeing Jack Gwynne shows. Began with shows in high school. In 1953 with US Special Services toured Germany with a magic-hyp-mentalism act. Moved to California in the 1950s. [Mag]

name: Jancini
bio: See: Booth, John

name: Janin
bio:
(Austro-Hungarian Empire: 1905-) Stage name of Jan Frantisek Kralicek. Pro illusionist with canary named "Puszek". [Nad]

[See also: Nelson, James M.]

name: Janino la Cheveretta
bio: (Britain?: fl.1310s) Pro bagpiper ("Cheveretta") & sleight-of-hand artist ("called Le Tregetour"). In 1311 gave two performances before King Edward II for which he was paid 40 & 20 shillings. [CI]

name: Jansen, Al[vin H.]
bio: (USA: c1906-c1970) Elder son of Harry "Dante" Jansen from whom he learned magic & music as a young assistant, conducting the orchestra. In 1931 published his "Sim-Sala-Bim" fox-trot music for the Dante show. On original AMA Board of Directors 1962-68. [Pr]

name: Jansen, Harry
bio: See: "Dante"

name: Janson, Nick
bio: (London, England: 2 Feb 1931- ) Stage name of Barry Wootten. Inspired as young boy by Murray. Pro escape artist. 1990 [?.....] Guinness World Record for escape from 1300 pairs of handcuffs. TV bits. [Bo2]

name: Jappsen, Gerhard
bio: (Germany: 20 Jan 1929-) Pro magician as "Jadini". Dealer in coins & electronic props (as "Zauber Jadini") in Geltingen, West Germany. [Nad]

name: Jaquet-Droz, Henri[-Louis]
bio: (La-Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland: 13 Oct 1752-15 Nov 1791) Son of Pierre with whom he toured Europe with his father's automata. Later toured on own. Also associated with J.-F. Leschot & Henri Maillardet. Died in Naples. [Hou;Sal]

name: Jaquet-Droz, Pierre
bio: (La-Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland: 28 Jul 1721-28 Sep 1790) Clock maker in his hometown. Noted builder & exhibitor of androids. Made other smaller automata to fit in his clocks. Worked with the help of his son Henri and J.-F. Leschot. Played Madrid (1758) & Paris (1774). Died wealthy. [Dif;Hou,92-101;St;Mec]

name: Jardine, Bob
bio: (Little Falls, New Jersey: 12 Apr 1936-) Pro close-up. Owner & magic bartender of a magic bar in New York City. Then magic bartender at Magic Castle in Hollywood 1980-84. 1983 AMA Best Close-up Magician. Video (1985). Now works mainly corporate & trade shows. [Mag;Wh2;Wh]

name: Jarrett, Guy
bio: (Belmont County, Ohio, USA: 23 [or 15] Sep 1881-20 May 1972) Left home in teens to join a travelling carnival where, working as a pitchman, he was inspired by seeing the sideshow illusions there & catching the shows of the Herrmanns and Kellar. Pro illusion designer since 1907 when he made his first illusions for a West Coast tent-show. Moved East with T. Nelson Downs in 1908. Assistant & illusion builder for Howard Thurston 1910-11 & stage manager for Dunninger (1925). Invented Bangkok Bungalow (1908), Jarrett Pedestal (1908), etc. Contentious memoir is Magic and Stagecraft (1936). Trick in Sphinx. See also Jim Steinmeyer (ed), Jarrett (1981, 185pp), which is an intelligently annotated reprint of the previous book.

name: Jarrow, Emil
bio: (Jarocin, Prussia, Germany: 4 Apr 1875-4 Mar 1959) Born Emil Jarowcinski, a German Jew. Pro strongman (at age 16 with Buffalo Bill Wild West Show in Europe) Moved to USA in 1892 with that show. After breaking a leg (c1894) became a comedy patter magician. Also juggler (by 1909). Invented Bill in Lemon (by 1909), the Salt Trick (by 1920), & the Tobacco Trick (by 1927), the first & third of which were his pet effects. Became one of the highest paid magicians in vaudeville. Toured Australia in 1927. Retired from vaude in early 1930s & moved to New York City. Wrote one booklet, Rope Magic (1941). Trick in Arcane. See David Charvet, The Bill in Lemon Book, including The Life and Times of Emil Jarrow (1990, 70pp). [Fi;Wal;Magic SYMboI4/91;Dam;Ho]

name: Jarrow, Richard C[harles] "Dick
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 28 Oct 1919-1991) Emil Jarrow was his father's distant cousin. Pro card & coin man. Co-authored (with Bud Dietrich) The Trade Show Handbook (1973, 46pp). Father of Charles & Jane Jarrow. [Wh]

name: Jarrow, Jane [Ellen] "Janie
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 23 Oct 1950-) Only daughter of Richard Jarrow. Taught by Jay & Fran Marshall and coached by father. Noted for her "Alice in Wonderland" and "Bookcase" acts, the latter winning the IBM Junior Prize in 1964. [Wh]

name: Jason, Eddie
bio: See: Joseph, Eddie

name: Jason, George
bio: (Tiflis, Georgia, Russian Empire: -23 Oct 1959) Stage name of George S. Ketiladze. Moved as youth to Canada, then to New York City. College teacher & semi-pro comedy magic with music (Jason as pianist) in 1940s-50s. Trick in HMM. [St] “Jasper, The Great” SEE: Marshall, Jay

name: Jastrow, Dr Joseph
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 30 Jan 1863-8 Jan 1944) Son of a rabbi. Brought to USA in 1866. A pioneer American psychologist since taking his PhD at Johns Hopkins in 1886 under Prof. G. Stanley Hall. First to do a laboratory study of magicians in action, proving that the sleights by his 2 subjects, Alexander Herrmann & Harry Kellar, were not quicker than the eye. See Joseph Jastrow, "The Psychology of Deception", Popular Science Monthly, V.34 (Dec 1888), 145-157; Joseph Jastrow, "Psychological Notes upon Sleight of Hand Experts", Science, V.3 (1896), 685-689. See also Jastrow's Fact and Fable in Psychology (1900, 375pp) & Wish and Wisdom: Episodes in the Vagaries of Belief (1935, 394pp). Miscredited by psychologists with having invented the famous Boomerang Illusion = Jastrow Illusion, which he'd merely borrowed from the old British "Funny Noses" game.

name: Javier, Mago [pronounced HAH-vee-err]
bio: (Jalisco, Mexico: 3 Dec 1939- ) Stage name of Francisco Javier VILLASEÑOR VILLALVAZO since 1955. Learned in 1950 from book. Pro comedy magician since 1955 (while also working variously as showmaker, photographer, printer, book-binder, & clerk). Also does vent (with "Paquito") & marionettes. Works mainly school shows & birthday parties. Freely translated English-language works as Primavera Magica (1983), El Misterio de la Segunda Voz: La Ventriloquia en 10 Lecciones (1985), etc. Articles in Linking Ring (since 1987 with Parades in 1989 & 1991) & Laugh-Makers. [LR11/89;Wh2]

name: Javier & Ana
bio: See: Antón, Javier

name: Jax
bio: See: Jaks, Dr. Stanley

name: Jay, Joshua Adam
bio: (Canton, Ohio: 30 Oct 1981- ) Student. Semi-pro magician with close-up. 1998 Desert Magic Seminar Top Teenage Talent. Tricks (since 1996) in Apocalypse, Trapdoor, Linking Ring, Precursor, MUM, Magic Menu, ONYX, Looking Glass, Magic, Top Hat, Genii, Channel One, and Cyber Sessions. Wrote Joshua Jay's Magic Atlas (1999) with German tr by Oliver Erens as Zauber-Atlas (2000, 260pp). [Wh01]

name: Jay, Ricky
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 1948- ) Stage & pen name of R. J[ay] "Ricky" Potash. Inspired by and learned from grandfather Max Katz at age 4. TV debut at age 7. Pro originally as Ricky Potash, then as "Tricky Ricky" &, finally, "Ricky Jay". Won IBM junior competition c1960. Early pet effects: Dancing Cane & Card Throwing, now mainly card sleights. Set world record card throw of 135 feet on 4 Nov 1976 (Guinness Book of Records 1980 [London ed only]). This was beaten in 1977 by layman Tommy Jackson (166') & again in 1979 by magician Kevin St. Onge (185' 1"), the still (1990) current record. Thus Jay's claim in 1986 to having thrown cards "higher, harder, faster, and further than anyone in history" was no longer true. Note also that T.A. Waters' claim (1988, p.61) that Jay's "current record distance throw is 190 feet, 6 inches" was withdrawn from the 1989 paperbound edition. 1984 Blackstone Jr Award. Curator of the Mulholland Collection of Conjuring and the Allied Arts in Los Angeles, 1985-1990, when the collection was seized by the U.S. Government. Partner with Michael Weber in "Deceptive Practices" consulting firm 1993-present. Played his "Ricky Jay & His 52 Assistants" show in New York City in 1994, Chicago in 1995, & Hollywood in 1996. Technical adviser on several movies, including The Escape Artist (1982), Leap of Faith (1992), Wolf (1994), Forrest Gump (1994 for which he designed the gaffed wheelchair), & I Love Trouble1994; and supporting roles in David Mamet movies such as House of Games (1987, as a con artist). Wrote Cards as Weapons (1977); Learned Pigs & Fireproof Women (1986, 343pp; repr London: 1987, 358pp) with German tr as Sauschlau & Feuerfest (1988); & Many Mysteries Unraveled; or Conjuring Literature in America, 1786-1874 (1990, 48pp). Bios are Mark Singer, "Profile: Secrets of the Magus", New Yorker (5 Apr 1993), 54-73; Maurice Zolotow, "Is Ricky Jay Playing With A Full Deck?", Los Angeles Magazine (Aug 1987); & Laurie Werner, "It's Just Magic. Really", Los Angeles Times (6 Feb 1994), Calendar section, 6,78. [LR3/95; Magie12/89; Wat; Des]

name: Jean de La Vigne" [pen name]
bio: See: Caroly, Jean

name: Jean-Marc
bio: (Paris, France: 13 Aug 1925- ) Stage name of Jean-Marc Bujard. Learned in 1945 from Dr Jaks. Pro close-up & stage magician since 1955. Did international tours & cruises. His very original act "Magie des Coquillages" featured large (20-inch) seashells. Noted collector of cards & decks. Secretary-General of SNIVS 1984-present. Articles in several magic magazines. [Mer;Wh2]

name: Jean-Pierre
bio: (Switzerland: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Jean-Pierre Guébet, aka "Chouf-Chouf". Semi-pro comedy & general magic since late 1960s. Lives in Menton, France. 1977 Tours 1st prize for comedy magic. Law degree from U of Lausanne (1982). Played Magic Castle in 1982. [Bou2;Mag]

name: Jeans, Walter Cerretta, MIMC
bio: (Birmingham, England: 5 Jan 1877-21 Sep 1942) Stage name of Walter Janes, aka "Walter Cerreta". Pro since 1893 to mechanic to dealer in Leeds. Prolific & major inventor, including the mirror-tunnel (1912), Silver Hat (1912), Million Dollar Mystery (1927), & probably the Color Changing Knife. Bio is Peter Warlock, Walter Jeans: Illusioneer (1986, 88pp). [Pr]

name: Jecewiz, Father Jerome [Thomas] "Jerry" [pronounced JEZZ-uh-witz]
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 18 Jun 1950- ) Of Lithuanian descent. Learned at age 13 from library book (Practical Magic), at a Larry Weeks' convention, & group lessons from Max Londono. Performed since 1965. Columnist in Top Hat in 1960s. Roman Catholic priest (ordained 1975) in New York City area. Comedy stage magician (particularly with livestock), as "Father Jerry" & "Priesto". Since 1975 tours his 40 & 90 minute fund-raising "Priesto" shows in the Northeast with a 6-person crew. Pet effects: Duck Vanish & Sub Trunk. Video (1988). TV bits. [Magigram3/87;Wh2]

name: Jee, Jerry
bio: See: de Bodt, Gérard

name: Jeffalo
bio: See: Atkins, Jeffery

name: Jefferini
bio: (Britain: fl.1830s) Minor pro in the music halls of London & the provinces in 1833 with a program mixing songs, pictures, & several magic tricks. [Hou;Cl]

name: Jeffreys, Michael
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 4/7 [……] 1960-) Inspired at age 14 seeing magician at school show. In 1975 became one of the 25 original Junior Magicians of the Magic Castle. Writer & speaker as President of Jeffries Success Seminars in Los Angeles. Semi-pro close-up magician. Wrote Selling with Magic (1989, 200pp), Speaking with Magic (1989, 255pp), The Enlightened Magicians: "The Best of the Best" (1990, 271pp). Articles in Genii. Video Flirting with Magic (1990). [Mag;Wh5]

name: Jeffries, Gene
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Proprietor (as successor to "Douglas Magicland") of "Jeffries Magicland" in Dallas, Texas, 1970-1983 when sold to Howard & Cheryl Hale who continue to operate it as simply "Magicland".

name: Jeffries, Peter
bio: (Britain: fl.1990s) Awards: The Magic Circular's 1991 Cecil Lyle Award; the British Magical Society's 1995 Fred Walker Memorial Society.

name: Jenness, George A[rthur]
bio: (Enfield, England: Sep 1901-7 Nov 1988) Inspired at age 12 seeing Maskelyne's Mysteries & learned reading a school-prize book by Devant. Pro book dealer in London since 1932, specializing in conjuring 1941-73. Book-collector. Wrote Maskelyne and Cooke: Egyptian Music Hall, London 1873-1904 (1967, 93pp). Column in Magician Monthly Tricks in Magician Monthly & Linking Ring. Articles in Collectors Annual. His memoir as a bookseller is in J.B. Findley's Fifth Collectors Annual (1953). [Magicol2/75]

name: Jennings, Larry
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 17 Feb 1933-18 Oct 1997) Born Alfred Lawrence Jennings, legally changed to Larry Jennings in early 1950s by US Navy to avoid payroll confusion with another sailor of same birth name. Plumber to contractor by trade. Learned magic from Ron Wilson. Then moved to Hollywood to study under Dai Vernon. Semi-pro magician. World-class cardman as both inventor and sleight-of-hand artist. Popularized Dick Washington's old LePaul Wallet as the Jennings Wallet. A teacher of Louis Falanga, etc. Co-publisher (with Louis Falanga) of "L&L Publishing" from 1986 to c1990 when succeeded by Bruce Cervon. Died from diabetes combined with heavy drinking. His many inventions in card magic include the Larreverse (by 1967), Immediate Side Steal (by 1977), Pineapple Surprise (1970s), Card in Beer Bottle (1970s), & Pivot Palm (by 1995). See Jeff Busby (ed), Larry Jennings on Card and Coin Handling (1977, 67pp); Jeff Busby, The Coin and Beer Can (1977); Jim Patton & Ron Vergilio, A Visit with Larry Jennings (1982, 8pp); Mike Maxwell, The Classic Magic of Larry Jennings (1986, 288pp); Stephen Minch, Larry Jennings' Neoclassics (1987, 40pp); Mike Maxwell, Larry Jennings: The Cardwright (1988, 204pp). Tricks in Arcane, Epoptica, Epilogue, Apocalypse, Richard's Almanac, Magic, etc. Videos (1975, 1985, 1979) & video bit (1994). [Mag;Wh;Thauma#34]

name: Jensen, Norman [Edwin] "Norm" "Skip
bio: (New York City, NY: 24 Feb 1926-) Learned magic while in grammar school. At age 15 left school and started working at Stuart Robson's magic shop on 42nd Street in 1941. Did shows in US Navy in WW II. Max Holden's shop manager in New York City 1946-49 plus club dates. Then, as "Mr. Magic", MC of ABC-TV kid-magic show in late 1940s to 1950. Articles in Phoenix and the TV magic column in Hugard's Magic Monthly 1949. Associate Editor The New Phoenix 1954, when he left to work for a detective agency run by amateur magus Jerry Lukins. After 3 or 4 years went into the business side of entertainment (including as Tannen's manager in 1958-59) until retired in 1981. Moved to Florida c1986. [Wh]

name: Jeppsson, Carl-Erik
bio: (Trelleborg, Sweden: 29 Jul 1919-17 Nov 1988) Engineer in Katrineholm, Sweden, moving in 1955 to Göteborg. Semi-pro magician as "Jean Cennard".

name: Jerome
bio: (USA: 20 Jan 1893-22 Jun 1935) Stage name of F[rancis] Jerome Loveland.

name: Jersey, Tom
bio: See: Derner, Adolf

name: Jeudevine, F. H. "Pop
bio: (USA: 11 Jan 1878-24 Dec 1951) Barber in Canandaigua, New York. Amateur small magic since c1905. [Th]

name: Jillette, Penn
bio: (Greenfield, Mass.: 5 Mar 1955- ) Pro juggler, fire-eater, unicylist. Aka "Penn" of "Penn & Teller" pro comedy magic act since 1975, originally billed as "The Bad Boys of Magic". Did street juggling in Philadelphia in 1977. Penn is the tall (6'6") articulate partner, an avid computer buff, including hoaxes. They played the Los Angeles Stage Company 1984-85. Co-star of movie Penn & Teller Get Killed (1989). Did their 1st TV special in 1990. Toured USA 1990-91 with their "Refrigerator Tour". 1996 AMA Magician of the Year (with Teller). Wrote (with Teller) Cruel Tricks for Dear Friends (1989, 203pp), How to Play with Your Food (1992), How to Play in Traffic (1997, 227pp). [New Yorker15 May 1989;Ran;Wall Street Journal1 Nov 1990;WWE]

name: Jimae, Jimmy [pronounced JIH-MAY]
bio: (Seattle, Washington: fl.1930s-80s) Pro manip. In 1930s-40s played hotels & theaters across Canada (1936), USA, & Australia (1938). First magician with weekly spot on network TV (Don Ameche Show). On Ed Sullivan TV show in 1950. Gave up magic for business ventures, retiring in 1985 & moving to Cessnock, NSW, Australia. [Tay;Wal]

name: Jiménez-Martínez, Enrique
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 23 Jul 1953-) Inspired at age 7 seeing Chinese magician Fong-Tu-Yeen on TV & Chams at his school. Advertiser in Mexico City. Amateur magician since age c10, specializing in close-up card & parlor magic. Pet effects: 4-Ace effects & Diminishing Cards. Collector. Articles (mainly on Mexican magic history) in Magic Circular, Linking Ring, Genii, Journal of Magic History, Perennial Mystics, etc. 1989 CMI Order of the Magic Lamp. [Wh2] "Joannys, The" SEE UNDER: Droult, Charles A.

name: Job, [Harold W.] "Harry
bio: (Australia: 23 Dec 1909- ) ..... Assistant in Andrade's branch magic shop in Sydney .....-1938 & then its owner 1938-71. Still alive in 1993. [McC]

name: Jochum, W.
bio: See: "Bellachini, Joachim"

name: Jodivil
bio: (Castelo Branco, Portugal: 5 Jul 1938-) Stage name of José Dias VILHENA since 1974 when he became a semi-pro illusionist. His assistant-wife is "Margot" (Maria do Rosário Jacinta Nobre Vilhena). In 1975 co-founded the Associação Portuguesa de Ilusionismo. 1977 Grand Prize at the 4th Festival Mágico in Portugal and 1979 2nd prize for illusions at the 5th Festival. [Cam;Bou2]

name: Joferk
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 22 Mar 1939-) Stage name since 1960 of José Fernando Pacheco COIMBRA. Pro. 1st prize for general magic in 1973 & 1975 at the 2nd & 3rd Festival Mágico in Portugal. [Cam] "Joglar, Frank" [columnist for Hugard's Magic Monthly] SEE: Christopher, Milbourne

name: John, Mr
bio: See: Eriksson, John Erik

name: Johnson, Charles "Charlie
bio: (Hannibal, Missouri: 12 Jul 1898-6 Sep 1974) A non-magician, he retired as a mechanical engineer & turned semi-pro magic dealer-manufacturer by founding Johnson Products in 1966 [sic], which made quality coin props. Sold in 1967 [sic] to his machinist, Sam LaPorte. Then founded Milson Magic, which his son, Lynn Johnson inherited. [Se]

name: Johnson, George
bio: (Plymouth, England: 1877-30 Jul 1962) Publicist in London. Amateur magician, publisher 1910-45, & collector. Published-edited The Magic Wand 1914-45. Wrote the scarce Conjurers' Tales (1910, 80pp) with 7 short stories of magic portrayed as fact, The History of "The Magic Wand" (1923, 16pp), & C-O-N-J-U-R-I-N-G (1949). As "H.G. Sparks" wrote Pack a Deck (n.d.). A carbon copy of his unpublished 106-page typescript autobiothe c1940, "A Wizard's Wallet", in the Findlay Collection was sold in 1979 to Till book dealers in London. Tricks & articles in Magic & Conjuriana.

name: Johnson, George N.
bio: (England: 14 Dec 1914-) Foreign service officer. Posted to the British Legation in Helsinki, Finland, 1945-52, thence with the Foreign Office in London. Amateur magician. Articles in Simsalabim. [St]

name: Johnson [Jr], Hiawatha [Z.] "Hi
bio: (Lynchburg, Virginia: 20 Jul 195- ) Afro-American. Learned at age c5 when "my brother showed me how to rub a penny through my arm." Musician & composer at Randolph-Macon Woman's College in home town. Also pro magician since 1975 as "Hiawatha". Specialist in theatrical & bizarre magick. Pet effects: Needle thru Tongue & Nest of Bags. Wrote Characters (2 vols, 1988, 1989), a set of lecture notes. Articles in Linking Ring, Genii, Magic Manuscript, Apocalypse, etc. [Wh2]

name: Johnson, J. J.
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Pro close-upper. Co-editor (with Chris Powers) of Opus, 1987-present. Video: Laid Back Too (1990).

name: Johnson, [Gerald Bruce] "Jerry
bio: (Forest Lake, Minnesota: 12 Jul 1932- ) Learned at age 11 from a Robbins' 15¢ pamphlet whose ads led to the Thurston & Blackstone books. Computer specialist in Minneapolis. Semi-pro stand-up comedy & novelty magician since c1965. Wrote 2 Linking Ring "Parades" in 1989. [LR10/89;Wh2]

name: Johnson, [Claiborn] Lynn
bio: (Santa Monica, California: 25 Oct 1936- ) R&D Engineer with Lockheed Corporation. Semi-pro magic dealer-manufacturer. Son of Charles Johnson from whom he inherited Milson Magic in 1974. In 1975 bought Worth Magic Novelty Company from the estate of Jim Simon, renaming his business Milson-Worth. Located in Sun Valley, California, it makes & markets a line of high quality props in wood & metal. [Wh2]

name: Johnson, Ross [Alan]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 27 Sep 1945-) Inspired at age 18 meeting Eugene Burger. Ex-teacher. Promentalist in Chicago since 1986. Pet effect: Q&A. 1988 PEA Mentalist of the Year (for Tony Raven's Balls of Brass). Articles in Invocation, Magick, & Vibrations. [Wh2]

name: Johnson, Roy [Arthur], MIMC
bio: (Leicester, England: 14 Apr 1932-) Learned c1947 by tricks from Paul Clive's magic shop. Pro close-up, mental, & cabaret magician since 1953 (with his debut at the Windmill Theatre). Has lectured in USA, Australia, & Europe since late 1960s. Wrote The Roy Johnson Experience (1970, 76pp), The Roy Johnson Lecture Notes (1970), Second Time Around (1971, 84pp), Feature Three [c1975, 16pp), Third Dimension (1977), Final Call (1979), Everyman Cards (1979, 20pp), A World of Clocks (1984, 19pp), Pure Gold (1988, 99pp), Silver Special (1989, 92pp), & Transatlantic Inspiration (forthcoming). Tricks in Pentagram, Abra, Magic Wand, Genii, MUM, Epoptica, Talisman, Magick, etc. 3 audios; 5 videos (c1983-1990). [La2;Wh2]

name: Johnson, Thomas
bio: (Britain: fl.1630s) Wrote Dainty Conceits (London: 1630, 12 leaves). Contains a few card tricks. The only known copy is in the Huntington Library. REF: Edgar Heyl in MUM Jan & Feb 1960.

name: Johnson, V. E., MA
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Wrote Chemistry and Chemical Magic (1911, 150pp; repr 1920), Electricity and Electrical Magic (150pp), & Mechanics and Some of its Mysteries (150pp).

name: Johnsson, [Frederick] "Rick
bio: (Newport, Rhode Island: 26 Jan 1937-25 Feb 1989) Inspired in 1952 when father taught him the old coin-from-behind ear, then self-taught from books. Teacher. Amateur close-up magician. Proposed the Too Perfect Theory in 1970. Wrote Practical Impossibilities (1976), etc. Columnist (since 1976) & reviewer (since 1985) for Linking Ring. Tricks in Pallbearers Review, Hierophant, etc. [LR5/89] Johnston, Bert W. A. (Toronto, Canada: 14 Sep 1878- ) Pro. Began as a medicine show magician. Toured a full-evening show thru northern and western Canada in 1920s. Later (1930s) toured Canada with the Marks family dramatic shows. [Bo3]

name: Johnston, Hugh R.
bio: (USA: 1890-3 Dec 1957) Pro vaudeville cardman since 1904 or 1905. Nominally co-author (actually entirely written by F.B. Sterling) of Modern Card Miracles: A Complete Card-Act with Patter (1919). Trick in Felsman's (Oct 1919). [Pr]

name: Johnston, Rory [Wesley]
bio: (Freeport, New York: 22 Aug 1955-) Learned at age 16 as circus clown from books, catalog tricks, & circus magician Fred Marco. Pro stand-up comedy magician since age 18. Invented Godzilla's Revenge, Color-changing Cigarette, Shrinking Bottle, Great Ruby Robbery, & Chest Amazing. Wrote lecture notes Magic in Black & White (1977). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Johnstone, Duncan [Blair]
bio: (Dennistoun, Glasgow, Scotland: 12 Oct 1905-4 Feb 1985) Clerk in a Glasgow brewery. Semi-pro magician (as "Stanley Marne") and magic collector. Pet effects: Cups and Balls & Cords of Fantasia. Honorary Secretary of the Scottish Conjurers' Association for 50 years since 1926. Died at his home in Glasgow. His collection was auctioned by Sotheby's in late 1985. Tricks in Sphinx, etc. Bio by E.A. Dawes in The Wizard Exposed (1987), vii-xiv.

name: Johnstone, George
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 5 Apr 1919-) Stage name of George John Johnston since 1943. Raised in Dedham, Massachusetts. Learned at age 9 from Mysto Magic set. Debut assisting Blackstone 1939-42. Thence pro with straight magic until 1949 when switched to comedy magic. George & assistant-wife Betty played the NY Palace in 1951. Wrote booklet Horizons in Magic (1943). Wrote series in Linking Ring on trouping with Blackstone. Wrote column in The Dragon, "Johnstone's Column" in New Tops (since 1961), & "News and Views from the Colonies" column in Magigram (since 1971). [Bo#258;Des;Wh2]

name: Jogestja
bio: See: James, Stewart

name: Jo-Jo, Mister
bio: See: Heuer, Rudolf

name: Jolley, Graham P[eter], AIMC
bio: (Leeds, England: 24 Nov 1945- ) Inspired at age 8 seeing David Nixon TV show. Ex-businessman. Pro comedy mentalist since age 28 (1974). Works mainly audiences of businessmen. Also the QEII cruise ship. Pet effects: Psycho II & Geneva Watch. TV bits. Trick in Genii. [Opus6/88;Wh2]

name: Jolson
bio: (Idanha-a-Nova, Portugal: 14 Jun 1922-) Stage name of Raúl da Silva Pinto. Pro illusionist. Worked many European circuses over 60 years. Appeared in Italian film Feminine al Neon (1962). [Cam]

name: Jon, Finn
bio: (Oslo, Norway: 14 Mar 1939-) Stage name of Finn Johan Hauger since 1968. Learned at age 12. Ex-plumber in Oslo. NMK Nordic Champion 1962, 1963, 1965, 1966 (the most ever won at that convention prior to Roberto's 4th award in 1988). Turned pro magician in 1963, becoming an international star since late 1960s. 1968 FISM 2nd prize for stage magic. A master of thread magic in which he is a major innovator. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal 1969 & repeatedly played the Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris 1978-88. Pet effects: small scale levitation & animation. Believes "the key to successful magic in our time relies on the visual effect--it must look interesting instantly, like bubble magic." Wrote Soap Bubbles Book (1989, 39pp), New Magic, & Invisible Elastic Thread. Articles in Norwegian Magic Circle annual & New Directions. 5 videos (3 in 1984, 1 in 1986, 1 in 1987). See Georges Proust, Magic of Finn Jon (1984). [Dif;Wh2]

name: Jonas, Philipp
bio: (Germany?: fl.1760s-1st decade of 1800s) Of Jewish family. Famous pro cardman and sleight-of-hand artist in Britain 1766-1773 & France 1774-1780 when retired to London as a money-lender. Severely disfigured by a "learned" dog at Bartholomew Fair in 1807. [Daw#225;Fr;Dam;Cl;Dif]

name: Jonason, Linda
bio: (Decatur, Illinois: 25 May 1951- ) A former dancer, baton twirler, & beauty queen (1971 "Miss Sacramento") when learned magic as assistant to Bob Brown since 1973, working as "Bob Brown & Linda". Studied further with Mike Rogers and Channing Pollock. Then semi-pro with own magic dance act as "Magical Moods". Now married (Mrs Abrams since 1984) & a successful real estate developer in Orange County, California. [MM5/88;Wh]

name: Jones [Jr], Bascom [Sidney]
bio: (San Diego, California: 28 Oct 1924-23 Mar 1994) Nephew of T. Page Wright whose magic library (nearly 2,000 items) he inherited at age 8 & learned by reading it at age 11. Debut at age 12 in school shows. Professional writer. Amateur mental magic as "Bascom". In 1947 co-invented (with Fred Shields) Unbelievable, a now classic card effect. 1988 PEA Achievement in the Art of Mentalism Award. Wrote (with Fred Shields) "Double Daring" column in Genii 1947-61. Editor-publisher of Magick 1970-death. Wrote King of the Cold Readers (1989, 77pp) & 19 Rules of Mentalism. Many effects in Genii & Magick, using own plus several pen names. [Wh2]

name: Jones, Carl Waring
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 24 Aug 1887-5 [sic] Jan 1957) Wealthy newspaper publisher (The Minneapolis Journal) & amateur magician. Publisher (1938-57) of magic books, beginning with Hilliard's Greater Magic. His magic book collection is now housed in the rare book division of Princeton U Library. Memoir in LR (Feb 1944).

name: Jones, [Charles Frederick] "Chuck
bio: (Trenton, New Jersey: 18 Aug 1942- ) Raised in Los Angeles. Inspired at age 11 seeing Dell O'Dell on local TV. Debut in teens. Pro illusionist since age 20. Tours a full-evening show since c1965 with partner-wife Jan Jones. Invented Mis-Made Lady in 1968 (premiered that September by Orson Welles on TV). Pet effects: Mis-Made Lady & Sword Suspension (with impalement). SAM illusion award. 1987 Dragon Award with Jan. Article in Genii. [Jef;Mag;Wat;Wh2]

name: Jones, Davey
bio: See: Marlin-Jones, Davey

name: Jones, Frederick E.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Wrote Mind Reading Secrets and Sealed Billet Reading (1911, 36pp).

name: Jones, Jan[ice Arleen]
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 4 Aug 1943-) Married Chuck Jones in 1964. Learned c1965 as his pro assistant. In 1967-68 "Chuck and I talked about a divided lady effect--mix-up was my idea. An innocent remark has become a magic classic", Mis-Made Lady. Edited The Magician's Assistant (1982, 100pp). 1987 Dragon Award with partner Chuck. [Wh2]

name: Jones, [Lawrence L.] "Larry
bio: (USA: c1926-24 Aug 2003) Aka "Baron LaValle" & "Capt. Squirrelly". Lawyer & justice of the peace in Louisville, Kentucky. Semi-pro magician & illusionist. Appeared on TV (Ed Sullivan show in 1959), at magic conventions, & the Magic Castle. Pet effect: multiple live goldfish production. [Mag;HMM7/58,9/59]

name: Jones, John Davenport "Little Johnny
bio: (Bluefield, West Virginia: 10 Jul 1898-15 Jan 1995) Pro magician since 1932. Did USO shows in WW II. Retired in 1964. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote So You Want To Be A Magician (32pp). [MUM2/82; Daw2]

name: Jones, Lloyd E[verett]
bio: (Grass Valley, California: 7 Jul 1906-18 Sep 1984) Aka "E. Samuels" as pen name. Pharmacist in Oakland. Semi-pro magic dealer-collector-publisher. A founder & first President of the Pacific Coast Association of Magicians in 1933. Book dealer-publisher as Magic Limited by 1940. SAM President 1955-56. A major collector of magic books since 1943 when he bought the Rybolt Collection, which totalled 9,200 items (some 5,000 titles). Jones then added the collections of Joseph Ovette, Raymond Gerike, Charles Nyquist (some 1,000 books c1970), & Robert Andrews. Sold his superb collection in 1975 to Byron Walker, thence concentrating on his magic publishing business, Magic Limited. 1979 AMA Special Fellowship. Published-edited What's Doing 1940, The Bat 1943-51, Bat Jr 1951-55, S.O.B. Jr 1970-78, & Bat Droppings 1979-84. Wrote Meet the Boys of The Pacific Coast (1934, 48pp), The Dime and Penny (1945, 19pp), The Medicine Man Pitch (1954, 9pp), S.B.S. [1973, 43pp], etc. Book reviewer for Tops & Genii. Tricks in HMM. [Se] "Jongeleur, Mother" [pen name in Genii] SEE: Orben, Robert

name: Jónio
bio: See: Camacho Barriga, João António

name: Jonson, Wilfrid [G.], MIMC
bio: (Croydon, Surrey, England: 17 Sep 1899 [sic]-21 Jan 1974) Semi-pro since 1925, then pro. Edited the 2 issues of George Johnson's The Magical News (1924). Co-authored (with Harry Leat) Masked Magical Glossary (1928, 31pp), an eccentric effort to disguise 200 familiar jargon terms under a layer of their newly coined terms. Wrote "London Notes" column for Sphinx since 1930. Wrote Mr. Smith's Guide to Sleight of Hand (1945, 95pp), But Not to Play (1946, 120pp), Conjuring (1950, 96pp), Card Conjuring (1950, 92pp), the last two being reprinted in USA by Dover as Wilfrid Johnson's Magic Tricks (1953, 100pp) & Wilfrid Johnson's Card Tricks (1953, 96pp) that were and finally in combined volume as Magic Tricks and Card Tricks (1954, 100+96pp; repr 1957). Tricks in Magic Wand. [WWM]

name: Jordan, Charles T [horton]
bio: (California, USA: 1 Oct 1888-24 Apr 1944) Inspired in 1898 (age 10) seeing Kellar. Invented many card effects, including Jordan Count (1919), Gray Code (1919), Ultimo trick deck (1919), & Unknown Leaper. Sold his good collection of magic books to Earl F. Rybolt in 1943. Wrote Thirty Card Mysteries (1919, 45pp; repr 1974), Ten New Impromptu Card Tricks (1920, 24pp), Ten New Slight of Hand Card Tricks (12pp), Ten New Miscellaneous Tricks (22pp), Ten New Prepared Card Tricks (24pp), Ten New Pocket Tricks (23pp), & Four Full Hands (1947, 40pp). See also Karl Fulves (ed), Charles T. Jordan: Selected Tricks (1975) & Charles Jordan's Best Card Tricks (1992, 252pp). Also wrote pulp detective short stories (including magic) in the early 1920s. [Bat8/48;Dor;Magic1/20,pp31-32]

name: Jorgan"/"Jorgano
bio: See: Börsch, Jörgen

name: Joro
bio: See: Hennig, Bruno

name: Jory, Victor
bio: (Dawson City, Alaska: 23 Nov 1901-1982) US stage & film actor since 1929, including as the star in The Shadow serial (1940). Amateur magician. Trick (a center tear) in Phoenix #203 (1950). Did card sleights in Hollywood movie Fighting Man of the Plains (1950). Played the magician in the Broadway revival of The Spider in 1952. [Katz]

name: José Luis
bio: See: Mazoy Kuri, José Luis

name: Joseffy
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 3 Mar 1873-26 May 1946) Stage name of Joseph (born Josef) P. Freud. Moved to USA at age 19. Pro magician (ex locksmith & musician). Mechanic for Burlingame in Chicago in 1900 when he pirated W. W. Wood's non-thread Rapping Hand. Invented Caesar Gimmick (in 1930). See David P. Abbott, The Marvelous Creations of Joseffy (1908, 24pp) for an exaggerated view of his creative abilities. Most of his props were acquired by Eugene Bernstein. [Par;Dif;Berg;Go2;CMM1/08]

name: Josefini
bio: (Romania: fl.1950s-80s) Pro illusionist & manipulator in circus. Autobio is Din tainele illusionosmului (1961).

name: Joseph
bio: (Jersey City, New Jersey: 1958-) Stage name of Joseph Gabriel Wierzbicki, aka "Joseph Gabriel". Pro bird magic with Polish-born assistant-wife Lucy. [Mag;Wat]

name: Joseph, Eddie
bio: (Calcutta, India: 3 Dec 1899-1 Jun 1974) Of English parentage. Aka "Eddie Jason". Inspired at age 12 seeing Nicola show. Businessman in Calcutta & Bombay and semi-pro magician since age 18 (c1917) to 1945 when turned full-time pro. 1947 Sphinx Award. Edited the 8 issues of The Magical Digest (Bombay) 1947-48. Later moved to England, working for Max Andrews. Died in London. Prolific author, including Intuitional Sight (1938, 20pp), A Practical Lesson in "Cups and Balls", Advanced Lessons in Cups and Balls (28pp), Magic and Mysteries of India [1940, 80pp], How to Pick Pockets (1940), The Last Word on the Cups and Balls (1942, 68pp), Coin & Money Magic (1942, 116pp), Greater Card Tricks (1942, 101pp), How Gamblers Win, The Art of Body Loading & Productions (1950, 40pp), A Magician Goes to Dinner (1954, 23pp), The Hindu Cups and Balls (1956, 48pp), & The Manuel of the Three Shell Game (1959, 30pp). See Hugh Miller, The Art of Eddie Joseph (1969, 353pp; repr 1978). Tricks in Jinx, Conjurors' Magazine, Tops, Swami, etc. Invented Ink-U-Bator (by 1940), Will Domination (by 1940), Staggered (1949), Mirage (1956), etc. NOTE: Miscredited with inventing McCaffrey's Premonition. [Tops12/52]

name: Joseph, George
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Former Detroit card hustler. Since 1980 Director of Surveillance at the Dunes Casino in Las Vegas. Wrote 'Hand Mucking': The Art of Switching Cards in Play (1982, 50pp) & The Overhand Shuffle Action Palm (1982, 6pp).

name: Josephine
bio: (Britain: 31 Jan 1943-) Stage name of Josephine Shadbolt (née Booth) after marrying "Brian Sefton" (Shadbolt) in 1977. He then taught her but only to develop her own act. Teacher of business subjects. Semi-pro cabaret & kid shows. 1980 British Ring Shield, Dittia Shield, & Craig Trophy. [Mar]

name: Josolyne, Agnes Blanche
bio: (West Kirby, England: 28 Oct 1909-) Mrs Sydney Josolyne (née Parry) with whom as "La Celeste" she worked 2-person mind-reading act. Stage debut in Jan 1924. At Blackpool for 12 consecutive seasons 1938-50. [Daw2]

name: Josolyne, Sidney [Edgar]
bio: (Walthamstow, England: 18 Feb 1892-24 Jan 1965) Minor pro music-hall sleight-of-hand magician in London. Having evidently pirated Selbit's Walking thru a Wall, he sold it to Houdini in 1914 for £1. Worked a two-person mental act with "La Celeste" (the 1st & 2nd Mrs Josolynes). Wrote Weird Wonders for Wizards [1925].

name: Joy, William I [rvin] "Bill
bio: (Youngstown, Ohio: 15 Oct 1920-11 Dec 1996) Learned at age 12 from Gilbert magic set & books. Systems analyst. Semi-to-pro magician as "Joy the Magician". Troped his "How's Tricks" illusion show with 5 assistants & 2 tons of equipment. With multiple sclerosis, he performed from a wheelchair since 1969. 1972 Syl Reilly Award. A Mason & President of the Invisible Lodge since 1974 [sic]. Editor of The Trestle Board 1974-present. Articles in Genii, Tops, MUM, & Linking Ring. [Wh2]

name: Judah, Stewart
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 16 Feb 1893-11 Jun 1966) Stage name of Joshua Stewart. Semi-pro cardman since 1920. Charter member Queen City Mystics (Cincinnati) 1922. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Invented Transpo-Silko (by 1941), Flying Matches (by 1946), Obedient Silks (1952), & Keys of Judah (1955). Wrote Subtle Problems You Will Do (1937, 75pp, with John Braun). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, New Phoenix, Talisman, Pallbearers (2 all-Judah issues), Chronicles. See John Braun (ed), The Magic World of Stewart Judah (1966, 96pp).

name: Judd, Professor A[ugustus] M.
bio: (England: fl.1870s) Woodturner for Charles de Vere. Dealer at 5 Brownlow Street, Drury-lane, London. Offered to perform tricks, illusions, & vent at private parties. Issued his first catalog (undated) of 40 pages, The Professional Wizard's Guide to the Selection and Purchase of Magical and Conjuring Tricks. The 1879 edition had grown to 98 pages.

name: Judd, Professor W[illiam] J.
bio: (England: 1850- ) Moved to USA. Bought J.M. Hartz's shop in 1876. Issued his first catalog in 1876: Illustrated Descriptive Catalogue with prices of Conjuring Tricks, Magical Apparatus, etc. Other catalogs were issued in 1877 (Illustrated and Descriptive Catalogue of the Magical and Conjuring Repository), 1879, 1886, & 1890. Also wrote Wizard's Book of Dialogues (1884, 42pp), probably the 1st patter book. [Albo95]

name: Jules, Stuart
bio: See: Traub, Jules

name: Julianelly
bio: (Spain: 1910-1956) Stage name of Miguel Julián Dominguez. Pro. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1945.

name: Juno
bio: (Germany?: 16 May 1944-) Stage name of Horst Lohr. Magician in Germany. 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in manip; 1986 MZvD Magician of the Year; 1987 MZvD 1st prize in card magic, 2nd in manip, & 2nd in kids magic. [Nad]

name: Jupiter, Mr.
bio: (Hungary: fl.1980s-90s) Stage name of Gergely MOLNAR. Pro stage magician with assistant-wife Ilona, specializing in a cane, candle, & dove act in nightclubs. Living in Vienna, he performed in Western Europe for several years. Moved back to Budapest where he works both cabaret (with wife Ilona) & close-up. Dealer ("Jupiter"). President of Houdini Magic Club in Budapest.

name: Jur
bio: (Bydgoszcz [ex-Bromberg], Poland: 17 Apr 1931- ) Stage name of Jerzy Strzelecki. Former scene painter. Learned from a library Conradi-Horster book. Pro manipulative magician since 1961. Toured East Europe, Egypt, Morocco, Britain, Spain, Portugal (1978), Thailand, & Japan. Consultant on the Polish magic film, Strachy. Also did a musical comedy act in circuses & variety theaters. [Win;Mec]

name: Juris, Dr.
bio: See: Bluemle, Robert L.

name: Juza, Karel
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 19 May 1921-5 Apr 1990) Graduate of the Conradi-Horter magic school in Berlin. Amateur illusionist & collector. President of Unie Prazskch Magiku. Editor of Cáry Máry. [Mec;Nad]

name: Ka-Ro-Ly
bio: See: Caroly, Jean

name: Kadan Sami
bio: See: "Leon, The Great"

name: Kader, Prince
bio: (France: c1920-) Stage name of Charles Chaise. Pro street magic since 1945. Operated a magic & joke shop in Vincennes. [Dif]

name: Kadi, Aben El
bio: (Spain: 11 Sep 1910- ) Stage name of Daniel Mendez. At age 13 learned immunity to heat. Pro fakir & pseudo-hyp act. Toured South America, North America, & Europe. [St]

name: Kahlert, [James Howard] "Jim
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 3 Sep 1940- ) Learned at age 10 or 11 from father's gift of tricks & his instruction. Moved to Los Angeles in 1974. Pro close-up & parlor magician and magic teacher since 1976. Invented Baffling Bingo (1982), etc. Tricks in Genii. 3 videos. [Wh5]

name: Kahlow, Larry J[ohn]
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 25 Aug 1950-) Learned in 1958 from magic set from Eagle Magic Store in Minneapolis. Pro close-up since 1971. Demonstrator at Collins Pentz' Eagle Magic 1971-76 and its owner since buying it in 1976. Wrote 10 Easy Magic Tricks (1976) for General Mills Inc. [Wh2]

name: Kahn
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of R.K. Dunning. Originally an auctioneer & theater lessee. Manager of Carl Herrmann in Glasgow 1887-88.
