Then since 1891 pro ventriloquist (as "Dunning") & (since 1893) magician (as "Kahn") with ball manip, Vanishing Birdcage, etc. Worked popular double act with wife (as "Miss Kahn, Queen of Sleight of Hand, and Khan, The Master of Mystery"). Together they did Second Sight. They toured South Africa 1891-93 & 1898-99. [Magic3/01,2/02;Cl] Kahn, Miss, later Madame (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Mrs R.K. [not Alfred] Dunning. Billed as "Queen of Sleight of Hand", doing a silk act, including the Crystal Casket & the Handkerchief & Soup Plate. Worked double with husband as "Miss Kahn and Kahn" since 1891, as group with the "Four Mystic Saxbys", and solo from 1901 to 1906 doing stage magic & illusions. [Magic3/01,2/02;Cl]

name: Kains, Maurice "Harry" & "Maury
bio: (Lansing, Michigan: 13 Dec 1896-29 Oct 1969) Inspired at age 15 seeing street magician. Avid amateur magician in Flatbush, New York City, by 1916 when he roomed with & learned from the Bambergs. In US Army in WW I. Then to Hollywood as movie cameraman since c1920, eventually with color. Developed his own prizewinning magic style. Invented “‘Ultissimo’ Prediction” (by 1947). Articles. Died in Los Angeles. [Th;Bam, p.45]

name: Kaiser
bio: See: Harrison, Vincent

name: Kajar
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Stage name of Reuben Bowen. Minor pro. Several TV bits in New York City since 1950, including CBS's It's Magic (1955). His wife-assistant was Jean Darling, child co-star of "Our Gang" movie shorts in the 1930s. [HMM5/50,10/52]

name: Kalama
bio: See: Perót, Auguste

name: Kalanag
bio: See: Schreiber, Helmut

name: Kaldy, Robert
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 18 Jan 1951-) Learned at age 14. Fireman in Vienna. Part-time pro magician with stage name of "Karo" since 1965 & pen name of "Robert Kaldy-Karo". Does kid-shows, close-up, & illusions. In 1977 co-founded (with Michael Swatosch) the "1. Wiener Zaubertheater". In 1981 co-founded both the same-named magic club & founder-editor of its journal, Innovator, 1981-present. 1985 MZvD Writer of the Year award (shared with Eberhard Riese). Collector. Wrote 25 books & booklets since 1978, including Manipulations Ideen (1979, 64pp), Symbolkarten (1983, 62pp, with M. Swatosch), Zauberei mit Creditkarten (1987, 72pp), Magie mit Krawatten (1988, 94pp), Magica Historica (4 vols, 1988-89, 32pp each), Kalanag (1988, 36pp, with M. Swatosch), & Meister der Magie (1991). Articles in Innovator, Aladin, Magie, Magische Welt, Magischer Anzeiger, Zauberkunst, Hokus-Pokus (Switz.), MUM, Magigram, Lang's Hokuspokus fidibus (1984), etc. [Al;Wh5]

name: Kali
bio: See: Linker, Klaas G.

name: Kalin, Mark
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) 1980 AMA Junior Achievement Award. Semi-pro in teens to pro illusionist in Las Vegas, etc. Pet effect: Impaled, which he was the first to do commercially. [Wat] Kalish, Charles "Charlie" [pronounced KAY-lish] (USA: -Mar 1982) Engineer in New York City. Prominent amateur card worker, specializing in gambling fakes. Made clever props (now collectors items). In 1971 bought for $30,000 what was left of the delapidated Circus Museum collection of antique magic apparatus & memorabilia, distributing it among several collectors, including Albright, Ellenbogen, & Klosterman. Wrote lecture notes on Amedeo, Ken Krenzel, Harry Lorayne (1964), Harvey Rosenthal, & Danny Tong. Trick in HMM.

name: Kalma
bio: (USA: 1890-) Stage name of Elmer H. Brunner. Pro vaude illusionist in 1910s. Then owner of camera shop in Florida & semi-pro magician. Pet effects: Floating Ball & the Sawing. [St;HMM11/60]

name: Kalman, William
bio: (Montreal?, Canada: 3 Nov 1905-) Pro close-up magician. Dealer in Montreal, Canada, by 1946 to at least 1951. Wrote Novel Passe Coin Routine and Climax (1947, 11pp mimeo). Tricks in HMM.

name: Kalmar, Bert
bio: (New York City, New York: 16 Feb 1884-17 Sep 1947) Avid amateur magician since age 9. Then pro as a boy magician in tent shows & later vaudeville. Trouted one of Goldin's Sawings in early 1920s. Also "tin pan alley" song writer since teaming in 1923 with composer Harry Ruby (Harry Rubenstein, 1895-1974). They wrote "My Sunny Tennessee" 1921, "Thinking of You" 1927, "Three Little Words" 1930, etc, plus 9 Broadway musicals. Hollywood music executive for films since 1930. Active member of Los Magicos by 1939. In 1941 Kalmar wrote the words & Ruby the music to the International Brotherhood of Magicians's official song, "Here's To The IBM". A movie bio is Three Little Words (1950) starring Fred Astaire (as Kalmar) & Red Skelton (as Ruby). [St;Katz]

name: Kaloofra
bio: See: "Lester, Harry"

name: Kalver, Bruce MIMC
bio: (Providence, RI: 30 Jul 1956 - ) Magician, author, inventor, balloon artist, lecturer. Learned magic from his grandfather, Samuel Woolf, a one time builder for Houdini and Hardeen who helped build the first milk can. Began learning magic at age 5. First performance at age 10. Opened Rhode Island's only magic shop, The Magic Room 1974 - 1984. Composer of songs for musical Moments of Illusion including the song "Have You Ever Wished You Could Float in the Air." (1974). Toured dinner theatres around the USA with his wife in 1977-78. Worked cruise ships out of Miami, FI 1982 - 1984. Host of radio talk show, The Nostalgia Times Radio Programme 1992-2008. Balloon artist (1967 - Present). Worked with Larry White on the creation of the Lizzie Borden Seance at the Borden Home in Fall River, MA. 1992 AIMC with Silver Star. President of The Society of American Magicians (2008-2009). Invented: Coin Chase (1976), Close-Up Linking Ring Bracelets (1979), Faxual Thoughts (1998), Incredible Shrinking and Growing Head Illusion (2000), Ring on Brandy Snifter (2000), Polly Learns a Card Trick (2002), Meal or No Meal (2008), Knock Knock Flea Circus (2010). With his grandfather, created The Samuel Woolf Code (1968, 2000). Wrote Professional Portfolio for Balloon Artists (1999), Restaurant Portfolio (2001), Birthday Party Portfolio (2002), The Lizzie Borden Séance Portfolio (2003). Editor of the SYM's The Magic SYMbol (2002 - 2006). Filmed Airnimations Balloon Videos/DVD's (1997-2004), The Himber Ring Video/DVD (2000). Creator of SAMtalk - The Internet Newsgroup for the S.A.M (2000).

name: Kam, Curtis
bio: (USA: c1960-) Learned magic in early teens. Semi-pro to pro close-up in restaurants in New Haven & Hawaii where he became resident magus at Waikiki's Hale Koa Hotel. Wrote All the World's a Stage (1982, 54pp) & Professional Close-up (1996, 110pp). Tricks in Apocalypse, etc. [Lo2]

name: Kam, Lawrence
bio: (Honolulu, Hawaii: 4 May 1914- ) Semi-pro club magician with sleights & illusions as "Kam the Conjuror". Invented the Plunger Rising Cards & published in 1931 (2 years before Lance Charles claimed it). Tricks in Sphinx. [WWM;HMM1/56,p.384]

name: Kamiguchi, Ryusei
bio: (Chiba, Japan: 2 Jan 1969 - ) Stage name of Kamiguchi Shin-ichi. Inspired in 1975. Pro since 1986. working both Japanese Wazuma and western style including stage illusion and close-up. Learned from Haruo Shimada and Syoyo Murakami. Pet effect: Butterfly Trick.

name: Kamo
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1946-) Stage name of Kazimierz Perkowski. Pro illusionist & manipulator. 1982 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix. [Mec]

name: Kańdzia, Andrzej
bio: (Katowice, Poland: 1961- ) Prize-winning pro illusionist & manipulator. [Mec]

name: Kane, Nat D.
bio: (USA: -1955) Operated a music studio at 171 West 71st Street in New York City, a popular meeting place for local magi in the early 1940s-50s. Semi-pro. Gave lessons in sleight-of-hand at his studio. Trick in HMM.

name: Kane, Peter
bio: (Britain: ca.1939-18 Mar 2004) Cardman. Invented Watch the Aces! = Wild Card (Apr 1962) & Jazz Aces (by 1971). Wrote several booklets including A Card Session with Peter Kane (1967, 21pp), Another Card Session with Peter Kane [1971], A Further Card Session with Peter Kane (1975), Combined Card Sessions (1982, 69pp), & Kane's Variant (1996, 11pp). 2 audios. See Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), The Very Best of Peter Kane (1984, in French). Tricks in Epoptica. [Wat]

name: Kanter, [Mitchell] "Mike
bio: (USA: -died in 1960s) Pro dealer in Philadelphia since 1930, initially mail order, then since 1932 running a large retail store ("Kanter's Magic Shop") that issued big catalogs. Bill Brema was shop assistant 1943-45. Major collector of magicians photos. In 1962 retired & sold his shop to Lee Grey & Ed Voorhees. Wrote "Kanter's Komments" column in Genii in late 1930s-40s.

name: Kaplan, George G[ilbert]
bio: (USA: 1902-2001) Inspired c1914 seeing The Great Leon show. Accountant (CPA) in New York City. Amateur magician. Joined the SAM Parent Assembly #1 in 1928 and named its Dean on his 93rd birthday in 1995 when he was still active in magic. Invented The Bombay Mystery card trick (1944). Tricks in Hugard's Magic Monthly 1944-53. Wrote The Fine Art of Magic (1948, 341pp; with a 1955 French tr). [Th]

name: Kaplans, Konstantin Josefovich
bio: (Russia: 1906-) Pro illusionist & sleight-of-hand-man. ..... [Mec]

name: Kappelmacher, Johan
bio: (Austria: fl.1930s-40s) Chemist. Amateur magician. Member of the Vienna Magic Circle. By 1949 had moved to Buenos Aires where as "Juan Kappelmacher" he invented plastic props. [Bam,p271]

name: Kaps, Fred
bio: (Rotterdam, Holland: 8 Jun 1926-22 Jul 1980) Stage name of Abraham "Bram" Pieter Adrianus Bongers. Inspired as child. Aka "Mystica" at start of career until Dec 1950 when he became "Fred Kaps". Student of Henk Vermeyden. Top-line pro close-up and stage magician. FISM Grand Prix 1950 (as "Mystica"), 1955, 1961, making him the only 3-time winner of magic's most prestigious competition award. Toured all Europe in 1955 & USA in 1956. Called "World's Greatest Magician" in 1972 by George Anderson, a widely shared opinion. 1980 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Died of cancer. See Mad Magic #31 (1981) for all-Kaps issue; & Freddie Jelsma, Fred Kaps (1988). Tricks in Arcane (USA), etc. Audio, video "Kaps on Coins" (with 11pp booklet of same title). [Win]

name: Kaps, Warren J.
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: fl. since 1950s) Raised in Jersey City where he was taught by Leslie Geust. Yale-trained lawyer. Assitant at Chang's stage show visit in Brooklyn in 1953. After military service in private law practice in New Jersey & New York since 1976. President SAM 2001-2002. Tricks in MUM. Kara, Madame [MUM7/2001;MUM1/84] (England: fl.1880s) Stage name of Isabella English, Mrs William "D'Alvini" Peppercorn (see). Pro. [CI]

name: Kara, Paul
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Vaudeville mindreader, billed as "Kara—The Man With the X-ray Mind". Wrote Karaism manuscript. [HMM7/58]

name: Karachi
bio: (England: fl.1930s) Stage name of Arthur Claud Darby. Indian act. In 1934 (or 1924?) staged an open-air version of the Indian Rope Trick (with his son "Kyder" as assistant) in England for the International Metaphysical Institute. [Dif]

name: Kardani
bio: (Durban, South Africa: 12 Oct 1913-15 Jul 1995) Stage name of Sheik Dada Kader, of Indian extraction. Inspired at age 8 by street magician Jaffer Khan. Pro since 1933, originally as "Mysterious Dada", then since 1935 as "Kardani" & "The Great Kardani". Four world tours. Dealer in Johannesburg from 1936 until retired c1976, passing business to son, "Kardani Jr". Wrote Kardani's Ten Card Miracles (1950; repr 1970) & Magic Illusions and Magicians (1983, 92pp). Articles in Dragon, Magigram, & Linking Ring. [Bo#210;Wh2]

name: Kardani Jr
bio: (South Africa: fl.1970s-90s) Stage name of Adam Kader. Took over as sales manager of his father's magic shop c1976, operating it as "Kardani Jr Magic Studio".

name: Kardec, Allan
bio: (Lyon, France: 30 Oct 1804-30 Mar 1869) Pen name of Léon-Hippolyte Denizart-Rivail. Pioneer advocate of Spiritualism (which he termed spiritisme) in France. Wrote Le livre des esprits (1857) & Le livre des médiums (1861), both bestsellers (200,000 copies in France) with translations throughout the world. Founded journal La Revue Spirite in 1858. [Dif] “Kardeen, The Great” SEE: Becker, Herbert L.

name: Kardoma
bio: (Bradford, England: 29 Sep 1891-c1959) Stage name of Leonard Crompton Clifford. Pro as "The Boy Magician" c1911-13. Did a patriotic flag act in 1942. Worked until the 1950s. Specialty: silk productions.

name: Kardwell, Joseph "Joe
bio: (New York City, New York: 28 Dec 1935-) Learned at age 15 from tricks bought at local magic shops. Pro stage act as "The Kardwells" 1953-72. Since 1972 advertising agency president on Long Island & co-president of a division (Kardwell International Inc) that sells playing cards to casinos, private clubs, & magi. Semi-pro magician with cards & doves as "Kardwell". In 1974 co-founded Magic Magazine, selling his interest in 1975. [Wh2]

name: Kardyro, Tony
bio: (Teano, Italy: 23 Sep 1908-30 Jan 1994) Stage name of Anthony Thomas "Tony" Barbato since 1930. Moved to USA at age 3. Learned at age 10 from two 25¢ books: Thurston on cards & Downs on coins. Around 1932 married Faye Barbato (born c1913) who then became his lifelong assistant. Pro card & coin close-up since c1933 as "Tony London" & "Tony Kardyo", adding stage magic dove act in 1940 as "Señor Torino, the Continental Deceptionist". In 1984 a stroke forced his retirement. Invented the dove bag(1) & Flash Cig-O-Silk (1956). Wrote 15 books, including Your Deck—Your Card (1948, 20pp, edited by Harold Robinson), Dovetail Deceptions (1955, 26pp), & Kardyro's Kard Konjuring (1955, 34pp). Trick in HMM. Autobio is Magical Highway (1988). [NJ#4;Wh2]

name: Karger, George
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Pro magazine photographer &, later, antique dealer in New York City. Amateur magician. Member SAM 1940-41 when expelled for exposing (in a LIFE magazine article), the first such expulsion by the SAM (the 2nd being in 1994). Photographer for Tannen's original Stars of Magic series. Contributor to Conjurors' Magazine. Collector of magic books, which he sold c1953 to John Brown Cook & John J. McManus. [Th]

name: Karges, Craig [J.]
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro mentalist. 1989 PEA Mentalist of the Year. Works college & cruise ship shows. Wrote The Craig Karges Connection: Mentalism with You in Mind (1989, 52pp). TV bits. "Karland, The Great" SEE: Frischkorn, Dr Carl S.

name: Karlini
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 1907-1963) Stage name of Ludwig Trinka. Pro illusionist. Founded the Prague "Tesla" Illusion Club. Toured Poland. [Mec]

name: Karlyn
bio: See: Burrows, J.F.

name: Karmelini
bio: See: "Carmelini"

name: Kar-Mi
bio: (USA: 1872-c1957) Stage name of Joseph B[ryant] Hallworth (or Hollingsworth) since 1916, previously as "Vanoran" & "Joe Van Victorina". Pro illusionist based in Malden, Massachusetts who toured with a 15-minute vaude act. Featured effects: "Selma" and "Swallows a Loaded Gun Barrel and Shoots a Cracker from a Man's Head", both being his inventions. [Jay;Rey]

name: Karmilovich, Ted
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Semi-pro mentalist on East Coast as "Ted St. James". Also in 1980s as "Mickey Maven" did a comedy take-off of Max Maven's act. Invented "Mother of All Book Tests". Video bit (1988). (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of C.H.H. Walter. Minor pro. [Bur]

name: Karo
bio: See: Kaldy, Robert

name: Karr, Todd
bio: (Southfield, Michigan: 1965-) Inspired by & learned from gift of magic trick from grandmother. Amateur magician & collector of magic magazines. Beginning at age 12, editor of Periodical for Collecting Conjurors 1977-79 (15 issues). Also edited, as "John Print", Fool's Fooler 1978 (2 issues, made for Bob Lund). Edited-published Magician's Gallery (1981). Chavez College student in 1989. Part-time writer for a Los Angeles newspaper. Advisor on French TV series "Attention Magie" (1992-93). Associate-editor Magic (1992-94). Wrote Backyard Magic (1996, 32pp). Article in 1996 Linking Ring. [Se;Wh01]

name: Karro
bio: (Russia: 1888-) Stage name of Stanislav Adolfovich Mineiko. Pro in Russian circus. [Mec] Karson, Joseph A. "Joe" (Providence, Rhode Island: 12 Nov 1912-dead) Stage name of Josef A. Chrzanowacki, of Polish descent. Inspired at age 10 seeing a Chinese magician. Pro with travelling burlesque show (Girl in the Pumpkin static illusion) & club worker. Then retail dealer-prop maker ("Karson's Xclusives") in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1940s. Invented Rapid Flight Cards (by 1940), Slicko suspended tumbler (1940), Zombie (1943), Phantasia (by 1947), Fastest Card Trick (1948), Miracle Ball (1959), & No Feet. Wrote booklets Complete Club Act (1934), Karson's Miniature Mysteries (1934, 18pp), Sensational Poison Swallowing Act (1934), Illusion Magic, Hypno Tricks (1940, 22pp), Tips on Zombie (1946, 11pp), Illusion Secrets (by 1947); Further Tips on Zombie (1963, 58pp), etc. Tricks in Sphinx & MUM. [Th;Albo95]

name: Karston, Joe
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Pro stage magus. Invented The Jack-O-Lantern Girl (by 1936) & Battle of the Toy Soldiers (by 1936). His pet publicity effect was the nested Prediction Chest invented for him by Carl Owen.

name: Karta, Jack
bio: See: Iversen, Tommy

name: Karton
bio: See: Pozzi, Piero

name: Kaschi
bio: (Germany?: 28 Jan 1925-) Stage name of Karl-Heinz Mangels. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Kasfikis, Kostan
bio: (Russia: 1892-1934) After Russian Revolution (1917) travelled on Greek passport. Pro illusionist, touring Europe with a big show with many assistants. His assistant until 1929 was "Kleo Dorotti" (which see). Pet effect: the Buzz-Saw. Killed in a one-car auto crash in Spain when his crated Buzz-Saw slid forward and crushed his head. His Russian-born widow continued the act. [Bam,pp182-3;St;Mec] (USSR: fl.1940s) Pro illusionist in Soviet circus. [Dif]

name: Kasfikis, Valeria
bio: (Russia: fl.1930s-50s) Born Valeria Cherni (?). Pro assistant-wife of Anastasios Kasfikis. Widowed in 1934, she continued his act, but initially as an all-girl illusion show, first briefly as "Valeria", then since later that year as "Cleopatra", touring Europe, S. America (including the Avenida Theatre in Buenos Aires in 1947), Puerto Rico (1952), & the USA. Played the NY Palace in 1952 (with 2 women & 1 boy assistants), 1953 (2 assistants), & 1955 (with 1 male & 1 female assistants). Played the Vienna Ronacher in 1958. Retired in the USA. Milbourne Christopher recalled (in 1973) that "She was the best female illusionist I have ever seen." [HMM9/52,12/53,9/55] (Tunis, Tunisia: 28 Sep 1932- ) Stage name of Abdel Majid Kassaadji, of Turkish descent. Pro illusion & pick-pocket act. Moved to France in 1956. Toured Portugal 1960 & 1966. Starred at Cabinet Fantastique 1970. Kassagi, Henry Wrote 2 booklets in French: Devenez magicien (1966) & La magie pour tous (1973). TV bits. [Win;Dif;Cam]

name: Kassner, Alois
bio: (Gross Gohlau, near Breslau, Germany [now Gałow, Poland]: 28 Aug 1887-23 Mar 1970) Learned c1908 as assistant to "Tasco", a minor pro. On own as pro since 1911. In WW I as soldier performed in hospitals. Then during period 1919-30 built the largest show in Germany, based mainly on his purchase of Thorn's big show around 1920 when the latter retired. With 18 assistants & 13 tons of properties toured the best theaters of Germany & Central Europe. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1939. Pet effect: Vanishing Elephant, which he featured from 1929 or 1930 to 1940. After WW II, stuck in East Germany, he toured a smaller show. Played Switzerland in 1952. In 1953 moved to West Berlin where following his farewell performance (at the Friedrichstadtpalast) in 1954 [sic] retired & later died. [Pr;Win;St]

name: Kassner, Erna
bio: (Germany: -18 Jan 1966) Born Erna Stänicke. Pro assistant to husband Alois Kassner. Their two daughters, Elvira & Helma, also served among Kassner's 18 assistants before WW II. [Win;Mül]

name: Kastrozza, Prof. San Martino de
bio: (Werro, Latvia, Russian Empire: 31 Mar 1877-21 [sic] Jun 1946) Stage name of Julius Skrastin (NOT Skrastni). Son of a dyer. Began in circus. Pro society magician. In 1900 played St. Petersburg & was made Professor & Court Conjuror to Nicholas II. Toured Russia, Persia, & Spain until the 1917 Revolution after which he toured Finland, Holland, & Germany. His assistant, Arabella, did paper-folding. Died in Braunau, Austria. [Win;St]

name: Katakura, Yuichi
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Pro card magician. Manager of Tricks Magic Sales Company, Ltd, in Tokyo, one of 3 largest dealerships in Japan.

name: Katawü
bio: (Montallegro, Italy: 10 Mar 1924-) Stage name of Salvatore Impiduglia. 1973 FISM 1st prize for illusion; 1976 FISM 3rd prize for illusion.

name: Kater, James
bio: See: Thompson, James Cater

name: Katlyn
bio: See: Miller, Katlyn

name: Kato, Hideo
bio: (Shimoochiai, Tokyo, Japan: 6 May 1943-) Learned in 1956 when found a Tenyo branch in a department store. Cardman. Pro inventor since 1963 with Tenyo Company in Tokyo. Invented Card Happening (1969), Wandering Hole (1979) or 1980), GeomeTrick (1988), Mind Scanner (1991), etc. Pet effect: Card Happening. Dubbed "Mr Computer" by Dai Vernon. Also directs Tenyo's shop at Leisure Island. Tenkai Prize 1991. Translated The Tarbell Course in Magic into Japanese 1975-81 in 7 vols. Wrote the 600-page Card Magic Kenkyu [Study of Card Magic]. Tricks in Genii, Talisman, & Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]

name: Katterfelto, Gustavus
bio: (Germany: 1730-25 Nov 1799) Stage name of Gustav Katerfeld. Pro. Moved to London in 1781. Noted for bombastic ads. [Daw;Daw#152;Fr;Cl;Hou]

name: Kattner, Wilbur T[rue] "Will
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 13 Sep 1917-20 Aug 1998) Inspired at age 5 seeing S.S. Henry in Chautauqua. Learned from a gift magic set. Teacher in Richmond, Washington. Amateur magician since 1931 & as "Howard Holden" 1932-34. Reinvented Think! Ink! (c1941). IBM Gold Medal for "Climax!" (with torn corner, 1945). Also originated "The Shattering Flask", "Prognostication", & "Houdini Escapes". Column ("Future Magic") in Linking Ring in 1940s. Wrote 5 booklets, including You're On! (1944, 22pp), Off the Beaten Path (1947, 24pp), & Destiny & Beyond (1990, 30pp). TAOM President 1967-68. Minor dealer in Fort Worth, Texas, publishing Small Magic Talk from Texas as house organ since 1977. Tricks in Sphinx, HMM, Phoenix, LR. [Th;WWM;Wh2]

name: Katz, Max
bio: See: "Malini, Max"

name: Katzenstein, Dr Hans
bio: See: Kayton, Dr Howard B.

name: Kaufman, Gerald L [ynton]
bio: (New York City, NY: 12 Mar 1893-27 Apr 1968) Learned in 1908 at Martinka's magic shop. Did Needle Trick since 1912. Architect in New York City. Amateur magician. Aka "G. Lawson Kendall". Worked a 2-person mindreading act with his wife. Wrote Murder by Magic (1933, a mystery novel). It's About Time (1935, 168pp). How's Tricks? (1938, 133pp). The Book of Modern Puzzles (1940; 2nd rev ed 1954, 188pp), & Kaufman's Kwik Kard Kodes (1958, 11pp). Articles in Magic Cauldron, etc. Illustrations for Sphinx. [Th;SAM;WWM] Kaufman, Richard [Jeffrey] "Richie" "Moo Moo" (Queens, New York City, NY: 16 May 1958-) Inspired at age 5 by uncle's gift of some S.S. Adams novelties. Learned around age 8 from a Gilbert "James Bond" magic set & father's gift of magic shop tricks. Noted illustrator of magic books since age 16. Founded, published, & co-edited Lorayne's Apocalypse 1978. Publisher (with Alan Greenberg) as "Kaufman and Greenberg" 1979-97, thence alone as "Kaufman & Co." Editor-publisher of Richard's Almanac 1982-87. Columns in Magic Manuscript 1982-84, Genii 1987-1989, Opus 1990-present. Since 1988 has built "world's largest collection of A.C. Gilbert Mysto magic sets". 1995 Christopher Award. Editor-publisher of Genii since Jan 1999. Prolific author. Wrote (& published as "Kaufman & Greenberg") The Interlocked Production of Coins (1977), Balls! Lessons in Side-Arm Snookery (1977), On the Up and Up (1978), CardMagic (1979, 183pp; French tr 1983 by Vollmer), The Gene Maze Card Book (1980), CardWorks (1981), CoinMagic (1981, 266pp), The Complete Works of Derek Dingle (1982, 219pp), David Roth's Expert Coin Magic (1985, 370pp), Sankey Panky (1986), The Uncanny Scot: Ron Wilson (1987), New Magic of Japan (1988, with Phil Goldstein), Sawa's Library of Magic (Vol One, 1988, 179pp), The Secrets of Brother John Hamman (1989, 252pp), Williamson's Wonders (1989, 96pp), 100% Sankey (1990, 86pp), Gary Kurtz: Unexplainable Acts (1990, 101pp), Tom Mullica Starring in Show-Time at the Tom-Foolery (1992, 220pp). Articles in A-B-C of Magic Sets, Magic, etc. Video segment (1986); video (1989). [Bo#291;Wh2]

name: Kaufmann, Adi
bio: (Germany: 4 Jul 1916-) Magician. 1983 MZvD Writer of the Year. [Nad]

name: Kaufmann, Johann Gottfried
bio: (Germany: 1751-1818) Mechanic. Maker of automata. Father of Friedrich Kaufmann (1785-1866). The two made a fine trumpet player c1810. [St]

name: Kawecki, Walentyn
bio: (Russia?: 1889-1942) Stage name of Walentyn Konstantynowicz Glejzarow. Aka "Wijczenko". Pro illusionist, transformist, & dramatic actor in Poland since 1909 with assistant-wife Klaudia Grigoriewna Glejzarowa. [Mec]

name: Kawero
bio: (Germany?: 14 Dec 1940-) Stage name of Klaus Wernicke. 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in closeup. [Nad]

name: Kaye, Harry [J.]
bio: (Brighthouse, Yorkshire, England: 27 Apr 1896-21 Dec 1951) Pro in 1920s-30s. In 1930 became first editor of The Budget. Later a businessman & semi-pro magician. British Ring Past President. Collector of magic books. His collection passed to Lloyd Jones. [Go2;St;WWM]

name: Kaye, Marvin [Nathan]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 10 Mar 1938-) Inspired by and learned from an A.C. Gilbert magic set. Writer. Also semi-pro comedy & kid-show magician as "Count Emkay". Wrote The Stein and Day Handbook of Magic (1973, 310pp; reprinted in England as The Complete Magician, 1974, 252pp; reprinted in the US as The Creative Magician's Handbook, 2001, 310pp), The Stein and Day Handbook of Mental Magic (1975, 324pp), & Catalog of Magic (1977, 279pp). Also wrote several mystery stories (since 1971), some involving magic. [CA]

name: Kayton, Dr Howard B., MD
bio: (Bielefeld, Germany: 26 Nov 1890-26 Mar 1952) Born Hans Katzenstein. Learned magic in early youth. Physician in Munich. Amateur magician specialized in sleight-of-hand & fakir tricks. Articles in Magie. Moved to USA in 1939 as refugee from Nazism & changed name to Kayton. Physician in Bellrose, New York. Sold his large magic collection in 1949 to John McManus. Invented The Bewitched Paper (pre-1934, using rubber cement), Ghost Writer (also with rubber cement), & Soft Soap (1941). [Th;WWM;HMM/3/50]

name: Kazam, Ali
bio: (Mexico: 1965-) Stage name of Luis Roberto Rivas. Closeup. [Ran]

name: Keable-Elliott, Ian, MIMC
bio: (England: fl.1980s) Co-founded & edited 1st volume of OPUS magazine 1987. MIMC 1988. TV bit. Co-authored (with Cheryl Evans) The Usborne Complete Book of Magic (1989, 64pp).

name: Keane, J. Warren
bio: (USA: c1879-30 Mar 1945) A world-class cardman & billiard-ball manipulator. Moved from California to the East Coast in 1903. Popular pro vaude magician. Played the Boston Keith's in 1908, etc. Voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Keene". [Ho;Mo]

name: Keating, [Frederic Serrano] "Fred
bio: (New York City: 27 Mar 1897 [sic]-29 Jun 1961) Debut as magician c1915. In short film Illusions (1929). Pro suave comedy magician. Pet effect: Vanishing Birdcage. In New York played the Palace 1929 (2 weeks) & 1930 (twice) and the Capitol Theatre in 1931. Made first "final" pro appearance as magician in July 1932, heading the last straight vaudeville bill at the New York Palace. Declared bankruptcy in 1932. To help, Tallulah Bankhead hired him in 1933 as her leading man in her play Forsaking All Others. Hollywood film actor 1934-40. Hosted "The Fred Keating Show", a syndicated 30-minute radio variety series, in 1940. Later emceed some charity magic shows. Attempted suicide in 1948. His return to pro magic in 1951-53 worked only slightly better than his one-shot return to the stage in 1954 (in Dear Charles), again under the angelic wings of Miss Bankhead). Died of heart attack. NOTE: His official bio sheets gave year of birth falsely as "1902". [Pr;Ch;St;Ho;WWM]

name: Kebby, Michel
bio: (Bristol, England: 1 Aug 1915-) Semi-pro. [Go2]

name: Keck, Manfred
bio: (Germany: 4 Oct 1883-27 Jul 1963) Veterinarian in Stuttgart. Amateur magician noted for fine sleight-of-hand card work. Member of MZvD. Died in Stuttgart.

name: Keech, Cecil
bio: (Britain: -Sep 1961) Moved to Australia in 1909 to become a pro magician and, later, mind-reader. Expert diabolo juggler. Managed the New York Novelty Co in Sydney 1911-?. Owned his own shop in Sydney 1918-20. Managed magic department in the David Jones Department Store in Sydney in early 1930s, selling his personally made card tricks under his brand name of "Seekay". Invented the Kuller Pack (marketed in USA in 1948 by Abbott's). [McC;Wal;Pr] Keel, John A. (Hornell, New York: 1930-) Pen name of Alva John Kiehle. Amateur magician as young boy; then, since age 14, a pro writer & journalist. Memoir of mid-1950s trip to Egypt, Iraq, & India and meeting magicians there is Jadoo (1955). [CA] Keen the Magician

name: Keene
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Pro magician in medicine shows. Taught his assistant, Eddie Clever, 1920-24. (USA: c1870-28 Jan 1928) Stage name of John P. Culbertson. Toured with The Baldwins, giving the magic in their act. Later toured his own show with 9 assistants & a special car thru the Eastern & Southern USA. A close friend of Kellar. Retired c1913 to Carlisle, Pennsylvania, where he ran a printing shop & owned an amusement park.

name: Keene, Robertson
bio: See: "Robertson-Keene"

name: Keith, B[enjamin] F[ranklin]
bio: (Hillsboro Bridge, New Hampshire: 26 Jan 1846-26 Mar 1914) Circus impresario until switched to theater in 1883 when he opened the 1st vaudeville house in the USA, the Gaiety Museum, in Boston. Owned or controlled nearly 1,500 theaters throughout the USA & Canada at time of his death (in Palm Beach) when management passed to his chief aide, E.F. Albee. [Lau]

name: Kellar, Harry
bio: (Erie, Pennsylvania: 11 Jul 1849-10 Mar 1922) Stage name of Henry [reportedly born Heinrich] "Harry" Keller since 1878. Son of German immigrants. A Mason. Learned at age 11 assisting the Fakir of Ava. Solo debut at age 16. Toured USA with Davenport Brothers 1869-73 and Central & South America with W.M. Fay 1873-75. Thence as star of own illusion show with two world tours 1875-78 & 1879-84 before limiting work to USA. Named 1st Dean of American magicians in 1907. Retired in 1908, naming Howard Thurston his successor. Given farewell benefit at the New York Hippodrome in 1917. Probably invented Coffee and Milk (by 1876), invented Kellar Rope Tie (by 1878), the 2nd (non-Maskelyne) Levitation of Princess Karnac (with Paul Valadon, 1904), Golliwog Ball (by 1903). His exaggerated memoir is A Magician's Tour: Up and Down and Round About the Earth (1886 214pp). Bio is Tom Ewing, Kellar's Egyptian Hall: The Story of America's Premier Temple of Illusion (1990, 48pp). NOTE: John Booth's 1990 claim that Kellar's ashes were stolen from Rosedale Cemetery is plausibly denied by them. [Ch;Pr;Wal;Gi;Mo;Bo3;Magic4/04,3/07]

name: Keller, Cy[ril A.]
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 14 Oct 1927-) Learned at 10 from library books. Lessons from Ernest Marx. Banker in home town. Semi-pro close-up & stand-up magician. Pets effects: 3-Card Monte, Card to Wallet, & all Vernon effects. Tricks in Hugard's Magic Monthly, Phoenix, & MUM. Played the Magic Castle & Oprah Winfrey Show. [Wh5] Keller, Don [not a nickname] [R.] (Phoenix, Arizona: 11 Aug 1946-) Learned at age 8 from father. Pro since 1963, initially with Santa's Workshop in Colorado. In US Air Force 1967-71 where continued to perform. In Vegas 4 months in 1972 working in a magic shop. Then cruise ships in 1972. Moved permanently to Hollywood c1975. [Wh]

name: Keller, Harry
bio: See: Warnecke, Bruno

name: Kellerhof, Alfred
bio: (Siegburg, Germany: 10 Jan 1928-) Magic dealer with big selection of books in Bonn since the mid-1950s. Published Der Zaubertrichter as house organ 1956-57. [Roh] Kelley, Justin A. "Jess" (Boston, Massachusetts: 27 May 1882-29 Jan 1948) Pro in Boston, often in clown costume. [St]

name: Kellmann, Oscar
bio: See: "Hugard, Jean"

name: Kellner, Frantisek
bio: (Grafenschlag, Bohemia [now Czechoslovakia], Austrian-Hungarian Empire: 1875-1930) Resident of Prague. Pro illusionist, touring his own magic theater. Aka "Mister Ilusi". Founded the Kellner dynasty of Czech circus magicians. [Al]

name: Kellock, Harold
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Freelance writer with no background in magic who was commissioned by Bess Houdini to write Houdini: His Life-Story, by Harold Kellock from the Recollections and Documents of Beatrice Houdini (1928, 379pp), first serialized in American Magazine.

name: Kelly, Frank
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Amateur card magician in New York City. Invented Twin Deception, which he published in Phoenix in 1944 as "Double Double" & was later marketed by Tannen's as "Twin Deception". Invented Miracle Match by 1948 & Z-Ray Camera in 1949. NOTE: Wrongly credited with invention of the Kelly Bottom Placement = Ovette Master Move.

name: Kelly, George Marquis
bio: (Muncie, Indiana: 9 Feb 1906-8 Jan 1980) Pro illusionist since graduating high school in Anderson, Indiana, in 1924, as "Marquis the Magician" & "George Marquis". Press agent for Rajah Raboid. Began doing his own Ghost Show in 1941 as "Dr. Marquis". Aka "Dr. Chaos". In 1946 filled in briefly as "Dr. Ogre Banshee". Since 1946 he gradually destroyed his career thru alcholism, although still working by 1976 with wife Willa Levolo who was known as the Hollywood Mistress of E.S.P. [Pr;Walk2]

name: Kelmar
bio: See: Traphagen, William H.

name: Kelvin, Paul
bio: See: Brooke, Ken

name: Kemeny, Dr Desider
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1894-) Lawyer. Amateur magican as student of Conradi & Kassay. [WWM]

name: Kemp, Joseph E.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Magician in Whittier, California. Wrote Emergency Full Evening Show (1949, 21pp).

name: Kempenen, Wolfgang [originally Farkas] von
bio: (Pressburg, Lower Hungary: 23 Jan 1734-26 Mar 1804) Court Counselor of the Exchequer of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in Vienna. In 1769 invented, built, & 1st exhibited his world-famous Automaton Chess Player. In 1783-85 toured Europe: Dresden, Paris, London (1785), & Russia. [Ch;St;Fr]

name: Kempenie
bio: (USA: c.1900-Feb 1991) Stage name of Ermine Kemp. Pro since 1920s, beginning in vaudeville, then touring northwestern USA with full-evening show.

name: Kenfield, Dr Richard C[harles], MD
bio: (Peoria, Illinois: 2 Mar 1936- ) First performed in junior high school. Chavez graduate. Later tutored by Neil Foster. Pro in 1960s. Then a physician. Collector of magic books & antique apparatus. [LR10/84; Genii1/54; Wh5]

name: Kennard, Frank
bio: (England: fl.1890s) Pro sleight-of-hand & shadowgraphy. Invented Twentieth-Century Silks by 1903.

name: Kennaugh, Alan, MIMC
bio: (Workington, England: 29 Feb 1928-25 Oct 1991) Learned at age 9 from magic set. Working as a lighting technician in late school years in local opera house saw & met many magicians. Tutored by Edward Victor in 1945. TV feature writer in London. Semi-pro close-up & comedy stage magician, specialized in card magic. Articles in most major magic journals, starting in 1948 with Conjurors' Magazine & Max Andrews's Magic Magazine. Edited The Budget. Vice President of British Ring. Columnist in Magigram 1967-1991. Wrote & appeared on own TV shows. Companion of Elizabeth Warlock since 1983. [MC12/84; Magigram7/90; Wh5]

name: Kennedy, John
bio: (Washington, DC: 1954- ) Inspired at age 8 when an uncle showed a coin trick. Pro (since age 26) close-up to pro mail-order dealer ("Kennedy Enterprises") in Mission Viejo, later as "John Kennedy Magic" in Irvine, California. Invented Animated Self-Lighting Cigarette in 1983, Little Black Box in 1989, etc. Wrote Lecture Three (1983, 32pp), etc. Video (1995). [Wat]

name: Keno
bio: See: White, George

name: Kent, Georg
bio: (Leignitz, Germany [now Legnica, Poland]: 30 Nov 1901- ) Stage name of Georg Kentsch. A pro acrobat turned illusionist in 1939. After WW II worked in East Germany & toured 15 European countries. Retired in 1976 to live in Alterburg. [Win]

name: Kenton
bio: See: Knepper, Kenton

name: Keops, Fernando
bio: (Italy: fl.1970s-90s) Stage name of Fernando OTERO TORRES. Moved to Mexico. Pro stage magician & cardman in Mexico & USA.

name: Kerndörffer
bio: See: Funke, J. Jacob

name: Kerr, Paul
bio: (Portland, Oregon: 1921- ) Taught at age 5 by amateur cousin. Debut in 1931 with partner Lee Grabel. 1933 PCAM 1st place in Miscellaneous Magic. Pro since 1938 working mainly nightclubs & a few vaude houses. Retired from magic in 1962 to work for government until 1982 when retired from that. [Genii1/90]

name: Kersten, Dr Peter
bio: (Forst, Germany: 27 Aug 1929-Jan 2004) Stage name of Dr Peter Lehmann. Amateur in East Germany until 1973, thence pro, including kid-shows as "Zauberpeter". Toured 30 countries of the world, (including the USA) 1976-80. Had own TV show in East Germany. [Win]

name: Kersten, Peter Heinz
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 27 Aug 1929-) Stage name of Peter Stockhammer. Dentist in Vienna. Semi-pro illusionist as "Dr. Kersten & Co". Pet effects: Costume Trunk, Disembodied Princess, De Kolta Chair, Sympathetic Silks. President, Vienna Magic Club, 1963-89. AMA Award of Merit 1978. Also a popular singer. [Magie10/89;Al;Mec]

name: Kessler, [Alfred] "Fred
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 5 Apr 1876-4 Dec 1949) Stage name of Alfred Kegel. Senior railway official. Semi-pro variety magician for 40 years in Vienna & Germany. A teacher of Oscar Enzfelder in 1943. Died in Vienna. NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Vegel". [Vo57;St;Al]

name: Ketch, Jack
bio: See: Murray, John

name: Ketzelman, José
bio: (Argentina: fl.1940s) Wrote Cartomagia (Buenos Aires: 1946).

name: Keyserlingk, Wolf von
bio: (Germany: 16 Feb 1941- ) Pro. 1978 MZvD 2nd prize in closeup; 1979 FISM 3rd prize in closeup; 1981 MZvD 1st prize in closeup, 1st in card magic, & 3rd in manip; 1981 MZvD Magician of the Year. Tricks in Magie. [Nad]

name: Keyes
bio: (England: fl.1820s) Minor pro. Played Bartholomew Fair in 1828 in partnership with Laine. NOTE: Surname also given as "Keys".

name: Keyes, B. B.
bio: (Sandwich, Massachusetts: 1837-Nov 1895) Lived in Boston. Co-invented (with W.E. Robinson) Astarte in 1889.

name: Khaldah
bio: (Syria: -12 Jan 1939) Moved to USA, performing in New York City since c1900. Semi-pro mystic as expert billet reader & pencil reader, performing at private parties. Once managed by Frances Rockefeller King. Article on him in New York Sunday World (28 Oct 1906). [CMM11/06]

name: Khan, Rajah
bio: See: Harrison, Charles

name: Khan, Roland
bio: (Oxnard, California: "5/8" [check.....] 1929-) Stage name of Roland E. Hill. Movie set designer in Hollywood. Semi-pro stage magician. Pet effect: Bullet Catch. NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Kahn"..... [Wh5]

name: Kharduni
bio: (Britain: fl.1950s) Stage name of Thomas Dickenson. Pro dealer (Kharduni's Magic Shop) in Wallasey, Cheshire, England, in mid-1950s.

name: Kharkov
bio: (England: fl.c.1940s) Stage name of Banks, son of Alfred "Ching Wu" Banks and brother of A. Claude "Cingalee" Banks. Minor pro. Khelm is (Argentina?: c1932-) Of Andalusian-Egyptian parentage. Learned in Argentina as main female assistant (& mistress) of David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg from 1951 to 1956 when left show in Madrid for a woman lover and a brief stint with the latter's gang of Spanish smugglers. She then sought tutoring in small tricks and toured a successful 15-minute club act of magic in the Near East, Italy, & France. Thence married & retired sometime before 1963. [Bam]

name: Ki Ming
bio: See: Platt, John J. "Johnny"

name: Kia [also Khia] Khan Khruse
bio: (India: fl.1810s-20s) Pro in England 1815 to c1828. Invented (or, at least, introduced to Europe) the Needle Trick (c1818). [Daw]

name: Kiang Hoé
bio: See: Perót, Auguste

name: Kieres, Władysław
bio: (Chrzanów, Poland: 1925- ) Taught by Oklahoma. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Wrote Z magia na Ty (1960, 95pp) & a booklet, Magiczny stolik (1963, 8pp). [Mec;Nad]

name: Kiga, Yasuo
bio: (Japan: 16 Jul 1937-) Amateur close-up magician in Tokyo. 1972 Tenkai Prize. Wrote Kiga Yasuo Sakushin-shu [Yasuo Kiga's Creative Works in Magic] (1973).

name: Kikuchi, Yutaka
bio: (Fukuoka, Japan: 4 Aug 1938- ) Learned in 1956. Pro illusionist since 1969. Works as "Shogun Samurai Kikuchi" with a 2-4 assistant dragon act. Often tours this act to foreign conventions. Builder-dealer ("Yutaka Kikuchi Magic Company" in Fukuoka) of stage apparatus for himself & others (including Ren Clark). Makes but did not invent Fickle Fire (by 1988) & Silk to Flame (by 1997). [Des;Wh2]

name: KIM Taek Song
bio: (Kanggye, Korea: 14 Dec 1933-) Pro manip & illusionist since 1961 in North Korea & world tour. 1972 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix. [Win;Dif]

name: Kimar
bio: (Auxerre, Yonne, France: 14 Jun 1895-) Stage name of Henri Guimard[-Chambon]. Theatrical director. Amateur magician. Co-founded Sphinx Sarrois club in 1931. 1933 1st Prix Magicus; 1933 Prix Robert-Houdin; 1936 Prix Roger-Barbaud. Wrote Le Peintre chiffonnier et le Charicaturiste express & Construire, équiper, organiser un théâtre Amateurs. Articles in Journal de la Prestidigitation & Magicien. [Rob1]

name: Kindbom, Sven Eric
bio: (Ystad, Sweden: 23 Apr 1929- ) Taught at age 7 by Hector el Neco. Sales manager. Semi-pro magician since 1946 with illusions & general magic. With assistant as "Carboni & Carbonita". Pet effects: Sub Trunk, Broom Suspension, Girl in Cellophane Bag (which he invented). Wrote chapters in 3 Swedish magic books & column "Magic Mosaic" in Trollkarlen. TV bits in Scandinavia, Germany, Holland, Belgium. [Wh8]

name: King
bio: (Brazil: fl.1950s-60s) Stage name of Nicolas J. Condoyannis. Resident of São Paulo. Pro stage magic. Brazilian Magic Competition 1964 Grand Prix for Invention, 2nd prize for classic magic, & 3rd prize for manip. Edited Tourniquet magazine 1965-66 (3 issues) & the Enciclopédia Mágica (1976).

name: King, [Robert Lawrence] "Bob
bio: (Rochester, New York: 29 Aug 1939-) Learned at age 10 when uncle taught him the French Drop. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 15. Mentors were Mike Skinner & Eddie Fechter. Full-time restaurant magician 1962-74. Accountant in hometown. Runs mail-order, wholesale, & teaching magic shop (Bob King's Magic Studio) in Rochester 1980-present. Lecturer. Invented Shrinker (1984), Mirreversal (1986), Psychictrivia (1987), & New Wave Prediction. Wrote Master Gambling Demo (1988, 17pp), Magician Foolers (1989, 36pp), More Magician Foolers, Opening Night Magic (1995), & Cards to Pocket Plus (1995). Tricks in Linking Ring, Apocalyspe, Richard's Almanac, Pallbearers Review, Precurser, & books by Lorayne. [Lo;Lo2;Wh]

name: King, Carlton
bio: (Britain: 1896-1977) Stage name of William H. Davison. Pro magician in British music halls. Moved to USA in 1930. Worked with assistant-wife "Dot". Trick in Gen (1952).

name: King, David
bio: See: Bamberg, David

name: King, Frances Rockefeller
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-40s) Started in show business as a chorus girl. After a mildly crippling auto accident, she became the main booking agent for the B.F. Keith Circuit & later for NBC. Henceforward always addressed as "Miss King". Booked & managed several prominent magicians & mentalists including Allan Shaw, Nate Leipzig, Dunninger (1919-30), Dai Vernon (1924-35), Cardini, & Khaldah. Married A. Frank Jones, Dunninger's manager & PR man (c1923-40). They retired in the 1940s. [Zo]

name: King, Francis
bio: (Königsberg, East Prussia, Germany [now Kaliningrad, Russia]: 1872-4 Apr 1905) Stage name of Franz Kling. Pro stage magician by 1899. Toured USA & Brazil. Died in a madhouse. [Vo57;CMM7/07]

name: King, Harry
bio: (England: fl.1900s-40s) Moved to USA in 1909. Pro illusionist, playing fairs & amusement parks in USA & Canada. Also did 2-person mental acts, first with Karl George as "The Rajah Brothers", later in Chicago nightclubs & salons with a female partner as "King & Zorita".

name: King, Horace, MIMC
bio: (England: 18 Mar 1906-11 Feb 1985) Pro in London. Combined music & dance in his magic act with his assistant-wife Betty as "A Crinoline Cameo". Then in 1959, as "Korolyov", he did a Russian-costume act, also with Betty. [St;HMM11/59]

name: King, James "Jimmy
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-90s) Became son-in-law of U.F. Grant in 1964. Invented Turkish Turmoil by 1969. Dealer (MAK Magic) in Columbus, Ohio, as successor to U.F. Grant.

name: King, Lionel
bio: (Britain: -1958) Stage name of Lionel Klimsch. Pro music-hall cardman in Britain. Pet effect: Nap Hand. Appeared 8 times before royalty. [Wad]

name: King, Louis
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Pro vaude comedy magic. Teamed with Ziska in the 1910s-20s when they did a burlesque version of Snowstorm in China until Ziska's death in 1926.

name: King, [Paxson McCormick] "Mac
bio: (Hopkinsville, Kentucky: 2 Dec 1959- ) Taught magic 1967-68 by both grandfathers. Pro comedy magician since 1981, working closeup, comedy club stages, & for corporate clients. Pet effects: rope routine, Vanishing Earthworm, Dollar in Telephone, & Vanishing Head in Paper Sack. 1989 Crandall Trophy. Tricks in Magic, etc. Wrote Mac King's Tricks With Your Head (forthcoming 2002). [Wat;Wh2;Wh01]

name: Kingsfield
bio: (England: fl.1580s) Pro in London. Worked Bartholomew Fair in 1582 where he exhibited the well-known decapitation trick, The Decollation of John Baptist, as reported by Reginald Scot.

name: Kingfisher" [pen name]
bio: See: Holland, John

name: Kinson, Jack
bio: (Lancashire, England: 1910-7 Nov 1955) Pro since 1933. Featured mice. After his death, wife Mary toured the act for a time. [Daw2]

name: Kio, Emil
bio: (Moscow, Russia: 11 [sic] Apr [Old Style: 30 Mar] 1894-19 Dec 1965) Stage name of Emil Teodorovich Hirschfeld-Renard since c1920. After 1917 Revolution moved to Germany where he learned magic & performed with the Circus Ciniselli. Returned to USSR in 1921, working in circus side-show. Famous pro circus illusionist since 1932 when he moved his act into the ring. In 1939 named Peoples Artist of the RSFSR. Toured Romania, Britain, Denmark, & Japan. Father of Emil Kio Jr and Igor Kio, the latter taking over the act on his father's death. Kio Jr, Emil Wrote the partly autobiographical Fokus i Fokusniki [Tricks and Tricksters] (Moscow: 1958, 110pp) & Illiuzionisty i Volshebniki (Moscow: 1958), These were 2 of the first three magic books (the other being Vadimov's) published in the Soviet Union. [Win;Ch;Dif;La2] (Ordzhonikidze, USSR: 12 Jul 1938-) Elder son of Emil Kio. Stage name of Emil Emilievich Kio. Learned as apprentice to father Emil Kio since 1961. Pro circus illusionist since 1966 when he took over his father's troupe with partner Eleonora Boleslavovna Prochnizkaya (ex-Bolshoi Ballet). Often toured East Germany. [Ch]

name: Kio, Igor [Emilievich]
bio: (Moscow, USSR: 13 Mar 1944- ) Younger son of Emil Kio from whom he learned at age 5 as apprentice. In 1959 became father's assistant & understudy. Pro circus illusionist on own since 1966. Toured USA with the Moscow State Circus in 1967-68. Played Belgium with the Circus Oscar in 1970. [Ran;Dif;Ch]

name: Kirbye, Professor George W [ashington]
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 29 Jun 1828-8 Jan 1893) Pro magician-vent-equilibrist. Died in Atlanta. Wrote Kirbye's original Second-Sight Mystery and pretended Clairvoyance Exposed (1855, 16pp), Origin and History of Ventriloquism (1861, 64pp), etc. His publicity sketch is Autobiography, or a Sketch of the Life and Adventures of George W. Kirbye (c1861, 32pp), the only known copy being in the Christopher Collection.

name: Kirchner, Charles W. "Chuck
bio: (Lakewood, Ohio: 19 Aug 1942- ) Inspired at age 7 seeing a magician in Cleveland. Learned at age 9. Semi-pro clown magician. Edited New Pips 1957-60. Dealer as founder-owner of Magic City in Paramount (formerly Los Angeles & Long Beach), California, 1974-present, the largest wholesaler of magic apparatus on the West Coast. President of Magic Dealers Association for 6 years. [MUM7/94;Wh2]

name: Kirk, Vic[tor Fredrick]
bio: (Long Beach, California: 16 Sep 1942-30 Dec 2000) Learned at age 9 buying tricks from magic shop. Pro stage magician since c1972, mainly in San Francisco area (where he worked the Magic Cellar), plus much cruise-ship work. Added mentalism with partner-wife Mary after they married c1977. Pet effect: Second Sight. Died of cancer. [Wh]

name: Kirkendall, George W.
bio: (USA:c1932-29 Sep 2001) Specialist in bizarre magick. Dealer-maker in Columbus, Ohio, of magic coins, coin boxes, reels, & other small metal props.

name: Kirkham, Charles [Wesley] "Kirk" "Chuck
bio: (Battle Creek, Michigan: 6 Jul 1926 [sic]-3 Dec 2001) Semi-pro in high school. Served in 11th Airborne in WWII. In 1947 turned pro magician, working that season as assistant to Blackstone. In 1954 bought Will Rock's Harry Thurston props & name and adopted the latter's billing as "Thurston's Mysteries of India". In 1956 assisted Orson Welles in his Las Vegas act & on / Love Lucy TV show. Major collector of illusions, some of which he used in his stage show with assistant-wife Phyllis & their late son, Chris. TV bit on Regis Philbin show. Wrote TV Dove Classics (1959, 32pp). Retired in the 1980s in Las Vegas where he died of Alzheimer's. [LR2/02; Argosy2/62; Wat;Wh]

name: Kirkham, Phyllis
bio: (Shelbyville, Indiana: 18 Mar 1926-1994) Born Phyllis Lines. Learned c1943 as assistant to future husband Charles Kirkham (they married c1948) whom she continued to assist until their retirement in the 1980s in Las Vegas. [Wh]

name: Kirkland, George
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s) Blind. Pro magician. See The Life of George Kirkland, the only Blind Conjuror in the World [c1900].

name: Kirsch, Professor William [C. R.]
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 25 [or 24] Sep 1873-21 Mar 1945) Pro, living in home town. Toured USA (playing every state) & Mexico. Wrote Scientific Magical Experiments (1909, 8pp).

name: Kismet
bio: See: Sunshine, Martin

name: Kissell, Roy
bio: (USA: -1988) Ex-carny. Pro magician & dealer in Detroit, Michigan, originally with Abbott's shop there (by 1952) and then with the Fox Fun'N Magic Shop. Co-wrote (with Cedric Richardson) the "Dusting Off Some Old Ones" cplumn in Tops. Often collaborated with Karrell Fox. A mentor of David Ashton, Mark Tripp, & Al Ulman Jr. [LR2/02]

name: Kitami, Maki
bio: (Hokkaido, Japan: 10 Dec 1940- ) Stage name of Shoku Yoshida. A leading pro stage magician. Works in the Wazuma (traditional Japanese magic) style. Pet effect: Thumb Tie. Was former  $ 9^{th} $ president of Nihon Kijutsu Kyokai [Japanese Professional Magicians Association]. [Wat]

name: Kitchie, Joe
bio: (Japan: fl.1880s) Pro juggler-magician. Toured Australia (1887) & USA (c1888). Probably the same as the "Tom O'Kitchi" who had been a boy assistant to D'Alvini in 1883-86 in South America & the West Indies. [Wal]

name: Kitensai, Sho-ichi
bio: (Japan: Sep 1843 – around 1910) Stage name of Kumetaro Hazumi. Initially Rakugoka (comic teller) in Japanese vaudeville, and then became one of early magicians performing in western style in 1875. He apparently learned from Joseph Vanek while he visited Japan in 1874.

name: Kjeldsen, Georg
bio: (Denmark: 19 Mar 1853-18 Aug 1944) Pro illusionist since 1892. Toured Scandinavia & Russia. [St;Vo58]

name: Klăui, Peter
bio: (Wallisellen, Switzerland: 20 Dec 1947- ) Son of a history professor. Learned magic at age 12 from book. Pro since 1977. Kid-show magic. Also "The Magic Boys" circus act with partner Ernst Rath. [Win;Al]

name: Klamm, R[obert] W[illiam] "Bob
bio: (Kansas City, Kansas: 11 Mar 1930-) Legally blind, he learned magic as a child, thereby making himself popular at parties. Pro kid-show & gospel magician. Pro dealer since 1978 as "Klamm the Magic Man" (and since 1988 as simply "Klamm Magic"), originally with a magic shop in Kansas City, Missouri, & then strictly mail-order in Independence, Missouri. Wrote 6 booklets, including The Magic of God's Word (1984), Buying Magic is Tricky Business (1986), & Comedy 101 (1996, c30pp). [Wh]

name: Klause, Roger [Willis]
bio: (Vivian, Louisiana: 19 Mar 1938 – 30 Aug 2008) Moved to Borger, Texas, at age 5. Inspired at age c17 seeing magic at high school show. Learned from books. Insurance sales rep in Borger. Since late 1950s a close student of Dai Vernon, Charlie Miller, & Faucett Ross. Semi-pro close-up, platform, & stage magician. Wrote In Concert (288pp). 2 videos (1985), video segment (1988). Tricks in Gen, Epilogue, Richard's Almanac, Genii, Magic, Ammar's Encore III, & Magic Menu. See Jay Evans, The Lecture Notes of Roger Klause (1982, 14pp). TV bit. [Gen2/64;Wh]

name: Kleefeld, James W[illiam] "Jim
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 28 Jun 1949- ) Self-taught at age 10 from bought tricks. Educational consultant in Cleveland, Ohio, area. Semi-pro strolling & childrens magician since age 16. Historian & collector (particularly magic-related comic books). Wrote Fantasio 6: The Color Changing Lighter (1982, 64pp, with David Ginn) & The Volunteer Book (1990). Columns in MUM (1979-present) & Laugh-Makers (1984-present). Articles in Apocalypse, Australian Magic Magazine, Focus Focus, New Directions, New Invocation, New Tops, Magical Arts Journal, Magic Manuscript, Mortimer's Magic Magazine, etc. Illustrated several books by David Ginn & David Roper. [MUM2/85;Wh2]

name: Klein, Helmut
bio: (Germany: 11 Jan 19-) 1981 MZvD 1st prize in closeup; 1981 MZvD Closeup Magician of the Year. [Nad]

name: Klein, James M. "Jim
bio: (Watertown, New York: 3 Jun 1947- ) First interested in magic in 1975 when he learned at Fedko School of Magic. Pro since 1978 as "Jim the Magician", "Jimbo the Clown", "Professor Gabriel", & "Magic Santa". With Joe Homcheck's The Magic Shop in central Pennsylvania 1979-87. Started his own American Magic Company in Harrisburg, Pa., 1986-present. Edited Patterman 1981 [sic]-82 (10 issues). Wrote The Magic of Riedel (1988). Editor-publisher Mortimer's Magic Magazine (1989-1993), Magic of the Bible (1989-in progress), & Magician's Home Companion (1994-in progress). [Wh2] Klein, Joseph A. "Joe" (USA: 28 Apr 1865-21 Dec 1928) Founding partner in 1909 with Theo "Okito" Bamberg in the Bamberg Magic and Novelty Company in New York City. SAM Member #295. Edited both Record & National Magic News in 1909 (total of 4 issues) for their shop. The company failed in 1914. [Bam]

name: Kleinman, Benjamin [J.] "Ben
bio: (USA: c1910-13 Oct 1994) A New Yorker. President of International Guild of Prestidigitators since 1961. Co-edited Magic Around the World 1969-72. Articles in Genii.

name: Klepke, Günter
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 19 Jul 1930-) In 1978 took over the late Regina Schmidt's "Zauberkönig" magic shop in West Berlin, which he continues to operate there. [Roh]

name: Kleppini, Engelberto
bio: (Germany: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro handcuff king who toured Germany with circuses. Challenged Houdini in 1902. [Hou]

name: Klimax
bio: See: Powell, Bert

name: Klinckowstroem, Carl Graf von
bio: (Potsdam, Germany: 26 Aug 1884-29 Aug 1969) Member of Society for Psychical Research (London) since 1909. Anti-spiritualist & magic historian. Wrote Yogi-Künste (1922, 32pp) & Die Zauberkunst: Meister, Geschichte, Tricks (1954, 138pp). Articles. [Mül]

name: Kline, [W. Robert] "Bob
bio: (Indiana, Pennsylvania: 17 Mar 1912-26 Jun 2004) Taught the Ash Trick at age 6. Art teacher since 1944. Semi-pro stage magician. Developed his "Klinecraft" line of props, which he marketed as well as doing custom jobs. Pirated Jack Hughes' Visible Coins in Glass in 1947, marketing it as Copenetro. Invented (?) Cardmento (1949). In 1970s worked full-time as magician in a local theme park. Moved in early 1980s to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he continued to build & sell props. Wrote Routines and Tips on the Prize Winning Copenetro (1975). [LR2/90]

name: Klingl, R[udiga Michael]
bio: (Austria: fl.1870s-1910s) Mechanic. Opened magic shop (Zauber-Klingl) in Vienna in Sep 1876, making & selling superb props. Later absorbed Carl Husa's local "Zauberkönig" shop. Klingl's catalog listed several Hofziner inventions. Father of Siegmund Klingl. Klingl props are now highly prized by collectors. [St;Dif]

name: Klingl, S[iegmund]
bio: (Austria: 1878-1 Aug 1951) Son of Michael & Rosa Klingl. Pro dealer in Vienna as his father's partner from the 1890s until 1910 when he took over the shop. Carried many of the fine props made by Willi Seidl's factory. Closed during WW II. In 1951 the shop passed to Siegmund's widow, Frederica Klingl, who ran it into the 1980s, although more as a novelty shop. [St]

name: Klingler, Paul J.
bio: (USA: c1930-23 May 1989) Paid debut at age 12. Pro kid-show & magic teacher on East coast as "Paolo the Magic Clown". [Se]

name: Klingsor
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 7 Nov 1929-) Stage name (from the evil magus in Wagner's Parsifal) of Claude Isbecque. Inspired in 1942 seeing a tent-show at a park fairground & learned from father's magic book. Agricultural engineer & semi-pro magician (until 1968). AFAP Master Magician. Since 1957 dealer in Brussels (Klingsor Magic Shop). 1958 Paris AFAP Grand Prix Magicus. Owning most of Kalanag's stage props, which he bought in 1967, he features a Kalanag pastiche act. Also specializes in psychokinetic effects. Full-time pro since 1968. In Paris played the Folies-Bergère & the Olympia. Collector of apparatus (Robert-Houdin's Orange Tree), etc. Chronos, Pythagoras, & Mammoth Rising Cards. Wrote Les tours de cartes montantes (1954), Les grandes illusions américaines (1977), Les Secrets de la mnémotechnie (1983), Magie visuelle pour la scène et la salon (1984), Les Secrets de la magie électronique (1986), & Recollections of Kalanag (1993). Publisher of journals Illusion (1957-60) & Art et Illusion (1960-63). [Dif;Bou;Bou2;Wh2]

name: Klosterman, Ken[neth Fuller]
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 26 Jan 1933-) Learned at age 9 from uncle's gift of a Brema Bill Tube & his Tarbell Course. Briefly a pro with a dove act in his 20s. Then into his family's Mid-West bakery chain, which he now owns, based in Cincinnati. Semi-retired since a heart attack in 1978, working as part-time pro stage magician with assistant-wife as "Ken & Judy" working local cities plus conventions throughout USA. Pet effect: Needle Swallowing. TV magic spot commercials locally 1975-80. Co-founded Venture III magic in 1982, which ran until 1993. IBM President 1995-96. Major collector of magic books (5,000 hardbound & 2,000 softbound), apparatus (6,000 historical pieces from 50 pre-1955 collections), etc, which he exhibits in his "Salon de Magie" in an old mine shaft on his 230-acre farm in Loveland, Ohio. Wrote Rising to Any Occasion (1982, 40pp), a forcing book. Articles in Magic-Gram, Linking Ring, & Apocalypse. Video bit on 1989 MVN #2. [Bo#286;LR7/95;Smithsonian Magazine1/91;Albo95; Wh2]

name: Klox, Jon
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Stage name of John Forrest. Pro with clock act. [Daw2]

name: Klyve, Goran [pronounced KLEW-vay]
bio: (Norrköping, Sweden: 16 Nov 1944- ) Taught by father c1950. Engineer in home town. Amateur mentalist & stage magician. Pet effect: Alpha Mind. Since 1985 works part-time for Harries, which markets his several inventions & designs: Tissel Tassel (1986), Clair-Voyance (1986), Alpha Mind (1987), Dart Prediction (1987), The Horse Race (1988), Mental Vision (1988), & Tilting Candle (1990). [Wh5]

name: Knauss, Friedrich von
bio: (Stuttgart, Germany: 7 Apr 1724-1789) Court mechanic at the courts of Hesse, Austria-Hungary, etc. Maker of automata, working often with his elder brother Ludwig. In 1753 invented the first writing machine. Of the four he built, his finest (1760) is preserved in the Technisches Museum für Industrie und Gewerbe in Vienna. His grand clock, the "Maria-Theresien Uhr" of 1761 is still in the Imperial Palace in Vienna. Other automata are in various European collections. Died in poverty. See Selbstschreibende Wundermaschine auch mehr andre Kunst und Meisterstücke (1789). [Hou,91-92]

name: Knauss, [Johann Philipp] Ludwig
bio: (Austria: 29 Sep 1715-1750) Court clock & automata maker for the Hessian & Austrian courts. Working with his younger brother Friedrich they created the "Ritterspieluhr" in 1750, a fine clock with mechanical knights that is preserved at the Hofburg in Vienna.

name: Knepper, Kenton
bio: (Cedar Rapids, Iowa: 11 Oct 1958- ) Pro with what he calls "linguistic deception, suggestion, symbolism, wizardry". Wrote The Wonder Words books & tapes. 1999 Tony Andruzzi Award. [Wh01]

name: Koch, Hans-Heinrich
bio: (Germany: 18 Jun 1938-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Koch, Paul W. [pronounced COOK]
bio: (USA: c1905-26 Jul 1966) Aka "Kay". Amateur magician in Allentown, Pennsylvania. Major collector of magic magazines. At his death, it was the 2nd largest such collection in the USA & was bought in 1974 by George Daily. Wrote the original "The Magic Chef" column in Magic Cauldron.

name: Kodell, Jack
bio: (Mankato, Minnesota: 4 Nov 1927 – Orlando, Florida: 17 May 2012) Stage name of Jack E. Koudelka. Pro since age 13. Introduced parakeet magic in 1945. Toured 13 countries in Europe, South Asia, & Africa, including such top venues as the London Palladium in 1949. In 1960 retired from pro magic (going into the incentive motivation business), although still a regular at the Round Table in Chicago. Several TV bits. Audio. Retired again in 1997, moving to Orlando, Florida. [Hudd; Genii2/88; Genii5/88; St;Des;Wh2]

name: Kohl, Dick
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 22 Feb 1939-) Stage name of Richard Carroll Kohlhafer. Inspired as child by uncle. Accountant with Westinghouse in Maryland. Semi-pro comedy magician since c1975 as "Kohl & Company" with brother Al Kohlhafer and a third assistant drawn from the family. 1987 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. TV bits in USA, Britain, Germany, Japan, & Chile. [Wh]

name: Kohler, Dr Walter
bio: (Thuringia, Germany: 1899-1984) Physician. Amateur magician. Avid collector of apparatus, much of which he sold to Rudiger Deutsch. His daughter, Julia, is an amateur performer. [Albo94]

name: Kohrs, Charles [Arthur] "Charlie
bio: (Burlington, Iowa: 8 May 1915-1993) Younger brother of Lewis Kohrs. Moved in 1930 to Santa Barbara where he learned magic from Señor Maldo & worked in his magic shop. Salesman in Los Angeles. Semi-pro close-up & stand-up. Worked the close-up room at the Magic Castle 1963-c1983. Also a world-class distant-voice thrower. [Wh]

name: Kohrs, Lewis [Paul]
bio: (Burlington, Iowa: 2 Apr 1911-6 Sep 1982) Inspired as boy seeing T. Nelson Downs. Taught by Eddie McLaughlin. Did street magic in Burlington to draw a tip to advertise an insurance company. Moved to California in 1930. PhD high school librarian until retired in 1976 when he became a pro dealer in second-hand magic books in San Diego, California. His widow sold his fine collection (2,200 volumes) to Byron Walker in 1983. Wrote I'll Bet You Can't: A Choice Collection of Easy Challenge Tricks (1946, 66pp). Hobbies: Akido (black belt), conservation, & classical music. Older brother of Charles Kohrs.

name: Koishi, Parte
bio: (Gifu, Japan: 24 Jun 1952- ) Stage name of Shisei Koishi. Learned at age 18 in university magic club. Pro since 1977. With "Bona" Ueki as comedy magic team of "The Magic Napoleons" & since 1986 as simply "The Napoleons", both male. Invented Barber Chair illusion (1986), etc. 1984 Desert Magic Seminar top style award. 1988 FISM 3rd prize for illusion. Pet effect: "Challenge the Guinness". TV appearances in Japan, USA, & Chile. Husband of Yuka Shimoda. With partner did 1 book (1990) & 2 videos (1990). [Wh2]

name: Kolar, [Joseph J.]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 16 Dec 1883-21 Aug 1949) Pro magician & escapist, billed as "The Great Kolar". Inspired by and learned in family-troupe of vaudeville magi led by his father. Catch-phrase: "Give my regards to the Chief of Police." Father of Betty Jane Kolar. Invented Mystic Rose by 1924, Clippo by 1927, Tu Long Mystery by 1928, Straw and String Trick by 1928, Challenge Tag Trick by 1928, Kolar Card Trick by 1928, Seven Keys to Baldpate by 1931, & the Card Gallows. Wrote Party Magic Stunts. Also "Chats by Kolar" column in Conjurors' Magazine. [Th]

name: Kolar, Betty Jane
bio: (River Forest, Illinois: 9 Jan 1923-) Daughter of J.J. Kolar. Briefly enjoyed spectacular publicity in the early 1930s until suddenly dropped magic. [Ir]

name: Kolb, Fred[erick]
bio: (Jersey City, New Jersey: 13 Jan 1915-11 Mar 1985) Billed as "Master of Mystery". Semi-pro card, mental, & thimble magic for clubs. Wrote Exciting Experiments in E.S.P. (1970, 76pp). Tricks in Genii & Magick. [Go2]

name: Kole, André
bio: (Arizona, USA: 30 Sep 1936-) B.S. in Psychology from Arizona State U. Stage name sine c1956 of Robert John "Bob" Gurtler Jr. A Chavez graduate. Pro gospel & stage magician. 1955 TAOM AI Sharpe Trophy for Originality in Presentation. Invented Table of Death (1954), Spikes thru Balloon (by 1958), Dream Vision (by 1987), Squeeze Box, & Head Mover Illusion designer for Copperfield & others. 1982 AMA Performing Fellowship. Autobio is From Illusion to Reality (1984). Wrote (with Jerry MacGregor, Mind Games: Exposing Today's Psychics, Frauds, and False Spiritual Phenomena (1998, 250pp)). Father of "Tim Kole". [LR4/2003;Ran;Wat;Walk]

name: Kole. Tim
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Stage name of Gurtler. Son of "André Kole". Pro illusionist. In 1987-88 worked with assistant Tamara Fyre as "Fyre & Kole", then with Rhodesia-born Jenny Lynn since their marriage in 1988. Since 1992 with the "Spellbound" show at Holiday Hotel, Las Vegas.

name: Kollmann, Prof. Dr. Artur
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 8 Jan 1858-8 Aug 1941) Physician. Professor at Leipzig U. Amateur magician. Since 1919 lectured on "The Psychology of Magic", publishing "Das Taschenspiel" in Archiv für die gesamte Psychologie, V.80 (1931), 257-264. Articles in Zauberwelt under pen name of "Dr. Avon". Died in Leipzig. Major collector. Donated his Kollmann Collection to the Museum für Völkerkunde in Leipzig (aka "Grassi-Museum"), which was destroyed in WW II during an RAF air bombing on the night of 3/4 Dec 1940. [St;Al;Roh]

name: Kolma
bio: See: Bornstein, Mike

name: Kondo, Hiroshi
bio: (Nagoya, Japan: 1 Feb 1949- ) Learned at age 11 from magic store tricks. Pro inventor with Tenyo Company in Tokyo 1972-present, now director of its development division. Invented Zig-Zag Cig (1981), Midas Machine (1981), Vault-Vision (1988), Diabolicus (1991), etc. 1986 Tenkai Prize. Wrote Creative Works of Shigeru Sugawara (Tokyo: 1978) & Kondo Hiroshi no Hon [The Book of Hiroshi Kondo] (Tokyo: 1987). Article & tricks in Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]

name: Konorah
bio: See: "Berol, Max" Belmonte, Nora

name: Konthur, Rudolf
bio: (Germany: 9 May 1948-) 1979 MZvD 3rd prize in general magic; 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in general magic & 3rd prize in closeup; 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Koornwinder Jr, Dick
bio: (Holland: fl.1970s-80s) Pro pitchman late 1970s-early 1980s, now close-up. Invented Koornwinder Kar (1971). Wrote Dick Koornwinder's Diverting Kreations (1985, 15pp).

name: Kopp, Herr
bio: (Germany: fl.1790s) A skilled pro with the Cups-and-Balls. Known only from the details of his fine routine in the Encyclopaedia Britannica (3rd ed, 1797).

name: Kopp, Martin
bio: (Munich, Germany: 8 Oct 1876-May 1953) Tinsmith in Munich. A pioneer in Bavarian cinema. Amateur magician. Invented many tricks. [St] "Koran the Mind-reader" SEE: Taylor, Perry

name: Koran, Al
bio: (East London, England: 4 Mar 1914-12 Jun 1972) Stage name of Edward Doe. Hairdresser to pro mentalist. Invented The Jonah Card in 1948 & One Word in Thousands in 1954. Based on Stewart James' Ball of Fortune, invented Medallion by 1967. And, adapting a Willmann effect & method, also invented Ring Flite by 1967. Co-authored (with Jack Lamonte) Mastered Amazement (1947, 66pp; repr 1987). Wrote (actually ghosted) Bring Out the Magic in Your Mind (1964). Moved to USA (Chicago) in 1969. See Hugh Miller, Al Koran's Professional Presentations (1967, 131pp; repr 1971); Lecture Notes of Fantastic Koran (1971); Hugh Miller, Al Koran's Legacy (1973, 180pp); & Martin Breese, The Magic of Al Koran (1984, 93pp). Trick in The Wizard. Audio. [La2;Wat]

name: Korbin, Gran
bio: See: "Sager, Faquir"

name: Kordon-Verl
bio: (Graz, Austria: fl.1930s) Stage name of Herr Fridolin. A fake clairvoyant who toured Europe c1930 with his manager, Dr Langer. Exposed as a swindler in Vienna by Ottokar Fischer & Albin Allan and later in Germany by Dr Hellmuth Teumer. [Al]

name: Korem, [Daniel H.] "Dan" "Danny
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: fl.1960s-90s) Learned at age 9 by visiting Top Hat Magic Co. Investigative reporter, TV producer, author. Then, since, 1976 full-time magician, specializing in card magic, closeup, stand-up, & mentalism. Lecturer. Publisher 1981-84 of 4 Racherbaumer books. Wrote Upside-Down Toppit (2 vols, 1978, 1980), Korem without Limits (1985, 181pp), & Powers: Testing the Psychic and the Supernatural (1988). Contributor to Linking Ring. [LR8/94;Wh2]

name: Korengo, Joe
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: c1927-) Stage name of Jozsef Eisinger since 1949. Inspired at age 10 seeing a magician with the Beketof Circus; and self-taught by deducing his moves. Encouraged to become a pro by Rezšō "Rodolfo" Gács. Pro debut in 1949 as a single. Double act as "The Korengos" since 1952 with assistant-wife Irma. Toured East Europe with the Sub Trunk & Sword Cabinet. Fled Hungary in the 1954 uprising, moving to and working in Italy, Canada, & finally, the USA. They played the Ed Sullivan Show (TV) in 1962. [N/#1]

name: Korim, Sir Felix
bio: (USA: 1905-14 Oct 1986) Stage name of Brewerton "Brew" H. Clarke Sr. Sign painter/artist (ex-singer-actor) in Utica, New York. Semi-pro illusionist noted for his accidental stage blunders and failed apparatus. Married his long-time assistant, Clara Decker ("Choai"), in 1941. Did camouflage in USAF in WW II. As a Mason, in 1953 he founded & was first International President of the Invisible Lodge. Wrote Pointers on Good Presentation (1953, 10pp). Tricks in Genii.[Genii8/92]

name: Körling, Knut
bio: (Ystad, Sweden: 21 Aug [sic] 1900-20 Sep [sic] 1988) Aka "Chevalier Shalimar" & "The Baron". Semi-pro stage illusions & general magic with 2 assistants. Wrote Simsalabim (1943, 31pp). [St;Go2]

name: Kornhauser, Mark
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro close-up to nightclub comedy magic. First to make & market Lou Lancaster's Twister. Video segment (1990). [Wat]

name: Kornegay, Doug[las R.]
bio: (Houston, Texas: 21 Jan 1933-) At age 8 inspired seeing school-show magician & getting Xmas gift magic set. Theatrical stage technician. Part-time pro stage magician since c1977. Pet effects: Head Chopper & Life to Death (Head to Skull). 1966 TAOM Willard Trophy for Best Act. Articles in many journals. TAOM Secretary-Treasurer 1967-75. TAOM President 1988-89. [Wh3]

name: Korolyov
bio: See: King, Horace

name: Kort, Milt[on], MIMC
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 13 Oct 1917-1 Aug 2003) Inspired in 1928 seeing vaudeville magician. Learned from Hoffmann's Modern Magic & Harold Sterling in whose magic shop he soon demmoed. Pharmacist in Detroit until retired in 1988. Semi-pro close-up magician. Invented O-korto Coin Box in 1950. Although named as last editor of Hugard's Magic Monthly in 1965, publication ceased before Kort could issue any copies. Wrote Kort is Now in Session (1962, 64pp), Off Color Card Tricks (1970, 55pp), & contributed many tricks to Bobo's Modern Coin Magic. See Stephen Minch, The Magic of Milt Kort (1999, 376pp). Articles in Genii, Pallbearers Review, Swami, Mantra, Precurser, New Pentagram, Psycho-Gizmo, Abra, Gen, Modern Magi, New Phoenix, Epilogue, Cardiste, Kabbala, Ibidem, Epoptica, & Magic and Spells Quarterly. [LR10/97;Wh2]

name: Kosky, Gerald
bio: (Oil City, Pennsylvania: 27 Feb 1907-2 May 1987) Learned at age 14 when his magic-buff father took him to Gamages to buy from Goldston. Costume accessory salesman in Los Angeles. Semi-promagic performer ("Mr. O'So" & "Professor'Iggins") & lecturer. Co-edited (with William Taylor) Pacific Coast Magic News 1935-36 (17 issues). Invented Invisible Card Change (1955) & Astro-Question-Chart (1956). Co-authored (with Arnold Furst) The Magic of Tenkai (1974, 143pp) and wrote The Magic of Gerald Kosky (1975, 247pp). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, HMM, New Phoenix, Ibidem, Genii, Talisman. 1982 AMA Literary Fellowship. [LR3/82; Genii7/49; Th; Mag; SAM]

name: Kostka, Leo [Allan]
bio: (Oakpark, Illinois: 4 Aug 1942- ) Learned at age 10 from father's gift of magic set. Real estate investor. Semi-pro straight magician since age 13. In 1980 turned pro magician, specializing in spirit séance shows. Pet effect: Living & Dead Test using skeleton hand. The Magic Castle's Houdini Séance Room substitute medium 1982-85 & its 3rd (following Sandy Spillman) Resident Medium 1985-present, having performed over 1,000 of these 1-hour séances thru 1989. Also works private parties. Invented Crystal Spirit Bell (1980), Resurrection Card (1980), Poltergeist Cabinet (1982), & The Skeleton Hand Writes (1983). Articles in Magick, New Invocation, Vibrations, & Seance. [Wh2]

name: Kotkin, David
bio: See: "Copperfield, David"

name: Koval, Frank
bio: (Chadderton, Lancs., England: 12 Aug 1941- ) Stage name of Frank Briggs since 1970. Learned at age 10 from father's gift of Scarne's Magic Tricks. Pro since 1991 with mental & general magic. Collector, historian, & lecturer. Wrote Robert Heller: Music and Mystery (1985, 20pp) & The Illustrated Houdini Research Diary (forthcoming in installments beginning 1992). Articles in MUM, Abra, Magiram, New Pentagram, Escapism, Yorkshire Life Magazine (6/84), The Scots Magazine (1/85), Lancashire Magazine (Jan/Feb 85). AIMC 1992. [Wh5]

name: Kovari, George, MIMC
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1939-) Born György Ferenc KOVARI. Inspired at age 10 seeing Potassy & Rodolfo perform in circus. Student of Rezső "Rodolfo" Gács. Moved to Britain at age 18. Pro stage magician since age 20, aka "The Great Kovari" since c1974. Also inventor & dealer (Kovari Magic Productions) in London. Wrote Kovari's Master Magic & Chinese Sticks Routine. Video (1987). Article in Gen. [La2;Wh2]

name: Kowal, Horst
bio: (Germany: 22 Nov 1925-) Magician. Active member of MZvD. [Nad]

name: Kowalski, Ed[mund Lee]
bio: (Perry Hall, Maryland: 20 Mar 1955- ) Interested in magic as long as he can remember. Writer, actor, & stage director in East Lansing, Michigan. Semi-pro mentalist since 1973, working as "Jeremy Greystoke" since c1980. Reviews or articles in Yogi-Gram, New Tops, & Epoptica. [Wh2]

name: Kozak, [Michael Thomas] "Mike
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 1933- ) Inspired at age 12 from Blackstone comic books & seeing the Blackstone show. Floor covering salesman. Amateur close-up magician. Wrote Master Sponge Ball Routine (1973) & Close-up Magic of Kozak (1984 lecture notes). Invented Blushing Card (1981) & Rings of Roberta (1984). [Wh2]

name: Kraft, Frederick [L.]
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Lives in Okala, Florida. Amateur. Wrote (with Arthur Kraft) Coin Magnetrix (1970s, 78pp) & Magneticoins (1970s, 58pp). "Krajak" NOTE: Fictitious magician created by Bob Wagner as a hoax in the Jul 1966 Linking Ring "Parade".

name: Kramien, Stan[ley Richard]
bio: (Portland, Oregon: 9 May 1925 – 27 Mar 2015) Assistant to Warren Gram in 1946-47, touring the Western states. Pro illusionist as "The Great Kramien" since 1949. Mentor of Loren Michaels (c1971). His principal assistant was Kathleen Lison until replaced in 1984 by David Charvet. Toured "Magicazam" illusion show. 1979 Jack Gwynne Trophy. Wrote several booklets. See David Charvet, Kramien: A Pictorial Look at the Life of a Tall Grass Showman (1989). [Mag;Wat;Tay;Wh2]

name: Krams, Larry, AIMC
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 1 Apr 1940- ) Inspired at age 8 by Blackstone show in New York City. Pro since 1957, specializing in comedy stage magic & mentalism. Founded the Magicruise in 1984, which he continues to produce. AIMC 1988. Articles in Genii. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Krass, Nathan
bio: (Odessa, Russia: -22 Nov 1949) Moved to USA by 1899. Rabbi since 1903. Amateur magician. [WWWA]

name: Kratky-Baschik, Anton
bio: (Kozlana, Bohemia [now Kożlany, Czech Republic]: 11 Jan 1821-28 Aug 1889) Stage name (adding grandmother's maiden name) of Anton Kratky by at least as early as 1858. Pro harmonica musician in Prague until learned magic 1850-52 as musical accompanyist to Bellachini (Berlach). Debuted on own in 1854. Began his tour of Britain in 1858 (including a Nov 3rd show at Windsor Castle for Queen Victoria), including Dublin in Feb-Mar 1859. Continued in Britain with the Barnum Circus 1859-60. Toured thru Germany 1860-62. In 1864 moved to Vienna where he operated a magic theater for 7 months that year. Toured Austria, Hungary, & the Balkans 1864-72. Returned to Vienna in 1872 where he operated the Theater der Zauberei from 1873 (during the Vienna World's Fair) until 1875 when he relocated it in a 900-seat magic theater in the Prater park and renamed it the "Kratky-Baschik Zauber Theater". It continued (after his death in that city) under, successively, nephew Mathias Kratky until 1902 and Ottokar Fischer until 1911. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Basnik" in English & French sources. REF: Gerda Barth, "der Hexer von Wien", Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993), 41-49. [Pr;Win;Dif;Vo57;St;Bo#199;Magic3/07,4/07]

name: Krejcik, Petr
bio: See: "Petrick"

name: Krenzel, Ken, PhD
bio: (lower east side Manhattan, New York City, NY: c1926 – 2 February 2012) Inspired at age 7 seeing a magician at school. Learned from library books. Semi-pro in high school & college doing mentalism, originally as "Israel Kren-Zel". Child psychologist (using magic as therapy) in New York City. Semi-pro card, close-up, & mental magician. Invented Telepathic Scrabble (1956). Articles since 1949 in Phoenix, New Phoenix, New Jinx, HMM, Gen, Genii, Hierophant, Epilogue, Richard's Almanac, & Apocalypse. See Harry Lorayne, The Card Classics of Ken Krenzel (1975) and Stephen Minch Ken Krenzel's Close-Up Impact (1990) & Ken Krenzel's Ingenuities (1997, 224pp). Videos (1988; 3 in 1989). [MUM9/93; Lo2; Wh2] Kreskin, The Amazing (West Caldwell, New Jersey: 12 Jan 1935-) Stage name of George Joseph Kresge Jr until legally changed to Kreskin. Aka "Arthur Mazin" & "A. Mazin". Inspired around age 5 reading "Mandrake the Magician" comic book. Learned around age 8 reading books on psychology & hypnotism. Semi-pro ½-hour magic shows since age 9, adding mentalism at age 11. BA degree in psychology from Seaton Hall U in New Jersey. Thence pro mentalist doing a Dunninger-style act. In 1989 again openly used such magic props as Telekinetic Timber in his Houdini Séance at the American Museum of Magic. Reputedly quite wealthy. Misleading autobio is The Amazing World of Kreskin (1973, 209pp). Also authored Fun Way to Mind Expansion (1984, 172pp) & Secrets of the Amazing Kreskin (1991, 166pp), with Robert Bahr). Star of own TV series, "The Amazing World of Kreskin" 1972. [Ch; MUM8/94; CA; HC]

name: Krieger Prof. Louis "Pop
bio: (Germany: 15 Sep 1851-26 Jun 1934) Stage name of Ludwig Krieger. German Jew. Illiterate. Learned magic working in circus. Moved to USA c1885. Pro society magician as the leading Cups-and-Balls operator in the New York area plus a tour of Europe. Joined SAM in 1902 as Member #14. Catch phrase: "Watch the Professor." Featured Aerial Fishing. Was Malini's manager for a time. Father of Willie Krieger & father-in-law of Norma Krieger & Al Flosso (since 1924). [Br,pp9-14;Pr;MUM10/95;Dam;Cl]

name: Krieger, Norma
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Wife of William Krieger. As "Norma" did single act as illusionist. Pet effect: Aerial Fishing.

name: Krieger, William "Willie
