bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) One of 3 sons of Louis "Pop" Krieger. Pro sideshow & vaude magician & puppeteer in New York City. Alcoholic husband of Norma Krieger.

name: Krinog, George
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 19 Sep 1897-1946) Pro since 1919. Moved to USA in 1922. Dealer ("Magic Studio") in New York City since 1923. Act with cards, cigs, silks, & razor blade swallowing. Vanished over the Pacific in a USO airplane in 1946 and presumed dead. [SAM]

name: Kristal, Kay
bio: (Oxford, England: 29 Jan 19 - ) Stage name of Kay Swadling, daughter of Valerie & Robert Swadling. Learned in 1984 from books, videos, & audios. Pro close-up & patter-act cabaret magicienne since 1986. Has toured Europe & USA. British Ring Conventioners Trophy. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Królikowski, Jerzy
bio: (Poland: 1927-) Pro illusionist & manipulator for 35 years in Polish circus & variety venues. With assistant-wife Krystyna (born 1931) won the 1956 Warsaw Circus Arts Festival silver medal.

name: Kross
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 21 Jan 1938 - 1 Jul 2011) Stage name of Sanford M. Kraus. Financial planner in New Jersey. Learned in 1962 from local magic shop. Semi-pro mentalist since 1963, billed as "The Amazing Kross" & "The Incredible Kross". Pet effect: White Dwarf & 4th Dimensional Telepathy. Invented Talking Tarot in 1977. Known to colleagues as "Sandy Kross" until c1985 when changed to "Ford Kross". Wrote Out of the Deep Freeze (1979, 20pp), Suggestive Mentalism (1986, 15pp), & It Aint Body Building (1989). Column in Vibrations 1980-present. Articles in Invocation, Magick, etc. [Wh2]

name: Krosso, Professor
bio: (Pomerania, Germany: fl.1850s) Billed in London in 1852 as "The Modern Samson". Pro strong-man & illusionist, his only illusion being Decapitation.

name: Kroupa, Jiri
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 8 Dec 1928-) Pro manip in post-WW II Czechoslovakia.

name: Krug, Ludwig
bio: (USA?: fl.1930s-40s) Resident of New York City when he patented an improved version of Ed Massey's Penetration Frame around 1934. Also marketed his aluminum table-base thru Tannen's in 1948.

name: Kubikuzena, Sara
bio: (USSR: fl.1970s-80s) Pro stage magicienne. Won (with partner Sultangali Sukurov) 1978 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix & 1979 FISM Grand Prix.

name: Kudarz, Robert
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 27 Oct 1857-5 [sic] Dec 1922) Stage name of Thomas W[illiam] Driver. A printer's compositor by trade. Semi-pro magician 1883-1891 when he toured both New Zealand & Australia. In 1884 married Nellie Lingard (born 1861) and settled permanently to Wellington, NZ. Billed as "The Napoleon of Necromancers". Also performed as "Driver". Teacher of Emile Lazern. SAM Member #167. Founded the 1st magic club (The Magic Circle) in New Zealand, which operated in Wellington from 4 Jul 1912 until 1914. Died in poverty, his remains being reinterred with monument by life-long friend W.E. "Billy" White. Contributed to Mahatma, Magic, & MUM. Wrote manuscript book on ANZAC magicians, the only copy now with the Wellington Society of Magicians as gift from White's widow. [Wal; MUM11/99]

name: Kuethe Jr, F[rederick] William "Bill" [pronounced KEY-THEE]
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 7 Nov 1932- ) Real estate & bank executive. Amateur magician & noted collector of magician's coins & tokens (over 750 items). Also has perhaps the world's largest collection of forcing books. Used various pen names, including "The Magic Chef" (in succession to Paul Koch) & "Veritas". Publisher-editor Magical Bloodhound 1962-76, The Magic Cauldron 1964-76, Journal of Necromantic Numismatics 1966-77, & The Magic Cauldron: New Series 1977-present. Wrote A Conjuring Bibliography of “Forcing” Items (1962, 4pp), Checklist of Magical Periodical Literature in Print (1963), Magicians' Tokens and Related Items (1978), & A Catalogue of the Edgar G. Heyl Collection of Magicians' Tokens, Medals and Related Items (1993). Tricks in New Phoenix. [Se;Wh]

name: Kukol, Franz
bio: (Austria: c1877-) Ex-Austrian army officer with a circus background. Pro 1903-1914 as assistant to Houdini. Co-invented (with Houdini & Vickery) Milk Can Escape in 1908. [Silver]

name: Kuma, K. T.
bio: (Seoul, Korea: 4 Feb 1884 - 27 Mar 1963) Stage name of the Korean-born Japanese Kinjiro Tanaka KUMAJO (or, as he wisely claimed in the USA during WW II & the Korean War, possibly the Korean, KIM Yen-Soo). Learned at age 5 as apprentice to Japanese magician. Debut in 1892. Pro. Moved to USA in 1904. In 1915 introduced to the West the ancient Chinese so-called Kuma Tubes. Played the New York Palace in 1925, 1927, 1949, & 1950. [Pr;Ch;Ran]

name: Kumar, S. K. Vasantha
bio: (India: fl. 1960s-70s) Aka "Professor Kumar". Lived in Mysore. An editor of Magic Bird. Wrote Illusionseseme (Seattle: 1971, 215pp). Tricks in Genii.

name: Kunard, Professor R.
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s-90s) Wrote The Book of Card Tricks for Drawing-Room and Stage Entertainments (1888, 180pp), The Book of Modern Conjuring [1890, 216pp], & the above two combined as The Book of Conjuring and Card Tricks (1901, 220pp), all published in London. (Araria, Bihar, India: 3 Jan 1947- ) Stage name of Salil Kumar Kundu since 1963. Learned in 1956 when eldest brother taught 2 tricks, then from books. Pro since 1975, specializing in fire & livestock effects. Invented Girl to Flower Bush in 1989. Lecturer & demonstrator. Founder-President International Magical Youth Organization & editor of its journal The Gimmick. 1987 India Magic Circle "Magician of the Year". Kundu, Solyl "Dipu" Also edits The Magical Info. Wrote Magic that Sells You (1988, 10pp), Six of Solyl (1989, 15pp), & Magic of the Wings (1990, 16pp). Effects in New Pentagram, Magic Info, Sorcerer, Magicana, Abra, Magigram, & books by Ian Adair & Jim Reilly. [Wh5]

name: Kunz, Emil
bio: (Germany?: 29 Mar 1933-) Magician & magic collector in Germany. [Nad] (England: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Fred Brezin. Pro with pseudo-Japanese stage act. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1909.

name: Kuroki, Kenichi "Ken
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Student at Chuo U in Tokyo. Semi-pro close-up magician. Invented Self Service (1989). 1990 Nihon Close-up Magic Grand Prix. Trick in Genii. TV bit in Britain.

name: Kuronuma, Johnny
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Stage name of Noboru Kuronuma. Pro close-up in Kyoto. 1989 Nihon Close-up Magic Grand Prix.

name: Kurtz, Gary
bio: (Canada: fl.1980s-90s) Choreographer & dancer in Montreal. Semi-pro close-up magician, particularly with coins. A sensation at the 1987 & 1989 FFFF conventions. Lecturer. Wrote U.P: The Ultimate Progression (1994, 12pp). See Richard Kaufman, Gary Kurtz: Unexplainable Acts (1990, 101pp). Tricks in Genii.

name: Kü-Wang-Sü
bio: See: Stein, Jacoby

name: Kwan
bio: See: CHU Pak Kwan

name: Kwong, Jimmy Chan-Chow
bio: (Hong Kong: 18 Apr 1934-5 Apr 1994) Pro since 1960. Did both Oriental & Western magic acts. Aka "Mr. X". Played Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Taiwan, & China. Magic consultant to major Hong Kong movie & TV companies. In 1989 moved to USA where he also performed. Taught MAK Shing Yan, SO Siu Hin, CHAN Koon Hey, CHU Sun Yun, TSAND Ling Ching, TSAND Ling Yeun, AU Won Leung, WU Chi Wai, & LAW Shing Tai.

name: Kyall, Richard
bio: (Britain: -2000) 1985 British Ring Shield with assistant-wife Joanna. 1986 British Magical Champion of Illusion. Killed doing a motorcycle stunt. [LR12/2000]

name: Labéro, Joe
bio: (Germany?: 1891-1951) Stage name of Josef Laber (or Fryderyk Sitek). Pro with memory act. Also animal hypnotism act with snakes, crocodiles, & lions. Wrote Wundermänner: Ich enthüfte Eure Geheimnisse (Leipzig: 1932, 128pp). [Al;Mec]

name: Labero, [Bengt] Joe
bio: (Sweden: 28 Jul 1963-) Learned at age 8 from magic book. Pro since age 20 with closeup & illusions. Tours worldwide with trade shows & conventions. Current show has 18 big illusions. [Wh8]

name: Labri, Professor
bio: (Nyborg, Denmark: 1863-1935) Stage name of Dines Petersen. Pro, working mainly markets. Famous for his nonsense patter. [Vo58]

name: Lacaze
bio: (France: fl.1830s-50s). Pro cardman, his best tricks using marked cards, which technique he taught to Robert-Houdin. Founder-owner of an elegant little magic theater, Le Théâtre Mariques, in the Champs Elysées in Paris 1835-50.

name: La Devo
bio: See: Goldston, Leah

name: Laengner, Klaus
bio: (Germany: 6 Jun 1922- ) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: La Farge, Lucille
bio:
Lafayette, The Great (Munich, Germany: 24 Feb 1872-9 May 1911) Stage name of Siegmund Ignatius Neuburger [sic] until he had it legally changed to The Great Lafayette. Brought to USA at age 12. Major pro stage illusionist by 1900. Foreign tours of London (1900), Paris (1907), & Britain (1910-11) where he died in a theater fire during performance in Edinburgh, Scotland. A notable eccentric. Invented Lion's Bride in 1901. See Arthur Setterington, The Life and Times of The Great Lafayette (1991, 112pp). NOTE: As Volkmann & Dammann proved, his passport falsely gave his surname as "Neuberger", place of birth as "Wiesbaden", & year of birth as "1873". [Pr;Dif;Ch;Fi;Daw;Go2;Mo;Dam; Magic1/01,3/09] "Lafayette -- The Argentine Wizard" SEE: Briant, E. Leslie La Follette, The Great [pronounced la-FOE-let] (Baltimore, Maryland: 8 Dec 1886-8 Nov 1960) Stage name of George P. Reuschling, aka "Rush Ling Toy". Inspired as kid seeing Lafayette, Ziska, & Si Stebbins. Pro magician & quick-change artist. In 1946 moved from Boston to St. Petersburg, Florida, where he ran a magic shop for several years. Articles in Barnstormer. [Pr;Ch;Ho;WWM]

[See also: Lyle, Cecil]

name: Lagerberg, Pontus
bio: (Sweden: 10 Dec 1903-) In insurance business in Stockholm. Amateur magician. Edited Trollkarlen 1946-51 & 1953-54. LaGerould, Terry "The Kidd" (Michigan, USA: fl.1970s-90s) Pro close-up cardman, long at major casinos in Las Vegas, Reno (Caesar's Palace), & Lake Tahoe. Tricks in Apocalypse & Magic. See Bruce Florek, The Tahoe File: Card Magic by Terry Lagerould (1982, 23pp); and Wayne Whiting & Terry LaGerould, Terry LaGerould's Pastebord Presentations (1992, 122pp). [Lo2]

name: Laine
bio: (Britain: fl.1820s) Played Bartholomew Fair in 1828 in partnership with Keyes. [Fr]

name: Lair, Michael P [aul]
bio: (Greenville, S. Carolina: 12 Nov 1959-) Learned at age 6 from father Robert L. Lair, a magician. Senior applications programmer/analyst with Timken Roller Bearing Company. Part-time pro close-up magician since 1981, billed as "Michael the Magician". Specialties: coin, cane, & fire magic. Wrote 4 booklets: Silver (1985), Silver 2 (1986), Candles (1988), & Act I (1992, 31pp). A 1982 Linking Ring "One Man Parade". [Wh2]

name: Lake, [James Bernard] "Jimmy
bio: (Stockport, Cheshire, England: 12 Jan 1910-1985) Moved to Canada in 1927. Ran a ceramic workshop & school in Toronto. Semi-pro gospel magician. IBM President 1951-52. Edited Gospel Maginews 1959?-68? Edited one or more "Canadian Parade" in Linking Ring. Author.

name: Lake, Lester
bio: (New Trenton, Indiana: c1905-26 Aug 1977) Pro stage magician as "Marvelo" in 1930s & 40s. Invented the Lake Guillotine (1932), Disecto (around 1938), Chinese Chopper (by 1940), Shredder (by 1940), Butterfly Cabinet (by 1940), & Wa-Ter-Lu (by 1947). Wrote The Skull Speaks (12pp).

name: Lal, K.
bio: (India: 1924-) Pro illusionist since age 16. Pet effects: Sub Trunk, Zig Zag, Thru the Eye of the Needle, etc. Has toured his large stage act thru Far East, Australasia, & Middle East. Many TV bits. Performs with son K. Lal Jr who also performs alone. [LR8/98]

name: Lam, Louis
bio: (Holland: fl.1930s-early 40s) Expert card magician. Wrote 3 booklets: Would You Believe It? (1935, 21pp), Watch Me Closely (1937, 30pp), & Be Deceived (1939, 27pp), all showing Lam's originality. Reportedly arrested by the Gestapo and executed during WW II. REF: New Phoenix #357 (1961), 258.

name: Lamarque, Abril
bio: (Cuba: 28 Aug 1904-25 Jan 1999) Moved to USA. Art director for several national magazines. Prominent amateur magician in New York City (in early 1940s) & Washington, DC (after moving there in mid-1946). Articles & tricks in HMM. Illustrated HMM. [Th]

name: Lamb, Geoffrey [Frederick], AIMC
bio: (Lewisham, London, England: fl.1960s-80s) Learned at age c12 from from Devant's Tricks for Everyone & a box of tricks. Teacher until retired in 1952 to become the author of some 50 popular educational books; and, beginning in 1968, eight on magic: Pegasus Book of Magicians (1968, 189pp), Mental Magic (1973, 56pp), Table Tricks (1974, 86pp), Victorian Magic (1976, 136pp), Magic, Witchcraft and the Occult (1977, 176pp), Pencil and Paper Tricks (1977, 80pp), Illustrated Magic Dictionary (1979, 157pp), & Magic for All the Family (1987, 124pp). Articles in Abra, Magic Circular, & Magigram. AIMC 1977. [CA;Wh2]

name: Lambert, Charles
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Aka "Mazarian" & "Mazarian Arathorn" as a bizarrist magician. Articles in New Invocation.

name: Lambert, D[avid] R.
bio: (Boston, Mass.: 17 May 1942- ) Dr. Lambert, a cognitive psychologist (PhD, UC San Diego, 1977), is an amateur magician (by age 10) and member of the International Brotherhood of Magicians (IBM). Wrote A Cognitive Model For Exposition of Human Deception and Counterdeception (San Diego: Naval Ocean Systems Center, 1987, 25pp. plus 9 appendices), a comprehensive taxonomy developed for the US Navy.

name: Lambert, Hubert [MacArthur]
bio: (Ireland: 1916-) Journalist with the Irish Times in Dublin. Semi-pro magician. Aka "Bertlam". Pet effect: the Bullet Catch. Tricks in New Phoenix, Linking Ring (1951), Genii, etc. [St]

name: Lambert, Leslie, MIMC
bio: (England: 1883-13 Dec 1941) Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Played St. George's Hall in 1908. Left magic c1913 to join "Room 40", the Royal Navy's super secret code-breaking section. From 1924 as "A.J. Alan" he was the BBC radio story-teller "Mystery Man". In 1938 he joined the government's main code-breaking operation at Bletchley Park., serving there until his death, a story that has been researched by Jeff Busby. REF: Dawes in Budget, V.67 (1973), 75-78, V.69 (1975), 171-173.

name: Lambie, [H. G.] Allan
bio: (Paisley, Scotland: 1894-22 Dec 1964) Moved to Canada at age 16. Close-up. Known as "King of the Quickie". Tricks in Jinx, Dragon, & Tops. See Tony Taylor & Micky Hades, The Magic of Allan Lambie (1970, 50pp).

name: Lamont, Peter
bio: (Britain: fl. 1990s) Amateur magician, fortune-teller, & psychic. Researcher at the U of Edinburgh on psy phenomena. Co-authored (with Richard Wiseman) Magic in Theory (1999, 175pp). Wrote The Rise of the Indian Rope Trick (2004, 264pp).

name: Lamonte, Jack
bio: (England: 9 May 1920-) Learned in youth. Pro close-up comedy magician & illustrator. In WW II with Royal Navy, giving over 200 shows in Ceylon. Did mainly sleight-of-hand in humorous style. Later, living in London, did illustrations for Magic Wand & Wizard. Edited Wizard 1954-56. Tricks in Magic Wand, Wizard, HMM, etc. Co-authored (with Al Koran) Mastered Amazement (1947, 66pp; repr 1987) & wrote Stunts with Stage Money (1948, 31pp).

name: La Montia, Johnny
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Learned magic from library books at age 30. Pro as founder-owner of Marketing Magic, which designs effects for corporations. Holds a Guinness world record for longest non-stop magic show (48 hours) made at David Copperfield's Project Magic. [Mag]

name: Lampini, P. P.
bio: (Belfort, France: fl. 1st decade of 1900s-40s) Stage name (or vice-versa) of Prince P. Masculin. Moved in 1903 to USA where soon learned magic. Pro comedy stage magician. Toured Australia 1916 (when he took a young Melbourne woman as assistant-wife) & c1938. Played Vancouver, Canada, in 1935. The Lampinis later moved to Australia. [Tay;Dor;Wal]

name: Lancaster, Lou
bio: (Roanoke, VA: 31 Oct 1936- ) Pro close-up & coinman. Founder-owner of "The Professional Magic Studio on N. Highland Ave in Hollywood in the 1960s. Invented Twister in 1981-82. Wrote Tricks Trade (1985). Video (1985). {LR8/05]

name: Lançon, Harry
bio: (France: 19 Feb 1886-10 Jan 1950) Stage name of Henri Lataste. Taught by Bénévol. Proventriloquist & magician. Wrote Tous ventriloque (1912). [St;Dif] (England: fl.1770s-90s) Major pro fair magician until retired or died soon after 1794. Dead by 1800. Succeeded by "Gregory". [Cl;Fr]

name: Lane, Charles
bio: (England: -19 Oct 1977) With assistant did a 2-person high-speed telepathy act as "The Zodias". [Daw2]

name: Lane, Frank
bio: (New London, Connecticut: Dec 1896-18 Jun 1987) Pseudonym of Morand Francis Caldwell. Pro inventor-improver-dealer (Frank Lane & Co. in Boston). Invented The Devil Whispers card trick (by 1932), the Lazy Magician effect with record trick method by 1933, etc. Famous for his mutually contrived long-running "feud" with Ted Annemann in the 1930s. Lane, Frank Bennett Edited Funny Talk 1938-42 (48 issues), reprinted as Funny Talk for Magicians (230pp). Wrote Help Yourself (1931), Here's How (1934), Two Hours with Frank Lane (nd, mss), & Funny Stuff for Funny Magicians (with Bob Weill). [Go2;Ho] (USA: 1875- ) A minister of the gospel in Vineland, New Jersey. Learned magic c1888 so as to combine it with his preaching. Billed as "The Mystic Philosopher" he took his "Magic with a Meaning" show, which included some large illusions and ran about 1 and a half hours, to the Chautauqua & Lyceum circuits. He is the earliest known gospel magician. [Magic2/11]

name: Lane, Peter, MIMC
bio: (Ealing, London, England: 23 Feb 1941- ) Stage name of Peter Geoffrey Humphries (since 1965). Learned at age 7. Quantity surveyor. Semi-pro childrens magician since 1965. Collector, specializing in British magazines, posters, & other magicana. Executive Librarian of the Magic Circle. Edited Hocas 1982-86. Articles in Abra, Cauldron, Magic Shelf, New Pentagram, etc. [Wh2]

name: Lang, Prof. Berthold
bio: (Austria: fl.1970s-90s) Theatrical historian in Vienna. Edited Vom Hexer zum Magier (1976) & Hokuspokus fidibus: 100 Jahre Wien Zaubertheater (1989). Article in Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993).

name: Lang Neil, C.
bio: See: Neil, C. Lang

name: Langbein, Christian F. G.
bio: (Germany: fl. 1st decade of 1800s) Pen name of G. A. Joachim. Wrote Der Taschengesellschafter (1805).

name: Lani
bio: (Hong Kong, China: 8 Sep 1955- ) Born SHAM Yuk-lan. Secretary until 1975 when became assistant as "Lani" to "Johnny Aladdin" Randall who taught her magic. Specialty: Sleight-of-hand. They played USA & Europe. They married in 1985, she becoming Lani Randall. Left stage for motherhood c1986. [Wh2] Lansbury, Bruce Produced “The Magician” CBS-TV series (1973) with Bill Bixby, consultant Mark Wilson. Lansbury, Edgar Produced “The Magic Show” starring a little known Canadian magician named Doug Henning when the show was originally called “Spellbound” when it was at the Royal Alexandria Theatre in Toronto in December of 1973, opening on Broadway May 28, 1974.

name: Lansing, Robert
bio: (San Diego, California: 5 Jun 1928-) Stage name of Robert Brown. Popular TV & film actor since the late 1950s. Became an avid magic hobbyist, studying several years with Mike Skinner. [Mag;Katz]

name: Lantz, Charles E.
bio: See: "Charles, Lance"

name: LaPlatt, Algernon
bio: See: Platt, John J.

name: LaPorte, Sam[uel F.]
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 15 Mar 1938- ) Machinist. Hired in 1965 by Charles Johnson to make precision-gaffed coins for Johnson Products in Arcadia, California. Bought out Johnson in 1967. A non-magician, he hired Mike Caveney in 1972 as part-time consultant to develop the business, which with 20 craftsmen is now the world's largest of its type. Father of Sammy LaPorte. [Wh] (Pasadena, California: 29 Jul 1964-) Son of Sam LaPorte. Machinist. Plant superintendent of Johnson Products. Non-magician.

name: Lardner, Foster
bio: (USA: 24 Nov -17 May 1934) Pro in theater. Semi-pro magician in New England. [WWM]

name: Larette, C. H.
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 18 Apr 1889-14 [sic] May 1943) Stage name of Cornelius "Cornel" Hauer. Jew. POW in Russia in WW I. Pro manip (cards, cigarettes, & coins) in Vienna as "C.H. Larette". Moved before WW II to Holland where he became a dealer (Studio de Magie) in Amsterdam. Court Magician to Queen Wilhelmine. Taught Ritsko Van Vliet in 1940. Shot & killed himself before facing 2nd Gestapo interrogation for listening to English radio. Wrote De Goochelkunst (Amsterdam: 1939). Trick in Phoenix #210. Van Vliet has written an article on Larette & Vermeyden for Magie. [Al;St;Dif;Dam;MUM7/91]

name: Larkin, Stanley
bio: (Stanmore, Sydney, Australia: 16 Feb 1909-) Amateur. Articles. [Go2]

name: Laroche, J.
bio: (France: c1820-c1880) Pro by 1840. [Vo55]

name: Larsen, Dante [Jay]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 6 Apr 1961- ) Son of John & Irene Daniel, adopted son of Bill Larsen Jr, half brother of Heidi Larsen. Editor. Amateur magician & magic collector. Assisted at Magic Castle in Hollywood for years. Assistant Stage Manager of annual "It's Magic" shows in 1980s. Co-Associate Editor (with Heidi Larsen) of Genii 1988-90, editor of its "Bagdad" page since 1989 plus convention review articles, & Editor 1990-93. [Wh2]

name: Larsen, Erika
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 14 Jun 1968-). Youngest daughter of Bill & Irene Larsen. Edited Genii from 1993 until the end of 1998 when the owner-editorship passed to Richard Kaufman. Now works a spook show and mindreading act (with her daughter Liberty). [Wh01

name: Larsen, Geraldine [Frances] "Gerrie
bio: (Traverse City, Michigan: 2 Jun 1906-1998) Born Geraldine Conrad. Married William W. Larsen Sr in 1925. Semi-pro kid-show magicienne, aka "The Magic Lady". First President of Magigals in 1939 (& held that office again in 1960). A Chavez graduate 1944. Edited Genii 1953-57. Wrote The Diary of a Magician's Wife (1941) & Nothing Up His Sleeve (1943). Syndicated TV weekly kid-show 1/2-hour series as "The Magic Lady" 1951. Later Mrs Art Baker (he was famous radio & movie interviewer 1957-66), lastly Mrs Rubin Jaffe (he died in 1976). Edited Genii's "25 Years Ago in Genii" column. SAM Hall of Fame. Mother of Milt & Bill Larsen Jr.

name: Larsen, Heidi
bio: (Hollywood, California: 14 Sep 1966-) Daughter of Irene & Bill Larsen Jr. Amateur (taught Dancing Cane by Peter Pit). Associate Editor of Genii 1987-1993.

name: Larsen, Irene
bio: (Stühlingen, near Munich, Germany: 25 Sep 1936-) Raised in Austria & West Germany. Learned stage magic in 1956 as assistant to John Daniel, moving to USA next year when she married him. Assisted in his Spook Show tour in late 1950s. Married Bill Larsen Jr in 1963. Learned close-up from Jay Ose. Co-editor (with Bill Jr) of Genii 1963-90. 1987 AMA Literary Fellowship (with Bill Jr). Academy of Magical Arts President since 1994. Mother of Dante, Heidi, & Erika Larsen. [Genii8/89;Wh]

name: Larsen, Milt[on Page]
bio: (Pasadena, California: 9 Apr 1931- ) Younger son of William & Geraldine Larsen from whom he learned at age 6 as assistant in their full-evening show. Amateur comedy magician as "The Great Larseni". Pet effect: Serpent Silk. Pro TV comedy writer. Producer of the annual "It's Magic" show in Los Angeles 1956-1988. Founder of the Magic Castle in 1963. Founding President, Society for the Preservation of Variety Arts, Inc, 1975-present. Collector of vaudeville memorabilia, which is housed in the Variety Arts Center. SAM Hall of Fame. Younger brother of Bill Larsen Jr who he succeeded as President for Life of the Magic Castle. [Genii5/66;Mag;Wh2]

name: Larsen, William W[alter]
bio: (Green Bay, Wisconsin: 31 Dec 1904-5 Jul 1953) Inspired & learned from tricks bought by his father. Moved to Southern California in 1922. Criminal lawyer. Semi-pro mentalist & magician. Founder-editor Genii magazine 1936-53. In 1939 toured a full-evening show thru USA with wife Gerrie & sons Bill Jr & Milt. Owned Thayer Studio of Magic in Los Angeles 1942-1950 when sold to Clayton Jacobson. Retired from law practice in 1945 to give full time to magic. Founder of the Larsen magic dynasty. SAM Hall of Fame. Co-invented (with T. Page Wright) Boudoir of a Dancing Girl (by 1928). Published several booklets jointly with his friend Wright, including The L.W. Mysteries for Children (1928) & L&W Mental and Spirit Mysteries (1929). Plus many joint articles with Wright in Sphinx under various pen names. Under own name & pen name of "Dr. Frederick Straussborg" wrote many published manuscripts, mostly on mentalism, many republished as The Mental and other writings of William Larsen, Sr (1977, 212pp). Also under own name: Magically An Idea or Two (1933, 46pp), Contact and Non-Contact Mind-Reading (1945, 4pp), Tricks for Television (1949, 12pp), Puppetrix (1949, 14pp), etc. As "Jack Hamilton" wrote Descriptive Program of Dante's Sim Sala Bim. [Th]

name: Larsen Jr, William W[alter] "Bill
bio: (Pasadena, California: 8 May 1928-11 Feb 1993) Learned by age 9 assisting in family magic act. Semi-pro. Married Irene Daniels in 1963. Since retirement as TV producer in 1967, President for Life of the Magic Castle (at an annual salary of $150,000). 1983 CMI Order of the Magic Lamp. SAM Hall of Fame. Editor of Genii 1957-1990. 1987 AMA Literary Fellowship (shared with Irene Larsen). Elder brother of Milt Larsen. Adoptive father of Dante Larsen & father of Heidi & Erika

name: Larson, Charles H. "Charlie
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1870-21 Mar 1950) President of 23 Oldsmobile auto dealerships in New York until retired in 1929, a multi-millionaire. Amateur magician since 1929 when he was inspired seeing a Professor Adler in Europe. In 1938 founded The Inner Circle of Magicians. By 1939 he had created the world's largest collection of apparatus (20,000 pieces) kept in his private "Larson Museum of Magic" in New York City. In 1944 he sold an estimated 40,000 items valued at $50,000 to Tannen's. The choicer items together with his strong book collection he sold in late 1949 shortly before his death to John McManus. [SAM]

name: LaRue, [W. Ramon] "Buddy
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro escape artist, mentalist, & astrologer. Ran a mail-order business in magic magazines (as "Sir Edwards") out of his hotel room in Indianapolis, Indiana, in the late 1940s. Reprinted a facsimile edition of The Linking Ring, Vols.1 & 2. Wrote the Sir Edwards Store Demonstration Sales Plan. [Life 19 Jun 1950]

name: Lassaigne, Auguste
bio: (Toulouse, France: 30 Nov 1819-4 Nov 1885 [sic]) Pro in French provinces & Paris since c1845 with magic & vent. Aka "Auguste". With wife Prudence Bernard also worked a hyp act with second sight, as when they appeared in Paris in 1847 at the Salle Bonne-Nouvelle. Played London in 1857. In 1864 gave his version of Pepper's Ghost in Paris. Later a partner of Trewey. Bio is Mémoires d'un magnétiseur (1851, 150pp). [Dif;Vo55]

name: Lato
bio: See: Lopilato, Anthony

name: Latour, Harry
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-60s) Stage name of Harry Paget. Pro, working as stage manager for the Great Masoni, etc. Wrote Magical Suggestions (1921). 1953 Magic Wand Trophy. Left pro magic by 1955 to work for a photographic agency.

name: La Tude
bio: (France: fl.1700) Pro. Earliest known performer of handcuff escape (by 1700) & perhaps its inventor.

name: Latz, Harry L[ee]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 19 Jan 1896-) Learned magic in 1910. By 1918 was owner of the Alamac Hotel, whose Latzcellar was main gathering place for magicians in Atlantic City until by 1923 when he opened the skyscraper Alamac Hotel on West 72nd St in Manhattan with its Congo Room on the top floor. In 1926 turned to advertising. Amateur close-up & pocket magician. Column in Genii. [SAM;Dor;Bam,52,100]

name: Lauder, Peggy
bio: (Germany: 2 Sep 1908-5 May 1960) Stage name of Olga Gantz. Learned as assistant to her uncle, "John Olms". Then on own between the world wars with a manipulative act while blindfolded. Died in Berlin.

name: Laughlin, Lyle F[red]
bio: (Oakdale, California: 4 Apr 1906-26 Oct 1996) Amateur magician 1918-1930, semi-pro 1930-36, pro since 1936. Aka "Carl-Lyle" & "Carlyle". Specialized in sleight-of-hand & close-up magic on West Coast. Pet effects: Dancing Hank &

name: Vanishing Radio. Invented Three-to-One Ropes
bio: (by 1936). Retired from magic in 1954 to run a camera repair shop until final retirement in late 1960s, living in Oakland, then El Cerrito. A Mason. Tricks in Genii & HMM. [SAM;Wat]

name: Laurant, Eugene
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 19 Aug 1875-19 Feb 1944) Stage name of Eugene Lawrence Greenleaf since 1898. Learned by lessons from Bernier, a French pro. Pro star since 1898 in vaude, Lyceum (since 1899), & Chautauqua. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. Trick in Sphinx. [Pr;Genii3/41;Ho;WWM]

name: Laureau, Marcel
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Aka "Erix". Collector in Paris. Wrote Le Théâtre Robert-Houdin, à la Belle Epoque', 1879-1914 (1948) with English tr by Findlay as The Robert-Houdin Theatre, 1879-1914 (1968, 11pp).

name: Laurencio
bio: (Boussugues-les-Mons, Belgium: 15 May 1884-22 Jul 1927) Stage name of Laurent-Ghislain Camby, of Belgian-French parentage. Pro in youth as a dancer, singer, imitator, & magician. Later as magician (as "Jackson"), combining ventriloquism (as "Frenski"), juggling (as "Kukiko"), transformism, music, & acrobatics in his mixed act. Toured his "Revue des Attractions" thru Belgium, Holland, Germany, Switzerland, etc. [Dif;Vo58]

name: Laurice
bio: (USA: 12 Sep 1877-23 Feb 1932) Stage name of Laurice Katoff.

name: Laurie, Madame
bio: See: Goldston, Leah

name: Lautenstein, Egon von
bio: (Braunschweig, Germany: 19 Mar 1901-16 Oct 1967) Stage name of Adolf Wöhlbier. Pro since 1922 with manip & stage tricks on German & Danish variety stage for next 3 decades with tours to other European countries. Married János Bartl's only daughter, Elli. Arrested by the Gestapo in Romania in 1943 for defeatist remarks. Released but lived in hiding under assumed name in Dresden for next half year. Lavand, René With Kalanag's show for some time after WW II; but, unable to reestablish his own career, retired to open a camera shop in Hamburg. Died in an auto accident in Hamburg. [Win;St;Roh]

name: LaValle, Baron
bio:
(Argentina: fl.1950s-90s) Stage name of Renato Lavandeira. Has only one hand (his left). Star pro in Argentina with Hofzinser-type act. Vernon observed him dealing "fifths, sixths and even sevenths" & other sleights "done to perfection". On Ed Sullivan TV show in 1950s & 60s. Toured Mexico in 1960s. Wrote Lentidigitacion/Lentidigitation (1989, 120pp) with English tr as Slow Motion Magic (Vol. I, 1989, 115pp; Vol. II, 1991, 128pp); Magic from the Soul (1993, 228pp); & his autobio, The Mysteries of My Life (169pp). 2 videos (1992).

[See also: Jones, Larry]

name: Lavassor, Louis
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 1845-1930) Concert pianist. Early American magic collector. Began to perform & collect after meeting Robert Heller in 1866. Sold his important prop collection to John Snyder.

name: La Vellma
bio: See: Lustig, David J.

name: Law
bio: (England: fl.1830s) Minor pro magician-vent when he played the London Tavern in 1836. [Fr]

name: Lawrence, Professor
bio: (Jamaica: -1955) West Indian black. Pro there by 1919. Moved to USA.

name: Lawston, Vick
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-70s). Inspired seeing a school-show magician. Dealer (The Lawston Fun and Magic Co.) in Queens Village, NY, by 1940 when he published a decent catalog (116pp). Thence moved his shop to various locations in Connecticut (by 1965) and Florida (by 1965 to at least 1970)

name: Lawton, Don
bio: (Richmond Center, Wisconsin: 5 Mar 1922-12 Jun 1988) Inspired at age 10 by magician at school show. Immediately learned from library books. Pro comedy magic. Moved to St. Louis in Dec 1945. Worked briefly in the Lindhorst Magic Den in St. Louis, Missouri, until 1946 when he became manager of Fred Andrews's new "St. Louis Magic Studio" until it sold to Bev Taylor who renamed it the Town House Magic Co. Lawton bought the business in 1955 and later renamed it the Don Lawton Magic Shop. Closed in or soon after 1966. Moved to Hollywood, California. AMA Board of Directors 1969-70. Manager of the Magic Castle for several years after 1970. 1971 AMA Stage Magician of the Year. Edited Lines from Lawton (1953-66), wrote Lots of Lawton (1971, 160pp), & published New Lines from Lawton 1985-88. Video (1988). [Monti;Bo#214;Albo95;Mag]

name: Lazern, Emile
bio: (New Zealand: fl.1890s-1920s) Stage name? Aka "Walter J. Hansen", "Nesnah", "Gregals", "Hornman". Taught by Robert Kudarz. Pro illusionist. Performed made up as a Frenchman. Spent several years in British music halls, including the Crystal Palace in 1896 with Charles Dalton. Played Australia in 1898, 1905 (as "The Magician in White"), & 1911. Toured New Zealand & the Orient (including Burma & India) in 1904. Performed as late as 1921 with the Clay circuit. Catch phrase: "Watch me closely". [CMM7/07,10/07]

name: Lea, Hubert H.
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-30s) Edited Magic Circular 1914-38.

name: Lea, Nelson
bio: See: Lee, Richard Nelson

name: Lead, Brian, AIMC
bio: (Blackburn, England: 31 Aug 1952- ) Learned at age 11 from magic sets & Will Dexter's books. English teacher. Amateur magician & magic historian. Collector. Edits Memel (journal of Modern Mystic League) 1984-present & Northern Lights (journal of Northern Magic Circle) 1987-present. Wrote Houdini: The Myth Maker (1987, 56pp, with Roger Woods) & Laughing at Locksmiths: The Legend and Legacy of Harry Houdini (1988, 19pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Magic Manuscript, Abra, Magic Info, Magic Mag, Magicol, Magic Circular, Magicana, Budget, & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Le-a-Far
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 3 Oct 1910-27 Jan 1990) Stage name (by reversing his given name) of Rafael Pinto. Typographer by trade turned pro actor. Semi-pro comedy magic with pseudo-Chinese act since 1939 with tours in Europe, Brazil, & USA (1980). Performed in 2 Portuguese movies: Aldeia da Roupa Branca & Bocage. [Cam]

name: Leakey, Basil
bio:
(USA: fl.1930s) Chemist. Amateur magician. Wrote Handbook of Chemical Magic (1939, 36pp).

[See also: "Adair, Alan"]

name: Leaney, [David Gilbert] "Gil
bio: (England: 1921-3 Jan 1993) Joined H. Stanley, J. Hughes, & A. Dowler as partner in their Unique Magic Studio in London in 1947. Then on own as "Magic to Design" in Kenton, Middlesex, late 1940s to mid-1950s. Pro society & nightclub magician (with 2 assistants) in London in 1950s. Illusion builder for Dante, Murray, Lyle, Harbin, Fogel, Voltaire, Bailey, and, most recently, Paul Daniels (as Technical Consultant for 12 years). 1987 AMA Creative Fellowship. [Daw94]

name: Leat, Harry [A.]
bio: (London, England: 1874-12 Jan 1949) Inspired around age 8 seeing conjuror at school show. Self-taught. Manager of Ornum's Magic Depot 1889-1915 & part-time assistant to Maurice Garland. Around 1890 also had own prop factory in Walworth. First editor of Munro's The Magic Wand 1910-13, during which time he disguised its one-man writing by using several pen names: "H.L.", "Hal", "Nine-stone-ten", "Amateur", "B. Wayne", "Vento", & "Shadow". Pro dealer on own since 1915 in London as strictly wholesale. Edited Leat's Leaflets 1925-40 (55 issues) as house organ. Noted for his outspokenness & practical jokes. Invented Run Rabbit Run in 1939. Father of Harry Leat Jr who inherited the business. Autobio is Forty Years In & Around Magic (1923, 77pp). Wrote Thoughtful Magic (1923), Magic of the Depots (1923), Diversified Magic (1924, 104pp), U.S.A. Depot Magic (1925, 92pp), Tragic Magic (1925, 122pp), Magical Cartoons and Interpolations (1927), Magical Cartoons and Interpolations (1927). Co-authored (with Wilfrid Jonson) Masked Magical Glossary (1928, 31pp), an eccentric effort to disguise 200 jargon terms under a layer of freshly coined terms. [Daw94; St; McC]

name: Leavitt, M[ichael] B[ennett]
bio: (England: -1969) Assistant in his father's magic shop in London before 1949 when he took it over. Sold it to Supreme Magic Co in 1969. (USA: 1843-27 Jun 1935) Famous American impresario who created the American burlesque around 1868. Booked several top magicians including Kellar (since 1888), A. Herrmann, Washington Irving Bishop, The Zancigs (1903-04), Servais Le Roy, Talma, Imro Fox, & F.E. Powell. Memoir is Fifty Years of Theatrical Management, 1859-1909 (1912), with a chapter (pp.504-519) on his magicians. [Var, NYT]

name: Le Bas, Albert
bio: (Ireland: c1928-Sep 1972) Semi-pro stage magician & illusionist but still Ireland's top magician. Pet effect: Miser's Dream, which was billed as "Where the Money Is". [Fi]

name: Lebert, Carl
bio: (England: -May 1907) Pro doing private shows in London since 1894 with a program of chapeaugraphy, troublewit, juggling, & magic. Depressed by poverty suicided. [CMM6/07]

name: Lebram, Ludwig
bio: (Köslin, Germany: 29 Mar 1884-27 Dec 1969) Pro magician. Bought the props of Bellachini-Berlach and worked in Berlin as "Leonard Bellachini" until 1935 when moved to Finland. There took stage name of "Professor Leonardi". Married Gertrud "Gerty Bellachini" Will. Returned in 1963 to Berlin where he died. [St]

name: Lechner, Ernst
bio: (Germany: 2 May 1923- ) Amateur. President of MZvD 1970-75. [Nad]

name: Le Dair, Jack, MIMC
bio: (Plymouth, England: 1 Nov 1880-19 Jun 1952) Stage name of John Albert Warton, aka "Wilton Warton, the Canadian Conjurer". Introduced to magic by Arthur "Amasis" Hartop. Pro variety stage magician of the old school. Specialized in working giant matchsticks. Played St. George's Hall in 1923. Wrote Tricks of a Trouper (1946, 69pp; repr 1968), a compilation of his tricks in Abracadabra.

name: Lee, Berri
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Introduced to magic working as parking attendant at the Magic Castle in Hollywood where he learned from its members. In late 1960s protégé of Cary Grant who launched his career. Pro comedy magic. Worked major production stage shows (Wayne Newton, etc) & TV (Steve Allen, Dinah Shore, etc). [Mag]

name: Lee, Hank
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 17 Dec 1950-). Stage name of Harry Levy. Learned as child. Semi-pro performer in Boston area. Pro dealer-manufacturer (Hank Lee's Magic Factory) in Boston since 1975 when he opened in his mother's basement & now the largest in New England. [Wh]

name: Lee, Richard Nelson
bio: (England: 8 Jan 1806-) Minor pro magician. Began career as a juggler with Gygell's troupe. Soon turned actor & manager of theatrical booths at the London fairs. NOTE: Surname also spelled Lea. [CI]

name: Lee, Stacey
bio: (London [sic], England: 23 Sep 1966- Interested in magic since age 8. 1983 finalist in Magic Circle's Young Magician of the Year contest. Pro close-up & stage magicienne, specializing in dancing effects. Also works with male assistant "Julian" whom she recently married. Dealer (Stacey's Magic Palace) in Ilford, Essex, since 1986 with a London branch opposite British Museum. Articles in Genii, etc. [Wh2]
years: 23 Sep 1966- Interested in magic since age 8. 1983 finalist in Magic Circle's Young Magician of the Year contest. Pro close-up & stage magicienne, specializing in dancing effects. Also works with male assistant "Julian" whom she recently married. Dealer (Stacey's Magic Palace

name: LEE Tai-king
bio: (China: c1897-22 Mar 1981) Learned in Shanghai from MO Wu-chi. Pro. Moved to San Francisco in 1949 where performed as "Professor Lee", notably in his last years at the Magic Cellar. Pet effect: dancing on broken glass.

name: Lee, William John
bio: See: Armstrong, William J.

name: Lee, [William] Wallace
bio: (Lone Oak, Georgia: 7 Aug 1892-12 May 1969) Developed his famous doubletalk at age 9. Calling it "X-Jargon", it differs from the usual double-talk in that it introduces meaningless words only at crucial points to create confusion rather than comedy. Taught this art to Bill Spooner. Pro since 1913 as "Wallace, the Magician". Specialties: chalk talk & vent. Having moved to Durham, North Carolina he edited Now and Then 1933-38 (6? issues). Wrote X-Jargon [1937]; When, Where, and How to Doubletalk; Magic, Doubletalk, and Monkey Business; Primer of Doubletalk; Crypthesia; The Calendar of Your Fingers; Fakierithmetic; & Math Miracles (1950, 89pp). Tricks in HMM. [LR6/86; WWM; Ho]

name: Leech, Al
bio: (USA: 19th October 1917 - 1974) News reporter with Associated Press, then United Press. Amateur cardman. Wrote 7 booklets: Don't Look Now! The Smart Slant on Misdirection (1948, 23pp; repr 1971), For Card Men Only (1949, 30pp), Manipulating with Leech (1952, 30pp), Card Man Stuff (1953, 24pp), Handbook of Card Sleights (1954, 31pp), Cardmanship (1959, 28pp), & Super Card Man Stuff (1965, 60pp). See Al Leech's Legacy (1980, 124pp). Tricks in New Phoenix.

name: Leedy, Charles A[rmor] "Charlie
bio: (Sharon, Pennsylvania: 20 Dec 1871-6 Oct 1945) Boy magician at 16. Semi-pro Lyceum magician. Wrote tricks & the "Patter Lines" column for The Sphinx. Journalist in Youngstown, Ohio. [WWM;St]

name: Leeming, Joseph
bio:
"Leeroy the Magician" SEE: Roth, Roy A.

[See also: Sarandrea, Joseph M.]

name: Lees, Walt[er]
bio: (Lincoln, England: 30 Sep 1943- ) Inspired at age 5 seeing 1st magician. Pro childrens & close-up magician since 1966. Worked as pitchman 1968-77. Edited New Inside Info 1969. 1972 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. Edited Pabular 1978-81. Freelance editor of Repro Magic's house organ, Club 71, since 1984. Wrote several booklets, including Four Professional Card Tricks from the Repertoire of Walt Lees (1981, 36pp), More Professional Card Tricks (1981, 37pp), The Best of Close-up (1984), plus ones on magic of Ron MacMillan, Simon Lovell, Mike Bornstein, Pat Conway, etc. 3 audios. See also Lewis Ganson, The Immaculate Card Magic of Walt Lees (1975). Articles & tricks in Gen, Club 71, etc. [Wh2]

name: LeFleur, Armand
bio: (France: fl.1980s-90s) Pro. In Nov 1991 somehow -- he claimed by accident -- managed to saw his 23-year-old assistant, Yvonne Guerette, in two halves in front of 200 horrified school children in Compiegne, France. (Genii2/92)

name: Le Foe, Count Dominic
bio: (England: fl.1950s) Stage name of Alan Cooper-Smith (or Alan Curtis?). Pro.

name: Legman, Gershon
bio: (Scranton, Pennsylvania: 2 Nov 1917-23 Feb 1999) Born George Alexander Legman. Folklorist & writer on erotica & humor since 1935 (editor of Neurotica 1948-51, etc). Bibliographer for Kinsey's sex institute. Amateur magician in 1940s-50s. Friend of Martin Gardner & Jay Marshall. As "John Thursday" wrote several booklets on magic, including Card Tricks (1945). Moved to France in 1953 in protest against US Post Office censorship. Expert on origami, the Japanese art of paper-folding, which he popularized in the West in 1955. [CA]

name: Legrand
bio: (France: fl.1840s-50s) Parisian clock maker who made automata & other mechanical props for Lennot and Robert-Houdin. Convicted in 1850 of copying & selling some of Robert-Houdin's inventions to minor English showman Lettson. [Wal]

name: Legris, Jules[-Eugène]
bio: (Paris, France: 12 Oct 1862-3 Nov 1926) Inspired at age 14 reading Robert-Houdin's memoirs. Pro illusionist, initially with partner Alexandre Cony. Starred for 2 decades at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1894-1914. Charter member of the CSP 1904. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Lehn, Donald B.
bio: (New York, NY: 28 Jul 1952- ) ..... Pro since 1975, as "Moonbeam" 1976-82, then after moving to Spain in 1981, as "Malo, el Malísimo" 1982-present. Since 1987 he also worked in Madrid as English translator of all the Editorial Frakson books. ..... [Wh5]

name: Leichtmann, Joseph
bio: (Germany: 1854-23 Mar 1929) Jew. Pro. Moved to Vienna in 1880 where he became a magic dealer (as "Zauberkönig"). Then moved to Munich. Father of Melanie Leichtmann. Father-in-law (by another daughter) of Otto Mösch. [Roh]

name: Leichtmann, Melanie
bio: (Vienna, Austria; or Munich, Germany: 1885-) 3rd daughter of Joseph Leichtmann. Pro since age 10, first with her father, then on own billed as "Professorin der Magie". Married Eduard Steinböck. In 1910 founded a magic shop in Cologne (Köln). In 1933, after husband's death, turned over business to daughter Melanie Steinböck and retired in Leipzig. The daughter continued the shop as "Zauberladen" until 1973 when sold to Rolf Kehl who operated it as "Zauberkönig Köln". [Roh;St;Dam]

name: Leipsic, Nate" [misspelling]
bio: See: "Leipzig, Nate"

name: Leipzig, Nate
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 31 May 1873-13 Oct 1939) Stage name of Nathan Leipziger. Brought to USA as child. Inspired by and learned from reading The Secret Out around age 10. Optician & semi-pro magus in Detroit until 1902 when moved to New York City to become a pro as "Nate Berol" doing a vaudeville rag-picture act in partnership with Felix Berol (Max Berol's brother). Then as a society magician & in 1904 on into vaudeville. Invented the coin roll (by 1902) & Royal Rising Pencil (by 1905). Possibly invented the side-steal (by 1909). Pet effects included the Torn and Restored Cigarette Paper (by 1907). Toured England 1905-06, 1907 (when he received The Magic Circle's 1st Gold Medal), 1910; the Continent 1906; Australia 1911; & England again 1914, after which he remained in the USA where he used stage name of "Lincoln" during WW I. One of the 5 original members of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1932. Member of the "Secret Six". Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. SAM President 1938-39. Died of cancer. SAM Hall of Fame. See Lewis Ganson, Dai Vernon's Tribute to Nate Leipzig (1963, 192pp) & Victor Farelli, Thanks to Leipzig! (1948, 53pp). Tricks in Sphinx, LR, & HMM. [MUM2/97;Pr;Wal;Ch;Jinx#31;Ho;WWM; Magic7/04,6/06,11/07;HMM12/53]

name: Leipziger, Nathan
bio: See: "Leipzig, Nate"

name: Leirpoll, Jarle
bio: (Norway: 26 Jul 1963-) Freelance filming & editing for TV. Semi-pro magician with parlor & close-up. Invented Card in Mousetrap (1985). 1997 Norwegian Magic Circle Magician of the Year. Articles in Genii, Magic, Pegasus, Arcane (France), Magiens Verden, etc. Wrote Pocket Power (1995, 64pp; with translations in German, Italian, & French). [Wh01]

name: Leité, A[velino Alberto de Carvalho Lorenzo]
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 31 Aug 1923-7 Aug 1981) Amateur. Active in Portuguese magic associations & conventions. Articles in Quatro Ases. [Cam]

name: Leitensdorfer, [John] Eugene
bio: (Brent, Switzerland: 21 Oct 1772-11 Mar 1845) Stage name of Gervasio Probasio Santuari. Moved to USA in 1809. Pro since 1814. Wrote Ventriloquism Explained; And Juggler's Tricks or Legerdermaine Exposed (Amherst: Amherst College, 1834, 156pp). Died in Missouri. Bio is Roger Linden, John Eugene Leitensdorfer (1994, 18pp). [Collectors' Forum10/93;Ch]

name: Leith, June
bio: (Thurso, Scotland: fl.1980s) 1986 British Ladies Magical Champion (Blackpool). Specialty: a music-mine act where a puppet comes alive in a toy shop.

name: Lele, Dr K[eshav] B[hashav]
bio: (Satara, Bombay Province, India: 1884-23 May 1963) Surgeon. Amateur magician as "Master Key". Founder-editor of The Indian Magician 1932-37, which was the 1st magic magazine in India; & Marathi Magic Monthly 1950-51. Wrote magic books in Marathi.

name: Lemano
bio: (Marianka, Poland: 1922-1987) Stage name of Roman Lemanik. Pro illusionist & manipulator. [Mec;Nad]

name: Lemare, Paul
bio: See: Nix, John B.

name: Lemmy, David
bio: (Newark-on-Trent, England: 7 Jan 1905-Aug 1975) Aka "Ali Bey". Businessman and amateur magician. In 1945 turned pro with spectacular illusion act.

name: Lenahan, John
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Pro street magician in USA & Europe. Also does close-up. Video (1985).

name: Lénard, Dr Vilmos
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 2 Mar 1885-early 1945) Physician in Budapest. Amateur magician. Major collector of magic. In 1924 co-founded the Magyar Amateur Mágusok Egyesülete, the leading magic club for amateurs in Hungary between the world wars. Teacher of William Feher, Arpad Romek, & Harry Silan. Discovered the synagogue records of Houdini's birth in Pest. Murdered by the Germans at end of WW II.

name: Lendvai, Géza
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 29 Dec 1953- ) Learned in 1969. Pro comedy magician since 1972. Private collector (mainly posters & playbills) as "Büvésh-Archiv" [Magic Archiv] in Budapest since 1978. In USA in 1992. Wrote Zauber ausschneidung anfäuer 13+1 Produktionen aus Papier, Vol.I (1984). [Wh2]

name: Lenert, Tina
bio: (Caracas, Venezuela: 6 Jan 1948- ) Of American parents. Moved to USA. Studied mime in Los Angeles. Pro mime who since the mid-1970s gradually added magic to her distinctive stage act. Married Mike Caveney in 1979. 1988 Desert Magic Seminar 3rd Prize. 1991 Dragon Award to Tina & Mike. [Wat]

name: Lenier, Jules
bio: (New York City, NY: 1929- ). Learned magic at age 11. Pro since age 17. Demonstrator in both Joe Berg's & Bert Green's magic shops in Hollywood. Dealer ("Magic Eye Magic") in 1965 when he was mentor of J. Paul Moore. 1st editor of Talisman 1970 (Resida, California). 1977 AMA Close-up Magician of the Year. AMA Board of Directors 1980-82. Wrote The Complete Hypnotic Act (1974, 30pp). Articles in Talisman. Also authored several non-magic books & magazine articles. Husband of "Minnette" (see). [Mag]

name: Lenox, Professor
bio: (England: fl.1850s) Aka "Wizard of the South". Toured Australia in 1854 & 1856, the latter with lavish apparatus made by Legrand of Paris. [Wal] SEE: Hilliar, William J.

name: Lenz
bio: See: Allen, Len

name: Lenz, Ismail
bio: See: Lenz, Robert

name: Lenz, Robert
bio: (Wiesbaden, Germany: 6 Apr 1849-1912) Son of a croupier in Wiesbaden. Pro illusionist in Russia. Toured Persia. Aka "Ismail Lenz" & "Roberta". Houdini's main detractor when the latter was in Moscow in 1903. Died in the Caucasus. [Vo56;Dif;Mec;Hou]

name: Lenz, Sidney S[imon]
bio: (near Chicago, Illinois: 12 Jul 1873-1960) Retired wealthy from lumber business before age 27 and turned to whist in 1909. International whist & bridge champion and major contributor to the popularity of bridge. Wrote many short stories with bridge settings. Skilled amateur sleight-of-hand artist in New York City. He declined to play card games for stakes because of his ability to deal "seconds". First amateur elected honorary member of the SAM. Leon, The Great (New York City, NY: 5 Aug 1876-13 Mar 1951) Stage name of Leon Harry Levy, aka "Chunda Hula" & "Kadan Sami". Top pro vaudeville illusionist. Played Rio de Janeiro in 1909 (as "Transformista Leon"), the London Palladium in 1915, the New York Palace in 1925, & the New York Hippodrome 1928 (at $1,000 per week). Invented Fire and Water (1913), the Death Ray Gun (1921), & the Light Bulb Cabinet (1928). Retired by illness around 1931 to live in Hollywood where he became a Mason & member of Los Magicos. In 1937 all his apparatus (3 tons) was sold for $950 to Les Levante. Thru the 1940's again became active by inventing, designing, building, and selling apparatus. SAM Hall of Fame. Father of Leon M. Leon and grandfather of Les Arnold. See Eugene Gloye (ed), The Great Leon's Miniature Haunted House (1960, 34pp). Bio is Mike Caveney, The Great Leon: Vaudeville Headliner (1987, 133pp). [Pr;Mo;Ho]

name: Leon, Leon M[arcus]
bio: (Brockton, Massachusetts: 27 Jan 1903-15 Jun 1998) Born Leon Marcus Levy, legally changed in 1929. Inspired & taught by father The Great Leon for whom he worked as a stage assistant until 1924 when he moved to Hollywood & entered the movie industry as a sound technician. Thence a hobbyist magician. Uncle of Les Arnold. Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, etc. [Genii8/85;Mag;Wh2]

name: Leon, Prince
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Worked a sideshow-type comedy magic act with fellow-midget Gus Wayne as his assistant.

name: Leonardi, Professor
bio: See: Lebram, Ludwig

name: Leonardi, Pian
bio: See: Heubeck, Georg

name: Leoni, Julius
bio: See: Sundman, Julius

name: Leony
bio: (Barreiro, Portugal: 2 Oct 1935- ) Stage name of Leonel Carlos Paulino Campos. Pro comedy magic. Moved to Brazil in 1975, working clubs. [Cam]

name: Lepass
bio: (Bulgaria: fl.1960s) Stage name of Assen Lepov. Pro stage magician & manipulator in Sofia. AFAP Master Magician. [Bou]

name: LePaul, Paul
bio: (Olney, Illinois: 2 Aug 1900-8 [sic] Jun 1958) Stage name of Paul Shields Braden since 1928. Inspired in 1917 seeing Nate Leipzig. Pro cardman (manip & tricks) since 1920, first in vaudeville, then hotels & nightclubs. Played the New York Palace twice in 1933. Adviser on Hollywood movies Miracles for Sale (1939) & The Illusionist (c1939) and had a bit part in Eternally Yours (1939). In WW II toured with USO in Europe, Africa, & Japan. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1955. Toured Europe with USO in 1956. Retired by cancer in 1957, dying in St. Louis. Invented Cards to Envelope. Pet effect: The LePaul Wallet (invented by Dick Washington). Wrote The Card Magic of LePaul (1949, 230pp; repr 1959) & LePaul Presents the Card Magic of Bro. John Hamman [1958, 47pp]. His act was filmed by M-G-M as a short subject (c1939). [Pr;Monti;Par;HMM6/58;Tay;Ho]

name: LeRoy
bio:
Leroy the Magician (USA: c1892-Jan 1953) Stage name of Leroy S. Lowner. Pro stage magician & illusionist. [HMM5/53] Le Roy, The Wizard (USA: 5 Apr 1883-) Stage name of John Franklin Lavins. Minor pro magician & vent. Toured the States with mixed success from 1920 to 1941 whence did school shows across Colorado, Wyoming, Nebraska, & Kansas.

[See also: McCafferty, LeRoy]

name: Leroy, Arthur
bio: (New York City: 15 Nov 1911- ) Stage & pen name of Arthur Leroy Levy. Pro in New York City since 1925 when he became Louis "Pop" Krieger's assistant. US Army Special Services in WWII. Did a marionette-circus-magic show ("Matinees for Moppets") at the 1,200-seat Brooklyn Academy of Music 1952-1960-? (with assistant Peggy Bridges doing marionettes). Wrote Jimmy Shannon's At Your Fingertips (1934, 12pp), Futuristic Fantasies, Magic from A2Z (1934), Grand Finale (1939), & Outline of Mystery (1947). As "Eaton Hope" reviewed for Sphinx until 1953. As "Leroy" tricks & articles in Grant's Inner Circle Magazine, Sphinx, & HMM.

name: Le Roy, H[enri?]
bio: (France: c1875-Jan 1960) Nephew & student of Carmelli. USA correspondent of Journal de la Prestiditateurs.

name: Le Roy, [Jean Henri] Servais
bio: (Spa, Belgium: 4 May 1865-2 Jun 1953) Son of a Belgian hotel manager & a British mother. Pro illusionist since 1886. Married "Talma" in 1890. Toured the USA with Frederick Eugene Powell & Imro Fox as "The Great Triple Alliance" 1898-1900 with Le Roy sometimes doing shadowgraphy as "Signor Charles Marina". Toured the world as "Le Roy, Talma & Bosco" 1904-1930. Briefly in 1910 as partner in Halton & Jansen Co magic shop in Chicago. Pro dealer-manufacturer in London 1910-13, having bought the City Magical Company and renamed it after himself. Retired from stage in 1930 when crippled in an automobile accident. Invented the Three Graces (1890), Duck Pan (by 1904), duck vanish (c1905), Stolen Jam (by 1911), Asrah (by 1914), and possibly the Modern Cabinet. Bio is William V. Rauscher, Monarch of Magic: The Story of Servais LeRoy (1984, 66pp). [Pr;Vo58;Fi;Ch;Wal;Magic5/04,4/06;HMM10/60]

name: Le Roy, W[illiam] D[avis]
bio: (La Salle, Illinois: 5 Aug 1862-10 Jun 1919) Pro concert violinist since age 16. Learned magic at age 19. Pro magic debut in San Francisco in 1885. Aka "Will Norman". Moved to Boston in 1887. Major pro magic dealer (as "W.D. Le Roy") in Boston 1893-1910. Issued catalogs of from 64 to 212 pages. The shop (which also housed his Boston School of Magic) was on the 2nd floor at 103 Court Street. Le Roy was the 1st to market (and name) Burling Hull's famous Svengali & Mene-Tekel gaffed decks (both in 1909). Also marketed "The Great Cagliostro" (= Balsamo) Card Trick" (since 1908) & "Chromatic" cards (since 1909). Lived in Chicago 1910-13. Returned to Boston where reopened his shop (at original address) 1913 until his death. Joe Frustaglia was employed to make feather flower & tin props. Died in his Boston home. [Albo95;Han,pp.11,14,65-66;Magic10/03]

name: Leschot, Jean-Frédéric
bio: (Switzerland?: 1746-1827) Watchmaker and builder of famous automata & singing birds in Chaux de Fonds, Switzerland, in partnership with Pierre Jaquet-Droz who was his adoptive father. NOTE: dates also given as 1747-1824. [Hou]

name: Lesiowski, Edward
bio: (San Francisco, California: 12 Nov 1907- ) Of Polish descent. Pro in vaudeville with cards, watches, eggs, & spirit cabinet. [WWM]

name: Lesley, Ted
bio: (Düren, Rhineland, West Germany: 1 Aug 1937-24 Oct 2008) Stage name of Friedrich Karl "Teddy" Helzel since 1955. Learned in 1948 from school teacher Carl Bornhausen. Originally a pro actor in film. Then, since 1974, pro stage & close-up magician & mentalist since 1974. Pet magic effects: Bill in Cig, Linking Fingerrings, Coin in Bottle, Credit-Card Card Trick, & Rising Cards. Pet mental effects: The Delsey-Miracle, The Pegasus Page, Psychometry, and Q&A. Magic supervisor for 1978 movie The Magician of Lublin. Invented Working Performer's Marked Deck (1981), Credit-Card Card Trick (1985), Vanishing TV (1985, by black art), Working Performer's Hydrostatic Glass (1987), Delsey Miracle (1988), Automatic Pegasus-Page (1988), etc. Collector of Himber props. General manager with partner (Bernd Martin Langschied) of a theatrical booking agency & show production company ("Magic Productions Show-Service GMBH") in West Berlin since 1981. PEA Mentalist of the Year 1992 & PEA Dunninger Award 1992. Wrote Das Markierte Spiel (1982), English tr as Marked: The Marked Deck Manual (1983; enlarged ed 1987, 52pp, as Ted Lesley's Working Performer's Marked Deck Manual); The Kismet Connection (1986, 27pp); & Paramiracles (1994, 294pp; Engl tr by Bill Palmer & Oliver Erens). Articles in Magische Welt, Genii, Magigram, Spell-Binder, & Magick. TV bits. [MUM10/96:Wat:Wh21] [MUM10/96;Wat;Wh2]

name: Lespinasse
bio: (Espinasse-Vozelle, France: 6 Feb 1839-1906) Stage name of Joseph Baugie. Minor pro, originally as "Baugy d'Espinasse", later as "Lespinasse".

name: Lesprit [pronounced leh-SPREE]
bio: (France: fl.1830s) Pro street conjuror in Paris with Cups-and-Balls. Mentioned by Robert-Houdin. Lesta, The Great (USA: 7 Jun 1888-1981) Stage name of Clifford L. "Cliff" Jones. Minor pro travelling school-show magician in South in 1920s-50s. His assistant c1930 was Tommy Martin. Inspired Clare Cummings & Bob Ellis's Out to Lunch trick c1944. [Pr;Ho] Lester, Harry "The Great" (Poland: 8 Sep 1876-14 Jul 1956) Stage name of Marian [sic] Czajkowski, aka "Kaloofra". Moved to USA. Pro vaude & carnival illusionist. Played Vancouver in 1954. [Tay;HMM7/52]

name: Lester, Jerry
bio: (USA: 1911-Mar 1995) Pro rowdy comedian & semi-pro comedy magician. His career peaked as MC of Broadway Open House TV show, 1950-51. [HMM5/51]

name: Lester, Leslie
bio: (Manchester, England: 1905-16 Aug 1968) Stage name of Herbert Leslie Farmer. Pro manipulator with cards & cigs in variety theaters throughout Britain.

name: Le Tort, Professor Joseph H.
bio: (Sweden: 1825-) Pro by 1851. Worked as late as 1875. [Vo58]

name: Le Tort, Nils
bio: (Denmark: 30 Apr 1856-7 Feb 1929) Stage name of Niels Jacobsen. Pro. Authored Prof. Le Torts berømte Tryllekunster (1914). [Vo58]

name: Letta, André
bio: (Scotland: -29 Jun 1957) Stage name of Andrew Letta, "The Scottish Court Magician". Pro magician, puppeteer, vent. [Daw2]

name: Levani
bio: See: Esler, James A.

name: Levante, Esme [pronounced leh-VAHNT]
bio: (Australia: 27 Nov 1924-1989) Stage name of Esme Ray Kathleen Cole. Learned at age 5 assisting pro father "Les Levante" & with featured act in latter's show from 1942. Pro comedy magic with her own cabaret act from 1954 until retired in 1968 to run a theatrical agency in Sydney, Australia. [Mar]

name: Levante, Les [pronounced leh-VAHNT]
bio: (Sydney, New South Wales, Australia: 5 Mar 1892-21 Jan 1978) Stage name since 1921 of Leslie George Cole, aka "The Great Levante". Raised in Wangaratta, Victoria. Taught by Tom Selwyn. Semi-pro illusionist 1910-20, thence pro. In 1919 married Gladys Costin who became his musician & shadowgraphist (see under Gladys Cole). Toured Far East & Pacific islands 3 times in period 1920-c1933. Lived in England 1933-1940. Bought (for $950) all 3-tons of The Great Leon's apparatus in 1937 & slowly added it to his show. In 1940 returned to Australia, touring New Zealand 3 times. British Ring Past President. 1973 AMA Performing Fellowship. Retired in 1975 at age 83. 1977 AMA Masters Fellowship. Father of Esme Levante. Bio is Kent Blackmore, Levante: His Life No Illusion. NOTE: Surname often misgiven by himself as "Vante-Cole". [Pr;Wal;Le;Fu2;Ho;WWM]

name: Lever, Derek "Dynamite
bio: (Manchester, England: 30 Aug 1937-) Aka "Derek Jones". Learned at age 11 from an Ernest Sewell magic set. Billed at age 11 as "World's Youngest Fire Eater". Pro comedy magician, fire eater, & illusionist since 1953. Dealer ("Taurus Magic Supply" in Manchester and, later, Wyre) since 1974. Founder & organizer of the British Magical Championships held annually in Blackpool since 1986. Opened the Tommy Cooper Joke Shop in Blackpool in 1990. President British Ring 1997-98. Wrote Stranger than Fiction (1961), Jack Hughes World of Magic (1981), & Ken Brooke & Friends (1987). Edited Magic Mag 1981-86. Column, "A Dealers View of Magic", in The Budget, 1982-present. [LR1/98;Wh2]

name: Leveridge, Mark [Graham], AIMC
bio: (Bexley Hill, Kent, England: 25 Feb 1956-) Learned in 1963 from Al Koran booklets in breakfast cereal box. Former teacher. Semi-pro magic dealer since 1977. Since 1981 a full-time pro close-up & cabaret magician & dealer. 1981 British Ring Zina Bennett Cup. Dealer in Bath, then Exeter, England. Several tours in Europe & twice in USA. Marketed many of own inventions thru his firm. Wrote In a Flap (1976), More Flapping (1980), The Art of Hopping Tables (1984), The Magic Party (1988), British Close Up Magic Symposium Book (1989, 56pp), The 2nd British Close Up Magic Symposium (1991, 62pp), The 3rd British Close Up Magic Symposium (1993, 52pp), plus many pamphlets, lecture notes, etc. Articles in Abra, Magigram, MUM, Magic Manuscript, & Genii. 4 TV bits. [MUM1/92;Wh2]

name: Levine, Harry
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 20 Jul 1963-) Learned at age 6 from magic set. Pro close-up magician since age 20. Tricks in Apocalypse, Trapdoor, & in books by Lorayne, etc. [Lo;Wh2]

name: Lewchuk, Professor Nicholas P.
bio: (Ukraine, Russian Empire: 1896-26 Jul 1989) Immigrated to Canada with parents in 1902. Photographer, sculptor, artist, printer, builder, & inventor. Midway owner. Early IBM Member (#850). Worked with Joe Ovette. Built the famous welcome statue in Canora, Saskatchewan, where he died. Autobio is Lewchuk's Creative Magic (1987, 358pp). [Bo3]

name: Lewin, Nicholas Ralph "Nick
bio: (Thames Ditton, England: c1952-) Started performing at age 11. Met his first magical mentor, Ken Brooke, at age 15. Studied theatre at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama. Became a fulltime comedy magician in 1969, and did his first cruise in 1970. Moved to LA in 1974. First appeared on television on "The Merv Griffin Show" in 1979, and performed his own version of the Linking Finger Rings, now his signature effect. Has since appeared on many TV shows as a variety performer and also as an actor in such shows as "Dynasty," "Trapper John" and "Amazing Stories." In the 1980s produced international corporate events based on magical themes. In this role he was able to feature many of his favorite magicians, including Shimada, Norm Nielsen, Magic Christian, Albert Goshman, Bruce Cervon and Chuck Jones. In 1995 created “Comedy Magic,” the first one-man afternoon show in Las Vegas. This ran at the Maxim Hotel for five years. In 1975, co-edited “Sleight of Crime,” a successful book for the general public. Since 2006, has written “Meetings with Remarkable Magicians,” a weekly column in Magic New Zealand ezine. Since 2007 has written a similar column for “The Linking Ring,” and in 2008 received their award for best columnist. [LR11/97; Mag]

name: Lewis, Albert E.
bio: (England: fl.1910s) Manager of Hamley's Magical Salon c1912-14. Aka "Yelma" & "Yelmah". Wrote Tricks of To-day (1914, as "Yelma").

name: Lewis, Angelo John
bio: See: "Hoffmann, Professor"

name: Lewis, Bob
bio: (Winston-Salem, North Carolina: 9 Jun 1909-15 Feb 1986) Became interested in magic in 1936 while working as a show-business dancer. Pro comedy magician & banjo player. Top comedy magic act working variety 1940s-70s with assistant-wife Ginny (died 1988). They were regulars on the Ed Sullivan and Gary Moore TV shows. Co-invented (with Clare Cummings) Idiot Rope (1954). [LR3/86]

name: Lewis, Charles
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Pro with paper magic. Played St. George's Hall in 1923.

name: Lewis, Eric C[harles]
bio: (Northampton, England: 23 Nov 1908-6 Jun 1993) Inspired at age 11 seeing a busker. Semi-pro to pro magician. Aka "Yung Lu" 1936-39. Operated Magikraft Studios, a small workshop in Northampton making small apparatus 1946-52 when switched to mechanical display work. Aka "The Great Zonzo" 1952-60. Moved to California in 1968. With Jim Simon of Worth Magic Novelty Company in Sun Valley 1968-70; in own workshop 1970-72, as builder for Hollywood Magic, Albo, & Mark Wilson; worked on Robert Albo's apparatus collection in Oakland 1972-73; again with Simon 1973-75; with John Gaughan & Associates in Los Angeles 1975-81 when retired from active public performing. Thence busy as consultant, lecturer, researcher, & writer. SAM Hall of Fame. Father of Martin Lewis. AMA Best Stage Magician 1970 (shared) & 1975. 1974 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1985 AMA Masters Fellowship. 1985 SAM Hall of Fame. 1989 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award (shared with Peter Warlock). Invented Fantastic Frame (1940), co-invented (with Cyro) Lighted Bulbs from Mouth (1941), & the Twister illusion (1978). the Twister illusion (1978). Prolific author (21 books), including Well I Never! (1931), Magical Mentality (1934), Magic As We Do It (1935, 28pp, with Dan Bellman), The Magic of 1936 (1936, with Dan Bellman), The Magic of 1937 (1937, 73pp), Magic for Moderns (1937, 39pp), Studies in Mystery (1941, 35pp), More Studies in Mystery (1941, 41pp), Modus Operandi (1943, 67+142pp), Magic to Entertainment (1946, 72pp), Open Sesame (1947, 154pp, with Wilfred Tyler; 1969), The Oriental Magic of the Bambergs, Vol.1 (1973, 228pp, with Albo & Bamberg), Martin's Miracles (1985), & P.T. Selbit (1989, with Peter Warlock). Edited (with Tony Branson) Personality Patter 1943-46 (30 issues) & The Masque as house organ 1947-48 (2 issues). Memoir is Fifty Years of Magic (3 vols: 1980, 1981, 1983, 213+254+237pp), informally known from their subtitles as "The Miracles Trilogy". Illustrator of his own books as well as those by others. Wrote over 200 articles for various magazines including Abra, Genii, & Linking Ring. [Albo95;Daw94;Mag;Wh2]

name: Lewis, Henry, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 12 Oct 1919- ) Learned in 1935 from library books. Auctioneer until retired in 1987. In Army performed as "El Duarte, Mayfair's Man of Mystery". Semi-pro mentalist since 1945. MIMC 1986. Executive Curator of the Magic Circle collection Articles in Magic Circular, Abra, Budget, & Magigram. [MC6/90;Wh2]

name: Lewis, James [nmn] "Jim
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 1 Jun 1953-) Moved to Los Angeles at age 12. Learned at age c13 from tricks at Joe Berg's shop. Pro close-up & stand-up magician since age 26, initially at fairs. Now works private & corporate parties. Also mail-order dealer of exclusive effects in Santa Monica since c1984. Marketed P. Howard Lyons' Mis-Made Dollar Bill c1984. Invented Visible Coins thru Glass Table (1986). Wrote Thinking About Magic (c1983). Tricks in Magic Arts Journal & Genii. Video: Million Dollar Mysteries (1992). [Mag;Wh]

name: Lewis, Martin [James]
bio: (Northampton, England: 1 Sep 1946-) Inspired seeing father Eric C. Lewis. Moved with family to California in 1968. Learned at age 21 from Bruce Cervon and others. Pro. Invented Sidewalk Shuffle in 1971. House magician at the Magic Cellar 1971-73 where he did close-up. Since then works mainly stand-up in comedy clubs, cabaret, revue shows (Las Vegas & Reno), & cruise ships. 1976 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. In 1985 as "Shuffler" co-founded (with Steve Burton) the MicroMagicon, the first on-line computer conference of magicians. Reopened his father's Magikraft Studios in Moreno, California 2-2004. See Phil Goldstein, Martin Lewis Notations (1982, 10pp); & Eric C. Lewis, Martin's Miracles (1985, 1550). Tricks in Talisman Arcane See Phil Goldstein, Martin Lewis Notations (1982, 10pp); & Eric C. Lewis, Martin's Miracles (1985, 155pp). Tricks in Talisman, Arcane. 1 video (1994). [Bo#253;Mag]

name: Lewis, Shari
bio: (New York City, NY: 17 Jan 1934-2 Aug 1998) Stage name of Phyllis Hurwitz. Inspired by & learned from pro father "Doc" Abraham B. Hurwitz her 1st magic trick at age 2½ & mind-reading at age 4. Learned vent from books at age 11. Debut at age 2½ doing Troublewit and at age 14 had own New York TV show. Pro magician to pro ventroloquist, for which latter she became nationally famous on TV in 1957 when as Shari Greenjeans she created her vent dummy "Lambchop" act on the Captain Kangaroo TV show. Died of uterine cancer. Co-authored (with father) Magic for Non-Magicians (1975). Edited Presto! Press (1976-78, 6 issues) [Mag;CA]

name: Lewis, Thomas C. "Tom
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Wealthy jewellery store owner in New Haven, Connecticut. Amateur magician. In 1917 backed John A. Petrie in founding the Petrie-Lewis Manufacturing Co. in New Haven. Soon pulled out to retire to California.

name: Lewis, Trevor [Alun], MIMC
bio: (Holyhead, Gwynedd, Wales: 1 Dec 1932-) Learned in 1945 from magic set, library books, & Liverpool Magic Circle. Chief Engineer Officer with Sealink (retired). Semi-pro comedy close-up & stage magician. Also does kid-shows. Has played throughout Europe & visited USA 8 times. 1969 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. 1971 British Ring Zina Bennett Close-up Trophy. 1976 FISM 1st prize in card magic, the first Briton to take this award. 1980 Crandall Trophy. Wrote 4 books on kid-show magic, including More Party Pieces (1985, 54pp) & Still More Party Pieces (1990, 50pp). Tricks in Abra, Pabular, New Pentagram, Magic Circular, Magic Magazine, Magigram, Linking Ring (+ 1978 one-man "Parade"), Genii, etc. Welsh TV series "Triciau Trevor" [Trevor's Tricks]. Audio. See Phil Willmarth, Trevor Lewis Close-Up (1981). Video (1990). [Australian Magic Monthly6/90; Magigram6/89; Abra#2328;Wh2]

name: Lewis, Vern
bio: See: Wickes, Samuel L. Whittington

name: Lezama, Frank
bio: (Puebla, Mexico: 9 Jul 1908-27 Oct 1987) Stage name of Francisco "Frank" LEZAMA MEZA. Taught as child by uncle Gabriel Romero, an international pro magician & hypnotist. Pro nightclub manip act throughout USA 1936-52. Founded Mexico's 1st magic club in 1940. Pro dealer 1952 until his death, his son & widow continuing the business. 1984 Order of the Magic Lamp. Invented Ever Lit Magic Candle (c1950). Wrote Mystérios de la Magia (1940, 178pp), Prestigitacion y Sus Mystérios (1945, 225pp). Tricks in several USA & Spanish-language magic journals, including Genii. [Wh3]

name: L'Homme Masqué
bio: See: "Homme Masqué, L'"

name: Li-Chang
bio: See: Forns Jordana, Juan

name: Li-Chung-Soo
bio: See: Younger, Edmund

name: Li Chung Soy
bio: See: Henry, S. S.

name: Li-Ho-Chang
bio: See: "Chang"

name: Li-King-Si
bio: (Paris, France, 1906-) Stage name of Édouard Cassel. Debut in 1926 in French music halls with classic magic as "Farhat". Pro with pseudo-Chinese act (with assistant "Mi-Chi-Ko") in the 1940s-50s with a 1957 TV appearance in the USA. [Dif;Ch]

name: Li Sing Foo
bio:
(Poland?: 1936-) From a well-known circus family of Chinese descent. Pro illusionist. Active in Polish circus & local amusement centers. Prize winner at magic festivals in Czechoslovakia & Bulgaria.

[See also: Hartop, A. W.]

name: Li-U-Fa, Grażyna Falkowska
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1953-) Illusionist. Works mainly in Polish circus.

name: Liberg, Olle Oson
bio: (Sweden: 23 Mar 1921-) Amateur magician in Stockholm as "Sir Teen". Wrote Trollkarlens ABC (1944), Cigarrett- och tändstickstricks (1944), 25 mynttricks (1944), Reptricks (1945), Modern magi för amatörer (1948), & Hokus Pokus efter Middan (1950). [St]

name: Libertz, Arnold
bio: See: "Marvillo"

name: Libonati, Thomas “Tom
bio: (USA: -1952) Lived in Chicago. Graphic artist & amateur magician by 1940. Illustrated Ovette's Tricks and Illusionettes (1944).

name: Liebenow, Erhard [Paul]
bio: (Danzig [now Gdansk], Germany [now Poland]: 19 Feb 1935- ) Learned at age 9 by contact with pros. Banished with parents to West Germany after WW II. Public relations manager in Bonn since 1960s. Semi-pro stage & close-up & lecturer since 1963. Toured USA (1971, 72, 75, 80), Europe (regularly), Canada (1975), Brazil (1977), & Japan (1987). 1975 Baden-Baden 3rd prize in close-up; 1975 MZvD 2nd prize in card magic; 1986 MZvD Writer of the Year. Wrote in German Royal Flush (1976, 142pp) & Grand Ouvert (1978, 78pp). Also 4 lectures notes in English & 3 in German. Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, Aladin, Journal de la Prestidigitation, Cardini Club Revue, Sele Magic, Ilusionismo, Triks, De Magier, Coelhinho Magico, Cary Mary, Lodski Dom Kultury, Abra, MUM, Genii, Magic Around the World, Linking Ring (1 Parade), Swami, etc. [LR3/95; Magie1/83; Genii1/80; Mec; Des; Cam; Wh 2]

name: Liebholz, Hermann
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 1838-1875) Former wood-turner. Pro magician in Hamburg where he made & sold a famous line of magic sets. His daughter was adopted by Ernst Basch. [Vo56; CMM8/08]

name: Lightner, J[oseph] G. "Joe
bio: (Napoleon, Mississippi: 1 Apr 1882 [or 1884]-31 Jul 1946) Pro as "Lightner the Wizard" on Chautauqua & Redpath circuits from 1906 to 1914 when switched to politics, becoming mayor of Odessa, Missouri. Kept active as amateur magician. 3rd & last Editor of The Seven Circles 1934. [WWM]

name: Lilge-Oeser, Amanda
bio: See: Oeser, Marie

name: Linardini, Harry
bio: (Auxerre, Yonne, France: 17 Jun 1891-14 Nov 1922) Stage name of Paul-Lucien Linard. Proescapist since 1912. [Dif]

name: Lincoln
bio: See: "Leipzig, Nate"

name: Linda
bio: See: Jonason, Linda

name: Lindblom, Gustaf
bio: (Sweden: 19 Aug 1883-16 Mar 1976) Civil engineer in Stockholm. Amateur magician. Founding-President of Swedish Magic Circle 1946-51.

name: Linden, Anthony Vander
bio: See: Vander Linden, Anthony

name: Linden, Herbert von der
bio: (Germany: 8 Jun 1921- ) Magician as "Von Kalvani". Magic dealer-manufacturer in Detmold,

name: Lindgren, Gerhard
bio: (Sweden: 16 Jun 1913-1 May 1980) Book publisher in Katrineholm. Semi-pro magus as "Eugen el Cester". Toured Finland in 1952.

name: Lindgren, Karl Gerhard
bio: (Finland: 1880-10 Jan 1944) Pro actor turned magician, working as "Mr Bluffman" in cabarets & private parties. After his death his props & books went to Julius Sundman. [St;Vo58;Dif]

name: Lindhorst, Will L.
bio: (USA: 22 Apr 1890-7 Mar 1954) Pro since 1908-1911 when he joined Thurston show as an assistant. Did own sleight-of-hand act since 1927 when he toured the Orpheum circuit as "The Original Chandu, King of Magic". Hosted "Chandu the Magician" radio show in St. Louis & Cincinnati. Piano salesman. Missouri state Representative 1935-38. Dealer in St. Louis (as, successively, Lindhorst Magic Shop, Lindhorst Magic and Radio Co., Pioneer Magic Studios, & Lindhorst's Magic Den) by 1919 until his death. Wrote A Bag of Tricks [1931], Modern Tricks: A New Bag of Tricks (1934), & Flash Magic (1937), etc. Bio is Roger Linden, Lindhorst, The Man of Mystery (1997, 11pp). [Monti; Collectors' Forum10/93]

name: Ling-Chong
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 20 Apr 1899-17 Dec 1964) Stage name of Octávio José de Matos. Pro illusionist with pseudo-Chinese act since 1934. Toured Europe & Africa. Wrote Ling Chong (Luanda: 1940, 36pp). [Cam]

name: Ling-Fu
bio: See: Forns Jordana, Juan

name: Ling-Kai-Fu
bio: See: Ciuró, Wenceslao

name: Ling Look
bio: See: Guder, Ferdinand

name: Linga Singh
bio: See: Dutt, Amar Nath

name: Linker, Klaas G[eerl]
bio: (Leek, Holland: 13 May 1944-) Learned in 1956. Pro as dealer since he founded Goochelstudio Kali (in Dordrecht) in 1969. Since 1971 sponsors the annual Kali-Day ("Kali-Dag") of Magic, which in 1989 had an attendance of c600. [Wh2]

name: Linn, Colin H[enderson]
bio: (Dunedin, New Zealand: 10 Apr 1934-) Learned at age 13 from books. Director of an Australasian company. Amateur close-up magician, as "Colini" late 1940s-early 1950s. Wrote Stand Up Card Magic & Further Stand Up Magic. [Wh2]

name: Linnhauser, George
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY: 9 Oct 1891-) Learned in 1913. Semi-pro. [Go2]

name: Lino [Ferreira] do Nascimento
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 28 Mar 1866-14 Jun 1928) Amateur illusionist. In 1912 co-founded the Internacional Instituto de Recreações Scientificas. 1927 ASAP Concours Magicus 2nd prize. Tricks in Boletim Mágico (Brazil), O Illusionista (Portugal), Le Prestidigitator (France), Presti (Belgium), etc. Died in Paris. NOTE: Misspelled "Uno Ferreira". [Cam]

name: Lippincott, Jack
bio: (USA: -15 Oct 1994) Professor of psychology. Amateur magician. Did magic at USO shows in early 1940s in St. Louis, Missouri. Invented Quarter Go = Lippincott coin box (1949). Died in St. Louis.

name: Lippincott, Malcom
bio: (USA: 5 Dec 1895- ) Pro since 1915, originally with circus until 1919 when he began touring his own magic act. In 1922 added mind-reading act with assistant-wife Maxine. Did mainly private society shows from 1923 until the Great Depression years of the 1930s when he played mainly schools, theaters, & fairs. [St]

name: Lippy Jr, John D.
bio: (USA: c1897-1967) Pro magician (with degree in chemistry), touring with 5-person illusion show in the 1920s-30s. Wrote Chemical Magic (1930, 103pp; rev ed 1959, 164pp, as Modern Chemical Magic, with Edward L. Palder).

name: Lischke, Oscar E.
bio: (Neustadt, Saxony, Germany: 1835-17 Oct 1903) In 1852 in Hamburg opened a magic shop (in which Charles Arbré became involved much later). It was bought c1890 by E. Chambly. Uncle of Richard "John Olms" (see) Lischke. Died in his hometown. [Roh] Liskcarew, A. J., MMC (Sierra Leone: fl.1910s) Black African. Magician, illusionist, & minor dealer in Freetown, Sierra Leone. (USA: -23 Mar 1987) Pro with a dove, billiard ball, & cigarette act on the MCA circuit in the late 1940s. Close-up in the 1960s. Finally as a bartender-magician in Oakland, California. Trick in Epoptica.

name: Literas, Rodolfo [Raul]
bio: (Argentina: fl.1920s-60s) Aka "Literod". Co-owner (with his brother) of the Bazar Yankee, the only shop with a magic department in Buenos Aires in the mid-1920s & the largest one in the mid-1950s. Attended the 1965 IBM Convention. In 1966 was a founding member of CEDAM's filial in B.A. [Bam,pp.253,295]

name: Literod
bio: See: Literas, Rodolfo

name: Little, George H.
bio: (USA: fl.early 1900s) Minor pro with pseudo-Chinese act as "Ah Foon" until gave that stage name to Harry Usher sometime before 1914. [Pr]

name: Little, [Robert H.] "Bob
bio: (Upper Darby, Pennsylvania: 11 Sep 1931-) Learned as boy from Gilbert magic set. Pro comedy magician since college. Dealer ("Guaranteed Magic") in Hatboro, Pennsylvania, c1958-present. Regularly does dealer shows at European conventions since c1977. Wrote The Lecture Notes of Bob Little (1975, 56pp). [Wh]

name: Littlewood, [Kenneth Guy] "Ken
bio: (Australia: c1924-27 Apr 1990) Learned at age 7. Pro since age 20 working theaters & clubs worldwide. Known for silent dove & manip act. Met his assistant, Toshi, in Japan in 1958 and married her, introducing the sword-suspension into their act. [LR7/90; Mag] Litzau, Edward A. (USA: fl.1930s) Amateur card man. Wrote How It's Done (1938, 36pp), which he privately published but then in 1940 sold all rights to Abbott's.

name: Livingstone, Al
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Stage name of Alfred O. Walgren. Pro manip. [Des]

name: Ljungberg, Gay
