bio: (Halmgstad, Sweden: 28 Feb 1952-) Taught at age c10 by amateur father & reading books. Since 1982 co-proprietor (with wife Birgitta) of Gycklaren--Magic Marketing in Halmgstad. Full-time pro performer since 1983 with family shows & comedy. Pet effects: Thumb Tie, B&R Banknote, & T&R Necktie. 1986 Swedish Champion of Childrens Magic. Wrote Ballong Djur (1983, 16pp), My Way (1984, 20pp), Ballong Konster (1985, 16pp, lecture notes). Edited Magic Master quarterly since 1982. Tricks in Pabular. [Wh5]

name: Lkein, Helmut
bio: (Germany: 11 Jan 1951-) Aka "Brix". 1981 MZvD 1st prize in closeup & closeup magician of the year. [Nad]

name: Llacer Sánchez, José M[ária]
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 26 Jan 1949-) Learned in 1960 from magic set. Close-up magician. Works with partner as "Llacer & Ketty". Pro dealer ("Selecciones Mágicas") in Barcelona, 1973-present. Wrote 53 Trucos con el Falso Pulgar (1980, 91pp; 2 reprints). Articles in Illusionismo & CEDAM. [Xe;Wh2]

name: Llorens
bio: (Tarrega, Lleida, Spain: 12 Apr 1910- ) Born Llorenç CANELLA S. Learned magic at age 9. Moved in 1925 to France where he was renamed Laurent Canellas. Pro with circus, etc, thru Europe. AFAP Bronze Medal 1982 & Gold Medal 1985. [Xe]

name: Lloyd [Albert]) Arthur
bio: (Medford, Massachusetts: 5 Nov 1891- ) Son of Welsh immigrant metal worker. Moved to England as child. Debut at age 16. Billed as "The Human Card Index" & "The Humorous Card Index". Provaude magician since 1910. [Jay;Pr;Dor;Ho]

name: Lloyd, Harold [Clayton]
bio: (Burchard, Nebraska: 20 Apr 1893-8 Mar 1971) Hollywood film comedy star 1914-38. A Mason since 1926 & Shrine Imperial Potentate in 1950. Amateur magician since childhood when learned from tricks in newspapers. Occasionally assisted visiting magicians. Specialized in card magic, despite having lost the thumb & index finger of his right hand in a freak accident in 1919. Member of Los Magicos. Autobio (with Wesley W. Strout) is An American Comedy (1928). Bio is Richard Schickel, Harold Lloyd: The Shape of Laughter (1974). [Katz] NOTE: The trick he is credited with in Jinx #51 was ghosted (with Lloyd's permission) by J.G. Thompson Jr, the editor (Annemann) having found Lloyd's own contributions "terribly old ones that he liked." REF: Abrams (1992), 385.

name: Lloyd, Paul
bio: (USA: 1905-2 [sic] Sep [sic] 1952) Roman Catholic priest. Lived several years in China as a missionary. Then amateur magician in St. Louis, Missouri. Active in IBM as its chaplain.

name: Llusion, Julie
bio: (England: 2 Sep 1960-) Stage name of Julie Proudlove. Learned by age twelve from pro parents, Stanley & Mrs Proudlove. Pro. 1976 Craig Trophy. [Mar]

name: Lobenstern, Stan
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-90s) Dealer ("Rabbit in The Hat Ranch") in Casselberry, Florida.

name: Locke, G.
bio: See: "Warlock, Peter"

name: Lockhart, Will
bio: (Scotland: 1890s) Minor magic dealer & prop maker (Will Lockhart & Company) in Plaistow, Scotland, in 1890s. Wrote The Secrets of Advanced Prestidigitation (London: 1894, 30pp). [Daw94]

name: Loew, Emil [Max], AIMC
bio: (Rotterdam, Holland: 8 Jun 1909-8 Oct 2002) Learned at age 6 from gift magic set. Inspired by Larette. Semi-pro since 1920 as "Emalo". Toured Europe 1927-40 when he was personal friend of Okito, Frakson, Goldin, etc. Moved to USA c1941. Accountant (now retired) Miami Beach, Florida. Since 1967 has been a major magic impresario, bringing to the USA over 60 major European lecturers, including Buckingham, Pavel, & Flip. Originated Magic Carpet Tours in 1970 & Magic Cruises. Edited Emil Loew Magicians Lecturing Service Newsletter 1969-78 & Magic Carpet Gazette 1970 (1 issue). Articles in MUM, Linking Ring, & Pallbearers Review. Autobio is The Joys of Magic (2001, c75pp). [Wh2]

name: Loewy, Prof. Morris
bio: (USA?: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro. Invented Card to Wallet c1905.

name: Logan, Waldo H.
bio: (USA: c1899-Jan 1957) Oil company president in Chicago & treasure hunter. Amateur magician and magic collector. Made a fortune in the mid-1930s as a Chicago stock broker. Prominent in the SAM. Impoverished, he moved to Miami where he worked as a hotel desk clerk until his suicide by sleeping pills. [HMM1/57]

name: Loggie, John
bio: See: "Logrenia, Professor"

name: Logrenia, Professor
bio: (Scotland: c1828-1880) Stage name of John Loggie, aka "Loggie Logrenia, Wizard of Scotland". Minor pro since 1850s. Worked with Sam Sharpley's show in the 1870s. Moved to New York City in 1875. Wrote Logrenia's Wizard Guide [late 1870s, 28pp]. [Pr;Fr;Mo;Vo56]

name: Logrenia, Charles
bio: (Britain: fl.late 1800s-1st decade of 1900s) Son of Prof Logrenia. Minor pro working in oriental costume as "Ali Zada". [CMM12/06,8/08;Pr]

name: Lohrey, Carl S.
bio: (USA: fl.1st decade of 1900s-50s) Pro dealer in Dayton, Ohio, by 1925 to at least 1955. Invented Mis-Made Flag in 1908, Whereisit by 1926, & Glassilkgo in 1927.

name: London, Dr.
bio: See: Calvert, John

name: London, Jack
bio: (USA: -13 Nov 1981) Stage name of Harold "Harry" Rifas. Studied in Abe Hurwitz's group in New York City in 1940s. Pro card magic, mentalism, pocket-picking, & escapes. Invented the Pop-up Tie (1946). The panelists on a 1954 What's My Line failed to guess his profession. Wrote The Superb Mentalism of Jack London (1981, 38pp). [HMM5/54,5/58]

name: London, Ron
bio: (Fort Wayne, Indiana: 26 Dec 1941- ) Stage & radio name since 1964 of Ronald Harry "Ron" Mabis. Learned at age 5 from Xmas magic set. Pro in radio c1963-71. Pro comedy close-up & stand-up magician, escapist, & lecturer since 1971. Has played Magic Castle over 16 times as performer & lecturer. Dealer-manufacturer of magic props in West Lafayette, Indiana. Opening act for such stars as Bob Hope, Pat Paulsen, & Louis Mandrell. Wrote M.C. Handbook (1989, 20pp). Articles in Linking Ring & Genii, plus column in Laugh-Makers. Wrote 3 promotional & advertising booklets. [Wh2]

name: London, Tony
bio: See: "Kardyro, Tony"

name: Londono, Max[imiliano]
bio: (South America: fl.1950s-70s) Moved to USA. Dealer, performer, lecturer, & teacher in New York City. Gave group lessons, Father Jerry Jecewiz being one of his students in the mid-1960s. Invented Milk in Lightbulb (by 1958) & Rainbow Ropes (by 1974). Wrote Eternal String. Disappeared from New York magic scene c1980 amidst many rumors. [HMM9/62 ad]

name: Lonergan, D. J. "Doc
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Opened his "New Moderne Magic Studio" in Chicago in 1933. Wrote Diachylon Deceptions (1934, 24pp).

name: Long, Harvey L.
bio: (San Francisco, California: 16 Apr 1916-25 Dec 1992) With bride Maxine worked as assistants to Jack Gwynne 1941. Pro in journalism & advertising in Seattle, Washington. Semi-promagician. PCAM President 1976-77. Wrote Optical Illusions: It's All In How You Look at It & Fund Raising Magic (1977, 59pp, with Kate Gross). Many articles in magic magazines. Memoir in Charvet (1986), 90-101.

name: LONG Tack Sam
bio: (North China: 1885-7 Aug 1961) Stage name of LONG Tuck Sam, used only on foreign tours. (In Mandarin Chinese his name would be pronounced LUNG T'a-shan, for the three characters dragon-prominent-mountain.) Inspired at age 9 as a run-away with a street magician. Learned age 9-17 as apprentice to Chinese conjurer. Pro magician, juggler, & acrobat, originally as "Tan Kwai" until after his USA debut in 1914. Toured the world with great success: Europe (c1912-14, 1929), USA (1914-21, 1922-23, 1925-27, 1929, 1930, 1932, 1934), England (1922, including twice at the London Coliseum), Australia (1923, 1925, 1928-29, 1931, 1932-33, 1935), New Zealand (1923-24), China (1924-25, 1928, c1931-32), Argentina (1929). His 7 appearances (1915 to 1933) at the New York Palace was an all-time record for a magician there. Retired well-to-do in Linz, Austria. SAM Hall of Fame. His catch-phrase, “Damn clever, these Chinese.” was reportedly coined by him. [Pr;Ch;Wal;Go2;Bo'86;Tay;St;Ho;Bam]

name: Longo, Dimitrius
bio: (Russia: 1888-) Stage name of Dimitry Ivanovich Longo. Fakir in Russian circuses. Famous for Sword Swallowing & Walking on Swords. [Mec]

name: Lonn, Johnny
bio: (Sweden: 17 [sic] Dec 1944- 7 Apr 2013) Stage name of Björn Lönngvist. Pro comedy magician. 1967 FISM 3rd prize for manip. 1969 NMK Nordic Champion. [Mec]

name: Loo, De Yip "Louis
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-90s) Of Chinese parentage. Stage manager for Blackstone. Pro illusionist in Chicago. [Des]

name: Loomis, Dennis [Richard] "Denny
bio: (Manister, Michigan: 31 Aug 1943 – 2 May 2013) Learned at age 5 from Mysto Magic set. Pro illusionist & escape artist since 1970 with full-evening show & at school assemblies. Works with assistant-wife Annette. In late 1980s also starred in Rick Allen's fund-raising shows in northern California. Wrote The Dennis Loomis Cups and Balls Routine (1985, 32pp). Articles in Tops, Linking Ring & MUM. [Wh2]

name: Lopez, Blanca
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Daughter of a Venezuelan newspaperman & printer who immigrated to USA in 1919. Co-owner of the Carlos Lopez Press in Long Island City, New York.  $ 1^{st} $ woman to hold office (1st VP) in the SAM Parent Assembly 1956-57. Worked in magical therapy. Production manager of Hugard's Magic Monthly since 1943-62 & editor 1962-64. [Printing News 10 Oct 59]

name: Lopilato, Anthony M. "Tony
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-80s) Aka "Lato". Pro stage magician. Tricks in Tarbell #5.

name: Loramus
bio: (Tours, France: 6 Nov 1834-9 Jun 1895) Stage name of Alexandre-Charles Dabain. Pro. Pet effect: Self Decapitation. Brother-in-law of Pietro Gallici with whom he founded the Théâtre Gallici-Loramus in Orleans in 1895, just before his retirement & death. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Lorayne, Harry
bio: (lower east side Manhattan, New York City: 4 May 1926-) Professional memory expert. World-famous for his memory systems. Did a Giant Memory act for 20 years in the 1940s-60s. In this field wrote How to Develop a Super-Power Memory (1957, 217pp), which sold 8 million copies in 18 languages; & then 12 others, all best-sellers. Part-time close-up magician. 1975 IBM Star of Magic award. 1981 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1983 SAM Magician of the Year. 1997 Tannen's "Louie" Award. Prolific author in magic including Close-up Card Magic (1962, 272pp), Deck-sterity (1967, 160pp), Reputation Makers (1971, 287pp), Volume 7 (1972, 490pp) of The Tarbell Course in Magic, Rim Shots (1973, 148pp, which is also a force book where 21st word of every trick is "that"), Afterthoughts (1975, 144pp), The Magic Book (1977), Quantum Leaps (1979, 248pp), Best of Friends (2 vols, 1982, 1985, 559+560pp), Star Quality: The Magic of David Regal (1987, 278pp), & Trendsetters (1990, 275pp). See also Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Harry Lorayne (1977, in French) & Richard Vollmer, Lorayne on Cards (2 vols, 1979). Edited-wrote Apocalypse (1978-present, Video segment (1986) & 2 videos (1987 & 1993)). Tricks in New Phoenix, HMM, New Directions, Hex, Linking Ring (2 Parades), Magic Menu, etc. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Lord
bio: (Hungary: 6 Jun 1892- ) Pro manipulator 1920s-30s, mainly in Germany.

name: Lorento, Professor
bio: (USA: fl.1870s) Wrote Amateur Amusements (New York: 1878, 376pp), & Lorenzo's Wizard's Guide; or, Magic Made Easy (New York: [1878], 30pp).

name: Lorenzo, Hugo
bio: (Germany: fl.1890s-1920s) Aka "Svengali". Pro second-sight act, touring USA & Britain since 1895 as, successively, "The Modern Sphinx", "The Svengalis", "The Lawrence Svengali Trio", "The Lorenz Svengali Trio", "Svengali and Trilby", "Svengali and Miss Terry". Played the London Hippodrome in 1900 for 8 weeks & the Sydney Tivoli in 1907. [Pr;Cl]

name: Lorraine, Sid
bio: (St. Neots, Huntingdonshire, England: 24 Apr 1905-15 Oct 1989) Stage name of Sidney Richard Johnson since 1915. Moved to Canada at age 9. Inspired seeing carry Harry Usher do the Sphinx & other tricks. Learned in 1914 by buying carnival slum magic. Commercial artist. Illustrated many magic books, magazines, & catalogs. Semi-pro comedy magician. Billed as "The Magical Chatterbox" on Toronto radio 1930-32. 1977 AMA Best Lecturer. 1982 FFFF roastee. 1984 AMA Literary Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. With wide contacts, a good memory, & fine files, he was a major & generous reference source for many magicians. Invented Slop Shuffle (in 1924) & Triumph (by 1937) and marketed some 50 effects: Jumbo Bill (c1925), Caught (1927), The Black Queen (by 1928), Nickel Trick (1930), Snappy (1931), Daddy Long Legs (1933), Magic Blotter (1933), Jig Saw Card Trick (1933), Sealed Message (1933), Liquor Cards (1935), ABC Trick (1935; 2nd version 1947), Drunk Card Trick (1937), Cigarette Case (1940), Snake's Alive (1942), Sugar Short (1942), Victory (1942), We Predict (1942), Mug of Coffee (1943), Ration Card Trick (1943), Ribboniffy (1943), Dine Out (1938), Kilroy Turns Up (1946), Space Cards (1950), Wet & Dry (1958), Chinese Folder (1965), Eye Spy (1966), Thumb Fun (1966), 1-2-3 Memory Trick (1967), Egyptian Mystery (1967), Image (1968), Moon Rock (1969), L.S.P. (1970), Eyes Have It (1971), Fold'n Fun (1971), Shoo-Shoo Fun (1971), Double Feature (1972), Magic Manor (1973), Blank Surprise (1974), Three Flies (1975), Handi-Ruff (1976), Sensicard (1976), Wax Works (1977), Sh-h-h-h--Sleep--Sleep (1978), Daily Discovery (1980), It's a Date (1980), Mirror Image (1980), Tiny Card Trickery (1980), Penny and Nickel (1982), Psychic Phish (1984). Wrote Patter (1938; 3rd ed 1944, 64pp), A Magician in the House (1939, 43pp), More Patter (1950, 107pp), Gags, Routines, & Patter (1962, 64pp), & Sid Lorraine's Scrapbook (1985, 168pp). Edited-published 5 Reference Files (1975-85). Many tricks, articles, & columns in 18 magazines, particularly Linking Ring (since 1924), Tops (column 1933-57), Hugard's Magic Monthly, Ibidem, Swami, & New Tops. (column 1961-89). Audios (1978, 1979, 1980, 1983). See [Jay Marshall], Sid Lorraine: The Early Stuff (1973); [Larry Silverman & Norm Wyvern], A Tribute to Sid Lorraine (1985, 28 unnumbered pp). [LR6/95; Bo#220;Se;MC10/82;Th;LR7/26;LR9/43; MUM3/84;Wh]

name: Lorzo, Dale
bio: (Eureka, California: 31 Dec 1947- ) Stage name of Lornell Dale Knaus, son of Swiss immigrants. Inspired seeing Mandrake show. Learned in 1961. Pro stage & platform magician & kid-show performer since 1970. Moved to Sacramento, California, c1971. Since 1973 does local magic shows for McDonald's (as "Ronald McDonald"), etc. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Lossau Romano, Hardy
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 2 Jul 1931- ) Stage name of Hardy Lossau, aka "Romano". Pro stage magician in East Germany with assistant-wife Zwetana. Toured Europe, Asia, & Africa with his full-evening show. Worked with parrots. [Win]

name: Louine, Harry
bio: (LeMars, Iowa: 24 Dec 1880- ) Stage name of Louis N. Miller [not, as Taylor writes, Harry Louine Miller]. Pro vaude magician since 1904, billed as "King of Coins", a title he took from Tommy Downs. Invented Dissolvo (by 1940). [Tay]

name: Loudini
bio: See: Zgoda, Lou

name: Louis, Nat
bio: See: Tannen, Lou

name: Louperti
bio: (Halle, Germany: 22 Nov 1907-7 Jun 1985) Stage name of Harry Scharlach. Pro since 1928. Specialized since 1934 in manip act with cigars, billed as "Der Mann mit den 100 Brasil". Lived & worked in East Germany after WW II. Played the East Berlin Friedrichstadtpalast in 1946 & 1953. His long-time assistant-wife Charlotte died in 1966. Retired in 1978. [Win]

name: Love
bio: See: Milander, Love Björn

name: Love, Edward G.
bio: (Britain: 31 Aug 1905-16 Feb 1983) Amateur, specialized in card-fanning. Wrote Card Fan-Tasies (1946, 50pp; 3 reprints), a classic. Trick in Intermagic.

name: Love, William Edward
bio: (London, England: 1806-1867) Son of a wealthy London merchant. Left school at age 15 to become a pro ventriloquist (specialized in "distant voice"), polyphonist, & quick-change artist. Toured England, Belgium, & France. Famous from 1836 until forced into retirement by paralysis in 1858. Bio is George Smith, Memoirs and Anecdotes of Mr. Love (1831, 48pp). [Daw; Magic8/07]

name: Lovell, Simon
bio: (Chelmsford, London: fl. since 1970s) Con artist until his early 30s. Then close-up comedy magician. Noted for second-dealing. 1987 British Magical Champion of Comedy. Moved to USA in 1993. See Walt Lees, Simon Lovell's Magic of Showbusiness (1982). Wrote Close-up Magic to Tap Dance To (1989, 135pp), Second to None (1993, 43pp), Card Tricks can be Fun! (1994, 35pp), Simon Says!: The Close-Up Magic of Simon Lovell (1997, 264pp), etc. Articles in Club 71 & Magic Menu. 4 videos (1990-93). [Wall Street Journal, 27 Jul 05, p.D10]

name: Lovick, John
bio: (Libby, Montana: 7 Mar 1962-) Semi-pro magician as "Handsome Jack" with parlor magic. Wrote Switch!: Unfolding the $100 Bill Change (forthcoming 2001) & The Paper Engine (forthcoming 2001, as co-author). [Wh01]

name: Lowe
bio: (England: fl.1760s) Pro magician. Played London taverns in 1763 with a variety of tricks with watches, rings, swords, cards, letters, candles, & mind-reading. [CI]

name: Lowe, Fred[erick], AIMC
bio: (England: 1920-1 Feb 1972) Amateur magician, mentalist, & lecturer on gambling cheating. Dealer & prop maker (particularly brass) as "Fredlo Developments" in Fareham, Hampshire, from 1967 to his death when the business & stock was acquired by Ken Brooke's Magic Place. Loyd, Sam[uel] Invented Christened Reverse = Fred and the Hong Kong Coin. Wrote lecture notes. Article Self-Control in Magic (1957, 4pp, as insert in Top Hat). Trick in Intermagic. [Daw94]

name: Loyd
bio:
(Philadelphia: 31 Jan 1841-10 Apr 1911) Studied to be an engineer but moved on to other jobs that included magician, ventriloquist, owner of a chain of music stores, and finally as a full-time puzzle maker. A world-class practical joker. A major designer of chess problems since publishing his first at age 14. America's most prolific inventor of puzzles, including such enormously successful ones as Trick Donkeys (at age 17) which he sold to Barnum; the Sliding Squares Puzzle ("14-15 Puzzle" or "Boss Puzzle", 1878); the "Get Off the Earth" geometrical vanish (1896); and the Buttonhole Puzzle (Pencil and Loop Trick. By 1902)which he sold to President John McCall of the New York Life Insurance Company. Often collaborated with the Englishman Henry Ernest Dudeney, who was the world's most prolific puzzle inventor. Unlike Dudeney, Loyd had the habit of plariarizing the thricks of others (particularly Dudeney's) and publishing them as his own. Bios are Encyclopedia Britannica (15^{th} edition); Martin Gardner (editor), Mathematical Puzzles of Sam Lloyd (2 vols, New York: Dover, 1959-1960)...

[See also: Enochs, E. Loyd]

name: Lu-Brent; Lu Brent, B.
bio: See: Brent, Lu

name: LU Chang Fu
bio: (China?: fl.1930s) Pro with Miser's Dream, Desert Sands, Butterfly Trick, Needle Trick, & Floating Ball. Toured Europe (mainly Germany but also England) in 1930s. [Ran] LU Tsu Bing One of the legendary Chinese "Eight Immortals", specifically the guardian spirit of barbers & magicians. [Dif]

name: Luciene, Stuart
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s) Invented illusions: The Princess of Bakhten (1926), Whirling Wheel (1926, with Stanley Norton), etc, which he published in The Magic Wand in the 1920s. Reportedly invented (by 1928) Cheating the Gallows (1).

name: Lucile
bio: (France: -1 Jan 1967) Stage name of Léontine Pascau. Daughter of director of a travelling theater. Married "Robertson" (Robert Colson) in 1910, working a 2-person mindreading act in his show until she retired in 1946. Mother of Odette Colson. [Dif]

name: Lucille
bio: See: Barnett, Daphne Lucille

name: Luckner, [Friedrich Wilhelm] Felix Graf [Count] von
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 1886-1943) Ran away to sea at age 13. Learned a few tricks assisting a troupe of Hindu fakirs in Australia. German WW I naval hero nicknamed "The Sea Devil" for sinking 14 Allied ships with his commerce raider Seeadler. Amateur magician, performing for his crew & the Kaiser. Bio is Lowell Thomas, Count Luckner: The Sea Devil (1927, 308pp).

name: Lucson
bio: (France: fl.1940s-60s) Stage name of Lucien Prinsard. 1950 FISM 2nd prize in close-up. [Bou]

name: Lüders, C. E.
bio: (Germany: fl.1900s-10s) Wrote several beginners booklets, including as "Adolf Bourse" Der Tausendkünstler (1905, 96pp; with several reprints) and under his real name Der kleine Bellachini in der Westentasche (1917, 64pp; several reprints to 1941). Aka "Martens".

name: Ludovic
bio: (France: fl.1920s-30s) Stage name of Louis [-E.-C.-A.] Duquesne.

name: Ludow, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Ludovic Heraud. Lived in Paris. 1961 FISM 2nd prize in card magic. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1967.

name: Lugano, Bobby
bio: (Austria: 27 Feb 1917-19 Mar 1994) Stage name of Kurt Drössler. Engineer in Vienna. Semi-pro manipulator. Father of "Jimmy Lugano". [Al;Mec]

name: Lugano, Jimmy
bio: (Austria: 3 [or 6] Mar 1941-) Stage name of Günther Drössler, son of "Bobby Lugano". Prosince 1977 as "The Laughing Wizard". Works cruise ships. [Mül;Nad] Lukins, Jerome A. "Jerry" (USA: fl.1920s-50s) Lawyer in New York City where he later ran a detective & security agency (for which Norm Jensen worked since 1954). Amateur card & coin man. Sphinx 1946 award-winner for his version of the Homing Coins. Wrote My Favorite Partner. Tricks in HMM. [SAM]

name: Lumière, Auguste [pronounced Iyoo-MYAIR]
bio: (France: 19 Oct 1862-1954) Chemist and manufacturer of photographic equipment. In 1895 co-invented (with younger brother Louis-Jean) the cinematograph type of motion picture camera. Amateur magician. Member of ASAP. Wrote the Preface to Ceillier's classic Manuel pratique d'illusionnisme (2 vols, 1935-36). Co-Honorary President of Amicale Robert-Houdin de Lyon since 1941. Advocated that magic be taught in all French government schools. Essays in French magic magazines & books on the utility of magic. See the French bios of his brother by Georges Sadoul, Louis Lumière (1964), and Maurice Bessy & M. Lo Duca, Louis Lumière, inventeur (1948).

name: Lumsden, Alf G.
bio: See: "Czerny"

name: Lunar, Ingleby
bio: See: Ingleby Lunar

name: Lund, Robert J. "Bob", MIMC
bio: (Saginaw, Michigan: 4 May 1925-20 Oct 1995) Of Norwegian ancestry. Around age 7 saw an amateur. "From that time on I aspired to be a magician; but I was not much good at it". Newspaper reporter & automotive writer in Detroit. Amateur magician & collector. Many articles in over 20 magic journals including Collectors Annual, Magicol, & Abra plus articles on magic for several newspapers & popular magazines. Last editor of The Conjurors' Magazine 1948-49. Edited Magic Collectors Association Newsletter 1962-63. In 1978 founded the American Museum of Magic in Marshall, Michigan, which is continued by his widow-partner, Elaine Lund. 1983 AMA Award of Merit. 1988 AMA Literary Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame 1990. 1995 Christopher Special Award for Outstanding Accomplishment. See Dan Waldron, American Museum of Magic: Its True Story (1990, 48pp). [Se: Magicol#90; St: Wh2]

name: LUNG Tung
bio: (China: fl.1900s-20s) Famous pro in Peking, whose career overlapped that of the Dowager Empress & the new republic. Never toured abroad. [Dif]

name: Lupin, Arséne
bio: (Łódź, Poland: 21 Mar 1955-) Stage name (taken from the famous thief-hero of Maurice Leblanc's detective stories) since 1980 of Sławomir Jacek Piestrzeniewicz. Learned in 1977 in local magic club. Physician in Łódź. President of the Krajowy Klub Iluzjonistów 1981-1991. 1982 FISM 2nd place in manip. Karlovy Vary Grand Prix winner. Pro manipulator since 1983. Invented Arsène's Rope in 1983. 1991 FISM 2nd prize in manip. Wrote Kartenmanipulation auf der Bühne (1983, 30pp), Ein sehr schöner Trick (1983, 15pp), 10 Karten (1984, 15pp), & Seminar 1. Articles in Hokus Pokus (Poland). [Hokus-Pokus (Switz.) 89;Mec;Wh2]

name: Lupin, Jean
bio: See: Arnolis, Jean

name: Lupo, Vito
bio: (Queens Borough, New York City, New York: 4 Aug 1960-) Learned at age 12. Tannen's Magic Camp 1st place at age 14. 1976 SAM 1st place. Pro stage comedy-mime magic since 1978 with assistant Ann Marie, marrying her in 1982. 1979 FISM 1st prize in general magic. Toured abroad since 1979, playing Japan (1979), Europe, & South America. Many TV bits.[MUM6/99;Opus2/89;MM5/89;MM12/81;Des;Wat;Wh2]

name: Lupupa, Marcus
bio: (Rhodesia [now Zambia]: 1934-) Black. Ex-policeman in Zambia. Pro magician. Did school shows with  $ \frac{1}{2} $ &  $ 1\frac{1}{2} $ hours acts assisted by his son Anthony. [Dif]

name: Lustig, David J. "Dave
bio: (USA: 4 Sep 1893-30 Sep 1977) Aka "La Vellma". Pro vaude magus & vent since 1910. Later switched to mind-reading. Wrote & directed silent movies for Stellar Productions in NY City 1923-25. Theater manager there 1925-27. Began some ghost-writing for Dunninger in late 1920s. Wrote several booklets since 1920, including Magic and Mind Reading Tricks You Can Do (1920, 51pp), Vaudeville Magic (1920, 30pp), Vaudeville Ventriloquism (1920, 29pp, with Robert W. Doidge), La Vellma's Vaudeville Budget (1921, 85pp), Vaudeville Mind Reading and Kindred Phenomena (1929, 64pp); Vaudeville Hypnotism (1930, 35pp); The Art of Thought Reading (1956). On Dunninger's payroll designing many of his "Brainbuster" tests 1943-47. Ended career as movie publicity agent for Columbia. SAM Hall of Fame. [LR8/97;Zo]

name: Lutz, Lucky
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 18 Apr 1941- ) Stage name of Ludwig Johann Kurz. Learned at age 10 from a street performer & a dealer. Assistant to Marvelli 1963-68. Pro since 1967 with stage magic & sleight-of-hand in variety, night clubs, cruise ships, & trade shows. 1977 West German 1st prize in stage magic; 1978 Karlovy Vary 2nd prize in stage magic; 1980 West German 1st prize in card magic. Wrote lecture notes. Articles in Magie, Zauberkunst, & Innovator. [Al;Wh5]

name: Lux, Vernon E[dward]
bio: (Rochelle, Illinois: 28 Jun 1906-1962) Semi-pro since 1927. President of the International Society of (Junior) Magicians from its founding in 1932 to 1946 when it dissolved. Dealer (Lux Magic Studio in Mount Morris, Illinois) in 1940s. Edited the ISJM's official monthly journal The Dragon 1932-46. [LR11/95; Go2]

name: Luzifer, Fred
bio: (Germany: 12 Jan 1902-16 Jan 1976) Stage name of Gottfried Wunderlich. Pro since 1925 with magic & muscle-reading & 2-person telepathy with assistant-wife. After WW II lived in East Germany, dying there in Warnemünde. [Roh]

name: Luzifer, Mark
bio: (Germany: fl.1930s-80s) Stage name. Pro with telepathic act. Played the Ronacher in Vienna in 1939. After WW II lived in East Germany.

name: Lybarger, Jess[ie L.]
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Sewing machine wholesaler. Semi-pro magician. Invented Spongeball Manipulation in 1926.

name: Lyford, Nelson
bio: (USA: 2 May 1893-22 Jul 1947) Semi-pro. Moved to Britain where he became prominent member of Glasgow Society of Magicians &, later, Scottish Conjurers' Association. Active in the Boy Scout movement. [Daw2]

name: Lyle, Mr.
bio: See: Elliott, Lyle A.

name: Lyle, Art
bio: (Lowell, Massachusetts: 1894-) Inspired by and learned from Erdnase's Expert at the Card Table in 1907 at age 13. Pro comedy manipulator & sleight-of-hand artist. Tricks in New Phoenix, Genii, & HMM. Taught Paul Chosse in 1963. [Th]

name: Lyle, Cecil, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 1892-9 Mar 1955) Stage name of Cecil Cohen. Pro illusionist since debut in variety theaters in 1912. Soon billed as "The Magic Milliner". Played major variety houses in Britain, including the London St. George's Hall in 1914 & 1919-21, the Palace in 1922, & the Aldwych in 1941. Bought many of the props of De Biere, Golden, Devant, Williams, Carmo, & Amac. Toured Australia 1937. Bought Horace Goldin's act after the latter's death in 1939. 1941 Magic Circle Gold Medal with Star. World tour 1950-52. His wife-assistant Lucille La Farge worked the Sympathetic Silks & Find the Lady. Invented Flying Gramophone (1912), Paper Hat Trick (1920), & Squaring the Circle (by 1945). [Pr;Go2;Ch;Wal;Ho;St;Mar]

name: Lyle, Henry L.
bio: (USA: -1981) Pro as "Henri--The Card Stylist". Card fan specialist. Worked hotel circuit & supper clubs in 1940s-60s. Wrote as "Henri" All You Need to Know about Card Fan Designs [early 1940s].

name: Lynch, Vincent P.
bio: (USA: 20 Dec 1906-Sep 1941) Amateur. Effect in Jinx.

name: Lynn, Bob
bio: (USA: c1930-Nov 2005) Prominent psychic entertainer, bizarrist, & escapist as "Tony Raven". Collector. Co-founded the Psychic Entertainers Association 1978. PEA President 1978-83. Published-edited The Blue Sheet 1962-63 (6 issues), Private Journal 1972-73 (3 issues). As "Tony Raven" published-edited Invocation 1974-78, Raven Report 1977-79 (4 issues), & New Invocation 1979-81. Co-edited (with Scott Gordon) Psychikos 1980-81 (2 issues). Wrote The Necromantic Grimoire of Augustus Rupp (1974), a forcing book. Audio (1980). See Marc Tessler, Bizarre Magic: An Interview with Bob Lynn (1977, 8pp).

name: Lynn, Dr. H. S.
bio: (Bristol, England: 17 Oct 1831-1899) Stage name since 1873 of Hugh Simmons, aka "Washington Blythe", "Washington Simmons", & "Simmons". Debut as amateur (in Royal Navy) in 1858. World-travelled pro from 1862 until retired in 1895. Father of J.W. Lynn. Illustrator & author. As "Washington Simmons" wrote The Wizard's Pocket Book (1863, 16pp). Autobio is The Adventures of the Strange Man, Dr. H.S. Lynn (1873, 57pp; other eds 1877, 1878). A later memoir is How It's Done & Recollections of India (1882). [Pr;La;Wal;Mo]

name: Lynn, J. W.
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Son of H.S. Lynn. Small-time pro illusionist. Wrote 2 articles on the Box Trick for Strand Magazine (Mar-Apr 1907).

name: Lynn, Terral "Terry
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: c1890-died in 1960s) Stage name of Isaac Hellerman. Army aviator in WWI. Perfume manufacturer c1919-c1939. Inspired seeing Paul Rosini in 1939. Became pro magician in 1940, playing niteclubs & hotels in Central & Eastern USA. Toured Canada in 1954. Pet effect: Miser's Dream. Articles in Linking Ring & Conjuror's Magazine. [LR4/97,5/97; Collectors' Forum7/93]

name: Lyon, Sheila
bio: (Everett, Washington: 7/1 ..... 1947- ) Ran a public relations firm until 1978 when she married Darryl (The Amazing) Beckmann. Learned magic that year from books. Thence pro kid-show magicienne as "Sheila, the Magic Lady. Also lecture-demonstrator on history of magic and co-proprietor of Beckmann's "Market Magic & Novelty" shop in Seattle. Wrote lecture notes Women in Magic (1989). [Wh5]

name: Lyons, Dr L. Vosburgh "Voz", MD
bio: (New York City, NY: 1892-1976) Physician in New York City. Amateur magician. Invented Devano Pack in 1936 and possibly Linking Pins. Tricks in Jinx & Ibidem. [Th]

name: Lyons, Pat
bio: (Toronto, Canada: 21 Mar 1933- ) Born Jeanette Louise Patterson. Married P. Howard Lyons. Pro illustrator with studio gallery ("Pat Answers") in Toronto. Did covers for Ibidem 1955-79 & Aziz (forthcoming). Her "The Vanishing Leprechaun" (developed with Bill Elliott & copyright 1968) is the best known modern horizontal version of the Geometrical Vanish puzzle. Her giant model was featured on the David Frost TV show. [Wh2]

name: Lyons, P[hilip] Howard, FCA
bio: (Winnipeg, Canada: 23 Jun 1928-25 Sep 1987) Aka "phl". Learned as schoolboy. A leading accountant in Canada with firm of Deloitte, Haskins & Sells. Amateur magician, noted for his creativity and humor and generosity to fellow magicians. Invented the Mis-Made Dollar Bill in 1956. Co-founded (with Bob Weill) the invitation-only Ibidem Event at the Oban Inn at Niagara-on-the-Lake 1979-85. Editor-publisher of Ibidem 1955-79. Edited Magic Square 1962-64 & Aziz (forthcoming). Wrote the anonymous classic, Smut Magic (1978). Co-edited (with Allan Slaughter) the monumental 1,025-page Stewart James in Print: The First Fifty Years (1989). Also edited Journal for the Preservation of Ephemeral Stuff (10 issues). Tricks in Ibidem, Epoptica, Genii, Magic, etc.

name: Macaire, Sid
bio: (USA: fl.1870s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro. Dealer (general & mental magic) in Chicago. Issued an undated 22-page catalog. Sold in 1895 to H.J. Burlingame. Toured the British provinces and settled in Dublin, Ireland. Then in England and finally moved to Bristol in 1905 or 1906 to manage the Empire Theatre. Wrote Mind-Reading or Muscle-Reading? (Dublin: 1889, 80pp; repr in London). Also, reportedly, Shadowgraphie. [Daw#200;CMM11/06,6/07;Sel;HMM5/51]

name: Macaluso
bio: (Sicily, Italy: fl.1850s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Pet effect: plucking coins from a candle flame. Played Paris in 1858 as a young man. [Dif]

name: Macarady
bio: (Russia: 1894-1975) Stage name of Joseph Nusynowicz. Pro. Toured Europe. Lived in Portugal for a time before finally moving to Brazil. NOTE: Mac, Mc, and M' are all alphabetized here as if they were spelled "Mac".

name: McAlister, Shaun
bio: (Athlone, Ireland: 2 Jan 1914-1939) Pro sleight-of-hand. Worked a while as demonstrator at Gamage's. [Go2]

name: Macallister, Andrew
bio: (Edinburgh, Scotland: 1800-1 Sep 1856) A carpenter's joiner (not a "bricklayer" as Wraxall mistranslated). Learned assisting (as "Domingo") Phillippe c1836. Apprenticed to J.H. Anderson. Then toured on own as a pro illusionist. Moved in 1847 or 48 to USA where he was fairly successful. Played Boston 1951 & 1953-54. NOTE: Name sometimes misspelled "Macalister". [Pr;Cl;Mo;St]

name: McAllister, [Robert G.] "Bob
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 1935-) Inspired at age 8 seeing magician at school assembly & bought 1st trick at drug store. Moved at age 12 to Norfolk, Virginia, where in 1950s he worked in the Edmar Magic Shop. Pro kid-show magician & vent (with "Chauncey de Pew"). Invented Vanishing Cup (1950s), The Giant Paddle (1960), Watch the Spot (1961), etc. TV magic performer-producer 1963-80. TV bits. 1973 AMA Award of Merit. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, Genii, etc. [Wh2]

name: Macallister, J. M.
bio: (Ayr, Scotland: c1837-21 Oct 1899) Stage name of John Mawer (or Moir or Mahr). Claimed at separate times to be the son (impossible) & the nephew (possible) of Andrew Macallister. Moved to USA where he was a minor pro illusionist since c1870 with a popular give-away show. Died in San Francisco. [Pr;Ch;Mo;Cl]

name: McArdle, John
bio: (Lexington, Kentucky: 17 Apr 1887-5 Feb 1983) Wealthy businessman in New York City. Amateur magician. SAM President 1948-49. Published facsimile reprints of 3 rare old classics: Hocus Pocus Junior's Anatomie of Legerdemain (1950), Rid's Art of Jugling (1952), & Scot's Discovery of Witchcraft (1954). Wrote McArdle's International Dictionary of Magitain (1963, 131pp, published in only 59 copies) & The Anatomy of Magic (1974), both being rather eccentric books.

name: McAthy, George
bio: (Oswego, New York: 24 May 1910-7 Sep 1971) Inspired by seeing Thurston show. Protégé of Gene Gordon. Semi-pro comedy magician & ventriloquist. Aka "Mandroop the Magician". Invented The Phantastic Phial (by 1940), Houdini Outstripped (by 1945), & Insurance Policy (in 1947). Since 1961 full-time as "Hokey the Clown". Maker of vent figures. Wrote several booklets, including Gags, Tricks and Patter (1936), Smart Business for Magicians and M.C.s (1946, 31pp), Smart Tricks for Magicians and M.C.s (1947, 35pp), Smart Tricks for Magicians and M.C.'s (1950, 40pp), Smart Talk with Added Material (1952, 32pp). Co-edited (with Tommy Windsor) The Dope Sheet 1945-48. Columnist for Linking Ring ("Out of My Hat") & New Tops. Contributor to Dope Den. [LR11/71;Th;WWM]

name: McBride, [John] Jeff[rey]
bio: (Goshen, New York: 11 Sep 1959-) Learned at age 8 from a stolen library book. Pro since age 16 with stage magic, illusions, & close-up. His act combines magic with mime, myth, martial arts, & Kabuki. Played the Mikado Theatre in Tokyo a few years in the mid-1980s. Tours mainly Europe & Japan. Pet effect: The Temple of Astral Light (light beam levitation). Since 1985 has been incorporating Neo-Pagan ritual magic into his act. 1985 Atlantic City Variety Entertainer of the Year. 1986 IBM Star of Magic. 1987 Monte Carlo Grand Prix. 1987 Tannen's "Louie" Award. 1988 Back Stage's Bistro Award for variety performer (shared with George Schindler). 1994 AMA Magician of the Year. Originated mask manipulation (1976) & invented The New Wave Rising Card (1987, retitled Kundalini Rising). See Adam J. Fleischer, Changing the Face of Magic (1985, 25pp). Wrote The Art of Card Manipulation (....., 3 vols). Articles in Genii. Video segment (1986). TV bits in Italy, Britain, France, & Japan. [LR4/97;LR5/94;MUM4/95;Genii5/92;MM12/83;Wat;Wh5]

name: McCaa, William F.
bio: (Leeds, Yorkshire, England: 6 Mar 1911-) Amateur debut as school-boy. Semi-pro since 1929 with stage show. Aka "Mac". Pet effects: Linking Rings & Razor Blades. [Go2;WWM]

name: McCafferty, LeRoy
bio: (USA: -1951) Skilled amateur billiard-ball manipulator & general magician while in technical highschool in 1904 in Washington, DC. Then popular semi-pro there. Played a birthday party at the White house for one of Teddy Roosevelt's kids in 1908. Died in Waterbury, Connecticut. Aka "LeRoy" & "Charon".

name: McCaffrey, William H. "Bill
bio: (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 19 Feb 1899-) Interested in magic since childhood. Business executive & semi-pro cardman & mentalist. SAM President 1933-34. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Invented Prize Winner (1934) = Premonition, Mirakel (by 1936), and Money Paddle (by 1945). Tricks in Sphinx & Genii. [Th;WWM]

name: McCarron, Brett W[hitney]
bio: (Seattle, Washington: 23 Mar 1959- ) Learned in 1966 from library books & mail-order tricks. Semi-pro stage mental & comedy magician since 1974. Dealer in Olympia, Washington, as Medicine Creek Productions 1976-81 & Magic World Productions 1981-present. Wrote The Prop Shop (1975, 64pp), The Gambling Magician (1976, 80pp), VCR Magic (1988, 92pp), The Solomon Principle (1989, 21pp), plus 2 computer disk books: PC-Magic (Vols I & II, 1988 & 1989). Articles (10) in Genii 1974-79. [Wh2]

name: McCathie, John
bio: (Britain: -c1920) Bookbinder. Amateur magician. Invented & improved many tricks, particularly props made of cardboard. [St]

name: McCarthy, Daniel
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Cardman. Played PCAM & Magic Castle. Wrote 5 booklets: Underground Hits Bottom, Suedes and Shades, Dreams of Reality, Quirks and Enodations, & After Hours. Trick in New Directions.

name: MacCarthy, E. Brian
bio: (Britain: 19 Oct 1910-16 Oct 1968) Amateur sleight-of-hand since his debut at age 11. Wrote Slow Sleights (1934; 20pp; repr 1946), Modern Sleights (20pp), The Chameleon Cups and Balls (36pp), Impromptu (1939, 87pp), & Sleights Supreme (1947, 92pp). Tricks in Magic Wand. [Go2]

name: McComb, William "Billy", MIMC
bio: (Belfast, Northern Ireland: 12 Apr 1922-30 Apr 2006) Son of physician Sir Charles Henry McComb. Learned in childhood out of "either natural curiosity or instinct to deceive!". Amateur in 1940s as "Innis More", "Callidus", & "The Great Liam". 1946 Cotswold Gold Cup. Qualified as a physician in 1949 but never practiced. 1949 British Ring Shield with partner June Cochrane (later with own act as "June Merlin") whom he married later that year. Pro stand-up & stage magician since 1949. Separated from wife in 1967 & moved to USA. 1977 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. 1984 AMA Performing Fellowship. In 1984 became 1st living European magician elected to the SAM Hall of Fame. Member of the Board, Academy of Magical Arts, 1988-present. 2000 Christopher Lifetime Achievement Award. Invented Hot Book (1945), Slow Cage Vanish (1945), Half-dyed Silk (1949), Double Sawing in Half (1960), McComb-ical Deck (1960), Banana Split (c1963), etc. Wrote The First Book of William (1947, 51pp), McComb's Magic (1972, 184pp), & The Professional Touch (1987, 129pp). Columns in Magic Magazine, Hughes' News, Magiram, & Budget. Articles in Abra, Dope Sheet, Magiram (series), Budget (series), Tops, & Genii. Several British TV series. 7 audios; video segment (1988); video (1988). [Jef; Australian Magic Monthly 7/90; NT9/66; Mag; Le; Wat; Wh2]

name: McCord, Louis Jerome "Lou
bio: (Allegheny, Pennsylvania: 25 Oct 1884-5 Aug 1972) Aka "Silent Mora". Learned c1894 by lessons from local magician John Lawrence McKissock. Pro sleight-of-hand. A Chautauqua star 1917-29. Famous by 1925 for his Mora Wands (hand-made Chinese Sticks). 1947 Sphinx Award. Wrote Mora's Memo (1908). Tricks & articles in Barnstormer & Tarbell #5. [Pr;LR8/46;Ho]

name: McCreanor, [Gerald Theodore] "Gerry
bio: (Adelaide, Australia: 22 Dec 1934-) Learned in 1956. Builder-salesman in Adelaide. Part-time kid-show & close-up magician. Aka "Merlin" when working shopping centers, schools, clubs, etc. Pet effects: matchbox tricks & 4-Ring Routine. Co-editor (with Murray Cooper) Blueprint 1978-81. [Wh2]

name: McCree, Shaun [Terence]
bio: (Slaidburn, England: 8 Apr 1963- ) Pro manipulation & close-up magician. Won British Ring Dittia Shield (for manip) 1981 & 1987. 1989 British Magical Champion of Manipulation. 1989 International Close-up Competition 3rd prize. [Daw2]

name: McCullagh, Brian
bio: (Australia: fl.1990s) Amateur & magic historian in Sydney. Wrote Sydney's Magic Heritage (1994, 319pp), The Magical Writings of Edwin A. Dawes (1997, 30pp, with sup to 1997), Chung Ling Soo's Mechanists (1998), & Early Australian Magic Catalogues, 1886-1912 (1998, 24pp).

name: McDonald, Abel
bio: See: "Maldo, Séñor"

name: McDonald, Charles
bio: (Portsmouth, Virginia?: fl.1880s) Invented Cremation (by 1889).

name: McDonald, Jon W. "Mac" "One-Arm
bio: (Southern USA: c1895-c1982) Pro magician (also con artist) until retired in 1949. A teenage Lou Tannen was an early assistant when Mac operated a travelling magic shop out of his truck in the late 1920s. Although nicknamed "One-Arm", he was missing only a hand. Invented You Do As I Do and popularized the McDonald Aces. Bio is C.C. Allen, The Legend of Mac McDonald (1986, 33pp). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "MacDonald".

name: McDonald, Kenrick "Ice
bio: (USA: 1960-) Son of an Afro-American pastor. Learned in 1970 from a magic set. Pro male model to pro magician. Specialty: Dove Act. [LR5/2001]

name: MacDougall, [Samuel] Michael "Mickey
bio: (USA: 1906-) Learned in 1917 as apprentice to Horace Goldin as Indian boy in rope trick and in 1918 by reading Erdnase. Semi-pro cardman, including working a Svengali pitch cross-country & at 1933 Chicago World's Fair. Sometimes did a nightclub act. Then a gambling investigator & lecturer, competing bitterly with John Scarne in 1940s. Later left magic to be a stamp & coin dealer. Wrote Gamblers Don't Gamble (1939, 166pp, with J.C. Furnas), Card Mastery (1944, 81pp), MacDougall on Dice and Cards (1944, 90pp), Card Mastery (1944, 81+205pp), Don't Be A Sucker! (1945, 80pp), & MacDougall on Pinochle (1951, 90pp). Memoir is Danger in the Cards (1943, 31pp). [Wh91;Bo2;Jinx#131;Berg,48,49]

name: McDougall, Richard
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Young sleight-of-hand artist combining mime & comedy in his act. TV bit in Britain. [Fi2] "McDuff, Algonquin" [joint pen name where "McDuff" is a fictitious "3rd" collaborator] SEE: Bryson Jr, Rhett & Cleveland, Dexter

name: McEwen, Philip Hartley
bio: (Scotland: -1936) Aka "The Great McEwen". Small-time pro magician by 1899 in USA. Then added muscle-reading & hypnotism, being highly rated by Newmann. Managed by Felix Blei 1908-09. Moved around c1912 to Australia, where he toured as late as 1917. Also toured India 1913. Died in Australia. [Pr;Wal]

name: Mac Fink
bio: See: Fontaine, Michel

name: McGee, [Debra Ann] "Debbie
bio: (Kingston-on-Thames, Surrey, England: 31 Oct 1958-) Dancer in theater, films, & TV since age 12. Learned magic from Paul Daniels & books. Pro assistant to Daniels 1979-present, marrying him in 1988. Also does a single act. 2001 DRAGON Award for Paul Daniels & Debbie. [Wh2]

name: McGill, Ormond [Dale]
bio: (Palo Alto, California: 15 Jun 1913-19 Oct 2005) Inspired & learned as a pre-teen from a Gilbert Mysto Magic set then at age 14-15 from the Tarbell Course. Pro since 1940 as stage hypnotist (as "Dr. Zomb" 1941-53), mentalist, illusionist. Toured a midnight spook show thru western USA & Canada c1942-52. Toured the Pacific Basin in 1955. Wrote 21 Gems of Magic (1946, 63pp), The Encyclopedia of Stage Hypnotism (1947, 275pp), Psychic Magic (1951, six 25-page vols), Atomic Magic (1951, 41pp), The Mysticism and Magic of India (1977), Entertaining with Magic (1977, 231pp), Magic with Soap Bubbles (1987), Real Mental Magic (1989, 143pp), etc. Articles in Fate & New Journal of Hypnotism. His bio is forthcoming (1990) from Chuck Mignosa. [LR12/2005;Bo#228;Fu;Tay;Wh2]

name: McGlynn, Dr. Edward
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Stage name of Cliff West. Edited The Ghost (New York City: 1936-37, 10 issues).

name: Mac Gregor
bio: (Wroclaw, Poland: 1949- ) Stage name of Grzegorz Olejnik. Pro general magic & manipulator. Toured Syria, Iran, & Jordan. 1974 Karlovy Vary 1st prize. [Mec] MacGregor, The Right Honorable John, OBE, MP (Glasgow, Scotland: 14 Feb 1937-) Politician. Secretary of State for Education & Science in Thatcher's cabinet, 1989-90. Leader of the House of Commons, 1990-92. Amateur magician, specialized in mind-reading. TV bit. [Fi2]

name: McGuire, [Edward Gilland] "Eddie
bio: (River Point, Rhode Island: 1891-1968) As a boy took private lessons from T. Nelson Downs, or so he claimed (Downs did correspond with him). Aka "Tex McGuire", "Don Cortez", "The Great Gilland". Amateur card magician & professional gambler. Introduced Walter "The Phantom of the Card Table" Scott to the New York "inner circle" magicians in 1930 in his own effort to penetrate that exclusive group. Notorious eccentric given to tall tales. For example he claimed to be the “manager” & advance man for Malini, who could only remember him booking a hotel in Newport. Died insane in hospital. Wrote The Phantom of the Card Table (1930; repr 1969, 69pp) & the alleged manuscript McGuire on Malini. Bio is Edward S. Cannon, Suppose You Lost Your $100,000 Overnight? (1942; repr 1978). See also "The Vernon Touch" columns in Genii for Mar, Apr, & Jun 1990; and Busby, Secret of the Palmettos (1998), 1-20.

name: McIlhaney II, William H. "Bill
bio: (Roanoke, Virginia: 10 Mar 1951- ) Learned at age 5 from Xmas gift Remco Sneaky Pete magic set. Semi-pro performer & lecturer. Moved to Southern California in 1974. Radio researcher & pharmacological consultant. Collector of fine apparatus, particularly props by Anverdi. His collection of over 1600 films includes 75 on magic (including TV specials). Article in Magic (1996). [Bo#283;CA;Wh2]

name: McIntosh, Gene [Allen]
bio: (Houston, Texas: 28 Aug 1932- ) Inspired at age 10 by Mandrake radio show & seeing Blackstone. Railway clerk & hypnotist. Part-time pro illusionist since 1944 as "Gene De Jean". Invented surrounded versions of several standard illusions. 1966 TAOM Best Stage Magic. [Wh3]

name: MacKay, Hugh
bio: (Edinburgh, Scotland: 9 Jun 1890-9 Jul 1943) Amateur magician & mentalist. Used pen names of "Dr. S. Holmes" & "Sirius". Wrote Classical Conjuring (1925), A System for Card Signals (1926), A Transmitter for Telepathists (1928), A Monograph on Card Transmission (1934, 8pp), Card Prediction by Indexes and other Tricks (1935). Edited Magical Criticisms 1921-22, 1942 (11 issues), Magical Observer 1923-25 (24 issues), The Outlook on Magic 1927-32 (8 issues); The Phoenix 1931-33 (2 issues); Puzzle Page 1936 (2 issues), Literary Selections for Conjurers 1938-39 (4 issues), & Periodic Epistle to Conjurers 1942 (1 issue). [Daw#130;Go2]

name: M'Kean, Lewis Gordon
bio: (Scotland: fl.1830s) Pro second-sight act in Scotland & England.

name: MacKenzie, George M.
bio: (Britain: -1975) Engineer. Inspired as boy. As magician played variety houses after WW II, including 2 years with Rameses. Returned to engineering in 1929 but continued to perform part-time as "The Uncanny Scot". Then dealer & prop maker as "Mac's Mysteries" in Glasgow 1939-49. Edited Mac's Mysteries & Mac's Monthly as house organs 1944-48. Wrote Compre's Corner (1947). [Daw94]

name: Mackenzie, Oliver
bio: (South Queensbury, Scotland: c1896-21 Jul 1983) Ex-actor. Semi-pro magician. Originated Drinks Trick (with cards). Owned many Martin props. [Daw2]

name: MacKenzie, Robert [Kenneth] "Bob
bio: (Berkeley, California: 5 Sep 1936-) Learned at age 10 from a found copy of Hay's Learn Magic. TV critic & news reporter in San Francisco. Amateur close-up & mental magician. 1955 PCAM Best New Act. Pet effects: Princess Card Trick & Slydini's Coins Thru. Video (forthcoming). [Wh2] McKechnie, [Stephen Mair or Muir] "Steve" (Glasgow, Scotland: 10 Oct 1910-25 Jun 1987) Semi-crippled by infantile paralysis at age 2. Moved to Australia at age 10. Learned from a gift magic book. Furniture maker until 1930s when turned pro magician as "Weirdo". Also did pseudo-Eastern magic as "Chung Wu" (1941) & illusions as "The Scotch Magician." Pro dealer (Weirdo's Magic and Novelty Shop) in Sydney 1940-87. Sold his magic collection (1,500+ books plus several thousand magazines) to Margaret Yates in 1984. Wrote as "Weirdo" Card Tricks with a Borrowed Pack & Magical Gags and Giggles (32pp). [McC: Magicana4/91; Magico]\#841 [McC; Magicana4/91; Magicol#84]

name: McKinven, John [Alexander]
bio: (New Castle, Pennsylvania: 11 Mar 1920-) Son of a Scottish immigrant. Saw the Thurston show at age 9. Woodturner. Amateur magus. Collector in Lake Forest, Illinois. Wrote Roltair: Genius of Illusions (1980), Stage Flying (1995, 112pp), & The Hanlon Brothers (1998). Article in Linking Ring. [Bo#315]

name: McKissock, John Lawrence
bio: (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 27 Apr 1869-5 Apr 1964) Inspired seeing a farmer do the Tears of Buddha. Plumber by trade. Semi-pro magician with sleights & illusions. First teacher (c1894) of 10-year old Louis "Silent Mora" McCord.

name: Mackowski, Dr Leo Heinrich
bio: (Austria: 8 Jun 1920-Jan 1995) Magician (as "Peer Pleggs") & magic collector in Vienna where he died. [Nad] "Maclaines, The" SEE: "Cameron, Loudon" & "Cameron, Juanita"

name: McLaughlin, [Edward James] "Eddie
bio: (Iowa, USA: 25 Jul 1897-21 Mar [or May] 1965) Travelling salesman for a banana company. Semi-pro magician living in Burlington, Iowa and working the Chicago area. Close friend of T.N. Downes. [Pr] McLaury, William F.] "Bill" (USA: fl.1950s-2000s) Amateur illusionist. Wrote Encyclopedia of Escapes (1964). Around 1990 ran a magic shop in Charlotte, N. Carolina.[Cam]

name: Maclay, Alice
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-60s) Daughter of Fred Smith, a magician. Pro cabaret & kid-show magicienne in London & Scotland, billed as "Alice in Conjurland". [Mar]

name: McManus, John J.
bio: (USA: 1889-7 Sep 1955) Lawyer in New York City & President of Rolls-Royce USA. Retired wealthy. Amateur magician & collector since 1946. Acquired the fine Levassor Collection from John Snyder's widow in 1948 & that of Dr Howard Kayton in 1949. Purchased the huge Charles H. Larson apparatus & book collection in late 1949. In 1950 co-founded Magic Collectors Association. Acquired the T.C. Worthington prop & memorabilia collection in 1952. Bought part of the Karger book collection & in 1953 the Dreilinger book collection. Called "King of Magic Collectors". Donated his large apparatus collection (including props of Hofzinser, Robert-Houdin, & Houdini) to the Circus Museum in 1954 & his fine book collection to the Library of Congress in 1955, just before his death. [St;Albo95]

name: MacMillan, Ron[ald R.G.]
bio: (Britain:20 Sep 1932-20 Jan 2005) Learned in youth from books. 1957 British Ring Shield winner. Pro manipulator & sleight-of-hand to dealer as founder-owner since 1962 of the International Magic Studio in London. British Ring President 1988-89. See Lewis Ganson, Ron MacMillan's Symphony of the Spheres (1963, 23pp; repr 1971); & Walt Lees, Ron MacMillan's Modern Art of Coin Manipulation (1982, 85pp).

name: McMillen, Jack [nmn]
bio: (Stockton, California: 19 Apr 1911-died in early 1990s) Learned at age 11 from books, including Hatton & Plate's. Debut at age 12. Railway manager (retired 1976). Semi-pro close-up magician 1930s-80s in San Francisco, including as instructor at Golden Gate Magic shop. Specialized in gambling demos & card & coin work. 1991 AMA Lifetime Achievement Award. Invented JM Card Rise (1927), Witchcraft Card Rise (1930), & Astral Vision (by 1942). Wrote Take a Card (1930, 10pp, with Judson Brown) & Sleights & Swindles (15pp). Tricks in Sphinx, Phoenix, & Genii. [Th;Wh2]

name: McWilliams, [James] Paul "Mack
bio: (Columbia, Tennessee: 17 Sep 1904-) Of Scots-Presbyterian descent. Pro small-time comedy magic since 1925. In 1940 married dancer Connie Brook who became his stage assistant. Retired in 1950s. [Pr;WWM]

name: Madd, Jan
bio: (Cherbourg, France: 1946-) Stage name of Jean-Claude Coquelin. Inspired seeing magic show at age 9. Trained in local circus. Pro stage illusionist, touring theaters thru Europe. Starred at Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1973-74. With his partner-wife Chantal Saint-Jean founded-operates the 132-seat Le Théâtre de Magie de Paris) on a river barge on the Seine, 1990-present, giving their "Metamorphosis" show. TV bits in New York, Tokyo, & thru Western Europe. NOTE: Misspelled "Jean Mad" & "Jann Madd". [Genii10/91;Bou;Bou2]

name: Madame Card
bio: See: Card, Madame

name: Madaree
bio: (India: fl.1870s-80s) Indian, probably Hindu. Played London in 1880.

name: Madden, Richard F. "Dick
bio: (Butte, Montana: 13 Jun 1914-1 Aug 1988) Accountant in San Francisco. Amateur magician. Trick in Jinx. [Th]

name: Maddison, Walt
bio: (Leeds?, Yorkshire, England: c1932-) Telegrapher in Leeds. Amateur close-up magician since age 14, mainly with cards. Wrote Aces: Practical Card Routines (1983, 43pp). Tricks in New Phoenix. [Lo2] Maddock, A. H. (Britain: fl.1910s-20s) Stage name of J. Bell. Dealer (A.H. Maddock) with shop in Wellington Arcade, Glasgow, by 1919. House organ: Maddock's Magic Searchlight (6 issues) Oct 1919-May 1920.

name: Madge-E-Kwand
bio: (England: 12 Jun 1908-13 May 1983) Stage name of Kathleen Bettie Staite. Learned from books. Pro. [Mar]

name: Madsen, [Wilfred Henry] "Bill
bio: (New Bedford, Massachusetts: 7 Feb 1925-5 Jul 1983) Danish ancestry. Inspired at age 8. Engineer & WW II USAF cryptographer. Semi-promagician-mentalist. Editor (initially as "Arleccchino") of The New Jinx 1962-68. Wrote Hex! (1969, 109pp). [N.10/63] Maeda, Tomohiro "Tomo" [pronounced TOMO-HEE-RO MAH-EDA] (Japan: 19 Nov 1965) Close-up. Played the Magic Castle in 1988-89. 1990 Atsukawa Creativity Award.

name: Maelzel, Leonard
bio: (Regensburg, Bavaria: 5 Aug 1772-21 Jul 1838) 2nd exhibitor of Kempelen's Automaton Chess Player, 1805-37, touring Europe & the Americas. Patented the metronome in 1816, although it was probably invented by Winkel of Amsterdam. NOTE: Given name not "Johann Nepomuk" as reported by Christopher. [Ch]

name: Maffei, Marquis Francesco Scipione di
bio: (Verona, Italy: 1 Jun 1675-11 Feb 1755) Archeologist & writer in Verona. Wrote Arte Magica dileguata (Verona: 1749), which argues that the works of magicians did not need a supernatural explanation, including & explaining some tricks to support this view. [St]

name: Magaldo, Ruyard
bio: (Argentina: fl.1970s-80s) Amateur?

name: Magdola
bio: (France: fl.1930s-60s) Stage name of Magdeleine Carsalade, née Saussol. Pro mentalist as single & as partner-wife of Louis "Carolus" Carsalade. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1948. 1952 FISM 1st prize in mentalism (with "Carolus"). Later also used stage name "Eveline". [Dif]

name: Maggi, Dr. Vito, AIMC
bio: (Monza, Milano, Italy: 23 Mar 1927-) Industrial pharmaceutical chemist (retired). Amateur magician since 1950, specializing in manipulation, close-up, & lectures. Then 1955-85 as part-time & full-time pro. Aka "Maxim". AIMC 1988. As "Maxim" wrote Eros (1988, 62pp), Eros bis (1989, 59pp), & Eros tris (1991, 88pp). Former editor of Magia Moderna. Articles in Magia Moderna. [Magic Info3/83; Qui Magia1/89; Bou;Wh2] "Magic Boys, The" SEE: Kläui, Peter & Rath, Ernst "Magic Chef, The" SEE: Koch, Paul W.

name: Magic Christian
bio:
"magic hands, the" SEE UNDER: Thumm, Manfred

[See also: Stelzel, Christian]

name: Magic Orvellis
bio: (Italy?: fl.1980s) Stage name of Frank & Guido Orvelli. Pro stage magicians & illusionists in Germany since c1983. TV bits.

name: Magic, Mac
bio: See: Höller, Hannes

name: Magic-lan
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Ian Sutz. Dealer (Ian's Magic Factory) in Florida. Authored 3 booklets, including The Best Dam Tricks (1980), a monograph on the "dental dam" as magic prop.

name: Magic-Lady
bio: See: Cox, Mr

name: Magiconi, Profesor
bio: See: "Svengali" [A. Wasowicz]

name: Magic'son
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Jean Lefrancois. Lived in Caen. Pro stage magician with doves, manip, balloon sculpture, & kidshows. AFAP Master Magician. [Bou;Bou2]

name: Magicton
bio: See: Davis, Jean

name: Magicus, Professeur
bio: See: Blind, Adolphe

name: Magini
bio: (England: fl.1930s-90s) Stage name of Stanley Hammond. Pro. 1940 Sphinx Award.

name: Maginnis, Mr.
bio: (England: fl.1790s-1st decade of 1800s) Pro. In period 1795-1801 played London (at Sadler's Wells, he claimed), New York, Halifax, Newburyport (1795), & Boston (1796 & 1800-01). Featured bullet catch on sword-point, cake baking in hat, and coin, card, & egg tricks. [Ch;Mo;St]

name: Magnuson, W[alter] G. "Walt
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-70s) Pro pseudo-psychic. Aka "Del-Ardo". Edited The Seer 1929 (2 issues) & Mystic 1929 (1 issue), the house organs of the International Mentalists Association. Wrote many manuscripts for mentalists, including one in 1928 and The 20th Century Mindreading Act (1935, 33pp; reprint 1988), a classic on cold-reading. Trick in Jinx. Mago NOTE: Hispanic word for magician. When used as stage name (particularly in Mexico), as in "Mago Delhi" or "Mago Frank", they are listed here under their specific name, that is, as "Delhi, Mago", "Frank, Mago", etc.

name: Magony, Mr
bio: (England: fl.1st decade of 1800s) Minor pro with cards, decapitated & restored rooster, etc, in 1801. [Magic11/09]

name: Magrée, Mister
bio: (Basel, Switzerland: 14 Dec 1964-) Stage name of Marcel Grether. 1988 Vienna 1st Prize. 1989 Vienna 2nd prizes in Close-up & Manipulation. ..... [Wh5]

name: Magrum, C[lement] Thomas "Clem
bio: (Rock Island, Illinois: 4 Jul 1907-31 Jul 1996) Learned at age 10 from reading. Inspired to turn pro around age 19 seeing Reno, Downs, Laurant, Thurston, Blackstone, etc. Pro stage magician & manipulator (coins & cards) plus occasional hand shadows & chapeaugraphy in school assembly shows since 1926, working coast-to-coast. After Army service in WW II with USO in Europe in 1945. Retired in 1967 in Davenport, Iowa, but still did about 10 school shows per year until 1991 when fully retired. Pet effect: 10-Coin Star (two-handed). Articles in Linking Ring & Genii. [LR3/94;LR8/40;Genii5/43;LR3/50;Wh]

name: Maguire, Leon M.
bio: (USA: 1899-14 Dec 1951) Pro club magician in Brooklyn who worked the New York City area. Aka "Joe Kerr". A clever mechanic who made his own props and tricks as well as selling them to other magi. Invented Hydrocoke (Nov 1944) & Foto-Flite (1946). Tricks in Hugard's Annual (1937), Tarbell #5, & HMM.

name: Magus
bio: See: Baret, Marie-Paul-Pierre

name: Magus, Jim
bio: (Rochester, New York: 11 Jun 1953- ) Stage name of James L[eonard] Saltarella. Learned magic in 1963. Banker in Marietta, Georgia. Semi-pro mentalist since 1968, specializing in bizarre magick & seances. Wrote Horror Magic (1971), Sex & the Single Magician (1974), Entertaining with Horror (1982), Turn of a Friendly Card (1985, 40pp), Astro Disks I (1989, 58pp), Astro Disks II (forthcoming), Mysteries of the Runes (forthcoming), Tales from the Talking Board (1992, 57pp), Arcana of Bizarre Magick (200pp), Magical Heroes: The Lives and Legends of Great African American Magicians (1995, 229pp), Raising the Dead for Fun and Profit (84pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Magick, New Invocation, Seance, Vibrations, & Genii. [Magische Welt9/90;Wh2]

name: Mahatma
bio: (Bucharest, Romania: 30 Mar 1873-1943) Stage name of Hermann Kurtz, a Romanian Jew. Originally an architect; but after 1900, when he lost his fortune, decided to turn his magic hobby into his profession, working mainly without apparatus. Moved to Paris by 1906 when he debuted there. Then toured major variety theaters across Europe. In 1935 jointly with The Great Marcel became the first magicians to appear on French TV. Arrested in France by the Gestapo in 1943 & died during transportation to the Mogabir-Fransnitrie extermination camp. [Dif;Dam] "Mahendra the Mystic" SEE: Berg, Joe Taylor, Perry

name: Mahendra, M. S. "Doc
bio: (USA: c1886-19 Sep 1970) Stage & pen name of Frank B. Sterling. Learned the Stebbins Stack in San Francisco in 1907. Pro magic & mentalism since 1930s. Wrote as Sterling Modern Card Miracles (1919, with Hugh R. Johnston) & as "Mahendra" Amazing Card Miracles (1938, 60pp), "Needle Routine": Patter Presentation (12pp), "Rapping Hand"--Patter Presentation, & Crystal Gazing Act [1940].

name: Maillardet, Henri
bio: (Switzerland: 1745-) Worked for Jaquet-Droz (father & son) & Jean-Frédéric Leschot, managing their affairs in London. Made automata (androids) that were exhibited in London. Elder brother of Jean-David. [Sh]

name: Maillardet, Jean-David
bio: (Fontaines, Switzerland: 1748-) Younger brother of Henri. Worked at Neuchâtel with Robert family making automata, particularly of magicians. [Dif;Hou]

name: Maillardet, Julien-Auguste
bio: (Switzerland: 1779-1852) Son of Jean-David with whom he built automata at Neuchâtel.

name: Maire, John
bio: (England: fl.1970s) Stage name of W.J. Whitehead.

name: Mając, Gérard
bio: (Nice, France: 28 Apr 1943-) Stage name of Gérard Fater. Moved to Paris as child. Pro comedy magician & stage pickpocket. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal 1968. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Bronze & Silver Medals 1975. In 1978 became the 1st (& still only 1 of 3) recipient of the AFAP Golden Wand. Wrote Le merveilleux magicien (1971); Les secrets des tricheurs (1975), English tr as The Secrets of the Card Sharps (1977); Y'a un truc (1976); Le grand bluff (1978); Les pickpockets (1981); & Le pouvoir de la magie (1986). Video bit (1994). [Bo2;Bou]

name: Majcher, Eustachy
bio: (Tarnów, Poland: 1925- ) Pro illusionist & manipulator. Debut in 1945. Aka "Elma". Articles in Hokus-Pokus (Poland). [Mec]

name: Majeroni, Commendatore Amadeo
bio: (Ravenna, Italy: 1877-14 Jun 1932) Pro with an old-fashioned full-evening show. Pet effects: Bridal Chamber, Growing Box, & Inexhaustible Hat. Toured South America, playing Buenos Aires' Politeama Theatre c1930. [Bam,p155]

name: Majikans
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of Leo Burns. Wrote Magic Feats: A Miscellany of Practical Magic (1948, 37pp). Tricks in Abra.

name: Mäkelä, Solmu [pronounced MAY-kay-lay]
bio: (Helsinki, Finland: 18 Jun 1922-) Inspired to learn in 1930 by seeing magicians. Pro circus magician (manip & card tricks) since 1940. President of Taikapiiri, Finland's senior magic club, since 1960. Major collector of circus & magic posters (totalling c8,000). Mail-order dealer in Helsinki since 1970. 1980 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. Wrote 2 popular (50,000 copies sold) magic books: the 310-page Suuri Taikakirja [Big Book of Magic] (1951; 6th ed, 1982) & Taikurin Taskukirja (1970; 2nd ed 1974) plus several booklets including A Bibliography of Finnish Conjuring Works (1966). Edited Simsalabim 1959-present. [Win;Dif;St;Wh2]

name: Makentosh, Doug[las Geoffrey]
bio: (Scranton, Pennsylvania [sic]: 29 May 1907-14 Jan 1990) Pro escape artist. Demoed at U.F. Grant's New York shop 1938. Aka "Hardeen Jr" while working Hardeen's second unit until 1944. Hardeen, at his last show on 29 May 1945, declared Doug his successor. Then, as "Douglas 'Doug' Geoffrey", managed Holden's magic shop in New York City 1944-46?. RKO theater circuit tour in 1946 when pet effects were Sub Trunk, Breakaway Pigeon Box, & Flight of Time. On Tannen's staff since 1960. [Yankee Magic Collector#4:Pr]

name: Makman, Michael "Mike
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 1941- ) In NY City since 1965. Actor. Pro comedy magician as "Professor J.P. Putter". Tricks in MUM & Linking Ring (1999 Parade). [LR5/99;MUM11/94]

name: Malabar
bio: (Ireland: 20 Feb 1800-6 Nov 1890) Stage name of Patrick Feeney. Pro. Well-known in Scotland as juggler. Bio is J.B. Findlay, Juggling through Four Reigns (1945).

name: Malbrough, [John Joseph] "Jay
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 10 Jul 1935-23 Dec 1998) French-Canadian parents. While in US Air Force worked part-time as demonstrator in a San Antonio magic shop. Briefly assistant to Bill Neff. Performed & lectured thru USA. A teacher of Chuck Vincent. Writer for Genii. Wrote The Magic of the Forks Hotel [c1978, 35pp]. [Mag]

name: Malcolm
bio: (Britain: fl.1850s) Minor pro. Toured England and, in 1857, played the London suburbs. [Fr]

name: Maldino
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 9 Sep 1911- ) Stage name of Friedrich "Fred" Mahlo. Bought 1st trick at age 12. Pro manipulator & illusionist. Inventor. Collector. Wrote 4 books, including Bekannte und unbekannte Deutsche Zauberer aus den zwanziger Jahren. Articles in Magie. Lives in Berlin (West). [Magie1/90;Mül;Al]

name: Maldo, Señor
bio: (Mexico: 1896-8 Dec 1959) Stage name of Abel Maldonado. Of Spanish parents, his father being a magician. Nicknamed "McDonald" by his many Anglo magician friends. Pro magician who worked in Mexican costume. 1937 PCAM T. Page Wright trophy. Lived in Santa Barbara, California, where he ran his Magic & Fun Shop (1950s) in the Paseo & owned a nearby Mexican-style restaurant. Tutored Charles Kohrs & Dick Zimmerman. SAM Hall of Fame. [Genii9/37;Tay]

name: Malek, David
bio: (US) Pro close-up, trade shows; game protection specialist. Legendary sleight-of-hand with cards and dice. Presentations for law enforcement, casinos and celebrity clients; gambling consultant for film and television productions.

name: Maletzki, Henri
bio: (Russia: fl.1890s-1910s) Major pro in Russia. Moved to Germany, presumably after the 1917 Revolution. Taught Bruno Christoph.

name: Malik, Shahid
bio: (Pakistan: fl.1970s-90s) Moved to England. Pro escape artist & straight magic with assistant-wife Lisa. 1985 British Ring Shield winner. [Bo2]

name: Malini, Max
bio: (Ostrov, Poland: 1873-3 Oct 1942) Stage name of Max Katz Breit. Polish Jew. Moved to New York City at early age. Inspired by and learned from Professor Seiden in NYC as apprentice at age 15. Pro close-up, working mainly private society dates. Gave card lessons to H.R. Evans c1901. Played London in 1904. World tours, including China 1913, Australia 1914 & 1916, and Argentina 1931. Joined the SAM in 1922 as member No.1000. Voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936. A master performer. Died in Hawaii. His memorabilia were given in the mid-1980s to the Mulholland Library by his son Oziar Malini. Invented the Button Trick (by 1902), the Malini Egg Bag, & the Torn and Restored Straw Wrapper. Popularized Chink-a-Chink (by 1927). Bio is Lewis Ganson, Malini & His Magic (1963, 107pp; repr 1973). Malini's "Just Malini" manuscript is a typescript of only about a dozen double-spaced pages. Mark Mitton is writing a bio with the cooperation of Oziar Malini. Trick in Magicana #1. [Jay;Pr;Pentagram9/55;Wal;Dif;Bam,pp.155-8;H "Mellini",4/03;HMM6/51;HMM11/55]

name: Malini, Oziar K. "Ozzi
bio: (Manila, Philippine Islands: 22 May 1913- ) Son of Max Malini who with his pregnant wife rushed from China to Manila so their son could be born an American citizen. A skilled amateur & pro magician in southern California until 1946. Thence inactive in magic except, since the 1960s when rediscovered by David Alexander, as occasional lecturer on his father's life & magic. [Wh2]

name: Mällini
bio: See: Tischer, Heinrich

name: Malmros, Gert
bio: (Sweden: 11 Aug 1938-) Pro close-up magician. Also works as "Jack Monroe". Wrote 4 booklets in English in 1981: Disappearing Aces, The Jumping Coins, The Chink a Chink Coins, & Coin Assembly.

name: Malo -- el Malísimo
bio: See: Lehn, Donald B.

name: Malogo
bio: (Germany: 7 Apr 1958-) Stage name of Manfred Geiss. 1984 MZvD 2nd prize in card magic. [Nad]

name: Malone, Bill
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: fl.1980s-90s) Learned by pitching Svengalis with Eddie Fields. Pro table-hopper. Video bit (1993). TV bit (1994). Took over Frank Everhard's "Sam the Bellman" routine. Planning (in 1995) to open a magic bar at the Boca Raton Hotel in Florida. Trick in Magic Menu.

name: Maloney, Peter [nmn]
bio: (Honeoye Falls, New York: 30 Dec 1941-) Learned at age 10 from books. Later teachers were Clayton "Tony" Birch & Francis Carlyle. Actor-writer-director for stage, film, & TV in New York City. Semi-pro close-up magician since 1974. Played the Magic Towne House 1978-79, "Chamber Magic" 1979-80, Le Chat Noir 1980, & Mostly Magic since 1980-present. Collector of props & prints. In movie Desperately Seeking Susan (1985) as the bumbling magician. Articles in Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]

name: Maltby, Geoff
bio: (London, England: 17 Feb 1948-) Pro dealer with shop in London (Repro Magic) since 1970. Began by reprinting magic posters. Then became one of first British dealers to import American packet tricks, mainly those of Emerson & West. Later added apparatus building rooms. Publishes Club 71 magazine since 1971. Invented Visible Picture Painting (1979). Tricks in Club 71. [Wh5]

name: Maly, Charles J. "Charlie
bio: (Sardinia, Ohio: c1890-18 Jul 1985) Aka "Alexandra". Pro, specializing in mentalism & muscle reading. Moved to Minneapolis where in late 1920s he became an early mentor of Charlie Miller. In 1927-28 he teamed with Doc Brumfield to form the Welworth Company of Indianapolis to publish Jack Merlin's classic "... and a Pack of Cards". Member of the "Secret Six". Wrote Dunninger's Act Complete (n.d.) & Celestial Agent (1944, 44pp, plagiarized from Faucett Ross manuscript). [Wh91;Dor;An]

name: Manchhachand, Professor Nathu
bio: (Mahwva, Bhawnagar State, India: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Learned by age 18. Pro with Western-style sleight-of-hand, mainly at private parties in Bombay area. [Magic4/01,1/07]

name: Mander, Alec
bio: (England: fl.1920s-30s) Pro. Played St. George's Hall in 1925. As "Ed. Morelle" also did a pseudo-Chinese act. Premiered Histed's Square Circle in 1932.

name: Mandrake
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 11 Jul 1940- ) Stage name of Alberto SOBRINO GÓMEZ. Learned in 1959. Pro, specializing in escapes. Founder-Director Boletin Unico de Magia (BUM) 1976-present. Published Magia con Monedas (75pp), Chistes de Magia (25pp), Diccionario Magico (translation of 150 magical terms), Colección de Tarjetas, Rutina de Flameos (forthcoming), & Magia con Globos (forthcoming). [Wh3]

name: Mandrake, Leon
bio: (New Westminster, British Columbia, Canada: 11 Apr 1911 [sic]-24 Jan 1993). Stage name of Leon , his undisclosed surname being neither "Wagner" (his maiden aunt's surname) nor "Jackson" (his step-brother's), as widely presumed. Inspired at age 7 seeing several vaude magicians. Debut at age 11. Toured as assistant in Ralph Richards' show 1926-29?. Thence on own. Pro illusionist, working as "Leon" as late as 1942. From 1930s to 1942 also worked the north Pacific Coast as "Leon the Ventriloquist". Known as "Mandrake the Magician" since late 1942 when Card Mondor & Roy Benson suggested that stagnate, borrowing from Lee Falk's comic strip character of that name. He added "Narda" (Lola, his 1st wife) & "Lothar" as assistants. In 1947, to replace the recently divorced Lola, hired "Velvet" (born 6 Oct 1924), an ex-Blackstone assistant, & married her that year. In 1949 became the 1st to include a Costume Change in a Sub Trunk routine. In 1950s toured USA, Alaska, & Hawaii. In 1956 (having bought Claude "Alexander" Conlin's act from Bob Nelson) appeared as mindreader "The Great Alexander" on Portland, Oregon, TV. In 1957 returned to Canadian Pacific Coast where thence, except for a Far East tour in 1967, did university shows. 1978 AMA Performing Fellowship. Semi-retired in 1981 & fully retired by emphysema in 1985. Father of Lon & Ron Mandrake. Bio is Sheldon O'Connell, Mandrake--Incomparable (1998, 234pp). NOTE: According to Card Mondor & Geoffrey Hanson his many claims (repeated by his elder son) to have coined & used the "Mandrake" name (from the magical herb) in the 1920s are sheer publicity hype. (Lee Falk's comic strip character was first published on 11 Jun 1934.) The same with his claims to have been named as Dante's successor, having toured Europe & Australia, etc. [Genii9/92; Conjurors' Magazine 9/48; Genii 11/81; Tay; Wat]

name: Mandrake, [Leon Franklin] "Lon
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 3 Feb 1948- ) Real name (as on birth certificate). Son of Leon & Velvet Mandrake. Taught from age 12 by father. Biology teacher in British Columbia. Semi-pro mentalist with a magic & science theme since 1983 with wife Linda. Collector. Articles in Genii. [Wh2]

name: Mandrake, Ron[ald Anthony]
bio: (Miami, Florida: 28 Apr 1949- ) Real name (as on birth certificate). Son of Leon & Velvet Mandrake. Taught from age 12 by father. Semi-pro close-up magician & stage illusionist with single act since 1964 in Canada. [Wh2]

name: Manea, André
bio: (Tahiti: fl.1970s-80s) A native Tahitian. Fireman & prominent Mormon in Papeete. Semi-promagician, the tops in Tahiti, according to Geoffrey Hansen.

name: Manek Shah
bio: See: Shaw, Mark

name: Manfredi, Blaise
bio: (Note, Malta: fl.1640s) Aka "Le Maltois". First of the Water-Spouters. Toured Germany & France (as "Blaise de Manfré"), working in public & at private parties. Taught this art to Floram Marchand. [Dif;Cl;St]

name: Manfredo
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 11 Jan 1899 [sic]–21 Dec 1981) Stage name of Bruno Manfred Gottschalt. Dentist. Interested in magic since childhood. Semi-pro magic dealer ("Spezialwerkstätten magischer Neuheiten") in precision-made props in Dresden by 1925 when he published a 6-page publicity brochure. Absorbed the shop (in Leipzig) of Reinhold Pfalz in 1930. Invented many stage & closeup tricks. Contributor to Magie. Died in Dresden. [St]

name: Manglamele, Vito
bio: (Sortino, Sicily: 1827- ) Pro lightning calculator since age 8. Toured Italy & France a few years. [Dif]

name: Manicardi
bio: (France: fl.1860s) Pro in French provinces by 1868.

name: Mann, Al
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: 20 Jan 1924 – 29 Aug 1999) Stage name of Gilbert S. Aleman since 1958, previously as "Allemann". Learned in 1932 from neighborhood kids. Master mariner. Semi-pro mentalist since 1949. Pet effect: Mind Reading. Invented over 32 mental effects. Wrote over 100 manuscripts & booklets, including Mental-Ettes [1976], The Third Ecstasy (1976), Pocket Slates [c1976, 32pp], The Apodosis [1978], The Tesseract [1978], The Psychic Ring (1988), & The Purloined Thought (1990, 156pp). Tricks & articles in Swami & Vibrations. 2 audios (1985). [Vibrations8/84;Wh2]

name: Manning, Otis
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-60s) Amateur in Toledo, Ohio, to pro nightclub magician. Tricks & articles in Jinx, Phoenix, & HMM.

name: Mannix [IV], Daniel P[ratt]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 27 Oct 1911-1997) Learned at age 11 or 12 from Mysto Magic set. Semi-pro magician 1935-1947 as "The Great Zadma", initially three years in carnival with William Doerflinger in Nova Scotia & the Southern States. Specialized in sword-swallowing & fire-eating. Thence a pro non-fiction writer of popular books that have become noir classics, including Step Right Up! (1951, 222pp; pb repr 1952; repr as Memoirs of a Sword Swallower), on side shows; The Beast (1959, a bio of Aleister Crowley), We Who are Not as Others (1976; reprinted 1989 as Freaks), Those About to Die, The History of Torture, & The Hell-fire Club. Also wrote children books, one becoming the Disney cartoon film The Fox and the Hound (1981). Freelance writer for such magazines as Colliers (series of 6 articles in 1944-45 on magic under his "The Great Zadma" pen name) & True. [Wh5]

name: Mans, Salvatori
bio: (Italy: c1859-) Pro illusionist. Moved in 1898 to Portugal where he stayed for a time. Still alive in 1958 at age 99. [Cam]

name: Mantovani, Alexandre
bio: (Leghorn, Italy: 1867- ) Founding Honorary President in 1888 of Italy's first magic club, the Circolo Illusionisti di Firenze. At that time he was living in São Paulo, Brazil.

name: Manuel
bio: (USA?: 8 Oct 1883-20 Dec 1934) Of ½-Portuguese descent. Stage name of Manuel Robert "Bob" Thomas. Lived on the West Coast of the USA. Inspired by & learned from Downs' The Art of Magic. Masterful pro vaudeville coin manipulator since 1913 when billed as "The King of Koin Kings" and then, by 1923, as "The Master of the Mighty Dollar". Died in Los Angeles. [Pr;Bo#157;HMM8/58;Berg;Cam]

name: Manwaring, Greg[ory Allen]
bio: (Gary, Indiana: 2 Jul 1962-) Learned in 1975 from library books & the Mark Wilson Course in Magic. Film animator. Amateur close-up magician. Illustrated several books & booklets, including Vernon's Revelations (1984). [Wh2]

name: Marbony, Bobby
bio: (Germany: 7 Oct 1925-) Stage name of Sebastian Schmid. 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in kids magic. [Nad]

name: Marcalbert
bio: (France: -6 Jan 1982) Stage name of Marcel "Marc" Albert, son of Georges Albert. Pro illusionist & close-up since 1940s. Substitute magician at Cabinet Fantastique 1970-81. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Silver Medal 1977 & Gold Medal 1978. AFAP Interim President 1981-82. [Bou;Bou2]

name: Marcel
bio:
Marcel, The Great (Paris, France: 25 Aug 1899-8 Nov 1944) Stage name of Marcel[-Albert] Galasse. Pro illusionist, impersonator, shadowist, rag picture artist, & musician. Joined the ASAP in 1921. In 1935 he & "Mahatma" became the first magicians to appear on French television. [Dif;WWM]

[See also: Mocella, Marco]

name: Marcelliee, Rhadolph
bio: (Cambridge, Massachusetts: -summer 1971) Afro-American. Learned c1907 from Henry Percival. Pro since 1910s. Toured the Warner and Loew vaude circuits, and Canada & Europe. [Ebony1/50]

name: Marchand, Floram
bio: (Tours, France: fl.1640s-50s) Famous water-spouter, having been taught by the originator, Blaise Manfredi. Toured France, Germany, other Continental countries (except Spain), & England (1650). Exposed by his former English promoters, Thomas Peedle & Thomas Cozbie, in their The Falacie of the Great Water-Drinker Discovered (1650, 4 leaves). [Daw;Ch;Cl]

name: Marcketti, Professeur
bio: (Paris, France: 16 Nov 1849-17 Aug 1931) Stage name of Édouard-Jean Marche. Son of a ballad-singer. Pro by 1870. NOTE: Misspelled "Marketti" by Volkmann. [Dif; Vo55]

name: Marco
bio: (France?: 1835-c1903) German-Polish parentage. Minor pro magician in Paris where he was called the "Petit Turque" because of the Turkish fez that he wore. Disappeared c1903 when he was said to have been murdered in the Bois de Boulogne. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Marco, Tony
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 2 Oct 1948- ) Stage name of Pedro Mário DIAS since 1961. Moved in 1953 to Beira in the Portuguese colony of Mozambique where his pro father António ALVES (see) taught him magic. Pro debut at age 10 as "Marco António Jr". In 1960 moved to the capital, Lourenço Marques, took his "Tony Marco" stage name in 1961, & played hotels, night clubs, & circus until 1964 when he moved with father to Johannesburg, South Africa, working various venues in that region. [Cam]

name: Marcom, Gloria
bio: (Idaho, USA: 1928-17 May 2002) Born Gloria Ruth Jacobsen. Raised in Cokeville, Wyoming. Married to Tom Palmer 1947-1964. Learned assisting him in his award-winning acts & worked her separate "Vampira" act since 1960. Moved to Dallas, Texas. Demoed for 5 years at Douglas Magicland where she met Dr Ralph "MarcoM" Marcom, marrying him in 1968. 1975 TAOM Stage Trophy (for Vampira act). Since 1981 often works with him as "Lady Gloria".
