Authored as Gloria Palmer The Vampira Act (1960, 20pp, ghosted by Tom Palmer). [LR2/95; Mar; Wh]

name: Marcom, Dr Ralph, MD, AIMC
bio: (Levelland, Texas: 30 Mar, in or before 1926-). Son of a physician. Learned as kid from tricks bought from Douglas Magicland. A Marine Corps drill instructor during Korean War. Did TV magic in 1950s. Entered medical school in 1962 & became a country physician in northeast Texas. In 1968 married Gloria "Vampira" Palmer, who inspired him to again take up magic as a semi-pro. TAOM Close-Up Trophy 1971. TAOM Comedy Trophy 1972 & 1973. TAOM President 1974-75. Since 1981 they occasionally work a local Renaissance Faire as "MarcoM the Mountebank and Lady Gloria" & he also works single. Avid collector of magic movies. AIMC 1987. Wrote The Magic of Marcom (1974, 70pp). [LR2/95;Wh]

name: Marconick
bio: (The Hague, Holland: 30 Mar 1930 – 22 Dec 2008) Stage name of Heinz Nikolas "Nick" Stolk, taken from his Dutch Air Force service as a "Marconist" (radio operator). Prolific inventor of over 100 marketed tricks in period 1945-67, including Silken Bombshell (by 1959). The Jan 2006 Linking Ring published a premature obituary. Practiced magic since 1945. Gave over 400 shows in the military 1950-56. Many awards since 1952, including 1955 FISM 1st prize in manip & 1961 FISM 1st prize for general magic. Pro stage & close-up since 1956, touring Europe. Wrote A Man and a 1000 Scarfs (n.d.). See Lewis Ganson & Hugh Miller, Marconick's Silk Magic (1964). Wrote Marconick Original Magic (7 vols, 1967-1982), etc. See also Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), Marconick's New Original Magic (3 vols, 1979, in French) & Vollmer's Marconick's Super Magic (1982, in French). Tricks in Magic Info. [Mag;Wat;Wh2]

name: Marcus, Paul [Benjamin]
bio: (Rangiora, Canterbury, New Zealand: 22 Sep 1928-11 Aug 2001) Of Lebanese-Polish parents. Orphaned, he was adopted by an Irish-Scots couple & renamed Patrick John Sweeney. In 1933 taught several close-up effects by foster-father. Amateur magician, specializing in mentalism & card magic. Articles in Abra, Swami (New Zealand), Swami (India), Magicana (New Zealand), New Tops, Mental-Wise, New Phoenix, Linking Ring, Magigram, & New Pentagram. [Wh2]

name: Mardo, Señor
bio: (Cuba: fl.1940s-60s) Stage name of Charles Mardo. Moved to Florida (Jacksonville) by early 1950s. Pro. Pet effect: Cups-&-Balls. Wrote Routined Magic (1945, 29pp), The Hands Only (1947), Applause (1947, 32pp), Magic for Bartenders (1950, 26pp), White Sorcery (1951, 28pp), The Cups and Balls (1955, 34pp; 2nd ed 1983)), The Act (1967, 36pp), etc. Edited Junior Magic 1954 (7 issues).

name: Mardoni
bio: (Elburn, Illinois: 7 Oct 1904-27 Feb 1987) Stage name of Clayton Meryl "Clayt" Hines since 1928 when he went pro with a mindreading-escapist-magic act. Did the second-sight bit as "Mardoni & Louise" with wife Louise (née Garman) whom he married that year. Originally on the Chautauqua circuit. Later worked nightclubs, hotels, etc. SAM Hall of Fame (1985, including Louise). Tricks in Genii. [Pr;Bo#185;St]

name: Maréchal Jr. Greer
bio: (Dayton, Ohio: 30 Jun 1921- ) Inspired by and from assisting high school chum. Amateur debut with 2-assistant full-evening show at Princeton U in 1942. US Army in WW II. Research chemist in New York City. Wrote Magic for the Millions (1957, 396pp; repr 1977 as The Complete Magician), still a good introductory textbook.

name: Margery, Arthur [James]
bio: (London, England: 11 Aug 1871-22 Jul 1945) Learned in 1885. Amateur debut in 1887. Pro since 1897 as society magician. Modelled his act after Robert-Houdin's. Pet effect: Miser's Dream. Major collector of magic books & playbills. Long-time magic book dealer. Most of his fine book collection was destroyed in WW II by German bombing. Wrote Magicana, an illustrated Catalogue of Books (1924, 24pp). Articles on magic history in many magic magazines. [Go2: St: Dif: Vo56: Bur: WWM: Daw94: Magic2/01] [Go2;St;Dif;Vo56;Bur;WWM;Daw94;Magic2/01]

name: Margo, Mdlle.
bio: (County Cork, Ireland: -13 Jun 1936) Learned assisting the Great Roland in 1904. Solo pro stage sleights & illusions 1911-1918 thoughout British Isles plus a world tour (including Australia in 1912). Played the Olympia in Paris in 1916. Her husband acted as her assistant. Died in England. [Mar;Wal]

name: Margot
bio: (Caldas da Rainha, Portugal: 16 Jan 1943-) Stage name of Maria do Rosário Jacinto Nobre Vilhena. Pro assistant-wife of "Jodivil". [Cam]

name: Margules, Sam
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-50s) Son of a Russian-Jewish lawyer father & a Romanian mother. Assisted Goldin on latter's 1923 or 1924 USA tour. Aka "Ramee Sami". Became a lawyer (for Goldin by 1938). Trick in HMM (1946).

name: Marian, Rudolf
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 30 Nov 1854-17 Mar 1928) Pro society magician, working mainly in Vienna. Wrote Das Ganze der Salon-Magie (Vienna: 1889, 240pp, ghosted by Plessing) & Das Buch der Kartenkünste (Vienna: 1890, 159pp). [Vo57;Al;St]

name: Marick, Mr
bio: (Gifu, Japan: 1 Jan 1949 - ) Stage name of Akira Matsuo. Most successful psychic entertainer in Japan. Started as magic dealer, and then became pro. His international awareness began at PCAM convention in Hawaii in 1972, awarded the best close-up magician. Restyled as Psychic entertainer and debuted in TV program in 1988, soon creating sensation nationally. His special TV programs always got high audience rating.

name: Marie, Mystic
bio: (Scotland: c1885-19 Jul 1906) Stage name of Mary Henry who in 1897 had married Henry Werner Walford. Sister-in-law of "Dr. Walford Bodie" and his sometime hypnotic subject.

name: Marina, Signor Charles
bio: See: Le Roy, Servais

name: Mario
bio:
Mario the Great (USA: -13 Jan 1931) Stage name of J. Edward Wood. Pro. Committed suicide.

[See also: Höbel, Eugen]

name: Marion
bio: See: Byron, Marion

name: Marion, Fred[erick]
bio: (Prague, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 15 Oct 1892- ) Stage name of Josef Kraus. Pro non-contact mind-reader. Wrote In My Mind's Eye (1950). See S.G. Soal, Preliminary Studies of a Vaudeville Telepathist (1937), for a 96-page study of Marion by the noted English parapsychologist, which concluded that Marion worked from tiny clues.

name: Mariska
bio: See: D'Almoras, Raymond

name: Mar-Jah"; "Marjah
bio: See: Ovette, Joseph

name: Mark, David
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 18 Sep 19-) Learned at age 7 from schoolmate. Pro comedy stage & walk-around magic since age 16 (in 1960s). Lecturer. Dealer (Sorcerer's Cellar Magic Shop) in Cleveland around 1983. As publicity stunts has done aerial escape (1985) & Bullet Catch (1986). Columns "Stage Struck" in Magic Manuscript & "Stagecraft" in Linking Ring (since 1993). Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, Magic Symbol, & Hocus Pocus. Hosted 2 TV magic series. [WWE;Wh2]

name: Mark, Richard
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 16 Apr 1940- ) Stage & pen name of Richard Mark Steinbook. Inspired at age 12 by father doing mentalism & seeing Dunninger, Rajah Raboid, & Myrus. Physician, scientist, & medical school professor at Jackson Memorial Hospital, U of Miami. Amateur mental magic since 1952. Several inventions since 1975. Wrote Mindbending Magic (1979, 27 pp) & Mindbending Presentations (1988, 17 pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript, Magick, New Invocation, MUM, & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Marks, Dennis
bio: (New York City, NY: 2 Aug 1932-11 Jan 2006) Learned from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set around age 8. Debut doing kid shows in high school. TV writer. Produced Metromedia's "Wonderama" show, which reportedly booked more magicians than any other TV show in America. President, Marksman Productions, in Los Angeles. Articles in Apocalypse, Magick, Genii, Epilogue, New Tops, & Vibrations. [Mag;Lo;Wh]

name: Marks, Tony
bio: (USA?: fl.1940s-60s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Played Vancouver several times 1942-62. [Tay]

name: Markschiess-van Trix
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 29 Nov 1920- ) Stage name of Julius Markschiess van Trix. Collector in East Berlin since 1946 of circus, variety, magic, cabaret, & fair memorabilia. Since 1979 has been official collector of the Märkisches Museum, which opened to the public in East Berlin in 1989. This collection now (1989) includes 100,000 books, 9,000 posters, 40,000 photographs, & 125 costumes. Wrote several books, including Artisten-und Zirkus Plakate--Magie (1976, 269pp, with Bernard Nowak), English tr as Circus People and Posters (1977). [Wh2]

name: Marlicz
bio: (Lwów, Poland [now Lvov, Ukrainain]: 1926-) Stage name of Ryszard Rotter. Pro actor & illusionist.

name: Marlin-Jones, Davey
bio: (Winchester, Indiana: 8 May 1932-2 Mar 2004) Born unhypenated, adding one later because another actor in Equity was named Marlin Jones. Learned magic at age 12 from pro cousin. Pro comedy magician touring with band shows as "Davey Jones, the World's Wackiest Wizard & His Circus of Magic" at ages 13-18. Regular act at annual Abbott's Get-Together's late 1940s-early 1950s. Hosted 2 TV magic shows in Ohio: "The Davey Jones Show" in Dayton 1954 & "Captain Davey" in Columbus 1954-55. Played private society dates in Washington, D.C., 1970s-80s. Did magic as "Davey Jones". Professional theater director (did 817 stage shows). TV drama-film critic (acerbic yet very funny & using magic tricks) with CBS affiliate in Washington, D.C., 1972-87 & NBC affiliate in Detroit 1978-86. Professor of Theater at U of Nevada at Las Vegas 1989-death. Pursued theatrical & academic career as "Davey Marlin-Jones". Wrote Comedy Tricks and Gags (1950, 35pp). Column ("Davey's Locker") in Tops. Tricks in Magick. Edits Sorcerer's Attic 1988-present. [Wh]

name: Marlitt, Frank
bio: (Radeburg, Germany: 28 Feb 1889-9 Jul 1945) Stage name of Karl Strohbach. Pro with both apparatus & sleight-of-hand tricks, Worked mainly in Dresden & mostly in variety theaters. Died in Berlin.

name: Marlo, Ed[ward] "Eddie
bio: (USA: 10 Oct 1913-7 Nov 1991) Born Edward F. Malkowski. Inspired at age 7 seeing a magician do the broken match in hank. Learned at age 10 with the 21 Card Trick. Machine tool worker. Widely influential amateur close-up magician in Chicago where he virtually created his own "school" of close-up magic. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1955. In 1968 began his continuing collaboration with Jon Racherbaumer. 1968 AMA Creative Fellowship. 1976 AMA Literary Fellowship. Best known for his exhaustive treatment of effects, often involving dozens of variations on each. Prolific inventor & improver of card tricks, moves, & subtleties, including Elevator Cards (c1951), Propelled Lapping (with C. D'Amico in 1952), Penetration (1953), Open Travellers (1) (in 1962); Incomplete Faro (by 1964), FUFU Switch (1964), Olram Subtlety (1965). Extraordinarily prolific author, including Pastboard Presto (1938, 20pp), Havana Deal (1940, mss, writing as "Manuel Pedro"), Amazing Isn't It? (1941); Card Fan Productions (1941, 17pp; repr 1958 & 1969, 24pp); Deck Deception (1942, 24pp); Let's See the Deck (1942; repr 1964, 32pp); Shoot the Works (1943; 3rd ed, 1971, 48pp), which was also a force book; Off the Top (1945, 27pp); Discoveries (1946); Marlo in Spades (1947, 51pp); A Devilish Miracle (1948, 8pp, with D'Amico); Card Control (1952); Future Reverse (1952, 9pp); The Cardician (1953, 190pp; repr 1966 & 1980); The Magic Seven (1954, 23pp); Miracle Card Changes (1954, 23pp), Revolutionary Card Technique (1954, 1954-63); Classical Foursome (1956, with D'Amico), Coining Magic (1957, 40pp); Peek and Shuffle Controls (1958, 103pp); Riffle Shuffle Systems [2 vols, 1959]; Marlo Meets His Match (1959); The Multiple Shift (1961, 59pp); Tilt! (1962, 23pp), Estimation (1963, 80pp); Ed Marlo on The Acrobatic Cards (1968, 80pp); Card Switches (1961, 65pp); Marlo's Objectives (1973); Marlo in The New Tops (Vol 1, 1989); M.I.N.T. (1989, 365pp); So Soon? (1989); The Card Magic of Edward Marlo (1993, 240pp). See also Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), The Very Best of Ed Marlo (1978, in French); Mike Maxwell, M.I.N.T. (1988, 365pp). In addition, most of Jon Racherbaumer's many books & periodicals faithfully record Marlo's work. 5 videos (1984). Many tricks & methods in Phoenix (since 1945), New Phoenix, New Tops (since 1963), Genii, Talisman, Epilogue, Ibidem, Swami, Mantra, Arcane, Epoptica, New Directions, Technomagic, etc, etc. "Marlowe the Magician" SEE: Pronk, Eugene

name: Marne, Stanley
bio: See: Johnstone, Duncan Blair

name: Maro, Edward
bio: (Montpelier, Vermont: 25 Sep 1869-26 Feb 1908) Stage name since 1890 of Walter T[ruman] Best. Pro magician (ex-photographer) since 1889 & first of the many Lyceum circuit magicians from 1892 to his death in Philadelphia from typhoid fever. His only pupil was J. Elder Blackledge. [Pr;MUM6/93]

name: Maron, Gerd
bio: (Halle, Germany: 27 May 1923-) Stage name of Gerhard "Gerd" Walter Wiegand since 1945. Interested in magic in 1933 seeing a magician. Played Stardust Hotel in Las Vegas & the Lido in Paris. Invented A Toy Dog Comes to Life & The Girl from the Hat. Articles in Magische Welt. [Wit]

name: Marotta, Rich
bio: (Greenwich Village, New York City, NY: 7 Oct 1945-) Learned at age 8 from a family friend, a gambler. Left job as a university psychology instructor for career in magic, moving to San Francisco in 1977. Pro since 1978 with comedy close-up, stand-up magic, & stage illusions. Now mainly works comedy clubs. Invented Fish Bowl on Head (1978) & Live Bird from Picture Frame (1986). Wrote 2 lecture notes (1982 & 1986). Trick in Genii. TV bits. [Mag;Wh2] Marquat, Carlos A. (Argentina: 1900- ) From a French theatrical family. Businessman in Rosario. Amateur magician. In 1933 founded Argentina's first magic club, the Rosario Magic Circle, which lasted only a few years. Retired from business in 1950 to become a professional magician with large show as pseudo-Indian magician "Wahli Tamarah". Marquis the Magician

name: Marriot, Mr.
bio: (England?: fl.1830s) Minor pro ("Professor of Recreative Philosophy"). Played a charity date in Liverpool in 1831. [Hou]

name: Marriott, Arthur
bio: See: Giddings, Alfred

name: Marriott, William. S.
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s-1920s) Pro spirit act in Britain as "Dr. Wilmar" by Apr 1909 when he played St. George's Hall. Posing in the USA as a psychic researcher he conned David P. Abbott out of the secret of the Spirit Painting (which Abbott had perfected on the basis of the invention of the Bangs sisters). Then, in 1910, posing as its inventor, sold the performance rights to P.T. Selbit for the equivalent of $12,000 (including continuing royalties), the then highest price ever paid for an illusion. In 1922 Marriott & Clive Maskelyne presented Spirit Photography & other spirit manifestations at St. George's Hall. [Pr;Cl;Magic6/09] "Marriotts, The" SEE: Giddings, Alfred

name: Marschall, Franz
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 26 Aug 1855-21 Mar 1936) Learned as a boy & from lectures by Georg Heubeck. Prominent amateur magician in Vienna. Aka "Zaubermarschall". Performed for Archduke Franz Ferdinand. In 1908 co-founded (with Ottokar Fischer) the famous Vienna Magic Club of which he was, successively, President & Honorary President until his death. Marsh Jr, S. A. (Barnet, England: 6 Dec 1912-) Aka "EI Raschid". Semi-pro kid-show magic.

name: Marshall, Blair
bio: (Canada?: fl.1970s-90s) Pro stage magic. Introduced Gale Molovinsky's Gamolo Levitation at the 1976 SAM convention. In Montréal, Canada, in 2000 when he bought the title and props of the old ShazZam show (John & Cathy Daniel) from Lee Edwards.

name: Marshall, Frances Ireland "Fran
bio: (USA: 25 Mar 1910-26 May 2002) Born Frances Marie Ahrens Vandevier. Learned magic in 1931 clerking at L.L. Ireland's magic shop in Chicago. Married Ireland in 1940. Widowed in Apr 1954, she married Jay Marshall three months later. Pro dealer (Magic, Inc.) in Chicago. 1973 AMA Literary Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. 1989 AMA Lifetime Achievement Fellowship. 1996 Christopher Lifetime Achievement Award Edited Kid Stuff (6 vols, 1954-74), The Sponge Book (1960, 43pp), The Success Book (3 vols, 1973, with Jay Marshall), Dr. Harlan Tarbell (1956), Come Out Flying (1974, 52pp), etc. Wrote Chicago news columns in Linking Ring, New Tops, & Magic Manuscript (since 1989). Memoirs are You Don't Have to Be Crazy (1946, 202pp, writing as Frances Ireland), With Frances in Magicland (1952, 133pp), & My First Fifty Years (1981, 68pp). [LR7/94;Se]

name: Marshall, Horace
bio: (USA: 1902-1976) Pro prop maker (Marshall Magic) since 1920 in Akron, Ohio. Specialized in feather flowers of which he was the main producer. In 1929 bought the R.S. Schlosser Magic Company & incorporated as H. Marshall & Co. Magic Store. After Horace's death the business was continued for 9 years by his widow, Marie Marshall (see). Wrote Magic as a Business (1933, with E.R. Springston). Marshall, [James Ward "Jasper"] "Jay", MIMC (Abington, Massachusetts: 29 Aug 1919 [sic]-10 May 2005) Raised in Melrose, Massachusetts. Inspired in 1926 seeing Houdini & Thurston shows. Learned in 1934 from Neil's The Modern Conjurer and a used Tarbell Course (for which he traded his bicycle). Pro general magic & vent since 1939, sometimes as "The Great Jasper". Invented Jaspernese Thumb-Tie in 1939. Pet effects: Linking Rings, T&R Newspaper, rope routines, Troublewit, etc. Also a Punch-&-Judy puppeteer. Played 49 states, Australia, & Europe. Married Al Baker's daughter Naomi in 1940 (divorced 1953). Played the USO (WW II), New York Palace in 1952, 1954, & 1957; the London Palladium & the Savoy cabaret for 2 weeks each in 1955; Radio City Music Hall (repeatedly); the Ed Sullivan Show (14 times since 1954, the record). Catch-phrase: "I am one of the better, cheaper acts." Created his famous glove-puppet "Lefty" c1944. In 1948-49 played the magician in the Lerner-Weill Broadway musical comedy Love Life. In 1954 married Laurie Ireland's widow, Frances, in New York City at a ceremony officiated by amateur magician Judge George Starke. Co-owner (with Frances) & President of the Ireland Magic Company (now Magic, Inc.) in Chicago, a major retail & publishing house 1958 Magic Circle Silver Wand. 1982 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Later "partially retired". A major collector of books on magic & puppetry. 1991 Magic Circle's Carlton Award for Comedy. 1999 Christopher Lifetime Achievement Award. SAM Dean of Magicians 1992-present. Edited New Phoenix 1954-58. Edited TV, Magic and You (1955, 124pp, with F. Marshall), How to Perform Instant Magic (1980), & The Success Book (1973, with F. Marshall). Wrote Jaspernese Thumb-Tie (1939; 2nd ed rev 1944). Articles in Midget Magician, Magic Cauldron. Many TV bits including 14 times on Ed Sullivan Show since 1954. Video (1984). [MUM7/92;Bo#191;Se;MUM6/79;Wh91;Fi; Mag;Des;LR3/53;LR3/83;SAM;Wh2]

name: Marshall, Jon
bio: (Stafford, England: 20 Jan 1950-) Billed as "The Man with the X-Ray Eyes". Pro cabaret act in 1980s. Director, Magic Carpet Theatre with school shows. [Abra#1302,1618,2014]

name: Marshall, Marie
bio: (USA: 1920s-80s) Wife of Horace Marshall (see). Their Marshall Magic shop in Akron, Ohio, since 1920 was famous for its feather flowers. On Horace's death in 1976 she continued the business (with the assistance of Richard Hughes) until 1985 when she sold to Hughes who changed the name to Hughes Magic. 1985 AMA Special Fellowship (shared with Orson Welles & Shigeo Takagi).

name: Marshall, W. H. E.
bio: (Folkestone, England: 22 Jul 1900-) Aka "Marco". Inspired & learned in 1917. Semi-pro. [Go2]

name: Marshall, William
bio: (Persia?: fl.1830s) Claimed to be son of a Scottish army officer & a Persian mother. Pro stage magician. Played Boston in 1835 as "Rahab Marchal [sic]". Later also as "Fakir of Ava" before I.H. Hughes took that stage name. [Mo;Ch]

name: Marteau, O. F.
bio: See: Fischer, Ottokar

name: Martens
bio: See: Lüders, C. E.

name: Martenus
bio: See: Wallace, Len

name: Marteret, Dr Étienne
bio: (Vendeuvre-sur-Barse, Aube, France: 5 Aug 1894-1968) Ophthalologist in Paris. Amateur magician by 1945. Collector & historian. AFAP Bronze Medal 1973, Silver Medal 1978, & Gold Medal 1984. Articles in Escamoteur, etc. [Dif]

name: Martin, Dr.
bio: See: "Hathaway"

name: Martin, Bradley
bio: See: Martin, [Thomas Bradley] "Tommy"

name: Martin, Harold
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-70s) Proprietor of Martin Magic Shop (specialized in used pros) in Peoria until 1974 when sold his shop to John Snider and retired to Florida.

name: Martin, John
bio: (Lithuania: 1881-2 Jan 1968) Born Jan Martin. Mechanic. Repaired & made apparatus for a Russian magician, touring & performing with him for 9 months. Moved in 1904 to England (London) where spelled given name "John". Watchmaker in Hatton Garden. Also made superb small props & gimmicks in aluminium & brass, initially working exclusively & secretly for Davenport's & then De Biere (1922-34). Then for such individual performers as Cardini, Frakson, Howard de Courcy, Lyle, Russell Swann, Virgil, & Graham Adams. His famed Martin Pack (by 1956) was a fine version of the earlier Willmann Deck. [Daw94;La2]

name: Martin, Leo
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-30s) Pro. Chief assistant to Selbit in late 1920s. In 1932 became manager of Hamley's magic department. Toured Selbit's Sawing in the English variety halls in 1935.

name: Martin, S.
bio: See: Collins, Stanley

name: Martin, Steve
bio: (Waco, Texas: 14 Aug 1945-) Raised in southern California since age 5. Paid debut in 1959 with his "Mouth & Magic" act in Wally Boag's It's Vaudeville Again show. Semi-pro as magic shop demonstrator at Disneyland 1962-63 & Knott's Berry Farm 1963-c65. Added pro comedy in 1968, initially as writer for the Smothers Brothers, while doing a club act of magic & balloon sculpture. Since the 1970s a star of American TV and film. In Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid (1981) he does coin rolls and shadowgraphy. Since the 1980s he does both a takeoff of Blackstone Jr's pickpocket act (with a dog as harassed subject) & his "The Great Flydini" magic satire act at the Magic Castle & on TV. Bio is Greg Lenburg & others, Steve Martin (1980). Wrote Picasso at the Lapin Agile & Other Plays (1996, 150pp), a collection of 4 of his plays, including 2 about magic. [Katz]

name: Martin, [Thomas Bradley] "Tommy
bio: (Nashville, Tennessee: 20 Apr 1910-11 Feb 1991) Newspaper reporter until learned magic briefly assisting "The Great Lesta" and later under Malini. Pitched the Shell Game across the country with "One-Arm" McDonald & Lou Tannen. Pro on own since 1933. His famous act (reviving & featuring the Egg on Fan was conceived & built for him by E. Loyd Enochs. Played the New York Capitol Theatre in 1935 (2 weeks), the New York Radio City Music Hall in 1936 (the first magician there), the London Palladium in 1936 (for 2 weeks as "Bradley Martin"), the Paris Alhambra in 1936, the New York Roxy in 1939, & the London Palace in 1944. His assistant-wife was Rosemary Deering, a ballet dancer. Pet effect: Egg on Fan. Moved to Houston, Texas, in 1953, working as a booking agent until retired in 1962 to become a real estate appraiser. [Pr;Bo#261;Jinx#65;Ho;Berg,50]

name: Martin-Bontemps, Auguste-Alfred-Marie
bio: (Saint-Servan, Ille-et-Vilaine, France: 4 Mar 1875-10 Nov 1936) Pro table magician as "Ha-Hem-Bey". Wrote Les cigarettes: étude technique de passes (1928, 205pp) & Après-diner (1935, with Caroly II). [Dif]

name: Martineau, Francis B. "Frank
bio: (Raymore, Saskatchewan, Canada: 10 Mar 1922-). Commercial artist in Vancouver. Semi-pro night club magician with silks, Sword-thru-Neck, Linking Rings, etc, plus juggling. In Canadian Army 1944-46 gave 300+ shows for troops. Wrote 4 booklets: Victory Bouquet (1944, 16pp), Walsh Cane Routines (1945, 33pp), Rope Hectic! (1946, 19pp), & Miracle Silk. Famous for his 6,000 illustrations for & hand-lettering of the entire text of Rice's 3-volume Encyclopedia of Silk Magic (1948-62). [LR8/95;NT11/69;Bo3;St;Tay]

name: Martinez, Chuck
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro dealer (Magicians' World) in San Diego, California, c1971-1987. Left pro magic for film production work including as director of the comedy Nice Girls Don't Explode (1987) with Paul Harris as screenwriter.

name: Martinez, Daryl [Edward]
bio: (San Jose, California: 13 Aug 1955- ) Inspired by & learned from a family friend's gift of a Svengali deck. Pro close-up since 1972, mainly with the 31 tricks of his own invention such as Ultimate Ambition, Double Dazzling Triumph, Half & Half, Jumping Knot of Pakistan, & Cardboard Chameleons. Aka "Daryl" since 1980. Repeated tours of Europe & Japan. A major performer & lecturer. 1978 IBM 1st place in close-up; AMA Best Close-up Magician, 1980, 1981; 1982 FISM 1st prize in card magic; 1985 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize; 1988 AMA Best Parlour Magician; 1989 & 1993 AMA Best Lecturer; 1993 Desert Magic Seminar 2nd prize. Wrote ?Daryl? (1980), Daryl's Lecture Notes #2 (1982), Daryl's Psychological Assembly (1985), Daryl Does Den Haag (1988), The Vernon Chronicles (3 vols, 1987, 1988, 1989), Focus (1990, 1990, etc.). Contributed original tricks to Linking Ring, Richard's Almanac, Chaos, Arcane (France), & Revue de la Prestidigitation as well as to several books. Video (1985), video segment (1988), & video Encyclopedia of Card Sleights (8 vols, 1996-97). See Stephen For Your Entertainment Pleasure: Magic by Daryl (1982, 90pp); & Stephen Minch, Daryl's Ambitious Card Omnibus (1987, 152pp; French tr 1989 by Vollmer). [Bo#255; Mag; Wat; Wh2]

name: Martínez [Agusti], Josep Ma.
bio: (Gavà, Catalonia, Spain: 7 Apr 1946-) Pro magic impresario. Magic shop owner (El Rey de la Magia) in Barcelona 1984-1992-present. [Xe]

name: Martini
bio: (England: fl.c.1940s) Stage name of A. Smith. Owner of an architectural firm in Preston, Lancashire. Semi-pro magician with manip act & also a pseudo-Chinese act as "Wun Sli Wun".

name: Martinka, Antonio [later Anthony]
bio: (Prague, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 1832-4 Dec 1915). Illusion builder for Kratky-Baschik. Moved to USA in 1872, changing given name to Anthony. Pro dealer in New York City with younger brother Francis since 1873. Joined the SAM in 1902 as Member #18.

name: Martinka, Francis J.
bio: (Prague, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 7 Mar 1843-4 Nov 1924) Born Franz Martinka. Moved to USA in 1872 with elder brother Antonio. Pro dealer ("Martinka's Palace of Magic") in New York City 1873-1917 during which time it was the leading magic shop in the USA & the gathering place of famous magicians. Sold in 1917 to Charles Carter (whence known as "Martinka & Company"). Co-founded (with Ellison and Mortimer) the SAM in 1902, although held only Membership #19. Visited London in 1902. [St]

name: Martins Oliveira, Saturnino José
bio: (Miragaia, Oporto, Portugal: 2 Nov 1895-25 May 1965) Math teacher. Amateur magician, having been taught by Horácio Ramos. Became the leading force in & teacher of magic in Portugal. Founded the Internacional Instituto de Recreações Scientificas in 1912, the 1st major Portuguese magic club. Edited O Illusionista 1921-22, the 1st major magic periodical published on the Iberian peninsula. Director of Le Monde Occulte (1924-25, 6 issues, edited by Ceillier) Wrote 21 books & booklets in Portuguese, including O Rei das Diabruras (1917, his first), Inaudisme Scientifique (1924, 32pp in French & Portuguese), Blacaman e os seus truques (1926), Magia Teatral (1940, 320pp; 2nd ed 1948), Magia do Fogo (1944, 325pp), Magia do Sécolo XX (1962, 217pp, his last book). [Cam;Dif]

name: Martyn, [Victor Clifton] "Topper
bio: (Maida Vale, London, England: 30 Oct 1923-24 May 2004) Of Australian [sic] parents. Inspired & learned assisting parent's stage act ("Martyn & Florence") since age 2. Pro debut in 1925. Juggler-magician, working nightclubs, variety, cabaret, ice shows (the first juggle-on-ice), & circus. In 1959 moved to Sweden where he became a citizen. 1969 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix. 1970 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic (shared with Armandi). 1972 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. 1973 & 1982 FISM 2nd prizes in comedy magic. Set 1986 Guinness record for fastest magician (69 tricks in 4 minutes), a dubious distinction but fine publicity, one that Dr Eldoonie later beat and The Napoleons parody. Has toured Europe, North & South America, Africa, & Japan. Collects books, posters, etc on circus, magic, & the occult. 1986 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. 1990 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1996 Magic Circle Carlton Award. Wrote Easy Juggling for Magicians [1975] & lecture notes. Articles in Magic Cauldron, Genii, Magical Bookie, Mystics Magazine, etc. See also Gene Anderson, Topper's Mad, Mad Magic (1974). [MC4/88;Bo#217;Hudd;Genii3/78;Mag;Wh2]

name: Martz, George
bio: (Germany: c1901-1971) Immigrated as youth to USA. Partner since 1941 with Eddie Fields in their two-person mind-reading act. A suicide in a nursing home where he cut his wrists in the bath. REF: Minch (1992), 92-214.

name: Maru
bio: (Schmölln, Germany: 21 Jul 1920-1 Sep 1982) Stage name of Rolf Mahn. [Roh]

name: Marucci, Peter [Patrick Thomas]
bio: (Guelph, Ontario, Canada: 15 Sep 1939- ) Of Italian extraction. Learned at age c10 from books (Mulholland, Elliott, etc) & lessons from Charlie Roe. Syndicated columnist & restauranteur in Fergus, Ontario, where he moved in 1984. Semi-pro close-up & restaurant table-hopping magician since 1985. Invented With a Train of Salt. Columnist for Linking Ring. [LR4/89;Wh2]

name: Marvel, Dick
bio: (Porto, Portugal: 25 Jan 1940- ) Stage name of Manuel OLIVEIRA ALVES DA SILVA, earlier aka "Marvelino". Learned in 1947 by assisting in shows. Pro since 1958 with close-up & stage magic (that features doves, rabbits, & miniature dogs). Moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1958, touring throughout South America with assistant-wife "Mery Marvel" (until 1977 when they separated) & son "Joe Marvel" (1969-72). Won several South America awards. Moved back to Portugal in 1977. Pro dealer ("Magic Stúdio Dick Marvel") in Espinho, Portugal, since 1979. Wrote Uma dedeira e muitos efeitos (1967; 2nd ed, 1989). Articles in several journals in Latin America, Portugal, Spain, Germany, Italy, & England. TV bits in South America. [Cam;Wh2]

name: Marvel, Joe
bio: (Espinho, Portugal: 1 Sep 1957- ) Stage name of José Manuel de PINHO OLIVEIRA E SILVA. Son of "Dick Marvel" & "Mery Marvel" with whom he moved in 1958 to Brazil. Learned assisting his father 1969-72 part-time, then full-time assistant. Student of David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg who taught him shadowgraphy. Since 1974 pro shadowgraphist & illusionist, doing club work in Argentina. In Portugal 1977-79 where he toured the casinos & won 1st prize at Figueira da Foz magic festival. In 1979 returned to Buenos Aires, playing local clubs & touring Europe, Near East, & Mexico (1985). Now lives in Portugal & tours abroad. TV bits.

name: Marvel, Mery
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 12 Jun 1942- ) Stage name of Maria José de Faro de PINHO PEIXOTO. Grand-daughter of Viscount Faro e Oliveira. Assistant-wife of "Dick Marvel" & mother of "Joe Marvel". Moved to Brazil in 1958, remaining there to work throughout South America as a single after separating from her husband in 1972. In 1974 moved to Buenos Aires, Argentina, where she mainly works TV & childrens shows. Occasionally tours Argentina. Also directs a childrens program agency. [Cam]

name: Marvelli, Fredo
bio: (Neustadt, Upper Silesia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Prudnik, Poland]: 4 May 1903-6 May 1971) Stage name 1923-55 of Friedrich "Fritz" Jaeckel. Moved to Germany. Pro from 1923. MZvD Congress 1st Prizes 1937 & 1938. Since 1939 worked in the Hofzinser tradition. Toured several countries, including South America & USSR. Known as the "Paganini of the Magical Art". Retired in 1955, giving his stage name to Olof Becher. Died in Andorra. [Win;St]

name: Marvelli Junior
bio: (Rendsburg, near Kiel, Germany: 7 Jun 1932-) Stage name of Olof Becher. Son of a middle-school teacher. Aka "Rico" as amateur. Student of Al Torsten. Then student of Fredo Marvelli who gave his "Marvelli" stage name to him on retiring in 1955. Pro circus & stage magician in West Germany with tours to over 40 countries. Played the East Berlin Friedrichstadt-palast in 1960. Assistant is his wife "Kari Karina". [Win;Magisches Magazin1/58]

name: Marvello, Harry
bio: (Dundee, Scotland: 9 Feb 1879-24 May 1967) Stage name of Harry S. Hutchison, aka "Harry Stiles", aka "Stiles, 'The Racing Knut'". Inspired by and learned as student and apprentice of "Herr Dobler" (Smith). Pro from 1896. Wrote The People's Book of Card Tricks (1909, 48pp). Toured Jeans' The Silver Hat 1913-19. Retired from magic to become a journalist.

name: Marvello, Kathleen & Kent
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s) Pro 2-person mind-reading act. Played St. George's Hall 1921 & 1923.

name: Marvello, Mark "Markie
bio: (Winthrop, Massachusetts: 17 Nov 1964- ) Stage name of Mark Laine Sokol. Inspired at age 10 seeing Henning & Mark Wilson on TV. Pro since 1980 with close-up act at trade shows, etc. Dealer (mail order) in Revere, Massachusetts, as Marvello Enterprises since 1988, with a retail shop in Boston since 1990. Marvello Enterprises also booked variety acts. Closed by mid-1990s when Marvello vanished from the magic scene. [Wh5]

name: Marvelo
bio: See: Lake, Lester

name: Marvillo
bio: (Germany: 23 Feb 1927-8 May 1989) Stage name of Arnold Liebertz. Survey engineer. Semi-pro dealer & inventor. Often travelled to England. Wrote How Do You Do It Yourself? (1962, 15pp) & Marvelous Mysteries of Marvillo (1975, 39pp). Articles.

name: Marvin
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 2 Oct 1932- ) Stage name of Jaroslav Randacek. Pro manip.

name: Marx, Ernest B. "Fess
bio: (USA: c1900-29 Aug 1956) Learned in 1912 at boarding school in Providence, Rhode Island. Physical education teacher in Baltimore City College. Semi-pro close-up & mental magic. Collector. Pet effect: Billiard Balls. Close friend of Thurston, Blackstone, & Harbin. Teacher (Baltimore night school course in Pyramid Club) of Bob Brooks (1946), Christopher, Fetsch (ca1930), Phil Thomas, & Cy Keller (1946). Sometime editor of Tablets of Osiris. Tricks in MUM. Died in Baltimore.

name: Masculin, Prince P.
bio: See: Lampini, P. P.

name: Mashford, Robert G.
bio: (Sydney, Australia: 4 Sep 1912- ) Aka "Mysto". Inspired & learned as a boy seeing magician blunder with the Passe-Passe Bottles. Pro stage act with assistant and small illusion. [Go2]

name: Maskell, Alan [David], MIMC
bio: (Cambridge, England: 27 Feb 1957-) Learned as child from box of tricks & semi-pro magician father, Eric. Zoo keeper since 1973. Moved to London in 1976 to work at London Zoo. Seriously learned from Curry's Magician's Magic in 1977. Semi-pro magician since 1979, specializing in close-up & cabaret. Articles in Abra. MIMC 1988.[MC11/88;Wh2]

name: Maskelyne, E[dwin] A[rchibald] "Archie
bio: (Britain: -26 Sep 1920) 2nd son of J.N. Maskelyne, his magic teacher. Co-manager of (and occasional performer in) Maskelyne's from 1911 until his death in 1920.

name: Maskelyne, Capt. [E.] Clive, M.C.
bio: (Britain: 1895-early Sep 1928) 2nd son of Nevil Maskelyne from whom he learned as apprentice. Pro illusionist. Played St. George's Hall 1920, 1923, & 1924. 3rd president of The Magic Circle 1924-26. Left the Maskelyne company in 1926 to tour abroad, including South Africa. In 1928 left for India & the Far East but on the outward voyage died at sea of pneumonia. His daughter Althea had been born in 1926. [Pr;Go2]

name: Maskelyne, James Nevil
bio: (England: -May 1960) Eldest son of Nevil Maskelyne. Although never interested in magic, became on his father's sudden death in 1924 a co-partner in Maskelyne's with his 3 younger brothers. As a railroad buff he edited Model Railway News (1937-57) & wrote Locomotives I Have Known. [Pr]

name: Maskelyne, Jasper
bio: (London, England: 29 Sep 1902-15 Mar 1973) 4th & youngest son of Nevil Maskelyne from whom he learned as apprentice. Pro debut in 1924. Did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Wee Tinn Cann" c1928 in addition to his usual stage act. Played the London Palladium in 1931. Ousted from Maskelyne's on vote of brothers John & Noël in 1933 & thence toured on own, including in South Africa. Pet effects: Linking Rings & the Razor Blade trick. In WW II, as a major in the British Army Camouflage Corps, headed the experimental section in the Mediterranean Theatre, transferring after VE-Day to India. (The importance of his moderately distinguished wartime deception role has been much exaggerated). Then returned to the stage until retired in 1950 to become a farmer in Kenya. Wrote Secrets of Magic (1929), which was ghosted & largely plagiarized Goldston. Ghosted autobiography is White Magic: The Story of the Maskelynes (1936, 287pp). Ghosted by Frank S. Stuart & largely false memoir of his Army camouflage work in WW II is Magic--Top Secret (1949, 191pp). A grossly misleading bio is David Fisher, The War Magician (1983, 315pp). A fine bio is Richard Stokes, Jasper of Make-Believe (2004-05). [Pr;Go2;Bo#190-191;Ch;St]

name: Maskelyne, J[ohn] N[evil]
bio: (Cheltenham, England: 22 Dec 1839-18 May 1917) Founded the great Maskelyne dynasty of English magicians. Best known among his colleagues as simply "J.N.". A Mason. Pro since 1865 when he co-invented (with George Cooke) & staged the Box Trick(1). Played such venues as the London Crystal Palace 1867 & 1873. Then, on 26 May 1873, with Cooke opened in the Egyptian Hall's Small Hall, a "three-month" contract that soon proved moved to the upstairs Large Hall, which they monopolized until 1904 when, with the building scheduled for demolition, they moved to St. George's Hall. There he brought in David Devant as partner 1905-15. In 1873 co-created (with G. Cooke) Will, the Witch and the Watch, which became the most popular of Maskelyne's many playlets. Invented Psycho (with farmer J.A. Clark, 1873-75), Cleopatra's Needle (1879), & the Dictionary Trick (by 1885). 1973 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" (posthumous centenary of his Egyptian Hall debut) award. Wrote Modern Spiritualism (1875, 182pp); Sharps and Flats (1894, 335pp; repr 1895 & 1971), an exposé of gambling cheating; & My Reminiscences (1909). See also George A. Jenness, Maskelyne and Cooke: Egyptian Hall, London, 1873-1904 (1967, 93pp). [Pr;Ch;Cl;Go2;La]

name: Maskelyne, Mary
bio: (England: c1906-10 Mar 2000) 5th & youngest child & only daughter of Nevil Maskelyne. Pro on-stage assistant with Maskelyne's troupe & own act 1929-35. In 1934 married tenor T. C. Sterndale Bennett. Retired when Maskelyne's Mysteries closed in 1935 to run her own entertainment agency & since 1942 as stage manager & wardrobe mistress at the Players theatre. [Pr]

name: Maskelyne, Nevil
bio: (England: 1862-21 Sep 1924) Eldest son of J.N. Maskelyne from whom he learned in 1886 as apprentice. Pro since 1886. Invented the Miniature Spirit Cabinet (1888), Dancing Handkerchief (1888), gooseneck (1894), & hoop-passing (1894). 2nd president of The Magic Circle 1906-24. Edited Magic Circular 1906-09. Co-wrote (with David Devant) the classic Our Magic (1911, 316pp; repr 1946 & 1992). Articles in Magic Circular. [Pr;Go;Go2]

name: Maskelyne, Noël
bio: (England: 23 Dec 1899-23 Aug 1976) 3rd son of Nevil Maskelyne from whom he learned magic. Electrical engineer to pro illusionist in 1927. Retired in 1934. [Pr;Go2;St]

name: Masklyn ye Mage
bio: See: Palmer, Tom

name: Masqué, L'Homme
bio: See: "Homme Masqué, L'"

name: Mason, Bob
bio: See: Stenner, Robert Mason

name: Mason Jr, Edward
bio: See: "Ned, Our"

name: Mason, Eric
bio: (Britain: -10 Jul 1977) Left his first job in a bank to work as a salesman for Goldston. Then on own as pro illusionist. Aka "The Great Masoni" since 1947. Bit part with birds in movie Passport to Pimlico (1949). Got rights to "Maskelyne's Mysteries" from Jasper Maskelyne in 1950 & used it in his 1950-51 season. Worked a Giant Memory act with his Chinese-English wife "Shan". Magic Circle Gold Medalist. Autobio is Showmanship Out of the Hat (1970, 50pp). [St]

name: Massecar, Ray [full name]
bio: (Waterford, Ontario, Canada: 20 Jun 1925- ) Of Pennsylvania Dutch stock. Learned magic at age c15. Travelling automotive parts salesman. Semi-pro magician c1943-c1975. Collector of books & memorabilia. Amanuensis of Stewart James. [Wh]

name: Massey, Edward M[orrell]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 3 Feb 1893 [sic]-15 Nov 1964) Advertiser. Semi-pro magician. Illusion builder-inventor in Ardmore, Pennsylvania, in 1930s-50s, for W.W. Durbin, Howard Thurston, etc. Invented the Penetration Frame (1927), Piercing a Woman = Rod thru Body (1931), Vivisection (1933), Finger Chopper (by 1941 when sold to Holden), Sawing through a Cigarette (by 1941), It's a Stopper (by 1941), It's a Corker (1943), Squeezaway Block (Mar 1946), Cabinet of Deodar (Aug 1946), Ribbon Fantastique (by 1947), Color Flight (Jan 1947), Card Dagger (Jan 1947), Commando Screen (by 1948), Massey Duplex Slate (by 1949), Trickette Penetration (1950), & Chinese Flame Clock (by 1958). Wrote New and Original Magic (1922, 205pp) & (as "Morrell Massey") Adventures of a Boy Magician (1934). See Frank Csuri (ed), Collected Works of Edward Massey (typescript). Also wrote (as "Morrell Massey") a detective novel, Left Hand Left (1932). Articles in magic magazines. Rhett Bryson is writing a book on Massey's life & magic. [Conjurors' Magazine 10/46; Han, pp52-53]

name: Massey, Théodore
bio: (France: fl. early 1800s) Amateur. Friend of Ponsin who described him as being "very ingenious at finding out methods relating to conjuring." Invented the transparent card by 1853.

name: Masters, Drew
bio: (Scotland: c1910-May 1990) Stage name of Andrew S. Masterson. Early winner of the British Ring Shield with his partner-wife Tess.

name: Masuda, Katsuya
bio: (Ishikawa, Japan: 2 Dec 1958 - ) Learned at age 13 from Tenyo's Billiard Balls. Close-up pro since 1988. Student of Johnny Hirose since age 27. Won 1998 TV M-1 Grand Prix Winner, 2005 Atsukawa Creative Award, 2008 Japan Magic convention Close-up 1 $ ^{st} $ prize, 2009 Japan Cup Magician of the Year. Invented Frozen in Time (1990), Mystery Hole (1990), Wow (2006) and others.

name: Mathevet, Raymond
bio: (France: fl.1960s-80s) Aka "Alix Rayma". AFAP Bronze Medal 1980, Silver Medal 1981, & Gold Medal 1986.

name: Matlin, Philip S. "Phil
bio: (Montréal, Canada: 1937-) Inspired in 1948 seeing a Blackstone show. Pro dealer since 1966 as founder-owner of Perfect Magic, a manufacturer, retail, wholesale, & mail order shop in Montréal. Also gives a twice-yearly magic course & co-sponsors conventions in Canada, notably the annual Magie Montréal. Article in Magic Menu. [Wh2]

name: Matley
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s) Minor pro. With the Needle Trick worked the London Aquarium & toured Britain with the Barnum & Bailey show (Fall 1898) as the "Needle King". REF: Barnum & Bailey, The Wonder Book of Freaks and Animals (London: 1898/99); Harvey L. Watkins, The Barnum and Bailey Greatest Show on Earth in the Old World (Paris: 1901). NOTE: Name may have been "Maxey" or "Maxie" who was billed as "The Human Sewing Machine" when played the Lynn Musee Theater in Lynn Massachusetts when Houdini saw him.

name: Matsuda, Michihiro
bio: (Japan: 9 Feb 1936-) Amateur close-up magician. Member of the Osaka Magic Club. 1978 Tenkai Prize. Most prolific writer on magic in Japan for both beginners and enthusiasts. Wrote Matsuda Michihiro Sakuhin-shu [Michihiro Matsuda's Creative Works in Magic] (1979). Articles in Fushigi & Svengali.

name: Matsumoto, Koichi
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 7 Apr 1947- ) Learned in 1960 buying trick in magic shop. Math teacher in Osaka. Semi-pro close-up magician. Pets effects: Ring on Wand, Coin Box, Cups-&-Balls. Collector since 1973, specializing in magic magazines. Invented Wandering Paper Pyramid (1983). [Wh2]

name: Matsuura, Dr Gene A[kira], MD
bio: (Hollister, California: 1 Jun 1940- ) Of Japanese parents. Learned at age 10 from brother's Linking Rings. Physician in San Francisco bay area since 1967. Amateur close-up magician, specializing in Linking Rings and Cylinder & Coins. Wrote Back to Back (1977, 24pp) & Tommy Wonder Entertains (1983, 41pp). [Wh2]

name: Matsuyama, Mitsunobu
bio: (Yokohama, Japan: 18 Jan 1948-) Learned at age 10 from books & props. Influenced by Tenkai, Takagi & Martin Gardner. Worked for Nissan Motor Co., Ltd for 28 years, starting as product design engineer and ending as general manager from overseas localization projects. Amateur magician for 4 decades, specializing in close-up magic, self-working, & mathematical tricks as well as magic history. Co-founder & co-sysop (with Y. Fujiwara) of "Magic Forum", Japans oldest online network for magicians, since 1988. Book authored: Anthology and New ideas of Self-working Magic (1999, Tokyo, 204pp). Regular contributor in The New Magic (1980-1993), One-Two-Three (1993-1995), The Magic (1992-2009), Gibeciere (2006- ). Tricks in Kijutsu Kaiho (1971), Maniac (1972), 15 Magicians' Omnibus (1975), Masquerade (1981), Epoptica Yearbook (1984), Trick Box (1992), Rigmarole (1993), Verbatim (1994), Arcane (1995), MAGIC (1996), Magic House (1993, 2000), Semi-Automatic Card Tricks (2002, 2004, 2006). Invented Time Tell (Chronometer Cards, 1975), his Pull Down Move card sleight (1974). Petal Count Force/Elimination Principle (1993) [Wh2]

name: Matthews, Dr [James] Brander, PhD
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 21 Feb 1852-31 Mar 1929) Noted theater critic (The New York Times) & drama historian. Professor of literature at Columbia U 1892-1924. Amateur magician since childhood. In winter 1863-64 saw Pepper's Ghost at a New York fair. Serious amateur magician (also juggler & Punch-&-Judy man) since 1867 when he visited the Paris Exhibition & bought props from André Voisin's "dingy" magic shop. Early member of IBM (#752). Friend of Houdini at whose funeral in 1926 he acted as one of the honorary pallbearers. Wrote Pen and Ink (1888, 229). Autobio is These Many Years (1917, 463pp). [WWWA;St;Silver;Dam2]

name: Matthews, James
bio: (England: c1820-1880) Minor pro illusionist & mindreader. Toured Capetown, South Africa, in 1875. In 1877 played the Polytechnic in London with Sylvestor's Talking Lion, Sidney Oldridge acting as his assistant. [CI]

name: Maule, Barry
bio: See: Shakespeareft, Len

name: Maurer, Otto
bio: (Gemersheim, Rheinland-Pfalz, Germany: 28 Oct 1846-15 May 1900) At age 5 moved with parents to USA. Tin smith in New York City when began repairing magic props by 1868. Thence, since 1872, as prop maker-dealer, first as the Magical Bazaar from a basement room in his grimy house at No.321 Bowery, which issued its earliest known catalog (68pp) in 1875. In 1884 his catalog had grown to 120pp. In 1887 Maurer was taught the back palm by a Spanish gambler from Mexico and he taught it to several magicians including Dr. J.W. Elliott & T. Nelson Downs who quickly spread its fame. Maurer operated since 1898 as The New York Magical Co. Died in New York City, his son taking over the business. [Albo95;Dif;Roh]

name: Maurer Jr, Otto
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro magician & juggler, playing both stage & society dates. After working some time in father's magic shop inherited it in 1900 & sold it in 1903 to John F. Gabriel. By 1907 was working in music section of a Newark department store. [Albo95]

name: Maurer, Paul
bio: (Drohobycz, Poland [now USSR]: 28 Oct 1925-) Stage name of Mieczysław Zbigniew Maurer. Learned at age c12 from books. After WW II studied musicology in Hamburg. In 1963 moved to Switzerland where he was a bank employee in Winterthur. Amateur close-up magician. With son Christoph (born 1966) as "Chris & Paul Maurer", a 2-person telepathy act that won 3 competition prizes in 1977-78 in Germany & Switzerland, including the 1978 MZvD 1st prize in mental magic. Invented ball-point thumb writer c1985. Editor of German edition of Hokus-Pokus 1986-present. Articles in Hokus-Pokus, Magie, Aladin, & Innovator. [Mec;Wh2] Maurice, The Amazing (USA: 23 Oct 1906-dead) Pen name of Morris Cohen. Pro mentalist, magician, & hypnotist. Worked mainly trade & industrial shows, niteclubs, & cruise ships. Wrote several booklets edited & published by Hades: Mentalistrix (1964, 36pp), The Big Buck in Magic (1965, 32pp), Paper Bag Magic (1967, 24pp), Mentalistrix Encore (1969, 31pp), Comedy Funnel Magic (1969, 24pp), Phone Book Magic (1974, 31pp). Tricks in several magic magazines & books. 2 years on TV with hypact.

name: Maurice, [John] Edward
bio: (London, England: 1894-25 Mar 1964) Pro. Wrote Showmanship and Presentation (1946, 46pp; repr 1968) & Stagecraft and the Magician (1950). Maurice, The Great (Algeria: c1886-17 Apr 1957) C. S. Maurice, of French-Jewish parentage, his father being Rabbi Joseph Cohn. Pro vaudeville & society card & manip act. Used French-accented English comedy patter when touring USA (1910, 1913, 1922-25, 1928, 1936, 1939-40), Britain (1911, 1915, 1920), & South Africa (c1920). Died in Hollywood. [Pr;Ho]

name: Maurice, Silent
bio: See: Chaude, Marius A.

name: Maurier, Henri[-Lucien]
bio: (Paris, France: 28 Sep 1865-5 Oct 1949) Pro acrobat since 1896 who turned to pro stage magic after a serious accident during performance in 1910. Pseudo-Japanese act as "Yorimoto" in 1910. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1917-20, being the last staff magician before its closing. President of ASAP 1928-41. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Maven, Max
bio: See: Goldstein, Phil

name: Maven, Mickey
bio: See: Karmilovich, Ted

name: Max, Prof.
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 24 Feb 1887-14 Jul 1964) Stage name of José PACHECO DE LIMA. Aka "Mr. Max". Pro stage magician. Founding President in 1922 of the Grémio Mágico Português. Toured Brazil in 1923. Father of "Max Júnior" (Alberto PACHECO DE LIMA, died 1962). [Cam]

name: Max Dif
bio: See: "Dif, Max"

name: Max Júnior
bio:
"Max the Magician" SEE: Howard, Max

[See also: "Max, Prof." [the Portuguese]]

name: Max, Mad
bio: (Oslo, Norway: 21 Mar 1949- ) Stage name of Oivind Haraldsen. Learned at age 8 from magazine. Pro kid-show magician, escapist, fakrist, & vent. Prize winner in England &

name: Maxam, Blake [Edward]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 6 Oct 1944-) Inspired seeing Harry Mendoza in 1952. Actor & writer Oakland. Part-time pro magician since 1962. Billed as "The Wizard of Ahs". Worked cruise ships (c1975), kid-shows, & taught magic classes (since 1985). Articles in Magick & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Maxam, Doc
bio: See: Freer, Winston

name: Maxel
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 5 Jan 1928-31 Jan 1980) Stage name of Manuel CIRUJEDA CREIXELL since 1947 when he began as a manipulator. 1964 FISM 3rd prize in general magic with his wife Maria Carreras as "Maxel & Mary". [Xe]

name: Maxey [misspelling?]
bio: See: Matly

name: Maxim
bio: See: Maggi, Vito

name: Maxo
bio: See: Pratt, E. L.

name: Maxwell
bio: See: "Holden, Max"

name: Maxwell, Rev J. B.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Gospel magician in Ozark, Kansas. Wrote 3 booklets on gospel magic: Conjuring for the Church (28pp), Magical Object Lessons (by 1940, 51pp), Still More Magical Object Lessons (1951, 37pp).

name: Maxwell, James
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-20s) Amateur specialized in card magic. Invented Carbon Card, which he published in Magic Wand in Mar 1920.

name: Maxwell, [Michael Gerard] "Mike
bio: (Oakland, California: 20 Jul 1959-) Learned at age 9 from mail-order magic set & library books. Writer/graphic artist-designer (& since 1988 as "A-1 Writing Service" in Sacramento, California). Semi-pro close-up & stand-up magician since age 14. Main writer for Jennings & Falanga's L&L Publishing house since 1986. President of A-1 MultiMedia (later A-1 MagicalMedia), which produces magic videos. Wrote Lake Tahoe Card Magic (1985), The Classic Magic of Larry Jennings (1986), The Commercial Magic of J.C. Wagner (1987), Larry Jennings: The Cartwright (1988), Daryl's The Psychological Assembly (1987), Bruce Cervon's The Black & White Trick (1989), Randy Wakeman Presents (1989), Michael Skinner's Ultimate 3 Card Monte (1990). Articles in Genii & Apocalypse. Video bit (1994).[Wh2]

name: Maxwell, Victor
bio: (England: fl.1910s-50s) Stage & pen name of George E. [or A. W.?] Thompson. Edited The Concert Magician 1914-16, for the Associated Concert Magicians club.

name: May, E. Leslie
bio: (Scotland: 1901-16 Apr 1980) Inspired & learned at age 7 from gift box of tricks. Soldier (Royal Army Medical Corps officer) for 25 years. Amateur mentalist. Articles in Jinx, New Phoenix, New Jinx, Pentagram, Magic Circular, Linking Ring, Swami, Mantra, etc. [NJ#19]

name: Maybach, Robert
bio: See: Farchmin, Robert

name: Maybers, Les
bio: See: Mayette, André & Veno, Robert

name: Mayer, Odo
bio: (Austria?: -23 Jan 1983) Magician in Austria. Edited Aladin for 25 years. [Nad]

name: Mayette, André
bio: (Lille, France: 1 May 1901-30 Apr 1978) Pro salon & card magician. Joined ASAP in 1925. Magic dealer (Magie Moderne) in Paris 1933-1965 when he passed the shop to Michel Hatte. Working with Robert Veno as "Les Maybers" won the 1936 Munich grand prix for their silk-magic act. ASAP 1st prize for invention 1929, 1930, 1932, 1935. ASAP Bronze Medal 1936. Founder-Director of Le Magicien 1937-72. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Silver Medal 1963. Collector. Tricks in Le Magicien. [Dif;Bou;Bou2;Rob1]

name: Maykel
bio: (Xixona, Spain: 14 Jun 1913- ) Stage name of Luis MIGUEL SANCHIS. Moved to Barcelona in 1920. Amateur since 1952, specialized in manip, mainly with cigarettes. 1966 Figueira da Foz 2nd prize in manip. [Xe]

name: Maymó Brothers
bio: See: Maymó Catalá, Fernando (with Ramon Maymó Catalá)

name: Maymó Catalá, Fernando
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 2 Feb 1922-) Son of Fernando MAYMÓ GOMIS. Learned at age 10. Performed comedy magic with brother Ramon MAYMÓ CATALÁ as the "Maymó Brothers". 1961 FISM 1st prizes in comedy magic & invention plus 1st prizes in Barcelona & Baden-Baden. CEDAM President 1966-71. TV bits in Italy, Switzerland, Belgium, & Germany. Father of Pedro Maymó. [Xe]

name: Maymó Gomis, Fernando
bio: (Llagostera, Gerona, Spain: 29 Jul 1897-31 Aug 1966) Son of a schoolmaster. Director of publishing firm (Graficas Maymó) in Barcelona. Amateur magician, aka "Señor Maymó". President of SEI 1948-50. President of FISM 1950 & 1964. Founder-President CEDAM 1952-66. Father of Fernando MAYMÓ CATALÁ. [Dif;Xe;Cam]

name: Mayne, Leger D.
bio: See: Dick, William B.

name: Mazakian, Eduard
bio: (England: fl.1930s-40s) Moved to USA where he lived for many years. Originally a marionettist, then a pro magician with pseudo-Chinese stage act as "Ho-Yam". Toured New Zealand, Australia, & Far East. Wrote The Magic of Ho-Yam (1949, 136pp). [St] (Czechoslovakia: 11 Mar 1920-) Pro stage magic with partner-wife Dagmar Mazakiova. 1958 FISM 2nd Prize in general magic. A teacher of Fee Eleisa. [Magie4/88;Dif;Mec]

name: Mazarian
bio: See: Lambert, Charles

name: Maze, Gene [A.]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 24 Oct 1928-) Pro boxer (1947-51), now carpenter in the Bronx, New York. Inspired watching John Scarne in 1950. Thence amateur close-up magician & expert cardman including ability to deal Centers from the Erdnase Grip. Pet effects: Card Warp & effects using gambling techniques. Card effects in New Phoenix, Apocalypse, Richard's Almanac, & Poland's First Addendum book. See Karl Fulves, Packet Switches, Parts 4 (1977) & 5 (1977); Richard Kaufman, The Gene Maze Card Book (1980, 92pp); & Stephen Hobbs, Gene Maze and the Art of Bottom Dealing (2000). Video: The Magic of Gene Maze (1992). [Wh91;Wh5]

name: Mazin, Arthur
bio: See: Kreskin

name: Mazony
bio: See: Wiencek, Hans-Joachim

name: Mazoy [Kuri], José Luis
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 8 May 1949- ) Lawyer. Amateur magician since 1974 as "José Luis", specializing in history, collecting, & briefly manufacturing. His magic shop (La Cueva del Gnomo, founded 1988) & magic factory & import-export business (La Galeria) in Mexico City were the largest dealerships in Mexico during their brief existence. Founding Life President of Circulo Mexicano de Ilusionistas 1977-present. 1984 PCAM 1st prize for stage magic. 1989 Order of the Magic Lamp. [Wh2]

name: Mazza, Dino
bio: (Camden, New Jersey: 31 May 1920-21 Feb 1964) Inspired at age 28 seeing cups & balls worked by amateur George Fish. Learned in Chavez course. Contributed tricks & illustrations to New Phoenix. NOTE: Mc as surname prefix is alphabetized above as if spelled Mac.

name: Mead, Eric
bio: (USA: c1966-) Worked a magic shop 4 years. Pro close-up, mainly in comedy clubs then the Tower Bar as magic bartender in Aspen since 1989. Wrote Innovations (1985, 45pp). Tricks in MAJ & New Directions. Video bit (1994).

name: Meador, Gary
bio: See: "Darwin, Gary"

name: Meckel, Hans
bio: (Germany: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pet effect: Kling Klang.

name: Mecwaldowski, Jerzy
bio: (Kalisz, Poland: 22 Feb 1937-) Learned magic in 1955 from books. Lawyer in Lodz. Semi-pro magician as "Caroni" with stage magic & silk tricks. Invented Juggling Magician in 1974. Co-founder in 1976 of the Krajowy Klub Iluzjonistów (KKI). Editor-writer of Hokus Pokus, Poland's only magic magazine, since 1976 with 63 issues into 1991. Wrote scenarios for 3 magic shows 1980-86. FISM jury 1985. Since 1988 writes-directs the galas for the annual Polish magic festival in Lodz. Wrote Czarodziejskie Bajki (1983, 68pp); Vademecum Sztuki Iluzji (1985, 112pp), a useful magic encyclopedia; Jak Pan to Robi (1988, 232pp); Encyklopedia Sztuki Iluzji, Pt.1 (Card Tricks) (forthcoming, 470pp). [Mec;Wh5]

name: Medici, Tiziano
bio: (Modena, Italy: 17 Jun 1954- ) Insurance agent. Learned in 1976 from tricks bought during visit to Knott's Berry Farm in USA. Semi-pro magician since 1978 with parlor, comedy, & children's magic. Aka "Elliott". Pet effect: Rabbit in Dove Pan from Flames. Tricks in Varieta (with "Fabian"). [Wh5] Medrington, [Capt. Arthur] Charles [P.], MIMC (Liverpool, England: 12 Sep 1888-13 Apr 1934) Amateur in Birkdale, Lancs. Wrote 5 booklets: The Magicians Book of Patter (16pp), New Card Tricks for Experts (1904), Magical Novelties (1906, 24pp), Magical Stage-Craft (1908, 12pp), & A Dozen of Magic (1917, 32pp). Article in Magic Wand. [Go2]

name: Mehây, Dr.
bio: (Hungary: fl.1870s) Pro card manipulator. [Vo57;Cl]

name: Mehmet, Haci
bio: (Turkey: fl.1720s) Pro escapist who worked a double-exchange from baskets at a Turkish public festival in 1720 with his partner Haci Sahin. [Bo2]

name: Meier, Carlhorst
bio: (Nürnberg, Germany: 25 Sep 1929-) Learned in 1939. Amateur close-up & mental magician in Nürnberg. Founded the annual "Mental Workshop" in Nürnberg. Tricks in New Phoenix, Magie, & MUM. [MUM10/96;Wh2]

name: Meier, Ernst [sic]
bio: (Koethen, Anhalt, Germany: 25 Apr 1902- ) Aka "Meiro Ernestini". Semi-pro cardman & illusionist. [Go2]

name: Méjean, Michel
bio: (France: fl.1930s-70s) Amateur magician. Aka "Alma". Wrote Nouveautés cartomagiques (n.d.) &

name: Méjean, René
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Magician & mentalist in Paris. Aka "Louis Carli". Editor-in-Chief of Magicien. [Bou]

name: Melander, Love Björn
bio: (Sundsvall, Sweden: 28 Apr 1964-) Learned at age 6 from amateur grandfather. Pro since 1984 as "Love" with stage & close-up. Has performed 7 times for Swedish Royalty. Invented Flash Pen (1981). Nordisk Magikongress 1985 1st prize in card magic & 1986 1st prize in closeup. Wrote 48 Card Trix (1990, 96pp). Articles in Trollkarlen. TV bits in Sweden (10), Finland (1), & Germany (1). [Wh8]

name: Méliès, [Marie-] Georges [-Jean]
bio: (Paris, France: 8 Dec 1861-21 Jan 1938) Inspired by a Maskelyne & Devant show. Amateur magician (taught by Voisin around 1884). Pro debut in 1885 at the Salle Beethoven in Paris. Played the Cabinet Fantastique in 1888. Owner-director of the Théâtre Robert-Houdin in Paris 1888-1924 when retired. Founded L'Académie de Prestidigitation in 1891. During the period 1896-1912 he was a world-famous pioneer film maker, often adapting his magical knowledge to invent special effects. Retired from magic & cinema in 1924. In 1925 married "Jehanne d'Alcy", his former assistant & mistress, becoming co-proprietor of her tiny toy-&-candy shop in Paris. Made a Chevalier of the Legion of Honor in 1931. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. Articles in Passez Muscade. Autobio is Mes Mémoires (Rome: 1938). Bios are Maurice Bessy & Giuseppe Lo Duca, Georges Méliès, mage (Paris: 1945), which includes Mes Mémoires; Georges Sadoul, Georges Méliès (Paris: 1961); Madeleine Malthète-Méliès, Méliès l'enchanteur (Paris: 1973); Paul Hammond, Marvelous Méliès (1974); and John Frazer, Artificially Arranged Scenes: The Films of Georges Méliès (1979). A fine documentary film is Georges Franju's Grand Méliès (France: 1952). Compilation of his works on DVD: "The First Wizard of the Cinema (1896 – 1913)" - 173 films including "The Grand Méliés" by Georges Franju. [Dif;Vo55;Rob1;Katz]

name: Melinda
bio: (Knoxville, Tennessee: 5 Mar 1965- ) Stage name of Melinda Saxe. Moved to Las Vegas at age 3. Daughter of Bonnie Saxe (Las Vegas show producer-director-choreographer). Taught by Gary Darwin & Jimmy Grippo. Pro illusionist since 1987, working in sexy wardrobe & billed as "The First Lady of Magic". Pet effect: Zombie. In Las Vegas played the Bourbon Street showroom 1987-88, the Landmark 1988-89, the M-G-M Marina in 1990, the Sahara in 1991, & the Lady Luck Casino in 1992-95. Married Lance Burton in 1993 but soon separated & divorced. Partner-manager-boyfriend since 1995 is Steve Zadrick. Now (1997) lives in Florida. 1997 CBS-TV special. [LR11/93; Parade24/8/97]

name: Mélino
bio: (Brignolles, Var, France: 28 Mar 1863-1932) Stage name of Louis-François Méline. Pro 2-person mindreading act with "Miss Diana" (Odette Duval). Died in Belgium. [Dif]

name: Mellini, Hermann
bio: (Schönebeck/Elbe, Germany: 17 Dec 1843-25 Aug 1923) Stage name of Hermann Mehl. Son of stage actor August Mehl. Taught magic c1859 by his brother-in-law, Friedrich Joseph "Wilhelm" Basch. Pro illusionist in Prague. Toured Austria, Hungary, Turkey, Russia, Scandinavia, & Switzerland. Then on 7 Sep 1889 founded the Mellini-Theater in Hannover, making a small fortune from his presentations, which included Houdini in 1902. Sold the theater in 1900 but remained as Director until 1902. Son-in-law of Friedrich Joseph Basch & brother-in-law of Ernst Basch whose magic shop in Hannover he took over on latter's death in 1908, selling it to Reinhold Pfalz in 1918. Died in Berlin. NOTE: Otto Heinemann pirated the stage name "Mellini" for his USA tour sometime before 1906. [Win;Vo56;Dif;Mec;Roh]

name: Mellon, Ed
bio: (USA: -6 Aug 1960) Amateur dealer in mental magic in Uniontown, Pennsylvania. Invented Card-Assyst & Quantimental. Published Mental-Wise 1953-60 as house organ.

name: Melmore, W. M.
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-30s) Pro escapist. Worked with the Cirnoc Brothers. [Go] "Melot, Hermann" NOTE: Sidney W. Clarke's error for Hermann, Melot, which see.

name: Mel-Roy
bio: (USA: -1966) Stage name of Wilbert W. Holley. Began as pro pseudo-psychic with message-reading act in 1927. Did astrology over radio from Mexican border in c1932-33. Switched to pro tent-show magic in 1933. Married his assistant of one year Treva Holley (1909-2004) in 1936. Did a midnight Spook Show in mid-1930s to 1939 when they retired in Los Angeles. [Pr;Walk2]

name: Melson, Howard "Mel
bio: (USA: 1890-1958) Worked as illustrator for Abbott's. Edited Tops 1940-58. Invented "Abbott's Phantom Clock" (by 1945).

name: Mendes, Prince
bio: (USA: 1919-30 Sep 1955) Stage name of John "Jack" Mendes. Of Portuguese descent. Billed as "The Royal Deceiver". Pro stage magic & manip à la Cardini since the 1930s. In US Army entertainment in WW II in Irving Berlin's "This is the Army" touring show & in the 1943 Hollywood movie of the same title.

name: Mendoza, David
bio: (Montebello, California: 7 Feb 1960- ) Learned at age 13 from borrowed books & magic store tricks. Pro illusion builder since 1980 as founder-owner-manager of MagiCraft studio in Los Angeles, which builds illusions for theme parks (Busch Gardens, Knott's, & Sea World) & magicians (including Al Belmont, Copperfield, and Siegfried & Roy). [Wh2]

name: Mendoza, Harry
bio: (New York City, NY: 19 Jan 1905-1970) Main stage name of Harry B[ernard] Solomon. Inspired at very young age by father (manager to F.E. Powell) and then at age 9 watching Ching Ling Foo. Semi-pro since age 12 when he played US Army camps in WW I as a boy magician. Pro 1923-28. Became businessman 1928-38, moving to Southern California. Founding member of Los Magicos in Los Angeles in 1933. Returned to the stage in 1938, playing vaudeville-movie theaters & nightclubs with comedy magic as "Bernard, The Devil's Friend", "Ata Sun Gai--The Shanghai Jester", & "Mister Fi Ying Yu, the Chinese Magical Impersonator". In WW II did USO camp shows & toured SW Pacific, Alaska, the Aleutians, England, & France. Worked several movies as actor-magician (including Three Little Words in 1950) & as technical advisor. Edited AGVA News' magic page since 1950. Left pro magic to work for the Hollywood Trophy Company. AMA Board of Directors 1963-70. Tricks in Sphinx & column in Genii. [Th;Mag;WWM]

name: Mendoza, John [Frederick]
bio: (Moline, Illinois: 17 Nov 1947-) Pro close-up since c1967. Wrote The Book of John (1978, 138pp); Close-Up Presentation (1979, 107pp); Mendoza Series of Personal Instruction (1980); John: Verse Two (1980, 137pp) with German tr by O. Erens as Die zweite Strophe des Buch von John (1990); & Mendoza Portfolio One (1983, 194pp). See Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of John Mendoza (1983, in French). 2 videos (1989), 3 audios. [Wh5]

name: Menge, R. N[orman] "Norm" [pronounced MIN-jee]
bio: (Arkansas?, USA: -10 Feb 1958) Edited Normans News 1943-44 (7 issues) in Hot Springs, Arkansas. Then since 1944 pro dealer, joining U.F. Grant as his partner in Grant's shop in Columbus, Ohio. Invented Climax Egg Bag (1944), Tricky Tumbler (by 1947), Witch's Wine (by 1947), Milk & Silk Cylinders (by 1947), & Egyptian Water Box (probably in 1950s).

name: Ménito
bio: (Paris, France: 1908-c1988) Stage name of André Ménétrier. Pro manip since 1932 with cigarettes, billiard balls, &, later, gloves. Toured Europe including Finland (1948). Left magic in 1960s to work as a movie adviser. [Dif; Magigram10/89]

name: Menna, Lisa [Jill]
bio: (Norwalk, Connecticut: 24 Jul 1964 [sic]) Raised in Humble, Texas. Learned at age 11 to entertain at birthday parties. Pro close-up & stand-up since 1982, mainly for corporate clients. Has performed in about a dozen countries. 1986 TAOM Close-Up Trophy, the 1st woman to receive it. 1994 U.S. Invitational Closeup Championship 3rd place. Invented Twinkle from My Eye (1983) & High Heel Card Stab (1985). Wrote lecture notes for 1989 Austrian convention & for 2 NY Symposium books. Video segment (1986). TV bits abroad. [MUM1/99;MUM1/98;Fi2;Wh2]

name: Mentzer, [Alfred J.] "Jerry
bio: (USA: 28 Apr 1940-) Pro magic manufacturing & publishing as founder-owner of mail-order Magic Methods in Greenville, South Carolina, c1972-present. Prolific author, including Card Cavalcade (5 vols, 1972-1979, 159+225+188+166+183pp); Close-up Cavalcade (3 vols, 1973-77, 163+159+163pp); The Magic of Paul Harris (1976, 67pp); Counts Cuts Moves and Subtlety (1977, 73pp) with Spanish tr by Anaya & Carmona as Cuentas Cortes Moviemientos y Sutilezas (87pp); On the Corner Short (1984, 15pp); Climax Coins Trix with 3" Coins (1986, 36pp); Card to Wallet: The Book (1991, 166pp); Magic with Credit Cards (1992, 80pp); Card File (1993, 237pp). Tricks in Linking Ring (+ 1-man "Parades" in 1965 & 1972), Magick, etc. [Wh2]

name: Mephisto
bio: See: Davison, Robert

name: Méphisto, Docteur
bio: See: Cordelier, François

name: Merbak
bio: See: Briggs, J[ames] Albert

name: Mercedes, Joe
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1888-7 Jul 1966) Stage name of Joe Cohen. Debut as a boy at the Clark Street Museum in Chicago. Since around 1912 did a 2-person mind-reading act in vaude with Nellie L. Clement who performed as "Mlle. Helene Stantone". Their 4-week run at the New York Palace in 1914 was a record never broken & they played there again next year. They married in 1918. Toured Britain 1921-22. Retired in 1932 to manage a travel agency in Chicago. They did a 1943 USO tour. [Pr]

name: Mercedes, Mrs Joe
bio: (USA: c1882-5 Feb 1971) Born Nellie L. Clement. Joined Joe "Mercedes" Cohen in 2-person mind-reading act c1912 as "Mlle. Helene Stantone". Married him in 1918. Crushed by a stage elevator trap in 1932, she was forced to retire. [Pr]

name: Meriweather, Mr.
bio: See: Cramer, Stuart

name: Merlin
bio: (Carmarthen, Wales: c450-536) Legendary wizard at King Arthur's Court & an inspiration for some modern magicians. A biography that reveals the man is Dr Norma Lorre Goodrich, Merlin (1987).

name: Merlin, Jack
bio: (Schenectady, New York: c1885-) Stage name of James "Jimmy" W. Myers from 1906 until later legalized. Learned at around age 20 assisting Nightingale. Debut in 1906 as amateur. Pro vaude comedy cardman since 1908 throughout the USA, England (1908-11), Australia (1916 & 1926), & Canada (1935). An alcoholic, he disappeared after 1935. Authored (ghosted by Doc Brumfield) the classic "... and a Pack of Cards" (3 parts, 1927-1928; revised 1-vol ed by Jean Hugard, 1940, 93pp). Trick in Expert Card Technique. [Pr;Wal;Magic10/10;Tay]

name: Merlin, Jean [-Joseph-Georges]
bio: (Paris, France: 18 May 1944- ) Merlin is his real family name. Learned at age 6 from father's magic set he found in attic. Pro close-up magician since age 20, specializing in comedy, rope, kid-show, & balloon magic. Also works trade shows. Taught Gaëtan Bloom c1966. Aka "Melkiston". Pet effect: Paper Balls Over the Head. 1973 FISM 2nd prize in close-up. AFAP Bronze Medal 1979. Co-published (with James Hodges) Mad Magic 1975-84. Some 600 lectures in Europe & USA (1973). Wrote Premier livre de Close-up (3 vols, 1973-79), Ropes Series (4 vols, 1973-81), My personal routine of six foulards (1983), La plupart des foulards ont quatre coins (1984), Prédiction définitive (1986, with Italian, German, & Dutch translations), & Le grand livre des ballons (1985; English tr as Great Balloons, 120pp). Articles in Mad Magic, Journal de la Prestidigitation, Arcane (France), & Magicus Journal. [Dif;Le;Bou;Wh2]

name: Merlin, June
bio: (Belfast, Northern Ireland: 26 Jun 1919- ) Stage name of June Elizabeth Cochrane, a former Miss Northern Ireland who married Billy McComb in 1949, winning the British Ring Shield with him that year. Learned assisting him plus coaching from Al Koran & Bob Harbin. Pro stage magic since 1949. In British film The Intimate Stranger (1956; in USA as Fingers of Guilt) did her act plus extra bits. Separated from husband in 1967 & now retired in southern Spain. [Mar]

name: Merlini
bio: See: Rawson, Clayton

name: Merlini, Jim
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-60s) Stage name of T. James Bartlett. Amateur? Wrote Pastebroard Parade (1956, 22pp). Articles in Abra & Magic Wand.

name: Merlino, Mario
bio: (Bydgoszcz, Poland: 1933- ) Stage name of Marian Grzelczak. Pro illusionist. [Mec]

name: Merriss
bio: See: Wolf, Carl

name: Mertens, Fritz
bio: (Austria: 10 Jun 1896-24 Feb 1971) Stage name of Friedrich Lahner. Amateur comedy magician in Vienna. In 1934 played role of the magician ("Tokitho") in operetta Der singende Traum. Wrote Wir lernen zaubern (1941, 72pp; rev ed, 1950, 99pp) & Zaubern: Magische Spezialitäten aus Wien (1955, 146pp, with Otto Scadelli).

name: Merton, Hal B.
bio: See: Peterkin, Walter

name: Mertz, Ray[mond Robert]
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 1949-9 Jun 2001) Learned in 1955 from pocket tricks & taught friend Harry Harrison c1957. Printer near Buffalo. Student of Karl Norman in 1973, Semi-pro magician with bar, close-up, kid-show, & restaurant magic. Worked the Forks Hotel since 1975. Wrote Magic of Ray Mertz (2 vols), Eddie Fechter Lecture Book, & The Close-Up Magic of Ray Mertz and Friends (1987, 83pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Hocus Pocus, Apocalypse, Magic Menu (columnist), & Genii. Awards. [Wh2]

name: Messenger, Ted
bio: (Crosby, North Dakota: 3 Jan 1927- ) Stage name of Richard Glenn "Dick" Walker. Inspired in 1934 by seeing Willard the Wizard show. Semi-promentalist in southern California 1940-51. In 1950 published-edited all 4 issues of Coven, a financial disaster, the 5th issue being confiscated by his printer & now lost. Articles in Coven. Invented Chinese Yoga Levitation (1950) & Witch Doll (1951). In late 1950 became a lion trainer for World Jungle Compound (later Jungleland) for 15 years, thence a technical writer for computer makers until retired in Riverside, California. [Wh2]

name: Messter, Oskar
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 22 Nov 1866-1943) Optical engineer, working in father's factory in Berlin, which produced scientific optical instruments. Among their clients were several magicians, including Bellachini. In 1892 Oskar took control of the firm. In 1895 he began developing movie cameras. He produced & directed many short films from 1897 to 1917 when his company was absorbed by UFA. In 1897 he had introduced the close-up shot to German & perhaps world cinema. He is considered the "father" of German cinema. Memoir is Mein Weg mit dem Film (1936). A bio is Albert Narath, Oskar Messter, der Begründer der deutsche Kino und Filmindustrie (1966). [Bar;Katz]

name: Métayer, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1930s-70s) Manipulator, mentalist, giant memory, & close-up. Aka "Jean Corta". AFAP Master Magician. Editor of Journal de la Prestidigitation 1952-66. [Bou;Bou2]

name: Metcalfe, Dean
bio: See: "Dean, Carl"

name: Mexican Jim
bio: See: Notting, Herbert

name: Mexico, Willy
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 18 May 1940-) Pro sleights and illusions in West Germany since 1974. Hastoured Europe. [Win]

name: Meyenberg, William
bio: See: "Frazee"

name: Meyer, David [Clarence]
bio: (Hammond, Indiana: 25 Dec 1943- ) Grandson of Joseph E. Meyer. Learned magic in 1957 from a friend. Amateur performer 1958 until recently. Worked for Magic, Inc., in Chicago in 1974. Magic historian. Book publisher ("Meyerbooks") in Glenwood, Illinois, mainly on herbs & folk medicine but including 6 on magic: Moulton's Houdini's History of Magic in Boston (1983), Legerdemaine, Or Sleight of Hand from the Encyclopaedia Britannica (1986), The Wizard Exposed (1987), Bamberg's Illusion Show (1988), Alfredson's Newmann (1989), & Alfredson's Jean Hugard (1997). Article in Collectors' Forum. [Wh2]

name: Meyer, Joseph E.
bio: (Kenosha, Wisconsin: 5 Sep 1878-9 Mar 1950) Printer. An avid poker player, he wrote, typeset, & printed "Protection": The Sealed Book (1908, 121pp; repr 1911, 123pp; 1999, 191pp), a classic exposé of gaffed gambling devices gathered thru gambling-catalog printing contacts in Chicago. Despite the title-page claim of being published in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Meyer published it in the basement of his house in Hammond, Indiana. An herbalist since 1910 & banker since 1933. Grandfather of David Meyer.

name: Meyer, Orville [Wayne] "Orv
bio: (Harvard, Nebraska: 25 Aug 1911-22 Jun 1992) Inspired at age 15 (1926) seeing traveling magician. Learned in 1926 from books. Debut in 1930 in school shows, billed as "Nebraska's Magician". Invented his own version of the Bullet Catch in 1931, which he gave to Annemann in 1933. Moved permanently to Denver, Colorado, in 1933. Semi-pro club & mental magician since 1933 as "The Wizard of Ah's". Pet effects: Rising Cards, Card in Cig, Linking Rings, & Chinese Sticks. Reinvented Think! Ink! by 1944. In WWII in US Army tours camps with USO. Then became a personnel specialist with US Civil Service Commission. Also later as astrologer & psychic reader. 1989 PEA Achievement in the Art of Mentalism Award. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote 13 Jumbo Card Effects (1937); Magic in the Modern Manner (1949, 184pp), Telepathy in Action! (1961, 39pp), & The Amazing Magic Square and Master Memory Demonstration (1961, 18pp). Tricks in Sphinx, Jinx, Phoenix, HMM, Genii, LR, MUM, Magick, Vibrations, & Magic Manuscript. [MUM12/92;LR8/84;MUM3/52;Th:WWM;Wh2]

name: Mia
bio: (Presov, Czechoslovakia: 11 Jan 1953- ) Born Marie "Mia" Izarikova. In 1974 married Petr "Petrick" Krejcik who then trained her as his pro assistant, working as "Petrick & Mia" since 1975. In 1979 they escaped from Czechoslovakia & moved to USA. In 1980 they got the AMA Visiting Magician of the Year award. In 1983 they received the Dragon Award. Became USA citizen in 1986. [MUM11/91; Genii3/83; Wh]

name: Miaco
bio: (USA: 1912-1949) Stage name of Stephen A. "Steve" Frisbie. A mute. Pro sleight-of-hand with cards, billiard balls, & cigarettes. Played restaurants & nightclubs. Trick in HMM. Died poor in New York City. [Ho]

name: Micalet
bio: (Catalonia, Spain: 1909- ) Stage name of Miguel Carbonell. Pro comedy magician for nearly 20 years in Barcelona. Skilled carpenter & wood carver. Hired as assistant & stage manager by Fu-Manchú for his 1933-34 tour of Spain & Portugal and followed him back to Mexico 1934-35. Member of the Asociation Catalana de Aficionados al Illusionismo. [Bam, pp.169, 187, 190, 199]

name: Michael
bio: See: Sondermeyer, Michael

name: Michael, Lillian
bio: See: Altani, Oskar

name: Michaels, Gary
bio: (Dayton, Ohio: 31 Mar 1955- ) Stage name of Gary Smith Michaels (since legal change in 1976 from Gary Michael Smith). Learned at age c9. Demoed at Moon Fun Shop in Milwaukee at age 14. Network routing engineer in Michigan. Taught dice-stacking by Clarke Crandall & Cups & Balls by Paul Gertner. Semi-pro magician since 1975 with close-up & dice effects. Pet effects: Dice Stacking & Hex Nut Stacking, which he invented & premiered at 1976 FFFF. Demoed at O'Neal's Magic in Columbus 1975-77. [Wh5]

name: Michaels, Loren
bio: (Upland, California: 18 Oct 1955- ) Born Michael Loren Maxwell, now legally Loren Christopher Michaels. Learned at age 7 from father's gift of magic set & books. Started on road at age 16 assisting in Stan Kramien show. Pro close-up & stage magician since age 21, specialized in fire eating, fire fans, dancing torch, Razor Blade trick. 1977 Guinness world record (3.4 seconds) for strait-jacket escape. Toured own "Mirage" illusion show for several years. Invented Dagger Dove Suspension (1987). Wrote Sssssh!: A Lecture on Silent Magic (1986, 50pp). [Wh] "Michaels, Robert D." NOTE: A fictitious hoax magician of "extraordinary skill" jointly created by Bob Farmer, Michael Weber, Mike Close, & David Ben at an Ibidem Event. Their "Project ICBM" was intended to enroll him in the IBM & then jointly produce a Linking Ring "Parade" consisting of clever but inherently unworkable effects. "Although," as Ben wrote me in 1989, "Mr. Michaels has been rather inactive lately, one of his items--Invisible Triumph--was published by Harry Lorayne in Apocalypse. I created and submitted that routine."

name: Michalski, Karol J.
bio: (Poland: fl.1950s) Learned from father, a chemist & semi-pro magician who also called himself "Chandu". Moved to USA. With Ringling B&B Circus 1954.

name: Michalski, Martin
bio: (Germany: 3 Feb 1927-) Magician and collector-designer of magic sets in Ravensburg. Issued 3 magic sets. Wrote popular books for children: Der perfecte Magier (1963, 115pp), Das grosse Ravensburger Zauberbuch (1987), Zauberbuch für Kinder, Hokuspokus Zauberspass, Meine tolle Zaubershow, & 1 for adults: Zaubern: Spiel der Illusion (c1993). [Nad]

name: Michelassi, Antonio
bio: (Italy: fl.1640s) Pro magician in Florence where he called himself "Pimpirlimpi". Published an 8-page booklet on card magic, Nuovi giuochi di carte (1650), which describes, among other things, a system for stacking cards. [St]

name: Michelle
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Combines dancing with her magic act. 1986 Craig Trophy.

name: Mi-Chi-Co
bio: (Germany?: 21 Jan 1923-) Stage name of Louise Hermanndörfer. [Roh]

name: Michie, Doyne E. [pronounced MICKY]
