bio: (Steele, Missouri: 12 Aug 1921-) Learned in 1941 from college roommate amateur. Sales promoter & PR. Semi-pro close-up & club act magician since 1945 (full-time pro in early 1950s). Presbyterian minister 1950s-c1983. Since c1980 uses magic in his "The Therapy of Laughter" workshops for medical workers & businessmen. TV bit. Wrote Field's Famous Poker Hustle (1992, 16pp). [Wh2]

name: Mick
bio: (France: fl.1910s-20s) Stage name of L.-L. Philip. ASAP member before WW I.

name: Mickie Baby
bio: (Portugal: 19 Nov 1922- ) Stage name of Gilberto FIALHO BETANCOURT. Moved to Brazil. Worked with Carbel in 1938. Took 5th prize at the Círculo Brasileiro de Ilusionismo competition in Rio de Janeiro in 1957. TV bits. [Cam] Miesel, William P[eter] "Bill" [pronounced ME-zl] (Erie, Pennsylvania: 12 Sep 1935 – 23 Dec 2012) Inspired in 1941 seeing Harlan Tarbell at school show. Learned in 1944 assisting with a friend's Mysto Magic set. Grocery store assistant manager. Amateur card, close-up, & mental magician. Collector. Invented Open Travellers(2) in 1961. Editor of Menta-Lens 1964 (2 issues) & Precursor 1983-2012. Compiler-editor of Fork Full of Appetizers (2 vols, 1982, 1984). Wrote The Creative Card Magic of William P. Miesel (1980, 177pp), Improvisations, Best of Mental-Wise, Moe and His Miracles (1986), & Visionary Card Effects (1996, 184pp). Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, New Phoenix, Ibidem, Cardiste, Mental-Wise, Talisman, Magicol, Genii, Epoptica, Arcane (1-man issue in #13), etc. [LR11/86; MUM5/86; Wh2]

name: Miette
bio: (France: -1855) Son of a magician. Famous pro street conjuror in Paris for 35 years from 1796 to 1820. Worked on the Cups-and-Balls on the Quai des Grand-Augustins & the Pont-Neuf with his son. In 1805 also operated a tiny magic theater on the Rue de Madame. Pet effects: the Watch Mortar & Cake Baking in Hat. Mentioned by Robert-Houdin. Depicted by Just L'Hernault in Champfleury's Les excentriques (1852, 1857). A bio is Dany Trick, Miett: Physicien (1994, 16pp). [Dif;St]

name: Mifflin, John W. "Doc
bio: (Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania: 4 May 1899-) Debut around age 10. Semi-pro since c1927, using magic as salesman for Chesterfield cigarettes. Then as retail magic dealer 1933-37 (The Fun Shop), and since 1937 with partner as the wholesale Fun Novelty Company, both in Shamokin, Pennsylvania. [Th]

name: Mignosa, [Charles Philip] "Chuck
bio: (Cambridge, Massachusetts: 1 Mar 1944-) Inspired at age 8 seeing a circus magician & immediately learned from library books. Consultant in materials compatibility & process control in San Jose, California. Semi-pro mentalist & comedy magician since 1975, as "The Baba" (1979-present) & "Brian Christopher" (1984-present). Assistant to Ormond McGill since 1979 & McGill now also assists Mignosa. PCAM President 1987. PEA President 1988-89. 7 PCAM 1st prizes in Comedy & in Mentalism 1975-86. Invented Double T&R Paper. Edited Ormond McGill's Real Mental Magic (1989). Writing forthcoming (1990) bios of Ormond McGill and Ralph Adams Sr. [Wh2]

name: Mikado
bio: See: Hebenstreit, Horst

name: Mikkek, Vladimir
bio: (Yugoslavia: fl.1980s-90s) Pro manipulator. 1984 Austria 2nd prize in manip; 1985 Lódź 3rd prize; 1987 Karlovy Vary 2nd prize in manip; 1991 FISM 3rd prize in manip. [Nad]

name: Milan, Alan
bio: (Wakefield, England: 19 Jun 1930-27 Nov 1989) Stage name of Alan Cracknell. Pro in Britain as "Milan" with ghost shows featuring unusual psychic & mental effects. Played music halls & worked in a magic shop with Ken Brooke. Moved to USA where, as "Milan the Great", he toured theaters, carnivals, & fairs. Pet effect: Russian Roulette. Founding partner (with Ken Klosterman & Bill Pryor) of "Venture III" magic business 1982-86.

name: Milano, Fred
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 9 Mar 1910-27 Oct 1963) Stage name of Alfred Kistenmacher. Journalist & advertising man. Semi-pro magician with partner as "Milano-Pax" & "Frederic und Patricia Pax". Inventor of many original effects, including Königskronen-Trick. Semi-pro magic dealer in Berlin. Died in Hamburg. Wrote 2 booklets on easy tricks: Miniatur-zauberkunst (1930, 28pp) & Neue Zauberkunststücke (1930, 31pp), which totaled a record-breaking 6,000,000 copies sold, having been distributed as an advertising brochure by a Nürnberg margarine company. Articles in Zauberspiegel, Linking Ring, & Magisches Magazin. "Milky the Clown" SEE: Cummings, Clare Fox, Karrell

name: Miller, Mr
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 5 Mar 1908-) Stage name of Per Åke Millberg. Master shoemaker in Nyköping. Semi-pro magician as a skilled manipulator. First Swedish manipulator to appear in the variety program at the China Theatre (Stockholm) in Jul 1946.

name: Miller, [A.] Caro "Gig
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Long-time resident of San Jose, California. Musician. Semi-pro magician, aka "Caro". Pet effects: flash production of livestock & rag pictures. Founded the Mystic Thirteen of San Jose in 1932. Toured with the Fitzkee troupe in 1939-40 when billed as an Australian. Husband of Lynn Miller.

name: Miller, Charles Earle "Charlie
bio: (Indianapolis, Indiana: 25 May 1909-13 Aug 1989) Inspired by and learned magic from older brother at age 7. Moved to El Paso, Texas, at age 19. Moved to Los Angeles in 1933. Professional card sharp (until 1950s) & reported inventor of the notorious "beanshooter" holdout device. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand. Voted into the 12-member New York "Inner Circle" in 1936, despite living in the remote town of El Paso. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1955. A house magician at the Magic Castle since early 1960s. 1973 AMA Masters Fellowship. Worked cruise ships in late 1970s. In nursing home from 1988 until his death. Did not, as widely presumed, invent the buckle & Buckle Count, which he admitted in a pre-WW II letter was taught him at that time by A.J. Cantu. Did invent Ace Transformation (1941, which is miscredited to Buckley & to Paul Rosini). Many tricks in Expert Card Technique (1940). Wrote Black Art Well Tricks (1969, 32pp). See also Robert Parrish, An Evening with Charlie Miller (1961, 72pp); & Frank Csuri (ed), The Magic of Charlie Miller (typescript), a legendary compilation distributed in the 1960s in only 6 copies to the underground. Wrote the "Magicana" column in Genii 1964-88. Tricks in Genii, Talisman, & Arcane. Audio, videos, & video segment (1988; 1991). [Genii5/89;Par;Jinx#140;Mag;Wh]

name: Miller, David Prince
bio: (Mansfield, England: 1808-24 May 1873) Learned c1830 as apprentice to Lightwood. Small-time pro touring England & Scotland. In 1839 copied Anderson's Bullet Catching trick. Father of Louisa Miller with whom he worked a mind-reading act. In 1861 sold by mail-order from his London address his "Wizard's Box of Magic" (6 tricks) plus versions of the Dancing Sailor. Wrote Magic Made Easy [c1850, 8pp] & several other magic booklets. His frank autobio is The Life of a Showman (1849, 147pp; 2nd ed, 1851, 192pp). [La;Fr;Daw94,p34]

name: Miller, Ed[ward J.]
bio: (Louisville, Kentucky: 18 Dec [sic] 1892-27 Mar 1986) Pro since 1908 at age 16 & toured a large show since 1921. Associated with Harry Thurston & Professor Blankenbaker. In 1927 moved to Chicago where he opened a magic shop that also made fine metal & wood props. Owned large collection of lithos, programs, etc. [Magicol#80;St;Albo95,pp55-56]

name: Miller, [Michael] Gordon
bio: (Jackson, Michigan: 29 May 1939-) Learned magic in 1955 from newstand magic book & meeting an old-time pro. Pro stand-up comedy magician since 1961. Uses "Gordon Miller" as stage & pen name since 1976. Editor for Abbott's since 1968 (their catalogs #22 & #23 and some 14 books), including Abbott's Anthology of Card Magic (3 vols, 1968; rev 1989). Editor of New Tops 1980-present. 1981 Crandall Trophy. [Wh2]

name: Miller, Hugh
bio: (Wishaw, Scotland: 27 Apr 1937-) Writer. Amateur magician. With Unique Studios as manager 1963-64 & co-owner 1965-70 Wrote 9 books on the magic of Roy Baker, Horace Bennett, Eddie Joseph, Al Koran, Marconick, & Rink, which see. Also Magic for Minors (1960s?; repr 1972, 88pp), A Pocketful of Miracles: The Handbook of Impromptu Magic (1969), Secrets of Gambling (1970; repr 1972, 128pp), & Hypnotism (1977). Now writes crime thrillers (The Dissectors, Skin Deep) and true-crime books. [CA]

name: Miller, Jack
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY: 11 Feb 1884-23 Dec 1962) Inspired by and learned from father's gift of magic trick from Maurer's at age 10. Then apprenticed with The Great Cosgrove. Debut in 1898 with cups & balls. Professional illustrator & amateur magician. Later pro magician. Billed in 1920s as the "Giant Card King". Famous for his Egg Bag and his 5-ring Linking Rings routines. Taught George Gore, Julian M. Olf, etc. Invented King Koin. See Bob Novak, Jack Miller's Linking Ring Routine (1945, 36pp), Jack Miller, Jack Miller's Egg Bag Routine (1959, 10pp), & George Gore, The Linking Rings of Jack Miller (1973, 76pp). Tricks in Sphinx & Chronicles.

name: Miller, Jack M.
bio: (Syracuse, New York: 15 Jul 1922-24 Feb 2002) Learned at age 10 from gift Chandu magic set. Engineer. Semi-pro stage magician. Aka "Mr. Magic" thru 1950s & "Milo" thru 1960s. Speciality: "Anything with a dye tube". Invented Top Hat Surprise (1968) & Gem Busters (1969). Dealer & collector in Syracuse area. [Wh2]

name: Miller, John M.
bio: See: "Balabrega"

name: Miller, Katlyn
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Billed as "The Electric Lady". Semi-pro illusion & fire act. Adviser to Copperfield, Reveen, & Burton. [Mag;Wat]

name: Miller, L.
bio: (USA: fl. 1950s-70s) Acasino card dealer since the 1950s. Wrote Blackjack Exposed (1970, 25pp).

name: Miller, Leonard H.
bio: (USA: 1905- ) Interested as boy. With circus for 10 years. Specialized in fire magic. Wrote Thrilling Magic (1946, 25pp).

name: Miller, Louisa
bio: (England: fl.1850s) Daughter of David Prince Miller. Pro with clairvoyance act. [Fr]

name: Miller, Lynn
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-dead) As a founding member in 1939 of Magigals, she coined that word, only the second bit of magical jargon (after "Mysto") I am aware of that was coined by a woman. Pet effects: Floating Ball and Rag Pictures. Toured with Fitzkee's troupe 1939-40. Wife of Caro Miller.

name: Miller, Mark
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) A Chavez graduate. Pro. [Mag]

name: Miller, [Loretta] "Moi-Yo" "Miki
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 24 Apr c1917-) Learned as assistant to Dante since he hired her at age 16 in Melbourne in 1933. As she was under-age, he had to take out guardianship & post an £80 bond so she could accompany him on his East Asian tour. Promoted principal assistant in 1935 when he changed her billing to "Moi-Yo Miller". Pro until retired to live in southern California with her husband, Arturo Montes (died 1995), Dante's former stage manager, whom she had married in 1949. In late 1970s Bill Larsen Jr brought her out of retirement to lecture at conventions. 1982 AMA Special Fellowship. 1993 Dragon Award (with Arturo Montes). Moved back to Australia in 2002. NOTE: Given name sometimes misspelled "Floretta". The story about her rigged beauty contest in Australia is false. Both errors were she told me were "the figment of a press agent's imagination". [Pr;Wh2]

name: Miller, Paco
bio: (Quito, Ecuador: 13 Jun 1918- ) Stage name of Edmundo JIJÓN SERRANO. Inspired at age 17 seeing Chang show. Pro ventriloquist & magician since 1932. Moved to Mexico in 1940. Has full stage show. Pet effect: Okito Floating Ball. 1981 Government of Ecuador Gold Medal as Artist. 1984 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. Articles in Latin American magic magazines. [Ran;Wh3]

name: Miller, Roy
bio: (Brooklawn, New Jersey: 25 Nov 1921-) Learned at age 15 from library books. Sales manager. Semi-pro close-up & mental magician since age 30. Articles in MUM & Magick. [MUM6/68;Wh2]

name: Miller, Tom
bio: (Denmark: 16 Apr 1932- ) Stage name. Semi-pro magician & mentalist with pickpocket act & childrens show. Works Denmark & Iceland. Magic dealer. Holds world's record for Blindfold Car Drive (69.7 km) in 1984. NOTE: Not to be confused with "Miller" (Per Åke Millberg). [Dif]

name: Miller, [Henry] Welsh
bio: (USA: 1864-21 May 1936) Pro coin manipulator. Aka "D'Almora". Played the Casino de Paris c1901 & London's Palace Theatre Jun 1901 for 1 week. Grown insane in later years, he committed suicide (a "jumper"). [Pr;CMM3/07;HMM7/56]

name: Million, Jack
bio: See: Iversen, Tommy

name: Mills
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 15 Dec [sic] 1902-6 Mar 1981) Stage name of Arnold Ahlm. Pro comedy magician. Toured Sweden, Norway, & Finland. Magic dealer 1940-50. A founding-member in 1946 of the Swedish Magic Circle. [St;Dif]

name: Mills, Fred
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s) Invented Multum in Reverse, which Burtini introduced in 1948.

name: Milo & Roger
bio: See: Brandon, Arthur “Milo” & Coker, Roger

name: Milton
bio: (Mirabello Sannitico, Campobasso, Italy: 25 Feb 1944- ) Stage name of Fernando Giovannitti since 1960. Learned magic in 1955 after seeing Bustelli. Bank employee in Turin. Semi-pro magician since 1964, specialized in dove manip. Lecturer. Wrote Magia delle Tortore (lecture notes). Articles in Magia Moderna, II Prestigiatore Moderno, Revue de la Prestidigitation, Magie, & L'Illusioniste. [Wh5]

name: Milton, Herbert [Ernest]
bio: (Britain: 1 Sep 1897-1960) Pro cardman & close-up. Invented Sympathetic Clubs (1913). Specialized in public school shows in England. Played St. George's Hall 1923, 1924, & 1932 when he used jumbo cards for visibility. [MC]

name: Milton, Max
bio: (Göteborg, Sweden: 21 Apr 1932-) Stage name of Arne Strömbom. Semi-pro prize-winning card & close-up magician. Toured USSR in 1957.

name: Minar, Antoine
bio: (Kromeriz, Moravia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 1896- ) Son of a Czech goldsmith & watchmaker. Pro illusionist, touring central & southern Europe after WW I. Moved to Algeria until sometime after WW II, thence France. AFAP Master Magician. Wrote Mille et un tours originaux de magie (2 vols, 1949, 1950). Articles. [St;Bou]

name: Minch, Stephen "Steve
bio: (Tacoma, Washington: 10 Dec 1948- ) Inspired & learned from library books at age 7. At age 14 found first magic shop. BS in psychology. Pro writer of magic books, specializing in mental magic & close-up. Managed Micky Hades branch magic shop in Seattle 1976-87. Founded Hermetic Press in Seattle in 1989. Prolific author, mainly writing up the tricks of John Carney, Alex Elmsley, John Hamman, Larry Jennings, Milt Kort, Ken Krenzel, Daryl Martinez, Martin Nash, Dai Vernon, Bruce Cervon, Eddie Fields, Joe Rindfleisch, plus 3 of the 5 vols of The New York Magic Symposium series and Spectacle (1990, 168pp). His own books & booklets are The Book of Thoth (1974, 45pp), Mind and Matter (1975,52pp), Creations of a Magical Madman (1977), Lovecraftian Ceremonies (1979), Mind Novas (1980), The Robin Hood Caper (1982), Mind Melds (1984), Eyeless in Gaza (1984), Lovecraftian Ceremonies (1991, 48pp), & From Witchcraft to Card Tricks (1991), A Life Among Secrets (1992, 229pp), Ken Krenzel's Ingenuities (1997, 224pp), Kort (1999, 375pp). Also numerous articles in most major & some minor US magic magazines. [Lo2;Wh2;Wh2001] (USA: 31 Aug 1893-27 Jul 1952) Inspector with glassworks in Maplewood, New Jersey, since 1941. Semi-pro comedy stage magic with his "The Man with the Lamp Post" act. Invented "Framed" card trick c1944.

name: Minerva
bio: (England: fl.1900s-10s) Daughter of Mr Snelling of Newcastle. Pro escape artist who toured Europe. In 1907 moved with husband "Vano" to USA where she also toured. Divorced Vano in Chicago in 1909. Married Guy Jarrett in 1911, separating around 1919. [CMM, 288; Sphinx12/09; Collectors' Forum4/92]

name: Minguet é Yrol, Pablo
bio: (Spain: fl.1730s) Author of Engaños a Ojos Vistas [Deceptions in Plain View] (Madrid: 1733, 110pp; repr Madrid: 1733, 218pp; with many later reprints). This was the first book on magic in Spanish. Illustrated with many woodprints, it covers tricks with tumblers, silks, torn-&-restored ribbons, cards, & paper folds. [Dif;St]

name: Minguet y Vindex
bio: (Spain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pen name. Wrote Juegos de manos y de sociedad (Barcelona: 1900; several reprints).

name: Mingus, Prof.
bio: (East Orange, New Jersey: 1857- ) Stage name of Walter Mingus Hopler. Learned in 1893. Pro stage illusionist 1893-96 when retired. Invented Aerial Fishing in 1893.

name: Mingus, LeRoy H.
bio: (USA: 1897-1979) Pro dealer (Mingus Magic Shop) in Pennsylvania by 1953 when issued a magic set. Specialized in making feather flower props.

name: Minnette
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Minnette Lenier, wife of Jules Lenier. Billed as "The Sophisticated Lady of Magic". Pro stage magic & mind control act. [Mag]

name: Minns, Clement
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Pro vent-magician. Played St. George's Hall in 1926. Minoe the Mystic (India: 1881-14 Feb 1951) Stage name of Mino C. Cooper, a Parsi. Taught by Charles Bertram during the latter's tour in India c1899. Pro with Western magic since c1900, initially as a society magician. Beginning in late 1906 toured a large show thru India, Burma, S. Africa, & Near East. During WW II toured the Middle East. Then retired in Bombay where he died. Dubbed "Grand Patriarch of Magic" by the Society of Indian Magicians. Article in Jinx. [St;Magic1/07]

name: Mir, Alex
bio: See: Miroli, Alejandro

name: Mirakel, Dr
bio: (Germany: 21 May 1902-) Stage name of Dr Hellmuth Schlechtriem. [Roh]

name: Mireider, Frank
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Pro magician & escapist. Dealer in New York City in mid-1930s. Served in US Army in WW II.

name: Mireldo, Henri
bio: (France: 1910-) Stage name of Henri Chretienneau. Pro stage & circus illusionist. 1952 FISM prize for large tricks. Starred in Paris at Cabinet Fantastique 1964-65. AFAP Master Magician. Father of Viviane Mireldo. [Dif;Bou]

name: Mireldo, Viviane
bio: (France: c1951-) Stage name of Viviane Chretienneau, daughter of "Mireldo". Pro. Pet effects: dove & candle productions. Starred in Paris at Cabinet Fantastique 1963-64. [Dif]

name: Miret [-Azopardo], Charly
bio: (Madrid, Spain: 10 Nov 1931- ) Learned at age 9 from Boscar's Juegos de manos. Engineer (living in Germany since 1957). Semi-pro magician since 1970 as "Azardo", specialized in close-up, mental, & stage magic. Pet effects: Newspaper Tear & Ring on/off Rope. Member of Escuela Mágica de Madrid, IBM, SEI, CEDAM, MZvD, etc. 1999 S.E.I. Gold Medal of Merit. Despite paralysis in both legs since 1997 remains fairly active as a performer & at conventionsc. Articles & tricks in Misdirection, Ilusionismo, Lampara Magica, Circular de la Escuela Mágica de Madrid, Magie, Misdirection, and C.I.P. Has translated lecture notes of Ascanio, Tamariz, & Camilo into German. [Xe; Illusionismo11/99; Magia Moderna 12/2000; Wh5; Wh01]

name: Miris, Fatima
bio: (Cuneo, Piemonte, Italy: 27 Oct 1882-1954) Stage name of the aristocratic Contessa Maria Frassinesi d'Arco. Pro quick-change artist, one of Fregoli's better imitators. Included some illusions in her act. Played the Coliseu in Lisbon in 1893 & London in 1908. [CMM10/07]

name: Miroli, [D.] Alejandro [J.]
bio: (Argentina: -14 Dec 1968) Aka "Alex Mir". Founder & 1st president of Círculo Mágico Argentino in 1938, that country's 2nd and now oldest magic society. Dealer (Trucos Famosos) in Buenos Aires with a 165pp catalog in 1962. Wrote several books in Spanish including Burbujas magicas & Moderno Prestidigitator.

name: Mishell, Ed[ward E.], MIMC
bio: (New York City, NY: 1896 [sic]-11 Jul 1983) Lawyer. Amateur magician. Illustrator of many magic works. Wrote Wax Fax (1953, with Ted Collins), Hold-Out Miracles (1969, 57pp), & Elastrix (1979, 40pp, with Abe Hurwitz). Reviewer for Genii. Invented Fanorama fanning deck by 1964. SAM President 1972-73.

name: Misterius
bio: See: Bai, Ottorino

name: Miyako, Ukon
bio: (Japan: fl.1600s) Pro in Japan. [St]

name: Mocella, Marco
bio: (Naples, Italy: 20 Jul 1966-) Learned at age 7 from library books. Lawyer. Semi-pro magician as "Marcel", specialized in close-up & kid-show magic. Pet effects: Baking a Cake & coin magic. Tricks in Magia Moderna & Qui Magia. [Magia Moderna2/91;Wh5]

name: Mock-Sad-Ali
bio: (USA: fl.1900s-20s) Stage name of Charles B. "Mox" Mathas (or Mathies), aka "Max Adali". Learned assisting the original "Mock-Sad-Ali" at fairs. Pro. [Pr;An]

name: Moe
bio: See: Seidenstein, Morris

name: Moehring, John [Charles]
bio: (Houston, Texas: 19 Jul 1942-) Learned at age 10 visiting Howard's Fun Shop in Houston. TAOM Best Junior Magician 1960 & 1961. TAOM Best Performance 1962. Pro stage magician billed as "The Texan Trixter" 1960-70, beginning with theme parks & cruise ships & then working major venues in USA & 2 years Spain, France, & Germany. Played the Ed Sullivan Show (TV) in 1964. Moved to North Carolina. From 1971 a film & audiovisual producer & semi-pro magician. A tutor of The Barans & Michael Christian. 1990 TAOM Club Act Award. Wrote A Texan Trixter (1986, 99pp; reprinted). Moved to Las Vegas in 1993. Tricks in Genii. Associate editor of Magic since 1996. [Bo#329;Wh2]

name: Mogul, [Albert] "Al
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Billed as "Prince Mogul" & "The Prince of Mystery" in the 1930s-40s, then just as Al Mogul. Pro mentalist-magician in New York City area and then California. Pet effect: Billet Reading.

name: Mohala
bio: See: Floyd, Mary

name: Mohr, Professor Harmon
bio: (USA: fl.1880s) Pro illusionist, ventriloquist, & lightning caricaturist. Toured with assistant "Mlle. Oena". [Mo]

name: Moingeon, Ernest
bio: (France: c1885-20 Apr 1967) Amateur lightening calculator. 1958 FISM 1st prize in mathematic. [Dif]

name: Moir, John
bio: See: "Macallister, J. M."

name: Mokana
bio: See: Goldston, James Meyer

name: Mole, H. C., MIMC
bio: (England: 1878?-) Wrote (with Percy Naldrett) Moments of Mystery (1914) & The Magic of Tomorrow (1919, with Medrington & Hammond). Memoir is Those Entertaining Years (1949, 46pp). Contributor to Magic Wand

name: Molinas, Commandant Clement
bio: (Marseilles, France: 20 Apr 1875-) Army officer (retired). Soldier of the Legion of Honor. Amateur magician. Charter member of the Amicale Robert-Houdin du Sud-Est (Nice) 1936. [WWM]

name: Molini, Antonio
bio: (Trieste, Austria: 1856-12 Aug 1912) Of Italian parentage, his father being a pharmacist. Pharmacist himself. Amateur magician. Student of Frizzo. Invented the Organ Pipes. In 1904 in Trieste before an audience of 400 he won the 1st place cash prize (40 florins) contest against two pro magicians. [Dif:Vo57;St;Pr]

name: Moll, [Hans-Dietrich] "Dieter
bio: (Magdeburg, Germany: 15 Jun 1925- ) Learned at age 12 from uncle's present of tricks from Bartl's. Storekeeper in Magdeburg, East Germany. Amateur magician, aka "Dimo". Collector since 1950. Co-authored Artistik Auswahl-Bibliographie (1968), Unterhaltungskunst A-Z (1975 & 1977) & Das grosse Hokuspokus (1981). [Wh2]

name: Molovinsky, Gale
bio: (Allentown, Pennsylvania: 29 Jul 1942-) Learned while in junior high school as assistant to Ken Huftmaker. Thence pro close-up, stage, standup, & kid-show magician. Dealer in Potomac, Maryland. Invented the Gamolo Levitation illusion (initially hydraulic, later electronic), which was premiered in 1976 by Blair Marshall at the SAM convention in Philadelphia. It provided stage magicians, for the first time, with a relatively cheap, light-weight (70-pound) levitation as opposed to a mere suspension. Dubbed the Gamolo Levitation in 1977 by Al Cohen. Molovinsky then took "Gamolo" as his stage name. [Mag;Wh]

name: Molton
bio: (Germany: 7 Jul 1904-24 Nov 1937) Stage name of Hermann Börgermann. Pro magician. Usually worked seaside resorts in summers & minor variety theaters in winter. Died in Saarbrucken.

name: Monarque
bio: See: Arnolis, Jean

name: Mondeux, Henri
bio: (Neuvy-le-Roi, Tours, France: 22 Jun 1826-29 Jan 1861) Pro lightning calculator. [Dif]

name: Mondor, Card [Edward]
bio: (Seattle, Washington: 1 Oct 1922-7 Jan 2001) Real name, Card being a family name on mother's side & Mondor being that of his French-Canadian father. Inspired at age 13 seeing 3 Blackstone shows. Learned with The Great Virgil Illusion Show 1941-Apr 1942. Pro since 1942 with flash magic act & comedy magic. With Hollywood Victory Committee 6 months in 1942 & USO (in N.Africa & Europe) 1942-45. Toured US movie houses with Kroger Babb's "Dr. Ogre Banshee's Chasm of Spasms" in 1947 & then, 1948-51, as "Dr. Draculas" with his own "Den of Living Nightmares" (with Dick Newton as partner 1948-49) stage & film horror show. In 1951 took the Virgil show to Australia. Then returned to USA to work in film distribution. Moved permanently to Australia in 1961, working as TV & film distributor. Proprietor of Aladdin's Magic Shop (buying from Gerald Taylor) in Melbourne (later Tasmania) 1980-86 when sold it to John Williams. Invented Hollywood Six Card Repeat (1942), Hollywood Cocktails (1943), & Hollywood Nip-A-Drink (1944). Wrote Clowning Around For Kids (1989). Writing a Spook Show how-to book. [Walk2; Genii4/47; Tay, p.32; Wh2]

name: Mondrac
bio: (Germany?: 29 Mar 19-) Stage name of Philipp Schaeffer. 1987 MZvD 2nd prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Monhaupt, Hermann
bio: (Breslau, Germany: 1827-1887) Pro apparatus conjurer for 3 decades. One of earliest magicians to use electricity. Known for his elegance & humor, he ended his act by giving bouquets of flowers to the ladies. Originally toured Silesia & the provinces, gradually collecting a large fortune until returning to his home city. For his generous gifts to charity, a street in Breslau was named after him. Died in his hometown. [Vo56; CMM8/08]

name: Monroe, Arthur B.
bio: (USA: c1892-) Ex-telegrapher & professional private investigator specialized on gambling cheating methods with exposé lecture demonstrations (in 1940s) of those nefarious practices. Amateur magician. Invented Voodoo trick (1937). [Jinx#138]

name: Montag, J. B.
bio: (Germany: fl.1840s-50s) Wrote 3 books: Der wohlbewanderte Kartenkünstler (1844, 139pp), Die entlarvien falscher Spieler (1845), & Die unterhaltendsten und belehrendsten arithmetischen Kartenkünste (1854, 76pp).

name: Montague, Duke
bio: (USA: fl.late 1930s-mid 1960s) Stage name of Mr Osgood. One of two (other being J.B. Bobo) top school-show magicians in the Bible Belt. Did a standard act (Vanishing Wand, production boxes, Clippo, etc) including memory stunt by his assistant-wife Myrnella. Inspired Mike Rogers in 1945. Retired by illness & died in poverty. [Tay]

name: Montague, Frederick, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 8 Oct 1876-15 Oct 1966). Member of Parliament then House of Lords when elevated to the peerage as Lord Amwell. Amateur magician. Popularized the Bluff Pass in 1928. Wrote Westminster Wizardry [1928]. Tricks in Abra. [Go2]

name: Montalbano, Dean A[ngelo]
bio: (Fort Reily, Kansas: 6 Oct 1968-) Learned at age 4 from gift magic set. Pro stage magician & mentalist since 1981 as "D'Angelo Montalban" & "R.T. Stark". Articles in Linking Ring (2 Parades), MUM, Tops, Genii (column), Magick, Magigram, Invocation, & New Tops (column). [Wh2]

name: Montandon, Roger
bio: (Galveston, Texas: 7 Jan 1918-) Dealer (Montandon's Magic) in Tulsa, Oklahoma, c1941-c1960. Co-invented (with Logan Wait) Invisible Bovine c1941. Marketed Wait's OOM at the same time, as the essential ingredient. Book collector (c2000 volumes) sold piecemeal in 1988-89. Wrote (with Logan Wait) Not Primigenial (20pp). Edited Juggler's Bulletin 1944-49 (52 issues), Juggler's Bulletin Annual (3 issues, 1950, 1951, 1952), & Collectors' Bulletin 1959-64. Article in Genii. [Wh]

name: Montes, Arturo
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 21 Dec 1917-30 Sep 1995) Joined Dante show (with his identical twin sisters, Victoria & Eugenia) in Mexico City in 1943 [sic]. Went with Dante as Stage Manager to Europe & Britain 1946-48. Married Moi-yo Miller in 1949. With Dante until 1954 when he toured with Lee Grabel's show. Then left magic to work as an engineer with Lockheed until retired in southern California. 1993 Dragon Award (with Moi-yo).

name: Monti, Harry
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 17 Aug 1935- ) Stage name of Harry Lee Montieth. Learned at age 6 from trick in comic book. Pro close-up. Works restaurants, nightclubs, & trade shows. Has played the Magic Castle yearly since 1964. Married Mary Gertrude "Trudy" Thomas (born 1944) in 1971. SAM President-elect for 1999-2000. Wrote (with Trudy Monti), History of S.A.M. Assembly No.8 (1996, 192pp). [Monti; MUM1/74; Mag]

name: Monti, Jo
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 30 Mar 1959-) Stage name of Joseph Louis Safuto. Inspired seeing the Tony Curtis Houdini movie. Learned at age 7 from brother. Initially did escapology then sleight of hand as semi-pro since age 16. Moved to California. Pro new wave vaudeville magic since 1984. Pet effect: Can of Soda Pop from Shoe. Tricks in Apocalypse, MUM, Linking Ring. 1985 Backstage Magazine Variety Act of the Year award. [Wh2]

name: Moodaya, Mooty
bio: (Madras, India: fl.1840s) Pro. Toured Europe including England (in 1840). [Cl; Magic8/10]

name: Moody, W. H.
bio: (Birmingham, England: 1869-) Learned c1889 by tuition from Prof H.S. Lynn. Minor semi-pro & businessman in Northamptonshire. [Magic12/01]

name: Moon, Mr.
bio: (England: fl.1800s-10s) Minor pro magician & likely card sharp. His only effects were card tricks and the old cut-and-restored cock's head. [Fr]

name: Moonbeam
bio: See: Lehn, Donald B.

name: Moore, Alonzo
bio: (USA: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Afro-American. Apprenticed (?) as assistant (billed as "Theosis") to Ed Maro. Thence on own by 1903 working a dime museum in Chicago & minstrel shows through the South until dropped from sight after 1905. [Pr]

name: Moore, Bob "Romany
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Card magic. Wrote 2 booklets including The Moore the Merrier Lecture (1983).

name: Moore, E. J. "Ernie
bio: (New York City, NY: 10 Oct 1881-25 Apr 1957) Stage name of Ernest Joseph Limeberger, aka "Gabby Moore" & "Mysterious Moore" & billed as "The Talkative Trickster". Pro since 1898, working big-time vaudeville after 1910. Toured Britain in 1920, including the London Coliseum & Palladium. Pet effect: Tears of Buddha (since 1922). In 1930 left the stage to manage other magicians. Moved to Columbus, Ohio, where he ran a magic shop & played only local shows. Invented Splitting a Hare (1921, his rabbit mini-version of Sawing thru a Woman), Dagger-It (by 1940), Do-U-Smoke (by 1940), Moore Color (by 1940), Instanto Rope (by 1947), Perplexo Rope (by 1948), Daz-E-Slate (by 1948), Linking Ropes (1953), & Amaz-U. Wrote (with Robert Nelson), Super Prediction Wrote (with Robert Nelson), Super Prediction Tricks.[Pr;HMM5/57]

name: Moore, J. Paul
bio: (Rockford, Illinois: 28 Oct 1941- ) Learned in 1965 working for Jules Lenier at Magic Eye Magic shop. Actor & pro magician, specialized in close-up & walk-around with cards, coins, & objects at hand. Claims to have been San Francisco's 1st street magician c1970. Aka "Alfie" and billed as "King of the Street Conjurors". (Portrays "Alfie" character as a London-born founding who ran-away at age 12 to assist mentalist "Carlisle".) Moore now works theme-parks & cruise ships. Wrote lecture Busking as a Mercenary Art. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Moorehouse, [Henry L.] "Hank
bio: (Oak Park, Illinois: 23 Apr 1934 – 1 July 2011) Learned in 1947 from hometown Mazda Magic Company tricks. Pro comedy close-up & stage magician since 1969. Dealer (Top Hat Treasures in Michigan) in 1970s. SAM President 1981-82. Since c1981 works at Abbott's when not touring. Wrote Words from the Wizard (48pp) & Handbook for Adult Banquet Shows (20pp). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Mora, Mystic
bio: (Australia: -1965) Pro magicienne. Did act of pseudo-Japanese magic. Married Dr Richard Rowe in 1910. Together they worked a popular 2-person telepathy act, she billed as "Mora, the White Mahatma". [Alm;Daw2]

name: Mora, Hedi
bio: See: Basch, Hedwig

name: Mora, Silent
bio: See: McCord, Louis

name: Moreau, Henri
bio: (Paris, France: 22 Jan 1891- ) Amateur in Paris. Aka "Achem". [WWM]

name: Moreau, Pierre
bio: (Gilly-sur-Loire, Saône-et-Loire, France: 19 Aug 1849-26 May 1890) Pro, working mainly saloons & specializing in card magic, superbly so according to Raynaly and Odin. Died in Lyon of influenza. [Dif; HMM8/52]

name: Moreau-Sainti
bio: (France: 1799-1860) Stage name of Théodore-François Sainti. Minor opera singer & voice teacher in Paris. A skilled amateur magician. Around 1820 founded the world's first magic society, the Société Philomagique de Paris. He was also a credulous investigator of psychics. Morell, Reginald A. (England: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Wrote Hamley's Up-to-Date Mystical Sleights and Illusions (1900, 30pp).

name: Morelle, Ed.
bio: See: Mander, Alec

name: Moreno
bio: (Texas, USA: 12 Aug 1908-) Stage name of James B. Williams. Learned in US Navy at age 16 from catalog tricks. Pro since early 1930s, working school shows to med shows to tent shows to carnival illusion sideshow. Also magic shop dealer on occasion. Played mainly the Southwest. [Genii4/89;WWM]

name: Moretti, Hans
bio: (Berkersdorf, near Tarnopol [now Ternopol], Poland [now in Ukraine]): 24 Jul 1928- Stage name of Johannes "Hans" Cewe. Moved to West Germany in 1940. Trained in circus until c1950. Pro comedy escape artist working with assistant-wife Helga. Premiered his famous Russian Roulette routine in 1965 in Lisbon. 1975 Baden-Baden 2nd prize for stage magic. Also does his Paper-Tree Levitation. FISM 1st prizes for illusion in 1976 (with Sword Box) & mentalism in 1979 (with Russian Roulette). 1983 MZvD Magician of the Year. Made record number of appearances on the Paul Daniels Magic Show on BBC-TV. Many other TV bits. 1984 AMA Performing Fellowship. In Oct 1988 set Guinness record for Burning Rope Escape timing. Video (1987). Father of Hans Pantar and Peter Moretti. [Fi;Win;Wh2]
years: Berkersdorf, near Tarnopol [now Ternopol], Poland [now in Ukraine]

name: Moretti, Peter
bio: (Dillingen, West Germany: 31 Mar 1957- ) Stage name of Peter Cewe. Son of Hans & Helga "Moretti" & younger brother of "Hans Pantar". Pro escapist in Europe with assistant-wife Sonja. Pet effects: his brother's Russian Roulette with crossbows, his father's Paper-Tree Levitation, Sword Box Escape, & Double Bullet Catching with Teeth.

name: Moretti, Sonja
bio: (Pirmasens, West Germany: 3 Jul 1962-) Wife of "Peter Moretti" with whom she works as assistant. [Mül]

name: Morgan, Earl
bio: (Kansas City, USA: -1960 or 61) Pro (ex-auto mechanic) vaude cigarette manip and bubbles act, the latter being possibly the first of its kind. Then to semi-pro (again as an auto mechanic). Invented Match to Flower (c1940) & marketed his Nesto Candles (by 1948). Inspired the hero-role in Frances Ireland's magic play, "Cigaretto Takes a Wife" (late 1930s). Dealer in Chicago area in 1940s. Then moved to Kansas City. TV debut in 1952. [Ir; HMM8/52]

name: Morgano, Carolus
bio: See: Braniek, Karl

name: Morine
bio: (Britain: 22 Mar 1933-) Stage name of Molly Elizabeth Palmer "Mo" Vickers. A florist by trade. Semi-pro magician since marriage to Bruce Vickers who taught her & with whom she did a double act, working cabaret & cruise ships. 1965 British Ring special prize. 1966 Craig Trophy. [Mar]

name: Morinura
bio: See: Powell, Bert

name: Moris
bio: (South America: fl.1920s) Pro. Played St. George's Hall 1924.

name: Moritz, Mr
bio: (Germany: fl.1790s-1810s) Pro. Moved to England where he opened a magic & variety theater, The Temple of Apollo, off the Strand in London in 1807. An article on him by J.B. Findlay is in Findlay's Sixth Collectors Annual (1954). [Fr;Cl;St;Magic11/09]

name: Morley, Thomas
bio: (Britain: 6 Jul 1892-12 Aug 1987) Noted collector of magic books. Lived on Isle of Man. [Daw2]

name: Moroso, Denis
bio: (S. Daniele del Friuli, Udine, Italy: 19 Apr 1920-) Learned magic in 1932 after seeing a magician. Stage name of Licio Domenico Moroso. Pro stage magician since 1945, specialized in sleight-of-hand. 1952 FISM Grand Prix. Toured Portugal in 1953. Articles in Journal de la Prestidigitation. [Dif;Wh5]

name: Morrell
bio:
"Morrell junior, the Prince of Magic SEE: Dennison, Gene" Morrell, R[eginald] A. (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Wrote Up-to-Date Mystical Sleights and Illusions (London: 1900, 25pp) & New Magical Sleights and Fakes (London: 1906, 50pp, with Frederick Lloyd). Trick in Mahatma.

[See also: Dennison, Edward]

name: Morris, Dr.
bio: See: "Morris, Philip"

name: Morris, [E. W.] "Bud
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Resident of Oakland, California. Wrote Magic with Electronics (1966, 14pp; rev ed 1973, 19pp), I Am Curious (Magic) (1970, 53pp), Extra Sensory Deception (1971, 40pp), Magic in the Morris Manor (1974, 128pp, with Sam Dalal), & More Magic with Electronics (1975, 60pp). Edited Magick Thesaurus [1976]-1978 (21 issues). Tricks in Swami & Mantra.

name: Morris, [John] Chester [Brooks] "Chet
bio: (New York City, NY: 16 Feb 1901-11 Sep 1970) Son of successful stage actors. Inspired and learned magic at age 12 from father's gift of a Mysto Magic set. Semi-pro vaude magic since 1913. Debut as child actor in both legitimate theater and cinema in 1917. Moved to Hollywood in 1928 with debut as adult film star next year. Inspired by Caryl Fleming to become serious about performing magic. In WW II did nearly 400 USO magic shows. Played variety in London in 1949. In 1950 he starred in NBC-TV's half-hour crime-magic drama The Great Merlini. Suffering from stomach cancer, committed suicide by barbiturates. Bio in James Robert Parish and William T. Leonard, Hollywood Players: The Thirties (1976), 408-415. Trick in Jinx #58 (1939). [Magic3/95;Th;Katz]

name: Morris, Don
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Tennis pro. Comedy magician. Wrote (with Steve Beam) Inside Outs (1979, 27pp).

name: Morris, Paul
bio: (Norwich, Connecticut: 22 Jul 1903-24 Mar 1965) Stage name of Morris Bernstein. Clothing executive in Brooklyn. Inspired by seeing The Spider play to become an amateur magician. Invented Card Under the Collar & Slow Motion Monte. Tricks in Sphinx, Phoenix, Genii, HMM. [Th]

name: Morris, Philip
bio: (Kalamazoo, Michigan: 8 Jan 1935-) Stage name of Philip Morris Smith. Inspired around age 7 seeing Blackstone show. Pro mentalist & magician, originally touring with a Ghost Show 1953-1956 as "Dr. Evil" & "Dr. Morris". Hosted TV kid-show series 1960-67. Toured his own illusion show 1967-1973. Circus ringmaster 1967-78. Founder-owner since 1967 of Morris Costumes Inc, Charlotte, North Carolina, a wholesale-retail costume & magic prop & book business. That year it absorbed the Edward O. Dr. Brane and House of Humor shops. Known for his philanthropic support of various magical enterprises. Authored several books on magic & allied subjects. Magic cartoons for New Tops. [Walk2;Wh]

name: Morris, Richard
bio: (Britain: -1793) Amateur sleight-of-hand artist since boyhood & pro fortune-teller as "Dick Spot". See The Life and Mysterious Transactions of Richard Morris Esq. (1789, 38pp; 2nd ed 1799).

name: Morrissey, Herb[ert Louis]
bio: (Montréal, Quebec, Canada: 6 Feb 1938-13 Aug 2003) A notable practical joker. Inspired seeing a Blackstone show & learned at age 12 from a Xmas magic set. Pro with a manip act, playing Quebec nightclubs for 12 years from late 1950s to mid-1970s. Leading pro dealer in Canada since 1959, first manufacturing as Herb Morrissey Products in Montréal, then with shop as New Era Magic, finally since 1978 as Morrissey Magic Ltd in Toronto. Wrote Troublewit Simplified (1979). His son Dan joined the business in 1986. [Bo3;;www;Wh]

name: Morrison, John Francis "Jack
bio: (Britain: 1905-24 Apr 1976) Industrial chemist. Collector of magic books & tricks. Originated the one-hand riffle shuffle. [Daw2]

name: Morritt, Charles
bio: (Saxton, Yorkshire, England: 13 Jun 1860-10 Apr 1936) Took lessons from Dobler. Debut in 1878. Pro illusionist, sleight-of-hand artist, & hand-shadowist. London debut 1886. Toured USA 1887-88 with A. Herrmann. In 1889 played the Maskelyne's Egyptian Hall with a 2-person thought-transmission act with his sister, Miss Lillian Morritt. Toured Australia in 1897 with the Biograph company. In 1915 in London briefly and unsuccessfully teamed with Carl Hertz. Thence toured the provinces with his own small show. Died in Chorley, Lancashire. Invented Oh! (1891), Morritt Cage (1893), Flyto (by 1895), & Disappearing Donkey (1912). [Pr;Wal;Go2;Cl;Magic8/02]

name: Morro, Fred
bio: (Uckermünde, West Pommerania, Germany: 28 Jun 1884-27 May 1955) Stage name of Carl Löschwitz. Son of a circus owner. Pro. Toured Turkey, Romania, Holland, Belgium, Scandinavia, & England before WW I. Died in Magdeburg. [Vo57]

name: Mortimer, Dr W[illiam] Golden, MD
bio: (Bradford, York, England: 8 May 1896-1966) Pro childrens shows since 1919, aka "D'Albert", with magic, vent, marionettes, and Punch & Judy. [WWM]

name: Mortimer, Dr W[liam] Golden, MD
bio: (New York City, NY: 27 Dec 1854-3 Mar 1933) A Mason. Learned as a young child. Studied with Robinson (Robertson?) "The Fakir of Vishnu" in California c1872. Pro sleights & illusions since 1873, touring the eastern states with a Heller-type magic show called first "Mortimer Brothers" then "Mortimer's Mysteries". Briefly (1879-82) partnered by (but didn't tour with) E.J. Dale, the late Robert Heller's former assistant. Retired in 1885 to become a physician & amateur magician. SAM Member #2 & its founding President 1902-05. SAM Hall of Fame. [Magic12/01;Mahatma6/02;CI;Hou]

name: Morton
bio: (Germany: fl.1910s) Stage name of Heinrich Kayzer. Pro. [Mec]

name: Morton, Bill
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro in the Midwestern and Southern states, including his “Asylum of Horrors” show. Did 10,000 shows by 1956 when he opened a magic shop in Lincoln, Nebraska.

name: Morton, "Pop
bio: (USA: c1872-13 Jan 1932) Pro side-show magus, specialized in touring bathing resorts such as Coney Island. Died in poverty. [Dif; HMM8/57]

name: Mösch, Georg
bio: (Wiesbaden, Germany: 24 Apr 1891-17 Sep 1961) Proprietor of magic shop ("Zum Zauberkönig") in Wiesbaden where he died. Son? of Otto Mösch. [Roh]

name: Mösch, Otto
bio: (Munich, Germany: 26 Jul 1860-18 Feb 1963) Son-in-law of Joseph Leichtmann (by the latter's 4th daughter). Founded magic shop ("Zum Zauberkönig") in Munich in 1884. Died in Munich. Father? of Georg Mösch. [Roh] Moskowitz, Joel A. (New York City, New York: 18 Jun 1932-) Learned & age 7 from library books & friends. Forensic psychiatrist in California. Semi-pro close-up & mental magician from ages 18 to 35, thence amateur. Wrote The Sorcerer's Apprentice on use of magic in child psychotherapy. Tricks & articles in Genii, Linking Ring, Pallbearers Review, & Magic Around the World. [Wh2]

name: Mossey, Dr Richard O[rville] "Dick", MD
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 18 Sep 1924-) Surgeon (now semi-retired). Amateur magician since c1938. First IBM "Junior" magician. Long-time active senior officer of the IBM, including President 1965-66. Collector, particularly of Nests of Boxes & Prediction Chests. [Wh]

name: Mosteller, Dr Fred[erick], PhD [pronounced MOSS-teller]
bio: (Clarksburg, West Virginia: 24 Dec 1916- ) PhD in math 1946. Famous statistician at Princeton U. Amateur magician by 1943. Tricks in Phoenix. [Th]

name: Motley
bio: See: Peacock, Victor

name: Moto, Ger
bio: (Holland: 1908-) Stage name of Ger Elschot. Schoolteacher (now retired). Amateur magician, mainly close-up. Black art act with "Francisco", which took the 1949 FISM 1st prize for presentation. Still (1990) active in local magic clubs. [Wh2]

name: Moulton, H. J.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Senior researcher at the Boston Public Library. Hired by Houdini in 1918 to compile press notices of magicians in Boston. His manuscript was completed in 1919 & published as Houdini's History of Magic in Boston 1792-1915 (1983). (Vienna, Austria: 1869-c1930) Stage name of Alfred Wolfsegger. Aka "Alfredi" & "Alfred Moudini". Pro manipulator, later escapist. Played Hamburg. Wrote as "Alfredy Mourdiny" Der Zauberkünstler oder der Liebling der Gesellschaft (n.d., 32pp). NOTE: Missspelled "Murdini" & "Mudrini". [Mec;CMM12/06]

name: Mr. Electric
bio: See: Roy, Marvyn

name: Mr. Escape
bio: See: Baker, Steve

name: Mr. Fingers
bio: See: Weiner, Irv

name: Mr Z
bio: See: Zaleta, Lex

name: Mudrini" [misspelling]
bio:
Mueller, Jesse A. (San Francisco, California: 18 Oct 1890-) Lawyer-banker in San Francisco. Amateur close-up magician. [Dor;WWM]

[See also: "Mourdini"]

name: Mueller, John
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Pro. Main demonstrator at Tannen's 1964-1984 when retired.

name: Muerta, Manuel
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 11 Mar 1968-) Stage name of Guido Schmalriede. Pro close-up & stage magic. 1994 FISM 1st Prize for Comedy Magic; 1998 Sarmoti award (Flicking Fingers); 2000 FISM 2nd Prize for Close-up. Trick in Kaufman's Flicking Fingers (1998). [Wh01]

name: Muir, [James] "Jimmy
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) Pro on West Coast. Known to friends as "Rosebud Muir". Lived in Oakland, California. Did vaudeville & club act, including Vancouver in 1961. Worked with assistant Cleo. Wrote series of pattern booklets: Laugh Lines #1 (1944) to #7 (1952), plus Giggles, Gaglets and Guffaws (1957, 7pp). Also wrote How to MC and Put a Show Together (c1950). [Tay]

name: Mukherjie, S. D.
bio: (India: 2 Apr 1916- ) Pro illusionist as "Esdeem", retired by late 1960s in Calcutta. Government official in Defence Department. Magic writer, critic, & inventor. Founder of Magic Net & Magic Lamp magazines in 1950s-60s. Tricks in Swami & Mantra. [Mantra3/76;Bou]

name: Mulack, Friedrich
bio: (Bendorf [sic], Germany: 12 [sic] Aug 1838-22 Mar 1919) Learned in 1852 as assistant to magician Carl Ehrhardt. Pro on own since 1866. After Franco-Prussian War of 1870-71 toured mainly in Saxony. Fatherd 21 children. Died in Eisleben. [Vo56]

name: Mulholland, John [Wickizer]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 9 Jun 1898-25 Feb 1970) Inspired at age 5 seeing Kellar show. Learned at age 13 when tutored by John William Sargent at $5 per hour. Debut at age 15. Teacher of industrial arts at Horace Mann School in New York City 1918-24. Major magic collector since 1913. By c1922 when cataloged by Erik Barnouw, the collection was already considered 2nd only to Houdini's. At age 26 (c1924) was taken by mother on a round-the-world trip, observing magi in all countries visited. Pro performer-lecturer, probably the first according to Parrish. Married Pauline Nell Pierce in 1932. Played Loew's State Theatre in 1940 & Radio City Music Hall in 1941, both in New York City. Last editor of Sphinx 1932-53. SAM Hall of Fame. A major collector of magic books (some 3,500 by 1937 & over 4,000 by his death) & memorabilia. He sold his superb collection to The Players club where it was housed until 1984 when sold to an anonymous patron (actually Carl Rheuban) who housed it in the private Mulholland Library of Magic and Allied Arts in Los Angeles until sold in 1991 to David Copperfield. Wrote Magic in the Making (1925, 134pp, with Milton M. Smith), Quicker Than The Eye: The Magic and Magicians of the World (1932, 259pp), John Mulholland's Story of Magic (1935, 79pp), Beware Familiar Spirits (1938, 360pp, partly ghosted by Barrows Mussey), The Art of Illusion (1944, 142pp; reprinted as Magic for Entertaining), The Early Magic Shows (1945, 18pp), John Mulholland's Book of Magic (1963, 329pp), Magic of the World (1965, 190pp), The Magical Mind (1967, with Dr. George N. Gordon), & Practical Puppetry (1961, 191pp). Also co-authored (with Cortland Fitzsimmons) a mystery novel, The Girl in the Cage (1939), starring "Peter King" as magician-detective. Articles in Collectors Annual, Magic Cauldron, etc. [WWWA; Par; Genii11/65; Pr; Go2; Bo; Bo#226&312; Jinx#30; Ho] Muller [misspelling] NOTE: Editors & writers who drop the umlauted "ü" from subject's surname must spell it "Mueller", never "Muller".

name: Müller, Horst [pronounced MEW-ler]
bio: (Wilhelmshaven, Germany: 30 Dec 1925-) Learned in 1947 as a POW. Owner-manager of computer manufacturing firm in Hemmingen, West Germany. Amateur stage magician, specializing in liquid magic. Nickname: "H.M.". Winner of several 1st prizes in Germany & Israel plus 1981 MZvD 2nd prize for invention. President of German Magic Circle (MZvD) 1975-90. 1979 FISM jury. Recipient of 1983 MZvD Kalanag-Gedächnis-Ring & 1887 MZvD Karl Schröder-Gedächnis-Ring. Wrote Primus Interpares (1988). Articles in Magie & Arcane. [Wh2]

name: Müller, Reinhard
bio: (Münstermaifeld, Germany: 10 Jan 1935-). First interested in magic in 1950. Principal of Mathematics & Physics in Passau, West Germany. Amateur close-up, card, & mental magician. Pet effect: topological effects with jumbo cards. Invented Three Card Catch. Frequent competitor & prize winner, including 1975 MZvD 3rd prize in closeup, 1978 MZvD 2nd prize for invention, 1982 MZvD Writer of the Year, & 1983 Baden-Baden 3rd prize in closeup. Wrote Falsch-Zähl-Methoden (1972), Gilbreath Prinzipien (1982), Phantomwürfel (1982), Riesen-karten (3 parts, 1983, 1984, 1986). Wrote several major research monographs including: Ambitious Cards (1977), Erklärt 251 englische Fachausdrücke aus der Kartenmagie (1978), Gilbreath's Principles (1979; 1996 rev), Cartas Gigantes (1981), Wild Cards (1983), Flying Cards (1985), Los 4 Aces (1985), Estimación (1986), Card Cases (1987), The Glimpse (1988), The Gray Code (1989), The Card Index, White Line Problem, Marlo on Faked Decks, Cards up the Sleeve, Hofziner and the Magic of the 19th Century: Card Magic in Germany (1993; 1994 rev, 22pp), Viaje de una Carta a Interior de Recinto cerrado [Card in Some Object] (1996, 8pp), & The Card Effects of Robert-Houdin (1996, 9pp). REF: Magie, Vol.63 (1983), 82-84. Articles in 8 German-language & English-language magazines including Magie (c300 articles since 1960), Magische Welt (118 articles), Hokus-Pokus, & Arcane. 2 videos (1982, 1984). NOTE: See note in previous entry. [Wh2]

name: Müller, Volker
bio: (Langenau, Germany: 24 [or 27] Aug 1948-) Pro, working a comedy act with partner Gerd Winkler as "Volker & Gerd". [Mül;Nad]

name: Mullica, Tom
bio: (Waupun, Wisconsin, USA: 19 Aug 1948-) Inspired by & learned magic at age 7 (1955) from his mother's Xmas gift of a Sneaky Pete Magic Kit. Practiced alone on a Wisconsin farm for 10 years before meeting other magicians. Invented Mullica Wallet (1968). Began his pro career in comedy magic as a demonstrator for Abbott's 1974-75. Moved to Atlanta, Georgia, where he became a magic bartender (1976) and then (1976) owner of the Tom-Foolery Magic Bar Theatre in Atlanta until it closed in Dec 1987. 1984 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. 1988 FISM 3rd prize for comedy magic. Played the Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris 1989-91. Articles in Magic, etc. Column in Genii 1991-92. TV appearances in USA & Europe. Videos (1984, 1986, 1996), video segment (1986). See Richard Kaufman, Tom Mullica Starring in Show-Time at the Tom Foolery (1992, 220pp). [Lo2;Wh5]

name: Munari, Geno
bio: (Burbank, California: 7 Mar 1946-) Learned around age 11 from a Mulholland book. Moved to Las Vegas in 1964. Pro magician since c1970, working mainly club dates & conventions. Specializes in gambling demos. Dealer ("Geno Munari's Magic Shop") in Las Vegas since ..... Co-authored (with Grippo) The Magic of Jimmy Grippo (1981). Tricks in Genii & MUM. 2 videos: The Concave Stripper (1991) & The False Riffle Shuffle and Second Deal (1991). NOTE: Given name misspelled "Gene". [Wh]

name: Munro, George Mackenzie
bio: (Scotland?: c1864-26 Aug 1929) Aka "G.M. Ornum". Businessman in London. Amateur magician. Then semi-pro dealer (Ornum's [later Munro's] Magical Repository) in London 1889 until sold to Stanley Norton around 1918. Founding publisher of The Wizard 1905 & The Magic Wand 1910-14. Edited The Wizard 1908-09. Much bio material in Harry Leat's Forty Years In & Around Magic (1923).

name: Munro, Mark
bio: (Youngstown, Ohio: c1966-) Learned magic at age 7. Pro close-up as demonstrator for Tannen's.

name: Munroe, Al[bert Foster]
bio: (Fall River, Massachusetts: 1893-21 Jan 1961) Promotion manager of the Detroit Times newspaper. Amateur magic collector. Edited Scroll of Merlin 1943-44 (6 issues) & Al Munroe's Magical Miscellany 1943-50 (61 issues). Tricks & articles in Sphinx, Linking Ring, & Conjuriana. In a Detroit nursing home since 1958. [Bo#301;HMM11/58]

name: Murata, Arthur
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Of Japanese descent. Semi-pro close-up. House magician at Magic Cellar in 1970s.

name: Murata, Bill
bio: (Hawaii, USA: fl.1940s-80s) Of Japanese descent. Music recording producer. Aka "Chew Gum Long". Edited The Kahuna 1949-50 (19 issues). Anonymous author of Tenkai's Manipulative Card Routine.

name: Murdoch, William
bio: (Scotland: fl.1920s) Aka "Wu-Tai-Shan", "San Ana", & "Prince Omar". Pro.

name: Murillo
bio: See: Beeckmans, Roger

name: Murray
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 11 Nov 1901-22 Jan 1988) Stage name of Leo Norman Maurien Murray Stuart Carrington Walters, aka "Murray Walters". Learned from magic books. Pro escapologist-illusionist since 1915. His British debut was at the London Coliseum in Oct 1926. Played St. George's Hall in 1927. Retired from stage (due to illness) in 1954. Later (late 1950s?) became a dealer (Murray's Magic Mart) in Blackpool, England, running it until fully retired in 1987. 1986 AMA Masters Fellowship. Bio is Val Andrews, Murray (1974, 112pp). NOTE: Did not, as reported by Goldston & Andrews & cautiously by Waters, coin term "escapologist" in 1926. That was done by Houdini in 1910. [Pr;Wal;Hudd;Go;Go2;Ho]

name: Murray, John E. "Johnnie
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-90s) First magician to perform while flying over South Pole (31 Oct 1956) & North Pole (Spring 1957). Aka since 1961 "Jack Ketch" (from a stock character in Punch-&-Judy shows). Tricks in Phoenix & New Phoenix. Published-edited Trick Brain (1971, 12 issues) & Woofle Dust (1972, 3 issues), both in Portland, Maine. Then pro as dealer (in Greenville, South Carolina, in 1970s) & magic illustrator. Wrote Inside (1984, 118pp).

name: Murtyl, L.
bio: (France: c1895-8 May 1970) Stage name of Léon Cortat. In 1944 founded the Entre-Nous Magiciens club in Paris. Founding Editor of its journal, Entre-Nous Magiciens, 1944. Charter member of the IBM French Ring 1948.

name: Muse, Ray[mond Fletcher]
bio: (USA: 1896-15 Nov 1965) Semi-pro. Aka "Amuso". Introduced Charlie Miller to Erdnase in late 1920s. SAM President 1945-46. Taught Marvyn Roy in late 1930s & his grandson, Dale Hindman, c1958. Articles in Genii. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame.

name: Mussey, [June] Barrows
bio: (Staten Island, New York: 30 Mar 1910-27 Jul 1985) Inspired in 1921 seeing Howard Thurston show. Learned in 1921 from Xmas gift of Hoffmann's Later Magic. Thence "Hadji Baba", touring the East & mid-West at age 13. Semi-pro in college when he was protégé of John Mulholland at age 19. Translated and co-edited (with Fulton Oursler) Fischer's Illustrated Magic (1931). Ghosted part of Mulholland's Beware Familiar Spirits (1938). In US Marine Corps in Pacific in WW II. Moved to West Germany in 1950 to work as journalist. Wrote, as "Barrows Mussey", Magic (1942); and as "Henry Hay", Learn Magic (1947, 279pp; with 1970 German tr), Cyclopedia of Magic (1949), & The Amateur Magician's Handbook (1950, 319pp; with 3 further revised editions to 1982). [WWM; YankeeMC#4]

name: Musson, Clettis V[alentine]
bio: (USA: -Aug 1988). Learned magic at age 10. Joined the IBM in 1927. Pro with carnivals, circus, fairs, & school shows. Worked the Doc Hensley Road Show as "Kimi" & did a mental act as "Valentine". Had a full evening show. Wrote Thirty-Five Weird and Psychic Effects (1937, 40pp), Forty-Four Foolers (1944; 2nd ed 1972, 49pp), Fire Magic (1952, 44pp), Minute Magic (1953, 36pp), Situation Comedy for Magicians (1954, 52pp; repr 1966), Close Up Capers (1982, 49pp), Exclusive Weird and Psychic Effects (1983), Further Weird and Psychic Effects (1983), & Additional Weird and Psychic Effects (1983). Edited Wizard-Gram--New Series (1953-65), a Chicago magic club monthly. Article in Ireland's YB: 1952.

name: Mustapha
bio: (International Zone of Tangier: fl.1980s) Proprietor of a hairdresser's shop in Tangier. Semi-promagician in discos & cabarets. Pet effects: Walking on Broken Glass, Fire-eating, Skewer thru Tongue, productions & vanishes. [Trixigram1/89]

name: Mustes
bio: See: Tessier, Pierre

name: Musty, Spiridione
bio: (Barletta, Italy: 19 [or 12] Nov 1885-27 Jul 1962) Pro since 1905 with magic buffoon act. Toured Europe. Retired in 1953 in Nürnberg where he died. [Al;Mül]

name: Mutaza-John
bio: (Mecklenburg, Germany: 23 Jul 1895-19 Nov 1969) Stage name of Friedrich John. Died in Schwerin. [Roh]

name: Mutobe, Dr. Yoshihiko
bio: (Japan: fl.1990s) Closeup worker. 1 video bit (1993).

name: Myliana
bio: See: Mylius, Gertrude

name: Mylius, Georg
bio: (Berlin?, Germany: 26 Feb 1883-17 Jul 1960) Senior engineer in Berlin. Amateur magician, specialized in micro-magic, which term he coined (as Mikro-magie) sometime before 1930 & virtually introduced as a special field of magic. Also coined term Eckenzauber (meaning impromptu magic).

name: Mylius, Gertrud
bio: (Berlin?, Germany: 19 Jul 1892-10 Jun 1988) Wife of George Mylius. Amateur, specializing in salon magic as "Myliana".

name: Myrus
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro stage & nightclub mentalist & mindreader who claimed psychic powers with the public. Expert with center tear & cold reading. Did TV mentalism in Cleveland 1941-43. Played the Cotillion Room in New York in 1944. On TV played the Arthur Godfrey show in 1951 & the Tonight show in 1956. Retiring from performing, he moved to Florida to run a mail-order psychic business. An exposé of his act is Robert Nelson, TV Mentalism (1966, 37pp).

name: Mystag
bio: (La Rochelle, France: 17 Sep 1919-1988) Stage name of Robert François. Debut in 1951 with assistant-wife Danielle François. Pro magician, working mainly cafes, possibly the last in France to do so successfully. His wife at time of death was Linda. Wrote 3 booklets in French, including Mes premiers tours dévoilés. [Dif;Bou;Bou2]

name: Mystere, Docteur
bio: See: Vaillant, Gaston-Victor

name: Mysteria
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s) Pro in 1913 at a trade exhibition in Dundee, Scotland, with a Black Art Act and selling a pamphlet of magic tricks. He may be Bert Powell.

name: Mysterious Brown
bio:
"Mysterious Lady, The" SEE: Eagle, Georgiana

[See also: Brown, Dota C.]

name: Mysterious Smith
bio: See: Smith, Mysterious

name: Mystia
bio: See: Désirée, Mdlle. Aimée

name: Mystic Clayton
bio: See: Clayton, The Mystic

name: Mystic Mora
bio: See: Mora, Mystic

name: Mystica
bio: See: "Kaps, Fred"

name: Mystico
bio: See: Tuffs, J. Elsden

name: Mysticus
bio: See: Evans, Dr. Henry Ridgely

name: Mystina
bio: (Leeds, Yorkshire, England: 28 Nov 1962-) Stage name of Tina "Tiny Tina" Powell. Taught by magician-father & George Thompson. Prize-winning pro dancer age 16-18 with world tour. Then the diminutive (4'11") woman turned pro cabaret & stage magicienne with a dance-acrobatic-magic act. Craig Trophy 1985 & 1987. 1987 British Ladies Magical Champion (Blackpool). 1987 British Ring Shield. [Wh2]

name: Mysto
bio: See: Buckley, Arthur Mashford, Robert G.

name: Mysto, Dr
bio: See: Cooper, John R.

name: Mysto, Carl
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-10s) Pro escapist-illusionist. In 1904 in Salford he challenged Houdini to duplicate Mysto's coffin escape, which Houdini not only did but also exposed. Close friend of Walter Jeans. [Silver]

name: Mystrias
bio: See: Causyn, Jacques

name: Mytox
bio:
"Nabisco, The Great" SEE: Schindler, George

[See also: Klaus, Herrmann]

name: Nadja-Nadr
bio: See: "Handy-Bandy"

name: Nadolski, Roman
bio: (Zgagowo, Poland: 8 Mar 1949-) Learned as young boy. Avid amateur magician & magic collector in Toruń, Poland. In 1972 married partner-wife Wiesława Nadolska (nee Tuszynska, born 8 Mar 1949 in Debowa Laka). Active member of the Krajowy Klub Iluzjonistów since 1979. Specializes in stage magic but also interested in closeup. Gave first magic show in 1982. [Wh2]

name: Nadyne
bio: See: Nardini

name: Naga
bio: (Elven, Brittany, France: 26 Nov 1930-) Stage name of Huguette Chanot, wife of "O'Shan" from whom she learned mentalism in 1950 (they married 1 Jan 1951). Pro stage mentalist in partnership as "O'Shan & Naga" since 1951. As the "medium" in their act, particularly in publicity stunts, she is often reported as the star. Many TV & radio appearances in many countries. [Bou;Wh2] Nagisa, Haruhiko Pro since 1961.

name: Nagle, Charles "Charlie
bio: (USA: -10 Jan 1951) Pro magician in New York City. Initially in clubs, later private parties. Tricks in Jinx. [Ho] Nagler, Dr [William Merle] "Bill", MD, AIMC (Detroit, Michigan: 9 May 1951- ) Taught at age 4 by Nate Leipzig, his uncle's cousin. Physician & psychiatrist. Semi-pro since age 12 with close-up & mental magic. Tricks in Magic Circular, New Directions, etc. [Wh2]

name: Naidra, Madame
bio: See: Sjak, Aleksander

name: Naldrett. Percy
bio: (Worthing, Sussex, England: 17 May 1888-28 Sep 1973) Printer by trade. Semi-pro magician since 1905. Magic collector. Wrote Magic of the Moment (1912, 50pp), Magical Notes and Notions (1913, 36pp), Miscellaneous Magic (1913, 48pp), Moments of Mystery (1914, 48pp, with H.C. Mole, More Miscellaneous Magic (1919, 50pp), More Collected Magic (1921, 91pp), & Further Expert Magic (1923). Edited Magic Circular 1938-49. Bio is J.B. Findlay, Percy Naldrett, a Memoir together with a check list of his publications (1969, 17pp).

name: Namreh
bio: See: Weber, Herman L.

name: Napolitana, Horatio
bio: (Naples?, Italy: fl.1580s) Wrote one book in Italian, Libretto de secreti noblissimi et alcuni giocchi con destrezza di mano, cose vere e experimentale [A Book of Amazing Secrets and Some Sleight of Hand Tricks], which was published in Milan in 1585 and gave a crude description of 17 tricks in his 8-page pamphlet. The only known copy is in the British Museum. The author is called a "Hand Manipulator" and therefore presumably was either a skilled amateur or pro magician. [CI] "Napoleons, The (Magic)" SEE: Koishi, Parte & Ueki, Bona

name: Nardini
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-60s) A Chavez graduate. Pro magic bar act as "Nardini & Nadyne" billed as "America's Favorite Bartenders". They also did the Sub Trunk. [Tops6/46] "Narek-Shah" [Clarke's misspelling of "Manek Shah"] SEE: Shaw, Mark

name: Nartell Twins
bio: See: Conlin [Sr], Claude Alexander

name: Nash, Martin [Allan] "Marty
bio: (Vancouver, Canada: 18 Mar 1933 – 20 Jul 2009) Learned at age 6 when shown some card tricks. Debut at age 13. At 16 toured with a carnival tent-show. Pro cardman since 1967, billed as "The Charming Cheat". Lecturer, specialized in gambling demos. Now semi-retired. See the many major books & booklets published since 1975 by Steven Minch on Nash's work, including Ever So Sleightly (1975), Any Second Now (1977), & Sleight Unseen (1979). 3 videos (1998). [Lo;Mag;Wh2]

name: Nazarov, Pavel Aleksieyevich
bio: (USSR: 1918-) Pro illusionist & manipulator with Linking Rings, etc. [Mec]

name: Neale, Dr Robert E[dward] "Bob", PhD
bio: (Mount Clemens, Michigan: 23 Jun 1929- ) Inspired at age 8 seeing Tarbell doing Eyeless Vision. Professor of Psychiatry & Theology at Union Theological Seminary 1962-86. Ordained minister of the Church of Christ. Amateur magician, puzzler, & origami expert. Specializes in topological magic. Invented Bunny Bill (1964), Trapdoor Card (1983), Six Card Swindle (1984), Off the Barrelhead (1986), Whatsabox (1991), etc. Wrote Transactions (1971), Six Card Swindle (1985, 23pp), More on the Six Card Swindle (.....), Three Magic Arrows (1991, 10pp), Whatsabox (1991, 7pp), More Than Lecture Notes #1 (1991, 16pp) & #2 (1991, 20pp), Tricks of the Imagination (1991, 215pp), Magic & Meaning (1995, 200pp, with Eugene Burger), Folding Money Fooling (1997), Life, Death & Other Card Tricks (2000, 414pp). Tricks in Pallbearers, Epilogue, New Pentagram, Ibidem, Mentalwise, Genii, & Magic. Columnist in Linking Ring 1993-98. [Wh2]

name: Neckelsonn
bio: (Russia: 24 Jun 1867-12 Sep 1935) Stage name of Lew Ossip. Pro. Moved to France where he became well-known. Toured Australia (1915), North Africa, & northern South America. Played France as late as 1923. Billed as "The King of Modern Magic". Pet effects: Coin Catching, Dyeing Silks, Hat Production. Died in Paris. NOTE: Misspelled "Nickelson". [St;Wal]

name: Ned, Our
bio: (USA: 1850s) Pen name of Edward Mason Jr. Wrote Ventriloquism Made Easy; also an Exposure of Magic, and the Second Sight Mystery (Philadelphia: 1860, 96pp). NOTE: An "Uncle Ned" wrote an article, "New Tricks" in the New York Herald, 17 Mar 1901. REF: Sharpe (1983), 37.

name: Nedbalski, Robert [J.] "Ned
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-90s) Magic dealer in the Denver, Colorado, area. Taught the Bullet Catch in 1970 by close friend Orville Meyer. Articles in Linking Ring.

name: Nees-Lajn
bio: (Denmark: 5 Feb 1903-Aug 1967) Stage name of Peter Martin Nielsen. Pro illusionist, 2-person mindreader (with his wife), & hypnotist. Toured Sweden. A mediocre performer with much apparatus (now in Danish National Museum in Brede). [Dif]

name: Neeschi
bio: (Germany: 24 Aug 1942-) Stage name of Bernd Schindler. Magician. [Nad]

name: Neff, [William T.] "Bill
bio: (Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania: 1 Sep 1905-12 Feb 1967). While at Indiana, Penn., high school in 1923, learned magic studying a book with friend Jimmy Stewart (see) and, coached by Jack Gwynne, did their first church show in 1920. Since 1924 a star pro vaude illusionist. Invented Miracle Rope in 1930s. Later carried 13 assistants & 21 tons of props for his comedy-horror "Madhouse of Mystery" show. Wrote Neff's Novel Necromancy. TV bit. [Walk2;Fu2;WWM]

name: Neighbors, David
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Close-up magician in Denver, working mainly coins & some cards. Wrote Slightly Gaffed (1986, 25pp), Innovation (1986, 14pp), Coinjuring (1987, 78pp), etc. See also Ken Simmons, David Neighbors' Freshly Minted and David Neighbors on the Double Coin Gimmick (46pp). Tricks in Onyx.

name: Neil, C[harles] Lang
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Journalist & advertising agent. Magic buff (no evidence that he did magic himself). Wrote the classic The Modern Conjurer and Drawing-Room Entertainer (1902 [sic], 386pp; repr 1922; 1937, 414pp). Also Modern Card Manipulation (1906, 93pp) & After-Dinner Sleights and Pocket Tricks (1906, 92pp). Husband of Mlle Patrice. For bio material see E. Dawes in Magic Circular, V.74 (1980), 83-86, 107-109, 127-130.

name: Neiswonger, [Richard Charles] "Rick
bio: (Canton, Ohio: 29 Jun 1951- ) Learned at age 12 thru catalogs, local magic shop, & magic club. Works in sales & marketing in St. Louis, Missouri. Semi-pro magician since 1967 with stage hypnotism, close-up, & stand-up comedy magic. Specializes in riverboat gambler close-up act as "Slick Rick". Aka "Ricky Penn". Articles in New Tops 1960s-70s. [Wh2]

name: Nelmar
bio: (USA: 26 Jul 1908-6 Nov 1963) Stage name of Anthony Nelmar Albino. Pro. Dealer in magic books & magazines in Chicago. Edited Magic Gazette 1933-34 in Chicago. Wrote such booklets as Ghost Rings (1933) & Twenty Hypnotic Tricks (1933).

name: Nelms, Henning [Cunningham]
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 30 Nov 1900-23 May 1986) Lawyer to theatrical director to writer. Amateur magician. Wrote the classic Magic and Showmanship: A Handbook for Conjurers (1969, 322pp; French tr 1984 by Vollmer; Spanish tr). Also, as "Hake Talbot" wrote 2 mystery novels: The Hangman's Handyman (1942) & Rim of the Pit (1944), the latter a classic. [CA]

name: Nelson, Earl
bio: (USA: 1950-) Stage actor. Semi-pro close-up magician. AMA Best Close-up Magician 1979, 1986. Edited West Coast Quarterly 1981-defunct. Wrote Variations (1979, 137pp) & The Chop Cup Book (with Alan Wakeling). Videos (1984). [Wat]

name: Nelson, James M.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Wrote (under pen name of "Janel") Startling Effects (1921; 2nd ed rev, 1964, 40pp). Briefly did Ghost Shows as "Janel" in 1930s.

name: Nelson, Larry
bio: (Ohio: 24 Feb 1900 – 11 Oct 1980) Brother of Robert Nelson. In 1914 performed a two-person mindreading act with brother Bob. In 1916, while still in high school, founded Alla Rageh and Company. During the 1920s worked as a mentalist using the name Alla Rageh. Toured his own spook show in the 1930s. Later worked as a tealeaf reader in Los Angeles. During the 1950s and 60s, worked as a children's entertainer in elementary schools in Los Angeles.

name: Nelson, Robert A[lan] "Bob
bio: (Columbus, Ohio: 16 Nov 1901-21 Feb 1973). Inspired around age 10. Debut at age 13 with paid mental act. Semi-pro with partner with Syl Reilly until 1921. Pro as stage mentalist-telepathist since 1921 when founded Nelson Enterprises in Columbus, Ohio. It became the world's largest company dealing in mentalist's props & literature (until sold in 1972 to Micky Hades). Radio program ("Voice of Destiny") 1928-35 as "Dr. Korda RaMayne, PsD", which he also used on stage in a crystal-gazing act. In the 1940s, after Claude "Alexander" Conlin Jr retired, Nelson bought his entire act, later selling most of it to Leon Mandrake. Invented Multiplying Rabbits (by 1944) & claimed the Psychomatic Deck (by 1948). The most prolific author of books & booklets on mentalism (34 by 1945 alone), including Hellstromism (1935, 21pp), The Encyclopedia of Mentalism (1944, 120pp; repr 1971), Miracles in Mentalism (1945, 64pp), Super Prediction Tricks (1947, 55pp), The Art of Cold Reading (1951; repr 1971, 47pp), Club and Party Mentalism (1961, 50pp), Still More Miracles in Mentalism (1962, 74pp), Comedy Mentalism (3 vols, 1962, 1963, 1964, 59+61+63pp), TV Mentalism (1966, 37pp), & The Last Book of Nelson: An Autobiography, Plus (1970, 55pp). Columns in Tops, Linking Ring, & Magic is Fun. Article in Genii. [Collier's, 4 Oct 47; Walk2; Th]

name: Nelusco
bio: See: Bamberg, Eduard

name: Nemo
bio: See: Neumann, Paul

name: Nemo, Prof.
bio: See: Cramer, Stuart

name: Nemoto, Takeshi
bio: (Fukuoka, Japan: 10 Mar 1936- ) Learned magic in 1956 in school. Protégé of Tenkai. Moved from amateur, thru semi-pro, to pro magician in 1976. Specializes in close-up magic, particularly with cards & coins. Owner of a magic bar in Osaka. Wrote Tokyo Trickery (1967, 86pp) plus several books in Japanese. [Wh2]

name: Neo, Dr. Masashi
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Lives in Nagoya. Close-up worker. 1 video bit (1993).

name: Neptune, Johnny
bio: See: Silver, Ray

name: Nery
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 19 Aug 1926- ) Stage name of António NERY NOGUEIRA. Married a circus trapezist, turning pro circus magician in 1952. Toured Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, & Holland. Since 1977 with the Cardinal Circus in Portugal. [Cam] Nesbitt, The Great (Stockton, England: 1886-1936) Stage name of

name: Nesnah
bio: See: “Lazern, Emile”

name: Neuman, John
bio: (USA: c1859-) Pro muscle reader in USA & abroad since the 1890s.

name: Neumann, Paul
bio: (Karlsberg, N. Silesia, Germany: 14 Jun 1868-29 Nov 1961) Painter & sculptor in Berlin. Amateur magician specialized in pocket tricks. Aka "Nemo". In 1920 co-founded the Berlin Magic Circle. As "Paul Neumann-Karlsberg" wrote Zauber im Gesellschaftskreise (1933, 173pp). Inspired Salvano in 1945. Died in Berlin.

name: Neve, Richard
bio: (England: fl.1700s-20s) A hack writer (also wrote A Guide for Builders [1703]) with some knowledge of magic. Wrote The Merry Companion; or Delights for the Ingenious (London: 1716, 176pp; 2nd ed 1721), which covers 177 tricks: 33 by sleight-of-hand, 50 with cards, plus some mathematical puzzles & jests. The magic section is mainly cribbed from Hocus Pocus Junior (the 2nd or later edition). "New Houdinys, The" SEE: Enzfelder, Dagmar & Enzfelder, Oskar

name: Newcombe, Peter, MIMC
bio: (Britain: -1987) Stage name of Ernest N. Hogg. Insurance executive in London. Amateur close-up magician. Protégé of Francis White in The Magic Circle since 1946. Honorary Secretary, The Magic Circle, 1954-66.

name: Newel
bio: (Austro-Hungarian Empire: 12 Oct 1903-) Pro manip in Czechoslovakia until after WW II. Newmann, C. A. George "Doc" (near Kenyon, Minnesota: 28 Nov 1880-30 Dec 1952) Pen name of Christian Andrew George Naeseth, aka "Newman the Great". Inspired as boy by a medium, a hypnotist, & magician "Harry Heller". Learned at age 10 from magic books & a magic set. Debut at age c13 as amateur mentalist & magician. Pro mentalist & hypnotist since 1896 as "Newmann the Boy Wonder". Reinvented contact mind reading in 1896. Toured the small-time in the Northwest & West Coast. Invented no contact mind reading by 1920. A major collector of magic books by 1916. Typically, his claim in 1937 that with "over 7,500 'publications' ... mine is the largest collection in the Western hemisphere" remains unproved and probably false. That he had a vast accumulation, including many books on hypnotism & the occult is undoubted, but his magic collection, much of which he sold off piecemeal (including some items to McManus), was at best a "strong" magic collection (at least 1,600 titles in 1,800 volumes) with many desirable but not so costly titles. Wrote Newmann's Magical Library (1945) & at least 11 mimeoed booklets, including Clever Card Conjuring (1922, 19pp, 100 copies). Articles in Thayer's Magical Bulletin, Magic World, Tarbell #5, & Linking Ring. Bio is James B. Alfredson, Newmann: The Pioneer Mentalist (1989, 50pp; repr 1990, 60pp). See Leo Behnke (editor), The Collected Mental Secrets of C.A. George Newmann (1991, 600pp). [Pr;Jay;Th]

name: Newmarch, F[rancis] "Frank
bio: (Rotorua, North Island, New Zealand: 17 Apr 1908-2000) Taught one trick by father at age 14. Registrar of High Courts for 43 years. Semi-pro magician since 1931 with manip & stage act as "Baffles". Several competition prizes. By 1990 was the oldest performing magician in New Zealand. 1990 Grand Master of Magic Award (New Zealand). Tricks in Pentagram & Magicana. [Magicana4/76;Wh5]

name: Newton, [Richard Leroy] "Dick
bio: (Everett, Washington: 29 Dec 1927- ) Debut at age 13. Pro comedy stage & close-up magician 1940s-50s throughout USA. Partner with Card Mondor booking their "Den of Living Nightmares" midnight spook show in 39 states 1947-49. TV executive & semi-pro magician since 1959. As Creative Services Director for Wil Shriner syndicated TV talk show, 1987-88, helped book 19 magicians. [Wh4]

name: Newton, Hal
bio:
Neyhart, A. P. "Art" (USA: fl.1930s) Although a layman (a consulting electrical engineer in Los Angeles) he invented the Neyhart Houlette rising cards apparatus by 1935 (when first marketed— at $75), which permits any card called for to rise from a small houlette held in the magician's hands while surrounded. [Sphinx2/35]

[See also: Hall, Newton]

name: N'Gai [pronounced EEN-gah]
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Ronald "Ronnie" Marleigh-Ludlow. Originally a market trader. Thence pro street magician until WW II when became music-hall mind-reader, wearing turban & long robe. Member of Grand Order of Water Rats in 1943. Wrote 2 booklets: The Horse Race (n.d., 10pp) & The Prophecies of N'Gai: Magic in his Words (n.d.). [Le]

name: N'Hutter, Raphael
bio: See: Hutter, Nicholas

name: Niberco, Nic
bio: (Holland: -18 Jan 1992) Stage name of Nic Peter. Also as "The Niberco Brothers" (with Von Berkel & Bob Haleber). Pro manipulator. 1947 Paris Congrès Grand Prix. Toured Portugal in 1953. 1970 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. 1988 FISM jury. Tricks in Informagie & Abra. [Dif; Abra#747]

name: Nic, Chevalier
bio: (Bornholm, Denmark: 3 Feb 1891-Aug 1964). Stage name of Niels Hansen. Pro illusionist. Dealer as owner of Nordeuropaeisk Trylleapparatfabrik (in Copenhagen) 1932-64. NOTE: Sometimes misnamed "Chevalier Nic Jllusion" due to misread punctuation on his posters. [Dif]

name: Nicholás Méridar, Roberto
bio: (Santander, Spain: 5 Oct 1941- ) Debut at age 13 as "El Gran Robert". Pro stage magician, initially as "SandoKan Junior", then since 1968 as "Nicholls & Honey" with his Filipino assistant-wife "Honey" (Tita). In Portugal they played the Coliseu in Lisbon in 1971 & the Casino Estoril in 1980. Recently does comedy magic as "Nic Sanders". [Xe]

name: Nicholl, Capt. Leonard C.
bio: See: "Yung Len Tu"

name: Nicholson, Grady S.
bio: (Terrell, Texas: 5 Jul 1901-Sep 1945) Raised in Ardmore, Oklahoma. Learned magic as boy. Credit manager with furniture company in Oklahoma City. Semi-pro since 1920 (billed as "Mysto Nicholson, The Jolly Joker") with club & full-evening act, specializing in coin manip. Taught Bert Easley c1925. Moved to Hollywood in 1939. [Th;WWM]

name: Nickell, Joe
bio: (Lexington, Kentucky: 1 Dec 1944-) Pro stage magus 1968-73. PI for detective agency 1973-75. PhD 1987. Active in CSICOP since 1984. Wrote several books exposing the paranormal. [CA]

name: Nickle, Robert
bio: (Troy, New York: 2 May 1842-5 Nov 1889) Stage name of John Newbanks. An amateur, he turned pro when he bought out Jim De Barr's show & took it on the road, using the name "Nickle" because De Barr had said he "wasn't worth a dime". Died in poverty. Wrote 2 booklets. Although the Breakaway Fan was a pet effect of his by 1886, he could not, as later suggested by Yost, have been its inventor, being only 1 year old when the trick fan was marketed in England. NOTE: He lied in telling some people his real name was "Charles Robert Nicholls". Also misspelled "Nickel". [Pr;Mo;Buf; CMM11/06] SEE: Beltempo, Domenico

name: Nico
bio: (Lake Geneva, Wisconsin: 18 Oct 1871-7 Dec 1959) Son of "Nicoli". Learned assisting father. Minor pro (since 1892), initially on Lyceum circuit as "Nicoli". Did illusions, later adding a pickpocket act. Briefly with Harry "Blackstone" Bouton as "Bouton & Kelso". Assisted his younger brother "Nicola" at beginning of the latter's 1910 world tour. As "Von Arx" (since 1912) toured his own show in 1912-14 in Australia, South & East Africa, & India. Around 1916 also worked S.E. Asia & Shanghai as "The Great Chalbert". In 1918 played US Army camp shows in Europe (again as "Chalbert") with his brother. Managed Nicola's 1921-24 world tour. Continued on own in USA as "Von Arx". In 1940s-50s ran a spook show (as "Chasan"). [Pr;Wal;Rey]

name: Nicola
bio: (Burlington, Iowa: 14 Dec 1880-1 Feb 1946) Stage name since 1907 of William "Will" M[ozart] Nicol. Learned assisting father "Nicoli" in 1894. Pro on own since 1897. Played a minor theater in Paris in 1900. 1st world tour in 1910-13 to Hawaii, China, S.E. Asia, India, Australia, S. America. In 1918 played US Army camp shows in Europe with his brother. 2nd world tour in 1921-24 to South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, Java, & China. In 1926 bought non-British rights to Selbit's illusions. Played the New York Hippodrome in 1926 & the Palace in 1927. 3rd world tour 1928-30 to Hawaii, Australia, China, Burma, Singapore, China, & Hawaii. 4th world tour 1938-39 to New Zealand, Australia, Java, Bali, & Singapore where he lost all his props in a ship sinking while leaving there on Nov 13th. With reduced show did USO tours throughout world in WW II. SAM Hall of Fame. Silent movie of his act. Younger brother of Charles Nicol. Husband of Marion Nicola, who sold his remaining props to Tad Ware. [Ch;Pr;Rey;Wal;Mar;St;Dif;WWM]

name: Nicola, Marion
bio: (Aleda, Illinois: fl.1920s-80s) Born Marion Eddings. Learned in 1921 as apprentice to Nicola whom she married in 1938. Retired on husband's death in 1946. Wrote (with Tad Ware) a draft bio of Nicola.

name: Nicolay, Faure
bio: (France: fl.1870s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro illusionist. Performed for Emperor Napoleon III. Played Portugal in 1878. Moved to Rio de Janeiro by 1901. Wrote Memorias e Confidencias (Rio: 1901, 184pp). [Magic12/01,12/02;Cl;Cam]

name: Nicolay, Gaetano
