bio: (France: fl.1860s-70s) Pro illusionist. Toured Portugal in 1868 & 1872. [Cam] Nicoli, The Great (USA: -1955) Stage name of John McNicol who later dropped the "Mc". Photographer in Monmouth, Illinois. Semi-pro illusionist, playing locally. Father of "Nicola" and "Von Arx".

name: Nielsen, Gene
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Semi-pro mentalism & close-up. Articles in Talisman, Magick (under pen name "Cicardi"), etc. 5 audios (1988, etc). In 1985 (with wife Valerie) invented the Zip-Loc "Ultimate Transparent Change Bag". Video bit (1988).

name: Nielsen, Leo
bio: (Denmark: 28 Mar 1927- ) Aka "Topp". Pro dealer & prop maker (Topp's Magic) in Saksköbing, Denmark, since 1959. Viggo Jahn was, between engagements, an active partner in the business. Edited Topp Nyt.

name: Nielsen, Norm[an Dale] MIMC
bio: (Kenosha, Wisconsin: 17 Feb 1934- ) Son of a Danish baker. Learned at age 12 from town barber Herman Raditz and auto mechanic Ralph Pharr, both amateur magicians. Inspired to become a pro by seeing Neil Foster work a magic convention. Chavez School student in 1952-53. With US Army. Demonstrator at Berg's shop in Hollywood in 1956. Tutored Paul Svengari (1962-64), etc. Dealer-maker of high quality magic props (Nielsen Magic) in southern California and then Las Vegas since 1964. Pro stage magician & manipulator since 1965. Invented Floating Violin in 1966. Pet effects: Floating Violin (since 1966) & Christian Fechner's Floating Piano (since 1982). Taught at Chavez in 1979. Has played the Moulin Rouge & Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris, Portugal's Casino Estoril (1971), and Las Vegas show rooms. 1970 AMA Best Stage Magician. Pro stage magician. 1978 AMA Magician of the Year (shared). 1990 Jack Gwynne Award at Abbott's. 1995 MIMC with Gold Star. 2005 DRAGON Award (with wife Lupe). Published Bottle Book & Magic Castle Walls of Fame (1988). TV bits. [LR9/97; Bo; Fi; Win; Mag; HC; Wh2]

name: Niessner, Rudolf
bio: (Austria: c1868-1940) Pro magician of the old school, juggler with soap bubbles, & shadowgraphist.

name: Nightingale, Fred B. "Nighty
bio: (Deerfield, New York: 26 Dec 1885-1965) Taught by circus magician. Pro since 1908 in vaudeville. Autobio is Magic for Magicians (1964, 304pp).

name: Nikola
bio: See: "Clive, Henry"

name: Nikola, Louis
bio: (Southampton, England: 14 Mar 1878-11 Nov 1936) Stage name (from Guy Boothby's novel, Dr Nikola) of Walter J. Obree Smith. Pro since 1901 as magician & shadowist. Toured France, Germany, Egypt, India (1911), Australia (1917), & New Zealand (1918). Played St. George's Hall 1908-11, 1919-24, 1927, & 1931. Ill health forced early retirement. His props were bought by Edgar Benyon. Co-invented (with Roy Enoc) Milk Pitcher (by 1917) & invented Nikola Card System (by 1927). Popularized Magic Welding (in 1942). Wrote The Drawing Room Magician (1912), Hand Shadows (1913, 109pp), The Nikola Card System (1927, 27pp), & Magical Masterpieces (1934, 251pp). Tricks in Boy's Own Paper (1900). NOTE: Sometimes misspelled "Nicola". [Daw#223;Wal;St;Go2;Vo56;Ho;Magic5/11]

name: Nilsson, Christer
bio: (Nyköping, Sweden: 22 Sep 1931- ) First interested in magic in 1945. Semi-pro illusionist as "Christer el Ricco" with a magic & balloon act 1955-74. Since then an amateur & collector in Nyköping. Proprietor of Sveriges Magi-Arkiv, the world's largest collection of Scandinavian magicana (books, magazines, apparatus, posters, etc). 1977 Swedish Magic Circle Knight of Magic. Edited Trollkarlen 1966-1989. Wrote Trollare och andra underhållare [Magicians and Other Entertainers] (1990, 288pp, 330 illus), the largest book about magicians & allied artists ever published in Scandinavia. Articles in Trollkarlen & Linking Ring. [Wh2]

name: Nimble, Max B.
bio:
"Nine-stone-ten" [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

[See also: Howard, Max]

name: Nino
bio: See: Guerrero, Nino

name: Nivelli, Herbert
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 9 Sep 1906-3 May 1977) Stage name (by reversal) of Herbert Levin. German Jew. Pro manip & illusions. Youngest member of Berlin Stock Exchange until Jews were excluded. Fled in 1933 to Czechoslovakia where he opened 7 magic shops. Spent WW II in various Nazi concentration camps including Auschwitz, surviving by performing for and teaching magic to his captors. In 1947 immigrated under the Displaced Persons quota to the USA where he continued to perform stage magic until his death. Played the NY Palace in 1953, 1954, & 1957. A brief bio is William V. Rauscher, Nivelli: Magician of the Holocaust (1987, 7pp). [LR11/86]

name: Nix, John B.
bio: (Britain: c1855-c1925) Learned in 1865 as assistant to J.H. Anderson. Thence popular public & private magician as "Dr. Nix" & "Paul Lemare". Variously billed as "The Boy Conjuror" & "The Royal Conjuror". [Pr;Vo56;Daw94;Magic5/03]

name: Nixon, Dr. Cecil E.
bio: (West Indies: c1881-1962) Of English father. Brought to USA around age 5. A mechanic in San Francisco who was a semi-pro builder of automata, including the famous Isis & Galatea. [Th]

name: Nixon, David [Porter], MIMC
bio: (North London, England: 29 Dec 1919-1 Dec 1978) Pro. Toured with ENSA in WW II. Long-time host & star of BBC-TV show "It's Magic" in late 1960s and the ITT-TV "The David Nixon Show" in the 1970s. 1971 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" award. King Rat of the Grand Order of Water Rats 1974-76. Also popular British TV panelist. [Huff; La2; Fi]

name: Nixon, Doc
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City, NY?: 23 Feb 1884-) Stage name of William J. Dixon. Learned at age 10 as apprentice to family of Chinese magicians, or so he claimed. Pro magician & illusionist since 1906. In 1909 traded his flat in Brooklyn for Theo Bamberg's "Okito" name & act. Toured Brazil in 1910. He adopted more stage names (as opposed to pen names) than any other magician: "Nixon-Okito" (1909), "Savant--Japanese Magician" (1910), "Savant Nixon" (1911), "Neek Suen" (1914), "Ling [or Lung?] Chang Yuen", "Yuen Chan Foo", "Chang Foo Yuen", "Chan Omar", "Dr. Omar", "Chanamar", "Willie Foo Lee", "Wjaynx", "Chandu the Magician" (1933), etc. Last reported doing magic in 1939. Then did house chores while living with a Roman Catholic order in St. Louis & thence dropped out of sight. Wrote Hong Kong Mysteries (1921, 39pp; new edition by Fred Rickard, 1986, 75pp; 1921 ed repr by Walter Graham in 1987 as The Nixon Manuscript in Book Form; Nixon Ghost Manuscript (1929), 1931 Magical Surprise, etc. Articles in Sphinx & Linking Ring. [Pr;Dor;Ho]

name: Nixon, Vic[tor William]
bio: (Reading, England: 1888-) Pro magician since 1902, initially as "Carl Rosella" with an illusion show. Toured Far East 1903-10. After WW I toured as "Satan, the Red Hot Illusionist". In 1921 became "The Great Nixon". Switched to mentalism in 1934. Owned shop (Nixon's Magic Depot) in Bournemouth for 3 decades. Moved to Canada in 1950s. Father of "Vic Perry".

name: Nizzini, Carlo
bio: (Germany: fl.1870s) Stage name of Edmund Wallner. Minor pro sleight-of-hand & apparatus conjuror. Wrote Magie im Salon (1872, 146pp).

name: Noakes, Ernest E., MIMC
bio: (England: 28 Dec 1873-6 Feb 1956) Pro London society magician by 1903 when he was also a minor dealer & vent. Played the Magical Theatre in the Crystal Palace for 50 weeks in 1906-07 & again in 1909. Associated (with Wilfred Zelka) in City Magical Company until 1910 when bought out by Servais Le Roy. Wrote Magical Originalities (1914, 161pp). Played St. George's Hall 1917. Memoir is Mirthful Memories of a Magician (1920, 85pp). Later taught Alan Shaxon. [LR8/89]

name: Noble, Lee
bio: (Randolph, Massachusetts: 5 Jan 1916-30 Apr 2003) Stage name of Edwin Lee Burchell. As "Edwin the Enigma" contributed tricks to Sphinx in his teens. Became pro magician c1938, originally as "Lee Burchell", thence as "Lee Noble". Played the New York Loew's State in 1946. Dropped magic to do a straight comedy act 1949-1967 as "Lee Burchell". Worked as engineer for NBC-TV 1967-81. Mail-order magic prop & book dealer in 1970s-80s. Since moving to Florida in 1981 has worked part-time as magician-mentalist. Manager of Old Town Magic Shop in Orlando, Florida, since 1991. Died in an auto accident. Wrote Hundred Dollar Book Plus! (1972, 29pp). Tricks in Sphinx & Phoenix. [Wh]

name: Nocha
bio: (Spain: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of J. Achon. 1950 FISM 2nd prize for presentation with silks, rings, & the Card Stab.

name: Noë
bio: (Switzerland: 20 Nov 1907-14 Jul 1944) Stage name of Emile Zemp. Pro music-hall magician.

name: Noël
bio: (France: fl.1770s) Pro. Operated a small theater in Paris in the Rue de Richelieu where he exhibited various mechanical tricks and an automaton that answered the spectators thoughts. [CI]

name: Nokihara, Hiroshi
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 14 Apr 1951- ) Founder & Managing Director, DP Group Ltd, 1983-present. DP is a mail-order export-import company in Chiba, Japan, dealing in stationery, toys, & magic. The recently added magic line of cheap items aimed at beginners & amateurs is exported wholesale & sold in Japan by mail-order only. [Wh2]

name: Nord, Bill
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Semi-pro in New York City. Invented Skull-ocation (1948), Ashes of Satan (1948), Diablo Slate (1949), Bill-Ze-Bub (1950), The Private Eye (1951), Thought Master (1953), & Magic of Manhattan. Tricks in Sphinx, Phoenix, & HMM.

name: Nordenstam, Bernadotte
bio: (Örebro, Sweden: 26 Apr 1863-30 Aug 1942) Pro. Moved to Christiana, Norway. Died in Oslo. His Norwegian-born sons Fridtjov (born 1910) & Eystein (born 1913) both followed in his footsteps as magicians in Norway. [Vo58]

name: Nordnes, Terje
bio: (Rena, Norway: 30 [sic] Nov 1905-8 May 1985) Pro 2-person mind-reading act as "Calostro" 1922-45. Invented the Fickle Nickel effect & method in 1938, fooling Dante with it. Co-founded the Magiske Cirkel Norge in 1928 & Den Magiske Ring Oslo in 1948. Edited Magikeren: Nordisk Fagblad for Magikere 1928-58, Norway's first magic periodical. Co-edited (with Hilding Eriksson) Magiens Verden 1948- ?. 1972 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. [St;Dif;WWM]

name: Norma
bio: (Ystad, Sweden: 17 Feb 1862-21 Feb 1920) Pro & inventor of many tricks sold by Carl Willmann's shop in Hamburg. Taught Oswald Thureo. [Dif; Vo58] SEE: Krieger, Norma

name: Norman
bio: (London, England: 15 Oct 1905-) Stage name of Norman D. Appleing. Debut in magic at age 15 & vent at 21. Semi-pro magician & vent. Articles. [Go;Go2] Norman, The Great (England: c1885-1975) Stage name of Norman Hazeldene. Lithographer. Semi-pro magician. Invented Elusive Rabbits=Hippity-Hop Rabbits (by 1947). [Le]

name: Norman, Anthony
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Norman Binns. Wrote Basic Card Technique (1948, 298pp).

name: Norman, Karl
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 17 Nov 1918- ) Learned in 1931 from library books & magic sets. Toolmaker. Semi-pro magician since 1938 doing kid shows and close-up sleight-of-hand. Was Gene Gordon's 1st demonstrator in 1946. Worked the Forks Hotel bar in Buffalo 1970-1980s. 1982 FFFF "Best" award. Wrote Here's How (1984, 0pp). Tricks in Linking Ring. See Mike Porstman, Karl Norman (1993, in German) translated into English by Anthony Brahams as Forty Years at the Forks (1995). [LR3/2000;Wh5]

name: Norrington, George [Thomas]
bio: (Carshalton, Surrey, England: 2 Jan 1950-) Taught magic in 1970 by Noel Stanton. Mail-order dealer (George Norrington Magic) in Dorking, Surrey, since 1980. Pro since 1983, working mainly kid-shows. Has edited-published 12 George Norrington's Who's Who in Magic, covering British agents, dealers, etc, 1980-91. [MC6/91;Wh2]

name: Norris, Professor William S.
bio: (England: 1822-14 Jun 1904) Son of a magic apparatus maker. Pro debut in 1851. Had a wholesale & retail Conjuring Depot in Knightsbridge in 1857 & then in Portman Square in 1861. A master wood craftsman, he made fine props, which are now collectors items, many being in The Magic Circle Museum. Had small magic theater, dealer's stall, & workshop at the Crystal Palace, London, 1868-85, giving over 14,000 shows there. Last of the old-time conjurors to wear flowing robes, doing so for his many daily stage appearances to cover his workshop clothes. [Daw94;LR8/89;CI]

name: North
bio: See: Bigbee, North

name: Norton, Alice
bio: (England: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro magicienne. Worked a "jewel" act, possibly the first of its kind, when she played the London Hippodrome in 1907. [Mar]

name: Norton, C. Porter
bio: See: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Norton, Coe
bio: (Tacoma, Washington: -1998) Stage actor and pro magician. Married actress Laura Lee Green in 1962 while both were in the couring company of Auntie Mame. The Nortons then became a leading cruise-ship magic team. Coe died of Alzheimer's and Laura (who had been born in New Bern, North Carolina) died 23 Jun 2001. [LR10/64]

name: Norton, Stanley
bio: (England: fl.1910s-30s) Stage name of S. Leslie Geere. Pro dealer in London, having bought out Munro's in 1917, although continuing to trade as "Munro's Magical Mart" until 1919 when, taking Bert Bretma as partner became the Norton-Bretma Manufacturing Company until 1920 when bought out by Bretma. Co-invented (with Stuart Luciene) Whirling Wheel. Invented the "Pick of the Pack" changing card (1920). Wrote A Few Jardine Ellis Secrets (1925). Contributed to Magic Wand. [Daw94]

name: Norton, Wash[ington]
bio: (New Orleans: 2 Feb 1839 – 16 Nov 1899) First start in show business at age 9. Had his start in the US in minstrel shows. Traveled to Europe, South Africa & South America. After 1877 sailed to Yokohama, Japan with modest success, continued on to Shanghai, Hong Kong & Singapore. Met little success and moved to Penang, Calcutta, Bombay and Australia. Then vanishes for a while and reappears in 1887 in Nevada with conjuring show with emphasis on the Black Art act led by Achmed Ali Bey. Show moved to Japan with the name "Wash Norton's World's Greatest Magic" and was a sensation there. Although the show was centered around conjuring it including other forms of entertainment such as costume changes, upside-down painting, music, comic drama & dance. Retired around 1889 on his farm in Shasta county. (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 5 Jan 1879-1 Sep 1959) Popular pro vaudeville singer, comedian, & composer. Amateur magician. Norworth, Jack Husband (1908-13) of singing star Nora Bayes with whom he wrote the popular song, "Shine On, Harvest Moon" (1908). He sometimes included magic in their act, as in his "Magical Musical Medley" show in 1911. Also wrote "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" & "Come Along, My Mandy". Retired to Southern California. [Daw#5;Lau;Magic12/11]

name: Nosek, Terrence R[obert] "Terry
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 17 Jul 1936-12 Apr 2005..) Learned magic at age 8. Marketing research executive. Semi-pro mentalist since 1968. Demonstrator at Magic Inc in Chicago 1975-81. Moved to Las Vegas. Aka "Dr. Sigmund Fraud". PEA President 1983-84. Wrote The Collected Works of Sigmund Fraud (1984, 71pp). Articles in Ireland Yearbook, Linking Ring, New Tops, Magick, New Invocation, Vibrations, MUM, Boston Barnstormer. TV bits. [LR8/2003;Wh5]

name: Notis, Professor
bio: (Italy: -1953) Stage name of Mario Amando Vigna. Pro circus in Europe to pro gambler. Moved to Argentina, working as a pro magician-jugger in South America. Invented the Notis Cascade card flourish. [St;Wat]

name: Notting, Herbert
bio: (England: -25 Nov 1908) Minor itinerant magician who worked the Midlands & Yorkshire. Aka "Mexican Jim". Murdered in Swadlingcote under mysterious circumstances after leaving a local pub. [Magic12/08]

name: Nottle, [Leslie George] "Les", MIMC
bio: (London, England: 14 Oct 1920-22 Dec 1996) Inspired around age 7 seeing a magic show. Engineer/salesman in London. Part-time pro magician since age 20, working both adult & childrens shows. Also Punch & Judy. Lecturer.

name: Nourse, [Anna] Inez
bio: (Fox Lake, Wisconsin: 23 Jun 1889-Oct 1983) A 5'1" banjo player on Northwest vaude circuits until 1916 when hired as music director by Harry Boughton for his "Fredrik the Great" troupe. Married Harry (then "Blackstone") in 1919, continuing as his principal female assistant until 1929 when they separated & divorced. 1st female IBM Member. Thence on management staff of 2 magicians, including George Marquis. While touring with Marquis & "Rajah Raboid" in Mexico, married the latter's brother, Robert Kitchen. When widowed, retired to Sarasota, Florida, but continued to attend magic conventions. [Mar;LR2/99]

name: Novak, John [Andrew]
bio: (New Philadelphia, Ohio: ca.1931-17 Jul 2004) Escapist, bizarrist, & dealer in Texas. Edited ASA 1974-75 (13 issues) & Escape 1977-80 (13 issues). Wrote The Art of Escape (8 vols).

name: Novra, Henry
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s-70s). Pro magician, aka "Mons Henri" & "The Wizard of the West". Dealer (the "Magical Repository") in London at 95 Regent Street as partner (with George Novra) in this toy shop from c1844 to 1858 when he became sole owner, converting the shop to magic only. It continued until 1877. Published Catalogue of Conjuring Tricks and Puzzles, from Henry Novra's Magical Repository [c1858-59, 32pp] & Descriptive Catalogue of Conjuring Tricks, from Henry Novra's Magical Repository (1861, 29pp), both reprinted 1995. Bio is J.B. Findlay, "Henry Novra Conjuring Dealer", Sphinx (May 1951). [Daw94]

name: Nunez, Professor
bio: See: Clarence, H. G.

name: Nurmi, Bruno [pronounced NOOR-mi]
bio: (Finland: 3 Sep 1900-1979) Stage name of Bruno Ludvig Nurmi-Johansson. Circus barker & magician, aka "Mr Bruno". The "father" of ventriloquism in Finland. [St]

name: Nürnberg, O.
bio: (Werdick, Kreis Rothenburg, Germany: 13 Jun 1851- ) Pro. [Sal]

name: Nyquist, Charles W[alter] "Charlie
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 19 Mar 1912-25 Jan 1997) Lawyer, moving to Washington, DC, in 1938 and to San Francisco in 1947. Amateur magician since 1920, having learned from friends. Specialized in card magic. Collector of magic books & magazines, selling most (some 1,000 volumes) to Lloyd Jones c1970. Tricks in Jinx, Sphinx, Phoenix, HMM, Linking Ring, Genii, etc, and contributor to several major books. Retired from the law in 1976. [Th;Wh]

name: Oakie, Jack
bio: (Sedalia, Missouri: 12 Nov 1903 [sic]-23 Jan 1978) Stage name of Lewis Delaney Offield. Stage comedian since 1922 and in films since 1927. Amateur magician. Regular customer at Thayer's in 1940s. Autobio is Jack Oakie's Double Takes (1980). [Katz]

name: Oaks, John Harold
bio: (USA: 9 May 1889 - 24 Sep 1918) Pro magician & escapist 1906-1910. Young Johnny "Mighty" Oaks toured the country including Canada starting in about 1909 until after a few close calls, among other things he decided to leave the road and devote full time to his store and thriving mail order business. Founder-owner of Oaks Magical Company in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, in 1910. Very shortly after enlisting in the Navy and before going into training he sold half interest in the store to Harvey Harwood, local Oshkosh newspaper man. After Oaks death in Sept of 1918 (Spanish Flu), Harwood ran the store until the early 1930's. The store and much of its inventory was then sold to professional magician and Berlin WI resident, Gerald Heaney. The mail order part of the business was bought by Ed Miller of Chicago. [Albo95]

name: O'Brien, Mike, MIMC
bio:
(Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Learned magic at age 16-18 from books. Official with the London government (retired in 1986). Semi-pro comedy close-up magician. 1971 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. 1987 British Ring Tom Harris Cup. Articles in Magic Circular, Genii, & Magic Info. TV bits. [MC8/89]

[See also: "Edgar, Professor"]

name: O'Brien, [Ronald James] "Obie
bio: (Ottawa, Ontario, Canada: 3 Jun 1932-). Moved to USA in 1953 (citizen since 1961). Learned in 1953 as college freshman. Math teacher (MS) at State U of New York from 1961 until retired c1992. Amateur close-up magician. Co-founded (with Eddie Fechter) the FFFF in 1971 and its sole impresario since Fechter's death in 1979. IBM President 1993-94. Invented 2 jumbo card tricks: Kolossal Kolored Kards & Almost Real Magic. Wrote Fork Full of Appetizers (3 vols, 1982, 1985, 1990 forthcoming). Articles in Linking Ring, Genii, MUM, etc. [LR7/93;LR10/85;Wh2]

name: O'Connor, Billy
bio: (Ireland: c1895-1974). Stage name of Eugene Dêvot. Of French parentage & fluent in French. Pro comedy cardman since before WW I. Played St. George's Hall 1921 & 1923-24. Assisted Selbit at the Alhambra in Paris in 1924. Played the Empire in Paris 1928 & 1931. His son Robert O'Connor continued the act in the 1950s. Invented Instanto Pack & marketed it in 1919. Tricks in Magic Wand, Pentagram, New Pentagram. [Pr;Dif;Ho;Bam,p66;Al]

name: O'Day, Buddy
bio: (USA: c1915-2 Aug 1996) Stage name of William F. Tackett. Pro comedy magician since 1934, originally in burlesque. Also did chalk talks. Retired in 1973 but occasionally worked charity as "Weirdo the Magician". Tricks (including 2 Parades) in Linking Ring.

name: O'Dell, Dell
bio: (Wisconsin, USA: 1902-5 Feb 1962) Stage name of Nell [sic] Newton. Of Irish-French parents. Raised in Kansas. Inspired by magic shows in her father's carnival where she worked as a strong woman (could balance a sofa on her chin). Pro comedy magicienne, the most successful in the USA in the 1930s-50s. Famous for her rhymed patter. Had TV show in southern California c1950. Wrote Magical Moments (45pp). Columnist for Linking Ring & Magic is Fun. Wife of popular juggler Charles Carrer (see) who built & repaired many of her props. [Th;Mar;HMM10/51;Pr]

name: Odin, Claudius
bio: (Paris, France: 19 Jun 1869-29 May 1959) Pro close-up. A founding member of ASAP in 1903. Joined the ASAP in 1905. 1906 Chambre Syndicale de la Prestitidigitaion 2nd prize for invention. Died in poverty. Wrote Les anneaux chinois (1928), English tr by Victor Farelli as The Odin Rings (1931, 68pp); and Les cartes biseautées (1928, 44pp) with English tr as "The Odin Cards" in HMM 1952-54. [Dif; Vo55]

name: Odin, Fernand
bio: (France: fl.1960s-90s) Pro dealer-maker ("Manufacture Fernand Odin") of illusions in Saint-Étienne.

name: Odips
bio: (France: -1983) Stage name of Pierre Saint-Denis. Burlesque comedy magic & marionnettes. Joined the management of the Cabinet Fantastique in 1944. 1951 FISM 2nd prize for presentation. AFAP Master Magician. Often worked with partner-wife as "Odips & Betty Berkel". [Bou]

name: O'Dowd, [Michael A.] "Mike
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 27 Jan 1941- ) Learned in 1952 from Don Lawton. Aka "Mr. Destin" (1963). Pro magician & illusionist since 1975. Pet effects: Sub Trunk, Eggs from Hat, Cups & Balls. Dealer (O'Dowd Conjuring Books) in used & rare magic books, periodicals, & apparatus in Barnhart, Missouri, since 1975. In 1985 married magicienne Rita Jane Corona (neé Larocco, born 28 Dec 1949 in St. Louis). Articles in Legerdemain, MUM, & Genii. [Monti;MUM7/81;Wh2]

name: O'Dowd, Michael
bio: (Dublin, Ireland: c1924-) Learned as a child from a neighbor. Moved to Canada where he is a marine surveyor in Toronto. Amateur magus with specialty in gambling cheating methods about which he lectures widely to college students and police. REF: “Michael the card sharp!, The Sunday Press (Dublin), 26 Aug 1979.

name: Odress
bio: (France: 21 Sep 1867-19 Dec 1911) Stage name of Joseph-Charles-Mathieu Juppier. Pro. Died in Egypt.

name: Odronoff
bio: (Bahia Blanca, Argentina: 1889-10 Dec 1975) Stage name of Juan Mañuel Zolezzi [sic]. Pro second-sight act with assistant-wife Lizz. They played the Lisbon Coliseu 1922, 1923, & 1929. Wrote El libro de Odronoffs. [Cam;Dif]

name: Odry [de Pascar], Zuard
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1873-) Guitar virtuoso. Taught magic by Hueszelmann, Dr Hajduska, & Bernthaller. Amateur magician. Founding member of MAME in 1924. Teacher of Dr Nitsch. [WWM]

name: Oehler, Andrew
bio: (Alstadt, Germany: 16 Mar 1781- ) Moved to Louisiana where he learned magic. Pro, including a ghost show. Toured the Caribbean, Mexico, & American Indian territory. Retired in 1809 in Trenton, New Jersey. Autobio is The Life, Adventures, and Unparalleled Sufferings of Andrew Oehler (1811, 226pp). [Ch]

name: Oeser, Marie
bio: (Austria: 1854-1932) She was a protégé of Conradi & Kratky-Baschik. Debut in 1874. Played the Kratky-Baschik Zauber [Magic] Theater in Vienna. Used stage name "Amanda von Oeser", then after marrying a Herr Lilge, "Amanda Lilge-Oeser", & "Armida". [Vo57;Al]

name: Ogata, Tomosaburo
bio: (Japan: 31 Jan 1883-25 Aug 1973) In 1935 became founder-editor of TAMC, official organ of the Tokyo Amateur Magicians Club and Japan's 1st magic magazine. His collection on early Japanese magic books and posters is one of the best and is kept as the Ogata library in Tokyo.

name: Ogden, Tom
bio: (Phoenixville, Pennsylvania: 12 Nov 1951-) Inspired by Mark Wilson's TV show at age 12. Learned vent from teacher & magic from library books. Pro comedy close-up & stage since 1973, first for a few years as a circus magician. Pet effect: Sword thru Neck. Taught magic groups in 1970s. Moved in 1982 to Hollywood where he also occasionally appears as TV actor. AMA Parlour Magician of the Year 1984, 1985. Has marketed several original effects, including Carnival Cards & Stripped Poker. Co-author (with Walt Hudson) of A Volunteer from the Audience. 4 lecture notes. Wrote Two Hundred Years of the American Circus (1993, 402pp) & Wizards and Sorcerers (1997, 246pp). Columns in MUM, Magic Manuscript, & Genii. Articles in Apocalypse, Top Hat, etc. [Wat;Mag;Wh2]

name: Oger, Prof.
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 9 Aug 1896-25 Apr 1978) Stage name of António LOPES DO REGO. Pro stage magician. Publisher & Director of O Mágico 1951-60 (6 issues). [Cam]

name: O'Hara, Clive
bio: See: "Clive, Henry"

name: Oiram
bio: (Teano, Italy: 22 Feb 1913-) Stage or pen name (by reversal) of Mario Altobelli.

name: Okal, [William Ralph] "Bill
bio: (Lancaster, New York: 3 Apr 1937- ) Learned at age 11 from Scarne books in public library. Pro close-up, street, & platform magician. Worked Fechter's Fork's Hotel in Buffalo, New York, 1964-80. Moved in 1982 to San Francisco Bay area where he performs regularly on stage at Ghirardelli Square, The Cannery, & Pier 39. Also private & trade-show gigs. Wrote Card Magic (1982, 175pp) & A New Look at Some Classic Close-Up (1988, 45pp). Articles in State of the Art. [Wh2]

name: Okati, Professeur
bio: (Ouzouer-le-Marché, Loir-et-Cher, France: 4 Mar 1892-26 Jan 1950) Stage name of Étienne-Louis Pitou. Pro illusionist & stage magician. Director of the Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1933-47. Founding President IBM French Ring 1933-50. Author. [Dif:Vo55]

name: Oki, George
bio: (Germany: -18 Dec 1982) Stage name of F.W. Burmeister of Rostock. Wrote Magische Neuheiten (1932, 30pp typescript). Later moved to Hamburg where he became a dealer in second-hand magic. Died of automobile accident injuries.

name: Okinu
bio: (Japan: c1895-6 Dec 1980) Stage name of Iwa Kato. Learned assisting Tenkai, whom she married in 1913. Often simultaneously performed Tenkai's sleights with watches, cards, & other small props. Taught Mariko Taki. Retired on husband's death in 1972. [Win;Ch]

name: Okita
bio: See: de Vere, Julia

name: Okito
bio: See: Bamberg, Theo

name: Oklahoma
bio: (Prague, Bohemia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 3 Feb 1917-1987) Stage name of Jaroslav Ždárský, aka "Jarry Torre". Pro since 1935 with manip in Czechoslovakia, specializing in cigarettes. Did full-evening illusion show 1945-50. Taught Władysław Kieres. Toured the Soviet block, Finland, & West Germany. Retired in 1978. [Win]

name: Olai, Fritz
bio: (Denmark: 24 Mar 1910-c1980) Businessman in Copenhagen. Semi-pro magician, known for his elegant "Symphony in Silk" magic act. President of Danish Magic Circle in 1940s. Later dropped out of magic.

name: Olbrini, Carlo
bio: (Italy?: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pro. Billed as "The Great Illusionist of the World". Performed in Europe in 1907.

name: Oldridge, Sidney, MIMC
bio: (Britain: c1862-4 Feb 1940) Learned assisting James Matthews in 1877. Pro on own and long with David Devant troupe. [Cl]

name: Olf, Julian M.
bio: (New York City, NY: 18 Sep 1942- ) Learned magic by 5 years of lessons from Jack Miller. Professional actor & Professor of Theater, formerly at Stony Brook College, now at U of Massachusetts in Amherst. Part-time pro magician. Wrote "The Actor and the Magician", The Drama Review (Mar 1974) plus other articles on performance theory. [Wh2]

name: Olgo, Professor
bio: (near Pressburg, Hungary: 1901-18 Jul 1979) Stage name of Berthold Jassinger. Pro lightning calculator & memory act. Died in Budapest. [Mül]

name: Oliveira, J[oaquim] G[onçalves d']
bio: (Abadim, Portugal: 24 Jun 1854-1 Feb 1928) Moved to Lisbon at age 16. Pro illusionist since 1870. Toured Brazil & played the Cirque d'Hiver in Paris before 1900. By 1907 had his own magic shop & factory in Lisbon. Co-founded the Núcleo Mefistofélico Lusitano magic society in 1912. Wrote 5 books in Portuguese including Magica, Physica e Prestidigitação (1883, 32pp), Recreações Scientíficas (1887, 40pp), Prestidigitação Moderna o Recreações Photográficas (1900, 64pp), & O Prestidigitador Moderno (1910, 122pp; 2nd ed, 1912; 3rd ed, 1917, 160pp; 4th ed, 1921, 180pp). NOTE: Not to be confused with "Oliveira das Mágicas", the Portuguese dramatic writer Joachim Augusto de Oliveira (1827-1901). [Cam]

name: Oliver, David
bio: (USA: Apr 1966-) Inspired at age 6 seeing Mark Wilson on TV. Beginning at age 14 worked 10 years as a demonstrator at Hank Lee's in Boston, Pro. Pet effect: Floating Ball. [MUM4/01]

name: Olivier père [pronounced oh-LIV-ee-ay]
bio: (France: fl.1790s-1820s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist in Paris, touring the Continent c1790-c1820 with a Pinetti-type act. Pet effects: Flying Coins & Smashed-and-Restored Watch. Possibly the 1st magician to work bare armed. Father of Olivier fils. NOTE: Name sometimes spelled "Olivier". [Cl;Dif]

name: Olivier fils
bio: (France: fl.1810s-30s) Son of Olivier. Pro magician-ventriloquist in Paris. Played Berne, Switzerland, in 1815. Wrote Nouveau manuel des sorciers, ou la magie blanche dévoilée (1837). NOTE: Name sometimes spelled "Olivier", although it appears as "Olivier" on his 1815 Berne poster. [Dif]

name: Olkowski, Frank
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 17 Sep 1912- ) Pro manip with cards, balls, cigs. Aka "Fanto the

name: Ollivier [misspelling?]
bio: See: Olivier

name: Oims, John
bio: (Meißen, Saxony, Germany: 30 Aug 1880-6 Aug 1955) Stage name of Richard Lischke. Nephew of Oscar Lischke whose magic shop in Hamburg inspired Richard to take up magic. Debut as assistant to Arthur "Biberti" Bieber. Then pro on own. Toured Mexico (1912) & USA (1914). After 1918 began his famous watch-&-clock act in imitation of Gus Fowler. Billed as the "Uhrenkönig" [Watch King]. His niece, Peggy Lauder, was his assistant until she went on own. Toured USA vaudeville as "Johnnie & Nellie Olms" in 1924, Brazil in 1926, & played Paris in 1926 as "Holms". Returned to Germany where he did comedy magic as "Bosco-Olms". Retired in WW II when all his apparatus was destroyed. Died in Berlin. [Win;Pr;Vo57;St;Dif;Lau]

name: Olson, Robert A[lan] "Bob
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 23 Dec 1938-) Learned at age 7 or 8 from Mysto Magic set. Museum consultant on games, puppetry, & magic. Coin columnist (with John Hope) in Hugard's Magic Monthly 1958-60. Wrote Sick Sorcery (1961, 48pp, with Bob Pearce). Turned pro magician in 1970 with historical magic acts (as "Richard Potter" & "Mr. Bayly") and comedy close-up for commercial shows. Collector of tokens, magic sets, and early props & paper. [Des;Wh2]

name: Olson, Rev. Robert E. "Bob
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 31 Aug 1927- ) Learned at age 11 from a magic set, thence public library books. Reverend Olson (ordained in 1955 in the Assemblies of God) is a gospel magician, working stage & close-up and touring since 1958. Collector. Prolific magic author. Wrote bios of Carl Rosini (1966); Howard Thurston, titled The Worlds Greatest Magician (1981); Edmund Spreer, titled Illusion Builder to Fu-Manchu (1986); & again Thurston titled The Complete Life of Howard Franklin Thurston (1993, 2 vols, forthcoming). Also wrote several booklets, including The Added Touch (1963, 38pp), Two Hands-Three Pockets-Four Magic (1966, 32pp), etc. Articles in Sphinx, Genii, Big Bob's Magic News, Christian Conjuror, Magic Sounds, & Linking Ring (5 awards). Columnist on Gospel Magic in New Tops 1961-77. Also uses "REO" as illustration & pen name. [Wh]

name: Olsson, Kent G[eorge]
bio: (Malmö, Sweden: 21 Jul 1944-) Inspired at age 5 seeing Hector El Neco show. Semi-pro as "Clay Adams". Pet effect: Orange-Lemon-Egg-&-Canary. Collector. Articles on magic, escapology, pickpocketing, vent, & bios of magi in Swedish National Encyclopedia. Articles in Nordisk Magi, Trollkarlen, Tryllejornalen, Tricks, etc. [Wh5]

name: Often, Jac
bio: (France: 13 Apr 1913-) Stage name of Alfred Mihiel, aka "Jack Holten", who claimed to be the Compte [count] d'Orcinas. Ex-pro gambler. Pro manipulator with thimbles, cards, lit cigarettes, silks, etc. Toured France, Germany, Africa, & USA. A French Jew, he was released in Nov 1940 from a German POW camp (Stalag 13) by Helmut "Kalanag" Schreiber who gave him props & arranged bookings. Co-founded the Amicale Robert-Houdin in Nice in 1945. Moved to USA c1966 to work for a hotel chain. Trick in La baguette magique. [Geni9/59]

name: Omah
bio: (Haltwhistle, England: 7 Aug 1889-) Stage name of Alf. L. Gregg. Pro since c1902 with pseudo-Oriental act in variety & at private parties. [WWM]

name: Omar Pasha
bio: (Russia: fl.1970s-90s) Pro illusionist. Lives in Germany, later France. With his touring troupe has played major theaters throughout world, including the Palladium in London, Madison Square Garden Felt Forum in New York in 1971, the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1984, France in 1987, & the Berlin Wintergarten in 1992. Pet effect: Indian Rope Trick. Specializes in Black Art effects. TV bit in Britain. [Fi2;Ran]

name: Onosaka, Ton
bio: (Takamatsu, Shikoku, Japan: 14 Apr 1933-) Stage name & childhood nickname of Azuma ONOSAKA. First interested in magic at age 10. Pro dealer ("Magic Land") in Tokyo since 1977. 1980 Tenkai Prize. Publishes the monthly Magic News & the quarterly Fushigi, the latter which he edited 1981-88. 1985 AMA Award of Merit. Founder-impresario of the annual Nihon Close-up Magic Grand Prix contest since 1984. Operates the 50-seat closeup & lecture Mini-Mini Theater in Tokyo 1988-present. A major figure on the Japanese magic scene as advisor to TV magic shows & convention organizer. Invented Lucky Lady, Tonte, etc. Wrote Onosaka Ton no Hon [The Book of Ton Onosaka] (1981). Articles in Magic News, etc. Illustrator of many books, articles, & instruction sheets. [LR1/97;Wh2]

name: Opawsky, Franz
bio: (Austria: 24 May 1929-) Pro in Baden. [Al]

name: Opel, [John Henry] "Harry
bio: (Limestone, New York: 29 Jan 1883-11 Mar 1955) Pro stage magician since 1900 & juggler. Toured the USA in vaudeville, fairs, & theaters. Then for several years gave mainly full-evening shows. Edited the unique The Voice from the Attic 1929-52 (46+ issues; repr 1982-83 by Bruce Dunn) & Fax 1939 (12 issues), each issue of both being a single handwritten copy sent to different friends. [Jinx#30]

name: Opp1, Martin
bio: (Germany: 7 Jul 1938-) Kid-show magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Opré
bio: (Holland: -1846) Pro master mechanic who built mechanical props & automata for Eliaser Bamberg (by 1790), Pinetti (by 1805), De Grisy (The Harlequin automaton by 1828), etc. Invented the Vaulting Figure automaton, which was bought by Eliaser Bamberg by 1790 & inherited in 1833 by his son, D.L. Bamberg, who soon gave it to his son, Tobias. Tobias Bamberg ..... Opré (or his son) was also a popular conjurer in Holland. In summer 1836 he performed in Belgium in Brussels & Liège with a Mme de Linsky with straight magic & his automata. [Hou,138-140;Bam,12-13;Sh]

name: Orben, Robert
bio: (New York City, NY: 4 Mar 1927-). Learned at age c13 from 10-year older brother who had learned from books. They would busk for money at East Coast mountain resorts. At age 18 his 1st job was for a year as demonstrator in Stuart Robson's magic shop in New York City c1945-46. Prolific author of patter books for magi, including The Encyclopedia of Patter (1946, 40pp), Magicdotes (1948, 44pp), Professional Patter (1950, 48pp), Flip Lines (1952, 50pp), & Sight Bits (1952, 40pp). His Comedy Technique (1951, 72pp) is a how-to book. Columns in Magic is Fun & Genii (since 1952, originally as "Mother Jongeleur"). Later in the 1950s turned toward writing comedy for general theatrical performers. Professional comedy writer for Jack Paar & Red Skelton; White House speech writer 1974-77. [CA;Se;Wh] Orchard, Tom(my Frank Thomas Henry) “The Amazing Orchanté” (Auckland, New Zealand: 13 September, 1943) Inspired at age of 10 after seeing “The Fun Doctor” (Norman Tate) perform at his school. As a teenager he taught himself magic, ventricroquism, hypnotism, fire-eating, sword swallowing and the bed of nails. Pro. stage and close-up performer since 1960. Performed all over New Zealand and Australia. Moved to the UK in 1985, and worked throughout Europe until emphysema forced him to retire in 1995. Appeared on UK TV “50 Greatest Magic Tricks,” Channel 4, 2002. 1988 Specialty Act of the Year, Disco and Club Trade International Awards, UK. 2002 Magic New Zealand Lifetime Achievement Award. 2007 Variety Club on NZ Scroll of Honour. Regular columnist for Magic New Zealand ezine for three years.

name: O'Rély
bio: (France: fl.1930s) Pen name of Louis Mercier. Wrote L'illusionniste moderne (1931).

name: Oriano
bio: (Bochówko, Poland: 1950- ) Stage name of Stanisław Czaja. Pro manipulator. Prize winner. [Mec]

name: Ormonde, Doctor
bio: (Kirkwall, Orkney: c1841-28 Jan 1902) Stage name of Andrew Garrioch Omond. Chemist. Then pro magician. Toured "La Belle Sunflower Coterie". Assistant to Signor Blitz Jr in Cincinnati. Toured Australia (1878), then India. Wrote How to Hypnotise (Edinburgh: 1891) & Mystery Unveiled: Anti-Spiritualistic Tricks, Lightning Calculations, and Memory Feats (Edinburgh: 1898, 180pp). [Daw2]

name: Ornson
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 10 Aug 1873- ) Stage name of Joseph P. Hogg. Pro with Black Art, illusions, juggling, & spiritualism. As the "Ornson Brothers", he worked with cousin John A. Zimmer, a juggler.

name: Ornum, G. M.
bio: See: Munro, George Mackenzie

name: Orrin, J[ames] F., MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1897-28 Apr 1976) Invented Milko (by 1922), the Spider Web Card (by 1932), & Ping Pong Trick (1957). Wrote The Conjurer's Vade Mecum [1922], Put It Over (1933, 200pp), On With The Show, Part II (1943), Cardboard, Glue, and Elastic (1946), etc.

name: Orsini, Fingers
bio:
Ortiz, Darwin [Joseph] [pronounced or-TEEZ] (S. Bronx, New York City, NY: 11 Dec 1948-) Learned at age 7 "as an offshoot of card playing & exposure to sleight of hand in street gambling." Pro card magician & professional gambler since leaving law school in 1973, specializing in close-up card magic & gambling exposés. Operated The Darwin Ortiz Gambling School in Manhattan 1979-82 when moved to Washington, DC. International consultant to casinos & police on gambling cheating methods. Wrote Gambling Scams (1984, 262pp), Darwin Ortiz on Casino Gambling (1986), Darwin Ortiz at the Card Table (1988, 163pp), The Annotated Erdnase (1991, 270pp), Strong Magic (1994, 380pp), & Card Shark (1995). Trick in Arcane. Video bit (1994). [Wat;Wh2]

[See also: "Perry, Vic"]

name: Orton, Carl
bio: See: Williams, C[arl] O[rton]

name: Osborn, Norm[an A.]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1928-20 Sep 2001) Learned in 1939 from uncle who taught him a few tricks. Ran (with Gene Thomas) a small magic manufacturing firm ("O'Lantern Magic"), making glass props for Berland. Part-time pro close-up & platform work 1976 to 1988 when went full-time. Specializes in card magic. Later (1989) rans a small mail-order book business ("Magic Book House") in Park City, Illinois. Invented the Double Count, a false count with cards. Wrote Unlimited (1953, 30pp; 2nd ed revised with Ed Marlo, 1983, 45pp). Tricks in Linking Ring, Hade-E-Gram, Ireland's Year Book, & Ibidem. [Wh2]

name: Osborne, Paul [Ferris]
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 5 Jan 1948-) Learned at age 5 when Mark Wilson gave him a magic set. Pro illusionist & illusion designer since 1955. 1962 TAOM Stage Award. 1967 TAOM Club Act Trophy. Proprietor of Illusion Systems in Dallas, Texas, since 1979. Invented several illusions. Wrote Illusion Systems (4 vols, 1975-85) & Illusions (1995, 190pp). Illusion column in Genii 1979-present. [LR8/96;Wat;Wh2]

name: Osborne, [Thomas James] "Tom
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 3 Dec 1901-17 Apr 1963) Pro close-up, including many original effects. Worked clubs & private shows. Jack Gwynne Trophy 1937. Invented Razz-A-Ma-Tazz 4-card discovery (by 1947). NOTE: Often miscredited since 1936 with Carl-Lyle's 3-to-1 Rope Trick, which Osborne merely marketed since 1936. Wrote Cups and Balls Magic (1937, 58pp; repr 1973), Three Shell Games (1938, 58pp), 3 to 1 Rope Trick (1938, 14pp), Fun at Dinner with Napkin Folds (1943, 38pp), Coin Tricks (1945, 30pp), Napkin Folding (1945), Shower of Sweets (1945), & Poker Demonstration (1946, 16pp). Tricks in Jinx & Phoenix. [Th;Ho;HMM11/53]

name: Oscarelli
bio: See: Rey, Oscar

name: Ose, Jay [pronounced OH-see]
bio:
(Minneapolis, Minnesota: Nov 1911-5 Nov 1967) Norwegian parentage. Pro close-up. First Host and Resident Magician at the Magic Castle 1963-66. Was technical adviser on Hollywood film The Cincinnati Kid (1965) and had bit parts in Waterhole #3 (1967) & The Flim-Flam Man (1967). TV bits. [Mag] "Osey, N." NOTE: Pseudonym used by Houdini in writing as overseas correspondent for Mahatma.

[See also: Van Barren, Hans Johan, MD]

name: O'Shan
bio: (Gourin, Morbihan, France: 3 Jul 1926-) Stage name of Yves Chanot. Learned at age 9. Promentalist-illusionist since 1947. Specialized in 2-person mindreading act with wife Huguette ("Naga") since 1951. Called "our 'French' Goldstein" by Jean Merlin. Honorary President of Mindon Mania 1989-present. AFAP Master Magician. Member of American Society for Psychical Research. Collector (c400 books on mentalism & c600 on general magic). Articles in Arcane, Mad Magic, Cahiers de la Magie, & in books by Dif, Robelly, etc. TV & radio bits in many countries. [Dif;Bou;Wh2]

name: O'Shaughnessey, Dick
bio: (USA: c1917-23 Jan 1991) Pro night club magician. Aka "Mr. Magic Man". Active in USO tours abroad. A regular at The Mint in Las Vegas & the Mogambo in Hollywood. TV bits with Ed Sullivan Show & Tonight Show. Died in Arcadia, California.

name: Osmann, Alexander
bio: (North Africa?: fl.1870s) Pro. A "man of colour", billed as "The African Wizard" in London 1871-73 as A. Herrmann's assistant at Egyptian Hall where he also worked single at matinees. Also worked single at the Royal Polytechnic. [CI] "Osodrac" SEE: Barbas Cardoso, João Maria “Osram, The Man of Multiple Mysteries” SEE: Austin, A. Everett “Chick”

name: Osterlind, Richard J[oseph] "RJ
bio: (Bridgeport, Connecticut: 6 Mar 1948- ) Learned at age 7 from local magic shop & Vic Lawston catalog. Pro mentalism & challenge magic since 1974, originally as "Dorien", later under own name. Pet effects: Linking Finger Rings & Center Tear. Invented Ultra Board (1982), Breakthrough Card System (1983), Two Faced (1984), Change of Mind (1985), Industrial Strength Link (1986), Imp Pad (1986), Epitome Board (1987), Out of Hand (1987), Radar Deck (1990). Wrote several booklets (most with Jeff Busby): Two Perfected Professional Routines (1983, 19pp), Breakthrough Card System (1983, 9pp), Three Miracle Routines (1986, 40pp), The Surrounded Slow-Motion Center Tear (1986, 27pp), The Blindfold Book (1987), Rich with a Twist (1989), The Challenge Signed Torn and Restored Newspaper (forthcoming 1989), Thought Scan (1992, 28pp), SeaFire Sequence (1995, 39pp). Articles in Epoptica. [Wh2]

name: Ostin, Bob
bio: (Liverpool, England:  $ 23^{rd} $ Sep 1929 –  $ 15^{th} $ May 2013) Stage name of Robert W. Arkley. Semi-pro close-up in clubs & at kid-shows. Won British Ring close-up competition. Invented Dice Prediction (1953), Spooky Dice, Beam Shot = Laser Beam (1969), & Submarine Card. Wrote Fingertip Fantasies (1968, 88pp). Tricks in Abra, New Pentagram, Linking Ring, Magigram, New Talon, Genii, etc. Audio.

name: Oswald, Charles
bio: See: Williams, C[harles] O[swald]

name: Oswald, Oscar, MIMC
bio: (England: 26 Mar 1904-Jul 1976) Stage name of Cuthbert Alfred Games Quantrill. Became interested in magic in 1915. London policeman & gaoler. Then pro kid-show magician, vent, & Punch & Judy worker. Pet effects: The Rings, Thumb Tie, Pretty Polly, & Troublewit. Dealer (Magical Mart, etc) in London 1949-76 when bought out by John Styles. Edited Magical Digest 1949-59 as house organ.

name: Ottilidio
bio: See: Teale, Oscar S.

name: Otto, Adolph
bio: (Germany: fl.1880s-90s) Pro expert prop maker in Neubukow, Mecklenburg. Wrote Anleitung zur Ausübung der modernen Salon-Magie für Dilitanten und Künstler (1891, 20pp) & Vortrag zur I-V Zauber-Soiree (c1890, 5 parts, 8pp each).

name: Otto. Arthur
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Ran a small magic shop ("Arthur Otto's") in London c1894-c1905. Wrote The Beginner's Guide to Conjuring (nd [by 1910], 61pp). [Daw94]

name: Otto, Greg
bio: (Canada: fl.1970s-90s) Learned magic by age 7. Pro magician. TV actor-comedian (on the Bob Newhart Show, etc). Now pro stand-up comedian & semi-pro magician, playing such venues as Magic Castle & Magic Island (Balboa Island). [Mag]

name: Otto, Harry
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 12 May 1881-) Joined circus at age 13. Pro comedy magician by 1915 as “Public Deceiver”. Around that time he married Lida Butterworth, the mother of Howard Thurston's 1st wife (Grace). Retired to run a print shop in Kansas City by the 1950s. [LR6/69]

name: Otwinowski, Wojciech
bio: (Poland: -May 1978) Magician as "Wojtek-Plastyk". His show was titled "Czarodziejska Kreska". Died in Lódź, Poland.

name: Oudini
bio: (USA?: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Pen name as deliberate play on the famous Houdini. Wrote Secrets of the Great Mysteries (1909, 60pp), a knowledgeable popular exposé of Houdini's escapology tricks. Robert Doidge bought up many copies to keep these secrets within the magic trade.

name: Ouellet, Gary [Q.], QC
bio: (Quebec, Canada: 9 Jan 1945-7 Jun 2002) French-Canadian. Inspired by and learned magic from a Gilbert magic set at age 6 (or 8?). Lawyer, living in Quebec & working mainly in Ottawa as CEO of main government relations firm in Canada. Semi-pro magician, specializing in close-up. Consultant to several stage magicians. Long-time translator for Tenyo Company, as that Japanese firm's North American magic consultant. Partner with Guy Camirand since 1979 in the Camirand Academy of Magic. 1989 FFFF Roastee. Died of sudden heart attack. Wrote 11 booklets, including Meir Yedid's Incredible Close-Up Magic (1982), Eric DeCamps Coin Connection (1987), The Class Act of Tony Binarelli (1991), & The Silver Passage (26pp), plus 2 books, Close Up Illusions (1990, 350pp) & The Pass (1994, 138pp). Articles in Genii & Apocalypse. Videos. [Bo3;Wh2]

name: Ourada, Josef
bio: (Havlovice, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 5 Dec 1914- ) Dealer ("Magické Studio") in Karlovy Vary, Czechoslovakia. In 1966 founded the annual Karlovy Vary Magic Festival, which he has directed since. Founding President of the Ceský Magický Svaz [Czech Union of Magicians] 1969-82 & its Honorary President since 1982. Director of Moderní Magie since 1970. [Mec]

name: Oursler, [Charles] Fulton
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 22 Jan 1893-24 May 1952) Aka "Samri Frikell", "Sandalwood", & "Anthony Abbot". Inspired at age 6 seeing a magician do Wine & Water and pull a rabbit from hat. Learned by lessons from Eugene Polley ("The Great LeClaire"). Mystery writer (as "Anthony Abbot") of 13 novels; and editor of Liberty 1931-42 & Reader's Digest 1944. Although not an alcoholic he was active in Alcoholics Anonymous since 1939. Semi-pro magician. Died of a heart attack. Tricks in Eagle Magician. Wrote Spirit Mediums Exposed (1930, 96pp, as "Samri Frikell"); and The Spider (1927), a play about a magician, which became movies in 1931 & 1945. Wrote pamphlets for Thurston. His novel of Jesus, The Greatest Story Ever Told (1949), was a world-wide bestseller. [WWWA; CA]

name: Ovette, Joseph "Joe
bio: (Naples, Italy: 20 Jan 1885-24 Jul 1946) Stage name of Giuseppe Joseph Olivo, billed as "Magical Ovette" & "The Great Ovette". Brought to New York City at age 3. Pro fire-eater turned magician at age 12 with Kickapoo Medicine Show. In WW I entertained troops near the front. After 1919 toured USA & Canada, working fairs, vaudeville, & his own show. Also did a pseudo-Chinese act as "Lung Chang Yen" & a mind-reading act as "Mar-Jah". Moved to Canada. Worked with assistant-wife Frances. Dealer (Treasure Magic) in Cornwall, Ontario, with 1927 catalog (50pp). Died of throat cancer in a Buffalo hospital. His collection of magic books was acquired by Lloyd Jones. Invented the Master Move = Kelly Bottom Placement by 1927. Edited Echo 1932-35 (16 issues). Co-edited "Hocus Pocus Parade" in Linking Ring 1941-42. Wrote Magician's New Field (1916, 30pp), Trickery Tricks (1917, 24pp), Advanced Magic (60pp), Practical Telepathy, Publicity Miracles (1928), Eggstraordinary Ways of Egghibiting with Eggs (1932, 36pp), Tricks and Illusionettes (1944, 31pp; repr 1952), Miraculous Hindu Feats (1947, 15pp), Fast Ones (1952; repr 1971, 31pp), & The Gambler's Paradise (12pp). Articles in magic magazines.

name: Owen, Anthony
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Pro. Edited The Dungeon (1993-95), The Magicians' Yearbook (1996-98), The Young Magician (1996-present), & The Magic Circular (1998-present), 2 videos. [LR11/2000 1-man Parade]

name: Owen, Carl [Paul LeRoy]
bio: (Panama, Shelby County, Iowa: 22 Aug 1889-10 May 1975) 7th child of a farmer of Welsh descent. A woodworker who entered magic in 1913 when went to work for Thayers' "The Magic Shop of the West" in Los Angeles. Pro magic builder & dealer, founding Owen Magic in 1933 until sold in 1963 to Les Smith, although he continued to work there until his death. Invented Dr. Q Slates in 1917; probably invented the Monster Guillotine (late 1920s); and probably invented the Flash Appearance Portal (by 1928). 1968 AMA Special Award Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Bio is Richard Buffum, "Keep the wheels turning ..." (1977, 303pp).

name: Owen, [Henry] Emmett
bio: (Panama, Shelby County, Iowa: 1891-1955) Younger brother of Carl Owen whom he joined as a woodworker at Thayer's in 1919. Co-owner (with Carl) of Owen Brothers, later Owen Magic Supreme, 1933 until his death.

name: O'Williams
bio:
Öye, Ragnar (Norway: 30 Aug 1896-) Amateur magician in Oslo. In 1928 co-founded (with Iversen & Nordnes) the Norwegian Magic Circle & its President 1948-49. [St]

[See also: Clément, Guillaume]

name: Ozanam, Jacques
bio: (Bouligneux, Ain, France: 1640-17 Apr 1717) Studied for the priesthood but became a mathematician. This non-magician wrote Recréatifs mathématiques et physiques (1693), which went through several editions, the last being in 1790. English tr as Recreations Mathematical and Physical (1703). Of its 12 sections, the last covers conjuring, beginning with a full description of the Cups & Balls routine followed by 48 minor tricks with cards, coins, etc. The author was admitted to L'Académie Royale des Sciences in 1701. [Dif] "Pablo, The Great" SEE: "Chang"

name: Page, Dr. Byrd
bio: (England: 1853 [sic]-10 May 1916) Stage name of Frederick Richard Broadbridge. A top pro society drawing-room & concert comedy manipulator in London. Affectionately called “The Doctor”. [Vo56;Cl;HMM3/52]

name: Page, Patrick "Pat
bio: (Scotland: 17 Mar 1929 - 11 Feb 2010) Inspired by & learned from a second-hand Goldston book. Demonstrator for Davenport's magic shop in London. Pro close-up since c1952 & dealer. International performer, lecturer, innovator, & writer. Created "Sound of Magic" and "Trick-a-Tape" line of audio recordings. Big admirer of Al Flosso. Wrote Bell's Magic Book (1973, 140pp), Bell's Book of Tricks (1974, 121pp), The Big Book of Magic (1976, 235pp), Magic by Gosh (1985, 149pp, with Albert Goshman), The Pull Book (1987, 54pp), How to Entertain Children with a Glove Puppet (1990, 42pp), etc. Articles in Club 71. Audios & 2 videos (1984, 1985).

name: Page, Robert Allan "Bob
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 6 Sep 1921- ) At age 9 inspired seeing Thurston & started reading books. Printing estimator. Amateur close-up magician. Invented Page Transform (a math principle), Weight Your Thought (window reader cards), & Business Card Paradox. Tricks in Pallbearers Review. [Wh2]

name: Paine, H. S.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-1940s?) Machinist. Made the first Walsh Canes in the late 1920s for Russ Walsh. Next or next to last owner of the Chicago Magic Company, which Ralph Read had begun in 1912.

name: Paini, Dario
bio: (Trieste, South Tirol, Italy: 7 Nov 1867-12 Oct [sic] 1935) Of Italian parentage. Pro stage card magician. Pet effects: Card Stab & knotted silks. Invented several card tricks, including reportedly the Card Stab. Introduced card tricks to the German stage, according to Reinhold Müller. German citizen since 1904. A teacher of Graziadei. Died in Bad Salzelmen (now Straßfurt). [St;Zm;Vo57;Nad]

name: Pair, Pierre
bio: (Hungary: 1894-13 Jul 1934) Painter. Semi-pro magician with small tricks & illusions. Lived many years in Paris. Died in Budapest.

name: Palanca y Lita, Ricardo
bio: (Spain: fl.1870s-80s) Translated Robert-Houdin's Les Tricheries des Grecs as Secretos de los Garitos (Valencia: 1879; reprinted 1879 & 1911). Wrote El moderno prestidigitador (Valencia: 1887; 2nd ed 1900).

name: Palatine, Highman
bio: (Italy: -1791) Minor pro. Played Paris in 1753. Moved to England in 1763. Played Paris in 1777. In 1788 in London lost a magic competition with M. Boulevard. Pet effect: cut-&-restored sleeve ruffle. Died in England. [Cl;Dif]

name: Palen, Joseph J. "Joe
bio: (USA: c1911-26 Aug 1984) Lived in Chicago. Known for his fine performance of "Eclipse" with Peter Tappan. [LR10/84]

name: Palermo
bio: See: Chefalo, Magdalena

name: Palfreyman, John [Victor], MIMC
bio: (Millbrook, Cheshire, England: 22 Oct 1925-) Learned in 1933 from reading & Xmas gift tricks. Electrical engineer. Semi-pro kid-show & cabaret magician since 1941 & MC since 1968. Illusion builder for David Nixon, Tommy Cooper, & TV shows. Dealer in unusual & rare props. Collector (over 2,000 books, stage money ads, coins & tokens). Invented Looping Rope Laces (1941), etc. British Ring President 2000-01. Wrote Magic in a Game & many lecture notes. Articles in Magiram, Abra, MUM, & Magic Circular. [LR3/2001;Wh2]

name: Palladino, Eusapia
bio: (Minerverno Murge, Bari, Italy: 21 Jan 1854-16 May 1918) Famous pseudo-psychic. Former wife of a magician. See Hereward Carrington, Eusapia Palladino and Her Phenomena (1909).

name: Pallme, Herman
bio: (London, England: 3 Jul 1869-1924) Learned assisting uncle A. Herrmann. Moved to USA in 1889. Took stage name "Herrmann" after his boss's death in 1896. Wrote Entertaining by Magic (1906, 63pp; repr 1910). [CI]

name: Palmer, Bill, AIMC
bio: (Houston, Texas: 25 Jul 1942- ) Stage name of Willard Aldrich Palmer III. Pro entertainer since age 18, first as musician, then as magician. Works Renaissance Faires (as "Merlin", which was also his CB Simulator handle on Micro MagiCon, of which he was a charter member), Magic Island, etc, in Huston area. Performs everything from closeup to illusions. Wrote A Guide for the Texas Renaissance Festival Performer (1980, 64pp), Think Magic! (1980, 37pp), The Early History of the Paddle Trick (2nd ed, 1994, 26pp), etc. Translator of German books by Punx, Lubor Fiedler, & Ted Lesley. German instruction sheets for Stevens Magic Emporium. [WWE;Wh2]

name: Palmer, Gloria
bio: See: Marcom, Gloria

name: Palmer, Jay
bio: (Nashville, Tennessee: 1 Nov 1899-1970) Stage name of William J. "Willie" Burns. Learned assisting Houdini & Leon (1922). Pro. As "Palmer & Doreen" (his Liverpoolian partner-wife) toured the world with "The Magic Kettle" act, their pet effect. In WW II in US Army Special Services entertaining troops in England, France, Germany, & Far East. FISM 1st prizes in comedy magic (with "Doreen") 1950, 1951. USO tours in early 1950s. Played the Palladium in London c1955. President, Magicians Guild of America, 1954. Toured Europe in 1958. [St; Lau; Sphinx4/51]

name: Palmer, Johnny "Ace
bio: (Warren, Ohio: 2 Aug 1960- ) Learned 1st card trick at age 4 from father. BA from Kent State U with major in theater & minor in psychology. Pro close-up plus some illusions. Lives in Huntington Beach, California. 1983 IBM Gold Cups award; 1985 FISM 2nd prize in close-up; 1988 AMA Best Close-Up Magician; 1996 AMA Lecturer of the Year. TV bits. [LR4/98;Bo#256;Jef]

name: Palmer, [Thomas S.] "Tom
bio: (Cheyenne, Wyoming: 22 May 1925-22 Dec 1991) Born Timothy McGuire & legally rechristened Thomas Stewart Palmer in his first year by his foster parents. Learned at age 8 from a magic set. Pro comedy magic & illusionist (as Tom Palmer) 1950s-early 70s. Married 1947-64 to Gloria Jacobsen (now Gloria Marcom) for whom he designed her "Vampira" act in 1960. Invented Satan's Seat illusion by 1959. Won 7 TAOM awards (the record) 1959-63. Took Antonio C. Andruzzi as alternate legal name since 1970. Switched to bizarre magick (as "Tony Andruzzi", "Masklyn ye Mage", & "Daemon Ecks"). Edited New Invocation 1981-1990. In 1984 founded the Invocational, the annual conclave of bizarrists, which he hosted until 1990. Wrote Modern Illusions (1959, 40pp), The Tie Pitch (1960, 12pp), ghosted Gloria Palmer's The Vampira Act (1960, 20pp), The Famous Flea Act (1962), Cagey Doves (1962; repr 1968), & The Comedy Act of and by Tom Palmer (1969, 47pp), all under original name. Then, writing as Masklyn ye Mage, The Negromicon of Masklyn ye Mage (1977), The Grimoire of the Mages (1978), Daemon's Diary (1980), & The Legendary Scroll of Masklyn ye Mage (1982). Articles in Sphinx, Tops, Genii, Magick, Dope Sheet, Invocation, & New Invocation. Video (1988). [LR3/92; Wat;Wh2]

name: Pan, Peter
bio: See: Hurwitz, Abraham

name: Pan Zero
bio: (Lauenburg, Germany [now Lebork, Poland]: 26 May 1919-9 Feb 1981) Stage name of Rudolf K. Panzer. Interested as a child. Merchant. Then, after 1962, pro illusionist in West Germany. 1967 FISM 3rd [sic] prize for grand illusion. World tour in 1970 included Japan & the Paris Olympia. Died in his home town. [Win;Mec]

name: Pancrazi, E.
bio: (France: 1940s-80s) Resident of Paris. Amateur. Aka "Pancrazy". AFAP President 1955-58. AFAP Gold Medal 1975.

name: Panda, Paula
bio: (Amarillo, Texas: fl.1970s-80s) Originally a stock-company actress, learned magic as a mentalist's assistant. Thence as "Sabrina" a single act with mentalism & hypnotism. Since 1976 as "Alexandra", a magicienne. [MM10/81]

name: Pang Sue Foon
bio: See: "Alma, The Mysterious"

name: Pankratz Dr Loren D., PhD
bio: (Portland, Oregon: 27 Feb 1940- ) Psychologist with the VA Medical Center in Portland from c1970 until recently going into private practice. Although had a magic set as kid, did not take up magic seriously until c1974 when he met Jerry Andrus. Amateur magic historian. Articles in Magick, Magicol, Linking Ring, Genii, & MUM. Also studies con artists, particularly those who deceive psychologists. [Wh]

name: Pannain, Remo
bio: (Rome, Italy: 2 May 1961- ) Learned in 1969 from a magic set. Lawyer. Amateur magician since 1972 with close-up & cabaret. Pet effects: 6 Card Repeat, Linking Rubber Bands, Deck in the Balloon. Wrote II Falso Pollice (1988, 25pp) & Le Palline di Spugna (1990, 20pp). Tricks in Qui Magia, Magia Moderna, II Mago, Inoltre, etc. 1989 AFAP 2nd prize in close-up. [Wh5]

name: Pantar, Hans
bio: (Landsweiler, Germany: 12 Jul 1955-) Stage name of Hans Moretti Jr. Son of Hans Moretti and elder brother of Peter Moretti. Escape artist & death-defying acts such as his version of Russian Roulette with crossbows. Worked Las Vegas (Bally's Casino) in the late 1980s with his American-born assistant-wife Maureen.

name: Pantel-Patrix
bio: (Insterburg [now Tschernachowsk], Germany: 27 Jun 1894-20 Jan 1967) Stage name of Benno Pantel, aka "Patrix". Watchmaker. Semi-pro comedy magician. Salesman for Horster's in Berlin c1919-25. Thence toured Germany. Invented many tricks sold by Horster, Bartl, & other dealers. Died in Birkland/ Oberbayern. [St]

name: Panzer, Rio
bio: (Germany: 22 Apr 1888-18 May 1983) Stage name of Peter Bäumchen. [Roh]

name: Paraszkiewicz, Henryk
bio: (Suwałki, Poland: 1939- ) Amateur illusionist & manipulator. Aka "Henrico-Magico". 1982 Łódź laureate for comedy act. [Mec]

name: Parizet, Sieur
bio: (France: fl.1820s) Student of Fitz James. Promagician & ventriloquist. Pet effect: Bullet Catching. [Dif]

name: Park, Andrew
bio: (Honolulu, Hawaii: 8 Nov 1918-1991) 2nd generation Hawaiian of Korean father & Franco-Portuguese mother. Inspired at age 6 seeing carnival side-show magicians & then Long Tack Sam. Pro (self-taught) with sleights, some illusions, & table-hopping in nightclubs. With John Calvert show touring the USA 1937-40. Dealer-teacher (Island Studio of Magic) since 1942, Tenkai being his best customer in WW II. In USO until 1947. Billed as "Hawaii's Prince of Magic". Later worked only private parties. [Wh2]

name: Parkinson, Reg
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Amateur. Wrote Denise: Prestidigitateur and Illusionist (1985?) & Myron Carruthers: A Magician and Gentleman (1986).

name: Parker, Al
bio: (Belgium: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Alphonse Luyten. Adopted son of Jean Arnolis. Ex-dancer. Postman in Brussels. Semi-pro magic, paper tearing, & balloon sculpture. NOTE: Not to be confused with the American AI Parker. [Dif]

name: Parker, Larry
bio: (England: fl.1960s-80s) Pro comedy magician. [Wit]

name: Parker, Prof. Francis
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 28 Oct 1892-Jan 1934) Stage name of M. Gollhofer. Amateur. [Go2]

name: Parr, David
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 12 Oct 1963-) Pro with close-up, parlor, mentalism, bizarre magic, & séance magic Video reviewer for Genii (1995-97). Wrote Brain Food (1998, 135pp). Tricks in Linking Ring, Magic Menu, & New Invocation. [Wh01]

name: Parrish [Jr], Robert [Harkness] "Bob
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 26 Dec 1918-4 Mar 1994) Inspired at age 12 seeing Gerald Heaney at school & learned from library books. Public relations & writer. Semi-pro mentalist since 1934. Moved to Chicago in 1937. Won the IBM's Coke Cecil Trophy in 1940 at his first magic convention. US Army 1942-46. Editor Magico/1988-death. Prolific author. Wrote You'd Be Surprised (1938, 65pp, with John Goodrum), Do That Again! (1939, 76pp, with Oscar Weigle), For Magicians Only (1944, 121pp; repr 1946), New Ways to Mystify (1945, 124pp), The Magician's Handbook (1958, 240pp, being a combined reprint of For Magicians Only & New Ways to Mystify), Words About Wizards (1994, 55pp), plus ghosted last 3 booklets of Rufus Steele. Also wrote or co-authored books on George Boston, Bert Allerton, Tenkai, & Charlie Miller, which see. Articles in Dragon, Jinx, Sphinx, Linking Ring, Abra, MUM, New Tops, Pallbearers (1 all-Parrish issue), Yankee Magic Collector, etc. [St;Wh2]

name: Partagas
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 15 Sep 1848-28 Dec 1931). Stage name of Don Joaquin PARTAGAS JAQUET. Pro since 1879. Dealer in Barcelona since 1881 when he opened "El Rey de la Magia", Spain's first magic shop. Invented Partagas Sell=Dunbury Delusion, which he taught to Victor Farelli c1908. Wrote El prestidigitador Optimus (n.d.) & Magia Espectral. After his death his shop passed to Carlos Bucheli and remains open today. [Xe;St] Pasha NOTE: Turkish title indicating a man of high rank or office. Magicians who have adopted this include "Gogia Pasha" & "Omar Pasha". They will thus be found here under the names Gogia & Omar.

name: Pasqua, Gianni
bio: See: "Roxy"

name: Pasquini, Luigi
bio: (Bologna, Italy: 5 Dec 1948-) Optician. Learned magic in 1982. Semi-pro in general magic since 1987. Pet effect: doves. Several prizes since 1986 in Italy, Austria, & France. [Wh5]

name: Passo
bio: (Poland?: 1876-1947) Stage name of Pavel Alexsieevich Sokolov. Pro illusionist, manipulator, puppeteer. [Mec]

name: Pastor, [Antonio] "Tony
bio: (New York City, NY: 28 May 1832-26 [sic] Aug 1908) A pioneer impresario of variety & vaudeville. Began working for Barnum. Opened his own 1st concert saloon, Tony Pastor's Opera House, in 1865 & his last, the Fourteenth Street Theatre, in 1881. [Lau]

name: Paterson, John
bio: (Canada: fl.1970s-80s) Pro, working with assistant "Pandora" (Maureen) since 1972. Manager of the short-lived Vancouver branch of Micky Hades International since c1983. Articles. [Mag]

name: Patrice, Mdle.
bio: (England: fl.1880s-1910s) Stage name of Patrice (Mrs C. Lang) Neil. Of French ancestry. Taught by Trewey & Bertram. Pro sleight-of-hand. Tricks in Magician Monthly 1911-12, making her one of earliest female magic writers. See E. Dawes, "Mademoiselle Patrice -- Lang Neil's Vanishing Lady", Magic Circular, V.74 (1980), 107-109. [Mar;Dif]

name: Patrice, Madame
bio: See: Dawes, Amy

name: Patrick, Jo
bio: (France: 6 May 1943-) Stage name of Jean-Pierre Constant [sic]. 1973 FISM 2nd prize for illusion; 1976 FISM 2nd prize for mentalism. Dealer (Jo Patrick-Fairyland's).

name: Patrick, Stephen R.
bio: (USA: 28 Dec 1907-) Amateur magic book & magazine collector in Fairport Harbor, Ohio, since 1930s. Edited-published The Spotlight 1940-60 (3 issues) & The Magical Bookie 1960-74 (48 issues).

name: Patrix
bio: See: "Pantel-Patrix"

name: Patrizio, Ernesto
bio: (Savigliano, Piedmont, Italy: 1840-1896) Stage name of Ernesto Patrizio di Castiglione Scagnetto. In mid-1860s toured Italy with partner Zanarelli. On own played Turin (1867), Switzerland, Belgium, Paris (1875), Italy (1876), Spain (1876), Portugal (1876), Mexico, USA (1878), Spain (1882). From c1883 to c1886 he made a money-losing tour with (D'Alvini as assistant) of South America (including Brazil) & the West Indies (including Cuba). Pet effect: Cannon-Ball Catching. His wife Rita Gail Patrizio acted as assistant & worked a giant memory act (by 1878 in USA). Died in Barcelona in poverty. [Sil;Dif;Pr;St;Mo]

name: Patry Jr, John [Joseph]
bio: (New Haven, Connecticut: 18 Aug 1972-14 Nov 1993) Taught 1979-84 by retired pro father. Firefighter/paramedic in West Haven. Semi-pro close-up & stage magician since age 7. Invented Rising Force (1990), Penetrusion (1990), Total Neurosis (1990), Artist Nightmare (1991), etc. Founded Patry Magic Productions in 1987, which had 6 employees. Wrote The Magic of John Patry, Jr. (1991, 130pp). Articles in Top Hat & MUM. [Wh5]

name: Patten, Dennis [Samuel George], MIMC
bio: (London, England: 12 Nov 1932- ) Learned at age 11 from sister's book, Goldston's Young Conjurer. Illustrator of magic works since 1954. Pro since 1958 with magic, vent, & Punch. Art Editor Gen 1958-68 & Magic Info 1972-c81. Editor Magic Info c1981-present. Articles in Magic Magazine, Gen, & Magic Info. Illustrated many magic catalogs & some 22 books. 1991 John Nevil Maskelyne Prize as magical illustrator. [Wh2]

name: Patterson, [Edward] "Edd
bio: (Red Bank, New Jersey: 30 Sep 1920-) Inspired seeing magician do the Thumb Tie & visiting S.S. Adams factory. At age 17 was assistant to Don Rose. Pro, mainly doing school shows, originally with full-stage show with assistant-wife Virginia (married in 1941). Has done over 17,000 school shows with magic, chalk drawing, & talking animal puppets. See William V. Rauscher, Edd Patterson Presents The Art of Magic, The Magic of Art (1990, 80pp). [LR8/91;Wh2]

name: Patterson [Jr], [Julius Gustavius] "Pat
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-60s) Former stage manager to Virgil & McDonald Birch. Pro magician. Did spook shows in 1950s as "Don Brandon", "Kara-Kum", & "Dr. Zorka". Made low-budget horror films in 1960s, including Body Shop, A Taste of Blood, & Three on a Meathook. [Walk2]

name: Patton, [James Michael] "Jim
bio: (Fullerton, California: 10 Aug 1940- ) Learned from public library books during junior high school. Debut in high school with manip stage act. US Army Intelligence in Germany 1962-65. Sales management to pro close-up magic in early 1970s. Demoed at The Magic Corner magic shop in Hollywood in 1976. Frequent performer at Magic Castle where he was a bartender 1985-c1991 and again in 2005. MIMC.. Wrote (with Ron Vergilio) A Visit with Larry Jennings (1982, 8pp). Articles in Apocalypse, Precursor, Richard's Almanac, etc. Ghosted Miller's "Magicana" column in Genii c1986-1988 & by-lined it 1988-92. [Mag;Wh]

name: Paufler, Herbert Martin
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 23 Nov 1908- ) Engineer. Amateur magician in East Germany. Inventor of hundreds of mechanical & electronic props, which he built for himself & other magicians including Widano. Wrote Paufler-Skriptum (1961), Wadimow und seine Bücher (1963), & Magie, Magnete und Motoren (1963). Articles in Zauberkunst & Magie. Awarded the "Dr Teumer-Ring" 1965 & 1970-72. A biography by Peter Rückert was published in German in 1992. [Mec]

name: Paul, Bill
bio: (Canada: fl.1950s-60s) Invented Fraidy-Cat Rabbit. Modified it jointly with dealer Gene Gordon who suggested the black-to-white fright-change plot. First marketed in 1953 through Gordon's Magic Shop, Paul personally making over 4,000 copies. Thence widely pirated.

name: Paul, John "Johnny
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 15 Jan 1912-31 [sic] Aug 1991) Born John Paul Zielinski Jr. Around age 18 legally changed to John Paul. Began as a juggler. Learned magic as young man by tuition from Jim Sherman at National Magic House in Chicago. Ex-juggler. Pro close-up since mid-1930s. Worked the LaSalle Hotel's Gay Nineties Lounge c1936-1947. Owner & bartender-magician of Johnny Paul's Lounge in Chicago (Cicero) 1947-1959 when moved to Los Angeles area where he ran 2 supper clubs. Resident magician at Showboat Hotel in Las Vegas from 1962 until retired in 1990. 2 videos (1986). [Fi;HC;Wat;Wh]

name: Paul, Paula
bio: (USA: 1954-) Stage name of Paula Slape. Pro magicienne. [Ran]

name: Paul, Sam[uel] O.
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 28 Jun 1880-) Aka "Paul the American Magician". Learned magic in 1910. Pro since 1920. [Dor]

name: Pauline
bio: (USA: -11 Nov 1942) Stage name of Joe Poulin. Pro stage hypnotist since 1909, having learned as a stooge for Herbert Flint & Philip McEwen. A vaudeville star. Played the London Palladium in 1912 & the New York Hippodrome twice in 1928. [Pr;Lau]

name: Paulmier
bio: (France: fl.1780s-90s) Pro. Active in France 1789-98. In 1798 played the Théâtre Bleuettes Comiques in Paris with sleight-of-hand & tricks based on physics.

name: Paullini, Antonio
bio: (Germany: fl.1710s) Pen name of Johann Jakob Schmauss. Wrote Curieuses Cabinet Ausländisches und anderer Merkwürdigkeiten (Frankfurt & Leipzig: 1717), which includes material on Indian conjurors with their Mango Tree & Basket tricks, etc. [St]

name: Paulsen, Oscar H.
bio: (East London, South Africa: 2 Feb 1899-28 Dec 1980) Semi-pro comedy act. Former IBM British Ring President. [Go2]

name: Pavel
bio: (Opolany, Prague, Czechoslovakia: 4 Apr 1945 – 9 Feb 2011) Stage name of Pavel Lubomir "Paul" Pomezny. Learned at age 9. Debut at age 10. Foreign trade specialist at U of Prague. Semi-pro general magic & inventor. 1966 Concours Magicus (Paris) for invention. Moved to Switzerland in 1969 when he became full-time pro. Marketed his original tricks as "Pavel's Topmagic" since 1971. Dealer (Studio de Magie) in Geneva 1977-present. 1982 FISM 1st prize for invention (his Walking Knot). Many lecture tours since 1967 in USA (8 times), Germany, Portugal, France, England, & Japan. Invented some 900 effects, including Walking Knot (1982). Wrote as "Pavel" Wie entwickle ich einen neuen Trick? (1964, with Mila Trinka); Zwei Dutzend und Eine Neuheit (1965, with Josef Manas); La Magie de Pavel (1969), English ed by Peter Warlock as The Magic of Pavel (1971); 10 Nouveaux Tours de Pavel (6 vols, 1969-77), Pavel's 15 Micro Tricks (1971), plus several lecture notes in German, French, & English. Articles in most major journals since 1966, including Swami. 3 videos. Many TV bits, including the Ed Sullivan show in 1968. [J. de la Prestidigitation11/76; Magigram8/72; Wh2]

name: Paviato, Aurelio [Carlo]
bio: (Vigevano, Pavia, Italy: 22 Dec 1958-) Pro magician (close-up, parlour & platform) since 1978. 1982 FISM 1st prize (tied with Ammar) for close-up. Member of the Spanish Magic School (Escuela Mágica de Madrid) since 1980. Has performed for Italian national TV. Wrote Impromptu Reverse Matrix (1982, 10pp). Carte & Monete...e altri artifici (174 pp, Florence Art Edizioni, 2007); Contributions to Magia & Gibeciére. [Wh5]

name: Pavlik, Rudolf
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 1922-1970) Pro illusionist. Founded the post-WW II Prague Magic Club. [Mec]

name: Payne, Stan[ley Arthur]
bio: (USA: c1916-12 May 1958) Inventor & dealer (Star Magic Co.) in Portland, Oregon. Invented

name: Paysan de Nort-Hollande, Le fameux
bio: (Holland: fl.1740s-50s) Pro. The "Famous Peasant of North Holland" worked the Paris fairs often from 1746 to 1753. [St;Dif;Cl;Hou,69]

name: Peacock, Victor, MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1896-20 Jan 1968) Amateur kid-show magician (as "Motley") & magic teacher. Investigator of psychic fraud. Translated Tréborix's Diversions with Dice (1953).

name: Peck, David
bio: See: "Caspian, David"

name: Peck, Doc
bio: (Glens Falls, New York: 30 Jan 1894-) Stage name of Dr Gordon C[adwell] Peck, DDS. Wealthy dentist in Glens Falls. Interested in magic since 1908. Amateur magician with act ranging from sleight of hand to occasional full-evening stage shows. [SAM]

name: Peck, Elwyn C.
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Aka "El-Wyn. Pro. Pioneered the modern Ghost Show. [Tay]

name: Pecor, Dr Charles J[oseph] [pronounced PEA-kor]
bio: (Augusta, Georgia: 5 Oct 1938-) Interested in magic since age 10. PhD in Drama & Theatre from U of Georgia & Assistant Professor of Speech at Macon Junior College, Macon, Georgia. Amateur magician as "The Wizard of Wit". Wrote The Magician on the American Stage, 1752-1874 (1977, 313+90pp), which was his doctoral dissertation; The Craft of Magic (1979, 272pp); Sinister Variations (1994, 59pp); Staging Magic (rev ed 1996, 24pp), & The Ten Year Tour of John Rannie. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, Journal of Magic History. 2 lecture notes. Also writes science fiction novels & short stories. [Wh2]

name: Pecoraro, Nino
bio: (Italy: fl.1920s-30s) Pseudo-psychic medium who produced manifestations he claimed came from the spirit of famous psychic Eusapia Palladino. His tour of the USA in the mid-1920s was managed by Hereward Carrington. He was exposed by both Houdini & Dunninger. See Dunninger, Inside the Medium's Cabinet (1935).

name: Pedersen, Bernhard
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 29 Jan 1876-) Aka "Bi-Tar-Sheng". Former customs official in China. Pro club & private party act. Founding member of the Board of the Danish Magic Circle 1934-35.[Go2]

name: Pedro
bio: See: Bedognetti, Peter

name: Pedro, Inge
bio: See: Peterson, Per Ingemar

name: Pedro, Manuel
bio: See: Marlo, Ed

name: Pedro & Lily
bio:
Pedro da Física [Pedro of Physics] (Valongo, Portugal: c1843-1918) Stage name of Pedro de Freitas. Moved to Lisbon where he was a carpenter specialized in making theatrical apparatus. Amateur magician specialized in manip. In 1880 co-founded the Grupo Artístico de Prestímanos, the world's 2nd magic association. 1897 Concurso de Illusionismo 4th place. [Cam]

[See also: Peterson, Per Ingemar]

name: Peixoto, João
bio: (Minas Gerais, Brazil: 17 May 1879-6 Sep 1946) Magic dealer (Academia de Ilusionismo Brasileiro) in São Paulo since 1910. All subscribers to his shop's Boletim Mágico received for promotional purposes the fictitious title "Membro do Circulo Mágico Internacional". IBM Member #784. Father of Norman Peixoto. Published 2 magazines: O Prestidigitador 1918-19 & Boletim Mágico 1921-25. Wrote Tratado Completo de Prestidigitação e Ilusionismo (1937), Curso Prático de Prestidigitação e Ilusionismo (1943), & Truques de Magia Selecionados (1946).

name: Peixoto, Norman
bio: (Brazil: -22 Jul 1967) Son of João Peixoto. Used stage name of "Mister Norman". Wrote O Mágico Amador (1944). Revived his late father's journal, Boletim Mágico 1956-57. [Fam]

name: Peki
bio: (Germany: 29 Dec 1950-) Stage name of Peter Kinnigkeit [sic]. Semi-pro with flower-production act billed as "Peki's Phantasie-Show". 1975 MZvD 1st prize in manip; 1978 MZvD 2nd prize in manip; FISM 1979 2nd prize (shared) in manip & 1985 3rd prize in manip. Tricks in Magie.

name: Peladini, Tomoso
bio: (Livorno [Leghorn], Italy: fl.1740s) Pro sleight-of-hand. In Berlin c1747. Pet effects: Decapitated Bird & Card-to-Bird. NOTE: Surname also spelled "Peladine". [St;Cl]

name: Pelaez, Cesareo Rafael "Zar
bio: (Santa Clara, Cuba: 16 Oct 1932 – 24 Mar 2012) Born to a Spanish father & Canary Islander mother. Aka "Marco the Magi" since 1977. Inspired at age 5 seeing Fu-Manchú show in Cuba. Moved to USA in 1962. Took PhD in psychology at Brandeis U in 1978. Teacher of psychology at Salem State College. Semi-pro magician & illusionist. Founder-producer-director since 1976 of Le Grand David troupe at the Cabot Street Cinema Theatre in Beverly, Massachusetts, which opened in 1977. This large troupe of semi-pros does its act each Sunday, working in the Fu-Manchú tradition with bits from Okito and Chang. Since 1985 this troupe also plays occasionally at the Larcom Theatre in Beverly. 1981 AMA Magician of the Year. 1981 SAM Hall of Fame. 1985 SAM Magician of the Year (shared with "Le Grand David" & "Seth the Sensational"). SAM President 1985-86. 1995 Christopher Award for Outstanding Illusionist. Edits the Cabot St. Cinema Theatre, the company's bi-weekly since 1976. A brief bio is William V. Rauscher, Marco the Magi: Wise Man of Magic (1983, 34pp). [LR2/94;Wh2]

name: Pelletier, François
bio: (France: fl.1760s) Pro. Played Paris yearly 1762-68. [St;Cl] (France: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Jean-Paul Vittet. Close-up & stage magic with silks & liquids. Dealer (Jims Visual Magic) in Romans, France.

name: Pemper, Frank (Michael Anthony)
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 29 Nov 1913-24 May 1998) Aka "Ricardo, the Debonaire Deceiver". Semi-pro since 1929. Salesman until retired in 1975. Semi-pro dealer in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, where he died. Wrote Ricardo's Card Artifice (1977, 96pp, which sold c600 copies). 1 video (1993). TV bits. [LR7/98]

name: Pendragon, Charlotte "Char", MIMC
bio: (Kalispell, Montana: 26 Feb 1954-) Born Charlotte Brown. Raised in California. Stage name of Charlotte Yarbrough, wife of Jonathan since 1976. For their joint career as "The Pendragons" see next entry. Pet effect: Origami Illusion. Also works alone stunting in Hollywood movies. MIMC 1991, being one of the first women to receive that honor. Articles in Magic Manuscript & Genii. [Genii12/91;MM9/89;Jef;Wh]

name: Pendragon, Jonathan
bio: (Fullerton, California: 28 Jul 1953-) Stage name of Claude Douglas "Jonathan" Yarbrough. Began pro career as escapist, mental magician, & close-up card worker. Then, since 1976, with partner-wife Charlotte as "The Pendragons", initially with a dove act. Soon a star illusion team playing major venues in USA, Europe, & Japan. Their pet effects: the world's fastest Substitution Trunk routine & the Impaling. Their fast-paced style relies heavily upon their athletic skills as body-builders. They also work separately stunting in Hollywood films. They were the AMA Stage Magicians of the Year, 1986 & 1987; 1988 AMA Magician of the Year; & received the 1989 Tannen's "Louis" Award. TV bits.
