[LR5/95; Geni3/86, 12/91, 1/92; Jef; MM9/89; Wat; Mag] "Penn and Teller" SEE: Jillette, Penn & Teller, R.

name: Penn, Dale
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Afro-American. Taught by Ronald Haines. Pro cruise-ship & trade-show close-up, mentalism, & pickpocket act. [Mag]

name: Pennington
bio: (England: fl.1840s) Minor pro. Toured the provinces and London suburbs with his assistant-wife, billed as "Wizard of the World" and the "Only Female Illusionist in the World".

name: Penstone, Ormonde
bio: (South Africa: 1860-24 Mar 1932) Pro with manip & smoke pictures. Toured Britain in 1902, working with Mdlle D'Anjou. Played St. George's Hall in London in 1925. Played "Charlie Chaplin" role with Fred Karno's "Mumming Birds". [Bur;Magic3/02]

name: Pentz, Collins [Rice]
bio: (Faribault, Minnesota: 27 Jan 1877-8 Feb 1956) Dealer (Eagle Magic Co.) in Minneapolis since 1903. In last years lived in the back of his shop. When retired to old folks home in mid-1950s gave business to long-time employee Doris Davids (see) who sold it on her retirement in 1971. In 1976 it was acquired by Larry Kahlow. Edited Eagle Magician 1915-22 (72 issues), P.A.L.M. 1919 (2 issues), Mystic 13 Magazine 1934 (1 issue), E.M.C.A. Magic News 1936-38 (21 issues), Better Magic News 1946-47 (4 issues), Reviews of Books and Tricks 1946-51, & Truth about Magic 1946-53 (69 issues). Wrote several booklets, including Helpful Hints to Amateurs (n.d.). Published Card Tricks You will Like (1935). Compiled Stage Tricks, Illusions and Escapes (1935) & Everybody's Magic (1945).

name: Pepi [or Peppi?], Onkel
bio: (Ebersberg, Germany: 10 Mar 1909-) Stage name of Dr. Ernst Schramm. 1967 FISM 2nd prize for invention & 3rd prize in closeup. [Nad;Roh]

name: Pepper, Professor John Henry
bio: (London, England: 17 Jun 1821-25 Mar 1900) Chemist. Joined the staff of the Royal Polytechnic Institution in 1848 as chemist & popular-science lecturer, becoming Honorary Director in 1852. Henry Dircks was his main assistant. Famous for presenting Dirck's Pepper's Ghost, which Pepper modified & debuted in 1862. Left the Polytechnic by 1872 to tour on own, covering England 1872, USA 1872 (with Dircks), & Australia 1879-1890 when returned to England where he soon retired. Invented Cabinet of Proteus (1865) & Metempsychosis (1879, jointly with J.J. Walker). Metempsychosis (1879, jointly with J.J. Walker). Wrote The Boy's Playbook of Science (1860, 440pp; repr 1866, 1868, 1869); Scientific Amusements for Young People (1861, 124pp; repr 1864), The Playbook of Metals (1861, 502pp; repr 1862), The Boy's Book of Science (1870, 506pp), Cyclopaedic Science Simplified (1869, 685pp; 4th ed rev 1876, 734pp), & The True History of the Ghost (1890, 46pp). [Daw; La; Vo56; Wal]

name: Peppercorn, William
bio: See: "D'Alvini"

name: Percival, Henry S.
bio: (Britain?: fl.1910s) Wrote Progressive Prestidigitation (1911, 24pp).

name: Percival, John H.
bio: (Providence, Rhode Island: 28 Aug 1888-) Semi-pro in Providence. Pet effect: Miser's Dream. Mentor of H. Adrian Smith since 1924. A major early collector who gave his library to Providence Public Library (Special Collections). Still alive as of 1980. [Go2]

name: Perico
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 3 May 1911-28 Jul 1987) Stage name of Jaime ALBIOL [RODA]. Pro kid-show magician, billed as "El amigo de los niños". 1st prizes in variety arts at FISM (1964) & Figueira da Foz (1966). [Xe;Cam]

name: Perkeo
bio: See: Tröstler, Reinhard

name: Peron, Kyle S.
bio: (Somers Point, NJ, USA: 5 Nov 1969 - ) Magician, graphic designer, illustrator, author, lecturer. Stage name of The Magical Illusions of Kyle and Kelly. Learned magic from his brother, Kevin, at the age of 15. First performance was at age 16 with his brother. Part-time professional since 1986. Magical focus on stage manipulation, illusions and family-friendly performances. Is a deaf entertainer and has bio written up in the book Silent Magic by Dr. Simon Carmel (2008). Co-leader of the Philadelphia Society of Young Magicians (1991 - Present). Won The Charles Hopkins Award for Magical Excellence given for his involvement in teaching youth in magic (1998). Co-editor of the SYM's Magic SYMbol (1997 - 1998). Wrote The Chair Suspension Ebook (2006, 16pp). Encore! Creativity in The Art of Magic (2007, 21pp). Blue and Gold! The Entertainers Complete Guide to Working the Scout Market (2009, 60pp). Articles in The Funny Paper (2008 - Present); The Joey (2009 - Present); Northern Peeks (2008 - Present); Magic New Zealand Ezine (2006 - Present). Co-invented: Magic Enhancer CD Volume 1 (2008).

name: Perót, Auguste
bio: (Josat, Haute-Loire, France: 6 Oct 1869-18 Jan 1905). Pro illusionist, aka the pseudo-Oriental "Kiang-Hoé", Stéphane (by 1904), & the pseudo-Egyptian "Kalama" (in 1904).

name: Perrin
bio: (France: fl.1780s-90s) Pro. Worked streets & rooms in Paris 1785-91. [Dif;Cl]

name: Perry
bio: (Germany: 26 Aug 1953-) Stage name of Paul Helmut. Magician with partner-wife Eva Maria Paul (born 12 Sep 19) as "Perry & Eve". 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad]

name: Perry, Vic
bio: (Woking, England: 19 Dec 1919-14 Aug 1974) Stage name of Victor Nixon Jr. Son of "The Great Nixon" with whom he originally toured as "Geoffrey the Boy Conjurer--direct from Czechoslovakia" & "Fingers Orsini--The American Boy Wizard". Pro pickpocket act. After release from British Army in 1945 toured Australia, the West Indies, & the USA where he settled in Chicago & became a citizen. [Hudd;St;LR11/74]

name: Perry, Warner
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Dealer (Mars Magic) out of home in Washington, D.C., by 1945 to 1946. Tricks in HMM.

name: Peru, Monsieur
bio: (France: fl.1810s) Pro travelling magician. Toured Britain in late 1810s. A teacher of Billy Purvis.

name: Peter, Willy [Martin]
bio: (Olten, Switzerland: 15 Nov 1918-) Air traffic controller with Swissair (retired). Amateur close-up magician since 1954 when inspired to learn by seeing a magic gala. Aka "Tex Williams" since 1960. Edited Hocus-Pokus 1964-66. President, Club Zürcher Magier, 1965-74. President, Swiss Magic Circle, 1974-86. 1979 FISM jury. FISM President 1979-82. [Wh5]

name: Peterka, Alois
bio: (Austria: 1861-) Minor pro who worked only in Vienna.

name: Peterkin, W[alter] G.
bio: (USA: 1876-27 Aug 1948) Edited Mahatma 1900-01. Pro stage magician for several years as "Hal B. Merton". Left magic to become businessman in Amityville, New York.

name: Peters, Howard, MIMC
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s-90s) Stage name of Peter Deadman. Pro escape artist. MIMC 1988. BBC-TV bit in 1993 doing the Water Torture Cell. [La2;Bo2]

name: Petersen, Vald
bio: (Denmark: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Pro. Performed yearly for the Danish royal family.

name: Peterson, Per Ingemar
bio: (Nykroppa, Värmland, Sweden: 8 Oct 1921-) Learned as boy from books & watching good magicians. Amateur since 1943 and pro since 1951. First with single act as "Inge Pedro" 1951-67. 1952 FISM 2nd prize for presentation. Several 1st prizes in Stockholm & Oslo. Thence with Greek assistant-wife (ex-international acrobat) as "Pedro & Lily" 1968-present. They've played major venues through 25 countries in Europe, Africa, & Near East. Articles in Trollkarlen. TV bits in Scandinavia, England, Germany, Italy, & Hungary. [Trollkarlen#149;Wh5]

name: Petit, Philippe
bio: (Nemours, France: 13 Aug 1949- ) A wire walker since age 17. Then a street magician, having revived that art in Paris c1966. Later world famous as a funambulist, illegally walking a tightwire between the twin towers of Notre Dame Cathedral, the Sydney Harbour Bridge, and in 1974 between the towers of the World Trade Center, for which latter feat he won the Guinness Record for "the tightrope [sic] walk over the highest drop" (1,350 feet above the street). With Ringling & Barnum & Bailey Circus 1975. In 1989 he wire-walked across the Seine to the Eiffel Tower. Lives in New York City. Autobios are On the High Wire (1985) & To Reach the Clouds (2003, 227pp). Bio in John Culhane, The American Circus (1990), 338-345.

name: Petrashek, [Richard A.] "Pete" [pronounced pe-TRA-shek]
bio: (Table Rock, Nebraska: 20 Aug 1925- ) Taught the French Drop c1934 by a Gypsy boy to make a stone disappear & learned from mail-order tricks. Radio-TV news photographer/reporter in Omaha 1949-89 when retired. Semi-pro magician as "Peter the Near (great)" in the Midwest since late 1950s & full-time since 1989. Pet effects: Hot Rod, Thumb-Tip tricks, & 3-Card Repeat. Invented Holding the Bag (1970) & Purse Tear (1975). SAM Librarian since c1975. 1989 SAM Magician of the Year. Retail-wholesale dealer (Midwest Magic) in Omaha. Articles in MUM, Genii, Linking Ring, & Magigram. [MUM3/81;Wh5]

name: Petrick
bio: (Prague, Czechoslovakia: 3 May 1952- ) Stage name of Petr Krejcik. Learned 1st 3 tricks in 1966 in hospital from comedian-magician Petr Pavel & joined local magic club. Czechoslovak champion 1969, 1970, 1974. Pro since 1970, specialized in stage, close-up, & parlor magic. Pet effect: ball manipulations. 1973 FISM special award for originality & professionalism. In 1974 married Mia Izarikova, training her as his assistant. Lecturer. They escaped to USA in 1979. 1980 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year for "Petrick & Mia". 1983 Dragon Award to "Petrick & Mia". Became USA citizen in 1986. Inventor of Straw thru Card (1980), Linking Razor Blades, Bewildering Bracelets, & The Transformers, which he sells wholesale & mail-order since 1980. [MUM11/91; Genii3/83; Wat;Wh2]

name: Petrie, John A[lbert]
bio: (New Haven, Connecticut: 23 Aug 1870-2 Feb 1954) Interested in magic since childhood. Dealer and manufacturer in New Haven since late 1890s (John Petrie Magical Company). In 1908 co-founded (with A.C. Gilbert) the Mysto Magic Company, which he left in 1912 when conned out of the business by Gilbert. Then on a small scale as the Swastika Magic Co. In 1917 returned to major magic manufacturing with wealthy amateur magician Thomas C. Lewis as the Petrie-Lewis Manufacturing Company, which they incorporated in 1923. Invented Goblin Tube (by 1926), etc. Father of J. Walter "Tod" Petrie, his younger son and successor. Bio is Barbi Walker & Robert Seaver (editors), The P&L Book (1992, 277pp)

name: Petrie, J[ohn] Walter "Tod
bio: (New Haven, Connecticut: 1899-1962) Younger son of John A. Petrie. Semi-pro magician working mainly local kid shows as "Tod" with a mental magic, sleight-of-hand, & mechanical act. Manufacturer & inventor with Petrie-Lewis Manufacturing Company in New Haven since graduating from school in 1917, taking over the business on his father's death in 1954. On his own death in 1964 the business was taken over by his widow, Lenna, who ran it until 1968 when sold to Abbott's.

name: Petrix
bio: See: Schröder, Peter

name: Petroff, Peter
bio: See: Gill, Richard

name: Pfalz, Reinhold
bio: (Hildburghausen, Germany: 1869-6 Mar 1939) Operated a magic theater. Then after acquiring Mellini's shop (in Hannover), a famous dealer-prop maker (issuing many catalogs) in Leipzig 1918-1930 when his shop was acquired by Manfredo. Died in Leipzig.

name: Pfeiffer, Klaus-Peter
bio: (Germany: 3 Sep 1958-) 1981 MZvD 2nd prize in closeup. [Nad]

name: Pfeiffer, Rainer
bio: (Germany: 6 Nov 19-) 1984 MZvD 1st prize in closeup & Closeup Magician of the Year. [Nad]

name: Phalke, Dadasahib
bio: (Trimbkeshwar, Nasik, India: 30 Apr 1870-16 Feb 1944) Honorific of Dhundiraj Govind Phalke. Pro magician. Trained in printing & photography, he effectively founded the Indian film industry in 1913 when he released that country's first feature film. Produced and directed over 100 films before his retirement in 1931. In one of his short films, Professor Kelpha's Magic, he played the conjuror. REF: Erik Barnouw & S. Krishnaswamy, Indian Film (New York: Columbia U Press, 1963), 10-21. [Katz]

name: Phantini
bio: See: Grant, Gene

name: Pharos
bio: (England: 12 Mar 1875-) Stage name of Mr Mawson. Minor pro with Black Art act by 1907, billed as "The Egyptian Wonder Worker". Husband of "Ibhar". Gave his last performances during WW II for troops in England. Then retired in Hastings. His son, "Pharos Jr", did an act with wife as "Pharos & Marina, the Two Brainwaves".

name: Philadelphia, Jacob
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 14 Aug 1734?-) Stage name of Jacob Meyer aka "Meyer", son of Jewish immigrants from Polish Galicia. Learned c1750 by tuition from Dr Christopher Witt, a Rosicrucian occultist. Moved to England around mid-1750s. After 1765 become the first American magician to perform in Europe. Pro illusionist & sleight-of-hand artist. Toured England (c1765), Ireland, Portugal (1765?), Spain, Russia, Romania ( ? & 1772), Turkey, Sweden, Prussia, Vienna (1774), Lüneburg, Weimar (1777), Göttingen (1777), Strasbourg (1779), & Switzerland. When not on tour, lived with his wife & 2 children in Köthen by 1783 until last reported there in 1797. Wrote Kleines Kraftätlein seltsamer und approbirte Kunststücke [Little Treatise on Strange and Appropriate Feats] (Vienna: 1774). This 72-page book is the earliest published work on magic by an American-born conjuror. The only known copy is in the Christopher Collection. [Dam;Daw;Ch;Sal;St]

name: Philius & Jane
bio: See: Weidmann, Theophil

name: Phillippe
bio: (Alès, Gard, France: 28 Dec 1802-27 Jun 1878) Stage name of Jacques-André-Noé Talon. Inspired seeing performance by J.H. Anderson while working as a pastry chef in Aberdeen, Scotland. Learned in Britain c1836 by tuition from J.H. Anderson. Pro on own since 1837. Toured most major European cities, including Dublin (1837), Edinburgh (1837), Glasgow (1840), Paris (1841-42), London (1845, 1846), Breslau (1854), St. Petersburg (1860). Died in Bokhara. Father of

name: Phillips, Henry
bio: (Britain: fl.1860s-70s) Minor music-hall illusionist 1864-1876. Pet effects: Decapitation of a Lady, the Speaking Bust, Living Head in Glass Bottle (Tanagra style), alleged automaton card-player (a la Psycho), Lynn's Another Man Cut Up To-day, an Aerial Suspension, & the Living Head supported on 2 brass bars. [CI]

name: Piatt, Ray[mond Paul]
bio: (Phillipsburg, New Jersey: 30 Apr 1934-) Maintenance engineer. Taught magic by Bill Marko from ages c9 to c16 when inspired by seeing Dunninger to become amateur mentalist. Since 1970s has invented & marketed over 70 mental effects, including Caper-Case (1982) & the Piatt-Stride Two-Way Wallet (1989). His Magic Makers company (with wife Lisa) in Bath, Pennsylvania, makes top-quality leather & other props for mentalists as well as his "L.O.L. (Live on Location) Video" line. Effects in Vibrations & MUM. [MUM2/9;Wh5]

name: Piccoli, Carmelo
bio: (Illasi, Verona, Italy: 18 Jul 1915-) Roman Catholic priest. Amateur magician. Collector. Wrote Siamo Tutti Maghi (3 vols, 1977, 580pp). [Wh5]

name: Pickman, Jean-Lambert
bio: (Liège, Belgium: 12 Mar 1857-24 Oct 1925) Pro magician as "Alberti", then famous mind-reader as "Pickman" since c1893. Retired in France soon after WW I. [Dif]

name: Picton, Thomas
bio:
Piddingtons, The SEE: Piddington, Lesley & Piddington, Sydney

[See also: "Preston, Paul"]

name: Piddington, Lesley [Pope]
bio: (Australia: c1925-) First wife of Sydney Piddington with whom she worked a uniquely successful 2-person mindreading act 1947-52. Divorced c1963.

name: Piddington, Robyn [Greig]
bio: (Australia: 3 Apr 1947-) Second wife of Sydney Piddington. Has performed with him in 2-person mindreading act since 1975.

name: Piddington, Sydney
bio: (Randwick, Australia: 14 May 1918-29 Jan 1991) While a Japanese POW in Changi Prison, Singapore, in WW II developed with Russell Braddon a 2-person mindreading act to entertain fellow prisoners. Then, 1947-52, with Lesley Pope, a radio actress whom he had married in 1946, presented his Piddington "telepathy" act--first on Australian radio, then in 1949 on the London BBC, gaining stunning success, The Piddington's being the 1st Australians to head the bill at the London Palladium. They performed in Britain, Europe, & Africa before retiring in 1952. Resumed his act with new assistant-wife Robyn Piddington in 1975 with a widely publicized long-distance act involving an off-shore Soviet trawler. Always ended each performance with: "There you are--you are the judge." Sensationalized early bio is Russell Braddon, The Piddingtons (1950, 238pp). [MC4/89; Hudd]

name: Pierce, Dr J[ames] E. "Doc", DC
bio: (Norristown, Pennsylvania: 17 Jul 1883-4 Apr 1931) Pro vaude manip from 1898 and later an escape act as "Pierce the Mysterious". Retired to become a chiropracter in Philadelphia. Founder-editor of The Magic World monthly 1917-24 for which Walter Gibson was Associate Editor since 1920. [Dor]

name: Pierce, [Donald] Ray
bio: (Waco, Texas: 3 Jul 1956-) Learned at age 8 from magic set from grandfather. Pro producer-director-choreographer (ex-actor) & stage illusionist since age 20. Moved to Hollywood c1980. Pet effects: Death Rack, Thumb Tie, Motorcycle Vanish. 1989 AMA Award of Merit. Articles in Genii. [Jef; Wat; Wh6]

name: Pierre, Maurice
bio: (Paris, France: 18 Jul 1926 - 8 Dec 2010) Learned at age 12 from old library books. Pro magician ages 17-25. Thence semi-pro close-up magician & mentalist in Paris. Pet effects: Linking Rings & card magic. AFAP Bronze Medal 1971 & Gold Medal 1973. In 1979 awarded the AFAP Golden Wand (still only 1 of 3 recipients). FISM Secretary General since 1979. AFAP President 1980-81 & 1982-88. 1988 FISM jury. FISM President 1993-94. Wrote a book on magic with paper clips & rubber bands. Articles in Revue de la Prestidigitation & Journal de la Prestidigitation. [Mec;Wh2]

name: Pierre, Roger
bio: (USA: fl.1970s) Chef. Amateur magician. Wrote The Magic of Francis Carlyle (1975, 186pp).

name: Piesse, G[eorge] W[illiam] Septimus
bio: (Britain: 30 May 1820-23 Oct 1882) Optician, analytical chemist, &, later, perfumier in London. In 1855 in partnership with Wilhelm Lukin opened their "Laboratory of Flowers" at 12 New Bond Street, which included a few magic items. Wrote Chymical Natural and Physical Magic (1858, 201pp; repr 1859; 3rd ed 1865, 267pp), the last edition adding many standard conjuring tricks. REF: Dawes in MC, V.77 (1983), 42-45.

name: Pietro, Commandeur
bio: (Pardiès-Piétat, Basses-Pyrénées, France: 30 Nov 1878-5 Jun 1941) Stage name of Pierre-André Morlaas. Pro hypnotic act. Toured several years with Carmelli's travelling theater, which he bought in 1919 & renamed the "Music-Hall Pietro". Wrote L'hypnotisme, le magnétisme, le spiritisme à la portée de tous (1910). [Dif;St]

name: Pikart
bio: (Hospitalet, Barcelona, Spain: 12 Sep 1919-) Stage name of Juan PICART BATLLE. 1964 FISM 2nd prize for grand illusions with son as "Pikart & There". [Xe]

name: Pike
bio: (England?: fl.1830s) Minor pro. Had a booth at Bartholomew Fair in London in 1831, being one of the last magicians to perform there.

name: Pilkington, Jack
bio: (Fleetwood, Lancashire, England: 18 May 1884-) Amateur sleight-of-hand. Articles.[Go;Go2]

name: Piluland, Elias
bio: (Germany: fl.1660s) Wrote Hocus Focus Junior, Oder Taschen-Spiel-Kunst (1667), a 108-page free translation of Hocus Focus Junior with some additional tricks. A copy is in the Price Collection. Reprinted at least 6 times under different titles up to 1768, thereby widely diffusing its information throughout Germany.

name: Pimpirlimpi
bio: See: Michaelassi, Antonio

name: Pinchbeck, Christopher
bio: (Clerkenwell, England: Aug 1670?-18 Nov 1732) Famous clock & automata maker, & inventor of Pinchbeck metal, a cheap copper-zinc alloy that simulates gold. Exhibited his automata with conjurer Isaac Fawkes 1727-31 and, following the latter's death, with Fawkes Jr. Possibly invented the Orange Tree (1730). Bio is R. Shelton, Christopher Pinchbeck and His Family (1976). [Daw;Daw#226;Hou;Dictionary of National Biography]

name: Pinchbeck, William Frederick
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1800s) Descendent of Fawkes' partner, Christopher Pinchbeck. Toured USA with a learned pig. Wrote The Expositor; or Many Mysteries Unravelled (Boston: 1805, 100pp; facsimile repr 1996), the 1st book on magic both written & published in the USA. Later also published Witchcraft or The Art of Fortune Telling Unveiled (USA, 108pp). [Pr]

name: Pinelli
bio: (Germany: 17 Jul 1933-) Stage name of Hans Wechsler. Pro comedy magician. [Nad]

name: Pinetti, Giuseppe
bio: (Orbetello, Tuscany, Italy: 1750-c1806 [sic]) Stage name of Giuseppe Merci, son of Luigi Merci, a village innkeeper in Tuscany. Aka "Willedal de Merci". Originally a teacher of physics in Rome, he became a top-line stage pro, playing the best theaters in Italy (1766), Switzerland, Germany (1780, 1782, 1796), France (1783-84), London (1784-85), France (1785), Russia (1789), Lisbon (1791), Italy (1793 & 1796), Poland, & finally Russia (1805?) where he became a pioneer balloonist and died in Berdichev. Possibly invented both Dancing Card (by 1784) and Jumping Plume (by 1784). Wrote Amusements physiques (Paris: 1784), English tr as Physical Amusements and Diverting Experiments (1784, 65pp). For contemporary exposures see Decremps (1784) & J.W.A. Kosmann (a Berlin math professor), Des Herrn Ritters Pinetti de Merci physikalische Belüstigungen (1796, 160pp; 2nd ed 1797, 160+128pp). Bio material on his last years in Russia is in É.-G. Robertson, Mémoires récréatifs scientifiques et anecdotiques (1831). [Dif; Hou; Ch; Pr; Escamoteur3/53; St]

name: Piniarz, Mieczysław
bio: (Przemysł, Poland: 1923-1991) Pro after WW II with stage name of "Aris". Collected magic posters, books, photos, & documents. [Mec;Nad]

name: Pirlimpimpim
bio: See: Francese, Alberto

name: Pit, Peter
bio: (Geffen, Holland: 11 Mar 1933-21 Feb 1999) Stage name of Hermann Claassen until legal change to Peter Pit. Student of Henk Vermeyden. Pro comedy magician (ex-amateur circus juggler), comedian, stage producer. 1958 FISM 1st prize for general magic for his Dancing Cane routine of which he is a master. Moved to USA in 1960. Secretary, Board of Directors, Academy of Magical Arts, 1972-94, thence Director Emeritus. 1978 AMA Best Stage Magician. Co-authored (with Paul Butler) The Magic Castle (1989, [56pp]). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Pitt", much to his annoyance. [Mag;Wh]

name: Pitchford, Robert
bio: (Wales: fl.1940s) Younger brother of Valentine "Cardini" Pitchford who built his act. Since 1942 as "The De Fakas", pro comedy magician with assistant Isabelle Pett whom he married at the Abbott's Get-Together in 1947. Pet effects: Rope Stretching & Production of 8 Glasses of Beer. [Conjuror's Magazine 9/47]

name: Pitt
bio: (Freiburg, Germany: 28 Feb 1906-20 Nov 1984) Stage name of Friedrich Stutz. Died in Hannover. [Roh]

name: Pittmann, George H[arrison]
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-40s) Inspired in 1912. Investment consultant in Mamaroneck, NY. Amateur card & close-up. [Th]

name: Pitts [Jr], [William] Bill
bio: (Fort Smith, Arkansas: 5 Feb 1926- ) Learned as child from amateur father. Owner of industrial supply firm in home town. Amateur magician since 1934. Invented No-Fake Hydro Glass (1943). As semi-pro c1949-c1955 toured spook show through eastern Arkansas movie houses as "Doctor Templar's Chamber of Chills". A Mason, he joined the Invisible Lodge (Member #29) in 1953. Collector. Dealer in collectibles for 15 years as "Aladdin Enterprises". IBM President 1978-79. Articles in Sphinx, Conjurors Magazine, Genii, Dragon, MUM, Linking Ring, Tops. Wrote "Future Greats" column in Tops for 15 years. [Wh2]

name: Pizzuti, Claudio
bio: (Albano, Roma, Italy: 4 Apr 1940- ) Learned at age 10. Employer. Semi-pro close-up magician since c1965, as "Rodrigo". Specialized in coin magic. Wrote Sulle ali della Magia (2 vols, 1988/1990, 110pp) & Magicata (2 vols, 1989/1990, 55pp). Tricks in Magia Moderna, Inoltre, & Qui Magia. [Wh5]

name: Pladek [Jr], Oscar [Joseph]
bio: (Passaic, New Jersey: 27 Nov 1928-) Taught in 1938 by cousin John Mintz. Chemist. Amateur close-up & platform magician. Articles in Pallbearers Review, MUM, & Pabular. [Wh2]

name: Plate, Adrian
bio: (Utrecht, Holland: 10 Jun 1844-24 Feb 1919) Originally an officer in the Dutch Army. Amateur magician, specialized in mental magic. Moved to USA in 1877 where he worked in New York City as a merchant until his death. Invented the palm change (by 1897). Wrote (with Henry Hatton) Magicians' Tricks--How They Are Done (New York: 1910, 344pp; London: 1911), a classic. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. [St]

name: Plato, Roland
bio: (USA: 19 Mar 1895-) Pro manip & stage magic since age 17. Billed as "The Magic Man". In 1941-42 as "Plato & Jewel, the Gay Deceivers" & "Dapper Deceivers", worked cabarets & theaters. In late 1940s worked mainly school shows with a 45-minute act. [St;Tay]

name: Platt, John J[oseph] "Johnny
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 15 Oct 1903-6 Jun 1990) Learned in 1910 from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set. Semi-pro with club act since 1919 specialized in billiard balls as "Algernon LaPlatt". IBM #109. Pro close-up & stage since 1933. Aka "Hadji Baba" (in 1933 at Chicago Worlds Fair) & "Ki Ming". Played carnival, vaude, & burlesque. 15 years as MC & magician at Gay 90's Room of Hotel La Salle in Chicago. USO in WW II in USA, China, & Middle East. Later a house magician at the Magic Castle. Pet effects: Cups-&-Balls and Kuma Tubes. 1970 AMA Best Close-up Magician. 1979 AMA Performing Fellowship. Wrote Cups & Balls (1975, 13pp). Tricks in Sphinx, Linking Ring, MUM, Genii, & Tarbell #5. [LR2/67;Berg,23,46;Mag;Wat;WWM;Wh2]

name: Playfair, Patrick
bio: (England: fl.1900s-20s) Stage name of Charles James Smith. Member of the first Committee of The Magic Circle 1905. Articles in Magic Wand.

name: Pleggs, Peer
bio: See: Mackowski, Dr Leo

name: Pleasing
bio: (Austria: fl.1880s) Amateur in Graz, Austria.

name: Plessis, Dominique
bio: (France: 1950-) Stage name of Dominique Lebel. Pro magician, specializing in work with large balls. As "Domi-Nho" won FISM 1st Prize in invention 1970, 2nd Prize in general magic 1973, 1st Prize in general magic 1976. Under own name won 1982 FISM 3rd prize in general magic. Wrote Les secrets de la mémoire (1984).

name: Plough, Alvin R[ichard] "Al
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 1891-7 Jul 1965) Pro magician briefly until 1913. Thence writer & public relations in Cincinnati. Invented Protean Flower (by 1940). Edited Linking Ring 1948-1965. Article in Nov 1951 LR as "Nivel Holgup".

name: Poinc, Eugene [Jerome] "Gene
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 20 Apr 1930-23 Jul 2002) Learned at age c8 from magic set & library books. Artist and TV, cinema, & book writer. Semi-pro magician since late 1940s & fortune-teller (as "Hasil") since 1950. Staff artist with Genii 1953-60 & 1991. Writer for Sterling Creations 1980-84. Pet effects: Professor's Nightmare, Coins thru Table, & Disembodied Princess. Invented sliding disk in "Ultimate Chinatown Half" (1980) and the "Crocodile Coin" utility gimmick (1981). Wrote Imagination: The Illusions of Eugene Poinc (1981, 101pp), Illusions for Princes or Paupers (1983, 91pp), & The Practitioner: Journeys into Grey. Column in Genii 1954-56 & sporadic since 1980. Also wrote for men's magazines as "Erik Fredricks". [MUM11/02:1 R2/02:Wh5]

name: Poisson, Jean, MIMC
bio: (France: 1915-12 Jul 1985) Son of a lawyer. Inspired by & learned as a boy from a box of tricks given by his grandmother. After working small-time dates and in the circus, he made the big-time in 1942. In 1949 while living in Brussels founded the Belgian Ring #86 (IBM). Aka "John Fish". Then as a sales rep with Cointreau, he worked magic into his sales pitch. Taking up mentalism, did private bookings as "Jean Sonis". AFAP Master Magician; MIMC. [Bou]

name: Poland, Ellison W[ebber] "Penny
bio: (Glencoe, Kentucky: 8 Jan 1922-18 Mar 2002) Teacher, engineering writer, corporate president. Father taught him at age 6 his 1st trick which he traded to friends for more. A leading semi-pro close-up worker in the South since age 23. Wrote Wonderful Routines of Magic (1969, 251pp; repr 1992), The First Addendum to Wonderful Routines of Magic (1973, 80pp), & Second Addendum to Wonderful Routines of Magic (1995, 203pp). Tricks in Linking Ring & MUM. [Wh5]

name: Poletti, Cavaliere Antonio
bio: (Vicenza, Italy: fl.1850s-60s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Pet effects: the Gun Trick, Dancing Egg, Magic Hat, the Prolific Scarf, & the Bottle of Tantalus. Played various rooms in London May 1857-May 1861, billed as "The Roman Illusionist". [Daw#91;Go2;Cl]

name: Polini
bio: (Łódź, Poland: 9 Oct 1931-) Stage name of Waldemar Włodzimierz Wagner. Pro illusionist. Founding President of the KKI 1976-81. [Mec;Nad]

name: Pollex, C. V.
bio: (London, England: 1899- ) Aka "Domino". Semi-pro sleight-of-hand.

name: Pollman-Steens, Georgy
bio: (France: fl.1950s-60s) Stage name of Georges Martin. Pro escapist. [Dif]

name: Pollock, Channing
bio: (near Fairfield, California: 16 Aug 1926-19 Mar 2006) Named after the playwright of the same name but no familial relation. Inspired seeing a pitchman selling Svengali decks. Briefly used "Chan" as stage name. Quit college & moved to Los Angeles to become a Chavez student & graduate teacher there. Graduating in 1952 with a pro dove (inspired by Abe Cantu) & card manip act, he became world-famous within 2 years, playing the NY Palace in 1954, the Ed Sullivan TV show in 1954, 1959, & 1960. London's Palladium in 1955 & 1958, London's Hippodrome in 1955, & Paris's Moulin Rouge in 1956. Invented the Toss Vanish(2) & the double dove production. Left magic (for movies) in 1961, teaching & giving his act to "Franklin". Became a European film star, making several movies, only 4 of which show his magic: European Nights (Italy, 1962), The Red Sheik (Italy, 1963), Rocambole (Italy, 1963), & Judex (France, 1963). Returned to USA in 1965. Retired in 1969 but still occasionally appears or lectures at magicians gatherings. Tutored Svengari (1969), James Dimmare, etc. 1976 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1984 CMI Order of the Magic Lamp; 1991 AMA Masters Fellowship. 1991 SAM Hall of Fame. [LR8/96; Magic11/96; QuiMagia3/89; Ran; Genii2/69; Mag; Dif; Tay; Des; HC; Hudd; Wh]

name: Pollux, Les
bio: (Basel, Switzerland: 1933-) Stage name of Rudolf "Lux" Haegler. Pro magician. Was first to create an act using the Boomerang Card to hit objects. Played many clubs throughout the world including the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1962.

name: Polo
bio: (Argentina: fl.1960s) Minor pro who worked the provinces with his assistant-wife. Son of Faluggi.

name: Polo, Marco
bio: (Venice, Italy: 1254 or 1255-8 Jan 1324) Venetian merchant who travelled through Asia .....-1295. In 1298 finished the manuscript of his The Description of the World (ghosted by Rusticello of Pisa), which thence circulated in many hand-written copies & translations. First printed in 1477 (in German). Best general bio is Henry H. Hart, Marco Polo: Venetian Adventurer (1867–3060).

name: Pomeroy, John D.
bio: (USA: 1938-27 Jul 2000) Professional bookbinder in Edmonds, Washington. Semi-pro magician and maker of hand-crafted quality props & illusions as “Gem Mfg. Co.”. Invented the Gem Book Test. Produced his “Bloody Jack” magical musical in the 1980s. Wrote Mentology (1973, 41pp), Dove, Silk & Flower Magic (1975, 42pp), Basic Make-up for Magicians, The Gem Dictionary Book Test. Weeks before his cancer-related death he finished his book on Claude Alexander Conlin.

name: Ponelli, Rudy
bio: (Germany?: 1 Nov 1935-) Stage name of Rudolf Abenheimer. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Ponrepo, Viktor
bio: (Prague, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 16 Jun 1858 [or 1853?] -4 Dec 1926) Stage name of Dismas Slambor. Pro, touring a spirit-illusion show with 4 assistants since 1893. Wrote Moderni Salonni Kouzelnictvi [Prague: 1903], in French as L'Illusionniste moderne de salon (1900). Fascinated by the new motion pictures, in 1907 he opened Prague's first movie theater, which was visited by Thomas Edison in 1911. Founding member of the Magicky Klub Praha (Prague Magic Club) in 1922. [Dif;Mec]

name: Ponsin, J[ean]-N[icholas]
bio: (Reims, Marne, France: 19 Mar 1801-) Pen name of Charles-Édouard Ponsin. Teacher of drawing at the Lyceum at Reims. Amateur magician, already adept at card sleights in his early 20s when he became a close friend of Decremps. Also taught by Comus II, Théodore Massey, and others. Wrote the classic Nouvelle Magie blanche dévoilée (2 vols, 1853, 1854; repr 1858 in 1 volume as La Sorcellerie ancienne et moderne expliquée), English tr by S.H. Sharpe as Ponsin on Conjuring (1937, 176pp; repr 1987). [Dif]

name: Pooley, John
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Engineer, then elementary school teacher. Semi-pro magician, working mainly school shows. Now dealer (John Pooley's World of Magic) in Riverside, California. [Se;Mag] SEE: Armstrong, William J.

name: Poogie Poogie
bio: See: Alstrand, William D.

name: Pooshee Pooshee
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: 25 Nov 1910-) Learned assisting Fasola, Thurston (2 years), & Charlton. Pro nightclub & stage magician since 1926, touring USA, China, & Europe (late 1930s & late 1940s). Pet effects: Vanishing Birdcage (as opener) & Smoking Clay Pipes. Invented Paradox (1952). Geoffrey Hansen understands he died in a psychiatric ward in France. [St;Jinx#30;Ho]

name: Poppe, Johann Heinrich Moritz
bio: (Germany: fl.1810s-1830s) Professor of technology at Tübingen U. Wrote 9 books on magic: Der physikalische Jugendfreud (1811, 268pp), Magischer Jugendfreud (1817, 3 vols, 278, 186, 271pp), Wunder der Mechanik (1824), Auserlesenes Zauberkabinett (1827), Die Kunst Geistererscheinungen (1829, 92pp), Der neue Tausendkunstler und Magiker (1935), Magie (1837, 835pp), Der junge Physiker (1838, 272pp), Neuer Wunder-Schauplatz (1839, 6 vols, 376, 342, 324, 340, 338, 342pp).

name: Porta, Giambattista della
bio: (Naples, Italy: 1538?-4 Feb 1615) Natural philosopher & researcher. Died in his home city. Drawing heavily from Hero of Alexandria, Porta wrote Magiae naturalis (Naples: 1558, in Latin) with English tr as Natural Magick (London: 1658, 409pp). Also translated into German, French, Italian, Dutch, & Arabic. [Magie1935,#2,p38]

name: Porthault. Alain
bio: (France: c1950-) Pro pickpocket and dealer in stolen passports in Europe since age 16. In 1983, (having paid his debt to society and with a genuine Israeli passport) moved to the French section of St. Martin (in the Caribbean) where he became that island's leading pro magician as "Diabolo" doing street (and beach) and restaurant magic. Pet effect is an Ace of Spades prediction revealed when he drops his trousers to reveal the Ace tattooed on a buttock. Also has a mouse trained to find (by smell) a selected card.

name: Portland, James
bio: (Britain: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of James Pulton. Minor pro & teacher of sleight-of-hand in Canonbury, London.

name: Portwood, Al[fred Thornton]
bio: (Colville, Washington: 8 Apr 1927- ) Taught magic by Eric Ecklund in 1939. Oil company executive in southern California until retired in 1985. Amateur magician. Aka "Alpo". Charter member (#57) of AMA. Invented Blankety Blank Poker (1972). Wrote How to Detect Marked Cards (1973, 10pp), a satire. Articles in Genii. [Wh2]

name: Posgate, Bruce [Dale]
bio: (Sunderland, Durham, England: 7 Dec 1901-13 Nov 1990) Inspired seeing a magician at age 7. Learned since age 14 from library books. Sales correspondent (now direct mail manager). Semi-pro kid-show magician since debut in London in 1924. Aka "Uncle Bruce" since 1924. Moved to Canada in 1947. 1975 Louis Bertol Trophy. IBM President 1980-81. Wrote Magic in Miniature (1950s), Kid Show Showmanship (1961, 52pp; 3 reprints), Dove Pan-O-Rama (1972, 48pp), Table Hopping (1974, 54pp), Art of Blowing Bubbles (1980, 14pp), Necklace Trickery (1982, 64pp). "Forum" columnist in New Tops 1961-89. Articles in Magic Circular, Abra, Linking Ring, Ibidem, etc. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Postgate", to his distinct annoyance. [Magigram3/89;LR8/68;Wh2]

name: Potash, Ricky
bio: See: Jay, Ricky

name: Potassy, Paul [Ludwig Alexander]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 23 Oct 1923-) Son of Hungarian parents, a family of engineers. Learned at age 13 after seeing Morelli. Pro humorous magician since 1940 plus pickpocket act & mentalism. POW 1943-47 in Russia where he performed in camp ("A deck of cards saved my life; otherwise I would have been shot!"). Moved to Hungary (Budapest) in 1947, to Germany in 1956, & to Spain in 1961. Although has no pet effects, famous for Razor Blade Trick. Speaks 8 languages, which he applies to his multi-lingual patter act. Assisted by his wife Lita. Worked major venues across the world & private parties. TV series in Germany plus over 150 TV bits throughout the world. Officially retired in 1991. Invented The Magic Salt in 1940. Wrote Magic for All Ages (1975, 40pp). Articles in many magazines. 150 TV bits in Europe & USA. His biography by Alfred Czernewitz was published in German in 1991. 1 video. [Win;Wh2]

name: Pottage, Joan
bio: (Holland?: fl.mid-1600s) Pro conjuror in Amsterdam. The first recorded magicienne, if indeed this person was female. [Cl]

name: Potter, Jack
bio: (Manchester, England: 13 Jul 1903-10 Oct 1978) TV engineer. Amateur magician. Wrote the standard, very useful, but seriously flawed reference, The Master Index to Magic in Print (14 volumes, 1967-1975). 1968 AMA Literary Fellowship. Trick in HMM.

name: Potter, Richard
bio: (Hopkinton, Massachusetts: c1786-20 Sep 1835) Mulatto. Aka "Black Potter". Learned c1810 assisting John Rannie. Pro. [Ch;Pr;Mo] (Massachusetts, USA: fl.1830s) Inspired by & learned from father Richard Potter. Pro for a brief period until drunkenness ended his career. [Pr]

name: Poulleau, Georges
bio: (Lyon, France: 5 May 1897-7 Sep 1979) Aka "Diavol" & "Sagar Nadir". Debut at age 16. Co-founded Magic-Club Rennes in 1913. Book collector. Published-edited Les Circulaires Magiques 1922-26, Nos Idées (with Jean Plaine) 1927, & Les Cahiers de la Magie 1962-67. AFAP Master Magician. AFAP Silver Medal 1970 & Gold Medal 1976. [Dif;Bou]

name: Poultier
bio: (France: fl.1780s) Pro magician. Played the Théâtre Bleuettes-Comiques in Paris in 1789. Soon left magic to become a politician. [Dif]

name: Powell, Bert
bio: (Huntingdon, Herefordshire, England: 15 Feb 1876-) Stage name of Frank E. Gerrard. Inspired at age 9. Pro with magic, second sight, dark & light séances, & memory feats. Worked a time with Professor Acton. Played England (occasionally), the British Asian colonies (including Singapore in 1897), Greece (1899), South Africa (1899-1902, as "The Military Mystic"), & Cairo (1902). Aka "Kuang Sen" with a pseudo-Chinese act, "Hyza Khan" with pseudo-Indian act, & "Morinura" with pseudo-Japanese act, but usually as "Stuart Wayne". Also did a clairvoyancy act as "Mysteria". Aka "Klimax". [St;Vo56;Magic10/1900,2/02,12/02]

name: Powell, Frederick Eugene
bio: (Chester, Pennsylvania: 1 Mar 1856-27 Feb 1938) Inspired in 1862 seeing Signor Blitz show in Philadelphia. Amateur debut at age 16. Pro since 1876. Toured USA, West Indies, Mexico, & South America. With partners Le Roy & Imro Fox as "The Great Triple Alliance" toured the USA & Canada 1898-1900. In 1902 toured Hawaii, Australia, & New Zealand. Made 2nd South American tour. In 1909 made 3rd South American tour. Named 2nd Dean of American Magicians in 1922. Lived in New Haven since 1924 in semi-retirement. Willed his props & memorabilia to John A. Petrie. Bio is Thomas A. Ewing, Frederick Eugene Powell: The Man and His Magic (1986). [Pr; MUM6/92; Wal; Go2; Ho]

name: Powell, Ralph Emerson
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 12 Nov 1903-) Pro comedy magician since 1921 in vaudeville & since 1925 with full-evening show. [WWM]

name: Powers, Chris
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s-90s) Pro close-up magician resident in London. Played the Hollywood Magic Castle with partner J.J. Johnson. Co-editor (with J.J. Johnson) of Opus, 1987-present. Video: Laid Back Too (1990, with "J.J.").

name: Powers, Clyde W.
bio: (USA: 15 Jul 1876-21 Oct 1930) Stage manager of the Hippodrome in New York City. Semi-pro magician. Briefly co-owned Powers and Dane magic shop in NYC. Manager of Gilbert & Petrie's Mysto Magic Shop (in the Weber & Fields Theatre building) since 1910. Then in 1914 Powers bought out the Mysto Magic Shop to found the Clyde W. Powers Magic Shop on 42nd Street. Later that year he bought out Yost & Company of Philadelphia. Powers was bought out in the 1920s by Frank Ducrot.

name: Powers, Michael [Thomas] "Mike
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 20 Jan 1947-) Teacher in LaPorte, Indiana. Learned magic at age 30. Semi-pro close-up magician specialized in cards & coins since age 35. Invented Holey Terror (1983) & Quarter Fusion (1983). Wrote Powerful Magic (1983, 105pp) & Top Secret Stuff: The Close Up Magic of Michael Powers (1990, 172pp). Tricks in Apocalypse & MUM. [MUM3/94;Wh5]

name: Pozniak, Stefan
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 7 Jul 1937-) Pro illusionist & manipulator. Vice-president of Krajowy Klub Iluzjionistów, then President since 1991. Wrote Magia niejedno ma imie (1990, 101pp). [Mec;Nad]

name: Pozsonyi
bio: (Székesfehérvár, Hungary: 5 Feb 1919-) Stage name of Sándor SZÁVA. Debut in 1936-38 in circus. Pro apparatus magician plus some pickpocket work. Since 1947 worked a 2-hour stage illusion show with several assistants. Honored member of Corodini Magic Club in Budapest.

name: Pozzi, Piero
bio: (Milan, Italy: -16 Dec 1976) Pro manip as "Karton". Articles in Magia Moderna & Vademecum del Prestidigiatore. (England: 15 Dec 1947-) Learned in 1962 buying tricks. Lawyer. 1974 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. Semi-pro close-up & cabaret magician since 1974. Pet effects: C&R Rope, Pratt, Chris[topher Leslie], MIMC Sponge Balls. Secretary of The Magic Circle since 1985. Articles in Magic Circular, Abracadabra, & MUM. [Daw2;Wh2]

name: Pratt, [Herbert E.] "Bert", MIMC
bio: (Britain: c1900-18 Jan 1985) Heating engineer. Amateur & magic collector with over 3,000 books. In 1950s helped edit The Midget Magician, under joint pen name (with Wilfred Huggins) of "Albert F. Wind". Librarian of the Magic Circle's Reference Library until 1960 when succeeded by Henry Davies. Under pen name of "Ptinos" wrote articles for Collectors Annual & the "Browsing Around" column (1951-60) on collecting for The Midget Magician, which was reprinted under his own name as Browsing Around in Magic (1972, 52pp). [Wad]

name: Pratt, E[dgar] L[awton]
bio: (USA: c1879-) Pro card sharp since a youth when taught by Dr Gardner Groves in Providence, Rhode Island. "Missing a third finger of his left hand allowed him to deal very clean bottoms", as Martin Gardner saw. A close friend of Erdnase (1897-1905) & James Harto. Later a pro card magician, as "Maxo". Retired in Philadelphia long before 1949 when Gardner interviewed him there.

name: Press, Percy
bio: (London, England: 1902-28 Apr 1980) Inspired by & learned from some tricks bought around age 13. Pro. Column in Hughes' News. Memoir is A Traveller's Tale (audiotape). Father of:

name: Press Jr, Percy
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Stage name of Leslie Press. Inspired by & learned from father Percy Press. Pro. Also does Punch & Judy.

name: Presti, Peter
bio: (Holland: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Pieter Betlem. Pro close-up magician.

name: Presti, Tony
bio: See: Vander Linden, Anthony

name: Presto
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro magician & fire-eater. [Des]

name: Presto, Dr.
bio: See: White, Ralph

name: Presto, Fay
bio: (Highgate, London, England: 17 May 1948-) Stage name of Letitia Mary "Tish" Winter since 1984. Male cross-dresser since age 18. Refers to herself explicitly as a "transsexual" (but no surgery) & cunningly as "A woman with a history but no past." Self-taught magic at age 35. Pro (ex-motorcycle messenger) cabaret close-up magicienne since 1984. Helped create the London fashion for cabaret close-up & table-hopping since the mid-1980s. Reputedly the highest paid magicienne in Britain by 1989. REF: Kris Kirk & Ed Heath, Men in Frocks (1984), 78-80. [Genii3/88;Wh2]

name: Presto, Valentine
bio: See: Chudleigh, Reginald

name: Preston, Al
bio: (Holland: 17 Aug 1929-Jul 1980) Stage name of Arnoldus Noordchoek. 1964 FISM 1st prize (shared) in general magic for "Al Preston & Valerie". Starred at Cabinet Fantastique in Paris 1971-72 & 1975-76. [Dif]

name: Preston, Paul
bio: (USA: fl.1850s-60s) Stage name of Thomas Picton. Pro. Wrote The Fireside Magician (New York: Dick & Fitzgerald, 1870, 132pp).

name: Preston, William
bio: (Pineville, Kentucky: 6 May 1915- ) Stage name of William Preston Slusher. Learned at age c14 from Tarbell Course. Pro with full-evening show. Plays mainly college shows. Pet effects: Vanishing Bird Cage & Needle Swallowing. Article in Linking Ring. IBM President 1977-78 [?.....]. [Wh2]

name: Prevost, J.
bio: (Toulouse, France: c1520-1592) Amateur magician and friend of poets. Evidence collected by Jacques Voignier indicates J. Prevost is possibly the French poet Jean Prevost. Author of evidently the world's first book devoted entirely to conjuring, La Premiere partie des svbtiles et plaisantes inventions (Lyon: 1584, 96 leaves of text plus 4 of table of contents (=200pp), including 34 woodcuts; facsimile reprint 1987). That this book probably precedes Scot's work of the same year is suggested by the 1 & 2 Jan 1584 dates of its prefaces. Explains many popular tricks of his day, including the Egg Bag, Paddle Trick, Grandmother's Necklace, the Funnel, Ice Pick, Bridle, Blood Writing on the Arm, Flick Book, & Himber Wallet. Omits card tricks, Cups-and-Balls, and the Bonus Genius, which were probably planned for a promised but evidently never published second volume. An English tr is Clever and Pleasant Inventions: Part One (1998, 231 pp, edited by Todd Karr & Stephen Minch). [Dif;Bo#232]

name: Price [Jr], David [Livingston]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 15 Dec 1910-30 Jul 1998) Inspired at age 6 seeing a minister perform tricks. Joined the IBM in 1929 (#3245). Pro magician 1930-40 as David Price, "Dave Price", & "De Livingston". Retired from stage by foot injuries in WW II to become a CPA auditor with the IRS 1947-64. Thence a major amateur collector of magicana. Owner & archivist of Durban's Egyptian Hall properties since 1953 when he bought them from Thomas Dowd. Price's Egyptian Hall Museum of Magical History (now in Brentwood, Tennessee) is now "50 or 60 times the size of the original Durbin collection." Wrote Magic: A Pictorial History of Conjurers in the Theater (1985, 551pp), a useful & nearly comprehensive book. Articles & card tricks in Sphinx, Linking Ring, Genii, Conjurors' Magazine, New Tops, & 13 other magic journals. His son, David Price III, a former magician himself, took over the Museum on his father's death in 1998. [LR10/98;LR8/94;Bo#196;Se;Wh2]

name: Price, Harry
bio: (Shrewsbury-Salop, England: 17 Feb 1881-29 Mar 1948). Famous professional psychic researcher. Magic collector. Presented his fine collection of books on magic & psychic phenomena to the London U Library in 1936. Wrote several major books on psychic phenomena, including Revelations of a Spirit Medium (1922, as co-editor with Eric J. Dingwall), Short Title Catalogue (1929), Rudi Schneider (1930, 239pp), Leaves from a Psychist's Case-Book (1933), Supplement to Short Title Catalogue (1935), The Haunting of Cashen's Gap (1936, 211pp, with Lambert), Confessions of a Ghost-Hunter (1936), 50 Years of Psychical Research (1939, 383pp), The Most Haunted House in England (1940, 255pp), Search for Truth (1942), Poltergeist over England (1945, 423pp), & The End of Borley Rectory (1946, 358pp). Exposés of Price's own fraudulent writings on Borley Rectory are Dingwall, Goldney, & Hall, The Haunting of Borley Rectory (1955) and Trevor H. Hall, Search for Harry Price (1978). Bio is Paul Tabori, Harry Price: The Biography of a Ghost-hunter (1950, 316pp); Tabori & Underwood, The Ghosts of Borley (1973, 240pp). [Go;Go2;St;La2]

name: Pridmore, Sydney S.
bio: (England: -Oct 1895) Student of Charles Bertram. Pro society magician since 1885. Committed suicide, reportedly after unintended rude behavior during performance before the Prince of Wales. [CI]

name: Priestley, J[ohn] B[oynton]
bio: (Bradford, England: 1894-1984) Famous English novelist. Amateur magician and one-time member of The Magic Circle. Wrote the Introduction to Devant's My Magic Life (1931). Wrote The Magicians (1954), Lost Empires (1965), etc.

name: Prince, Arthur [Joseph]
bio: (London, England: 17 Nov 1881-14 Apr 1948) Amateur expert all-round magician and top pro ventriloquist. Vice-President of the Magicians' Club. Wrote The Whole Art of Ventriloquism (1915, 94pp). [Go2;Lau;Dif] "Prince, Charles A." SEE: Andrade, Will

name: Prince, James
bio: (England: fl.1980s) Stage name of Jim Eckford.

name: Prince, Dr Walter Franklin, PhD
bio: (Detroit, Maine: 22 Apr 1863-7 Aug 1934) PhD 1899. Prominent psychic researcher since 1917, having written several books on the subject. [WWWA]

name: Print, John
bio: See: Karr, Todd

name: Priolé, Henry
bio: (France?: fl.1910s) Pro illusionist. Worked Germany in 1911.

name: Pritchett, Logan
bio: (USA: c1925-26 Mar 1989) Pro magician, aka "Dr. Zuko". Tricks in New Phoenix. 1969 TAOM Comedy Trophy. Dealer in Little Rock, Arkansas, calling himself "the near honest dealer".

name: Proctor, F[rederick] F[reeman]
bio: (Dexter, Maine: 1852-4 Sep 1929) Ex-juggler (as "Levantine"). Major vaudeville impresario in the USA from 1880 until 1929 when he sold to RKO just before his death. Bio is W.M. Marston & J.H. Feller, F.F. Proctor: Vaudeville Pioneer (1943, 191pp). [Lau] "Professor, The" [nickname] SEE: Vernon, Dai

name: Pronk, Eugene C. "Gene
bio: (USA: c1921-24 Feb 1999) Aka "Marlowe the Magician" & "Pronk the Magician". Learned magic at age 8. Pro magician & escape artist since 1940. Took over from Card Mondor as "Dr. Ogre Banshee" c1946. In 1947 bought John Calvert's spook-show which he toured for a time. Then, under own name, trouped his big (14 assistants) "Magic and Model Show". Then long-time dealer in Oklahoma City. [St]

name: Proskauer, Hugo
bio: (England?: fl.1860s-80s) Pro magic teacher and performer. Played the Royal Polytechnic Institution and the Crystal Palace. Dealer-manufacturer (Hugo Proskauer's Magical Repository) founded in 1866 in London at 480 Oxford Street. In 1876 had legal squabbles with his neighboring magic dealer, Joseph Bland. The shop operated until at least 1882 when the address was renumbered 29/31 New Oxford Street. It issued 2 catalogs, including 1882/83 (94pp). [Daw94]

name: Proskauer, Julien J.
bio: (New York City, NY: 14 Jun 1893-18 Dec 1958). Printer-businessman. Amateur magician since 1909 & psychic investigator. Aka "Psycho". SAM President 1935-36. Headed the splinter group from the SAM that founded the Magicians Guild of America in 1944. Published Conjurors' Magazine 1945-47. Wrote Spook Crooks! (1932, 300pp); How'd ja do That? (1934, 92pp), a piracy of Johnston & Sterling's Modern Card Miracles (1919); Suckers All! (1934, 318pp); Puzzles for Everyone (191pp); & The Dead Do Not Talk (1946, 198pp, ghosted by Walter B. Gibson). Articles in Sphinx & Conjurors' Magazine & tricks in Genii. [SAM; Go2; St]

name: Prost, Jean-Yves
bio: (Lyon, France: 23 May 1944- ) At age 15 or 16 inspired & taught by Diavol. Physician in Lyon. Amateur close-up magician since age 28. Aka "Hivaldo". President of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Lyon magic club 1972-present. AFAP Bronze Medal 1977 & Silver Medal 1983. Co-publisher-editor (with Michel Balandras) Arcane 1975-present. Organizer since 1978 of the "EuroTour" lecture circuit for many American magicians. [Wh5]

name: Proudlock, Edward
bio: (South Bank, Yorkshire, England: 4 Jun 1882-9 Jan 1958) Stage name of Edmund Dunn Proudlock. Learned magic at age 9. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand. Pet effect: Linking Rings. 1928 Magicians' Club Gold Medal. See Bagshawe, Proudlock's Version of Sympathetic Silks [1936, 22pp]; & Bagshawe, Proudlock's Routine with Thimbles (nd, 32pp). Trick in Magic Wand. [Go;Go2

name: Proudlove, Julie
bio: See: "Llusion, Julie"

name: Proudlove, Stan[ley W.]
bio: (England: fl.1970s-80s) Aka "Dovini". Pro. Father of "Julie Llusion".

name: Proust, Georges
bio: (France: 1945-) Pro card magician & mentalist, specialized in private shows as "Jo Prest". Founding member of Club Magique de Paris in 1969. Dealer-teacher (Académie de Magie) in Paris. Collector of books, catalogs, & props. Founded his Musée de la Magie in 1993 in Paris. Wrote Les techniques de base de la prestidigitation (1983), Magie du feu (1984), & The Magic of Finn Jon (1984). [Bou]

name: Prunier, Russell
bio: (USA: fl.1930s). Pro. Invented Linking Coathangers (1939). Trick in Jinx.

name: Pryor, [Charles William] "Bill
bio: (Wheeling, West Virginia: 12 Jan 1934-) Inspired in 1946 seeing a Blackstone show. Math teacher in Edgewood, Kentucky. Semi-pro comedy platform & strolling magician since 1960. Pet effects: Passe Passe Bottles & a Pitch Act. Co-founder-partner in Venture III since 1982. Invented The Impossible Dream, Bionic Card, Mental Block, etc. Articles in Mortimer's Magazine & MUM. [Wh5]

name: Ptinos
bio: See: Pratt, Herbert

name: Puchinger, Günter
bio: (Wels, Austria: 17 Jul 1940-) Learned at age 18. Major pro magic dealer-manufacturer-inventer in West Germany since 1970, originally alone. Then as co-founder & partner (with R. Braunmüller) of Zauberzentrale München 1975-81. Then again on own (as "G. Puchinger"), first in Munich, now since 1985 in Raisting. Specializes in making illusions, stage magic, special effects, & props for pro European magicians, circuses, theaters, etc. Also produces complete magic shows for amusement & holiday parks. Performs with partner as "Die Carmans". Invented several major illusions, including Kubus (1974), Kub-Zag (1984), & Mini-Kub-Zag (1987). Also Puppe zu Frau & Super-Simplex-Appearance. Writes his firm's bi-monthly, Kundeninformation. [Wh2]

name: Puech, Didier
bio: (Toulouse, France: 1 Jan c1963-) Learned in 1980 from books by Jacques Delord. Amateur since age 17. Collector. Editor of Magicus Journal since 1980?. Articles in Magicus Journal, Arcane, & Illusionniste. [Wh5]

name: Puff, Dr. Harold F[rederick]
bio: (Newport, Kentucky: 5 Jan 1916-) Inspired at age 10 seeing Thurston show & learned from catalog tricks. Professor of Management at Miami U 1948-82 when retired. Semi-pro magic lecturer & collector. Column in The Dragon. Articles in Sphinx, MUM, Linking Ring, Genii, Tops. [Wh5]

name: Pulè, Vanni
bio: (Kalkara, Malta: 18 May 1949- ) Debut at age 14. College lecturer. Top pro entertainer in Malta since 1970, working as cabaret magician & stage illusionist, fire eater, musician, and until recently, as composer & singer. Works magic with assistant-wife MaryAnne. Wrote The Magic of Vanni Pulè #1 (28pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Magiram, Magic Info, & Adair's Encyclopedia of Dove Magic #5. Many local TV bits. [Trixigram9/89;Wh2]

name: Punjab -- India's Royal Illusionist
bio: See: "Clifford, Jack J."

name: Punx
bio: (Hartlebury, Worcestershire, England: 27 Oct 1907-11 Feb 1996) Stage name since 1940s of Ludwig Franz Wilhelm Hanemann, of German parents. Moved to Germany as a boy. Inspired when grandfather took him to see Dante, soon becoming an avid amateur with his debut in 1930. In 1932 co-founded the Bremen branch of the German Magic Circle. Profession: advertising salesman. Serving as an NCO in German Army medical corps in WW II, he was captured in France in 1944 and interned in Britain where he began performing as "Punx". Repatriated to West Germany in 1946. Pro since 1948 when became the 3rd recipient of the Hofzinser Ring (for his innovative act of magic as theater), which was re-awarded in 1950 for life. On retiring in 1985 he passed the Ring to Werner Geissler-Werry. Dean (for life) of the PEA since 1989. Now lives in Munich. Prolific inventor. His "Der Wahrtraum" was PEA's 1984 best mental trick of the year. Wrote 32 Blatt und lauter Rätsel (1950, 32pp); Setz Euch zu meinen Füssen (1977, 82pp), English tr by Bill Palmer as Magical Adventures and Fairy Tales (1989, 92pp); Der Wahrtaum (1978), English tr by Robert Cassidy as The Prophetic Dream (1980); Meine drei besten Kartenroutinen (1985, 24pp); Experimente mit dem Überraum (8 vols, 1978-85?), English tr by Bill Palmer as Fourth Dimensional Mysteries (1990, 237pp); Abschiedsvorstellung (1987, 136pp), English tr by Bill Palmer as Farewell Performance (1991, 198pp); etc, etc. 119 articles in Magie (since 1932), Liliput, Magisches Magazin, Magische Welt, Mentalists Technical Bulletin, New Invocation, Vibrations, Seance, & Linking Ring (1994). Did 46 prime-time shows on German TV. [LR5/89,85-86;Win]

name: Purssord, Walter
bio: (England: -Aug 1905) Pro music hall magician. [CI]

name: Purvis, William "Billy
bio: (Auchindinny, near Edinburgh, Scotland: 13 Jan 1784-16 Dec 1853) Moved to Newcastle around age 2. Billed as "The Newcastle Conjuror". Originally trained as a carpenter & joiner. Learned successively from three travelling conjurors: Monsieur Peru (a Frenchman), Sanshias (a German), and Mr. Hunt (an Englishman). Debut in 1819. Thence a minor pro comedy magician who toured Scotland & northern England. Bios are Joseph Philip Robson, The Life and Adventures of the Far-Famed Billy Purvis (1849, 240pp), which was commissioned by Purvis for £20; [Thomas Arthur], The Life of Billy Purvis (1851, 144pp; reprints); & Allen Berlinski, Purvis: The Newcastle Conjuror (1981, 40pp).

name: Putter, Professor J.P.
bio: See: Makman, Mike

name: Pyle, Jack
bio: (USA: -18 Jul 1987) Pro memory & card expert since 1950s in Chicago.

name: Q, Dr." [pen name]
bio: See: Conlin [Sr], Claude Alexander Larsen [Sr], William W.

name: Queen, Trixie
bio: (England: 1 Jun 1906- ) Stage name of Ida Emily Want until married W. Richmond Murray. This 4'11½" [sic] tall entertainer worked clubs as a novelty whistling & male-impersonation act until 1944 when inspired to take up magic by one of Willane's magic booklets. Thence pro magicienne in male-evening dress until retired "when I realized I was no longer the image I'd always aimed at--the favorite nephew of the old lady in the front row." [Mar]

name: Quick, Count
bio: See: Colville, Charles

name: Quick, Mr.
bio: See: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Quimby, Dr Shirley L[eon], PhD
bio: (San Francisco, California: 21 Aug 1893-15 May 1986) Professor of Physics at Columbia U. Amateur magician. One of few men entrusted with Dr Samuel C. Hooker's famous "Impossibilities". Past editor of MUM. [SAM;Daw2]

name: Quine, John [David] [pronounced KWINE]
bio: (Akron, Ohio: 29 Aug 1941- ) Learned at age 10 from Mysto Magic set. Machinist. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 13, specialized in cards & coins. Invented Quines Keeper. Tricks in Apocalypse, Linking Ring, & Mentzer's Card Cavalcade. See Tom Craven, The Card Magic of John Quine (1988, 20pp). [Wh2]

name: Quinn, John P[hilip] [pronounced KWIN]
bio: (Randolph County, Missouri: 19 Mar 1846-) Left home at age 14 to become a professional gambler. In 1888, after 25 years as a card sharp & confidence man, he reformed. Then wrote such gambling exposés as Fools of Fortune; or, Gambling and Gamblers (1890; repr 1892, 640pp; 1895), 19th Century Black Art; or, Gambling Exposed (1891, 104pp; repr 1896), The Highway to Hell (1895, 58pp, as taken from his 1891 book), Gambling and Gambling Devices (1912, 306pp; repr 1969), and Why Gamblers Win (n.d.). On the exposé lecture circuit in Britain 1907-10, including 10 weeks in 1909 in London at St. George's Hall. Still lecturing in the USA as late as 1912 at age 67. Avid amateur magician in his later years, frequenting Clyde Powers' magic shop in New York City around WW I. REF: Jinx, 785.

name: Quy, Tuck
bio: See: Tuck Quy

name: Rabelais, François
bio: (France: c1494-1553) Satirical writer. His Pantagruel (1532) refers to the cups-&-balls in Chapters 1 & 16 and his Gargantua (1534) refers to French conjurors in Chapter 24. See Todd Karr, "R[a]belais and Magic", Linking Ring (Aug 1996), 54-55.

name: Raboid, Rajah [pronounced RAY-boyd]
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 22 Jan 1896-11 Jan 1962) Stage name of Maurice P. Kitchen. Pro. Began in carnivals with a minor illusion show as "Ray Boyd". In 1924 as "Rajah Raboid" switched to mind-reading & crystal-gazing at which he was very successful. Specialized in Ghost Shows after 1930. On 17 May 1931 made world's 1st blindfold airplane flight. To avoid US laws against radio mind-reading, in 1933 he broadcast out of Laredo Nuevo, Mexico. In late 1930s used "half"-man Johnny Eck in the Sawing for one spectacular performance. Died wealthy in a mansion in Florida, contrary to rumors of poverty. [Pr;Bo#163;Walk2]

name: Raceford, Royal
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-30s) Pro illusionist. Bought Devant's "Magical Master" act in 1917. After Chung Ling Soo's death toured a copy act since 1918. [Daw2] Racherbaumer, Jon [William] "Rock" "Rocky" (Elmhurst, Illinois: 22 Jan 1940-) Inspired by age 9 seeing Tarbell's full-evening show in Elmhurst. Learned at age 9 when friend taught him to vanish a nickle in a glass of water &, later, by reading. Semi-pro close-up to amateur cardman (while working for an airline). Pet effect: Ambitious Card. Ed Marlo's main student & amanuensis since 1968 when they first met. Editor-writer of Hierophant 1969-71, Kabbala 1971-73, Avatar 1973, & Sticks and Stones 1977-78. Invented the Shank Shuffle (1972). Prolific author, including The Artful Dodges of Eddie Fields (1968, 109pp), The Universal Card (1975, 35pp), The Ascanio Spread (1976, 35pp), The Lost Pages of the Kabbala (1981), Card Finesse (1982), Marlo Without Tears (1983, 317pp), At the Table (1984, 192pp), Cardfixes (1990, 200+pp), The Wild Card Kit (1992, 88pp), Card Finesse II (1992, 278pp), Paul Diamond's Big-Easy Card Cunning (1992, 44pp). "Sticks and Stones" column in New Tops since 1990. Since 1970 occasionally uses pen name "Jonathan Dunbury". Tricks in Talisman, New Directions, & Genii. 1 video (forthcoming 1991). Associate Editor of Genii since Nov 1999 ("Jan 2000" issue). [Lo;Wh2]

name: Radine
bio: (Columbia: 25 Jul 1905-) Stage name of Guillermo Isquierdo Guerrero. Learned as assistant for 20 years to South American magician "Prof. Navarro". Then on own as pro mentalist with female assistant.

name: Radner, Sidney H[ollis] "Sid
bio: (Holyoke, Massachusetts: 8 Dec 1919 – 25 Jun 2011) Learned at age 9 from magic set. Owner of rug-cleaning plant in his home town until semi-retired in 1988. Semi-pro escape artist since 1941, now turned to gambling sleights & lecturing on gambling cheating. Has one of 2 or 3 largest collections of gambling devices in USA, having begun collecting in 1939. Donated most of his collection of Houdini props & memorabilia (world's largest since 1942) to the Houdini Museum in Appleton, Wisconsin in 1989, with lesser items to the Houdini Magical Hall of Fame at Niagara Falls in Canada. 1991 AIMC. Due to the unethical exposure practices of the Houdini Museum, withdrew his collection by 2004. Authored Magic for Fun (1956, 93pp, ghosted by Walter B. Gibson), How to Play Poker and Win (1957, 94pp, ghosted by Gibson), Radner on Dice (95pp), How to Spot Card Sharps and Their Methods (1957, 95pp, ghosted by Gibson), Harry Houdini's Magic Books in The Library of Congress (forthcoming), etc. Featured as a comic book character in Racket Squad in Action magazine in 1950s. [Bo#268;WWA;Wh2]

name: Rae, Oswald "Ossie
bio: (Reading, Berkshire, England: 19 Dec 1892-8 Oct 1967) Theatrical journalist and pro patter magician. Founded the IBM's British Ring in 1928 and was its President 1928-44. Played New York City 1930. Invented Flexible Glass (before 1946). Wrote 8 books & booklets, including Practical Patter (1922), More Practical Patter, Between Ourselves (1926, 91pp), Sub Rosa (1928, 108pp), Original Magic (1930), Wizardry with Watches, & The More You Watch (1938). Articles in Demon Telegraph. [Go2;St;Ho]

name: Rafayelle
bio: See: Dennison, Gene

name: Raffles, Mark
bio: (Manchester, England: 22 Jan 1919-) Stage name of Albert Taylor Jr. Inspired at age c5 watching semi-pro uncle perform. Pro magician since 1938, originally with a silent manip act as "Ray St. Clair" & "F.V. St. Clair". With ENSA 1943-45. Pick-pocket act since mid-1940s, taking "Mark Raffles" as his more appropriate stage name in 1950. Coached Patricia Hayes for her pick-pocket role in film The Corn is Green (1945). Turned illusionist with assistant-wife Joan in 1984 after they bought Jack & Audrey Shaw's "Wychwoods" act involving various illusions with their troupe of miniature poodles. 1986 British Magical Grand Prix Champion. Father of Tim Raffles. Wrote The Pickpocket Secrets of Mark Raffles (1982), etc. Column ("Rich Pickings") in Abra. Video (1989). Autobio is Diamond Jubilee Memoirs: Magic All the Way (1997, 126pp). REF: Dawes in Magic Circular (Jul-Sep 1988), 128-131, 156-159, 184-187. [L R1/06; R2; Hudd] [LR1/06;Bo2;Hudd]

name: Raffles, Tim
bio: (Manchester, England: 10 Dec 1951-) Stage name of Tim Taylor. Son of Mark Raffles from whom he learned magic at age 10. Pro general magic since age 30 with partner as "Raffles & Dallas". Pet effects: doves & fire. [Wh2]

name: Rai, Senor [pronounced RAY]
bio: (USA?: fl.1970s-80s) Pro magician. With Hanneford Circus 1973-88. In 1988 at Vegas World's "Rocket Ship 1999" show.

name: Raimondi, Vinicio
bio: (Rome, Italy: 5 Feb 1938- ) Learned card tricks in 1949 from a family friend. Mechanical engineer. Semi-pro magician-manipulator since 1965 & full-time pro since 1980. Pet effect: Cigarette Manip. Works cruise ships, TV, etc. Collector (c700 books). Invented Raimondi Silx in 1975 (Supreme exclusive). Wrote Nove Lezioni per Diventare un Mago (1983, 166pp), Il Libro della Magia (1986, 174pp), Magia della Sigarette (1988, 196pp), Lezioni de Arte Magica (5 vols, 1982-1991, c1,000pp, with Lamberto Desideri). Articles in Magia Moderna, Le Magicien, Qui Magia. [Qui Magia5/91;Wh5]

name: Rainho, James "Jim
bio: (Fermelã, Aveiro, Portugal: 6 Aug 1930-) Born Caetano Rainho. Moved to USA in 1939. Learned in 1943-44 working a carnival side-show at Revere Beach, Massachusetts. Pro since 1947 as club & cabaret magician & mentalist. In US Army 1951-53. Since 1962 pro prop-maker & dealer as James Rainho Products-Simplex Magic, which he founded in Cambridge & moved to Medford (both in Massachusetts) in 1966. Also works mentalism as "Mr. James" and kid shows as "Mr. Magic", "Capt. Mephisto", & "Sheriff Jim". Prolific inventor, including Color Changing Records (in 1947), Flame of Kan-Del (1955), and Voodoo Rite (1974). Wrote Jim Rainho's Pass Out (1978, 8pp). Tricks in Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, Magick, & Ireland Year Books. [MUM2/92;Cam;Wh2] "Rajah Brothers, The" SEE UNDER: King, Harry

name: Rajah, Prince
bio: (Scotland: c1931-) Stage name of David Haggerty. Retired Rolls Royce worker. Semi-pro magician. 1958 British Ring Dittia Shield. Specializes in stage illusions & cutting out a lady's tongue. Assistants have been his sister Maisie & now Margaret MacLean.

name: Raji, Prince Ali
bio: See: Bodinei, George

name: Ralston
bio: See: Fink, Ray J.

name: Ram, Master
bio: (Ellmore, India: 7 Jul 1898-) Pro psychic act. Wrote booklets on palmistry. [Go2]

name: Rama
bio: (Holland: fl.1950s-60s) FISM 1st prizes for invention, 1958 & 1964. [Dif]

name: RaMayne, Dr. Korda
bio: See: Nelson, Robert

name: Rameses
bio: (London, England: 1876-31 Jul 1930) Stage name of Albert Marchinski. Actor to pro magician & illusionist (by 1909 to at least 1929) to theater owner. Had played the Palladium in 1911. [Pr;Go2;Daw;St;Magic6/10]

name: Ramigani
bio: (Krakow, Poland: 1907-Jun 1982) Stage name of Jan Ławrusiewicz. Pro illusionist & manipulator. [Mec]

name: Ramiro
bio: (Spain?: fl.1920s-30s) Aka "Don Ramiro". Pro illusionist who performed in Germany 1921-32. Pet effect: Vanishing Automobile.

name: Ramo Samee
bio: (Seringapatam, India: -24 Jul 1849) Pro magician & juggler. In England 1815-38, USA 1819-20. [Daw;Cl;Mo]

name: Ramo, Rajah
bio:
Ramon. The Great (USA: -1969) Stage name of John Hanniford. Pro.

[See also: "Ray-Mond"]

name: Ramos, Horácio
bio: (Portugal: 10 Mar 1854-28 Sep 1931) Stage name of Horácio GUIMARÃES RAMOS. Amateur magician. In 1880 built a small theater in Oporto for performance by himself & other amateurs. 1897 Concurso de Ilusionismo 2nd place. Co-founded the Internacional Instituto de Recreações Scientificas in 1912. Teacher of S.J. Martins Oliveira. [Cam]

name: Ramos Pinto, António
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 20 Aug 1854-17 Dec 1944) Amateur who performed while travelling widely abroad (Spain, France, Germany, England). With brother José RAMOS PINTO performed as the Ravemport Irmãos [Brothers]. In 1912 co-founded the International Instituto de Recreações Scientificas. [Cam;St]

name: Ramsay, John "Johnny", MIMC
bio: (Ayr, Scotland: 13 Mar 1877-16 Jan 1962) Inspired by & learned from mother who taught him a couple of simple tricks at age 7. Grocery store owner. Celebrated amateur close-up magician. British Ring Past President. 1946 Amsterdam International Magic Congress 2nd prize; 1947 Paris International Magic Congress 2nd prize in manip; 1949 FISM 2nd prize in manip, 1950 FISM 1st prize in close-up. Mentor of Andrew Galloway. Bio section in Andrew Galloway, The Ramsay Legend (1969, 62pp; repr 1975; 2nd rev ed, 1985). See also Galloway, The Ramsay Classics (1978, 112pp) & The Ramsay Finale (1982, 86pp). And Victor Farelli's John Ramsay's Routine with Cups and Balls (1948, 88pp); John Ramsay's Cylinder & Coins (1948, 33pp), John Ramsay's Triple Restoration (1949, 21pp), & Four Little Beans (1952, 19pp). A 45-minute video-tape of Galloway presenting Ramsay's effects first appeared in 1985 (reissued 1989). [Le;Go2]

name: Ramsés, Conde
bio: (Belém, Brazil: 5 Jun 1942-c1987) Stage name of Roberto, Conde [Count] dos Reis Cavalero. Published-edited Magirama 1967-75. Wrote several booklets. [Fam]

name: Randal, Jason
bio: (USA: 1950-) A karate teacher with Chuck Norris Schools, learned magic by trading karate lessons for magic with Paul Green. Pro escape artist & comedy mentalist since 1973. MA in sociology in 1976 & PhD in social psychology from Columbia Pacific U in 1982. Wrote The Psychology of Deception: Why Magic Works (1982, 208pp) & Magic for Professionals. Article in Genii (1976). Many TV bits since 1982. Played the magician in Tequila Sunrise (1988) and did the opening credit coin tricks for movie Pretty Woman (1990). [Jef; Mag;Wh]

name: Randall, Charlie
bio: (Durango, Colorado: 15 Aug 1958-) Systems engineer. Amateur magician. Magic publisher as co-owner (with Richard Hatch) of H&R Magic Books. Tricks and articles in Apocalypse, Magick, & Magic. [Wb011]

name: Randall, Kelley
bio: (Natrang, Vietnam: 25 Aug 1967- ) Daughter of "Johnny Aladdin" & "Taki". Raised in California. Model in Japan. Taught magic by mother, then father. Pro as assistant in Aladdin's show in Las Vegas & at Magic Castle in 1988. Now TV acting & real estate in Los Angeles. [Wh]

name: Randi, James
bio: (Leaside, Toronto, Canada: 7 Aug 1928-) Stage name of James Hamilton Randall Zwinge until legally changed in 1984 to James Randi. Inspired at age 12 seeing Blackstone show, then self-taught by buying tricks. Pro since 1946 (age 17) when joined travelling carnival as pseudo-psychic mentalist "Prince Ibis". Moved to USA in 1948. Thence pro escape artist & straight magic. Invented & marketed Ghost Window in 1958. A leading debunker of psychic fraud. Co-founded CSICOP in 1976. 1986 McArthur Foundation Fellowship ($272,000 over 5 years). SAM Hall of Fame. 1989 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. In 1989 he designated Dean Gunnarson, his main protégé, as his successor as escapist, and gave Gunnarson his apparatus. IQ: 168. Wrote The Magic of Uri Geller (1975, 308pp), Houdini (1976, 191pp, with Bert Sugar), Flim-Flam! (1980, 340pp), The Truth about Uri Geller (1982), Test Your ESP Potential (1983), The Faith Healers (1987, 314pp), The Amazing Randi's World of Magic (1989), The Mask of Nostradamus (1990), & Conjuring (1992, 314pp). Tricks in HMM, Ibidem, Swami, Chronicles, etc. Many TV bits & specials. 2 audios. Wh2] [Bo2;CA;WWA;WWE;HC;True7/56;HHM9/56,5/58;

name: Randlett, Sam[uel Ludwick]
bio: (Newark, New Jersey: 11 Jan 1930-) Learned at age 10 from Camel's It's Fun to be Fooled booklet, then Fischer's Illustrated Magic. Piano teacher. Amateur close-up & card magician. Also origami expert. Wrote The Art of Origami (1961, 192pp) & The Best of Origami (1963, 185pp). Articles & tricks in HMM & Ibidem. Edited The Flapping Bird: An Origami Monthly (25 issues). [Wh2]

name: Rani
bio: (Sweden: 15 Oct 1896-23 [sic] Feb 1973) Stage name of Willy Nord. Pro with pseudo-Indian act.

name: Rannie, John
bio: (Scotland: fl.1780s-1810s) Learned c1784. Promagus-vent in USA & Caribbean, 1801-1811. Performed Card on Ceiling in Boston in 1802, evidently its premier in the USA. Wrote The European Ventriloquist's Exhibition (Portsmouth, New England: 1808, 10pp brochure). Bio is Charles Pecor, The Ten Year Tour of John Rannie. [Ch;Mo]

name: Ransom, Elmer P[endleton]
bio: (New York City, NY: 19 Sep 1862-2 Feb 1942) Inspired at age 6 seeing Bonus Genus done by his father. Pro since 1880. Played Tony Pastor's Theatre in 1890. Joined SAM in May 1902 as Member #20. SAM President 1910-11. Articles in Sphinx. [St;Ho;WWM] Ransom, T[homas] S[aunders] "Tom" "Tommy" (Toronto, Ontario, Canada: 4 Oct 1931- ) Learned at age 7 from father's gift of tricks. College instructor & land surveyor. Amateur stage debut in 1949. Specializes in close-up & puzzles. Collects books on magic & gambling. Invented Pin thru Balloon (1954). Tricks in Apocalypse, Bat, Cardiste, Cauldron, Genii, Ibidem, Levitator, Linking Ring, New Phoenix, & Phoenix. Edited Wit & Wizardry: The Magic of Norm Houghton (1998). [Wh2]

name: Raoul
bio: See: Chart, Ralph

name: Rapp, Augustus "Gus
bio: (Jeffersonville, Indiana: 29 Jan 1871-30 Jul 1961) Stage name of Francis Augustine Rapp. Inspired around age 9 by a 10¢ booklet and immediately learned from a library copy of Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Pro by 1896 with medicine show. Wrote Comedy Stunts (1950, 20pp). Autobio is The Life and Times of Augustus Rapp, the small town Showman (1959, 136pp; repr 1990, 201pp). [Pr]

name: Rasche, Franz
bio: (Germany: 12 Feb 1911- ) Magician in Germany. Aka "Francisco Raschini". [Nad]

name: Raschini, Francisco
bio: See: Rasche, Franz

name: Raskin, Max
bio: (Scotland: c1912-1 Mar 1968) Amateur magician. First President of Scottish Association of Magical Societies 1952. On Scottish TV with "Magic with Max" series. [Daw2]

name: Rasmussen, Aage
bio: (Denmark: 26 Sep 1898-28 Sep 1976) Painter in Copenhagen. Amateur magician. Edited the Danish Magic Circle's magazine, Magi, 1935-50 & 1965-70. Dealer-prop maker (Hokus-Pokus) in Copenhagen in 1960s-70s. Became President of Danish Magic Circle in 1970. 1973 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. [St]

name: Rasmussen, Axel
bio: (Denmark: 13 Apr 1908-Jul 1988) Amateur since 1923. Main Scandinavian dealer in magic books (in Holse, Denmark). Edited Den blaa Trylleserie (12 vols, 1949-51), Smaa Korttricks fra Magikeren (5 vols, c1955), Trylle Journalen 1957-67, Magical Book News 1960-62. [Dif]

name: Rastelli
bio: (Samara, Russia: 19 Dec 1896-13 Dec 1931) Stage name of Enrico Rastelli. Died in Bergamo, Italy. [Roh]

name: Rath, Ernst
bio: (Pfäffikon, Switzerland: 30 May 1950-) Pro with partner Peter Kläui in circus magic act as "The Magic Boys". [Nad]

name: Rauscher, Rev. William V[ernon] "Bill
bio: (Long Beach, New Jersey: 17 Oct 1932-) Inspired by Edd Patterson. Learned magic at age 10 from a Gilbert Mysto Magic set, then from Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Debut at age 13. Episcopal Priest & Rector since his ordination in 1957. Retired as rector in 1997. Amateur magician, including a full stage show. Pet effect: Houdini's The Flight of Time, which he revived in 1977 using the original apparatus. 1988 Zweers Scholarship Award. SAM National Chaplain 1989 & IBM Chaplain 1995-97. Magic historian & lecturer. 1991 Christopher Award for best book (on Calvert). 1994 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote 3 books relevant to magic: Arthur Ford: The Man Who Talked with the Dead (1973, with Allen Spraggett), The Spiritual Frontier (1975), & John Calvert (1987). Also wrote & privately published 8 monographs: The Wand: In Story and Symbol (1983, 24pp), Marco The Magi (1983, 34pp), Monarch of Magic: Servais LeRoy (1984, 66pp), E.S.P. or Trickery?: The Problem of Mentalism within the World of Magic (1984, 53pp), Walter B. Gibson (1986, 22pp), Nivelli (1987, 7pp), I Sold My Linking Rings (1988, 13pp), Edd Patterson presents the Art of Magic, The Magic of Art (1990, 80pp), & The Great Raymond (1997, 37pp). Articles in Linking Ring (winning 5 awards) & reviews in Genii & Magicol. [Bo#281;Wh2]

name: Ravel, [James] "Jim" "Jimmy
bio: (USA: -10 Apr 1990) Began as a pro dancer at age 11. Pro magician since 1940s, originally with a magic dance act. Collaborated with Cantu to develop the Dove-from-Silk production. Opened a magic factory & shop in Chicago & developed his pickpocket act as "Mr. Pickpocket", dropping his business to tour the States for the next 12 years. In early 1970s opened & managed the magic shop at Knott's Berry Farm & recreated his Ravel Manufacturing Co. 1988 AMA Special Fellowship. See Paul Butler, Jim Ravel's Theatrical Pickpocketing (1988, 137pp).

name: Ravel, Nic
bio: See: van Driest, Nick

name: Ravelli
bio: See: Wohl, Dr Ronald A.

name: Raven, Tony
bio: See: Lynn, Bob

name: Ravessoud, André
bio: (Switzerland: fl.1970s-80s) Pro illusionist living in Yverdon. Aka "Andreal's". NOTE: Misspelled "Ravisoud".

name: Ravian
bio: (Poland: 1920s-30s) Stage name of Jan Jabłoński. Pro illusionist. Wrote Tajemnice magii, czyli jak zostać iluzjonista. [Mec]

name: Ravisoud" [misspelling]
bio: See: Ravessoud, André

name: Raw, Stuart Drayton
bio: (Britain: -1942) Aka "Paul Rupert", "Rupert Howard", "Merlin", & "Danton" (1939-40). Pro magician & magic teacher who founded the Rupert Howard School of Magic in London in 1928. Wrote The Rupert Howard School Course of Magic [1931, 25 vols]. Then trouped his large "Merlin" show in Britain. Picked by Dante in 1939 to be his successor, carrying on his act as "Danton", but this did not happen. His "Merlin" show was bought by Brunel White who resold it to Benyon. [St]

name: Rawson, Clayton "Clayt
bio: (Elyria, Ohio: 15 Aug 1906-1 Mar 1971) Commercial artist 1929-38. Mystery writer since 1938 & editor of True Detective Magazine & Ellery Queen's Mystery Magazine 1963-71. Amateur magician. Co-authored Scarne on Dice (1945; 2nd ed rev 1945, 422pp). Ghosted Scarne's Complete Guide to Gambling (1961, 714pp). Wrote Pasteboard Parade (1956, as Merlini), How to Entertain Children with Magic You Can Do (1962, 175pp). Tricks in Sphinx, Jinx, Phoenix, & Hugard's both under own name and with pen names of "The Great Merlini" & "Don Diavolo". As mystery writer wrote several clever short stories and 4 novels featuring "The Great Merlini" as magician-detective: Death from a Top Hat (1938, made into a movie as Miracles for Sale), Footprints on the Ceiling (1939, made into a movie as Blue, White and Perfect), The Headless Lady (1940), and No Coffin for the Corpse (1941, made into a movie as The Man Who Wouldn't Die). Writing as "Stuart Towne" he also wrote 3 novelettes (published in Red Star Mystery magazine in 1940), two of which were collected in Death Out of Thin Air (1941), all featuring magician "Don Diavolo" as detective. [CA;Th;SAM]

name: Raxelli
bio: See: "Raxon, Fredo"

name: Raxon, Fredo
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 24 Jul 1923- ) Stage name of Fred Frackmann since 1952. A merchant by trade, in 1946 he was inspired to become a magician by seeing Curt Voigt.
