Pro magician since 1949, initially as "Raxelli" 1949-52, thence as "Fredo Raxon". Manipulator, pickpocket, & mentalist, patterning in several languages. Articles in Vibrations. [Wit]

name: Ray
bio: See: Rea, Sieur

name: Ray, Conny
bio: (Gothenburg, Sweden: 19 Nov 1937- Stage name of Thorbjörn Holmqvist. Learned in 1951 from magic book (100 Roliga Trollkonster). Art director in Lerum. Semi-pro kid-show magician since 1959. Lecturer in Scandinavia, England, & USA. Many TV bits. Wrote En bok om Barntrolleri (1980, 36pp), Conny Ray's Trolleribok (1984, 32pp), Childrens Magic the Swedish Way (1985, 40pp, in English), Idébok för Barntrollare (1985, 40pp), Idébok för Barntrollare 2 (1986, 14pp), & Presentationsteknik (1989, 196pp). Translated Jay Marshall's How to Perform Instant Magic as Trolla själv (1982). [Laugh-MakersV7/#4;Wh2]
years: 19 Nov 1937- Stage name of Thorbjörn Holmqvist. Learned in 1951 from magic book (100 Roliga Trollkonster

name: Ray, Dany
bio: (Paris, France: 21 Jan 1921-8 Dec 1989) Stage name of Raymond Dagnaud since 1945. Son of a dentist. Pro comedy manip since 1945. Played top venues in Europe (Lido de Paris, Casino Estoril 1966, etc) & Asia with assistant-wife Marcelle. AFAP Gold Medal 1986. Died in Paris. [Magie3/90;Dif]

name: Ray, Del
bio: See: "Del Ray"

name: Ray, Geoff
bio: See: Rushworth, Geoffrey W.

name: Ray, Jimmy
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-70s) Stage name of James R. Dussault. Pro close-up with cards & coins. Wrote Between the Acts (1961, 32pp) & Cruise Book (1980, 31pp).

name: Rayanne
bio: (Birmingham, England: 1918-) Stage name of Winifred L. Martins-Moore. Minor pro mental telepathy and escapology act after WW II with partner Jack Martens-Moore. [Hudd]

name: Ray-Mond
bio: (USA?: fl.early 1900s) Son of Maurice "The Great Raymond" Saunders. Pro comedy manipulator.

name: Raymond, Delbert
bio: See: "Del Ray"

name: Raymond, Gene
bio: (Australia: c1917-) A popular magician in his country, although not widely travelled outside.

name: Raymond, Litzka
bio: (Mt. Carmel, Pennsylvania: 11 Jan 1901-11 May 1996) Stage name of Pearl "Perlitzka" Beatrice Evans (née Gonser), aka "The Great Litzka". The widow Evans, a concert harpist, met illusionist Maurice Raymond in London c1926, joined his troupe, & married him on an American ship off Montevideo in 1927. Pro chief assistant (& harpist) to Raymond & also with own vaudeville act of pseudo-Chinese magic, including her rooster, "China Boy". Again widowed in 1948, she married Walter B. Gibson in 1949, his third wife, & co-wrote books with him. SAM Hall of Fame. [Gib;Ch;Pr]

name: Raymond, Luella
bio: (Pittsburg, Pennsylvania: 1885-28 Dec 1974) Born Luella Cross. Minor vaudevillian. Learned magic as assistant to The Great Raymond in 1903, marrying him in 1905. Mother of "Ray-Mond" Saunders. Left her husband in Spain in 1911, divorcing in early 1912. Married British magician Henry Houston in India in Dec 1912, becoming his stage assistant until he switched to management in a year or two. Died in England. [Pr;Ch]

name: Raymond, Maurice François
bio: (Akron, Ohio: 30 May 1877 [sic]-27 Jan 1948) Stage name of Morris Raymond Saunders, aka "The Great Raymond". Claimed to have been inspired by & learned at age 9 assisting uncle "Addison the Magician", a pro juggler-magician. Claimed to have joined a circus with his magic act at age 14. Toured the USA as a minor magician-escapist 1903-07. His 5 (he misclaimed 7) world tours with his full-evening show 1907-34 made him more famous abroad than in the USA. 1st tour (1907-12, misclaiming it as his "3rd"): Latin America (1907-09), Britain (1909-10), Portugal (1910), Spain (1911), Italy, Egypt, India, China, Japan, Hawaii (1912). 2nd tour (?-1916-?): Latin America, Portugal (1916), Spain, France, Britain. 3rd tour: the Continent & South America. 4th tour: Portugal (1926), South America (1927-30). 5th tour: South America (1934). Thence played vaudeville & occasional full-evening shows in the USA. Retired in 1945. Died in New York City; buried in Akron. SAM Hall of Fame. A "big" Mason. Husband of Luella & Litzka Raymond. Father of "Ray-Mond" Saunders. Bio is William V. Rauscher, The Great Raymond (1997, 376pp). NOTE: Many of Raymond's claims, particularly early ones, are sheer false publicity. [Pr;Ch;Bam;Gib;Dor;Tay;Ho]

name: Raymonde
bio: (Belgrade, Serbia: 9 Apr 1894- ) Stage name of Raymondon Gallatovich. Brought to USA as youth. Interested in magic in 1910. Pro with illusion & kid-show act. Dealer (Raymond Magical Studio) in Brooklyn, New York, in the 1940s specializing in collapsible rubber production items. Taught Ellenbogen, etc. [SAM]

name: Raynaly, Édouard-Joseph
bio: (Paris, France: 7 Aug 1842-19 Dec 1918) Drawing-room comedy act. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1888-1901. Wrote the classic Les propos d'un escamoteur (1894, 244pp). Also wrote La sorcellerie amusante, Tours de cartes, & L'art de la mnémotechnie (1895), La vérité sur la mnémotechnie (1897, 72pp). Articles in Illusioniste (1902-03). Charter member of the CSP 1904. [Dif;Vo55]

name: Rea, Sieur [pronounced RAY]
bio: (England: fl.1780s-1810s) Pro, assisted by his 2 sons. At Bartholomew Fair 1781-92. Played London & Weymouth in 1810. Pet effects: Egg Bag, Palingenesia, etc. Probably the same as "Ray" who had entertained King George III. [Cl;Fr]

name: Read, [Robert Graham] "Bob
bio: (Sheffield, Yorkshire, England: 12 Sep 1940-20 Nov 2005) Learned in 1947 from joke shop tricks. Textile executive. Semi-pro comedy close-up magician. Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner 1967 (its first) & 1973. 1983 Desert Magic Seminar 2nd prize. Magic historian, specializing in street magicians. Lecturer. Has large collection of prints (c700) of Cups-&-Balls performers. Wrote Thanks to Pepys (1974, 60pp), The Penultimate Cups and Balls (1975, 28pp), $100 Glass Thro' Table (c1980, 7pp), The Cups and Balls in 19th Century Graphic Art (1984, 40pp), Cups and Balls in 19th Graphic Art: Second Spasm (1990). Articles in Abra & Pabular. TV bits in Britain & USA. [Wh2]

name: Read, Ralph W.
bio: (USA: -26 Mar 1952) Inspired at age 9 by a dime-museum magician in Denver. Learned at age 13 from vaude magician. Debut at age 15. Pro mindreader. In 1908 took over Roterberg's mail-order business & founded the firm of Read & Covert [not Calvert] in 1910, which became the Chicago Magic Co in 1912. Improved but did not invent the Mental Masterpiece prop. Later moved to New York City & finally (1948) California. Wrote The Calostro Mind Reading Act (1934); The Three Shell Game (1938, 58pp); The Radio Vision Mind-Reading Code (by "Calostro"); 'One Man' Mind Reading Secrets (by "Calostro"); & Flash Paper Tips (1951, 50pp, with Stuart Robson). Ghosted or edited several others. Edited Volumes 3 (1943), 4 (1945), & 5 (1948) of the revised Tarbell Course in Magic. A memoir is Conventioners Caravan (1949, 12pp). Articles in Linking Ring. [Th]

name: Reay, Kevin [Robert]
bio: (Hartlepool, Cleveland, England: 9 Feb 1958-) Learned first magic at age 5. Originally an admitted card sharp. Then since 1983 a top pro close-up worker living in London & specializing in gambling demos. 1984 International Day of Magic competition prize in close-up, 1985 British Ring prize in close-up, & 1988 Magic Circle Close-Up Competition winner. [Wh5]

name: Recha
bio: See: Schäfer, Reinhold

name: Redan, Ellinor
bio: (Wernersville, Pennsylvania: 28 Jun 1874-) Pro magicienne (as partner of husband Harry Redan) 1903 to c1930 when retired. Pet effects: flags & handkerchiefs. 1st woman member of SAM.[WWM]

name: Redan, Harry
bio: (Clinton, Missouri: 11 Aug 1869-8 Oct 1939) Pro full-evening and vaudeville magus from 1892 until c1930. Husband & partner of Ellinor Redan. [WWM]

name: Redans, Alex
bio: See: Snader Jr, Craige

name: Redmon, Don
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro performer. Dealer as co-owner (with Don Stallard) of "The Don Redmon Company of Quality Made Magic" in Louisville, Kentucky, 1947-1952. From 1950 to 1952 while Theo "Okito" Bamberg was employed as a prop maker the company produced superb "Okito-Redmon" apparatus. [Albo95]

name: Redmond, Mr.
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s) A fairly major dealer (Magical Repository) in London at Grosvenor House, Albany Road, Camberwell, in 1876.

name: Redmond, Dr.
bio: (Ireland: -Aug 1922) Minor pro music hall magus-vent-mind reader-escape artist. Played the London Pavilion c1890.

name: Reeder, Brad[ley Scott]
bio: (Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania: 1966-) Inspired c1976 seeing live magic show, learned c1977 from magic set. Semi-pro comedy magician, juggler, & comedian 1984-1988 when went pro. Works mainly comedy clubs & colleges. Producer-director of annual "Comedy Magic Bash" convention in Raleigh, North Carolina. Wrote Sparks: The Funkenring Book (1986, 44pp, with Bill Robinson). Tricks in Linking Ring. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Reese, Bert
bio: (Posen, Poland: 1841-1928) Stage name of Berthold Riess. Student of Charles H. Foster. World-famed pseudo-psychic who fooled Edison c1926. Exposed by Houdini. [Jinx#22]

name: Reeve, Harry, MIMC
bio: (Britain: fl.1950s-80s) Aka "Evere" & "U Ling Foo". Inspired at age 8 by grandfather's gift box of tricks. Learned magic in 1946. Teacher & semi-pro magician until 1983 when went full-time pro. MIMC 1988. Column in Abra.

name: Reeve, Josephine
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Pro sleight-of-hand act in Britain around 1925.

name: Regal, David [Milchen]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 1956- ) Learned at age c12. Pro actor-comedian-magician in New York City where he is Director of Programming at ACTV. Specializes in close-up, originally as pro, now as amateur. Invented Deja-Vu Deck & Pastebord Massacre. See Harry Lorayne, Star Quality: The Magic of David Regal (1987, 277pp). Wrote Close-up & Personal (1999, 264pp). Articles in Apocalypse, Magic Arts Journal, & Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]

name: Regent, Rex
bio: (Scotland: -8 Mar 1942) Stage name of Thomas Sutherland. With wife performed as "Rex and Reine, Scotland's Only Deaf and Dumb Conjurers". [Daw2]

name: Regnault, Mdle.
bio: (France: fl.1690s) Wife of M. Tiphaine, a fair exhibitor in Paris. Pro with cups-&-balls, etc, in Paris in 1697. She was the earliest magicienne of whom Sidney Clarke was aware.

name: Reichenbach, Arthur D. "Rick
bio: (USA: 1895-dead) Company director in Allentown, Pennsylvania. Amateur magician. IBM President 1952-53.

name: Reid, Bernard [Lawrence] MIMC
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 4 Aug 1941- ) Learned small packet tricks at age c7. Edited New Zealand Society of Magicians Newsletter 1958 (46 issues). Pro since 1965, initially as illusionist, later adding pickpocketing. Worked double act with partner as "Diabolo & Danielle" 1962-74. Aka "Bernard" 1968-present. Also worked with former wife Esme. Moved to USA in 1970. Regular cruise-ship worker (Holland-America Lines, QE II, Croisiere Paquet, Royal Cruise Line) since 1974 plus such venues as Aladdin Hotel in Vegas & Mostly Magic in New York (1990). Wrote Professional Card Tricks You Can Do (1976, 32pp). Articles in Tops & Magican for which he has written a regular column for the last 20 years. Awarded medallion by Princess Cruises for 15 years continuous service as a cabaret performer 2009. MIMC with Gold Star 1996. NZ "Grand Master of Magic" 2001. Long time member of SAM, IBM and The Magic Castle. [Magicana#205,#226;Wh5]

name: Reid, John
bio: See: Geddes, [John R.] "Johnny"

name: Reid, [Wallis James] "Wally
bio: (Saginaw, Michigan: 23 May 1938-) Learned in 1950 from books & observation. Semi-pro illusionist since 1960. Aka "Wallis the Magician" 1955-66, thence under own name. Invented Queen of Hearts Illusion 1971 (used by Reveen & others), The Puzzle Illusion 1974 (used by Henning), Elusive Bunny Box 1974 (Abbott's), Magicians Helper boxes 1974 (used by Copperfield), & Dove In/Addition 1983 (Hank Lee). Wrote Magic: "On Stage" (1980, 124pp) & Midnight Fantasy Sketchbook (1987, 134pp). Articles in Tops, Linking Ring, & Talisman. [Wh2]

name: Reilly, J[ames] V[ictor] "Jim" MIMC
bio: (Wellington, New Zealand: 31 May 1928-) Learned at age 8 from father. Chartered secretary & administrator in Hamilton. Semi-pro childrens & club show magic since 1959. Assistant editor of Magicana 1964-1980 whence editor to 2000. Edited The Best from Down Under (1972, 139pp). Articles in Abra, Magigram, Genii & tricks in Encyclopedia of Dove Magic & The Best from Down Under. Invented Bunny Hat (1970) & Cage of Doves (1973). Major manufacturer of Troublewits. Variet Artists Club of New Zealand Scroll of Honor 1984. Grand Master of Magic Award (New Zealand) 1988. MIMC with Gold Star 1996. AMA Literary Fellowship 2004. Wrote Darling Jennie: The Story of Jennie Anderson, New Zealand's First Professional Magician (1991, 28pp). Same Man Different Clothes (1993, 132pp) [Booth #264;Wh2]

name: Reilly, S[ylvester] W. "Syl
bio: (USA: -1959) Partner in mental act with Bob Nelson until 1921. Then pro dealer & publisher (S.W. Reilly Co.) in Columbus, Ohio, specializing in mental & spook effects & issuing a catalog in 1936. In 1931 founded Magi-Fest, the first regional conference of magicians in the USA. Invented Fa-ko Cards (1928), Stop-Lite (by 1945), Dun-A-Trix (by 1945), etc. Wrote Reilly's Ghost Show Routine & Fascinating Tricks with Ghostlite Luminous Paint (1936) & Table-Lifting Methods Used by Fake Mediums (1957 mimeo). [Walk2] Reine de l'Espérance [Queen of Hope] (England?: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Elizabeth Hope. Pro magicienne, performing as early as around 1898 in fine evening dress with plunging neckline. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1902.

name: Reine de Solange, Mdle.
bio: (Paris, France: 7 Nov 1869-1 Oct 1953) Stage name of Pauline Manin. Taught by her uncle, Cazeneuve, with whom she toured as star assistant in Argentina & Africa in 1892. Then, on own, with spirit exposé act in Turkey, Egypt, & Morocco until retired in 1903. [Dif;Cl]

name: Reinhart, Robert "Bob
bio: (New York City, NY: 13 Dec 1906-17 Dec 1999) Amateur magician since age 12. BA from Harvard. Later semi-pro. Pro stage actor-producer and occasional reviewer (including magic shows) for Variety & New York Herald-Tribune. Produced 2 magic shows for Theater Guild in 1933 & 1934. Joined S.S. Adams Company by 1951. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Rhinehart" by Annemann & "Rhinehardt" by Vernon. [WWM]

name: Reis, Tony [pronounced RACE]
bio: (Setúbal, Portugal: 30 Jan 1941- ) Stage name of António REIS DA CRUZ BISCAYA DA SILVA, aka "Mr Tony". Inspired at age 16 seeing Conde de Aguilar perform. Government official. Semi-pro magician since age 18, specializing in general & kid-show magic & mentalism. Dealer ("Estúdio Mágico Tony Reis") in Setúbal. Edited Magia e Imprensa since 1979 & O Prestidigitador since 1988. Articles. [Cam;Wh2]

name: Reisner, Tony
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 17 Jun 1952- ) Stage name of Tony Reisner [not "Rayzner"]. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Dealer (as Tony Reisner Magic) in new & antique magic in Gänserndorf, Austria, in 1980s-90s. NOTE: Falsely reported dead in 1987. [Mec;Nad]

name: Reisz Jr, H[oward] Frederick
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 13 May 1939-) Lutheran clergyman. Learned magic at age 11. Semi-pro club & close-up magician since age 15. Aka "Fred the Fantastic" since 1974. Articles in MUM. [Wh5]

name: Relvas, Eduardo [pronounced RER-vahsh]
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 14 Dec 1896-3 Jun 1977) Student of J.G. d'Oliveira. Debut as amateur in 1913. Pro stage illusionist as "Savler" in casinos, theaters, & cinemas throughout Portugal 1917-22. Thence a driving force in organizing magical activities in his country. In 1922 founded the Grémio Mágico Português. Dealer & prop maker in 1927. In 1949 founded the Tertúlia Mágica Lisbonense. 1961 Coimbra 1st prize in general magic. Wrote Arte Mágica (4 vols, 1970-74). Articles (mostly historical & biographical) in Enigma, Plateia, etc. [Cam]

name: Remarque
bio: See: Dennison, Edward

name: Remerbi
bio: (Obory, Poland: 1910- ) Stage name of Tadeusz Grabowski. Taught by Jan Bremer & Nemo. Prominulator in circus & cabaret. [Mec]

name: Remigiusz
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1932-23 Dec 1977) Stage name of Jerzy Troszczyński. Pro illusionist & manipulator. [Mec]

name: Remons. Original
bio: (Berlin: 28 Mar 1890-) Pro stage magician. Played many major variety houses, including the Vienna Ronacher in 1956.

name: Reneaux, James "Jimmy" "Jim
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-90s) Originally resident of Michigan. Learned in 1940s from Hugard's Magic Monthly. Pro since c1947. Managed Abbott's New York shop in early 1950s until it closed in 1954. Then worked for The Magic Center. Played the NY Palace in 1956. Several world tours to his credit. Wrote Tricks of the Trade (1953, 10pp mimeo) & The Professional Technique for Magicians (1968, 43pp).

name: Renelys
bio: (France: 1960s-80s) Stage name of René Lachartre. Stage & close-up magician. Parisian.

name: Reno, Madame
bio: (USA: -26 Jul 1927) Stage name of Emma Burdick (née Austin) who married Edward Burdick ("Ed Reno") in 1886. Trained by her husband and then off on her own on the Lyceum & Chatauqua circuits. [Pr]

name: Reno, Edward M[unn] "Ed
bio: (Baldwinsville, New York: 23 Aug 1861-2 Apr 1949) Stage name of Edward Munn Burdick. Pro since c1879. A star of both Lyceum (by 1906) & Chautauqua (1912-c1931) circuits. Trick in Tarbell #5. [Pr;Par]

name: Renoff
bio: (France: c1880-1972) Pro. 1947 Paris 2nd prize for invention. [Dif]

name: Retas, Prof. [Mathieu]
bio: (Romania: fl.1970s-90s) Pro stage illusionist, mentalist, contact mind-reader, etc, in Bucarest.

name: Retta
bio: (Brtchko-on-the-Sava, Bosnia: 20 Jan 1888-29 May 1942) Stage name of Sreta Obradovitch. Orphaned at age 8. Pro illusionist, touring Europe & Near East 1910s-30s. Wrote several books on telepathy, hypnotism, & psychic charlatans. [Dif]

name: Reum, Dr Earl [pronounced ROOM]
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 27 Feb 1931-) Learned in 1938 from Tarbell, etc. Educator. Semi-promagician since 1946. Dealer (Major Magic) in Denver in mid-1950s. Pet effects: Zombie & Professor's Nightmare. Edited As Reumer Has It (1954-55, 7 issues). Wrote Magic for the Civic Club (1968, 24pp). [MUM4/75;Wh5]

name: Reuschling, George P.
bio: See: "La Follette"

name: Reveen, Peter MIMC
bio: (Adelaide, Australia: 8 Oct 1935 – 8 Apr 2013) Born Peter James [sic] Ryan, now legally changed to Peter Reveen. Learned at age 8 from Boys Book of Conjuring. Pro stage hypnotist-illusionist, billed as "Reveen, The Impossibilit" since 1954. His assistant-wife since 1956 is Coral Reveen, a former juggler's assistant and usherette. Moved in 1961 to Canada where he got citizenship in 1966. Produced & starred in several major full-evening shows 1967-80. First magician to get star billing in Las Vegas when he played the Tropicana in 1975. Claims his hyp act holds "all-time records for any live theatrical event in Canada, having by [1989] played to in excess of 6,000,000--the equivalent of 25% of the country's population." Plays Las Vegas since 1989. Toured Australia 1974 & 1990. MIMC with Gold Star 1981. 2000 DRAGON Award (with wife Coral). Pet effects: Cheating the Gallows, Knight's Tour, & Selbit's Divided Lady. Wrote The Superconscious World (1987) on hypnotism with autobio. Articles in Skeptical Inquirer. [Australian Magic Monthly7/90;Bo#229;Geni9/74;Mag;Wh2]

name: Revillo
bio: (USA?: -c1899) Stage name of Eugene Olliver. Pro in USA by 1883, touring a kid-show act. Started tour of South America in 1899 jointly with Balabrega but soon died in Caracas, Venezuela, of yellow fever. [Pr;Mo] "Rex The `Ace' Magician'" SEE: Hauptmann, Henry "Harry

name: Rex, Professeur
bio: See: Sauty, Charles-Émile

name: Rex, Bert
bio: (Bad Frankenhausen, East Germany: 19 Sep 1956- ) Inspired by a book by Zmeck. Tutored in manip by Walter Umlauf. Pro since 1982 with cards, coins, & Dancing Hank. Tricks in Zauberkunst, etc. [Win2]

name: Rey, Oskar
bio: (Switzerland: 14 May 1890-21 [or 31] Jul 1971) Industrialist in Wil, St. Gallen, Switzerland. Amateur magician as "Oscarelli" & "Rey-Wil". Founding-president of the Swiss Magic Circle in 1939. Edited its magazine Hokus-Pokus 1952-61. Later lived in Zurich.

name: Reynolds, Bobby
bio: (Jersey City, New Jersey: 5 Oct 1934-) At age 9 inspired by & learned from Al Flosso & his shop. Pro magic (plus pitchman & carnival sideshows) since age 13. Worked for a time for Walter DeLenz. [Wh]

name: Reynolds, Charles [Raymond], MIMC
bio: (Toledo, Ohio: 9 Sep 1932- ) Learned at age 7 from Gilbert Mysto Magic set. Photographer in New York City. Amateur magician &, since c1975, consultant. 1974 AMA Award of Merit. 1976 AMA Award of Merit (for Charles & Regina). 1978 AMA Creative Fellowship. In 1985 became full-time illusion consultant as "Charles Reynolds Illusion Associates". 1988 Harry Blackstone Award from International Platform Association. Created dozens of effects for Doug Henning's 8 TV specials & Merlin, including the Vanishing Elephant, Motorcycle to Suspended Box, & Things That Go Bump in the Night. For Blackstone Jr he created many effects, including the Vanishing Elephant (different method). Wrote 100 Years of Magic Posters (1976, 112pp, with Regina Reynolds), Houdini: His Legend and His Magic (1977, 192pp, with Doug Henning), & The Blackstone Book of Magic & Illusion (1985, 230pp, with Harry Blackstone Jr & Regina Reynolds). Articles in Abra, Magick, Magic Manuscript, Vibrations, etc. NOTE: Accepts being called "Charlie" only in conversation with friends. [Wat;Wh2]

name: Reynolds, Regina [Benedict]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: fl.1970s-90s) Born Regina Benedict. Editor-writer on photography. Married Charles Reynolds with whom she collaborates in magic &, since 1985, in their "Charles Reynolds Illusion Associates" firm. Co-authored 101 Years of Magic Posters (1976, with Charles Reynolds) for which they shared the 1976 AMA Award of Merit; & The Blackstone Book of Magic & Illusion (1985, with Blackstone Jr & Charles Reynolds). [Wh2]

name: Rey-Wil
bio: See: Rey, Oskar

name: Reywils, Max
bio: (Toulouse, France: Sep 1901-19 Apr 1960) Pro magician & escape artist. Founder-President of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Toulouse 1944-53. [Dif]

name: Rezvani, Medjid Kan
bio: (Isfahan, Iran: 16 Sep 1900-1962). School teacher. Semi-pro close-up. Moved to Paris. Famous for his cups-&-balls with tomatoes. BBC-TV bit in 1955. See Maurice Sardina, La magie du sorcier (1946), with English tr by Fitzkee as The Magic of Rezvani (1949, 89pp; repr 1973); & Sardina, Rezvanimagie (1949).

name: Rheiner, Conrad
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Lived in Philadelphia. Invented the behind the back force, publishing it in his Touch of Mephistopheles (1921 or 22).

name: Rheuban, Carl M.
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Lawyer-businessman in Los Angeles. Amateur magician since youth. Co-edited (with David Hutchins) Sorcerer's Magazette 1963-64 (2 issues). In 1983 Rheuban founded the First Network Savings Bank, paying himself $11 million in dividends over the next 6 years. In 1984 he bought the Mulholland Collection for $575,000 and next year created the Mulholland Library, hiring Ricky Jay as curator. In Apr 1990 his company went bankrupt and was seized (along with the library) for liquidation by the US Government (which auctioned it off in 1991 to David Copperfield). "Rhinehart, Robert" [misspelling by Annemann] SEE: Reinhart, Robert

name: Rhodin, Max von
bio: (Riga, Latvia, Russian Empire [now Latvia]: 18 Oct 1898-11 Sep 1987) Stage name of Bruno Alexis Nicolai Rhodin. Son of "Max Alexander" & his 2nd wife, "Rosa Alexander". Moved to Hungary. Pro since debut at age 11 with plate spinning. Moved to Denmark where he lived most of his life. General magic plus hyp act. Also did mindreading act with "Madame Trilby" who was his 1st wife Alva von Rhodin. Younger half-brother of "Brazil Jack". Died in Oslo, Norway. [Dif]

name: Rhombello
bio: (Denmark: fl.1870s) Stage name of Therisia Margarete Welkier, 1st wife of Max Alexander whom she assisted. Mother of "Brazil Jack".

name: Rhundei
bio: (Spain: -1979) Stage name of Jesus LOPES GONZALES. Pro. Charter member of Club de Ilusionistas Profesionales in Madrid in 1956. "Rhyss" [misspelling by D. Bamberg] SEE: Ryss

name: Ribié, Louis-François
bio: (France: fl.1770s-80s) A dissolute dramatic author and actor. Pro cups-and-balls worker at Paris fairs around 1780, giving shows with his wife, a fire-handler & strong woman. [CI]

name: Ricado
bio: (USA: 1908-) Stage name of Richard McGreevy. Initially a law student, turned pro magician 19 years later. Finally toured a full-evening show. [St]

name: Ricard, Eddie
bio: See: Bamberg, Eduard

name: Ricardo
bio: See: "Fantasio"

name: Ricardo, Bob
bio: (Brazil: fl.1950s-70s) Stage name of Ricardo de Mello. Resident of Rio de Janeiro. Published O Jornal do Prestidigitador 1959-65 (7 issues). Brazilian Magic Competition 1964 3rd prize in childrens magic, 1965 3rd prizes for childrens magic & comedy magic. Co-founded the Clube de Ilusionistas da Guanabara in 1966. Visited Portugal & Belgium in 1979.

name: Riccardi, Fernando
bio: (Rome, Italy: 25 Dec 1921- ) Learned in 1931 from father's Xmas gift of magic set. Has stage name of "Nikkadir" since 1935. Government employee (now retired). Semi-pro close-up magician since 1938. Also many Italian awards as lecturer. Founding President of IBM Ring 204 (Rome) in 1971. His daughter Laura Riccardi illustrates magic articles. Wrote Divertire Meravigliando (1985, 130pp), I più bei giuchi di prestigio (1988, 127pp), & Ombrecines (1990, 56pp). Articles in Qui Magia, Revue de la Prestidigitation, Il Prestigiatore Moderna, Clam, Magia Moderna, etc. [Magia Moderna12/72; Qui Magia7/89; Wh2]

name: Riccardo
bio:
Rice, Professor A. E. (Australia?: fl.1870s-80s) Pro magician (Chinese Rings, etc) & muscle reader ("Mind-Reader"). Toured Australia for years beginning in 1876 and New Zealand in 1885.

[See also: Webster, Richard]

name: Rice, Harold R.
bio: (Salineville, Ohio: 22 May 1912-10 Jul 1987) Inspired as boy by meeting S.S. Henry & seeing his show. Semi-pro magician in college with an all-silk act & in 1929 founder-owner of Silk King Studios in Cincinnati, designing & making quality silk props (meanwhile working as a college art teacher). When he married Thelma Ryle in 1937, she became his partner & eventual successor to Silk King Studios. 1944 PhD from Columbia U. Art professor until retired in 1978. IBM Secretary 1940-46. Wrote the classic Rice's Encyclopedia of Silk Magic (3 volumes, 1948, 1953, 1962, 520+554+490pp) & several booklets, including Thru the Dye Tube (1943, 48pp, with Wayne F. van Zandt), Capers with Color (1967, 19pp), & Rice's More Naughty Silks (32pp; repr 1969, 40pp). Edited "My Pet Effects" column in Linking Ring 1932-40. Article in Genii. [Se]

name: Rich, Prof. Gus
bio: (Salem [now Winston-Salem], North Carolina: 1833-1917) Stage name of William Augustus Reich, billed as "Magician of the South" & "The Wizard of the Blue Ridge" (in 1880s-90s). Of Moravian (church & ethnic) descent. After 7 years of school, he apprenticed and became a professional tinsmith in Salem, making most of his own props. As a semi-pro magician (sleight-of-hand & an apparatus trick) he toured the South & Mid-West by wagon for some 30 years after the American Civil War. Since 1981 Max Howard performs an historical act based on Rich, whose props are preserved in the archives of Old Salem.

name: Richardine, Ricardo
bio: (Columbia, South America: fl.1900s-60s) Stage name of Ricardo Deben. Trouped a full-evening show thru Latin America for over 50 years. The Great Richiardi was an assistant. Played New York (the Puerto Rico Theatre) in 1957 & 1962 and Chicago (the Senate Theatre) in 1957, all with his sister Marga & son Richardine Jr as featured co-illusionists. [Par;Geni11/59;Geni12/62;HMM3/57]

name: Richardine Jr
bio: (Columbia?: c1925-c1985) Stage name of Ricardo Deben Jr. Learned assisting his famous father. Changed stage name to "Dantel" in 1970. Died of heart attack. [Genii 12/62]

name: Richards, Dr.
bio: See: Richards, Sidney

name: Richards, Ralph
bio: (USA: fl.1910-30s) Stage name of Ralph A. Ennes. Pro with full-evening show of stage magic & crystal gazing. Toured mainly the smaller cities of the Southern & mid-Central States & Canada with success from 1910 to the mid-1930s. [Pr]

name: Richards, Sidney
bio: (England: 2 Jan 1866-dead) Pro, touring Latin America (1910s-20s) & Portugal (1930) as "Dr. Richards" with assistant-wife Grace.

name: Richardsen, Rolf
bio: See: Röhl, Richard

name: Richardson, Cedric R.
bio: (South Africa: c1918-22 May 1982) Moved to Britain and, later, the USA. Pro as "Cedric" then "Ray Bentley" in 1930s-50s. Managed Abbott's Detroit branch shop since 1952. Co-wrote (with Roy Kissell the "Dusting Off Some Old Ones" column in Tops magazine. [Genii1/39]

name: Richardson, H. E.
bio: (England: fl.1960s) General & childrens magician as "Edricardo". Richiardi, The Great (Peru: 1885-1937) Stage name of Ricardo Izquierdo. Learned assisting in Richardine show, whose famous name & pet effects he closely imitated when went on own. Pro illusionist resident in Lima, Peru. World tour 1930-36 under auspices of Portuguese impresario A.M. Gaspar, playing Europe (1930-32), the Portuguese colonies in Africa & Asia, and ending with South America (c1935-36). Was touring the USA 1936-37 when killed in an auto accident in Atlanta, Georgia. [Ch;Cam]

name: Richiardi, Ricardo
bio: (c1952-) Taught by father "Richiardi Jr" who acted in his father's show as an assistant magician. Pro black-art act, which he learned in 1971 working as assistant to Omar Pasha.

name: Richiardi Jr
bio: (Lima, Peru: 24 Nov 1923-6 Sep 1985) Stage name of Aldo IZQUIERDO COLOSI since 1937. Learned at age 6 assisting his father "The Great Richiardi". After unsuccessfully trying with his mother to continue his late father's show in the USA, returned to Lima for 2 years of schooling. Then, having studied singing & dancing, debuted as pro illusionist in 1943 in Buenos Aires. Pet effects: Broom Suspension, Buzz Saw, & Sub Trunk. Toured his large show thru South America (1943-45), Mexico (c1948), USA (1949, 1956-57, 1971, 1973), Britain, Europe (1952-53, 1955-56), Japan (1966), etc. 1972 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1979 SAM Magician of the Year; 1982 AMA Magician of the Year. TV bits on Ed Sullivan show (1956-58, 8 times). Father of Ricardo Richiardi. [Ran;Ch;Fu;Fu2;Cam;HMM10/56,11/56;6/61]

name: Rick, Slick
bio: See: Neiswonger, Richard

name: Rickard, Ed
bio: See: Bamberg, Eduard

name: Rickard, Fred[eric Lake], AIMC
bio: (Vandalia, Missouri: 14 Jan 1907-28 Nov 1989) Learned in 1920 from Xmas gift magic set. Chemist & metal spinner. Semi-pro magician, specialized in large illusions. Invented a modernized Dizzy Limit in 1945. Worked with Bill Larsen Sr ("Thayer's") 1944-45, Merv Taylor 1951-52, & Owen Magic Supreme 1952-57. SAM Hall of Fame 1986. 1987 Henry Ridgely Evans History Award (shared with Walter B. Graham). Tricks in MUM & Genii. Reedited Nixon's Hong Kong Mysteries (1986, 75pp). [Wh2]

name: Rid, Sa
bio: (England: fl. early 1600s) Probably a pen name & very likely that of Samuel Rand, a London shopkeeper and compiler-writer of several books. Rid wrote The Art of Iugling or Legerdemaine (London: 1612, 24 unnumbered leaves; repr 1614). This was the first English-language book devoted entirely to conjuring, although largely pirated (often verbatim) from the original 1584 edition of Scot's Discoverie of Witchcraft. Only 3 copies of Rid's 1612 edition are known to have survived. [TS]

name: Riddo, Ernesto
bio: (France: 1886-) Stage name of Marcel Faraut. Pro illusionist. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1923.

name: Riding, [Joseph] "Joe", MIMC
bio: (Preston [sic], Lancs., England: 20 May 1932-23 Apr 2005) Learned c1964 reading a Lorayne memory book & Scarne on card tricks. Prize fighter ages 16-20 when retired in 1952. Pro close-up & comedy cabaret magic since 1979. Pet effects: Counting the Cards & memorizing the deck in 1½ minutes. Dealer in St. Annes-on-Sea. MIMC 1988. Invented Only 3-Card Trick With 4 Cards. Articles in Abra, Gen, & Magigram. [Wh2]

name: Rieck, Armin
bio: (Germany?: 26 Oct 1932-) Magician & collector of dice in Reinbek, Germany. [Nad]

name: Riedel, Clint[ton Charles]
bio: (Lancaster, Pennsylvania: 30 Mar 1908-11 Mar 1995) Inspired in 1920 seeing a Thurston show. Learned by buying tricks. Sign painter-artist by trade until retired in 1937. East Coast part-time pro stage magician since 1925 & full-time from 1937 to 1960 when left the stage. Specialized in silk manip & livestock. His wife, Mildred "Millie" Riedel (married in 1925, died 1992), was his stage manager throughout. Apparatus builder for U.F. Grant, etc, from the 1930s to 1973 when fully retired. Invented Rice Box to Lantern, etc. Articles in Linking Ring & Mortimer's Magic Magazine. Bio is James M. Klein, The Magic of Riedel (1988, 246pp). [Wh2] Riediger, Gottlieb [pronounced REE-dih-guhr] (Germany?: fl.1740s) Pro sleight-of-hand at Paris fairs in 1740s. [Dif]

name: Riese, Eberhard "Ebs" [pronounced REE-za]
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 17 Jun 1951- ) Highschool teacher. Amateur magician since 1969. 1985 MZvD Writer of the Year award (shared with Robert Kaldy). Vice-President MZvD since 1987. FISM judge since 1988. Co-editor (with O. Drenker) of Magie since 1990. Articles in Magie. Producer & teacher of many magic acts in Germany, including Andy, Clemens Valentino, Franklin, Tom Voss, & Topas. [Wh5]

name: Rieth, Rudolf [pronounced REETH]
bio: (Germany: 9 Sep 1889-16 Mar 1954) Actor in Halle & Weimar. Amateur manipulator. Died in Düsseldorf, West Germany. [St]

name: Rigal, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Florist in Grenoble. Semi-pro close-up, general magic, & manip with balls, cigarettes, & cards. AFAP Master Magician. 1964 FISM 3rd prize in invention. Founding-President of the Club des Magiciens de la Haute-Savoie 1965-68. 1967 Baden-Baden 1st prize. 1967 FISM 1st prize in invention. [Bou]

name: Rigney, Francis J[oseph] "Frank
bio: (Waterford, Ireland: 20 Jan 1882-20 Apr 1962) Sketch artist & newspaperman. Moved to USA in 1914. Wrote & illustrated Fun With Paper Folding (1928, with William D. Murray; repr 1951, 95pp), A Beginner's Book of Magic (1950, 145pp; repr 1964), & Cub Scout Magic (1960, 145pp). Illustrated Hugard's Magic Monthly (since 1945), Kaplan's The Fine Art of Magic (1948), and Hugard & Braue's The Royal Road to Card Magic (1948). Tricks in HMM. Invented Five Knots (1948). [LR9/95; St] "Rigoletto Brothers, The" SEE UNDER: Rigoletto, Henry

name: Rigoletto, Henry "Harry
bio: (USA?: fl. 1910s-50s) Jewish. With brother Charles as "The Rigoletto Brothers", a popular provaude mad-cap comedy juggling, acrobatic, & magic act, with Henry doing the magic. They toured the USA, Britain, & Australia (1926). His pet effects: the Needle Trick, Sympathetic Silks, & Legs Table. They played the NY Palace often 1952-55. [Go;Wal]

name: Rikard
bio: See: Bamberg, Edouard

name: Rikil, Mr. John
bio: (England: fl.1420s) The most famous pro of his time at sleight-of-hand. "Tregetour" to the late King Henry V reigned 1413-22). [CI]

name: Riley, Hugh R[ichard], AIMC
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 30 Oct 1914-10 Dec 1997) Learned magic at age 11 as member of Stark Brothers Greater Shows, a "mud circus". Transportation consultant. Semi-pro mentalist since age 11. Aka "Rilemon". SAM President 1958-59. Has lectured on mentalism in USA, Britain, & Australia. Wrote Mentalism for Magicians: Mysteries of the Mind (1977). Articles in Magick, Linking Ring, MUM, Genii, Abra, & Magic Circular. [Mag;Wh4]

name: Riley, Little Red
bio:
"Rinaldi, The Great" SEE: Townner, Harland

[See also: Combest, Daniel]

name: Rinaldo
bio: See: Carlisle, Stanton

name: Ring, Ken(neth Anton Dermot)
bio: (Walton-on-Thames, UK: 16 January, 1945) Self-taught when worked as The Magic Santa in 1985. Pro. Magician 1986-2006. Worked as Mr Goodtimes the Clown in 1987. From 1988 to 2006, as Mathman, he conducted mathematical shows in schools throughout New Zealand. Awarded QEII (Queen Elizabeth II) Award in 1992 for his work in schools. President of the New Zealand Society of Magicians 1993-1996. Major magical influences: Alan Watson and Richard Webster. Wrote Flipscript (1979), Simple Mathematical Card Tricks (1992), 15 Mathematical Tricks Using Your Favourite Number (1992), Math Magic Show (1994), Rubberband Magic (1995). Contributed effects to Linking Ring and Magicana.

name: Ringo
bio: (New York City, NY: -Sep 1988) Stage name of Harry Ringel. Learned magic as a young boy. Psychology major at New York U. Minor pro, working close-up in clubs & restaurants. Pet effect: Linking Rings, hence his nom de magique. Moved to Los Angeles where he became a downstairs fixture at the Magic Castle. [Mag]

name: Rink
bio: (Holland: -30 Nov 1985) Stage name of Johan H. van Rinkhuyzen. Pro close-up. 1955 FISM 2nd prize for micro-magic. See Hugh Miller, Rink's Original Rope Mysteries (1972, 28pp). Tricks in Genii, etc.

name: Rinn, Joseph F. "Joe
bio: (New York City, NY: 31 Jul 1868-13 Oct 1952) Owner of a fruit & produce market in New York City when he met Houdini in 1889, showing him some new tricks. Amateur magician & psychic investigator, often collaborating with Houdini in the early 1920s. Investigated Eusapia Palladino (1910), John Slater (1921), etc. Authored mystery magic play Zeno, which played in New York City 1923-25. Memoir is Sixty Years of Psychical Research (1950, 618pp). [MUM12/52; SAM; Gib]

name: Ripley, G. Sherman
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Amateur. Aka "Dr. Chang". Wrote Giant Card Magic (8pp), An Introduction to Magic (1946; repr 1955; 1960, 127pp), & Magic for Boys (1954).

name: Riser, Harry [Edward]
bio: (Vincennes, Indiana: 12 Mar 1928-) Executive manager, now disc jockey in Indianapolis. Learned at age 8 from library books & Gilbert magic set. Amateur close-up & parlor magician ever since. Closely associated with Charlie Miller in 1950s. Lecturer since late 1950s. Taught many magicians. Pet effects: 3-Ring routine, Egg Bag, Ball & Cone. Wrote "Riser's Repertoire" column in MUM since 1985. Tricks in Ibidem, Epoptica, & Arcane #6 (1981), which is an all-Riser issue. See Ed Brown, The Feints and Temps of Harry Riser (1997, 279pp). [Wh2]

name: Ritani
bio: (Germany: 9 Feb 1922-) Stage name of Richard Tanieswki. Amateur magician. 1955 FISM 2nd prize for general magic. Invented Floating Flying Saucer.

name: Ritson, Richard [Carter] "Dick
bio: (Sheffield, England: 1 Sep 1896-4 Aug 1969) Semi-pro magician with pseudo-Chinese act as "Wu-Ling, The Oriental Mandarin" & "The Amazing Mr. Wu", with "The Pagoda Mysteries". Noted prop collector. Articles in Midget Magician & Wizard. [WWM;Daw94,p.74]

name: Ritter, Werner
bio: (Germany: 11 Jan 1948-) 1975 MZvD 1st prize in closeup. [Nad]

name: Ritzer, Franz
bio: (Germany: 26 Apr 1925- ) Magician & collector of playing cards in Wasserburg, Germany. [Nad]

name: Rivkin, Steven E.
bio: (Washington DC: 9 $ ^{th} $ October 1953 - ) Great nephew of golden age Hollywood composer Bernard Herrmann, Travel Agency Manager for 20 years. Half time entertainment at RFK Stadium for Washington Whips Soccer team 1968, performed music and theatre while at College of Santa Fe, Grad Psychology 82. Joined the Psychic Entertainers Association 1995, Mystery School 1995, member of Shadow Digest, past member of IBM and SAM, published many articles appearing in MUM, Oracle, Vibrations, Bruce's annual Grymoire and others. Invented various tricks and routines. Local entertainer. No longer performs and working on various magic related writing projects. Noted collection of vintage spirit magic and séance equipment. Stage names and pseudonyms used are Stefan Dardik and Naimandus, specializes in mentalism and bizarre magick.

name: Rix, Claude
bio: (France: 1928-) Stage name of Claude Albert. 1958 FISM 2nd prizes for manip. 1960 Festival de Illusionismo (Oporto, Portugal) Grand Prize. 1961 FISM 3rd prize for manip. 1964 FISM 2nd prizes for general magic & close-up. AFAP Silver Medal 1978. Wrote Original Close Up Routines (31pp) & Five Little Beads (1986). [Dif]

name: Rob, Dieter
bio: (Germany?: 6 Dec 1935-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Robart
bio: (Britain: c1934-) Stage name of Robin Ingleby.

name: Robbins, Al[bert Christie]
bio: (Harrison [near Newark], New Jersey: 25 Dec 1901-1 Jun 2000) Learned c1912 from a railway telegraph operator. PR director & musician. Became semi-pro magician in 1920, billed since 1921 as "Al Robbins, the Genial Gent of Magic". Full-evening close-up for private organizations. Pet effects: rope magic & Linking Rings. Invented Lighted Candle & Silk in 1939. Ended as a full-time pro magic teacher and performer in Bakersfield, specializing with a snake act. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. [SAM;WWM;Wh5]

name: Robbins, D[avid] "Dave
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s). Pro dealer (D. Robbins & Co.) in Manhattan and later Brooklyn by since 1946 or earlier. Co-edited (with Irv Feldman) Magic Is Fun as house organ 1946-47. Issued a catalog in 1950 (96pp). Edited Practical Magic (1953, 79pp), as reprinted from his magazine.

name: Robbins, Todd
bio: (USA: 1958-) Pro sideshow magician. Articles in MUM. [MUM2/98,3/98]

name: Robelly
bio: (Orléans, France: 4 Jun 1894-Jan 1976) Stage name of Robert Rouet since 1913. Formerly "Professeur Wilson", "Abdouz-el-Ménir", & "Ten-Okio". Pro comedy magician since 1908. ASAP Silver Medal 1932. Founder-President of Groupe Régional des Magiciens de la Touraine 1941-53. AFAP Master Magician. Robert-Houdin Gold Medal. Director of L'Escamoteur 1947-66. Father of "Rogello". Wrote 8 books in French, including Trucs et Grands Trucs (1936), Galerie Magique (1938, 276pp), Trucs et Secrets (1940), Trucs et Évasions (1926), the classic Le Livre d'Or (1949), & Trucs et Pépins (1966). Articles in Illusioniste, Escamoteur, Prestidigitateur, Passe-Muscade, Journal de la Prestidigitation, etc. [Dif;Rob1;Bou]

name: Robert, André [pronounced row-BEAR]
bio: (France: 1942-) Stage name of André Laugier. Learned card magic at age 8. Semi-pro close-up & cardman since c1968. 1973 FISM 2nd prize in card magic; 1975 Baden-Baden 8th prize in close-up; 1979 FISM 2nd prize for card magic. Also teacher & lecturer. Wrote books in French on card magic, including Précis de cartomagie (1972), Card Révélations (1980), & Expertformance (1983). Edited two magic magazine annuals. Trick in Apocalypse. Dealer in magic books in Marseille. [Bou;Lo]

name: Robert, Serge
bio: See: "Veno, Dr. Robert"

name: Roberta
bio:
Griffin, Roberta

[See also: Byron, Roberta]

name: Robert-Houdin, [Georges-]Émile
bio: (St.-Gervais, France: 23 May 1851-13 Oct 1925) Eldest son of Jean-Eugène Robert-Houdin by his 2nd wife. Learned assisting father in 1846. Director of Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1873-83. Retired to become a painter. [Dif] Robert-Houdin, [Jean-Eugène] [pronounced row-BEAR ooh-DANH) (Blois, France: 7 [sic] Dec 1805-13 Jun 1871) Born Jean-Eugène Robert. Soon after his marriage to Cécile Houdin in 1830, he adopted "Robert-Houdin" as his stage name & had it legalized on 10 Sep 1856. Apprenticed as a watchmaker in Blois, he learned magic c1827 from accidental purchase of the 2-volume 1792 edition of the Dictionnaire encyclopédie des amusements des sciences, mathématiques et physiques, which included tricks copied from Ozanam, Guyot, Decremps, Pinetti, etc. Claimed he had received advanced lessons in 1829 from Torrini (see). Pro illusionist & sleight-of-hand artist. Founder-owner-director Théâtre Robert-Houdin in Paris 1845-1852 when he passed it to his brother-in-law, "Hamilton", although continuing to perform there until retired in 1854. Called "The Father of Modern Magic" since as early as 1909 (by Hilliard). Had played Belgium (1846, 1849, 1853), London (1848 & 1853), Germany (1853, twice), & Algeria (1856), the last bringing him out of retirement at the request of the French government. A prolific inventor, including the handkerchief pull, The Orange Tree (1845), Light and Heavy Chest (1845), Shower of Plumes (1845), Flower in Buttonhole (1845?), Le carton fantastique (1848), Aerial Suspension (1849), Diavolo Antonio (1849), and possibly both silent code (1849) & Stop Trick (by 1868). Wrote Les Tricheries des Grecs dévoilées (1861; 4 reprints to 1892), with 4 English translations: by anonymous as The Sharper Detected and Exposed (1863, 268pp), by Professor Hoffmann as Card Sharping Exposed (1882, 316pp), by M.I. Smithson as The Tricks of the Greeks Unveiled (1882, 188pp), & by J[oseph] N. Forster as Card Sharpers: Their Tricks Exposed (1891, 280pp). This last was pirated, title & all, by W.J. Hilliar (1902, 201pp). A German tr is Die Kunstgriffe des falschen Spiels (1862, 176pp). A Spanish tr by Ricardo Palanca y Lita is Segretos de los Garitos (1879; repr 1891 & 1911). Also wrote Les Secrets de la Prestidigitation et de la Magie (1868, 412pp; with 3 reprints to 1882). English tr by Professor Hoffmann as The Secrets of Conjuring and Magic (1878 [sic], 371pp). Spanish tr as Los Secretos de la Prestidigitation y de la Magia (1881). Also wrote the posthumously published Magie et physique amusante (1877, 295pp; repr 1882, 1892, 1898, etc). English tr by Professor Hoffmann as The Secrets of Stage Conjuring (1881, 252pp). Spanish tr as Magia y Fisica Recreativa. Autobio is Confidences d'un Prestidigitateur (1858, 2 vols, 408+415pp; repr 1859, 1861). English tr by Lascelles Wraxall as Memoirs of Robert-Houdin (1859, 293pp; repr 1942 & 1964). Dutch tr as Bekentenissen van een Goochelar on Kunstenaar (2 vols, 1861). Spanish tr by A[velino] Martinez as Confidenciás de un Prestidigitador (1894). German tr ed by A. Adrion as Die Memorien des Robert-Houdin (1969). Bios are William Manning, Recollections of Robert-Houdin (1891, 66pp; repr 1898); Houdini, The Unmasking of Robert-Houdin (1908, 319pp); Henry R. Evans, A Master of Modern Magic (1932, 58pp); J. de Montgon, Robert-Houdin (1939); Jean Chavigny, Le roman d'un artiste: Robert-Houdin rénovateur de la magie blanche [1943], 2nd ed rev (1969); Alain Sergent, Le Roi des Prestidigiteurs (1952); Michel Seldow, Vie et secrets de Robert-Houdin (Paris: 1971, 185pp); S.H. Sharpe, Salutations to Robert-Houdin (1983, 193pp). [Magicol#57;Dif;Pr;Ch]

name: Robertini
bio: See: Dammann, Günther

name: Roberts, Allan
bio: (New Zealand: -1940) Pro. Aka "Gus Ford" & "Popo Adair". Toured his own company thru his homeland for many years, doing mainly school shows & selling pocket tricks. Credited by Edgar Benyon for launching his career. Died in poverty.

name: Roberts, Eddie
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-60s) Stage name of Edward Gaillard. Pro. On Nicola's staff during 1938-39 Pacific Tour with his assistant-wife in a second-sight act. Then since 1940s in nightclub second-sight act as "Lucille & Eddie Roberts" & "The Roberts". [St;Ch;Wal]

name: Roberts, Lucille
bio: (USA: c1909-1977) Stage name of Mrs Edward Gaillard, assistant-wife of the above.

name: Roberts, Whitey
bio: (USA: 1902-) Billed as "The Magic Juggler". Stage name of Alston Peterson. Pro vaudeville. [Mag;Wat]

name: Robertson, Professeur
bio: (Lorient, France: 22 Jun 1887-30 May 1968) Stage name of Robert-Adrien Colson. Pro debut at age 18 in Paris cafés with card tricks as "Roberty". In 1910 he took the stage name "Robertson" and married "Lucile" with whom he did a 2-person mindreading act and worked magic as a single. Toured with Bénévol's troupe 1913-37. When Lucile retired in 1946, she was succeeded in the act by Miss Lucy Sloves. Father of Odette Colson. [Dif;Cl]

name: Robertson, G.
bio: (Glain, Liège, Belgium: 15 Jun 1763-2 Jul 1837) Stage & pen name of Étienne-Gaspard Robert. Debut with phantasmagoria as amateur in 1784 & as pro in 1794. Became a pioneer balloonist in 1812. Wrote Mémoires récréatifs scientifiques et anecdotiques du physicien aéronaute G. Robertson (2 vols, 1831-1833). [Daw;Pr;Cl;Ch;St]

name: Robertson, Robin
bio: (Canada?: fl.1960s) Cardman. Wrote Handle with Care (1964, 46pp).

name: Robertson-Keene
bio: (England: 5 Mar 1880-7 Dec 1968) Stage & pen name of Charles Job Keen, aka "Profr. Day". Pro with sleight of hand, juggling, & chapeaugraphy. Lived in Essex County. Wrote as Robertson-Keene Novel Notions in Magic (1905, 189pp), More Novel Notions (nd [1907], 112pp), Ventriloquism for Beginners [c1936], & as "Will Baffel" Easy Conjuring without Apparatus [n.d.]. As "Ye Jester" wrote "New Lamps for Old" column in The Magician. Prolific contributor to The Magician Monthly under own & pen names. [St]

name: Robin, Henri [pronounced onh-REE row-BANH]
bio: (Hazebrouck, Nord, France: 12 July 1811-24 Feb 1874) Stage name of Henri-Joseph Donckèle by Apr 1844 when in France he gave his first documented performance. Toured Italy 1844-45, Germany 1847, England 1850-52, the Continent 1853-61, & England 1961-62. Thence operated his "Salle Robin" magic theater in Paris from 1862 until he retired in 1869. Thence the landlord of an apartment house in Paris. His programs were limited to apparatus tricks, second sight, automata, & since 1865 spirit exposés. No sleight of hand. Wrote 3 publicity booklets in French: Album des soirées de Mr. et Mme. Robin [1846, 8pp] & L'Almanac illustré 'Le Cagliostro' (2 issues of 32pp each: 1864 & 1865). A closely researched bio is Edwin A. Dawes, Henri Robin: Expositor of Science & Magic (1990, 57pp). NOTE: Jean Caroly was responsible in 1902 for popularizing the myths that Robin was a Dutchman named Dunkell born in 1805. Although Robelly corrected these errors in 1952, they persist in most books. [Escamoteur#33:Dif:Cl:Daw] "Robini" [misspelling of "Rubini"] SEE: Anderson, Phillip Prentice

name: Robinson
bio: (Britain: fl.1770s) Pro who billed himself as "Conjurer to the Queen" in 1778 when he shared a booth at Bartholomew Fair with Mr Flockton. [CI]

name: Robinson [or Robertson]
bio: (USA: fl.1870s) Aka "The Fakir of Vishnu". Pro. By early 1870s successfully toured the Pacific Coast states. Taught W. Golden Mortimer c1872 in California. [Magic12/01,p22]

name: Robinson, Ben[jamin Albert]
bio: (Tarrytown, New York: 15 Dec 1960- ) Learned at age 7. Pro comedy magician in theaters, colleges, & nightclubs. Specialized in the Bullet Catch from 1985 to 1993 during which time he performed it 5 times. Wrote Twelve Have Died (1986) & The John Booth Index (1990, 243pp). 1990 Milbourne Christopher Foundation Award; Howard Bamman Trophy for Best Article in The Linking Ring, "Al Flosso: An American Original Revisited at 100". TV commercials for Levis & American Express. Articles in Magicol & MUM. [Bo#233;Daw2]

name: Robinson, Fred
bio: (Britain: 1910-23 Feb 1986) Railwayman. Amateur sleight-of-hand magician & card expert. Founding editor of Pabular in 1974. His daughter, Annabelle, won the Craig Trophy in 1969.

name: Robinson, Geoffrey [A.], OBE, MIMC
bio: (Rugby, England: 1913-) Hospital chartered accountant. Amateur magician. Former Honorary Treasurer of Magic Circle & President (1944-1950s) of British Ring. Pioneered British TV magic in 1950s with his "Whirligig" series. Inspired the New Era comedy team at conventions. Chairman of Old Tyme Music Hall. Plays musical saw. Edited Magical Gazette 1941-42 (3 issues). Wrote Magic as a Pastime (1960, 115pp). [Daw2]

name: Robinson, Hector
bio: (London, England: 17 Dec 1909-12 Feb 1999) Middle child & younger son of William E. "Chung Ling Soo" Robinson. Learned magic as child. Oriental & Persian rug salesman in England until retired. Amateur magician as "Sung Ling Soo" [sic], performing in Chinese costume. Collector. Lectured on Chung Ling Soo in Britain & the USA (in 1982) until became too ill c1990. [Wh2] "Robinson, L. A." SEE: Herman, Frank J.

name: Robinson, Lou
bio: (USA: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Pro magicienne with act called "The Crucible" using liquid air. Played the London Pavilion in 1905. NOTE: No relation to W.E. Robinson. [Mar]

name: Robinson, Olive "Dot
bio: (USA: fl.1880s-1910s) Born Olive Path. The diminutive dancer-singer in Boston was since 1887 principal assistant of William E. Robinson, first in his Black Art act, then with Kellar's troupe, finally with Robinson's "Chung Ling Soo" act as "Suee Seen" 1900-18. Married Robinson in 1906, becoming his 2nd wife. Returned to USA in 1920. [Pr]

name: Robinson, [E.] Tweed
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 7 Oct 1934-) Learned at age 10 from library books. Semi-pro magician 1948-52. Now ad agency executive in Warsaw, Indiana. Collects books on classic & close-up magic. Writing book on Al Baker's bio & tricks. [Wh5]

name: Robinson, William E [Ilsworth] "Billy
bio: (New York City, NY: 2 Apr 1861-24 Mar 1918) Of Scottish-English parentage. As a youth apprenticed as a mechanic & metal worker. Turned pro magician in 1880 as "Robinson, the Man of Mystery", including a black-art act with assistant Olive Path whom he later (1906) married (his 2nd marriage after Bessie Smith). Stage manager to Harry Kellar c1887-1893. With A. Herrmann, 1893-96, as stage manager, chief mechanic, performer (as "Achmed Ben Ali"), & understudy. During this early part of his career he made props & large apparatus for Patrizio, Balabrega, Powell, Kellar, A. Herrmann, & L. Herrmann. Then on own again 1900-18 & world famous with his pseudo-Chinese stage act, initially in Paris in Apr 1900 as "Hop Sing Loo" (a failure) but then in London since May 1900 with great success as "Chung Ling Soo". Toured the Continent in 1901. In 1908 played Paris & Brussels. In 1909 toured Australia & New Zealand. In 1912 again played Paris. Began a world tour in 1917 that evidently got only as far as Bombay. In 1918 he was mortally wounded doing the Bullet Catch onstage at the Wood Green Empire Theatre in London, dying the next morning. Father of Hector Robinson. Invented Astarte (in 1889 with B.B. Keyes), Gone! (1894), possibly Drum that Can't be Beaten (by 1903), & Shooting through a Woman (early 1907). Wrote Spirit Slate Writing and Kindred Phenomena (1898, 148pp). Tricks in Magic. Articles on magic in Scientific American & The Modern Wizard. Bios are Will Dexter, The Riddle of Chung Ling Soo (1955, 223pp); Val Andrews, A Gift from the Gods--The Story of Chung Ling Soo (1981, 204pp); Gary R. Frank, Chung Ling Soo: The Man behind the Legend! (1987, 35pp); & Gary R. Frank, Chung Ling Soo: The Man of Mystery (1988, 52pp) [Pr;Fi;Dif;Wal;Bus; Magic12/02,12/03,7/06,7/08,12/08]

name: Robison, Fred [P.]
bio: (Curwensville, Pennsylvania: 7 Apr 1888-13 Jul 1945) Inspired seeing F.E. Powell show. Owner of printing shop in hometown. Semi-pro since 1910 as club-show magician, mixing small magic, ventriloquism (with "Jerry"), & rag pictures. [SAM;St;WWM]

name: Robson, Stuart "Poppa" "Rob
bio: (London, England: 12 Jun 1892-21 Aug 1946) Moved to USA (New York City). Minor actor & theatrical director. Stage manager in 1920s for Florenz Ziegfeld, including some of his "Ziegfeld's Follies". Pro magic dealer in New York City, first privately, then since 1940 publicly as "The Conjurer's Shop". His widow, Dorothy, sold it in mid-1947 to Abbott's. Wrote Tips on Thumbs (1938, 36pp), Tips on Flash Paper (1938; repr 1951, 50pp, as Flash Paper Tips with Ralph W. Read), & More Tips on Flash Paper. Edited Conjurer's Chatter 1940-46, his house organ.

name: Rocambole
bio: See: Comitre, José

name: Rocco
bio: See: Silano, Rocco

name: Roch, Leonore
bio: (Falkenstein, Auerbach, Germany: 14 Aug 1944-) Pro partner-wife of Peter Roch as "Peter und Lonny". [Win]

name: Roch, Peter
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 25 Mar 1937- ) Pro in East Germany with partner-wife Leonore as "Peter und Lonny". 1975 Prague Magic Festival prize. [Win] Rochas [d'Aiglun], Colonel A[lbert] de (France: 1837-1914) Historian of science. Contributer to La Nature & wrote Les origines de la science et ses premières applications (Paris: 1883, 288pp), which drew heavily on Hero of Alexandria.

name: Rock, Will
bio: (North Auburn, Massachusetts: 25 Apr 1907-4 [sic] May 1995) Stage name of William George Rakauskas, of Lithuanian parents. Inspired in Mar 1920 seeing Eugene Laurant show. Semi-pro illusionist since 1928. In 1931 worked as assistant & secretary to The Great Raymond. In 1938 bought a few of Howard Thurston's major illusions from Jane Thurston. Then a few months later that year bought the entire Harry Thurston illusion show in 1938 for $1,000. For next 4 years barnstormed the USA & Canada. In US Army in WW II performing for the troops. After the war never returned to the stage, instead working as a Detroit dry-cleaning plant's salesman until retired in 1983. In 1954 sold his Harry Thurston props to Chuck Kirkham. Died in Mt. Clemens, Michigan. [LR7/95;Pr;Bos;Tay;Jinx#146;WWM]

name: Roden
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 28 Aug 1913- ) Stage name of Agapito ALMONICID GARCIA. Learned manip in 1936. Pro close-up as "Roden". Technical director of & co-magician in Fu-Manchú show in Barcelona & Madrid in 1956. 1969 Spanish National Congress (in St. Sebastian) 1st prize in comedy magic (shared with "Sager"). Wrote Mosaico Mágico (1962), Iniciación a la Prestidigitación y juegos de magia, Manipulación de dedales, Juegos con cartas redondas, & Rutinas con la caja Okito. [Xe;Cam;Fu1]

name: Rodolfo
bio: See: Gács, Rező

name: Rodrigo
bio: See: Pizzuti, Claudio

name: Roëtig" [misspelling]
bio: See: Röthig, Franz

name: Rogello
bio: (Orléans, France: 9 Apr 1921- ) Stage name of Roger Rouet, son of Robert "Robelly" Rouet. Charter member of his father's Groupe Régional des Magiciens de la Touraine 1941. Giant Memory act. 1947 Paris special prize for allied arts; 1948 FISM 1st prize for allied arts. [Dif;Rob1]

name: Rogers, Don
bio: (USA: 20 Feb 1900-5 Jul 1971) Stage name of Ernest K. Schieldge. Recruited in 1922 by IBM founders Len Vintus & Gene Gordon as IBM Member #3. Original co-editor (with Gordon) of The Linking Ring 1922-26. Wrote Merrie Magical Chatter (24pp). [Bo#197]

name: Rogers, James "Jimmy", MIMC
bio: (Chiswick, London, England: 19 Mar 1902-21 Aug 1980) Inspired seeing Chung Ling Soo. Semi-pro to pro magician. Did an early (pre-Pollock) dove act. [Go;Go2]

name: Rogers, [Michael Frederick] "Mike
bio: (Clay Center, Kansas: 19 Sep 1938-11 Jun 2001) Raised in Lander, Wyoming. Inspired at age 7 by school-show magician Duke Montague. Self-taught until joined US Navy in 1956. Left US Navy career as Warrant Officer 1956-76 to do pro close-up at trade shows, specializing in card magic & Cups-&-Balls and a top trade-show magician. A master of the Floating Cane. First to manufacture high-quality precision die-cut rabbits for Multiplying Rabbits. Mentor of Steve Bruecker. Internet pseudonym: "Bart Bosco". Invented miniature leather-covered baseballs for Cups-&-Balls. Wrote The Complete Mike Rogers (1975, 258pp) & Opinions (1986, 9pp). Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, Swami, & Epoptica. 10-year column in MUM. Videos (1987 & 1989). See also Mel Brown, Steve Bruecker & Mike Rogers Present Their Three Shell Game Routine (1985, 15pp). [Wh] Rogers, Wayne [Murray] (The Amazing Chicane) Lower Hutt, New Zealand 14 $ ^{th} $ Nov 1944- Known as The Amazing Chicane. Full time professional since 1993. Inventor/manufacturer of Missing Spade & Appearing Shovel 1996, Appearing Ladder from Briefcase 1998, Pinocchio's Nose & Appearing Broom 1999, In Your Face 2009. Published Commercial Chicanery (1992), Out of the Pole Vault (1998). First NZ magician to lecture at Magic Castle (1993) and lecture throughout UK (2002) Winner The Magic Circle Millennium Competition 2000 with "Signed Cad on Blue Stake" NZ Grand Master of Magic Award 2004. Articles in Magigram, The Gen, Genii, Magic Circular, LR &Magicana

name: Rogers, Terri
bio: (Ipswitch, Britain: 4 May 1937 - 30 May 1999) Popular pro vent with her dolly Shorty Harris. TV appearances in the UK and US. She was the only variety act ever to appear at Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club. Prominent amateur magician particular with the invention of topological magic tricks. Her life partner was Val Andrews. Invented Star Gate by 1985 & The Key (a force book) by 1991. Wrote several booklets on magic, including Secrets (1986, 82pp), Wipe Off (1986, 23pp), More Secrets (1988), & Top Secrets (1998, 128pp). Tricks in Talon, New Talon, & Repro 71. Video (1986).

name: Rohde, Dr Wolfgang
bio: (Prenzlau, Germany: 21 May 1944-) Physician in Prenzlau. Co-authored with Peter Schröder the computerized Almanach (1991, updated to 1995 supplement). [Roh]

name: Röhl, Richard
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 23 Jul 1896-26 Nov 1950) Semi-pro in Hamburg. Aka "Rolf Richardsen". Noted for original tricks. Published in Magie. [Vo57;St]

name: Rohmer, Sax
bio: (Birmingham, England: 15 Feb 1883-1 Jun 1959) Pen name of Arthur Henry Ward (formerly "A. Sarsfield Ward") since 1910. Popular novelist, best-known for his "Fu Manchu" series of 13 novels & 3 short stories published since 1913. David Bamberg, an avid fan, took "Fu-Manchú" as his stage name in 1929. Rohmer's interest in the occult led in 1919 to meeting Houdini who inspired him to study conjuring, including Goldston's "locked books". Befriending Goldston, became a member of The Magicians' Club. He also credits Houdini for having saved his reputation in 1921 by giving him the solution to his novel Fire-Tongue, which was then being serialized in Collier's Weekly. His Salute to Bazarada and Other Stories (1939) includes his short novel about a magician ("Bazarada") who was based on Houdini. Bio is Cay Van Ash & Elizabeth Sax Rohmer, Master of Villainy (1972, 312pp). [Daw;Go2;Bam]

name: Rohnstein, Dr Reinhard
bio: (Spandau, Germany: 23 Feb 1877-19 Mar 1955) Physician in Spandau. Expert amateur cardman. Wrote Neue Kartenkunst [Berlin: c1910]. Invented Follow the Leader (by 1929). See Charly Eperny, Das Rohnsteinbuch (5 vols, Vienna: 1959-61). Died in Spandau [sic], West Germany. [Vo57;St]

name: Rojas, Edwin [Ramon]
bio: (Miami, Florida: 25 Jun 1963- ) Learned in 1974 from Fassini's magic shop in Hialeah. Pro comedy stage magician since 1980 as "Edwin". Pet effects: You Do As I Do & Bill in Lemon. Several local awards. Articles in Top Hat. [Wh2]

name: Rojas Benavides, Ernesto [pronounced ROW-hahs]
bio: (Mexico City, Mexico: 31 Mar 1934- ) Learned in 1940 from Xmas gift Mysto Magic set. Lawyer, university professor, & government official in Mexico City. Amateur magician since age 12 specialized in mentalism & bizarre magick as "Dr E.N. Igma" & "Baron von Rätzel". Pet effects: ESP demonstrations. [Wh3] Roland, The Great (Prague, Austro-Hungarian Empire: 30 Oct 1872-1 Nov 1946) Stage name of Eduard Krause. A shoe salesman in Prague when inspired seeing Goldin's act. Pro illusionist & quick change artist in early 1900s. Played Switzerland in 1906 & Britain in 1907. His Irish assistant went on to become Mdlle Margo. [Vo57;Cl;Magic5/07;CMM10/06]

name: Rolfs, Charly
bio: (Germany: 6 Jan 1925-) Stage name of Karl Rolf Schlechte. [Roh]

name: Rolland
bio: (Vilna, Lithuania, Russian Empire: 1913-7 Jul 1984) Stage name of Marian Kryński. Pro illusionist. Appeared in Polish movie Czarodziej. TV. [Mec]

name: Rollin
bio: (France: -1793) Possibly the grandchild of "Comus" (Ledru). Pro, earning enough to buy a chateau. Guillotined during the French Revolution. Grandfather of the Rollin who was Interior Minister in the 1848 Provisional Government. [Fr]

name: Roltair, Henry
bio: (London, England: 1853-1910) Moved to USA in teens. Pro illusionist. Played the London Crystal Palace c1885. Invented Spider Girl illusion by 1893. Toured Britain with Barnum & Bailey Circus in fall 1898. Created & managed the illusion concession at Dreamland Park in Coney Island since 1906 (it burned in May 1911). Bio is John A. McKinven, Roltair: Genius of Illusions (1980). [Fi;Ch;Sphinx8/50]

name: Roltare, Charles
bio: (USA: 4 Feb 1873-14 Oct 1932) Stage name of Charles Roltare Eggleston. Debut in 1889. Stage actor turned magus. Pro. First editor of MUM 1911-12. SAM President 1911-12. Retired from stage in 1914. [MUM10/99]

name: Romagnoli, Angelo
bio: (Italy: fl.1870s) Pro. Highly inventive. [CI]

name: Roman, Madame Artot
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s) Minor pro. Played the Cambridge Music Hall in Mar 1886.

name: Romanoff, Professor
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Stage name of Carlton B. Case. Wrote Card Tricks (1930).

name: Romanoff, Prof.
bio: (Licata, Sicily, Italy: 1891- ) Stage name of Gian Battista Romano. Pro illusionist in Palermo. Wrote L'emulo di Bosco (1936). Edited (with Guido Varvaro) M.A.G.I.A. 1936?, 1937, 1938. Edited Lampo 1958. NOTE: Presumably not the lightning calculator "Romanoff" who played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1909. [Sil]

name: Romany
bio: (Britain: fl.c.1910s) Female escapologist billed as "Romany, the Handcuff Queen" who toured rural Britain. [Mar]

name: Romero, Freddy
bio: (Mexico: fl.1940s) Did a comedy drunk acrobatic dancing act with his wife Sonya [sic] as "Sonya & Romero". Freddy included much small magic. Featured actor in two of David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg's non-magical detective movies made in 1944: Asesinato en los Estudio [Assination at the Movie Studio] & Carne de Gallina [Goose Flesh]. In 1945-46 the couple toured with Bamberg's Magic Circus show in Mexico City, Havana, Venezuela, Colombia, & Peru where they left the show, both doing their drunk dancing act & Freddy as Bamberg's comedy magician foil in their hilarious 20-minute "Magic Bazaar" skit. [Bam;OI]

name: Romhany, Paul
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 25 Oct 1968 -) Learned magic at age 8 from a book and was then introduced to magic by next door neighbour and professional magician Wayne Rogers (The Amazing Chicane). Pro since 1991 with visual comedy magic as Charlie Chaplin. Pet effects are Dream Prediction and Floating Broom. His major influences include Ricki Dunn, Chuck Jones, Wayne Rogers, Alan Watson. Has a Bachelor of Music from Auckland University (1990) & diploma in teaching (1991), teaching degree in piano from Royal College of Music London. Received PCAM Gold Medal People's Choice Magic Champion 2004. Invented over 50 marketed routines. His favorites and best selling ones are: Dream Prediction (2001), Time Change (2005), CSI – case of the half-died hanky (2007), The Big Ten (1999), Bearly Impossible (2007). Wrote Lunch Is Served (2009, 186p), Entertaining on a Cruise Ship (2008), Secrets of A Ventriloquist (1988, 2009), Extreme Magic Makeover (2009), Magic From Down Under (2009), Magician To Speaker (2009). Regular articles in Magicana (1980 – 1989).

name: Ronaldo
bio: (Holland: fl.1950s) Student of Henk Vermeyden. 1958 FISM 3rd prize in general magic.

name: Ronay, Mac
bio: See: "Carthy, AI"

name: Roner, Fred
bio: (Lvov (Lemberg), Poland: fl.1920s-80s) Jew. Stage name of Alfred Rosner. Pro, specializing in card magic & pocket-picking. Published a 16-page publicity brochure in 1929 in Vienna. In 1938 moved to USA where he lived in New York City & worked commercially from his Greenwich Village studio as an artist in oils & watercolors. [Dam;St]

name: Roody
bio: (Italy: fl.late 1920s-mid 1930s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist & illusionist. Played New York City in 1934. [Rey] (Sydney, Australia: 30 Sep 1928-) Born Connie Maddison. In 1972 became assistant of Maurice Rooklyn, marrying him in 1980. Since 1974 when husband taught her she does own card manip act Rooklyn, [Connie Maddison] "Konni" as "The Queen of Hearts" & since 1980 also does childrens shows as "Konni The Klown" with magic, rag pictures, & balloon sculpture. [Wh2]

name: Rooklyn, Maurice "Maury", MIMC
bio: (Blackburn, England: 6 May 1905-22 Jul 1992) Inspired at age 4 seeing a magician. Moved to Australia at age 5. Learned at age 11 reading Hopkins' Magic, Stage Illusions. Pro illusionist & manipulator since age 15 & with own show by 1928. In 1934 was shot on 2 occasions doing Bullet Catch. Toured Britain 1936-40 with his billiard-ball act. Thence returned home, touring a large illusion show in Australia, Japan (1947), & New Zealand (1947 & 1949) until 1954. Always billed as "The Amazing Mr. Rooklyn". Won 1958 FISM 1st prize in manip. 1974 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1984 AMA Masters Fellowship. A fall down stairs in 1987 rendered him quadriplegic. 1991 SAM Hall of Fame. Memoir is Spherical Sorcery and Recollections of a 'Pro' (1973, 287pp). [Fu2;McC;Wal;Magicana#198;Wh2]

name: Roper, David
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Wrote The Comedy Magic Textbook (1987, 145pp).

name: Rose. Madame
bio: (Britain: fl.1880s) Pro, touring the London & the British provinces 1880-84 with Mdlle. Beatrice.

name: Rose, Don[ald W.]
bio: (Newburgh, New York: 2 Jan 1908-c1987) Amateur since 1918. Pro illusionist since 1927 with full-evening show. Aka "Don Amazo". Pet effect: Rising Cards. Invented the "Don Rose Doll House". [SAM]

name: Rose, Evelyn
bio: (Holland: fl.1960s) Stage name of Elli Rosshirt. Dancer until, believing she was getting too old for that, decided to become a magician, taking lessons from Henk Vermeyden around 1962. Pro. [Mar]

name: Rosella, Carl
bio: See: Nixon, Vic

name: Rosenberger, Marion
bio: (Leipzig, East Germany: 20 Mar 1949- ) Pro with husband Tilo and his parents as "Die Rosinis". [Win]

name: Rosenberger, Rolf
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 29 May 1921- ) Pro illusionist & kid-show magic in East Germany. [Win]

name: Rosenberger, Tilo
bio: (Dittersbach, Germany: 10 Oct 1944-) Son of Ursula & Rolf Rosenberger. Pro. [Win]

name: Rosenberger, Ursula
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 11 Aug 1921- ) Pro magic as assistant-wife of Rolf Rosenberger since 1955. [Win]

name: Rosenfeld, H. Orginski
bio: (Poland: fl.1840s-50s) Jew. Pro magician. Played England 1849-55. [Dam;Cl;Fr;St]

name: Rosenthal, Ed[ward Melvin]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 22 Dec 1927 – 12 Feb 2010) Learned from his amateur magician father who also bought him tricks. Before college was semi-pro with mentalism, kidshows, & trade shows. In 1961 became world's first shopping mall magician with a week's stint at Shopper's World in Framingham, MA. In 1966 bought the stock of Holden's bankrupt Boston magic shop. Succeeded Herman Hanson as producer of the Boston Magicales 1968-76. Also produced some IBM annual shows. Moved in 1976 to Scottsdale, Arizona, where he is now (2001) retired as a hearing-aid specialist, gives private lessons in magic, and collects small props & magic books.. [LR10/61;Wh01]

name: Rosenthal, Harvey [Martin]
bio: (New York City, NY: 17 Mar 1937-) Learned at age 8 from aunt's gift of Gilbert Mysto Magic set. Sociologist & criminologist in New York City. Amateur close-up magician, specialized in cards & coins. Semi-pro as magic lecturer (since 1964), publisher, & teacher. Wrote Close-Up Sampler (1976, 16pp), The Card Magic of Harvey Rosenthal (1977), etc. Tricks in Hugard's Magic Monthly, New Jinx, Pallbearers Review (+3 all-Rosenthal issues), Epilogue, Genii, Gen, Chronicles, Trapdoor, Blueprint, Magic, & books by Kort, Alton Sharpe, Fulves, etc. [Wh2]

name: Rosenthal, Ken
bio: (USA: 1970s-80s) Engineer by profession. Semi-pro magician as designer of hi-tech magic & optical illusions. Consultant on David Copperfield's Vanishing Learjet Illusion (1981). Invented Dimension 8, the famous effect of drops of water falling upwards. [Mag]

name: Rosini, Carl
bio: (Lodz, Poland: 14 Jan 1885-23 Feb 1969) Born Johan Rosen to Russian Jewish parents. Inspired at age 13 seeing Prof Baker show in Lodz. Learned at age 14 assisting magician Natan Schwartz in Russian circus for 6 months, following Schwartz to Germany. Moved c1900 to England where by 1905 he took "John Rose" as legal name & "Carl Rosine" as stage name. Pro manipulator and illusionist. Invented Vanishing Cane in 1906. Toured the Continent 1909-10 (including the Paris Olympia in 1910) & South America 1910. Moved to USA c1913. Toured South America 1919 with Theo "Okito" Bamberg as assistant & shadowist. Toured Canada & USA with Henry Huber 1937-38 in their "Battle of Magic" show. Ran the Headless Woman exhibit at the NY World's Fair 1939-40. With USO in WW II in USA, Middle East, Persian Gulf, & North Africa. Retired in 1948. Died in Clearwater Beach, Florida. President of Magic Collectors Association 1951-52. SAM Hall of Fame. Bio is Robert E. Olson, Carl Rosini: His Life and His Magic (1966, 100pp). [Pr;Ho]

name: Rosini, Margaret "Peggy
bio: (England: 1886-1 Jan 1978) Born Margaret Barclay. Ballet dancer on British variety stage. Met John "Carl Rosini" Rose in 1905 & married him in 1907, working as his assistant until their retirement in 1948. Her sister and co-assistant Dolly married Henry Huber in 1938. [Pr]

name: Rosini, Paul
bio: (Trieste, Austria: 29 Sep 1902-19 Sep 1948) Stage name of Paul Vucic [not “Vucci”]. Moved to USA in 1912. In 1917, as "Henry", assisted Julius Zancig in 2-person mind-reading. Learned magic in 1919 when Theo Bamberg taught him Cups-&-Balls and later by assisting Carl Rosini, from whom he took his stage name, much to Carl's annoyance. Pro close-up since early 1930s, mainly in nightclubs. Skilled but financially unsuccessful. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. 1939 Sphinx Award. His catch-phrase (said to his musicians) was "Play a teenie tiny valse". See Rufus Steele, Paul Rosini's Magical Gems (1950, 68pp, ghosted by Robert Parrish). Tricks in Tarbell #5, Magicana #1, & HMM. [LR8/99;Pr;Par;Berg;Ho]

name: Rosinis, Die
bio:
Rosenberger, Rolf Rosenberger, Tilo

[See also: Rosenberger, Marion]

name: Rosinoff, Barkann
bio: See: "Barkann, Roger"

name: Roskoff
bio: (Grasse, Alpes-Maritimes, France: 28 Jul 1854-15 Mar 1931) Stage name of Antoine-Joseph Hugues. Pro at the Théâtre Isola in the 1890s. Pro two-person mind-reading act (with the pretend-Hungarian "Fosca") in Carmelli's theater 1905 and with Bénévol's troupe 1905-08. [Dif;Rey]

name: Ross, Faucett W. "Faucy
bio: (USA: 19 Nov 1900-18 May 1987) Pro since around age 30 working fairs & carnivals. Ghosted the early Vernon booklets, including The Dai W. Vernon Super Card Subtleties (1932). Member of the "Secret Six". Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Actual author of Celestial Agent (1944, 44pp), which was stolen by Charles J. Maly & published by Laurie Ireland under Maly's name. See Lewis Ganson, Magic with Faucett Ross (1975, 227pp). Tricks in Genii. Audio.

name: Ross, Ian
bio: See: Flora, Brian R.

name: Ross, Kerry
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 8 Aug 1956- ) Learned at age 15 in SAM-sponsored Boy Scout troop. Pro since 1974, specialized in comedy escapism & magic. Corporate & cruise ship worker. Lecturer. Invented Corny Card Box (1981). TV bits. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Ross, Richard
bio: (Danzig-Langfuhr, Poland: 10 Feb 1946-19 May 2001) Stage name of Richard Rozenboom, son of Dutch father & Polish mother. Moved to Holland as baby. Inspired by & learned at age 16 buying tricks in a magic shop. FISM Grand Prix 1970 & 1973. Pro stage & close-up since 1974. Wrote The Ring Routine (1982). Video (1988). Operated the "Magic Art Center" in Bennebroek, Holland. [Bo#218;HC]

name: Ross, Rick
bio: (Canada: c1944-) Semi-pro close-up, stage, & platform magician. [LR5/87]

name: Ross, Stuart
bio: (USA: 24 Feb 1902-5 Oct 1949) Magician in Michigan. Press agent for several prominent magicians including Birch and Reno.

name: Ross, Dr. Sydney
bio: (USA?: fl.1930-50s) Pro magic (& palmistry). Worked the Rainbow Room in New York City for 7 years in the late 1930s and early 1940s where he was billed as "The Mysterious Dr. Ross". Played the Waldorf-Astoria Flamingo Room in 1946. TV bit in 1951.

name: Rossetti, Carlo
bio: (Turin, Italy: 18 Oct 1876-26 Sep 1948) Journalist & diplomat. Amateur magician in Milan. Major collector of magic books. Wrote Bibliographie Italienne de la Prestidigitation (5 vols, 1909-14), Il Trucco c'e ... ma non si vede (1926; repr 1940, 1946, & 1984), & Magia delle Carte (1935, 480pp; revised eds 1940, 482pp; 1946; & 1984). Tricks in Magic Wand, etc.

name: Rossi, Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Pro. With Tenyo Company in Tokyo in the 1970s. Articles in Talisman.

name: Rossignol, Claude
bio: (France: fl.1750s-60s) Pro. Worked the St.-Germain fair 1754-62. [Cl;St]

name: Ross-Kam
bio: (Sullivan, Indiana: 15 Jul 1901-9 Sep 1977) Stage name of Charles A. "Charlie" Rosskam Jr, son of the actor and stock show impresario. Pro stage magician with assistant-wife Madeline. IBM President 1954-55 [or 1955-56?.....].

name: Rössner, Max
bio: (Saxony, Germany: 1852-30 Jul 1906) Pro since 1868. Aka "Alexander Max". Assisted by the child "D'Alvini". Founded a cheap magic theater ("Kastans Panoptikum") in Berlin in 1893. [CMM9/06;Vo56;St]

name: Rotenberg, August “Gus
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 1 Jan 1864 [sic]-23 Sep 1928) Born Augustus Roterberg. Moved to USA in early years & learned cabinet making. Pro dealer in Chicago ("A. Roterberg", at 145 East Illinois Street) by 1894 (when he issued his 3rd catalog) until 1916, having sold his mail-order business in 1908 to Ralph Read and his shop in 1916 to Arthur & Carl Felsman. In later years collected postage stamps. Died in Chicago. Invented Multiplying Thimbles (8 on 2 hands version). Wrote The Modern Wizard (1894, 120pp), Later Day Tricks (1896, 104pp), New Era Card Tricks (1897, 284pp), & Card Tricks (1902, 168pp). His 400-page 3-volume notebook is in the Christopher Collection. [St;HMM2/60;Albo95]

name: Roth, David
bio: (New York City, NY: 13 Mar 1952- ) Learned at age 11 from magic set. Expert pro close-up coinman since 1972. Invented Portable Hole (1974), Tuning Fork effect (1974), etc. 1975 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. 1978 AMA Best Close-up Magician. House magician in magic department at F.A.O. Schwarz store in Manhattan. See Richard Kaufman, David Roth's Expert Coin Magic (1985, 371pp). Video (1985) & video segment (1986). [Bo#235;Wh2]

name: Roth, David M.
bio: (USA: 1875-1972) Pro mnemonic expert in Los Angeles. Famous for his mail-order Roth Memory Course (since c1910). In early 1920s helped David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg develop a systematic 2-person mind-reading code that Bamberg modified with The Ushers who then used it. [Bam;Zo]

name: Roth, Roy A[rnold], MIMC
bio: (Swansea, South Wales: 4 Nov 1929-) Learned at age 8 when father showed him Okito Box & his magic books. Master bookbinder. At age 21 started selling wallets to Harry Stanley's Unique Magic Studio. Semi-pro close-up & stage magician with assistant-wife Irene. At age 27 turned pro as "Leeroy the Magician". Since c1968 proprietor of RAR Magic in Swansea, personally crafting quality magic supplies, mainly in leather (wallets, cones, close-up cases, etc) & wood. MIMC 1988. Numerous inventions, including Grind-A-Ring = Ring Cruncher (1967), Zig-Zag Wallet (by 1975), Credit Card Grinda (1995 with Larry Becker). Wrote Bendix Bombshell (1985) & lecture notes in French, German, & English. Articles in Stage, MUM, & Abra. [MC7/86;Wh2]

name: Rothbart, Dr Ladislaus "Laszlo
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1887-1950s?) Hungarian Jew. Amateur magician since boyhood. Inventor of many tricks, particularly with cards. In 1938 founded in Budapest the Circle of Amateur Hungarian Prestidigitators. Wrote Deck in Hand: Magic of the Magyars (44pp). Survived the Nazi extermination camps in WW II, but committed suicide a few years later. Tricks in Jinx. [WWM]

name: Röthig, Franz
bio: (Hamburg?, Germany: c1875-c1925) Pro sleight-of-hand artist by 1899. Played the Paris Olympia in 1902. In 1903 toured Britain (as "Francis Rothig") & the USA. From 1909 to 1913 toured France, London (1911 when, billed as "The Parisian Conjuror", played the Alhambra), Italy, Switzerland, & North Africa. Moved to South America in 1914, dying in Chile in poverty sometime in the 1920s. NOTE: Misspelled "Roëtig" by Dif. [Vo57; Dif; Magic8/03]

name: Rothler, Dr Steven
bio: (Szekszard, Hungary: 1902-) Physician. Amateur magician. Student of Gustav & Bela Bernthaller. Joined M.A.M.E. in 1925. [WWM]

name: Roubalski, Pierre
bio: (France: 1901-) Engineer. Amateur magician. Moved to Argentina. AFAP Master Magician. [St]

name: Rouclere, Harry
