bio: (Paterson, New Jersey: 3 Jun 1866-3 Feb 1942) Stage name of Harry Terhune. Learned assisting a magician. Debut at age 8 as "The Boy Magician". Pro since 1878. Assistant to Prof E. Cooper Taylor 1884-86. Then on own. SAM Hall of Fame. [Pr;St;SAM;Dor]

name: Rouclere, Mildred
bio: (USA: c1869-7 Jan 1938) Stage name of Mildred May Terhune née Searing. Married Harry Rouclere in 1889. Taught magic by him. SAM Hall of Fame.

name: Rouclere Jr
bio: (Ridgewood, New Jersey: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Mrs Mildred Yull née Terhune. Inspired by & learned from parents, Harry & Mildred Rouclere. Pro by 1939 when she was only magicienne in USA giving a full-evening show. Pet effect: Natural Growth of Flowers. [SAM]

name: Roudnev, Vladimir "Volodya
bio: (Moscow, USSR: 19 Apr 1945- ) Self-taught at age 15 (1960) from books. Pro comedy magician 1969-present. Speciality: His own sponge-ball routine. Awards: Cuba (1978), Colombo (1980), & Moscow (1985). Founding-President of the Moscow Magicians Club 1982-present. [Wh2]

name: Rougeole, Sieur
bio: See: Roujol, Père

name: Roujol, Père
bio: (France: fl.1780s?-1830s) Pro magic dealer & prop maker in Paris 1820s-30s. His "modest little shop" in the Rue Richelieu was the gathering place for French magi prior to the Jul 1830 revolution, although later Jules de Rovère & Robert-Houdin met there. "Roulette" Roujol is most likely the "Sieur Rougeole" whom Pinetti mentioned in 1784 as being a tinsmith in the Louvre from whom he bought metal props. [Dif] SEE: Wells, Ozzie

name: Rovère, Jules de
bio: (France: fl.1810s-30s) Of noble birth. Pro sleight-of-hand artist in Paris. Coined the word "prestidigitateur" in 1815 and later also coined "prestidigitation". Toured France, Germany, & Switzerland by 1824; and England in 1828. Possible inventor of Horn of Plenty (by 1828). [Dif;Cl]

name: Rovi, MIMC
bio: (Caenarfon, North Wales: c1920-9 Jun 1996) Stage name of Ivor Parry. Printer by trade until retired. Semi-pro cardman since age 14. British Ring President 1984-85. See Lewis Ganson, Rovi

name: Rovit
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 4 Feb 1941- ) Stage name of Victor Manuel Ferreira Alves. Pro illusionist with assistant-wife Maria Teresa Alves. [Cam]

name: Rowe, Dr. Richard "Doc
bio: (Ballarat, Victoria, Australia: 17 [sic] Jul 1880-2 Apr 1952) An apprentice jockey, he entered vaudeville in 1895. Pro magician since 1898, excelling with cards, coins, balls, & handkerchiefs. Featured a gambling exposé act. Also did a telepathy act since 1910 with "Mystic Mora", his wife, touring as "Baldwin's Mahatma Co" in imitation of Samri Baldwin. World tour 1916-21. Wrote Thirty Pocket Tricks. Died in Melbourne. [Alm;Wal]

name: Roxo, Rudy
bio: See: Jacobsen, Clayton Lowell

name: Roxy
bio: (Seville, Spain: 16 May 1896-15 Jan 1968) Stage name of José Alias Guerra. Moved to Portugal & then in 1914 permanently to Brazil. Accountant in Rio. Amateur magician. In 1930s used stage name "Kiang-Tsin". Tricks in HMM. [Cam;Fam]

name: Roy
bio: See: Horn, Roy

name: Roy, Carol
bio: (Wichita, Kansas: 27 Nov 1929-May 2009) Born Carol Doris Williams. As a dancer-iceskater-rodeo rider in New York City (where Liberace called her "Miss Show Biz") she met Marvyn Roy in 1954. Learning magic from him, became his assistant & wife in 1956. Dubbed "Mrs. Electric" by Vince Edwards c1965. 1984 Dragon Award for Marvyn Roy & Carol. Articles in Genii & MUM. [Mar;LR5/97;Wh2]

name: Roy, [William] Fergus, AIMC
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 14 Jan 1935-) Inspired & learned in 1963 when he married Betty Davenport. Compere. Co-owner (with Betty) of Davenport's in London. Pet effect: Linking Rings. Retired as business executive in 1980 to devote himself to the Davenport business. Wrote (with Val Andrews) Illusions (1985, 144pp) & all Davenport catalogs since 1980. Articles in Abra. AIMC (1985). Father of "Bill Davenport" & "Roy Davenport". [Wh2]

name: Roy, Marvyn, MIMC
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 1 Apr 1925- ) Stage name of Marvin A. Levy. Learned at age 7 from aunt's gift of Mysto Magic set. Taught by Ray Muse c1939. Demoed for Floyd Thayer c1941-42. Assistant (with Wakeling) for Peter Godfrey in late 1940s. Pro since 1949 when he introduced his "Mr Electric" act. His assistant-wife since 1956 is Carol Roy. They often played the Paris Lido from 1957 thru late 1960s. Played the American Exhibition in Moscow 1959 & Radio City Music Hall in 1961. Added "The Diamond Illusionist" act to their repertoir in 1965. Played Portugal's Casino Estoril in 1968 & 1972. Other later acts are "Mr. Puzzle & Carol", "The Magical Jeweller" (close-up), & their "The Gambler" (giant cards), his latest. Pet effect: Globes from Mouth & other classics. 1975 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1984 Dragon Award to Marvyn & Carol Roy. SAM Hall of Fame. 1990 Christopher Award for best new illusion (Lady and the Diamond). Author of The Magic of Marvyn Roy (forthcoming). Articles in Genii, MUM, Magick, & several European magazines. TV bits. 1 video (1992). [Jef; Mag; HC; HMM3/61; Wh2]

name: Royer, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1600s) A water-spouter & fire-swallower from Lyon who toured the Continent. [St;Ch;Cl]

name: Royes, Irwin
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: fl.1980s) A dwarf. Amateur stage illusionist. [Des]

name: Royston
bio: (England: -8 Oct 1976) Stage name of Roy Carter. Pro small-time music-hall magician. Edited Regency Tatler (1946, 1? issue).

name: Rubens, Jack Mark
bio: (London, England: 1899- ) Amateur card man, numerologist, & psychic investigator. Founded Psychic News. [Go2]

name: Rubini, Signor
bio: See: Anderson, Phillip Prentice

name: Rubini, Eugen de
bio: (Moravia, Austro-Hungarian Empire: fl.1910s-20s) Moved to USA. Pro contact and non-contact mind-reader who was very popular in Europe (Hungary & Holland) by 1919, thence to the Orient (Java), and then in the USA since arriving in San Francisco in 1921. Worked with closed eyes but peeked a lot. Gave lessons to Houdini but without success. REF: G. M. Stratton, “The Control of Another Person by , Obscure Signs,” The Psychological Review, Vol.28 (1921), 301-314. [Berg;Jay]

name: Rubinstein, Dr Michael, DVM
bio: (New York City, NY: 11 Jan 1956-) Learned at age 9 from aunt's gift of tricks. Veterinarian (studied in Italy). Amateur close-up magician, specialized in coin magic. 1983 Bologna 1st prize in close-up. Wrote Intermediate and Advanced Coin Technique (1982, 121pp; originally in Italian), Creative Coin Magic (2 vols, 21+21pp), & Inside Street Magic (1985). 5 videos (1986, 1988). [Lo2;Ruh]

name: Rudeen, Dolf von
bio: See: Rudin, Dolf

name: Rudin, Dolf
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 11 Jun 1906-29 Nov 1993) Born Dolf, Ritter von Rudin (inheriting a title given his great-grandfather by Emperor Franz Josef in 1868). Inspired at age 23 seeing amateur magician. Learned by lessons in 1929 from Ottokar Fischer. Amateur card magician since 1932 in Vienna where won an award in 1933. Moved to USA in 1938 & Hollywood in 1939 where worked as film editor until retired in 1973. Legal name change to "Dolf von Rudeen" in 1953 to match American pronunciation. Semi-pro parlor & close-up magician (at Magic Castle, etc). Several SAM awards. Collector of playing cards. Articles in Genii. [Th;Mag;Wh2]

name: Ruegg, Théodore[-Auguste-Louis]
bio: (Geneva, Switzerland: 26 Mar 1883-18 Sep 1941) Amateur with sleight-of-hand & illusions. Aka "Harry Bertall". Joined the French ASAP in 1921. Moved to Bellegarde (Ain), France, by 1930. Operated a studio, "Marseille-Magie" in Marseille. Wrote Bibliographie de la prestidigitation française ancienne et moderne (1931, 94pp). In 1937 became first President of the Club des Magiciens Bibliophiles. Edited, jointly with Marcel Vassal as "Les Bervas", Le Poilu Physico (1939, 2 issues). [Dif;WWM]

name: Ruffin, Daniel
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Engineer. Semi-promagician (cards, coins, etc.) & mentalist. Aka"Anderson". Collector of magic history. Edited Le Magicien. Wrote Je jeu des balles d'eponge, Eventails de cartes, & Dictionnaire des espressions magiques Anglo-Américaines. [Bou]

name: Ruggiero, [Nicholas Stefano] "Nick
bio: (Springfield, Massachusetts: 26 Dec 1929-) Learned as kid from public library books. Coached by Joe Karson while working in his shop c1948. An assistant to Blackstone 1949-50. After army service became a tool-and-die craftsman, working semi-pro as magician. Prop maker with Owen Magic Supreme 1982-83. In 1984 joined Rich Bloch as partner in Collector's Workshop where he continues to work. [Wh] Rui [Rodrigues] de Sá, José [pronounced RRWEE-der-SAH] (Abravezes, Portugal: 16 Jun 1932-) Offset printer in Lisbon. Avid amateur magician, aka "Saiur". Active in magic clubs, conventions, & magazines. [Cam]

name: Rullman, Leo
bio: (Madison, Wisconsin: 28 Nov 1875-21 Aug 1946) Joined the SAM in 1913. Amateur magician, magic book collector, & semi-pro mail-order magic book dealer since 1900 from his apartment in New York City. His one venture as publisher (of H.R. Evan's Adventures in Magic) in 1924 was a money-loser. Edited MUM. Articles on old books in Sphinx. Article on collecting in Greater Magic (rev ed). His collection & stock was bought at the end of 1946 by the Fleming Book Company. [SAM;Go2;St;Albo95]

name: Rungie, [Herbert William] "Herb
bio: (Shawano, Wisconsin: 19 Jan 1907-17 Sep 1993) Inspired by & learned from father's gift of a Mysto Magic set. Watchmaker-jeweller by trade in his home town since early 1940s. Amateur comedy magician. Marketed many original tricks. Wrote Impromptu Card Routine (by 1947, 24pp ms) & Dream Poker with a Kicker (1983). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, New Jinx, Sphinx, Tops, Double Talk, etc. [Th]

name: Rupano
bio: (Venice, Italy: fl.1770s) A leading pro. Performed in Paris in 1776 at the Vaux-Hall & for the Royal family at Fontainebleu. [Dif;Cl;St]

name: Rupert, Paul
bio: See: Raw, Stuart Drayton

name: Rusca, Pietro
bio: (Italy: fl.1740s) Wrote II Maestro de'Giuochi (Milan: 1743), a rare early Italian book on conjuring.

name: Rusduck
bio: (USA: -24 May 1959) Pen name of J. Russell Duck. Police officer. Amateur cardman. Invented the Stay-Stack = Reflected Stack in 1957. Edited The Cardiste 1957-58 (11 issues). Tricks in Phoenix, New Phoenix, & HMM. [Genii2/66]

name: Rushworth, Geoffrey W. "Geoff
bio: (England: Jul 1931- ) Inspired at age 3 seeing a fairground magus. Semi-pro magician after WW II, including working (with his wife) as "Carddan & Patricia" and later as "Geoff Ray". Worked cabarets & cruise ships. Also did a manip act on a unicycle. Zina Bennett Trophy. IBM British Ring President, 1991-92. [LR2/92]

name: Russell, Fred
bio: (London, England: 29 Sep 1862-14 Oct 1957) Stage name of Thomas Frederick Parnell. Famous ventriloquist & pioneer of single-figure technique with "Coster Joe", his vent figure. Wrote Ventriloquism and Kindred Arts (1898, 96pp). Co-founded the Variety Artists Federation in 1906. Founder-editor of The Performer in 1906. [Daw2]

name: Russell, T. Van
bio: See: Bowyer, Tom

name: Russell, William A[ustin] "Billy
bio: (Batavia, New York: 21 Jan 1880-5 Dec 1966) Semi-pro performer, inventor, manufacturer in home town since 1905. 1951 Sphinx Award. Wrote Tricks of the Magic Trade (1910). Trick in Linking Ring. [Dor]

name: Ruthchild, Myriam
bio: (East Liverpool, Ohio: 15 Feb c1945-) Born Mary Hail [sic]. Pro mentalist-astrologer since the 1970s. Married to Lee Jacobs 1977-88, legally changing her name to "Myriam Ruthchild" during that period. Wrote Cashing in on the Psychic (1978), Psychotechnics (1981), etc. 1 audio (1982).

name: Rutledge, Ned
bio: (USA: 1926-) Inspired at age 10. Learned at age 12 by lessons from ex-pro Ralph Erlewine. Wrote (with J.G. Thompson Jr) Card Party (1965, 70pp) & Between Two Minds (1969, 75pp). Trick in HMM. [Th]

name: Ryan, [Richard Henry] "Dick
bio: (Fort Wayne, Indiana: 16 Jul 1928-) Inspired in 1938 seeing Blackstone & Dante. Pro close-up & platform magician since 1948. A pioneer since the 1950s in the industrial & trade-show field where he is widely rated among the world's top six. Also a major booking agent since 1950s. Wrote Confidential Booking Report #1 (1989, 57pp) & #2 (1990, 57pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Genii, & Tops. [Wh2;HMM4/59]

name: Ryan, [James Patrick] "Jim
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 6 Feb 1899-1 Apr 1992) Son of Irish immigrants. Inspired & learned in 1933. Taught by Laurie Ireland & Joe Berg. Bartender in Chicago by trade with his own Ryan's Magic Tap 1934-55. Semi-pro magician-bartender. See Phil Willmarth, Jim Ryan Close-up (4 vols, 1981). Tricks in New Phoenix. [LR5/92; Magic Menu10/97]

name: Rybakowicz, Anthony
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Pro mentalist. Originally worked as "Helmar" until Nelmar persuaded him to change to "Dr. Anthony".

name: Rybolt, Earl F.
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 6 Mar 1889-3 Oct 1954) Amateur magician. Collector of magic literature by 1919 when he got the H.J. Burlingame Collection from Dr A.M. Wilson. Added the collections of Walter S. Kaye & Charles T. Jordan. By 1937 he had 9,200 magic books, booklets, & single copies of magazines. In 1943 sold his fine library to Lloyd Jones. [Go2]

name: Ryss
bio: (Paris, France: 28 Mar 1880-30 Mar 1932) Stage name of Georges Gay. Billed as "Satan's Barman", he invented and specialized in the Magic Bar act, the modern Any-Drink-Called-For act, which he took to South America in 1927, playing the Casino in Buenos Aires in 1931. He inspired copy acts by Okati, The Great Marcel, De Roze, "Think-a-Drink" Hoffman, & Joan Brandon, among others. NOTE: Misspelled "Rhyss" by D. Bamberg. [Dif; Vo55; Bam]

name: Saal, Al[fred P.]
bio: (Toledo, Ohio: 6 May 1891- ) Learned magic at age 15 by buying tricks thru Roterberg's catalog. Debut at age 18. Pro sleight-of-hand (specializing in cigarette manipulation), shadowist, & ventriloquist. Claimed invention of producing multiple lit cigarettes ("The Man With The Lights"). Invented "Cards and Liquids" (by 1940). Retired to become a funeral director in Toledo. [Dor;Jinx#22;LR8/27, 6/33, 11/2000]

name: Sachs, Edwin [Thomas]
bio: (England: -26 Sep 1910) Athlete as young man. Then sports writer in London, including years with the Field. Wrote two books on Lacrosse, a game he helped introduce to Britain. Amateur magician, having learned from Cremer's The Secret Out (1871) & influenced by seeing A. Herrmann at the Egyptian Hall 1870-73. Then travelled 3 years in the Dutch East Indies, performing for local audiences. His articles on sleights were serialized in the Exchange & Mart. These were reprinted as his one magic book, the classic Sleight of Hand [1877, 204pp]. 2nd ed (1885, 408pp; repr 1980) & 3rd ed (1900, 424pp; repr as "4th" ed 1946 & "5th" ed 1953). [Magic6/01; Sphinx11/10; Vo56]

name: Sadowitz, Jerry
bio: (New Jersey, USA: 4 Nov 1961-) Born in the USA and raised in Glasgow after the breakdown of his parent's marriage. His mother returned to her native Scotland. Jerry took an interest in magic while at school. Pro comedian known for his offensive humor. He was actually promoted as 'too shocking to appear on TV.' Some of his earliest performances as a magician were at a Glasgow pub, the Weavers Inn. Pro comedian. Creative amateur card magician. Wrote with Peter Duffie Alternative Card Magic (1982, 33pp), Contemporary Card Magic (1984, 47pp), & Inspirations (1987, 119pp). On own wrote Card Hits (1984, 38pp) & Cards on the Table (1989, 105pp). Tricks in Genii.

name: Sadowniczy, Aleksander
bio: (Warsaw, Poland: 1928-Jul 1982) Sleight-of-hand artist, lawyer, & long-time Polish circus director. [Mec]

name: Sager, Faquir
bio: (Barcelona, Spain: 22 Feb 1922- ) Stage name of Francesc PINOL [REGAS]. Did a fakir act as Faquir Sager & illusions as "Gran Korbin". 1964 FISM prize for fakir act. [Xe]

name: Sager, Ludwig
bio: (Germany?: 23 Apr 1930-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Saghibu, Mago
bio: See: "Silvan"

name: Sahin, Haci
bio: (Turkey: fl.1720s) Pro escapist who worked a double-exchange from two baskets at a public festival in Turkey in 1720 with his partner Haci Mehmet. [Bo2]

name: Saikawa, Toyohisa
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Semi-pro close-up & stage magician in Tokyo. 1986 Nihon Close-up Magic Grand Prix. 1988 FISM 3rd prize for close-up. 1990 Nihon Close-up Magic Prize-of-Prizes.

name: Saint, Dr. Edward
bio: (USA: 8 Feb 1891-22 Oct 1942) Stage name of Charles David Meyers. Pro carry memory expert & crystal gazer as "Sesrad". Then Bess Houdini's manager & companion since 1934 when she moved to Hollywood. Originator of National Magic Day in 1938.

name: Saint-Lary, Yves de
bio: (France: fl.1960s) Pro manipulator & illusionist. Starred in Paris at Cabinet Fantastique 1960-63 & 1966-68. [Bou]

name: St. Andre
bio: (Holland?: fl.c1800) Stage name of van Gussem. Popular magician in Holland. [Bam,p12]

name: St. Clair, Ray
bio: See: “Raffles, Mark”

name: St. Eve, Steve
bio: See: Dusheck, Steve

name: St. James, Ted
bio: See: Karmilovich, Ted

name: St. John, Vivian
bio: (England: c1883-22 Jul 1961) Stage name of Tom Storey. Toured fairgrounds for some time as a magician & barker. Edited Cornish Pixie 1943-46.

name: St. Leon, Victor
bio:
St. Onge, Kevin [John] [pronounced saynt-ANGH] (Detroit, Michigan: 14 Jul 1957-) Learned at age 13 from books. Pro magician since age 25, specialized in card manipulation & stage illusions. Works conventions, festivals, restaurants, nightclubs, schools, private parties, radio, & TV. On 12 Jun 1979 he set the still-current "official" Guinness world record distance shot of 185 feet, 1 inch for card throwing. This beat the previous records set by Ricky Jay in 1976 & non-magician Tommy Jackson in 1977. REF: Guinness Book of World Records (every edition since 1980). Guinness also unofficially recorded his records for highest throw (to top of 14 story building), hardest (through 8 sheets of paper), & fastest (98 mph). St. Onge denies Jay's assertion that he (St. Onge) uses throwing in his card-magic act. [WWE;Wh2]

[See also: Gross, Art]

name: St. Pierre, Louis [Anthony]
bio: (St. Paul, Minnesota: 1888-18 Nov 1971) Ran away as a boy to join circus as a tumbler & juggler. Later a full-time pro magician, touring a stage show. Settled in Rockford, Illinois, to run a theater chain, continuing as an amateur magician. Together with son, bought the late Bert Wheeler's "Hollywood's Magic Shop" on Hollywood Boulevard in late 1947, renaming it Hollywood Magic Inc. AMA Board of Directors 1965-71.

name: St. Pierre Jr, Louis [Anthony]
bio: (Rockford, Illinois: 18 Jul 1926- ) Worked for telephone company. Amateur magician. Then after WW II military service, moved to Hollywood in early 1947. Later that year bought (with his father) the late Bert Wheeler's "Hollywood's Magic Shop", which then became Hollywood Magic Inc where he worked demos. Owner since 1971. Also operates a branch shop in Costa Mesa since c1978. [Wh]

name: St. Roman
bio: (Jaroslau, Galicia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Jarosław, Poland]: 14 Oct 1829-8 Jul [sic] 1917) Stage name of Samuel Thiersfeld, a Jew. Originally a confectioner but became interested in magic during military service. Pro illusionist 1857-1900, touring most European & some other countries. Retired in 1900, living his last years in Vienna. Invented Card through Handkerchief (by 1897). Bio is H.F.C. Suhr, Jedermann Zauberkünstler!

name: Kunststücke des berühmten Zauberers St. Roman
bio: (1899, 162pp). [Pr;Vo57;Dif;Dam;St]

name: Sakai, Hiroyuki "Hiro
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Works in Tokyo. 1988 Nihon Close-up Magic Grand Prix. 1989 Atsukawa Creativity Award. Wrote the original Japanese-language edition of New Magic of Japan. Invented Armband Mystery (1989). Tricks in Genii, Magic, etc. 1 video bit (1993).

name: Sakamoto, Taneyoshi
bio: (Japan: 1898-1988) Early influential amateur magician. Mechanical engineer in profession. Wrote Kijutsu No Sekai [World of Magic] in 1943. Sphinx Award for 1937.

name: Sakutaroo
bio: (Japan: fl.1870s) Pro magician. Toured Australia with Osaka Troupe in 1872. [Wal]

name: Salazar, Jerry
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro San Francisco coffee-house table-hopper to street magician in late 1970s & early 1980s. Wrote Three Ring Routine (1980). [Camp]

name: Salem, Peter
bio: See: Isaacs, Peter

name: Salern, Guel
bio: (Germany: 25 Feb 1888-29 Nov 1939) Stage name of Georg Scheck since 1907. Pro cabaret magician. [Vo57]

name: Salinas
bio: (Spain: fl.1890s) Pro magician when he toured Portugal in 1897 & took 3rd place at the Concurso de Ilusionismo. [Cam]

name: Salisse, John [Joseph], CBE, MIMC
bio: (Bournemouth, England: 24 Mar 1926-) Inspired c1946 by library bio of Robert-Houdin. Businessman. Amateur comedy magician & vent. Aka "John Morris". Honorary Secretary, The Magic Circle, 1966-85. SAM Hall of Fame. Co-wrote (with Anne Davenport) A Candid View of Maskelyne's 1916-1917 (1995). [Bo#312; WW;Wad] Salminen, [Sulo] Reijo [Uolevi] [pronounced RAY-you SAHL-mi-nin] (Lahti, Finland: 4 Dec 1930-) Learned in 1937 from reading Taikurin Kirja. Debut in 1938. Pro stage magician & manipulator of billiard balls since 1946. Frequent competitor in international magic congresses, including 1950 Stockholm 1st prize for pro & 1955 Stockholm Grand Prix. 1988 FISM jury. 1990 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic. Articles in Trollkarlen, Genii, Magie, etc. TV shows in Finland, Sweden, & Germany. [St;Wh2]

name: Salmon, Reginald "Reg", MIMC
bio: (England: 1896-15 Jul 1969) Stage name of Seymour [sic] Salmon. Executive with photographic agency (Fox Photos). Semi-pro cabaret & variety magician with full illusion show.

name: Salo, Arvo
bio: (Finland: 24 May 1895-) Pro builder in Helsinki. Amateur magician. Secretary of Taikapiiri 1948-49 & again since 1950. Contributor to Simsalabim.

name: Saltano, Maurice
bio: (France: 1930-) Stage name of Maurice Joubert. Pro general magic since 1940s, later with assistant Monique Dorian. They played the Cirque Medrano in Paris in 1958.

name: Saltarino, Signor
bio: (Germany: 1863-11 Jan 1941) Stage name of Hermann Waldemar Otto. Pro variety artist. Although not a magician, his 4 books on famous circus & variety artists include bios of several magicians of the 1800s: Pauvres Saltim-banques (1891, 212pp), Fahrend Volk (1895, 150pp), Artisten-Lexicon (1895, 275pp; 2nd ed, 1895, 316pp), & Das Artistentum und seine Geschichte (1910, 244pp). Died in Düsseldorf.

name: Salvano
bio: (Chojnice, Poland: 17 Sep 1929- ) Stage name of Tomasz Chełmiński. Inspired in 1945 seeing Nemo's show. Pro since 1948 with illusions, manip, etc. Toured Poland since 1954. Produced his large illusion show since 1961. Invented Silk from Bottle to Bottle (1963) & Silk to Cape (1968). Since 1966 has toured extensively abroad in Central & Western Europe, England, Africa, Japan, & USA with shows & lectures. 1970 Karlovy Vary 3rd place in manip. 2 videos (1985). A teacher of Jerzy Drewla. [Win;Mec;Magigram6/81;Wh2]

name: Salvin, Jack, MIMC
bio: (Britain: c1886-14 Jul 1959) Semi-pro. 1951 FISM prize in mentalism for Mr & Mrs Salvin. Chairman of Occult Committee of The Magic Circle & member of Society for Psychical Research.

name: Salwak, Dale [Francis], MIMC
bio: (Greenfield, Massachusetts: 7 Feb 1947-) Raised in Amherst, Mass. Inspired at age 5 seeing a magician & later learned from father's copy of Ripley's Magic for Boys. Debut at age 10. Did 1st pay show in 1957. Moved to Indiana in 1962. Chavez College graduate 1965. Semi-pro stage magician, specializing in manip with Zombie, cards, & canes. Moved to California in 1969. College English teacher (1974 PhD in English lit). Since 1974 produces his annual "Stars of Magic" for college audiences. Since 1978 co-owner (with Neil Foster until 1988) & director of Chavez College of Magic. Awarded 1975 Jack Gwynne Trophy & 1980 Bill Baird Trophy. 1990 AMA Lecturer of the Year. Edited The Magic Carpet 1962-69. Wrote A Trip to the Orient (1962), Spooks on Stage (1963), & For That Special Occasion (1965). Column ("American Spotlight") in Magic Circular 1990-present. Articles in Genii, New Tops, Maya-Jaal, Magic Circular, Linking Ring, & Magic Manuscript. [LR11/95;MUM4/92; Australian Magic Monthly6/90; MC9/90; Bo#207; Mag;Wh2]

name: Salwaro
bio: (Gelsenkirchen, Germany: 19 Feb 1902-22 May 1964) Stage name of Erich Möckel. After WW I, pro acrobat, juggler, & magician at fairs & in circus. During WW II performed for Axis troops throughout Europe. Later did magic only. Dealer, mainly for Vermeyden whose life he saved during the German occupation of Holland. Died in Gelsenkirchen-Horst. [St]

name: Sambalo
bio: (Paris, France: 1905-14 Aug 1975) Son of Hadschi Sambalo. Took up his father's Black Art act. Billed as "Der Geisterfürst" [Prince of Ghosts]. Aka "Omar Pasha". [Mül]

name: Samee, Ramee
bio: See: Margulis, Sam

name: Samee, Ramo
bio: See: Ramo Samee

name: Samek. Frantisek
bio: (Czeskie Budziejowice, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Czech Republic]: 26 Jul 1874-3 Jun 1957)

name: Samelson, Peter
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Pro close-up & illusions. Wrote Theatrical Close-Up (1984, 89pp). Magic Manuscript 1-man issue Sep/Oct 1987.

name: Samper
bio: (Portugal: fl.1970s) Stage name of Acácio SANTOS PEREIRA. Pro magician specializing in hyp act. [Cam]

name: Samson, Jørgen
bio: (Denmark: 30 Oct 1926-2002) Pro. Featured act of producing (from body loads) enough tables and flowers to fill the stage. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Jürgen". [Dif]

name: Sanada, Toyozane [pronounced TOE-YO-ZAH-NAY]
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) Pro card manipulator & stage magician. Lives in Osaka where he operates a 2nd floor magic shop. 1982 FISM special award for manip. 1982 Tenkai Prize. Wrote Sanada Toyozane no Card Manipulation (1983). Trick in MUM. NOTE: "Toyomi" as given name is never used by him, although technically an alternate Kanji reading as given by the uninformed.

name: Sanas
bio: See: Delcassan, André

name: Sanders, Arthur
bio: (Drammen, Norway: 4 Jul 1887-20 Feb 1957) A craftsman who produced fine props (coins, cards, etc) for Willmann, Conradi, Beber, & Hamley's. Also as street magician in Oslo & Paris. [Vo58]

name: Sanders, Fetaque [pronounced FEE-take]
bio: (Nashville, Tennessee: 12 May 1915-2 Jun 1992) Real name. Afro-American. Inspired by J. Hartford Armstrong. Billed as "The Great Fetaque". Pro stage magician (also vent & hyp) since 1930s, playing from Broadway to the New York World's Fair. Played USO camp shows 1942-45. Toured a Spook Show in fall 1947. Also played school assemblies. Usually played black venues. Retired in 1958 due to illness. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. Article in Phoenix. See Samuel Patrick Smith, Sell Your Act with Posters (1987) & Sell Your Act with Letters (1989). [MUM9/92; LR6/73; Walk2; SAM; Wat] Sanders, James J.(USA: 11 Jun 1894-) Inspired at age 12 seeing itinerant magician. Manufacturer by trade in Nashville, Tennessee, since 1916. Amateur magician, specialized in pocket-knife manipulation. [Th]

name: Sanders, Richard
bio: (Canada: c1966-) Pro trade show & restaurant magician in Toronto & Montreal. 1982 & 1983 Magie Montreal 1st prizes in close-up. Toured Europe in 1986. Wrote (with Jay Sankey) When Creators Collide (1987, 74pp). Tricks in New Directions, Arcane, Magical Arts Journal, New Directions, Genii, Magic Menu. [Genii7/91]

name: Sanderson, George P [ercival]
bio: (Sheffield, England: 23 Jun [sic] 1904-Aug 1986) Aka "Sigma" since 1919. Learned at age 13. Engineer by profession. Semi-pro magician from 1919 (age 15) until retired in 1970. Moved to Malta. Wrote The Concealed Art of Magic (1972, 174pp), Right Under Their Noses (1977), & Priceless Magic (1981). Articles.

name: Sandford, Frank, MMC
bio: (Britain: 1st decade of 1900s-1910s) Semi-pro. Pen names "Effess" & "F.S." as contributor to Magic.

name: Sandh, Ernst
bio: (Sweden: 22 Feb 1909-2 Apr 1972) Resident of Stockholm. Semi-pro magician as "Zandor". [St]

name: Sandro
bio: (Puerto Rico: fl.c1960s) Invented Magician's Credit Card (by 1976).

name: Sands, George
bio: (New London, Connecticut: 27 Feb 1920-) Born George Cohen. Self-taught & lessons from Abe Hurwitz in 1937. In teens worked as "Kanj-o", now as "Sandsational". Invented Sandsational Rope (1942), Ropesational, & Rope Warp. Demonstrator with Lou Tannen's 1939-42 & 1948 to machinist to salesman. In 1951 he & Hurwitz taught Bill Derman. Pro dealer (Sandsational Magic) from home in Phoenix, Arizona, since 1960s. Now semi-retired as dealer & lecturer. Wrote 7 booklets including Sands' Improved Ropesational (1962) & 3 Sandsational Rope Effects. Tricks in New Phoenix, HMM, Bat, Ibidem, Linking Ring, Genii, Coffee Break Chronicle, MUM, etc. Video. [Genii3/92;MUM1/92;Wh5]

name: Sandu
bio: See: Stadelman, Paul

name: Sandy
bio: (Valladolid, Spain: 30 Nov 1909-Jul 1962) Stage name of Fernando CALVO LÉON. Pro nightclub cardman. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1951 & 1961. Founded the Club de Ilusionistas Profesionales in Madrid in 1956. [Cam]

name: Sanger, "Lord" George
bio: (Britain: 1827-1911) Minor pro magician, billed as "The Wizard of the West", at his debut in 1848 in a fair booth. Later major circus showman until 1905 when he retired. Autobio is 70 Years a Showman (London: 1908, 128pp; 1st US ed, 1926, 249pp. Bios are John Lukens, The Sanger Story (1956); & Val Andrews, 'Gentleman George' Sanger (1989, 100pp).

name: Sankey, Jay
bio: (Canada: 1965-) Pro close-up & stage. Articles in New Directions, etc. Video segment (1986), audio (1987), & video (2002, 3 tapes). See Richard Kaufman, Sankey Panky (1986, 122pp) & 100% Sankey (1990, 88pp). Wrote (with Richard Sanders) When Creators Collide (1987, 74pp). Tricks & articles in Richard's Almanac, Magic Manuscript, Magic Menu, etc. [L&L Presents, #19 (2002)]

name: Sanlaville, André
bio: (Lyon, France: 30 Oct 1924- ) Amateur magician in Lyon. Aka "Andrellys". Joined the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Lyon in 1944 & was its President 1960-65. AFAP Master Magician. Major impresario of top talent magic shows in Paris, Berlin, Athens, Tokyo in 1940s-70s. [Dif;Sil;Bou]

name: Sanshias
bio: (Germany: fl.1810s) Pro travelling magician, including Britain in late 1810s. A teacher of Billy Purvis. Santanen, Jukka [pronounced YOO-kah SAHN-tah-nin] (Finland: 5 May 1927-) Pro manip & 2-person mindreading act with wife. Now retired.

name: Sanvert, Jean-Jacques
bio: (Paris, France: 27 Apr 1953- ) Inspired at age 8 by grandfather doing card tricks and at age 14 seeing a magic show at the Cabinet Fantastique when he began to practice. Professor of Law & Psychology in Paris. Also teacher of t'ai-chi. Semi-pro close-up (mainly cards) magician since 1979, originally sometimes as duet with Bernard Bilis. 1979 FISM 1st prize in card magic. Plays Le Double Fond in Paris. Invents card tricks, mainly influenced by Marlo. Tricks in Mad Magic, Journal de la Prestidigitation, Apocalypse, Lost Pages of the Kabbala, & Lorayne's Best of Friends I & II. 2 videos (1981, 1988). Co-editor Le Magicien since 1992. [Lo;Lo2;Wh2]

name: Sarandrea, Joseph M.
bio: (USA: c1897-27 Sep 1968) "Professor Paradise" & "Professor Zingare" as stage names. Under pen name "Joseph Leeming" wrote several books, including Magic for Everybody (1928), Fun with Boxes (1937), Tricks Any Boy Can Do (1938), Fun with Paper (1939), Fun with String (1940), More Fun with Magic (1948, 89pp), Papercraft (1949), & Tricks and Stunts with Playing Cards (1949). One was translated into German as Das Zauberbuch (Stuttgart: 1965).

name: Sardina, Maurice
bio: (Paris, France: 11 Apr 1891-27 May 1977) Learned magic in 1903. Engineer in Nice. Amateur magician. AFAP Master Magician. Edited Journal de la Prestidigitation 1945-49. Wrote La magie du sorcier (1946), with English tr by Fitzkee as The Magic of Rezvani (1949); Les 'erreurs' de Harry Houdini (1947), with English tr by Victor Farelli as Where Houdini Was Wrong (1950, 120pp.), which is Sardina's famous answer to Houdini's effort to discredit Robert-Houdin; & Rezvanimagie (1949). Translator of magic books, including Keith Clark's classic Encyclopedia of Cigarette Tricks in 1958. Tricks in J de la Prestidigitation. [Dif;Bou]

name: Sargent, Colonel H. J.
bio: (England: 1 Jan 1843-5 Feb 1896) Pro magician, illusionist, actor, & manager. Billed as "The Wizard of the South". Pro. In 1891 played Waterloo House in London on a bill with Hercat. Died destitute in a workhouse in Leeds.

name: Sargent, John W[illiam]
bio: (Europe?: fl.1920s) Played St. George's Hall in 1925, billed as "The Continental Mystic". (USA: 8 Jul 1852-24 Sep 1920) Aka "The Merry Wizard". Pro. Joined the SAM in May 1902 as Member #9. SAM President 1905-06. Secretary to Houdini 1918-20. Mentor of John Mulholland. SAM Hall of Fame 1990.

name: Sarrazin
bio: See: Vassal, Marcel

name: Sarwell
bio: (France: 9 Feb 1885-24 Oct 1918) Stage name of Albert-Édouard Wild. Pro magician & skilled manipulator.

name: Sassi
bio: (Italy: fl.1870s) Pro.

name: Satan
bio: (Seattle, Washington: 5 Sep 1893-17 Apr 1967) Stage name of Wilfred Alouis (or Alouis Wilfred) Seltten. Died in Philadelphia. [Roh]

name: Satan, Dr
bio: See: Daniel, John

name: Satanas
bio: See: Delcassan, André

name: Sataniano
bio: (Torún, Poland: 8 Jul 1931- ) Stage name of Adam Banaszkiewicz. Inspired as young boy & gave first show in 1962. Pro illusionist & manipulator since 1967, working restaurants, schools, & 5 times on cruise ship Stefan Batory. [Nad]

name: Sateli
bio: (Poland?: 26 Sep 1924-11 Apr 1988) Stage name of Jerzy Herbert Kupranek. Magician. Died in Guthersloh, West Germany. [Nad]

name: Satori
bio: (Germany: fl.1990s) Stage name. Pro mentalist. Wrote Making Contact: The Real Secrets of Contact Mindreading (1998, 68pp, with intro by Max Maven).

name: Saunders, Hyman
bio: (England: fl.1770s-80s) Pro sleight-of-hand artist in Europe (until 1770) and Colonial America (1770-72 with side-trips to the Caribbean (1775 & 1779). [LR7/2004; Ch; Dif]

name: Sautter, Christa
bio: (Germany: 8 Nov 1953-) Magicienne. Member of MZvD. Dealer ("Magische Schatztruhe GmbH") in Mindelheim, Germany, in early 1990s. Wife? of Gorm Sautter. [Nad]

name: Sautter, Gorm
bio: (Germany: 14 Nov 1948-) Magician in Mindelheim. Husband? of Christa Sautter. [Nad]

name: Sauty, [Charles-]Émile
bio: (Switzerland: c1901-12 Jul 1967) Ex-journalist. Pro illusionist as "Professeur Rex", working with wife "Rexia", son "Bengalis" (Marc Sauty), & daughter "Josy Rex" as assistants. Founded magic studio (Académie Suisse de Magie) in Geneva in 1928. Founded the Cercle Suisse Robert-Houdin in 1941. Edited La Baguette Magique in 1941. Wrote several magic books, including Tours de Cartes (1943, 118pp) & Hypnotiseurs et Mystificateurs (1944), & translated others. Article in Escamoteur #35. His magic studio was bought after his death by Jean Garance. [Dif]

name: Savage, Howard [R.]
bio: (New York City, NY: 9 Jul 1908-30 Oct 1935) Illustrator for the New York American newspaper. Amateur magician. Cartoonist (with brother James) & illustrator, 1934-35, for The Sphinx. 1934 Sphinx Award for "The Mentalist's Handy Code".

name: Savage, Ken, MIMC
bio: (England: c1929-29 Oct 1988) Electrician in Plymouth. Semi-pro kid-show (as "Uncle Ken") & club magician. MIMC 1987.

name: Savant
bio: See: Nixon, Doc

name: Savil
bio: See: Castro, Fernando

name: Saville, Dr Thomas K[eith] "Tom", PhD
bio: (Delphos, Iowa: 16 Oct 1935-). Learned at age 9 from magic shop tricks. At age 20 learned card tricks to entertain kids. Doctorate in social psychology (1968) & Associate Professor of Psychology at Metropolitan State College at Denver (since 1971) where (since 1982) he teaches a course in parapsychology. Semi-promentalist since age 42. Aka "Dr. Savi". President of the PEA 1984-87. Edited Vibrations 1984-86. Wrote Of Psychology and the Tarot (1981) & Red Hot Cold Reading (1984, 78pp, with Herb Dewey). [Wh2]

name: Savler
bio: See: Relvas, Eduardo

name: Savren, Professor James
bio: (England: c1824-15 Feb 1891) Barber by trade. Semi-pro magic assistant, including with Ludwig Döbler, Compars Herrmann, J.H. Anderson, & Robert-Houdin. A pioneer collector of magicana with the then largest collection of magicians posters & playbills in England, which went to H.E. Evanion. Bio in James Hagy, Early English Conjuring Collectors: James Savren and Henry Evanion (1985, 141pp). [Pr;Cl]

name: Sawa, Dr Hiroshi
bio: (Japan: 26 Dec 1941- ) Dentist in Seki. Amateur close-up magician of whom Dai Vernon says "originality tingles from his fingertips". 1973 Tenkai Prize. 1983 Desert Magic Seminar 6th/7th place (tied with Tim Conover). Wrote Sawa Hiroshi Sakuhin-shu [Hiroshi Sawa's Creative Works in Magic] (1974). Tricks in Genii, etc. See Richard Kaufman, Sawa's Library of Magic, Vol.I (1988). Video segments (1986 & 1993). TV bit in Britain. [Mag;Wat]

name: Sawyer, Thomas A[lan] "Tom
bio: (Santa Monica, California: 7 Jan 1949- ) Lawyer in Santa Ana, California. Magic historian & bibliographer. Specialized in Professor Hoffmann, by 1990 his collection totalled some 250 Hoffmann titles. Edited-published The Hoffmann Collector 1974-86 (17 issues), sometimes using "Arthur Dodge" as pen name. Wrote My Dear Friend Baldwin (1972, 9pp), Professor Hoffmann: A Study (1977, 67pp, with J.B. Findlay), Professor Hoffmann: A Bibliography (1983, 102pp), Stanley Collins: Society Entertainer & Magic Collector (1984), The Hoffmann Collector: The First Ten Years (1986, 146pp), Foxing Around (1987, 50pp), Victorian-Age Conjuring Books: A Guide for Collectors and Bibliographers (1988, 70pp; 2nd rev ed 1991), The Unmasking of Arthur Dodge: Selected Articles from The Hoffmann Collector (1989, 49pp), S.S. Baldwin and the Press (1993, 110pp), Some Notes on the Baldwins (1997, 20pp), & several shorter books, many printed & bound by himself in small editions. Articles in Magicol, Magical Bookie, & Magic Cauldron. Edits Aphelion 1992-present. Much of this output, while interesting, is too clever by far. [Wh]

name: Saxburger, Heinz
bio: (Burkal, near Tönder, Denmark: 14 Oct 1930-) Stage name of Hans Jacob Saxburger-Hinrichsen. Pro illusionist. Toured all 5 continents in 1970s-80s. Played the East Berlin Friedrichstadtpalast in 1972. By 1983 had done 54 TV bits, including in USA & Britain. [Win;Dif]

name: Saxbys, Four Mystic
bio: See: "Kahn, Miss"

name: Saxon, Lucille P[ierce]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: fl.1940s) Learned assisting Blackstone. Thence pro on own with sleight-of-hand, marionettes, & puppets. [Th]

name: Sayani, Hamid
bio: (India: fl.1940s-70s) Pro magician in Bombay. Trick in Swami.

name: Scadelli, Otto
bio: (Krummau am Kamp, Austria: 28 Apr 1887-8 Nov 1952) Stage name of Otto Letizki. Pro magician & ventriloquist in Vienna. Co-authored (with Fritz Mertens) Zaubern: Magische Spezialitäten aus Wien (1955, 146pp). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Scatelli" by Stenman. [Vo57;Al;St]

name: Scalbert, Geoffrey
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-80s) Amateur cardman. Invented "Mystery of the 7th Card" telephone trick (1945). Wrote Scalbert's Selected Secrets (1981). Tricks in Abra. Brother of Leslie Scalbert.

name: Scalbert, [F.] Leslie
bio: (Britain: -1957) Brother of Geoffrey Scalbert.

name: Scalzo, Frank
bio: (Sicily, Italy: 1919-dead by 2004) Moved with family to USA at age 4. Taught by Slydini, Vernon, & Cardini. Owner of a dry-cleaning chain in Pennsylvania. Amateur stage illusionist as “Baron Scalzo” & “The Amazing Scalzo & Co” until 1968 when went full-time. Pet effect: dove act. 1969 Gwynne Trophy. Sadie Scalzo, his wife-assistant for 59 years died in 2003. [Tops7/69;Genii3/64;MUM6/63;Des;Wh2]

name: Scarlett, [Robert] Peter, MIMC
bio: (Brighton, England: 30 Jan 1940-) Inspired in early 1950s by a Norman Hunter article in a boys' magazine. Salesman. Semi-pro magician. Does stage magic with assistant-wife Ilona. President, British Ring 1985-86. Lecturer. Scarne, John "Johnny" [pronounced SKAR-knee] (Steubenville, Ohio: 4 Mar 1903-7 Jul 1985) Stage name of Orlando Carmelo Scarnecchia, of Italian immigrant parents. Learned 1916-18 by detecting card sharps sleights, reading a magic book, & tuition from Charles Dagmar ("The Great Dagmar"). Invented a version of Card in Wallet (1918) & probably the Marlo Wedge (1918?). Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Played the Versailles Club in 1941. About that time became noted expert on gambling systems, particularly cheating methods, & drifted away from magic. Later invented the popular parlor board games Teeko and Scar-Nee (1955). In 1956 he dropped pro magic & founded John Scarne Games, Inc., to market his own games. See Audley V. Walsh, John Scarne Explains Why You Can't Win [1933, 33pp; repr 1972, 44pp]. Wrote Scarne on Dice (1945, with Clayton Rawson), Scarne on Cards (1949, 402pp; rev 1965, 435pp), Scarne on Card Tricks (1950, 308pp, ghosted by Ben Braude; repr 1974), Scarne's Magic Tricks (1951, 256pp; repr 1977), Scarne's Complete Guide to Gambling (1961, 714pp, ghosted by Clayton Rawson), etc. Column in the Police Gazette. Tricks in Gen, HMM, Pallbearers, and Epilogue. Autobios are The Amazing World of John Scarne: A Personal History (1956, 412pp) & The Odds Against Me (1966, 537pp). [Bo2;Wh91]

name: Scatelli, Otto" [misspelling]
bio: See: Scadelli, Otto

name: Schäfer, Reinhold
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 5 Feb 1892-12 Nov 1966) Son of a Berlin tailor. Assistant to "Taft" 1913-23. Stage names: "Reini Schäfer" c1919-1923, then "Taft" 1923-30, then "Recha" since 1930. Pro circus illusionist. Played the Paris Cirque d'Hiver in 1929. After WW II worked mainly in circuses, including in Belgium & Austria. Died in Berlin. [Win;St]

name: Schaffer, Steno
bio: (Trieste, Austria [now Italy]: 1903-13 Jan 1987) Pro stage magician. Honorary President C.M.I. since 1955. [Magia Moderna1981]

name: Schaffer, Sylvester
bio: (USA: c1884-20 Jun 1949) Pro vaudeville magician, juggler, acrobat, etc. Played the Boston Keith's in 1914 & the NY Palace in 1914. [Var,Mo;Lau]

name: Schaper, Herman
bio: (Germany?: 3 May 1933-) Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Schaumberg, Walter
bio: (Germany: 5 Jul 1907-20 Jul 1974) Magician. Active member of MZvD. [Nad]

name: Scheldon, Paul
bio: (Rostock, Germany: 7 Jan 1880-27 Feb 1942). Stage name of Paul Stallbom. Learned in youth. Pro since 1900. Popular stage illusionist. Specialized in sucker effects. Before WW I toured much of Europe including Russia. Died in Berlin. His widow Ellen continued his act for a short time. NOTE: Last name sometimes given as "Stahlbohm". Schenk, Bruno [Win;Vo57;Go2;St;WWM;Dam2] (Breslau, Germany [now Wrocław, Poland]: 9 Sep [or 29 Apr] 1857-29 Nov 1932) Son of a merchant. Pro debut in 1876. Manipulator & illusionist. Toured Germany, Austria, Italy, & Hungary. Since 1882 toured his own "Eden-Theater", which with 1,900 seats was the largest travelling theater in Germany. Played Finland in 1891 & Denmark in 1902. Buried in Oberhausen/Dresden. [Vo56;Sal;Win;St]

name: Scherer, Christian [Rudolf]
bio: (Wohlen, Aargau, Switzerland: 23 Mar 1948-) Learned in 1962 from magic set. Psychologist. Semi-pro magician since 1968 with cards, close-up, & platform magic. 1980 Bonn 1st prize for card magic, 1990, 1993, 1996 Swiss champion in card magic. Has invented several close-up tricks marketed by Pedro Magie since c1984. Wrote Eine Handvoll Kartenkünstücke (1978) with French tr by Vollmer as Goldfingers Card Magic (1981); & Card News (1982) with French tr by Vollmer as Nouvelles techniques modernes aux cartes (1983) & English tr as Card Magic (1984, 133pp); Das gespiegelte Kartenspiel (1992); Karten à la Carte (1997); Abgezockt! Eine Falschspiel-Demonstration (1999); Sensitive Finger. Eine Kartenroutine mit verbundenen Augen (1999); Der glücklose Falschspieler. Eine Dice-Stacking-Routine (2000). Lecture notes: Seminarheft Christian Scherer (1982); Kreative Magie (2002); lecture notes for Sveroni: Sveroni original (1991); Typisch Sveroni (1995); Variationen (2006), Heureka (2008). Translated The Expert at the Card Table into German (1991). Articles in Magische Welt & Apocalypse. 2 DVDs Christian Scherers Kartenmagie Teil I + II (2006). [Wh2]

name: Scheuer, Wolfgang
bio: (Potsdam, Germany: 7 Jun 1934- ) Learned as child. Pro manip, illusionist, & kid-show magician in East Germany since 1954. Played the East Berlin Friedrichstadtpalast in 1971. Bio & tricks in Mauerspechte (1992). [Win]

name: Schichtl, Michael August
bio: (Munich, Bavaria, Germany: -Feb 1911) Pro who worked fairs in Bavaria including Munich. [St]

name: Schindler, George, MIMC
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 31 Mar 1929- ) Inspired at age 11 seeing magician at school. Learned at age 12 from gift Gilbert magic set. Assisted at Holden's NY shop 1949-50. Semi-pro debut at age 18 & full-time pro since 1970. Co-founder (with Frank Garcia) & Director of the School for Magicians (in New York City) 1973-78. In 1975 did TV commercial as the "Great Nabisco". Played "Shandu the Magician" in Woody Allen's "Oedipus Wrecks" episode in the film, New York Stories (1989). Teacher of Shelley Carol. 1988 Back Stage's Bistro Award for variety performer (shared with Jeff McBride). AIMC 1989; MIMC 1990. Gold Star 1991. Producer of 6 magic shows. SAM President 1992-93. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. Named Dean of American Magicians by SAM 2005 succeeding Jay Marshall. Invented Sealed Surprise (1951); Coin in the Ring (1972). Snap Thru Coin in Bottle (1978). Wrote Beginner's Curriculum (1973), Amedeo's Continental Magic (1974, with Frank Garcia), Magic with Cards (1975, with Frank Garcia), Magic with Everyday Objects (1976), Presto!: Magic for Beginners (1977, 192pp), Ventriloquism (1979), & Basic Balloon Sculpture (1983). Articles in MUM & Magic Manuscript. DVD: Entertainment First (2008). Column in Genii (1950s). Trick in HMM. 3 audios. Many TV & radio bits, including 6 TV commercials. [Se;Wh2]

name: Schlosser, R[udolph] S. "Rudy
bio: (Germany: fl.1910s-20s) Moved to USA as a youth. Opened his "Star Magic" shop in New York City in 1911. Later operated as "R.S. Schlosser Magic Co." A mechanical genius, he was Houdini's favorite designer & builder of apparatus. After 1925 moved his shop to Ohio, successively in Wadsworth, Akron, & finally Youngstown. Sold his shop c1929 to Frank McCue & Carl Waldman. A life-long eccentric, he died in an insane asylum in Cleveland. REF: Albo (1995), 35; Caveney (1987), 103-105.

name: Schmalriede, Guido
bio: (Germany?: 11 Mar 19-) Closeup magician. Deutsche Jugendmeisterschaft 1984 1st prizes in both closeup & card magic and 1985 1st prize in closeup & Ken Brooke prize; 1987 MZvD 1st prize in closeup. [Nad]

name: Schmidt, Madame
bio: See: Schmitt, Anita

name: Schmidt, Alfred
bio: (Germany: 12 Aug 1924-) Magician & collector of magic books in Duisburg, Germany. [Nad]

name: Schmidt, Joseph K[enneth] "Joe
bio: (Pinconning, Michigan: 17 Feb 1920-) Learned at age 14 from a cheap card book. Retired from the US Air Force to live in West Germany. Amateur card magician, having invented several moves, including the first Tilt Pass & Bottom Placement in 1981. Major illustrator of magic books & magazines, including some 80 works by Fulves and The Man Who Was Erdnase (1991). Wrote 5 booklets: The Impromptu Close-Up Card Rise (1968), Modern Close-Up Card Problems (1981, 88pp), R.C. Buff's Knot on the Square, The Best of Buff, Conrad Bush's Color Isolation, plus 6 on run-up systems. Articles in Hugard's Magic Monthly, Genii, Pallbears Review, Epilogue, New Tops, Talisman, Epotica, & Magick. [LR1/96;Wh2]

name: Schmidt, Regina
bio: (Germany: 1907-11 Jun 1978) Married George Schmidt (died 1988). Director-owner of Berlin magic shop ("Zauberkönig-Berlin", founded 1884) that she'd taken over from the Krohners around WW II. On her death (in Berlin) the shop went to Günter Klepke. [Roh]

name: Schmitt, Anita
bio: (Lithuania or Estonia: fl.1960s) Dancer. Assistant in Helmut "Kalanag" Schreiber's show. Then, since 1961, his live-in mistress & main female assistant as "Angela Ferrari" & "Madame Schmidt".

name: Schneider, Al[vin]
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Close-up artist. Dealer (Goldshadow Industries) in Minneapolis. Edited house organ, Goldshadow Newsletter 1981-1982-present? Wrote Matrix (1976) & Off (27pp). Trick in Genii. Video.

name: Schneider, Lev
bio: (Russia: fl.1980s-90s) Immigrated to USA as an adult. His ability as a muscle-reader is, according to Randi, "just short of supernatural."

name: Schoke, U. O. "Chic
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Amateur card magus in Chicago. Invented "Chic Trick" (1945). TV bit on Tonight Show 1957. [HMM5/46, p222]

name: Scholtyssek, Manfred
bio: (Germany: 12 Oct 1927-) Scientific assistant in teachers training college in East Germany. Semi-pro magician & mentalist & magic teacher. Wrote Hokus Pokus Wirbelwind (1978, 48pp). Current editor of Zauberkunst. Tricks in Zauberkunst & Hokus-Pokus (Poland). [Mec;Nad]

name: Schramade, Dora
bio: (Rotterdam?, Holland: 1885-1930) Daughter of Theodoor Schramade. Pro magicienne with father as "De Schramade's".

name: Schramade, Theodoor
bio: (Belgium: 1850-1919) Moved to Rotterdam, Holland, in 1865. Pro magician. Father of Dora Schramade.

name: Schreiber, Helmut [Ewald]
bio: (Fornsbach, near Stuttgart, Germany: 23 Jan 1903 [sic]-24 Dec 1963) Amateur magician since age 11 when read Suhr's Das Goldene Buch der Magie. Lied that he was born in 1893, probably to qualify for entry into the German magic club MZ on 1 Apr 1919 as member #82. Founded the Munich branch of the MZ in 1921. Debut in Munich in 1923. Edited Magie 1927-45. From 1921 to 1945 was involved in German movie-making, rising from a volunteer worker to producer with Berman Bavaria Film. Claimed to have produced more than 180 films. On 19 Aug 1933 he performed the world's 2nd (after Astroi in France in 1906) magic act in a dirigible (the Graf Zeppelin at 1,700 meters high on the monthly Germany-to-South America route). On 4 May 1934 appeared with Adami & 2 other magi in a Berlin radio magic special, Germany's 1st. President of MZvD 1936-45. Awarded the Hofzinser Ring 1936-1948, its 2nd recipient. Performed for Hermann Göring at his Karinhall estate on 25 Dec 1938. Since 1947 as "Kalanag" (from Kipling's Jungle Book elephant "Kala Nag" [Black Snake]), world-famous pro illusionist with star German [sic] assistant-wife "Gloria" (married 1942) until 1961 when she was replaced by his mistress Anita Schmitt (billed as "Angela Ferrari" & "Madame Schmidt"). From 1949 until 1961, Kalanag toured the largest illusion show in post-war Europe. Also toured Spain (1949), England (1951), Africa, France (1955), Brazil (1956), Canada (1957), and USA (1957 & 1960). The show was starkly reduced in size in 1961. Died of a stroke in Gaildorf near Stuttgart. His widow sold his props in 1967 to Klingsor. Wrote Simsalabim wirbelt um die Welt (1949, 96pp). Memoir is Der Magier erzählt sein Leben (1962) with English translation as series in Genii (1963-64). Bios are Robert Kaldy-Karo & Michael Swatosch-Doré, Kalanag: Zauber des Zauberns (1988, 36pp); Klingsor, Recollections of Kalanag (1993); & Michael Swatosch-Doré, "Helmut Schreiber--Kalanag", Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993), 66-72. NOTE: On his true birth date see Magie (Sep/Oct 1985), 269, 271. [Win; Ch; Pr; Dif; Le; Go2; Fu; Rob1; HMM12/54,11/59,11/67]

name: Schröder, Eugen
bio: (Berlin?, Germany: 16 Jun 1864-13 Jun 1933) Pro. Co-founder (with Paul von Kalnassy & Karl Meyer) of the "Amateur Vereinigung für magische Kunst" [Amateur Association for Magical Arts] in Berlin in 1901. Co-founder (with Conradi-Horster, etc) of "Maja", a magicians club in Berlin in 1905. Died in Berlin. [St;Dam2;Roh]

name: Schröder, Karl
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 8 Dec 1876-25 Jul 1960) Merchant in Hamburg. Amateur magician. Founder of the Magischer Zirkel (Hamburg), the later MZvD, in 1912 & its President 1912-23, 1928 [sic]-36, 1946-49. First editor of Magie 1918-23. Articles in Die magische Post 1947-49 reprinted as Magische Reminiszenzen (1952, 45pp). See also H.W. Tagrey (with Karl Schröder) Indische Gaukler und ihre Tricks (1926, 17pp). Died in

name: Schröder, Margarete
bio: (Germany: 2 Aug 1883-1 Oct 1923) Worked as "Fara". Died in Berlin? [Roh]

name: Schröder, Peter
bio: (Bremen, Germany: 26 Nov 1928- ) Magician (as "Petrix") in Espelkamp, Germany. Collector of magic literature & puzzles and magic historian. Co-authored with Wolfgang Rohde the computerized Almanach (1991 with 1994 supplement). [Nad]

name: Schröpfer, Johann Georg
bio: (Nürnberg, Germany: 1739-7 Oct 1774) Ran a Ghost Show using a Magic Lantern. In debt, he shot & killed himself. He is the protagonist of Friedrich von Schiller's incomplete novel, Der Geisterseher (1789). [Dam2;Al]

name: Schubert, Fred
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Lived in New York City. Founding President of The National Conjuror's Association in 1911. Founding President of The Knights of Magic in 1920.

name: Schuler, Dr Carl von
bio: (Germany: 5 Sep 1876-15 Jan 1934) Physician near Leipzig. Known for his research on occult phenomena & their relation to conjuring tricks. Schulien, [Charles Robert] "Charlie" [pronounced shoe-LINE] (Chicago, Illinois: 1930-1998) Son of Matt Schulien from whom he learned magic at age 10. Auctioneer. Proprietor since 1975 of Schulien's Restaurant & Saloon where he performed close-up magic as amateur since 1950. Father of Bobby Schulien. [Wh2]

name: Schulien [Sr], Matt
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 19 Nov 1890-1 Mar 1967) Son of a German immigrant saloon keeper in Chicago. Inspired & learned at age 12 from a magician at his father's bar. Proprietor since 1930 of Schulien's Restaurant and Saloon. 1949 Sphinx Award. Father of Charlie Schulien. See Philip Willmarth, The Magic of Matt Schulien (1959, 168pp) & Eugene Burger, Eugene Burger on Matt Schulien's Fabulous Card Discoveries (1983, 44pp). Trick in HMM. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Schulein" because that best matches his Americanized pronunciation as "shoe-LINE".

name: Schulien, Robert C [harles] "Bobby
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 16 Jul 1954-) Son of Charlie Schulien. Interested in magic at age 6 watching Matt & Charlie. Pro close-up (cards only) since 1979 at Schulien's Restaurant & Saloon (in Chicago) of which he was a co-owner until it closed 27 Jan 1999. [Wh2]

name: Schulte, [George] F.
bio: (Chicago: Illinois: 22 May 1887-) Wrote several patter books beginning with Talks for Tricks (1916, 48pp) & including Magical Monologues (c1919, 42pp) & Patter Paragraphs (1921, 36pp). [Dor]

name: Schultheiss, Jacob C.
bio: (Tübingen, Germany: 30 Aug 1871-) Charter member in 1912 of the German Magic Circle (MZ) of whom he was its first Treasurer. [Roh]

name: Schultz, [Edward Lloyd] "Edd
bio: (Braintree, Massachusetts: 13 Jul 1948-) Episcopal priest. Inspired seeing Mark Wilson TV show at age 13. Semi-pro stage magician & illusionist as "Foo Ling Yoo" & "Zauber & Co." ..... (since 1984 with assistant-wife Rev. Debra Kissinger) the Magician". Founded mail-order magic "Zauber & Co." in 1988. Publisher-editor of The Illusionist quarterly since Feb 1993. [Genii6/93;Wh5]

name: Schulz, Thomas
bio: (Germany: 28 Mar 1970-) Amateur magician & collector. [Nad]

name: Schulz, Werner
bio: (Grevesmühlen, Germany: 9 Apr 1925-5 Aug 1961) Performed as "Schulz-Sculdano". [Roh]

name: Schuman, Ed[ward Anthony]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 9 Oct 1916- 23 May 2002) Learned at age 10. Product manager. Semi-pro close-up, platform, & kid-show magician. Tricks in Tarbell #7 & MUM. SAM President 1968-69. 1988 SAM Hall of Fame. [MUM7/67;Wh2] (Berlin, Germany: 31 Jul 1934-) Learned in 1946 from school library book. Amateur & collector of Schuster, Peter magic literature & history in Berlin. Translated Selow's book as Die Kunst Frauen zu zersägen (1964). Has used stage name of "Peter Fabian" since at least as early as 1968 [sic]. Editor of Zauberlin, organ of Magischer Zirkel Berlin. Articles in Magie & Zauberlin. [Wit;Bou;Wh2]

name: Schwanenfeld, Sebastian von
bio: (Bavaria?, Germany: 1757-4 Oct 1845) In 1795 came from Bavaria to Vienna where he became a famous magician in the Prater park, selling his pitch to his last assistant, Basilius Calafatti, in 1834. Died rich in Vienna. [Al]

name: Schwartz, Ann Myrece
bio: (Ludlow, Massachusetts: 1 Nov 1946-) Taught since age 7 by semi-pro father, Walter Schwartz. Nurse (RN) in Bridgeport, Connecticut. Semi-pro kid-show magicienne since age 12 (1968). Billed as "The Dancing Magicienne" 1960-80 & "The Lady of Magic" 1980-present. Article in Linking Ring. [Wh2]

name: Schwartz, Harold G.
bio: (USA: 28 Feb 1906-7 Jun 1947) Learned from pro father Louis O. Schwartz. Dentist. Semi-pro club magician as "Harada".

name: Schwartz, Louis C. "Lou
bio: (USA: -1955) Learned from pro father Louis O. Schwartz. Pro as "Lou Schwartz & Co" and with brother Walter as "The Schwartz Bros" & "Schwartz & Co".

name: Schwartz, Louis O.
bio: (Albany, New York: 28 Feb 1866- ) Pro stage magician, specialized in Black Art. Billed as "The Schwartz Bros" (1892) & "Schwartz, the Man of Mystery" (early 1900s). Father of Louis C., Harold, & Walter Schwartz, all pro or semi-pro magicians.

name: Schwartz, Natan
bio: (Germany: fl.1890s) Pro magician. Toured Russia & Germany (c1899) with a Russian circus. Pet effect: Egg Bag. In 1899 his assistant was the later famous Carl Rosini.

name: Schwartz, Sam, MIMC
bio: (Austria: 14 Apr 1911- ) Lawyer (retired). Brought to USA in 1913. Amateur since c1952 when taught by Dr Benjamin Pressman. Cardman. Invented Incredi-Box & inspired Himber to make the Himber Wallet. Wrote Play it Again Sam (1977, 34pp) & put together the force book Astrology, The Hidden Force (1984). Tricks in Pallbearers (+1 all-Schwartz issue), Tops, Linking Ring, M-U-M, Swami (India). [Spellbinder9/84;Wh]

name: Schwartz, Walter A[rnold] "Walt
bio: (Rensselaer, New York: 23 Sep 1906- ) Learned as child from pro father Louis O. Schwartz. Production control supervisor. Part-time pro stage & club magician since 1918. Pet effects: Chinese Sticks, Rice Bowls, Mutilated Parasol, C&R Pearls. An editor of The Sphinx. Wrote Cigam (1931, 62pp) & Gimac (1933, 38pp). Articles in Sphinx. Father of Ann Myrece Schwartz, a semi-pro magicienne in own right. [Wh2]

name: Schwarz, Ernst
bio: (Germany: 23 Feb 1944-) Pro magician with assistant as "Mr Black & Ursula". 1978 MZvD 2nd prize in general magic; 1981 MZvD 1st prize in general magic. [Nad]

name: Schwarzkopf Jr, H. Norman
bio: (USA: 22 Aug 1934- ) U.S. Army officer. Amateur magician since 1941 when inspired seeing Blackstone show. Further inspired by watching magicians perform in Middle East 1946-47. IBM Member since 1971. Performed for family, friends, Cub Scouts, & other groups when in Washington, D.C. Employed extensive & effective deception measures in the 1991 Gulf War. 1991 Honorary Life Membership to the Magic Castle. 1991 Honorary Member of the Houdini Historical Center. Autobio is It Doesn't Take a Hero (1992, 530pp).

name: Schwarzman, Howard "Howie
bio: (New York City, NY: 21 Nov 1927- ) Taught at age 5 by amateur uncle. Originally an amateur magician (USO shows in WW II, etc). A wholesale men's sportswear salesman until 1977 when he turned pro magician, specializing in card & coin close-up. Author-lecturer-dealer (Howard Schwarzman's 'Limited Edition's' Magic) in Baltimore. Hen Fetch Award, Elsworth Award, Frank Thompson Award. Invented Impeccable Double Lift. Articles in Precursor & Magic Manuscript. [Se;Wh2]

name: Sciaberno
bio: See: Sena, Antonio

name: Scolari, Ovidio
bio: (Italy: 1877-20 Jul 1934) Pro in Rome. Inventor & improver. Then dealer ("Casa d'Arte Magica") in Milan. Published-edited II Vademecum del Prestigiatore (1929-33). Wrote Magia Facile per Tutti (1930) & Nel Regno dei Misteri (1930). Trick in Magic (1908). [Go2;St]

name: Scot, Reginald
bio: (Smeeth, Kent, England: 1538-9 Oct 1599) Country gentleman farmer. Entered Oxford U in 1555. Learned magic c1580 by tuition from John Cautares. Amateur magician. Wrote the classic The discouerie of witchcraft (1584, 560pp; repr 1651, 1665, 1886, 1930, 1964, 1972, 1989). A Dutch translation, Ondecking van Tovery, was published in 1609. While generally showing the wonders of witches to be based on non-supernatural methods, two long chapters specifically describe & explain the sleights & other natural methods of conjurors. King James I, who believed in witchcraft, ordered that Scot's exposé be burned. Enough copies survived to lead to several reprints. [Tops9/38, 11/38, & 1/39;Bo#232;Mc;St;TS]

name: Scoto
bio: See: Scotto, Girolamo

name: Scott, Big
bio: (Scotland?: fl.1810s-30s) Stage name of Mr Longhurst. Minor pro showman & magician in Scotland. Billed himself as "Emperor of all the Conjurers". Wounded in the cheek doing the Bullet Catch in the 1820s. J.H. Anderson apprenticed as his assistant until c1831 & married his daughter Hannah in 1842. [CI]

name: Scott, John
bio: (Britain: fl.1780s-90s) Had a toy-&-magic shop in London at 417 Strand near the Adelphi in the late 1700s. He was the leading prop maker-dealer in Britain at that time, specializing in semi-scientific & mechanical tricks. The Grossman Collection had printed instruction sheets for some of Scott's tricks that were numbered, suggesting, as Eddie Dawes writes, that Scott had "at least a master list" if not a catalog. [CI; Daw94]

name: Scotto, Girolamo
bio: (Italy: fl.1570s-1st decade of 1600s). Descendant of the Irish Douglas clan. His name in Latin is Hieronymus Scotus. A knight from Placentia & diplomat. Amateur sleight-of-hand cardman who exhibited his skills at the various courts he was assigned to, including Tyrol ((1572), Pfalz, Brandenburg, Cologne (1579), Coburg (1580), Königsburg, & London (prior to 1594 & again in 1602). Bio is Edgar Heyl, "New Light On the Renaissance Master," Sphinx (1948), 38-40, 42, 50. [Daw#196;Ch;Dif;St;Cl]

name: Seabrooke, [Terence Kenneth] "Terry", MIMC
bio: (Watford, England: 26 Dec 1932 – 11 Jan 2011) Learned at age 12 from friends & Davenport props. Pro comedy magician (ex-banker & insurance saleman) since 1974. Best known for his Burnt Bill in Envelope routine. 7 Royal Command shows. Toured world-wide. 1981 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. 1996 Magic Circle Carlton Comedy Award. 1996 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote autobio + tricks Seabrooke's Book: Around the World With a Baking Tin (1987, 112pp). Wrote American Lecture (1975, 24pp), A Professional Idiot (1981, 19pp), Beyond Compere (1993, 160pp). Articles in MUM, Abra, Magic Circular, Budget, Genii, Linking Ring (+ 1979 1-man "Parade"), & Mantra. 2 audios (1978); video (1987). [Mag;La2;Wh2]

name: Seagraves, William [John] “Bill” MIMC
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 10 Nov 1941-) Introduced to magic by his father Bill Seagraves who was an amateur magician working backstage in Variety Theatre assisting magicians. Marine Engineer by trade working in Aberdeen, Scotland. First performance was at age 12 with local entertaining group in N.E. of Scotland. 1980 turned professional at 21. Ken Dodd Comedy Award 1999. The British Magical Champion of Comedy 1999. For services to Scottish Magic The James Craig Trophy 1999. Scottish Association Murray Wand for Showmanship 1989, 1990, 1999. President of Scottish Association of Magical Societies 1996-1997. President of Aberdeen Magical Society from 1994, until 2000. Made Honorary Life President of Aberdeen Magical Society 2000. MIMC with Gold Star 2003. Emigrated to New Zealand 2000.

name: Sealtiel, Walter
bio: (Germany: 1890-) Joined MZvD in 1920. Prop pickpocket act, which he introduced to New York City in 1929. [Wal] Searles, Lynn [changed to Lin in late 1950s] (Fairport, New York: 13 Sep 1914-24 Dec 1972) Learned magic in 1929. Pro writer of Western novels. Semi-pro magician. Invented the Stung card effect by 1931, Aces Up in 1950, Cannibal Cards in late 1950s, & Auto Break. Scriptwriter in early 1960s for Mark Wilson's "Magic Land of AllaKazam" TV series. Killed during holdup of his magic shop in Pasadena. Wrote The Card Expert (1938, 48pp; repr 1962, 54pp), Lucky Aces (1950, 12pp), The Ultimate Aces (1958), & Slow Motion Poker Deals (1959, 8pp). Tricks in New Jinx, Ibidem, & Pallbearers. [WWM]

name: Sears, Harry
bio: (USA: fl.1st decade of 1900s-1910s) A fine vaude illusionist. European tour in 1908 including the London Hippodrome with Maskelyne's Side Issue, etc. Produced the "Blue Pearl" magical extravaganza in London in 1911. Retired around 1912 to become a prosperous gold-mine owner in California. Still alive in 1929. [Bam, pp.45,309; Magic10/08]

name: Sebastian
bio: (Germany: 29 Nov 1955-) Stage name of Christoph Mack. Manipulator. 1978 MZvD 3rd prize in manip; 1981 MZvD 1st prize in manip; 1983 Baden-Baden 1st prize in manip. [Nad]

name: Secondi
bio: (Italy: fl.1870s) Pro.

name: See, Neil [Stanford]
bio: (USA: c1928-18 Feb 1989) Learned magic at age 10. Computer expert. Amateur close-up magician, having studied with Vernon, Miller, & Carlyle. Major collector of magic books since the 1960s, including purchases from the Ellenbogen & George McIntyre collections. His important collection of books, periodicals, manuscripts, posters, & small props was dispersed at public auction (by Swann Galleries) on 10 May 1990. Expecting around $150,000, the 449 lots sold for $334,000, setting records for many titles.

name: Seebach, David [Allen]
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 20 Mar 1951-) Learned at age 6 or 7 from brother's Mysto Magic set. Used stage name "Divad" 1966-80, his act now being billed as "Wonders of Magic". Pro illusionist since 1969. Pet effects: Modern Cabinet production, Guillotine, & Bow Sawing. 1980 Gwynne Trophy. Wrote "Subject: Illusions" column in & New Tops (early 1970s & again since 1986). [Wh2] "Seekay" [brand name of trick cards] SEE: Keech, Cecil

name: Seeman, Prof. Adolph
bio: (Germany?: fl.1880s-1920s) Learned assisting father Hartwig Seeman. Briefly a pro magician in USA by 1890 until switched to carnival management by 1920 when he was with the Rubin-Cherry shows. Then vanished. [Pr] Seeman, Professor Baron [Ernst] Hartwig [Johan] (Stralsund, Pommerania, Germany: 3 Jun 1833-25 Mar 1886) Pro illusionist since 1860. Toured Germany, Austria, Constantinople, Egypt, Russia, Sweden (1860), Norway (1860), England (1869-71), Cape Colony (1872), India (c1872), & USA (1880-86), where he died in Texas. Possibly invented Aga (1880). A Mason. Father of Adolph Seeman. NOTE: Despite being German, gave the false impression in USA of being Sweden's foremost magician & a member of Swedish nobility. This tale was accepted by both Clarke and Price. [No56:St:Pr]

name: Sefton, Brian
bio: (England: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Brian Shadbolt. Pro manip. Won 1979 British Ring Shield. Married to "Josephine". [Mar]

name: Sehm, Norm[an]
bio: (USA: -1987) Pro escapist 1930s-50s. Dealer (Sehm Magic Studio) in Rochester, New York, since 1924. Bought the late Elmer Eckam's "Art in Magic" shop in 1965, specializing in magic of the 1930s-40s. (Europe: fl.1870s-80s) Pro magician. Moved to USA. Retired by 1885 to own & manage a bar in the New York Bowery. Catch phrase: "Watch the Professor." Hired Max Malini as a handyman & soon taught him his first magic tricks. [Jay]

name: Seidel, Willy [misspelling]
bio: See: Seidl, Willi

name: Seidenstein, Morris "Moe
bio: (Avalon, Pennsylvania: 31 Mar 1909 – 24 Apr 2003) Aka "Moe from Pittsburgh". Moved to New York City in 1929. Inventive amateur cardman 1927-1936. 1930 & 1931 IBM 3rd prizes for card tricks. 1932 IBM 4th prize for pocket trick. 1934 IBM 2nd prize for card tricks. Bio is William P. Miesel, Moe And His Miracles With Cards (1986, 58pp). Reports of his death in the 1970s were disproved in 2001 when he resurfaced. He retired from work as an office manager in 1970. [LR10/2001]

name: Seidl, [Wilhelm] "Willi" [pronounced SIDEL]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 11 Apr 1914-) Metalworker whose factory in Vienna produced quality props for Klingl's magic shop. Amateur manipulator & illusionist. 1958 FISM 2nd prize for illusion; 1979 FISM jury. President of Austria's 2nd largest magic club (Vereinigung für magische Kunst) 1958-present. NOTE: Name misspelled "Willy Seidel". REF: Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993), 54. [Mec]

name: Seika, Miss
bio: See: "Selika"

name: Seitz, Werner G[ünther]
bio: (Stuttgart, Germany: 12 Feb 1940-) Learned from 2 pro uncles. Mechanical-electronic engineer. Semi-pro close-up & restaurant magician since 1958. Aka "Johnny Laker". Moved to Copenhagen, Denmark. Wrote Pride: The Copenhagen Coin Routine (1970). Articles in Magie. [Wh2]

name: Selbini, Lalla
bio: (Britain?: fl.1910s) Stage name of Mrs. Lallah Mary Pantzer. Born of show-biz parents. Principal female assistant to Lafayette until his death, then pro illusionist on own 1911-12. [Pr]

name: Selbit, P. T., MIMC
bio: (Hampstead, London [sic]: 17 Nov 1881 [sic]-19 [sic] Nov 1938) Stage name of Percy Thomas Tibbles since 1898. Learned c1895, including lessons from Hilliar. Pro illusionist since 1900. Aka "Joad-Heteb" & "Joad Heteb" with pseudo-Egyptian act 1902-08. MIMC 1907. In London played the Empire (1903), St. George's Hall (1906-07, 1908, 1914, 1920, & 1923-25), the Hippodrome (1909 & 1922), etc. Toured France, Germany, & Russia (all in 1908), the USA (1910-11 & 1924), and played the Paris Alhambra (1910, 1916, 1924) & the Paris Empire (1929). Often collaborated with his older brother, Sidney C. Tibbles, a leading illustrator, particularly of magic books & magazines. Died at home in suburban Reading as result of "Chronic Alcoholism". Prolific inventor of illusions, including the Magic Bricks (1906), Wrestling Cheese (1912), Walking through a Wall (1914), Sawing through a Woman (1920), Spike Cabinet (1923), Girl without a Middle (1924), Through the Eye of a Needle (1924), Broadcasting A Woman (early 1930s), & possibly Siberian Chain Escape. Wrote The Magician's Handbook (1901, 188pp; repr 1902), Marvels of Magic (1906, 24pp), The Magical Entertainer (1906, 56pp), The Magic Art of Entertainment (1907, 105pp), Conjuring Patter (n.d. [1908], 2 vols of 14pp each), & A Night with the Moon: A Practical Lightning 'Chalk-Talk' for Amateurs (c1909; repr 1911 & 1913). Edited Munro's The Wizard 1905-1908, 1909-1910. Tricks & articles in The Showman (1901), Tricks, The Wizard, & Magician Monthly. Bio is Eric C. Lewis & Peter Warlock, P.T. Selbit: Magical Innovator (1989, 201pp), a nearly definitive study. [Ch;Fi;Pr;Dif;Vo56;Magic10/00,5/06]

name: Selow, Michael
bio: (France: 1908-31 Aug [sic] 1983) Pen name of Michel Seldow, born Michael Seldowicz of Russian-Jewish extraction. Journalist in Paris. Amateur magician. AFAP Bronze Medal 1960. Wrote Les Illusionnistes et leurs secrets (1959), with German tr by Peter Schuster as Die Kunst Frauen zu zersägen (1964); & Vie et secrets de Robert-Houdin (1971, 185pp).

name: Selika
bio: (Spain: -28 Dec 1956) Stage name of Carmen Rodriguez, assistant-wife of Florence with whom she toured the world as "Selika" & "Miss Seika".

name: Selleno
bio: (Inowrocław, Poland: 1939-) Stage name of Czeław Paszul. Pro illusionist. [Mec]

name: Sellers, Tom
bio: (Britain: 1890-3 Nov 1961) Amateur. 1936 Sphinx Award. Invented Silk Cabby (1933), Just Chance = Bank Night (1935), New Principle Card Trick (1936) with its slit card (1936), & reportedly Monkey Bar (by 1955). Wrote 15 booklets, including Tricks that Work (1927), Card Tricks that Work (1934; repr 1948, 24pp), 21 New Card Tricks (1936, 20pp), Immediate Magic (1937, 19pp), Scots Magic (1939, 24pp), 20 Tricks (1943, 20pp), & Top Twenty (1958, 25pp). Tricks in Jinx, Magic Wand, Gen, & Psycho.

name: Selvaggio
bio: (Italy: 1904-) Stage name of Francisco Mancini. Pro. Toured Portugal in 1926 & 1940. Moved to Portugal in 1950. [Cam]

name: Selwyn, Tom
bio: (Lowell, Massachusetts: 22 May 1878-26 Jan 1950) Of British parents. Brought to England. Debut at age nine. Pro since age 16 at Huber's Dime Museum, NYC. Toured England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, S. Africa, India (1903), Australia (1908), France, & then back to Australia where he left the stage in 1928 for commerce from which he retired in 1940. [Wal;St;Pr]

name: Sena, Antonio
bio: (Naples, Italy: 18 Dec 1887-1977) Pro illusionist since c1901, working as "Chabernot". During the Facist regime was self-exiled, touring many countries under the stage name of "Sciaberno". [Magia Moderno3/79;Cam]

name: Senko, Mister
bio: (Varna [sic], Bulgaria: 12 Feb 1905-Sep 1987) Stage name of Efstati Hristof Karajontchev. Began in 1923 in Sofia as assistant to French circus magician Deloné. Pro illusionist with 2-hour show & 2 assistants. AFAF Master Magician. Named Peoples Artist of Bulgaria in 1985, the first Bulgarian magician so honored. Died in Sofia. [Win;Bou]

name: Septembre, René
bio: (France: -Oct 1984) Stage name of René Kohler. Pro livestock stage-magic act, often with partner Jeannette Karll as "The Septumbres". On USA TV in 1957. [Dif;Ch]

name: Serge
bio: See: Féaudiérre, Maurice

name: Serip
bio: (Quinta da Granja, Portugal: 13 Feb 1952-) Stage name of Dr João de Deus Madeira PIRES. Holds university degree in psychology. Learned magic at age 14. Pro comedy magic. Moved to Germany. 1980 Karlovy Vary 1st prize in comedy magic. Sometimes performs with assistant "Romy". [Cam; Top Hat Magic9/86] Seth the Sensational (Manchester, New Hampshire: c1972-) Stage name of Seth Llwellyn Bartlett since 1977. Semi-pro magician & juggler since 1976 at age 4 when his god-father, Cesareo Pelaez, made him an assistant with Le Grand David show. Taught by David M. Bull & Pelaez. 1985 SAM Magician of the Year Award (shared with Bull & Pelaez). [Wh2]

name: Seth, [Jacob] Don[ald]
bio: (Grand Rapids, Michigan: -1966) Pro vaude & WW II USO magician. Moved to Arizona in early 1950s. Then manager of magic department of Bert Easley's Fun Shop in Phoenix, Arizona. In 1958 founded Rabbits In Our Hat Magic Club for young magi, which gave shows at the PCAM conventions in 1961 in Phoenix & 1963 in Oakland. Mentor of Lee Earle, Paul Estes, Jack Sutherland, etc.

name: Setteducati, Mark
bio: (Manhattan, New York: 1 Nov 1955- ) Learned at age 12. Skilled card worker in New York City. Inventor of toys: Catch Word (1982), Rubik's Game (1982), Bingo Bandit, Dracula Bank, etc. Developed the Blackstone Travelling Magic set. Inventor of magic tricks: Garfield Magic Deck (1987), etc. In 1994 marketed his The Magic Showcase, a magic set that Wittus Witt judged the most innovative one of the previous decade. Tricks in MUM. [MUM2/94]

name: Setterington, Arthur, MIMC
bio: (Hull, England: 22 Mar 1924-2006) Inspired at age 4 seeing a magician. Learned at age 7 from mother's gift of an Ernest Sewell magic set. Methodist lay preacher. Aka "Arturo" & "Wyke". Semi-pro magician & magic collector. Inventor, including Cube in a Tube. Zina Bennett Trophy 1960 & 1968. MIMC 1986. Wrote Stranger Mysteries (1967, 20 pp), The Joe Smith Mysteries (1968, 20pp), Micro-Magic Ghost Show (1970, 40pp), The Power of Persuasion (1972, 28pp), Straight Line Mysteries (1972, 49pp), Off Beat Mentalism (1975, 28pp), The Book of Magic (1986, with Edwin A. Dawes), Magic in the Air (forthcoming), & The Life and Times of the Great Lafayette (1991, 112pp). Has published over 640 effects in magazines, beginning with Abra in 1947. Also in Magic Circular & Swami. Memoir is Pass the Salt (1965). [MC5/88]

name: Severn, [William Irving] "Bill", AIMC
bio: (Brooklyn, New York City: 11 May 1913-7 or 8 May 1992) Newspaper worker. Amateur magician since age 9 & pro semi-pro since teens. Prolific author of 25 magic books, including Magic Wherever You Are (1957, 122pp), Magic and Magicians (1958, 178pp), Shadow Magic (1959, 179pp), Rope Roundup (1960; repr 1976 as The Book of Rope and Knots), Magic with Paper (1962, 149pp), Magic Across the Table (1972, 122pp), Bill Severn's Big Book of Magic (1973, 238pp), Magic in Mind: Mental Magic Tricks (1974, 152pp; repr 1993), Bill Severn's Guide to Magic as a Hobby (1979, 280pp), Bill Severn's Best Magic (1990, 210pp), & Bill Severn's Amazing Magic (1992, 192pp). Magic columns in Linking Ring (1931) & Boy's Life for the Boy Scouts of America. Trick in Swami. [CA]

name: Sewell, Ernest
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-40s) Pro magician who played public school shows, etc, including at Egyptian Hall. Then toured Australia (with Harry Lauder's troupe) in 1914 when he included Living Marionettes in his act. Issued the famous Ernest Sewell magic sets that inspired, among others, Arthur Setterington, Stanton Carlisle, Margaret Yates, & Derek Lever. [Wal]

name: Sewell, Len J.
bio: (Australia: c1890-) Amateur magic inventor. Wrote Magi Magic (1947, 31pp). Tricks in Genii.

name: Seymour, Cyril Victor
bio: (Brondesbury, London, England: 6 Mar 1895-) Aka "Monsieur Voit-Plus". Semi-pro comedy with French chef & kid-show acts. [Go2]

name: Shackleton, Edgar
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s) Amateur. Brother of Dr H. Park

name: Shackleton, Dr H. Park, MIMC
bio: (Britain: -4 Jun 1963) Amateur. Brother of Edgar Shackleton. "Shadow" [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

name: Shadow Man
bio: See: Dewey, Herb

name: Shah, Ali
bio: (Crewkerne, Somerset, England: 3 Jun 1908-)

name: Shakeshaft, [Leonard] "Len
bio: (England: fl.1900s-50s) Owner of Midland Magic Co in Coventry 1924-1950 when he retired. Wrote under pen name "Barry Maule", Second Sight Explained (1906, 12pp; repr c1939). Contributed to Barnstormer.

name: Shalimar, Chevalier
bio:
"Shaman" NOTE: A fictitious magician created in 1940 as a hoax by Ted Annemann & carried on by Bruce Elliott & Walter Gibson until 1945. Inspired Bill Madsen's similar "Damon" hoax-magician in New Jinx 1965-68. [Phoenix#93; Abrams (1992), 459]

[See also: Körling, Knut]

name: Shan
bio: (England?: fl.1940s) Chinese-English. Stage name of Shan Wong, Mrs Eric Mason. Pro in Giant Memory act with husband.

name: Shan, Dr. Bey
bio:
"Shandu the Magician" SEE: Schindler, George

[See also: Greystoke, R. Temple]

name: Shankar, Professor
bio: (Udupi, Karnataka, India: 5 May 1951- ) Hindu. Inspired in 1960 by magician at school. Pro illusionist since graduating in psychology from Mysore U 1972. Over 3,000 stage shows (with full troupe) throughout India & the Arab Gulf states by 1989. Articles in Indian magic journals. [Wh2]

name: Sharpe, Alton [C.] "Al
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 1924-21 Dec 2004) Pro sleight-of-hand. Then lawyer & semi-pro magician. In 1951 bought Joe Berg's shop in Chicago, which he ran as the Sharpe Studio of Magic until 1957 when sold to Clarke Crandall. Bought Ade Duval's silk act after the latter's retirement in 1955. Wrote Expert Hocus-Focus (1961, 173pp) & Expert Card Mysteries (1969, 141pp), etc. Editor-publisher in Beverly Hills of Ollapodrida irregularly since 1983. Died of a massive blood clot on the brain. [Bo#260]

name: Sharpe, S[amuel] H[enry] "Sam", MIMC
bio: (Retford, Nottinghamshire, England: 31 Aug 1902-22 Jul 1992) Born into a family of jeweler-watchmakers. Inspired at age 8 seeing Besoni work a kid-show. Learned from box of tricks. Poultry farmer & apiarist (retired). Amateur & major historian & theorist of magic. In 1921 co-founded the Hull and East Riding Magicians' Society & since 1974 the Honorary Vice-President of its successor, the Hull Magicians' Circle. In 1923 invented Sharpe Scissors, "probably the first mini-version of Sawing Through a Woman". MIMC 1936. 1983 AMA Literary Fellowship. Translator of Hofzinser & Ponsin (see). Prolific author, including Neo Magic (1932, 130pp; 2nd ed rev 1946, 137pp), Conjured Up (1935), Good Conjuring, Great Magic (reprinted with the 2 previous in 1938 as Magic Artistry), The Magic Play (1976, 148pp), Oriental Conjuring and Magic (1981, 384pp, with Will Ayling), Salutations to Robert-Houdin (1983, 133pp), Words on Wonder (1984), Conjurers' Optical Secrets (1985, 188pp), Conjurers' Psychological Secrets (1988, 178pp), Devant's Delightful Delusions (1990, 232pp), Conjurer's Hydraulic & Pneumatic Secrets (1990, 160pp), & Conjurer's Mechanical Secrets (1991, 137pp), all important books.
