Articles (over 200) in Sphinx, Magic Circular, Linking Ring, Midget Magician, etc. [MC2/88; Genii6/84; Wh2]

name: Shaw
bio: (Britain: fl.1850s) Minor pro. Taught William George Smith c1856.

name: Shaw, Allan
bio: (Hamilton, Ontario, Canada: 20 Jan 1875-19 Jun 1953) Moved to USA in early 1890s. Major coin manipulator since his debut in 1894 in New York City. Full-time pro since 1897. Toured Europe (1898), Australia (1901, 1905, 1910), South Africa (1902-03). Played London's St. George's Hall in 1911, 1919-21, & 1923. Played the Paris Alhambra in 1914. Invented Coin Roll & Coins up the Sleeve. Arthritis forced his retirement in 1936. Next year moved to Australia where he died in Sydney. NOTE: Given name often misspelled & commonly mis-identified both as an American & an Australian by birth. [St;Wal;Bo3;Tay;Ho;Magic2/02,3/03]

name: Shaw, Audrey
bio: (Britain: fl.1950s-80s) Pro with husband Jack Shaw since 1953. After his death in 1976 she revived "The Wychwoods" act with a female assistant. Mark Raffles bought the act in 1984. [MUM10/85]

name: Shaw, Elwin T.
bio: (USA: -Aug 1966) Worked for Herman Hanson at Holden's Magic Shop in Boston. Aka "Le Conjuror". Pro magic & pick-pocket act.

name: Shaw, Jack
bio: (Fleetwood, England: c1928-27 Mar 1976) Pro with assistant-wife Audrey with their "Manhattan Magic" act 1953-55. Then in electrical business until 1962 when they introduced their "The Wychwoods" act that used 15 miniature poodles. Played the London Palladium (1963, 1971, 1973) & Radio City Music Hall (for 7 weeks in 1967). Continued with this act until 1974. Audrey revived the act after his death. [MUM10/85]

name: Shaw, Mark
bio: (Bombay, India: 11 Apr 1875-2 Dec 1972) Minor pro in 1900s-30s, aka "Prince Yuga", "Hugo", & "Manek Shah". Often played St. George's Hall, London, as "Prince Yuga". Played Pastor's in New York in 1907. (England: 1960- ) Raised in South Africa & now lives in the USA. Amateur mentalist & magician when in 1980 (with partner Michael Edwards) deceived the Project Alpha parapsychologists with their effects, exposing it themselves in 1983. Pet effect: Spoon Bending & Buried Alive. Now a pro mentalist in USA & abroad. [Ran]

name: Shaw, W[illiam] H. J.
bio: (USA: fl.1870s-1910s) Dealer ("Shaw's") in Chicago, etc, since 1875. By 1902 he had moved to St. Louis, Missouri; and then by 1919 to Victoria, Missouri. Wrote 4 booklets: Magic and Its Mysteries (1893, 61pp), Magic Up To Date (1896, 104pp), Shaw's Book of Acts (1896), & New Ideas in Magic, Illusions, Spiritualistic Effects (1902, 93pp). [Albo95]

name: Shaxon, Alan, MIMC
bio: (Harrow, England: 28 Dec 1933 – 20 Oct 2012) Stage name of Alan Arthur Howson. Learned at age 8 by loan of Lang Neil's The Modern Conjurer. Lessons from Ernest E. Noakes. Inspired by Robert Harbin (who later willed Shaxon most of his props). Debut in teens. In banking 1949-57. Then since 1957 a pro variety & cruise-ship performer-lecturer, working his "Sophisticated Sorcery" act with assistant Anne Dolby whom he married in 1956. Pet effects: Aerial Fishing, Thumb Tie, Human Gasometer, & Hydrostatic Glass. MIMC 1958. Invented Final Epic (1970). British Ring President 1990-91. Awarded The Maskelyne in 1991. Wrote My Kind of Magic (1970, 77pp) & Practical Sorcery (1976, 64pp). Series in Abra, Magic Circular, & Magic Info. Articles in Genii, Magigram, MUM, Pentagram, Swami, etc. TV bits. [Bo#225;Wat;Wh2]

name: Sheets, [Robert Warren] "Bob
bio: (Grand Forks, North Dakota: 15 May 1950-) Raised in Chula Vista, California 1952-69. Full-time pro since 1969 (age 18), specialized in comedy magic. Aka "Jolly Jester". With circus in California 1969-71; trade show worker in Chicago 1971-72; as magic bartender in Chicago, California, & Aspen 1972-81. Taught Doc Eason in 1977. Partner with Bob Sheets as "Sheets & Spill" c1978-1984. Moved to Maryland in 1981. Owner (& star performer with Spill) of Brookfarm Inn of Magic in Chevy Chase 1981-84 & Inn of Magic in Wheaton 1984-86. Pet effects: Blindfold Deck Stab, C&B, 3-Card Monte, & Walking Thru a Rope. Since 1987 runs Impossible Productions in Gaithersburg, Maryland. One of very few modern magi to work wearing a "bag of tricks" at his waist. Video bit (1994). [Wh2]

name: Shek Ben Ali
bio: (Calcutta, Bengal, India: 26 Aug 1906-Mar 1978) Stage name of Mohari Ali, an Indian Moslem. Pro variety comedy magician since 1936 with world tour beginning in Yarmouth, England. Pet effect:

name: Shelley, [Michael F.] "Mike
bio: (Charleston, West Virginia: 4 Mar 1942-) Learned at age 8 from books. Pro performer. Manufacturer-dealer ("Magical Mysteries") since 1987 in Hollywood, Florida. Prolific inventor, including Zig-Zag Card Outdone (1987), Envelopes of Mind, Candy Dandy, Blind Date (1987), & Time Control (1988). Columnist for Magic Manuscript since 1989. [Wh2]

name: Shelley, [Anthony John] "Tony", MIMC
bio: (Walsall, England: 10 Jul 1938-16 May 2004) Learned at age c10 from books & school friend. Pharmacist. Amateur debut at age 11 as "Fu Ling Yu". Semi-pro comedy magic act with assistant-wife Liz (married 1968) for which they won the 1969 British Ring Shield. British Ring Past President. IBM President 1989-90, the 3rd Briton to hold that office. [LR7/89;Wh5]

name: Shephard, Stephen "Steve
bio:
(USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro comedy magician on West Coast. Did Birdcage & closed with an interrupted striptease. Designed the Girl in the Fishbowl as permanent display at Bimbo's 365 Club in San Francisco in WW II. Partner in San Francisco's short-lived Cafe Society nitery, which folded in 1948. Tricks in HMM & Magicana #1. [Tay]

[See also: Thurston, Jane]

name: Sheppard, Tam
bio: (Scotland: -1942) Dealer ("Tam Sheppard's Magic Shop") in Glasgow until his death when acquired by Davenport's.

name: Sheridan, Jeff
bio: (Bronx, New York City, NY: 8 Oct 1948- ) Real name Jeff Mazzio. Inspired at age 9 by uncle doing card tricks. Learned at age 10 from books & other magicians. Student of Paul Draylin. Pro since 1967 as street magician with silent act in New York City. Worked in Al Flosso's magic shop 1969-71. Teacher of David Kotkin aka David Copperfield. Wrote Lim-Tricks (1987, 94pp). Trick in MUM. See Edward Claflin, Street Magic (1977). [Se]

name: Sherman, James C. "Jim
bio: (USA: -10 Jan 1972) Minor pro vaude magician in USA, France, & England. US Army in WW I. In early 1926 was commissioned to write what would become known as the Tarbell Course in Magic but withdrew after doing 12 lessons when he realized he wouldn't make enough money. Then magic dealer in Chicago, first in 1926 as the "Palmer Gift Shop", then again in the Palmer House as the "National Magic Company" 1936 to 1950. At the 1936 IBM convention exhibited a Mickey Mouse figure whose head, like Hero's Horse, could be cut through but not severed. First teacher of Johnny Paul. In WW II performed in hospitals for soldiers & trouped over the USA with Edgar Bergen. Retired to Beverly Hills, California, where his mansion had a 75-seat private magic theater. His brother, Ransom Sherman, ran a magic shop in Los Angeles. Wrote 4 booklets: 29 Svengali Tricks, 25 Stripper Tricks, 25 Wonderful Card Tricks (1945), & Flash Lites (1950, 32pp). Wrote "Chicago Chatter" column in early Genii. [St]

name: Sherman, Robert "Bob
bio: (Minsk, Russia [now Belarus]: 15 Jun 1892-28 Mar 1969) Aka "Sherms". Moved to Canada. At age 13 joined a minstrel show. Pro magician since age c17 when demoed at Whitlam's Japanese Magic & Novelty Store in Toronto. Moved to USA in 1910. In 1912 managed "Philadelphia Magic" shop in Philadelphia. Then on own as well-known dealer-manufacturer (Sherms Magic Company, Inc.) in Bridgeport, Connecticut, 1926-1946. Did Ghost Shows as "Hermes" & "X". Memoirs in Linking Ring (Mar-May 1968). [Walk2;Bo3;Albo95].

name: Sherman, Roger
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Semi-pro table-hopper, specialized in card & coin close-up. Wrote With Deck in Hand (30pp) & Trick Stuff (1982, 51pp).

name: Sherms, Bob
bio: See: Sherman, Robert

name: Sherry, Fred
bio: (Austria: fl.1960s) 1964 FISM 3rd prize for manip; 1967 FISM 2nd prize for manip.

name: Sherwood, Arthur, MIMC
bio: (Britain: 30 Jul 1874-) Inspired in 1880 seeing a magician. Debut in 1888. Semi-pro since 1921. Famed for his silk act as late as 1936. [Magazine of Magic Summer 1933;Go;Go2]

name: Sherwood, John C[layton]
bio: (Battle Creek, Michigan: 25 Jul 1950-) Inspired in 1958 seeing a local magician at a school function. Since 1962 his mentor was Neil Foster. Journalist with Battle Creek Enquirer. Semi-pro magician since 1983, with Chavez, mental, & logical mysteries. Pet effect: Zombie. Writer & commentator on magic. Wrote The Conjurer's Calculator (1976) & The Circuited Sorcerer (1977). Columns in New Tops since 1966. Articles in New Tops.

name: Sheshal
bio: (India: fl.1830s) A Hindu. Did a static suspension of himself in Madras in 1832 for which he became known as "The Brahmin of the Air". [Fr]

name: Shevlin, Clay H[amilton]
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Amateur magic historian & collector since 1972. Wrote Historians' Guide to Conjuring (1981, 160pp).

name: Shields, Cyril
bio: (England: fl.1920s-30s) Stage name of C.J. Hyde. Pro. Played St. George's Hall 1924. Was probably the first to present magic on British radio. Wrote Broadcast Conjuring Tricks (1930).

name: Shields, Frank[lin Cedric]
bio: (Cairo, Illinois: 26 Mar 1916-4 Jul 1989) Learned around age 12 reading Neil's The Modern Conjurer. Bartender. Semi-pro close-up. As bartender-magician worked bars first in Chicago & then, since the 1940s, in the San Francisco Bay Area where he also played the Magic Cellar. Noted for innovative handling of standard tricks. A teacher of Jeff Busby. Retired in 1980 by a stroke that left his right arm paralyzed. Died of cancer. Trick in Arcane. [Epoptica9/89;Wh]

name: Shields, Fred[erick Michael]
bio: (San Diego, California: 1919-19 Jan 1982) Actor, theatrical writer, & TV executive until retired. Amateur magician & mentalist. In 1947 co-invented (with Bascom Jones) Unbelievable, a now classic card trick. Co-wrote (with Bascom Jones) the "Double Daring" column in Genii 1947-61. Published effects in Genii under several pen names. On original AMA Board of Directors 1962-72. [Mag]

name: Shiels, Tony "Doc
bio: (Salford, Lancashire, England: 1938-) Inspired as young lad seeing Dante, Cecil Lyle, Galli Galli, & other magi at the Blackpool Palace Theatre. Artist by profession. Part-time pro magician since c1963. Pro tent show with mental magic & mentalism. A pioneer in bizarre magick. His daughter, "Cait Sidh", also participated as a witch. Wrote 13!!!: a devil's dozen of macabre miracles (1968, 24pp), Something Strange (1968, 20pp), Daemons, Darklings and Doppelgangers (1969, 64pp), Entertaining with E.S.P. (1974, 109pp), And Then There Were Three (1974, 35pp, with Tony Raven & Roy Fromer), Bizarre: The Surreal Sorcery of Tony "Doc" Shiels (1989, 87pp), & The Cantrip Codex (1989). Under pen name of "Niacail O'Siaghail" wrote The Shiels Effect: A Manual for the Psychic Superstar (1976, 72pp). Tricks in Magick, etc. 1 audio. 1 video (1989). [NJ#49;Wat]

name: Shimada, Deanna
bio: (Yorktown, Australia: c1948-) Born Deanna Perkins. Model. Assistant-wife of Haruo Shimada since 1965. Mother of Lisa Dimmare.

name: Shimada, [Haruo]
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 19 Dec 1940- ) Learned at age 13-18 assisting Tenyo. Pro club & stage work since age 18. Worked a dove act after seeing Channing Pollock in the 1962 Italian film European Nights. Left Japan in 1965 to tour Australia (where he met, hired, & married his Australian-born assistant, Deanna) and Mexico. Moved to USA in 1970 where he premiered his famous oriental-style Parasol Act that year. 1972 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year. AMA Magician of the Year, 1973, 1974, 1976. Played Portugal's Casino Estoril in 1974. In 1975 premiered his Dragon Illusion finale. 1975 Tenkai Prize. 1989 AMA Performing Fellowship. Played the Las Vegas Riviera "Splash" show 1990-94. Father of Lisa Dimmare. Wrote Shimada Haruo no Hon [The Book of Haruo Shimada] (1977). Videos (1985). TV bits including 1975 Henning special (with his Parasol Act). [Bo#240;Genii11/85;HC;Mag;Win;Wh]

name: Shimoda, Yuka
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s-90s) As "Yuka", she does a silent manip act. Editor of Onosaka's Magic News (monthly in Japanese) in late 1980s. 1988 FISM 3rd prize in general magic. Wife of Parte Koishi of "The Napoleons".

name: Shimomura, Tomoyuki
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 29 Jun 1960- ) Learned at age 10 from books. Specializes in close-up & mental magic. Joined Tenyo's development section in 1988 as an inventor. Invented Hyper Vision (1989). Tricks in Magic Manuscript. [MM11/89;Wh2]

name: Shioya, Chojiro
bio: (Japan: fl.1600s) Pro in Japan. Potentially the first to use the Black Art principle to perform the legendary “Donba Jutsu” (swallowing a horse) trick [Gibeciere, Winter 2009]. "Shokyokusai" [also spelled "Shoukyokusai" NOTE: A Japanese dynastic name that indicates a tutorial lineage, not necessarily a blood line.

name: Shokyokusai, Hiroko
bio: (Saitama, Japan: 20 Dec 1913 – 27 Aug 2007) Stage name of Shizue Yamazaki. She learned from Madame Tenkatsu. Pro illusionist. Past-President of the Nihon Kijutsu Kyokai [Japanese Professional Magicians Association].

name: Shokyokusai, Ko-ten-ichi
bio: (Japan: ) He and his troupe appeared in Europe in 1911 thru 1920. Although his early life is not clarified, he once was a part of Ten-ichi troupe. Pet effect: Butterfly Trick and Water Fountain Trick.

name: Shokyokusai, Sumie
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 1 Jan 1938-) Stage name of Shizuko Sugita. Pro stage magicienne. President of Nihon Kijutsu Kyokai [Japanese Professional Magicians Association]. FISM President 1994.

name: Shokyokusai, Ten-ichi
bio: (Japan: Feb 1853 - 14 Jun 1912) Stage name of Shokyoku Hattori. Son of a Samurai. Pro since debut in Tokyo in 1888. Probably invented Ten-Ichi Thumb Tie (by 1901). Toured USA 1901-03. Toured Europe 1903-04, playing the Berlin Wintergarten (1903 for 6 weeks). Played the Tokyo Kabuki-za in 1905. Uncle of Tenyo's mother. [Pr; Sphinx8/37]

name: Shokyokusai, Tenji
bio: (Japan: c1881 - 6 Jun 1921) Stage name of Katsuzo Shokyoku. Adopted son of the original Ten-Ichi from whom he learned as principal male assistant by 1908. Originally worked as "Tenji Shokyokusai". Pro on own since 1912 as "Ten-Ichi II". Toured USA in 1905-06 and Europe 1906-08.

name: Shokyokusai, Tenkatsu
bio: (Japan: 21 May 1886 - 11 Nov 1944) Aka "Tenkatsu SHOKYOKUSAI". Pro sleight-of-hand & illusions. Learned as principal female assistant to Ten-Ichi with whom she toured the USA in 1901 & 1924. Pro with own troupe, touring USA in 1924-25. Played the Tokyo Kabuki-za in 1930s. Japan's first famous magicienne. [Pr]

name: Shokyokusai, Tenyo
bio: (Tsuruga, Japan: 21 Sep 1888-30 Sep 1980) Stage name of Matsutaro YAMADA. Son of a Ten-ichi's niece. His mother worked with the Ten-Ichi troupe. Pro stage magician & illusionist since 1905. Pet effect: Thumb Tie. Pro dealer-maker in Tokyo since 1930 when founded the Tenyo Co, largest magic firm in Japan. Retired in 1960, passing the company to his son Akira YAMADA. Mentor of Tenko HIKITA. 1978 5th Order of Merit, awarded by Emperor Hirohito. Wrote Kijutsu to watashi [Magic & l] (1976, 405pp). [St;Wat;Ir]

name: Shonting, Howard [Le Roy]
bio: (Columbus, Ohio: 1909- ) Taught at age 7 by Howard Thurston. Pro stage, close-up, & mentalism since age 18. Now semi-retired in Arizona, teaching & lecturing on magic. [Wh2]

name: Shungopavi
bio: (USA: -1913?) American Hopi Indian. Pro illusionist, 1904-1910. [Pr]

name: Shute, Merlyn T.
bio: (Canada?: fl.1980s) Wrote Nine Modern Classics (1980), Nits 'N Bits (1980), Cups-Cups-Cups (1980), The 'How To' Book of the Chop Cup (1980, 32pp), Little Things (1982), Out of Your Pocket (1982), The 'How To' Book on the Zombie (1983), & How to Force a Card (1983). All the above published by Morrissey Magic.

name: Siamois
bio: See: Chandéri, François

name: Sicnarf
bio: (Britain: fl. 1910s) Pen name (by reversal of given name) of Francis Chill. Wrote A Half Hour of Magic (1910, 28pp). A promised sequel never appeared. NOTE: Name often misspelled "Signarf" by Stanyon.

name: Sid, Salem
bio: (Syria: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Moved to USA. Small-time pro in New England. Noteworthy for having taught Si Stebbins the so-called Si Stebbins Setup (first version) in 1895-96.

name: Sidi Ali
bio: (Germany: fl.c1930s) Stage name of Joseph Scherer. Pro in Germany & USA. Died in Baltimore.

name: Siegel, Lee
bio: (USA: 1945-) Professor of religion at U of Hawaii. Amateur magician since age 8 when father took him to the Hollywood Magic Shop & bought him some tricks. Wrote Net of Magic: Wonders and Deceptions in India (1991, 454pp) based on his 1987-88 visit there.

name: Siegel, Paul J.
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: c1933-) Inspired seeing local magicians & learned from magic shop purchase of a Hindu Vase. Amateur mentalist. Published 1st trick at age 14 in Genii. 1969 TAOM Stage Trophy. Wrote Windows to the Mind (1968, 33pp), Doorway to Delusion (1972, 33pp), & Mentalism à la Mode (1975, 55pp). NOTE: Surname misspelled "Siegal". [NJ#36]

name: Siemens, John
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 25 Jun 1883-14 Sep 1957) Pro manipulator with cards, coins, & balls. Toured Germany 1905, France 1911, London (the Palace Theatre) 1913, Germany 1922 (including the Berlin Wintergarten), Brazil 1924, Vienna 1925, Holland 1925, & Belgium 1925. Moved to USA in 1930. Died at Saranak Lake, New York. [Vo58;Al]

name: Sierak, Horace
bio: (Australia: fl.1920s-30s) Pro illusionist since debut in Australia in 1922. Pet effect: the Sawing. Toured North American vaude circuits from mid 1920s to early 1930s. [Bo;Wal]

name: Sigg, Klaus
bio: (Germany?: 18 Feb 19-) Magician & magic collector in Frankfurt, Germany. [Nad]

name: Sigma
bio: See: Sanderson, G. P.

name: Signarf" [misspelling]
bio: See: "Sicnarf"

name: Silan, Harry Z.
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 1896-) Professor at the Pedagogical Seminary. Taught magic by Dr Lénárd. Amateur, specialized in billiard ball, card, & rope magic. Treasurer of MAME in 1929.[WWM]

name: Silano, Rocco
bio: (USA: 1959-) Studied with Slydini. Pro stage & close-up. 1986 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. 1994 U.S. Invitational Closeup Championsip 2nd place. Invented D'Lite (independently of Mayoral's Mystic Light Beams) in 1989. Videos (1987, 1988, 1994). See Steve Schneiderman, If It Fits... Sleeve It: The Magic of Rocco Silano (1991, 71pp).

name: Silber, Charles "Charlie
bio: (USA: -c1968) Ex-hoofer. Pro magician. Pro dealer in Hollywood (Magic House of Charles at 6613½ Hollywood Blvd) since 1940s (by 1943). Teacher. Invented Out Of My Hat rabbit in the hat puppet that did the tricks (1942 award winner in Oakland). Magic adviser on Silvan Venice police chief. Learned at age 7, to his father's consternation. Debut by age II. Aka "Mago Saghibu". Since age 20 pro manip act to full-evening show. Played Portugal's Casino Estoril in 1958 & Paris' Olympia in 1959. In 1962 brought his card & dove act to Japan. Dropped the dove act in 1969. World tours until 1970 when concentrated on performing in Italy. 1973 FISM guest star at Paris "Gala" with special award. MIMC 1976. Collector (over 4,000 books). CMI Honorary President. 1991 AMA Magician of the Year.1994 Louie Award. Italy's most famous living magician, he has appeared in 78 of his own TV shows in Italy (all on RAI-TV national network) between 1970 & 1988 and over 100 TV guest appearances in USA, Europe, & Italy. Has marketed a million Silvan magic sets. Invented "Silvan Dove Levitation" (1973) & "Zig-Zag 4" (1980). Wrote 7 booklets for children, including the best-selling Silvan Supermagic (1984). Also the useful 272-page history Arte Magica (1977) and Silvan il Mondo dell `Occulto (1994). Column in Magia Moderna c1979-present. Did 1 LP phonograph record for teaching. [Bo#292;Mag;Wat;Wh2]

name: Silver, George
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) Minor pro in Chicago area in early 1920s when he did the Needle Trick, etc. Under pen name of "Dr. X" wrote On the Other Side of the Footlights: An Expose of Routines, Apparatus and Deceptions Resorted to by Mediums, Clairvoyants, Fortune Tellers and Crystal Gazers in Deluding the Public [1922, 120pp].

name: Silver, Jack
bio: (Scotland: -1977) Engineer with the Post Office. Dealer (Scottish Magic Studio, then in early 1960s with daughter Ray as Silray Magic Co) in Edinburgh 1950-1972, pioneering in lucite (perspex) plastic props. Father of Ray Silver, grandfather of Michael Hooper, & great grandfather of Bernd Clayton. [Daw94]

name: Silver, Ray
bio: (Edinburgh, Scotland: 19 Jul 1932- ) Stage name of Agnes Silver, aka La Ray, daughter of Jack Silver. Pro magicienne since 1949 (age 17) working first variety, then kid-shows, & then since early 1960s as dealer with her father as Silray Magic Co in Edinburgh & later Thundersley, Essex, in 1971. Wife, successively, of two magician-dealers, Edwin Hooper (1957-71) & Dennis Lucas ("Johnny Neptune"). Her son Michael Hooper was briefly with Supreme, but both he & she later dropped magic. Her daughter by Neptune, Shirley Ray, is a magician and balloon worker. [Mar]

name: Silverman, Kenneth "Ken
bio: (New York City, NY: 5 Feb 1936-) Learned at age 10 or 11 from Mysto Magic set. Amateur magician now specialized in closeup. Pet effects: Okito Coin Box, Cardini's Cards, Card to Pocket. Pro writer & teacher. Wrote A Cultural History of the American Revolution (1976); The Life and Times of Cotton Mather (1984), which won a 1985 Pulitzer Prize & a 1985 Bancroft Prize; Edgar A. Poe: Mournful and Never-ending Remembrance (1991), which won a 1991 Mystery Writers of America Edgar Award; and Houdini!!!: The Career of Ehrich Weiss (1996, 465pp), the best of all Houdini biograpies, which got the 1997 Christopher Award. [CA;Wh5]

name: Silvester, Dr.
bio: See: Sylvester, Alfred

name: Sima, Eugen
bio: See: Fornalski, Jósef

name: Simbar
bio: See: Wien, Frank

name: Simek, Stefan [Gustav] "Steve
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 29 Oct 1957- ) Learned at age 6 from grandfather's gift of magic set. Semi-pro stage illusionist since 1972 as "Steve Stevenson". Pro dealer-manufacturer as founder-proprietor since 1976 of "viennamagic", in Vienna. Improver of Vanishing Stereo (1987) & Electronic Airborne Glass (1988). Articles in Magie & Magische Welt. [Wh2]

name: Simmons
bio: See: Lynn, H. S.

name: Simmons, Ken
bio: (Colorado Springs, Colorado: 9 Nov 1959-) Realtor in hometown. Wrote Cards with a Different Touch (1981, 57pp), Close-Up with Cards (1982, 64pp), Riffling the Pasteboards (1986, 73pp), Scotch and Soda (1986, 3 vols, 31+53+?pp), Riffling the Pasteboards Again (1987, 74pp), David Neighbors' Freshly Minted, David Neighbors on the Double Coin Gimmick (46pp), & Master Index to Marlo's Revolutionary Card Technique (1991, 169pp). Published-edited Onyx since 1997. Tricks in New Tops, Magic Manuscript, Kabbala, & Linking Ring (1997 Parade).

name: Simms, Warren [E.]
bio: (USA: -1976) Stage name of William E. Simms. Magician & ventriloquist. SAM President 1944-45. Credited as inventor of the horizontal-load coin dropper.

name: Simon, [James Benjamin] "Jim
bio: (Shaller, Iowa [sic]: 4 Jun 1905-23 Apr 1975) Cabinetmaker & signwriter. Semi-pro stage magician as "Mystic Benjamin" 1947-52. Pet effects: Doll House & dove & duck productions. Founded Worth Magic in Fort Worth, Texas, in 1960, making high quality magic props that he sold mainly to Joe Berg's National Magic Company in Chicago. Simon moved his shop to Sun Valley, California, where he operated as Worth Magic Novelty Company until his death, selling mainly wholesale to Hollywood Magic, Magic Inc, & Berg. In 1975 Lynn Johnson bought the business from Simon's estate and now operates it as Milson-Worth.

name: Simon, William "Bill
bio: (USA: 7 Apr 1927-6 May 1988) US military service 1944-45. Businessman. Amateur cardman. Voted runner-up among the 10 living Card Stars in 1955. Wrote Controlled Miracles (1949, 21pp; repr 1963), Effective Card Magic (1952, 181pp), Sleightly Sensational (1954, 36pp), & Mathematical Magic (1964, 187pp; repr 1993). Tricks in Phoenix, New Phoenix, HMM, Ibidem, & Magic.

name: Simonette, Joseph
bio: (Melphi, Italy: 28 Sep 1899- ) Debut while serving in US Navy in WW I. Semi-pro mental magician as "Simonette the Mystic" in New York City in 1920s. [Go2]

name: Simonoff, Lòóy [Jehovah] "Louis
bio: (New York City, NY: 2 Jul 1928 – 12 April 2011) Father came to USA from a village on the Russo-Polish frontier. Inspired by and learned as a young boy from his father who taught him to backpalm cards. An early devotee of Erdnase. Associate Professor of Mathematics & Lecturer on Magic at the U of Nevada at Las Vegas. Except for his magic course, which he began teaching in 1979, an amateur, specializing in card magic. Pet effect: P. Harris's Color Stunner. Articles in Apocalypse & Genii. Contributor to books by P. Harris & A. Ackerman. Invented Lóóy's False Count, Flippant, etc. [Lo;Wh2]

name: Simonson, Nils
bio: (Sweden: 31 Jul 1892-22 Oct 1968) Amateur in Stockholm, specialized in mental magic. Aka "Le Chevalier Noir". Founding member of the Svensk Magisk Cirkel in 1946. Edited the bi-annual bi-lingual (Swedish & English) Swedish Magic Gazette 1955-57 (6 issues). [St;Dif]

name: Simvolokov, Ilya Kalistratovich
bio: (Kasionushka, Voronezh, Russia: 15 Jun 1918-) Pro circus magician in USSR. [Win]

name: Sinclair, Professor Charles
bio: (Britain: fl.1850s) Minor pro magician & vent. [Fr]

name: Sinclair, Frank
bio: (Bradford, Yorkshire, England: 22 Jul 1911-15 Apr 1991) Stage name of Frank Herbert Harris. Inspired as child, his mother being with the Chung Ling Soo troupe. Policeman. Semi-pro after WW II, specialized in the Bullet Catch. Wrote Catching a Marked Bullet in the Teeth (1983, 20pp). Articles in Linking Ring & Magigram.

name: Sinclair, [George] Robert "Bob", MIMC
bio: (Callander, Scotland: 14 Jan 1925-14 Feb 1993) Semi-pro with manip act. 1961 British Ring Shield.

name: Singh, Linga
bio: See: Dutt, A. N.

name: Singh, Rajah
bio: See: Briggs, J. Albert

name: Sino
bio: (Güstrow, Germany: 20 Nov 1921- ) Stage name of Hans-Jürgen Schrein. Learned at age 15. Pro since 1948. Played cabarets & casinos across the world & appeared on the Ed Sullivan TV show. Created many original effect with top hat that became his "The Magic Top Hat Parade" act. Invented a version of the Indian Rope Trick, Light Bulb Production, Fading Flower, and Tie Tricks (colored). [Wit;Roh]

name: Sioli, Alessandro
bio: (Milan, Italy: 27 May 1935-) Learned in 1947 when bought a magic set. Semi-pro stage magician since 1967 as "Mr Soliman". Pet effects: doves, fire, etc. President, Ring 223 Milano, 1977-present. [Wh5]

name: Sir Edwards
bio: See: LaRue, Buddy

name: Sir Felix Korim
bio: See: "Korim, Sir Felix"

name: Sir Teen
bio: See: Liberg, Olle Oson

name: Sirdani
bio: (South Africa: 11 Nov 1900-28 Feb 1982) Stage name of Sydney "Sid" Daniels, older brother of drummer Joe Daniels (of "Joe Daniels and His Hotshots"). Pro music-hall pickpocket & magic act. His catch-phrase was "Don't be fright." Toured Australia in 1938. Wrote Don't Be Fright: Radio Magic (1946, 72pp). Played the NY Palace in 1951. [Wal]

name: Sirius
bio: See: Mackay, Hugh

name: Siroco
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Ralph Arbitelle. Taught by Francis Carlyle in early 1950s. Pro stage magician. A teacher of Chuck Vincent. Video. [Mag]

name: Siska, Andrew George
bio: (Garfield, New Jersey: 29 Mar 1908- ) Teacher in New Jersey. Semi-pro stage & club magician since 1925 as "Siska". Specialized in card magic & vent. [SAM]

name: Siskoff
bio: (France: 10 May 1863-16 Mar 1921) Stage name of Barthélemy-Marius-D. Verdin. Pro manipulator of the old school. Joined the ASAP in 1905. Died in Nice. [St]

name: SYMbol Oct 1992-May 1993, & L&L Presents 1997-present. Video bit (1993).
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Ex-radio disk jockey turned pro restaurant magician in Connecticut. Wrote Professional Restaurant Magic. Articles in Genii & MUM. Editor The Magic Menu 1990-present,

name: Sisti, Jim
bio: (Ferrara, Italy: 14 Dec 1919-31 Jul 1989) Music teacher in Bologna & amateur magician with a famous pseudo-Chinese act as "Chun Chin Fu". Specializes in silk magic. Invented Sitta's Rope Trick & Sitta's Leopard Silk. Founding-editor of Magia Moderna 1954-89. President, Club Magico Italiano, 1957-89. FISM jury 1979, 1988. FISM President 1988-89, his term to have run to 1991 but interrupted when he died in a fire at home. Wrote The Colorful Magic of Alberto Sitta (52pp). [Magia Moderna6-9/83; Qui Magia1/89]

name: Siul
bio: (Spain: 1892- ) Stage name of Luiz Rodriguez. Pro. Played the Lisbon Coliseu 1922-23.

name: Siva
bio: See: Avis, Jack

name: Sjak, Aleksander
bio: (Russia: 1864-1922) Pro magician with assistant-wife "Madame Naidra". [Nad]

name: Skifington, [Glenn] Ross
bio: (Aukland, New Zealand: 3 Oct 1948-) Learned at age 9 from Xmas gift of David Nixon magic set. Trained as an actor at the Mercury Theatre Auckland 1970-71. Graduated from Auckland University New Zealand with a Diploma in Fine Arts in 1971 and in 1972 a Diploma of Teaching from Auckland Secondary Teachers College. Taught art and drama at Tamaki College 1973-74. Moved to Australia in 1975 and worked extensively in television, film and theatre. Performed in The Magic Show in 1975 (understudy to Larry Anderson). Member of The Australian Society of Magicians since 1976. Awarded the Order of The Sphinx, Gold Bar, for his services to the Society. Pro stage illusionist since 1977. IBM Order of Merlin 2008. Entertainer on cruise ships since 1978 including QE2, Silver Cloud, Crystal Symphony, Star Princess, Radisson Voyager and Legend. Founded Patrick Productions in 1980 as an illusion production company producing shows and events. First original show Tricks in 1979 for The Last Laugh toured nationally 1979/1980. Wrote, produced and directed his illusion show(s) Electricks in 1984 touring for the Casino circuit in 1984, 1990 and 2001 for the Glen Street Theatre. Wrote Patricks Hat Trick a magical entertainment for kids in 1997 which has played through to 2001. Created and directed Silvers Grand Magic Circus in 1985 performing the role of ringmaster/illusionist. Other original shows include The Fabulous Fontaines (1993) Chiller a horror show for kids (1993) Lounge Wizard a magic cabaret touring 2001/2004. Throughout 2002, 2004 and 2006 toured nationally and internationally with The Bell Shakespeare Company in The Comedy of Errors. Awarded a Lifetime Achievement Award for "A lifetime contribution to the Art of Magic" at the 27th Australian Convention of Magicians 2000. In 2005 a second "A Lifetime Achievement Award" from Magic New Zealand. [Ran;Wh2]

name: Skinner, Michael "Mike
bio: (USA: c1947-3 Sep 1998) Learned at age 17 from books at New York City branch library. Then a student of Eddie Fechter. Moved to Hollywood in 1967, studying under Dai Vernon & Larry Jennings. Top-line pro close-up. AMA Best Close-up Magician 1971 & 1974. Mentor of Bob King & Robert Lansing. Cruise ship worker & magic shop demonstrator. Resident magician at Golden Nugget (Lily Langtry Room, etc) in Las Vegas since 1976. See Jeff Busby, Michael Skinner's Intimate Magic (1982, 45pp); Mike Maxwell, Michael Skinner's Ultimate 3 Card Monte (1990, 20pp); & Classic Sampler (1996, 113pp). Tricks in Talisman, Epilogue, Arcane, Magic, Magic Menu. The protagonist of William Murray's 5 detective novels (a night club magician & private investigator) is based on Skinner. [Mag;Wat]

name: Slade, "Dr" Henry
bio: (USA: -1905) Pro pseudo-psychic. Invented nail writer (by 1872) & flap slate (by 1872). Toured England for 3 months in 1876, Germany in 1877. A credulous account in 1877 by a prominent German physicist is Johann Carl Fredrich Zöllner, Transcendental Physics (1881 tr). Died in a New York City hospital.

name: Slaight, [John] Allan
bio: (Galt, Ontario, Canada: 19 Jul 1931- ) Inspired at age c9 seeing Giordmaine demo at Eaton's in Toronto. Semi-pro & pro platform magician 1943-56, adding mentalism in 1948. Now owner Standard Broadcasting Corporation in Toronto & amateur cardman & mentalist. Co-edited (with Howard Lyons) Stewart James in Print: The First Fifty Years (1989, 1025pp) & edited The James File (2000, 3 vols, 1770pp). Tricks in Apocalypse, Arcane, Chronicles, Epoptica, Genii, Ibidem, Linking Ring, Magick, New Pentagram, Pallbearers Review, Precursor, & Talisman. [Wh2]

name: Slater, Ralph
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro hypnotism act. Famed for a 1948 performance at Brighton, England, for which he was sued for damages by a woman who in 1952 won a judgement of £1,000 [=$2,800], news reports varying on the amount. Although subsequently reversed by Court of Appeal, this case led to banning hypnotism as entertainment in Britain. After a brief tour in the USA in 1952 he returned to performing in Britain.

name: Slayton, Charles C[hurchill]
bio: (Springfield, Ohio: 17 Apr 1887-) US Navy officer. Amateur magician. SAM President 1947-48. [WWM]

name: Sleight, Walter "Wally
bio: (Grimsby, Lincolnshire, England: 25 May 1921-) His real name, aka "Sleight of Hand" since 1942. Pro stage & club work since age 11 when he first learned as call-boy for Goldin, Levante & J. Maskelyne. Specializes, appropriately, in sleights with cards & rope routines, but uses only 3 sleights: classic force, 2-handed pass, & palming. In the RAF in WW II toured Australia, India, & Ceylon. Then in cinema industry for 10 years. Wrote column ("Sleight of Hand") in For Sale 1985 & Magigram 1988-89. Over 20 TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Slem, Rev. O. T.
bio: See: Stover, Mel

name: Sliwa-Wyszomirski, Andrzej
bio: (Cieplice, Poland: 1941- ) Pro manipulator with assistant-wife Eweline Miller. Now lives in Germany. [Mec;Nad]

name: Sloggett, Charles E.
bio: (Australia: 1889-1962) Small-time pro illusionist who toured Australia from the mid-1910s to mid-30s as "The Incomparable Sloggetts". [Pr]

name: Sluys, Sylvain
bio: (Belgium: fl.1980s) Pro stage & close-up magician. Works a New Wave magic act of tricks, music, & special text. [Mer]

name: Slydini, Tony
bio: (Poggia, Italy: 1 Sep 1901-15 Jan 1991) Stage name of Quintino Marucci, aka "Tony Foolem". Learned as boy in Italy from amateur father. Moved to Argentina as teenager, working in vaude until the Depression. Moved to USA (New York City) in 1930. Pro close-up widely rated a master of sleight-of-hand. Managed Delmar's "The Magic Center" since 1951. Pet effect: Paper Balls Over the Head (by 1949). Wrote The Art of Using the Lap as a Servante (1953, 4pp). Played Venezuelan clubs & TV in 1957. Invented Paper Balls to Hat (by 1947), Rope Miracle (1949), & Imp Pass (1966). 1970 AMA Performing Fellowship; 1974 AMA Masters Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Teacher of Johnny Carson, Doug Henning, Frank Scalzo, Chuck Vincent, etc. Retired to nursing home in 1988. See Lewis Ganson, The Magic of Slydini (1960, 208pp; repr 1971); Leon Nathanson, Slydini Encores (1966, 157pp); Karl Fulves, The Best of Slydini (1976, 2 vols, 108+126pp); Karl Fulves, The Magical World of Slydini (2 vols, 1979); & Mad Magic #30 for all-Slydini issue. Tricks in Gen, Pallbearers, Chronicles, Apocalypse, etc. NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Marussi" & birth year often misgiven as "1910". [Dif; Mag; HC; Win]

name: Slyter, Clarence
bio: (West coast, USA: fl.1930s-50s) Pro. Toured Western & Mid-western clubs & theaters 1936-1947 with a comedy drunk act where miming seeing double, triple, & quadruple, the objects in his hands would multiply. Aka "Professor Slyter". Invented Multiplying Whiskey Glasses (late 1930s) & Multiplying Candles (c1940). [Pr]

name: Smart, Fred
bio: (USA: c1935-) Pro with his own "Smart's Magic Circus" that toured the American midwest for auto dealerships with 600 shows per year.

name: Smit, Tel
bio: (Holland: fl.1960s-80s) Student of Henk Vermeyden. FISM 1st prizes in manip 1967 & 1970.

name: Smith, Al
bio: (England: fl.1970s-90s) Pro close-up. Dealer (Magick Enterprises) in Sheffield. Wrote Cards on Demand (1980, 37pp) & Cards at Bay (1982, 19pp). Tricks in Talon & Linking Ring (1-man "Parade" Feb 1982).

name: Smith, Albert
bio: (Chertsey, England: 24 May 1816-23 May 1860) Popular author & lecturer. Also conjured & used vent hand. Seasons at Egyptian Hall, London, in 1850s. [Daw]

name: Smith, Albert E[dward]
bio: (Faversham, Kent, England: 4 Jun 1875-1 Aug 1958) Brought to USA in 1888. In 1894, with sleight-of-hand & illusions, framed an act with chalk-talker J. Stuart Blackton, which soon appeared on the Lyceum circuit. In 1897 the partners turned to film making by forming the Vitagraph Company, which began production the next year. Its quick success caused them to drop their magic act after a couple of years. They sold Vitagraph to Warner Brothers in 1925 for $735,000. Died wealthy in Hollywood. Autobio is Two Reels and a Crank (1952). Bio is in Anthony Slide, The Big V: A History of the Vitagraph Company (rev ed: 1987). Appeared in documentary film A Vitagraph Romance (1912).

name: Smith, Albert P.
bio: See: "Smith, Mysterious"

name: Smith, [John William] "Bill
bio: (Long Beach, California: 25 Feb 1955- ) Learned at age 13. Worked in Stan Allen's magic shop in Los Alamitos, California, 1973. Comedy stage magic by 1973 when he won a PCAM prize. Then with a duck act since 1974. Pro since 1975. Assistant to Blackstone Jr 1977-86. Illusion builder since 1979 ("Magic Ventures" in Westminster, California, until moved to Las Vegas) for Blackstone Jr, Henning, Burton, Orson Welles, Copperfield, The Pendragons, André Kole, Al Belmont, Melinda, etc, now (1993) making some 50 illusions (at $5,000 to $30,000 each. Also wrote comedy material for Copperfield. Performs with wife Gigi & son Taylor. Articles in Genii & 2 books. [Bo#221;Mag;Wh2]

name: Smith, Charles Neil
bio: (USA: 1887-) Learned at age 10 reading Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Pet effect: Dancing Hank in 1st decade of 1900s. Pro. Wrote the "Uncle Felix" column in Sphinx around 1920.

name: Smith [Jr], Fred W[illiam]
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Amateur in Buffalo, New York. Invented Smith Myth c1945. Trick in New Phoenix.

name: Smith, G. Hendry
bio: (Scotland: 1891-1971) Semi-pro & collector.

name: Smith, George William
bio: (Newark, England: 1836-21 Mar 1904) Son of magician "Buck" (William Smith). Lessons from Shaw c1856. Pro (ex-tailor) since 1857. Aka "Smith of Bristol" since 1857 & "Herr Dobler" after c1865. Wrote as "Herr Dobler" Expose of the Davenport Brothers (Belfast: 1869, 48pp). Claimed & possibly invented Handkerchiefs and Soup Plates (by 1875). Played Dublin in 1889. Famous practical joker. Still performing (in Scotland) as late as 1903. Died in Aberdeen, Scotland. [Vo56;Cl;Magic4/04]

name: Smith, H[arold] Adrian, MIMC
bio: (East Providence, Rhode Island: 17 Sep 1908-13 [sic] Jan 1992) Learned magic from book in 1922. Engineer & manager for a Boston manufacturer. Semi-pro magician 1932-33 specializing in sleight-of-hand & mental magic. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Dove Vanish. SAM President 1940-41 & IBM President 1948-49, being the  $ 2^{nd} $ person (after Eugene Bernstein) to hold both offices in these two leading American magical societies. MIMC 1958. SAM Hall of Fame 1977. Named 7th SAM Dean of American Magicians in 1983. 1989 Henry Ridgely Evans History Award. Magic collector since 1924. Bought the Arthur F. Baird Collection of some 300 standard works in 1929; the Peter Graef Collection of 1,500 books in 1936 (purchased from Graef's widow in Chicago); & the 6,000-volume Milton A. Bridges Collection in 1940. Smith added to these, ending with over 10,000 items, mainly books. Gave this fine collection to Brown U in 1988. Wrote 6 booklets: Flap Slate Wrinkles (1931, with U.F. Grant), Master Mysteries of 1933 (1933), Instant Magic Square (1933), It's In the Bag (1935), Card System Deluxe (20pp), & Superb Tricks (1953, 47pp). Articles on magicana in MUM, Sphinx, Tops (1936-40 column) & Linking Ring. [MUM3/92;Bo#189;SAM;Se;St]

name: Smith, [Henry Sydney Joseph] "Harry
bio: (London, England: 6 Jan 1905-1977) Moved in 1907 to Toronto, Canada, where his father managed a local variety theater. Learned at age 7 from father's magician friends. Cardman since age 12. Pro dealer (with wife Sophie Smith, née Sophia Scheid) as "Arcade Magic and Novelty Store" in Toronto, 1939-1977 when she took over, running it until 1979. Mr Smith was a mentor of James Randi, Howard Lyons, Doug Henning, & many other young Canadian magi. [Tops6/71]

name: Smith, Henry [nmn]
bio: (Castle Gresley, Derbyshire, England: 27 Jan 1936-) Learned at age 8 by joining mail-order magic club. A Major in the Salvation Army in Taunton until became a freelance Christian minister. Semi-pro since 1976 as "Uncle Henry". Full-time pro since 1983, specializing in gospel & kid-show magic. Writes-edits "The Gospel Column" in Magigram since 1985. President, Fellowship of Christian Magicians-Europe, 1988. Wrote 2 booklets: Simple Gospel Magic with Economy Props (1987, 19pp) & Colourful Gospel Magic (1988, 24pp). 1 video (1988). [Wh2]

name: Smith, J. Stewart
bio: (USA: -8 Jan 1981). Card magician. Self-published 16 booklets on card magic from 1950 to 1966. These plus his 17th manuscript were reprinted as The Collected Works of J. Stewart Smith (1983, 478pp). Trick in HMM.

name: Smith, Leonard W.
bio: (Little Marlow, England: 20 Dec 1915-) Aka "Cardos". Semi-pro with card, cigarette, and hate effects. [Go2]

name: Smith, Les[lie Charles]
bio: (Vanceboro, Maine: 9 Aug 1915- ) Inspired at age 7 seeing a magician do Bonus Genus. At age 10 began building his own props. Pro illusionist 1939-50, touring a show on East coast & Canada. Since 1963 major illusion builder as owner of Owen Magic Supreme in Azusa, California. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote (with Gertrude Smith), "Keep the wheels turning..., V.2 (1992, 372pp). Bio section in Richard Buffum, "Keep the wheels turning ...." (1977). [MUM11/2002;Wh]

name: Smith, Lindsay E.
bio: (Yankton, South Dakota: 21 Jun 1939- ) Learned at age 10 from a neighbor magician. In public relations. Amateur magician since 1949, specializing in kid-shows. Wrote (with Bruce Walstad) Sting Shift: The Street-Smart Cop's Handbook of Cons and Swindles (1989, 125pp). [Wh2]

name: Smith, Mysterious
bio: (France: -16 May 1957) Moved to USA where he changed his name to Albert P. Smith. Pro illusionist trouping a good sized show ("Mysterious Smith Co.") out of Cedar Rapids, Iowa, and, later, Warrenville, Illinois, from early 1920s until mid-1930s when he sold his show to Harry Thurston. After a brief stint as a photographer in the South he toured Iowa with an act of small magic and spirit effects. Retired in 1942 & moved to Florida. [Par;Bos;Berg]

name: Smith, Richard B.
bio: (USA: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Invented lone in 1904.

name: Smith, Samuel Patrick "Sammy
bio: (Eustis, Florida: 24 Jul 1961- ) Learned at age 8 from amateur great-uncle, Robert Conrad Smith. Started magic publishing business in 1976 with Burling Hull as partner. Full-time pro since 1982 doing school, church, etc dates. Benefactor of Burling Hull in his later years & researching a bio of him. Wrote a series of booklets on publicity aspects of magic, including Sell Your Act with Posters (1987, 40pp) & Sell Your Act with Letters (1989, 85pp). Also wrote Big Laughs For Little People (1991, 200+pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Magic Manuscript, Magical Arts Journal, New Tops, & Genii. Audios (1984 & 1985). [Wh2]

name: Smith, Sophie
bio: See: Smith, [Henry S. J.] "Harry"

name: Smith, Walter
bio: (USA?: ) Invented Acrobatic Silks by 1969.

name: Smith, Walter J. Obree
bio: See: "Nikola, Louis"

name: Smith, Rev Willard S.
bio: (Ipswich, Massachusetts: 9 Oct 1898-dead) Inspired at age 14. Minister. Amateur magician plus rag pictures. In WW II was a chaplain in US Army in Europe. Articles & column in Linking Ring, article in Conjuror's Magazine, tricks in HMM. [Th]

name: Smith, William
bio:
"Smith Jr, A. R." SEE: Hull, Burling

[See also: "Buck, Mons."]

name: Smothers, Tom
bio: (USA: 2 Feb 1937- ) With younger brother Dick starred in the popular CBS-TV weekly The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour 1967-69. Learned magic in 1970 when coached by Harry Blackstone Jr for his role as a tap-dancing magician in Brian De Palma's 1st movie, Get to Know Your Rabbit. Played this same role later that year at Caesar's Palace in Las Vegas for 5 or 6 weeks with Blackstone Jr on stage in a comic battle of magicians. [Jef]

name: Smullyan, Ray[mond M.]
bio: (Far Rockaway, NY: 1919- ) Mathematician. & logician Put himself through college by working part-time as a magician (mainly sleight-of-hand) at parties and supper clubs. Ph.D from Princeton. Prof of Philosophy at Indiana U since 1981. Wrote 8 popular books on logic problems and puzzles..

name: Snader Jr, Craige M[cComb]
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 13 Jul 1929-16 Nov 1994) Taught at age 5 by amateur uncle Henry McComb Bush, a distant relative of Billy McComb. Moved to Mexico in 1960. Semi-pro mentalist 1978-83, thence full-time pro as "Alex Redans". Publisher of magic books (Exclusive Magical Publications) in Mexico City. Editor-publisher of Magic Sounds 1973-79. 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. Wrote Mind Square (1985, 84pp), The World's Smallest Magic Apparatus (1987, 14pp), & Contents and Index for pre-Epotica Writing 1976-1981 by Jeff Busby (1988). Articles in Hade-E-Gram, Linking Ring, Genii, MUM, Magicol, New Directions, etc. A word-smith, he coined the term "tape-respondence" by 1950 to mean correspondence by magnetic tape. [Wh2]

name: Sniadecki, Eugeniusz
bio: See: Fornalski, Jósef

name: Snipes, Felix E.
bio: (Jackson, Mississippi: 20 Dec 1933- ) Inspired at age 6 by school assembly magic show; learned from library books. Full-time mental, platform, & comedy magician in the Baptist ministry since 1981, based in Atlanta & touring the southern states. Articles in Magick. Collector (2,500 books). [Wh2]

name: Snowden, Alan, MIMC
bio: (London, England: 14 Dec 1920-) Inspired at age 14 seeing Dante in London. In RAF in WW II in India with photographic intelligence. Newspaper staff in London with Daily Sketch 1947-1961 & The Daily Telegraph 1961-1987 when he retired. Semi-pro close-up & mental magician since age 30. Pet effects: Book Tests, Salt Pour, etc. Editor of The Magic Circular 1973-1990. Articles in several magic & public magazines. MIMC 1976. Magic Circle Silver Wand 1976. [MC4/90;Wh2]

name: Snyder, Al.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-60s) Commercial artist in Charleston, West Virginia. Semi-pro magician since 1913 with 2-hour show in smaller towns of the mid-Atlantic states. Edited-published The Osirian 1925. Invented Sponge Balls to Square (c1935), according to Darwin.

name: Snyder [Jr], George
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Operated his "Snyder's Magic Shop" out of the Greyhound Bus Station in Cleveland, Ohio, in the 1940s. [Albo95] (Carthage, Ohio: 7 May 1888-13 Jun 1946) Semi-pro expert cardman, prop maker. Ran mail-order Snyder Magic Shop in Norwood, Ohio, since early 1930s, specializing in gaffed cards (which he named the "Fox Lake" line) & fine wood props. Bought fine prop collection of Louis Lavassor around late 1920s. Invented Psy-Key Lock (by 1936), Flip (by 1936), & Houdini Card (by 1944). IBM President 1939-41. Mentor of Don Alan. His widow sold his prop collection to John McManus. His business was absorbed in early 1950s by Ronald Haines. [Albo95]

name: Sobanski, Julie [Lynn]
bio: (Milwaukee, Wisconsin: 23 Jun 1969-) Bought first trick at age 16, started serious study at 18 when inspired by Copperfield. Semi-pro magicienne (children's magic & some close-up) & escape artist since age 18. 1988 Ben Berger Travelling Trophy 1st place for Escapes. Featured effect: Straitjacket Escape on roller skates. Tricks in Genii. [Wh5]

name: Socrate, [Philippe]
bio: (Pau, France: 1 Jan 1950-) Learned at age 8. Studied medicine. Pro stage magic & comedy close-up since 1982. 1982 FISM 1st prize in general magic. Wrote Lecture Notes (1982). Invented Spider Gimmick (first dispenser of invisible thread) in 1983. Articles in Genii, Budget, Revue de la Prestidigitation, & Mad Magic. 2 videos (1984, 1986), 1 video bit (1994). [Wh2]

name: Sokol, Anatoly Georgievich
bio: (Russia: 1907- ) Pro illusionist in Soviet Union with assistant-wife Rozalia Markovna Cadocha (born 1911). [Mec]

name: Sokolska, Nina
bio: (Ukraine, Russian Empire: 1898-) Stage name of Nina Veiningerova. Taught by a German magician. Pro stage magicienne, touring Europe in 1930s. [Dif]

name: Solari, Robert "Bob
bio: (Hackensack, New Jersey: 2 Jul 1961- ) Learned at age 5 from family friend. Bonded locksmith in Clifton, New Jersey. Non-performing inventor, manufacturer, & mail-order dealer in some 50 effects since 1986, including Hell Bent (1991). Trick in MUM. Videos (1993 & 1994). [Wh2]

name: Solimann
bio: (Orum, Jutland, Denmark: 1 Jun 1885-22 Oct 1947) Stage name of Wilhelm Frederik Feldvoss. Pro stage comedy magician with large full-evening show, including geese, doves, rabbits, & cats. With partner-wife Solimanné (see) was one of top acts touring Scandinavia 1920s-40s. Superb misdirection. Lived in Sweden since 1939. Father of "Solimann Junior". [Dif;St;Vo58]

name: Solimann Junior
bio: (Denmark: fl.c.1940s) Stage name of Gunnar Feldvoss, son of "Solimann" & "Solimanné". Pro.

name: Solimanné
bio: (Halden, Norway: 27 Sep 1895-2 Oct 1953) Stage name of Jenny Margrete Feldvoss. Wife of "Solimann" with whom she toured as a clairvoyant & moved to Sweden in 1939. Toured on own as magicienne 1948-49. Mother of "Solimann Junior". [Vo58]

name: Solomon, David “Dave
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Expert cardician in Chicago inner circle. Wrote Sessions (1983, 138pp, with Simon Aronson) and Solomon's Mind (1985, 18pp). Articles in Marlo's Magazine, Magic, Technomagic, & Trapdoor. Solomon, Harris A. (USA: 9 Apr 1905-1968) Psychologist, teacher, writer in Syracuse, New York. Amateur magician. Taught Tony Dunn 1952. IBM President 1960-61. Columns in Genii & Linking Ring, trick in HMM.

name: Solomon, Harry B[ernard]
bio: (New York City, NY: 19 Jan 1905-) Pro in vaudeville and club shows until at least 1940s. Aka "Bernard, the Devil's Friend". Trick in Sphinx. [WWM]

name: Soltau, Kurt
bio: (Germany: 8 Oct 1923-) Mail-order dealer in Annaberg/Buchholz, Germany, in 1980s-90s, with Dietmar Boettcher as partner since early 1990s.

name: Soma, Francisco
bio: (Naples, Italy: fl.1580s) Aristocrat. Amateur cardman. Performed & possibly invented General Card (by 1582). [Ch]

name: Somerdin, Jerry
bio: (New York City, NY: 6 Sep 1931-) Interested in magic since age 17. Teacher. Went semi-pro after age 28 with close-up & as inventor-manufacturer-dealer in Old Bethpage, New York. Pet effects: Floating Dollar Bill & $100 Bill Switch. [Wh2]

name: Somerfeld, Bob
bio: (USA: 1932-) Journalist. Amateur mentalist. Wrote The Mindreader's Digest (1951) & Pieces of Mind (1952). [St]

name: Somerfield, Signor T.
bio: (England?: fl.1850s-80s) Pro "Practical Magician, and Manufacturer of Conjuring Tricks and Apparatus, Worcester Street, Wolverhampton, England, and St. Andreasberg, Germany". Established 1855. Published a catalog in Wolverhampton ca1870. Wrote Modern Magic and Mystery Made Easy (1890).

name: Somers, Harris "Harry
bio: (USA: 11 Jul 1870-) Glassblower. Semi-pro magician of the old school. [St] Somerset, The Duke of, DSO, MIMC (Ceylon: 1 May 1882-26 Apr 1954) Born Evelyn Francis Edward Seymour. Amateur magician. President of The Magic Circle from 1935 until death in 1954. Tricks in Sphinx. [WWW]

name: Sommer, Wolfgang
bio: (Germany: 16 May 1944-) Semi-pro magician with partner as "Robby & Inge". 1984 MZvD 1st prize in general magic. Wrote Showy Magic. Articles in Magie. President of the MZvD 1990-present. [Nad]

name: Sondermeyer, Michael
bio: (Witten, Westfalia, W. Germany: 25 Sep 1952- ) Learned at age 7 from magic set. Pro childrens magician since 1977 as "Michael". Pet effect: Malini Egg Bag. Magic publisher ("sic!-Verlag") in Senden in 1990s. Wrote Zaubern mit Kindern im Vorschulalter (1978, 71pp), Das Joro-Buch (1993, with Uwe Schenk), & Zaubern für Kinder (with Uwe Schenk). Articles in Magische Welt, MUM, & Ginn's Fantasio Cane and Candle Book #5. [Wh5]

name: Songest, Joseph Edward "Eddie
bio: (London, England: 11 Feb 1904-) Semi-pro.[Go2]

name: Sońka, Złota Raczka
bio: (Poland?: 1891-dead) Stage name of Fedosja Karpowna Lyczkowa. Pro illusioniste. Worked circuses. [Mec]

name: Sonya & Romero
bio: See: Romero, Freddy

name: Soo, Chung Ling
bio: See: Robinson, William E.

name: Sonoda, Teruhide "Terry
bio: (Oita City, Oita, Japan: 20 Sep 1948-) Learned at age 10 from brother. Pro (ex-jugger) close-up magician. Demonstrator at a Tenyo shop for 8 years. Since c1982 a leading freelance magic illustrator in Japan, including Tenyo instructions since late 1970s. [Wh2] "Soprendo, The Great" SEE: Durham, Geoff

name: Sorcar
bio: (Tangail, Asokpur, India: 23 Feb 1913-6 Jan 1971) Stage name of Padmashree Pratul Chandra Sarcar, a Bengali. Pro illusionist. The most famous Indian magician of his time. Performed in Western costume until after John Booth's advice in 1948 adopted National dress. Sphinx Award 1948, 1949. Played the 1950 SAM-IBM Chicago Convention. Toured Europe (1952, 1955-56), USA (1957), Australia & New Zealand (1957), USSR (1962), & Japan (6 times 1937-70), where he died, his 2nd son flying in to complete the tour. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote History of Magic (1960, 133pp). Autobios are Sorcar on Magic: Reminiscences and Selected Tricks (1960, 288pp) & TW'sGM: The Great Sorcar (1966). Trick in Genii. A bio is Sorcar: Maharajah of Magic (1966, 100pp). [Pr;Ch;Bo;Bo#280;Fu;Dif;An; Genii2/56,3/66;HMM2/56,4/56,8/57]

name: Sorcar Jr
bio: (Tangail, Asokpur, India [now Bangladesh]: 31 Jul 1946- ) Stage name of Prodip Chandra "Johar" Sarcar. Second son of "Sorcar", who taught him since childhood. Pro illusionist since 1969. Pet effects: The Sawing, X-Ray Eyes, Vanishing Elephant, & Dwarfing a Clown. Tours his large illusion show to Japan (21 times), USA, Soviet Bloc (1985), Near East, Africa, etc. Invented Human Bomb Illusion (1969), Maxi Mini (1969), Dissolving Girl (1971), Stitching Girls (1984), The Living Portrait (1984), Jeep Jumbo (1984), etc. Wrote several books in his native Bengali, including Magic-Magic (1968), Chemical-Magic (1969), Magiker Galpo (1970), Psycho-Magic (1971), Cheating Faak (1975), Jadubidyar Bidya (1978), Mathemagic (1981), Sorcar's The Art of Sorcery (1982), & A Visit to the Land of Cards (1989). Articles in several Indian newspapers & magic journals. [Bo;Wh2]

name: Sorensen, Jerry
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 31 Jul 1927-) Of Danish parentage. Amateur. Tricks in Phoenix. [Th]

name: Sõrum, Björn
bio: (Norway: 18 Feb 1933-) Illusionist. Former chairman of Norwegian Magic Circle. Former co-editor of Magiens Verden. FISM judge 1979, etc. 1982 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic.

name: Soto Sunetaro
bio: (US: 1858 – New York City: 10 Feb 1910) Real name Wellington King Tobias. Pro stage magic. Toured USA with a pseudo Japanese act (1891-1907). Long believed to be Japanese but research by Mitsunobu Matsuyama published in Winter 2008 of Gibecière reveals otherwise. [St;Mo]

name: Sotova, Albina Sergievna
bio: (Moscow, USSR: 28 Feb 1933- ) She followed her mother into the circus where she was taught in the Moscow Circus School. Originally working as an equestrian, she became a circus illusionist in 1973. [Win2]

name: Southall, Gus[tave A.]
bio: (England: 1902-26 Sep 1971) Close-up. Expert cardman. 1961 FISM 1 $ ^{st} $ prize in closeup for a dice & poker chip routine. Tricks in HMM, Pentagram, Epoptica, etc.

name: Spadoni, Marion
bio: (Werder, Germany: 30 Mar 1905- ) Stage name of Marinka Krause. Daughter of acrobat Paul Krause-Spadoni. Pro stage illusionist. Rearranged the Palast Theater, a variety house, in East Berlin in 1945, renaming it the Friedrichstadt Palast in 1947. [Win]

name: Spalding, Jack
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Invented Silk through Cane.

name: Spangler, [C.] Bruce
bio: (Denver, Colorado: 31 May 1941-) Learned at age 5 from Xmas gift Gilbert magic set. Technical director with US West in Colorado. Semi-pro stage & cabaret magician since 1957 with assistant-wife Kathy. Also does mental magic & fire eating. Aka "Sigam" 1950-70. Collector. Invented Needle thru Arm in 1957 as "The Flesh Penetration" (first marketed in 1958, later as "You-Do Voodoo"), etc. [Wh2]

name: Spark, Prof
bio: See: Gresham, Jon

name: Spark, Ian Mclennan
bio: (Scotland: -May 1990) Semi-pro magician as "The Great McLennan", "McLennan and his Lovelies", & "Keith McGregor".

name: Sparks, H. G." [pen name]
bio: See: Johnson, George

name: Speaker, Theo
bio: See: "Yogi"

name: Speight, Derrick [Clifford], MIMC
bio: (Batley, Yorkshire, England: 2 Apr 1926-) Learned at age 14 from magic set & books. Senior personnel executive. Amateur comedy magician. Collector. MIMC 1976. Articles in Magic Circular & MUM. [Wh2]

name: Spence, Dolly
bio: (England: fl.1930s-40s) Niece of Will Goldston. Started in magic as child but became an aerialist. Moved to USA, returning to magic. Assistant to Jack Gwynne 1935-37 & Theo Hardeen 1937-45. Also performed solo. [SAM]

name: Spencer, Garrick M. "Spence
bio: (USA: -4 Aug 1942) Wealthy New York corporation lawyer and patron of the arts. Amateur magician, rated by Dai Vernon as skilled in sleight-of-hand. Took private lessons from Vernon to whom he gave the nickname "The Professor". In 1936 bankrolled the founding of the Academy of the Art of Magic, the formal association of the New York "Inner Circle" magicians. In return for this gesture, the other 11 members voted him a founding member of the group. He also financed Dai Vernon's famous Harlequin act in 1938.

name: Spencer, Horace
bio: (England: -1941) Brother of noted painter, Sir Stanley Spencer. Minor pro in Britain in 1920s-40s. Aka "Howard". An alcoholic, his work was mainly limited to busking in London saloon bars & Thames pleasure steamers. Drowned during a WW II blackout when he rode his bicycle into the Thames. [Fi]

name: Spencer, [Cynthia Dalton] "Cindy
bio: (Lynchburg, Virginia: 2 Aug 1959- ) Born Cynthia Dalton. Originally a diamond consultant in Lynchburg. Learned magic as assistant to Kevin Spencer c1981, thence with him as full-time pro since 1983 when they married. Wrote The Healing of Magic (1986, with Kevin). [Wh2]

name: Spencer, Kevin [Wayne]
bio: (Cannelton, Indiana: 15 Dec 1958-) Inspired by a TV magician at age 8. Learned from parents Xmas gift of magic set. Pro illusionist since 1983 when he married Cindy Dalton. They tour the Southwest & Midwest. Toured Australia & Mexico. Since 1984 have taken their "Healing of Magic" physical-mental therapy program to hospitals by teaching sleight-of-hand to neurologically damaged patients. Wrote The Healing of Magic (1986, with Cindy). Article in Magic Manuscript. Videos (1989). [LR8/98;Wh2]

name: Sperber, Burton S. "Burt
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 1929- ) At age 10 inspired by & learned from uncle Maury Leaf. Landscape contractor. Amateur mentalist. Pet effect: Out of This World. Published-edited Miracles of My Friends (1982, 161pp), one of the more elegantly printed & bound of all magic books. Articles in Magick. Publishes-edits A Real Miracle since 1992. Major collector of magic catalogs (1,200) & automata. [Wh2]

name: Sperling, Walter
bio: See: "Tagrey, H. W."

name: Spice, Robert
bio: (England: 26 May 1846-8 Apr 1920) Pupil of Robert-Houdin & associate of John Henry Pepper. Moved to USA in 1872. Professor of Chemistry at Cooper Union in New York City. Early SAM Treasurer.

name: Spicer, Dennis
bio: (England: -1964) Pro variety magician.

name: Spill, Steve
bio: (San Francisco, California: 3 Jan 1955-) Stage name of Steve Cory "Spill" Spillman after initially working under real name. Son of Sandy Spillman who taught him his first tricks in the early 1960s. Debut at age 13. Pro comedy close-up. As magic bartender worked the Jolly Jester in Aspen, Colorado, c1976-c1980. Partner with Bob Sheets as "Sheets & Spill" c1978-1984. Regular at Inn of Magic in Washington, DC, area 1981-84. Played Harrah's, Lake Tahoe, 1987-88. Has toured USA, Europe (1986), Canada, Africa, & the Caribbean. Wrote My Hands Can be Yours (1973, 79pp), Imagine Magic (1974), Spill Bar & Grill (1980), plus 3 cartoon booklets. Articles in Genii, Talisman, Magick, etc. 4 videos (1982, 1983, 1988, 1989). [Wh]

name: Spillman, Sanford [nmn] "Sandy
bio: (Kansas City, Missouri: 13 Oct 1916-1994) Inspired by Chandu the Magician radio serial. Former journalist, writer, & broadcaster. Pro mentalism & hypnotism since age 25, initially in San Francisco. An early TV magician. The Magic Castle's 2nd (following Ed "Carlisle" Fowler) Houdini Séance Room Resident Medium 1975-85 when retired to run a bed-and-breakfast place. AMA Board of Directors 1980-87. Father of Steve Spill. Wrote The Bunco Beat (1950) for Better Business Bureau. Articles in Magick, MUM, Seance, & Vibrations. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Spillman, Steve
bio: Spina, Anthony "Tony" [pronounced SPEE-nah] (New York City, NY: 5 Apr 1930-) Inspired seeing Cardini in 1944. Learned in 1945 at age 15 as protégé of Lou Tannen in whose shop he worked part-time as demonstrator & stock boy. Semi-pro magician (& auto dealer) since age 16 as "Spina, Mysteries of Modern Magic". Specialties: doves & illusions. Pro dealer (co-owner of Tannen's) in NYC since 1969 & sole owner since 1988. 1984 SAM Magician of the Year. Invented Astro-Sphere, etc. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, etc. [Bo#219;Se;Wh2]

name: Spina, Jennifer
bio: (Poplar Bluff, Missouri: 14 Oct 1947- ) Born Jennifer Ward. Originally a journalist. Learned magic in 1984 when she married Tony Spina. Edited Magic Manuscript 1985-87. Thence pro trade-show, corporate show, & former occasional cruise-ship work. Founder-owner of "Magic Communications" in NY City. Articles in Magic Manuscript. [Wh]

name: Spinetti, Signor
bio: (Britain: fl.1780s) Stage name, trading on that of the famous Pinetti, the skilled Italian magician who had played London in the Winter 1784-85 season. At Easter 1785 "Spinetti" was hired by Hughes to perform in London at the Royal Circus in the pantomime of The Talisman of Oresmanes. [Fr]

name: Spinoza
bio: (Tryggelev, Denmark: 31 Dec 1913- Stage name of Johannes Rønde Kristensen. Learned as child from popular articles on Dunninger & R. Dixie. Pro illusionist since 1932 with music-hall, cabaret, & mainly circus (with 4-5 assistants) throughout Scandinavia & Europe. Charter member of the Danish Magic Circle since 1934. Although he has "tried to slow down a bit", in 1989 toured "149 places in 165 days with circus in Finland". Avid collector of magic books, also trading & selling them. Lives in Copenhagen. Wrote 10 Minutter med 10 Fingre (1937, 12pp; repr 1950) & Spinoza's Tryllebog (1982, 96pp). [Win2; Dif; St; Wh5]
years: 31 Dec 1913- Stage name of Johannes Rønde Kristensen. Learned as child from popular articles on Dunninger & R. Dixie. Pro illusionist since 1932 with music-hall, cabaret, & mainly circus (with 4-5 assistants

name: Spitari, Laurance W.
bio: (England: -25 Sep 1936) Active by 1909 when lived in Southampton. Pro vent & magician as "Laurance Glen". Edited A.W.S. Magazine "Spill, Steve" 11-14 & The Wizard's Annual (newsletters of the Associated Wizards of the South) 1913-16. Wrote Pocket Book of Patter (c1919, as "Spitari"), The Magician's Road to Fame (1922, as "Glen") & The Humours of Entertaining (n.d., as "Spitari").

name: Spokane II, R. Sid
bio: See: Diaconis, Persi

name: Spoof, Will
bio: See: Upton, P. C. "Phil"

name: Spooner, William E[dward] "Bill", PhD
bio: (Wilmington, North Carolina: 15 Aug 1936-) Inspired at age 7 by uncle's tricks. Learned from Mysto Magic set. Science teacher in North Carolina. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 19. Pet effects: the Hoo coin & routines with cards, coins, & dice. A master of "double talk", having learned "X-jargon" from Wallace Lee. IBM President 1985-86. Wrote 6 booklets, including Here's 'Hoo' with Coins (1974, 12pp) & A Magical Spoonerism Lecture (1975; rev ed 1989, 14pp). Writing book on history of the Lota Bowl. Tricks & articles in MUM & Linking Ring, & in books by Poland and Mentzer. [LR7/85;Wh]

name: Spreer, [Johannes] Edmund
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 13 May 1902-8 Jun 1983) Precision mechanic in Berlin 1924-25. Then into pro magic as illusion builder to David "Fu-Manchú" Bamberg 1926-1946 & 1953. 1979 AMA Creative Fellowship. Died in Mexico City where he had lived since 1933. 1984 CMI Order of Magic Lamp (posthumous). Bio is Robert E. Olson, Illusion Builder to Fu Manchu (1986, 219pp), a valuable but error-ridden & often misleading book. [Bam; Genii8/83]

name: Springer, Jess L.
bio: (New Philadelphia, Ohio (or Pennsylvania?): 18 Apr 1882-11 May 1933) Semi-pro illusionist & mentalist in his hometown. [WWM]

name: Sprong, J. C. "Johnny
bio: (Colorado Springs, Colorado: fl.1920s-30s) Amateur card magician. A friend of Dai Vernon to whom he tipped Edwin Hood's disclosure that "S.W. Erdnase" was "E.S. Andrews" spelled backwards. Also gave Vernon his first lead to the Center Deal.

name: Squinters
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-40s) Stage name of Joe Barrow. Pro small-time theater & street magician. Pet effect: the Human Pump (a routine for the old Funnel trick) that he falsely claimed to have invented (by 1923). Con man (worked the "Groiney Bounce" game) in 1940s. [Abra#2320]

name: Squire, Edward Summers
bio: (USA: fl.1910s) Wrote Tricks and Magic Made Easy (1919, 188pp) (Cannanore, Kerala, India: 15 Jun 1948- ) Stage name of A.P. Sreenivasan. Inspired at age 7 seeing street magicians. Electrical engineer in Bombay 1971-74. Restauranteur (Blue Mountain Restaurant) in Ootacamund, South India, Sreenivas 1974-present. Semi-pro close-up, manipulative, & stage magician, working mainly restaurants & clubs. In 1986 married Anitha who sometimes assists on stage. Two one-man "Parades" in Aug 1989 & Nov 2003 Linking Ring. Wrote Card Circus (1996, 32pp). [LR11/2003;Wh2] St. NOTE: "St." as a abbreviation for "Saint" in such surnames as St. Onge & St. Roman is alphabetized here as if spelled "Saint".

name: Stadelman, Paul
bio: (Kentucky, USA: -1970) Pro magician (aka "Sandu") to pro ventriloquist. Column (as "Thor") in Thayer's Magical Bulletin in 1920s. In 1934 founded the Abbott Get-Togethers in Colon, Mich. Wrote Secrets of Sandu (1933, 22pp) & Sandu Writes Again (1934). Invented Polka Dot Paint (by 1953). [St]

name: Staff, Frank
bio: (London, England: 1877-25 May 1952) Semi-pro kid-show magician. Wrote Wait and See. Honorary Secretary, The Magic Circle, 1936-40. [Go2]

name: Stainer, Alan, MIMC
bio: (England: fl.1910s-20s) Resided in London. Pro. Played St. George's Hall in 1918 & 1925.

name: Stamm. Stephan
bio: (Germany: 13 Mar 1927-) Magician & collector of magic literature in Leverkusen, Germany. [Nad]

name: Stanek, Jerzy M[arek]
bio: (Tarnów, Poland: 20 Apr 1957- ) Learned in 1980 from a book. Teacher. Pro magician since 1989 with stage magic & card manipulation. Pet effect: card boomerang. 1989 Polish 3rd Prize in stage magic. Composed "Magic Song" for the 1985 FISM convention. Articles in Hokus Pokus. [Wh5]

name: Stanfield, [Charles Eugene] "Chuck
bio: (Indianapolis, Indiana: 3 Mar 1953-21 May 1991) Learned fire eating from Tom Ogden. Debut as fire eater in circus. Computer programmer. Semi-pro magician since 1976 with own show of magic, tumbling, juggling, & fire eating. Died of AIDS-related diseases. [Genii7/91]

name: Stanfield, John C.
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) Resident of East Point, Georgia. Invented Colorfusing Knife in 1939 and marketed it in 1952 when it won a Linking Ring award & became a best-seller. Wrote Nothing In My Hands (1954, 40pp). "Stanley, The Great" SEE: "Blackstone, Harry"

name: Stanley, Frank
bio: (England: fl.1910s) Pro. Played St. George's Hall in 1918.

name: Stanley, Gus
bio: (Utica, New York: 1881-16 Nov 1948) Stage name of Guy Stanley McKeown. Pro for some 45 years. [St]

name: Stanley, Harry
bio: (Britain: c1905-20 Sep 1991) Pro magician & dealer in London (Unique Magic Studio) from 1946 until he retired in 1970, Supreme acquiring his business. Edited Gen (Unique's house organ) 1946-58. Wrote I Wouldn't Want to Play Cards with You! (1974, 12pp) & Can You Hear Me Mother?: Sandy Powell's Lifetime of Music Hall (1975). Memoirs are 25 Years of Unique Magic (4 audiotapes). 1987 AMA Special Fellowship.

name: Stanley, Jack
bio: See: "Jaks, Dr"

name: Stanley, Thomas
bio: (England: fl.1550s) Pro. In 1554 performed before Queen Mary's Court. [CI]

name: Stanton, Noel [David]
bio: (London, England: 25 Dec 1937-) Learned in 1952 from a pitchman selling a gaffed 3-Card Trick. Civil servant with Patent Office in London. Semi-pro close-up magician since 1975, mainly at private parties. Pet effects: Cups-&-Balls & Aces-&-Tens. Invented "1,2,3,4,5" & published it in 1965 (and marketed by Alan Alan as "Countdown"). Tricks in Abra & Gen. [Wh2]

name: Stantone, Mlle. Helene
bio: See: Mercedes, Mrs. Joe

name: Stanwyck, Barbara
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 16 Jul 1907-20 Jan 1990) Stage name of Ruby Stevens since 1925 when she debuted as stage actress. Film debut in 1927 & a star since late 1930s. Amateur magician since early age, entertaining friends & guests. Tricks in Jinx #52. Bio is Al DiOrio, Barbara Stanwyck (1983). [Katz]

name: Stanyon, Prof. [William] Ellis
bio: (Husbands Bosworth, Leicestershire, England: 8? Jan 1870-2 Sep 1951) Inspired at age 12 seeing magician at school do the Die-thru-Hat, which Stanyon puzzled out & did. Learned c1883 reading Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Lessons from Hilliar. Taught Ross Conyears in 1889. Introduced Paper Folding as a stage act by 1895. Invented the Top-of-Pocket Dodge in 1903 (popularized by Henry Hardin in 1905) & adapted the plate lifter to (mental) magic in 1905. Pro magician, magic dealer, & magic teacher in West Hampstead, London, from 1895 until his death when his son Cyril Stanyon took over the business for a few years. Grandson Cliff E. Stanyon became an amateur magus. Wrote Conjuring for Amateurs (1897, 122pp), which was pirated in US repr as Herrmann's Conjuring for Amateurs (1902); & Conjuring with Cards (1898, 100pp), which was pirated US repr; authorized US repr as Card Tricks, 1901, 129pp). Both revised & reprinted as Magic (US: 1902, 244pp). Also wrote his 21 "Serials" booklets (1899-1910): #1 New Coin Tricks (1st Series) (1899), #2 A Bibliography of Conjuring & Kindred Arts (1899, 24pp), #3 New Coin Tricks (2nd Series) (1900), #4 New Handkerchief Tricks (1900), #5 New Card Tricks (1900, 24pp), #6 New Miscellaneous Tricks (1900), #7 New Juggling Tricks (1901, 24pp), #8 New Card Tricks (2nd Series) (1902), #9 Original Tricks of Clement de Lion (1902), #10 New Miscellaneous Tricks (2nd Series) (1903), #11 New Fire Tricks and Chemical Magic (1st Series) (1903), #12 Great Paper Tricks (1904), #13 Great Handcuff Tricks (1904, 16pp), #14 Great Silent Thought Transmission (1904), #15 New Billiard Ball Sleights (1904), #16 Original Explanatory Programmes (1907), #17 New Fire Tricks (2nd Series) (1907), #18 Fire and Chemical Magic (3rd Series) (1909), #19 New Handkerchief Tricks (2nd Series) (1909), #20 New Card Tricks (3rd Series) (1910), #21 New Card Tricks (4th Series) (1910). Later booklets included Remarkable Evolution of the Afghan Bands (1930). Published-edited Magic 1900-20 (177 issues; 2 facsimile reprints in 1996). [Daw94; Vo56; La2; Bur]

name: Starke, George
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-50s) City marshal and since 1951 a judge in New York City. Inspired in 1936 by Sam Horowitz show. Lessons from Horowitz. Thence an amateur magician. Invented "Hornswoggled" (1944). Edited Stars of Magic series 1945-52. Officiated at the weddings of Martin & Charlotte Gardner and Jay & Frances Marshall. Tricks in HMM. [Th]

name: Starr, Michael J.
bio: (USA: c1962-30 May 1995) Manager of "Hades' Seattle Magic Sentre" from around 1987 until his suicide by gunshot.

name: Stashower, Daniel
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 21 Sep 1960- ) Inspired at age 5 by his Knife-Swallowing uncle. Writer in Alexandria, Virginia. Semi-pro close-up & kid-show magician. A Houdini buff. Wrote 2 mystery novels, both featuring magic & magicians: The Adventure of the Ectoplasmic Man (1985), with Sherlock Holmes & Harry Houdini; & Elephants in the Distance (1989), about "Paul Galliard" & his attempt to do the Bullet Catch. Also Teller of Tales: The Life of Arthur Conan Doyle (1999, 472pp). [Wh2]

name: Stavio Della Carta
bio: (Gävle, Sweden: 5 Dec 1875-6 Feb 1927) Stage name of Gustaf [sic] Brynolf [sic] Lindborg. School headmaster. Skilled amateur cardman. Coined the Swedish word krakering for the riffle. Wrote Handbok i den högre salongsmagiens kortkonster (Stockholm: 1923, 163pp). Stebbins, Dr Robert A., PhD (Canada: 1938-) Professor of Sociology at the U of Calgary. Wrote The Magician: Career, Culture, and Social Psychology in a Variety Art (1984). Became an amateur magician c1982 as a direct result of the field research and interviews of magicians leading to that book. (Claremont, New Hampshire: 4 May 1867-12 Oct 1950) Stage name of William Henry Coffrin, aka Stebbins, Si "Wm. Vino". Pro circus "rube" & card manipulator. Invented the Si Stebbins System (1898). As "Wm. Vino" wrote Si Stebbins' Card Tricks (nd [before 1910], 20 leaves). Also wrote Si Stebbins Legacy to the Magicians (1935).

name: Steele, Jim
bio: (Guisborough, England: 22 Mar 1895-30 Jul 1988) Stage name of James Henry Smith, aka "Catch'im, the Original Conjurer". Semi-pro, inventor, & contributor to Magic Wand, Eric C. Lewis books, etc.

name: Steele, [William Francis] "Rufus
bio: (Janesville, Wisconsin: 1881-9 Sep 1955) By his own dubious accounts, a pro gambler, soldier (WW I), engineer, journalist, hotel clerk. Inspired & learned magic c1900 by private demo from Dr J.W. Elliott. Amateur magician. Voted into the New York "Inner Circle" by 1940. Died in Chicago. Authored several booklets, including Card Tricks You Will Do (1928), Card Tricks that are Easy to Learn (1935, 47pp), & 50 Tricks that You Can Do (1946, 63pp). His last 3 (all ghosted by Robert Parrish) were 52 Amazing Card Tricks [1949, 64pp], Paul Rosini's Magical Gems (1950, 68pp), & The Last Word on Cards (1950, 63pp). Trick in Tarbell #5. [Par;LR9/48,6/96]

name: Steen, Charles N.
bio: (USA: fl.1880s-1920s) Pro by 1888 with illusions, escapes, & second-sight act as "The Steens" (with 1st wife Martha until divorced in 1904 & 2nd wife Rose). Toured Australia (1893), Britain (1900 & 1914), & southern France (1929). [Pr;Wal;Magic10/1900] "Steens, The" SEE: Steen, Charles N.

name: Steens
bio: (Moutiers-Saint-Jean, Côte-d'Or, France: 27 May 1881-29 Nov 1939) Stage name of [Charles-Louis-] Fernand Brisbane. Pro manip until 1907 when switched to escapism. Toured France, Germany, Italy, Portugal (1907 & 1932), S. America, etc. [Dif;Vo55;Rob1]

name: Steens, Georgy-Pollmann
bio: See: "Pollmann-Steens, Georgy"

name: Steer, Frank
bio: (England: -1866) Pro dealer in London from 1818 until his death. His shop was willed to grandson Frank Hiam. [Daw94]

name: Steffensen, Conny
bio: (Denmark: 7 Dec 1917-) Engineer in Copenhagen. Amateur magician, aka "Cobe". Edited Djinn 1945-51. English translator of an Aage Darling book (1953). [St]

name: Stein, Jakoby
bio: See: Jacoby-Stein

name: Stein, Sol[omon]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 13 Oct 1926-) In 1942 at age 15 became youngest-ever IBM member. Demoed at Stuart Robson's 42nd Street magic shop 1942-43? Then in US military in WWII. Founding editor in 1943 of Blinking Ring, club newsletter of IBM Ring 26 (New York). Co-owner of Stein & Day Publishers 1962-1989, which among many titles published two on magic: Marvin Kaye's The Stein and Day Handbook of Magic (1973) & Kaye's The Stein and Day Handbook of Mental Magic (1975). Wrote 2 Broadway plays and several books, including a novel about a conjuror called The Magician (1971). [WWA; CA; Wh/1995; Hokuspokus (1993), 95] Zauberkunst Steiner, Robert A. "Bob", CPA, AIMC (Newark, New Jersey: 6 Mar 1934- ) Inspired at age 4 from a pick-a-card trick. Taught at age 7 by Jimmy Grippo. Accountant, public speaker, writer. Part-time pro magician since 1978, specializing in mentalism & bunco. Moved to California in 1979. Aka "Merlin" since 1981. A founding member of the Bay Area Skeptics in 1982. SAM President 1988-89. AIMC 1990. Wrote Don't Get Taken! Bunco and Bunkum Exposed (1989, 220pp). Articles in MUM, Skeptical Inquirer, etc. [MUM8/89;Wh2]

name: Steinhardt, Rudolph
bio: (Labore Volya, Hungary: 1886-) Amateur. Secretary-General of MAME 1929 to 1930s. [WWM]

name: Steinmeyer, [James Hahne] "Jim", AIMC
bio: (Oak Park, Illinois: 1 Nov 1958-) Learned in grade school from older brother Harry. Pro illusion designer, mainly to Doug Henning (since 1981). Also magic consultant to Orson Welles (5 years) & "Blacke's Magic" TV series (1986). Illusion designer for Copperfield, Blackstone Jr, Orson Welles, Paul Daniels, Siegfried & Roy, and The Pendragons. 1986 AMA Award of Merit. Designer & consultant for Disney since 1986. In 1989 co-produced a CBS-TV special & the British TV Channel 4 "The Secret Cabinet" mini-series". AIMC 1990. 1991 AMA Creative Fellowship. 1996 Christopher Award for illusion design. Prolific inventor of illusions (nearly 40 for Henning alone), including Magic Elevator (1976), Walking through a Mirror (1976), Miracle Levitation (1984), Backstage with a Cane Cabinet (1984), The Little Doll's House (1986), Pole Levitation (1986), Knot Unexpected (1986), & Interlude (1990). Edited Jarrett (1981, 185pp) & co-authored (with John Gaughan) Antonio Diavolo (1986, 24pp) & The Mystery of Psycho (1987, 64pp). Wrote Device & Illusion (1991, 134pp), Modern Art and other mysteries (1996, 48pp), Art & Artifice, and Other Essays on Illusion (192pp), The Mind and Magic of David Berglas, Scriptwriter for "Snoopy's World of Magic" touring show 1989. Writing a bio of Alan Wakeling Articles in New Invocation & Magic (column name The Conjuring Anthology.) [Wat;Wh2]

name: Stelzel, Christian [Michael]
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-10s) Pro illusionist. She worked the minor variety circuits in Britain 1904-13. (Mauthausen, Austria: 17 Jul 1945- ) Learned at age 13 from Hans Friedrich card trick book. Industrial designer & semi-pro magician until 1975 when went full-time. Generally bills himself as "Magic Christian". Specializes in manip, close-up, comedy, & TV illusions shows. Works industrial shows throughout Europe. Works with Piatnik Card Company developing & writing instructions for trick decks. President, Magischer Klub Wien, 1989-present. World lecture tour 1990-91. Many prizes including FISM 2nd prize in manip 1970; 1st prizes in manip 1973, 1976, 1979; & 1st prize in close-up invention 1979. Many inventions including Ketten-Zauber (1979) & Colorchanging Lighter. Articles in Genii, Magie, Apocalypse, Aladin, etc. Writing books on Graziadei & Stelzel's own original magic, & The Magic of Austria. [Wh2]

name: Stencel, Robert "Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Accountant in Rochester, Michigan. Inventive amateur card & coin close-up magician. Tricks in Pallbearers Review, Close-up Folio, Richard's Almanac.

name: Sténégry, Professeur
bio: (France: fl.1880s) Pro illusionist in Paris in 1887. [Rey]

name: Stengel, Karl
bio: (Zeutern/Baden, Germany: 18 Oct 1833-19 Oct 1895) Well-known pro in Germany, Scandinavia, France, & Switzerland. In 1875 named Court Conjuror by Kaiser Wilhelm I. Died wealthy in Wiesbaden. [Vo56;St]

name: Stenman, [Gustaf] Börje [pronounced BYUR-yeh STAYN-mahn]
bio: (Finland: 17 Apr 1920-17 Oct 1979) Bureaucrat in Helsinki. Amateur magician & magic historian. Co-founded (with Julius Sundman, etc) Taikapiiri magic club in 1945. Edited Simsalabim 1945-59.
