Wrote Hokus Pokus (1945), Litet Trollerilexikon: Biografiska, bibliografiska, terminologiska, historiska och andra fakta ur magiens värld (5 parts, Helsinki: 1952-53, 183pp), & Suomen Taikatemppukirjallisuus: Bibliography of Finnish Conjuring Works (Helsinki: 1957). [St;Dif]

name: Stenner, Robert Mason
bio: (Lakeland, Florida: 1924-2 Feb 1998) Inspired at age 10 seeing Thurston show, he learned from a Mysto Deluxe Magic Set. Pro magician, puppeteer, & vent since age 15 as "Larry Latz" 1939-45 & "Bob Mason" since 1945. Specialized in mental magic. Worked as actor in Hollywood movies & TV (mainly Westerns) since 1943. Assistant & understudy to John Calvert in 1944, partner with Leon & Velvet Mandrake in early 1950s, assistant to Kirk Kirkham in 1960s. In late 1960s played school assemblies with both a puppet & vent act for elementary schools & mindreading act for upper grades. Invented O-2-Matica Deck. Wrote (as "Bob Mason") Sensational Question & Answer Act (1981, 23pp). Articles in Tops. [Wh2]

name: Stéphane
bio: See: Pérot, Auguste

name: Stephens, Warren [Lee]
bio: (Lansing, Michigan: 12 [sic] Dec 1931-4 Apr 2006) Inspired in 1941 by a magician at picnic. Graduated MSU with a BA in Ed. 1957. High school teacher (retired). Semi-pro to pro magician with close-up, comedy magic, & MC work. Since 1950s has lectured in North American & Western Europe. Proprietor of Stephens Magic Mfg in Roseville, Michigan, since 1950s. Invented over 300 tricks, moves, & bits, marketing over 50, including Splendo (at age 12), Oh Wee Gee, Kangaroo Silk, Lots A Knots, Dovenette, Thru-Ball, Bang-Poof, Di-Mini-Fish, Alley Oops, Wobble Wand, Wilting Flower, Wilting Bouquet, Astro Links, & Silly Spots. Wrote 8 sets of lecture notes. Articles in Linking Ring, MUM, Magigram, Precursor, Tops, Apocalypse, Pentagram, etc. 2 videos (1988). [LR3/2003;Wh2]

name: Steranko, James "Jim
bio: (Reading, Pennsylvania: 5 Nov 1938 - ) At age 9 learned back-palming & one-hand cuts from father. Commercial artist, cartoonist, editor, & semi-pro rock musician. Former amateur escapist & innovative cardman. Wrote Steranko on Cards (1960, 102pp), & the rare, possibly unique, unpublished manuscript, The Ultimate Move (1962), which was ripped off by Marlo. Contributed an extended (52-page) piece on escapism to a 1963 Genii issue. Left magic in early 1960s, in justified disgust over the rip-offs of his inventions, particularly by Ed Marlo. At first he turned to music; then, in 1965 he became a sci-fi illustrator, gaining great fame in that field. Autobio is Steranko: Graphic Prince of Darkness (1998, 32pp). [Genii11/62; Genii10/64; Wat]

name: Sterling, F. B.
bio: See: "Mahendra, M. S. `Doc'"

name: Sterling, Harold
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-50s) Stage name of Harold E. Fackler, aka "Thelmo" as pen name. Pro magician (including 7 years with the Redpath Bureau and school assembly bureaus with wife Gloria) to bread salesman to magic dealer (Sterling Magic Co.) in Detroit c1939-c1954 when sold to Gene DeVoe. Invented Short and Long Rope (by 1939), Production Moderne (by 1940), Sterling Egg Bag (by 1941), & Miko (in early 1940s). Wrote (as "Thelmo") First Book of Magic (1929) & (as "Sterling") Fifty Tricks with a Bottomless Tumbler (1949).

name: Sterling, Max
bio: (Britain: 1870-18 Nov 1941) Stage name of John George Englehart MacLachlan. Pro music-hall magician. Famous for his "The Magic of Japan" act (by 1906). Played St. George's Hall in 1907. Edited The Magical World 1910-14 & Servais LeRoy's Magical Monthly 1911-13. Wrote Stillwell's Handkerchief Manipulation Act (1902, 16pp) & Problems in Mystery for Practical Magicians (1909, 56pp). [Vo56; Magic6/06]

name: Stern, [Maxwell P.] "Duke
bio: (Bangor, Maine: 21 Feb 1944-) Learned first magic in 1954. Served as Army medic in Vietnam 1968. Full-time pro close-up & trade show magician since 1969, playing China, Africa, & France. [Wat;Wh2] (Trenton, New Jersey: 6 Oct 1913-29 Jul 1973) Son of English immigrants. Taught by father, a pro magician. Pro manager of magic shops: Abbott's in Indianapolis, Paul Diamond's in Ft. Lauderdale, Harris Magic in Atlanta, his own shop, & finally with Abbott's in Colon as their main convention rep. Taught Bob Bluemle, etc. A top-rated demonstrator. Invented the Four-to-Two Rope Trick (by 1945). Wrote Latest Thimble Magic (by 1947, 21pp). Recorded Abracadabra Is My Game (1973), a 33-rpm record for kids. Bio in Karrell Fox, Abra-K-Fox. [Des]

name: Stevenard, H.
bio: (France: fl.1840s) Mechanic & showman. Made & exhibited a clever range of automata, including the "Prestidigitateur" & the "Magicien", which he showed in Paris in 1843. NOTE: Misspelled "Stenevard". [Dif]

name: Stevens, Amy [Jo]
bio: (Wichita, Kansas: 20 Jun 1960- ) Daughter of Joe & Martha Stevens. Began as assistant in father's act since age 2. Aka "Candide". Then, after her BA in Journalism (1982) & a brief stint in TV promo, to Stevens Magic Emporium as producer of its Greater Magic Video Library series since 1984. Also an MA in Communications (1987). Articles in Genii (since 1987) & Magic (1991). [Wh2] Stevens, Chandler A. (Portland, Oregon: 10 Sep 1916-) Learned magic in 1926. Personnel director in Salem, Oregon. Semi-pro magician as "Chandler the Magician". Pet effects: Aga Floating Lady & Needle Threading. Former President PCAM. Articles in Bat. [Genii7/50;Wh2]

name: Stevens, Joe J.
bio: (Wichita, Kansas: 26 Apr 1936 [sic]- ) Inspired at age 10 seeing Blackstone. Pro dealer (ex-Fuller Brush manager) since 1975 as co-founder (with wife Martha) of Stevens Magic Emporium in Wichita, Kansas. Specialty: mentalism. Pet effect: Slydini's Silk in Apple. Founder-producer of the annual Desert Magic Seminar in Las Vegas 1977-present. 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. 1985 AMA Award of Merit. Article in Genii. Father of Amy Stevens. [LR6/94;Wat;Wh2]

name: Stevenson, Al[wyn]
bio: (USA: -1963) New York magician-dealer (The Wizard's Shop in the 42 $ ^{nd} $ Street Subway Arcade). Invented the Deck on the Ceiling (1958) & Blanka Deck (1959). Invented the process for making spongeballs by machine, later adopted by Goshman. Wrote 75 Tricks with a Stripper Deck (1957, 48pp;  $ 2^{nd} $ ed rev, 1962, 40pp) & 75 Tricks with a Svengali Deck (1964, 40pp). Many tricks in Hugard's MM, [MUM/6/01]

name: Stevenson, Barry
bio: (England: c1933-) Learned as child from father's Xmas gift of magic set. Policeman. Amateur magician. Invented Poppit Bead Trick (1955). Tricks in Tarbell #7, etc. [Lo2]

name: Stevenson, Donald
bio: (Britain: fl.1900s-50s) Aka "Martin Mayhew" around 1908. Engineer by profession. Semi-promagician.

name: Stevenson, James H. "Jim
bio: (USA: 24 Nov 1867-2 Feb 1934) Long with a business house in New York City. Semi-pro doing private local shows. Joined the SAM in 1902 as Member #8. Moved to South America to work there with his twin brother.

name: Stewart, James [Maitland] "Jimmy" "Jim
bio: (Indiana, Pennsylvania: 20 May 1908-2 Jun 1997) Learned while at high school together with friend Bill Neff in 1923 from a magic book; and, with coaching from Jack Gwynne, they turned semi-pro magicians, working church & other local shows with Stewart as assistant to Neff. Stickland, William G. "Bill", MBE On Gwynne's advice Stewart took to acting. Broadway stage debut in 1932 & Hollywood film debut in 1935, becoming a star actor with Mr Smith Goes to Washington in 1939, the year he joined the IBM. In Aug 1940 did a one-shot burlesque magic act with Henry Fonda in Houston for the British war effort. In Sep 1941 did a one-shot Allied Relief Fund benefit magic act in hometown with Neff. Pet effect: Dead Man's Hand. Best bio is Donald Dewey, James Stewart (1996, 512pp). [HMM7/56;Jinx#57;Fu2;Katz;WWA] (Dorset, England: 12 Oct 1902-25 May 1984) Real estate agent. Semi-pro magician plus vent, marionettes, & shadowgraphs. Aka "The Wessex Wizard" & "Marius & Mariette" (with wife as assistant). Secretary, The British Ring, 1932-84. British Ring Past President. Wrote Wessex Wizardry (1931), It (1936), Join the Party (1947, 72pp, with Eric P. Wilson), & Introducing Bill's Magic (1970, 273pp). IBM President 1971-72, the first Briton to hold that office. IBM Medallion of Honor. Awarded the MBE in 1978 for services to magic. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Strickland". [WWM]

name: Stiles, Harry
bio: See: "Marvello, Harry"

name: Stiles, Kirk LeRow
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-70s) Cartoonist in Florida. Semi-pro magician. Edited Magic and Spells Quarterly 1970-72. Wrote Thimbles with a Light Touch (1971, 33pp). Tricks in Swami (1973) & Mantra (1974-75).

name: Stillwell, George
bio: (USA: -1934) Pro sleight-of-hand. Invented the handkerchief ball (ca1895). Toured the world with his famous handkerchief act in 1896. Played South Africa in 1903. See Max Sterling, Stillwell's Handkerchief Manipulation Act (1902, 16pp). [Wal;Magic6/03]

name: Stilwell, Carl J.
bio: (USA: fl.1910s-20s) Pro sleight-of-hand, mainly with the Chautauqua circuit. [Dor]

name: Stilwell, [William Michael] "Mike
bio: (Annapolis, Maryland: 19 Sep 1953- ) Aka "Magic Mike" & "Bumper". Inspired on 10th & 12th birthday parties by travelling magician Bill Smith Jr. Learned in 1963 from library books: Fitzkee's Showmanship for Magicians, Hay's Cyclopedia of Magic, & Thurston's 400 Fascinating Magic Tricks You Can Do. Debut at age c15. Semi-pro since 1971, particularly as magic bartender at J.C. Wagner's Magic Lounge in San Diego 1975-79. Since 1984 full-time pro close-up restaurant table-hopper, working the Corvette Diner 1987-2002. Bought Bumper & Son magic factory in San Diego from his uncle, Ted "Suds" Sudbrack, in 1984, changing its name to Bumper & Company. [Wh]

name: Stock [Jr], George W.
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: fl.1890s-1920s) Son of ex-pro European magician. Pro. [Dor]

name: Stodare, Colonel
bio: (Liverpool, England: 28 Jun 1831 [or possibly 1832]-22 Oct 1866) Stage name of Joseph Stoddart, older brother of Alfred "Stodare" Stoddart. Pro in the provinces by 1859 until Apr 1865 when he began his stay at Egyptian Hall, London, where he introduced Tobin's sensational Sphinx illusion on Oct 16th. Died in London of TB, after which Madame Stodare continued his act at Egyptian Hall 1866-67. Invented Stodare Egg (mid-1860s) and invented or popularized Kling-Klang (mid-1860s). Wrote The Art of Magic (1865, 32pp), A New Handy-Book of Magic (1865, 26pp), & Fly-Notes (1865, 126pp; repr 1867), which reprinted several articles from Routledge's Every Boy's Annual. See E. Dawes in New Pentagram (Jul 1988), 39-41; & Edwin Dawes, Stodare: The Enigma Variations (278pp). . NOTE: His name was long believed to be John Alfred 'Jack' Inglis (or English) until Dawes published the facts in 1988. [Daw;Cl;Magic9/01;La;Vo56]

name: Stodare, Alfred
bio: (England: fl.1850s-60s) Stage name of Alfred Stoddart since the death in 1866 of his famous older brother, "Col. Joseph Stodare". Previously (by 1859) as "Alfred Inglis" worked provincial theaters, including Dublin (1859), as a pro magician-ventriloquist. REF: E. Dawes in New Pentagram (Jul 1988), 39-41.

name: Stoddard, Ed[ward]
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Specialized in mental magic. Invented Mental Miracle (1950), Perfected Sealed Message Reading (1951), Intuition (1951), the “Brainstorm Book Test”, & The Seventh Sense (1952). Trick in HMM (1950). Wrote The First Book of Magic (1953, 69pp).

name: Stolina, Otto
bio: (Oelde, Westfalen, Germany: 17 Nov 1901-4 Feb 1993) Pro dealer ("Stolina Magie") in Oelde from after WW II until 1976 when Robert Fislage took over. Wrote Schule der Zaubertricks (1951, 112pp). [Roh]

name: Stone, Ben [Davis]
bio: (Texarkana, Texas: 26 May 1921-11 Jun 2001) Amateur. US Postal inspector until retired in 1971. Inventor: Delben Two Hole Wrist Chopper (1949), Delben Rope Gimmick, etc. Semi-pro manufacturer with wife-partner Del Stone as DelBen Magic Manufacturing in Springfield, Missouri. In mid-1980s partnered with Joe Stevens of Wichita and Ed Tambarello of Houston to manufacture metal props as "Mid-America". Then sold DelBen Magic Manufacturing to Danny & Darlene Gurganus of Danny's Kix and Trix in Spring, Texas. Then Ben & Del opened "Mr. E's Magic" as retail shop in Springfield, Missouri. [L R11/01]

name: Stone, Capt. Joseph E., MC
bio: (Birmingham, England: 29 May 1888-) Amateur. Wrote Tricky Tricks & Telling Talk (1934, 64pp). [Go2]

name: Stone, Paul
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s). Pro dealer, having bought the Ken Brooke Magic Place in 1982, and opened next year in Blackpool as Ace Place. Closed c1990.

name: Stone Sr, Dr Raymond V., MD
bio: (USA: 17 Apr 1892-) Inspired seeing A. Herrmann in 1906. Amateur magician in Alhambra, California. Debut in 1909-11 as "Ramo, the Boy Magician". Then switched to the medical profession. Tricks in Genii. [Th]

name: Stone, Dr Solomon "Sol", PhD
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 24 Nov 1922- ) Inspired at age 7 seeing Thurston show. Learned at age 13 from birthday gift of Hoffmann's Modern Magic. Clinical psychologist. Semi-pro close-up magician 1937-57; amateur since 1957. Wrote Patter Punches (1947, 35pp). Many original tricks & routines in Hugard's Magic Monthly, Apocalypse, & Magic Manuscript plus in books by Lorayne, Kaufman, Gardner, & Minch. [Lo2;Wh2]

name: Stone, Tom
bio: See: Bengtsson, Thomas

name: Stoner, [Richard Lee] "Dick
bio: (Fort Wayne, Indiana: 4 Apr 1930-) Pro since 1948 (age 18) when he learned at age 18 from amateur father. Does comedy magic at trade shows. President, Stoner Magic & Costume Company since 1949, with retail shops in Fort Wayne & South Bend, Indiana. 4 videos (1990-92). [Wh2]

name: Stork, [Henry] "Harry" N.
bio: (Rochester, New York: 19 Apr 1863-2 Mar 1907) Mechanic. Magic dealer (Stork Magic Shop) in Detroit since 1882. Long-time assistant to Kellar. Invented the "large" ring for Linking Rings (c1893) and possibly Vanity Fair (by 1894). Left magic for business in Rochester in 1900. Died of spinal meningitis. [Magic10/02; CMM4/07]

name: Stout. Gilbert
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Magic dealer-manufacturer (as Gilbert Stout) in London by 1904 to at least 1908. Issued 5 catalogs. Wrote Conjuring for Conjurers (1907, 16pp [or 24pp], with Charles Dratton). One trick in Magic (Feb 1906).

name: Stover, Mel[ville Edward]
bio: (Winnipeg, Canada: a Tuesday in May 1912-27 Mar 1999) Learned at age 10 from Book of Knowledge. University technician. Amateur magician, specializing in close-up & mathematic. Invented Color Changing Pencil (1953) & Jig Saw for Tots (1979). Articles in Tops, Linking Ring, Phoenix, New Phoenix, Ibidem, Chaos, Precursor, Genii, Magic Cauldron, etc. Also as "Rev. O.T. Slem" in Fork Full of Appetizers II. [Wh2]

name: Strack, Lucas [or Ludwig]
bio: (Ebsdorf [now Ebsdorfergrund], Germany: 23 Apr 1861-17 [or 18] Nov 1930) In early years with Ernst Basch as music director, gradually switching to magic. Then beginning in 1885 on own as pro illusionist, first as "L. Bellachini", then as "Der Marburger Bellachini", & "Bellachini-Strack". A publicity brochure is Joachim Bellachini, Moderne Magie: Hofkünstler L. Bellachini [c1900, 16pp]. [Vo56;St;Win;Dif]

name: Strange, [Thomas] Glenn
bio: (Spartanburg, South Carolina: 19 Apr 1947-) Learned in 1980 from co-worker. Machine designer for American Hoechst in his home state. Semi-pro comedy magician since 1981, working mainly business, school, & church groups. 2 local prizes for close-up. Pet effects: Sponge Balls, Bill-to-Wallet, & Professor's Nightmare. Wrote Do-It-Yourself Lecture and Coloring Book (1987, 39pp). Tricks in Trapdoor & MUM. [Wh2]

name: Strange, Doctor Jonathan
bio: See: Cooke, Jonathan E. "Ted"

name: Straussborg, Dr. Frederick
bio: See: Larsen, William W.

name: Strick, Teddy" [misspelling]
bio: See: Strik, Teddy

name: Strickland" [misspelling]
bio: See: Stickland

name: Stride, Richard J[oseph]
bio: (Biddeford, Maine: 15 Jul 1927- ) Learned simple tricks at age c4 from father. In real estate development in home state. Semi-pro magician since age 14, specialized in close-up, platform, & mental magic. Wrote several booklets since 1981, including Pseudo-Psychic's Guide to ESPPeri-Mentalism (1987, 35pp) & A Charlatan's Guide to One-(& More-) Upmanship (1990, 24pp). Invented RandoMental (1973), IncrediMental Books (1982), Pseudo-Psychic's Off-Center Tear (1989), Piatt-Stride Two-Way Wallet (1989, with Ray Piatt), etc. Tricks in MUM & Magick. [MUM2/92;Wh2]

name: Strik, Teddy
bio: (Lyon, France: 8 Oct 1899-4 Feb 1950) Stage name of Georges Amard. Aka "Teddy-Strik". Pro illusionist, touring France, Europe, & Scandinavia often as circus magician. NOTE: Surname misspelled "Strick". [Vo55;St]

name: Strong, Wes[ley Milo]
bio: (Mitchell, S. Dakota: 23 Aug 1911-26 Sep 1998) Amateur magus since college. BA degree in chemistry. Postal Service worker. In 1976 bought "Weller Magic" from Charles Weller's widow, continuing that famous line of collapsible latex props in Sun City West, Arizona. [Wh]

name: Strout [Jr], [Sewall] Cushing "Cush
bio: (Portland, Maine: 19 Apr 1923- ) Learned in teens as apprentice to Ernest A. Carter & reading books. Semi-pro close-up in high school, college, & army. History teacher at Williams, Yale, & Caltech until 1964 when became Professor of American Studies at Cornell U (now emeritus) & amateur magician. Articles in Genii, Pallbearers Review, Epoptica, Club 71, & New Tops. [Wh2]

name: Stuart, Donald B.
bio: (New Zealand or London: 1894-) Moved to Australia as a child. Pro comedy magician in music halls. Moved to Britain where he often appeared as "Abanazar". Toured Australia in 1927. Very tall (6'7"). [Hudd;Wal]

name: Stuart, J[ohn] Marberger "Jack
bio: (New York City, NY: 3 Apr 1927-2 Jan 1993) Senior partner in a "Wall Street" law firm. Semi-pro magician since 1950. Also actor & playwrite. His 1969 off-Broadway production, Make Me Disappear, was first play to feature a Vanishing Elephant. Founder & Chairman of Dragon Award Committee 1983-present. Wrote (with wife Marjorie L. Stuart) You Don't Have to Slay a Dragon (1975, 313pp), a comic novel & (with separate 7-page instruction booklet, Mentalist's Dream) a mentalists force-book. 1988 FISM jury. Chairman of Milbourne Christopher Foundation Award Committee since 1989. 1991 AIMC. SAM Hall of Fame 1994. Invented several illusions, including Rocket to Mars (1958). Wrote Stuart on Illusions (forthcoming 1989). Articles in Hugard's Magic Monthly, Genii, & Linking Ring. Column in MUM. REF: Who's Who in World. NOTE: Middle name often misspelled "Marburger". [Wh2]

name: Stuart, James "Jimmy
bio: (Birkenhead, England: 1865-7 May 1901) Pro society magician, specialized in sleight-of-hand. Turned to music halls in 1892. While playing the Egyptian Hall in 1893 his health failed and Maskelyne replaced him with David Devant, thus beginning the 21-year long Maskelyne-Devant association. Died of pneumonia. [Magic3/02;Vo56;St;Cl]

name: Stuart, Marjorie L[ouise]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 7 Jan 1926-31 Jan 2005) Born Marjorie Louise Browne. Artist, engineering librarian, author in New York City. In 1954 married J. Marberger Stuart who taught her magic. They co-authored their 1969 off-Broadway magic play Make Me Disappear and co-wrote & illustrated their novel-cum-forcing book, You Don't Have to Slay a Dragon (1975, 313pp). Has designed or invented several stage illusions & tricks, thus making her the first & only female "back room boy" in magic of whom I am aware. REF: Jane's Who's Who in Aviation and Aerospace. [Wh2]

name: Stull, Robert [Judson] "Bob
bio: (San Jose, California: 23 Jan 1893-2 Jul 1981) BS in electrical engineering. Semi-pro magic dealer in San Francisco, first (with partner Jerry Arends & soon Tom Dethlefsen) as San Francisco Magic Studio in Jan 1941 at 583 Market Street, then independently in 1944 [sic] as Stull Magic Manufacturing Co. at 583 Market Street, later (1945) 341 Market St. Invented Stull Watch. By 1948 moved to New London, Connecticut, to build (with Alston Rogers) the radar for the Navy's land-based submarine trainer. 1979 AMA Creative Fellowship. Claimed to have coined the word "broadcasting" for radio. Tricks in Genii & HMM. [Albo95;HMM12/48] (Gröbersdorf, N. Silesia, Germany [now Poland]: 2 May 1885-4 Jan 1962) Stage name of Josef Stuller. Pro. After military service in WW I moved Stuller-Bosco, José to Danzig where he opened "Werkstätten für Magische Kunst", a magic factory & publishing house that published 14 booklets by H.W. Tagrey 1923-26. Joined Magischer Zirkel 1920. Published Das Magische Echo magazine in 1924. Toured Germany. Wrote as "José Stuller" Magische Novitäten (1928, 43pp). After WW II moved to West Germany where he opened a new magic factory in Northeim-Hannover. [St]

name: Stumpf, Dr Hans Gerhard
bio: (Pössneck, Germany: 23 10 1926-) Founding editor of Zauberkunst in Saalfeld, East Germany, in 1956.

name: Stursa, Anton "Toni
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 18 [or 20] Mar 1902-19 Mar 1965) Artist & illustrator. Amateur magician. Invented or improved many tricks. Major illustrator of magic books (for Fischer, Trunk, & Allan) & articles (for Magie). Designed playing cards for Piatnik company in Vienna where he died.

name: Stuthard, Joe
bio: (Canada: 16 Sep 1911-27 Apr 1992) Aka "The Canadian Funatic". Learned in the 1930s from books (including Erdnase) & working carnivals, fairs, & streets. Invented Trilby Deck (1949) & Stinger Kliptrik monte trick (1950). Wrote Svengali Subtleties (1948, 19pp) & Stooging Around (1949, 34pp). Moved to Britain. In 1953 co-founded (with Harry Baron) The Kaymar Magic Company in Billericay, Essex County, England, where he worked briefly. Moved back to Canada & then around 1956 on to Australia where he ran a travelling magic pitch stand in Sydney for several years until retired, leaving the business to Rod Junor. [McC]

name: Styles, John [Robert], MIMC
bio: (Walthamstow, London, England: 28 Sep 1934-) Inspired seeing local stage magicians in 1946. Pro kid-show & close-up magician, vent, and Punch & Judy worker. Pet effect: Coin in Bottle. Bought the late Oscar Oswald's "Magical Mart" in 1976, running it as a mail order business from his house in Sidcup, Kent. Magic adviser for films Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom (1984), Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989), & Bullseye (1990). Articles in Magical Digest & Magigram. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Stysínski, Marek
bio: (Czestochowa, Poland: 1943-) Pro manipulator. [Mec]

name: Suavet, Robert
bio: (France: fl.1960s-90s) Semi-pro with stage magic, close-up, & rag pictures as "Rob Suvac". Charter member of the Club des Magiciens de la Haute-Savoie in 1965. In 1980 co-founded Le Cenacle Magique 5. 1985 French 1st prize in allied arts. [Mer]

name: Suey, Richard
bio: (Peru: fl.1950s) Stage name of Ricardo Sueyras. Pro magician in nightclubs & cabarets throughout South America. Toured Portugal with his Chilean assistant-wife Maria Haydee Weller in 1959. [Cam]

name: Sugár, Péter
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 19 Aug 1948-) Self-taught in 1964. Pro close-up & stage magician (and artist) since 1975. Aka "Peters". Specializes in cards, silks, and Cups-&-Balls. Articles in Hungarian magazines. [Wh2]

name: Sugawara, Shigeru
bio: (Kamaishi, Japan: 29 Aug 1949- ) Learned at age 12 from magic book. Pro with Tenyo Company 1965-present, where he has been a major inventor since 1969, mainly with See thru Card (1976), Squeeze Play (1977), & Black Hole (by 1993). His engineering skills have made many inventions by other Tenyo inventors practical. 1977 Tenkai Prize. See Hiroshi Kondo, Sugawara Shigeru Sakuhin-shu [Shigeru Sugawara's Creative Works in Magic] (Tokyo: 1978). [Wh2]

name: Sugden, Raymond S[tanley]
bio: (Lawrenceville, Pennsylvania: 2 [or 7?] Nov 1888-20 Jul 1939) Pro by 1918, performing as "England's Court Magician". Headed Thurston's 3nd unit 1926-30 as "Tampa", mainly touring the Southern states. Notably unsuccessful, he retired from magic to become a radio broadcaster in Pittsburgh. [Pr]

name: Suhr, H. F. C.
bio: (Germany: -30 Nov 1915) Pro in Hamburg. One of 9 co-founders of the Magischer Zirkel (Hamburg), the later MZvD. Wrote 11 books in German, including Zauber-Soirée (1894, 94pp); Jedermann Zauberkünstler! (1899, 162pp), on St. Roman); and Das grosse Buch der Zauberkunst (1903, 222pp). In late 1897 edited & published the short-lived monthly Der Zauberkünstler: Monatsschrift für Salon-Magie. [St]

name: Sukurov, Sultangali
bio: (USSR: fl.1970s-80s) Pro stage magician. With partner Sara Kubikuzena won 1978 Karlovy Vary Grand Prix & 1979 FISM Grand Prix.

name: Sulamith
bio: See: Auzinger, Leopoldine

name: Sullivan
bio: (USA: fl.1820s) Of Irish parents. Pro in Britain around 1820s. [Fr]

name: Sun, Wong Toy
bio: See: Guest, Claud

name: Sundman, Julius
bio: (Finland: 23 Dec 1917-1986) Pro magician as "Julius Leoni" in cabaret, etc. In WW II with Finnish Army Special Services entertaining troops. Afterwards in music halls & circus, touring Sweden, Ireland, Portugal (1949 & 1957), and USA (1953 & 1958). 1st President of the main Finnish magic society, Taikapiiri, 1945-1960 when moved to USA with assistant-wife Nadja. Wrote Taikatemppuharrastelijan käsikirja (1939, as "Julius Leoni"), Korsutaikuri (1942), Hauskoja Taikatemppuja (1944; 2nd ed 1945), Taitava Taikuri (1950), & Suuri Taikuri-kirja (1959, 264pp), all in Finnish. [St;Dif;Tay]

name: Sunell, August
bio: (Finland: 13 Sep 1885-declared legally dead 1 Jan 1976) Around 1908 with younger brother Uno Sunell taken by their parents to USA where they soon developed their Houdini-type magic & escape act. Pro. The brothers returned to Finland in 1910 where they briefly operated the Cirkus Bröderna Sunell. August returned alone to USA c1913. [St;Dif]

name: Sunell, Uno
bio: (Finland: 22 Feb 1888-9 Mar 1935) Younger brother of August Sunell with whom he moved to USA c1908. Pro magician & escapist. Returned to Finland in 1910 where, falling ill, was replaced in their act by Harry Harries in 1912. Later worked single in circus throughout Scandinavia, including Sweden 1913-18. Died in Helsinki. [St;Dif;Vo58]

name: Sunetaro
bio: See: Soto, Sunetaro

name: Sungur, Zati
bio: (Bursa, Turkey: 10 Mar 1898-6 Jul 1984) Inspired by & learned magic in Germany after WW I. Pro illusionist since 1920. Toured Europe & S. America as "Zati Bey", "Sati Richmond", and "Conde Sati von Richmond" from mid-1920s to 1936 when returned to Turkey where he took the legal name of Zati Sungur & soon became its most celebrated magician. Introduced the Thin Sawing in 1932. Retired in 1965 to teach & manufacture magic. Karlovy Vary 1st prizes 1975 & 1981. Bio is in Metin And, Magic in Istanbul (1978), 49-61.

name: Sunshine, Martin L. "Marty
bio: (Harrisburg, Pennsylvania: 13 May 1897-7 Aug 1978) Pro mentalist since 1911. Also comedy magic as "Kismet". Invented Color Vision Box (by 1931). Co-owner (with Al Baker) of The Broadway Magic Shop in New York City 1931-ca1935. In 1932, as he later admitted, he sold a gaffed mail sack to famous medium Frank Decker &, posing as magician "M. Taylor", helped Decker at a phony seance held on Dec 8th in New York City. USO tours in the Pacific 1943 & Korea 1953. Trick in Tarbell #5. [LR3/98;WWM]

name: Surith, Melo
bio: See: "Melachini"

name: Suter, Michael "Mike
bio: (Niederrohrdorf, Switzerland: 17 Sep 1962-) Learned in 1983. Pro close-up & comedy magician since 1987. Partner (with Peter Bedognetti) in magic shop (Pedro Magie) in Zürich. [Wh2]

name: Sutherland, Jack
bio: (Denver, Colorado: c1942-17 Jul 1990) Worked originally at Easley's Fun Shop in Phoenix, Arizona, including 15 years as manager of the magic department. Owner of Sun Magic in Phoenix since c1980. Magic teacher. Murdered by his wife's purported lover.

name: Sutherland, Nellie
bio: (England: fl.c1890s) Pro magicienne who toured the English provinces for many years. [CI]

name: Sutton, George
bio: (England: fl.1820s-40s) Pro magician & vent. Wrote A Treatise on Ventriloquism (1833). Toured England with an automaton 1836-38. Toured the USA (1838 & 1844) & Lisbon (1845 with the Madrid Circus). Pet effects: Bullet Catching & innovative presentations of other standard tricks. [Fr;Cl;Mo]

name: Suvac, Rob
bio: See: Suavet, Robert

name: Suzanne
bio: See: de Courcy, Sue

name: Suzuki, Tooru
bio: (Japan: fl.1980s) Pro close-up in Tokyo. 1989 Tokyo Magic Awards 2nd place.

name: Svengali
bio: See: Lorenzo, Hugo

name: Svengari, Paul
bio: (Green Bay, Wisconsin: 17 Jun 1946-Nov 1990) Inspired at age 5 by magic set & a Houdini biography. Learned at age 12 from a magic set & lessons from local amateur. Debut in 1960. Pro stage magician with 2 (or more) assistants, principally Thomas C. "Tom" Polzak (since 1960) & wife Mary Lou (early 1970s until c1987 when they divorced). Private student of Norm Nielsen (1962-64) & Channing Pollock (1969). Former house magician at Magic Cellar c1969-c1975. Did illusion shows, close-up, & trade shows. Pet effects: Asrah, Thin Sawing, & Miser's Dream. [LR4/85;Wh2]

name: Swadling, Robert B. "Bob
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-90s) Invented Blasted and Dubious Dominoes. Won British Ring 1962 Shield (stage magic) plus the 1962 Dittia Shield (for manip). Married his assistant, Valerie, in 1963. Moved to France for a time before returning to Britain. Their daughter, "Kay Kristal", is a pro magicienne. See Harry Stanley, Robert Swadling's Ring of Fire (n.d.). [Mar]

name: Swadling, Valerie
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Pro. Learned magic as assistant to Robert Swadling whom she married in 1963. 1968 Craig Trophy. [Mar]

name: Swain, James "Jim
bio: (New York City, NY: 7 Jun 1956- ) Inspired at age 13 seeing a magician work at a Boy Scout meeting. Student at age 12 of Jeff Sheridan & Derek Dingle. By age 16 was doing his own stage act. 1971 SAM Junior Magician of the Year. Advertising salesman & writer in Hollywood, Florida. Semi-pro close-up magician & card manipulator since age 22. Invented Vanishing Aces (1976) & Poker Interchange (1980). Wrote The Man Who Walked Through Walls (1989, 276pp), a novel starring "Vincent Hardare", Houdini's fictional nephew; Don't Blink: The Magic of Jim Swain (1992), & Miracles with Cards (1996, 190pp). Articles in Apocalypse, Magic Manuscript, Richard's Almanac, Arcane, & Epoptica. [Lo;Wh2]

name: Swaine, Aimee
bio: (England: fl.1930s-40s) Wife of Jim Swaine. 1932 Magicians' Club Gold Medal. In WW II did a magic act touring ENSA with Zeanit. [Mar]

name: Swaine, Jim
bio: (England: fl.1930s-40s) Pro. Husband of Aimee Swaine. Swan, Charles Parker Charles Parker Swan was born April 18, 1928 in Somerville MA, grew up in Everett and graduated from Everett HS in 1946. After serving in the Army, he attended college in CA and graduated from Boston University in 1952. He retired from the Burroughs Corporation in 1989 after 37 years service. He and the former Claire Miles were married in 1955 and settled in Northborough MA where they raised their 3 children, Karen, Ellen & David. They are also the proud grandparents of 4 granddaughters. In 1970, he was elected Town Moderator and served the town for 33 years, retiring in 2003. His wit, well directed sense of humor as well as his expert knowledge of parliamentary law, saved many stressful situations on the town floor. He and Claire have also been active in many community activities as well as advocacy at state and local levels for the developmentally disabled population. His magic career started with a "Mysto Magic" set he received as a birthday gift at age 8. Soon after, he started doing shows at church "bean suppers", scouting events and service clubs all around New England. Later on, as a salesman for the Burroughs Corp. he used magic as part of his presentations. He has also taught magic inspiring and mentoring young people to an interest in it. He and Claire have performed at many magic conventions and are probably best known for his "How to Force a Watermelon" and other creative comedy routines. He was the Gazette Magic Santa for over 30 years, performing for children in hospitals and orphanages, while also entertaining many at club dates and corporate shows. While in high school, he worked in Holden's Magic Shop in Boston from 1942-1946. Herman Hansen was the proprietor and became a dear friend. While at Holden's, Parker met many famous magicians of the day and enjoyed demonstrating the many products in the shop. Even though he has retired from performing, magic continues to be an important part of Claire and Parker's lives. One of their daughters, Ellen, is a performing magician, and Karen is a collector. He is a charter member of the New England Magic Collectors Association and emceed their convention shows for many years.

name: Swann, Russell "Max
bio: (Washington, DC: 30 Oct 1905-1980) Semi-pro dramatic actor for 10 years. Then pro comedy magician since 1932, playing vaude & such nightclub dates as the New York Cotillion Room (1954). Also played Loew's State Theatre in New York City in 1936. Pet effects: Sun & Moon and Snake Basket. 1979 AMA Performing Fellowship. [Pr;Des;Ho;WWM]

name: Swatosch, Herbert
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 27 Apr 1964-) Learned at age 15. Merchant in Vienna. Semi-pro stage illusionist since age 18. Aka "Timoor". Works as partner with elder brother Michael Swatosch-Doré & Robert Kaldy-Karo in their "Masters of Sensation" show. Articles in Innovator. [Wh5]

name: Swatosch, Michael
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 19 Oct 1958-) Teacher in Vienna. Semi-pro magician, aka "Michel Doré" & "Doré". Learned at age 13. Teacher in Vienna. Semi-pro kid-show & mental magician since age 20 when in 1977 he co-founded (with Robert Kaldy) the "1. Wiener Zaubertheater" & in 1981 the magic club of same name. Co-editor (with Kaldy) of Innovator 1981-present. Partner with his younger brother "Timoor" (Herbert Swatosch) & Kaldy in magic show "The Masters of Sensation". Collector. Wrote Symbolkarten (1983, 62pp, with Kaldy-Karo). Articles in Innovator, Aladin, Magie, Magische Welt, Magischer Anzeiger, etc. [Wh5]

name: Swift. Allen
bio: (January 16, 1924 - April 18, 2010) Allen Swift (Ira Stadlen) was best known as the “Man of a Million” voices and was an all around performer. He was an actor, magician, playwrite and best known on the East Coast as the voice of the “Herring Maven” in advertising. He took the name from Fred Allen and Jonathan Swift and became Captain Allen Swift on WPIX-TV as the host of the “Popeye” TV show (1956-1960) where he did magic and used stories and puppets. When Buffalo Bob took ill it was Allen’s doing “Howdy Doody”’s voice for more than a year. The voice on the comedy “Safari” tape was Allen’s when he teamed with Lee Noble to produce the trick. Allen Swift appeared on many shows at SAM Parent Assembly #1 and New York’s IBM Ring #26.

name: Swinford, Paul [Wesley]
bio: (Covington, Kentucky: 29 Jan 1931-26 Apr 2000) Inspired at age 10 seeing Paul Hubbard act at school assembly. Learned by buying tricks from Johnson Smith & Douglas Magicland. Purchasing agent & personnel manager in Cincinnati. Amateur close-up magician, specializing in card tricks with mathematical twist. Did magic with US Air Force in Korean War. Co-invented (with Clyde Cairy) Cyberdeck (released in 1969 as "Computer Cards" & re-released as "Cyberdeck in 1986 & 1996). "Parade" editor, Linking Ring, 1974-77. Did close-up restaurant magic thrice weekly in Cincinnati. Wrote Faro Fantasy (1968, 62pp), More Faro Fantasy (1971, 64pp), & The Cyberdeck (1986). See Arcane #2 (1980) for all-Swinford issue. Articles in Epilogue, Pallbearers Review, etc. [LR11/74;Wh2]

name: Swiss, Jamy lan
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 30 Nov 1952- ) Learned at age 7 from father's gift of Color Vision Box. Pro since 1981. Magic bartender 1984-present: New York City (1984), Inn of Magic in Wheaton, Maryland (1985-86), etc. Also works close-up. Wrote Thoughts (1987, 47pp), Theories (1987, 64pp), Theatrics (1987, 43pp), An Interesting Application of That Principle (1987, 40pp), The Animated Ring (1987, 20pp; rev 1989, 18pp, as Theurgical Thread), 10 in 10 (1987, 10pp), A Rumor in Their Own Time (1988, 18pp), & Thaumatolotry (1989, 22pp). Articles & effects in Genii, Magic Manuscript, State of the Art, Magical Arts Journal, & Magic Menu. [Genii9/87;Wh2]

name: Switon, Pierre
bio: (France: 1939-) Pro card manipulator & general magic. Starred in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique 1971-72. With assistant as "P. Switon et Galia" & "Les Switon". Pet effect: Zombie. AFAP Master Magician. See Mad Magic #15 for an all-Switon issue. [Bou;Bou2]

name: Swivel, Harry W.
bio: (Troy, New York: 4 Jan 1893- ) Interested c1912. Personnel director in New Brunswick, New Jersey. Semi-pro since 1918 with club & church show. Aka "The Great Swivello". [SAM;WWM]

name: Syko
bio: See: Bamberg, David

name: Sylvano
bio: (Ireland: fl.1980s) Stage name of Pat Sullivan of "Sylvano & Susan". Pro stage magician. Lives in County Kerry, Republic of Ireland.

name: Sylvester, Alfred
bio: (London, England: 17 Oct 1831-30 Jan 1886) Learned as assistant lecturer to Prof. Pepper at the Royal Polytechnic Institution. Pro illusionist, although more in the role of lecturer-exhibitor than as an active performer. Toured the USA in 1866 (with a Sphinx) & 1870-71 (with a Pepper's Ghost). Aka "Hadji Mahommed Salib c1873 & "The Fakir of Oolu" since 1873 (when he debuted? his "Last Link Severed", an improved Aerial Suspension). Played Paris. Patented his improved "Ghost Illusion" (in 1863), "Prismatic Fountain" (in 1964), "Enchanted Canopy" (in 1866), "Talking Lion" (in 1868, an original invention"), "Last Link Severed" (in 1869), "Anoetus" (in 1873), & "Amphiarous" (in 1876). Moved in 1874 to Australia where he performed until his death. Toured New Zealand in 1875. Father of Alfred Sylvester Jr. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Silvester" (Waller perhaps to the contrary), "Sylvestor", & "Sylvestre". [Cl;Pr;Wal;Fr;Mo;Magicana]

name: Sylvester Jnr., Alfred
bio: (England: -15 Jun 1907) Learned assisting his father. Minor pro illusionist and vent with the Talking Hand. Moved to Australia with his father in 1874. On own since 1878 in Australia & New Zealand. Died in Adelaide of brain paralysis. [Wal;Magic5/04;10/07]

name: Sylvester, Fred
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 31 [sic] Dec 1926-) Stage name of Frederic [sic] Charles Sylvester Caba. Inspired in 1936 seeing Charly Eperny show. Pro since 1946 as "Fred Sylvester" with magic & pickpocket act. Pattering in 12 languages has toured over 40 countries since 1953 with assistant-wife Olga "Olly" as "The Two Sylvesters". Several prizes 1965-75. Wrote lecture notes. Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, & Aladdin. [Wh2]

name: Sylvestre, George
bio: (Cheltenham, England: 2 Apr 1887-3 Dec 1960) Stage name of Howard Conrad Waghorne. Oxford U BA. Pro (ex-college math teacher) sleight-of-hand. Pet effect: the Mutilated Sunshade, for which he billed himself "King of Sunshades". Toured Australia in 1912. Played St. George's Hall (London) 1920 & 1924. Co-founded (with Wilfred Tyler) the Cotswold Magic Society in 1943. [Wal]

name: Sylvestre, Ralph E.
bio: See: Burlingame, H. J.

name: Sylwester, Roger O.
bio: (Little Falls, Minnesota: 6 Dec 1939-) Learned at age 10 from Xmas gift Gilbert magic set. Lutheran minister. Semi-pro magician since 1958, specialized in platform & close-up. Trick in Hierophant #3. [Wh2]

name: Szabo, Attila
bio: (Hungary: 15 Dec 1958-) Pro magus in Hungary. [Nad]

name: Szag
bio: (Byelorussia, Russian Empire [now Belorus]: 1910-) Stage name of Anatoly Sergievich Novozhilov. Pro circus illusionist. Was, with Kio & Vadimov, 1 of 3 top magicians in USSR. [Mec]

name: Szirvani, Mansur Gulamovich
bio: (USSR: 1919-) Pro magician with illusions & sleights. In circuses since 1958. [Nad;Mec]

name: Szlachta, Andrzej
bio: (Gliwice, Poland: 1948-) Amateur illusionist. Vice-president Krakow Illusion Club 1976-83. [Mec] Sznek, John A. (Buffalo, New York: 1 May 1904-4 Feb 1971) Amateur magician. Articles in Magic Cauldron, etc.

name: Szubert, Andrzej
bio: (Chorzów, Poland: 27 Jun 1947- ) Pro illusionist & manipulator. Works with assistant Barbara Piekielska (born 1957) as "Duo Batrix". [Mec;Nad]

name: Szukiewicz, Eugeniusz
bio: (Russia: -1952) Pro illusionist & manipulator. In WW II performed for troops. Pet effect: The Miser's Dream. [Mec]

name: Tabarin
bio: (France: 1584-Aug 1633) Stage name of Jean Salomon. French comedian reported in 1619 as the first person to have performed (and possibly invented) chapeaugraphy, for which he had developed 10 separate characters. Died after a hunting accident. NOTE: In 1870 Léon Fusier first presented his 15-character "Monsieur Tabarin" act. [Mec]

name: Tabary, Francis
bio: (France: fl.1970s-90s) 1994 FISM Grand Prix for his rope act. 2 videos (1996).

name: Taburikan
bio: (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: 19 Apr 1925- ) Stage name of Hermógenes Cézar. Published-edited Miríade Mágica 1964-65 & Cadernos Mágicos 1966-68. [Fam;Cam]

name: Tadlock, [William L.] "Bill
bio: (Washington, N. Carolina: 17 Jun 1929-9 Jul 2008) Learned from a gift magic set. Banker (retired). Magic & mentalism in the Southeast. PEA President 1988-89 & 2000. IBM Treasurer 1995. [LR11/2000]

name: Taft
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 15 Jan 1883-18 Feb 1957) Stage name of Albert Sachse, son of a theatrical manager. At age 7 came to USA where he worked as a fake female freak in a sideshow. Then as a magician until saved enough money to return home. From 1908-14, billed as "The Taft American Magic Show", he toured Germany (including with the Circus Busch in 1912), Scandinavia, & Russia. Retired in 1923, giving his stage name to his assistant, Reinhold Schäfer (later famous as "Recha"). Died in Berlin. [Win]

name: Tagrey, H. W.
bio: (Elbing, Germany: 24 Apr 1896-died c1960s) Pen name of H. Walter Sperling. Pro magic dealer in Danzig. Joined Magischer Zirkel 1920. Edited-published Magisches Echo 1925-27. Retired in Bad Tölz, Bavaria. Prolific author of 19 magic books in German from 1923 to 1951, only the last two being under his real name. Samples are: Perlen der Magie (1923, 63pp), Bluffs (1925, 44pp), Moderne Tricks der Magie (1926, 64pp), Die moderne Zauberbühne (1926, 54pp), Cristal Gazing Acts (1926, 34pp), Urkomische Zauberei (1928, 23pp); and, as Sperling, Die verhexte Westentasche (1948) & Hokus-Pokus-Fidibus (1951, 174pp). [St]

name: Tahoe, T. C.
bio: (Great Falls, Montana: 24 Jan 1963- Stage name of Christian Dean Lange, specifically as "Mr Tahoe" 1980-84 & "T.C. [Too Cool] Tahoe" 1984-present. Learned at age 14 from How to do Card Tricks by Bill Turner while in hospital. Pro close-up & stand-up comedy magic since age 19. Pet effects: Color Changing Knife & Linking Rings (2 rings done to Purple Rain by Prince). Major influences were Slydini and Tommy Copper. IBM Western Region 1st place in manip 1980 & 1982. Also actor-comedian-director. Wrote Thoughts: A Lecture to Think About (1988, 75pp). TC's Big Book of Jokes (1995, 66pp). In The Play of Shadows: The Tarot Effect (2000, 114pp). Lunch is Served (2008, 188pp). Tarot Buzz (2009, 200pp). Articles in Magic Arts Journal, Genii & Magic Manuscript. [Wh2]
years: 24 Jan 1963- Stage name of Christian Dean Lange, specifically as "Mr Tahoe" 1980-84 & "T.C. [Too Cool] Tahoe" 1984-present. Learned at age 14 from How to do Card Tricks by Bill Turner while in hospital. Pro close-up & stand-up comedy magic since age 19. Pet effects: Color Changing Knife & Linking Rings (2 rings done to Purple Rain by Prince

name: Tahra Bey
bio: (Istanbul, Turkey: 1897- ) Stage name of Kirkor Kalfayan, an Armenian. Pseudo-psychic fakir in Paris from 1925 until 1932 when went to Brazil where he was challenged by Zati Sungur. Still alive in 1970s. Bio fragment in Metin And, Magic in Istanbul (1978), 51-52. [Dif]

name: Takagi, Shigeo
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 8 Aug 1930-7 Jan 1991) Interested in magic since age 6, including seeing a Malini show. Taught by Takomatsu. Psychotherapist & translator with the Diet Library until retired. Influential amateur close-up magician with ropes, cards, & 1-cup. Invented One Cup Routine, S-T Move, & Cash Card (by 1983). 1977 winner of special prize from Tenkai Prize Committee; FFFF Roastee; & 1986 AMA Special Fellowship. Edited The Magic 1989-death. In an obit, Max Maven wrote: "More than any other individual, he was responsible for the growth of quality close-up magic in Japan." Wrote on gambling, puzzles, hypnosis, psychology, memory, & philosophy. On magic wrote Encyclopedia of Card Magic (in Japanese) & Encyclopedia of Coin Magic (in Japanese). Co-authored (with Tenkai) The Card Manipulation of Tenkai (1968). Articles in Fushigi, Genii, Apocalypse, etc. See also Mad Magic #20 for all-Takagi issue; Jeff Busby, Shigeo Takagi's Coin Routine (1978, 8pp); & Richard Kaufman, The Amazing Miracles of Shigeo Takagi (1990, 120pp). 2 videos (1989). [Wh2]

name: Takase, Kiyoshi [pronounced TAH-KAH-SAY]
bio: (Japan: fl.1900s-1910s) Pro with illusions, sleights, & juggling. Played St. George's Hall in London in Dec 1912. NOTE: Missspelled "Talkase" by Clarke. Originally he was a member of the Ten-ichi Troupe and toured America and Europe as a principal member of the troupe when Ten-ichi traveled those countries from 1901 to 1905. When Ten-ichi returned to Japan in 1905, he remained abroad to pursue his career.

name: Taki
bio: (Fujisawa City, near Tokyo, Japan: 15 Feb 1940-) Stage name of Mariko TAKI. Female model in Japan. Taught by Tenkai & Okinu c1962. Pro in "Johnny Aladdin" show as "Taki" in Vietnam & Las Vegas c1962-66 with own spot. Pet effects: Interlocked Production of Cards (admired by Dai Vernon) & Dancing Cane (admired by Peter Pit). Married Aladdin c1964, moving to California that year. Mother of Kelley Randall. Moved to California c1969. [Wh]

name: Talamas
bio: (St.-Etienne, France: 25 Nov 1889- ) Stage name of Charles Leger. Assistant to Ernest Thorn. Pro until 1960s.

name: Talazac, [Jean-Jacques-Maurice]
bio: (Bordeaux, France: 28 May 1863-16 Aug 1916) Ex-wine merchant. Learned magic as assistant to Donato in 1885. Pro debut in 1886. Married Jeanne Lafite in 1894, thereafter working a 2-person mindreading act with her. They played the Théâtre Robert-Houdin in 1905. Wrote Manuel du parfait joueur: La fortune en a'amusant (n.d.). [Dif;St]

name: Talazac, Jeanne
bio: (France: fl.1890s-1st decade of 1900s) Born Jeanne Lafite. Married Jean Talazac in 1894 with whom, as the "Sorcièr Michaëlla", she did a telepathy act.

name: Talbot, Dr Clarence W[eɪl], MD
bio: (Nevada, Missouri: 3 Nov 1883-) Physician. Amateur magician with private magic theater in home in Spokane, Washington, seating 100 & specializing in spook effects & illusions. Aka "Talvada" & "The Fox Brothers". [WWM;Go2]

name: Talkase" [misspelling]
bio: See: Takase

name: Talma, Mercedes
bio: (London, England: 1868-13 Jul 1944) Stage name of Mary Ann Ford since 1890, although soon dropped the "Mercedes" to become simply "Talma". Learned that year assisting Servais Le Roy whom she married later the same year. Pro with own "Queen of Coins" act by 1895 when she toured South Africa. Moved to the USA. Retired there in 1930. [Pr;Mar;Se;Magic9/02]

name: Talma, T. Cussac
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s). Minor pro illusionist. Invented Costume Trunk (by 1902). Toured English music halls 1902-08. [Magic7/02,10/03,6/07; CMM10/06,2/08]

name: Talon, Edmond [Patrick]
bio: (Dublin, Ireland: 5 Dec 1937-1909?) Son of Jacques Talon, the famous "Phillippe", whom he succeeded in 1878. Pro in France. Died poor in Paris. NOTE: Falsely reported died in 1904 but still alive in Apr 1909 when met by Houdini. [Dif;Hou]

name: Talon, Jacques
bio: See: "Phillippe"

name: Talvada
bio: See: Talbot, Dr Clarence W.

name: Tam, [Wing Chuen] Albert
bio: (Hong Kong: 20 May 1959-) Pro with stage & close-up. Invented Illusionary Reflex (1984, a dice trick). [Wh01]

name: Tamarah, Wahli
bio: See: Marquat, Carlos A.

name: Tamariz[-Martel], Juan [Mañuel]
bio: (Madrid, Spain: 18 Oct 1942-) Outstanding close-up artist, theorist, & teacher. Learned from magic set 1946-48 & 1st book in 1956. Student of Frakson and "disciple" of Ascanio. Amateur 1956-69. Pro TV commercial & film director 1970. Full-time pro magician 1971-present. 1973 FISM 1st prize in card magic. Founded the Escuela Mágica de Madrid in 1971 & its annual "Escorial" workshops in 1974. Host-star of own TV series 1975, 1982, 1988, 1990, & 1992. Lectures internationally. A world-class cardman, judged by many to be the top one in Europe. 1993 AMA Magician of the Year. Wrote 19 books, including Trucki-Carto-Magia (1970, with Ramón Varela); The Five Points in Magic (1982, 55pp; revised 1988, 85pp); La Vía Mágica (1989, 192pp) with English tr as The Magic Way: The theory of false solutions and the magic way (1988, 184pp); Magia Potagia (4 vols); Sonata (1991, 312pp); The Magic Rainbow (forthcoming). Articles in Pabular, Apocalypse, Mad Magic, Misdirection, etc. Video (1993). [LR9/93; Wat; Wh2]

name: Tamesis, Baron
bio: See: Hornung, Werner

name: Tammy
bio: See: Calvert, Tammy

name: Tampa
bio: See: Sugden, Raymond S.

name: TAN Bah Chee
bio: (Singapore: 1922-1 Jan 1999) Turned to magic in mid-1930s. Co-edited (with Benjamin Kleinman) Magic Around the World 1969-72. Edited Magic Fan 1974-1979? Childrens entertainer.

name: TAN Choon Tee
bio: (Singapore, Straights Settlement: 25 August 1934-) Vocational teacher. Learned magic in 1951. Edited The Malayan Magician 1959-63? & Singapore Sorcerer 1968-72?. Wrote Tan Choon Tee on Mentalism (1963, 42pp; reprinted as 25 Experiments in Mentalism 1972, 40pp) & Variations on 2 Card Classics (1965, 23pp). Articles in Linking Ring, Magicana, etc. [Magicana#194]

name: TAN Hock Chuan "Bertie
bio: (Singapore, Straights Settlement: 2 Apr 1909-24 Sep 1991) School-master & math teacher. Amateur & semi-pro close-up magician since learned at age 9 from father. Debut at age 15. 1937 Sphinx Award. Invented the Singapore Force & the Invisible Flap (1951). Wrote Rough and Smooth Possibilities (1948, 18pp) & The Magic of Tan Hock Chuan (1970; repr 1977, 43pp). Articles in Sphinx, Magic Wand, Goldston's Magic Quarterly, Genii, Swami, etc. [Go2; Swami9/73; Wh2] "TAN Kwai" SEE: LONG Tack Sam Tanigawa, Tetuo [given name pronounced TEH-TSU-OH) (Japan: -23 Apr 1987) Pro card magic & close-up. Managed magic counter at Meitetsu department store in Nagoya.

name: Tannen, Irving "Irv
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Brother of Lou & Mike Tannen. Pro dealer as co-owner of Tannen's in NYC 1968-78.

name: Tannen, Louis T. "Lou" "Red
bio: (New York City, NY: 14 Feb 1909-19 Mar 1982) Brother of Irving & Mike Tannen. Bought 1st trick in 1918. Pro touring magician in his teens as "Nat Louis" as assistant to Jon "Mac" McDonald when Mac operated a travelling magic shop out of his truck in the late 1920s. Opened his first magic shop in 1929 (Nat Louis Magic Co.) in NYC. Invented Salt-Go (1944). Owner of Tannen's in NYC from 1944 to 1974 when retired to Florida where he died. Trick in MUM. [St;Se;Berg,49-50]

name: Tannen, Mike
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Brother of Irving & Louis Tannen. Operated Circle Magic Shop in New York City in 1940s. It published only one book: MacDougall's Card Mastery (1944).

name: Tanner
bio: (Britain: fl.1830s-60s) Minor intinerant conjuror, working around London with trained dogs, monkeys, & ponies. [Cl]

name: Tanner, Don
bio: (USA: 1924-30 May [or 27 Jun?] 1981) Telephone technician. Amateur magician & part-time magic dealer (Don Tanner Studio of Magic) in Columbus, Ohio. Edited The Servante Newsletter 1952-61, Tannergram 1959-65, The New Phoenix 1960-65, & The Mentalist 1962-63. Edited "Hocus Pocus Parade" in Linking Ring c1966-1974. Invented finger writer (by 1960). Wrote Grant's Fabulous Feats of Mental Magic (1954, 22pp), Victory Carton Illusions (1955, 21pp), How to Do Cigarette Tricks (1957, 20pp; repr 1973), How to Do Headline Predictions (1957, 16pp), Fifty Tricks and Ideas with Spring Flowers (1958, 15pp), Mammoth Medallion Miracles (1963), Flowers that Bloom with a Spring (28pp), & edited Fifty Ways to Use a Card Box (1969, 20pp), etc.

name: Tanner, Joe
bio: (USA: fl.1980s-90s) Pro escapist. Proprietor (with wife Pam) of Wheeler-Tanner Escapes in Great Falls, Montana, and later Spokane, Washington.

name: Tanner, Randy
bio: (USA: c1949-) Inspired at age 12 seeing S. David Walker pitch Svengalis at fair. Financial systems analyst. Amateur close-up magician. [Lo2]

name: Tappan, Peter W[ales] "Pete
bio: (New York City, NY: 26 Sep 1928-15 Mar 2007) Learned at age 12 from library books & magic set. Acoustical engineering consultant. Semi-pro close-up magician since age 18. Invented Quicksilver Cube (1965) & Floating Doll (1966). Wrote The Impostress Princess (1986, 114pp). Tricks & articles in New Tops, Linking Ring, MUM, etc. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Tarasiewicz, Jósef
bio: (Poland: fl.1910s-1930s) Pro illusionist in European circuses from 1918 to 1939. [Mec;Nad]

name: Tarbell, Dr Harlan [Eugene] "Doc
bio: (Delavan, Illinois: 23 Feb 1890-15 Jun 1960) Raised in & near Peoria. Inspired at age 11 seeing White the Magician. Learned at age 14 from travelling salesman. Moved to Chicago in 1911. Illustrator, naprapathist (a form of homeopathy), and semi-pro magician. Illustrator for Edwards' Monthly (1909-10), Burling Hull's products, and of catalogs for Read & Covert and Chicago Magic Company (since 1912). U.S. Army in France in WW I. Returned to Chicago in 1920. Then pro magician since 1923. Hired in 1926 as illustrator for a magic course to be written by Walter Baker, he was given the entire job later that year when Baker defaulted. Over the next year and a half he wrote a series of 60 mail-order lessons (including his 3,000 illustrations) that became the influential Tarbell Course in Magic, which sold 10,000 sets by 1931. Still in print (in revised edition) & still a standard, although quaintly dated in style. Also wrote How to Chalk Talk (1924, 94pp), Chalk Talk Stunts (1926, 101pp), Chalk Talks for Sunday Schools (1928, 152pp), Crazy Stunts for Comedy Occasions (1929, 102pp), & Fun with Chalk Talk (1931, 106pp). Illustrated Hilliard's Greater Magic (1938). SAM President 1949-50. SAM Hall of Fame. Invented or improved over 200 effects. Invented Chinese Laundry Ticket (by 1906), Satan's Color Change (a changing card, by 1908), color-changing handkerchief (in 1910 or 1911 for Okito), Tarbell Rope Trick (c1919), & Tarbell Egg Bag (1927). Tricks in Edwards' Monthly & MUM. Bios are Eugene E. Gloye, Harlan Tarbell: Creator of Magic and Magicians (1993, 60pp) & Frances Marshall, Dr. Harlan Tarbell (1956). [LR11/97,5/95, 9/46; Par;Bo;SAM;Th;Ho;WWM]

name: Tardy, Jean
bio: See: "Hardy l'Enchanteur"

name: Tarley
bio: (Poland: 1932-) Stage name of Lucjan Perliński. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Pet effect: Dove Production. [Mec]

name: Tarr, [William] "Bill
bio: (New York City, New York: 31 May 1925-) Learned in 1934 from books. Pro magician then pro sculptor (including a 1974 Guggenheim Fellowship). Wrote 3 well-selling beginners books: Now You See It, Now You Don't (1976), 101 Easy-to-Learn Classic Magic Tricks (1977; repr 1993, 220pp), & The Second Now You See It, Now You Don't! (1978). Also The BT-One (1985, 54pp). 2 videos (1987 & 1988). [Genii11/88;Wh2]

name: Tasco
bio: (Germany: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Stage name of Eduard Jänicken. Minor pro. Kassner began his career assisting Tasco in Hamburg c1908-c1911. [Win] Tate, Norman Edward “The Fun Doctor,” MBE (Papakura, New Zealand: 12 October 1890 – 28 October 1962) Inspired as a child after seeing a troupe of Japanese jugglers. Developed an act that included juggling, magic and sword swallowing. Gave up a grocery apprenticeship to become a fulltime performer before the age of 20. As “The Fun Doctor” he performed in schools, hospitals and prisons throughout New Zealand and Australia for more than fifty years. Awarded an MBE (Member of the British Empire) in 1959. He is estimated to have performed more than 50,000 shows and been seen by more than two million people. He inspired a number of later performers, including Jon Zealando, Richard Webster and Alan Watson.

name: Taunt, [Cyril H.] "Serl
bio: (Britain: 1902-4 Aug 1961) Aka "Chan D'Or, the Eurasian Illusionist". Former assistant to Ching Wu.

name: Tayade, Anand D[warkanath]
bio: (Bombay, India: 8 Jul 1964-) Son of D.A. Tayade. Taught at age 10 by father. Pro close-up magician. Also work's in father's magic shop. [Wh2]

name: Tayade, D[warkanath] A[basaheb]
bio: (Pimpalgaon-Baswant, Nasik district, India: 13 Sep 1917-24 Oct 2004) Learned at age c13 from street magicians. Pro since 1940. Magic dealer & manufacturer (Tayade's Magic Shop) in Bombay since 1944. Wrote Sulabha Jaduche Khel [Easy Magic Tricks, in Marathi]. Articles in Marmik & other Marathi-language journals. Father of Anand D. Tayade. [Wh2]

name: Taylor, Bev[erly Wilford]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 1924-15 Apr 2005) While serving in the US Army as an infantryman in Europe in WWII he played some USO shows. Founder-owner Town House Magic in St. Louis, Missouri, 1946-1955 when he sold to his manager, Don Lawton. Taylor later (1960) bought the Stevens Toy Company, which produced some 500 new toys, many with a magical theme. Published-edited Town House Magic Chats 1947-51 (43 issues). Bio is Bruce Hetzler, Bev Taylor's Town House Magic. [Albo95;LR4/97]

name: Taylor, [Robert] "Bob
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Pro with mental and card magic. Invented Jiggle Pass (by 1945). Wrote I'll Read Your Mind (1946) & The Jiggle or Shake Pass with Variations (1946, 11pp, with Neal Elias).

name: Taylor, Dana
bio: (Britain: c1887-) Minor pro as "Danar". Autobio is My Life in Magic (1967, 31pp).

name: Taylor, David [Robert]
bio: (Dunedin, New Zealand: 6 Mar 1947-) Learned at age 8 buying tricks at De Larno's shop. Contractor. Semi-pro stand-up comedy magician since age 15. Mail-order dealer ("David Taylor Magic") in Dunedin since 1969. Has invented 80+ effects, which he has begun to make & market. Articles in Magigram & Magicana. [Magicana6/79;Wh5]

name: Taylor, Prof. E[dward] Cooper
bio: (New Brunswick, New Jersey: 6 Feb 1852-16 Feb 1927) Learned at age 11 from book. Pro since age 15, initially assisting J.H. Anderson Jr 1967-69. Buying out Prof Everett Crosby's company & paper in 1869, he trouped for a year under Crosby's name. Toured throughout the USA (1869-1897, including the frontier states 1872-81). He did sleight-of-hand, illusions, escapes, & the Gun Trick. Aka the "Fakir of Ispahan" (1872). Harry Rouclere was an assistant 1884-86. Retired in 1897 in Massachusetts. SAM Hall of Fame (1973). Father of E. Cooper Taylor Jr. Bios are E. Cooper Taylor Jr, A Few Moments from the Career of Prof. E. Cooper Taylor (1977, 51pp) & E. Cooper Taylor III, Prof. E.C. Taylor: Frontier Magician (forthcoming). [Genii4/90;Pr]

name: Taylor Jr, E. Cooper
bio: (USA: 1890-1974) Son of the above. Born on tour. Assisted in father's troupe since age 7. After schooling became an actor & director with Edison & Griffith. In 1922 formed his own engineering company. Wrote & published in 1973 the first bio of his father. [Genii4/90]

name: Taylor III, E. Cooper
bio: (USA: 1922-6 Apr 2005) Son of the above. Amateur magician since the late 1960s. Writing Prof. E.C. Taylor: Frontier Magician (forthcoming).

name: Taylor, Dr Franklin V. "Frank", PhD
bio: (USA: 1910-12 Mar 1960) Psychology professor at Princeton U. Amateur magician since youth. Invented Peek Deck (1942), Materialization (1942), & Hallucination (1947). Tricks in Phoenix & HMM. [Th]

name: Taylor, Gerald, AIMC
bio: (Brisbane, Australia: 1 Sep 1927-) Inspired at age 10 seeing bar magic performed by customers in hotel that his parents managed. Semi-pro since age 16, pro since age 35. Dealer (Aladdin's Magic Shop) in Melbourne from 1966 until he sold it in 1980 to Card Mondor. Moved in 1981 to Queensland where he joined Arthur Coghlan who ran the magic show at "Magic Mountain" at Nobby's Beach, a permanent magic show (6,000 shows by 1985 when Arthur finished) and conducted the Magical Hall of Fame museum. Returned to Melbourne as proprietor of "Bernard's Magic Shop" 1986-c1993 until sold to Tim Ellis. Wrote The Classical Technique of Fire Eating [1967, 43pp] & 50 Easy Card Tricks (1980, 30pp). Edited & published Waller's Magical Nights at the Theatre (1980, 256pp). Wrote prize-winning article "Revolutionary Approach to Black Art" in Linking Ring (Jun 1967). [Wh2]

name: Taylor, Granville, MIMC
bio: (Nelson, Lancashire, England: fl.1950s-90s) Stage name of Granville Taylor, MIMC. Taught at age 8 by his magician uncle. Gave 1st public show at age 14. Turned pro as assistant to Murray in 1951, then assistant to Cecil Lyle 1953-55 when went on own as illusionist, eventually as "Faust the Magician". Toured Far East in 1968. Had big show in Japan (1971, 1973, 1975, 1976). Cruise ship shows since 1977. Has rights to Amac's Elusive Lady illusion, Devant's Window of the Haunted House, etc. Bills self as "The Last of the Great Masters of Magic". TV bits in Japan. 1 biographical video (1993). [Wh5]

name: Taylor, Harold "Three Tricks", MIMC
bio: (Didcot, Berkshire, England: 1909-31 Dec 1992) Inspired at age 8 seeing a magician. Pro since after WW II & a popular magical MC. Aka "Arsène". The 3 pet effects that comprised the basis of, although not quite his entire act, and gave him his nickname among fellow magi were Cut-and-Restored Rope, Sucker Egg & Silk, and Egg on Fan. Toured USA in 1966. British Ring Past President. British Ring Silver Wand. Wrote 1982 Harold Taylor Lecture Notes (1982) & Magic as Entertainment: "The Angle of a Pro" (1991, 16pp). 2 audios. Many TV bits. [Genii2/66;Bo#194;Hudd;La2]

name: Taylor, James
bio: (England: c1830-c1900) Minor pro stage magic & second-sight act with son. [CI;Vo56]

name: Taylor, Ken[neth John]
bio: (Wilmington, Delaware: 6 Nov 1945- ) Learned at age 9 from father & Dunninger's Complete Encyclopedia of Magic. Salesman in Oakland, California. Semi-pro apparatus magician. Pet effects: Milk-in-Lightbulb & Disecto. Played the Magic Cellar, etc. Illustrator for Lloyd Jones & Jeff Busby. [Wh2]

name: Taylor, Dr Leroy M.
bio: (USA: 1836-1904) Physician & businessman in Washington, DC. A Mason. Known for having the largest collection of occult books (2,000 titles by 1901) and his interest in psychic research. [Magic6/01]

name: Taylor, Merv[ille Andrew]
bio: (USA: 1904-5 Jan 1974) Metal worker. Semi-pro maker since 1947 of high-quality props (Merv Taylor Magic Company) in Hollywood, California. Used mainly stainless steel and acrylic Plexiglas (the first to use this material). Sold to Owen Brothers in 1959. Then co-licensee (with Bud Taylor & Jimmy Hume) of magic shop in Disneyland. SAM Hall of Fame. C. Prentice Taylor is researching a biography. [St]

name: Taylor, Rex
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Pro mentalism & straight magic since 1965. Wrote 3 booklets. Articles in Magigram.

name: Taylor, Tony
bio: (Portsmouth, England: fl.1920s-80s) Dental mechanic. Moved to Vancouver, Canada, in 1929. Inspired that year seeing Ralph Richards show & bought Richards' Book of Magic. Semi-promagician since 1935. Collector & magic historian. Articles in Dragon, Die Box, Magic Wand, & Linking Ring. Wrote Spotlight on 101 Great Magic Acts (1964, 95pp) & The Magic of Allan Lambie (1970, 50pp, with Micky Hades).

name: Taylor, Vic[tor Edward White]
bio: (Oxford, England: 1900-) Learned around age 8 from pro father. Small-time magician and Punch & Judy man. Autobio is Reminiscences of a Showman (1971, 116pp). Taytelbaum, Eddy-Jules-Sam] "Paddlebaum" (Paramaribo, Suriname, Dutch West Indies [now independent]: 17 Oct 1925- ) Learned at age 9 from a fellow-hospital patient. Architectural draftsman (until retired c1974) in Amsterdam. Amateur close-up cardman. Pet effects: Rising Cards, Paddles, Three Card Monte. Invented a center & bottom double-lift and claims the "so-called Ascanio-spread". FISM 3rd prize in card magic in 1955, 1st prize in close-up 1955, 1st prize in card magic 1958. Builder of fine small close-up props, prized by such collectors as Albo. Used to sell abroad thru Anverdi. Noted collector of coins & tokens. Articles in Mad Magic. Kenna Thompson is writing a book on Taytelbaum. [Wh2]

name: Teale, Oscar S[chutte] "Ott
bio: (New York City, NY: 9 Sep 1847-8 Apr 1934) A blacksmith's son. Inspired around age 7 seeing Wyman. Learned at age 13 reading Wyman's Hand-Book of Magic. Debut at age 22 (1869). Architect. Semi-pro magician 1873-74 as "Ottilidio". SAM member #38. SAM President 1908-09. Wrote Higher Magic (1920, 492pp). A researcher for & illustrator of some of Houdini's later books. Main editor of Elliott's Last Legacy (1923). Claimed to have ghosted Houdini's A Magician Among the Spirits (1924). Articles. SAM Hall of Fame 1990. [Go2;Silver]

name: Tear, [Archibald Edwin] "Archie
bio: (Northampton, England: 28 Oct 1906-9 Oct 1986) Pro sleight-of-hand plus mentalism. Debut in 1919. In 1932 became one of first magicians on TV. British Ring President 1958-59. Wrote Coincidental Thoughts (n.d.), A Double Prediction (n.d.), & Supremus Book Test (n.d.). [WWM; Daw2]

name: Té-Dé
bio: See: Drioux, Auguste

name: Teddy-Strik
bio: See: "Strik, Teddy"

name: Teen, Sir
bio: See: "Sir Teen"

name: Teixeira, Dr Jorge [Manuel Lopes]
bio: (Covilhã, Portugal: 1 Dec 1948-) Psychologist, public official, journalist, & amateur magician. Edited 2 magic sets. Wrote Nada na Manga (1980, 48pp).

name: Tejada, Fernando
bio: (Argentina: c1952-1988) Pro stage magic as "The Great Professor Marvo". Killed onstage in Columbia at age 36 while doing the Bullet Catch.

name: Teller
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 14 Feb 1948-) Stage & now legal name of Raymond Joseph Teller. Learned at age 5 from mother's gift of a Howdy Doody magic set. Originally worked street magic. Pro comedy magic act with Penn Jillette as "Penn & Teller" team since 1975. Teller is the short, silent partner in their highly successful act. Pet effects: His original "Shadows" trick & the Needle Trick. Co-authored (with Penn Jillette) Cruel Tricks for Dear Friends (1989, 207pp). Co-star of film Penn & Teller Get Killed (1989). 1996 AMA Magician of the Year award (with Penn). REF: Lionel Trilling, "A Couple of Eccentric Guys", The New Yorker (15 May 1989), 58-86.

name: Tempest, Marco
bio: (Zurich, Switzerland: 3 Dec 1964-) Pro manipulator & "cyber-illusionist". Originally with Martin Cottet in their "The United Artists" double act. Tours theaters & clubs throughout world. Originally presenteda New Wave-type act featuring such varied props as boomerangs, batons, & origami birds. Lately specializes in virtual magic interactions with video screens, flying & floating pixels, flying video screens and special "screen to life" effects with humans, automobiles, and other objects. Won 1987 World Cup of Magic.TV bit in Britain. [Ran;Fi2;Wh01]

name: Templar, Doctor
bio: See: Pitts, Bill

name: Temple, Austen
bio: (England: fl.1910s) Pro variety magician. Played St. George's Hall in 1918.

name: Temple, [James Williard] "Jim
bio: (USA: 3 Feb 1919-12 Dec 1996) Amateur. Invented Color Monte, which was first marketed in 1968 by Emerson & West, selling over 100,000 units by time of his death in Williamsburg, Virginia.

name: Temple, Phil[lip]
bio: (Aberdeen, Washington: 3 Apr 1939-) Inspired at age 11 by Xmas gift Mysto Magic set & seeing Blackstone show. Pro illusionist since 1960. Pet effect: Cannon & Nest of Boxes. Magic historian & collector (with largest collection of Dante memorabilia). Runs the "Magic Circus", a theater-poster mounting service in San Rafael, California. Compiled-published the Thurston-Dante Letter Set (1981, 475pp), which reprints 340 of their letters to each other. Edited-published Thurston Scrapbook (1985, 184pp) & Our Life of Magic (1989, 224pp). Wrote Dante: The Devil Himself (1991). Compiled (with Gary R. Frank) The Carter Scrapbook (1992, 96pp). Articles in Genii, Linking Ring, MUM, Magic Circular, New Tops, & Abra. [Wh2]

name: Templeton, Max
bio: (Britain: 1883-25 May 1964) Stage name of George Alfred McQuire. Pro magician & shadowist. Probably 1st to present handshadows on TV (in 1933). [Wat]

name: Ten-ichi
bio: See: Shokyokusai, Ten-ichi

name: Ten-ichi II
bio: See: Shokyokusai, Tenji

name: Ten-i-Chi
bio: (Holland: -c1914) Stage name of De Nijs [pronounced teh-NEES]. Pro. Father of Jules Ten-i-Chi.

name: Ten-i-Chi, Jules
bio: (Holland: 25 Feb 1893-4 Mar 1967) Son of the above. Stage name of Jules Edv. Frans De Nijs. Learned from father. Pro 1924-29. REF: G. Buckingham in The Budget (Apr 1967), 123; & in Magic Circular (Jan 1965). Died in Breda. [St]

name: Tendo, Mahka
bio: (Aichi, Japan: 18 Mar 1960-26 May 2009) Stage name of Takao YABUSHITA. Learned magic at age 12 from tricks bought at department store magic counter. Since age 21 pro stage & close-up manip, specializing in Jumbo Cards. Invented Card Roll-Down in 1983. 1985 FISM 2nd prize in manip. 1986 Desert Magic Seminar finalist. Does a weekly NHK-TV segment. [Wh2]

name: Tenkai
bio: (Nagoya, Japan: 1 Dec 1889-6 Jun 1972) Stage name of Sadajiro (aka Teijiro) ISHIDA. Learned assisting a Japanese magician. Pro. Married his assistant, Okinu, in 1913. Moved to USA in 1924. Toured Mexico in 1939. On 7 Dec 1941 Tenkai & Okinu were interned for two months in Hawaii, after which they were released to entertain US troops, performing during the war years as Chinese magician "Wen Hai". Taught Johnny Aladdin at that time. Invented Tenkai Palm (by 1954). Returned with Okinu to Japan in 1958. Taught Mariko Taki c1962. 1971 AMA Special Fellowship. Autobio is My Fifty Years in Magic (1975, 305pp, in Japanese). Wrote Tenkai's Manipulative Card Routine (ghosted by Bill Murata) & The Card Manipulation of Tenkai (1968, with Shigeo Takagi). See Robert Parrish, Six Tricks by Tenkai (1953, 15pp); Masatoshi Furota, The Thoughts of Tenkai: A Collection of His Superb Tricks (1971; also in Japanese); Gerald Kosky & Arnold Furst, The Magic of Tenkai (1974, 143pp), which includes an autobio sketch; Album Tenkai and Okinu Ishida [c1982, 200pp]. Tricks in Talisman, Kijutsu Kenkyu, & HMM. [Tay;Ho]

name: Tenkatsu, Madame
bio: See: Shokyokusai, Tenkatsu

name: Tenko HIKITA
bio: (Yokohama, Japan: 3 Jul 1934-31 Dec 1979) Stage name of Isao HIKITA. Inspired at age 8 seeing a local magician. Student of Tenyo. Pro escape artist and illusionist. Performed in Western dress since his debut. Added a dove act after seeing Channing Pollock's 1962 Italian film European Nights. Star of Japanese TV 1968-76, when he was the highest paid entertainer (magic or otherwise) in Japan. His career was effectively ruined by a heart attack in 1976. A come-back effort was ended by a fatal heart attack. [Genii2/80;Bo2]

name: Tenko, Princess
bio: (Japan: 29 Jun 1959-) Stage name of Mariko ITAKURA. As "Mari ASAKAZE" was a pop singer & recording star 1978-79. Learned magic as apprentice-assistant to the original Tenko HIKITA, by 1977. Succeeded to his name & show on his death in 1979 as "Tenko Hikita II". Pro stage illusionist with full-evening show. Now billed as "Princess Tenko". 1988 Japanese Magic Awards Best Professional Magician Award. Played a USA TV date & in 1988 a reduced (4-assistants) version at FISM in Holland. Played a 1-month run at the Kabuki-za theater in 1989. 1990 AMA Magician of the Year. 1990 special award from Tenkai Prize Committee. Tenyo [NT10/80;Bo#238;Genii11/89] SEE: Shokyokusai, Tenyo

name: Terhune, Max
bio: (Franklin, Indiana: 12 Feb 1891-5 Jun 1973) Pro vaudeville animal imitator & vent (with "Scuzzy"). Taught magic by Dota "Mysterious" Brown in 1929, he added close-up to his act. Pet effect: Miser's Dream. In early 1930s brought by Gene Autry to Hollywood where he appeared as cowboy in over 80 B-feature Westerns. Since 1936 co-starred as comedy sidekick (named "Alabi") in Republic's "Three Mesquiteers" (with John Wayne!) & Monogram's "Range Buster" series. His film career ended in the late 1950s. Several of these films had included "Scuzzy", which Republic insisted renaming "Elmer". Column in Genii in late 1930s.

name: Teros, Géo
bio: (France: fl.1950s-80s) Pro kid-show magician & shadowist. 1951 FISM prize for allied arts (hand shadows). AFAP Bronze Medal. Co-founding Vice President of SNIVS in 1984. [Bou] Tershay, Joe Terrell, G. Ray (USA: -1974) Pro supper club worker in 1930s-40s billed as "The Debonaire Deceiver". [American Magazine 4/48] (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Pro West Coast magician. Worked in tux & red fez. Card Mondor recalls: "Great sight act. Suave little guy did flash magic ended with pipes. Did 2 years at same club in Barbary Coast area" of San Francisco. [Tay]

name: Teschner, Ranier
bio: (Germany: 16 Oct 1940-) Card magician. 1975 MZvD 1st prize in card magic. 1976 FISM 3rd prize in card magic. 1978 MZvD 1st prize in card magic. [Nad]

name: Tessier, Pierre
bio: (Paris, France: 6 Oct 1898-) Engineer & officer of public instruction in Paris. Amateur magician specialized in manip. Aka "Mustes". AFAP Master Magician. AFAP President 1963-68. [Bou;WWM]

name: Testot, Felix [pronounced tess-TOE]
bio: (France: fl.1820s-40s) Minor pro from Paris. Toured France, England (1826, 1834, & 1843-44), Belgium, Germany, & Russia. Bio is J.B. Findlay, The Travels of Testot (1965, 36pp). [Fr;St]

name: Teumer, Dr Hellmuth
bio: (Limbach, Germany: 24 Jul 1894-1 Dec 1983) Dentist in Chemnitz. Amateur magician by 1932 when he founded the Chemnitz chapter of the German Magic Circle. Awarded German Magic Circle "Ehrenring" [Honor Ring] in 1936. Since 1938 as "Dr. Lamo" specialized in spirit tricks. Exposed several pseudo-psychics, including the notorious Kordon-Verl. Articles in Magie until 1945. Major collector of Asian arts. Died in Chemnitz, East Germany. [Al;St]

name: Thalmine, Prince
bio: (Curaçao, Dutch West Indes: 21 Oct 1925-) Stage name of Pedro Thielman. Pro magician, the first from his island. Toured a large show combining manipulation, apparatus tricks, & illusions thru the Caribbean West Indies.

name: Thayer, Floyd G[erald]
bio: (Jacksonville, Vermont: 18 Jul 1877-29 Jul 1959) Inspired by & learned around age 8 when bought a box of tricks. Brought by father in 1891 to Pasadena, California, where he began doing semi-pro club shows as "Gerald". Pro dealer-prop maker in southern California as, successively, The Magic Shop of the West 1902-12, Thayer & Christianer 1912-16, F.G. Thayer 1916-1917, Thayer Studio of Magic 1917, Thayer Manufacturing Company 1917-1933 when sold to the Owen brothers, and Thayer Magic Studio in Hollywood 1933-1942 when sold to Bill Larsen and retired. IBM member #248 (1923). SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote several booklets. Bio is included in Richard Buffum, "Keep the wheels turning..." (1977) & Les & Gertrude Smith, "Keep the wheels turning...", V.2 (1992, 372pp). See Glenn Gravatt, Thayer Quality Magic (4 vols). [St]

name: Thelmo
bio: See: "Sterling, Harold"

name: Theobald, J. D[azley]
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s-90s) Dealer (J. Theobald & Company) in London since c1840 in electrical goods, model steamboats and engines, etc., added conjuring apparatus by 1877 when reported by Hoffmann and at least up to 1894, the year of its last dated catalog. Wrote Amateur Experimentalist (1876, 30pp) & The Amateur Magician (nd, 31pp). And as Prof J.D. Theobald wrote Magic and Its Mysteries (1880, 144pp). [Daw94, 33-34]; TS#2,73; Magic7/03]

name: Theodore, Phillip
bio: (England: 18 Jun 1962-28 Jul 1987) Pro magician, clown, & mime. 1979 Young Magician of the Year (in Britain). [Daw2]

name: Thielemann, Hanns
bio: (Nossen, near Meissen, Germany: 3 Apr 1911-6 May 1986) Awarded the "Dr Teumer-Ring" 1968-70. Died in Meissen, East Germany. [Roh]

name: Thiels, [Victor-] Norbert
bio: (France: 7 Aug 1855-25 Feb 1925) Pro comedy magician. Co-founder in 1903 of the ASAP. [St]

name: Thiery, Harry
bio: (Venlo, Holland: 3 Oct 1936-) Pro. Under own name works as manipulator. As "Di Sato" does a sorcerer act. 1967 FISM Grand Prix. [Win;Dif]

name: Thigpen, Dr. Corbett H., M.D.
bio: (Macon, Georgia: 1919-19 Mar 1999). Psychiatrist. Co-author (with his mentor Dr. Hervey M. Cleckley) of the best-selling Three Faces of Eve (1957), one of the classic works on Multiple Personality Disorder. Retired in 1987 as Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at the Medical College of Georgia. Put himself thru college and medical school by performing as a magician and hypnotist. Also did Annie Abbott type tricks.

name: Thimblini
bio: (USA: -dead by 1945) Stage name of Irving Garfinkel. Minor pro, having begun demoing for Lou Tannen. Pet routine: sponge balls. Died in plane explosion over England.

name: Thom, Fred van
bio: (Kiel, Germany: 28 Nov 1934-) Stage name of Friedrich Thomsen. Pro magician. MZvD 1975 2nd prize in manip; 1978 1st prize in manip; 1986 Kalanag-Gedächnis-Ring. [Roh;Nad]

name: Thoma, Emil
bio: (Germany: 27 Mar 1893-20 Jul 1968) Bookseller in Munich. Prominent amateur magician. Aka "Ma-Tho". MZvD President 1949-52. 1953 Grand Prix of the Spanish 2nd National Congress. [St;Al]

name: Thomas
bio: (Germany?: 13 Oct 19-) Stage name of Thomas Oechsner. 1984 MZvD 3rd prize in manip; 1987 MZvD 1st prize in kids magic. [Nad]

name: Thomas, Capt.
bio: (Britain: fl.1860s) Pro. Taught Charles Andress. "Thomas, Professor" SEE: "Cardini" "Thomas the Magician" SEE: Hendricks, Thom

name: Thomas, Alexander
bio: (New York City, NY: 31 October 1952- ) Stage name, aka "Phineas Wyniama". Pro since age 20, originally straight magic. Now, as "Alexander Thomas" specialized in mentalism, séance, & psychic magic. Also lectures & works as psychic consultant. Student of Slydini. Authored Initiations: A Viewpoint on the Art of Cold Reading (1989, booklet+audio). [Wh2]

name: Thomas, Phil[ip Theodore] "Yogi
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: c1912-2 Jul 1998) Inspired as boy by church minister showing coin tricks. Lessons in teens from Ernest Marx. Bought & sold magic from his home in Baltimore 1927-35. Early mentor of Melbourne Christopher. Then pro magic shop dealer (Yogi Magic Mart) in Baltimore 1935-86, then briefly in Ellicott City. In 1990s with wife Ann managed a clown & magicians entertaining service in Baltimore. Trick in HMM. [Se;Albo95,pp31,57-58]

name: Thomas, Stanley, MIMC
bio: (England: c1904-3 Sep 1977) Semi-pro. Chinese act as "Lao Tang". British Ring Shield. Collected antique props. [Daw2]

name: Thompson, Frank
bio: (USA: -1976) Pro gambler. Amateur card & coin magician. See Ray Goulet, Frank Thompson's The Cold Deck (1976, 10pp).

name: Thompson Jr, J[ames] G[ilfillan] "Jim
bio: (Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania: 13 Mar 1910-1975) Inspired at age 12 watching Ed Reno. Learned from Gilbert Mysto Magic set & lessons from Charles Dietric. Banker in Middleburg, Penn. Amateur mental magician. Prolific author. Wrote 'My Best' (1945, 384pp; repr 1959; etc), Telastrophy (1954, 5pp), Top Secrets of Magic (3 vols, 1956-68, 380pp), Card Party (1965, 70pp, with Ned Rutledge), Between Two Minds (1967, 75pp, with Ned Rutledge), Magic to Delight (1970, 124pp), The Living End (1972, 165pp), Sleight Intended (1973, 64pp), & The Miracle Makers (1975, 306pp). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, New Phoenix, New Jinx, MUM, Pallbearers. Book reviewer for Linking Ring. Ghosted the trick attributed to Harold Lloyd in Jinx #51. [Th]

name: Thompson, James C[ater] "Jimmy
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 1889-1972) Aka "Kater Thompson" & "James Kater". Pro in vaude & Chautauqua until became booking agent, continuing as a prominent amateur cardman. Co-authored (with George DeLawrence) Modern Card Tricks and How to Do Them (1920, 80pp). [Pr;Dor]

name: Thompson, John [Max] "Johnny
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 27 Jul 1934) Born of Polish-Sicilian father & Irish-Polish mother named Lankowski. Adopted at early age by the Thompsons. Learned around age 8 from a Mysto Magic set & reading Erdnase. Debut at age 12 at amusement park. Pro close-up & stage.
