Works stage as "The Great Tomsoni & Company", the "Company" being his assistant-wife Pamela "Pam" Hayes. 1977 & 1982 AMA Stage Magician of the Year. 1986 AMA Performing Fellowship. Introduced a "Thurston" pastiche act at 1989 IBM Convention. AMA Board of Directors 1990-93. 1992 Dragon Award with Pam. Authored (edited & ghosted by Jeff Busby), Polished Polish Prestidigitation (1981, 39pp). See Jeff Busby, The Coin in Bottle--Plus (1982, 19pp). Trick in Epoptica. 3 videos (1987, 1988, 1988). [Bo#274;Jef;HC;MC;Wat;Wh]

name: Thompson, Kenna [Chris] [pronounced KEEN-ah]
bio: (Louisville, Kentucky: 4 Aug 1959- ) Learned at age 5 from demo of magic sets for Xmas. Pro general magic. Partner (replacing Alan Milan) Sep 1985-Nov 1990 in Venture III in Milford, Ohio, where he was full-time manager & writer-photographer of the shop's catalogs. Since Dec 1990 proprietor of KT Magic mail-order antique & collectable magic in Independence (then Hebron), Kentucky. Writing a book on Eddy Taytelbaum. [Wh5]

name: Thompson, Pam[ela]
bio: (Ridgewood, New Jersey: 4 Oct 1936-) Born Pamela Hayes. Model in New York City, then as "Pam Hayes" a Hollywood actress. Married John Thompson in 1973, joining his comedy stage magic act in 1976 as "The Great Tomsoni & Company", she being the "& Company". 1992 Dragon Award with John. [Wh]

name: Thompson, Robert H.
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 20 Dec 1899-) Semi-pro.[Go2]

name: Thoni, Hans Arnold
bio: (Interlaken, Berne, Switzerland: 20 Jul 1874-22 Mar 1935) Aka "As-Thy" & "Tho-Khim". Pro. [Dif]

name: Thor
bio: See: Stadelman, Paul

name: Thorborn
bio: (Sweden?: 1871-1948) Stage name of Leopold Sandström. Pro manipulator. NOTE: Dif reports him as a Swedish magician, Nilsson says that can't be. [Dif]

name: Thorn, Ernest
bio: (Jaroslau, Galicia, Austro-Hungarian Empire [now Jarosław, Poland]: 23 Sep 1853 - 20 May 1928) Stage name of Moses Abraham Thorn. Of Polish [sic]-Jewish parentage. Inspired at age 12 seeing St. Roman. Learned at age 14 assisting Henry "Cagliostro" Smith in Vienna and, later, Samuel Bellachini. Pro stage illusionist with brother Heinrich 1872-85 as "Chevalier Thorn & Chevalier Darwin [also "Darvin"], the Royal Illusionists". They toured the world 1878-79 & USA 1879-85. Thence on own, Ernest toured Europe 1885-1908 & S. America (Montevideo, Buenos Aires, & Rio de Janeiro) 1908, returning to Europe in October. Played London & Helsinki in 1912. His wife-assistant Julia died in 1918. Selling his big show to Kassner, he retired c1920 to Leipzig where he later died in poverty, a suicide. Invented Vanishing Horse (by 1885 with brother Heinrich), Noah's Ark (c1894), The Hammock = Avatar (1904), etc. Several of his tricks & illusions were marketed by Conradi-Horster. [Vo57;Dam;Dif;St;Pr;Wal;Win;Passez Muscade#21; Magic6/04,11/04]

name: Thorn, Heinrich
bio: (Austria: fl.1870s-90s) Pro. As "Chevalier Darwin" (also "Darvin") toured the world with brother Ernest Thorn 1872-1885 [sic] when Heinrich remained in the USA. Retired in Leipzig c1923. Co-invented (with Ernest) the Vanishing Horse (by 1885).

name: Thornton, Harold Edmund
bio: (Croydon, Surrey, England: 28 Mar 1903-) Semi-pro. [Go2]

name: Thornton, Jesse "Jess
bio: (USA?: -died 1940s) Stage name of James D. Taylor. Pro. Billed as "Tick Tock Moments", he did a Gus Fowler-type all-watch act in vaude in the 1930s. Later joined Abbott's as a mechanic-inventor. Invented Checko (by 1940), DI-IT (by 1940), Sympathetic Napkin Rings (by 1940), The Hand of the Caliph (by 1947), & The Caliph's Card Castle (by 1947). [Tay]

name: Thornton, John N.
bio: (USA: -1954) Resident of New Haven, Connecticut. Invented the Thornton Reel (by 1908). Retired some years before his death.

name: Thornton, John Stanley
bio: (Croydon, Sun Jun 1907- Self-tarles in Abra,

name: Thornton, Larry [Carl]
bio: (Orillia, Ontario, Canada: 10 Jun 1946- ) Learned at age 9 from library books. Draftsman in Calgary. Semi-pro kid-show magician since 1979. Collector of non-commercial films & videos of magicians (pros & amateurs) in performance. Has 16 hours on film & 120 hours on VHS videotape. Wrote The Movie Magic Files [1977], an early catalog of his collection. [Wh]

name: Thot
bio: (Geneva, Switzerland: 1908-) Stage name of Robert Ehinger. Pro magician & ventriloquist beginning in WW II. Presented illusions, the Inexhautible Hat, the Magic Bar, rag pictures. Inspired such ventriloquists as Fred Roby, Daniel Rémy, & Jean de Merry.

name: Thrasher, Robert [Grafton] "Bob
bio: (Kewanee, Illinois: 13 Apr 1908-5 May 1995) Sleight-of-hand artist since 1926. 1928 IBM Convention 1st place in manip (with balls). Pet effects: watch manip routine (since 1928) & C&R Rope tricks. Pro 1931-33 with club shows. Thence pro in industry. Articles in Linking Ring & Seven Circles. [WWM] Thumm, Manfred [Ernst] [pronounced TOOM] (Freiburg, Germany: 3 Jul 1933-) Learned at age 15 by performing with brother Rudi. Originally a sales manager with Phillips GmbH. Semi-pro magician since 1964. 1967 FISM 1st prize in illusion & 2nd prize in invention. Did his prize-winning Black Light act billed as "the magic hands" 1964-84. Also a general magic act as "Gordon & Eve" 1966-80. Pro magic dealer since 1973 as founder of "the magic hands" in Herrenberg, West Germany. Since 1978 his firm sponsors the annual "the magic hands Fachkongress" convention in Böblingen & later Sindelfingen. 1985 AMA Award of Merit. 1992 MZvD "Ehrenring" [Honor Ring]. [MUM7/93;Wh2]

name: Thureo, Oswald
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 13 Mar 1898-11 Oct 1983) Stage name of Ture Berg. Salesman. Taught magic by Robert Nordström. Semi-pro magician.

name: Thursby, [Anthony P.] "Tony
bio: (Dublin, Ireland: fl.1970s-90s) Aka "deReski". Pro manipulator & dealer (Banshee Magic shop) in Dublin.

name: Thursday, John
bio: See: Legman, Gershon

name: Thurston, Harry
bio: (Columbus, Ohio?: c1868-7 Mar 1941) Older brother of Howard Thurston. Operated a carnival illusion show in early years, then an advance man for Ringling Brothers Circus. Moved to Chicago where for 20 years he ran a grind carnival show on South State Street where he was deeply involved in local ward politics. Briefly turned pro illusionist, taking a troupe on the road under canvas 1931-33 & 1935. Then returned to Chicago to personally run a peep show where, among others, a teenage Bob Lund admits that at a dime every 30 seconds he satisfied some of his "considerable curiosity about the profound mysteries of female anatomy." Wealthy, he financed brother Howard in the latter's final years, owning most of the show. In 1938 illusionist Will Rock bought all of Harry's props. Retired to West Palm Beach, Florida, where he died. Much bio material is in George L. Boston & Robert Parrish, Inside Magic (1947), 27-60, 75-76. [St;Pr;Ch;LR7/95]

name: Thurston, Howard [Franklin]
bio: (Columbus, Ohio: 20 Jul 1869 [sic]-13 Apr 1936) Learned from a magic set given him c1888 by Ernest Marx's father. Pro cardman & illusionist by 1898. Toured England (1900-01), the Continent, USA (1902), Paris (1902), & London (1903). Then in 1905 began a world tour that covered Australia (1905), Fiji Islands, New Zealand, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Japan, Cochin-China, Singapore, Java, Sumatra, Burma, & India, returning to the USA in 1907. Kellar named him his successor in 1908. In 1918 became first magician to have a face-lift. SAM President 1927-29. Played his last full-evening show on 20 Apr 1931 at the Tremont Theatre in Boston. Thence did a shortened vaudeville act. In his time, the most famous magician in North America. Authored Howard Thurston's Card Tricks (London: 1901, 83pp, ghosted by W.J. Hilliar; repr 1903), Fifty New Card Tricks (1905), 100 Tricks Which You Can Do (1912, 112pp), 200 Tricks You Can Do (1926, ghosted by Walter Gibson), 200 More Tricks You Can Do (1927, 187pp, ghosted by Walter Gibson), & Fooling Millions (1928, 96pp). Fictionalized autobio (ghosted by J.N. Hilliard & Walter Gibson) is My Life of Magic (1929, 275pp), reprinted with Jane Thurston's memoir as Our Life of Magic (1989, 224pp). Bios are Robert E. Olson, The World's Greatest Magician: A Tribute to Howard Thurston (1981); & Robert E. Olson, The Complete Life of Howard Franklin Thurston (1993, 2 vols, forthcoming). See also T.C. Worthington, Recollections of Howard Thurston: Conjurer, Illusionist and Author (1938, 31pp); Thurston Scrapbook: Grace Thurston Manuscript (1985, 184pp); & Howard Thurston's Illusion Show Work Book (1991). His lengthy & revealing correspondence with Dante (340 letters 1922-35) was reprinted by Phil Temple (compiler) as the Thurston-Dante Letter Set (1981, 475pp). [Pr;Han;Genii8/91;MUM12/90;Wal;Bam pp23-36;Bo#164;Bo#208;Gi;Tay;Ho;WWWA]

name: Thurston, Jane [Jacqueline]
bio: (Weehawken, New Jersey: 24 Jul 1909-12 Nov 1994) Daughter of Mrs Nina Leotha Fielding Allison (died 1934). Legally adopted by Howard Thurston after his marriage (his 3rd) to Mrs Fielding in 1914. Learned growing up with Thurston & in the late 1920s by coaching from Cyril Yettmah & Herman Hanson. Pro from 1928 when she made debut as co-star in Thurston show. Left magic in 1938. After brief career as singer & dancer, married US Navy officer (and magic buff) Richard D[aniels] Shepard (died 1993) and settled in southern California. 1981 AMA Special Fellowship. Died in Holmes Beach, Florida. Her memoirs are in Our Magic Life (1989). [Bo#289:Bo#208:Han:Pr:Wh2]

name: Tibbles, S[idney] C.
bio: (Hampstead, London, England: c1880-) Elder brother of "P.T. Selbit". Pro graphic artist since age 16 when left school. Signing his work "S.C.T." he became a leading illustrator (in art nouveau style) of magic books & periodicals, including Hilliar's Novel Hand Shadows (1900), Howard Thurston's Card Tricks (1901), Tricks magazine (1901), Selbit's The Magician's Handbook (1901), Selbit's The Magical Entertainer (1906), & The Wizard magazine (1905-1910).

name: Tiden, Frederick [L. B.]
bio: (USA: 26 May 1877-12 Nov 1931) Stage actor. In 1922 at Times Square Theatre as star of play The Charlatan, performed magic (coached by Guy Jarrett), including his own version of Growth of Flowers, baffling Tarbell. Admitted to the SAM (#961). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Tilden".

name: Tigner, Steven S [amuel] "Steve
bio: (Potsdam, New York: 10 Dec 1939-) Professor of Philosophy at U of Toledo. Amateur magician & magic historian. Operated mail-order Tigner Magic Supply Company 1973-80, which eventually specialized in printed matter of historical interest. Wrote Sleight of Hand with Chalk (1973, 36pp). Edited Bulletin for Friends of Magic History 1976-78 & The Journal of Magic History 1979-80. Articles in both previous journals plus in MUM, Linking Ring, & Magicol. Also article "Magic and Magicians" in Handbook of American Popular Culture (Rev. ed 1989). [Wh2]

name: Tihany
bio: (Ketegyhaza, Hungary: 29 Jun 1916-) Stage name of Franz Czeisler since 1936. Learned in Europe as an orphan boy by tuition from Alfred "Alfredo Uferini" Ufer & then assisting Blacaman. Learned pick-pocketing watching Dr Giovanni. Promental magic (as "Fakir Sanda Ruh"); then illusions. Moved to Brazil in 1952 or 53 to work in the Circo Romana. In 1955 founded his own 4,000-seat Circo Tihany, featuring his magic & one of the world's more successful tent-shows. 1978 AMA Performing Fellowship. Closed his show in 1984 & retired to Florida. Rebuilt his show in 1985 in Mexico. 1987 AMA Masters Fellowship. Circus Tihany began its planned 2-year tour of the USA on 29 Sep 1989 in Houston, carrying a staff of 200 & a 4,000-seat tent. But the costs were too high so Tihany moved his circus back to Mexico in 1990 where it has continued (at least until 1993). ABC-TV & CBS-TV bits in 1989.

name: Tihany Jr.
bio: (Romania: 21 May 1936-) Stage name of Ludwig Czeisler. Learned assisting father. Pro illusionist, alternating with his father as star in the Circo Tihany in Brazil until it closed in 1984.

name: Tilden" [misspelling]
bio: See: Tiden, Frederick

name: Tilford, Douglas L[ee] "Doug
bio: (Cincinnati, Ohio: 20 Jul 1944-) Inspired as child seeing Blackstone show. Learned from tricks bought at Haines House of Cards. Semi-pro performer since age 14. Marketing Instructor at Griffin Technical Institute. Dealer in quality illusions & apparatus since 1978 in Experiment, Georgia, and then Daytona Beach Shores, Florida. Collector of antique apparatus. [Wh]

name: Tillar, Jack Kent
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 1930-) Professional music composer & arranger. Amateur magician, having been inspired by Fitzkee's The Trick Brain & the Tarbell Course. Invented Blister in 1972. Articles in Talisman.

name: Timmerman, Theo
bio: (Holland: -dead) Prop maker in Emmerloord, Holland, in early 1980s.

name: Tiong, Phoa Yan
bio: (Indochina: fl.1960s-80s) Resident of Holland. Pro. Author. [Des]

name: Tipton, Allen
bio: (Cradley Heath, Worcestershire, UK: 27 Nov 1932 - ) Pro Drama & Theatre tutor, has been an actor, director, choreographer & adjudicator. Coached & taught several major British stars. He became a magician at age 9, joining Staffs. Magical Society at 14. Is Honorary Life Member & Past President (8 times) of the Guild of Magicians and was made 'Magician Of the Month' by the IBM in 1980 for his reproduction of Dante the illusionist's Sim Sala Bim full length evening show. In 1950 appeared as ventriloquist on Hughie Green's Opportunity Knocks. Wrote several series: “Dear Magician” for Abracadabra.

name: Tischer, Heinrich
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 10 Sep 1851-16 Jan 1928) Pro of the old school. Aka "Mällini". Father of Karl Tischer. [Vo56]

name: Tischer, Karl
bio: (Germany: 1874-27 Jul 1925) Son of Heinrich Tischer. Pro. [Vo56]

name: Titus, Franz
bio: (Germany: fl. 1890s) Stage name of Franz Streissler. Wrote Neues Zauberbuch (1900, 95pp).

name: Tobin, Thomas William
bio: (Britain: fl.1850s-70s) Mechanic working as Secretary of the Royal Polytechnic Institution in London. Invented Sphinx (1864) & Palingenesia (1872).

name: Toch, Dr. Maximillian [pronounced TOKE]
bio: (New York City, NY: 17 Jul 1864-26 May 1946) Chemist & paint manufacturer in New York City. In charge of US Navy camouflage in WW I. Invented Toch system of camouflage. Amateur magician. SAM member #465. Invented several effects based on chemistry or physics. [WWM; WWWA]

name: Tocquet, Robert
bio: (France: fl.1950s-70s) Amateur magician & psychic investigator. Wrote many books on the paranormal, including Tout l'occultisme dévoilé (1952) & Les pouvoirs secrets de l'homme (1971). And 2 books on magic: Les tours de cartes à la portée de tous (1977) & La prestidigitation à la portée de tous (1977).

name: Todd Brothers
bio: (USA: fl.early 1900s) Minor pros in Philadelphia. Invented Creo=Vampire illusion.

name: Tokar, Scott
bio: (Whittier, California: 13 Aug 1965- ) Stage name of Scott Chester Tokarzewski. Learned at age 7 from magic set. Did kid shows at age 12. Pro close-up, working clubs & trade shows since 1984. Pet effects: Watch Steal & Floating Bill. 1986 Magic Castle Junior Achievement Award. 1988 IBM 1st Prize for close-up. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Tolmaque, Herr
bio: (France: fl.1870s-80s) Pro with a Spirit Cabinet exposé act in Europe & Australia (1875 & 1882) where he died sometime before 1910. [Wal;Cl]

name: Tomaso
bio: See: Arienzo, Tommaso

name: Tommsen, Jersey
bio: See: Derner, Adolf

name: Tommy mit der Zauberkiste
bio: (Germany: 12 Dec 1949-) Stage name (meaning Tommy with the Magic Box) of Wolfgang Brenzinger. 1981 & 1984 MZvD 1st prizes for kid magic. [Nad] "Tomsoni & Company, The Great" SEE: Thompson, John & Thompson, Pam

name: Tong, Dan[iel Fredrick] "Danny
bio: (Plymouth, Massachusetts: 1 May 1937-) Of English extraction. Inspired in 1953 by seeing 2 magi in school. Learned from library books. Assistant to Bernard "Fu Ling" Whitman 1954-55. Semi-pro close-up as "Danny Tong", then as "Dan Tong". Also as mentalist "Danton" since 1957. Has also worked cruise ships & banquets with assistant-wife Pauline as "The Dantons". Performed in USA, Canada, Mexico, Hawaii, & Far East. Lecturer since 1963. Full-time pro performer since 1974. Pet publicity stunt: Blindfold Drive. Prop maker-dealer as "TDC Products" in Port Charlotte, Florida. Wrote Lecture (1963, 10pp), Dan Tong's Close-Up Magic (1982), Restaurant and Table Magic (11pp), & Dan Tong's ESP (1982). Tricks in New Phoenix, New Jinx, Linking Ring, Pallbearers Review, Epilogue, Ibidem, Magick, Blueprint, Magic Manuscript, Mortimer's Magic Magazine, & MUM. TV & radio bits. [MUM11/95;NJ#11;Wh2]

name: Tong-Billy
bio: (Lisbon, Portugal: 24 Dec 1940-) Stage name of José Maria MARTINS. Taught by Bucheli in Spain. Minor pro mentalist & hypnotist. [Cam] NOTE: An early report that he appeared in Spanish film Pecato y Amor (1960) is false.

name: Tony
bio: See: Reisner, Tony

name: Tony, Henry
bio: (Alcarvá, Portugal: 29 Jul 1925-1987) Stage name of António de São José PROENÇA. Pro illusionist with circus. [Cam]

name: Toole Stott, Raymond, MBE, AIMC
bio: (England: 25 Nov 1903-10 Jan 1982) Ex-librarian. Freelance journalist. Amateur bibliographer. Compiled the superb A Bibliography of English Conjuring, 1581-1876 (2 vols, 1976, 1978). Also wrote the definitive Circus and Allied Arts: A World Bibliography (4 vols, 1958-71). Also wrote the definitive Somerset Maugham bibliography.

name: Topas
bio: (Stuttgart, West Germany: 20 Jul 1972-) Stage name of Thomas Fröschle. Amateur by age 15. 1988 FISM 2nd prize in manip. 1989 Christopher Award. 1991 FISM 1st prize in manip.

name: Töpfer, Professor Carl
bio: (Germany: -22 Aug 1871) Stage dramatist in Hamburg in 1840s when he befriended Alexander Heimbürger. Pro illusionist working in Germany in 1850s. Died in Hamburg.

name: Torell, Jan
bio:
(Lübeck, Germany: 14 Jun 1935-) Stage name of Gerrit Schnepel, of Dutch parentage. Learned at age 13. Disciple of Al Torsten. Pro stage magic with jumbo card, silk, & dice effects. At age 23 won MZvD Grand Prix at Baden-Baden. 1973 FISM 3rd prize in general magic; 1975 MZvD 1st prize in general magic; 1976 FISM 2nd prize in general magic. Wrote Magic by Jan Torell (Germany: 1975, 30pp).

[See also: Nielsen, Leo]

name: Torello, Max
bio: (Eskilstuna, Sweden: 11 Oct 1917-22 Dec 1986) Stage name of Tore Jensen. Pro in Stockholm with a miscellaneous act. 1974 Nordic Magic Convention's Knight of Magic.

name: Toreno
bio: (Norway: 16 Nov 1937-) Stage name of Tore Fredriksen. Pro stage magician. NMK Nordic Champion 1964. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1966 & 1971. 1973 FISM 1st prize in general magic. 1975 Baden-Baden 3rd prize. [NT1/66;Dif]

name: Torino, Señor
bio: See: Kardyro, Tony

name: Torkova, [Robert]
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 13 Oct 1956-) Learned at age 7 from father & uncle. Pro since 1980 with silent act of classical stage magic. Pet effects: Cone & Ball and Egg on Fan. House magician at Mostly Magic in New York City since 1984. 1986 Back Stage's Bistro Award & 1997 Christopher Award as Most Promising Newcomer. Collector & historian, particularly of Germain. Article in Magicol. [Wh2]

name: Tornedo, Carlo
bio: (Göteborg, Sweden: 19 Jun 1926- ) Stage name of Karl-Ewert Forsberg. Pro manip with cards, balls, & cigarettes since 1948. Also illusions. Stockholm Magic Convention Grand Prix 1949, 1950, 1951, 1952, 1953. FISM 1st prize in manip 1950. Played the Lisbon Coliseu 1956. As "Los Tornedos" with his Brazilian-born assistant-wife Meta (née de Sota) who also did a spirit cabinet bit. Since 1962 a booking agent in Europe (for Lena Horn, Johnny Ray, Victor Borge, & magicians Marvyn Roy & Johnny Hart, etc). [NT1/89;Dif;St]

name: Torrent, Edd
bio: (Manila, Philippines: 15 Oct 1936- ) Stage name of Edgardo Cabrera Torrente since 1977. Born into a family of magicians, he was taught magic by his father in 1953 (at age 17). Commercial photo-grapher. Part-time pro stage & parlor magician since 1957. Active in various aspects of the Filipino entertainment world. [Wh2]

name: Torresen, Roy
bio: (Brooklyn, New York: 30 Jun 1961-) Learned at age 10 from library book. Engineer in Norway. Amateur close-up magician with cards & coins. [Wh2]

name: Torrini
bio: See: de Grisy, Edmond

name: Torrini, Antonio
bio: (Rome?, Italy: c1784-) Opera tenor around 1802 when he met Count Edmond de Grisy, becoming his brother-in-law and principal assistant until the latter's death in 1829. Torrini then toured France on his own as magician "Signor Torrini" but, unsuccessful, soon retired from magic, moving to Paris where he gave singing lessons. His bio appears in Robert-Houdin's autobiography, the sole proven source on this man.

name: Torsberg, [J.] Vic[tor]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 14 Jul 1906-24 Dec 1979) Pro. Backstage assistant with Harry Thurston show 1932. Worked in Chicago for National Magic in 1936-1940s and for Ireland Magic in 1961. Worked a black-art act in 1950s as "Charlie Chan". Edited local Magic Masters' club bulletin Spook 1959-72. NOTE: Surname sometimes misspelled "Thorsberg". [Genii2/80; Bos]

name: Torsten, Al
bio: (Tula, Russia: 24 Feb 1917- ) Stage name of Alexander Franz Simoneit. Moved to Königsberg, East Prussia, before WW II. In German Army during the war. After the war, moved to Lübeck, West Germany, where he turned pro illusionist & manipulator. Mentor of Marvelli Jr & Jan Torell. Moved to Chicago, USA, in 1955. Columnist for Magie in 1980s. [LR10/58; Win; St]

name: Tosari
bio: (Wurzelsdorf, Germany [now Koßenov, Czech Republic]: 19 May 1898-11 Dec 1967) Stage name of Hans Hander. Student of Rodolfo & friend of Fredo Marvelli. Pro manip on own since 1924. Rated a "Half-Jew" by the Nazis he was limited to playing minor venues. Played a Warsaw cabaret 1942-43. In East Germany after the war. Awarded the "Dr Teumer-Ring" in 1967. Died in Dresden. [Win]

name: Toscaní
bio: (Poland: fl.1740s) Pro magician & showman. At Paris fairs 1744-48 exhibiting a theater of automata, including a miniature conjuror that did several tricks.

name: Towne, Stuart
bio: See: Rawson, Clayton

name: Towner, [Robert] Harland (formerly "Torchy")
bio: (Los Angeles, California: fl.1940s-90s) Aka "Torchy Towner", "The Great Rinaldi", & "The Wizard Harland". Studied acting in New York as a young man. Pro illusionist & fire-eater. Assistant to Virgil for 2 years in USA in late 1940s & in Far East in early 1950s. Toured RKO circuit in late 1950s as assistant with John Daniel's spook show. With "The Magic Land of Allakazam" TV series 1961-65 as "Evilo", the bad-guy wizard. Worked at Owen Brothers. Retired to Mt. Shasta c1977, specializing in the psychology of magic. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Harlen". [Mag;Walk;Wh]

name: Tracy, C[harles] R. "Bud
bio: (USA: c1896-1 Sep 1989) Pen name of "Bud" Raymond. Amateur. Magic historian & collector of magic books in Sioux City, Iowa, who retired to Florida. An authority on T. Nelson Downs, selling much of his collection to Warren Wexler. Wrote Directory of Magicians (1951, 312+68pp).

name: Traphagen, William H.
bio: (USA: 12 Apr 1867-22 Feb 1945) SAM Member #159. Aka "Kelmar".

name: Traub, Jules
bio: (USA?: fl.1930s-50s) As "Stuart Jules" was a minor pro magician. Dealer as owner of a magic shop in the New Yorker hotel in Manhattan. Then moved to Chicago under own name as owner of Fun, Inc, the USA's 2nd largest maker-wholesaler of novelties, until 1949 when he went partners with S.S. Adams in New Jersey.

name: Travers, Roland
bio: (USA: 1891-1970) Learned assisting Adelaide Herrmann until 1901, then on own as minor pro illusionist. [CMM5/08]

name: Trawanhore
bio: (Poland: fl.1930s) Stage name (from the Indian city of Travancore) of Kaszubowski. Minor pro illusionist & fakir, playing circuses & movie theaters in gaudy Hindu costume until 1939.

name: Tréborix
bio: (France: 1894-31 Oct 1982) Stage name of Robert Olivaux. Pro. Charter member in 1933 of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Nantes. AFAP Master Magician. Wrote L'A.B.C. de la mnémotechnie (1938); & Fantasies avec des à Jouer [1948], English tr by Victor Peacock as Diversions with Dice (1953 tr, 39pp). Memoir is La Boîte à récréations du Grand-Père à barbe [1961]. [Bou2] "Tree, Mr. and Miss" SEE: Tree, Leo & Tree, Myra

name: Tree, Leo
bio: (Portsea Town, England: 4 Apr 1884-11 Nov 1957) Stage name of William John Atkins (bastard son of Ellen Atkins) since 1922. Devised his own telepathic code at age ten. Pro two-person telepathy act, first in England & South Africa as the "Wesmar Brothers" (with a non-relative named Arthur) until 1915. Going to Australia he met musician "Myra Peers" (Myra Shacklock) in 1917, working with her since 1922 as "Mr. and Miss Tree" (they married in 1923). They then toured England 1924-49 when they moved permanently to Australia where they continued their act until his death. [Pr;Wal]

name: Tree, Myra
bio: (Brighton, England: -1974) Stage name of Myra Victoria Shacklock [sic], aka "Myra Pvaschkevicht". Married Leo Tree in 1923 with whom she did a two-person mind-reading act until retired in 1957. [Pr]

name: Tremaine, Jon
bio: (London, England: 26 Mar 1936-) Also as childrens magician as "Jon Day".....Did some ghost-writing for Corinda. [Wh5]

name: Tremlett, Douglas John "Doug
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 13 May 1955-) Since 1979 pro actor, director, producer, & magician in theater. As "Wally" was on TV for 2 years. Pet effects: Dancing Hank, Floating Ball, Black Art routines. Wrote Wally's Book of Sneaky Stunts, Party Tricks & Puzzles (1986, 80pp). Trick in Genii. [Wh5]

name: Trepel, Jack F.
bio: (Ripley, Indiana: 25 Dec 1886 [not 1896]- ) Florist at Radio City in New York. Amateur magician by 1909 when joined the SAM. As mentalist often worked a 2-person telepathy act with wife Mary. Trick in Genii. [Th;SAM]

name: Trewey, Félicien
bio: (Angoulême, Charente, France: 23 May 1848-2 Dec 1920) Stage name of Félicien Trevey. Inspired at age 7 seeing circus magician in Marseilles. Learned magic at age 15 assisting carnival troupe. Pro shadowist, chapeaugraphist, mime, juggler, & magician. Popular in London where he played the Empire in 1897 for several months & the Alhambra 1885-86 for 14 months. ..... Wrote Shadowgraphy: How it's Done (1893, 21pp), The Art of Shadowgraphy (1905), Papier Multiforme (1913), & Comment cela se fait [on hand shadows] (n.d.). Bio is Henri Colombon, Trewey, Premier Shadowgraphiste, mime, et comédien (France: 1909). Silent movie of his chapeaugraphy act (1896). See J.G. Hamley, The Act of Chapeaugraphy as Performed by the late Monsieur Trewey (1922). [Pr;Vo55;Go2;Bar] Tribini, Prof.(Denmark: 25 Aug 1915-13 Nov 1973) Stage name of Christian Jørgen Nielsen. Debut in 1931. Pro comedy magician & illusionist. With Cirkus Royal in Denmark 1940. Then at Bakken park, Copenhagen, as magic buffoon doing 12-14 shows daily in tent with his own troupe of variety artists until retired in 1971. [Dif]

name: Trick, Dany
bio: See: Cudennec, Daniel

name: Trikson
bio: See: Ackermann, Georg (his father)

name: Trimble, Jimmy
bio: (USA: -1971) Lived in Terra Haute, Indiana. Minor pro club worker with comedy, cards, & ropes 1930s-50s. Co-edited (with Dave Coleman) Presto (1937, 1 issue). Invented Sucker Subway (marketed in 1947) & The J. T. Rapping Skull (marketed by 1947). Tricks in Tops (1940) & Ireland's YB 1953. "Triple Alliance. The" SEE: Fox, Imro & Le Roy, Servais & Powell, F.E. Talma

name: Triplett, Norman
bio: (USA: 1861-1910) Psychologist, having taken his Ph.D. in 1886 from Clark University (Worchester, Mass.) under Prof. G. Stanley Hall, himself an amateur magician. Triplett's dissertation was "The Psychology of Conjuring Deceptions," The American Journal of Psychology, Vol.11, No.4 (Jul 1900), 439-510. Offprint (72pp).

name: Tripp, Mark [Arland]
bio: (Dearborn, Michigan: 8 Apr 1954-) Learned at age 6 from magic set. Pro since age 15 with general magic. Mentors were Karrell Fox & Roy Kissell. World tour with USO 1973-74. Pet effects: 3 Card Monte, Malini Egg Bag, 4-Ring Routine, Professor's Nightmare, & Dancing Cane. Writing series of booklets (forthcoming). Column "Tripp's Tips" in Genii 1986-present. Articles in Genii & Magic Manuscript. TV bits. [Wh2]

name: Tripp, W. Albert
bio: (USA: -late 1919) Magician, expert mechanic, & inventor. Pro dealer in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Then beginning in 1895 with S. Willson Bailey as "Bailey and Tripp Magical Co" in Boston. Although Bailey bought out Tripp after 3 months, the latter's name continued until his death, during which period he still made props for the company. [Albo95; Sphinx7/35; Dor, 77-78]

name: Triscalinus
bio: (France?: fl.late 1500s) After performing before French King Charles IX (reigned 1560-74) he was forced to admit to witchcraft. [Dif;Cl]

name: Trix, Toby
bio: See: Foley, Jean G.

name: Trixer, Hans E., MIMC
bio: (Dortmund, Germany: 26 Jul 1921-23 Sep 1994) Born Hans Eric Elsbach-Trixer, aka "Trixer" since 1938, & now his legally adopted surname. Learned magic in 1936 from Fischer's Das Wunderbuch der Zauberkunst. A Jew, he fled Germany to live in Holland 1939-52, except for period in Nazi concentration camps (where both parents died). Jeweller. Amateur close-up magician. 1949 Dutch Grand Prix. Invented glass "Soap Bubbles" in 1949. MIMC 1949. Moved in 1952 to Zimbabwe where he was a jewellery company director. Edited Triks (Amsterdam) c1950. Wrote ConjuRING Trix and Jardine Ellis Ring Effects (1955, 39pp). Articles in Pentagram, Gen, MUM, Genii, Arcane, & Epoptica. [Thaumaturgist11/94;Wh2]

name: Trnka, Miroslav "Mila
bio: (Plzeň [Pilsen], Czechoslovakia [now Czech Republic]: 28 Jul 1927- ) A respected pro magician in his country. Co-authored (with Pavel) Wie entwickle ich einen neuen Trick? (1964).

name: Troseth, George
bio: (Washington state, USA: c1895-18 Jan 1985) Pro with cards & small illusions. Column in Genii in late 1930s. [WWM]

name: Trost, Nick [K.]
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-90s; died 23 Oct 2008) Mentored by Bob Lewis & studied Hugard & Braue's Royal Road in 1948 [sic]. Pro card magician in Ohio. Invented Hot Dog Card Trick (1978), Kannibal Kards (1981), Mexican Monte (1981), & Fly Circus (1981). Prolific author of bookets, including Nick's Table Trix (1956, 11pp ms), Cardman's Secrets (2 vols, 1964, 25+50pp; repr 1971), & The Card Magic of Nick Trost (1997, 336pp). See Richard Vollmer (compiler-translator), The Very Best of Nick Trost (1983, in French). Tricks in New Phoenix, Linking Ring (Parades in 1955 & 1957), HMM (since 1956), Precursor, & New Tops (column May 1961-Dec 1994).

name: Tröstler, Reinhard
bio: (Germany: 29 May 19-) Magician as "Perkeo". Collector. Dealer in new & used magic books (as "Perkeo Zauber-Literatur" & recently with wife Ruth as "Zauber-Atelier Perkeo") in Etenheim-Münchweier, Germany, in early 1990s. [Nad]

name: Truesdell, John W.
bio: (USA: fl.1850s-80s) Began investigating psychic phenomena in 1856. Wrote the delightfully tongue-in-cheek exposé, The Bottom Facts Concerning the Science of Spiritualism (1883, 331pp). This sceptical citizen of Syracuse, New York, describes his detection of the psychic frauds of Henry Slade (in 1872), Charles H. Foster (1872), and Mrs Mary Hardy (c1876).

name: Truk
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 30 Apr 1918-10 Apr 1989) Stage name of Kurt Hufenbach 1946-56. Pro manipulator since 1946 in West Germany with cards & cigarettes and tricks with ties. Also with assistant-wife Hilde as "Astrid & Truk" 1951-56. Since 1956 was agent for Schmidt playing card company on Munich. Collector of playing cards. Wrote Keysers grosses Buch der Zauberei (1979). Died in Hanover. [Mül]

name: Trump$s Jr.
bio: See: Dick, Harris B.

name: Trunk, Hans
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 10 Nov 1887-1 Jan 1966) Learned magic as a boy. Director of large business firm in Vienna. Amateur sleight-of-hand magician by 1912 when joined the Vienna Magic Club & later became its Vice-President. Student of Ottokar Fischer. Invented Blue Phantom (in 1924), which Fischer marketed. Founding President of breakaway Magische Runde (in Vienna) 1931-38. In 1946 helped reconstitute the Vienna Magic Club, becoming its first post-WW II President. Memoir is Das Trunk Buch: Hans Trunk's Magische Memoiren (Berlin: 1943, 65pp). Wrote Und heute wird gezaubert: Ein magischer Leitfaden für Anfänger (Vienna: 1948, 79pp). Articles in German & English in Magie, etc. [St;Go2]

name: Truxa
bio: (Denmark: 7 Nov 1919- ) Stage name of Eric Kurt Bang. Debut at age 14. Pro, originally as illusionist, then since 1945, with Swedish-born wife Gulli as "medium", a mindreading act that made them the best known magic act throughout Scandinavia, including Finland in 1952. 50 times on radio, 30 on TV. Still performing in 1991. Wrote Trolla med Truxa [Magic with Truxa] (1970, 150pp). [St;Dif]

name: Truzzi, Arturo
bio:
(Bagnolo S. Vito, Mantova, Italy: 5 Jul 1925- ) Amateur in general magic since self-taught in 1955. Active in Italian magic circles. [Wh5]

[See also: Urk, J.]

name: Truzzi, Dr Marcello, PhD
bio: (Copenhagen, Denmark: 6 Sep 1935-2 Feb 2003) Born into an Italian circus family, his father, Massimiliano Truzzi, being one of the more famous jugglers of his time. Brought to USA in 1940. Learned magic from sideshow magician & Punch-&-Judy man Charles Rourke. Psychic researcher since c1968. Doctorate in sociology from Cornell U 1970. Resigned from CSICOP in 1976. Founding editor of Zetetic Scholar 1978-present. Founding Director of the Center for Scientific Anomalies Research in 1981. Co-authored (with Arthur Lyons) The Blue Sense: Psychic Detectives and Crime (1991, 314pp). Died of cancer in Ann Arbor. [Wh]

name: Tschuggmall, Christian Josef
bio: (Venns, Tyrol, Austria: 5 Jan 1785-26 Nov 1865) Major builder & exhibitor of automata. Toured Europe (including Poland & Russia) 1828-45. One automaton was a lively acrobat on a rope that also gave signs in answer to its master's questions. Died in Hesse. His son-in-law, Georges Giulani, showed these pieces in Innsbruck in 1870. Some are preserved in the Puppet Museum in Munich. [Dif;St;Mec]

name: TUCK Quy [also Quay]
bio: (China: fl.1850s) Pro magician-juggler. With "The Chinese Magicians" troupe from Nanking, he toured Hong Kong (1852), the USA (1853), & Britain (1853-54). [Daw#161;Fr]

name: Tucker, Maggie
bio: (Cheshire, England: 18 Apr 1947-) Born Margaret Diedre Bonner, now married to Stephen Tucker. Hand analyst & Rune Stone reader. Part-time pro magicienne until c1980 when turned pro touring England, Dubai, & Malta. Beginning with stage magic (Sawing a Man in Halves), switched to mentalism, & now with close-up, which won 3 prizes in 1989. Invented Limelight. Articles in Chicanery & 1989 LSM Year Book.

name: Tucker, Stephen [Paul Mark] "Steve
bio: (St. Helens [now in Merseyside], Lancs., England: 22 Apr 1958-) A "lapsed Roman Catholic". Learned stacked-card tricks around age 15 from father. Pro close-up magician since c1984, specializing in cards. Lectures, selling his own effects. Invented Mexican Revelation (1983), Nervous Card (1983), Centre of Attraction (1983), Musical Sponge Balls, etc. Since 1986 also does a burlesque mentalism act as "Hughie Gella", with which he won the 1988 British Champion of Mentalism. Other prizes. Married to magicienne Maggie Tucker (née Bonner). Co-edited (with David Britland) Talon 1978-81 and edited Spell-Binder 1981-84, Pabular ?-1985, & Chicanery 1986-88. See also D. Britland & M. Breese (editors), The Best of Spell-Binder: Collection One (1987, 150pp). Wrote 12 booklets 1983-86: from Cardiac Pacemakers (1983, 34pp) & The Gemini Book of Close Up Magik (1983, 73pp) to Thought Waves (1986). Tricks in Magigram, Pabular, Talon, Spell-Binder, Apocalypse, New Directions, Abra, Repro 71, Magic Master (Sweden), Arcane (France), Babel, Sentinel, Scaratica, Magic Manuscript, Genii, etc. 8 videos (1 in 1984, 2 in 1987, 2 in 1988, 3 in 1989). [Wh2]

name: Tucker, [Ellsworth Hosford] "Tommy
bio: (Haverhill, Massachusetts: 29 Mar 1915-5 Feb 1991) Learned at age 12 from a mail order magic course. Pro comedy magic since c1934. Invented Six-Card Repeat in 1936, Blackstone making it world-famous. Married Elizabeth ("Liz" & "Liza") in 1947 with whom did a world-famous 2-person mental act since 1948, touring 23 countries & working trade shows. Founder of Magitronix, which supplies electronic props to magicians. 1987 AMA Performing Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame for both Tommy & Elizabeth. Invented first transitorized trick in 1950s, first tiny matchbox-size voice receiver, & first transistor Jumbo Rising Cards. Audio & video (1985). Articles in MUM, Genii, etc. [Wh2]

name: Tudesco, Travitanto
bio: (Italy?: fl.1630s) Probably a real pro conjuror in London, as reported by Ben Jonson in 1632 in his play The Magnetick Lady.

name: Tuffereau
bio: (France: fl.1860s) Pro in Paris by 1868. (Wanstead, Essex, England: 5 Mar 1922-) Church of England & a Mason. Civil servant since 1939. Amateur magician as "Mystico". Wrote Teach Yourself Conjuring (1954, 182pp; repr USA 1956 as Teach Yourself Magic) & Making Magical Apparatus (1956, 99pp). [CA]

name: Tullock, Eddie
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-90s; died 6 May 2007) Pro trade-show magician since 1937, plausibly the founder of that specialty. In 1971, working only 9 months, he was believed to have earned more money than any other magician in the USA. 1987 AMA Performing Fellowship. Rated among world's top 6 trade-show magicians until retired in the early 1990s. Wrote Tullock: The Real Truth about Trade Show Magic (1996, 64pp, with Gene Urban & Kenton Knepper). NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Tulloch". [LR10/96;Wat] (Belgium: 1 Mar 1914-14 Sep 1985) Amateur historian & bibliographer of magic. Edited Presti (Brussels) 1948-53. In 1950 co-founded (with Klingsor) the Cercle Belge d'Illusionnisme. Co-authored (with Kurt Volkmann) Bibliographie Tummers, [Jean-Jacques-] Louis de la Prestidigitation, Vol.I ("Allemagne et Autriche") (1952, 187pp). Also wrote History of Playing Cards in Belgium (1957). Bought Dalton's (ex-Bouche's) collection of automata, which he later sold to Klingsor. Sold his rather good collection of magic books piecemeal in the early 1970s. Died in Brussels. Tuomivaara, Timo [pronounced TI-moa TWOA-mi-vaah-rah] (Tornio, Finland: 7 Apr 1938-) Son of a Finnish magician. Pro magician & escapist in the Houdini style. In 1976 set a 31.2 second record for straight-jacket escape in Tampere. [Win2;Mec]

name: Tupy, Professor
bio: (Ceará, Brazil: 21 Oct 1906- ) Stage name of Waldemar MENDES FERREIRA. Pro. Toured Brazil extensively, playing theaters & circuses. [Fam]

name: Turmi
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 9 May 1897-1 Mar 1974) Stage name of Erich Tauer. Magician in Germany. Died in Berlin/Neuköln. [Roh;Nad]

name: Turner, Edward
bio: (USA: 1916-) Originally, for 13 years, a circus clown. Then pro magician as "Professor Turner" & "Dr. Thirteen". Later ran a Spook Show. [St]

name: Turner, Richard
bio: (USA: fl.1980s) Pro demonstrator of gambling sleights for which he won the 1982 Las Vegas Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize. [Magische Welt (1981), #6]

name: Turner, W[illiam] O[liver] "Bill
bio: (Tacoma, Washington: 19 Sep 1914- ) Journalist & writer of Western novels. Amateur magician specialized in cards. Wrote Live Magic (ca1940, 24pp, on magic with livestock) & The Card Wizard (1949, 194pp; repr as How to Do Tricks with Cards, 1970, 160pp). [CA;St]

name: Turpin, Dick "Twister
bio: (Britain: c1909-) Inspired seeing a show. Learned in 1930. Pro street magician.

name: Turrini, [Manlio]
bio: (Feltre, Belluno, Italy: 31 Oct 1941-) Learned at age 14 from antique magic books. Ex-teacher of technology. Pro illusionist since 1973. Pet effects: levitations & Sword Box. Invented Turrini's Automatic Levitation in 1984, which won the 1985 FISM 1st prize in grand illusion. [Wh5]

name: Turtle, Professor
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-40s) Pro of the old style "miracle" school. Living in Portland, Oregon, c1930 when he inspired Lee Grabel. Possibly same as William C. Turtle of Waterloo, Iowa, who was a SAM member in 1926.

name: Tut, King
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Stage name of Mel Newsome. Comedy magician with partner Sue Parkinson as "King Tut an'Khamun". They won the 1989 Tom Harris Cup.

name: Twamley, Isaac
bio: (USA: 14 Feb 1849-15 Jun 1934) Stage name of Isaac Twamley. Learned as child. Semi-pro as "Prof. Twamley" in Baltimore. Specialized in small magic. [WWM]

name: Twinn, Sydney
bio: (Britain?: fl.1950s) Wrote The Chinese Linking Rings (1957, 19pp).

name: Tyler, Wilfred
bio: (Reading, England: 11 Oct 1909-22 Jun 1980) Self-taught as a boy. Insurance businessman. Semi-pro kid-show magician. Co-founded (with George Sylvestre) the Cotswold Magic Society in 1943. Edited Meteor 1949 (4 issues). British Ring President 1959-60. Wrote Open Sesame (1947, 154pp, with Eric C. Lewis; repr 1968) & Playing with Magic (1953, 107pp). Column in Hughes' News. Audio. [Le]

name: Tylney, Saxon
bio: (London, England: 12 Aug 1936- ) Learned from books as child. Pro magician since age 18 (1955), originally as assistant to Masoni, then with Levante. Does adult show as "Saxon the Magician" & childrens show as "Wizzo the Wizard". Played Greece each summer 1983-85. [Wh5]

name: Ucker, Brewalt
bio: (Germany: fl.1920s) Anagramatic pen name of Walter Breucken. Amateur in Essen. Wrote Meine Münzentricks (1928, 6+20pp) & Doublings: Der Manipulator als Pickpocket (1928, 20pp).

name: Ueki, Bona
bio: (Tokyo, Japan: 3 Apr 1952- ) Stage name of Yasuyuki UEKI. Learned at age 7 from hobbyist father. Pro comedy stage magician. With partner Parte Koishi as "The Magic Napoleons", known simply as "The Napoleons" since 1986. In 1988 they won the FISM 3rd prize for illusion. With partner did 1 book (1990) & 2 videos (1990). [Wh2]

name: Ufer, Alexander
bio: (Düben an der Mulde, Germany: 6 Feb 1901-1957) Learned assisting father Alfred for 4 years. Pro comedy illusionist. Aka "Alex Uferini" & "Camberry". In WW II in German Army entertaining troops. After the war played 2-months at the Hansa-Theater in Hamburg. [Roh]

name: Ufer, Alfred
bio: (Zeitz, Germany: 12 May 1863-12 Sep 1934) Learned assisting father Friedrich Wilhelm Ufer. Aka "Alfredo Uferini". Pet effect: Vanishing Horse. Taught Tihanyi. Father of Fredy & Arno Ufer. Died in Eidelstadt. [Vo56;Win;Pr]

name: Ufer, Arno
bio: (Cuxhaven, Germany: 2 Sep 1904-14 Sep 1953) Learned magic assisting father Alfred for 4 years. Aka "Arno Uferini". Pro shadowist since 1922 as "Arno Gatti", having been taught by his older brother Henry. Toured Germany with his wife, Marga Häpp, a former famous aerialist. In German Army in WW II. Then toured again with wife until his death in Hamburg. [Vo56;Roh]

name: Ufer, Fredy
bio: (Badeleben, Germany: 30 Oct 1897-1973) Learned assisting father Alfred. Aka "Fredy Uferini". Pro. Retired from stage work in 1935 to become an impresario. [Roh;Pr]

name: Ufer, Friedrich Wilhelm
bio: (Zeitz, Germany: 4 Jan 1838-23 Feb 1904) Son of a miller. Active in local theater group. Learned first card tricks from his mother. His brother-in-law, master shoemaker Paul Rohland, built many of his props. Pro debut in 1866 as "Guillelmo Uferini". Founder of the pseudo-Italian magic dynasty of "Uferini", famous throughout Central Europe. Father of Alfred & Paul Ufer. Father-in-law of Fritz "Boccani" Bock. Died in his hometown. See 100 Jahre Uferini (1950), a 16-page publicity pamphlet outlining the history of the family. [Vo56;Roh;Sal;Win;Pr]

name: Ufer, Henry William
bio: (Ballenstadt, near Hildesheim, Germany: 17 Jul 1895-14 Feb 1949 [sic]) Learned at age 6 assisting father Alfred. Pro. Aka "Henri Uferini", "Cherry", & sometime after 1919, "Wilba, King of Dice" with novel dice tricks. Joined the German Magic Circle (MZ) in 1919 as member #72. Played major theaters in Berlin, Hamburg, Leipzig, Vienna, Paris, & Zürich. In WW II, losing his props in an air raid, "Wilba" rebuilt his act. Enjoyed further success after the war until a stroke ended his career. Died in Hamburg. See Nutje Bumm, Über Wilba, die dritte Generation der Zauber-Dynastie Uferini (1946), an 8-page publicity brochure. [Vo56;Roh;St;Pr]

name: Ufer, Paul
bio: (Zeitz, Germany: 26 May 1865-21 [sic] Aug 1928) Stage name of Paul Ufer. Learned assisting father Friedrich Wilhelm, originally playing the role of the female assistant, "Paula". Later with own show as "Paolo Uferini" toured Central Europe. Father of Willi Ufer. [Vo56;Roh;Sal;Win;Dif]

name: Ufer, Tery
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: fl.1940s-50s) Married Fredy Ufer. Pro as his assistant as "Tery Uferini" & then with her own act. [Roh;Pr]

name: Ufer, Willi
bio: (Großammensleben, near Magdeburg, Germany: 21 May 1891-1 Feb 1944) Son of Paul Ufer. Aka "Willi Uferini". Pro working after WW I as "Uferini" in East Asia. Later worked as "Cotton". Died from heart attack on stage in Vienna. [Vo56;Roh;Mül]

name: Uferini
bio: See: Ufer

name: Uhlich, Ferdinand
bio: (Budapest, Hungary: 4 Oct 1837-12 Jul 1887) Of Austrian parentage. Major pro sleight-of-hand artist in Central Europe. [Sal;Al]

name: Uker, Verne W.
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Aka "Sinbad". IBM President 1958-59.

name: Ulman Jr, Al[fred]
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 24 Oct 1958-) Aka "Al the Only". Learned in 1970 ordering from Top Hat Magic catalog & instruction from Roy Kissell. Toured as crew with Ken Griffin show 1977-78. Pro restaurant worker since 1979, specializing in table-hopping & occasional stage shows (with assistant-wife Lori). Also does school & trade shows. Collector of magicians business cards (over 4,000). Wrote Life on a School Show Tour (1983, 29pp) & The Business of Restaurant Magic (1984; rev ed 1985, 60pp). Articles in Genii & Magic Menu. [Wh2] Ülsmann, Peter (Berlin, Germany: 1922-15 Apr 1987) Pro dealer in Berlin (as "Zauberzentrale Conradi-Horster") since 1959 when he bought A. Scholz's shop. On his death the shop passed to Andre Ülsmann. [Roh]

name: Unal de Capdenac, Georges
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Comedy illusionist & general magic as "Aldenac". Resident of Paris. Inventor, improver, & builder of tricks. AFAP Bronze Medal 1969 & Silver Medal 1979. [Bou] "Uncanny Scot, The"

name: Uncle Felix
bio: See: Smith, Charles Neil

name: Unthan, Carl Herman
bio: (Sommerfeld, East Prussia: 3 Apr 1848-1929) Born without arms. As child learned to use his feet to clean, dress, feed himself, & write. At age 12 began learning the violin. Vaudeville pro as "Herr Unthan" with a multi-talented act that included card tricks: a two-footed pass, second dealing, & the Waterfall flourish. Played the USA (1893, etc), Prague (1901), etc. Autobio is The Armless Fiddler: A Pedescript (1935, as tr from the German ed of 1925). [Magic10/03;Jay]

name: Upton, P[hilip] C. "Phil
bio: (England: -2 Aug 1990) Semi-pro. Taught at Davenport School of Magic. Aka "Will Spoof" & "Phil Wye".

name: Urban, Gene [Richard]
bio: (San Diego, California: fl.1990s) Pro motivational speaker at magic & corporate events. Invented Mind Scan (1992). Co-wrote (with Tullock & Knepper) Tullock (1996, 64pp). Contributor to Knepper's Wonder Words. Videos. [Wh01]

name: Urban, Ron
bio: (USA: c1936-) Pro in Chicago by 1955. In US Army in late 1950s. Thence (by 1958) specialized in Dove Magic. Played casinos in Las Vegas (1961) & Portugal (1965). [Mec;HMM3/58]

name: Urga, Mac
bio: See: Barck-Holst, Björn

name: Uriarte
bio: (Germany: fl.1890s) Pen name of Steiner Witzky. Dentist in Frankfurt. Amateur. Wrote Die Magie des XIX Jahrhunderts als Kunst und als Geheimwissen-schaft (1896, 198pp).

name: Urk, J.
bio: (Britain: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Minor pro with Linking Rings, card tricks, & fox terrier from borrowed hat. As "Burko" played Hull in 1901 & as Urk played Manchester in 1903. Aka "Truxo". [Magic11/01,3/03]

name: Usher, Mr.
bio: (Britain?: fl.1820s) Minor pro. Performed the Linking Rings (with 8 rings) in Worcester in 1827. His poster on that occasion advertised his act as "a representation of the Indian and Chinese Jugglers".

name: Usher, Harry T. "Hal
bio: (New York City: NY: 17 Nov c1887-29 Oct 1950) Aka "Ah Foon" (by 1914) & "Yousouf, the Needle King" (from 1914), working carnivals. Under own name since 1920 with mind-reading act with wife Frances (married in 1918 in Toronto). In 1927 they became vaude headliners as "The Ushers" with magic & second-sight. Retired c1935 to go back to the horoscope business in Venice, California, Harry becoming a member of Los Magicos. Died of heart attack in Los Angeles. [Pr;Genii12/40;Tay;Ho]

name: Uter, Ferdinand
bio: (Leipzig, Germany: 4 Feb 1878-15 Mar 1930) Amateur in Leipzig. An editor of Magie. President of German Magic Circle (MZvD) 1923-28 [sic].

name: Vacca, Amedeo
bio: See: "Amedeo"

name: Vacua, Miss Rosina
bio: (Britain?: fl.1890s) Pro. Worked both as Prof. [John?] Warren's assistant "Mephisto" and a single as "The Lightning Queen and Only Lady Electrician". [Mar]

name: Vadell, Malcolm
bio: (England: c1942-Feb 1977) Pro magician with assistant as "Vadel & Sue". Was engaged with his nude magic act at Casino de Paris, London, at time of death by suicide. [Daw2]

name: Vadimov[-Markelov], Alexander Alexievich
bio: (Nizhni-Novgorod [now Gorki], Russia: 17 Jun 1895-5 Mar 1967) Pro since 1917, initially in circus. Moved to Moscow in 1922 & to Berlin in 1927. Since 1931 worked in Indian fakir costume as "Alli-Vad". Pet effect: Floating Ball. In the 1950s he was a top club magician in Moscow. Died in Moscow. Wrote (as A. Vadimov) 3 books in Russian: Iskusstvo Fokusa [The Art of Magic] (1958), Magic in the Circus (1959), & Magic for All (1962). These were, with Kio's, the first 5 magic books published in the Soviet Union. See Herbert-Martin Paufler, Wadimov und seine Bücher (1963). Co-authored (with Mark A. Trivas, Ot Magov Drevnosti do Illiuzionistov Nashchikh Dnei: Ocherki istorii illiuzionnogo iskusstva [From Ancient Magicians to Illusionists of Our Day] (Moscow: 1966, 304pp; repr 1979, 271pp; with Czech tr (Bratislava: 1968, 368pp). [Win;Mec]

name: Vaillant, Gaston[-Victor]
bio: (Paris, France: 23 Sep 1877-4 Jul 1941) Civil servant in Paris. Amateur magician, performing as "Docteur Mystere". In 1903 became a founder of the ASAP & its Secretary-General until 1921 when forced out. Charter member in 1922 of the Société d'Études de la Prestidigitation. ASAP Honorary President 1934.

name: Vaillant, Marcel
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Pro stage magician as "Eric & Sylvie". AFAP Bronze Medal 1976 & Silver Medal 1979. [Bou]

name: Vakil, H[aji] M.
bio: (Calcutta?, India: c1920-27 Jul 1986) Moslem. Pro illusionist with full-evening show that toured India and the Near East for 30 years, performing for many dignitaries. Founded the Calcutta Magic Circle in 1953. Edited Cigam 1953-65. [Genii3/66]

name: Val, M.
bio: (France: fl.1780s-1st decade of 1800s) Pro society magician. The same as "Wal" who played Paris in 1789 & 1797. Claimed to have played Russia. Played London in 1803. Then returned to the Continent. [Fr;Cl]

name: Valadon. Paul "Val
bio: (Cologne, Germany: 1867-23 Apr 1913) Stage name of Adolph Waber. In 1881 learned as assistant to Ernst Basch. Pro two-person mental act & illusionist. Toured Britain (1887), Australia (1894), & South Africa (1894). In 1896 moved to England. With Maskelyne & Cooke in London 1900-04. Moved to USA to work with Kellar 1904-07, when replaced by Howard Thurston. Co-invented (with Kellar) the 2nd (non-Maskelyne) method for the Levitation of Princess Karnac (1904). Died of tuberculosis in Phoenix, Arizona. [Pr;St;Go2;Mo;Bur]

name: Valentin
bio: (Belgium: 1830-1912) Stage name of Valentin Dewaeghenaere. Major pro ventriloquist, the first to work sitting with the dummy on his knee. [St]

name: Valentina
bio: See: Abel, Deiter

name: Valentino, Val [full name]
bio: (Los Angeles, California: 14 Jun 1956- ) Learned at age 12 from library books. Pro maniulator & illusionist since c1975. Played the Body Shop (c1986-87). Moved to Las Vegas in 1987, playing the Union Plaza (1988-89) & Caesar's Palace in Tahoe (1990). [Mag;Wh]

name: Valeria
bio: See: Kasfikis, Valeria

name: Valerio
bio: (Austria: 27 Aug 1949-) Pro.

name: Valleau. Henry Brotherton
bio: (Alameda County, California: 9 May 1913-17 Nov 1984. Raised in Canada. To study law he moved) to San Francisco in 1931 where and when he turned pro magician as "The Great Valleau". Specialized in vaudeville stage magic, , and circus ten-in-one, and theater spookshows with hypnotism (since 1944 but only in Western states). Moved to Pasadena around 1940. Retired from full-time magic in 1949 to work for the Burns Detective Agency of Los Angeles. In 1960 moved to Boise, Idaho, where he ran his own private security & detective agency and also opened a magic shop, (Magic Unusual). Mentor of John Daniel & Vic Brisbane. Died of cancer at his home in Boise. Articles in New Tops & Linking Ring. REF: Walker's Ghostmasters (1994), 106,-107, 153. [Tay]
years: 9 May 1913-17 Nov 1984. Raised in Canada. To study law he moved

name: Valton, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Stage name of Jean Levaton. Mathematician. Semi-pro card manipulator. 1946 Amsterdam International Magic Congress 1st prize; 1947 Paris International Magic Congress 1st prize for manip; 1948 FISM 1st prize for manip. See his preface to Dr Jacques Géry's Les principes brillants de la manipulation des cartes (1949). Trick in HMM (1950). [Dif]

name: Vampira
bio: See: Marcom, Gloria

name: Van Barren, Hans Johan, MD
bio: (Utrecht, Holland: 1907-4 Jun 1994) Physician (pathologist) until retired in 1982. Amateur since age 12. After med school toured the world as "Oscarini". Moved to USA after WWII & became US citizen in 1948. Tricks in Sphinx, Conjurors' Magazine, Genii, & Tops, plus 3 in Rice's Encyclopedia of Silk Magic. Column in Magic Around the World.

name: Van Bern, Chris, MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1871-7 Feb 1950) Stage name of T.B. Byrne. Pro music-hall magician. Founding President of the Mahatma Magic Circle in Liverpool, 1915. Played St. George's Hall 1918, 1920, & 1921. Later switched to club magic act. His wife performed as "Iva Voyce" (see). Wrote A Whirlwind of Wizardry (1919, 94pp, with De Vega). [Le;Go2]

name: VanBurch, Kirby
bio: (Houston, Texas: 25 Jan 19— ) Inspired around age 7 seeing magician in school. Learned from mother's gift of magic set. Left school after 8th grade to turn pro magician, initially in local magic shops. Moved to Las Vegas c1976, initially with lounge shows, then as stage illusionist, including the M-G-M Grand in Reno. Europe-Asia tour as star of "Zauber-Zauber/Magic-Magic". Then star of the "Abracadabra" show in the Bagdad Showroom of the Aladdin Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas, 1988-present. Pet effects: Spiker, Magicians Flambe, & Overhead Substitution. [Wh]

name: Van Buren
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Fred Yoxall, aka "Yoxanis". Pro magician-illusionist.

name: Van Berkel, H.
bio: See: "Bercelini"

name: Van Berkel, William J. "Bill
bio: (Rotterdam, Holland: 24 Jan 1887-) After college in Holland moved to Los Angeles. Pro since 1929 with church, club, & school-show magic on West Coast with full-evening show with assistant-wife Verna. Specialized in livestock act, including owls, frogs, turtles, & alligators. Arrested and confessed in March 1950 to felony charges of using the two 14-year old female assistants in his "Miracle of Magic, Mirth and Mystery" school show to entice boy volunteers backstage for sex and afterwards drive them all to secluded places for more sex while he watched. He admitted having started doing this the previous October. [SAM; Genii11/41; Phoenix#199].

name: Van Cleve
bio: (Bartlesville, Oklahoma: 30 Dec 1930-6 Jul 1992) Stage name of Dr Cleve E[rst] Haubold, PhD, since 1950, aka "Elwood Rabit" since 1976. Theater director, professor of drama, & playwright. Semi-pro comedy close-up & stage magic. Invented Gag-Bag in 1959. Won 5 TAOM trophies since 1959, including the 1966 Comedy Trophy. Wrote 5 booklets, including Medicine Show Tonight! (1960, 16pp) & How to Win a Magic Contest (1978). Articles in Genii, MUM, Tops, & "Elwood Rabit Rites" comedy column in Linking Ring since 1976. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Vander Linden, Anthony
bio: (Bayside, Queens, New York: 18 Aug 1924-) Born Antoine André Van der Linden. Raised in Belgium (1926-36) where he was inspired at age 10 when his amateur uncle, a parish priest and amateur magician, showed him his first magic tricks and by seeing his first professional magician. Returning to USA as teenager learned magic from high school library books in Brooklyn. Food company manager and magic book dealer in Oyster Bay, New York. Semi-pro comedy magician as "Tony Presti, The Continental Magician" working club dates in the New York area since 1955. 1969 MAES Convention Comedy Trophy. A major collector of magic magazines. [MUM4/71;Se;Wh2]

name: Van Dien, Richard
bio: (Paterson, New Jersey: 16 Mar 1846-14 Mar 1937) Pro. SAM President 1915-17.

name: Van Dommelen, Tonny
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: 11 Jun 1927- ). Joined local magic group c1945. Student of Henk Vermeyden. Pro close-up & manipulator since 1950. 1958 FISM Grand Prix. Then played cabarets & variety theaters in some 20 countries. [Win]

name: Van Dyk, Charles-Louis
bio: (Holland: -1982) Criminologist. Amateur & close associate of Fred Kaps & Hans Trixer in Holland after WW II. Moved to Australia. As "Nic Ravel" was dealer (Boomerang Magic) in Sydney mid-to-late 1970s. [McC] SEE: "Wandas, Louis"

name: Van Dyke, Roy
bio: (Britain: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Roy Hobbs. Pro top-line balloon artist now specializing in comedy close-up magic for children & cabaret audience. Wrote The Encyclopedia of Balloon Magic (forthcoming 1989).

name: Van Dyke, Tony
bio: (Germany?: 11 Aug 1945-) Illusionist. 1982 FISM 2nd prize in illusion. [Nad] van Gussem SEE: St. Andre

name: Van Monas, Ric
bio: (Germany?: 23 Nov 1939-) Stage name of Wolfgang Eder. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Vandy, Paul
bio: (England: fl.1st decade of 1900s-30s) Stage name of C.E. Maynard, a pro juggler. Cut-price magic dealer in Wimbledon, then London, then Brighton (1914), then Hastings 1909-1930s. As house organ edited Conjuring 1914 (1 issue). Played St. George's Hall 1923. [Daw94] NOTE: His brother, C. Vandy, was a cut-price dealer (Magical Pastimes Co) in Barnes, London, in 1907.

name: Vanek, Professor Joseph
bio: (Pest, Hungary: 31 Jul 1818-11 Dec 1889) Serious amateur magician since childhood. Professor of Physics at the Pester Seminar 1843-1848. Superintendent of the Hungarian Treasury's printing office 1849 during the Kossuth regime. Fled that year to Turkey where he turned pro magician, being appointed Court Conjuror. Toured Turkey (c1850), south Europe, Greece, France (1854), England (1854-55). Returned to Hungary in 1855 under amnesty. Then toured Hungary (1855-59), Turkey (1859), Egypt, Persia, the Balkans, Greece, France, & Spain. His 3rd tour (1867-1878) took him to Persia, India (1868-69), Southeast Asia & the Far East, USA & Canada (1871-73), Japan (1874), & India (1878). Retired in Budapest in 1878 to run a coffee house & import Far Eastern goods. [Daw;Vo57;Dif;St;Bo#199;Win]

name: Van Hoven, Frank
bio: (USA: 5 Feb 1886-11 Jan 1929) Taught by Harry "Dante" Jansen. Pro comedy magic. Billed as "The Boy [later 'Man'] Who Made Ice Famous". Toured USA & Europe. [Pr;Go2;Lau;Fi]

name: Vanmoli [or Vanmoll?]
bio: (Lehe, Bremerhaven, Germany: 11 Jun 1894-17 May 1946) Stage name of Johannes Olschewski. Pro. Known for his "Parade der Knirpse [dwarfs]" trick series. [Roh;Al]

name: Vanoran
bio: See: "Kar-Mi"

name: Van Reese, M.
bio: (Hatton, North Dakota: 4 Dec 1908- ) Inspired as schoolboy seeing mentalist C.A. George Newmann. Learned in road shows. Pro in Chautauqua & Lyceum until retired due to ill health. [Th]

name: Van Russell, T.
bio: See: Bowyer, Tom

name: Vanson
bio:
Vantur, A. Vantur, A. (Nice, France: 25 Dec 1888-) Stage name of César Ventura. Amateur magus & vent in Nice. [Rob1;WWM]

[See also: Andrews, Val]

name: Van Vliet, Ritsko J[an], senior
bio: (Leeuwarden, Holland: 17 Jan 1924-) Learned in 1940 from Larette. Hotel manager in Leeuwarden & semi-pro magician specialized in mentalism & fakirism. Several awards from MZvD & ISPAM (Israel) since 1967. Collector of old magic graphics, props, tokens, books, etc. Wrote Güchelboek foar Jongerein en Beginners (1982, 68pp, in Frisian). Article in Magie on Larette. [Wh5]

name: Van Zandt, W[ayne] F.
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Amateur. Wrote such booklets as Paper Tearing for the Entertainer (1931), At the Touch of the Mystic Wand (1934, 28pp), Paper Tearing for the Amateur (1935), Advanced Magical Effects (n.d.), At the Touch of the Mystic Wand [1934, 28pp] & Thru the Dye Tube (1943, 48pp, with Harold Rice).

name: Varela [Veiga], Ramón
bio: (Spain: fl.1960s-90s) Amateur card magician in Madrid. Co-authored (with Juan Tamariz) Trucki-Carto-Magia (Barcelona: 1970). In 1971 co-founded the Escuela Mágica de Madrid.

name: Varga, Brigitte
bio: (Austria: fl.1980s) Pro illusioniste & manipulator. 1982 FISM 1st prize for lady magician. [Mec]

name: Varga, Nikola
bio: (Yugoslavia: 13 Mar 1950-) Magician as "Boby Vargas". Member of MZvD. [Nad]

name: Vargas, Boby
bio: See: Varga, Nikola

name: Varma, Rai Sahib H. L., BA, MBE
bio: (India: fl.1930s-40s) Politician, minister in Surguja State. Amateur magician. Wrote The Indian Rope Trick (1942, 162pp).

name: Varney, R. M.
bio: (Sorbie Tower, Wigtownshire, Scotland: 1 Aug 1881- ) Raised in USA. Inspired seeing Herrmann the Great. Semi-pro in Manchester, England, since 1906 with sleight-of-hand, handcuff escapes, and memory feats. In 1910 became founding editor of Magi, newsletter of the Order of the Magi in Manchester. [Magic3/06,1/07]

name: Varro, Steve[n David]
bio: (South Bend, Indiana: 23 Oct 1949-) Inspired seeing a magic show, he learned from library books. Pro stage magician since 1979, specialized in gospel magic. Wrote 5 booklets: Magic--A Tricky Business, Tricks of the Trade, Comedy is No Laughing Matter, Magic-With a Christ Centered Flair, & Gospel Magic--As I Do It. Articles in Christian Conjurer. [Wh2]

name: Vassal, Marcel
bio: (France: fl.1930s-50s) As "Sarrazin" worked as pro music-hall mind-reader in France. Charter member of the Amicale des Magiciens du Sud-Est (Nice) 1936. Wrote La transmission de pensée au music-hall & La mémoire au music-hall (1939; reprinted 1963), both classics. Edited, jointly as "Les Bervas" with Théodore Ruegg, Le Poilu Physico (1939, 2 issues). Charter member of the Amicale Robert-Houdin de Grenoble 1953.

name: Vaucanson, Jacques de
bio: (Geneva, Switzerland: 23 or 24 Feb 1709-21 Nov 1782) Maker of automata, including his famous flute player (1735), tambourine player, & mechanical duck, which were first exhibited in 1738 in Paris at the St.-Germain fair. He showed 3 other automata there later (1739?). In 1743 quit showmanship, sold his automata, & began making commercial machines, including one to weave brocade. Died in Paris. Wrote Le Méchanisme de fluteur Automate (Paris: 1738) with English tr as An Account of the Mechanism of an Automaton (London: 1742, 24pp). [Dif;St]

name: Veeser, Bob
bio: (USA?: fl.1950s) Card magician. Invented the Veeser Concept in 1956.

name: Veglio, Martin
bio: See: "de Courcy, Howard"

name: Vejr, Alan
bio: (Týniste, Czechoslovakia: 24 Feb 1942-) Learned at age 12. Became semi-pro at 17. Moved to Sweden in 1968. Pro illusionist since 1972 with assistant-wife Eve as "Eve'n Alan". Pet effects: Chair of Death, 3-Sword Suspension, Gone With Shadow. Does silent act to music in nightclubs, variety, hotels, casinos, cruise ships, parks, & circuses. Have played throughout Europe, North Africa, Near East, Far East, Chile, & USA. TV bits in Sweden, England, Spain, Japan, & Chile. [Wh8]

name: Vel
bio: See: Velle, Joseph

name: Velle, Gaston [pronounced VELL]
bio: (France: fl.1890s) Son of Hungarian magician Joseph Velle. Pro magician who turned to filmmaking, becoming director of trick photography for Pathé films around 1900. [Bar]

name: Velle, Joseph [pronounced VELL]
bio: (Buda, Budapest, Hungary: 1837-1889) Born Josef Velle. Orphaned in 1848 at age 11, he began performing sleight-of-hand tricks to support his brothers & sisters. Bosco encouraged him to go abroad. Soon left, travelling as "Prof. Velle" through Russia, Germany, Italy, England, & Portugal (1864), finally settling in France (by 1874 when he played the Folies-Bergère) where he worked illusions & card tricks in both circus and theaters. He invented a hat with traps to permit him to work surrounded in the circus ring. He is probably the "Hungarian conjuror named Well" whom Robert-Houdin reported in 1868 as having mastered the Boomerang Card and, therefore, possibly its inventor. Died in Italy. Father of Gaston Velle. [Dif;St]

name: Vellma, La
bio: See: Lustig, David J.

name: Velma
bio: (USA: fl.1960s-80s) Stage name of Velma Nahoom. Inspired in 1964 seeing Virgil & Julie show. Learned from box of tricks. Housewife in New York City & semi-pro magician. She is the subject of one of Desfor's more famous photos (1976). [Des]

name: Veneri, Signor Ernardo
bio: (Italy: fl. 1st decade of 1900s-1920s) Active in the early 1920s in Glasgow, Scotland, as a well-known drawing-room magician and in the Glasgow Society of Magicians. Possibly invented flesh break (c1909).

name: Veno, Robert
bio: (Paris, France: 1900-31 Oct 1967) Stage name of Robert Venot, aka "Serge Robert" & "Haru-Kawa". Amateur to pro manip. Working with André Mayette as "Les Maybers" won the 1936 Munich grand prix for their silk-magic act. Revived the Théâtre Robert-Houdin (in the Palais de la Mutualité) for six months 1941-42. Co-founded Syndicat National des Illusionnistes in 1944. Collected documents. Edited Le Magicien. Edited & illustrated several French magic books including Cours magica (1954) with one in Portuguese tr as A Prestidigitação (1977, 64pp). [Dif;Rob1;WWM] "Vento" [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

name: Venturini
bio: See: Winkler, Albert

name: Verbeck, Eugène
bio: (Landrecies, Nord, France: 3 Nov 1844-Aug 1905) Stage name of Eugène-Laurant Verbeke. Debut in Paris. Pro stage magician with sleight-of-hand, apparatus tricks, & 2-person mind-reading (with Mdlle Marguerite). Toured Finland 1883 & England 1885-87. Invented the change-over palm (by 1885). Died during a tour of the USA. [Daw#213;Cl;Vo55;St;Bur;Dif]

name: Verbeck Jun., Eugène
bio: (France: fl.1880s-1910s). Taught by father. Pro. Toured England with Guibal & Mille Marie Greville in late 1880s. Played Paris as late as 1915. [Cl;Pr]

name: Verdini
bio: (Czechoslovakia: 1909-1994) Stage name of Frank Hladik. Pro comedy magus throught Continent & Middle East until moved to Britain in 1948, initially at the Windmill. [Hudd]

name: Vere, Arprey
bio: (Britain: fl. 1870s-80s) Journalist (?) who exposed many of the Maskelyne & Cooke effects in his Ancient and Modern Magic [1880, 125pp], many copies of which J.N. Maskelyne had bought up & destroyed. This book originally was serialized in the Liverpool Weekly Post in 1878.

name: Vergas
bio: (Mexico: fl.1980s) Pro street magician in Tijuana, Mexico. See Mad Magic #46 (1983) for an all-Vergas issue.

name: Verheyden, Fernand
bio: (Belgium: 10 Apr 1877-5 May 1932) Chief railway architect in Belgium. Amateur magician, having learned at age 8 from box of tricks. [Go] "Verhulst, Anthony" SEE: Duijker, Hubrecht A.

name: Verli, Le Professeur E. de
bio: (Belgium: 1846?-1912) Pro illusionist. Performed as late as 1900. Known for his pretentious manner. [Dif;Vo58]

name: Vermeyden, [J.] Henk
bio: (Rotterdam?, Holland: 21 Nov 1908-16 Oct 1988) Inspired & learned as young boy. Secretary of Larette c1939-41. Founder-prorietor of magic shop (Triks Magic Studio) in Amsterdam 1940-86. Edited Triks magazine 1941-43, c1946-73. Enough evidence of his WW II collaboration with the Nazis existed to make him ineligible for any state decorations. Founded FISM in 1946 (formally in 1948). Founding President of the Nederlandse Magische Unie 1951-75. Unscrupulous in his attempted use of sexual blackmail among male colleagues. Although he never performed publicly, Vermeyden was a justly famous pro magic organizer, dealer, & teacher. His many students included Fred Kaps, Peter Pit, Marconick, Richard Ross, Flip, Evelyn Rose, Hardy, The Barans, Ger Copper, Jo Nex, Vladimirov, Tel Smit, Tonny van Dommelen, Ronaldo, & a few other Dutch & foreign magicians. 1975 AMA Special Fellowship. Retired in 1986. Died of a heart attack. Wrote Witte Magie: Ein Serie Sigaretten-Manipulatives Samengesteld (n.d.) with English tr as "White Magic" serially in Magic Magazine (1952). [Abra#2310]

name: Vernay, Jeanne
bio: (France: fl.1930s) Ex-singer. Popular magician in Paris, also working 2-person mindreading act with his sister, Miss Suzy Vernay. [Dif]

name: Vernello, Edward M. "Ed
bio: (Baraboo, Wisconsin: 1869-3 Aug 1907) Pro magician in Lyceum, vaude, & circus. Pro dealer (with wife Inez) as "Vernello (also Vernelo) & Co." in Chicago since 1900. Provided initial capital for publishing The Sphinx in 1902. Died of apparent liver failure. [Albo95;Wh90]

name: Vernello, Inez
bio: (USA: fl.1st decade of 1900s) Wife of Edward Vernello with whom she ran their magic shop (Vernello & Co.) in Chicago. Edited The Sphinx 1902-04 under pen name of "M[adame] Inez", making her the first female editor of a magic magazine.

name: Verner, David Derek "Neepie
bio: (New York City, NY: 14 Aug 1932- ) Younger son of Dai & Jeanne Vernon. Faucett Ross nicknamed him "Nepomuk" & "Neepie". Briefly an amateur magician. As "Nepomuk" contributed 3 original tricks in 1950 to Phoenix #200.

name: Verner, Jeanne Hayes
bio: (USA: -1984) Born Eugenia Maria Hayes. Roman Catholic. Learned assisting Horace Goldin in 1923 or 1924. Married Dai Vernon (Verner) in 1924, acting as his occasional assistant since 1925. Noted for her papier-maché face-fitting masks, which she made as "Jeanne Verner Masks" for Vernon (in 1929), Sam Horowitz, William J. "Foo Ling Yu" Arenholz (in 1930s), La Follette, Faucett Ross, Mike "Kolma" Bornstein (in early 1940s), Danny Dew, & a chorus line at Radio City Music Hall. Made prosthetic devices (rubber noses, etc) for Dr Jacob Daley. Mother of David Derek Verner. Long separated from her husband, she died in Southern California.

name: Vernet
bio: (Argentina: fl.1970s-died 1990s) Stage name of Alberto [A.] Vergonjeanne [E. Hijo]. Pro. Wholesale maker-dealer of "Vernet Products" in Cordoba. Article in New Tops. A rumored suicide. The "Vernet" name (pronounced ver-net, not ver-nay) & line of plastic props was continued by the "Michael & Greco Magic Products" company in La Plata in the mid-1990s. Vernon, Dai [nickname pronounced DIE in Canada & Hollywood since the 1960s, but DAY when he lived in New York City] (Ottawa, Canada: 11 Jun 1894-21/22 Aug 1992) Stage name of David Frederick Wingfield Verner. Learned at age 8 from father, an amateur magician & 2nd class clerk with the Canadian Ministry of Agriculture. Moved to New York City in 1913. Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Also, beginning in 1917, worked summers cutting silhouettes. Married Jeanne Hayes Verner (which see) in 1924. One of the 5 original members of the New York "Inner Circle" by 1932. In 1932 introduced magicians to the card cheats' Center Deal. Dubbed "The Professor" by Garrick Spencer by 1937 & hence known world-wide by that nickname. Voted one of the 10 living Card Stars in 1938. Worked NY-South America cruise ships. 1948 Sphinx Award. 1958 Magic Circle Silver Wand. Taught at Tannen School of Magic 1961-62. Moved to Hollywood in 1963 when he became Resident Magican at the Magic Castle. There he became the mentor of John Carney, Bruce Cervon, & Larry Jennings, and later of Jeff Altman, Steve Freeman, Ray Grismer, Earl Nelson, David Roth, Michael Skinner, etc. 1968 AMA Masters Fellowship. AMA Board of Directors 1976-79, thence Member Emeritus. 1983 CMI Order of Magic Lamp. SAM Hall of Fame. 1988 Fred Kaps Award. In 1989 Mike Rogers predicted that "There will never be another to influence the art of magic as has Dai Vernon." Many would agree that this is a good bet. Retired in late 1990 at age 96 to San Diego home of his elder son Ted to mend broken bones. Prolific inventor of card & other close-up effects, including Slow Motion Card Vanish (1926), Atomic Deck (by 1938), Slow Motion Aces (by 1941), Queen's Soiree (by 1945), Triumph (by 1946), Cutting the Aces (by 1946), the double undercut (by 1946), Travellers (by 1950), reinvented Farelli's close-up case (by 1955), Twisting the Aces (by 1960), Depth Illusion (by 1961), and Stripout Addition. NOTE: The Buckle Count was not invented by either Vernon or Miller (each later crediting the other) but, rather, taught to the latter by A.J. Cantu shortly before WW II, as Miller wrote at the time. Vernon's version of Hugard's original (1930) All Backs appeared in the 1940s. Authored several major booklets (ghosted by Faucett Ross), including The Dai W. Vernon Book of Super Card Subtleties (1933) & Select Secrets (1941, 41pp, ed by Crimmins; rev ed 1949, 42pp). Plus books written by Lewis Ganson: The Dai Vernon Book of Magic (1957, 239pp), Dai Vernon's Cups and Balls Routine (1958, 16pp), Dai Vernon's Symphony of the Rings (1958, 26pp), Dai Vernon's Inner Secrets of Card Magic (1959, 76pp), Dai Vernon's More Inner Secrets of Card Magic (1960, 88pp), Dai Vernon's Further Secrets of Card Magic (1961, 72pp), Dai Vernon's Tribute to Nate Leipzig (1963, 192pp), Malini & his Magic (1963, 107pp), & Dai Vernon's Ultimate Card Secrets [1967, 245pp]. Many tricks in Expert Card Technique. Wrote (with Faucett W. Ross) Revelations (1984, 224pp). Columnist ("The Vernon Touch") in Genii 1968-1990. See also Daniel Fitzkee & Fred Braue, Dai Vernon: The First California Lecture (1976, 22pp), Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Dai Vernon (1978, in French), and Stephen Minch, The Vernon Chronicles (6 vols: 1987, 272pp; 1988, 280pp; 1989, 219pp, plus 3 forthcoming). Tricks in Jinx, Phoenix, Genii, Pentagram, Close-up Folio, Arcane, Epotica, Pallbearers (4 all-Vernon issues), Epilogue, etc. Audios (1965, 1977, etc). His 2-volume video 1974 interview with Tony DeLap was issued in 1993. Bio is Bruce Cervon & Keith Burns (editors), He Fooled Houdini: Dai Vernon a Magical Life (1992, 308pp). [Bo2;HC;Se;Genii9/66;Mag;Ho;Bam]

name: Vernone, Annie
bio: (USA?: c1840-) Billed as "the only Female Professor of Modern Magic in the World" in 1857 when she performed in Hull, England, at age 17. [Daw;Daw#117]

name: Versini
bio: (Zabrze, Poland: 1938-) Stage name of Franciszek Burzycki. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Pet effect: Zig-Zag Girl. [Mec]

name: Vervacke, François
bio: (Belgium: 16 Feb 1847-20 Feb 1911) Pro magician of the old school. [Vo58]

name: Vic & Fabrini
bio: (Brazil: fl. 1980s-90s) Comedy stage magic with Vic as the magician & Fabrini as his "robot" assistant. 1988 FISM 1st prize for general magic. Have played the Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris. TV bit in Britain. 1992 Desert Magic Seminar 1st prize.

name: Vickery, James
bio: (Britain: fl.1910s-20s) Pro assistant to Houdini 1910?-1926. Co-invented (with Houdini & Kukol) Milk Can Escape (1908).

name: Victor, Alexander F.
bio: (Bollnas, Sweden: 1878-29 Mar 1961) Inspired at age 16 seeing "The Great Stephanio". Learned as technical assistant to the latter as far as Cairo where Stephanio died & Victor took over the show. Thence as pro on own as "Alexander the Great" touring Asia (India in 1895) & Europe. Moved in 1890s to USA where he toured until 1910 when he turned to the invention & manufacture of home movie projectors. Died in Monterey, California. Bio is David H. Shepard, The Victor Animatograph Company: And the Genesis of the Non-Theatrical Film (1975). [Bar]

name: Victor, Edward "Teddie
bio: (London, England: 20 Aug 1887-17 Apr 1964) Stage name of Edward Victor Neuschwander, of Swiss parentage. Expert pro cardman, manipulator, & shadowist. Played St. George's Hall often from 1914 to 1926. Played Abanazar in the Aladdin Xmas panto from 1937 on. Magic teacher (Bobby Bernard, etc). Invented the Eleven Card Trick (by 1945). Wrote Magic of the Hands (1937, 119pp), More Magic of the Hands (1942, 145pp), & Further Magic of the Hands (1945, 103pp), all classic books, plus some booklets. Tricks in Magic Wand. See Rae Hammond, The Magic of Edward Victor's Hands (1995, 250pp). 1952 Sphinx Award. In the 1940s produced the world's smallest magic set: "20 Tricks in a Match Box". Retired in 1960. His son, Patrick Victor (died 1956), was also a pro shadowist. [Pr;Hudd;La2;Ho;Magic6/09]

name: Victoria, Madame
bio: (France: fl.1860s) Billed as "Queen of the Wizards". Claimed to be pupil of Robert-Houdin. Pro stage act in Paris. Played Boston 1860-61, Liverpool 1861. [Daw#116;Mo]

name: Victòria, Fada
bio: See: Carlos, Mária Victòria

name: Victorina, Joe Van
bio: See: "Kar-Mi"

name: Viggo & Jane
bio: See: Jahn, Viggo

name: Viherjuuri, Hillari Johannes
bio: (Finland: 17 Jul 1895-14 Feb 1949) Journalist & amateur magician in Finland. Wrote (as "Giovanni Veli") many articles on magic for the Finnish daily & weekly press. Vice-President of Taikapiiri 1945-47. [St]

name: Vilar, Júlio
bio: (Oporto, Portugal: 9 Aug 1886-13 Sep 1970) Pro illusionist, transformist, sleight-of-hand artist, actor, singer of popular songs, & trapezist. Worked circuses & theaters, touring Portugal, Spain, Argentina, & Brazil. Moved in 1922 to Brazil where he died in São Paulo. [Cam]

name: Ville, Lee Pee
bio: See: Hansen, Leif Rosengaard

name: Villiod, Eugène
bio: (France: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) French policeman who wrote 3 major books describing the then state of the art among Parisian & provincial card cheats, con artists, & other crooks: La mâchine voler (1905, 383pp) and two others. All in English translation by Russell T. Barnhart as, respectively, The Stealing Machine (1977, 221pp), How They Cheat You at Cards (1979, 189pp), & Crooks, Con Men, and Cheats (1980, 131pp). [Genii10/77]

name: Vincent, Charles "Chuck
bio: (Castro Valley, California: 23 Jun 1958-) Stage name of Charles V[incent] "Chuck" Amaral Jr. Learned at age 14 from tricks bought in magic shop. Student of Slydini, Siroco, Malbrough, Ogden (group sessions in 1970s), & Furst. Pro illusionist with assistant Kathleen "Kathy" Metz (born 17 Jun 1961) since 1976 as "Charles and The Lady". Married her in 1980. 1982 PCAM 1st place in stage magic. 1984 SAM Award of Merit. Pet effects: Dancing Cane & Dove Magic. Also close-up. [Mag;Wh2]

name: Vinson, Jules
bio: (Paris, France: 17 Apr 1883-10 Dec 1955) Ex-acrobat. Worked as mechanician for Charles De Vere in Paris until 1924 when De Vere passed the shop to him, which Vinson continued to operate until c1939.

name: Vintus, Len
bio: (Shoal Lake, Manitoba, Canada: 19 Jun 1903-17 Jun 1999) Of Irish-English ancestry. Stage name of Melvin Justus Given "Mul" McMullen. Lumber manager by trade. Amateur magician. In 1922 co-founded (with Gene Gordon) the IBM (Don Rogers being recruited later) of which Vintus was its 1st President (1922-26) with membership #1. Edited Linking Ring 1926-27. Edited Magicians of the World (1978, 2 vols). SAM Hall of Fame.

name: Virgil
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Metal worker by trade. Amateur magician specializing in Jumbo Cards. Semi-pro magic dealer in Kansas City, Missouri. Made top-quality metal props for Paul Fox & Russell Swann. (Eugene, Oregon: 17 Jul 1900-12 Oct 1989) Stage name of Virgil Harris Mulkey since 1927. Aka "Mulkey" & "Moelke". Learned first trick at age 9. Semi-pro debut in 1918. Pro illusionist since 1925. Assistant to McDonald Birch 1927. Then again on own as "Virgil, the Magician" touring the Mid-West & West with a company of 6. Married Julie Capriotti in the late 1930s. Finally as "Virgil & Julie" (his assistant-wife). 1952 Sphinx Award. 5 world tours with a full-evening show, the first being 1952-56. 1971 AMA Masters Fellowship for "Virgil & Julie". Bio is David Charvet & Julie, The Great Virgil (1991, 250pp). [Pr;NT2/89;Fu;HMM5/56;Tay;Des]
