name: Virt. Radoslav
bio: (Gottwaldovo [now Zlin], Czechoslovakia: 15 Dec 1951- ) Amateur, specialized in kid shows. Collector. Tricks in Moderni Magie. [Nad]

name: Vitrio
bio: See: “Weil, John”

name: Vivalla, Signor [Antonio?]
bio: (Italy: -1857) Pro. Moved to USA where he worked as "Signor Vivalla" & "Signor Antonio". [CI]

name: Viviane, Mlle.
bio: (France: fl.1930s) Stage name of Viviane-Germaine Fautrad. Pro kid show & club magicienne. Joined ASAP in France. Moved to New York City c1938. [SAM]

name: Voignier, François
bio: (Gerardmer, Vosges, France: 30 Sep 1939-) Younger brother of Jacques Voignier. Learned at age 8 from tricks in old childrens magazines. Engineer in Morsang. Amateur magician & magic collector, specializing in tricks & literature. Articles in Escamoteur. [Mer;Wh2]

name: Voignier, Jacques
bio: (Strasbourg, Bas-Rhin, France: 9 Nov 1936-) Inspired at age 6 by magic show at school. Nuclear physicist (PhD) with French National Atomic Energy Laboratory. Amateur magician since age 12. AFAP Bronze Medal 1973 & Silver Medal 1978. Noted magic collector (began at age 20) in Paris (formerly in Strasbourg), specializing in tricks & literature. President of Club des Magiciens Collectionneurs 1976-present. His collection of antique apparatus (since 1784) made or used by Pinetti, Bosco, Comte, Cazeneuve, Rougeol, Voisin, De Vere, Caroly, Dickmann, etc, is the foremost in France. His library has 12,000 books, prints, playbills, program, & posters from 1550 to the present, mostly those of French magicians of the 19th & early 20th century. Wrote series in Escamoteur (1959-66) & Journal de la Prestidigitation (since 1972). Wrote Bibliography of French Modern Conjuring 1932-1989 and The Magic of France (1994). Elder brother of François Voignier. [Bou;Daw2;Wh2]

name: Voisin, André
bio: (France: fl.1830s-60s) Pro dealer & prop maker in Paris since 1834 when he opened a magic shop at No.81-83 Rue Vieille-du-Temple. In 1855 he exhibited a group of magnetically & electrically operated tables & boxes that for the first time exposed the public to these conjuror's secrets. By 1867, when Brander Matthews visited, his "dingy shop" was the main gathering place of magicians in Paris. Grandfather of Émile Voisin. [Dif]

name: Voisin, Émile[-Édouard]
bio: (Paris, France: 10 Jul 1857-7 Dec 1918) Pro magic teacher (including Méliès c1884) & dealer in Paris with his shop in the Rue Vieille-du-Temple, which he took over from grandfather André Voisin (see). First manager of the Cabinet Fantastique in the Musée Grévin 1886. Briefly co-director Théâtre Robert-Houdin in 1887. Invented the Knife-Throwing gaff (by 1897). [Dif;St]

name: Voit, Harold [Paul Walter]
bio: (Pullach, Bavaria, West Germany: 26 Jul 1948-) Inspired at age 12. Pro trade show & private party magician since 1981. Pet effect: Levitation. Dealer, publisher, & school (Zauberzentrale München) in Munich since 1977 when he joined Rudolf Braunmüller & G. Puchinger as a 3rd partner. Then sole owner since 1981. Articles in Magie & Magische Welt. Translated many English magic books into German. Designed magic in film Bagdad Cafe (1987; US 1988). [Wh2]

name: Volcard"/"Volkard
bio: See: Folkard, Charles J.

name: Volkmann, Dr Kurt
bio: (Kassel, Germany: 27 Sep 1897-8 May 1958) Lawyer in Düsseldorf. Amateur magician & magic historian. Joined the MZvD in 1927. Editor of Magie 1949. President of Magischer Zirkel von Deutschland 1952-58. Died in Kettwig. Major magic book collector. Gave part of his collection in Spring 1938 to the Museum für Volkerkunde in Leipzig, which was destroyed during the night of 3/4 Dec 1940 by an RAF bombing raid. Wrote "Geschichte der Zauberkunst", which appeared serially in Magie 1939-43 & 1950-58; Bibliografi over Dansk magisk Litteratur (1948); Das Becherspiel (1954, 36pp), English tr by Barrows Mussey as The Oldest Deception (1956, 48pp); co-authored (with Louis Tummers) Bibliographie de la Prestidigitation, Vol.I ("Allemagne et Austriche") (1952, 187pp). Articles in Conjuriana, Sixth Collectors Annual, etc. [St;Roh]

name: Vollmer, Richard
bio: (Strasbourg, France: 4 Apr 1950-) Learned at age 9 from relative's gift of magic set. Professor of English. Amateur card magician. Prolific writer, compiler, translator of magic. Wrote Cartomania (1977; 2nd ed 1983, 150pp), Le jeu-miroir (1985, 21pp), & Les trésors du pharaon (1988, 59pp). Compiled & translated 21 collections of tricks. Did French translations (all published by Jean-Pierre Hornecker) of 18 major books in English & German. Articles in Revue Français de la Prestidigitation, Arcane (France), & Lorayne's Best of Friends #2. [Lo2;Wh2]

name: Volta
bio: See: Hull, Burling

name: Voltaire
bio: (London, England: 7 Dec 1909-26 Apr 1986) Stage name of William Jean "Bobby Arren" Arrendorff. Moved to Canada in 1934. Learned assisting in med show. Pro in Britain with his electrical act since 1946 until retired (to become a farmer). Featured lighting electric lamps, including a lighthouse lamp. [Hudd;St]

name: Von Arx
bio: See: Nicol, Charles A.

name: Von Blitzen, Herr
bio: See: Brema, Carl

name: Von-Demberg, Prof.
bio: (Douro, Portugal: 11 Nov 1943- ) Stage name of Reinaldo Baptista. Taught in 1958 by Truckman. Did military service in Angola where he settled. Wrote magic page for the Luanda journal Semana Illustrada in 1967. Toured Angola, Mozambique, South Africa, & Rhodesia. Moved back to Portugal in 1975. 1977 Figueira da Foz 2nd prize for telepathy & 3rd prize for ventriloquism. [Cam]

name: Von Deusen, Doctor Wilhelm
bio: See: Gravatt, Glenn G.

name: Von Kalvani
bio:
"von Rudeen, Dolf" SEE: Rudin, Dolf

[See also: Linden, Herbert von der]

name: Vonetta
bio: (Pickering, North Yorkshire, England: fl.1900s-30s) Born Etta Ion. Stage name of Mrs T. Vincent Paul, aka "Von Etta". Pro illusionist & quick-change artist (ex-dancer) 1906-14. Played the London Hippodrome in 1907. Bio is Edwin A. Dawes, Vonetta: Mistress of Mystery (1982). [Mar;Magic3/07]

name: Voorhees, Edward F. “Ed
bio: (USA: 30 Aug 1924-17 Apr 2004) After service in WW II became a G.I. Bill student at the Chavez School of Magic, graduating in close-up, stage, & manip. In 1962 with Lee Grey bought Kanter's Magic Shop in Philadelphia from the retiring Mike Kanter. Lived in Philadelphia until his death.

name: Vorobiev, Alexander "Sasha
bio: (Moscow, USSR: 22 Sep 1953-) Took degrees in engineering & math. Pro manip and mentalism as "Char". Founding-president of the 350-member Russian Magic Society since 1991. [Ran;Wh5]

name: Vosburgh, [John Edwin] "Jack
bio: (Butte, Montana: 27 Dec 1918- ) Inspired at age 10. English teacher in high schools in Sayre, Pennsylvania, & Greene, New York. Amateur card & mental magician. Invented Future Deck. Wrote More than a Trick (1941, 22pp), Little Miracles, Mind Mirror. Tricks in Linking Ring, Genii, Jinx. NOTE: His first name misgiven as "Harry" by Annemann (Jinx, 1935, p.45; & then Hugard (1940). [Th]

name: Voyce, Iva
bio: (England: c1884-3 Feb 1975) Stage name of Florence Beatrice Byrne, Mrs Chris Van-Bern, aka "Cora Lister". Worked as a "Lady Baritone" but also did a magic act.

name: Vox, Val
bio: See: Andrews, Val

name: Vyson, Ed.
bio: (Britain: fl. 1st decade of 1900s) Wrote booklet Wizardry: A Treatise on Things Illusory [1906, 16pp].

name: Wächter, Udo [pronounced VEK-ter]
bio: (Germany: 30 Nov 19-) Magician and collector of magic books in Wesel, Germany, in 1980s-90s. [Nad]

name: Wade, John [Francis George], MIMC
bio: (London, England: 9 Dec 1930- ) Learned magic in 1945 buying tricks from Len Allen at Hamley's. Pro close-up cabaret magician since 1953. Popularized magic on radio in Britain with over 200 broadcasts for BBC alone. Did shipboard magic on 22 crossings on QE II 1972-74. Devised, wrote, & presented "The Music of Magic" BBC radio show 1990, featuring the BBC Concert Orchestra performing music associated with magic. Now working magic into the "Nutcracker" for the Royal Birmingham Ballet. Popular MC. Columnist for Abra since 1981. Articles in Abra, Magigram, MUM, etc. Wrote Do Get the Name Right (13pp, for MCs) & Radio Magic (1983, 7pp). 2 TV series, co-host with Paul Daniels & Terry Seabrooke of the 2 For My Next Trick TV shows, plus many TV bits. His hands are seen manipulating cards in closing titles of The Avengers TV series. Audio (1978). Memoir is The Trade of the Tricks (1974, 127pp). [La2;Wh2]

name: Wade, [H.] Mark
bio: (Dayton, Ohio: 27 Aug 1950- ) Learned magic in 1958 from library book & vent from Maher Course. Pro kid-show magic & vent act since 1975. Warm-up act for several TV shows. 1980 International Ventriloquist of the Year. Edits Kid Show Quarterly 1990-present. Wrote Kid-Show Marketing (1990 forthcoming, 72pp). Vent column for Laugh-Makers. 3 tapes on comedy writing for kid-shows. [Laugh-Makers4/84;Wh2]

name: Waddell, Marjorie D.
bio: (England: 14 May 1911-dead by 1989) Learned in early 1950s from two boxes of tricks. Semi-pro. 1955 Craig Trophy. 1958 British Ring Shield. Retired by blindness. [Mar] Wadimow [German & Polish spelling] SEE: Vadimov, A.

name: Wagner, [Robert Arthur] "Bob
bio: (Sacramento, California: 18 Jan 1934-) Learned in 1947 from boyhood friend. Math teacher in Los Angeles. Semi-pro stage, parlor, close-up, & mental magician since 1954. PCAM trophies 1961 & 1962. Aka "E. Scott Powers", "Strega", "Tsigane", & "Allah-Din", all c1963. Perpetrated the hoax "Krajax Parade" in the Jul 1966 Linking Ring. Has lectured clubs on Pacific Coast & Japan 1974-81. Wrote Magic Dungeon Mentalism (1972, 104pp, with Howard Adams), Damn Good Tricks (1973, 52pp), & Master Notebook of Magic (192pp). Tricks in Talisman, Son of Bat Jr, Bat Droppings, Fushigi, etc. Magic Around the World 770:Wh21 [Magic Around the World 7/70;Wh2]

name: Wagner, Günter
bio: (Germany: 15 Jul 1919-) With partner as "Tiamo & Alice". 1978 MZvD 3rd prize in closeup. [Nad]

name: Wagner, [John] "J. C.
bio: (USA: - 15 August 2010) Pro close-up & top-line bartender-magician. Co-owner of The Magic Lounge in San Diego 1977-81. Wrote Seven Secrets (1978, 59pp), etc. See also Mike Maxwell, The Commercial Magic of J.C. Wagner (1987, 164pp); & 7 Secrets (72pp). 2 videos (since 1991).

name: Wait [Jr], Logan
bio: (Parkersburg, West Virginia: 28 May 1906-) Aka "the Legerdemaniac". Pro on Lyceum, Chautauqua, & vaudeville circuits. Worked with Ben Franklin IV and later collaborated closely with Roger Montandon & the latter's magic shop in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Co-invented (with Roger Montandon) Invisible Bovine (c1941) & discovered OOM (c1941). [Wh]

name: Wakefield, James
bio: See: "Carl, Professor"

name: Wakefield, Percy John
bio: (Cricklade, Wiltshire, England: 5 Jun 1901- ) Aka "Professor J. Doubleau". Semi-pro stage & parlor comedy magician. [Go2]

name: Wakeling, Alan [Robert]
bio: (Hollywood, California: 2 Mar 1926-11 Nov 2004) Debuted in 1938 demming in magic shops of Floyd Thayer, Merv Taylor, and the Magic House of Charles. Pro. Assistant to Dante after WW II. Also assisted Peter Godfrey in late 1940s. Magic Castle Member #9. Creative Director for Mark Wilson 1966-1988 when retired. 1976 AMA Creative Fellowship. Creative consultant for "Snoopy's World of Magic" touring show in 1989, etc. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote The Chop Cup Book (1979, with Earl Nelson). Articles in Genii. See Jim Steinmeyer, The Magic of Alan Wakeling (1993, 345pp). NOTE: "Wa-Kee-Ling" was merely a gag nickname coined & used only by Marvyn Roy & never used by Wakeling himself. [Wat;Wh]

name: Wakeman, [Randal Paul] "Randy
bio: (Kansas City, Missouri: 1 Nov 1957-) Inspired in 1965 by a Svengali pitch at county fair. Industrial salesman in Joliet, Illinois. Semi-pro close-up with cards & coins since 1971. See J. Mendoza, Formula One Close-up: The Magic of Randy Wakeman (1985, 84pp), Randy Wakeman's Special Effects (1987, 112pp), & Mike Maxwell, Randy Wakeman Presents (1989, 153pp). Many tricks in Apocalypse & Genii. Two videos (1988, 1989). [Wh2]

name: Wal
bio: See: Val

name: Waldmann, Otto [pronounced VALD-mahn]
bio: (Germany: 1881-) Aka "Walton". Pro.Trick in

name: Waldron, Dan
bio: (Bay City, Michigan: 19 Aug 1925- ) TV writer-producer. Amateur magus since father's gift of Hoffman's Modern Magic. Collector. Close associate of Bob Lund since 1960. Wrote American Museum of Magic: Its True Story (1990, 48pp) & Blackstone: A Magician's Life (forthcoming 1999). Articles in Magicol.

name: Waldys, Joë
bio: (France: fl.1950s-70s) Stage name of Georges Mazot. Pro magician by 1953 when took 1st prize at the AFAP congress. Thence worked a pickpocket act. Played the Casino Estoril in Portugal in 1962.

name: Walke, George le
bio: (England: c1867-3 Aug 1951) Mechanic & magician. Made apparatus for Ornum's, Goldston, Hamley's, Davenport's, etc. See E. Bagshawe, The le Walke Mysteries (1927).

name: Walker, Byron E[ugene], AIMC
bio: (Oakland, California: 29 Apr 1933- ). Inspired by & learned at age 8 from Xmas gift of a Mysto Magic set. Pharmaceutical salesman by profession (having met Lloyd Jones thru Pete Biro). Thence semi-pro magic book dealer & publisher in San Leandro, California. AIMC 1988. Since 1975 when he bought the Lloyd Jones Collection, his collection of magic books is widely credited as being the world's oldest (dating back to the Burlingame Collection begun in 1872) & largest private collection. Thence substantially enlarged, particularly by purchase of the Lewis Kohrs Collection (in 1983) & of singles thru his second-hand book business. Cataloged in late 1970s by his then wife, Barbara "Barbi" Walker. [Bo#202;Se;Wh]

name: Walker, James John
bio: (Britain: fl.1870s) Co-invented (with J.H. Pepper) Metempsychosis in 1879. [Daw#218]

name: Walker, Mark
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 20 Mar 1953-) Auditor, now financial analyst. Learned age c5 from a Mysto Magic set. Semi-pro magician with kidshows & family audiences. Has world's largest collection of Ghost Show memorabilia. In 1981 invented the covered version of the Tube Illusion (= Geometricks+Henning's Tunnel of Awe). Wrote Spook Shows on Parade (1978, 76pp), The Master Illusionists (1983, 130pp), How to Haunt a House (1979, 16pp), The Great Halloween Book (1983, 170pp), & Ghostmasters (1991, 176pp). [Wh]

name: Walker, Roy
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s) Wrote Walker's Card Mysteries (1933, 99pp).

name: Walker, S. David
bio: (Kansas City?, USA: fl.1940s-80s) Pro. Lives in Kansas City, Kansas. Famous carnival pitchman throughout the Southern & Border states. Expert at pitching the Svengali Deck, which he did at one time with Harry Lorayne. In 1968 worked the Texas Hemisfair assisted by John Cornelius. Reportedly invented the popular Mylar helium balloons.

name: Walker, Val[entine] Augustus
bio: (Birmingham, England: 14 Feb 1890-17 Mar 1969) Aka "Val Enson". Pro variety magician & escape artist, billed as "The Wizard of the Navy". Played St. George's Hall 1920 & 1921. "Wallace the Magician" SEE: Lee, Wallace

name: Wallace, Professor
bio: (Australia: fl.1960s) Stage name of Ken Jaffrey who purchased this billing from the old-time original Prof. Wallace. Pro illusionist and Punch & Judy.

name: Wallace, Donald [George]
bio: (Bristol, England: 18 Sep 1929-) Did not become interested in magic until 1960 when his very young daughter showed him a trick. Pro local childrens magician, aka "Mr Magic" c1970-75. International mail-order book dealer (Magic Books by Post) in Bristol since 1973. Trick in Swami. [Wh2]

name: Wallace, Len.
bio: (Britain: fl.1930s) Pro performer as "Martenus". Worked a while as demonstrator at Gamage's.

name: Waller, Charles [Gordon]
bio: (Benalla, Australia: 8 Dec 1879-30 May 1960) Inspired at age 11 seeing George Heller show. Businessman in Melbourne. Highly creative amateur magician. Invented Harlequin Cigarette Holder (1923); Wonder Frame (by 1928); Hop, Skip and Jump (by 1928); Screen of Life (by 1936); Amazia (by 1936); & Mystery of the Telephone Booth (by 1936). Wrote Up His Sleeve (1920, 86pp); For Magicians Only (1923, 145pp); Waller's Wonders (1926, 94pp); Magic from Below (1929, 160pp); Happy Magic (1932); & Magical Nights at the Theatre (1980, 256pp), a major history of 295 magicians who played Melbourne theaters from 1854 through 1947. Tricks in Magic Mirror, Magic Wand, Sphinx, Linking Ring, & Genii.

name: Wally
bio: See: Tremlett, Douglas "Doug"

name: Walsh, Audley V[alentine]
bio: (New York City, NY: 10 Jun 1894-17 Jun 1957) Vaudeville comic who left c1927 to become a policeman in Ridgefield Park, New Jersey. In 1932 was inspired seeing magician in hospital. Learned from gift book from friend. Amateur specializing in gambling exposé act & lectures. In 1946 started his fine collection of gaffed gambling apparatus. Invented Magician's Dream (by 1938), Rabbit Wringer (in 1942), Mental Choice (1955), & probably introduced fanning powder to magicians. Wrote John Scarne Explains Why You Can't Win [1933, 33pp; repr 1967, 44pp], Spongeball Manipulation (1936, ed by Crimmins), Rackets Are My Racket (1951, 12pp), & Dice Deceptions (1953, 32pp, with Ed Mishell, the cover title being "Dice Dexterity"). Articles & tricks in Phoenix, Tarbell #5, New Phoenix, & Gen. [Th;HMM7/57]

name: Walsh, [William] Russell "Russ
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 14 May 1894-1971) Of Irish parentage. Manufacturer in Chicago. Semi-pro magician. Invented Walsh Cane (around 1915-29), The Magic Fountain Pen (a loading device, by 1924), Cane to Silk (by 1936), Appearing Cane (1947), & a Vanishing Wand using his cane principle (1960). SAM President 1934-35. IBM President 1949-50. See F.B. Martineau, Walsh Cane Routines (1945, 33pp). [St;Dor;WWM]

name: Walstad, Bruce A[lan]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 30 Mar 1951-) Inspired & learned at age 8 seeing a magician & buying mail-order tricks. Semi-pro magician since age 19, working school assemblies & family shows. Police officer since 1975 in Franklin Park, Illinois. Co-authored (with Lindsay E. Smith) Sting Shift: The Street-Smart Cop's Handbook of Cons and Swindles (1989, 125pp). [Wh2]

name: Walter, Miss
bio: (Belgium: fl.1920s) Born to French parents. Moved to France. Married Guillaume Clément (see). Pro illusioniste.

name: Walter, Joseph C[reston]
bio: (Oshkosh, Wisconsin: 29 Jan 1881-1951) Got 1st trick from Kellar in 1890s. Insurance salesman in home town. Semi-pro magician, playing vaudeville, schools, & clubs as "Walter the Magician". Column ("From Wisconsin") in Genii in late 1930s-early 1940s. Elder son was magician "Jack Curtis". NOTE: Legal surname sometimes misspelled "Walters". [SAM;WWM]

name: Walton, Roy
bio: (Acton, London, England: 1932- ) At age 10 inspired by & learned from a birthday gift box of tricks & amateur close-up magician since. Dealer (manager of Davenport's branch in Glasgow) since 1955. Son-in-law of George Davenport, having married in 1959 the latter's younger daughter, Jean (born 1937). One of the more creative cardmen in the United Kingdom, inventing Collectors (by 1969), Impact, & Cardwarp (1974). Teacher of Gordon Bruce. Wrote The Devil's Playthings (1969, 61pp), Cardboard Charades (1971, 54pp), Tale Twisters (1972, 12pp), Card Script (1973, 47pp; repr 1975), Some Late Extra Card Tricks (1975, 26pp), A Collection of Card Tricks Using Unprepared Cards and Trigger (1976, 12pp), That Certain Something (1979, 23pp), & The Complete Walton [2 vols, 1981, 1988]. See Richard Vollmer, The Very Best of Roy Walton (1980, in French). Tricks in Abra, Chronicles, Epilogue, Genii, Hierophant, Ibidem, Kabbala, Linking Ring (with 1980 "Parade"), Magic, Magic Circular, Pabular, Pallbearers, Pentagram, Spellbinder, & Swami. [LR80;Wh5]

name: Walton, Wally
bio: (England: fl.1920s) Pro. Billed as "The World's Worst Magician". Played St. George's Hall in 1924.

name: WAN Sing
bio: (China: fl.1850s) Pro. With "The Chinese Magicians" troupe toured the USA (1853) & England (1854).

name: Wan-Tien-Tay
bio: (Russia?: 1908-) Stage name of Sergei Valentinovich. Pro illusionist with assistant-wife Ludmila Andreievna (born 1908). [Mec;Nad]

name: Wandas, Elizabeth
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 7 Dec 1875 [sic]-1954) Stage name of Elizabeth Van Dyk (née Steelandt). Taught by husband Louis Wandas. Pro. Toured with her daughter Suzy as "The Wandas Sisters" until retired in 1936. [Dif;Vo58;Mar]

name: Wandas, Louis
bio: (Belgium: 1875-1912) Stage name of Charles-Louis Van Dyk. Pro. Husband of Elizabeth & father of Suzy. [Dif;Mar]

name: Wandas, Suzy
bio: (Brussels, Belgium: 5 Mar 1896-12 [or 17?] Jul 1986) Stage name of Jeanne Van Dyk, daughter of Elizabeth and Louis Van Dyk ("The Wandas"). Inspired by age 8 assisting in parents' magic-juggling-puppet act. Lessons from T.N. Downs & then pro since age 14 doing coin manipulation in family show & as single act from 1936 until retired in 1959 when she married Zina Bennett. 1981 AMA Performing Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. [Mar;Dif]

name: Wandman, Walter
bio: (England: -c1992) Stage name of Samuel McCord. Manufactured bakelite & metal props in Birmingham in 1930s-50s when retired to Exmouth. [Daw94] Ward the Wizard (USA: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of David Ward. Wrote Wiles of a Wizard (1967, 64pp).

name: Ward, Jennifer
bio: See: Spina, Jennifer

name: Ward, Leo
bio: (England: fl.1980s) Pro, from London street magic to stage magic. 1988 British Magical Champion of General Magic.

name: Ware, [Leonard Ellis] "Tad
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 1931- ) Owner of an ad agency in home town. Avid collector of apparatus of the early 1900s. Semi-pro dealer in magicana. Articles. [Bo#312;Albo95]

name: Waring, Professor Andrew G. "Andy
bio: (USA: 9 Jan 1847-7 Oct 1915) With Western Union Telegraph Company in New York City. Skilled amateur magician. Invented bottomless glass in 1878 to eliminate the exposé part of A. Herrmann's sucker version of Kling-Klang. [Le]

name: Waring, Peter
bio: (London, England: c1919-9 Jul 1949) Stage name of Peter Mainwaring [or John Roderiguez?]. Promagician & raconteur just after 1945, often playing the Windmill. Had a criminal record. Committed suicide in his prison cell. [Le]

name: Waring, Richard
bio: (Bradford, Yorkshire, England: 26 Jun 1932-) Stage name of Brian Barton-Chapple. Actor-writer until 1960 when became full-time comedy writer for BBC-TV. Amateur magician (since childhood) until 1989 when turned semi-pro. Weighing 18 stone (252 pounds) bills himself as "The Biggest Thing in Magic". With ex-model assistant Hazel does a trick-illusion-mentalism act. [Wh2]

name: Warlock, Elizabeth "Liz
bio: (England: 1932-) Stage & pen name of Mary Bell. Inspired & taught (in 1948) by father Alec "Peter Warlock" Bell. Tax consultant by profession. Amateur stage & close-up since 1953 when she became the first woman to win the British Ring Shield. Also 1955 Magic Circle Grand Prix. Moved to Canada in 1965, working in a mortgage house plus doing semi-pro close-up. Pro since 1977. First magicienne to play the Magic Castle's close-up room. Pet effects: Linking Rings & Homing Card. Moved back to England in 1983. Companion of Alan Kennaugh from 1983 until his death in 1991. In The Linking Ring wrote Toronto news column & then (since Feb 1985) "Our Side of the Pond" British news column. [Bo#227;Mar]

name: Warlock, Peter
bio: (Islington, London, England: 23 Jun 1904-16 Dec 1995) Stage name of Alec William Bell since 1937, aka "Jules Giraud", "Deb", "Rudi Jader", "Russell Sharpe", & "G. Locke". Learned in WW I from schoolmate. Bank official. Semi-pro magician since 1920. Published first trick in Magic Wand in 1921. 1950 Sphinx Award. 1952 British Ring Shield. British Ring Past President. In 1960s with Francis Haxton toured their "Trudy & Rudy" burlesque magic act in Holland & Italy. Pet effect: Jest of Gratoulet. Wrote "Our Side of the Pond" British magic news column in Linking Ring 1967-Jan 1985. 1970 AMA Literary Fellowship. 1974 Magic Circle "Magician of the Year" award. SAM Hall of Fame (1985). MIMC (resigned 1987). 1989 H. Adrian Smith Literary Award (shared with Eric Lewis). 1990 AMA Masters Fellowship. Invented Quadruple Penetration (1937), Book of the Mind (early 1950s), Five Thoughts Ahead (early 1950s), Twin Thoughts (1953), Red and White Ropes (1955), Sympathetic Selections (1956), & Stranger in Paradise (1956). Edited Pentagram 1946-59, Gen 1952-53, & New Pentagram 1969-89. Prolific author of books: Designs for Magic (1941, 74pp); Slates--a Learner's Course (1941 mss), revised as The Best Tricks with Slates (1942, 65pp); Plans for Deception (1942, 88pp); Patterns for Psychics (1947, 76pp; 2nd ed 1958, 42pp); Peter Warlock's Book of Magic (1956, 141pp; repr as The Complete Book of Magic); Warlock's Way (1966, 55pp); A-Haunting We Will Go [1970, 21pp]; The Magic of Pavel (1971); Pseudonyms (1980, 48pp); Walter Jeans (1986); P.T. Selbit (1989, with Eric C. Lewis); Aspects of a Warlock (forthcoming); & Buatier de Kolta (1993, 217pp). Edited Come a Little Closer (1953, 37pp). Columns in Magigram & Linking Ring. Tricks in several magic magazines including Jinx, HMM, Genii, Ibidem, Pallbearers (an all-Warlock issue), Swami, & Mantra. Video. Audio. [Bo#227;Th;La2;Wh2]

name: Warnecke, Bruno
bio: (USA: fl.1890s-1930s) Aka "Harry Keller". Promagician in rural Northwest. Pet effects: Vanishing Lady, Aga Levitation, Black Art, and Cups-&-Balls. Admired by C.A. George Newmann.

name: Warner
bio: (France?: fl.1870s-80s) Pro sleight-of-hand. Pet effect: Cups-&-Balls. Featured at the Théâtre Robert-Houdin 1879-80. [Dif]

name: Warren, John
bio: (Britain: 1873-24 Oct 1952) Pro illusionist & vent (with "Marmaduke"). Played St. George's Hall often 1905-24. Produced a Black Art play, The Magic Carpet in 1910. A memoir is Where the Leather Comes From, being the Memoirs of the Meanderings of a Modern Magician in Morocco (1903). [Cl;Magic5/07]

name: Warringer, Howard L[ewis] "Banjo
bio: (Albany, New York: 6 Jan 1914-31 Oct 1991) Learned at age 8 from books. Engineer with RCA until retired. Semi-pro magician since c1941 as "Damian" with straight & mental magic. Pet effects: rope tricks. Moved to Florida in 1954. Pro hypnotist. [Wh2]

name: Warsaw, A[be] J[acob] "Abe
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 7 Apr 1886-1949) Inspired at age 10 when sent for 10¢ magic book. Manufacturer of repair material for auto tires in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Semi-pro magician. Taught 6-year-old daughter June Horowitz c1919.

name: Warton, Wilton
bio: See: "LeDair, Jack"

name: Warwick, Rae
bio: (Paris, France: fl.1920s-30s) Married Oswald Williams, working as his featured assistant for many years. [Go2]

name: Washington, "Dick
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Hotel owner in Minnesota. Amateur magician. Friend of Paul LePaul for whom he invented the LePaul Wallet, giving it to Don Alan in 1953.

name: Wass, Verrall
bio: (Anerley, England: 13 Jun 1909-) Wrote Essence (1931), Astound Your Audience (2 vols, 1936), Visible Magic: 9 Tricks in Tribute to American Magicians (1944, 9pp), Magically Yours (1953, 146pp), & 4 others. Edited Verrall's Mystery Monthly 1936 (3 issues) & Verrall's Mystery Quarterly 1937-? (1 issue?). Tricks in Magic Wand & The Wizard.

name: Wassilak, Alan [Richard]
bio: (Long Beach, California: 28 Aug 1949- ) Learned in 1956 from Xmas gift Mandrake magic set. Administrative coordinator in Boston area. Part-time magician 1965-68 & 1984-present. Aka "Alan the Uncanny" since 1981. Specializes in comedy magic, working both close-up & stand up. Student of magic history. Magic illustrator, mainly for Ray Goulet's publications & Hades Publications. Draws "Basil the Baffling" cartoons for MUM since 1983 & "The Car(d)toonist's View of the Tarot Pack" for The Silent Messenger since 1987. Writes "The Philosopher's Stone" column in Boston Barnstormer since 1988 & the Boston news column for Magic Manuscript since 1989. Tricks in Linking Ring (including 1 Parade). [MUM2/89;LR5/97;Wh2]

name: Waters, T[homas] A[lan] "Tom
bio: (Chillicothe, Ohio: 27 Feb 1938-7 Aug 1998) Semi-pro writer of at least 7 paperback novels since 1967: 2 gothics (as T.A. Waters), science fiction (as "Thomas Allen"), spy, etc, of which at least 2 were also designed as force books: The Blackwood Cult (1968, where 9th word in every chapter is "read") & Love that Spy (1968, where 9th word in every chapter is "morning"). Semi-pro mentalist since c1968. Librarian, AMA (Magic Castle) Library, Mar 1991-Jun 1993. Died of a heart attack after leaving Planet Hollywood. Wrote An Operating Manual for the Mind (1971), an occultist pop-psychology textbook. Also several booklets on mentalism including Omnimancy: A Treatise on Fortunetelling (1981) & Grymwyr (1982, 35pp); plus The Encyclopedia of Magic and Magicians (1988, 372pp), which won the 1989 Christopher Award; & Mind, Myth & Magick (1993, 846pp). Tricks in New Phoenix & Genii. 3 audios (1982), 1 video (1990). [Bo#330; New Yorker 14/9/98]

name: Watry, Cesare
bio: (Italy: fl.1890s-1910s) Pro manipulation & hypnotism. Played the Lisbon Coliseu in 1897 & 1912. Inspired Fran-Klint in manip. [Cam;Dif]

name: Watson
bio: (Poland: 1926-) Stage name of Francizek Ciechoński. Pro illusionist & manipulator. Treasurer & Secretary of the Krajowa Sekcja Artystów Iluji (KSAI) since 1977. [Mec]

name: Watson, Alan, [Scott] MIMC
bio: (Wellington New Zealand: 26 Nov 1950-) Learned at age 7 from great-great uncle Oswald Ashton. In sales & marketing & semi-pro magician in Auckland until 1989 when turned full-time pro magician with close-up & childrens magic. President, New Zealand Society of Magicians 1981-83, 1986-89. Has played the Magic Castle five times. Founder & admin MagicNZ! BBS 1993 to 1999. Magic New Zealand e-zine founder director & editor 1999 to present. 1995 MIMC with Gold Star, 1997 The Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Shure Golden Microphone Award, 1999 Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Scroll of Honour, 2002 (with wife Michele) DRAGON Award, 2003 The Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Agnew Excellence Award, 2005 IBM Presidential Citation, 2006 The Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Golden Benny, NZ Grand Master of Magic & 2006 IBM Order of Merlin. Life Member of IBM, SAM & the New Zealand Society of Magicians. Articles & tricks in Genii, MUM, Magicana, Magic Circular & LR [Wh5] www.watson.co.nz

name: Watson, [Donald] "Monk
bio: (Jackson, Michigan: 23 Mar 1894-23 Mar 1981) Debut at age 8. Pro comedy magician. Wrote The Professional Touch (1945, 49pp). Elected mayor of Colon, Michigan, in 1951. [St;Wat]

name: Watson, Michele
bio: (Auckland New Zealand: 9 Dec 1947 - ) Born Michele Boyes-Hunter. She met Alan Watson in 1985 & married him 1988. Life Member of the SAM and Honorary Member of the New Zealand Society of Magicians. Director of Magic New Zealand 1999 to present. 2002 DRAGON Award for Alan Watson & Michele. Articles in MUM, Magicana, Magic Circular & Linking Ring.

name: Watson, Stanley
bio: (Hull, England: 28 Jan 1924-) Pro with assistant-wife Diane. Later took up a few specialties such as No-Cut Scissors. Watts, H. A. (Chatham, Kent, England: 8 Aug 1906-) Aka "Brian Baxter". School-master by profession. Semi-pro sleight-of-hand artist. [Go2]

name: Wayne, Don
bio: (Oklahoma City, Oklahoma: 8 Dec 1948-) Born Don Wayne Brockhaus, later legally changed to Don Wayne. Learned at age 5 from a left-behind magic book found in his new home. Pro debut c1966. 1970 TAOM Club Act Trophy. Moved out to Hollywood c1973. Soon joined Mark Wilson in helping develop his magic course & stayed on as consultant on his TV shows until 1976. Full-time consultant for 6 months in 1976 to Orson Welles on his never completed magic film, The Magic Show. Full-time consultant to David Copperfield 1977-present. 1980 AMA Award of Merit. [Wh] "Wayre, B." [pen name in Magic Wand] SEE: Leat, Harry

name: Weaver, Neil, MIMC
bio: (Britain: -28 Dec 1952) Inspired & taught c1890 by semi-pro father. Salesman in family shoe shop in London. Semi-pro card & coin manipulator by 1900. London correspondent for Mahatma 1901. In 1905 co-founded (with Herbert J. Collings & Ernest K. Adams) The Magic Circle. Remembered for having instigated the resignation of David Devant from The Magic Circle in 1910. [Abra#2273-#2275]

name: Webb, Clive
bio: (Britain: fl.1980s) Comedy magician. 1988 British Magical Grand Prix Champion.

name: Webb, Dominique
bio: (France: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Dominique Weber. Pro with illusion & hypnotic acts, the latter involving strip-tease. Dealer ("La Boutique Magique") in Paris in 1960s. Taught Gaëtan Bloom c1963. [Dif;Bou]

name: Weber, Herman L[udwig]
bio: (Lancaster, England: fl.1870s-80s) Stage name. Affected German accent. Minor pro in Liverpool. Taught Douglas Beaufort in 1880. (Allentown, Pennsylvania: 17 Jun 1900-23 Feb 1953) Aka "Namreh" (since 1919), "The Wizard Weber", & "Mr. Hocus Pocus". Inspired at age 7. Debut in 1921. Semi-pro in Chicago 1923-31. Also magic dealer ("Namreh's New Magic") in Chicago in late 1920s. 1934 Sphinx Award. As pro toured a Spook Show thru eastern USA 1935-41 & entire USA until Dec 1943 when retired from touring. Continued to write on magic & play local dates. Invented Sympathetique card trick (well before 1934). Wrote Namreh's Necromantic Novelties (1919-22, a series of booklets), Namreh's Potpourri (1927-29, a series of booklets), Namreh's New Magic (1928, a catalog), Namreh's Lincoln Rings [c1932], Money from Magic (1935, 32pp), Out of the Spook Cabinet (1947), etc. Tricks in Sphinx, Genii, & Hugard's Magic Monthly. [Walk2;St;Th;Jinx#149;Ho;WWM]

name: Weber, Jean
bio: (France: fl.1950s-70s) Member of the Comédie-Française. Eminent amateur sleight-of-hand artist in Paris. [Dif]

name: Weber, Michael "Mike
bio: (Long Beach, California: 6 Oct 1961-) Learned from semi-pro father Ronald Weber. Semi-pro close-up (law student &, since 1990, a lawyer). 1982 AMA Junior Achievement Award (shared). 1983 & 1993 Desert Magic Seminar 3rd prize; 1985 FISM 3rd prize in close-up. Co-partner with Ricky Jay in consulting firm "Deceptive Practices" 1993-present. Video (1987). Wrote Life Savers (1991). Reviewer for Inside Magic & Magic until 1993. Tricks in Genii, etc. [Bo#213]

name: Weber, William
bio: See: Wright, T. Page

name: Webster, Douglas E [dward] "Doug
bio: (Rockford, Illinois: 22 Nov 1953- ) Inspired & learned around age 9 from father's gift of Cups-&-Balls. Tutored by Walter B. Graham. Occasional paid party work. MA in biology. In US Navy 1979-87 as lieutenant, last 5½ years as deception planner, applying the theory of magic to military deception. With a Washington, DC, think-tank 1987-present, again working on military deception. [Wh]

name: Webster, Richard [Edward]
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 9 Dec 1946- ) Inspired at age 7 seeing magician at a birthday party. Semi-pro magician since 1976 & pro mentalist, childrens magician (as "Riccardo"), & close-up worker since 1981. Pet effect: Medieval Tarot, which he invented in 1986. Was the only full-time mentalist in New Zealand for more than 20 years. President of New Zealand Society of Magicians 1976-77. 1990 PEA Mentalist of the Year, 1995 The Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Scroll of Honour, 1997 The Variety Artists Club of New Zealand Benny Award for Top Specialty Act, 2007 PEA Dan Blackwood Memorial Award for Outstanding Contributions to the Art of Mentalism, 2008 MagicNZ Lifetime Achievement Award "in celebration of a lifetime dedicated to excellence in writing magical literature." Wrote Quick Readings with Numerology (1979, 12pp), Quick and Effective Cold Reading (1985, 74pp), How to Build Up a Psychic Practice with Full-length Cold Readings (1986, 76pp), How to Read Minds (1987, 16pp, for the laity), Psychometry from A to Z (1987, 74pp), Aura Reading for Fun and Profit (1988, 74pp), Cashing in on Past Lives (1989, 68pp), The Mail Order Psychic (1990, 72pp), Pendulum Power for the Psychic Entertainer (1990, 72pp), Home Psychic Parties for Fun and Profit (1991, 64pp), Good Luck from Beijing (1991, 92pp), You Are a Rainbow (1991, 24pp), Pitch Books (1991, 40+pp), Cold Reading for the Magician (1991, 24pp), Riccardo on Children's Magic (1992, 36pp), Money-Making Psychic Development Classes (1992, 76pp), Plan for Success (1992, 40pp), How to Make Money Giving Free Talks (1993, 72pp), Astrology for the Psychic Entertainer (1993, 72pp), Ladies' Nights (1994, 64pp), Entertaining Mentalism (1994, 64pp), Using Your Intuitive Edge for Fun and Profit (1995, 64pp), Cold Reading the Future with Numerology (1995, 64pp), Cold Reading Variations (1996, 64pp), The Astral Travel Workshop (1997, 56pp), The Brotherhood of Ring 160 (1998, 64pp), The Psychic Business (1998, 60pp), King of the Small Towns (2006, 60pp), The Tarot for Fun and Profit (2008, 68pp), Readings as Entertainment (2009, 128pp). Tricks in Magick, New Invocation, Magicana, Magigram, Genii, Seance, MUM, LR. 9 audios (1986-2006), 6 videos (1988 - 1995). [LR11/98;Wh2]

name: Wee Tinn Cann
bio: See: Maskelyne, Jasper

name: Weeks, Larry
bio: (24 $ ^{th} $ Sep 1919 – 13 $ ^{th} $ Oct 2014) Lester Fulton Weeks, best known as Larry Weeks was born in Salem, Mass. and died at a VA hospital in New York at age 95. His family moved to the Bronx, in New York in 1929. When he was ten his father, Aaron, an importer who worked for the Scandinavian Embassy, taught Larry a few magic tricks. Larry performed at P.S. 46 and attended Bronx Boys High School and Brooklyn College. Larry learned to juggle and earned the nickname “speedsational” for his amazing balance and rapidly paced act. He developed an act called “Juggling For Fun” which toured in New York, Boston and Montreal. In the late 1930’s Larry performed magic in New York City parks with Abe Hurwitz and his Peter Pan Magic Club. In World War II, Larry found himself at Ft Monmouth where he was seen by Irving Berlin and transferred to Fort Upton in 1942. He became part of the "This Is The Army" detachment as part of the traveling show which raised funds for the war effort. The show appeared on Broadway and played in 21 countries. Corporal Weeks, the baton twirling juggler was now juggling knives forks, potato spuds and apples an act built around the K.P. duties of the "Kitchen Police." It should be noted that Weeks was the originator of apple juggling in which he took a bite of the apple at each turn until he was juggling only the core. In 1943 he repeated his role in the Warner Brothers film of the same name. Once back in civilian life he both juggled and did magic, developing a children's show market. He also found a way to make seamless sponge balls and marketed them under the name of Spongecraft. He booked other performers and in September of 1966 came up with the idea of producing the first 'ALL DAY MAGIC CONVENTION" held at the hotel Lexington in New York City. For a $3.00 registration fee the attendees got a movie, close-up magic, a dealer demo, auction, raffle and a professional evening show. He drew 200 magicians and it was so successful that he scheduled another one three months later. He produced a total of 48 during his lifetime. Weeks was a friend to many of the famous magicians of our time including Cardini, Roy and Connye Benson, Frakson, Paul Rosini and in 1979 and 1980 produced two of the New York "Salute to Magic" shows featuring his friend Richiardi. Larry Weeks was a collector of vaudeville props, books, juggling and magic props, escape tricks and films specializing in Charlie Chaplin, WC Fields and Houdini. Larry always attended the collectors meetings and was a regular attendee at Sid Radner's Houdini Séances. He was very proud and boasted that his final resting place was a plot at the Machpelah Cemetery a few hundred yards away from the Houdini family graves. He was interred there with a grave side Jewish service, a military "Honor Guard" and the Society of American Magicians "Broken Wand" ceremony. He was also a longtime member of the IBM.

name: Wegener, Claus
bio: (Germany: 18 Dec 1953-) Magician (as "Dixon"), lecturer, & magic collector (books, posters, playing cards) in Darmstadt. 1978 MZvD 3rd prize in kid magic. [Nad]

name: Wehle, Ernst
bio: (Germany: fl.1830s) Pro. Claimed to be student of Jacob Philadelphia. Played Finland in 1834 & Moscow in 1837. Pet effect: the Decapitation à la Scot. [St]

name: Weibel, Richard J[ohn] "Dick
bio: (Allentown, Pennsylvania: 29 Jun 1929- ) Newspaper journalist in his hometown. Has degree in psychology. Learned magic at age 13 from novelty dtore tricks. Amateur mental magician & collector. Has written monthly "Conjuring Psychology" column for The Sphinx & The Linking Ring (1952), some reprinted as Conjuring Psychology (1980). Invented Triple Color Changing Silk (Abbott's). Wrote "An Annotated Bibliography of Conjuring Psychology" in Journal of Magic History (1979). Tricks & articles on history & psychology in Sphinx, Conjuror's Magazine, Genii, MUM, Hugard's Magic Monthly, Magic Manuscript, Magic Magazine, etc. Reviews in The Magnet, Journal of Magic History, & Collectors' Forum. [LR9/94;Wh2]

name: Weidmann, Theophil
bio: (Zürich, Switzerland: 15 Sep 1944- ) Inspired at age 5 seeing magician do the Sweets from Dove Pan. Economist. Semi-pro stage illusionist (with Egyptian theme) with partner-sister Jane (b.1953) since 1960 as "Philius & Jane". Has toured Europe since c1974. Pet effect: Blaney Ladder Levitation. Articles in Hokus-Pokus. [Wh2]

name: Weigle, Oscar [John]
bio: (West New York, New Jersey: 5 Dec 1918-) Learned in 1934 as member of International Society of Junior Magicians & visits to Holden's shop in New York city. Writer-editor. Amateur close-up magician plus some mental magic. Invented Color Changing Deck (by 1947 with Curry) & Color Scheme card effect (in 1948). Wrote Do That Again (1939, 76pp, with Robert Parrish) & Color Scheme (1949). Tricks in Dragon, Jinx, Phoenix, Genii, Tops, Pallbearers Review, Apocalypse, & Parrish & Goodrum's You'd Be Surprised. [Wh2]

name: Weil, John [pronounced VILE]
bio: (Austria: 21 Dec 1873-dead) Stage name of Joachim Lüfschitz. Jew. Pro card & coin man. Billed as "The Man of Mystery". Played the USA 14 years as "Vitrio". His brother Leon was world-famous as the mimic "Rogee". [CMM4/08]

name: Weill, Robert K. "Bob
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 1 Nov 1912-20 Apr 2000) Learn as kid from a German magic set. Corporate management consultant. Amateur close-up magician. Column "Bob's This 'N That" in Linking Ring 1930-c1940. In 1939 co-wrote and published (with Ralph Hinkson) the famous spoof-issue of The Jinx magazine known as the "Fake Jinx". First editor of "Focus Focus Parade" in Linking Ring 1941-48. Has large collection of magic books. In 1979 co-founded (with Howard Lyons) the invitation-only Ibidem Event at the Oban Inn at Niagara-on-the-Lake. Is now founder-impresario of the Oban Event. Wrote Funny Stuff for Funny Magicians (with Frank Lane). Invented "Cig to Pipe", "Slate Gag" (Abbott's), Comedy of Spirits (by 1940), etc. Many articles in Linking Ring (+ 1-man "Parade"), etc. [Th;Wh2]

name: Weinbruch, Emil
bio: (Germany: 19 Sep 1921-) Former mail-order dealer in Frankfurt. Performs as "Bora". [Roh]

name: Weiner, Irv[ing]
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 4 Oct 1923-14 Dec 1999) Aka "John Avery" & "Mr. Fingers". Son of deaf-mute parents. Taught first trick by mother in 1930, then self-taught from library books. Inspired to become a pro by seeing Blackstone at age 14. Attended Chavez School in 1947 on GI Bill, graduating to become an instructor there. Owner of "Irv Weiner's Studio of Magic" in Boston 1949-55. Pro close-up, specializing in college 2-hour one-man shows. Pet effects: Vernon's Travellers, Thumb Tie. Wrote Dabbling with Daub (1951, 7pp). Invented over 200 original effects published as "Manu-Secrets", including Soft Dice (1952), Flabbergasting! (1952), Red Tape Thumb Tie (1953), No Nest Cups & Balls (1953), Soft Dice (1954), The Travelling Salesman (1954), Just Imagination (1954), Alphabet Soup Card Trick (1955), Beyond Belief (1955), Red Tape (1955), Guillo Card (1956), & The Prophet's Beard (1957), with Ray Hyman). Tricks in Genii, New Jinx, MUM, Linking Ring, etc. [LR5/2004;MUM2/92;LR9/82;NJ#6;Mag;Wat;Wh5] "Weirdo" "Weirdo the Magician" SEE: "O'Day, Buddy"

name: Weise, Roland [Ernst]
bio: (Pössneck/Thüringen, Germany: 12 Jun 1928-) Learned magic in 1938 at school club. Journalist & director. Amateur magician as "Rolex". Major collector of the entertainment arts, particularly circus, variety, showmen, & showbusiness. Claims his "Archiv Internationaler Artistik" is largest such collection in Europe: 6,500 books, 32,000 journal issues, 13,000 posters & playbills, 16,000 programs, 30,000 photos, 185 circus & variety films, & 1,500 phonograph records. Has written on this subject extensively in German, Russian, Polish, French, & English-language publications. [Wh2]

name: Weisensel, George L [ewis]
bio: (Rochester, New York: 30 May 1898-11 Aug 1990) Inspired at age 15 seeing Houdini. Travelling dental salesman. Moved to Baltimore area in 1924. Semi-pro illusionist since 1926, touring Eastern states. Aka "Weisini". Invented the Splinter from the Hand gag (by 1936). [SAM;WWM]

name: Weisigk, Adolf
bio: (Brazil: 1894-) Amateur magician, living in Mozambique 1914-17. Moved to Portugal where he turned pro in 1919 as "Visir Al-Adim". Later returned to Brazil. Wrote several books on magic. [Cam]

name: Weisini
bio: See: Weisensel, George L.

name: Weiss, "Dr" Aaron
bio: (USA?: fl.1940s-60s) Pro escape artist & mentalist in USA. Aka "Docweiss" (also as "Doc Weiss"). With Mrs Weiss did world's 1st escape act (handcuffs, shackles, mail-bag, & straightjacket) on TV in New York on 31 Oct 1946. Tricks in HMM.

name: Weiss, Doc
bio: See: Weiss, "Dr" Aaron

name: Weiss, John P.
bio: (USA: 3 Jan 1907- ) Policeman in New York City where he founded the "Magicops" club. Amateur to semi-pro magus. Articles in magic magazines. [LR1/52;St]

name: Weldon, Bill [James]
bio: (McAlester, Oklahoma: 29 Jun 1920-) Learned at age c10, mainly from library books. Newspaper advertising manager with The Cleveland Press 1948-82. Part-time pro stage & platform magician since age 21. US Army Special Services in WW II, including 3 years with USO in England & Europe as magician & MC with "Yvette & Her G.I. Gang". Pet effects: Sucker Egg & Cards Across. Collector Tricks & articles since 1942 in Sphinx, Tops, Linking Ring (+ 4 one-man "Parades"), & MUM. [LR19/97,2/89,LR5/55;Wh2]

name: Well [probable misspelling]
bio: See: Velle, Joseph

name: Weller, Charles S. "Charlie
bio: (USA: 1878-1953) Insurance executive, real estate agent, & legislator. Amateur magician by 1904. 2 tricks in Magic (1905). In early 1930s coined the term Piff Paff Poof for Gene Gordon's famous unlinking pins effect. Dealer & famous maker ("Weller Magic") of collapsible latex magic props in Mitchell, South Dakota, beginning in 1939 with eggs and adding frankfurters in 1941 & his various bottles since 1947. Invented the Startling Coin Vanish (by 1940). His widow sold the business on her retirement at age 90 in 1976 to Wes Strong.

name: Welles, [George] Orson
bio: (Kenosha, Wisconsin: 6 May 1915-10 Oct 1985) Inspired by seeing magic shows. Learned from Mysto Magic set at age 5 and sleight-of-hand around 8. In 1937 applied his knowledge of magic to the theater in his play, Doctor Faustus, which used a black-art stage & 5 stage traps to instantly vanish & reveal the ghostly actors. Since his "War of the Worlds" broadcast in 1938, a world-famous radio, stage, & film actor-director. In summer 1941 (with Dolores Del Río as his assistant) he became a semi-pro magician, touring a magic act at the California State Fair, county fairs, & in theaters. Took formal card lessons from Cy Endfield in 1942 & Jean Hugard in 1943. In early 1943 did magic shows for USO units in southern California with Rita Hayworth as his main assistant. The high point of this period was his Mercury Wonder Show under canvas in Hollywood in 1943, assisted by Hayworth, Marlene Dietrich, & once by Johnny Carson. In 1946 produced, directed, acted in play Around the World, which had some of his magic, including possible 1st use of man-sized Square Circle, from which he produced himself. Practised hypnotism after learning it in 1947 while studying his "Cagliostro" role for the film Black Magic. Also practiced mind-reading trick to get women to talk freely. In 1950 toured Germany & Belgium with his "An Evening With Orson Welles" drama, comedy, & magic act with Eartha Kitt as singer-assistant. In 1951 toured a 1-man show in Scandinavia including his magic act. In Feb-Mar 1956 did a 25-minute magic & Shakespearean recitation act for 3 weeks at the Riviera Hotel in Las Vegas. In one Hollywood show Gay Blevins was his assistant. Magic consultant on film Trick or Treats (1962). Did a magic act in movie Casino Royale (1967). Life-time member of the Magic Castle since 1967. In Sep 1968 world-premiered Chuck Jones' Mis-Made Lady on American TV. Played magicians in films A Safe Place (1970) & Get to Know Your Rabbit (1972). His 1973 film F for Fake featured some of his magic. 1982 Commander of the Legion of Honor. 1985 AMA Special Fellowship. Died of a heart attack, famous but poor. 2 tricks in Phoenix. 1 article in Genii. His autobio is Orson Welles & Peter Bogdanovich, This Is Orson Welles (1992). The best general & magical bio is Frank Brady, Citizen Welles (1989). Another good bio is Barbara Leaming, Orson Welles (1985). Also Charles Higham, Orson Welles (1985), Simon Callow, Orson Welles: The Road to Xanadu (1995), and David Thomson, Rosebud (1996). Also Bart Whaley, Orson Welles -- The Man Who Was Magic (manuscript in progress). [MM10/83;Mag]

name: Wells, Ozzie
bio: (USA: fl.1940s-50s) Lived in Philadelphia where he studied acting. Pro with a pantomime comedy magic act. As "Roulette", a pretend Englishman, he played the NY Palace in 1954 with that same act. TV bit in 1958. [HMM1/59]

name: Wells, Dr. William A[dams] "Bill
bio: (Crewe, Virginia: 1 May 1940- ) Initially learned from Xmas gift magic sets c1949 & c1952. Inspired by Bobo to take up magic seriously. Aka "Marvello, the Boy Magician" in 1975. US Government policy analyst for EPA in Washington, DC. Semi-pro close-up magician, doing his "Colonial Act" as "Wells the Conjuror". IBM President 1983-84. Wrote & illustrated many trick instructions for Emerson & West and Al Cohen and booklets of Larry West, John Murray, & Scot York. Articles in Linking Ring. [LR7/83;Wh2]

name: Wellor
bio: (Klagenfurt, Germany: 22 Feb 1883-) Stage name of Josef Monsberg. [Roh] Wels, Byron G[erald] "By" (New York City, New York: 20 Apr 1924-) Learned at age c8 from father's gift of magic set. Writer-editor with Gernsback Publications. Semi-pro stage magician mainly as illusionist. Wrote Magic Made Easy (1977, 96pp), The Great Illusions of Magic (2 vols, 1977, 308+120pp), Here is Your Hobby: Magic, The Nonsense Magic of Byron Wels, The X-Rated Magic of Byron Wels. Articles in Magic Magazine, Magic Circular, etc. [Wh2]

name: Weltman, Manny
bio: (Cleveland, Ohio: 5 Sep 1931-16 May 1994) Moved to California around age 10. Inspired at age 10 seeing Blackstone. Film writer & actor. Amateur magic historian. Leading collector of Houdiniana (since age 11). Edited Houdini: A Definitive Bibliography (1991, 43pp). Wrote Houdini: Escape into Legend: The Early Years, 1862-1900 (1993, 54pp). Articles in Genii. [Wh]

name: Wen Hai
bio: See: "Tenkai"

name: Wendland
bio: (Czechoslovakia: -1943) Pro as "Zenati". Pet effect: Vanishing Radio. [Al]

name: Wenk, Timothy
bio: (Manhattan, New York City, NY: 21 Oct 1959-) Learned at age 8 when older brother got him interested & Howard Schwarzman took him to Tannen's. Started as part-time street magician. Pro since 1979 with close-up, mental, & kid-show magic. Works banquets, trade shows, & TV. 1991 FISM 2nd prize for invention. Invented Misled. Wrote Insomnia (1989, 30pp) & Stuff You'll Use (1991). Tricks in Apocalypse & Blue Print. [Wh2]

name: Werba
bio: (Portugal: 1921- ) Stage name of Manuel ALVES DE ABREU. Learned magic at age 9. Amateur debut in 1946. Pro illusionist since 1950, playing the Coliseu dos Recreios that year. Worked a 2-person telepathy act with assistant "Ninita" since 1951. [Cam]

name: Werner, Francis J.
bio: (New York City, NY: 18 Jun 1863-10 Aug 1927) Joined the SAM in 1902 as Member #10. SAM President 1906-08. Pet effect: Bill Tearing. First to perform the Broken Wand Ceremony when in Nov 1926 at Elks Club in New York City he broke a wand at Houdini's funeral.

name: Wernini
bio: (Sweden: 12 Oct 1912-27 Mar 1983) Stage name of Sten Werner. Semi-pro in Malmö, Sweden. 1953 Danish Magic Circle 1st prize. Articles in Trollkarlen. [St]

name: Wernolf, Professor
bio: See: Weston, Arthur

name: Werris, Samuel "Snag
bio: (USA: 1911-1987) Comedy writer for radio, movies (since 1944), & TV (since 1949). Wrote for Jackie Gleason shows (1962, 1966), Jerry Lewis, etc. Amateur magician in Los Angeles. Coached Lewis for his magic bits in The Geisha Boy (1958). Friend of Orson Welles by mid-1950s. Founding member in 1963 of The Magic Castle. REF: Internet Movie Database (2004)

name: Wessel, [Wilhelm] "Willi" [pronounced VIH-lee VESS-el]
bio: (Enger, Germany: 9 Apr 1947- ) Learned around age 15 from books. Lithographer in West Berlin. Amateur close-up & card magician. Former dealer in West Berlin. Wrote Close-up Ring and Rope Routine. Articles in Magische Welt. [Wh5]

name: Wessely, Otto [pronounced VESS-en-lee]
bio: (Leoben, Austria: 13 May 1945- ) Pro comedy illusionist with his assistant-wife Crista [sic], specializing in crazy comedy magic. Also cardman. Inspired by Richiardi Jr. Pet effect: the Razor Blades. Debuted in the Prater in Vienna 1963-69. Moved to France (Paris) in 1972, playing the Olympia that year. In 1975 co-starred (with Marc Yno) in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique. Switched to comedy magic in 1977. Did 2-hour "The Revolt of the Doves" show in Paris for 8 months in 1980. 1982 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic. Played the Las Vegas Hilton (1983 for 6 months), the Crazy Horse Saloon in Paris (c1984-1989, 1992), the London New Hippodrome (1989). Has toured Canada, USA, Europe, & Asia. TV bits. [Genii9/92;Win;Bou2]

name: West [Jr], Fielding [Franklin]
bio: (Boise, Idaho: 31 Aug 1949- ) Learned at age 10 from grandfather. BA in psychology. Car salesman (2 years) until age 25 when turned full-time pro comedy magician, first as "Mr Magic" (1975-78) thence as "Amazing Fielding". Hosted "Magic Gang" Jacksonville, Florida, TV kid show (44 shows) 1976-77. Works with assistant-wife Pam West, mainly in Las Vegas. Pet effects: Bird Squish & Head Popping Off, Sub Trunk, Tiger Production. Invented Fielding's Bird Switch, Fielding's Clothes Switch (Sub Trunk with tiger), Fielding's Ring Disappearance, Fielding's Needle Thru Hand. 1987 Desert Magic Seminar 3rd prize. Video segment (1990). Effects in Darwin's thumb trick books. [LR11/93;Wat;Wh5]

name: West, [Gilbert Lorenzo] "Larry
bio: (Ithaca, New York: 13 Dec 1931-24 Nov 1989) Learned from gift of Mysto Magic set at age 8. International broadcaster. Semi-pro close-up cardman. Mail-order dealer-publisher (with Arthur Emerson) as "Emerson & West" 1968-death. Co-invented (with Emerson) many small-packet effects. Edited "The Card Corner" column for Linking Ring 1985-90. Wrote Tricks You Can Count On (1960, 36pp, with Verne Chesbro), Tell-Tale Timepiece (1982, 44pp, with Emerson), Slightly Subtle Swindles, Corner the Market (1991, 61pp), Souvenirs (1991, 8pp), Courting the Queen (1991, 6pp). See Ray Eyler, The Count Lives, Long Lives the Count: The Magic of Larry West (1990, 34pp). [Wh2] "Westfield, Clif" SEE: Hull, Burling Weston, Arthur A. (Brighton, England: 1847-1 Apr 1880) Pro magician, billed as "The Sensational Conjurer". As "Professor Wernholf" [sic] was assistant to Smith of Bristol. In 1878 as "Boz" he exhibited the Psycho-like automaton he called "Yorick". Also did a Cabinet Act. Died in Scotland, a suicide. [St;Cl]

name: Wetherald, George
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Invented breakaway wand (by 1937).

name: Wethered, Judge Ernest H. C., OBE
bio: (Britain: 18 Jul 1878-17 Apr 1975) Learned from books by Hoffmann & Sachs & lessons from Charles Bertram. Judge until retired in 1950. Amateur magician. Past President of the British Ring. Articles in Linking Ring (1948). [Le]

name: Wetzel, Charles "Charley
bio: (USA?: c1888-) Master machinist and tool-and-die maker for the Petrie-Lewis Mfg. Co. in New Haven from its early years until closing in 1968. Older brother of Eddie Wetzel, who also worked for P&L as a machinist.

name: Wetzell, Oskar Wilhelm
bio: (Finland: 5 Dec 1888-27 Nov 1928) Bookbinder in Helsinki. Semi-pro magician. [St;Vo58]

name: Wetrik
bio: (Trento, Italy: 1906-dead) Stage name of Melchiore Zatelli. Died in Alexandria, Egypt.

name: Wexler, Warren [Marshall] "Wex
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 22 Sep 1932- ) Learned at age 10 giving magic shows for 2 cents in garage with cousin & a friend. Attorney in Chicago & semi-pro magus since 1967 aka "Warren the Wizard" since 1975 with magic & mentalism. Pet effects: Professor's Nightmare & Gag Bag. Collector of books & apparatus, particularly of Downs & DeLand. Tricks & articles in Ollapodrida, Perennial Mystics, Genii, Linking Ring, Magic Circular, Magicol, & books by F. Marshall, R. Nelson, & H. Lorayne. [Wh5]

name: Weyer, Alex
bio: (Mondérange, Luxembourg: 4 Feb 1872-18 Mar 1921) Stage name of J.-P. Decker, aka "Weyer le Mystérieux". Brought by parents to USA in 1887. Tutored by Maurer. Inspired by seeing A. Herrmann to go pro, which he did in a New York dime museum. Thence to music hall success in France & Italy. Moved to Egypt in 1918 where he soon retired, dying in Cairo. [Go2;Dif]

name: Weyganda, Peter
bio: (Germany: 2 Feb 1928-) Stage name of Peter Weyersberg. Pro circus magician since 1946. [Nad]

name: Whaley, Dr Bart[on Stewart] PhD
bio: (San Francisco, California: 26 May 1928-) Military intelligencer & historian 1951-68. Doctorate in Political Science, MIT, 1969. Deception theorist since 1968 as author of Stratagem: Deception & Surprise in War (1969, 965pp), Codeword BARBAROSSA (1973, 376pp), Cheating (1982, 339pp, with Dr J. Bowyer Bell under joint-pen name of "J. Barton Bowyer"), etc. Amateur student of magic as deception since 1973. Wrote The Encyclopedic Dictionary of Magic (1989, 787pp), which won the John U. Zweers Scholarship Award; Who's Who in Magic (1990, 463pp), which won the Henry Ridgely Evans History Award; (with Martin Gardner & Jeff Busby), The Man Who Was Erdnase (1991, 434pp), which won the SAM Special Library Award; The Language of Magic (2000, 37pp), and Orson Welles: The Man Who was Magic (2005 CD edition). Article & reviews in Epoptica. The John Neville Maskelyne Prize 1992. [CA]

name: Wheatley, Al[bert H.]
bio: (Australia: 1901-12 Nov 1964) Aka "Ching Ling Fu", "Tung Pin Soo", & finally "Chop Chop" (since 1947). Inspired in 1906 seeing magician on the steamship on which his parents moved with him to the USA. Learned buying tricks & books at age 10 & c1919-c1925 assisting Jean Hugard at the latter's Coney Island theater. Pro comedy magic as a pseudo-Chinese. Toured with the Ted Lewis big band. Played top theaters, nightclubs, & hotels. His assistant-wife was Charlene. Invented the magnetic self-cutting Chop-Chop Deck (1947), the famous Chop Cup (in early 1950s), Envello (1958), Colorama (1958), Micromental (1958), Mind-O-Matic (1960). NOTE: Christian name often misgiven as "Alvin" or "Arthur". [Tay]

name: Wheeler, Bert
bio: (Southeastern states, USA: 22 Feb 1909-24 Jul 1946) Pro dealer since 1938 (Hollywood's Magic Shop) on Hollywood Blvd. Knowing no magic, he opened the shop on Hollywood Blvd as cover for his real & then illegal backroom business as a distributor of pornographic movies. He hired Frank Herman to manage the magic. But when the focus-focus business quickly prospered, Wheeler dropped the porn, began to learn some magic for the first time, and moved to larger quarters on a corner of Hollywood & Vine. Got a private pilot's license, bought a plane, & died in a spectacular crash. The shop was bought from Wheeler's surviving sisters in late 1947 by Louis St. Pierre & his son.

name: White, Brunel
bio: (Britain: c1892-21 Oct 1944) Stage name of Thomas C. Morgan. Pro dealer in Llandilo, South Wales, in 1920s, & thence in London. Invented "Master Hat" (1919, for silk production). Wrote Original Mysteries for Magicians (1919, 82pp) & Modern Master Mysteries (1923, 107pp). Wrote (as "B.W.") weekly magic page for World's Fair 1935-40. Imprisoned in 1940 for violation of wartime censorship law. [St;Daw94]

name: White, Daisy
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-30s) Born on a March 17th. Learned magic as assistant in Frank Ducrot's act. Then pro demos at Martinka's & Hornmann's in NYC c1920-c1926. Famous among magicians for her slim (118 lb.) figure with an eye-catching décolletage that she used for misdirection while leaning over the counter demoing. Her business card read "Science of Sex and Numbers". Her hoax "love letters" to Houdini, discovered by his widow, were briefly believed in some salacious quarters.

name: White, George Davis
bio: (- Brooklyn: October 11, 1962) He is known in show business/magic history as the "Invisible Man" behind the success of Howard Thurston. An African-American boy, of 10-12 years, in 1899, he answered Thurston's ad for an assistant, never having been in a theater, much less on stage. Despite his age, Howard Thurston hired him. George quickly proved himself adept at assisting Howard, and they did play Tony Pastor's theater, and eventually, the act grew over the years, using larger tricks and illusions until he had a company of over 20, with George as his right hand man, who intuitively knew what Thurston needed during the show. As Mr. Thurston's show became a major theater attraction, Mr. White was depended upon to keep the show running smoothly backstage, as Thurston enthralled his audiences out front. Even though he was the star, Howard would introduce George to the audience saying, "This is my assistant George White, I have never done a show without him, and never will." Thurston died from a stroke in 1936, and after watching Thurston's props and working as a night watchman, he joined "Dante the Magician", (aka Harry Jansen) in 1940 and continued with his show, until 1944, when he decided to go back to New York. George then worked in Brooklyn, for The Ace Blasting, Art Glass, & Glass Products companies, that were run by employer and friend, Harry Soll. He died in a Brooklyn Hospital on October 11, 1962, having had kept little or no contact with the magic world he had spent most of his life in. For decades, many asked, "What happened to George White, Thurston and Dante's chief assistant?" It was a mystery for years, and a disappointment to all who admired and appreciated him, to learn he had died in obscurity.

name: White, Francis "Frank", MIMC
bio: (Battersea, London, England: 4 Sep 1906-7 May 1989) Aka "Wand & Fake". Accountant. Taught magic by David Devant. Semi-pro stage & cabaret magic. Honorary Secretary of The Magic Circle 1945-54. 8th President of The Magic Circle 1958-89. 1987 Magic Circle Gold Medal. SAM Hall of Fame. Wrote More Tricks of the Television Stars (48pp). Memoirs are 50 Years at The Magic Circle (audiotape).

name: White, Frederick George
bio: (Rhayader, Wales: 24 Oct 1912- ) Aka "Fredeen". Learned magic at age 14. Semi-pro with cards & silks. [Go2]

name: White, George
bio: (USA: c1890-) Afro-American. Inspired & learned at age 9 as pro assistant to Howard Thurston (1899-1935 when billed as "Keno"), Jane Thurston (1935-38), & Dante (1940). [Pr]

name: White, Jeff
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Pro stage & close-up. Wrote The Visual Artistry of Jeff White (1982, 50pp), Jumbo Coin Magic (1982), etc.

name: White, John
bio: (Britain: -1671) A hack writer for London book publishers. Wrote A Rich Cabinet with Variety of Inventions: Unlock'd and open'd, for the Recreation of Ingenious Spirits at their vacant hours (London: 1651, 90 leaves; 4th edition "with many Additions", 1668, 190pp). This popular work saw 9 editions up to 1773. Its several magic tricks were cribbed in part from Scot.

name: White, Joseph M[ichael] "Little Joe
bio: (Dorchester, Massachusetts: 1 Jan 1925-10 Sep 2001) Pro since 1944, initially as carnival sideshow magician, (as "The Midget Magician"). Then circus (Ringling Bros). Protégé of Will Lindhorst. Aka "The Wee Wizard". Thence kid-show, gospel magic, & mentalism. A 4'4" midget, he billed himself as "Micro, World's Smallest Magician/Mentalist". Also as "Shenanigans" with leprechaun magic act & "Merlin, Ancient Mystic". Dids many commercials, including "Little Oscar" for Oscar Meyer 1949-68. Wrote Magic for Heaven's Sake (1962), Scotch Brand of Magic (1964, 39pp), Micro-Mental Mysteries (1965, 73pp), 5 Micro-Mental Programs (1966, 60pp), & his autobiographical A Wee Wizard's Wiles (1987). Tricks in Linking Ring, (+ a 1960 "1-man Parade") Genii, Hugard's Magic Monthly, New Jinx, Invocation, etc. [Wh2]

name: White [Jr], [Laurence Barton] "Larry
bio: (Norwood, Massachusetts: 21 Sep 1935 - 21 Dec 2008) Tutored at age c5 by local magician Billy Snow. Elementary school science teacher. Amateur magician & magic manufacturer (as White Magic). Specializes in science magic. Invented over 11 marketed tricks. Wrote 9 magic books for children, including So You Want to Become a Magician (1972) & Razzle-Dazzle! (1987). "How's Tricks" column in Magic Manuscript. Magic editor of MUM. Tricks in Genii, MUM, Linking Ring, Mortimer's Magic Magazine. [LR7/92; Time4/Apr/88;Wh5]

name: White, Ralph [Leonard]
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-90s) Pro. Works as "Dr. Presto".

name: Whiteley, Harry
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Pro. Invented Rigid Rope. (Hulme, England: 1 Dec 1875-22 Apr 1945) Stage name of Harry Whiteley Cunliffe, aka "Harry Wilbey". Owner of Manchester Conjuring Trick Works 1905-c1914. Ran a circulating library for magicians at that time (the world's 1st) & revived it in 1930s. Wrote Miracles of Modern Magic [1905, 40pp]; & Marvels of Magic [1906, 24pp], which includes his catalog. REF: [Dawes #109-#111]

name: Whitlam, Joseph H.
bio: (Canada: -1939) Dealer in Toronto, Canada, as the "Japanese Magic and Novelty Store" 1913-1939 (& also as "Whitlam's Temple of Mysteries") in the Yonge Street Arcade. Soon after Whitlam's death Harry Smith bought the shop. [Bo3 for photo]

name: Whitman, Bernard "Bernie
bio: (Cambridge, Massachusetts: 22 Sep 1914-1991) Inspired seeing Thurston show. Learned from Mysto Magic set. Did shows in college. Aero-engineer with Chance-Vought 1935-45 & MIT until 1955. Semi-pro magician. Aka "Fu Ling" with pseudo-Chinese act since c1948, touring for 10 years with assistant-wife Jeri. Danny Tong was his assistant 1954-55. Then high school teacher of industrial arts from 1965 until 1979, during which time he established & toured the South Weymouth High School Magic Company. In 1984 gave David Brisbane, an assistant & protégé, ownership of the "Fu Ling" name and show. [Des;Wh]

name: Whitson, David [William]
bio: (Newcastle, Australia: 9 Mar 1961-) Inspired at age 7 seeing Mark Wilson's TV series. Pro stage & gospel magician since 1988. [Wh2]

name: Whittington, Bill [Edgar]
bio: (Merced, California: 14 Jun 1944-) Learned in 1955 from library books. Pro close-up since 1984, specializing in Cups-&-Balls and rope magic. Book collector. Reopened Golden Gate Magic in 1985, being joined as partners by Bob Koch (1985-1988) & Paul Chosse (1989-present). [Wh2]

name: Whittington-Wickes
bio: See: Wickes, Samuel L. Whittington

name: Whylie, Prof. J. C. [pronounced Y-lee]
bio: (England: fl.1940s) Amateur magician. Invented the Elusive Lady card trick in 1949.

name: Wiberg, Don[ald E.]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 7 May 1936- ) Inspired at age 10 by father doing several tricks. Learned from parent's gift of Gilbert Mysto Magic set. Thru high school & college worked demos at shops of Jim Riley & Frances Marshall. Semi-pro magician. Teacher of technology (retired). IBM President 1984-85.

name: Wichmann, Ralf [pronounced VIK-mahn]
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 5 Jul 1949 - 31 Dec 2009) Became interested in magic c1963, specializing in floating effects. Amateur magician in West Berlin, aka "Braco" since early 1960s. Specializes in & collects floating effects. Wrote Floating Routines for Table and Stage (1973, 139pp; French tr 1981 by Vollmer; pirated as The String Book; authorized repr in 1984 as The Invisible Thread Book, 82pp; new ed as The Invisible Thread Manual, 1997, 96pp), a classic. Also wrote Quadro Asse (1974). Wickes, Samuel L. Whittington "Sammie", MIMC (Leamington Spa, Warwickshire, England: 26 Dec 1893-6 Oct 1970) Aka "Seekhett, the Boy Conjurer" (at age 15), thence "Cellsus, the White Wizard", "Chang Ko Lau" & "The Amazing Chang" (in 1934), & "Vern Lewis". Pro comedy magic since age 15. In the late 1930s turned to Punch & Judy, breeding small livestock, and making musical instruments. Invented The Fire Cauldron, Bracer's Gag, & the Pencil and Peg. [Go2]

name: Wicks, Charles D., MMIC
bio: (Melbourne, Australia: 1900-19 Jul 1967) In business in Melbourne. Amateur magician. [Wal]

name: Widano
bio: (Dresden, Germany: 28 Jun 1938- ) Stage name of Christian Wiedemann. Pro illusionist in East Germany. Wrote Zauberhafte Miniaturen & Iluzja i Elektronika (in Polish). Tricks in Zauberkunst. [Mec;Roh;Nad]

name: Widenmann, Wilhelm
bio: (Germany: 11 Mar 1943-) Magician & collector (magic books) in Stuttgart. Wrote magic books. [Nad]

name: Wiegleb, Johann Christian [pronounced VEE-glehb]
bio: (Langensalza, Thuringia, Germany: 1732-1800) Apothecary in his home town. Based on Guyot, he wrote Die natürliche Magie (Berlin: 1779; 2nd ed 1782, 468pp), with Danish tr as Naturlig Hexerie for Konstnere og Haandverksmaend (Copenhagen: 1785). Also Natüliches Zauberlexicon (Nürnberg: 1784; Prag: 1789). [St;Dam2]

name: Wien, Frank
bio: (Germany: 28 Apr 1932-) Magician (as "Simbar"), lecturer, & collector of magic history in Norheim, Germany. [Nad]

name: Wiencek, Hans-Joachim
bio: (Germany: 1 Oct 1944-) Magician, aka "Mazony". Dealer ("Studio für Zauberkunst") in Bochum, Germany, by 1989. [Nad]

name: Wiersbe, Warren
bio: (USA: fl.1940s) Close-up. Wrote Action with Cards (1944, 18pp), Mental Cases with Cards (1946, 28pp), & Tantalizing Thimbles (1948, 40pp; repr 1969).

name: Wiesinger, Carl E[mil]
bio: (Buffalo, New York: 26 May 1918-6 Aug 2001) Inspired & learned at age 9 when called on stage by Thurston & bought his book of tricks. Advertising artist (retired). Semi-pro magician since 1940, excepting 2 full-time period in early 1950s & early 1970s doing club dates, parties, & school shows in western New York state. Worked close-up & platform regularly at the Forks Hotel in Buffalo 1972-91. Aka "Flamo" (early 1940s), "Carlo", & finally "Mr. Carl". Pet effects: Ball-to-Watch, Floating Wand, Thimbles, Four Ace Tricks, Professor's Nightmare Tricks in Tops, Conjurors' Magazine, & Linking Ring plus in books by Ginn, Miesel, & Mertz. [LR6/79;Wh5]

name: Wijzenko
bio: See: "Kawecki, Walentyn"

name: Wilba
bio: See: "Uferini, Henri"

name: Wilder
bio: (France: fl.1880s) Pro illusionist. Played the London Pavilion in 1887 with De Kolta's Vanishing Lady.

name: Wilder, Marshall P.
bio: (USA: 19 Sep 1859-10 Jan 1915) Hunchback dwarf. Amateur magician in New York City. SAM member #59. Pro humorist, including the autobiographical The People I've Smiled With (1889), The Sunny Side of the Street (1905), & Smiling 'round the World (1908). Wilfrid the Wizard (Richmond, Virginia: 22 Jan 1883-) Son of English parents. Stage name of Wilfrid Rutherford. Engraver. Semi-pro magician. Invented a version of the Rising Cigarettes (from pack) by 1928 & The Graph-o! Spirit Pencil by 1928. [St]

name: Wilker, Peter
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 1 Nov 1922- ) Learned age c10 watching street magi, reading books, & taking lessons. Professor of mathematics. Amateur magician. Retired to England in 1988. Edited Hokus-Pokus 1976-86. Edited-published Magische Blätter monthly leaflet 1986-88. Wrote The Creation of Magic (1991), Magische Studien 1-10 (1991), & Zauberei mit Bierdeckeln (1991), Methods for Minor Miracles (forthcoming), & Eine Force im Quadrat (forthcoming). Articles in Hokus-Pokus, Abra, & Magie (forthcoming 1993). [Wh5]

name: Willane
bio: (England: 1898-13 Jul 1955) Stage name of William H. Lane. Wealthy fruit wholesaler in Croydon. Took lessons from Edward Victor. Semi-pro magician. His act was that of a tipsy man to whom weird things happened. 1947 Paris International Magic Congress 1st prize for presentation; 1948 FISM Grand Prix. Founder of ARCAS magic publishing house 1945. Wrote Willane's Wizardry (1947, 64pp). Edited the 14 vols of Methods for Miracles (n.d.). See Rae Hammond, Willane's Complete Methods for Miracles (1985; repr 1994). [Dif;Wat]

name: Willard, Clarence E.
bio: (Painesville, Ohio: 9 Jul 1882-31 Jul 1962) Began with a magic act for several years, including heading a full-evening show, until around 1923 when he switched to a self-stretching act. Taught his stretching technique to Carlton. Retired from the stage shortly after appearing at the 1939 San Francisco World's Fair to become a realty manager and restaurant owner, although he continued active in the local Oakland Magic Circle. [Jay]

name: Willard, Frances [Louis]
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: 12 Dec 1940- ) Inspired & learned assisting her father Harry. Pro. Teamed with Glenn Falkenstein in 1978 to do a double mind-reading act. 1979 AMA Visiting Magician of the Year for her own act. Married Falkenstein in 1984. Her daughter Hannah married Michael Ammar in 1990. Video (1989, with Falkenstein). 1990 Dragon Award (with Falkenstein); 1991 Dunninger Award (with Falkenstein); 1994 SAM Hall of Fame (with Falkenstein; 1996 AMA Stage Magician of the Year (with Falkenstein). [Pr;Bo#206;Mag]

name: Willard, Harry Francis
bio: (Clarksville, Texas: 12 Dec 1895-28 Jun 1970) Son of Jim Willard. Aka "Willard the Wizard". Learned assisting father. At age 16 joined a circus briefly as sideshow magician. Pro tent-show illusionist in Texas, taking over his father's performance role in late 1910s, to become the most famous of the Willards. 1968 AMA Performing Fellowship. SAM Hall of Fame. Bio is Bev Bergeron, Willard the Wizard (1978, 154pp). [Pr]

name: Willard, Jim
bio: (Ireland: c1875-22 Jun 1936) Stage name of James Michael Maroney, aka "Willard the Wizard", the 1st to use that title. Moved to USA. Pro tent-show illusionist in Texas by 1895 until around 1914-19 when he passed the stage work to his son Harry, staying on only as manager. Had also briefly used the "Fredrik the Great" stage name & paper c1915. [Pr]

name: Willard, Robert
bio: (California, USA: c1887-1914) Oldest son of Jim Willard. Learned as apprentice to father. Protent-show magician in the North & Central States. [Pr]

name: Willard, Tommy
bio: (Texas, USA: 1903-6 Jul 1936) Son of Jim Willard. Pro tent show illusionist on own in Texas as "Willard the Wizard" & in 1935 as "Mel-Roy" while filling in for the real Mel-Roy. [Pr]

name: Williams
bio:
"Williams -- The Whimsical Wizard" SEE: Williams, Eric "Nitwit"

[See also: Clément, Guillaume]

name: Williams, Carl
bio: (Glamorganshire, Wales: 5 Oct 1922-) Moved to USA in early 1930s. At age 9 learned from Chandu magic set. Pro vent-comedy-magic with USO in WW II. Electrical engineer in southern California (working on top-secret aeronautical projects) until retired in 1988. Maker of fine props. [Bo#246;Albo95]

name: Williams, C[arl] O[rton]
bio: (Australia: fl.1st decade of 1900s-1930s) A key founding member of The Australian Society of Magicians in 1907. Edited The Magic Mirror in Sydney, 1909-12. Articles in The Magic Mirror. Used "Carl Orton" as stage name. [McC]

name: Williams, C[harles] O[swald], MIMC
bio: (Cardiff, Wales: 1865-30 Jan 1924) Watchmaker & jeweller in Cardiff. Semi-pro magician since 1903, working private drawing rooms as "Charles Oswald, the Cardiff Conjurer". Expert sleight-of-hand artist. Magic dealer in Cardiff by 1913 until his death when his daughter continued the business a few years. Early member of The Magic Circle. Persi Diaconis credits the discovery of rising sequences (the basic invariant of riffle shuffling) independently to Williams and C.T. Jordan. [Daw#174; Sphinx10/04; Zo,p.88; Magic5/06]

name: Williams, Claud
bio: (Glasgow, Scotland: 1891-1972) Pro variety comedy magician as "The Great Claud", working solo in an Eton suit. [Hudd]

name: Williams, Dick [Kent]
bio: (Hoisington, Kansas: 17 Jul 1927- ) Learned at age 7 from a Xmas gift Gilbert magic set. Amateur magician since age 13. Broadcaster since late 1940s. Hosted the WMC-TV "Magicland" live ½-hour weekly show in Memphis, Tennessee, Jan 1966-Jan 1989, the longest running magic show in TV history, with over 1,200 broadcasts, as certified in 2001 by Guinness World Records. Continued briefly with the station as announcer & weatherman until retired in 1989, keeping magic as a hobby. Wrote (with wife Virginia Williams whom he married in 1949) Booking Magic (1959, 15pp), Lights! Cameras! Magic!: A Guide to Performing Magic on Television (1994, 202pp), The Haunted Key (1997, 12pp), Dick Williams' Cups & Balls (1999, 12pp). Articles in Tops, Linking Ring, Dragon, & Magigram. [NT11/74;LR6/89;Wh2]

name: Williams, Eric [James] "Nitwit
bio: (Ledbury, Herefordshire, England: 28 Feb 1911-3 Jan 1981 [or Dec 1980]) Debut c1930. Law clerk in Ledbury. Semi-pro comedy magician since debut in 1929, presenting a variety of characters such as "Williams, The Whimsical Wizard", "Madame Le Frisson", & "Eastern Mystic". Edited Devils Chimney 1944-49 (8 issues). Wrote "Nitwittian Chatterings" column in Abra. [Le;WWM]

name: Williams, Gary Lee
bio: (White Plains, New York: 16 Sep 1954-) Learned at age 8 reading library books. Videographer. Semi-pro mentalist since 1977 as "Donovan". Wrote "Donovan's Brain" column in Hocus Pocus 1981-82. Edited Vibrations 1982-83 (20 issues). Tricks in Magick & NY Magic Symposium Collections 4 & 5. See Al Mann, The Donovan Papers (1982). [Wh2]

name: Williams, Geoff[rey]
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) 1979 AMA Junior Achievement Award. Wrote The Theatrical Approach to Magic: A Lecture (1984, 12pp) & Gathering Dust (1986, 176pp).

name: Williams, H. E.
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Proprietor of the "H. E. Williams Magic Shop" in Elwood City, Pennsylvania, in 1955 when he issued a rather substantial catalog.

name: Williams, John [Bernard]
bio: (Launceston, Tasmania: 29 Jul 1945-) Learned in 1963. Semi-pro kid-show and Punch & Judy since 1970. In 1987 bought Card Mondor's Aladdin's Magic Shop, which he now runs as mail-order from his home in Hobart, Tasmania. [Wh2]

name: Williams, Ned
bio: See: "Harbin, Robert"

name: Williams, Oswald
bio: (London, England: 1880-21 Mar 1937) Son of a clergyman. Debut at age 13. Major pro magician (ex-architect) from age 21 as illusionist with assistant-wife Rae Warwick. Noted for his whimsical & fast-paced act. Played the Paris Alhambra in 1907. Toured the USA in 1908. Played the London Coliseum in 1910 & St. George's Hall often from 1917 to 1931. Effectively succeeded Devant after the latter's retirement in 1920. Toured Australia 1924. After his death the rights to most of his many original effects went to Davenport's. Prolific inventor, including the Homing Bells (by 1909), Tea Chest (by 1909), Merry Widow Hat (by 1911), & Dizzy Limit (by 1924). Wrote Hints to Young Conjurers (1919) & Across the Footlights (1925). [Wal;Pr;St;Vo56;Dif;Go2;Mo;Ho;Magic2/10]

name: Williamson, David [Alan] "Dave
bio: (Xenia, Ohio: 17 Feb 1961- ) Learned at age 8 from a Mattel magic set. Pro performer-lecturer since age 15, first in a restaurant. 1980 TAOM Close-Up Trophy. 1981 IBM 1st place in Adult Close-Up & Gold Cups for close-up. Moved to Arlington, Virginia, in 1984.
