Demonstrator with Magic Masters 1986-88. Now performs for private parties in Washington, DC, area. Sometimes works with racoon puppet "Rocky". 1991 AMA Best Lecturer. See Richard Kaufman, Williamson's Wonders (1989, 95pp). Article in Magic. Video bit (1989) & 2 videos (1990 & 1993). TV bit in Britain. [Wh]

name: Willio, Henry [Heinrich?]
bio: (Köln, Germany: 1846-c1900) Pro since age 12. Toured London (1864-70), USA (1871-74), West Indies (1874), etc. [Vo56]

name: Willis, Professor [Edgar?]
bio: (Britain: -23 Aug 1901) Pro. Popular magician at the Royal Aquarium. [Era Annual (1902)]

name: Williston, W[illiam] R. "Bill
bio: (USA: -2 Aug 1959) Interested as boy seeing Adelaide Herrmann show. Railway representative in Rhode Island. An admirer of Van Hoven, he did semi-pro comedy & slap-stick magic, billed as the "Magical Buffoon". Mainly a night club worker. Invented the "Famous Air Mail Mystery" (by 1940). [SAM;Ho]

name: Willmann, Carl [pronounced VIHL-mahn]
bio: (Waren, Mecklenburg, Germany: 4 May 1849 [or 1848]-12 Feb 1934) Watchmaker in Waren then Hamburg. Amateur magician. Pro magic dealer in Hamburg since Nov 1874 [sic]. Co-invented (with Theo Bamberg) fall-apart box (by 1908). Partner with Janós Bartl 1919-1924 as "Vereinigte zauberapparate Fabrik Bartl & Willmann". In 1926 absorbed E. Chambly's local prop-making shop. Died in Hamburg. Father of John Willmann who inherited the business. Edited the first German-language magic magazine, Die Zauberwelt, 1895-1904. Wrote 6 books in German: Moderne Wunder (1886, 240pp; 3rd ed 1897, 320pp), Die moderne Salon-Magie (1891, 460pp; new ed 1926, 555pp), Der Gedächtniskünstler als Hellseher (1891, 85pp), Illustrierte magische Bibliothek (6 vols, 1900, 552pp total), Telepatische Unterrichtsbriefe [c1920, 51pp], and Das Programm eines modernen Zauberkünstlers [c1920, 152pp]. [Vo56;Dif;Albo94;Magic2/03]

name: Willmann, John [pronounced VIHL-mahn]
bio: (Hamburg, Germany: 1873-9 Oct 1955) Son of Carl Willmann. Watchmaker. Visited USA 1896-97. Inherited father's magic shop & factory in Hamburg he inherited in 1934 & renamed "John Willmann & Co." Then partner with Schuetz. Continued the business making apparatus until 1943 when it was bombed out during an Allied air raid. Father of Walter Willmann. Manuscript bio as recorded by Dr Otto Kässens, John Willmann: 70 Years in the Service of Magic (1952). [Roh;Albo94]

name: Willmann, Walter
bio: (Hamburg?, Germany: 1903-) Son of John Willmann. Immigrated to USA in 1924. After return to Germany, moved to Chicago in 1947 to work a year for Berg's Magic Studio. [Magische Welt1/82;Berg]

name: Willmarth, Phil[ip Reed]
bio: (New Castle, Pennsylvania: 19 Aug 1931 – 16 Sep 2014) Learned in 1940 from father's gift of a Will Lindhorst book. Owner of marketing research company. Semi-pro magician since 1959. Specialties: rope & impromptu magic. Also lecturer & MC. Assistant Editor The Linking Ring 1979-1992, Executive Editor since 1993. Wrote The Magic of Matt Schulien (1959), The Ring and Rope Book (1975), Jim Ryan Close-Up (4 vols, 1980-81), Trevor Lewis Close-Up (1981), etc. Editor & publisher of the Eugene Burger booklets. Regular contributor to Linking Ring since 1977, including editor of its "Hocus Pocus Parade" since 1978. Articles in MUM. [Wh2]

name: Willner, Joe
bio: (Austria: fl.1930s) Pro card magician, playing only the better cabarets. Emigrated in 1938, moving to South America.

name: Willtohn, Dody
bio: (France: -1981) Stage name of Adolphe Gonzalez. Pro manipulation & pickpocket act. AFAP Master Magician. 1961 FISM 1st prize for allied arts of magic. NOTE: Surname often misspelled "Wilthon". [Bou]

name: Wilmar, Dr.
bio: See: Marriott, William S.

name: Wilmeth, Don B[urton]
bio: (Houston, Texas: 15 Dec 1939- ) Learned at age c14 buying props from Douglas Magicland in Dallas & from books. Since 1967 Professor of Theatre & English at Brown U in Providence, Rhode Island, specializing in history of popular entertainment including magic. Amateur magician. Honorary Curator of the H. Adrian Smith Collection of Conjuring Books and Magicana at Brown U since 1988. Wrote or edited 9 books on the theatrical arts, including American and English Popular Entertainment (1980); The Language of American Popular Entertainment (1981), a dictionary of jargon, including that of magicians; & Variety Entertainment and Outdoor Amusements (1982). [WWE;Wh2]

name: Wilsmann, Dr. Aloys Christof [pronounced VIHLS-mahn]
bio: (Werl, Germany: 18 Apr 1899-20 Apr 1966) Writer. Amateur magician, specialing in mathematical card tricks with ingenious wording. Died in Nürnberg. Wrote Die zersägte Jungfrau: Von Magiern, Schwindlern und Charlatanen (1938, 238pp; Swedish tr 1939 as Svindlare, Magiker, Charlataner, 2nd German ed 1941, 237pp), Heitere Jagd auf Fragezeichen (1940, 118pp; 2nd ed 1941), & Wunderwelt unter der Tarnkappe (1959). Articles. See book by R. Braunmüller. [St;Al]

name: Wilson, Dr A[Ibert] M., MD
bio: (Aurora, Indiana: 23 Jun 1854-22 Apr 1930) Learned magic at age 11 by lessons from Heller. Physician in Kansas City, Missouri. Semi-promagician. Aka "N.K. Aristos". Third & greatest editor (& publisher) of The Sphinx Oct 1904-1930. Edited Magic: The Magazine of Wonder 1910-11. Acquired the H.J. Burlingame collection of magic books in 1918 and sold it next year to Earl Rybolt. IBM member #277. A colorful & strong personality. SAM Hall of Fame. [Bo#198;Genii1/41;Dor]

name: Wilson, Eric P.
bio: (Britain: fl.1920s-40s) Pro kid-show magic. Invented the Black Hand Gag Towel, according to Darwin (1988, p.7). Edited Magician's Weekly 1925 (9 issues). Wrote Join the Party (1947, 72pp, with Bill Stickland) & a booklet, The Art of Conjuring to Children, bound with Bert Easley's Doing Magic for Youngsters (1948). [Le]

name: Wilson, Greg
bio: (USA: 1965-) Son of Mark Wilson & Nani Darnell. Apprenticed as child & boy with his parents. Now works in their illusion-show consulting business. 1991 Christopher Award for best young magician.

name: Wilson, [William Caddie] "Mac", MIMC
bio: (Britain: 1903-) Pro since 1931. [Go2] (Edinburgh, Scotland: 13 May 1915-2006) Became interested in magic at age 10. Civil servant (retired). Semi-pro close-up & small stage magician. Pet effect: production of a glass of Scotch. MIMC 1948. Deputy Secretary, The Magic Circle's Deputy Secretary since 1954 & Honorary Vice-President since 1964. 1956 Silver Wand. 1993 SAM Hall of Fame. Articles in Magic Circular, Magigram, & MUM. [Daw2;Wh2]

name: Wilson, [James] Mark, MIMC
bio: (Dallas, Texas: 11 Apr 1929-) Inspired at age 8 seeing Tommy Windsor. Learned around age 10 from Thurston's Fifty New Card Tricks. Debut at age 15 (1942) demoing in magic shop. Pro illusionist, marrying his female assistant, Nani Darnell in 1952. Did TV magic since starting in Dallas in 1953. 1954 TAOM Al Sharpe Trophy for Originality in Presentation. Weekly national TV series as "The Magic Land of Allakazam" 1960-65. AMA Magician of the Year, 1972, 1974. Consultant to Bill Bixby's "The Magician" TV series 1973-74. Played the Las Vegas Hilton in 1974. Co-authored (with Walter Gibson) the Mark Wilson Course in Magic (1975, 472pp; French tr 1987 by Vollmer). Authored The Chop Cup Book (1979, ghosted by Earl Nelson & Alan Wakeling). Member of the Board, Academy of Magical Arts 1972-94 & Vice President since 1994. 1985 Dragon Award for Mark Wilson & Nani Darnell. 1988 AMA Masters Fellowship. 1994 SAM Hall of Fame. 1995 Louie Award. Father of Greg Wilson who learned in childhood in the early 1960s on Allakazam as one of his assistants. [Se;MUM8/02;HC;Win2;Mag;Rey]

name: Wilson, Nani
bio: (USA: fl.1950s-90s) A pro dancer, Nani Darnell, who became principal female assistant to Mark Wilson, marrying him in 1952, but keeping "Nani Darnell" as stage name. 1995 Louie Award. Mother of Greg Wilson. [Se]

name: Wilson, Ron[ald Murray]
bio: (Dundee, Scotland: 1 Oct 1926 – 17 Dec 2010) Aka "The Uncanny Scot". Learned 1st trick (broken-and-restored matchstick) around age 5. Semi-pro close-up since 1940s. Moved to Canada (Windsor, Ontario) in 1952 & then, in 1966, to USA (Los Angeles). Pro close-up & cabaret magic since 1966. 1972 AMA Magician of the Year & Best Close-up Magician. AMA Board of Directors since 1969 & its Vice President since 1974. Articles in Tops, Genii, & Talisman. See Richard Kaufman, The Uncanny Scot: Ron Wilson (1987, 157pp). [Mag;Wh2]

name: Wilson, [Anthony Preston] "Tony", MIMC
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 1 May 1942-) Learned at age 11. Retired educational psychologist. Past President of International Brotherhood of Magicians 2004-2005, New Zealand Society of Magicians, 1972-1973, Brotherhood of Auckland Magicians 1971 and 1980. Currently President of IBM Ring 160 Kiwi Magic the Tony Wilson Ring (Inc) Member of SAM and The Magic Circle London (MIMC with Gold Star) Recipient of the "Grand Master of Magic" (NZ) 1998. Articles in Magigram, Alakazam, Genii & LR.

name: Wimann, Professor
bio: (Guaratingueta, São Paulo, Brazil: 26 Aug 1903-14 Nov 1940) Stage name of Avelino PEREIRA DE SOUZA. Musical instrument repairer in Rio de Janeiro. Semi-pro magician. Played clubs in Rio & circuses in the interior. [Fam] "Wind, Albert F." NOTE: Joint pen name of Wilfred Huggins & Herbert Pratt in The Midget Magician. Winder, Roland F. "Roley" [surname pronounced WIN-der, not WINE-der], MIMC (Britain: -7 Dec 1970) Amateur magician & magic book collector. In 1974 his fine collection was auctioned off piecemeal by Sotheby's. That sale served to establish a modern pricing base for antiquarian magic books. Wrote the annotated Check List of the Older Books on Conjuring in the Library of Roland Winder (1966, 32pp). Articles in Magic Cauldron, etc. See Trevor H. Hall, The Winder Sale of Old Conjuring Books (1975). NOTE: First name has been misgiven as "Rowland".

name: Windsor, Tommy
bio: (Marietta, Ohio: 5 Jul 1906-2 Sep 1978) Stage name of Thomas Isaac Lowry. Learned assisting MacDonald Birch. Commercial artist. Since 1924 semi-pro comedy magician, vent, & magic dealer in his home town. Invented Dye Box in 1946. Daily local Virginia 1/2-hour TV show Nov 1953-Jul 1954. Wrote Magician's Merchandising Manual (1938, 42pp), Jackpot (1947, 4 issues as house organ), Tommy Windsor's Die Box Book (1947, 42pp), 64 Ways to Make Magic Pay (1952, 24pp), Suitcase Side Show (1962, 19pp), Tommy Windsor's Clip Art (1972), etc. Co-edited (with George McAthy) The Dope Sheet 1945-48. Column in Magic is Fun. Tricks in Dope Sheet & New Phoenix. [LR12/2005;Th;WWM]

name: Wingard, Herr
bio: (Calcutta, India: 1847-28 Dec 1912). Of Anglo-Indian parents. Minor pro. Toured India, China, Australia, & South Africa before settling in 1880 in Britain where he performed regularly until soon before his death there. [CI;Vo56]

name: Winkler, Albert [pronounced VINK-ler]
bio: (Germany: fl.1890s-1910s) Aka "Carlo Venturini". Played India with the Harmston Circus in 1902 with flag production & flying lamp. Later (by 1910) retired in Singapore. Invented Aga, the rights to which he sold in 1910 to Goldston of Gamage's, at least as claimed by Goldston. Note, however, that this invention is traditionally attributed to others. [Magic8/03]

name: Winkler, David S[tanley] [pronounced WINK-ler]
bio: (Waterford, Connecticut: 5 Oct 1949-) Learned in 1961 from Blackstone magic tricks given with bubble gum. Electrical contractor. Semi-promagician 1962-85, specialized in close-up cardtricks. Magic mail-order dealer ("Winkler's Warehouse of Wonders") in Oakdale, Connecticut, since 1986. [Wh2]

name: Winkler, Dietmar [pronounced VINK-ler]
bio: (Ehrenfriedersdorf, Germany: 31 Dec 1944-) Founder & curator of the Zirkus-und Artistenarchiv in East Berlin since 1960. Public Relations Manager of the East German State Circus. Wrote (with Gisela Winkler) Das grosse Hokuspokus: Aus dem Leben berühmter Magier (1981, 555pp; 2nd ed 1985, 551pp). Articles in Zauberkunst & Unterhaltungskunst. [Weltbühne12/4/88;Wh5]

name: Winkler, [Gerhard] "Gerd
bio: (Alsfeld, West Germany: 12 Jun 1951- ) Pro. 1981 MZvD 1st prize in comedy magic; 1983 Baden-Baden 1st prize in comedy magic; 1984 MZvD 1st prize in comedy magic & 3rd in card magic; 1985 FISM 2nd prize in card magic. Works comedy act with partner Volker Müller as "Volker & Gerd". Lives in Bochum, Germany.

name: Winkler, Gisela
bio: (Zittau, Germany: 3 Jun 1944- ) Reader in East Berlin publishing house of Henschelverlag. Non-magician. Married Dietmar Winkler in 1971. Co-authored with him Das grosse Hokuspokus (1981; 2nd ed 1985). Articles in Unterhaltungskunst. [Wh5] Winter, Professor Ludwig [pronounced VIN-ter] (Germany: fl.1840s) Pro. "Egyptian" and comedy magic in Breslau in 1849.

name: Wise, Howard D.
bio: (Mansfield, Ohio: 1882-) Teacher. Semi-pro magician. Inspired as boy seeing A. Herrmann, Kellar, Stock, & Bancroft. Learned by 1900 from box of tricks. Invented several chemical & mechanical effects including the Willmann Deck = Martin Pack.

name: Wiseman, Richard [John], PhD, AIMC
bio: (Luton, Bedfordshire, England: 16 Sep 1966-) Learned in 1977 by lessons from Rex Cooper, MIMC. Semi-pro close-up magician since 1985. In 1988 took First Class honors degree in Psychology from University College London. Later that year played the Magic Castle. Since 1989, on a 3-year scholarship, studied "The psychology of deception" (with particular attention to magicians) as part of his PhD work in the Department of Psychology at the U of Edinburgh, the 1st such work at the PhD level in Britain. Thence senior research fellow in parapsychology at the U of Hertfordshire. 1994 Cecil Lyle Award. Article in Abra. Wrote Guidelines for Testing Psychic Claims (1995, with Prof. Robert L. Morris) & Deception & Self-Deception (1997, 266pp). [Wh2]

name: Wishart, Reginald, MIMC
bio: (England: -24 Apr 1934) Stage name of John Gant. Minor pro. Played the London Crystal Palace. Pet effect: Bottle Escape. REF: Goldston (1929), 88-90.

name: Wishner, Sam
bio: (USA: fl.1920s-80s) Lived in Brooklyn. Pro magic clown as "Zovello". Teacher of magic. Invented "Zovelloscopes" (by 1936). New York NBC-TV series as "The Magic Clown" (with his hand-puppet "Laughy") 1949-1951 when replaced by Richard DuBois. Wrote The Manual for Teaching Magic (1983, 103pp). Tricks & dictionary column in HMM. [Se]

name: Witcher, Stanley
bio: See: Cubitt, A. S.

name: Witgeest, Simon
bio: (Holland: fl.1670s) Wrote an important early Dutch book on natural magic including many conjuring tricks with eggs, balls, coins, & cards: Het Nieuw Toneel der Konsten (Amsterdam: 1679, in Flemish, with later editions under various titles in 1682 [378pp] & 1695). German tr as Natürliches Zauber-Buch (Nürnberg: 1702, 920+54pp; many reprints). It was a source for Carl von Eckartshausen. A copy of the rare 1679 1st edition sold at auction in 1990 by Swann Galleries for $3,520.

name: Witkowski, Dan[iel] D. "Danny
bio: (Minneapolis, Minnesota: 1956-) Inspired at age 5 by a cereal-box magic trick. Pro during & since high school. Founder-owner since 1977 of MagicCom Inc. for illusion rentals & presenting magic productions at major public & sporting events. Video (1988). Wrote How to Haunt a House (1995, 96pp). [MUM10/85;LR4/88;Wh]

name: Witt, Wittus [pronounced VIH-tus VIT]
bio: (Bockhorst-Versmold, West Germany: 7 Aug 1949- ) Stage name of Hans-Günter Witt. Inspired in 1955 when father showed a card trick. Graphic designer & amateur magician. Famous street magician since 1973, playing the streets of Germany, Europe, & Canada. 1976 FISM 1st prize in comedy magic with partner Roy Gardner. In 1980 became full-time pro street, trade show, & stage magician. Collector, mainly of magic sets (with over 500 different ones, it is the world's largest). Editor of A-B-C of Magic Sets 1980-present & ABC of Faxic 1991-94. Wrote Taschenspieler-Tricks (1986; 2nd ed 1988); & Zauberkästen (1987), a fine book on magic sets; plus his series of 10 International Magic Yellow Pages since 1977. Column in Magische Welt 1979-present. Articles in Abra, Magic Info, Magicol, Magic Magazine. Illustrator for several magic periodicals & many magic books, including all cover designs & most illustrations for the 7 books published by Hannes Höller since 1973. Some 50 TV bits plus a special. [Genii2/92; Magicana6/91; Wh2] "Wizard, The White" SEE: Hull, Burling "Wizard of the East" SEE: Hennicke, Professor "Wizard of the North" SEE: Anderson, J. H. Anderson Jr, J. H. Anderson, Philip Prentice Hall, H. Young, E. W. "Wizard of the South" SEE: Cotten, Joseph Eagle, G. Barnardo Lennot, Professor B. Sargent, Colonel H. J. "Wizard of the West" SEE: Homar, Hermann Novra, Henry Sanger, "Lord" George de Saurin, Mons.

name: Wizardo, Heinz [pronounced VIH-zar-do]
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 21 Apr 1926-) Stage name of Heinz Krause since 1948. Inspired in 1939 by Marvelli show; learned from books. Pro close-up in East Germany since 1953. Collector of magic books, magazines, old props, movies, & many videos. Magic teacher (in Potsdam) since 1980. Consultant for the "Zauber auf Schloss Kückückstein" TV magic series (23 shows to present). Wrote Wizardo: Seminar I (1980) & Wizardo: Seminar II (1985). Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, Magisches Magazine, Innovator, & Zauberkunst. Bio & tricks in Mauerspechte (1992). [Magie4/86; Zauberkunst1986/#2; Win; Wh5]

name: Wo, Jo
bio: (Germany?: 13 Jan 1927-) Stage name of Hans Wolfsgruber. Magician in Germany. [Nad]

name: Wobensmith, James C. "Jim
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 9 Feb 1879-28 Dec 1973) Lawyer (since 1919) in Philadelphia, specialized in patent, trademark, & copyright law. Pennsylvania politician. Mason. Amateur magician since 1908 thru doing patent work for Howard Thurston. Invented Muslim Band Trick (marketed by Brema in 1922), etc. Founding President in 1920 of the SAM Philadelphia Assembly. Wrote Magic Patents, a Classified List of United States Patents Relating to Magic, Illusions and Allied Subjects (1928). SAM President 1930-31. 1972 SAM Hall of Fame. [SAM;Dor]

name: Woda, Reinhold [pronounced VO-dah]
bio: (Vienna, Austria: 26 Oct 1900-24 Nov 1970) A favorite student of Ottokar Fischer. Pro in Vienna before WW II. Wrote 5 books in German including Kartenkunst für Kenner (1940, 31pp) & Kartenkunststücke für Kartenkünstler (1947, 80pp). Tricks in HMM. [St;Al] Wohl, Dr Ronald A., PhD (Switzerland: 1936-) Amateur magician as "Ravelli", specialized in card magic and subtle mathematical tricks. Moved to USA in 1966. At Yale U 1966-67. Professor of Chemistry at Rutgers. Major collector of gambling equipment & books. Articles in Magische Welt, Ibidem, Gen, Pentagram, & Magie during period 1967-74. Also in MUM in 1991. [Wit;Wh5]

name: Wolf, Carl [Merriss]
bio: (Detroit, Michigan: 26 Dec 1932-12 Jul 2000) Learned at age 13 from library books. Chemical marketer. Semi-pro close-up & stage magician as "Merriss" since 1950. Invented Lock of Gibraltar around 1957, then manufactured it for Ken Allen who first marketed it in 1963. Also invented (c1963), made, & self-marketed the famous & often pirated Key-R-Rect. Founder-owner of Merriss Magic c1963-1997-present, originally in Detroit, later Bay Village (Ohio), lastly in Baton Rouge (Louisiana) where he continued to make Key-R-Rect. [Wh2]

name: Wolf, Dorothy
bio: (USA: -19 Jun 1965) For 22 years business manager of The Sphinx and assistant & secretary to John Mulholland. Known to have been his mistress. [Daw2]

name: Wolff, "Ed
bio: (San Antonio, Texas: 18 Jul 1881-) Inspired at age 8 seeing A. Herrmann. Head of an advertising agency in Rochester, New York. Amateur magician since 1929 when at age 48 he learned from a mail-order trick. He was Annemann's marksman for his 1935 Piff-Paff-Poof Bullet Catch. Wrote Practical Hypnotism (1936, 31pp). Trick in Tops (1941). [Th]

name: Wolfram, Eugen
bio: (Germany: 4 Jul 1906-3 Jul 1966) Awarded the "Dr Teumer-Ring" for 1972-74. Died in Dresden, East Germany. [Roh]

name: Wollert, Rolf
bio: (Stockholm, Sweden: 26 Nov 1932- ) French language teacher in Göteborg. Learned magic at age 12. Semi-pro stage magician as "Zarro-Zarro", playing variety theaters, galas, cabarets, restaurants, & streets. Often tours Africa. Now (1991) lives in Paris. [Dif;Bou] "Wonder, Tommy" SEE: Bemelman, Josef Wong, The Great (Swatow, Kwantung, China: 8 Aug 1908-18 Apr 1994) Stage name of NG Bo Oen. Learned in 1920 from watching a street magician & seeing thru his tricks. Pro stage magician since 1931. Pet effect: Linking Rings (with 6 rings lasting  $ 2\frac{1}{2} $ minutes). Founded the Magic Circle of Singapore in 1935. Dealer (Great Wong's House of Magic) in Singapore 1938-1989 when closed, destroyed by fire. 1989 New Zealand Convention best effect. Died in Singapore. Invented Diminishing Match Box (1970). See Tudor Brock, The Great Wong's Routine for the Linking Rings (1964, 16pp; new edition 1989). Trick in Linking Ring 2/70. [Wh2]

name: Wong Toy Sun
bio: See: Guest, Claud

name: Wood, Jack
bio: (Patea, Taranaki, New Zealand: 7 Jan 1917-1999) Learned at age 8 from hobby magazines. Semi-pro closeup magician since 1936. Aka "Deveen the Debonair Deceptionist". Pet effects: Card sleights & Egg Bag. Collector. Edited Te Tohunga 1947-48 & Magic Parade 1949-51. Contributor to Magicana. [Magicana10/76;Wh5]

name: Wood, Will B.
bio: (USA: -20 Feb 1908) Pro by 1889. Took 2 US illusion-device patents in 1899. Major stage magician in Latin America. Drowned in a ship sinking in the Caribbean. [Pr]

name: Woodfield, William R[ead] "Bill
bio: (USA: 21 Jan 1928-) Film & TV writer & TV producer. Writer for LIFE, Saturday Evening Post, Esquire, Playboy, etc. Amateur card magician with close interest in gambling methods. Major contributor to the biographical research on Erdnase in late 1940s. Wrote & published Magicana (1946, 2 issues). Wrote "Magicana" column in Conjuror's Magazine & Genii 1947-49. In the 1960s Frank Csuri edited & typed his notebook for limited circulation in the underground as Bill Woodfield's Gambling and Magic Notes (1961). [CA;Wh91;Wh]

name: Woods, Frank
bio: (London, England: 14 Mar 1863- ) Pro. [Go2]

name: Woods, Roger, AIMC
bio: (Rossendale, Lancs., England: 22 Jun 1953-) Solicitor in Helmshore, England. Learned at age 10 from David Nixon magic set. Lawyer as Senior Crown Prosecuter & Solicitor. Amateur close-up magician & magic historian. 1990 Northern Magic Circle's Eric Bland Trophy for magical journalism. Wrote Houdini the Myth Maker: The Unmasking of Harry Houdini (1987, 56pp, with Brian Lead). Articles in Linking Ring, Magic Circular, The Memel, Abra, & Northern Lights. [Wh2]

name: Woodward, Chris[topher David]
bio: (Birmingham, England: 7 Feb 1939-) Learned in 1948 as magician's assistant. Pro since 1960 with illusions. Aka "The Rainbow Man". Pet effects: "Anything by Harbin". In 1971 married Maurice Fogel's only child, Nadine. Collector since 1978 of Palladium & Hengler's Circus programs & posters. Article in New Pentagram. TV bit. [Genii7/63;Bo#328;Wh5]

name: Woodward, Homer S.
bio: (Angola, Indiana: 28 Dec 1842-12 May 1941) Pro in circus since age 13, working as sideshow magician. Assisted Antonio Blitz for a year. Thence on own as pro magician. Although lost his props in the 1871 Chicago fire, was back in business the next year. Later retired, moving to Omaha, Nebraska. Died wealthy. NOTE: Surname may be "Woodworth". [St]

name: Woodward Jr. [Kenneth V.] "Kenny
bio: (Uniontown, Pennsylvania: 22 May 1923- ) Learned in 1930s from travelling magicians & library books. Salesman (retired). Semi-pro general magician since 1941 working ``mud circuses' to the `legitimate stage'". Edited Mental Wise in late 1950s. Wrote "Woody's Place" column in New Tops since 1989. Articles in New Tops, Linking Ring, Mental Wise, & Laugh-Makers. [Wh2]

name: Woodward, [John] Milton "Jack
bio: (Eastbourne, England: 1900-25 Feb 1964) Inspired at age 5. Learned at age 10 from box of tricks. Debut at age 14. Pro (ex-drapery business) since 1937, initially as "The Red Admirals" with Millicent Cooper (1900-1990) in her quick-change act. British Ring President 1963-64, dying in office.

name: Woodward, [Harold Edward] "Woody
bio: (USA: 29 Sep 1900-2 Jul 1993) Bartender. Amateur magician, long active in San Francisco magic circles.

name: Woolf, Michael
bio: (Essex, England 12 June 1939 - ) From age 9 magic, puppetry, ventriloquism. Professional performer from school days. First puppeteer (Punch and Judy) on New Zealand television 1954. Magician, actor, announcer, writer. President NZ Actors' Equity 1974-78. Media lecturer, Wellington Polytechnic 1973-1990. Performer, collector and historian. Editor/Publisher "Magicana" Magazine 2000 - present. Member IBM & SAM. Lifetime

name: Worthington 3rd, Thomas C[hew]
bio: (Baltimore, Maryland: 13 Feb 1882-2 Jan 1953) A relative of Henry Ridgely Evans. First lesson from grandfather at age 6. Semi-pro magician. Debut in 1911. Founded Society of Osiris Magicians by 1925. Edited Tablets of Osiris, 1929-43. Wrote Recollections of Howard Thurston (1938, 31pp). Collector, donating his memorabilia & antique apparatus to the Circus Museum in 1952. [Go2]

name: Woulffe, Homar H.
bio: See: "Homar, Hermann"

name: Wraxall, Sir [Frederic Charles] Lascelles
bio: (England: 1828-11 Jun 1865) Translator of French & German books, specializing in military & diplomatic works. Translated (and abridged) Robert-Houdin's autobiography as The Memoirs of Robert-Houdin (1859; reprinted frequently until 1964), although misattributed in many late editions to Dr. R. Shelton Mackenzie, the minimal editor of its first American edition.

name: Wright, T[homas] Page
bio: (Fort Wayne, Indiana: 8 May 1905-21 Dec 1930) Amateur. Articles in Sphinx, most in collaboration with William Larsen Sr, since 1920. Aka "William Weber". Died in automobile accident. His collection of nearly 2,000 magic books & pamphlets went to his nephew, Bascom Jones Jr. Co-invented many tricks with Larsen, including Boudoir of a Dancing Girl (by 1928). Wrote Page Wright's Manuscript (1991, c350pp). See William Larsen, Page Wright's Notebook (57pp). "Wu, The Amazing Mr." SEE: Ritson, Richard

name: Wu-Fang-Sing
bio: See: Geary, Walter

name: Wu Ling
bio: See: Ritson, Richard

name: Wu-Li-Chang
bio: (Spain: -1945) Stage name. Pro with pseudo-Chinese act. Toured South America yearly. Died in Buenos Aires. "Wychwoods Act, The" SEE UNDER: Shaw, Audrey & Jack

name: Wye, Phil
bio: See: Upton, P. C.

name: Wyles, William Henry
bio: (Holborn, London, England: 27 Mar 1882-) Semi-pro since 1913. Wrote for Magic Wand &

name: Wyman Jr, John W. "Jack
bio: (Albany, New York: 19 Jan 1816-31 Jul 1881) Pro ventriloquist to pro magician. Authored (ghosted by E.W. Latham, a hack) Wyman's Hand-Book of Magic (1851, 70pp; with several editions) & Jokes and Anecdotes of Wyman, The Magician and Ventriloquist (1866, 112pp; repr 1871, 108pp). His nearly comprehensive scrapbook is in the Mulholland

name: Wyman, Professor
bio: (Britain: c1864-17 Oct 1904) Pro with sleight-of-hand tricks & shadowgraphy. Popular in music halls throughout the North of England. [Magic7/03]

name: Wyniama, Phineas
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name. Pro magician. Clown-magician with Barnum & Bailey Circus 1972-77, teaching at their Clown College 1976. Now a full-time mentalist & cold reader. Audio-tape autobio is Memoirs of a Circus Magician (1989).

name: X
bio: See: Sherman, Robert

name: X, Dr.
bio: See: Silver, George

name: X, Mr.
bio: See: Kwong, Jimmy Chan-Chow

name: Xavier
bio: (London, England: 2 [sic] Nov 1894-1972) Stage name of Cyril P. Clarke. Pro manipulator. Toured with Chung Ling Soo, Pooles Myrioramas, & Dr Bodie. Pro variety magician in 1930s, billed as "Xavier and Lady". Then semi-pro in London. [WWM]

name: Xenia, Madame
bio: See: Flosso, Lillian

name: Xevi
bio: (Cristina d'Aro, Spain: 19 Aug 1943- ) Stage name of Xavier SALA COSTA. Learned magic from book in 1957. Debut as "Xevi el Mago" in 1959. Pro. World tours 1972-80. ..... Many TV bits since 1965. Videos (1982, 1983). Film actor. Wrote El Meu Món Mágic (Barcelona: 1988, 150pp). [Xe;Wh5]

name: Yadu
bio: See: Belucci, Hector

name: Yamada, Akira
bio: (Shintomi-cho, Tokyo, Japan: 16 Oct 1931- ) Youngest son of SHOKYOKUSAI Tenyo from whom he learned magic. Founded the Tenyo Company in Tokyo in Apr 1960. With 48 employees (in 1989) it is the largest magic firm in Japan & one of world's 3 largest. [Wh2] SEE: Guder, Louis

name: Yamadeva
bio: (Japan: 1928 - 3 Aug 1993) Close-up magician. Winner of 1985 Tenkai Prize. Serious collector and historian on Japanese magic rather than performing magician. His collection is one of the best and is kept as the Yamamoto Library in Tokyo.

name: Yan Yow
bio: (China: fl.1850s) Billed as daughter of Tuck Quay. Pro sleights & fire-eating when she toured the USA with the "Chinese Magicians" troupe in 1853. (Japan: fl.1860s) Landed England in Feb 1867 to perform there and then traveled to Paris and other European countries as a member of a Japanese traveling troupe. He featured the Butterfly Trick. Learned from Itchosai Yanagawa. His name often appeared as Asi-kitchi-san in western newspapers at that time. He was also known as Chojuro Yanagawa.

name: Yanagawa, Itchosai
bio: (Japan: fl.1840s-60s, died c1870) Pro in Japan. Invented the Butterfly Trick or, at least, introduced it there in the early 1800s. NOTE: Given name misspelled "Icchosai". Found of the Yanagawa dynasty of magicians. He never went abroad but his pupils like Asakichi-san did. [Dif]

name: Yanagawa III, Itchosai
bio: (Japan: Nov 1847 -17 Feb 1909) Stage name of Jisaburo Aoki. Learned from Itchosai Yanagawa. One of early Japanese magicians who first appeared in Australia and NZ as a member of the Lenton and Smith's Great Dragon Japanese Troupe in 1867-1869. At that time his stage name was Chonosuke Yanagawa, later became Itchosai Yanagawa III. His pet effect were Butterfly Trick and Myoto Hikidashi (a box with two drawers, in which various items mysteriously appear, disappear and move from one drawer to the other). Performed for Emperor Meiji in 1892.

name: Yann, Tony
bio: (Switzerland: fl.1970s-80s) Daniel Eyenberger. Pro 1970-83 with a fish act. In 1980 co-founded Le Cenacle Magique 5. Credited as the only Gospel Magician in Switzerland and France today.

name: Yanoski
bio: (France: fl.1940s-70s) Stage name of Yves Bertault, aka "Yanosky". Amateur. Groupe Régional des Magiciens de la Touraine charter member in 1941 & its President since 1953. AFAP Silver Medals 1974 & 1978.

name: Yates, Jack
bio: (Accrington [sic], Lancashire, England: 28 Dec 1921- ) Mental magic. Wrote Minds in Close-Up (1954, 32pp; repr 1969) & Minds in Duplicate (1956, 32pp; repr 1969). Then moved to South Africa. Wrote Clue and other Mysteries (1986, 57pp). NOTE: The report of his death on 2 May 1971 was false. Still alive & active in magic as of 1992. Also not born in 1898. [Wh5]

name: Yates, Margaret [Patience Murray]
bio: (Sutton, Surrey, England: 9 Apr 1934- ) Learned in 1945 when bought an Ernest Sewell box of tricks, then took sleight-of-hand lessons from friend in The Magic Circle. Housewife. Semi-promagicienne since 1950, specializing in sleight-of-hand & childrens magic. Pet effect: Coins to Glass. Moved to Australia. 1961 Charles Waller Cup (Victoria Magic Circle). Collector in Warrandyte. Bought the Weirdo Collection (1,500+ books plus many magazines) in 1984. The Yates Collection is possibly largest private collection in Southern Hemisphere with 2,500 books & several thousand magazines. Articles in Magicol & Magic Circular. [Magicana4/91;Wh2]

name: Yeates Junior
bio: (England: fl.mid-1700s) Sleight-of-hand & Egg Bag work at the London fairs 1733-52, often with his father, Yeates Senior, who exhibited automata & waxworks. [Cl;Fr]

name: Yedid, Meir, AIMC
bio: (Tel Aviv, Israel: 6 May 1960- ) Inspired at age 5 by being shown some tricks. Learned around 6 or 7 from an Israeli TV show that taught a trick each week. MBrought to USA in 1970 at age 10. Pro close-up magician since 1978. Virtual inventor of finger routines plus several other close-up effects. Manager of Tannen's in NYC 1979-88. Losing a third of his right hand in a 1986 auto accident, now performs his famous finger routine left-handed. SAM 1st place in close-up 1981, & 1988. 1988 SAM originality award. Lecturer. Private dealer in Rego Park, New York (later Fair Lawn, New Jersey), since 1988. AIMC 1989. Wrote Off the Wall Lecture Notes (1983). See also Harry Lorayne, Meir Yedid's Finger Fantasies (1981); George Schindler, Close-Up Hallucinations; Gary Ouellet, The Incredible Close-Up Magic of Meir Yedid (1982, 136pp); Steven Schneiderman, Meir Yedid's Stage Stuff (1986); Harry Lorayne, Meir Yedid's Card Animations (1987); and Stephen Minch, Magical Wishes: Meir Yedid (1994, 96pp). Articles in Magic Manuscript. Video (1988). Much TV exposure in USA & abroad. [LR3/98;MUM9/94;Lo2;Fi;Wh2]

name: Yee, Shaun
bio: (Ipoh, Perak, Malaysia: 13 Jun 1944- ) Stage name of Thiam-Fook YEE since c1972. Inspired at age 12 or 13 & learned from gift magic book & some tricks. Graduated U of Malaya in 1967. Pro magician since 1969, specializing in manip but doing all types of magic & working most types of venues (night clubs, theaters, cruise ships, circus, TV, etc). Moved to Italy in 1982. Assistant-wife is Anna Yee (née Bonomi), an Italian, whom he married in 1982, training her as assistant in 1984. Wrote Cards in Action (1983, 48pp), Magia con Shaun Yee (1985, 19pp), Idee Sulla Manipolazione (1987, 30pp), Cardwitched (1988, 71pp), & Lecture Notes (1988, 36pp). Articles in Magigram & Qui Magia. [Wh2]

name: Yelma
bio: See: Lewis, Albert E.

name: Yettmah, Cyril "Yetty
bio: (England: c1883-8 Feb 1949) Pro. Invented Pigeon Catching in 1909, the Shadow Box, & the Lady from the Light. Played St. George's Hall in 1918. Worked as illusion builder for Howard Thurston in USA 1928-30. Then for Carter. Husband of Suzette Yettmah. [Pr]

name: Yettmah, Suzette
bio: (England?: fl.1930s) Wife of Cyril Yettmah who presumably taught her. Pro with Oriental act. Played St. George's Hall in 1932 with the Maskelyne troupe. [Mar]

name: Yiengst, Barry [Paul]
bio: (Hershey, Pennsylvania: 28 Dec 1948-) Learned at age 10 from gift magic set. Pro with illusion-escape act since 1984 with partner-wife Jan (married 1974) "operating the only magic show under canvas in the United States", working a 4-month summer/fall season at fairs & festivals in the northeast states with their Yiengst Magic Circus. In winter & spring they play indoor dates. Wrote Performing Escapes (30+pp). Articles in Escape, Escapism, & Escape Masters. [Wh2]

name: Yimka
bio: (Britain: fl.1940s-50s) Stage name of R.A. Scott. Pro prop maker in London for Unique Magic Studio. Best known as the builder of Arthur Dowler's Legs Table.

name: Yno, Marc
bio: (France: fl.1960-70s) Stage name of Pierre Marinot. Pro fantasy magician. In 1975 co-starred (with Otto Wessely) in Paris at the Cabinet Fantastique. NOTE: Not to be confused with Marc Aillaud who also worked as "Marc Yno". "Yoga" [Clarke's misspelling of "Prince Yuga" SEE: Shaw, Mark]

name: Yogano
bio: (France: fl.1960s-90s) Stage name of Pierre Moré. Pro illusionist working as a family. Father of Yogano Jr. [Bou2]

name: Yogano Jr.
bio: (France: fl.1980s-90s) Son of Yogano. Pro illusionist. 1988 FISM 3rd prize for invention (a levitation). 1990 Monte Carlo Grand Prix.

name: Yogi
bio: (Scotland: 1898-14 Nov 1963) Stage name of Theodore Speaker. Semi-pro variety magician in 1950s.

name: Yohe, Chauncy B. "C.B.
bio: (Bethel Park, Pennsylvania: c1904-26 Apr 1988) Engineer. Semi-pro mail-order book dealer in home town, issuing Book List No.3 in 1951 & No.7 in 1957. Wrote the mimeoed The C.B.Y Course in Magic (n.d.).

name: Yorimoto
bio: See: Maurier

name: York, Scott B. "Scotty
bio: (USA: fl.1970s-90s) Engineer in Alexandria, Virginia. Semi-pro close-up. Full-time magic bartender at Brook Farm Inn of Magic in Silver Spring in early 1980s, then part-time at the Inn of Magic in Wheaton, then at Casey's in Washington, DC, since 1988. Aka "The Silver Fox". Wrote The Scott York Lecture Book (1975, 54pp), Scott York on Coins (1975, 48pp), Scott York's Greenville Lecture Notes (9 pp), Scott York on the Cups and Balls (20pp), Decennial Prelection (22pp), Decanted Volume 1 (1991, 18pp), For Your Eyes Only (1993, 124pp), Revolutionary Routines with Aces (1995, 32pp, with Tim Conover), & Marked Coin to Wristwatch (1995, 13pp). See Jamy Ian Swiss, A Rumor in Their Own Time: A Close-Up Collaboration by Scotty York and Jamy Ian Swiss (1988, 18pp). Video bit (1994). [Wh5]

name: Yoshida, [James Kiyomi] "Jimmy
bio: (Honolulu, Hawaii: 9 Mar 1920 – 3 Jul 2011) Inspired by & learned in 1926 (at age 25) from amateur Harry Okamoto. Insurance & real estate agent in Honolulu. Semi-pro kid-show magician since 1960, aka "Tengu the Magician" (since 1946). Pet effects: Linking Silks & Bare Hand Silk Production. Also dealer since 1960 with magic shop (including school for magicians) in Honolulu. [MUM4/82;Wh2]

name: Yost, Thomas W.
bio: (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: 15 Mar 1832-11 Oct 1917) Pro dealer-prop maker (Yost & Company) in Philadelphia 1870-1902 when he retired, hiring Edward H. "Ned" Collins as manager. Yost sold the company in 1914 to Clyde W. Powers of New York.

name: Young, E. W.
bio: See: Young, Wellington

name: Young, John [H.], MIMC
bio: (Stafford?, England: c1904-) Inspired at age 6. Civil engineer (retired). Joined The Magicians' Club in 1928. Semi-pro stage magician & prop maker. Assistant to Leonard Nicoll in London in early 1930s. MIMC 1933. Served in the Royal Engineers 1940-46, ending as a major. Edited Magic Circular 1949-72. [MC1/90]

name: Young, Dr Morris N., MD
bio: (Lawrence, Massachusetts: 20 Jul 1909-13 Nov 2002) Eye surgeon. Amateur collector of magic books. In 1950 co-founded Magic Collectors Association; and edited its official journal, Magicol 1950-52. Donated his large book collection in 1955 to the Library of Congress. Wrote Presto Prestige (1929, 48pp), Hobby Magic (1950, 207pp), The Art and Craft of Magic (1957, 15pp), & Bibliography of Memory (1961, 436pp), and co-authored (with Walter Gibson) 2 books on Houdini (see). Articles in Linking Ring, Conjuriana, & Collectors Annual.

name: Young, Paul
bio: (USA: fl.1950s) Probably invented Professor's Nightmare (in 1950s).

name: Young, [John] Phillip
bio: (Tulsa, Oklahoma: 12 Mar 1963- ) Artist, photographer, designer in Tulsa. Became interested in magic in 1973 seeing a 2-hour live magic show. Semi-pro close-up since 1981. Wrote Fingers Don't Entertain, People Do (1982) & Magical You! (forthcoming). Articles in Trapdoor & Magic Manuscript. Contributions to books by Steve Beam & Jeff White. Illustrator & graphic designer for many books since 1978. [Wh2]

name: Young, [E.] Wellington
bio: (Britain: fl.1840s-50s) Minor pro stage magician & vent. Billed as "The Enchanter of the East", "The Great Northern Wizard", & "The Great Wizard of the North". Performed for Queen Victoria & Prince Albert at Arundel Castle in 1846. [Fr;Cl;La]

name: Young, William Henry
bio: (Boston, Massachusetts: 26 Nov 1821-26 Apr 1874) Pro by 1840. Worked for Barnum. Bio is James Hagy, The One Young (1988, 94pp). [Mo;Cl]

name: Younger, Edmund
bio: (England: 28 Dec 1892-dead) Magic dealer in 1920s. Semi-pro stage magician in with pseudo-Chinese act as "Li-Chung-Soo" in 1930s-40s. Visited magicians in USA in 1939. Trick in Jinx.

name: Yrigoras
bio: (Spain: fl.1960s) Stage name of Miguel YRIGORAS RATO. 1966 Grand Prize at the 1st Festival Mágico in Portugal.

name: Yuga
bio: See: Shaw, Mark

name: Yuka
bio: See: Shimoda, Yuka

name: Yung Len Tu, MIMC
bio: (England: Sep 1888-) Stage name of Capt. Leonard C. Nicoll. Pro stage magician with oriental magic & illusions, assisted by Mdlle Hwung Sen & Co. Joined The Magic Circle in 1930. Played London with John Young as his assistant in the early 1930s. [Daw2]

name: Yvonne
bio:
222

[See also: Authors, Yvonne]

name: Z, Dr.
bio: See: De Soboll, F. Stephen

name: Z, Mr
bio: See: Zaleta, Lex

name: Zabin, Azra
bio: (Germany?: 1 Apr 1915-) Stage name of Paul Hetzel. Magician in Germany. [Nad] (Bangladesh: 1966-) From Orthodox Moslem family. Self-taught from books. Pro. The leading magicienne in South Asia.

name: Zaccharini
bio: (Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia: 24 Aug 1956-) Stage name of Anand "Zac" Zechariah, son of a prominent local politician. Learned at age 8 from aunt's gift of a David Berglas book. General manager of a Shell Company. Part-time pro sleight-of-hand artist & stage illusionist since 1972. Does a comedy club act called "Zaccharini's Magic Cocktail". Pet effects: Levitation, Linking Rings, & Dancing Cane. [Wh2]

name: Zachary, James E. "Jim", MIMC
bio: (USA: fl.1950-90s) Student of Slydini. Pro with a paddle & dice-stacking act (15 high). Worked as wood prop maker for Ken Allen c1960 & then on own as "Jim Zee". Probably invented Hot Rod (c1970). SAM President 1980-81. Retired from performing in 1987. TV bits. Video (forthcoming).

name: Zada, Ali
bio:
"Zadma, The Great" SEE: Mannix, Daniel P.

[See also: Logrenia, Charles]

name: Zaleta, Lex
bio: (Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania: 3 Jun 1947-) Learned in early teens from father & books, later lessons from Mysterious Novak & Slydini. High school teacher of English in Clarks Summit, Pennsylvania since 1969. Semi-pro stage, close-up, mental magic. Pet effect: Corinda's One in a Million. Dealer-demonstrator as "Mr Z Magic Enterprises" in Clark's Summit, Pennsylvania. Wrote A Demonstrator's Dream: Part One (1978, 20 pp), Getting Down to Business (1978, 48 pp); A Demonstrator's Dream: Part Two (1981, 20 pp), & Getting Down to More Business (1981, 38 pp). [Wh2] "Zam, The Great" SEE: Zamloch, Carl E.

name: Zamloch, Carl E.
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-60s) Football coach. Semi-promagician as "The Great Zam". Pet publicity stunt: Blindfold Drive. Magic Castle member #R-182 in 1963.

name: Zanardelli
bio: (Italy: fl.1860s) Son-in-law of Eugene Bosco. Minor pro prestidigitator in mid-1860s when toured Italy as first partner of Patrizio. [Dif]

name: Zancig, Ada F." Agnes
bio: (USA: fl.1920s) School teacher in Brooklyn & a devout Spiritualist. In 1917 married Julius Zancig, doing two-person mentalism with him 1920-29. [Pr;Bam]

name: Zancig, Agnes
bio: (Copenhagen?, Denmark: -8 Apr 1916) Born Agnes Claussen. A hunchback. Moved to USA. Married Julius Zancig in 1888. Pro two-person mentalism with him until her death in Washington, D.C. Authored Fortune Telling with Cards ([by 1905], 150pp). [Pr]

name: Zancig, Julius
bio: (Copenhagen?, Denmark: 7 Mar 1857-27 [sic] Jul 1929) Stage name of Julius Jörgensen (or Jensen). Moved to USA c1888. Iron foundry worker. Amateur mentalist with two-person mind-reading act with first wife Agnes. Pro since 1899 with assistants Agnes (1899-1915), Paul "Rosini" Vucci (1917), David Bamberg (1917-18 as "Syko"), and second wife Ada ("Agnes", 1920-29). In 1922 Ada converted him to Spiritualism. SAM Member #73. World tour 1903-04 of Denmark, South Africa (6 months), Ceylon, India, Burma, Hong Kong, Canton, Macao, Manila, Shanghai, Peking, Korea, & Japan. Toured England in 1906-08, 1909, 1911-13, & 1924. In 1927 moved to Santa Monica, California, where he died. Wrote New Complete Palmistry (1902, 299pp), How to Zancig (New York: n.d.), Two Minds with but a single thought (London: 1907, 78pp), Forty Lessons in Palmistry (1914), & Adventures in Many Lands (1924). See Laura Fixen, True Secrets of Mindreading as Performed by the Zancigs (n.d.); & F. Wicks, Thought Reading: Zancignalling (1907, 104pp). [Bam;Pr;Osirian9/1925;Go2;Vo58;St;Magic3/07;Silver]

name: Zandor
bio:
(Switzerland: fl.1940s-50s) FISM 2nd prizes in manip in 1948 & 1950.

[See also: Sandh, Ernst]

name: Zanoni
bio: (USA: fl.1930s) Stage name of Fred Foley. Semi-pro in Greensburg, Pennsylvania.

name: Zanzic
bio: (New Orleans, Louisiana: 28 Jul 1867-) Stage name of Harry Robertstein. Pro since 1886. [Pr]

name: Zarena, Miss
bio: (Scotland: 14 Jan 1927- ) Stage name of Mary Elizabeth "Mae" Howie. 1953 Craig Trophy. Continued stage act into the 1960s. [Mar]

name: Zarro-Zarro
bio: See: Wollert, Rolf

name: Zarrow, Herb[ert G.], CPA, MIMC
bio: (Paterson, New Jersey: 4 Nov 1925 – 11 May 2008) Inspired and learned at age 11-12 from Gilbert magic set & library books. Accountant in New Jersey. Amateur closeup with cards & coins. Innovator & improver in card & close-up magic. Invented Zarrow shuffle around 1953-54, having "worked on it at various times, from late forties" & published it in 1957 in Phoenix. MIMC 1995. Louie Award 1998. Tricks in Epilogue, Pallbearers, Chronicles, Apocalypse, Rigamarole, MUM, & Linking Ring plus books by Vernon, Fulves, Lorayne, Kaufman, Crosthwaite, etc. [MUM9/95;Wh2]

name: Zartola
bio: See: Heverly, Linden Vernon

name: Zaskabel
bio: (Czechoslovakia?: 1922-) Stage name of W. Ruzicka. Illusionist. [Nad]

name: Zauber
bio: See: Schultz, Edd

name: Zauber-Klaus
bio: See: Edelhoff, Klaus

name: Zaveen
bio: See: Zabin, Azra

name: Zavis, William [Maurice] "Bill", MIMC
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 8 Aug 1935- ) Inspired at age 5 seeing a magician (Joe Davis) & learned from a gift magic set. Paid debut with kid-shows at age 13. Theater actor-director-writer & pro magician (cabaret, stage, & close-up) until 1964 when became US Foreign Service Officer (USIA). Thence amateur magician since 1964 with lectures & convention performances in USA, Europe, & South Africa. Collector of magic books. 1973 FISM 3rd prize in close-up. Wrote Divers Deceits (1973, 80pp) & Sundry Deceits (forthcoming 1992). Tricks in Sphinx, Phoenix, Genii, Gen, Abra, Pabular, Epilogue, & Arcane. [Wh2]

name: Zea, Carlos
bio: (Columbia: fl.1980s) Pro manip & dove act. Prize-winner. Toured USA in 1989.

name: Zealando, Jon [Trevor John Hodson]
bio: (Auckland, New Zealand: 9 Oct 1939-) Inspired by John Calvert in 1950. Pro. since 1958. Magic, escapes, vent., fire-eating, psychic surgery expose. "World Surprise Show1969 & 1971"(Japan.) "That's Incredible 1983," Guinness Book of Records 1980. Life Member, "Brotherhood of Auckland Magicians." Inventions: "Ironing Board Levitation 1963;" "Electronic Flash Wand 1978;" "Chatter Ring Improvements 1997;" "Invisible Gimmick Card Rise 1982." Floating Ball Routine 1990. "Benny Award 1972:" (N.Z.Variety Artists Club.) 1985 (with late wife Janet) Grand Master of Magic 1985. Living legend Award 2006 - 50 yrs as a professional magician. The Brotherhood of Auckland Magicians. Articles in "Magicana," "Magiram," "Genii," "The Linking Ring" Zeanit. The Great (England: fl.1930s-40s) Stage name of Edward Greenwood, aka "Chung Ling". Pro stage illusionist. In WW II toured with Aimee Swaine in ENSA.

name: Zee, Eric
bio: (Britain: fl.1970s-80s) Stage name of Eric Lindsey. Pro stage illusionist as "Zee & Company". Premiered Eric Lewis' Twister illusion in 1982 in Britain. Played USA in 1982-83. Co-star (with Johnny Hart) at the short-lived Magic Castle in London 1985-86. Žejmo, Tadeusz (Poland: 1928-1987) Magician specialized in childrens magic. [Nad]

name: Zelka
bio: (London?, England: fl.1960s-70s) Stage name of Bernard Hughes. Son of Jack Hughes. Pro illusionist in 1960s. Joined as partner in father's "Maker of Magic" workshop in Kings Lynn, Norfolk, briefly in mid-1970s.

name: Zella, Frank" [pen name]
bio: (England: -Dec 1935) Stage name of Wilfrid F. Clarke. Pro maker of magic props in 1st decade of 1900s in London where he was Manager (and partner with Ernest Noakes) of The City Magical Company from 1906 until 1910 when it was bought by Servais Le Roy. Then as business manager for the Servais Le Roy Company 1910-13. SEE: Grant, U. F.

name: Zelleno, LeClair
bio: (USA: 17 Mar 1878-3 Jul 1934) Pro in Cincinnati by 1902, billed as "The Mystic". SAM member #74.

name: Zelpy
bio: (Rome, Italy: 18 Mar 1936-29 Apr 2003) Stage name of Prof. Dott. Giampaolo Zelli. Learned at age 13 from book. Professor of Surgery, U of Rome. Amateur magician with popular stage act in Europe. Pet effects: silk magic. 1967 FISM 2nd prize for general magic. Invented Polaroid Divination = The Polaroid Card (1965), The Magic Statue (1970), The Pigeon (1976, a dove that produces magicians). Wrote Magia delle mani (1967, 70pp). Articles in Magia Moderna, Qui Magia, Linking Ring, etc. [LR8/83;Wh5]

name: Zemour, Joseph
bio: (Algeria: 14 Jun 1872-28 Sep 1930) Pro magician & snake charmer. Toured thru North Africa. Noted for skill.

name: Zenner, Peter [pronounced ZENN-er]
bio: (Chesterfield, England: 16 Aug 1948-) Stage name of Peter Estyn Jones. Became interested in magic at age 10 and started performing at age 14. Did a silk act with girl assistant as "Estyn Jones & Estelle" 1964-68. Then solo as Estyn Jones doing mixed magic until gradual change to mentalism. Semi-pro mentalist & hypnotist since 1973 as "Peter Zenner" (from "Zenner diodes" & not, as widely assumed, from Zener Cards) & full-time pro since 1978. Articles in Budget, Vibrations, Abra, & Magick. [Abra#2202;Wh2]

name: Zens, M[ichael] F. "Mike
bio: (Kenosha, Wisconsin: 24 Feb 1877-Jul 1952) Inspired at age 8 seeing Alexander Herrmann show. Learned at age 8 reading magic instructions printed inside gum wrappers. Semi-pro magician. Assistant postmaster for Kenosha 1908-1940 when retired. Moved to Los Angeles in early 1940s. Invented Zens' Card Miracle (1907), Zens' Cards and Envelopes (1907), & later Quadruple Poker Deal. Wrote The Cardology of Tomorrow (1941). Moved from Kenosha to Los Angeles in early 1940s. Died in home town. After Zens' death Joe Berg bought all rights to his tricks. Trick in Chap's Scrapbook. [Th]

name: Zerzawy, Dr Kurt
bio: (Austria?: fl.1980s-90s) Theatrical historian in Vienna. Articles in Hokuspokus fidibus (1989) & Hokuspokus Zauberkunst (1993).

name: Zetterström, Hans
bio: (Sweden: 1877-1946) Publisher. Amateur magician. Wrote Sällskap där man haft roligt (1945), which includes a chapter about magicians he had seen. [St]

name: Zgoda, Lou[is A.]
bio: (Ambridge, Pennsylvania: c1910-11 Apr 1996) Pro performer & dealer in Ambridge & Beaver, Pennsylvania. As "Loudini" did fraternal, service club, & kid shows.

name: Zialcita, José
bio: (Philippines: fl.1960s-80s) From prominent political family. Pro sleight-of-hand artist. Has toured widely outside home country. Lives in Manila.

name: Ziegler, Helmut
bio: (Graz, Austria: 4 Mar 1929-) Inspired seeing magician in a rehabilitation hospital in 1969. Learned that year in the Graz Magic Circle. Foot-technology engineer. Amateur general magician & manipulator, specializing in stage & micro magic. 1980 Graz Grand Prix, 1987 Lodz Grand Prix, plus several 1st to 3rd prizes throughout Europe. Articles in Aladin (Austria) & Red Pages (Switzerland). [Mec;Wh2]

name: Ziekman, Cas G.
bio: (Amsterdam, Holland: -1988) Pro magician, specialized in kid-shows. Known for his uniquely designed Cups-&-Balls, which he made since 1946. Prominent dealer in Amsterdam since 1946 when he founded Mephisto-Huis. Published-edited De Magiër as house organ 1947-68. Toured Liberia in 1966. Sold Mephisto-Huis in 1974 to a 5-partner consortium (including Dirk De Graeve) who moved it to Belgium. Uncle of Robert Ziekman. [Mec]

name: Ziekman, Robert [Ignatius] "Rob
bio: (Nijmegen, Holland: 9 Sep 1946-) Learned at age 12 by lessons from his paternal uncle, Cas Ziekman. Popular semi-pro kid-show magician. Wrote Magic for Children (1989, 47pp). ..... [Wh5]

name: Zimmerman, Diana [Sandra]
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 26 Apr 1949- ) Learned at age 8 from a friend & by buying tricks. Debut at age 16. Pro with stage pickpocket act as "Diana, the Enchantress". Won various awards in 1961, 1963, & 1965. Married Dick Zimmerman at the Magic Castle in 1968. 1981 AMA Award of Merit. Articles in Genii. [Mag;HC;Wh2]

name: Zimmerman, [Charles] Richard "Dick
bio: (Charleston, West Virginia: 11 Aug 1937-) Inspired as child seeing Blackstone. Learned in 1944 from "Peter the Rabbit" magic set. Moved to southern California in 1947. Tutored by Señor Maldo 1952-60 & Bob Haskell 1956-60. 8 PCAM contest trophies for originality 1956-63. Invented Linking Hula Hoops (c1958). 1968 AMA Best Lecturer. Pro close-up & stand-up magician since 1975. AMA Board Member 1972-78, 1983-90. Director of AMA's annual "It's Magic" show in Los Angeles c1968-1988. 1986 AMA Award of Merit. Many articles in Genii since 1959. Many TV bits. [Genii11/83; HC; Mag; Wat; Wh2]

name: Zingone, Luis "Louis" G. [pronounced zin-GO-nee]
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Pro cardman, working vaudeville & private parties. Mastered Erdnase while working at a car wash. Invented Zingone Spread (by 1940). Did a Victor phonograph 3-record set (with 6-page illustrated manual) on card tricks (1941). Appeared in M-G-M Hollywood movies. Trick in Pallbearers. [Ho]

name: Zipfel, Bishop Paul [Albert]
bio: (St. Louis, Missouri: 22 Sep 1935-) Learned in 1950 from books & local magicians. Roman Catholic priest, later bishop. Amateur close-up & stage magician since 1961. Aka "Sneaky Priest". Pet effects: Cups-&-Balls & Linking Rings. Articles in Legerdemain, MUM, & Linking Ring. [LR9/04;Wh2]

name: Zirka
bio: (Ratibor, Germany: 1877-9 Jun 1910) Stage name of Agnes Martini. Married L'Homme Masqué who taught her magic. Invented tiptilt in 1903. Pro cigarette act since 1905, billed as the "La Reine des Cigarières" (The Queen of Cigarettes). [Dif]

name: Ziska
bio: (USA: 21 Sep 1875-4 Feb 1926) Stage name of William Griffin. Learned assisting A. Herrmann & J. Zancig. Pro comedy magician. [Pr;Bam,p.46]

name: Zmeck, [Joachim] "Jochen
bio: (Berlin, Germany: 28 May 1929- ) Learned at age 10 from friend & buying from magic shop. Ex-teacher. Pro comedy & kid-show magician since 1958 in East Germany. Tours of West Germany, Poland, Czechoslovakia, Austria, Switzerland, Finland, USSR, Syria, & Iraq. Collector (over 2,000 books & booklets). Invented or improved some 300 tricks. Awarded the "Dr Teumer-Ring" 1966. 1981 East German Art Prize. Wrote Wunderwelt Magie (1965; 7 reprints), Das grosse Buch der Magie (1968; 2 reprints), Handbuch der Magie (1978; 5 reprints), Bellachini und die Eierfrau (1981, for children), Zauber ABC (1986, for children), plus 22 booklets. Articles in Magie, Magische Welt, Magisches Magazin, Zauberkunst, Aladin, Innovator, & Hokus Pokus. Bio & tricks in Mauerspechte (1992). [Win;Wh2] "Zodias, The" SEE: Lane, Charles

name: Zola, Dr Boris "Doc", DDS
bio: (USA: fl.1930s-40s) Dentist in Saginaw, Michigan. Amateur magician. Made precision gimmicks for friends. Invented Squash, which was pirated by Percy Abbott & advertised by Abbott's in its 1st ad (Dec 1933 Linking Ring). Also invented Silver Extraction. [Ir]

name: Zolano
bio: (Germany: 17 Jan 1925-) Stage name of Willi Kessler. Magician. [Nad]

name: Zoller, Peps [A.]
bio: (Munich, Germany: 11 Sep 1937- ) Learned card tricks in 1945. Police captain (criminal department) in West Germany. Semi-pro close-up & stage magician (done to humorous patter) since 1959. Wrote Bube, Dame, Zocker, Knast (1970, 183pp). Articles in Magie & Intermagic. [Wh2]

name: Zollweg, Ron[ald Fredrick]
bio: (Rochester, New York: 29 Dec 1934- ) Learned in 1950 from school library books. Professor of English & Philosophy. Part-time pro close-up & stage (with some illusions) since 1953. Pet effects: Miser's Dream, Linking Rings, Gypsy String, & Cards Across. Aka "Ron Fredrick" 1973-present. Wrote The Professional Routines of Ron Fredrick (1982, 47pp) & It's Commercial (1986, 38pp). Articles in MUM & Precursor. [Wh2]

name: Zolotow, Maurice
bio: (New York City, NY: 23 Nov 1913-14 Mar 1991) Freelance non-fiction writer on show-biz biographies. Amateur magician. Wrote It Takes All Kinds (1952, 304pp), which includes good profiles of several magicians. In 1980s wrote profiles of Houdini & Ricky Jay for Los Angeles Magazine. A memoir is Confessions of a Racetrack Fiend (1983). Authored one novel, The Great Balsamo (1946), about magic & escapism. Contributing editor to The Conjurors' Magazine. Died of cardiac arrest. [CA;Wh2] "Zomahs, The" SEE: Giddings, Alfred

name: Zoss, [Thomas Warner] "Tom
bio: (South Bend, Indiana: 27 Jul 1945-) Learned at age 9 when introduced by father to Percy Abbott & Harlan Tarbell. Attorney with advertising firm in home city. Semi-pro comedy & mental magician since working wat thru college. Columnist since 1972 for MUM & New Tops. Wrote Finding the Money in Magic (1975), Becoming Known (1977), & Zoss Does Tricks Too! (1978). [Wh2]

name: Zufall, Bernard
bio: (New York City, NY: 6 Jun 1894- ) An officer with GE. Began interest in mnemonics & magic in 1908. Semi-pro Giant Memory act, billed as "The Human Encyclopedia". Also billed as "The Mental Magician". Had world's largest collection of works on mnemonics, which he presented to Yale U Library. Wrote Zufall's Memory Trix (6 parts, 1940). [SAM; St; WWM; LR6/39]

name: Zum Pocco
bio: (Valenciennes, Nord, France: 14 Oct 1942-) Stage name of Michel Décamps since 1961. Learned card trick at age 5 from a friend. Electronic & mechanical engineer (now in Val-de-Reuil since 1986). Semi-pro magician since age 19. Specialized in billiard ball manip and since 1967 in mind reading, with assistant-wife "Zumette". In 1970 opened a shop in Caen that sold only his rhinestone-covered billiard balls & magic books. AFAP President 1988-present. Wrote Magie des boules (1968, 44pp), Giant Billard Balls (1980, 14pp, with Peter Gloviczki, in English, French, & German), & (co-authored with Georges Cartier) Encyclopedie des boules de billard (2 vols, 1985, 1987, 250+300pp). Articles in Le Journal de la Prestidigitation. [J. de la Pr.10/88; Bou2; Wh2]

name: Zumette
bio: (France: 6 Aug 1941-) Stage name of Annic Décamps (née Rignol). In 1967 married Michel "Zum Pocco" Décamps, becoming his assistant in their 2-person mind-reading act.

name: Zweers, John U., MIMC
bio: (Chicago, Illinois: 19-15 Jan 2004). Learned from Gilbert Mysto Magic set & lessons from Bill Larsen Sr & Floyd Thayer. Semi-pro magician as illusionist, collector, historian, writer, & puppeteer in southern California. SAM President 1966-67. President, SAM Hall of Fame & Magic Museum 1970-present. SAM Hall of Fame 1980. MIMC 1986. Teacher of Michael D. Douglass. Co-authored (with Herman Hanson) The Magic Man (1974, 104pp). Articles in MUM & Genii. Associate Editor MUM. Editor Magic Museum Messenger. [MUM11/97;Se;Wh2]
